```rust
//! Detached phone display — a scrcpy-style attach, built natively.
//!
//! When the user clicks the android icon (or presses alt+a), RomaCode no
//! longer squeezes the phone into the terminal: it opens a **real desktop
//! window** owned by this same process — the live compositor framebuffer is
//! blitted straight into a native OS window (minifb: X11/XWayland, macOS
//! AppKit, Windows GDI — compiled in, no browser, no HTTP server, no
//! external binary, no MCP) exactly like attaching scrcpy to a device.
//!
//! scrcpy input parity, wired straight into the same device command queue
//! the TUI mouse path uses:
//!   left mouse       tap (drag beyond slop → swipe)
//!   right mouse      BACK
//!   middle mouse     HOME
//!   mouse wheel      vertical scroll (synthetic swipe)
//!   keyboard         typing + enter/backspace; esc = BACK; home key = HOME
//!
//! The terminal stays fully free for the agent; the live stream only runs
//! while a window is actually watching (`Display::demand`), so a closed
//! window costs nothing. Without a desktop display server (SSH console, CI)
//! the window simply cannot open and the inline terminal panel takes over.

use crate::device::{Frame, FrameHub, PhoneKey};
use crate::net::Net;
use romacode_shared::protocol::{AndroidAction, ClientRequest};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

/// Letterbox color for the aspect-fit desktop window background.
const LETTERBOX: u32 = 0x101014;
/// Finger slop (px): a press that moves less than this is a tap.
const SWIPE_SLOP: i64 = 10;

/// Collects the characters minifb receives while pumping (typed text) so the
/// next tick can send them to the device — the same Cmd::Text path the
/// fullscreen TUI uses.
struct CharSink(Arc<Mutex<Vec<char>>>);

impl minifb::InputCallback for CharSink {
    fn add_char(&mut self, c: u32) {
        let Some(ch) = char::from_u32(c) else { return };
        if let Ok(mut v) = self.0.lock() {
            if v.len() < 256 {
                v.push(ch);
            }
        }
    }
}

pub struct PhoneWindow {
    win: minifb::Window,
    /// Latest frames streamed from the brain.
    hub: FrameHub,
    /// Device input goes over the wire (taps, swipes, keys, text).
    net: Arc<Net>,
    /// Characters typed into the window since the last pump.
    chars: Arc<Mutex<Vec<char>>>,
    buf: Vec<u32>,
    buf_dims: (usize, usize),
    /// Content rect inside the window buffer: (x, y, w, h) — the aspect-fit
    /// device screen; the rest is letterbox.
    content: (usize, usize, usize, usize),
    /// Device framebuffer size the content rect maps into.
    device: (u32, u32),
    last_gen: u64,
    /// Left-press position in device coords (tap vs swipe decided on release).
    press: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    had_right: bool,
    had_middle: bool,
    last_buttons: (bool, bool, bool),
    frames_blitted: u64,
}

impl PhoneWindow {
    /// Create the desktop window. Fails when there is no display server
    /// (headless console / CI) — the caller falls back to the inline panel.
    pub fn open(hub: FrameHub, net: Arc<Net>, title: String) -> Result<Self, String> {
        // The brain streams device frames; geometry comes from the first one
        // (or the legacy default before it lands).
        let (dw, dh) = hub
            .take_frame(0)
            .map(|f| (f.w.max(1), f.h.max(1)))
            .unwrap_or((720, 1560));
        // half resolution: aspect-exact for the panel (2:1 integer downsample
        // keeps every device pixel crisp) and fits an 800 px-high desktop
        let (ww, wh) = (
            (dw / 2).clamp(160, 720) as usize,
            (dh / 2).clamp(320, 1560) as usize,
        );
        let win = minifb::Window::new(
            &title,
            ww,
            wh,
            minifb::WindowOptions {
                resize: true,
                scale: minifb::Scale::X1,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .map_err(|e| format!("no desktop display server ({e})"))?;
        let chars = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let mut win = win;
        win.set_input_callback(Box::new(CharSink(chars.clone())));
        Ok(Self {
            win,
            hub,
            net,
            chars,
            buf: vec![LETTERBOX; ww * wh],
            buf_dims: (ww, wh),
            content: (0, 0, ww, wh),
            device: (dw, dh),
            last_gen: 0,
            press: None,
            had_right: false,
            had_middle: false,
            last_buttons: (false, false, false),
            frames_blitted: 0,
        })
    }

    #[allow(dead_code)] // window state introspection for debugging
    pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
        self.win.is_open()
    }

    /// How many compositor frames reached the desktop window.
    #[allow(dead_code)] // exposed for e2e window scripts
    pub fn frames_blitted(&self) -> u64 {
        self.frames_blitted
    }

    /// Pump once per TUI tick: input → device commands, latest compositor
    /// frame → desktop window. Returns false when the window was closed by
    /// the user (caller drops it and falls back to the inline panel).
    pub fn pump(&mut self) -> bool {
        if !self.win.is_open() {
            return false;
        }
        // stream demand is owned by App.poll (window open → Stream on)
        self.pump_chars();
        self.pump_keys();
        self.pump_mouse();
        self.pump_frame();
        self.win.is_open()
    }

    /// Typed text → device (the same Cmd::Text the fullscreen TUI sends).
    fn pump_chars(&mut self) {
        let drained: Vec<char> = self
            .chars
            .lock()
            .map(|mut v| std::mem::take(&mut *v))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let mut text = String::new();
        for c in drained {
            match c {
                '\n' | '\r' => {
                    self.flush_text(&mut text);
                    self.send_key(PhoneKey::Enter);
                }
                '\u{8}' | '\u{7f}' => {
                    self.flush_text(&mut text);
                    self.send_key(PhoneKey::Del);
                }
                c if (c as u32) < 32 => {} // control chars the device can't type
                c => {
                    if text.len() < 128 {
                        text.push(c);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        self.flush_text(&mut text);
    }

    fn flush_text(&mut self, text: &mut String) {
        if !text.is_empty() {
            let t = std::mem::take(text);
            self.send_text(&t);
        }
    }

    /// scrcpy key parity: esc = BACK, home key = HOME. (enter/backspace are
    /// handled as chars so no platform double-fires.)
    fn pump_keys(&mut self) {
        if self
            .win
            .is_key_pressed(minifb::Key::Escape, minifb::KeyRepeat::No)
        {
            self.send_key(PhoneKey::Back);
        }
        if self
            .win
            .is_key_pressed(minifb::Key::Home, minifb::KeyRepeat::No)
        {
            self.send_key(PhoneKey::Home);
        }
    }

    fn mouse_pos(&self) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
        let (x, y) = self.win.get_mouse_pos(minifb::MouseMode::Clamp)?;
        self.to_device(x, y)
    }

    /// Window-buffer coords → device coords through the aspect-fit rect.
    fn to_device(&self, wx: f32, wy: f32) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
        let (ox, oy, cw, ch) = self.content;
        let (fx, fy) = self.device;
        if cw == 0 || ch == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let x = ((wx - ox as f32) * fx as f32 / cw as f32).round();
        let y = ((wy - oy as f32) * fy as f32 / ch as f32).round();
        if x < 0.0 || y < 0.0 || x >= fx as f32 || y >= fy as f32 {
            None
        } else {
            Some((x as u32, y as u32))
        }
    }

    /// Left button = tap/swipe (decided on release, like the TUI panel path);
    /// right = BACK; middle = HOME; wheel = vertical scroll — scrcpy parity.
    fn pump_mouse(&mut self) {
        let right = self.win.get_mouse_down(minifb::MouseButton::Right);
        let middle = self.win.get_mouse_down(minifb::MouseButton::Middle);
        let left = self.win.get_mouse_down(minifb::MouseButton::Left);
        if std::env::var("ROMACODE_WINDOW_DEBUG").is_ok() {
            let cur = (left, right, middle);
            if cur != self.last_buttons {
                eprintln!("[window] buttons left={left} right={right} middle={middle}");
                self.last_buttons = cur;
            }
        }
        if right && !self.had_right {
            self.send_key(PhoneKey::Back);
        }
        self.had_right = right;
        if middle && !self.had_middle {
            self.send_key(PhoneKey::Home);
        }
        self.had_middle = middle;

        if left && self.press.is_none() {
            self.press = self.mouse_pos();
            if std::env::var("ROMACODE_WINDOW_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                let at = self.press;
                eprintln!("[window] press down at {at:?}");
            }
        } else if !left {
            if let Some(p0) = self.press.take() {
                let p1 = self.mouse_pos().unwrap_or(p0);
                let out = press_outcome(p0, p1);
                if std::env::var("ROMACODE_WINDOW_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                    eprintln!("[window] press up {p0:?} -> {p1:?} (tap/swipe decided)");
                }
                self.send_action(out);
            }
        }

        if let Some((_, dy)) = self.win.get_scroll_wheel() {
            if dy != 0.0 {
                if std::env::var("ROMACODE_WINDOW_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                    eprintln!("[window] wheel dy={dy}");
                }
                // Frame-derived swipe so the gesture covers the middle 50%
                // of the actual device display rather than a hardcoded
                // 720×1560 region. Fall back to a sane default before the
                // first frame arrives so the wheel still works at boot.
                let (fw, fh) = self.device;
                self.send_action(wheel_cmd(dy > 0.0, fw, fh));
            }
        }
    }

    // ── device input over the wire ──

    fn send_action(&self, action: AndroidAction) {
        self.net.fire(ClientRequest::Android { action });
    }

    fn send_key(&self, key: PhoneKey) {
        self.send_action(AndroidAction::Key {
            key: key.as_str().to_string(),
        });
    }

    fn send_text(&self, text: &str) {
        self.send_action(AndroidAction::Text {
            text: text.to_string(),
        });
    }

    /// Blit the newest compositor frame; letterbox while the phone boots.
    fn pump_frame(&mut self) {
        match self.hub.take_frame(self.last_gen) {
            Some(f) => {
                self.last_gen = f.gen;
                if (f.w, f.h) != self.device {
                    self.device = (f.w, f.h);
                }
                let (w, h) = self.win.get_size();
                if (w, h) != self.buf_dims {
                    self.buf_dims = (w, h);
                    self.buf = vec![LETTERBOX; w.max(1) * h.max(1)];
                }
                self.content = blit(&f, &mut self.buf, w, h);
                let _ = self.win.update_with_buffer(&self.buf, w, h);
                self.frames_blitted += 1;
            }
            None => {
                // still pump the OS event loop so the window stays responsive
                self.win.update();
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The same tap/swipe decision the fullscreen TUI and the old browser page
/// made: a move beyond the slop is a swipe, anything shorter is a tap.
fn press_outcome(down: (u32, u32), up: (u32, u32)) -> AndroidAction {
    let dx = (down.0 as i64 - up.0 as i64).abs();
    let dy = (down.1 as i64 - up.1 as i64).abs();
    if dx + dy > SWIPE_SLOP {
        AndroidAction::Swipe {
            x1: down.0,
            y1: down.1,
            x2: up.0,
            y2: up.1,
        }
    } else {
        AndroidAction::Tap { x: up.0, y: up.1 }
    }
}

/// Mouse wheel → a vertical scroll swipe sized to the device frame. The
/// gesture covers the middle 50% of the display (`mid_x`, `h/4` ↔ `3h/4`) so
/// a 1080×2400 device scrolls across the whole height rather than the upper
/// left quadrant. Falls back to a 720×1560 default (the legacy emulator
/// geometry) when the bridge has not yet delivered a frame.
fn wheel_cmd(up: bool, w: u32, h: u32) -> AndroidAction {
    const DEFAULT_W: u32 = 720;
    const DEFAULT_H: u32 = 1560;
    let w = if w == 0 { DEFAULT_W } else { w };
    let h = if h == 0 { DEFAULT_H } else { h };
    let mid_x = w / 2;
    let bottom_y = (h * 3) / 4;
    let top_y = h / 4;
    if up {
        AndroidAction::Swipe {
            x1: mid_x,
            y1: bottom_y,
            x2: mid_x,
            y2: top_y,
        }
    } else {
        AndroidAction::Swipe {
            x1: mid_x,
            y1: top_y,
            x2: mid_x,
            y2: bottom_y,
        }
    }
}

/// Aspect-correct scrcpy-style blit: nearest-neighbour sample of the device
/// frame into the window buffer, centered and letterboxed — never cropped,
/// never stretched. Returns the content rect (x, y, w, h) for input mapping.
fn blit(src: &Frame, dst: &mut [u32], dw: usize, dh: usize) -> (usize, usize, usize, usize) {
    if dw == 0
        || dh == 0
        || src.w == 0
        || src.h == 0
        || src.rgba.len() < (src.w * src.h * 4) as usize
    {
        return (0, 0, 0, 0);
    }
    for p in dst.iter_mut() {
        *p = LETTERBOX;
    }
    let scale = (dw as f64 / src.w as f64).min(dh as f64 / src.h as f64);
    let cw = ((src.w as f64 * scale) as usize).clamp(1, dw);
    let ch = ((src.h as f64 * scale) as usize).clamp(1, dh);
    let ox = (dw - cw) / 2;
    let oy = (dh - ch) / 2;
    for y in 0..ch {
        let sy = y * src.h as usize / ch;
        let row = &src.rgba[sy * src.w as usize * 4..][..src.w as usize * 4];
        let dst_row = &mut dst[(y + oy) * dw + ox..(y + oy) * dw + ox + cw];
        for (x, p) in dst_row.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let i = x * src.w as usize / cw * 4;
            *p = (row[i] as u32) << 16 | (row[i + 1] as u32) << 8 | row[i + 2] as u32;
        }
    }
    (ox, oy, cw, ch)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::Arc;

    fn frame(w: u32, h: u32) -> Frame {
        Frame {
            gen: 1,
            w,
            h,
            rgba: Arc::new(vec![80u8; (w * h * 4) as usize]),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn blit_is_aspect_correct_and_letterboxed() {
        // 720×1560 into 360×780: perfect 2:1 fit — content fills the window
        let mut dst = vec![0u32; 360 * 780];
        let rect = blit(&frame(720, 1560), &mut dst, 360, 780);
        assert_eq!(
            rect,
            (0, 0, 360, 780),
            "matching aspect must fill the window"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            dst[0],
            (80 << 16) | (80 << 8) | 80,
            "corner must sample the frame"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            dst[360 * 780 - 1],
            (80 << 16) | (80 << 8) | 80,
            "bottom-right corner"
        );

        // a wider window letterboxes top/bottom, never crops or stretches
        let mut wide = vec![0u32; 500 * 780];
        let rect = blit(&frame(720, 1560), &mut wide, 500, 780);
        assert_eq!(rect.2, 360, "content width follows the device aspect");
        assert_eq!(rect.3, 780);
        assert_eq!(
            (rect.0, rect.1),
            ((500 - 360) / 2, 0),
            "centered horizontally"
        );
        // the letterbox columns keep the backdrop colour
        assert_eq!(wide[0], LETTERBOX, "left gutter is letterbox");
        assert_eq!(wide[rect.0 - 1 + 400 * 500], LETTERBOX, "gutter mid-screen");
        assert_eq!(
            wide[rect.0 + 400 * 500],
            (80 << 16) | (80 << 8) | 80,
            "content starts at rect"
        );

        // a taller window letterboxes left/right
        let mut tall = vec![0u32; 360 * 900];
        let rect = blit(&frame(720, 1560), &mut tall, 360, 900);
        assert_eq!(rect, (0, (900 - 780) / 2, 360, 780), "centered vertically");
        assert_eq!(tall[10], LETTERBOX, "top gutter is letterbox");

        // degenerate sizes never panic (2×2 window with a tall frame → 1×2 content)
        let mut tiny = vec![0u32; 4];
        let rect = blit(&frame(720, 1560), &mut tiny, 2, 2);
        assert_eq!(rect, (0, 0, 1, 2));
        let mut empty = vec![];
        assert_eq!(blit(&frame(0, 0), &mut empty, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0, 0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn press_decides_tap_vs_swipe_like_every_other_path() {
        assert!(matches!(
            press_outcome((360, 1200), (362, 1198)),
            AndroidAction::Tap { x: 362, y: 1198 }
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            press_outcome((360, 1100), (360, 400)),
            AndroidAction::Swipe {
                x1: 360,
                y1: 1100,
                x2: 360,
                y2: 400,
            }
        ));
        // slop is exclusive: exactly 11 px of travel is a swipe
        assert!(matches!(
            press_outcome((0, 0), (11, 0)),
            AndroidAction::Swipe { .. }
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            press_outcome((0, 0), (10, 0)),
            AndroidAction::Tap { .. }
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn wheel_maps_to_scroll_swipes() {
        // wheel up scrolls content down → swipe from below to above.
        // Coordinates are frame-derived (middle 50% of a 720×1560 default).
        assert!(matches!(
            wheel_cmd(true, 720, 1560),
            AndroidAction::Swipe {
                x1: 360,
                y1: 1170,
                x2: 360,
                y2: 390
            }
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            wheel_cmd(false, 720, 1560),
            AndroidAction::Swipe {
                x1: 360,
                y1: 390,
                x2: 360,
                y2: 1170
            }
        ));
        // 1080×2400 device scrolls across the whole display, not the upper
        // left quadrant the old hardcoded (360, 1100) coords hit.
        assert!(matches!(
            wheel_cmd(true, 1080, 2400),
            AndroidAction::Swipe {
                x1: 540,
                y1: 1800,
                x2: 540,
                y2: 600
            }
        ));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Multi-line text editor state for the chatbox.
use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;

#[derive(Default, Clone)]
pub struct Input {
    chars: Vec<char>,
    cur: usize,
    history: Vec<String>,
    hist_pos: Option<usize>,
    draft: String,
}

impl Input {
    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        self.chars.iter().collect()
    }
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.chars.is_empty()
    }
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.chars.clear();
        self.cur = 0;
        self.hist_pos = None;
    }
    pub fn set(&mut self, s: &str) {
        self.chars = s.chars().collect();
        self.cur = self.chars.len();
    }
    /// Take the text, record it in history and clear the editor.
    pub fn submit(&mut self) -> String {
        let t = self.text();
        if !t.trim().is_empty() && self.history.last() != Some(&t) {
            self.history.push(t.clone());
        }
        self.clear();
        t
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, c: char) {
        self.chars.insert(self.cur, c);
        self.cur += 1;
    }
    pub fn insert_str(&mut self, s: &str) {
        for c in s.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n").chars() {
            if c == '\t' {
                self.insert(' ');
                self.insert(' ');
            } else if c == '\n' || !c.is_control() {
                self.insert(c);
            }
        }
    }
    pub fn newline(&mut self) {
        self.insert('\n');
    }
    pub fn backspace(&mut self) {
        if self.cur > 0 {
            self.cur -= 1;
            self.chars.remove(self.cur);
        }
    }
    pub fn delete(&mut self) {
        if self.cur < self.chars.len() {
            self.chars.remove(self.cur);
        }
    }
    pub fn left(&mut self) {
        self.cur = self.cur.saturating_sub(1);
    }
    pub fn right(&mut self) {
        self.cur = (self.cur + 1).min(self.chars.len());
    }
    fn line_start(&self, from: usize) -> usize {
        let mut i = from;
        while i > 0 && self.chars[i - 1] != '\n' {
            i -= 1;
        }
        i
    }
    fn line_end(&self, from: usize) -> usize {
        let mut i = from;
        while i < self.chars.len() && self.chars[i] != '\n' {
            i += 1;
        }
        i
    }
    pub fn home(&mut self) {
        self.cur = self.line_start(self.cur);
    }
    pub fn end(&mut self) {
        self.cur = self.line_end(self.cur);
    }
    pub fn word_left(&mut self) {
        while self.cur > 0 && self.chars[self.cur - 1].is_whitespace() {
            self.cur -= 1;
        }
        while self.cur > 0 && !self.chars[self.cur - 1].is_whitespace() {
            self.cur -= 1;
        }
    }
    pub fn word_right(&mut self) {
        let n = self.chars.len();
        while self.cur < n && self.chars[self.cur].is_whitespace() {
            self.cur += 1;
        }
        while self.cur < n && !self.chars[self.cur].is_whitespace() {
            self.cur += 1;
        }
    }
    pub fn kill_word(&mut self) {
        let end = self.cur;
        self.word_left();
        self.chars.drain(self.cur..end);
    }
    pub fn kill_to_start(&mut self) {
        let s = self.line_start(self.cur);
        self.chars.drain(s..self.cur);
        self.cur = s;
    }
    pub fn kill_to_end(&mut self) {
        let e = self.line_end(self.cur);
        self.chars.drain(self.cur..e);
    }

    fn is_multiline(&self) -> bool {
        self.chars.contains(&'\n')
    }
    /// Up: move within a multi-line buffer, otherwise walk history.
    pub fn up(&mut self) {
        if self.is_multiline() && self.line_start(self.cur) > 0 {
            let ls = self.line_start(self.cur);
            let col = self.cur - ls;
            let ps = self.line_start(ls - 1);
            self.cur = (ps + col).min(ls - 1);
            return;
        }
        if self.history.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let pos = match self.hist_pos {
            None => {
                self.draft = self.text();
                self.history.len() - 1
            }
            Some(p) => p.saturating_sub(1),
        };
        self.hist_pos = Some(pos);
        let h = self.history[pos].clone();
        self.set(&h);
    }
    pub fn down(&mut self) {
        if self.is_multiline() && self.line_end(self.cur) < self.chars.len() {
            let ls = self.line_start(self.cur);
            let col = self.cur - ls;
            let ns = self.line_end(self.cur) + 1;
            let ne = self.line_end(ns);
            self.cur = (ns + col).min(ne);
            return;
        }
        if let Some(p) = self.hist_pos {
            if p + 1 < self.history.len() {
                self.hist_pos = Some(p + 1);
                let h = self.history[p + 1].clone();
                self.set(&h);
            } else {
                self.hist_pos = None;
                let d = std::mem::take(&mut self.draft);
                self.set(&d);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Hard-wrap into visual lines of `width` cells. Returns the lines and the
    /// cursor's (row, col) in that layout.
    pub fn layout(&self, width: usize) -> (Vec<String>, (usize, usize)) {
        let width = width.max(1);
        let mut lines = vec![String::new()];
        let mut col = 0usize;
        let mut cursor = (0usize, 0usize);
        for i in 0..=self.chars.len() {
            if i == self.cur {
                cursor = (lines.len() - 1, col);
            }
            if i == self.chars.len() {
                break;
            }
            let c = self.chars[i];
            if c == '\n' {
                lines.push(String::new());
                col = 0;
                continue;
            }
            let w = c.width().unwrap_or(0);
            if col + w > width {
                lines.push(String::new());
                col = 0;
                if i == self.cur {
                    cursor = (lines.len() - 1, 0);
                }
            }
            lines.last_mut().unwrap().push(c);
            col += w;
        }
        (lines, cursor)
    }
}
```

````rust
//! `romacode` — the screen. Connects to `romacode-server` (the brain) and
//! draws the sessions: transcript, tabs, sidebars, the live Android panel and
//! the scrcpy-style desktop window. No agent logic, no config file, no tools:
//! everything is a request on the wire and an event back.

mod app;
mod autostart;
mod device;
mod display;
mod input;
mod net;
mod session;
mod settings;
mod terminal;
mod tools;
mod tree;
mod ui;

use anyhow::Result;
use app::App;
use crossterm::{
    event::{
        self, DisableBracketedPaste, DisableMouseCapture, EnableBracketedPaste, EnableMouseCapture,
        Event,
    },
    execute,
    terminal::{disable_raw_mode, enable_raw_mode, EnterAlternateScreen, LeaveAlternateScreen},
};
use net::Net;
use ratatui::{backend::CrosstermBackend, Terminal};
use romacode_shared::protocol::{Reply, Welcome};
use std::io;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

fn setup() -> Result<Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>> {
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    // Roll back everything already applied when a later step fails — the old
    // code could bail out with the terminal left in raw mode (no echo, no
    // line discipline) after the process returned to the shell.
    let run = || -> Result<Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>> {
        let mut out = io::stdout();
        execute!(
            out,
            EnterAlternateScreen,
            EnableMouseCapture,
            EnableBracketedPaste
        )?;
        let mut term = Terminal::new(CrosstermBackend::new(out))?;
        term.hide_cursor()?;
        term.clear()?;
        Ok(term)
    };
    match run() {
        Ok(t) => Ok(t),
        Err(e) => {
            restore();
            Err(e)
        }
    }
}

fn restore() {
    let _ = disable_raw_mode();
    let _ = execute!(
        io::stdout(),
        DisableBracketedPaste,
        DisableMouseCapture,
        LeaveAlternateScreen
    );
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    if args.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("--snapshot") {
        return snapshot(&args[1..]);
    }
    // `romacode tools|doctor|github|db|fetch|…` run on the brain binary, so a
    // single command is the whole CLI (scriptable: exit codes + --json).
    if let Some(first) = args.first().map(String::as_str) {
        if autostart::UTILITY_COMMANDS.contains(&first) {
            std::process::exit(autostart::run_utility(&args));
        }
    }
    if matches!(args.first().map(String::as_str), Some("--version" | "-V")) {
        println!("romacode {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
        return Ok(());
    }
    if matches!(args.first().map(String::as_str), Some("--help" | "-h")) {
        println!(
            "romacode {}\n\nUSAGE: romacode [--server 127.0.0.1:7712] [--no-autostart]\n\nThe screen half of RomaCode. The brain (romacode-server) is auto-started in the\nbackground on first launch — you no longer need to run `romacode-server serve` in\na separate terminal. To drive the brain yourself, pass --no-autostart.\n\nKEYS\n  enter send (queues the query while the agent works) · alt+enter newline · tab Build/Plan · esc interrupt\n  ctrl+s send now — the agent reads it at its next step (or the selected queued query)\n  alt+e edit / alt+d delete queued query · alt+↑/↓ select it\n  ctrl+n new session · ctrl+w close · alt+←/→ switch · alt+1..9 jump\n  ctrl+b side panel · alt+a Android device · alt+[ / ] chat width\n  ctrl+p settings — one page (appearance, permissions, session, tabs & diffs,\n       input, alerts, AI & server, advanced) · / opens command menu · pgup/pgdn scroll · ctrl+q quit\n\nCOMMANDS\n  / opens the slash menu (every settings tree leaf, filtered)\n  /providers · /models · /provider [id] · /model [name] · /apikey <key> · /baseurl <url>\n  /customprovider <id> <base-url> [openai|anthropic]   (run in the brain)\n  /engine [native|langchain] · /mode [build|plan] · /rounds <1..200>\n  /webfetch [on|off] · /rnmap [on|off] · /timeout <5..3600> · /context <tokens> · /prefs\n\nUTILITY COMMANDS  (run on the brain; scriptable, exit codes, --json where noted)\n  romacode tools [list|describe <n>|search <w>|run <n> '<json>'] [--json]   everything the agent can call\n  romacode doctor [--json]       health check: config, provider, key, engine, tools, git/adb\n  romacode github <cmd> · git <cmd> · db <cmd> · fetch <url> · providers · models · tunnel …\n\nOPTIONS\n  --server <addr>     brain address (default 127.0.0.1:7712)\n  --no-autostart       do not spawn romacode-server when the brain is unreachable;\n                      require it to already be running (legacy two-terminal mode)\n  --snapshot <home|chat|new|android|phone|palette|tree|models|slash|root|providers|apikey|fetching|perm> [w] [h]\n                      headless render for development\n  --version · --help\n\nENGINE  the brain runs agent.engine = native | langchain (built-in LangChain in Rust)\n\nAUTO-START  when the brain at --server is not reachable, the screen spawns\n            `romacode-server serve --bind <addr> --cwd <current dir>` as a\n            detached daemon (log: ~/.local/share/romacode/server.log,\n            pid:  ~/.local/share/romacode/server.pid). The brain keeps running\n            after the screen exits. To stop it:  pkill -f romacode-server",
            env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
        );
        return Ok(());
    }

    let mut bind = net::DEFAULT_BIND.to_string();
    let mut autostart_enabled = true;
    // Capture the launch cwd so the auto-started brain runs against the same
    // project the user invoked the screen from. (Taken before any --cwd flag
    // in `serve` could chdir the brain — the brain's cwd comes from its own
    // --cwd argument, but we want the screen's *original* cwd here.)
    let launch_cwd = std::env::current_dir()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|p| p.to_str().map(|s| s.to_string()));
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--server" | "-s" => {
                if let Some(v) = it.next() {
                    bind = v.clone();
                }
            }
            "--no-autostart" => autostart_enabled = false,
            other => anyhow::bail!("unknown argument {other} (try --help)"),
        }
    }

    let default_hook = std::panic::take_hook();
    std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |info| {
        // Only the MAIN thread owns the terminal. A panic on a background
        // thread (reader/writer/request workers) used to run `restore()` and
        // stomp the live TUI: raw mode off, alt-screen closed — while the UI
        // kept drawing into a restored terminal.
        if std::thread::current().name() == Some("main") {
            restore();
        }
        default_hook(info);
    }));

    let net = connect_with_retry(&bind, autostart_enabled, launch_cwd.as_deref())?;
    // Handshake BEFORE the terminal is claimed, so version problems print as
    // plain text. A stale brain (an older romacode-server still running as
    // the persistent daemon — it keeps running after the screen exits) used
    // to be silently reused: its Welcome carried no saved providers/models,
    // so Select Model appeared empty even with a fresh screen binary. Now
    // the screen notices version drift and RESTARTS the daemon so both
    // halves match.
    let mut welcome = handshake(&net)?;
    if welcome.protocol_version != Welcome::PROTOCOL_VERSION {
        anyhow::bail!(
            "protocol mismatch: server v{}, screen v{} — reinstall both binaries together",
            welcome.protocol_version,
            Welcome::PROTOCOL_VERSION
        );
    }
    if welcome.server_version != env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") {
        if !autostart_enabled {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "brain v{} != screen v{} at {bind} — restart the brain:\n  \
                 pkill -f romacode-server && romacode-server serve",
                welcome.server_version,
                env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
            );
        }
        eprintln!(
            "romacode: brain v{} is stale (screen v{}) — restarting it so saved \
             providers/models match",
            welcome.server_version,
            env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
        );
        autostart::restart_server(&bind, launch_cwd.as_deref()).map_err(|e| {
            anyhow::anyhow!(
                "restarting the stale brain failed: {e}\n\
                 Stop the old one manually:  pkill -f romacode-server"
            )
        })?;
        let mut net2 = None;
        let mut last_err = String::new();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            match Net::connect(&bind) {
                Ok(n) => {
                    net2 = Some(n);
                    break;
                }
                Err(e) => last_err = e,
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(400));
        }
        let net = Arc::new(net2.ok_or_else(|| {
            anyhow::anyhow!("{last_err}\nrestarted brain did not come back on {bind}")
        })?);
        welcome = handshake(&net)?;
        if welcome.protocol_version != Welcome::PROTOCOL_VERSION {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "protocol mismatch after restart: server v{}, screen v{} — reinstall both binaries together",
                welcome.protocol_version,
                Welcome::PROTOCOL_VERSION
            );
        }
        if welcome.server_version != env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "brain at {bind} is still v{} after a restart — a different \
                 romacode-server binary is probably on PATH; stop it with \
                 pkill -f romacode-server and rebuild",
                welcome.server_version
            );
        }
        eprintln!("romacode: brain restarted at v{}", welcome.server_version);
    }
    let mut term = setup()?;
    let res = run(&mut term, net, &bind, &welcome);
    restore();
    term.show_cursor()?;
    res
}

/// `hello` handshake: everything the screen needs comes out of this reply.
fn handshake(net: &Net) -> Result<Welcome> {
    match net.hello(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")) {
        Ok(Reply::Welcome(w)) => Ok(w),
        Ok(_) => anyhow::bail!("unexpected handshake reply from romacode-server"),
        Err(e) => anyhow::bail!("handshake with romacode-server failed: {e}"),
    }
}

fn connect_with_retry(
    bind: &str,
    autostart_enabled: bool,
    launch_cwd: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Arc<Net>> {
    let mut last_err = String::new();
    for _ in 0..3 {
        match Net::connect(bind) {
            Ok(n) => return Ok(Arc::new(n)),
            Err(e) => last_err = e,
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(400));
    }
    // No brain answering. Auto-start it as a detached daemon and retry the
    // connection for a comfortable window; the brain's startup is dominated
    // by config load + provider catalog, both local.
    if autostart_enabled {
        match autostart::ensure_server_running(bind, launch_cwd) {
            Ok(()) => {
                eprintln!(
                    "romacode: auto-started romacode-server in the background \
                     (log: {}, pid: {})",
                    autostart::server_log_path().display(),
                    autostart::server_pid_path().display()
                );
            }
            Err(e) => {
                anyhow::bail!(
                    "{last_err}\nAuto-starting romacode-server failed: {e}\n\
                     Start the brain manually:  romacode-server serve"
                );
            }
        }
        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(15);
        loop {
            match Net::connect(bind) {
                Ok(n) => return Ok(Arc::new(n)),
                Err(e) => last_err = e,
            }
            if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
                break;
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300));
        }
        anyhow::bail!(
            "{last_err}\nAuto-started romacode-server did not become reachable \
             on {bind} within 15s — check the log at {}",
            autostart::server_log_path().display()
        );
    }
    anyhow::bail!(
        "{last_err}\nStart the brain first:  romacode-server serve  \
         (in your project directory), or drop --no-autostart to let the screen \
         spawn it for you"
    )
}

fn run(
    term: &mut Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>,
    net: Arc<Net>,
    bind: &str,
    welcome: &Welcome,
) -> Result<()> {
    let mut app = App::new(net.clone(), welcome, bind);
    // The "Mouse" setting is honoured live: capture is on by default, off when
    // the user turns it off, and it flips the moment the setting changes.
    let mut mouse_on = true;
    while !app.quit {
        if app.cfg.tui.mouse != mouse_on {
            mouse_on = app.cfg.tui.mouse;
            let mut out = io::stdout();
            let _ = if mouse_on {
                execute!(out, EnableMouseCapture)
            } else {
                execute!(out, DisableMouseCapture)
            };
        }
        if app.dirty || app.animating() {
            term.draw(|f| ui::draw(f, &mut app))?;
            app.dirty = false;
        }
        // 30 fps event loop: the live Android stream lands in shared state
        // asynchronously, so the UI polls it every tick regardless of
        // animation state — that keeps the device panel truly live. With the
        // scrcpy-style window open the tick halves to 60 fps so the desktop
        // window pumps input + frames between terminal events.
        let tick = if app.phone_window.is_some() {
            Duration::from_millis(16)
        } else {
            Duration::from_millis(33)
        };
        if event::poll(tick)? {
            // drain everything queued so typing/paste stays snappy
            loop {
                let ev: Event = event::read()?;
                app.on_event(ev);
                if !event::poll(Duration::from_millis(0))? {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if app.poll() {
            app.dirty = true;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Headless render for development: prints the screen as JSON cells.
/// usage: romacode --snapshot <home|chat|new|android|phone|palette|tree|slash|root|providers|apikey|fetching|perm> <w> <h>
fn snapshot(args: &[String]) -> Result<()> {
    use ratatui::backend::TestBackend;
    use romacode_shared::protocol::{
        Block, McpServer, Mode, Msg, SessionSnapshot, Todo, TodoState, ToolStatus,
    };
    let which = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("home");
    let w: u16 = args.get(1).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(160);
    let h: u16 = args.get(2).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(45);

    // a dummy in-process protocol server so App can hold a Net
    let welcome = Welcome {
        server_version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        protocol_version: Welcome::PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        provider: "anthropic".into(),
        model: "model-name".into(),
        mode_default: Mode::Build,
        engine: "native".into(),
        chat_width_pct: 36,
        sidebar: true,
        cwd: "~/projects/romacode".into(),
        branch: Some("main".into()),
        providers: Vec::new(),
        sessions: Vec::new(),
        device: None,
        missing_keys: Vec::new(),
        context_window: 200_000,
        price_in_per_mtok: 3.0,
        price_out_per_mtok: 15.0,
        max_tool_rounds: 25,
        webfetch_enabled: true,
        rnmap_enabled: true,
        remix_enabled: true,
        request_timeout_secs: 120,
        tui: Default::default(),
    };
    let bind = net::spawn_dummy_server(serde_json::to_string(&welcome)?)
        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;
    let net = Net::connect(&bind).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;
    let mut app = App::new(Arc::new(net), &welcome, &bind);
    if which != "home" {
        app.screen = app::Screen::Chat;
        let snap = SessionSnapshot {
            id: 1,
            title: "Retry logic for HTTP client".into(),
            messages: vec![
                Msg::User {
                    text: "Add retry with exponential backoff to the HTTP client and keep the per-request timeout at 10s.".into(),
                },
                Msg::Assistant {
                    blocks: vec![
                        Block::Text {
                            text: "I'll wrap the request in a retry loop with exponential backoff, starting at 200 ms and doubling each attempt.\nThe 10s timeout stays on every individual try.".into(),
                        },
                        Block::Tool {
                            id: "1".into(),
                            name: "Read".into(),
                            arg: "src/client.rs".into(),
                            status: ToolStatus::Ok,
                            extra: None,
                        },
                        Block::Tool {
                            id: "2".into(),
                            name: "Edit".into(),
                            arg: "src/client.rs".into(),
                            status: ToolStatus::Ok,
                            extra: Some("+11 −1".into()),
                        },
                        Block::Text {
                            text: "```diff src/client.rs\n@@ -40,1 +40,12 @@\n-    client.get(url).timeout(TIMEOUT).send().await\n+async fn get_with_retry(client: &Client, url: &str) -> Result<Response> {\n+    let mut delay = Duration::from_millis(200);\n+    for attempt in 1..=MAX_RETRIES {\n+        match client.get(url).timeout(TIMEOUT).send().await {\n+            Ok(res) if res.status().is_success() => return Ok(res),\n+            _ if attempt < MAX_RETRIES => { sleep(delay).await; delay *= 2; }\n+            other => return other.map_err(Into::into),\n+        }\n+    }\n+    unreachable!()\n+}\n```\nEach failed attempt now waits 200 ms, 400 ms, 800 ms before retrying, up to `MAX_RETRIES`. Want me to run cargo test?".into(),
                        },
                    ],
                    model: "model-name".into(),
                    mode: Mode::Build,
                    secs: Some(12.4),
                },
            ],
            mode: Mode::Build,
            running: false,
            tokens_in: 38_000,
            tokens_out: 4_100,
            turns: 4,
            todos: vec![
                Todo { text: "Read src/client.rs".into(), state: TodoState::Done },
                Todo { text: "Add backoff retry loop".into(), state: TodoState::Done },
                Todo { text: "Run cargo test".into(), state: TodoState::Active },
                Todo { text: "Update README".into(), state: TodoState::Open },
            ],
            mcp: vec![
                McpServer { name: "filesystem".into(), tools: 11, on: true },
                McpServer { name: "github".into(), tools: 24, on: true },
                McpServer { name: "postgres".into(), tools: 0, on: false },
            ],
            files: vec![romacode_shared::protocol::FileChange {
                path: "src/client.rs".into(),
                added: 11,
                removed: 1,
            }],
            lsp: vec![("rust-analyzer".into(), "ready".into())],
            pending_approvals: Vec::new(),
        };
        app.sessions[0].ingest_snapshot(snap);
        app.new_session_for_snapshot(true);
        if which == "palette" {
            app.palette = Some(app::Palette::default());
        }
        if which == "tree" {
            // render the flat Settings page at the top
            app.tree = Some(crate::tree::Tree::root());
        }
        if which == "models" {
            // the Select Model picker exactly as the Settings page opens it
            let mut st = crate::settings::Settings::root();
            st.screen = crate::settings::Screen::SelectModel;
            st.sel = 0;
            for m in ["deepseek-chat", "deepseek-reasoner", "claude-sonnet-5-5", "gpt-5"] {
                st.models.push(m.into());
                st.model_providers.push("deepseek".into());
            }
            app.settings = Some(st);
        }
        if which == "slash" {
            // render the `/` slash menu with a partial query so the filter shows
            let mut m = crate::tree::SlashMenu::open();
            m.query = "prov".into();
            m.refresh();
            app.slash = Some(m);
        }
        if which == "root" {
            app.settings = Some(crate::settings::Settings::root());
        }
        if which == "providers" {
            let mut st = crate::settings::Settings::root();
            st.screen = crate::settings::Screen::Providers;
            st.sel = 0;
            app.settings = Some(st);
        }
        if which == "apikey" {
            // API-key screen with a fetch error, so the error line is visible
            let k = romacode_shared::catalog::known_at(0).expect("at least one known provider");
            let mut st = crate::settings::Settings::root();
            st.begin_known(k);
            st.input = "sk-demo".into();
            st.cursor = st.input.chars().count();
            st.error = Some(
                "provider host api.example.com resolves to a blocked address".into(),
            );
            app.settings = Some(st);
        }
        if which == "fetching" {
            // API-key screen mid-fetch: the loading spinner must be visible
            let k = romacode_shared::catalog::known_at(0).expect("at least one known provider");
            let mut st = crate::settings::Settings::root();
            st.begin_known(k);
            st.input = "sk-demo".into();
            st.cursor = st.input.chars().count();
            st.loading = true;
            app.settings = Some(st);
        }
        if which == "perm" {
            // the brain asked for a y/n on a shell command: render the popup
            app.screen = app::Screen::Chat;
            app.sessions[0].mode = Mode::Build;
            app.pending_approval.push(app::PendingApproval {
                id: "apr-demo".into(),
                session_id: 1,
                name: "Bash".into(),
                effect: "Run host shell command in project directory:\ncargo test --release".into(),
            });
        }
    }
    let mut term = Terminal::new(TestBackend::new(w, h))?;
    term.draw(|f| ui::draw(f, &mut app))?;
    let buf = term.backend().buffer().clone();
    let mut cells = Vec::new();
    for y in 0..h {
        let mut row = Vec::new();
        for x in 0..w {
            let c = buf.get(x, y);
            let col = |c: ratatui::style::Color| match c {
                ratatui::style::Color::Rgb(r, g, b) => [r as i32, g as i32, b as i32],
                _ => [-1, -1, -1],
            };
            row.push(serde_json::json!([
                c.symbol(),
                col(c.fg),
                col(c.bg),
                c.modifier.contains(ratatui::style::Modifier::BOLD)
            ]));
        }
        cells.push(row);
    }
    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&cells)?);
    Ok(())
}
````

```rust
//! Connection to the brain: a minimal pure-std WebSocket client (RFC 6455)
//! plus the request/reply plumbing over the `romacode-shared` protocol.
//!
//! One TCP connection to the server:
//! * the **reader thread** parses server frames — replies resolve pending
//!   request slots, events flow to the UI through an mpsc channel;
//! * the **writer thread** sends (masked) client frames — client-to-server
//!   frames must be masked per the spec, server frames are not.
//!
//! Requests are synchronous (`Net::request`) with a generous timeout; UI-facing
//! flows background them and drain the result on the next tick so the render
//! loop never freezes on a slow or dead brain.

use romacode_shared::events::Event;
use romacode_shared::protocol::{ClientRequest, Reply, ServerEnvelope, Welcome};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read as IoRead, Write as IoWrite};
use std::net::TcpStream;
use std::sync::mpsc::{channel, Receiver, Sender};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

pub const DEFAULT_BIND: &str = "127.0.0.1:7712";

/// What the UI loop drains from [`Net::events`]. Besides wire events this
/// carries the req-0 Welcome REFRESH broadcast (settings/provider changes:
/// the server pushes a reply with req 0 — the request matcher can never
/// resolve it, so it is delivered here instead) and protocol drift, which is
/// surfaced instead of being silently swallowed (a dropped reply used to look
/// exactly like a 10-15 s freeze).
pub enum UiEvent {
    Wire(Event),
    Welcome(Welcome),
    Malformed(String),
}

/// Live connection to `romacode-server`.
pub struct Net {
    /// Requests for the writer thread: (seq, json).
    outbox: Sender<(u64, String)>,
    /// Streamed events for the UI loop (behind a mutex so the `Arc<Net>`
    /// can cross into worker threads; the UI drains it every tick).
    pub events: Arc<Mutex<Receiver<UiEvent>>>,
    pending: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Sender<Result<Reply, String>>>>>,
    next_seq: Arc<Mutex<u64>>,
    /// Bumped by the reader thread when the socket dies; `request` fails
    /// fast on it and `App::poll` drives the reconnect loop.
    pub closed: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>,
}

impl Net {
    /// Connect to `bind` and complete the WS handshake. Returns `Err` with a
    /// human-readable reason (bad address, server not up, no upgrade).
    pub fn connect(bind: &str) -> Result<Net, String> {
        // Bound the connect: an unresponsive address used to hang the caller
        // (the UI thread) for the OS-level SYN timeout (~2 min).
        let addr: std::net::SocketAddr = bind
            .parse()
            .map_err(|_| format!("invalid romacode-server address: {bind}"))?;
        let stream = TcpStream::connect_timeout(&addr, Duration::from_secs(3))
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot reach romacode-server at {bind}: {e}"))?;
        let _ = stream.set_nodelay(true);

        // --- handshake ---
        let key = ws_key();
        let req = format!(
            "GET /ws HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {bind}\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n"
        );
        let mut w = stream.try_clone().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        w.write_all(req.as_bytes()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        let mut status = String::new();
        reader.read_line(&mut status).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        if !status.contains("101") {
            return Err(format!(
                "romacode-server at {bind} did not upgrade to WebSocket ({})",
                status.trim()
            ));
        }
        loop {
            let mut line = String::new();
            let n = reader.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            if n == 0 || line.trim().is_empty() {
                break;
            }
        }

        let (outbox_tx, outbox_rx) = channel::<(u64, String)>();
        let (event_tx, event_rx) = channel::<UiEvent>();
        let pending: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Sender<Result<Reply, String>>>>> =
            Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
        let closed = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
        // All frame writes (writer thread, reader-thread PONGs, the liveness
        // pinger) go through one mutex: interleaved partial frames corrupt
        // the stream.
        let write_lock = Arc::new(Mutex::new(()));

        // --- writer thread (masked client frames) ---
        {
            let mut stream = stream.try_clone().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            let closed = closed.clone();
            let write_lock = write_lock.clone();
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("ws-client-writer".into())
                .spawn(move || {
                    while let Ok((seq, body)) = outbox_rx.recv() {
                        // Envelope: {"req": seq, "body": <already JSON object>}
                        let text = format!("{{\"req\":{seq},\"body\":{body}}}");
                        let guard = write_lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
                        let sent = client_send_text(&mut stream, &text);
                        drop(guard);
                        if sent.is_err() {
                            closed.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                })
                .ok();
        }

        // --- liveness pinger: a client PING every 30 s. A half-open TCP
        // connection never errors on its own; the first failed PING write
        // flips `closed` so `App::poll` starts the reconnect loop.
        {
            let mut stream = stream.try_clone().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            let closed = closed.clone();
            let write_lock = write_lock.clone();
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("ws-client-pinger".into())
                .spawn(move || {
                    while !closed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
                        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(30));
                        if closed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
                            break;
                        }
                        let guard = write_lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
                        let sent = client_send_frame(&mut stream, 0x9, b"romacode-ping");
                        drop(guard);
                        if sent.is_err() {
                            closed.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                })
                .ok();
        }

        // --- reader thread ---
        {
            let pending = pending.clone();
            let closed = closed.clone();
            let write_lock = write_lock.clone();
            let mut stream = stream;
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("ws-client-reader".into())
                .spawn(move || {
                    let mut buf = Vec::new();
                    loop {
                        match client_read_frame(&mut reader, &mut stream, &write_lock, &mut buf) {
                            Ok(None) => continue,
                            Ok(Some(text)) => {
                                let env: ServerEnvelope =
                                    match serde_json::from_str(&text) {
                                        Ok(e) => e,
                                        Err(e) => {
                                            // Undecodable envelope: surface it
                                            // instead of silently swallowing
                                            // (version drift used to degrade
                                            // into mysterious freezes).
                                            let _ = event_tx.send(UiEvent::Malformed(
                                                format!("malformed server envelope: {e}"),
                                            ));
                                            continue;
                                        }
                                    };
                                if let Some(req) = env.req {
                                    match parse_reply(&env) {
                                        Some(answer) => {
                                            let slot = pending
                                                .lock()
                                                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                                                .remove(&req);
                                            if let Some(tx) = slot {
                                                let _ = tx.send(answer);
                                                continue;
                                            }
                                            if req == 0 {
                                                // req-0 push: the Welcome
                                                // refresh broadcast.
                                                if let Some(Reply::Welcome(w)) =
                                                    answer.ok()
                                                {
                                                    if event_tx
                                                        .send(UiEvent::Welcome(w))
                                                        .is_err()
                                                    {
                                                        break;
                                                    }
                                                }
                                                continue;
                                            }
                                        }
                                        None => {
                                            // Reply-shaped envelope that could
                                            // not be parsed into a known Reply.
                                            let unresolved = pending
                                                .lock()
                                                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                                                .remove(&req)
                                                .map(|tx| {
                                                    let _ = tx.send(Err(
                                                        "malformed reply from romacode-server (screen/brain version mismatch?)"
                                                            .into(),
                                                    ));
                                                });
                                            if unresolved.is_some() {
                                                continue;
                                            }
                                            let _ = event_tx.send(UiEvent::Malformed(
                                                "server sent an unparseable reply (screen/brain version mismatch?)".into(),
                                            ));
                                            continue;
                                        }
                                    }
                                }
                                if let Some(ev) = env.event {
                                    if event_tx.send(UiEvent::Wire(ev)).is_err() {
                                        break;
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                            Err(_) => {
                                closed.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                                // Fail every in-flight request immediately:
                                // without this they each burned their full
                                // timeout after the connection died.
                                let mut map =
                                    pending.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
                                for (_, tx) in map.drain() {
                                    let _ = tx.send(Err(
                                        "connection to romacode-server was lost".into(),
                                    ));
                                }
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                })
                .ok();
        }

        Ok(Net {
            outbox: outbox_tx,
            events: Arc::new(Mutex::new(event_rx)),
            pending,
            next_seq: Arc::new(Mutex::new(1)),
            closed,
        })
    }

    fn seq(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut n = self.next_seq.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        *n += 1;
        *n
    }

    /// Send a request and wait for its reply. Fails immediately once the
    /// connection is known-dead (the old code always burned the full timeout
    /// after the socket died — every keypress froze the TUI for 15 s). While
    /// waiting, the closed flag is checked every 250 ms so a mid-request
    /// disconnect also fails fast.
    pub fn request(&self, body: ClientRequest, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Reply, String> {
        if self.closed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return Err("connection to romacode-server is closed".into());
        }
        let seq = self.seq();
        let (tx, rx) = channel();
        self.pending
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .insert(seq, tx);
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&body).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        if self.outbox.send((seq, json)).is_err() {
            self.pending
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .remove(&seq);
            return Err("connection to romacode-server is closed".into());
        }
        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + timeout;
        loop {
            match rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_millis(250)) {
                Ok(answer) => return answer,
                Err(std::sync::mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => {
                    if self.closed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
                        self.pending
                            .lock()
                            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                            .remove(&seq);
                        return Err("connection to romacode-server was lost".into());
                    }
                    if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
                        self.pending
                            .lock()
                            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                            .remove(&seq);
                        return Err(format!(
                            "no reply from romacode-server within {}s",
                            timeout.as_secs()
                        ));
                    }
                }
                Err(std::sync::mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => {
                    self.pending
                        .lock()
                        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                        .remove(&seq);
                    return Err("connection to romacode-server was lost".into());
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Fire-and-forget (device input, pings): no reply expected by the caller.
    pub fn fire(&self, body: ClientRequest) {
        let seq = self.seq();
        if let Ok(json) = serde_json::to_string(&body) {
            let _ = self.outbox.send((seq, json));
        }
    }

    pub fn hello(&self, version: &str) -> Result<Reply, String> {
        self.request(
            ClientRequest::Hello {
                version: version.to_string(),
            },
            Duration::from_secs(10),
        )
    }
}

/// Reply envelopes resolve to `Ok(Reply)`; error envelopes to `Err(message)`.
fn parse_reply(env: &ServerEnvelope) -> Option<Result<Reply, String>> {
    if let Some(err) = &env.error {
        return Some(Err(err.clone()));
    }
    let v = env.reply.as_ref()?;
    if v.get("ok")?.as_bool()? {
        serde_json::from_value::<Reply>(v.get("data")?.clone())
            .ok()
            .map(Ok)
    } else {
        Some(Err(
            v.get("error")
                .and_then(|e| e.as_str())
                .unwrap_or("request failed")
                .to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WS client framing.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// 16 random bytes, base64 — the masking key for the handshake. Uses the OS
/// randomness via /dev/urandom with a time+pid fallback.
fn ws_key() -> String {
    let mut bytes = [0u8; 16];
    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open("/dev/urandom") {
        use std::io::Read;
        let _ = f.read_exact(&mut bytes);
    } else {
        let t = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .as_nanos() as u64
            ^ (std::process::id() as u64) << 32;
        bytes
            .iter_mut()
            .enumerate()
            .for_each(|(i, b)| *b = (t >> (i % 8 * 8)) as u8 ^ (i as u8 * 31));
    }
    b64(&bytes)
}

fn b64(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    const T: &[u8] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
    let mut out = String::with_capacity((data.len() + 2) / 3 * 4);
    for chunk in data.chunks(3) {
        let b = [
            chunk[0],
            chunk.get(1).copied().unwrap_or(0),
            chunk.get(2).copied().unwrap_or(0),
        ];
        let n = ((b[0] as u32) << 16) | ((b[1] as u32) << 8) | b[2] as u32;
        out.push(T[(n >> 18) as usize & 63] as char);
        out.push(T[(n >> 12) as usize & 63] as char);
        out.push(if chunk.len() > 1 {
            T[(n >> 6) as usize & 63] as char
        } else {
            '='
        });
        out.push(if chunk.len() > 2 {
            T[n as usize & 63] as char
        } else {
            '='
        });
    }
    out
}

fn client_send_frame(stream: &mut TcpStream, opcode: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let len = payload.len();
    let mut mask = [0u8; 4];
    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open("/dev/urandom") {
        use std::io::Read;
        let _ = f.read_exact(&mut mask);
    } else {
        let t = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .as_nanos() as u64
            ^ (std::process::id() as u64) << 32;
        mask.iter_mut().enumerate().for_each(|(i, b)| {
            *b = (t >> (i % 8 * 8)) as u8 ^ (i as u8 * 17)
        });
    }
    let mut header: Vec<u8> = vec![opcode];
    if len < 126 {
        header.push(0x80 | len as u8);
    } else if len < 65536 {
        header.push(0x80 | 126);
        header.extend_from_slice(&(len as u16).to_be_bytes());
    } else {
        header.push(0x80 | 127);
        header.extend_from_slice(&(len as u64).to_be_bytes());
    }
    header.extend_from_slice(&mask);
    stream.write_all(&header)?;
    let masked: Vec<u8> = payload
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, b)| b ^ mask[i % 4])
        .collect();
    stream.write_all(&masked)
}

fn client_send_text(stream: &mut TcpStream, text: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    client_send_frame(stream, 0x81, text.as_bytes())
}

#[allow(dead_code)] // framing completeness; the reader maps opcodes directly
enum CFrame {
    Text(String),
    Close,
    Ignore,
}

fn client_read_frame(
    reader: &mut BufReader<TcpStream>,
    stream: &mut TcpStream,
    write_lock: &Mutex<()>,
    buf: &mut Vec<u8>,
) -> std::io::Result<Option<String>> {
    let mut hdr = [0u8; 2];
    reader.read_exact(&mut hdr)?;
    let fin = hdr[0] & 0x80 != 0;
    let opcode = hdr[0] & 0x0f;
    let mut len = (hdr[1] & 0x7f) as u64;
    if len == 126 {
        let mut ext = [0u8; 2];
        reader.read_exact(&mut ext)?;
        len = u16::from_be_bytes(ext) as u64;
    } else if len == 127 {
        let mut ext = [0u8; 8];
        reader.read_exact(&mut ext)?;
        len = u64::from_be_bytes(ext);
    }
    if len > 64 * 1024 * 1024 {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
            "frame too large",
        ));
    }
    let mut payload = vec![0u8; len as usize];
    reader.read_exact(&mut payload)?;
    match opcode {
        0x0 | 0x1 | 0x2 => {
            // 0x0 = continuation frame: fragment payloads accumulate until the
            // FIN bit. The old code ignored continuations entirely — fragmented
            // messages were lost and the buffer leaked.
            buf.extend_from_slice(&payload);
            if fin {
                let out = String::from_utf8_lossy(buf).into_owned();
                buf.clear();
                Ok(Some(out))
            } else {
                Ok(None)
            }
        }
        0x8 => Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionAborted,
            "server closed",
        )),
        0x9 => {
            // Server PING: RFC 6455 requires a PONG with the same payload —
            // a server may drop a client that never answers. The PONG is
            // written under the shared write mutex so it cannot interleave
            // with the writer thread's frames.
            {
                let guard = write_lock.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
                let _ = client_send_frame(stream, 0x8a, &payload);
                drop(guard);
            }
            Ok(None)
        }
        _ => {
            // PONG and any other unhandled control opcode carry no JSON
            // message — skip them instead of feeding an empty string to the
            // envelope parser (which used to surface a bogus "malformed").
            let _ = CFrame::Ignore;
            Ok(None)
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use romacode_shared::protocol::ClientEnvelope;

    #[test]
    fn b64_matches_known_vectors() {
        assert_eq!(b64(b"foobar"), "Zm9vYmFy");
        assert_eq!(b64(b"f"), "Zg==");
    }

    #[test]
    fn ws_key_shape() {
        let k = ws_key();
        assert_eq!(k.len(), 24, "{k}");
        assert!(k.ends_with("=="));
    }

    #[test]
    fn envelope_json_shape() {
        // the writer thread builds {"req":N,"body":<json object>}
        let body = serde_json::to_string(&ClientRequest::Ping).unwrap();
        let text = format!("{{\"req\":7,\"body\":{body}}}");
        let env: ClientEnvelope = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(env.req, 7);
        assert!(matches!(env.body, ClientRequest::Ping));
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// In-process dummy server for `--snapshot` (dev headless renders): speaks the
// same protocol on an ephemeral port, answers `hello` with a fixed Welcome
// and nothing else. No brain needed to render UI snapshots.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn spawn_dummy_server(welcome_json: String) -> Result<String, String> {
    let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")
        .map_err(|e| format!("dummy server: {e}"))?;
    let addr = listener
        .local_addr()
        .map_err(|e| format!("dummy server: {e}"))?
        .to_string();
    std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("ws-dummy".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let welcome = welcome_json;
            for stream in listener.incoming().flatten() {
                let _ = stream.set_nodelay(true);
                let mut reader = BufReader::new(match stream.try_clone() {
                    Ok(s) => s,
                    Err(_) => continue,
                });
                let mut line = String::new();
                if reader.read_line(&mut line).is_err() {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut key = String::new();
                loop {
                    let mut h = String::new();
                    if reader.read_line(&mut h).unwrap_or(0) == 0 {
                        break;
                    }
                    if h.trim().is_empty() {
                        break;
                    }
                    if let Some((k, v)) = h.split_once(':') {
                        if k.eq_ignore_ascii_case("sec-websocket-key") {
                            key = v.trim().to_string();
                        }
                    }
                }
                if key.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                // reuse the server crate's handshake math via RFC 6455 example:
                // compute accept = b64(sha1(key + GUID)) — inline SHA-1 (small).
                let accept = sha1_accept(&key);
                let resp = format!(
                    "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Accept: {accept}\r\n\r\n"
                );
                if stream
                    .try_clone()
                    .and_then(|mut s| s.write_all(resp.as_bytes()))
                    .is_err()
                {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut stream = stream;
                // Serve frames until the client goes away.
                let write_lock = Mutex::new(());
                loop {
                    match client_read_frame(&mut reader, &mut stream, &write_lock, &mut Vec::new())
                    {
                        Ok(None) => continue,
                        Ok(Some(text)) => {
                            // treat any request as hello; reply with the
                            // request's OWN req id — the client sequences start
                            // at 2, so the old hardcoded req:1 reply never
                            // resolved any pending request.
                            let req: u64 = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text)
                                .ok()
                                .and_then(|v| v.get("req").and_then(|r| r.as_u64()))
                                .unwrap_or(1);
                            let env = format!(
                                "{{\"req\":{req},\"reply\":{{\"ok\":true,\"data\":{welcome}}}}}"
                            );
                            if client_send_text(&mut stream, &env).is_err() {
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                        Err(_) => break,
                    }
                }
            }
        })
        .ok();
    Ok(addr)
}

/// Minimal SHA-1 for the dummy server handshake (same algorithm as the real
/// server; kept local to avoid a client→server dependency).
fn sha1_accept(key: &str) -> String {
    const GUID: &str = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11";
    let mut input = key.trim().as_bytes().to_vec();
    input.extend_from_slice(GUID.as_bytes());
    let mut h: [u32; 5] = [0x67452301, 0xEFCDAB89, 0x98BADCFE, 0x10325476, 0xC3D2E1F0];
    let ml = (input.len() as u64) * 8;
    let mut msg = input;
    msg.push(0x80);
    while msg.len() % 64 != 56 {
        msg.push(0);
    }
    msg.extend_from_slice(&ml.to_be_bytes());
    for chunk in msg.chunks(64) {
        let mut w = [0u32; 80];
        for (i, word) in chunk.chunks(4).enumerate() {
            w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([word[0], word[1], word[2], word[3]]);
        }
        for i in 16..80 {
            w[i] = (w[i - 3] ^ w[i - 8] ^ w[i - 14] ^ w[i - 16]).rotate_left(1);
        }
        let (mut a, mut b, mut c, mut d, mut e) = (h[0], h[1], h[2], h[3], h[4]);
        for (i, wi) in w.iter().enumerate() {
            let (f, k) = match i {
                0..=19 => ((b & c) | ((!b) & d), 0x5A827999u32),
                20..=39 => (b ^ c ^ d, 0x6ED9EBA1),
                40..=59 => ((b & c) | (b & d) | (c & d), 0x8F1BBCDC),
                _ => (b ^ c ^ d, 0xCA62C1D6),
            };
            let temp = a
                .rotate_left(5)
                .wrapping_add(f)
                .wrapping_add(k)
                .wrapping_add(*wi)
                .wrapping_add(e);
            e = d;
            d = c;
            c = b.rotate_left(30);
            b = a;
            a = temp;
        }
        h[0] = h[0].wrapping_add(a);
        h[1] = h[1].wrapping_add(b);
        h[2] = h[2].wrapping_add(c);
        h[3] = h[3].wrapping_add(d);
        h[4] = h[4].wrapping_add(e);
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(20);
    for v in h.iter() {
        out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
    }
    b64(&out)
}
```
