[view on disk](crates/client-tui/src/session.rs)

```rust
//! The screen's mirror of a server-owned session: the transcript blocks,
//! token counters, todo/file sidebars (all arriving as wire snapshots and
//! events) plus the strictly-local bits — the input box, scroll position and
//! the render cache.
//!
//! `apply` consumes the same `Event` stream the server uses to update its
//! own `session::Session`, so brain and screen can never drift apart.

use crate::device::Frame;
use crate::input::Input;
use crate::ui::draw::Row;
use romacode_shared::events::Event;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// The ui/ layer imports these names from `crate::session` — keep the
// namespace stable while the data itself moved to the shared protocol crate.
pub use romacode_shared::protocol::{
    Block, DeviceStatus, FileChange, McpServer, Mode, Msg, SessionSnapshot, Todo, TodoState,
    ToolStatus,
};

/// What the model is doing right now — drives the star dot in the working box.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Live {
    /// Request sent, nothing back yet.
    Thinking,
    /// Answer text is arriving.
    Streaming,
    /// A tool call is running.
    Tool(String),
    /// Between steps (tool finished, next round not started).
    Waiting,
}

/// Queries typed while the agent works are parked here until sent.
pub const QUEUE_CAP: usize = 20;

pub struct UiSession {
    pub id: usize,
    pub title: String,
    pub messages: Vec<Msg>,
    pub mode: Mode,
    /// Live turn timer, started when the client sends a message and cleared
    /// on the matching `Done` event.
    pub started: Option<Instant>,
    pub input: Input,
    /// Rows scrolled up from the bottom (0 = follow the stream).
    pub scroll_back: usize,
    pub tokens_in: u64,
    pub tokens_out: u64,
    pub turns: u32,
    pub todos: Vec<Todo>,
    pub mcp: Vec<McpServer>,
    pub files: Vec<FileChange>,
    pub lsp: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Bumped whenever the transcript changes (cache invalidation).
    pub rev: u64,
    pub cache: Option<(u16, u64, Vec<Row>)>,
    /// Queries typed during a task, waiting for ctrl+s (send to the agent).
    pub queue: Vec<String>,
    pub queue_sel: usize,
    /// When the last answer-text delta arrived (star dot twinkles on it).
    pub last_delta: Option<Instant>,
}

impl UiSession {
    pub fn new(id: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            title: format!("Session {id}"),
            messages: Vec::new(),
            mode: Mode::Build,
            started: None,
            input: Input::default(),
            scroll_back: 0,
            tokens_in: 0,
            tokens_out: 0,
            turns: 0,
            todos: Vec::new(),
            mcp: Vec::new(),
            files: Vec::new(),
            lsp: Vec::new(),
            rev: 0,
            cache: None,
            queue: Vec::new(),
            queue_sel: 0,
            last_delta: None,
        }
    }

    #[allow(dead_code)] // convenience for tests / future reconnect paths
    pub fn from_snapshot(snap: SessionSnapshot) -> Self {
        let mut s = Self::new(snap.id);
        s.ingest_snapshot(snap);
        s
    }

    /// Replace server-owned state with a snapshot; keep local input/scroll.
    pub fn ingest_snapshot(&mut self, snap: SessionSnapshot) {
        self.id = snap.id;
        self.title = snap.title;
        self.messages = snap.messages;
        self.mode = snap.mode;
        self.started = if snap.running {
            self.started.or_else(|| Some(Instant::now()))
        } else {
            None
        };
        self.tokens_in = snap.tokens_in;
        self.tokens_out = snap.tokens_out;
        self.turns = snap.turns;
        self.todos = snap.todos;
        self.mcp = snap.mcp;
        self.files = snap.files;
        self.lsp = snap.lsp;
        self.touch();
    }

    pub fn touch(&mut self) {
        self.rev += 1;
    }

    pub fn is_running(&self) -> bool {
        self.started.is_some()
    }

    /// Real-time model state for the working box, read off the transcript tail.
    pub fn live(&self) -> Live {
        if let Some(Msg::Assistant { blocks, .. }) = self.messages.last() {
            if let Some(name) = blocks.iter().rev().find_map(|b| match b {
                Block::Tool {
                    name,
                    status: ToolStatus::Running,
                    ..
                } => Some(name.clone()),
                _ => None,
            }) {
                return Live::Tool(name);
            }
            if self
                .last_delta
                .map_or(false, |t| t.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(700))
            {
                return Live::Streaming;
            }
            if blocks.is_empty() {
                return Live::Thinking;
            }
            return Live::Waiting;
        }
        Live::Thinking
    }

    pub fn tokens_total(&self) -> u64 {
        self.tokens_in + self.tokens_out
    }

    fn blocks_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Vec<Block>> {
        match self.messages.last_mut() {
            Some(Msg::Assistant { blocks, .. }) => Some(blocks),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Ensure the transcript tail is an assistant block, opening one when the
    /// snapshot landed mid-turn with User/Notice as the last message. Without
    /// this fallback, every streamed Text/ToolStart/ToolEnd delta was dropped
    /// until the next snapshot arrived.
    fn ensure_assistant_tail(&mut self) {
        if self.blocks_mut().is_none() {
            let mode = self.mode;
            self.messages.push(Msg::Assistant {
                blocks: Vec::new(),
                model: String::new(),
                mode,
                secs: None,
            });
        }
    }

    /// Optimistic local echo: the user prompt + an empty assistant block.
    /// The next snapshot from the server replaces all of this canonically.
    pub fn begin_turn(&mut self, text: &str, model: &str) {
        self.title = if self.turns == 0 {
            let t: String = text.lines().next().unwrap_or("").chars().take(30).collect();
            if t.trim().is_empty() {
                self.title.clone()
            } else {
                t.trim().to_string()
            }
        } else {
            self.title.clone()
        };
        self.messages.push(Msg::User {
            text: text.to_string(),
        });
        let mode = self.mode;
        self.messages.push(Msg::Assistant {
            blocks: Vec::new(),
            model: model.to_string(),
            mode,
            secs: None,
        });
        self.started = Some(Instant::now());
        self.scroll_back = 0;
        self.touch();
    }

    /// Apply one streamed event; returns true when something changed.
    pub fn apply(&mut self, ev: &Event) -> bool {
        match ev {
            Event::Text { delta, .. } => {
                self.last_delta = Some(Instant::now());
                self.ensure_assistant_tail();
                if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
                    match blocks.last_mut() {
                        Some(Block::Text { text: t }) => t.push_str(delta),
                        _ => blocks.push(Block::Text {
                            text: delta.to_string(),
                        }),
                    }
                }
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::ToolStart { id, name, arg, .. } => {
                self.ensure_assistant_tail();
                if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
                    blocks.push(Block::Tool {
                        id: id.clone(),
                        name: name.clone(),
                        arg: arg.clone(),
                        status: ToolStatus::Running,
                        extra: None,
                    });
                }
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::ToolEnd { id, ok, extra, .. } => {
                if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
                    for b in blocks.iter_mut() {
                        if let Block::Tool {
                            id: bid,
                            status,
                            extra: ex,
                            ..
                        } = b
                        {
                            if bid == id {
                                *status = if *ok {
                                    ToolStatus::Ok
                                } else {
                                    ToolStatus::Failed
                                };
                                *ex = extra.clone();
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::Usage { input, output, .. } => {
                self.tokens_in = self.tokens_in.max(*input);
                self.tokens_out = self.tokens_out.max(*output);
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::ApprovalRequest { effect, .. } => {
                self.messages.push(Msg::Notice {
                    text: format!(
                        "APPROVAL REQUIRED — exact pending effect:\n{effect}\nPress y to allow once, n to deny. No action runs until allowed."
                    ),
                });
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::UserInjected { text, .. } => {
                // A message sent mid-run: it lands in the transcript now and
                // the rest of the stream continues in a fresh block below it.
                let (model, mode) = self
                    .messages
                    .iter()
                    .rev()
                    .find_map(|m| match m {
                        Msg::Assistant { model, mode, .. } => Some((model.clone(), *mode)),
                        _ => None,
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| (String::new(), self.mode));
                self.messages.push(Msg::User { text: text.clone() });
                self.messages.push(Msg::Assistant {
                    blocks: Vec::new(),
                    model,
                    mode,
                    secs: None,
                });
                self.started = self.started.or_else(|| Some(Instant::now()));
                self.scroll_back = 0;
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::Notice { text, .. } => {
                // Esc pushes a local "Interrupted" AND the brain broadcasts
                // one: the transcript used to show the line twice.
                if text == "Interrupted"
                    && matches!(self.messages.last(), Some(Msg::Notice { text: t }) if t == "Interrupted")
                {
                    return false;
                }
                self.messages.push(Msg::Notice { text: text.clone() });
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::Error { message, .. } => {
                self.messages.push(Msg::Error {
                    text: message.clone(),
                });
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::Done { secs, .. } => {
                if let Some(started) = self.started.take() {
                    let elapsed = started.elapsed().as_secs_f32();
                    let secs = if *secs > 0.01 { *secs } else { elapsed };
                    if let Some(Msg::Assistant { secs: s, .. }) = self.messages.last_mut() {
                        *s = Some(secs);
                    }
                    self.turns += 1;
                }
                self.touch();
                true
            }
            Event::Snapshot { session } => {
                self.ingest_snapshot(session.clone());
                true
            }
            Event::Sessions { .. } | Event::Frame { .. } | Event::Device { .. } => false,
        }
    }
}

/// App-level device mirror: server status + the latest frame from `Frame`
/// events (also published into the shared `FrameHub` for the desktop window).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct DeviceView {
    pub status: Option<DeviceStatus>,
    pub frame: Option<Frame>,
    pub streaming: bool,
}

impl DeviceView {
    /// True when the device reports a usable online state.
    #[allow(dead_code)] // used by the fullscreen panel once key pages exist
    pub fn online(&self) -> bool {
        self.status
            .as_ref()
            .map(|s| s.phase == "online")
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    pub fn error(&self) -> Option<String> {
        self.status.as_ref().and_then(|s| {
            s.phase
                .strip_prefix("error:")
                .map(|e| e.to_string())
        })
    }
}

        s.scroll_back = 4;
        let mut snap = snap();
        snap.messages.push(Msg::Notice { text: "n".into() });
        s.ingest_snapshot(snap);
        assert_eq!(s.messages.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(s.scroll_back, 4);
        assert!(!s.input.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn events_build_transcript() {
        let mut s = UiSession::new(1);
        s.begin_turn("do it", "m");
        s.apply(&Event::Text {
            session_id: 1,
            delta: "hello".into(),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::ToolStart {
            session_id: 1,
            id: "1".into(),
            name: "Read".into(),
            arg: "{}".into(),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::ToolEnd {
            session_id: 1,
            id: "1".into(),
            ok: true,
            extra: Some("ok".into()),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::Done {
            session_id: 1,
            secs: 1.0,
        });
        assert!(!s.is_running());
        assert_eq!(s.turns, 1);
        match &s.messages[1] {
            Msg::Assistant { blocks, secs, .. } => {
                assert_eq!(blocks.len(), 2);
                assert!(secs.is_some());
            }
            other => panic!("wrong msg {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn device_view_phase_strings() {
        let mut v = DeviceView::default();
        v.status = Some(DeviceStatus {
            phase: "error:no device".into(),
            ..Default::default()
        });
        assert!(!v.online());
        assert_eq!(v.error().as_deref(), Some("no device"));
        v.status.as_mut().unwrap().phase = "online".into();
        assert!(v.online());
        assert_eq!(v.error(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_injected_event_lands_in_chat_and_opens_a_fresh_block() {
        let mut s = UiSession::new(1);
        s.begin_turn("first task", "m");
        s.apply(&Event::Text {
            session_id: 1,
            delta: "working on it".into(),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::UserInjected {
            session_id: 1,
            text: "also fix the footer".into(),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::Text {
            session_id: 1,
            delta: "ok, adding that".into(),
        });
        assert!(s.is_running());
        // user, assistant, user(steer), assistant — the new text sits BELOW it
        assert_eq!(s.messages.len(), 4);
        assert!(matches!(&s.messages[2], Msg::User { text } if text == "also fix the footer"));
        match &s.messages[3] {
            Msg::Assistant { blocks, model, .. } => {
                assert_eq!(model, "m");
                assert!(matches!(&blocks[0], Block::Text { text } if text == "ok, adding that"));
            }
            other => panic!("wrong msg {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupted_notice_is_not_duplicated() {
        let mut s = UiSession::new(1);
        s.messages.push(Msg::Notice {
            text: "Interrupted".into(),
        });
        let changed = s.apply(&Event::Notice {
            session_id: Some(1),
            text: "Interrupted".into(),
        });
        assert!(!changed);
        assert_eq!(s.messages.len(), 1);
        // other notices are never swallowed
        s.apply(&Event::Notice {
            session_id: Some(1),
            text: "something else".into(),
        });
        assert_eq!(s.messages.len(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn live_state_follows_the_response() {
        let mut s = UiSession::new(1);
        s.begin_turn("go", "m");
        assert_eq!(s.live(), Live::Thinking);
        s.apply(&Event::Text {
            session_id: 1,
            delta: "hi".into(),
        });
        assert_eq!(s.live(), Live::Streaming);
        s.apply(&Event::ToolStart {
            session_id: 1,
            id: "1".into(),
            name: "Read".into(),
            arg: "{}".into(),
        });
        assert_eq!(s.live(), Live::Tool("Read".into()));
        s.apply(&Event::ToolEnd {
            session_id: 1,
            id: "1".into(),
            ok: true,
            extra: None,
        });
        s.last_delta = None;
        assert_eq!(s.live(), Live::Waiting);
    }
}
```

## `crates/client-tui/src/settings.rs`

[view on disk](crates/client-tui/src/settings.rs)

```rust
//! Unified Ctrl+P settings panel — one overlay for commands + provider config
//! + the integrated tools builder.
//!
//! `Ctrl+P` opens it; the root list is grouped into clear sections (Commands,
//! Providers, Tools, Config).
//!
//! Every clickable row is mouse-hit-testable: `draw_settings` records a
//! [`HitRow`] per row each frame into `App::settings_hits`; `on_mouse` turns a
//! click into select+activate and a hover into selection, so the panel works
//! fully with keyboard **and** mouse. Input fields (API key, base URL, tool
//! JSON) support full cursor editing (←→ Home End Delete) and bracketed paste
//! is routed to the focused field.

use romacode_shared::catalog::{self, ApiKind, Known};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Screen {
    /// Unified root: every command + every provider action in one searchable list.
    Root,
    /// Pick a known provider from `KNOWN`.
    Providers,
    /// Enter an API key for a chosen known provider.
    KnownKey,
    /// Enter a display name for a custom provider (first step of the flow).
    CustomName,
    /// Enter a base URL for a custom provider.
    CustomBase,
    /// Enter an API key for a custom provider.
    CustomKey,
    /// Live-fetched model list (after a successful key + fetch).
    Models,
    /// Pick a model already saved under an existing provider.
    SelectModel,
    /// Browse the integrated tools builder catalog (38 tools, 8 categories).
    Tools,
    /// Type a JSON input for a selected tool, then run it.
    ToolsInput,
}

/// What a root-list entry does when activated.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RootAction {
    NewSession,
    CloseSession,
    NextSession,
    PrevSession,
    TogglePanel,
    ToggleAndroid,
    ToggleTerminal,
    WidenChat,
    NarrowChat,
    ToggleMode,
    ClearSession,
    Quit,
    AddKnownProvider,
    AddCustomProvider,
    SelectModel,
    OpenConfigFile,
    PrintEffectiveConfig,
    /// Open the integrated tools builder catalog.
    OpenTools,
}

/// One entry in the unified root list.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Entry {
    pub label: &'static str,
    pub category: &'static str,
    pub action: RootAction,
    pub key_hint: &'static str,
}

/// Every entry shown in the unified Ctrl+P panel, in display order.
/// Categories are emitted in the order they first appear.
pub const ENTRIES: &[Entry] = &[
    // Commands
    Entry { label: "New session", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::NewSession, key_hint: "ctrl+n" },
    Entry { label: "Close session", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::CloseSession, key_hint: "ctrl+w" },
    Entry { label: "Next session", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::NextSession, key_hint: "alt+→" },
    Entry { label: "Previous session", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::PrevSession, key_hint: "alt+←" },
    Entry { label: "Toggle side panel", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::TogglePanel, key_hint: "ctrl+b" },
    Entry { label: "Toggle Android window", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::ToggleAndroid, key_hint: "alt+a" },
    Entry { label: "Open native terminal", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::ToggleTerminal, key_hint: "alt+t" },
    Entry { label: "Widen chat", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::WidenChat, key_hint: "alt+]" },
    Entry { label: "Narrow chat", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::NarrowChat, key_hint: "alt+[" },
    Entry { label: "Switch Build / Plan", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::ToggleMode, key_hint: "tab" },
    Entry { label: "Clear session", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::ClearSession, key_hint: "/clear" },
    Entry { label: "Quit RomaCode", category: "Commands", action: RootAction::Quit, key_hint: "ctrl+q" },
    // Providers
    Entry { label: "Add Provider", category: "Providers", action: RootAction::AddKnownProvider, key_hint: "" },
    Entry { label: "Add Custom Provider", category: "Providers", action: RootAction::AddCustomProvider, key_hint: "" },
    Entry { label: "Select Model", category: "Providers", action: RootAction::SelectModel, key_hint: "" },
    // Tools — the integrated tools builder (38 builtin tools, 8 categories).
    Entry { label: "Tools — browse & run (38 builtin)", category: "Tools", action: RootAction::OpenTools, key_hint: "" },
    // Config
    Entry { label: "Open config file", category: "Config", action: RootAction::OpenConfigFile, key_hint: "" },
    Entry { label: "Print effective config (toast)", category: "Config", action: RootAction::PrintEffectiveConfig, key_hint: "" },
];

/// What kind of thing a mouse hit-test row points at — drives `on_mouse`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RowKind {
    /// A row in the root command list (index into the filtered `root_items`).
    RootItem(usize),
    /// A provider row (index into `KNOWN`).
    Provider(usize),
    /// A model row (index into `st.models`).
    Model(usize),
    /// A tool row (index into the filtered `tools_items`).
    Tool(usize),
}

/// One mouse-hit-testable row, recorded by `draw_settings` each frame.
/// Geometry is stored as plain `u16` quartets so this module stays free of the
/// ratatui dependency; `palette.rs` builds these from `Rect`s.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct HitRow {
    pub x: u16,
    pub y: u16,
    pub w: u16,
    pub h: u16,
    pub kind: RowKind,
}

impl HitRow {
    pub fn contains(&self, x: u16, y: u16) -> bool {
        x >= self.x && x < self.x.saturating_add(self.w) && y >= self.y && y < self.y.saturating_add(self.h)
    }
}

pub struct Settings {
    pub screen: Screen,
    pub sel: usize,
    /// Search query on the Root screen.
    pub query: String,
    /// Search query on the Providers screen (filters by provider name or id).
    pub provider_query: String,
    /// Search query on the Models / SelectModel screens (filters by model id
    /// or its provider id).
    pub model_query: String,
    /// Text input on KnownKey / CustomBase / CustomKey / ToolsInput.
    pub input: String,
    /// Cursor position inside `input` (chars). Input screens support full
    /// cursor editing: ←→ Home End Delete, and Backspace at the cursor.
    pub cursor: usize,
    pub provider_id: String,
    pub provider_name: String,
    /// Display name typed in the first step of the custom-provider flow.
    pub custom_name: String,
    pub kind: ApiKind,
    pub needs_key: bool,
    pub base_url: String,
    pub api_key: String,
    pub models: Vec<String>,
    pub model_providers: Vec<String>,
    pub error: Option<String>,
    pub loading: bool,
    /// Tools: search query.
    pub tools_query: String,
    /// Tools: selected row in the filtered list.
    pub tools_sel: usize,
    /// Tools: the name of the tool a ToolsInput screen is editing.
    pub tools_selected: Option<String>,
    /// Tools: the last run result (ok flag + pretty json or error string).
    pub tools_result: Option<(bool, String)>,
}

impl Settings {
    pub fn root() -> Self {
        Self {
            screen: Screen::Root,
            needs_key: false,
            sel: 0,
            query: String::new(),
            provider_query: String::new(),
            model_query: String::new(),
            input: String::new(),
            cursor: 0,
            provider_id: String::new(),
            provider_name: String::new(),
            custom_name: String::new(),
            kind: ApiKind::OpenAi,
            base_url: String::new(),
            api_key: String::new(),
            models: Vec::new(),
            model_providers: Vec::new(),
            error: None,
            loading: false,
            tools_query: String::new(),
            tools_sel: 0,
            tools_selected: None,
            tools_result: None,
        }
    }

    /// Filtered + ordered list of `(original_index, &Entry)` matching the query.
    /// Empty query returns every entry in declared order.
    pub fn root_items(&self) -> Vec<(usize, &'static Entry)> {
        let q = self.query.to_lowercase();
        ENTRIES
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, e)| {
                q.is_empty()
                    || e.label.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                    || e.category.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                    || e.key_hint.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
            })
            .map(|(i, e)| (i, e))
            .collect()
    }

    /// Filtered tool list (names) for the Tools screen, matching the query by
    /// name or category. The actual tool entries come from `App::tools`; this
    /// returns the indices into the full sorted list that match, so the draw
    /// and key handlers stay in sync.
    pub fn tools_filter(&self, all: &[String]) -> Vec<usize> {
        let q = self.tools_query.to_lowercase();
        all.iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, n)| q.is_empty() || n.to_lowercase().contains(&q))
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .collect()
    }

    /// Providers matching `provider_query`, as `(original_index, provider)`.
    /// `sel` on the Providers screen is an index into this filtered list.
    pub fn provider_items(&self) -> Vec<(usize, &'static Known)> {
        let q = self.provider_query.trim().to_lowercase();
        catalog::known()
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, k)| {
                q.is_empty()
                    || k.name.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                    || k.id.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Models matching `model_query`, as original indices into `self.models`.
    /// Matching the provider id too means "anthropic" finds that provider's
    /// models even when the id itself does not contain the word.
    pub fn model_items(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
        let q = self.model_query.trim().to_lowercase();
        self.models
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(i, m)| {
                q.is_empty()
                    || m.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                    || self
                        .model_providers
                        .get(*i)
                        .map_or(false, |p| p.to_lowercase().contains(&q))
            })
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .collect()
    }

    /// Providers plus the trailing "Custom provider…" row.
    pub fn provider_total(&self) -> usize {
        self.provider_items().len() + 1
    }

    /// The provider under the cursor on the Providers screen. `None` on the
    /// trailing custom-provider row.
    pub fn selected_provider(&self) -> Option<&'static Known> {
        let items = self.provider_items();
        if self.sel >= items.len() {
            return None;
        }
        let (idx, _) = items.get(self.sel.min(items.len().saturating_sub(1)))?;
        catalog::known_at(*idx)
    }

    /// The original model index under the cursor on a Models screen.
    pub fn selected_model_index(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        let items = self.model_items();
        items.get(self.sel.min(items.len().saturating_sub(1))).copied()
    }

    /// Number of selectable rows on the current screen, after filtering.
    pub fn visible_len(&self, tool_names: &[String]) -> usize {
        match self.screen {
            Screen::Root => self.root_items().len(),
            Screen::Providers => self.provider_total(),
            Screen::Models | Screen::SelectModel => self.model_items().len(),
            Screen::Tools => self.tools_filter(tool_names).len(),
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    /// Keep the cursor inside the visible list. Call after every key / wheel
    /// event and on entry so a stale index can never point past the end (the
    /// old code only clamped on Down, which made Up from a stale index jump).
    pub fn clamp_sel(&mut self, tool_names: &[String]) {
        let max = self.visible_len(tool_names).saturating_sub(1);
        self.sel = self.sel.min(max);
    }

    #[allow(dead_code)] // panel API parity with the palette
    pub fn field(&self) -> &str {
        &self.input
    }
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub fn field_mut(&mut self) -> &mut String {
        &mut self.input
    }
    pub fn begin_known(&mut self, k: &Known) {
        self.screen = Screen::KnownKey;
        self.sel = 0;
        self.input.clear();
        self.cursor = 0;
        self.error = None;
        self.provider_id = k.id.clone();
        self.provider_name = k.name.clone();
        self.kind = k.kind;
        self.needs_key = k.needs_key;
        self.base_url = k.base_url.clone();
        self.api_key.clear();
    }
    /// The custom-provider flow now starts with a NAME, then base URL, then
    /// API key, then the model fetch. The last row of the Providers picker
    /// opens this flow.
    pub fn begin_custom(&mut self) {
        self.screen = Screen::CustomName;
        self.sel = 0;
        self.input.clear();
        self.cursor = 0;
        self.error = None;
        self.provider_id.clear();
        self.provider_name.clear();
        self.custom_name.clear();
        self.kind = ApiKind::OpenAi;
        self.needs_key = false;
        self.base_url.clear();
        self.api_key.clear();
    }

    /// Slug used as the config id for a custom provider name.
    pub fn custom_id_from_name(name: &str) -> String {
        let mut id = String::new();
        let mut dash = false;
        for c in name.trim().to_lowercase().chars() {
            if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
                if dash && !id.is_empty() { id.push('-'); }
                id.push(c);
                dash = false;
            } else {
                dash = true;
            }
        }
        if id.is_empty() { "custom".to_string() } else { id }
    }
    pub fn begin_models(&mut self, models: Vec<String>) {
        self.screen = Screen::Models;
        self.sel = 0;
        self.models = models;
        // This is a single-provider list; a previous SelectModel visit may
        // have left per-row provider ids behind.
        self.model_providers.clear();
        self.model_query.clear();
        self.error = None;
        self.loading = false;
    }

    /// A failed live fetch must not leave an empty model picker: the key was
    /// already saved, so the built-in catalog still gives the user real model
    /// options to pick from (a pick persists through SaveModel like any other),
    /// with the fetch error surfaced alongside so nothing fails silently.
    ///
    /// The model list comes from the bundled in-memory catalog
    /// (`romacode_providers::catalog::bundled()`). The network-fetched
    /// `cached()` variant must never run here: it blocks the UI thread on
    /// expiry and uses a no-TLS client against HTTPS, so it always failed.
    pub fn begin_models_fallback(&mut self, reason: &str) {
        // 1. Bundled catalog only — in-memory, no network path.
        let mut suggestions: Vec<String> =
            romacode_providers::catalog::Catalog::bundled()
                .models(self.provider_id.trim())
                .iter()
                .map(|m| m.model_id.as_str().to_string())
                .collect();
        // 2. Fall back to the legacy static catalog if the dynamic one had
        // nothing for this provider (keeps every previously-known provider
        // working even when the network catalog is unreachable).
        if suggestions.is_empty() {
            suggestions = catalog::find(self.provider_id.trim())
                .map(|k| k.models.iter().map(|m| m.to_string()).collect())
                .unwrap_or_default();
        }
        if suggestions.is_empty() {
            self.loading = false;
            self.error = Some(reason.to_string());
            return;
        }
        self.begin_models(suggestions);
        self.error = Some(format!(
            "{reason} — showing the built-in catalog for {}; pick one or retry the fetch.",
            self.provider_name
        ));
    }
    pub fn begin_tools(&mut self) {
        self.screen = Screen::Tools;
        self.sel = 0;
        self.tools_sel = 0;
        self.tools_query.clear();
        self.tools_selected = None;
        self.tools_result = None;
        self.error = None;
    }
    pub fn begin_tools_input(&mut self, name: String) {
        self.screen = Screen::ToolsInput;
        self.input.clear();
        self.cursor = 0;
        self.error = None;
        self.tools_selected = Some(name);
        self.tools_result = None;
        // A sane default JSON object so Enter works immediately for no-param tools.
        self.input = "{}".to_string();
        self.cursor = 1;
    }

    // ── input editing (cursor-based) ────────────────────────────────────────

    fn clamp_cursor(&mut self) {
        self.cursor = self.cursor.min(self.input.chars().count());
    }
    pub fn input_char(&mut self, c: char) {
        let idx = self.char_index(self.cursor);
        self.input.insert(idx, c);
        self.cursor += 1;
    }
    pub fn input_backspace(&mut self) {
        self.clamp_cursor();
        if self.cursor > 0 {
            let idx = self.char_index(self.cursor - 1);
            self.input.remove(idx);
            self.cursor -= 1;
        }
    }
    pub fn input_delete(&mut self) {
        self.clamp_cursor();
        if self.cursor < self.input.chars().count() {
            let idx = self.char_index(self.cursor);
            self.input.remove(idx);
        }
    }
    pub fn input_left(&mut self) {
        self.clamp_cursor();
        self.cursor = self.cursor.saturating_sub(1);
    }
    pub fn input_right(&mut self) {
        self.clamp_cursor();
        self.cursor = (self.cursor + 1).min(self.input.chars().count());
    }
    pub fn input_home(&mut self) {
        self.cursor = 0;
    }
    pub fn input_end(&mut self) {
        self.cursor = self.input.chars().count();
    }
    /// Paste into the input: control characters (incl. CR/LF from terminals)
    /// are stripped so a pasted key or URL can never break the field.
    pub fn input_paste(&mut self, s: &str) {
        for c in s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()) {
            self.input_char(c);
        }
    }
    /// Paste into the Root search query (same control-char filter).
    pub fn query_paste(&mut self, s: &str) {
        for c in s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()) {
            self.query.push(c);
        }
        self.sel = 0;
    }
    /// Paste into the Tools search query.
    pub fn tools_query_paste(&mut self, s: &str) {
        for c in s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()) {
            self.tools_query.push(c);
        }
        self.tools_sel = 0;
    }
    /// Paste into the Providers search query.
    pub fn provider_query_paste(&mut self, s: &str) {
        for c in s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()) {
            self.provider_query.push(c);
        }
        self.sel = 0;
    }
    /// Paste into the Models search query.
    pub fn model_query_paste(&mut self, s: &str) {
        for c in s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()) {
            self.model_query.push(c);
        }
        self.sel = 0;
    }
    /// Visible form of the input: secrets masked, cursor rendered at position.
    pub fn input_display(&self, mask: bool) -> String {
        let cur = self.cursor.min(self.input.chars().count());
        let chars: Vec<char> = self.input.chars().collect();
        let (before, after) = (
            chars[..cur].iter().collect::<String>(),
            chars[cur..].iter().collect::<String>(),
        );
        if mask {
            format!(
                "{}▌{}",
                "•".repeat(before.chars().count()),
                "•".repeat(after.chars().count())
            )
        } else {
            format!("{before}▌{after}")
        }
    }
    fn char_index(&self, char_pos: usize) -> usize {
        self.input
            .char_indices()
            .nth(char_pos)
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .unwrap_or(self.input.len())
    }
}

pub type FetchResult = Result<Vec<String>, String>;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A failed live fetch must not leave an empty model picker: a KNOWN
    /// provider falls back to its catalog (now the dynamic OpenCode-structured
    /// catalog, with the legacy static catalog as a last-resort fallback), with
    /// the fetch error surfaced alongside. A custom provider has no suggestions
    /// and shows the error alone.
    #[test]
    fn fetch_failure_falls_back_to_catalog_suggestions_for_known_providers() {
        let known = catalog::find("groq").expect("groq is in the shared catalog");
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_known(known);
        st.begin_models_fallback("provider returned an empty model list");
        assert_eq!(st.screen, Screen::Models);
        // The new dynamic catalog is consulted first; if it has groq models,
        // those are shown. Either way the picker must not be empty for a known
        // provider, and the error must be surfaced.
        assert!(!st.models.is_empty(), "picker must not be empty for a known provider");
        let err = st.error.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
        assert!(err.contains("built-in catalog"), "error should mention the catalog: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("provider returned an empty model list"), "{err}");
        assert!(!st.loading);

        // a custom provider has no suggestions: the error alone is shown
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_custom();
        st.provider_id = "custom-1".into();
        st.begin_models_fallback("connection refused");
        assert!(st.models.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(st.error.as_deref(), Some("connection refused"));
        assert!(!st.loading);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cursor_editing_edits_the_middle_of_the_field() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_custom();
        for c in "abc".chars() {
            st.input_char(c);
        }
        assert_eq!(st.cursor, 3);
        st.input_left();
        st.input_left();
        assert_eq!(st.cursor, 1);
        st.input_delete(); // removes 'b' at the cursor
        assert_eq!(st.input, "ac");
        st.input_char('B');
        assert_eq!(st.input, "aBc");
        assert_eq!(st.cursor, 2);
        st.input_home();
        assert_eq!(st.cursor, 0);
        st.input_end();
        st.input_backspace();
        assert_eq!(st.input, "aB");

        // fix a base URL: https://wrong.io/v1 -> https://right.io/v1
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_custom();
        for c in "https://wrong.io/v1".chars() {
            st.input_char(c);
        }
        st.input_home();
        for _ in 0..8 {
            st.input_right();
        }
        assert_eq!(st.cursor, 8); // just before 'w'
        for _ in 0..5 {
            st.input_delete(); // drop "wrong"
        }
        assert_eq!(st.input, "https://.io/v1");
        for c in "right".chars() {
            st.input_char(c);
        }
        assert_eq!(st.input, "https://right.io/v1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn paste_strips_control_characters() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_known(&Known {
            id: "openai".into(),
            name: "OpenAI".into(),
            kind: ApiKind::OpenAi,
            base_url: "https://api.openai.com/v1".into(),
            key_env: "OPENAI_API_KEY".into(),
            needs_key: true,
            default_model: "gpt-4o".into(),
            models: vec![],
        });
        // terminals often terminate a bracketed paste with CRLF
        st.input_paste("sk-abc123\r\n");
        assert_eq!(st.input, "sk-abc123");
        st.query_paste("prov\tider");
        assert_eq!(st.query, "provider");
    }

    #[test]
    fn masked_display_hides_secrets_but_keeps_cursor() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_custom();
        for c in "abcd".chars() {
            st.input_char(c);
        }
        st.input_left();
        let shown = st.input_display(true);
        assert!(shown.starts_with("•••▌•"));
        let plain = st.input_display(false);
        assert!(plain.starts_with("abc▌d"));
    }

    /// Regression: "Add Custom Provider" must have exactly one entry point.
    #[test]
    fn custom_provider_has_exactly_one_entry_point() {
        let customs = ENTRIES.iter().filter(|e| e.action == RootAction::AddCustomProvider).count();
        let knowns = ENTRIES.iter().filter(|e| e.action == RootAction::AddKnownProvider).count();
        assert_eq!(customs, 1);
        assert_eq!(knowns, 1);
        assert_eq!(ENTRIES.iter().filter(|e| e.label.contains("Custom")).count(), 1);
    }

    /// The Tools entry exists exactly once and routes to OpenTools.
    #[test]
    fn tools_has_exactly_one_entry() {
        assert_eq!(
            ENTRIES.iter().filter(|e| e.action == RootAction::OpenTools).count(),
            1
        );
    }

    /// The three encodings terminals use for Backspace all edit the field.
    #[test]
    fn backspace_variants_edit_the_input() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.begin_custom();
        for c in "abc".chars() {
            st.input_char(c);
        }
        st.input.pop();
        assert_eq!(st.input, "ab");
        st.input_char('c');
        assert_eq!(st.input, "abc");
        st.input_backspace();
        assert_eq!(st.input, "ab");
        st.input_backspace();
        st.input_backspace();
        assert_eq!(st.input, "");
        st.input_backspace(); // no underflow on an empty field
        assert_eq!(st.input, "");
        assert_eq!(st.cursor, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn hit_row_contains_is_inclusive_origin_exclusive_far_edge() {
        let h = HitRow { x: 10, y: 5, w: 20, h: 1, kind: RowKind::Tool(0) };
        assert!(h.contains(10, 5));
        assert!(h.contains(29, 5));
        assert!(!h.contains(30, 5)); // far edge exclusive
        assert!(!h.contains(10, 6)); // height 1 → next row excluded
    }

    #[test]
    fn tools_filter_matches_name_substring() {
        let st = Settings::root();
        let all = vec!["math.add".into(), "math.sqrt".into(), "text.upper".into()];
        let idx = st.tools_filter(&all);
        assert_eq!(idx.len(), 3);
        let mut st = st;
        st.tools_query = "math".into();
        let idx = st.tools_filter(&all);
        assert_eq!(idx, vec![0, 1]);
    }

    /// Regression guard: the Settings category was fully removed from the Ctrl+P
    /// panel. No entry's category is "Settings" — the OpenCode-style settings
    /// dialog, the server-prefs editor, and the engine switcher are gone.
    #[test]
    fn no_settings_entries_remain_in_the_root_list() {
        assert!(ENTRIES.iter().all(|e| e.category != "Settings"));
        // Only the four surviving categories are present, in this order.
        let cats: Vec<&str> = {
            let mut c: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
            for e in ENTRIES {
                if c.last() != Some(&e.category) {
                    c.push(e.category);
                }
            }
            c
        };
        assert_eq!(cats, vec!["Commands", "Providers", "Tools", "Config"]);
    }
    #[test]
    fn provider_search_filters_by_name_or_id_and_maps_back() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.screen = Screen::Providers;
        st.provider_query = "openrouter".into();
        let items = st.provider_items();
        assert!(!items.is_empty());
        assert!(items.iter().all(|(_, k)| {
            k.id.to_lowercase().contains("openrouter")
                || k.name.to_lowercase().contains("openrouter")
        }));
        st.sel = 0;
        let picked = st.selected_provider().expect("filtered pick");
        assert_eq!(picked.id, "openrouter");

        st.provider_query = "no-such-provider-xyz".into();
        assert!(st.provider_items().is_empty());
        assert!(st.selected_provider().is_none());
        st.clamp_sel(&[]);
        assert_eq!(st.sel, 0, "cursor must never point past an empty list");
    }

    #[test]
    fn model_search_filters_by_model_and_provider() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.screen = Screen::SelectModel;
        st.models = vec!["alpha".into(), "beta".into(), "gamma".into()];
        st.model_providers = vec!["openai".into(), "anthropic".into(), "openai".into()];

        st.model_query = "openai".into();
        assert_eq!(st.model_items(), vec![0, 2]);
        st.sel = 1;
        assert_eq!(st.selected_model_index(), Some(2));

        st.model_query = "beta".into();
        assert_eq!(st.model_items(), vec![1]);
        st.clamp_sel(&[]);
        assert_eq!(st.sel, 0);
        assert_eq!(st.selected_model_index(), Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn visible_len_and_clamp_never_let_the_cursor_wrap() {
        let mut st = Settings::root();
        st.screen = Screen::Providers;
        st.sel = usize::MAX;
        st.clamp_sel(&[]);
        let last = st.provider_total() - 1; // includes the trailing custom row
        assert_eq!(st.sel, last, "stale index clamps to the last row, not past it");
        st.sel = 0;
        st.clamp_sel(&[]);
        assert_eq!(st.sel, 0);
    }

}
```

```rust
//! Built-in local terminal: Roxterm's VT grid/parser with a direct PTY.
//!
//! The local daemon, RPC server, runbook engine, and Roxterm shell-startup
//! injection are intentionally not used. Commands are run only in the user's
//! interactive shell inside this RomaCode process.
use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyModifiers};
use portable_pty::{native_pty_system, Child, CommandBuilder, MasterPty, PtySize};
use rox_vt::Screen as VtScreen;
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::mpsc::{self, Receiver, TryRecvError};
use std::thread::{self, JoinHandle};

const READ_CHUNK: usize = 8192;

pub struct RoxtermTerminal {
    pub screen: VtScreen,
    master: Option<Box<dyn MasterPty + Send>>,
    writer: Option<Box<dyn Write + Send>>,
    child: Option<Box<dyn Child + Send + Sync>>,
    output: Receiver<Vec<u8>>,
    reader_thread: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
    exit_code: Option<u32>,
    scrollback_offset: usize,
}

impl RoxtermTerminal {
    pub fn spawn(cols: u16, rows: u16, cwd: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let shell = std::env::var("SHELL")
            .ok()
            .filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
                if cfg!(windows) {
                    "cmd.exe".into()
                } else {
                    "sh".into()
                }
            });
        let cols = cols.max(2);
        let rows = rows.max(2);
        let system = native_pty_system();
        let pair = system
            .openpty(PtySize {
                rows,
                cols,
                pixel_width: 0,
                pixel_height: 0,
            })
            .map_err(|e| format!("open terminal PTY: {e}"))?;
        let mut command = CommandBuilder::new(&shell);
        command.cwd(cwd);
        command.env("TERM", "xterm-256color");
        command.env("COLORTERM", "truecolor");
        #[cfg(unix)]
        command.arg("-i");
        let child = pair
            .slave
            .spawn_command(command)
            .map_err(|e| format!("start shell {shell:?}: {e}"))?;
        let writer = pair
            .master
            .take_writer()
            .map_err(|e| format!("open PTY input: {e}"))?;
        let reader = pair
            .master
            .try_clone_reader()
            .map_err(|e| format!("open PTY output: {e}"))?;
        drop(pair.slave);

        let (tx, output) = mpsc::channel::<Vec<u8>>();
        let reader_thread = thread::Builder::new()
            .name("romacode-roxterm-reader".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let mut reader = reader;
                let mut buffer = [0u8; READ_CHUNK];
                loop {
                    match reader.read(&mut buffer) {
                        Ok(0) => break,
                        Ok(n) => {
                            if tx.send(buffer[..n].to_vec()).is_err() {
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                        Err(_) => break,
                    }
                }
            })
            .map_err(|e| format!("start PTY reader: {e}"))?;

        Ok(Self {
            screen: VtScreen::new(cols as usize, rows as usize),
            master: Some(pair.master),
            writer: Some(writer),
            child: Some(child),
            output,
            reader_thread: Some(reader_thread),
            exit_code: None,
            scrollback_offset: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Consume all available PTY bytes into Roxterm's VT parser.
    pub fn poll(&mut self) -> bool {
        let mut changed = false;
        loop {
            match self.output.try_recv() {
                Ok(bytes) => {
                    self.screen.feed(&bytes);
                    changed = true;
                }
                Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => break,
                Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected) => break,
            }
        }
        if self.exit_code.is_none() {
            if let Some(child) = self.child.as_mut() {
                if let Ok(Some(status)) = child.try_wait() {
                    self.exit_code = Some(status.exit_code());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
        changed
    }

    pub fn resize(&mut self, cols: u16, rows: u16) -> Result<(), String> {
        let cols = cols.max(2);
        let rows = rows.max(2);
        self.screen.resize(cols as usize, rows as usize);
        self.master
            .as_mut()
            .ok_or_else(|| "terminal PTY is closed".to_string())?
            .resize(PtySize {
                rows,
                cols,
                pixel_width: 0,
                pixel_height: 0,
            })
            .map_err(|e| format!("resize terminal PTY: {e}"))
    }

    pub fn send_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.scroll_to_bottom();
        let bytes = encode_key(key);
        self.write_input(&bytes)
    }

    pub fn send_paste(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.scroll_to_bottom();
        let bytes = if self.screen.bracketed_paste() {
            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(text.len() + 12);
            out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[200~");
            out.extend_from_slice(text.as_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(b"\x1b[201~");
            out
        } else {
            text.as_bytes().to_vec()
        };
        self.write_input(&bytes)
    }

    fn write_input(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
        if bytes.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let writer = self
            .writer
            .as_mut()
            .ok_or_else(|| "terminal PTY is closed".to_string())?;
        writer
            .write_all(bytes)
            .map_err(|e| format!("write terminal input: {e}"))?;
        writer
            .flush()
            .map_err(|e| format!("flush terminal input: {e}"))
    }

    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.exit_code
    }

    pub fn visible_rows(&self) -> Vec<rox_protocol::RowWire> {
        self.screen.viewport_rows(self.scrollback_offset)
    }

    pub fn scroll_scrollback(&mut self, rows: isize) {
        if rows >= 0 {
            self.scrollback_offset = self.scrollback_offset.saturating_add(rows as usize);
        } else {
            self.scrollback_offset = self.scrollback_offset.saturating_sub(rows.unsigned_abs());
        }
        self.scrollback_offset = self.scrollback_offset.min(self.screen.scrollback_len());
    }

    pub fn scroll_to_bottom(&mut self) {
        self.scrollback_offset = 0;
    }
}

impl Drop for RoxtermTerminal {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(child) = self.child.as_mut() {
            let _ = child.kill();
            let _ = child.wait();
        }
        self.writer.take();
        self.master.take();
        if let Some(thread) = self.reader_thread.take() {
            let _ = thread.join();
        }
    }
}

/// Encode common terminal keys as xterm-compatible input bytes.
pub fn encode_key(key: KeyEvent) -> Vec<u8> {
    let ctrl = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL);
    let alt = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::ALT);
    let shift = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::SHIFT);
    let modifier = 1 + u8::from(shift) + 2 * u8::from(alt) + 4 * u8::from(ctrl);
    let mut bytes = match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char(c) if ctrl => {
            let c = c.to_ascii_lowercase();
            let b = c as u32;
            let control = match c {
                '@' | ' ' => Some(0),
                'a'..='z' => Some((c as u8) - b'a' + 1),
                '[' => Some(0x1b),
                '\\' => Some(0x1c),
                ']' => Some(0x1d),
                '^' => Some(0x1e),
                '_' => Some(0x1f),
                '?' => Some(0x7f),
                _ if b < 0x80 => None,
                _ => None,
            };
            control.map(|b| vec![b]).unwrap_or_default()
        }
        KeyCode::Char(c) => {
            let mut buf = [0u8; 4];
            c.encode_utf8(&mut buf).as_bytes().to_vec()
        }
        KeyCode::Enter => vec![b'\r'],
        KeyCode::Backspace => vec![0x7f],
        KeyCode::Tab if shift => b"\x1b[Z".to_vec(),
        KeyCode::Tab => vec![b'\t'],
        KeyCode::BackTab => b"\x1b[Z".to_vec(),
        KeyCode::Esc => vec![0x1b],
        KeyCode::Up => arrow(b'A', modifier),
        KeyCode::Down => arrow(b'B', modifier),
        KeyCode::Right => arrow(b'C', modifier),
        KeyCode::Left => arrow(b'D', modifier),
        KeyCode::Home => csi_tilde_or_final(b'H', modifier),
        KeyCode::End => csi_tilde_or_final(b'F', modifier),
        KeyCode::Insert => csi_tilde(2, modifier),
        KeyCode::Delete => csi_tilde(3, modifier),
        KeyCode::PageUp => csi_tilde(5, modifier),
        KeyCode::PageDown => csi_tilde(6, modifier),
        KeyCode::F(n @ 1..=4) => {
            let final_byte = b'P' + n - 1;
            if modifier == 1 {
                vec![0x1b, b'O', final_byte]
            } else {
                arrow(final_byte, modifier)
            }
        }
        KeyCode::F(n @ 5..=12) => {
            const CODES: [u8; 8] = [15, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24];
            csi_tilde(CODES[(n - 5) as usize], modifier)
        }
        _ => Vec::new(),
    };
    if alt && !ctrl && !bytes.is_empty() && !bytes.starts_with(b"\x1b") {
        bytes.insert(0, 0x1b);
    }
    bytes
}

fn arrow(final_byte: u8, modifier: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
    if modifier == 1 {
        vec![0x1b, b'[', final_byte]
    } else {
        format!("\x1b[1;{modifier}{}", final_byte as char).into_bytes()
    }
}

fn csi_tilde(code: u8, modifier: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
    if modifier == 1 {
        format!("\x1b[{code}~").into_bytes()
    } else {
        format!("\x1b[{code};{modifier}~").into_bytes()
    }
}

fn csi_tilde_or_final(final_byte: u8, modifier: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
    if modifier == 1 {
        vec![0x1b, b'[', final_byte]
    } else {
        format!("\x1b[1;{modifier}{}", final_byte as char).into_bytes()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn key(code: KeyCode, modifiers: KeyModifiers) -> KeyEvent {
        KeyEvent::new(code, modifiers)
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_basic_terminal_keys() {
        assert_eq!(
            encode_key(key(KeyCode::Char('x'), KeyModifiers::NONE)),
            b"x"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_key(key(KeyCode::Char('c'), KeyModifiers::CONTROL)),
            &[3]
        );
        assert_eq!(encode_key(key(KeyCode::Enter, KeyModifiers::NONE)), b"\r");
        assert_eq!(encode_key(key(KeyCode::Up, KeyModifiers::NONE)), b"\x1b[A");
        assert_eq!(
            encode_key(key(KeyCode::BackTab, KeyModifiers::NONE)),
            b"\x1b[Z"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_modified_navigation_and_unicode() {
        assert_eq!(
            encode_key(key(KeyCode::Right, KeyModifiers::CONTROL)),
            b"\x1b[1;5C"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_key(key(KeyCode::Char('λ'), KeyModifiers::NONE)),
            "λ".as_bytes()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            encode_key(key(KeyCode::Char('x'), KeyModifiers::ALT)),
            b"\x1bx"
        );
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn interactive_pty_runs_a_shell_command_and_parses_output() {
        let cwd = std::env::current_dir().expect("current directory");
        let mut terminal = RoxtermTerminal::spawn(80, 24, &cwd).expect("open local PTY shell");
        for ch in "printf '%s\\n' $((1234+3456))".chars() {
            terminal
                .send_key(KeyEvent::new(KeyCode::Char(ch), KeyModifiers::NONE))
                .expect("write PTY key");
        }
        terminal
            .send_key(KeyEvent::new(KeyCode::Enter, KeyModifiers::NONE))
            .expect("submit shell command");

        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(3);
        while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
            terminal.poll();
            if terminal.screen.snapshot_text().contains("4690") {
                return;
            }
            thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));
        }
        panic!(
            "shell output was not parsed by Roxterm: {}",
            terminal.screen.snapshot_text()
        );
    }
}
```

## `crates/client-tui/src/tools.rs`

[view on disk](crates/client-tui/src/tools.rs)

```rust
//! Bridge between the **sync** ratatui/crossterm event loop and the **async**
//! RomaCode tools builder. Holds a dedicated tokio runtime + a permissive
//! [`Lifecycle`] preloaded with the builtin source, and exposes plain sync
//! calls the Ctrl+P settings panel's Tools section uses: `count`, `list`,
//! `categories`, `schema_json`, `run`.
//!
//! The tools builder is the "unlimited" half of RomaCode — 38 built-in tools
//! across 8 categories (math, text, data, code, file, web, system, time),
//! reachable here through the same `ToolSource` trait as every other source.
//! The full framework (8 sources, 5 composition primitives) lives in the
//! `rc-*` crates; this bridge surfaces its builtin catalog to the TUI.

use rc_lifecycle::Lifecycle;
use rc_sources::builtin::BuiltinSource;
use serde_json::Value;

/// One row of the Tools list (a snapshot of a registered tool's identity).
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ToolEntry {
    pub name: String,
    pub category: String,
    pub description: String,
    /// Which tool-source mechanism produced this tool (builtin, declarative…).
    /// Surfaced for a future "info" view; not rendered in the list today.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub source: String,
}

/// A sync façade over the async tools builder, kept on the `App` and reused
/// across settings-panel opens. Constructed once; cheap to borrow.
pub struct Tools {
    rt: tokio::runtime::Runtime,
    life: Lifecycle,
}

impl Tools {
    /// Build the runtime, construct a permissive lifecycle, register the
    /// builtin source, and discover every tool. Synchronous from the caller's
    /// point of view (the discovery future is driven on the runtime).
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
            .enable_all()
            .build()
            .expect("tools builder: tokio runtime");
        let life = rt.block_on(async {
            let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
            life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
            let _ = life.discover().await;
            life
        });
        Self { rt, life }
    }

    /// Total number of registered tools (the builtin catalog = 38).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {
        self.life.registry.len()
    }

    /// Every registered tool, sorted by name.
    pub fn list(&self) -> Vec<ToolEntry> {
        self.life
            .registry
            .list()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|i| ToolEntry {
                name: i.name,
                category: i.category,
                description: i.description,
                source: i.source,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Distinct categories, sorted (math, text, data, code, file, web, …).
    pub fn categories(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut cats: Vec<String> = self.list().iter().map(|t| t.category.clone()).collect();
        cats.sort();
        cats.dedup();
        cats
    }

    /// The JSON schema of one tool (for an info view), or `None` if unknown.
    pub fn schema_json(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        let t = self.life.registry.get(name).ok()?;
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&t.schema().to_json_schema()).ok()
    }

    /// Run a tool by name with a JSON input. Auto-approves (the Tools section
    /// is an explicit user action). Returns the tool's JSON output or an error
    /// string. Driven on the runtime so it never blocks the TUI's own (absent)
    /// async context — though a slow tool (web fetch) will block the UI thread
    /// for up to the sandbox timeout (15 s).
    pub fn run(&self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.rt
            .block_on(self.life.execute(name, input, true))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }

    /// Per-tool metrics snapshot (calls / successes / failures / latency).
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub fn metrics(&self, name: &str) -> Option<rc_lifecycle::ToolMetrics> {
        self.life.metrics_for(name)
    }
}

impl Default for Tools {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}
```

//! The Settings screen — Ctrl+P. ONE page, no drilling.
//!
//! Every row is a real setting. The layout is exactly what you see:
//! a main heading (APPEARANCE, PERMISSIONS, …) with its subsetting options
//! directly below it, all sections on one scrollable page. There are no
//! sub-screens to click through any more — the old
//! "open Settings → click the group → click the subgroup" flow is gone.
//!
//! Leaf paths are the dotted keys of the `romacode_shared::tui_settings`
//! catalog, so each row reads and writes the same value the brain persists:
//! ← → steps the value and the new value goes to the brain as a `tui.<path>`
//! preference. Rows that open a flow (Models, Providers, Tools, Config file)
//! hand off to the same-named screen inside the identical Settings panel.
//!
//! ```text
//! APPEARANCE ───────────────────────────────
//!   ○ Theme                              dark
//!   ○ Color mode                        system
//! AI & SERVER ──────────────────────────────
//!   ● Models / Providers / Tools / Config file
//! PERMISSIONS ──────────────────────────────
//!   ○ Manual             ask before shell commands
//!   ● Auto accept                       ✓ active   ← only the active row is marked
//! …every section follows on the same page…
//! ```
//!
//! Typing filters leaves (label or section); the `/` slash menu in chat
//! surfaces the same flattened list.

// ── data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Who owns a setting — drives the badge in the UI.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Owner {
    /// Lives in the brain's `config.json` (server side).
    Brain,
    /// Lives in the screen's `tui.*` tree (client side).
    Screen,
}

/// What a leaf does when activated.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum Leaf {
    /// A live setting: ← → step it through the catalog values.
    Setting { path: &'static str },
    /// A live setting pinned to one value (Manual / Auto accept).
    Preset { path: &'static str, value: &'static str },
    /// Hand off to one of the existing screen flows.
    Dest(Dest),
}

/// Where a `Dest` leaf routes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Dest {
    /// Open the Select Model screen (saved + fetched models).
    SelectModel,
    /// Open the Providers screen (add API keys, known + custom).
    OpenProviders,
    /// Open the integrated Tools builder.
    OpenTools,
    /// Toast the config file path.
    OpenConfigFile,
    /// Toast the effective config.
    PrintEffectiveConfig,
    /// Reset all settings to defaults.
    ResetSettings,
}

/// One node in the tree.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Node {
    pub label: &'static str,
    pub kind: NodeKind,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum NodeKind {
    Leaf { leaf: Leaf, owner: Owner, hint: &'static str },
    Group { children: &'static [Node] },
}

// ── the static sections ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Root-level sections, in display order. APPEARANCE comes first (it is the
/// section users reach for most); the renderer prints every section heading
/// with its rows directly below on the same page.
pub const ROOT: &[Node] = &[
    Node { label: "APPEARANCE", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: APPEARANCE } },
    Node { label: "AI & SERVER", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: AI_SERVER } },
    Node { label: "PERMISSIONS", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: PERMISSIONS } },
    Node { label: "SESSION", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: SESSION } },
    Node { label: "TABS & DIFFS", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: TABS_DIFFS } },
    Node { label: "INPUT", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: INPUT } },
    Node { label: "ALERTS", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: ALERTS } },
    Node { label: "ADVANCED", kind: NodeKind::Group { children: ADVANCED } },
];

// Manual asks before a shell command — the one action that leaves the project.
// Auto accept never asks. Reads, edits and web fetches run in both modes.
const PERMISSIONS: &[Node] = &[
    leaf("Manual", Owner::Brain, "ask before shell commands", Leaf::Preset {
        path: "session.permissions",
        value: "prompt",
    }),
    leaf("Auto accept", Owner::Brain, "run every tool without asking", Leaf::Preset {
        path: "session.permissions",
        value: "autoaccept",
    }),
];

const APPEARANCE: &[Node] = &[
    leaf("Theme", Owner::Screen, "color palette", Leaf::Setting { path: "theme.name" }),
    leaf("Color mode", Owner::Screen, "system / dark / light", Leaf::Setting { path: "theme.mode" }),
    leaf("Animations", Owner::Screen, "interface motion", Leaf::Setting { path: "animations" }),
    leaf("Release highlights", Owner::Screen, "show what's new", Leaf::Setting { path: "highlights" }),
    leaf("Window title", Owner::Screen, "terminal title", Leaf::Setting { path: "terminal.title" }),

];

const INPUT: &[Node] = &[
