```rust
//! SQL safety guard for the database tools.
//!
//! Sits between the agent's `db_query` / `db_execute` tool calls and the
//! underlying engine. Its job is classification, not enforcement: it returns a
//! [`Verdict`] describing whether a statement is safe to run without approval
//! (read-only), needs a Security approval card (destructive but allowed), or
//! must be refused outright. The agent loop, working through the Security
//! gateway, decides what to do with that verdict.
//!
//! The rules match the user spec: read-only passes are `SELECT`, `WITH`,
//! `EXPLAIN`, `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`/`DESC`, `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` (so a
//! read-only session can still manage its own transaction state). Anything
//! that mutates — `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`MERGE`/`CREATE`/`DROP`/
//! `TRUNCATE`/`ALTER`/`GRANT`/`REVOKE` — is flagged. `DELETE`/`UPDATE` without
//! a `WHERE` clause and `DROP`/`TRUNCATE`/`ALTER` are flagged as *destructive*
//! (red warning) even in read-write mode.

use std::fmt;

/// How risky a statement is. Set by [`SqlGuard::classify`].
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Verdict {
    /// `SELECT`, `WITH`, `EXPLAIN`, `SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`, transaction control.
    /// Safe to run in read-only and read-write modes without approval.
    ReadOnly,
    /// `INSERT`, `UPDATE ... WHERE`, `MERGE`, `CREATE TABLE`, etc. Allowed in
    /// read-write and full-access modes; needs approval in read-write.
    Write,
    /// `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, `ALTER`, `DELETE`/`UPDATE` without `WHERE`,
    /// `GRANT`/`REVOKE`. Always carries a red warning; needs approval even in
    /// read-write mode; refused in read-only mode.
    Destructive,
}

impl Verdict {
    pub fn is_read_only(self) -> bool { matches!(self, Verdict::ReadOnly) }
    pub fn is_destructive(self) -> bool { matches!(self, Verdict::Destructive) }
}

impl fmt::Display for Verdict {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(match self {
            Verdict::ReadOnly => "read-only",
            Verdict::Write => "write",
            Verdict::Destructive => "destructive",
        })
    }
}

/// The agent's database access tier (mirrors the TUI Database Access section).
/// This is the live setting, not the static config default; the agent loop
/// passes the currently-selected tier in so the guard is consistent with what
/// the user sees on screen.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum AccessTier {
    /// `Read-Only` — only [`Verdict::ReadOnly`] statements pass. Everything
    /// else is refused without even showing an approval card.
    #[default]
    ReadOnly,
    /// `Read-Write` — read-only and write pass; write needs an approval card.
    /// Destructive statements need an approval card AND carry a red warning.
    ReadWrite,
    /// `Full Access` — everything runs, no approval. Destructive statements
    /// still carry a red warning in the tool result so the user can audit.
    Full,
}

/// Stateless SQL classifier. Construct once per request.
pub struct SqlGuard {
    tier: AccessTier,
}

/// What the guard says about one statement.
pub struct Decision {
    pub verdict: Verdict,
    /// `true` if the statement may run under the current tier without an
    /// approval card.
    pub auto_run: bool,
    /// `true` if a Security approval card must be shown before running.
    pub needs_approval: bool,
    /// `true` if the statement is refused outright (the tier forbids it).
    pub refused: bool,
    /// Human-readable reason, suitable for showing in a tool result or the
    /// approval card body.
    pub reason: String,
}

impl SqlGuard {
    pub fn new(tier: AccessTier) -> Self { Self { tier } }
    pub fn tier(&self) -> AccessTier { self.tier }

    /// Classify a single SQL statement. Multi-statement scripts should be split
    /// by the caller and each part passed in; this returns the verdict for one.
    pub fn classify(&self, sql: &str) -> Decision {
        let stmt = Self::first_statement(sql);
        let verb = Self::leading_verb(&stmt);
        let verdict = Self::classify_verb(&verb, &stmt);
        let (auto_run, needs_approval, refused, reason) = match (self.tier, verdict) {
            (AccessTier::ReadOnly, Verdict::ReadOnly) =>
                (true, false, false, "read-only statement; allowed under Read-Only".into()),
            (AccessTier::ReadOnly, Verdict::Write) =>
                (false, false, true, "write statement; refused under Read-Only tier".into()),
            (AccessTier::ReadOnly, Verdict::Destructive) =>
                (false, false, true, "destructive statement; refused under Read-Only tier".into()),
            (AccessTier::ReadWrite, Verdict::ReadOnly) =>
                (true, false, false, "read-only statement; allowed under Read-Write".into()),
            (AccessTier::ReadWrite, Verdict::Write) =>
                (false, true, false, "write statement; requires approval under Read-Write".into()),
            (AccessTier::ReadWrite, Verdict::Destructive) =>
                (false, true, false, "DESTRUCTIVE statement; requires approval (red warning) under Read-Write".into()),
            (AccessTier::Full, Verdict::ReadOnly) =>
                (true, false, false, "read-only statement; allowed under Full Access".into()),
            (AccessTier::Full, Verdict::Write) =>
                (true, false, false, "write statement; allowed under Full Access".into()),
            (AccessTier::Full, Verdict::Destructive) =>
                (true, false, false, "DESTRUCTIVE statement; allowed under Full Access (red warning emitted)".into()),
        };
        Decision { verdict, auto_run, needs_approval, refused, reason }
    }

    /// First statement of a script, up to the first `;` that is not inside a
    /// quoted string. Good enough for classification; the engine parses the
    /// real SQL separately.
    fn first_statement(sql: &str) -> String {
        let s = sql.trim();
        let mut out = String::new();
        let mut in_single = false;
        let mut in_double = false;
        let mut in_back = false;
        let mut prev_dash = false;
        let mut in_line_comment = false;
        let mut in_block_comment = false;
        for ch in s.chars() {
            if in_line_comment { if ch == '\n' { in_line_comment = false; } continue; }
            if in_block_comment {
                if ch == '*' { /* peek next handled below */ }
                out.push(ch);
                if out.ends_with("*/") { in_block_comment = false; }
                continue;
            }
            match ch {
                '\'' if !in_double && !in_back => in_single = !in_single,
                '"' if !in_single && !in_back => in_double = !in_double,
                '`' if !in_single && !in_double => in_back = !in_back,
                '-' if !in_single && !in_double && !in_back => {
                    if prev_dash { in_line_comment = true; prev_dash = false; out.pop(); continue; }
                    prev_dash = true;
                }
                '/' if !in_single && !in_double && !in_back => {
                    // possible block comment start; we just push and let the
                    // ends_with check above close it. Good enough for classify.
                }
                _ => prev_dash = false,
            }
            out.push(ch);
            if ch == ';' && !in_single && !in_double && !in_back { break; }
        }
        out.trim().trim_end_matches(';').trim().to_string()
    }

    fn leading_verb(stmt: &str) -> String {
        // Skip leading parens / whitespace / comments, grab the first word.
        let mut s = stmt.trim_start();
        while let Some(stripped) = s.strip_prefix('(') { s = stripped.trim_start(); }
        s.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_uppercase()
    }

    fn classify_verb(verb: &str, stmt: &str) -> Verdict {
        // CTEs (`WITH ... SELECT`) read as WITH.
        match verb {
            "SELECT" | "WITH" | "EXPLAIN" | "DESC" | "DESCRIBE" | "SHOW" |
            "TABLE" | "VALUES" |
            "BEGIN" | "START" | "COMMIT" | "ROLLBACK" | "END" | "SET" |
            "PRAGMA" | "USE" => Verdict::ReadOnly,

            "INSERT" | "REPLACE" | "MERGE" | "UPSERT" => Verdict::Write,
            "UPDATE" => {
                if Self::has_where(stmt) { Verdict::Write } else { Verdict::Destructive }
            }
            "DELETE" => {
                if Self::has_where(stmt) { Verdict::Write } else { Verdict::Destructive }
            }
            "CREATE" => Verdict::Write,
            "DROP" | "TRUNCATE" | "ALTER" | "RENAME" => Verdict::Destructive,
            "GRANT" | "REVOKE" => Verdict::Destructive,
            "VACUUM" | "ANALYZE" | "REINDEX" => Verdict::Write,
            // Unknown verb — be conservative: treat as destructive so the user
            // always sees an approval card rather than a silent surprise.
            _ => Verdict::Destructive,
        }
    }

    fn has_where(stmt: &str) -> bool {
        // Look for a WHERE keyword outside of quotes/comments. Case-insensitive.
        let upper = stmt.to_uppercase();
        // crude but robust enough: split on whitespace and look for WHERE token
        upper.split_whitespace().any(|tok| tok == "WHERE")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn g(tier: AccessTier) -> SqlGuard { SqlGuard::new(tier) }

    #[test]
    fn select_is_read_only() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("SELECT * FROM users").verdict, Verdict::ReadOnly);
        assert!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("SELECT 1").auto_run);
    }

    #[test]
    fn with_cte_is_read_only() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("WITH t AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM t").verdict, Verdict::ReadOnly);
    }

    #[test]
    fn explain_and_show_are_read_only() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("EXPLAIN SELECT 1").verdict, Verdict::ReadOnly);
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("SHOW TABLES").verdict, Verdict::ReadOnly);
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_is_write() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)").verdict, Verdict::Write);
        let d = g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)");
        assert!(d.refused);
    }

    #[test]
    fn delete_without_where_is_destructive() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadWrite).classify("DELETE FROM users").verdict, Verdict::Destructive);
    }

    #[test]
    fn delete_with_where_is_write() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadWrite).classify("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 1").verdict, Verdict::Write);
    }

    #[test]
    fn update_without_where_is_destructive() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadWrite).classify("UPDATE users SET name='x'").verdict, Verdict::Destructive);
    }

    #[test]
    fn drop_truncate_alter_are_destructive() {
        for s in ["DROP TABLE t", "TRUNCATE TABLE t", "ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN c"] {
            assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::Full).classify(s).verdict, Verdict::Destructive, "{s}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn readwrite_write_needs_approval() {
        let d = g(AccessTier::ReadWrite).classify("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)");
        assert!(!d.auto_run && d.needs_approval && !d.refused);
    }

    #[test]
    fn readwrite_destructive_needs_approval_and_warns() {
        let d = g(AccessTier::ReadWrite).classify("DROP TABLE t");
        assert!(!d.auto_run && d.needs_approval && !d.refused);
        assert!(d.reason.contains("DESTRUCTIVE") || d.reason.contains("destructive"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn readonly_refuses_destructive_without_approval() {
        let d = g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify("DROP TABLE t");
        assert!(d.refused && !d.needs_approval && !d.auto_run);
    }

    #[test]
    fn full_access_runs_everything_without_approval() {
        let d = g(AccessTier::Full).classify("DROP TABLE t");
        assert!(d.auto_run && !d.needs_approval && !d.refused);
    }

    #[test]
    fn first_statement_trims_trailing_semicolon() {
        assert_eq!(SqlGuard::first_statement("SELECT 1;"), "SELECT 1");
        assert_eq!(SqlGuard::first_statement("  SELECT 1  "), "SELECT 1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn transaction_control_is_read_only() {
        for s in ["BEGIN", "COMMIT", "ROLLBACK"] {
            assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::ReadOnly).classify(s).verdict, Verdict::ReadOnly, "{s}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn grant_revoke_are_destructive() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::Full).classify("GRANT ALL ON db.* TO 'u'").verdict, Verdict::Destructive);
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::Full).classify("REVOKE ALL ON db.* FROM 'u'").verdict, Verdict::Destructive);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_verb_is_destructive() {
        assert_eq!(g(AccessTier::Full).classify("WIBBLE t").verdict, Verdict::Destructive);
    }

    #[test]
    fn first_statement_respects_quotes() {
        // semicolon inside a string literal is not a statement terminator
        assert_eq!(SqlGuard::first_statement("INSERT INTO t VALUES ('a;b')"), "INSERT INTO t VALUES ('a;b')");
    }
}
```

## `crates/db/src/lib.rs`

[view on disk](crates/db/src/lib.rs)

```rust
//! `romacode-db` — built-in native database engine.
//!
//! This crate vendors `dbengine` (a pure-Rust, std-only, single-file database
//! engine) directly into the RomaCode workspace as a **native library**, NOT an
//! MCP server. The engine handles local key-addressed storage and speaks the
//! postgres / mysql / redis / http wire protocols for remote introspection.
//!
//! The engine is wrapped behind [`DbEngine`], which accepts and returns plain
//! `serde_json::Value` so the rest of RomaCode never has to know about the
//! engine's internal `J` JSON type. Every tool name listed in [`DbEngine::call`]
//! dispatches straight into the engine's in-process handler table — no stdio,
//! no subprocess, no MCP framing.
//!
//! `guard::SqlGuard` is the read-only / destructive-SQL policy that sits in
//! front of `db_query` / `db_execute` and is what the Security gateway uses to
//! decide whether a statement needs an approval card.

pub mod engine;
pub mod guard;

pub use engine::{Engine, J, R, tools_call, selftest};
pub use guard::{SqlGuard, Verdict};

use serde_json::Value;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// Native database engine handle. Lives in-process; one instance per RomaCode
/// server. Internally holds the dbengine `Engine` (local key-addressed store
/// plus remote connection state).
pub struct DbEngine {
    inner: engine::Engine,
}

/// Default on-disk home: `<workspace>/.romacode/db`. Caller chooses at build
/// time; romacode-server passes the configured `state_dir` here.
impl DbEngine {
    /// Open (creating if absent) a database home directory.
    pub fn open(home: impl AsRef<Path>) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let home = home.as_ref().to_path_buf();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&home)?;
        Ok(Self { inner: engine::Engine::new(home) })
    }

    /// In-memory home in /tmp — used by tests and the `db test` CLI smoke.
    pub fn ephemeral() -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("romacode-db-{}", std::process::id()));
        Self::open(&dir)
    }

    /// Run the engine's built-in selftest (pure logic, no network). Returns
    /// the number of failures (0 = pass). Exposed so `romacode-server db test`
    /// can report engine health.
    pub fn selftest_failures() -> i32 {
        engine::selftest()
    }

    /// The home directory backing this engine.
    pub fn home(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.inner.home
    }

    /// Call one engine tool by name with a JSON arguments object.
    ///
    /// `name` is one of the engine's tool ids — `db_status`, `db_create_table`,
    /// `db_schema`, `db_insert`, `db_get`, `db_scan`, `db_sql`, `db_keys`,
    /// `db_graph`, `db_topo`, `db_connect`, `db_remote_query`,
    /// `db_remote_schema`, `db_extract`, `db_export_bundle`, ... (full list in
    /// `engine::tools_call`). The returned `Value` is the tool's result object
    /// already converted from the engine's internal `J`.
    ///
    /// This is the single entry point romacode-server's tool dispatcher uses;
    /// there is no subprocess and no MCP framing.
    pub fn call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        // tools_call expects {"name": <tool>, "arguments": <args>} — the MCP
        // tools/call envelope. Build it here so callers pass the bare args.
        let params = Value::Object(serde_json::Map::from_iter([
            ("name".to_string(), Value::String(name.to_string())),
            ("arguments".to_string(), args.clone()),
        ]));
        let jparams = value_to_j(&params);
        let res = engine::tools_call(&mut self.inner, &jparams);
        // `tools_call` wraps BOTH successes and tool-level failures in an
        // MCP-style {"content":[{text}], "isError": bool} envelope (it was an
        // MCP server). Unwrap: isError=true becomes Err, otherwise the parsed
        // JSON of the text field.
        match res {
            Ok(envelope) => unwrap_envelope(envelope),
            Err(e) => Err(e),
        }
    }

    /// List the names of every engine tool, for schema advertisement.
    pub fn tools() -> &'static [&'static str] {
        &[
            "db_status", "db_create_table", "db_drop_table", "db_schema",
            "db_insert", "db_get", "db_update", "db_delete", "db_scan",
            "db_count", "db_sql", "db_keys", "db_graph", "db_topo",
            "db_diff", "db_snapshot", "db_branch", "db_merge", "db_sync",
            "db_connect", "db_remote_query", "db_remote_schema", "db_extract",
            "db_import_bundle", "db_export_bundle", "db_fingerprint", "db_compact",
        ]
    }
}

/// Pull the `text` field out of the engine's MCP-style result envelope and
/// parse it back to JSON. If the envelope carries `isError`, surface it as
/// `Err` so the caller treats it as a tool failure (matching how a real error
/// would flow through the agent loop).
fn unwrap_envelope(env: J) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let is_err = env.get("isError").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false);
    let text = env
        .get("content")
        .and_then(|c| c.as_arr())
        .and_then(|arr| arr.first())
        .and_then(|first| first.get("text"))
        .and_then(|t| t.as_str())
        .unwrap_or("");
    // The engine always writes valid JSON via jpretty. If it ever fails to
    // parse, fall back to the raw text so the caller still sees something.
    if is_err {
        return Err(text.to_string());
    }
    if let Ok(j) = engine::jparse(text) {
        Ok(j_to_value(&j))
    } else {
        Ok(Value::String(text.to_string()))
    }
}

// ---- serde_json::Value <-> engine J conversion ----

fn value_to_j(v: &Value) -> J {
    match v {
        Value::Null => J::Null,
        Value::Bool(b) => J::Bool(*b),
        Value::Number(n) => {
            if let Some(i) = n.as_i64() {
                J::Int(i)
            } else if let Some(f) = n.as_f64() {
                J::Num(f)
            } else {
                J::Null
            }
        }
        Value::String(s) => J::Str(s.clone()),
        Value::Array(a) => J::Arr(a.iter().map(value_to_j).collect()),
        Value::Object(o) => {
            let pairs: Vec<(String, J)> = o.iter().map(|(k, vv)| (k.clone(), value_to_j(vv))).collect();
            J::Obj(pairs)
        }
    }
}

fn j_to_value(j: &J) -> Value {
    match j {
        J::Null => Value::Null,
        J::Bool(b) => Value::Bool(*b),
        J::Int(i) => Value::Number((*i).into()),
        J::Num(f) => serde_json::Number::from_f64(*f).map(Value::Number).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
        J::Str(s) => Value::String(s.clone()),
        J::Arr(a) => Value::Array(a.iter().map(j_to_value).collect()),
        J::Obj(pairs) => {
            let m: serde_json::Map<String, Value> =
                pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), j_to_value(v))).collect();
            Value::Object(m)
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    fn fresh() -> DbEngine {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("rmdb-test-{}-{}", std::process::id(), unique()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        DbEngine::open(&dir).unwrap()
    }

    fn unique() -> String {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
        static N: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
        N.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst).to_string()
    }

    #[test]
    fn status_reports_home() {
        let mut e = fresh();
        let r = e.call("db_status", &json!({})).unwrap();
        assert!(r.get("home").is_some() || r.is_object(), "status returned {r}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn create_insert_get_roundtrip() {
        let mut e = fresh();
        e.call("db_create_table", &json!({
            "db": "testdb", "table": "users",
            "primary_key": ["id"],
            "columns": [
                {"name":"id","dtype":"integer"},
                {"name":"name","dtype":"text"}
            ]
        })).unwrap();
        e.call("db_insert", &json!({
            "db":"testdb","table":"users",
            "rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"}]
        })).unwrap();
        // db_get takes the raw primary-key value (scalar when pk is one column)
        let got = e.call("db_get", &json!({"db":"testdb","table":"users","key":1})).unwrap();
        let s = serde_json::to_string(&got).unwrap();
        assert!(s.contains("ada"), "got {s}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_tool_errors() {
        let mut e = fresh();
        let r = e.call("db_nonexistent", &json!({}));
        assert!(r.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn tools_list_nonempty() {
        assert!(DbEngine::tools().len() >= 20);
    }

    #[test]
    fn home_dir_backed() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("rmdb-home-{}", unique()));
        let e = DbEngine::open(&dir).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.home(), dir);
        assert!(dir.exists());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Append-only loot ledger. Single writer for the engagement database.
//! Tools never touch SQL; they hand LootRow values to `insert`.

use rusqlite::{Connection, params};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum LootError {
    #[error("sqlite: {0}")] Db(#[from] rusqlite::Error),
    #[error("io: {0}")] Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("evidence required for {0}")] NoEvidence(&'static str),
    #[error("hash mismatch on {0}")] HashMismatch(String),
}

pub const SCHEMA: &str = include_str!("schema.sql");

pub struct Loot { conn: Connection, root: PathBuf }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Table { Host, Service, Vuln, Cred, Session, Card, Txn, Wallet, Artifact }

impl Table {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Table::Host => "host", Table::Service => "service", Table::Vuln => "vuln",
            Table::Cred => "cred", Table::Session => "session", Table::Card => "card",
            Table::Txn => "txn", Table::Wallet => "wallet", Table::Artifact => "artifact",
        }
    }
    fn needs_evidence(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Table::Vuln | Table::Cred | Table::Card)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LootRow {
    pub table: Table,
    pub cols: Vec<(&'static str, String)>,
    pub evidence_sha256: Option<String>,
}

impl LootRow {
    pub fn new(table: Table) -> Self { Self { table, cols: Vec::new(), evidence_sha256: None } }
    pub fn set(mut self, k: &'static str, v: impl ToString) -> Self {
        self.cols.push((k, v.to_string())); self
    }
    pub fn evidence(mut self, sha: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.evidence_sha256 = Some(sha.into()); self
    }
}

impl Loot {
    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, LootError> {
        if let Some(p) = path.parent() { std::fs::create_dir_all(p)?; }
        let conn = Connection::open(path)?;
        conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA)?;
        let root = path.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).to_path_buf();
        Ok(Self { conn, root })
    }

    pub fn root(&self) -> &Path { &self.root }

    pub fn insert(&self, row: &LootRow) -> Result<i64, LootError> {
        if row.table.needs_evidence() && row.evidence_sha256.is_none() {
            return Err(LootError::NoEvidence(row.table.name()));
        }
        let mut cols: Vec<&str> = row.cols.iter().map(|(k, _)| *k).collect();
        let mut vals: Vec<String> = row.cols.iter().map(|(_, v)| v.clone()).collect();
        if let Some(sha) = &row.evidence_sha256 {
            cols.push("evidence_sha256"); vals.push(sha.clone());
        }
        let placeholders = vec!["?"; cols.len()].join(",");
        let sql = format!("INSERT INTO {} ({}) VALUES ({})",
                          row.table.name(), cols.join(","), placeholders);
        self.conn.execute(&sql, rusqlite::params_from_iter(vals.iter()))?;
        Ok(self.conn.last_insert_rowid())
    }

    pub fn set_status(&self, table: Table, id: i64, status: &str) -> Result<(), LootError> {
        let sql = format!("UPDATE {} SET status = ?1 WHERE id = ?2", table.name());
        self.conn.execute(&sql, params![status, id])?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn counts(&self) -> Result<Vec<(String, i64)>, LootError> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for t in [Table::Host, Table::Service, Table::Vuln, Table::Cred,
                  Table::Session, Table::Card, Table::Txn, Table::Wallet] {
            let n: i64 = self.conn.query_row(
                &format!("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {}", t.name()), [], |r| r.get(0))?;
            out.push((t.name().to_string(), n));
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Typed selector. Keeps the model out of SQL.
    pub fn query(&self, selector: &str, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<serde_json::Value>, LootError> {
        let sql = match selector {
            "hosts" | "hosts:up" => "SELECT * FROM host WHERE status='up' LIMIT ?1",
            "services" | "services:open" => "SELECT * FROM service LIMIT ?1",
            "vulns" | "vulns:exploitable" => "SELECT * FROM vuln WHERE exploitable=1 LIMIT ?1",
            "creds" | "creds:live" => "SELECT * FROM cred WHERE status='live' LIMIT ?1",
            "creds:untested" => "SELECT * FROM cred WHERE status='untested' LIMIT ?1",
            "sessions" => "SELECT * FROM session WHERE burned=0 LIMIT ?1",
            "cards" | "cards:live" => "SELECT * FROM card WHERE status='live' LIMIT ?1",
            "cards:untested" => "SELECT * FROM card WHERE status='untested' LIMIT ?1",
            "txns" => "SELECT * FROM txn ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT ?1",
            "wallets" => "SELECT * FROM wallet WHERE balance_atom IS NOT NULL LIMIT ?1",
            _ => return Err(LootError::Db(rusqlite::Error::InvalidQuery)),
        };
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare(sql)?;
        let cols: Vec<String> = st.column_names().iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        let rows = st.query_map([limit], |r| {
            let mut o = serde_json::Map::new();
            for (i, c) in cols.iter().enumerate() {
                let v: rusqlite::types::Value = r.get(i)?;
                o.insert(c.clone(), match v {
                    rusqlite::types::Value::Null => serde_json::Value::Null,
                    rusqlite::types::Value::Integer(n) => n.into(),
                    rusqlite::types::Value::Real(f) => f.into(),
                    rusqlite::types::Value::Text(t) => t.into(),
                    rusqlite::types::Value::Blob(_) => "<blob>".into(),
                });
            }
            Ok(serde_json::Value::Object(o))
        })?;
        Ok(rows.collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?)
    }

    pub fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String, LootError> {
        let mut h = Sha256::new();
        h.update(std::fs::read(path)?);
        Ok(format!("{:x}", h.finalize()))
    }

    /// Export with hash verification; aborts on mismatch.
    pub fn export(&self, dest: &Path) -> Result<usize, LootError> {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dest)?;
        let mut n = 0;
        for t in [Table::Host, Table::Service, Table::Vuln, Table::Cred,
                  Table::Session, Table::Card, Table::Txn, Table::Wallet, Table::Artifact] {
            let rows = self.query(t.name(), 100_000).unwrap_or_default();
            std::fs::write(dest.join(format!("{}.json", t.name())),
                           serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&rows).unwrap())?;
            n += rows.len();
        }
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare("SELECT path, sha256 FROM artifact")?;
        let arts = st.query_map([], |r| Ok((r.get::<_, String>(0)?, r.get::<_, String>(1)?)))?;
        for a in arts {
            let (p, want) = a?;
            let src = self.root.join(&p);
            if !src.exists() { continue; }
            if Loot::hash_file(&src)? != want {
                return Err(LootError::HashMismatch(p));
            }
            let to = dest.join("artifacts").join(&p);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(to.parent().unwrap())?;
            std::fs::copy(&src, &to)?;
        }
        Ok(n)
    }
}
```

[view on disk](crates/offense/rc-loot/src/schema.sql)

```sql

PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS engagement (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, scope TEXT NOT NULL,
  started_at INTEGER NOT NULL, dry_run INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS host (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  addr TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, os_guess TEXT,
  first_seen INTEGER NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'up',
  UNIQUE (engagement, addr));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS service (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, host INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES host(id),
  port INTEGER NOT NULL, proto TEXT NOT NULL, banner TEXT, product TEXT,
  version TEXT, tls_subject TEXT, fingerprint TEXT, evidence_sha256 TEXT,
  UNIQUE (host, port, proto));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vuln (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service(id),
  cve TEXT, title TEXT NOT NULL, cvss REAL, confidence REAL NOT NULL,
  exploitable INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, evidence_sha256 TEXT);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cred (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  host INTEGER REFERENCES host(id), kind TEXT NOT NULL, username TEXT,
  secret TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'untested', tested_at INTEGER,
  evidence_sha256 TEXT);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS session (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, cred INTEGER REFERENCES cred(id),
  host INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES host(id), proto TEXT NOT NULL,
  established INTEGER NOT NULL, last_seen INTEGER NOT NULL,
  burned INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS card (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  pan TEXT NOT NULL, bin TEXT NOT NULL, brand TEXT, issuer TEXT, country TEXT,
  exp_mm INTEGER NOT NULL, exp_yy INTEGER NOT NULL, cvv TEXT, holder TEXT,
  avs_street TEXT, avs_zip TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'untested',
  gateway TEXT, decline_code TEXT, checked_at INTEGER,
  UNIQUE (engagement, pan));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS txn (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  card INTEGER REFERENCES card(id), gateway TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, currency TEXT NOT NULL, result TEXT NOT NULL,
  raw TEXT, at INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wallet (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  chain TEXT NOT NULL, addr TEXT NOT NULL, balance_atom TEXT,
  swept INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, UNIQUE (engagement, chain, addr));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS artifact (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL, path TEXT NOT NULL, sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
  bytes INTEGER NOT NULL, at INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chain (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  name TEXT NOT NULL, plan TEXT NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
  cursor TEXT, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS action_log (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, engagement INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES engagement(id),
  tool TEXT NOT NULL, args TEXT NOT NULL, effect TEXT NOT NULL,
  result TEXT NOT NULL, started INTEGER NOT NULL, ended INTEGER);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_service_host ON service(host);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_vuln_service ON vuln(service);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_cred_status  ON cred(engagement, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_card_status  ON card(engagement, status);
```

## `crates/offense/rc-opsec/src/lib.rs`

[view on disk](crates/offense/rc-opsec/src/lib.rs)

```rust
//! OPSEC layer. Every Net tool passes through here. Nothing bypasses.

use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::Duration;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum OpsecError { #[error("all proxies burned")] PoolEmpty }

pub struct Opsec {
    proxies: Mutex<Vec<String>>,
    burns: Mutex<Vec<String>>,
    idx: Mutex<usize>,
    rotate_every: usize,
    jitter: (u64, u64),
    seen: Mutex<usize>,
}

impl Opsec {
    pub fn new(proxies: Vec<String>, rotate_every: usize, jitter: (u64, u64)) -> Self {
        Self {
            proxies: Mutex::new(proxies), burns: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
            idx: Mutex::new(0), rotate_every, jitter, seen: Mutex::new(0),
        }
    }

    /// Sleep a jittered interval. Call before every request.
    pub async fn jitter(&self) {
        let (lo, hi) = self.jitter;
        if hi > lo {
            let ms = lo + (std::time::SystemTime::now()
                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap()
                .subsec_nanos() as u64 % (hi - lo));
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(ms)).await;
        }
    }

    /// Next proxy, honouring rotation and burn list.
    pub fn next_proxy(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, OpsecError> {
        let mut seen = self.seen.lock().unwrap();
        *seen += 1;
        let pool = self.proxies.lock().unwrap();
        if pool.is_empty() { return Ok(None); }
        let burns = self.burns.lock().unwrap();
        let live: Vec<&String> = pool.iter().filter(|p| !burns.contains(p)).collect();
        if live.is_empty() { return Err(OpsecError::PoolEmpty); }
        if *seen % self.rotate_every == 0 {
            let mut i = self.idx.lock().unwrap();
            *i = (*i + 1) % live.len();
        }
        Ok(Some(live[*self.idx.lock().unwrap() % live.len()].clone()))
    }

    pub fn burn(&self, proxy: &str) {
        let mut b = self.burns.lock().unwrap();
        if !b.iter().any(|x| x == proxy) { b.push(proxy.to_string()); }
    }

    pub fn burn_host(&self, host: &str) { self.burn(&format!("host:{host}")); }
    pub fn is_burned(&self, host: &str) -> bool {
        self.burns.lock().unwrap().iter().any(|x| x == &format!("host:{host}"))
    }
}
```

## `crates/providers/src/adapter.rs`

[view on disk](crates/providers/src/adapter.rs)

```rust
//! Provider adapters — the Rust analogue of OpenCode's `ProviderPackage`.
//!
//! Each adapter is a struct implementing [`ProviderAdapter`]. It declares its
//! id, default base URL, auth scheme (header name + env var), and the wire
//! protocol kind (Anthropic Messages vs OpenAI Chat/Responses). The adapter
//! does NOT make HTTP calls itself — it produces a [`ResolvedRequest`] that the
//! HTTP client ([`crate::client::HttpClient`]) executes.
//!
//! This mirrors OpenCode's separation: the adapter knows the shape of the
//! request (headers, body framing, auth); the client knows how to send it and
//! how to retry. RomaCode's old `request_anthropic` / `request_openai`
//! functions in `agent.rs` conflated both; this crate splits them cleanly.

use crate::schema::*;
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// The wire protocol a provider speaks. RomaCode's agent loop dispatches on
/// this to pick the SSE parser.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Protocol {
    /// Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`, SSE, `x-api-key` auth).
    #[default]
    AnthropicMessages,
    /// OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`, SSE, Bearer auth).
    OpenAiChat,
    /// OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`, SSE, Bearer auth).
    OpenAiResponses,
}

impl Protocol {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Protocol::AnthropicMessages => "anthropic-messages",
            Protocol::OpenAiChat => "openai-chat",
            Protocol::OpenAiResponses => "openai-responses",
        }
    }
}

/// How a provider authenticates. Mirrors OpenCode `AuthOptions`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AuthScheme {
    /// `x-api-key: <key>` (Anthropic). Falls back to Bearer if `auth_token` set.
    ApiKey { header: String, env_var: String },
    /// `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (OpenAI-style).
    Bearer { env_var: String },
    /// No auth header (local servers like Ollama).
    None,
}

/// The fully-resolved request the HTTP client will send: URL, headers, body.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ResolvedRequest {
    pub url: String,
    pub headers: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub body: Value,
    pub protocol: Protocol,
}

/// One provider adapter. Implementors are zero-sized (state lives in config);
/// the trait methods read config + the active credential and produce the
/// request shape.
pub trait ProviderAdapter: Send + Sync {
    /// The provider id this adapter implements (e.g. `"anthropic"`).
    fn id(&self) -> &str;

    /// Human-readable name.
    fn name(&self) -> &str;

    /// Default base URL (no trailing slash). Overridable via config.
    fn default_base_url(&self) -> &str;

    /// Auth scheme (env var name + header).
    fn auth(&self) -> AuthScheme;

    /// Wire protocol.
    fn protocol(&self) -> Protocol;

    /// Build the request URL for one model call.
    fn endpoint(&self, base_url: &str) -> String {
        match self.protocol() {
            Protocol::AnthropicMessages => format!("{}/v1/messages", base_url.trim_end_matches('/')),
            Protocol::OpenAiChat => format!("{}/chat/completions", base_url.trim_end_matches('/')),
            Protocol::OpenAiResponses => format!("{}/responses", base_url.trim_end_matches('/')),
        }
    }

    /// Build the auth header(s) from the resolved credential.
    fn auth_headers(&self, api_key: Option<&str>) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        let mut h = BTreeMap::new();
        match (self.auth(), api_key) {
            (AuthScheme::ApiKey { header, .. }, Some(k)) => { h.insert(header.clone(), k.to_string()); }
            (AuthScheme::ApiKey { .. }, None) => {} // some adapters allow no key (ollama)
            (AuthScheme::Bearer { .. }, Some(k)) => { h.insert("Authorization".into(), format!("Bearer {k}")); }
            (AuthScheme::Bearer { .. }, None) => {}
            (AuthScheme::None, _) => {}
        }
        h
    }

    /// Build the full request from messages + params. Adapters may override to
    /// add provider-specific body fields (e.g. Anthropic `anthropic-version`).
    fn build_request(
        &self,
        base_url: &str,
        api_key: Option<&str>,
        messages: &[Value],
        max_tokens: u32,
        model: &str,
        extra_headers: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
        stream: bool,
    ) -> ResolvedRequest {
        self.default_build_request(base_url, api_key, messages, max_tokens, model, extra_headers, stream)
    }

    /// The non-trait default implementation. Adapters that override
    /// [`build_request`](ProviderAdapter::build_request) call this to get the
    /// base request, then mutate it — avoiding the infinite recursion that a
    /// naive `self.build_request()` call would cause.
    fn default_build_request(
        &self,
        base_url: &str,
        api_key: Option<&str>,
        messages: &[Value],
        max_tokens: u32,
        model: &str,
        extra_headers: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
        stream: bool,
    ) -> ResolvedRequest {
        let url = self.endpoint(base_url);
        let mut headers = self.auth_headers(api_key);
        for (k, v) in extra_headers { headers.insert(k.clone(), v.clone()); }
        headers.insert("content-type".into(), "application/json".into());
        let body = match self.protocol() {
            Protocol::AnthropicMessages => serde_json::json!({
                "model": model,
                "max_tokens": max_tokens,
                "messages": messages,
                "stream": stream,
            }),
            Protocol::OpenAiChat | Protocol::OpenAiResponses => serde_json::json!({
                "model": model,
                "max_tokens": max_tokens,
                "messages": messages,
                "stream": stream,
            }),
        };
        ResolvedRequest { url, headers, body, protocol: self.protocol() }
    }
}

// ── Concrete adapters ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Anthropic — `x-api-key` auth, Anthropic Messages protocol.
pub struct Anthropic;
impl ProviderAdapter for Anthropic {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { "anthropic" }
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "Anthropic" }
    fn default_base_url(&self) -> &str { "https://api.anthropic.com" }
    fn auth(&self) -> AuthScheme { AuthScheme::ApiKey { header: "x-api-key".into(), env_var: "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY".into() } }
    fn protocol(&self) -> Protocol { Protocol::AnthropicMessages }
    fn build_request(&self, base_url: &str, api_key: Option<&str>, messages: &[Value], max_tokens: u32, model: &str, extra_headers: &BTreeMap<String, String>, stream: bool) -> ResolvedRequest {
        let mut r = self.default_build_request(base_url, api_key, messages, max_tokens, model, extra_headers, stream);
        r.headers.insert("anthropic-version".into(), "2023-06-01".into());
        r
    }
}

/// The registry of built-in adapters. Returns the adapter for a provider id,
/// or `None` for custom/unknown ids (which fall back to OpenAI-compatible
/// with a config-supplied base URL).
pub fn adapter_for(id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn ProviderAdapter>> {
    Some(match id {
        "anthropic" => Box::new(Anthropic),
        "openai" => Box::new(OpenAi),
        "openrouter" => Box::new(OpenRouter),
        "google" => Box::new(Google),
        "groq" => Box::new(Groq),
        "deepseek" => Box::new(DeepSeek),
        "mistral" => Box::new(Mistral),
        "xai" => Box::new(Xai),
        "zai" => Box::new(Zai),
        "ollama" => Box::new(Ollama),
        "lmstudio" => Box::new(LmStudio),
        "cerebras" => Box::new(Cerebras),
        "together" => Box::new(Together),
        "fireworks" => Box::new(Fireworks),
        "coarena" => Box::new(Coarena),
        "logfare" => Box::new(Logfare),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// Built-in provider ids (OpenCode `Provider` constants + RomaCode extras).
pub const BUILTIN_IDS: &[&str] = &[
    "anthropic", "openai", "openrouter", "google", "groq", "deepseek",
    "mistral", "xai", "zai", "ollama", "lmstudio", "cerebras", "together", "fireworks",
    "coarena", "logfare",
];

/// A generic OpenAI-compatible adapter for custom providers (config-supplied
/// base URL, Bearer auth via a config-named env var).
pub struct OpenAiCompatible {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub base_url: String,
    pub env_var: String,
}
impl ProviderAdapter for OpenAiCompatible {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.id }
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn default_base_url(&self) -> &str { &self.base_url }
    fn auth(&self) -> AuthScheme { AuthScheme::Bearer { env_var: self.env_var.clone() } }
    fn protocol(&self) -> Protocol { Protocol::OpenAiChat }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn adapter_for_known_ids() {
        assert!(adapter_for("anthropic").is_some());
        assert!(adapter_for("openai").is_some());
        assert!(adapter_for("zai").is_some());
        assert!(adapter_for("coarena").is_some());
        assert!(adapter_for("logfare").is_some());
        assert!(adapter_for("nonexistent").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn coarena_and_logfare_use_openai_compatible_endpoints() {
        let c = adapter_for("coarena").expect("coarena");
        assert_eq!(c.default_base_url(), "https://coarena.ai/api/v1");
        assert_eq!(c.protocol(), Protocol::OpenAiChat);
        let l = adapter_for("logfare").expect("logfare");
        assert_eq!(l.default_base_url(), "https://logfare.ai/v1");
        assert_eq!(l.protocol(), Protocol::OpenAiChat);
    }

    #[test]
    fn anthropic_endpoint_and_auth() {
        let a = Anthropic;
        assert_eq!(a.endpoint("https://api.anthropic.com"), "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages");
        let h = a.auth_headers(Some("sk-ant-xxx"));
        assert_eq!(h.get("x-api-key").map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("sk-ant-xxx"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn openai_endpoint_and_bearer() {
        let a = OpenAi;
        assert_eq!(a.endpoint("https://api.openai.com/v1"), "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions");
        let h = a.auth_headers(Some("sk-xxx"));
        assert_eq!(h.get("Authorization").map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("Bearer sk-xxx"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn anthropic_build_request_adds_version_header() {
        let a = Anthropic;
        let msgs = vec![serde_json::json!({"role":"user","content":"hi"})];
        let r = a.build_request("https://api.anthropic.com", Some("k"), &msgs, 1024, "claude-x", &BTreeMap::new(), true);
        assert_eq!(r.headers.get("anthropic-version").map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("2023-06-01"));
        assert_eq!(r.headers.get("x-api-key").map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("k"));
        assert_eq!(r.protocol, Protocol::AnthropicMessages);
        assert!(r.body["stream"].as_bool().unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn openai_compatible_custom() {
        let a = OpenAiCompatible { id: "myco".into(), name: "MyCo".into(), base_url: "https://api.my.co/v1".into(), env_var: "MYCO_API_KEY".into() };
        assert_eq!(a.endpoint("https://api.my.co/v1"), "https://api.my.co/v1/chat/completions");
        match a.auth() { AuthScheme::Bearer { env_var } => assert_eq!(env_var, "MYCO_API_KEY"), _ => panic!() }
    }

    #[test]
    fn ollama_no_auth() {
        let a = Ollama;
        assert!(a.auth_headers(None).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn builtin_ids_contains_zai() {
        assert!(BUILTIN_IDS.contains(&"zai"));
        assert!(BUILTIN_IDS.contains(&"anthropic"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Provider + model catalog — the Rust analogue of OpenCode's
//! `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts` + `packages/app/src/providers/catalog`.
//!
//! OpenCode fetches a catalog snapshot from `https://models.opencode.ai/...`
//! with a 5-minute TTL, ETag cache, and a bundled fallback. RomaCode mirrors
//! this: [`Catalog`] holds a list of [`ProviderInfo`] each with a map of
//! [`ModelInfo`]. It is populated by [`Catalog::fetch`] (HTTP GET against the
//! configured catalog URL) with [`Catalog::bundled`] as the zero-network
//! fallback. The catalog is the single source of truth for what providers and
//! models exist — the TUI, CLI, and agent loop all read it.
//!
//! Unlike RomaCode's old static `KNOWN` slice, this catalog is dynamic: a
//! remote update adds providers and models without a RomaCode release, and the
//! bundled snapshot is only the last-resort fallback (mirroring OpenCode's
//! `snapshot.txt`).

use crate::schema::*;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};

/// Default catalog URL (RomaCode-hosted equivalent of models.dev).
/// Mirrors OpenCode's `https://models.opencode.ai/experimental/v2.0/api.json`.
pub const DEFAULT_CATALOG_URL: &str = "https://catalog.romacode.dev/v1/catalog.json";

/// Catalog TTL — 5 minutes, matching OpenCode.
pub const TTL_SECS: u64 = 5 * 60;

/// The catalog: every known provider with its models.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Catalog {
    pub providers: BTreeMap<ProviderId, ProviderInfo>,
    /// When this catalog was loaded (unix ms).
    pub fetched_at: u64,
    /// Whether this came from the network or the bundled fallback.
    pub source: CatalogSource,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CatalogSource {
    #[default]
    Bundled,
    Network,
}

impl Catalog {
    /// The bundled fallback catalog (zero-network). Built from the adapter
    /// registry + a small static model list per provider. This is the
    /// equivalent of OpenCode shipping `snapshot.txt`.
    pub fn bundled() -> Self {
        let mut providers = BTreeMap::new();
        for entry in bundled_entries() {
            let mut p = ProviderInfo {
                id: ProviderId::new(entry.id),
                name: entry.name.into(),
                package: entry.id.into(),
                activation: Activation::Auto,
                default_model: Some(ModelId::new(entry.default)),
                ..Default::default()
            };
            for m in entry.models {
                let mid = ModelId::new(*m);
                p.models.insert(mid.clone(), ModelInfo::default_for(p.id.clone(), mid));
            }
            providers.insert(p.id.clone(), p);
        }
        Self { providers, fetched_at: now_ms(), source: CatalogSource::Bundled }
    }

    /// Look up a provider by id.
    pub fn provider(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&ProviderInfo> {
        self.providers.get(&ProviderId::new(id.to_string()))
    }

    /// All provider ids.
    pub fn provider_ids(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.providers.keys().map(|k| k.as_str().to_string()).collect()
    }

    /// Models for a provider.
    pub fn models(&self, provider: &str) -> Vec<&ModelInfo> {
        self.provider(provider).map(|p| p.models.values().collect()).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Find a specific model.
    pub fn model(&self, provider: &str, model: &str) -> Option<&ModelInfo> {
        self.provider(provider)?.models.get(&ModelId::new(model.to_string()))
    }

    /// Resolve a [`ModelSelection`] to the [`ModelInfo`].
    pub fn resolve(&self, sel: &ModelSelection) -> Option<&ModelInfo> {
        self.model(sel.provider_id.as_str(), sel.model.as_str())
    }

    /// Fetch from the network. On any failure, returns the bundled catalog
    /// (mirrors OpenCode's `try fetch -> catch -> bundled snapshot`).
    pub fn fetch(url: &str) -> Self {
        match Self::fetch_network(url) {
            Ok(c) => c,
            Err(_) => Self::bundled(),
        }
    }

    fn fetch_network(url: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        // Minimal HTTP GET via std (no TLS — HTTPS catalog URLs fall back to
        // bundled in the no-TLS build; a future TLS impl will enable live
        // fetch). This is acceptable because the bundled catalog is the
        // reliable path; live fetch is best-effort.
        let parsed = parse_catalog_url(url)?;
        let addr = format!("{}:{}", parsed.host, parsed.port);
        let addrs = std::net::ToSocketAddrs::to_socket_addrs(&addr).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let mut stream = None;
        for a in addrs {
            if let Ok(s) = std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&a, std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)) {
                stream = Some(s); break;
            }
        }
        let mut s = stream.ok_or("connect failed")?;
        // Bound the read: with no TLS this is a plain-HTTP GET against what
        // is usually an HTTPS-only host, so the peer may never send anything
        // readable back. Without a read timeout, `read_to_end` could block
        // indefinitely instead of falling back to the bundled catalog.
        s.set_read_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        use std::io::{Read, Write};
        let req = format!("GET {} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n", parsed.path, parsed.host);
        s.write_all(req.as_bytes()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        s.read_to_end(&mut buf).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let body = std::str::from_utf8(&buf).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        // skip headers
        let split = body.find("\r\n\r\n").ok_or("no body")?;
        let json = &body[split + 4..];
        let parsed_catalog: NetworkCatalog = serde_json::from_str(json).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        Ok(parsed_catalog.into_catalog())
    }
}

struct ParsedUrl<'a> { host: &'a str, port: u16, path: String }
fn parse_catalog_url(s: &str) -> Result<ParsedUrl, String> {
    let (scheme, rest) = s.split_once("://").ok_or("no scheme")?;
    let (hostport, path) = match rest.find('/') {
        Some(i) => (&rest[..i], rest[i..].to_string()),
        None => (rest, "/".to_string()),
    };
    let (host, port) = match hostport.rsplit_once(':') {
        Some((h, p)) => (h, p.parse().map_err(|e: std::num::ParseIntError| e.to_string())?),
        None => (hostport, if scheme == "https" { 443 } else { 80 }),
    };
    Ok(ParsedUrl { host, port, path })
}

fn now_ms() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// The on-wire catalog shape (a small subset of OpenCode's models.dev JSON).
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct NetworkCatalog {
    #[serde(default)]
    providers: Vec<NetworkProvider>,
}
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct NetworkProvider {
    id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    models: Vec<NetworkModel>,
}
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct NetworkModel {
    id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    context: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    output: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    tools: Option<bool>,
}
impl NetworkCatalog {
    fn into_catalog(self) -> Catalog {
        let mut providers = BTreeMap::new();
        for np in self.providers {
            let pid = ProviderId::new(np.id.clone());
            let mut p = ProviderInfo {
                id: pid.clone(),
                name: np.name,
                package: np.id.clone(),
                activation: Activation::Auto,
                ..Default::default()
            };
            for nm in np.models {
                let mid = ModelId::new(nm.id.clone());
                let mut m = ModelInfo::default_for(pid.clone(), mid.clone());
                m.name = nm.name;
                if let Some(c) = nm.context { m.limit.context = c; }
                if let Some(o) = nm.output { m.limit.output = o; }
                if let Some(t) = nm.tools { m.capabilities.tools = t; }
                p.models.insert(mid, m);
            }
            providers.insert(pid, p);
        }
        Catalog { providers, fetched_at: now_ms(), source: CatalogSource::Network }
    }
}

// ── Bundled fallback ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// One bundled provider row. This is the shape shared by the hand-written
/// core snapshot below and the generated full provider snapshot in
/// [`crate::catalog_snapshot`].
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct BundledEntry {
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub name: &'static str,
    /// Default API base URL ("" when it must be supplied in config).
    pub base_url: &'static str,
    /// Conventional API-key environment variable ("" when not needed).
    pub key_env: &'static str,
    /// Whether the provider needs an API key to resolve.
    pub needs_key: bool,
    /// `true` for the Anthropic Messages wire protocol, `false` for
    /// OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions.
    pub anthropic: bool,
    pub models: &'static [&'static str],
    /// The preferred default model (first in `models` by convention; stored
    /// explicitly so the catalog can surface it even though `models` is held
    /// in a sorted BTreeMap that loses insertion order).
    pub default: &'static str,
}

/// Resolution metadata carried by a bundled entry for providers that have
/// no dedicated adapter in [`crate::adapter`].
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BundledMeta {
    pub base_url: &'static str,
    pub key_env: &'static str,
    pub needs_key: bool,
    pub anthropic: bool,
}

/// Look up the bundled metadata for a provider id (case-insensitive).
/// Used by the legacy compatibility shim so generated providers resolve to
/// a base URL and API-key env var without a hand-written adapter.
pub fn bundled_meta(id: &str) -> Option<BundledMeta> {
    bundled_entries()
        .find(|e| e.id.eq_ignore_ascii_case(id))
        .map(|e| BundledMeta {
            base_url: e.base_url,
            key_env: e.key_env,
            needs_key: e.needs_key,
            anthropic: e.anthropic,
        })
}

/// All bundled rows: RomaCode's hand-written core first, then the generated
/// full bundled provider snapshot.
pub fn bundled_entries() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static BundledEntry> {
    BUILTIN_SNAPSHOT.iter().chain(crate::catalog_snapshot::EXTRA_ENTRIES.iter())
}

// ── Process-wide cached catalog (TTL-refreshed) ─────────────────────────────

static CATALOG: OnceLock<Mutex<Catalog>> = OnceLock::new();

/// Get the cached catalog, refreshing if older than TTL. Uses the bundled
/// fallback on first access / network failure.
///
/// BUG FIXED: this used to gate the TTL check on `source == Network` only.
/// Because `fetch_network` cannot actually complete a TLS handshake (it is a
/// plain-HTTP, no-TLS client reaching an `https://` URL — see its own
/// doc comment), `Catalog::fetch` always falls through to `bundled()`, so
/// `source` never becomes `Network`. The TTL check was therefore never true,
/// and EVERY call to `cached()` — every model-picker open, every `/models`,
/// every agent model resolution — re-ran a doomed network connection from
/// scratch before returning the fallback. Gating the TTL on `fetched_at`
/// alone (regardless of source) makes the bundled fallback itself cache for
/// the TTL window, so a live environment with no working catalog endpoint
/// pays the connection cost at most once per `TTL_SECS`, not once per call.
pub fn cached() -> Catalog {
    let m = CATALOG.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(Catalog::bundled()));
    let g = m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let now = now_ms();
    if now.saturating_sub(g.fetched_at) < TTL_SECS * 1000 {
        return g.clone();
    }
    drop(g);
    // Refresh in a separate scope; on failure keep the bundled one.
    let fresh = Catalog::fetch(DEFAULT_CATALOG_URL);
    let mut g = m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    // Always adopt a successful network fetch. On failure, still record the
    // fresh `fetched_at` so the TTL window above actually holds — otherwise
    // a permanently-unreachable catalog endpoint would retry every call.
    if fresh.source == CatalogSource::Network {
        *g = fresh;
    } else {
        g.fetched_at = fresh.fetched_at;
    }
    g.clone()
}

/// Force a refresh (e.g. after the user adds a credential).
pub fn refresh() -> Catalog {
    let fresh = Catalog::fetch(DEFAULT_CATALOG_URL);
    if let Some(m) = CATALOG.get() {
        let mut g = m.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        *g = fresh.clone();
    }
    fresh
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn bundled_has_providers_and_models() {
        let c = Catalog::bundled();
        // 14 hand-written + the full generated provider snapshot.
        assert!(c.providers.len() >= 300, "only {} bundled providers", c.providers.len());
        let a = c.provider("anthropic").expect("anthropic");
        assert!(!a.models.is_empty());
        assert!(a.models.contains_key(&ModelId::new("claude-sonnet-5-5")));
        for id in ["azure", "vercel", "openrouter", "huggingface", "nvidia", "cohere"] {
            assert!(c.provider(id).is_some(), "{id} from the catalog must be bundled");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn bundled_meta_covers_generated_providers() {
        let m = bundled_meta("vercel").expect("vercel meta");
        assert!(m.base_url.starts_with("https://"));
        assert!(!m.key_env.is_empty());
        assert!(bundled_meta("ANTHROPIC").is_some(), "lookup is case-insensitive");
        assert!(bundled_meta("no-such-provider").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_model_selection() {
        let c = Catalog::bundled();
        let sel = ModelSelection::parse("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5").unwrap();
        let m = c.resolve(&sel).expect("model exists");
        assert_eq!(m.model_id.as_str(), "claude-sonnet-5-5");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_provider_returns_none() {
        let c = Catalog::bundled();
        assert!(c.provider("nonexistent").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cached_returns_something() {
        let c = cached();
        assert!(c.providers.len() >= 10);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_catalog_url_https() {
        let u = parse_catalog_url("https://catalog.romacode.dev/v1/catalog.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(u.host, "catalog.romacode.dev");
        assert_eq!(u.port, 443);
        assert_eq!(u.path, "/v1/catalog.json");
    }

    #[test]
    fn network_catalog_decodes() {
        let json = r#"{"providers":[{"id":"openai","name":"OpenAI","models":[{"id":"gpt-5","name":"GPT-5","context":128000,"output":16384,"tools":true}]}]}"#;
        let nc: NetworkCatalog = serde_json::from_str(json).unwrap();
        let c = nc.into_catalog();
        let m = c.model("openai", "gpt-5").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.limit.context, 128000);
        assert_eq!(m.limit.output, 16384);
        assert!(m.capabilities.tools);
        assert_eq!(c.source, CatalogSource::Network);
    }
}
```
