```rust
//! `math.*` tools — pure arithmetic, no I/O. The default policy `allow`s
//! these (read-only, side-effect-free).

use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use rc_core::{Tool, ToolResult};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::need_param;

macro_rules! binop {
    ($struct:ident, $name:expr, $desc:expr, $op:expr) => {
        pub struct $struct;
        #[async_trait]
        impl Tool for $struct {
            fn name(&self) -> &str { $name }
            fn description(&self) -> &str { $desc }
            fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
                Schema::new()
                    .param(Parameter::required("a", ParamType::Number))
                    .param(Parameter::required("b", ParamType::Number))
            }
            fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
            async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
                // Schema-validated input can still be unrepresentable
                // (e.g. u64 > i64::MAX), so convert via need_param — a
                // missing/wrong-shape param is an error result, not a panic.
                let a = need_param(input, "a", ParamType::Number, Value::as_f64)?;
                let b = need_param(input, "b", ParamType::Number, Value::as_f64)?;
                Ok(serde_json::json!(($op)(a, b)))
            }
        }
    };
}

binop!(Add, "math.add", "Add two numbers (a + b).", |a: f64, b: f64| a + b);
binop!(Subtract, "math.subtract", "Subtract b from a (a - b).", |a: f64, b: f64| a - b);
binop!(Multiply, "math.multiply", "Multiply two numbers (a × b).", |a: f64, b: f64| a * b);

pub struct Divide;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Divide {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "math.divide" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Divide a by b (a / b). Errors on zero." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::required("a", ParamType::Number))
            .param(Parameter::required("b", ParamType::Number))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let a = need_param(input, "a", ParamType::Number, Value::as_f64)?;
        let b = need_param(input, "b", ParamType::Number, Value::as_f64)?;
        if b == 0.0 {
            return Err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other("division by zero".into()));
        }
        let r = a / b;
        // NaN / ±inf serialize as JSON null — surface a real error instead.
        if !r.is_finite() {
            return Err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other(format!(
                "result of {a} / {b} is not a finite number"
            )));
        }
        Ok(serde_json::json!(r))
    }
}

pub struct Sqrt;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Sqrt {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "math.sqrt" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Square root of a number." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("n", ParamType::Number))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let n = need_param(input, "n", ParamType::Number, Value::as_f64)?;
        Ok(serde_json::json!(n.sqrt()))
    }
}

pub struct Factorial;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Factorial {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "math.factorial" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Factorial of a non-negative integer (n!)." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("n", ParamType::Integer))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        // `as_i64().unwrap()` panicked on schema-valid u64 > i64::MAX
        // (e.g. 18446744073709551615) — that is now an error result.
        let n = need_param(input, "n", ParamType::Integer, Value::as_i64)?;
        if n < 0 {
            return Err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other("factorial of a negative number".into()));
        }
        // u128 to hold larger results
        let mut acc: u128 = 1;
        for i in 2..=n as u64 {
            acc = acc.saturating_mul(i as u128);
        }
        Ok(serde_json::json!(acc.to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct Gcd;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Gcd {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "math.gcd" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Greatest common divisor of two integers (Euclid)." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::required("a", ParamType::Integer))
            .param(Parameter::required("b", ParamType::Integer))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let mut a = need_param(input, "a", ParamType::Integer, Value::as_i64)?.unsigned_abs();
        let mut b = need_param(input, "b", ParamType::Integer, Value::as_i64)?.unsigned_abs();
        while b != 0 {
            let t = b;
            b = a % b;
            a = t;
        }
        Ok(serde_json::json!(a))
    }
}

/// All math tools, ready to register.
pub fn all() -> Vec<rc_core::tool::ToolArc> {
    use rc_core::tool::arc;
    vec![
        arc(Add),
        arc(Subtract),
        arc(Multiply),
        arc(Divide),
        arc(Sqrt),
        arc(Factorial),
        arc(Gcd),
    ]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::Tool;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn factorial_u64_overflow_is_error_not_panic() {
        // Schema-valid (is_u64) but unrepresentable as i64 — must be an
        // error result, never a panic that unwinds the agent loop.
        let out = Factorial
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "n": 18446744073709551615u64 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await;
        assert!(out.is_err(), "expected error, got {out:?}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn gcd_u64_overflow_is_error_not_panic() {
        let big = 18446744073709551615u64;
        let out = Gcd
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "a": big, "b": 6 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await;
        assert!(out.is_err(), "expected error, got {out:?}");
        // Normal (and negative) inputs still work.
        let out = Gcd
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "a": 48, "b": -18 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, 6);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn divide_by_zero_is_error_not_nan() {
        let out = Divide
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "a": 1.0, "b": 0.0 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await;
        assert!(out.is_err(), "0/0 must error, not serialize NaN as null");
        let out = Divide
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "a": 10.0, "b": 4.0 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, 2.5);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn missing_or_wrong_params_error_not_panic() {
        assert!(Add.execute(&serde_json::json!({}), &ToolContext::default()).await.is_err());
        assert!(Sqrt.execute(&serde_json::json!({ "n": "x" }), &ToolContext::default()).await.is_err());
        assert!(Factorial.execute(&serde_json::json!({}), &ToolContext::default()).await.is_err());
        assert!(Gcd.execute(&serde_json::json!({ "a": 4 }), &ToolContext::default()).await.is_err());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! `system.*` tools — environment introspection. The default policy *denies*
//! `system.*` (it can leak secrets and host info); a user must explicitly
//! allow a name or pattern to use these.

use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind, ToolArc};
use rc_core::{arc, Tool, ToolResult};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::need_param;

pub struct Env;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Env {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "system.env" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        "Read one environment variable by name (returns null if unset). WARNING: can leak secrets — denied by default."
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("name", ParamType::String))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let name = need_param(input, "name", ParamType::String, Value::as_str)?;
        let val = std::env::var(name).ok();
        Ok(match val {
            Some(v) => Value::String(v),
            None => Value::Null,
        })
    }
}

pub struct Hostname;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Hostname {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "system.hostname" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "The machine's hostname." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema { Schema::new() }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, _input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let h = hostname().unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into());
        Ok(Value::String(h))
    }
}

pub struct Cwd;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Cwd {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "system.cwd" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "The current working directory." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema { Schema::new() }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, _input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let c = std::env::current_dir()?
            .to_string_lossy()
            .to_string();
        Ok(Value::String(c))
    }
}

fn hostname() -> Option<String> {
    // Prefer /etc/hostname, fall back to HOSTNAME env, else the uname nodename.
    if let Ok(s) = std::fs::read_to_string("/etc/hostname") {
        return Some(s.trim().to_string());
    }
    if let Ok(h) = std::env::var("HOSTNAME") {
        return Some(h);
    }
    None
}

pub fn all() -> Vec<ToolArc> {
    vec![arc(Env), arc(Hostname), arc(Cwd)]
}
```

```rust
//! `text.*` tools — string operations, no I/O. The default policy `allow`s
//! these (pure functions).

use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind, ToolArc};
use rc_core::{arc, Tool, ToolResult};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::need_param;

macro_rules! str1 {
    ($struct:ident, $name:expr, $desc:expr, $body:expr) => {
        pub struct $struct;
        #[async_trait]
        impl Tool for $struct {
            fn name(&self) -> &str { $name }
            fn description(&self) -> &str { $desc }
            fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
                Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("s", ParamType::String))
            }
            fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
            async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
                let s = need_param(input, "s", ParamType::String, Value::as_str)?;
                Ok(serde_json::json!(($body)(s)))
            }
        }
    };
}

str1!(Upper, "text.upper", "Uppercase a string.", |s: &str| s.to_uppercase());
str1!(Lower, "text.lower", "Lowercase a string.", |s: &str| s.to_lowercase());
str1!(Length, "text.length", "Character count of a string (Unicode-aware).", |s: &str| s.chars().count());
```

```rust
//! `time.*` tools — clock helpers. `now` and `iso_now` are pure reads;
//! `sleep` is a test/delay helper (capped by the sandbox timeout).

use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind, ToolArc};
use rc_core::{arc, Tool, ToolResult};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

pub struct Now;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Now {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "time.now" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Current Unix epoch time in seconds (float, sub-ms precision)." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema { Schema::new() }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, _input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let d = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map_err(|e| rc_core::error::ToolError::Other(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(serde_json::json!(d.as_secs_f64()))
    }
}

pub struct IsoNow;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for IsoNow {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "time.iso_now" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Current UTC time as an ISO-8601 string (seconds precision)." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema { Schema::new() }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, _input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        Ok(Value::String(iso_now()))
    }
}

pub struct Sleep;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Sleep {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "time.sleep" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Sleep for `ms` milliseconds (capped by the sandbox timeout). Returns the elapsed ms." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("ms", ParamType::Integer))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let ms = input["ms"].as_i64().unwrap_or(0).max(0) as u64;
        let cap = if ctx.timeout_ms == 0 { ms } else { ms.min(ctx.timeout_ms) };
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(cap)).await;
        Ok(serde_json::json!(start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64))
    }
}

/// ISO-8601 UTC from the system clock, without pulling a datetime crate.
fn iso_now() -> String {
    let d = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
    let secs = d.as_secs();
    let days = secs / 86_400;
    let (y, m, day) = civil_from_days(days as i64);
    let s = secs % 86_400;
    let hh = s / 3600;
    let mm = (s % 3600) / 60;
    let ss = s % 60;
    format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{day:02}T{hh:02}:{mm:02}:{ss:02}Z")
}

/// Howard Hinnant's algorithm: days since 1970-01-01 → (year, month, day).
fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (z - era * 146_097) as u64;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    (y, m as u32, d as u32)
}

pub fn all() -> Vec<ToolArc> {
    vec![arc(Now), arc(IsoNow), arc(Sleep)]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn iso_format() {
        let s = iso_now();
        assert!(s.ends_with('Z'));
        assert_eq!(s.len(), 20); // YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
    }
    #[test]
    fn civil_known() {
        // 1970-01-01 is day 0.
        assert_eq!(civil_from_days(0), (1970, 1, 1));
        // 2024-01-01 is day 19_723.
        assert_eq!(civil_from_days(19_723), (2024, 1, 1));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! `web.*` tools — HTTP fetch + URL encoding. `fetch` consults
//! `ctx.check_net()` so the sandbox's net policy is enforced at the tool
//! level. URL encode/decode are pure functions.

use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind, ToolArc};
use rc_core::{arc, Tool, ToolResult};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::need_param;

pub struct Fetch;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Fetch {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "web.fetch" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        "HTTP GET a URL, return the response body as a string. Enforces the sandbox net policy."
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::required("url", ParamType::String))
            .param(Parameter::optional("max_bytes", ParamType::Integer).with_default(serde_json::json!(200_000)))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        ctx.check_net()?;
        let url = need_param(input, "url", ParamType::String, Value::as_str)?;
        let max_bytes = input["max_bytes"].as_i64().unwrap_or(200_000).max(0) as usize;
        let mk_err = |e: String| rc_core::error::ToolError::ToolFailed {
            tool: "web.fetch".into(),
            inner: e,
        };
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(15))
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| mk_err(e.to_string()))?;
        let resp = client
            .get(url)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| mk_err(e.to_string()))?;
        let status = resp.status().as_u16();
        // Stream the body with a running byte counter — a huge response is
        // truncated at `max_bytes` while reading, never read fully into RAM
        // before the cap is applied.
        let mut body_bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(8_192);
        let mut truncated = false;
        let mut resp = resp;
        while let Some(chunk) = resp.chunk().await.map_err(|e| mk_err(e.to_string()))? {
            if body_bytes.len() + chunk.len() > max_bytes {
                let take = max_bytes.saturating_sub(body_bytes.len());
                body_bytes.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..take]);
                truncated = true;
                break;
            }
            body_bytes.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
        }
        let body = String::from_utf8_lossy(&body_bytes).to_string();
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "status": status,
            "body": body,
            "truncated": truncated,
        }))
    }
}

pub struct UrlEncode;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for UrlEncode {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "web.url_encode" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Percent-encode a string for use in a URL query/component." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("s", ParamType::String))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let s = need_param(input, "s", ParamType::String, Value::as_str)?;
        Ok(serde_json::json!(url_encode(s)))
    }
}

pub struct UrlDecode;
#[async_trait]
impl Tool for UrlDecode {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "web.url_decode" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Percent-decode a string." }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("s", ParamType::String))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let s = need_param(input, "s", ParamType::String, Value::as_str)?;
        let dec = url_decode(s).map_err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other)?;
        Ok(serde_json::json!(dec))
    }
}

/// Percent-encode per RFC 3986 (unreserved set kept).
fn url_encode(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for &b in s.as_bytes() {
        match b {
            b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => {
                out.push(b as char);
            }
            _ => {
                out.push('%');
                out.push_str(&format!("{:02X}", b));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

fn url_decode(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        if bytes[i] == b'%' {
            if i + 2 >= bytes.len() {
                return Err("incomplete percent-encoding".into());
            }
            let hex = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[i + 1..i + 3])
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            let byte = u8::from_str_radix(hex, 16)
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            out.push(byte);
            i += 3;
        } else if bytes[i] == b'+' {
            out.push(b' ');
            i += 1;
        } else {
            out.push(bytes[i]);
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8(out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

pub fn all() -> Vec<ToolArc> {
    vec![arc(Fetch), arc(UrlEncode), arc(UrlDecode)]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn url_roundtrip() {
        let s = "hello world & foo=bar";
        let enc = url_encode(s);
        assert_eq!(enc, "hello%20world%20%26%20foo%3Dbar");
        assert_eq!(url_decode(&enc).unwrap(), s);
    }
    #[test]
    fn url_plus_decode() {
        assert_eq!(url_decode("a+b").unwrap(), "a b");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! **Branch** — conditionally route to one of N tools. Each branch carries a
//! condition (`path` into the input that must `equal` a value) and a tool to
//! run if it matches; the first match wins. A branch with no condition is the
//! fallback. The selected tool's output is the branch tool's output.

use crate::templating::{compose_kind, resolve};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::ToolResult;
use rc_core::executor::Executor;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BranchArm {
    /// Dot-path into the input to test (e.g. "op"). Empty/None = always match
    /// (the fallback arm).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub path: Option<String>,
    /// The value `path` must equal for this arm to fire. Ignored when `path`
    /// is empty (fallback arm).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub equals: Option<Value>,
    /// The tool to run if this arm fires.
    pub tool: String,
    /// Optional input template for the selected tool.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub input: Option<Value>,
}

pub struct BranchTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub executor: Executor,
    pub arms: Vec<BranchArm>,
}

impl BranchTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        executor: Executor,
        arms: Vec<BranchArm>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            executor,
            arms,
        }
    }
    pub fn into_arc(self) -> ToolArc {
        arc(self)
    }

    fn select(&self, input: &Value) -> Option<&BranchArm> {
        for arm in &self.arms {
            let matches = match (&arm.path, &arm.equals) {
                (Some(path), Some(expected)) => {
                    crate::templating::lookup(input, path) == *expected
                }
                // No path → fallback arm.
                _ => true,
            };
            if matches {
                return Some(arm);
            }
        }
        None
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for BranchTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        compose_kind("branch")
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other("branch cancelled".into()));
        }
        let arm = self.select(input).ok_or_else(|| {
            rc_core::error::ToolError::Other(format!(
                "no branch arm matched input {}",
                input
            ))
        })?;
        let step_input = match &arm.input {
            Some(t) => resolve(t, &Value::Null, input),
            None => input.clone(),
        };
        self.executor.run_inner(&arm.tool, &step_input).await
    }
}

mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::permissions::PermissionPolicy;
    use rc_core::sandbox::Sandbox;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    fn exec() -> Executor {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(rc_builtin::all_tools());
        Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default())
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn routes_on_op_field() {
        let ex = exec();
        let b = BranchTool::new(
            "compose.calc",
            "add or multiply",
            Schema::new()
                .param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("op", rc_core::schema::ParamType::String))
                .param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("a", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number))
                .param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("b", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number)),
            ex,
            vec![
                BranchArm {
                    path: Some("op".into()),
                    equals: Some(serde_json::json!("add")),
                    tool: "math.add".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{input.a}}", "b": "{{input.b}}" })),
                },
                BranchArm {
                    path: Some("op".into()),
                    equals: Some(serde_json::json!("mul")),
                    tool: "math.multiply".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{input.a}}", "b": "{{input.b}}" })),
                },
                BranchArm {
                    path: None,
                    equals: None,
                    tool: "math.subtract".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{input.a}}", "b": "{{input.b}}" })),
                },
            ],
        );
        let add = b
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "op": "add", "a": 2, "b": 3 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((add.as_f64().unwrap() - 5.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        let mul = b
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "op": "mul", "a": 2, "b": 3 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((mul.as_f64().unwrap() - 6.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        let fallback = b
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "op": "wat", "a": 10, "b": 3 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((fallback.as_f64().unwrap() - 7.0).abs() < 1e-9); // subtract fallback
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/dag.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/dag.rs)

```rust
//! **DAG** — run a dependency graph of tool calls in topological order. Each
//! node names a tool, an optional input template, and the nodes it depends on.
//! A node's template may reference `{{input.x}}` (the composition's input) and
//! `{{nodes.<name>.<path>}}` (a dependency's output). Returns a map of every
//! node's output, or a single nominated output node's value.

use crate::templating::{compose_kind, resolve_ctx};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use rc_core::executor::Executor;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DagNode {
    pub name: String,
    pub tool: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub input: Option<Value>,
    /// Names of nodes whose outputs this node reads. Used for ordering only —
    /// a node may still reference a non-depended node at its own risk.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub deps: Vec<String>,
}

pub struct DagTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub executor: Executor,
    pub nodes: Vec<DagNode>,
    /// If set, return only this node's output; else return a map of all.
    pub output_node: Option<String>,
}

impl DagTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        executor: Executor,
        nodes: Vec<DagNode>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            executor,
            nodes,
            output_node: None,
        }
    }
    pub fn with_output_node(mut self, n: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.output_node = Some(n.into());
        self
    }
    pub fn into_arc(self) -> ToolArc {
        arc(self)
    }

    /// Topologically sort the nodes (Kahn's algorithm). Errors on cycles or
    /// missing deps.
    fn topo(&self) -> Result<Vec<usize>, ToolError> {
        let n = self.nodes.len();
        let name_to_idx: HashMap<&str, usize> = self
            .nodes
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, nd)| (nd.name.as_str(), i))
            .collect();
        let mut indeg = vec![0usize; n];
        let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n];
        for (i, nd) in self.nodes.iter().enumerate() {
            for d in &nd.deps {
                let j = name_to_idx.get(d.as_str()).ok_or_else(|| {
                    ToolError::Other(format!("dag node `{}` depends on unknown node `{}`", nd.name, d))
                })?;
                adj[*j].push(i);
                indeg[i] += 1;
            }
        }
        let mut queue: std::collections::VecDeque<usize> =
            (0..n).filter(|&i| indeg[i] == 0).collect();
        let mut order = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        while let Some(i) = queue.pop_front() {
            order.push(i);
            for &j in &adj[i] {
                indeg[j] -= 1;
                if indeg[j] == 0 {
                    queue.push_back(j);
                }
            }
        }
        if order.len() != n {
            return Err(ToolError::Other("dag has a cycle".into()));
        }
        Ok(order)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for DagTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        compose_kind("dag")
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(ToolError::Other("dag cancelled".into()));
        }
        let order = self.topo()?;
        let mut outputs: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::new();
        for &i in &order {
            let node = &self.nodes[i];
            let nodes_ctx: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = outputs
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
                .collect();
            let ctx_val = serde_json::json!({
                "input": input,
                "nodes": Value::Object(nodes_ctx),
            });
            let step_input = match &node.input {
                Some(t) => resolve_ctx(t, &ctx_val),
                None => input.clone(),
            };
            let out = self.executor.run_inner(&node.tool, &step_input).await?;
            outputs.insert(node.name.clone(), out);
        }
        match &self.output_node {
            Some(name) => Ok(outputs
                .get(name)
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or(Value::Null)),
            None => {
                let mut map = serde_json::Map::new();
                for (k, v) in outputs {
                    map.insert(k, v);
                }
                Ok(Value::Object(map))
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::permissions::PermissionPolicy;
    use rc_core::sandbox::Sandbox;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    fn exec() -> Executor {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(rc_builtin::all_tools());
        Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default())
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn diamond_dependency() {
        // input.x → a = x², b = x³ ; c = a + b. Returns c.
        let ex = exec();
        let dag = DagTool::new(
            "compose.diamond",
            "x² + x³",
            Schema::new().param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("x", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number)),
            ex,
            vec![
                DagNode {
                    name: "sq".into(),
                    tool: "math.multiply".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{input.x}}", "b": "{{input.x}}" })),
                    deps: vec![],
                },
                DagNode {
                    name: "cu".into(),
                    tool: "math.multiply".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{nodes.sq}}", "b": "{{input.x}}" })),
                    deps: vec!["sq".into()],
                },
                DagNode {
                    name: "sum".into(),
                    tool: "math.add".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{nodes.sq}}", "b": "{{nodes.cu}}" })),
                    deps: vec!["sq".into(), "cu".into()],
                },
            ],

            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "x": 3 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await

            vec![
                DagNode { name: "a".into(), tool: "math.add".into(), input: None, deps: vec!["b".into()] },
                DagNode { name: "b".into(), tool: "math.add".into(), input: None, deps: vec!["a".into()] },
            ],
        );
        assert!(dag.topo().is_err());
    }
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/iter.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/iter.rs)

```rust
//! **Loop** — run a tool repeatedly, feeding each output back as the next
//! input, until a stop condition holds or `max_iters` is reached. Returns the
//! final value (or every iteration's output if `collect_all` is set).

use crate::templating::{compose_kind, resolve};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use rc_core::executor::Executor;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

/// Compare two JSON values for the loop's stop condition. Numbers compare by
/// their `f64` value (so `128` matches `128.0`); everything else compares by
/// strict equality. Strings match numbers only if the string parses to the
/// same number (so a tool that returns `"128"` still stops on `equals: 128`).
fn values_equal(a: &Value, b: &Value) -> bool {
    if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (a.as_f64(), b.as_f64()) {
        return (x - y).abs() < 1e-9;
    }
    a == b
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Until {
    /// Dot-path into each iteration's output.
    pub path: String,
    /// The value `path` must equal to stop.
    pub equals: Value,
}

pub struct LoopTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub executor: Executor,
    pub tool: String,
    /// Input template for each iteration; `{{prev}}` is the previous output,
    /// `{{input}}` the original input. `None` = pass prev through directly.
    pub input: Option<Value>,
    /// Stop when an iteration's output at `path` equals `equals`.
    pub until: Option<Until>,
    pub max_iters: usize,
    /// If true, return every iteration's output as an array; else the final.
    pub collect_all: bool,
}

impl LoopTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        executor: Executor,
        tool: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            executor,
            tool: tool.into(),
            input: None,
            until: None,
            max_iters: 100,
            collect_all: false,
        }
    }
    pub fn with_input(mut self, t: Value) -> Self {
        self.input = Some(t);
        self
    }
    pub fn with_until(mut self, path: impl Into<String>, equals: Value) -> Self {
        self.until = Some(Until {
            path: path.into(),
            equals,
        });
        self
    }
    pub fn with_max_iters(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
        self.max_iters = n;
        self
    }
    pub fn collect_all(mut self) -> Self {
        self.collect_all = true;
        self
    }
    pub fn into_arc(self) -> ToolArc {
        arc(self)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for LoopTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        compose_kind("loop")
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(ToolError::Other("loop cancelled".into()));
        }
        let mut prev = input.clone();
        let mut collected: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..self.max_iters {
            let step_input = match &self.input {
                Some(t) => resolve(t, &prev, input),
                None => prev.clone(),
            };
            let out = self.executor.run_inner(&self.tool, &step_input).await?;
            if self.collect_all {
                collected.push(out.clone());
            }
            // stop condition
            if let Some(until) = &self.until {
                let actual = crate::templating::lookup(&out, &until.path);
                if values_equal(&actual, &until.equals) {
                    return if self.collect_all {
                        Ok(Value::Array(collected))
                    } else {
                        Ok(out)
                    };
                }
            }
            prev = out;
            let _ = i; // iteration counter (for debugging)
        }
        if self.collect_all {
            Ok(Value::Array(collected))
        } else {
            Ok(prev)
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::permissions::PermissionPolicy;
    use rc_core::sandbox::Sandbox;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    fn exec() -> Executor {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(rc_builtin::all_tools());
        Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default())
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn loop_runs_max_iters_without_until() {
        // Each iteration: math.add {a: {{prev}}, b: 1}. Start input {a: 0}.
        // After 5 iters of adding 1 to prev... but math.add returns a number,
        // not {a:...}. Use a template that reads {{prev}} as the number.
        let ex = exec();
        let lp = LoopTool::new(
            "compose.count",
            "add 1, 5 times",
            Schema::new().param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("a", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number)),
            ex,
            "math.add",
        )
        .with_input(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{prev}}", "b": 1 }))
        .with_max_iters(5);
        // seed: the first iteration uses prev = input = {"a": 0}, so {{prev}} → {"a":0}
        // which isn't a number. Instead, seed with a number directly: input = 0.
        let out = lp
            .execute(&serde_json::json!(0), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((out.as_f64().unwrap() - 5.0).abs() < 1e-9); // 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn loop_stops_on_until() {
        // Keep doubling until >= 100. math.multiply {a: {{prev}}, b: 2}.
        let ex = exec();
        let lp = LoopTool::new(
            "compose.doubl",
            "double until >= 100",
            Schema::new(),
            ex,
            "math.multiply",
        )
        .with_input(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{prev}}", "b": 2 }))
        .with_until("", serde_json::json!(128)) // stop when prev == 128
        .with_max_iters(20);
        let out = lp
            .execute(&serde_json::json!(1), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((out.as_f64().unwrap() - 128.0).abs() < 1e-9); // 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 → 32 → 64 → 128
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/lib.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/lib.rs)

```rust
//! # rc-compose — L4 composition: new tools from old tools
//!
//! Five composition primitives, each producing a registered [`Tool`]:
//!
//! | primitive | what it does |
//! |-----------|--------------|
//! | [`pipeline`] | chain tools — each step's output feeds the next |
//! | [`parallel`] | fan out N tools concurrently, join as an array |
//! | [`branch`] | conditionally route to one of N tools (first match wins) |
//! | [`iter`] | loop a tool, feeding output back, until a condition or max |
//! | [`dag`] | run a dependency graph of tool calls in topological order |
//!
//! Because every composition is itself a `Tool`, compositions **nest** — a
//! pipeline step can be a branch, a DAG node can be a parallel, and so on.
//! That nesting is what makes the framework *multiplicatively* unlimited:
//! finite primitives compose into an unbounded space of tools.
//!
//! Template references (`{{prev.x}}`, `{{input.y}}`, `{{nodes.name.z}}`) are
//! resolved by [`templating`], shared by all five primitives.

pub mod branch;
pub mod dag;
pub mod iter;
pub mod parallel;
pub mod pipeline;
pub mod templating;

pub use branch::{BranchArm, BranchTool};
pub use dag::{DagNode, DagTool};
pub use iter::{LoopTool, Until};
pub use parallel::{ParallelStep, ParallelTool};
pub use pipeline::{pipe, PipelineStep, PipelineTool};
pub use templating::{lookup, resolve, resolve_ctx};
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/parallel.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/parallel.rs)

```rust
//! **Parallel** — run N tools concurrently and return their results as an
//! array. Each step's input is a template resolved against the composition's
//! input. Errors in individual steps become `{"error": "…"}` entries so one
//! failure doesn't abort the rest.
//!
//! Steps are spawned as tasks but never orphaned: each step shares the
//! caller's live cancellation flag ([`ToolContext::cancel`]), so when the
//! executor's timeout fires (or a parent cancels), every in-flight step
//! observes it, drops its work — which (with `kill_on_drop`) kills any
//! subprocess it had spawned — and the runner joins every task before
//! returning.

use crate::templating::{compose_kind, resolve};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use rc_core::executor::Executor;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

/// Poll the shared cancellation flag until it fires.
async fn wait_cancelled(flag: Arc<AtomicBool>) {
    loop {
        if flag.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ParallelStep {
    pub tool: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub input: Option<Value>,
}

pub struct ParallelTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub executor: Executor,
    pub steps: Vec<ParallelStep>,
}

impl ParallelTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        executor: Executor,
        steps: Vec<ParallelStep>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            executor,
            steps,
        }
    }
    pub fn into_arc(self) -> ToolArc {
        arc(self)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for ParallelTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        compose_kind("parallel")
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(ToolError::Other("parallel cancelled".into()));
        }
        // Resolve every step's input, then run all concurrently.
        let inputs: Vec<(String, Value)> = self
            .steps
            .iter()
            .map(|s| {
                let inp = match &s.input {
                    Some(t) => resolve(t, &Value::Null, input),
                    None => input.clone(),
                };
                (s.tool.clone(), inp)
            })
            .collect();
        let mut futs = Vec::new();
        for (tool, inp) in inputs {
            let exec = self.executor.clone();
            // Child context shares the parent's live cancellation flag, so a
            // timeout/cancel on the parent call reaches the spawned step.
            let child = ToolContext {
                cancelled: ctx.cancelled,
                cancel: ctx.cancel.clone(),
                ..ToolContext::default()
            };
            let cancel = ctx.cancel.clone();
            futs.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
                // Race the step against the shared flag: if the parent times
                // out or cancels, drop the in-flight step (killing its
                // subprocesses via kill_on_drop) instead of running to
                // completion detached.
                tokio::select! {
                    biased;
                    _ = wait_cancelled(cancel) => {
                        Err(ToolError::Other(format!("parallel step `{tool}` cancelled")))
                    }
                    r = exec.run_inner_ctx(&tool, &inp, &child) => r,
                }
            }));
        }
        // Join every spawned task — nothing is left detached. On the success
        // path each task has already finished; if cancellation fires while we
        // are still joining, the tasks self-abort via the flag (see above)
        // and their errors are reported as `{"error": …}` entries as usual.
        let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(futs.len());
        for h in futs {
            let r = h
                .await
                .map_err(|e| ToolError::ToolFailed {
                    tool: "parallel".into(),
                    inner: format!("task join: {e}"),
                })?;
            results.push(match r {
                Ok(v) => v,
                Err(e) => serde_json::json!({ "error": e.to_string() }),
            });
        }
        Ok(Value::Array(results))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::permissions::PermissionPolicy;
    use rc_core::sandbox::Sandbox;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    fn exec() -> Executor {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(rc_builtin::all_tools());
        Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default())
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn fan_out_three() {
        let ex = exec();
        let p = ParallelTool::new(
            "compose.par",
            "run 3 in parallel",
            Schema::new().param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("x", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number)),
            ex,
            vec![
                ParallelStep {
                    tool: "math.sqrt".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "n": "{{input.x}}" })),
                },
                ParallelStep {
                    tool: "math.factorial".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "n": "{{input.x}}" })),
                },
                ParallelStep {
                    tool: "math.multiply".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{input.x}}", "b": "{{input.x}}" })),
                },
            ],
        );
        let out = p
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "x": 5 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out.as_array().unwrap().len(), 3);
        assert!((out[0].as_f64().unwrap() - 5.0_f64.sqrt()).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(out[1], "120"); // 5! = 120 (returned as string by factorial)
        assert!((out[2].as_f64().unwrap() - 25.0).abs() < 1e-9);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn spawned_steps_observe_cancellation() {
        // Flip the shared flag while a slow step is running: the step must
        // bail out promptly via the flag (well before its 5s sleep ends)
        // instead of running to completion detached.
        let ex = exec();
        let p = ParallelTool::new(
            "compose.par.slow",
            "one slow step",
            Schema::new(),
            ex,
            vec![ParallelStep {
                tool: "time.sleep".into(),
                input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "ms": 5_000 })),
            }],
        );
        let ctx = ToolContext::default();
        let flag = ctx.cancel.clone();
        let flipper = tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
            flag.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        });
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        let out = p
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({}), &ctx)
            .await
            .unwrap();
        flipper.await.unwrap();
        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
        // The step reported cancellation as an error entry…
        let arr = out.as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(arr.len(), 1);
        assert!(arr[0]["error"].as_str().unwrap().contains("cancelled"));
        // …and did NOT wait out the full 5s sleep.
        assert!(elapsed < std::time::Duration::from_secs(2), "took {elapsed:?}");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! **Pipeline** — chain tools so each step's output feeds the next. A step may
//! take the previous output directly (no template) or take a template that
//! references `{{prev}}` / `{{input}}`. The pipeline is itself a `Tool`, so
//! pipelines can be steps in other pipelines.

use crate::templating::{compose_kind, resolve};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use rc_core::executor::Executor;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PipelineStep {
    /// The registered tool name to run.
    pub tool: String,
    /// Optional input template. If `None`, the step receives the previous
    /// step's output directly (the first step receives the pipeline input).
    /// If `Some`, the template is resolved against `prev` + `input`.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub input: Option<Value>,
}

pub struct PipelineTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub executor: Executor,
    pub steps: Vec<PipelineStep>,
}

impl PipelineTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        executor: Executor,
        steps: Vec<PipelineStep>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            executor,
            steps,
        }
    }
    /// Wrap as a `ToolArc` ready to register.
    pub fn into_arc(self) -> ToolArc {
        arc(self)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for PipelineTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        compose_kind("pipeline")
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other("pipeline cancelled".into()));
        }
        if self.steps.is_empty() {
            return Err(rc_core::error::ToolError::Other(
                "pipeline has no steps".into(),
            ));
        }
        let mut prev: Value = Value::Null;
        for (i, step) in self.steps.iter().enumerate() {
            let step_input = if i == 0 {
                // First step: template against prev=Null, or pass input directly.
                match &step.input {
                    Some(t) => resolve(t, &Value::Null, input),
                    None => input.clone(),
                }
            } else {
                match &step.input {
                    Some(t) => resolve(t, &prev, input),
                    None => prev.clone(),
                }
            };
            let out = self.executor.run_inner(&step.tool, &step_input).await?;
            prev = out;
        }
        Ok(prev)
    }
}

/// Convenience builder: a pipeline where each step takes the previous step's
/// output directly (the shell-pipe model). Errors on an empty step list
/// (instead of panicking on `steps[0]`).
pub fn pipe(executor: Executor, name: &str, steps: &[&str]) -> ToolResult<PipelineTool> {
    if steps.is_empty() {
        return Err(ToolError::Validation(
            "pipe() needs at least one step".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    let pipeline_steps: Vec<PipelineStep> = steps
        .iter()
        .map(|s| PipelineStep {
            tool: s.to_string(),
            input: None,
        })
        .collect();
    // The pipeline's input schema is the first step's schema (if any), else
    // a permissive empty schema.
    let schema = executor
        .registry
        .get(steps[0])
        .map(|t| t.schema())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    Ok(PipelineTool::new(
        name,
        format!("pipeline: {}", steps.join(" → ")),
        schema,
        executor,
        pipeline_steps,
    ))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::permissions::PermissionPolicy;
    use rc_core::sandbox::Sandbox;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    /// Build an executor with the builtin math+text tools registered.
    fn exec() -> Executor {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(rc_builtin::all_tools());
        Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default())
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn pipe_chains_text_then_math() {
        // text.length({s: "hello"}) → 5 ; math.sqrt({n: {{prev}}}) → √5.
        // Uses templates because the tools' shapes don't match for bare piping.
        let ex = exec();
        let p = PipelineTool::new(
            "compose.demo",
            "length then sqrt",
            rc_core::schema::Schema::new()
                .param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("s", rc_core::schema::ParamType::String)),
            ex,
            vec![
                PipelineStep {
                    tool: "text.length".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "s": "{{input.s}}" })),
                },
                PipelineStep {
                    tool: "math.sqrt".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "n": "{{prev}}" })),
                },
            ],
        );
        let out = p
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "s": "hello" }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let v = out.as_f64().unwrap();
        assert!((v - 5.0_f64.sqrt()).abs() < 1e-9);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn pipeline_with_input_template() {
        // Step 1: math.multiply {a: {{input.x}}, b: {{input.x}}}  → x*x
        // Step 2: math.add {a: {{prev}}, b: {{input.y}}}           → x*x + y
        let ex = exec();
        let p = PipelineTool::new(
            "compose.template",
            "x² + y",
            rc_core::schema::Schema::new()
                .param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("x", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number))
                .param(rc_core::schema::Parameter::required("y", rc_core::schema::ParamType::Number)),
            ex,
            vec![
                PipelineStep {
                    tool: "math.multiply".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{input.x}}", "b": "{{input.x}}" })),
                },
                PipelineStep {
                    tool: "math.add".into(),
                    input: Some(serde_json::json!({ "a": "{{prev}}", "b": "{{input.y}}" })),
                },
            ],
        );
        let out = p
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "x": 3, "y": 4 }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((out.as_f64().unwrap() - 13.0).abs() < 1e-9); // 3*3 + 4
    }

    #[test]
    fn pipe_rejects_empty_steps() {
        // Empty step lists must be a proper error, not a panic on steps[0].
        let msg = match pipe(exec(), "compose.empty", &[]) {
            Err(e) => e.to_string(),
            Ok(_) => panic!("expected pipe() to reject an empty step list"),
        };
        assert!(msg.contains("at least one step"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn pipe_single_step_works() {
        let ex = exec();
        let p = pipe(ex, "compose.single", &["text.upper"]).unwrap();
        let out = p
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "s": "hi" }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "HI");
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/templating.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-compose/src/templating.rs)

```rust
//! Template resolution for composition tools. A step's input template is a
//! JSON value whose string leaves may reference:
//!
//! * `{{prev}}` — the previous step's full output
//! * `{{input}}` — the composition's original input
//! * `{{prev.a.b}}` / `{{input.a}}` — a dot-path into either
//!
//! Whole-string templates are replaced by the referenced value (any type);
//! templates embedded in larger strings are string-substituted (result stays
//! a string). Objects and arrays are recursed.

use rc_core::tool::ToolSourceKind;
use serde_json::Value;

/// Walk a dot-path (`a.b.0.c`) into a JSON value. Numbers index arrays.
pub fn lookup(root: &Value, path: &str) -> Value {
    let mut cur = root;
    for seg in path.split('.') {
        if seg.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        cur = match cur {
            Value::Object(map) => map.get(seg).unwrap_or(&Value::Null),
            Value::Array(arr) => seg
                .parse::<usize>()
                .ok()
                .and_then(|i| arr.get(i))
                .unwrap_or(&Value::Null),
            _ => &Value::Null,
        };
    }
    cur.clone()
}

/// Resolve a template value against `prev` (previous step output) and `input`
/// (the composition's original input).
pub fn resolve(template: &Value, prev: &Value, input: &Value) -> Value {
    let ctx = serde_json::json!({ "prev": prev, "input": input });
    resolve_ctx(template, &ctx)
}

/// General resolver: any `{{dot.path}}` is looked up against `ctx`. This is
/// what the DAG uses, with `ctx = {"input": …, "nodes": {name: output, …}}`.
pub fn resolve_ctx(template: &Value, ctx: &Value) -> Value {
    match template {
        Value::String(s) => resolve_string_ctx(s, ctx),
        Value::Object(map) => {
            let mut out = serde_json::Map::new();
            for (k, v) in map {
                out.insert(k.clone(), resolve_ctx(v, ctx));
            }
            Value::Object(out)
        }
        Value::Array(arr) => Value::Array(
            arr.iter().map(|v| resolve_ctx(v, ctx)).collect(),
        ),
        other => other.clone(),
    }
}

/// Whole-string `{{path}}` → the looked-up value (any type); embedded
/// templates → string substitution.
fn resolve_string_ctx(s: &str, ctx: &Value) -> Value {
    if let Some(inner) = s.strip_prefix("{{").and_then(|x| x.strip_suffix("}}")) {
        if !inner.contains('{') && !inner.contains(' ') {
            return lookup(ctx, inner.trim());
        }
    }
    if s.contains("{{") {
        return Value::String(substitute_all(s, ctx));
    }
    Value::String(s.to_string())
}

/// Replace every `{{path}}` in `s` with the stringified value at `ctx.path`.
/// Walks the string by whole UTF-8 characters — the old byte-at-a-time loop
/// rendered every non-ASCII character outside a `{{…}}` span as mojibake.
fn substitute_all(s: &str, ctx: &Value) -> String {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        if bytes[i] == b'{' && i + 1 < bytes.len() && bytes[i + 1] == b'{' {
            if let Some(end) = s[i + 2..].find("}}") {
                let path = &s[i + 2..i + 2 + end];
                let val = lookup(ctx, path.trim());
                match &val {
                    Value::String(t) => out.push_str(t),
                    Value::Null => {}
                    other => out.push_str(&other.to_string()),
                }
                i = i + 2 + end + 2;
                continue;
            }
        }
        // Push the whole character (it may be multi-byte), not the raw byte.
        let ch = s[i..].chars().next().unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}');
        out.push(ch);
        i += ch.len_utf8();
    }
    out
}

/// Source-kind tag for a composition variant.
pub fn compose_kind(variant: &'static str) -> ToolSourceKind {
    ToolSourceKind::Compose(variant)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn whole_string_templates() {
        let prev = serde_json::json!({ "sum": 7 });
        let input = serde_json::json!({ "x": 5 });
        assert_eq!(
            resolve(&serde_json::json!("{{prev}}"), &prev, &input),
            serde_json::json!({ "sum": 7 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            resolve(&serde_json::json!("{{prev.sum}}"), &prev, &input),
            serde_json::json!(7)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            resolve(&serde_json::json!("{{input.x}}"), &prev, &input),
            serde_json::json!(5)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn embedded_templates() {
        let prev = serde_json::json!({ "name": "ada" });
        let input = serde_json::json!({ "greeting": "hi" });
        let t = serde_json::json!("{{input.greeting}}, {{prev.name}}!");
        assert_eq!(
            resolve(&t, &prev, &input),
            serde_json::json!("hi, ada!")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn recurses_objects_and_arrays() {
        let prev = serde_json::json!(42);
        let input = serde_json::json!({ "a": 1 });
        let t = serde_json::json!({ "from_prev": "{{prev}}", "list": ["{{input.a}}", "lit"] });
        let r = resolve(&t, &prev, &input);
        assert_eq!(r["from_prev"], 42);
        assert_eq!(r["list"][0], 1);
        assert_eq!(r["list"][1], "lit");
    }

    #[test]
    fn array_index_lookup() {
        let prev = serde_json::json!([10, 20, 30]);
        assert_eq!(lookup(&prev, "1"), serde_json::json!(20));
        assert_eq!(lookup(&prev, "5"), serde_json::Value::Null);
    }

    #[test]
    fn non_ascii_text_survives_substitution() {
        // The old byte-at-a-time loop turned é/ü/日 into mojibake outside the
        // template spans; the fixed loop pushes whole characters.
        let prev = serde_json::json!({ "name": "ada" });
        let input = serde_json::json!({});
        let t = serde_json::json!("héllo {{prev.name}} — ünïcode 日本語!");
        assert_eq!(
            resolve(&t, &prev, &input),
            serde_json::json!("héllo ada — ünïcode 日本語!")
        );
        // Missing lookup right after a multi-byte char still renders cleanly.
        let t = serde_json::json!("héllo {{missing}}!");
        assert_eq!(resolve(&t, &prev, &input), serde_json::json!("héllo !"));
        // Template with a value containing non-ASCII text.
        let prev = serde_json::json!("Grüße");
        let t = serde_json::json!("{{prev}}, wörld");
        assert_eq!(resolve(&t, &prev, &input), serde_json::json!("Grüße, wörld"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Errors for the RomaCode tools builder core.

use crate::schema::ParamType;
use thiserror::Error;

/// Every tool execution failure flows through `ToolError`.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum ToolError {
    #[error("tool not found: {0}")]
    NotFound(String),

    #[error("validation error: {0}")]
    Validation(String),

    #[error("parameter `{name}` (expected {expected:?}) — {detail}")]
    BadParam {
        name: String,
        expected: ParamType,
        detail: String,
    },

    #[error("permission denied for tool `{tool}`: {reason}")]
    PermissionDenied { tool: String, reason: String },

    #[error("sandbox violation: {0}")]
    Sandbox(String),

    #[error("execution timed out after {timeout_ms} ms")]
    Timeout { timeout_ms: u64 },

    #[error("output exceeded sandbox limit ({limit} bytes)")]
    OutputTooLarge { limit: usize },

    #[error("tool `{tool}` returned an error: {inner}")]
    ToolFailed { tool: String, inner: String },

    #[error("i/o error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

    #[error("json error: {0}")]
    Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),

    #[error("{0}")]
    Other(String),
}

/// Shorthand result alias.
pub type ToolResult<T> = Result<T, ToolError>;

impl From<ToolError> for String {
    fn from(e: ToolError) -> String {
        e.to_string()
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-core/src/executor.rs`

```rust
//! The [`Executor`] — the single point through which a tool is actually run.
//! It holds a [`Registry`], a [`PermissionPolicy`], and a [`Sandbox`], and for
//! every call it:
//!
//! 1. looks the tool up in the registry,
//! 2. asks the policy for a decision (`Allow` / `Ask` / `Deny`),
//! 3. validates the input against the tool's schema (filling defaults),
//! 4. enforces the sandbox (timeout, output cap),
//! 5. runs the tool's `execute`,
//! 6. clamps the output to the sandbox's size limit.
//!
//! The executor never prompts a human — `Ask` is surfaced as a decision the
//! caller (CLI, agent loop) must handle before calling `run` with
//! `approved = true`.

use crate::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use crate::permissions::{Permission, PermissionPolicy};
use crate::registry::Registry;
use crate::sandbox::Sandbox;
use crate::tool::ToolContext;
use serde_json::Value;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Executor {
    pub registry: Registry,
    pub policy: Arc<PermissionPolicy>,
    pub sandbox: Arc<Sandbox>,
}

impl Executor {
    pub fn new(registry: Registry, policy: PermissionPolicy, sandbox: Sandbox) -> Self {
        Self {
            registry,
            policy: Arc::new(policy),
            sandbox: Arc::new(sandbox),
        }
    }

    /// What would the policy decide for this tool? Callers use this to decide
    /// whether to prompt the user (`Ask`) before calling `run`.
    pub fn authorize(&self, name: &str) -> ToolResult<Permission> {
        let t = self.registry.get(name)?;
        Ok(self.policy.decide(t.as_ref()))
    }

    /// Run a tool by name. `approved` signals the caller already obtained
    /// human approval for an `Ask` decision.
    pub async fn run(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        input: &Value,
        approved: bool,
    ) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let tool = self.registry.get(name)?;

        // 2. permission gate
        match self.policy.decide(tool.as_ref()) {
            Permission::Deny => {
                return Err(ToolError::PermissionDenied {
                    tool: name.to_string(),
                    reason: "denied by policy".to_string(),
                });
            }
            Permission::Ask if !approved => {
                return Err(ToolError::PermissionDenied {
                    tool: name.to_string(),
                    reason: "requires approval (Ask)".to_string(),
                });
            }
            _ => {}
        }

        // 3. validate input (fills defaults)
        let validated = crate::validator::validate(&tool.schema(), input)?;

        // 4+5. sandbox: timeout + execute. The context carries a *shared*
        // cancellation flag: when the timeout fires we flip it before
        // returning, so any sub-task the tool spawned (e.g. a parallel
        // fan-out) observes cancellation and stops, instead of running on
        // detached after the caller has already seen a Timeout.
        let ctx = ToolContext {
            correlation_id: name.to_string(),
            timeout_ms: self.sandbox.timeout_ms,
            cancelled: false,
            cancel: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),
            allow_net: self.sandbox.allow_net,
            allow_fs_paths: self.sandbox.allow_fs_paths.clone(),
        };
        let fut = tool.execute(&validated, &ctx);
        let out = if self.sandbox.timeout_ms == 0 {
            fut.await?
        } else {
            match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(self.sandbox.timeout_ms), fut).await {
                Ok(inner) => inner?,
                Err(_elapsed) => {
                    ctx.cancel();
                    return Err(ToolError::Timeout {
                        timeout_ms: self.sandbox.timeout_ms,
                    });
                }
            }
        };

        // 6. clamp output
        let mut o = out;
        self.sandbox.clamp_output(&mut o)?;
        Ok(o)
    }

    /// Run without the permission gate — used internally by composition, where
    /// the *outer* composed tool has already been authorized and the inner
    /// steps are trusted parts of the same call. The inner tool sees a default
    /// context (its own fresh cancellation flag).
    pub async fn run_inner(&self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        self.run_inner_ctx(name, input, &ToolContext::default()).await
    }

    /// Like [`Executor::run_inner`], but the inner tool inherits the caller's
    /// cancellation state: it sees the parent's `cancelled` snapshot and
    /// *shares the parent's live cancellation flag*, so a timeout or cancel
    /// on the parent call propagates into spawned sub-tasks. Composition
    /// tools that fan out (parallel) use this.
    pub async fn run_inner_ctx(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        input: &Value,
        parent_ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let tool = self.registry.get(name)?;
        let validated = crate::validator::validate(&tool.schema(), input)?;
        let ctx = ToolContext {
            correlation_id: name.to_string(),
            timeout_ms: self.sandbox.timeout_ms,
            cancelled: parent_ctx.cancelled || parent_ctx.is_cancelled(),
            cancel: parent_ctx.cancel.clone(),
            allow_net: self.sandbox.allow_net,
            allow_fs_paths: self.sandbox.allow_fs_paths.clone(),
        };
        let fut = tool.execute(&validated, &ctx);
        // A step timing out produces an error result for that step only — it
        // must NOT flip the shared parent flag (that would cancel siblings).
        let out = if self.sandbox.timeout_ms == 0 {
            fut.await?
        } else {
            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(self.sandbox.timeout_ms), fut)
                .await
                .map_err(|_| ToolError::Timeout {
                    timeout_ms: self.sandbox.timeout_ms,
                })??
        };
        let mut o = out;
        self.sandbox.clamp_output(&mut o)?;
        Ok(o)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
    use crate::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
    use crate::Tool;
    use async_trait::async_trait;

    struct Add;
    #[async_trait]
    impl Tool for Add {
        fn name(&self) -> &str { "math.add" }
        fn description(&self) -> &str { "add two ints" }
        fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
            Schema::new()
                .param(Parameter::required("a", ParamType::Integer))
                .param(Parameter::required("b", ParamType::Integer))
        }
        fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
        async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
            let a = input["a"].as_i64().unwrap();
            let b = input["b"].as_i64().unwrap();
            Ok(serde_json::json!(a + b))
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn run_allow() {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register(crate::tool::arc(Add));
        let ex = Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default());
        // math.add is Allow in the default policy
        let out = ex.run("math.add", &serde_json::json!({ "a": 2, "b": 3 }), false).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, 5);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn run_ask_needs_approval() {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register(crate::tool::arc(Add));
        // force Ask for math.add via a policy with no allow rules
        let policy = PermissionPolicy {
            deny: vec![],
            ask: vec![crate::permissions::PermissionRule::new("*", Permission::Ask)],
            allow: vec![],
            default: Permission::Ask,
        };
        let ex = Executor::new(r, policy, Sandbox::default());
        let err = ex.run("math.add", &serde_json::json!({ "a": 1, "b": 1 }), false).await;
        assert!(err.is_err());
        // with approval it runs
        let out = ex.run("math.add", &serde_json::json!({ "a": 1, "b": 1 }), true).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, 2);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn validation_fills_defaults() {
        struct Echo;
        #[async_trait]
        impl Tool for Echo {
            fn name(&self) -> &str { "text.echo" }
            fn description(&self) -> &str { "" }
            fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
                Schema::new()
                    .param(Parameter::required("msg", ParamType::String))
                    .param(Parameter::optional("loud", ParamType::Boolean).with_default(serde_json::json!(false)))
            }
            fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
            async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, _: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
                let loud = input["loud"].as_bool().unwrap();
                let msg = input["msg"].as_str().unwrap();
                Ok(serde_json::json!(if loud { msg.to_uppercase() } else { msg.to_string() }))
            }
        }
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register(crate::tool::arc(Echo));
        let ex = Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), Sandbox::default());
        let out = ex.run("text.echo", &serde_json::json!({ "msg": "hi" }), false).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "hi");
    }

    /// A tool that shells out like the real `ShellTool`/`rust.*` tools
    /// (`kill_on_drop(true)`), sleeping long enough to hit the timeout.
    struct SlowShell(std::path::PathBuf);
    #[async_trait]
    impl Tool for SlowShell {
        fn name(&self) -> &str { "slow.shell" }
        fn description(&self) -> &str { "sleeps, then drops a marker file" }
        fn schema(&self) -> Schema { Schema::new() }
        fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
        async fn execute(&self, _: &Value, _: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
            // Quote the marker path like ShellTool does — it contains
            // characters (e.g. parentheses from ThreadId debug output) that
            // are shell-special.
            let q = format!("'{}'", self.0.display().to_string().replace('\'', "'\\''"));
            let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new("sh");
            cmd.arg("-c")
                .arg(format!("sleep 2; touch {q}"));
            cmd.kill_on_drop(true);
            let out = cmd.output().await.map_err(|e| ToolError::Other(e.to_string()))?;
            Ok(serde_json::json!({ "exit_code": out.status.code() }))
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn timeout_kills_child_process_and_returns_timeout() {
        // H16: the executor's timeout must not leave the tool's child process
        // running detached. The child would drop a marker file after 2s if it
        // survived; the kill_on_drop'd child is killed at the 200ms timeout,
        // so the marker must never appear.
        let marker = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "rc-h16-alive-{}-{:?}",
            std::process::id(),
            std::thread::current().id()
        ));
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register(crate::tool::arc(SlowShell(marker.clone())));
        let sandbox = Sandbox {
            timeout_ms: 200,
            ..Sandbox::default()
        };
        let ex = Executor::new(r, PermissionPolicy::default(), sandbox);
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        let res = ex.run("slow.shell", &serde_json::json!({}), true).await;
        // The timeout error comes back promptly.
        assert!(
            matches!(res, Err(ToolError::Timeout { timeout_ms: 200 })),
            "expected Timeout, got {res:?}"
        );
        assert!(start.elapsed() < std::time::Duration::from_secs(1));
        // Give a (hypothetically) orphaned child time to drop its marker…
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(2_500)).await;
        // …then assert it never did: the child was killed on drop.
        assert!(
            !marker.exists(),
            "child process outlived the executor timeout (orphan)"
        );
        std::fs::remove_file(&marker).ok();
    }
}
```

```rust
//! # rc-core — the foundation of the RomaCode tools builder
//!
//! The single contract every tool implements ([`Tool`]), the spine they are
//! stored in ([`Registry`]), the gate they run through ([`Executor`] +
//! [`PermissionPolicy`] + [`Sandbox`]), and the contracts they publish
//! ([`Schema`] + [`Manifest`]). Every other crate in the workspace builds on
//! this one and nothing else.
//!
//! ## The 8 universal tool-source mechanisms
//!
//! `ToolSourceKind` enumerates them: `builtin`, `declarative`, `llm_gen`,
//! `openapi`, `mcp`, `rest`, `graphql`, `cli`, `compose`, `marketplace`. Once
//! loaded, every tool from every source is just a `Tool` — the source is
//! metadata, not a special case.

pub mod error;
pub mod executor;
pub mod manifest;
pub mod permissions;
pub mod registry;
pub mod sandbox;
pub mod schema;
pub mod tool;
pub mod validator;

// Re-export the surface.
pub use error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
pub use executor::Executor;
pub use manifest::{Catalog, Manifest};
pub use permissions::{Permission, PermissionPolicy, PermissionRule};
pub use registry::{Registry, ToolInfo};
pub use sandbox::Sandbox;
pub use schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
pub use tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
pub use validator::Validator;

/// The framework version.
pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
```
