```rust
//! A [`Manifest`] — the serializable description of a tool, independent of
//! its runtime `Tool` impl. Sources produce manifests during discovery; the
//! lifecycle manager serializes them to disk (marketplace, declarative specs);
//! the registry holds live `Tool` impls. A manifest is everything you need to
//! *know* about a tool without loading it.

use crate::schema::Schema;
use crate::tool::Tool;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// The serializable identity + contract of a tool.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Manifest {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub category: String,
    pub source: String,
    pub version: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub schema: Schema,
    /// The permission class this tool belongs to (`read`, `ask`, `deny`, …).
    /// Empty = derive from category.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub permission: String,
    /// Optional: the path or URL or spec this tool was loaded from, for
    /// provenance and `rc info`.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub origin: Option<String>,
}

impl Manifest {
    /// Build a manifest from a live `Tool` (snapshots its identity + schema).
    pub fn from_tool(t: &dyn Tool) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: t.name().to_string(),
            description: t.description().to_string(),
            category: t.category().to_string(),
            source: t.source().as_str().to_string(),
            version: t.version().to_string(),
            schema: t.schema(),
            permission: String::new(),
            origin: None,
        }
    }

    /// Render this manifest as a pretty JSON string (for `rc info`, files).
    pub fn to_json_pretty(&self) -> Result<String, serde_json::Error> {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(self)
    }
}

/// A directory of manifests — what a source advertises before loading. The
/// lifecycle manager turns these into live tools on demand.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct Catalog {
    pub manifests: Vec<Manifest>,
}

impl Catalog {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
    pub fn push(&mut self, m: Manifest) {
        self.manifests.push(m);
    }
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.manifests.len()
    }
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.manifests.is_empty()
    }
    pub fn names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut n: Vec<String> = self.manifests.iter().map(|m| m.name.clone()).collect();
        n.sort();
        n
    }
}

    use crate::schema::{ParamType, Parameter};
    use crate::tool::{ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};

    struct T;
    #[async_trait::async_trait]
    impl Tool for T {
        fn name(&self) -> &str { "math.add" }
        fn description(&self) -> &str { "add two ints" }
        fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
            Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("a", ParamType::Integer))
        }
        fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
        async fn execute(&self, _: &serde_json::Value, _: &ToolContext) -> crate::error::ToolResult<serde_json::Value> { Ok(serde_json::json!({})) }
    }
```

```rust
//! Permissions — the gate the executor consults before running any tool.
//!
//! This mirrors the RomaCode server's model, and like the server gate it is
//! **fully open by default**: the default policy carries no rules and every
//! tool call is `Allow` — nothing is denied, nothing asks. The rule machinery
//! (deny → ask → allow → default evaluation order) is kept so an embedder who
//! *wants* restrictions can still opt in by building a non-default
//! [`PermissionPolicy`]; the executor itself never prompts a human — `Ask` is
//! surfaced as a decision the caller must handle before calling `run` with
//! `approved = true`.

use crate::tool::Tool;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// The three possible decisions for a tool call.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Permission {
    Allow,
    Ask,
    Deny,
}

/// A single rule: a glob pattern matched against the tool name, bound to a
/// decision. `math.*` matches `math.add`; `*` matches everything.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PermissionRule {
    pub pattern: String,
    pub decision: Permission,
}

impl PermissionRule {
    pub fn new(pattern: impl Into<String>, decision: Permission) -> Self {
        Self {
            pattern: pattern.into(),
            decision,
        }
    }
    /// Glob match: `*` matches any run of chars; `?` matches one char.
    pub fn matches(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        glob_match(&self.pattern, name)
    }
}

fn glob_match(pat: &str, s: &str) -> bool {
    let p: Vec<char> = pat.chars().collect();
    let t: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    glob_inner(&p, 0, &t, 0)
}

fn glob_inner(p: &[char], mut pi: usize, t: &[char], mut ti: usize) -> bool {
    while pi < p.len() {
        match p[pi] {
            '*' => {
                // try to match the rest of the pattern at every position
                if pi == p.len() - 1 {
                    return true; // trailing * eats everything
                }
                for skip in ti..=t.len() {
                    if glob_inner(p, pi + 1, t, skip) {
                        return true;
                    }
                }
                return false;
            }
            '?' => {
                if ti >= t.len() {
                    return false;
                }
                pi += 1;
                ti += 1;
            }
            c => {
                if ti >= t.len() || t[ti] != c {
                    return false;
                }
                pi += 1;
                ti += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    ti == t.len()
}

/// The full permission policy. Evaluation order:
/// 1. explicit `deny` rules (first match wins)
/// 2. explicit `ask` rules
/// 3. explicit `allow` rules
/// 4. the `default` (per-class, falling back to a global default)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PermissionPolicy {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub deny: Vec<PermissionRule>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub ask: Vec<PermissionRule>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub allow: Vec<PermissionRule>,
    /// The global default when no rule matches.
    #[serde(default = "default_default")]
    pub default: Permission,
}

fn default_default() -> Permission {
    Permission::Allow
}

impl Default for PermissionPolicy {
    fn default() -> Self {
        // Fully open, matching the server-side gate: no rules, every tool
        // allowed. Restrictive policies are opt-in (see the builder helpers
        // below); they are never the shipped default.
        Self {
            deny: vec![],
            ask: vec![],
            allow: vec![],
            default: Permission::Allow,
        }
    }
}

impl PermissionPolicy {
    /// Decide the permission for a given tool.
    pub fn decide(&self, tool: &dyn Tool) -> Permission {
        let name = tool.name();
        // deny first
        for r in &self.deny {
            if r.matches(name) {
                return r.decision;
            }
        }
        for r in &self.ask {
            if r.matches(name) {
                return r.decision;
            }
        }
        for r in &self.allow {
            if r.matches(name) {
                return r.decision;
            }
        }
        self.default
    }

    /// Builder helpers.
    pub fn deny(mut self, pattern: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.deny.push(PermissionRule::new(pattern, Permission::Deny));
        self
    }
    pub fn ask(mut self, pattern: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.ask.push(PermissionRule::new(pattern, Permission::Ask));
        self
    }
    pub fn allow(mut self, pattern: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.allow.push(PermissionRule::new(pattern, Permission::Allow));
        self
    }
    pub fn with_default(mut self, d: Permission) -> Self {
        self.default = d;
        self
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn glob() {
        assert!(glob_match("math.*", "math.add"));
        assert!(glob_match("math.*", "math.deep.nested"));
        assert!(!glob_match("math.*", "text.upper"));
        assert!(glob_match("*", "anything.at.all"));
        assert!(glob_match("a?c", "abc"));
        assert!(!glob_match("a?c", "ac"));
    }

    /// The shipped default is fully open: no rules, everything allowed —
    /// including the system.* tools that older defaults hard-denied.
    #[test]
    fn default_policy_is_fully_open() {
        let p = PermissionPolicy::default();
        struct T(&'static str);
        #[async_trait::async_trait]
        impl crate::tool::Tool for T {
            fn name(&self) -> &str { self.0 }
            fn description(&self) -> &str { "" }
            fn schema(&self) -> crate::schema::Schema { crate::schema::Schema::new() }
            fn source(&self) -> crate::tool::ToolSourceKind { crate::tool::ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
            async fn execute(&self, _: &serde_json::Value, _: &crate::tool::ToolContext) -> crate::error::ToolResult<serde_json::Value> { Ok(serde_json::json!({})) }
        }
        for name in ["math.add", "text.echo", "system.shell", "fs.write", "net.fetch", "anything.at.all"] {
            assert_eq!(p.decide(&T(name)), Permission::Allow, "{name} must be allowed by the default policy");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn deny_wins_over_allow() {
        // Rule-precedence test with an explicit opt-in policy (the shipped
        // default carries no rules at all).
        let p = PermissionPolicy::default()
            .allow("dangerous.*")
            .deny("dangerous.rm")
            .with_default(Permission::Ask);
        // We need a tool to decide against; build a tiny stub.
        struct T(&'static str);
        #[async_trait::async_trait]
        impl crate::tool::Tool for T {
            fn name(&self) -> &str { self.0 }
            fn description(&self) -> &str { "" }
            fn schema(&self) -> crate::schema::Schema { crate::schema::Schema::new() }
            fn source(&self) -> crate::tool::ToolSourceKind { crate::tool::ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
            async fn execute(&self, _: &serde_json::Value, _: &crate::tool::ToolContext) -> crate::error::ToolResult<serde_json::Value> { Ok(serde_json::json!({})) }
        }
        assert_eq!(p.decide(&T("dangerous.rm")), Permission::Deny); // deny rule wins
        assert_eq!(p.decide(&T("dangerous.other")), Permission::Allow); // allow rule
        assert_eq!(p.decide(&T("math.add")), Permission::Ask); // no rule → explicit Ask default
        assert_eq!(p.decide(&T("web.fetch")), Permission::Ask);
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-core/src/registry.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-core/src/registry.rs)

```rust
//! The in-memory tool [`Registry`] — a thread-safe store of every loaded
//! tool, indexed by name. The registry is the spine of the framework: sources
//! feed it, the executor reads it, composition reads it to resolve steps, and
//! the CLI lists it.

use crate::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use crate::tool::ToolArc;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::RwLock;

/// A thread-safe registry of tools. Cheap to clone (it is `Arc`-backed).
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Registry {
    inner: std::sync::Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, ToolArc>>>,
}

/// A read-only snapshot of one registered tool's identity.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ToolInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub category: String,
    pub source: String,
    pub version: String,
}

impl Registry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            inner: std::sync::Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),
        }
    }

    /// Register a tool. If a tool with the same name exists, it is replaced
    /// (the new version wins — see the lifecycle manager for upgrade policy).
    /// Returns the previous tool if one was displaced.
    pub fn register(&self, tool: ToolArc) -> Option<ToolArc> {
        let mut w = self.inner.write().unwrap();
        w.insert(tool.name().to_string(), tool)
    }

    /// Register many tools at once (e.g. from a source's `tools()`).
    pub fn register_all(&self, tools: Vec<ToolArc>) {
        let mut w = self.inner.write().unwrap();
        for t in tools {
            w.insert(t.name().to_string(), t);
        }
    }

    /// Look up a tool by name.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> ToolResult<ToolArc> {
        self.inner
            .read()
            .unwrap()
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| ToolError::NotFound(name.to_string()))
    }

    /// Does a tool with this name exist?
    pub fn contains(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.inner.read().unwrap().contains_key(name)
    }

    /// Remove a tool (retire it). Returns the removed tool if present.
    pub fn remove(&self, name: &str) -> Option<ToolArc> {
        self.inner.write().unwrap().remove(name)
    }

    /// Number of registered tools.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.inner.read().unwrap().len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.inner.read().unwrap().is_empty()
    }

    /// A sorted snapshot of every tool's identity (for `rc list`).
    pub fn list(&self) -> Vec<ToolInfo> {
        let r = self.inner.read().unwrap();
        let mut out: Vec<ToolInfo> = r
            .values()
            .map(|t| ToolInfo {
                name: t.name().to_string(),
                description: t.description().to_string(),
                category: t.category().to_string(),
                source: t.source().as_str().to_string(),
                version: t.version().to_string(),
            })
            .collect();
        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
        out
    }

    /// All registered tool names, sorted.
    pub fn names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut n: Vec<String> = self.inner.read().unwrap().keys().cloned().collect();
        n.sort();
        n
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Sandbox — the resource limits the executor enforces around every tool
//! call: a wall-clock timeout, an output-size cap, and network/filesystem
//! allow-lists that tools *should* consult before doing I/O.
//!
//! The shipped default is **fully open** (network allowed, whole filesystem,
//! like the server gate). [`Sandbox::strict`] remains available as an opt-in
//! lockdown for embedders who want one.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Resource limits for one execution.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Sandbox {
    /// Hard wall-clock budget, in milliseconds. `0` = no limit.
    #[serde(default = "default_timeout_ms")]
    pub timeout_ms: u64,

    /// Maximum bytes of output the tool may return. `0` = no limit. Tools
    /// that produce large outputs should truncate and note the truncation.
    #[serde(default = "default_max_output")]
    pub max_output_bytes: usize,

    /// Whether outbound network is permitted in this sandbox.
    #[serde(default = "default_allow_net")]
    pub allow_net: bool,

    /// Filesystem roots the tool may read/write. Defaults to the whole
    /// filesystem (`/`); an explicitly empty list disables FS access for
    /// tools that consult this list.
    #[serde(default = "default_fs_paths")]
    pub allow_fs_paths: Vec<String>,

    /// Maximum bytes the tool may read from a single file.
    #[serde(default = "default_max_read")]
    pub max_read_bytes: usize,
}

fn default_timeout_ms() -> u64 {
    30_000
}
fn default_max_output() -> usize {
    1_000_000
}
fn default_allow_net() -> bool {
    true
}
fn default_max_read() -> usize {
    10_000_000
}

/// The whole filesystem. `check_path` treats a root of `/` as "everything".
fn default_fs_paths() -> Vec<String> {
    vec!["/".to_string()]
}

impl Default for Sandbox {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            timeout_ms: default_timeout_ms(),
            max_output_bytes: default_max_output(),
            allow_net: default_allow_net(),
            allow_fs_paths: default_fs_paths(),
            max_read_bytes: default_max_read(),
        }
    }
}

impl Sandbox {
    /// A locked-down sandbox: no net, no fs, short timeout. Good default for
    /// untrusted/composed tools.
    pub fn strict() -> Self {
        Self {
            timeout_ms: 5_000,
            max_output_bytes: 100_000,
            allow_net: false,
            allow_fs_paths: Vec::new(),
            max_read_bytes: 100_000,
        }
    }

    /// Check that a network operation is permitted.
    pub fn check_net(&self) -> Result<(), crate::error::ToolError> {
        if self.allow_net {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(crate::error::ToolError::Sandbox(
                "network access is disabled in this sandbox".to_string(),
            ))
        }
    }

    /// Check that a path is under one of the allowed FS roots.
    ///
    /// Containment is proven, not guessed: the path is resolved via
    /// `canonicalize` when it exists (catching symlink escapes), and for
    /// not-yet-existing paths it is normalized *lexically* (`.` dropped,
    /// `..` resolved) before a component-wise prefix check against the
    /// canonical root. Anything that cannot be proven inside the sandbox is
    /// rejected — the function fails closed.
    pub fn check_path(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(), crate::error::ToolError> {
        if self.allow_fs_paths.is_empty() {
            return Err(crate::error::ToolError::Sandbox(
                "filesystem access is disabled in this sandbox".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        path_inside_roots(path, &self.allow_fs_paths)
    }

    /// Enforce the output-size cap. Truncates a returned string and appends a
    /// marker; returns an error if the value serializes above the limit and
    /// cannot be sensibly truncated.
    pub fn clamp_output(&self, value: &mut serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), crate::error::ToolError> {
        if self.max_output_bytes == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let s = serde_json::to_string(value).unwrap_or_default();
        if s.len() <= self.max_output_bytes {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // Try to truncate a string value in place.
        if let Some(str_val) = value.as_str() {
            let max = self.max_output_bytes.saturating_sub(40);
            if max > 0 && str_val.len() > max {
                let head: String = str_val.chars().take(max).collect();
                *value = serde_json::Value::String(format!(
                    "{}… [truncated: output exceeded {} bytes]",
                    head, self.max_output_bytes
                ));
                return Ok(());
            }
        }
        Err(crate::error::ToolError::OutputTooLarge {
            limit: self.max_output_bytes,
        })
    }
}

/// Split a path into its non-empty components (no `.`/`..` resolution).
fn components_of(p: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    p.split('/').filter(|c| !c.is_empty() && *c != ".").map(String::from).collect()
}

/// Normalize a path lexically: split on `/`, drop `.` and empty components,
/// and resolve `..` by popping. Fails closed if the path climbs above its
/// root (`/..`, `a/../..`) — such a path can never be proven to stay inside
/// a sandbox root.
fn lexical_components(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, crate::error::ToolError> {
    let mut comps: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for part in path.split('/') {
        match part {
            "" | "." => {}
            ".." => {
                if comps.pop().is_none() {
                    return Err(crate::error::ToolError::Sandbox(format!(
                        "path `{path}` escapes above its root — not provably inside the sandbox"
                    )));
                }
            }
            other => comps.push(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    Ok(comps)
}

/// Containment check shared by [`Sandbox::check_path`] and
/// [`ToolContext::check_path`](crate::tool::ToolContext::check_path):
/// `path` must be provably inside one of the canonical `roots`.
///
/// For paths that exist, `canonicalize` resolves symlinks first (so a
/// symlink inside an allowed root pointing outside is caught). For
/// not-yet-existing paths, lexical normalization is used instead — the
/// insecure fallback of a raw string prefix check is gone. Fails closed:
/// anything not provably inside is an error.
pub fn path_inside_roots(path: &str, roots: &[String]) -> Result<(), crate::error::ToolError> {
    let path_comps = match std::path::Path::new(path).canonicalize() {
        Ok(p) => components_of(&p.to_string_lossy()),
        // Not-yet-existing (or unreadable) path: normalize lexically and
        // fail closed on any `..` that climbs above the root.
        Err(_) => lexical_components(path)?,
    };
    for root in roots {
        let root_str = std::path::Path::new(root)
            .canonicalize()
            .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| root.clone());
        // A root of "/" (zero components) means the whole filesystem.
        let root_comps = if root_str == "/" {
            Vec::new()
        } else {
            lexical_components(&root_str)?
        };
        if path_comps.len() >= root_comps.len()
            && path_comps[..root_comps.len()] == root_comps[..]
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
    Err(crate::error::ToolError::Sandbox(format!(
        "path `{path}` is outside the allowed filesystem roots"
    )))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn strict_blocks_net_and_fs() {
        let s = Sandbox::strict();
        assert!(s.check_net().is_err());
        assert!(s.check_path("/etc/passwd").is_err());
    }

    /// The shipped default sandbox is fully open: network allowed and the
    /// whole filesystem reachable. Empty FS roots remain available to
    /// embedders who construct one explicitly.
    #[test]
    fn default_sandbox_is_fully_open() {
        let s = Sandbox::default();
        assert!(s.allow_net);
        assert!(s.check_net().is_ok());
        assert!(s.check_path("/etc/passwd").is_ok());
        assert!(s.check_path("/home/z/project/src/main.rs").is_ok());
        // An explicitly empty list still means "no FS access".
        let locked = Sandbox { allow_fs_paths: Vec::new(), ..Sandbox::default() };
        assert!(locked.check_path("/tmp/x").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn clamp_truncates_strings() {
        let s = Sandbox {
            max_output_bytes: 60,
            ..Sandbox::strict()
        };
        let mut v = serde_json::json!("x".repeat(500));
        assert!(s.clamp_output(&mut v).is_ok());
        let truncated = v.as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(truncated.contains("[truncated"));
    }

    /// A sandbox whose FS root is a fresh temp dir.
    fn rooted_sandbox() -> (Sandbox, std::path::PathBuf, std::path::PathBuf) {
        let base = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "rc-sbx-{}-{:?}",
            std::process::id(),
            std::thread::current().id()
        ));
        let root = base.join("allowed");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
        let s = Sandbox {
            allow_fs_paths: vec![root.to_string_lossy().to_string()],
            ..Sandbox::default()
        };
        (s, base, root)
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_dotdot_escapes() {
        let (s, base, root) = rooted_sandbox();
        // The M21 attack: a relative path that escapes through `..` — with
        // the old raw-prefix fallback this passed for not-yet-existing paths.
        assert!(s.check_path("allowed/../../etc/cron.d/x").is_err());
        // Absolute escape through more `..` than there are components.
        let esc = root.join("sub/../../../etc/cron.d/x");
        assert!(s.check_path(esc.to_str().unwrap()).is_err());
        // `/..` climbs above the filesystem root.
        assert!(s.check_path("/..").is_err());
        // Plain outside path still rejected.
        assert!(s.check_path("/etc/passwd").is_err());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn not_yet_existing_path_inside_root_is_allowed() {
        let (s, base, root) = rooted_sandbox();
        // A file that does not exist yet, but provably inside the root.
        let inside = root.join("newdir/deep/file.txt");
        assert!(s.check_path(inside.to_str().unwrap()).is_ok());
        // `..` that stays inside resolves fine.
        let inside2 = root.join("a/../b/c.txt");
        assert!(s.check_path(inside2.to_str().unwrap()).is_ok());
        // Existing file inside the root still passes via canonicalize.
        let f = root.join("real.txt");
        std::fs::write(&f, "hi").unwrap();
        assert!(s.check_path(f.to_str().unwrap()).is_ok());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base).ok();
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn symlink_escape_is_rejected() {
        let (s, base, root) = rooted_sandbox();
        let outside = base.join("outside");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&outside).unwrap();
        let link = root.join("leak");
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&outside, &link).unwrap();
        // Existing path via the symlink canonicalizes outside → rejected.
        assert!(s.check_path(link.to_str().unwrap()).is_err());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base).ok();
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Tool input schemas — a small, strong-typed subset of JSON Schema.
//!
//! A [`Schema`] is the contract a tool publishes about its input: the
//! parameters it accepts, their types, whether they are required, and their
//! defaults. The [`Validator`](crate::validator::Validator) checks a JSON
//! value against a schema before the tool ever runs.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// The parameter types a schema can express. Arrays carry an inner type so
/// `["a", "b"]` validates as `Array(String)`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum ParamType {
    String,
    Integer,
    Number,
    Boolean,
    Array(Box<ParamType>),
    Object,
    Any,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ParamType {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            ParamType::String => write!(f, "string"),
            ParamType::Integer => write!(f, "integer"),
            ParamType::Number => write!(f, "number"),
            ParamType::Boolean => write!(f, "boolean"),
            ParamType::Object => write!(f, "object"),
            ParamType::Array(inner) => write!(f, "array<{}>", inner),
            ParamType::Any => write!(f, "any"),
        }
    }
}

impl ParamType {
    /// Check a JSON value against this type. Returns `Ok(())` if it matches.
    pub fn check(&self, v: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), String> {
        let ok = match (self, v) {
            (ParamType::Any, _) => true,
            (ParamType::String, serde_json::Value::String(_)) => true,
            (ParamType::Integer, serde_json::Value::Number(n)) => n.is_i64() || n.is_u64(),
            (ParamType::Number, serde_json::Value::Number(_)) => true,
            (ParamType::Boolean, serde_json::Value::Bool(_)) => true,
            (ParamType::Object, serde_json::Value::Object(_)) => true,
            (ParamType::Array(inner), serde_json::Value::Array(items)) => {
                for item in items {
                    inner.check(item).map_err(|e| format!("array element: {e}"))?;
                }
                true
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        if ok {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(format!("expected {}, got {}", self, type_name(v)))
        }
    }
}

fn type_name(v: &serde_json::Value) -> &'static str {
    match v {
        serde_json::Value::Null => "null",
        serde_json::Value::Bool(_) => "boolean",
        serde_json::Value::Number(_) => "number",
        serde_json::Value::String(_) => "string",
        serde_json::Value::Array(_) => "array",
        serde_json::Value::Object(_) => "object",
    }
}

/// One parameter of a tool's input schema.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Parameter {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub typ: ParamType,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub required: bool,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub default: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub enum_values: Vec<serde_json::Value>,
}

impl Parameter {
    /// Build a required parameter shorthand.
    pub fn required(name: &str, typ: ParamType) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            description: String::new(),
            typ,
            required: true,
            default: None,
            enum_values: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
    /// Build an optional parameter shorthand.
    pub fn optional(name: &str, typ: ParamType) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            description: String::new(),
            typ,
            required: false,
            default: None,
            enum_values: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
    pub fn with_desc(mut self, d: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.description = d.into();
        self
    }
    pub fn with_default(mut self, v: serde_json::Value) -> Self {
        self.default = Some(v);
        self
    }
    pub fn with_enum(mut self, vs: Vec<serde_json::Value>) -> Self {
        self.enum_values = vs;
        self
    }
}

/// The full input schema of a tool: an ordered list of named parameters.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct Schema {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub parameters: Vec<Parameter>,
}

impl Schema {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
    pub fn param(mut self, p: Parameter) -> Self {
        self.parameters.push(p);
        self
    }
    /// Render the schema as a JSON-Schema-ish object for OpenAI/Anthropic tool
    /// definitions: `{ "type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...] }`.
    pub fn to_json_schema(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
        let mut props = serde_json::Map::new();
        let mut required = Vec::new();
        for p in &self.parameters {
            let t = match &p.typ {
                ParamType::String => serde_json::json!("string"),
                ParamType::Integer => serde_json::json!("integer"),
                ParamType::Number => serde_json::json!("number"),
                ParamType::Boolean => serde_json::json!("boolean"),
                ParamType::Object => serde_json::json!("object"),
                ParamType::Array(_) => serde_json::json!({ "type": "array" }),
                ParamType::Any => serde_json::json!({}),
            };
            let mut entry = serde_json::Map::new();
            if let serde_json::Value::String(_) = t {
                entry.insert("type".into(), t);
            } else if let serde_json::Value::Object(_) = &t {
                // array case: insert the type object directly
                if let Some(obj) = t.as_object() {
                    for (k, v) in obj {
                        entry.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
                    }
                }
            }
            if !p.description.is_empty() {
                entry.insert("description".into(), serde_json::Value::String(p.description.clone()));
            }
            if !p.enum_values.is_empty() {
                entry.insert("enum".into(), serde_json::Value::Array(p.enum_values.clone()));
            }
            if let Some(d) = &p.default {
                entry.insert("default".into(), d.clone());
            }
            props.insert(p.name.clone(), serde_json::Value::Object(entry));
            if p.required {
                required.push(serde_json::Value::String(p.name.clone()));
            }
        }
        serde_json::json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": serde_json::Value::Object(props),
            "required": serde_json::Value::Array(required),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn type_check_basic() {
        assert!(ParamType::String.check(&serde_json::json!("hi")).is_ok());
        assert!(ParamType::Integer.check(&serde_json::json!(42)).is_ok());
        assert!(ParamType::Number.check(&serde_json::json!(42)).is_ok());
        assert!(ParamType::Number.check(&serde_json::json!(3.14)).is_ok());
        assert!(ParamType::Integer.check(&serde_json::json!(3.14)).is_err());
        assert!(ParamType::Boolean.check(&serde_json::json!(true)).is_ok());
        assert!(ParamType::Array(Box::new(ParamType::String))
            .check(&serde_json::json!(["a", "b"]))
            .is_ok());
        assert!(ParamType::Array(Box::new(ParamType::Integer))
            .check(&serde_json::json!(["a"]))
            .is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn json_schema_shape() {
        let s = Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::required("n", ParamType::Integer).with_desc("count"))
            .param(Parameter::optional("greeting", ParamType::String).with_default(serde_json::json!("hi")));
        let j = s.to_json_schema();
        assert_eq!(j["type"], "object");
        assert_eq!(j["required"][0], "n");
        assert_eq!(j["properties"]["n"]["type"], "integer");
        assert_eq!(j["properties"]["greeting"]["default"], "hi");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The `Tool` trait — the single contract every tool implements, whether it
//! is built-in, declared, LLM-generated, imported from OpenAPI/MCP/REST/CLI,
//! or composed from other tools.

use crate::error::ToolResult;
use crate::schema::Schema;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// Which of the 8 universal tool-source mechanisms produced this tool. This is
/// metadata only — once loaded, every tool is just a `Tool`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ToolSourceKind {
    /// Shipped with the framework (`builtin`).
    Builtin,
    /// Built from a YAML/JSON declaration (`declarative`).
    Declarative,
    /// Generated by an LLM from a natural-language description (`llm_gen`).
    LlmGenerated,
    /// Imported from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec (`openapi`).
    OpenApi,
    /// Bridged from an MCP server (`mcp`).
    Mcp,
    /// A REST endpoint wrapped as a tool (`rest`).
    Rest,
    /// A GraphQL query wrapped as a tool (`graphql`).
    GraphQL,
    /// A CLI binary wrapped as a tool (`cli`).
    Cli,
    /// Composed from other tools — pipeline/parallel/branch/loop/dag
    /// (`compose`). The inner `&'static str` names the composition kind.
    Compose(&'static str),
    /// Pulled from a marketplace or URL (`marketplace`).
    Marketplace,
}

impl Default for ToolSourceKind {
    fn default() -> Self {
        ToolSourceKind::Builtin
    }
}

impl ToolSourceKind {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Builtin => "builtin",
            Self::Declarative => "declarative",
            Self::LlmGenerated => "llm_gen",
            Self::OpenApi => "openapi",
            Self::Mcp => "mcp",
            Self::Rest => "rest",
            Self::GraphQL => "graphql",
            Self::Cli => "cli",
            Self::Compose(_) => "compose",
            Self::Marketplace => "marketplace",
        }
    }
}

/// Per-call execution context: the sandbox in force, a correlation id, and a
/// cancellation flag. Tools that fan out (composition) pass a child context
/// derived from this one — the child shares the parent's *live* cancellation
/// flag (an `Arc<AtomicBool>`), so spawned steps observe a timeout or cancel
/// mid-flight instead of running to completion detached. The Executor
/// populates `allow_net` / `allow_fs_paths` from its
/// [`Sandbox`](crate::sandbox::Sandbox) so tools can self-check I/O policy.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ToolContext {
    /// A unique id for this invocation, for tracing/monitoring.
    pub correlation_id: String,
    /// Hard wall-clock budget for this single call, in ms. `0` = no limit
    /// (the executor still applies the sandbox timeout).
    pub timeout_ms: u64,
    /// Set to true by a parent to cancel a long-running tool. This is the
    /// spawn-time snapshot; see [`ToolContext::is_cancelled`].
    pub cancelled: bool,
    /// The live, shared cancellation flag. The executor flips this when the
    /// sandbox timeout fires, and composition tools pass clones down to
    /// spawned steps so cancellation propagates. Check it with
    /// [`ToolContext::is_cancelled`].
    pub cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    /// Whether outbound network is permitted in this call.
    pub allow_net: bool,
    /// Filesystem roots the tool may touch. Defaults to the whole
    /// filesystem; an explicitly empty list disables FS access.
    pub allow_fs_paths: Vec<String>,
}

impl Default for ToolContext {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            correlation_id: "default".to_string(),
            timeout_ms: 0,
            cancelled: false,
            cancel: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
            allow_net: true,
            allow_fs_paths: vec!["/".to_string()],
        }
    }
}

impl ToolContext {
    pub fn new(correlation_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            correlation_id: correlation_id.into(),
            timeout_ms: 0,
            cancelled: false,
            cancel: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
            allow_net: true,
            allow_fs_paths: vec!["/".to_string()],
        }
    }
    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, ms: u64) -> Self {
        self.timeout_ms = ms;
        self
    }
    /// Has this call been cancelled — either the spawn-time snapshot
    /// (`cancelled`) or the live shared flag (`cancel`)? Tools should check
    /// this (not the `cancelled` field) so they observe cancellation that
    /// arrives after they started.
    pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool {
        self.cancelled || self.cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
    /// Mark this call tree as cancelled: every holder of a clone of the
    /// shared flag observes it.
    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.cancel.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
    /// Check that network is permitted.
    pub fn check_net(&self) -> Result<(), crate::error::ToolError> {
        if self.allow_net {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(crate::error::ToolError::Sandbox(
                "network access is disabled in this context".to_string(),
            ))
        }
    }
    /// Check that `path` is under one of the allowed FS roots (no FS access
    /// when the allow-list is empty). Delegates to
    /// [`path_inside_roots`](crate::sandbox::path_inside_roots), which
    /// normalizes `..`/`.` lexically and fails closed.
    pub fn check_path(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(), crate::error::ToolError> {
        if self.allow_fs_paths.is_empty() {
            return Err(crate::error::ToolError::Sandbox(
                "filesystem access is disabled in this context".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        crate::sandbox::path_inside_roots(path, &self.allow_fs_paths)
    }
}

/// The single trait every tool implements. `execute` is async so tools that
/// do network I/O (REST, web fetch, MCP) can run without blocking the
/// executor's runtime.
#[async_trait]
pub trait Tool: Send + Sync {
    /// Stable, unique, dot-namespaced id, e.g. `math.add`, `web.fetch`,
    /// `compose.pipeline.myflow`. This is the key the registry indexes by.
    fn name(&self) -> &str;

    /// Human-readable summary; shown in `rc list` and `rc info`.
    fn description(&self) -> &str;

    /// The input schema. The validator runs against this before `execute`.
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema;

    /// Which source produced this tool.
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind;

    /// A category label for grouping (`math`, `web`, `compose`, …). Default
    /// is derived from the name's first segment when not overridden.
    fn category(&self) -> &str {
        // default: first segment of a dot-namespaced name, else "misc"
        self.name().split('.').next().unwrap_or("misc")
    }

    /// The tool's semver version (default `0.1.0`). The lifecycle manager uses
    /// this for upgrade/retire decisions.
    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        "0.1.0"
    }

    /// Run the tool. `input` is a JSON object matching `schema()`. The
    /// executor has already validated it and applied the sandbox.
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value>;
}

/// A boxed, shareable tool handle — `Arc<dyn Tool>` is the currency of the
/// registry and the composition layer.
pub type ToolArc = std::sync::Arc<dyn Tool>;

/// Helper: build a [`ToolArc`] from any `Tool`.
pub fn arc<T: Tool + 'static>(t: T) -> ToolArc {
    std::sync::Arc::new(t)
}
```

```rust
//! Input validation: check a JSON object against a tool's [`Schema`] before
//! the tool runs. The validator also fills in defaults for missing optional
//! parameters, so a tool's `execute` always sees a complete input.

use crate::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use crate::schema::Schema;
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

/// Validate `input` against `schema`. On success, returns a new JSON object
/// with defaults applied for any missing optional parameters.
pub fn validate(schema: &Schema, input: &Value) -> ToolResult<Value> {
    let obj = input.as_object().ok_or_else(|| {
        ToolError::Validation("input must be a JSON object".to_string())
    })?;

    let mut out = Map::new();

    // Copy through any caller-supplied values first (after type-checking).
    for (k, v) in obj {
        out.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
    }

    for p in &schema.parameters {
        match out.get(&p.name) {
            // Present — type-check it.
            Some(v) => {
                if let Err(detail) = p.typ.check(v) {
                    return Err(ToolError::BadParam {
                        name: p.name.clone(),
                        expected: p.typ.clone(),
                        detail,
                    });
                }
                // enum constraint, if any
                if !p.enum_values.is_empty()
                    && !p.enum_values.iter().any(|e| e == v)
                {
                    return Err(ToolError::BadParam {
                        name: p.name.clone(),
                        expected: p.typ.clone(),
                        detail: format!(
                            "value {} is not one of the allowed values",
                            v
                        ),
                    });
                }
            }
            // Absent — required? error. Optional? apply default or skip.
            None => {
                if p.required {
                    return Err(ToolError::Validation(format!(
                        "missing required parameter `{}`",
                        p.name
                    )));
                } else if let Some(d) = &p.default {
                    out.insert(p.name.clone(), d.clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(Value::Object(out))
}

/// Public facade matching the docs (`Validator::validate`).
pub struct Validator;
impl Validator {
    pub fn validate(schema: &Schema, input: &Value) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        validate(schema, input)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::schema::{ParamType, Parameter};

    #[test]
    fn fills_defaults_and_type_checks() {
        let s = Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::required("n", ParamType::Integer))
            .param(
                Parameter::optional("label", ParamType::String)
                    .with_default(serde_json::json!("hi")),
            );
        let v = validate(&s, &serde_json::json!({ "n": 5 })).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["n"], 5);
        assert_eq!(v["label"], "hi"); // default applied
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_bad_type() {
        let s = Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("n", ParamType::Integer));
        let err = validate(&s, &serde_json::json!({ "n": "five" }));
        assert!(err.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_missing_required() {
        let s = Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("n", ParamType::Integer));
        let err = validate(&s, &serde_json::json!({}));
        assert!(err.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn enforces_enum() {
        let s = Schema::new().param(
            Parameter::required("mode", ParamType::String)
                .with_enum(vec![serde_json::json!("a"), serde_json::json!("b")]),
        );
        assert!(validate(&s, &serde_json::json!({ "mode": "a" })).is_ok());
        assert!(validate(&s, &serde_json::json!({ "mode": "z" })).is_err());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! # rc-lifecycle — L3: the full tool lifecycle
//!
//! The [`Lifecycle`] manager ties the other layers together:
//!
//! 1. **discover** — walk every registered [`ToolSource`](rc_sources::ToolSource),
//!    collect the tools each produces.
//! 2. **register** — insert them into the [`Registry`].
//! 3. **validate** — check every tool's schema for duplicates / empty names.
//! 4. **load** — sources load eagerly (tools are ready-to-register on
//!    `discover`).
//! 5. **execute** — run a tool by name through the [`Executor`], timing the
//!    call and recording metrics.
//! 6. **monitor** — per-tool call/success/failure counts + latency, via
//!    [`MetricsStore`].
//! 7. **version** — a version report of every registered tool.
//! 8. **retire** — remove a tool from the registry.
//!
//! [`Lifecycle::permissive`] is a one-liner for examples/tests.

pub mod lifecycle;
pub mod monitor;

pub use lifecycle::Lifecycle;
pub use monitor::{MetricsStore, ToolMetrics};
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-lifecycle/src/lifecycle.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-lifecycle/src/lifecycle.rs)

```rust
//! The lifecycle manager — walks the sources, registers every tool, validates
//! them, executes calls (timing + recording metrics), and retires tools. This
//! is L3: discover → register → validate → load → execute → monitor → version
//! → retire.

use crate::monitor::{MetricsStore, ToolMetrics};
use rc_core::error::ToolResult;
use rc_core::executor::Executor;
use rc_core::permissions::PermissionPolicy;
use rc_core::registry::Registry;
use rc_core::sandbox::Sandbox;
use rc_core::tool::ToolArc;
use rc_sources::{SourceError, SourceRegistry};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::time::Instant;

pub struct Lifecycle {
    pub registry: Registry,
    pub executor: Executor,
    pub sources: SourceRegistry,
    pub metrics: MetricsStore,
    /// The policy in force (for `rc validate` and re-binding).
    pub policy: PermissionPolicy,
    /// The sandbox in force.
    pub sandbox: Sandbox,
}

impl Lifecycle {
    /// Build a lifecycle with the given policy + sandbox and an empty
    /// registry. Add sources with [`add_source`], then call [`discover`].
    pub fn new(policy: PermissionPolicy, sandbox: Sandbox) -> Self {
        let registry = Registry::new();
        let executor = Executor::new(
            registry.clone(),
            policy.clone(),
            sandbox.clone(),
        );
        Self {
            registry,
            executor,
            sources: SourceRegistry::new(),
            metrics: MetricsStore::new(),
            policy,
            sandbox,
        }
    }

    /// A fully-permissive lifecycle (allow everything, default sandbox) — handy
    /// for examples and tests.
    pub fn permissive() -> Self {
        Self::new(
            PermissionPolicy::default().with_default(rc_core::permissions::Permission::Allow),
            Sandbox::default(),
        )
    }

    /// Register a source. Its tools are loaded on the next [`discover`].
    pub fn add_source(&mut self, source: impl rc_sources::ToolSource + 'static) {
        self.sources.add(source);
    }

    /// Run every source's `tools()` and register the results. Returns the
    /// number of tools registered.
    pub async fn discover(&self) -> Result<usize, SourceError> {
        let tools = self.sources.all_tools().await?;
        let n = tools.len();
        self.registry.register_all(tools);
        Ok(n)
    }

    /// Register a single already-built tool (e.g. a composition) directly.
    pub fn register(&self, tool: ToolArc) {
        self.registry.register(tool);
    }

    /// Register many tools directly.
    pub fn register_all(&self, tools: Vec<ToolArc>) {
        self.registry.register_all(tools);
    }

    /// Validate every registered tool's schema: no duplicate parameter names,
    /// every parameter has a name. Returns a list of issue strings (empty =
    /// all good).
    pub fn validate_all(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut issues = Vec::new();
        for info in self.registry.list() {
            if info.name.is_empty() {
                issues.push(format!("tool with empty name"));
                continue;
            }
            if let Ok(tool) = self.registry.get(&info.name) {
                let schema = tool.schema();
                let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
                for p in &schema.parameters {
                    if p.name.is_empty() {
                        issues.push(format!("{}: parameter with empty name", info.name));
                    }
                    if !seen.insert(p.name.clone()) {
                        issues.push(format!("{}: duplicate parameter `{}`", info.name, p.name));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        issues
    }

    /// Execute a tool by name, timing the call and recording metrics. The
    /// `approved` flag signals the caller already obtained human approval for
    /// an `Ask` decision.
    pub async fn execute(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        input: &Value,
        approved: bool,
    ) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let result = self.executor.run(name, input, approved).await;
        let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_micros();
        match &result {
            Ok(_) => self.metrics.record(name, true, elapsed, None),
            Err(e) => self.metrics.record(name, false, elapsed, Some(e.to_string())),
        }
        result
    }

    /// Retire (remove) a tool from the registry. Returns true if it was
    /// present.
    pub fn retire(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.registry.remove(name).is_some()
    }

    /// Metrics for one tool.
    pub fn metrics_for(&self, name: &str) -> Option<ToolMetrics> {
        self.metrics.get(name)
    }

    /// Every tool's metrics, sorted by name.
    pub fn all_metrics(&self) -> Vec<(String, ToolMetrics)> {
        self.metrics.all()
    }

    /// A version report: every tool's name + version + source, sorted.
    pub fn version_report(&self) -> Vec<(String, String, String)> {
        let mut out: Vec<(String, String, String)> = self
            .registry
            .list()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|i| (i.name, i.version, i.source))
            .collect();
        out.sort();
        out
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_sources::builtin::BuiltinSource;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn discover_registers_builtins() {
        let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
        let n = life.discover().await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, rc_builtin::COUNT);
        assert!(life.registry.contains("math.add"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn execute_records_metrics() {
        let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
        life.discover().await.unwrap();
        let out = life
            .execute("math.add", &serde_json::json!({ "a": 2, "b": 3 }), false)
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!((out.as_f64().unwrap() - 5.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        let m = life.metrics_for("math.add").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.calls, 1);
        assert_eq!(m.successes, 1);
        assert!(m.avg_latency_us() >= 0.0);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn execute_records_failures() {
        let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
        life.discover().await.unwrap();
        // bad input: missing required param
        let err = life.execute("math.add", &serde_json::json!({ "a": 2 }), false).await;
        assert!(err.is_err());
        let m = life.metrics_for("math.add").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.calls, 1);
        assert_eq!(m.failures, 1);
        assert!(m.last_error.is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_all_passes_for_builtins() {
        let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
        // discover is async; block_on via current_thread runtime would need a
        // tokio test attribute. Instead register directly.
        life.register_all(rc_builtin::all_tools());
        let issues = life.validate_all();
        assert!(issues.is_empty(), "issues: {issues:?}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn retire_removes_a_tool() {
        let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
        life.discover().await.unwrap();
        assert!(life.registry.contains("text.upper"));
        assert!(life.retire("text.upper"));
        assert!(!life.registry.contains("text.upper"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn version_report_lists_tools() {
        let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource);
        life.discover().await.unwrap();
        let report = life.version_report();
        assert!(report.iter().any(|(n, _, _)| n == "math.add"));
        assert!(report.iter().all(|(_, _, s)| s == "builtin"));
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-lifecycle/src/monitor.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-lifecycle/src/monitor.rs)

```rust
//! Per-tool execution metrics, recorded by the lifecycle manager on every
//! call. Thread-safe (`Arc<RwLock<…>>`), cheap to clone.

use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct ToolMetrics {
    pub calls: u64,
    pub successes: u64,
    pub failures: u64,
    /// Cumulative latency in microseconds across all calls.
    pub total_latency_us: u128,
    /// The most recent failure message, if any.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
}

impl ToolMetrics {
    pub fn success_rate(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.calls == 0 {
            return 0.0;
        }
        self.successes as f64 / self.calls as f64
    }
    pub fn avg_latency_us(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.calls == 0 {
            return 0.0;
        }
        self.total_latency_us as f64 / self.calls as f64
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct MetricsStore {
    inner: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, ToolMetrics>>>,
}

impl MetricsStore {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Record one call's outcome. `latency_us` is the wall-clock cost.
    pub fn record(&self, name: &str, ok: bool, latency_us: u128, err: Option<String>) {
        let mut w = self.inner.write().unwrap();
        let m = w.entry(name.to_string()).or_default();
        m.calls += 1;
        m.total_latency_us += latency_us;
        if ok {
            m.successes += 1;
        } else {
            m.failures += 1;
            m.last_error = err;
        }
    }

    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<ToolMetrics> {
        self.inner.read().unwrap().get(name).cloned()
    }

    /// Every tool's metrics, sorted by name.
    pub fn all(&self) -> Vec<(String, ToolMetrics)> {
        let r = self.inner.read().unwrap();
        let mut out: Vec<(String, ToolMetrics)> =
            r.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone())).collect();
        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
        out
    }

    pub fn clear(&self) {
        self.inner.write().unwrap().clear();
    }
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/README.md`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/README.md)

````markdown
# rc-python

A full **Python** implementation of the RomaCode tools builder — a faithful
port of the Rust `rc-*` framework, plus a `python.*` language pack that
mirrors the Rust `rc-rust` pack.

## What's here

The same layer cake as the Rust workspace, in one stdlib-only package:

| layer | module | what it is |
|-------|--------|------------|
| core | `rc_python.core` | the `Tool` ABC, `ToolContext`, `ToolError`, `ToolSourceKind` |
| schema | `rc_python.schema` | `ParamType`, `Parameter`, `Schema` (+ JSON-Schema export) |
| registry | `rc_python.registry` | thread-safe `Registry` + `ToolInfo` |
| permissions | `rc_python.permissions` | `Permission`, `PermissionPolicy`, glob rules |
| sandbox | `rc_python.sandbox` | timeout / output-cap / net+fs allow-lists |
| validator | `rc_python.validator` | type-check + default-filling `validate()` |
| executor | `rc_python.executor` | the single run gate (policy → validate → sandbox → run) |
| manifest | `rc_python.manifest` | serialisable `Manifest` + `Catalog` |
| sources | `rc_python.sources` | `ToolSource` ABC + builtin/declarative/cli/rest + `ShellTool`/`HttpTool` |
| compose | `rc_python.compose` | `Pipeline` / `Parallel` / `Branch` + templating |
| lifecycle | `rc_python.lifecycle` | discover → register → validate → execute → monitor → retire |
| tools | `rc_python.tools` | the 7 `python.*` dev tools + `PythonSource` |

Runtime dependencies: **none** (stdlib only). Dev: `pytest`.

## Quick start

```python
import asyncio
from rc_python import Lifecycle, BuiltinSource, PythonSource

async def main():
    life = Lifecycle.permissive()
    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())      # the 14-tool builtin catalog
    life.add_source(PythonSource())       # the 7 python.* tools
    n = await life.discover()             # registers 21 tools
    print(f"loaded {n} tools")
    out = await life.execute("python.version", {}, True)
    print(out)                            # {'python': 'Python 3.12.x', 'exit_code': 0}
    print(await life.execute("math.add", {"a": 2, "b": 3}, False))  # 5.0

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Install (dev)

```sh
cd crates/rc-tools/rc-python
pip install -e .[dev]
pytest -q
```

Or run the tests with no install at all (the package is importable from the
source tree):

```sh
python3 -m pytest -q
```

## Parity with the Rust framework

| Rust (`rc-*`) | Python (`rc_python`) |
|---------------|----------------------|
| `rc_core::Tool` | `rc_python.core.Tool` |
| `rc_core::Registry` | `rc_python.registry.Registry` |
| `rc_core::Schema` / `ParamType` | `rc_python.schema.Schema` / `ParamType` |
| `rc_core::Executor` + `Sandbox` + `PermissionPolicy` | `rc_python.executor.Executor` + `sandbox.Sandbox` + `permissions.PermissionPolicy` |
| `rc_sources::{ToolSource, ShellTool, HttpTool}` | `rc_python.sources.{ToolSource, ShellTool, HttpTool}` |
| `rc_compose::{PipelineTool, ParallelTool, BranchTool}` | `rc_python.compose.{PipelineTool, ParallelTool, BranchTool}` |
| `rc_lifecycle::Lifecycle` + `MetricsStore` | `rc_python.lifecycle.Lifecycle` + `MetricsStore` |
| `rc_rust::{RustSource, all_tools}` | `rc_python.tools.{PythonSource, all_tools}` |

The only deliberate divergence: Python tool input/output is native Python
data (`dict` / `list` / `str` / …) rather than `serde_json::Value`, so there
is no separate JSON layer to bridge.
````

```python
"""rc_python — a full Python implementation of the RomaCode tools builder.

A faithful port of the Rust ``rc-*`` framework: the same layer cake
(core → schema → registry → permissions → sandbox → validator → executor →
manifest → sources → compose → lifecycle), the same ``Tool`` contract, the
same eight tool-source mechanisms, the same composition primitives — plus a
``python.*`` language pack mirroring the Rust ``rc-rust`` pack.

The framework is **stdlib-only** at runtime (no third-party dependencies);
``pytest`` is a dev convenience, not a runtime requirement.

Quick start::

    import asyncio
    from rc_python import Lifecycle, BuiltinSource, PythonSource

    async def main():
        life = Lifecycle.permissive()
        life.add_source(BuiltinSource())      # the 15-tool builtin catalog
        life.add_source(PythonSource())       # the 7 python.* tools
        n = await life.discover()             # registers 15 + 7 tools
        print(f"loaded {n} tools")
        out = await life.execute("python.version", {}, True)
        print(out)                            # {'python': 'Python 3.12.x', 'exit_code': 0}

    asyncio.run(main())
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# ── core layer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from .core import (
    VERSION,
    Tool,
    ToolArc,
    ToolContext,
    ToolError,
    ToolResult,
    ToolSourceKind,
    arc,
)
from .schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema
from .registry import Registry, ToolInfo
from .permissions import Permission, PermissionPolicy, PermissionRule, glob_match
from .sandbox import Sandbox
from .validator import Validator, validate
from .executor import Executor
from .manifest import Catalog, Manifest

# ── sources layer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from .sources import (
    BuiltinSource,
    CliSource,
    DeclarativeSource,
    HttpTool,
    RestSource,
    ShellTool,
    SourceError,
    SourceRegistry,
    ToolSource,
    builtin_all_tools,
    builtin_only,
)

# ── compose layer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from .compose import (
    BranchArm,
    BranchTool,
    ParallelStep,
    ParallelTool,
    PipelineStep,
    PipelineTool,
    lookup,
    resolve,
)

# ── lifecycle layer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from .lifecycle import Lifecycle, MetricsStore, ToolMetrics

# ── the Python language pack ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
from .tools import COUNT as PYTHON_COUNT, CATEGORY as PYTHON_CATEGORY, PythonSource, all_tools

__all__ = [
    # core
    "VERSION", "Tool", "ToolArc", "ToolContext", "ToolError", "ToolResult",
    "ToolSourceKind", "arc",
    # schema
    "ParamType", "Parameter", "Schema",
    # registry
    "Registry", "ToolInfo",
    # permissions
    "Permission", "PermissionPolicy", "PermissionRule", "glob_match",
    # sandbox / validator / executor / manifest
    "Sandbox", "Validator", "validate", "Executor", "Catalog", "Manifest",
    # sources
    "BuiltinSource", "CliSource", "DeclarativeSource", "HttpTool", "RestSource",
    "ShellTool", "SourceError", "SourceRegistry", "ToolSource",
    "builtin_all_tools", "builtin_only",
    # compose
    "BranchArm", "BranchTool", "ParallelStep", "ParallelTool",
    "PipelineStep", "PipelineTool", "lookup", "resolve",
    # lifecycle
    "Lifecycle", "MetricsStore", "ToolMetrics",
    # python pack
    "PythonSource", "all_tools", "PYTHON_COUNT", "PYTHON_CATEGORY",
]


def python_lifecycle() -> Lifecycle:
    """A convenience: a permissive :class:`Lifecycle` pre-loaded with the
    Python language pack **and** the builtin catalog. Add more sources
    (declarative, rest, …) on the returned lifecycle before calling
    :meth:`Lifecycle.discover`."""
    life = Lifecycle.permissive()
    life.add_source(PythonSource())
    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())
    return life
```

```python
"""rc_python.compose — L4 composition: new tools from old tools.

Four composition primitives, each producing a registered
:class:`~rc_python.core.Tool`:

| primitive | what it does |
|-----------|--------------|
| :class:`PipelineTool` | chain tools — each step's output feeds the next |
| :class:`ParallelTool` | fan out N tools concurrently, join as a dict |
| :class:`BranchTool`   | conditionally route to one of N tools (first match wins) |

Because every composition is itself a ``Tool``, compositions nest — a pipeline
step can be a branch, etc. Template references (``{{prev.x}}``,
``{{input.y}}``) are resolved by :mod:`rc_python.compose.templating`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from .branch import BranchArm, BranchTool
from .parallel import ParallelStep, ParallelTool
from .pipeline import PipelineStep, PipelineTool
from .templating import lookup, resolve, resolve_ref

__all__ = [
    "BranchArm",
    "BranchTool",
    "ParallelStep",
    "ParallelTool",
    "PipelineStep",
    "PipelineTool",

    "resolve_ref",
```
