## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/branch.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/branch.py)

```python
"""rc_python.compose.branch — conditionally route to one of N tools.

Arms are evaluated in order; the first whose ``when`` template resolves to a
truthy value wins. An arm with ``when = None`` is the catch-all (placed last).
The matched arm's tool runs against a template resolved from the input (or the
input directly when no template is given). Mirrors the Rust ``rc_compose::branch``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from ..core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolSourceKind
from ..executor import Executor
from ..schema import Schema
from .templating import resolve


@dataclass
class BranchArm:
    tool: str
    when: Optional[Any] = None  # None = catch-all (always matches)
    template: Optional[Any] = None


class BranchTool(Tool):
    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str,
        arms: list[BranchArm],
        executor: Executor,
    ) -> None:
        self._name = name
        self._desc = description
        self._arms = list(arms)
        self._executor = executor
        self._schema = Schema.new()

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Compose

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Any:
        for arm in self._arms:
            if arm.when is None:
                matched = arm
                break
            val = resolve(arm.when, None, input)
            if val:
                matched = arm
                break
        else:
            raise ToolError(
                f"branch `{self._name}`: no arm matched and no catch-all", kind="other"
            )
        step_input = (
            resolve(matched.template, None, input) if matched.template is not None else input
        )
        if not isinstance(step_input, dict):
            step_input = {"value": step_input}
        return await self._executor.run_inner(matched.tool, step_input)
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/parallel.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/parallel.py)

```python
"""rc_python.compose.parallel — fan out N tools concurrently, join as a dict.

Each step runs against a template resolved from the pipeline input (or the
input directly when no template is given), all steps run concurrently via
:meth:`asyncio.gather`, and the results are joined into a dict keyed by step
name. Mirrors the Rust ``rc_compose::parallel``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from ..core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind, ToolError
from ..executor import Executor
from ..schema import Schema
from .templating import resolve


@dataclass
class ParallelStep:
    name: str
    tool: str
    template: Optional[Any] = None


class ParallelTool(Tool):
    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str,
        steps: list[ParallelStep],
        executor: Executor,
    ) -> None:
        self._name = name
        self._desc = description
        self._steps = list(steps)
        self._executor = executor
        self._schema = Schema.new()

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Compose

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        async def _run(step: ParallelStep) -> Any:
            step_input = (
                resolve(step.template, None, input)
                if step.template is not None
                else input
            )
            if not isinstance(step_input, dict):
                step_input = {"value": step_input}
            return await self._executor.run_inner(step.tool, step_input)

        results = await asyncio.gather(*(_run(s) for s in self._steps))
        return {s.name: r for s, r in zip(self._steps, results)}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/pipeline.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/pipeline.py)

```python
"""rc_python.compose.pipeline — chain tools so each step's output feeds the next.

A step may take the previous output directly (no template) or take a template
that references ``{{prev}}`` / ``{{prev.x}}`` / ``{{input.y}}``. The pipeline
is itself a :class:`~rc_python.core.Tool`, so pipelines can be steps in other
pipelines. Mirrors the Rust ``rc_compose::pipeline``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from ..core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind
from ..executor import Executor
from ..schema import Schema
from .templating import resolve


@dataclass
class PipelineStep:
    """One step of a pipeline.

    ``template`` is optional: if ``None``, the step receives the previous
    step's output directly (the first step receives the pipeline input). If
    given, the template is resolved against ``prev`` + ``input``.
    """

    tool: str
    template: Optional[Any] = None


class PipelineTool(Tool):
    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str,
        steps: list[PipelineStep],
        executor: Executor,
    ) -> None:
        self._name = name
        self._desc = description
        self._steps = list(steps)
        self._executor = executor
        # a pipeline's own input schema is an empty object; each step's input
        # is shaped by its template. The first step receives the pipeline input
        # verbatim, so callers should pass a dict the first tool will accept.
        self._schema = Schema.new()

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Compose

    def category(self) -> str:
        # dot-namespaced: compose.pipeline.<name>
        return self._name.split(".", 1)[0] if "." in self._name else "compose"

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Any:
        prev: Any = input
        for i, step in enumerate(self._steps):
            step_input = (
                resolve(step.template, prev, input)
                if step.template is not None
                else prev
            )
            # The inner tool expects a dict; coerce a non-dict prev into
            # {"value": prev} so a pure-value pipeline still threads through.
            if not isinstance(step_input, dict):
                step_input = {"value": step_input}
            prev = await self._executor.run_inner(step.tool, step_input)
        return prev
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/templating.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/compose/templating.py)

```python
"""rc_python.compose.templating — template resolution shared by the composition primitives.

Handles ``{{prev}}``, ``{{prev.x}}``, ``{{input.y}}``, and ``{{nodes.NAME.z}}``
references, mirroring the Rust ``rc_compose::templating`` module. A reference
that cannot be resolved is left as-is (the caller will see the literal
``{{...}}``); a reference whose path does not exist resolves to ``None``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any, Dict

_PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+)\s*\}\}")


def lookup(value: Any, path: str) -> Any:
    """Walk a dotted path through ``value``. Returns ``None`` on any miss."""
    cur = value
    for part in path.split("."):
        if isinstance(cur, dict) and part in cur:
            cur = cur[part]
        elif isinstance(cur, list):
            try:
                cur = cur[int(part)]
            except (ValueError, IndexError):
                return None
        else:
            return None
    return cur


def resolve(tmpl: Any, prev: Any, input: Dict[str, Any], nodes: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> Any:
    """Resolve placeholders in ``tmpl``.

    Mirrors the Rust ``rc_compose::templating::resolve``:

    * a **whole-string** template ``"{{path}}"`` (no inner ``{`` and no spaces)
      is replaced by the referenced value **with its type preserved** — a
      number stays a number, a dict stays a dict. This is what lets a
      ``math.sqrt`` step receive ``{"n": "{{prev}}"}`` where ``prev`` is a
      float;
    * a template **embedded** in a larger string (``"count: {{prev}}"``) is
      string-substituted, and the result stays a string;
    * dicts and lists are recursed into, so templates can be structured.
    """
    nodes = nodes or {}
    if isinstance(tmpl, str):
        return _resolve_string(tmpl, prev, input, nodes)
    if isinstance(tmpl, dict):
        return {k: resolve(v, prev, input, nodes) for k, v in tmpl.items()}
    if isinstance(tmpl, list):
        return [resolve(v, prev, input, nodes) for v in tmpl]
    return tmpl


def _resolve_string(s: str, prev: Any, input: Dict[str, Any], nodes: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    # whole-string "{{path}}" → the looked-up value, type preserved
    inner = _whole_placeholder(s)
    if inner is not None:
        return resolve_ref(inner, prev, input, nodes)
    if "{{" in s:
        return _PLACEHOLDER.sub(
            lambda m: _render(resolve_ref(m.group(1), prev, input, nodes)), s
        )
    return s


def _whole_placeholder(s: str) -> "str | None":
    """If ``s`` is exactly ``{{path}}`` with no inner ``{`` and no spaces,
    return the trimmed inner path; otherwise None."""
    if not s.startswith("{{") or not s.endswith("}}"):
        return None
    inner = s[2:-2]
    if "{" in inner or " " in inner:
        return None
    return inner.strip()


def resolve_ref(ref: str, prev: Any, input: Dict[str, Any], nodes: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    head, _, rest = ref.partition(".")
    if head == "prev":
        return lookup(prev, rest) if rest else prev
    if head == "input":
        return lookup(input, rest) if rest else input
    if head == "nodes":
        return lookup(nodes, rest) if rest else nodes
    # unknown root → leave the literal placeholder value
    return None


def _render(v: Any) -> str:
    if v is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return v
    import json
    try:
        return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return str(v)
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/core.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/core.py)

```python
"""rc_python.core — the foundation of the RomaCode tools builder (Python port).

The single contract every tool implements (:class:`Tool`), the per-call
context (:class:`ToolContext`), the source-kind enum
(:class:`ToolSourceKind`), and the error type (:class:`ToolError`). Every
other module in the package builds on this one.

This is a faithful Python port of the Rust crate ``rc-core``: the same trait
shape (``name`` / ``description`` / ``schema`` / ``source`` / ``category`` /
``version`` / ``execute``), the same context fields, the same source kinds.
The only divergence is that Python tool input/output is native Python data
(``dict`` / ``list`` / ``str`` / ``int`` / ``float`` / ``bool`` / ``None``)
instead of ``serde_json::Value`` — there is no separate JSON layer to bridge.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple


class ToolSourceKind(Enum):
    """Which of the universal tool-source mechanisms produced a tool.

    Mirrors ``rc_core::tool::ToolSourceKind``. Once loaded, every tool is just
    a :class:`Tool` — the source is metadata, not a special case.
    """

    Builtin = "builtin"
    Declarative = "declarative"
    LlmGenerated = "llm_gen"
    OpenApi = "openapi"
    Mcp = "mcp"
    Rest = "rest"
    GraphQL = "graphql"
    Cli = "cli"
    Compose = "compose"
    Marketplace = "marketplace"

    @property
    def as_str(self) -> str:
        return self.value


class ToolError(Exception):
    """Every tool-execution failure flows through ``ToolError``.

    Carries a ``kind`` (one of ``not_found`` / ``validation`` / ``bad_param``
    / ``permission_denied`` / ``sandbox`` / ``timeout`` / ``output_too_large``
    / ``tool_failed`` / ``io`` / ``json`` / ``other``) and a ``detail``. The
    string form is ``[kind] detail``, which composes cleanly in pipelines.
    """

    def __init__(self, detail: str, *, kind: str = "other") -> None:
        super().__init__(f"[{kind}] {detail}")
        self.kind = kind
        self.detail = detail

    # ── constructors mirroring the Rust enum variants ───────────────────────
    @classmethod
    def not_found(cls, name: str) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(f"tool not found: {name}", kind="not_found")

    @classmethod
    def validation(cls, msg: str) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(msg, kind="validation")

    @classmethod
    def bad_param(cls, name: str, expected: str, detail: str) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(f"parameter `{name}` (expected {expected}) — {detail}", kind="bad_param")

    @classmethod
    def permission_denied(cls, tool: str, reason: str) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(f"permission denied for tool `{tool}`: {reason}", kind="permission_denied")

    @classmethod
    def sandbox(cls, msg: str) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(msg, kind="sandbox")

    @classmethod
    def timeout(cls, timeout_ms: int) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(f"execution timed out after {timeout_ms} ms", kind="timeout")

    @classmethod
    def output_too_large(cls, limit: int) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(f"output exceeded sandbox limit ({limit} bytes)", kind="output_too_large")

    @classmethod
    def tool_failed(cls, tool: str, inner: str) -> "ToolError":
        return cls(f"tool `{tool}` returned an error: {inner}", kind="tool_failed")


ToolResult = Tuple[Any, Optional[ToolError]]  # convenience alias; we raise in practice


@dataclass
class ToolContext:
    """Per-call execution context.

    The executor populates ``allow_net`` / ``allow_fs_paths`` from its
    :class:`~rc_python.sandbox.Sandbox` so tools can self-check I/O policy.
    Composition passes a child context derived from this one.
    """

    correlation_id: str = "default"
    timeout_ms: int = 0
    cancelled: bool = False
    allow_net: bool = True
    # Whole filesystem by default (matching the Rust default); an explicitly
    # empty list disables FS access for tools that consult the list.
    allow_fs_paths: List[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["/"])

    @classmethod
    def new(cls, correlation_id: str) -> "ToolContext":
        return cls(correlation_id=correlation_id)

    def with_timeout(self, ms: int) -> "ToolContext":
        self.timeout_ms = ms
        return self

    def check_net(self) -> None:
        """Raise :class:`ToolError` if outbound network is not permitted."""
        if not self.allow_net:
            raise ToolError.sandbox("network access is disabled in this context")

    def check_path(self, path: str) -> None:
        """Raise :class:`ToolError` if ``path`` is outside the allowed FS roots.

        An empty allow-list means no FS access at all. Paths are canonicalised
        before the prefix check so ``..`` traversal cannot escape a root.
        """
        if not self.allow_fs_paths:
            raise ToolError.sandbox("filesystem access is disabled in this context")
        canonical = os.path.realpath(path)
        for root in self.allow_fs_paths:
            root_canonical = os.path.realpath(root)
            if canonical == root_canonical or canonical.startswith(
                root_canonical + os.sep
            ):
                return
        raise ToolError.sandbox(f"path `{path}` is outside the allowed filesystem roots")


class Tool(ABC):
    """The single trait every tool implements.

    ``execute`` is a coroutine so tools that do network or subprocess I/O can
    run without blocking the executor's event loop.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Stable, unique, dot-namespaced id (e.g. ``math.add``)."""

    @abstractmethod
    def description(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable summary."""

    @abstractmethod
    def schema(self) -> "Schema":  # noqa: F821 — forward ref to rc_python.schema.Schema
        """The input schema; the validator runs against this before ``execute``."""

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        """Which source produced this tool (default: builtin)."""
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    def category(self) -> str:
        """Category label for grouping. Default: first segment of the name."""
        return self.name().split(".", 1)[0] if "." in self.name() else "misc"

    def version(self) -> str:
        """Semver version (default ``0.1.0``)."""
        return "0.1.0"

    @abstractmethod
    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Any:
        """Run the tool. ``input`` matches :meth:`schema`."""


def arc(tool: Tool) -> Tool:
    """Return ``tool`` unchanged. In Python tools are plain objects shared by
    reference, so there is no ``Arc`` wrapper — this helper exists only for
    API parity with the Rust ``rc_core::tool::arc``."""
    return tool


# In Python tools are plain objects shared by reference; `ToolArc` is just an
# alias for `Tool`, kept for API parity with the Rust `ToolArc = Arc<dyn Tool>`.
ToolArc = Tool


# The framework version (matches pyproject.toml).
VERSION = "0.1.0"
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/executor.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/executor.py)

```python
"""rc_python.executor — the single point a tool is actually run (Python port of ``rc_core::executor``).

For every call the executor:

1. looks the tool up in the registry,
2. asks the policy for a decision (``Allow`` / ``Ask`` / ``Deny``),
3. validates the input against the tool's schema (filling defaults),
4. enforces the sandbox (timeout, output cap),
5. runs the tool's ``execute``,
6. clamps the output to the sandbox's size limit.

The executor never prompts a human — ``Ask`` is surfaced as a decision the
caller (CLI, agent loop) must handle before calling :meth:`run` with
``approved = True``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from typing import Any, Dict

from .core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolError
from .permissions import Permission, PermissionPolicy
from .registry import Registry
from .sandbox import Sandbox
from .validator import validate


class Executor:
    def __init__(self, registry: Registry, policy: PermissionPolicy, sandbox: Sandbox) -> None:
        self.registry = registry
        self.policy = policy
        self.sandbox = sandbox

    def authorize(self, name: str) -> Permission:
        """What would the policy decide for this tool? Callers use this to
        decide whether to prompt the user (``Ask``) before calling ``run``."""
        tool = self.registry.get(name)  # raises ToolError if absent
        return self.policy.decide(tool)

    async def run(self, name: str, input: Dict[str, Any], approved: bool) -> Any:
        decision = self.authorize(name)
        if decision == Permission.DENY:
            raise ToolError.permission_denied(name, "denied by policy")
        if decision == Permission.ASK and not approved:
            raise ToolError.permission_denied(name, "requires approval (Ask)")
        return await self._run_inner(name, input)

    async def run_inner(self, name: str, input: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """Run without the permission gate — used internally by composition,
        where the outer composed tool has already been authorized and the
        inner steps are trusted parts of the same call."""
        return await self._run_inner(name, input)

    async def _run_inner(self, name: str, input: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        tool = self.registry.get(name)
        validated = validate(tool.schema(), input)
        ctx = ToolContext(
            correlation_id=name,
            timeout_ms=self.sandbox.timeout_ms,
            cancelled=False,
            allow_net=self.sandbox.allow_net,
            allow_fs_paths=list(self.sandbox.allow_fs_paths),
        )
        if self.sandbox.timeout_ms > 0:
            try:
                out = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    tool.execute(validated, ctx),
                    timeout=self.sandbox.timeout_ms / 1000.0,
                )
            except asyncio.TimeoutError as e:
                raise ToolError.timeout(self.sandbox.timeout_ms) from None
        else:
            out = await tool.execute(validated, ctx)
        # clamp output (may raise ToolError.output_too_large for huge results)
        self.sandbox.clamp_output(out)
        return out
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/lifecycle.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/lifecycle.py)

```python
"""rc_python.lifecycle — L3: the full tool lifecycle (Python port of ``rc_lifecycle``).

The :class:`Lifecycle` manager ties the other layers together:

1. discover — walk every registered :class:`~rc_python.sources.ToolSource`,
   collect the tools each produces.
2. register — insert them into the :class:`~rc_python.registry.Registry`.
3. validate — check every tool's schema for duplicates / empty names.
4. load — sources load eagerly (tools are ready-to-register on discover).
5. execute — run a tool by name through the :class:`~rc_python.executor.Executor`,
   timing the call and recording metrics.
6. monitor — per-tool call/success/failure counts + latency, via
   :class:`MetricsStore`.
7. version — a version report of every registered tool.
8. retire — remove a tool from the registry.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from .core import Tool, ToolArc, ToolError, ToolSourceKind
from .executor import Executor
from .permissions import Permission, PermissionPolicy
from .registry import Registry
from .sandbox import Sandbox
from .sources import SourceRegistry, ToolSource


@dataclass
class ToolMetrics:
    calls: int = 0
    successes: int = 0
    failures: int = 0
    total_us: int = 0
    last_error: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def avg_us(self) -> float:
        return self.total_us / self.calls if self.calls else 0.0


class MetricsStore:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._store: Dict[str, ToolMetrics] = {}

    def record(self, name: str, success: bool, elapsed_us: int, err: Optional[str]) -> None:
        m = self._store.setdefault(name, ToolMetrics())
        m.calls += 1
        m.total_us += int(elapsed_us)
        if success:
            m.successes += 1
        else:
            m.failures += 1
            m.last_error = err

    def get(self, name: str) -> Optional[ToolMetrics]:
        return self._store.get(name)

    def all(self) -> List[Tuple[str, ToolMetrics]]:
        out = list(self._store.items())
        out.sort(key=lambda kv: kv[0])
        return out


class Lifecycle:
    def __init__(self, policy: PermissionPolicy, sandbox: Sandbox) -> None:
        self.registry = Registry()
        self.policy = policy
        self.sandbox = sandbox
        self.executor = Executor(self.registry, policy, sandbox)
        self.sources = SourceRegistry()
        self.metrics = MetricsStore()

    @classmethod
    def permissive(cls) -> "Lifecycle":
        """A fully-permissive lifecycle (allow everything, default sandbox) —
        handy for examples and tests."""
        policy = PermissionPolicy.default_policy().with_default(Permission.ALLOW)
        return cls(policy, Sandbox())

    @classmethod
    def new(cls, policy: PermissionPolicy, sandbox: Sandbox) -> "Lifecycle":
        return cls(policy, sandbox)

    def add_source(self, source: ToolSource) -> None:
        """Register a source. Its tools are loaded on the next :meth:`discover`."""
        self.sources.add(source)

    def register(self, tool: Tool) -> None:
        self.registry.register(tool)

    def register_all(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> None:
        self.registry.register_all(tools)

    async def discover(self) -> int:
        """Run every source's ``tools()`` and register the results.

        Returns the number of tools registered.
        """
        tools = await self.sources.all_tools()
        n = len(tools)
        self.registry.register_all(tools)
        return n

    def validate_all(self) -> List[str]:
        """Validate every registered tool's schema. Returns a list of issue
        strings (empty = all good)."""
        issues: List[str] = []
        for info in self.registry.list():
            if not info.name:
                issues.append("tool with empty name")
                continue
            try:
                tool = self.registry.get(info.name)
            except ToolError:
                continue
            schema = tool.schema()
            seen = set()
            for p in schema.parameters:
                if not p.name:
                    issues.append(f"{info.name}: parameter with empty name")
                if p.name in seen:
                    issues.append(f"{info.name}: duplicate parameter `{p.name}`")
                seen.add(p.name)
        return issues

    async def execute(self, name: str, input: Dict[str, Any], approved: bool) -> Any:
        """Execute a tool by name, timing the call and recording metrics."""
        start = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            out = await self.executor.run(name, input, approved)
        except Exception as e:
            elapsed = int((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1_000_000)
            self.metrics.record(name, False, elapsed, str(e))
            raise
        elapsed = int((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1_000_000)
        self.metrics.record(name, True, elapsed, None)
        return out

    def retire(self, name: str) -> bool:
        """Retire (remove) a tool from the registry. Returns True if present."""
        return self.registry.remove(name) is not None

    def metrics_for(self, name: str) -> Optional[ToolMetrics]:
        return self.metrics.get(name)

    def all_metrics(self) -> List[Tuple[str, ToolMetrics]]:
        return self.metrics.all()

    def version_report(self) -> List[Tuple[str, str, str]]:
        """Every tool's name + version + source, sorted by name."""
        out = [(i.name, i.version, i.source) for i in self.registry.list()]
        out.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
        return out
```

"""rc_python.manifest — serialisable tool identity (Python port of ``rc_core::manifest``).

A :class:`Manifest` is the description of a tool independent of its runtime
:class:`~rc_python.core.Tool` impl. Sources produce manifests during
discovery; the registry holds live ``Tool`` impls. A manifest is everything
you need to *know* about a tool without loading it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional

from .core import Tool
from .schema import Schema


@dataclass
class Manifest:
    name: str
    description: str
    category: str
    source: str
    version: str
    schema: Schema = field(default_factory=Schema.new)
    permission: str = ""
    origin: Optional[str] = None

    @classmethod
    def from_tool(cls, t: Tool) -> "Manifest":
        """Build a manifest from a live tool (snapshots identity + schema)."""
        return cls(
            name=t.name(),
            description=t.description(),
            category=t.category(),
            source=t.source().as_str,
            version=t.version(),
            schema=t.schema(),
            permission="",
            origin=None,
        )

    def to_json(self) -> str:
        import json
        return json.dumps(
            {
                "name": self.name,
                "description": self.description,
                "category": self.category,
                "source": self.source,
                "version": self.version,
                "permission": self.permission,
                "origin": self.origin,
            },
            indent=2,
        )


@dataclass
class Catalog:
    """A directory of manifests — what a source advertises before loading."""

    manifests: List[Manifest] = field(default_factory=list)

    @classmethod
    def new(cls) -> "Catalog":
        return cls()

    def push(self, m: Manifest) -> None:
        self.manifests.append(m)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.manifests)

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return len(self) == 0

    def names(self) -> List[str]:
        n = [m.name for m in self.manifests]
        n.sort()
        return n

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/permissions.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/permissions.py)

```python
"""rc_python.permissions — the gate the executor consults (Python port of ``rc_core::permissions``).

Like the Rust policy (and the RomaCode server gate) this is **fully open by
default**: the default policy carries no rules and every tool call is
``ALLOW`` — nothing is denied, nothing asks. The rule machinery
(deny → ask → allow → default evaluation order) is kept so an embedder who
*wants* restrictions can opt in with a non-default policy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import List

from .core import Tool


class Permission(Enum):
    ALLOW = "allow"
    ASK = "ask"
    DENY = "deny"


def glob_match(pattern: str, s: str) -> bool:
    """Glob match: ``*`` matches any run of chars, ``?`` matches one char."""
    return _glob_inner(pattern, 0, s, 0)


def _glob_inner(p: str, pi: int, t: str, ti: int) -> bool:
    while pi < len(p):
        c = p[pi]
        if c == "*":
            # trailing * eats everything
            if pi == len(p) - 1:
                return True
            # try to match the rest of the pattern at every position
            for skip in range(ti, len(t) + 1):
                if _glob_inner(p, pi + 1, t, skip):
                    return True
            return False
        if c == "?":
            if ti >= len(t):
                return False
            pi += 1
            ti += 1
            continue
        # literal
        if ti >= len(t) or t[ti] != c:
            return False
        pi += 1
        ti += 1
    return ti == len(t)


@dataclass
class PermissionRule:
    """A glob pattern matched against the tool name, bound to a decision."""

    pattern: str
    decision: Permission

    @classmethod
    def new(cls, pattern: str, decision: Permission) -> "PermissionRule":
        return cls(pattern=pattern, decision=decision)

    def matches(self, name: str) -> bool:
        return glob_match(self.pattern, name)


@dataclass
class PermissionPolicy:
    """The full permission policy.

    Evaluation order: explicit ``deny`` (first match wins) → ``ask`` →
    ``allow`` → ``default``.
    """

    deny: List[PermissionRule] = field(default_factory=list)
    ask: List[PermissionRule] = field(default_factory=list)
    allow: List[PermissionRule] = field(default_factory=list)
    default: Permission = Permission.ALLOW

    @classmethod
    def default_policy(cls) -> "PermissionPolicy":
        """Fully open, matching the Rust ``rc_core`` default and the server
        gate: no rules, every tool allowed. Restrictive policies are opt-in
        via the builder helpers (``deny_`` / ``ask_`` / ``allow_`` /
        ``with_default``); they are never the shipped default.
        """
        return cls(deny=[], ask=[], allow=[], default=Permission.ALLOW)

    # Python's dataclass default_factory makes `default_policy` the canonical
    # constructor; expose `__init__`-friendly `default()` too for ergonomics.
    @classmethod
    def default(cls) -> "PermissionPolicy":  # type: ignore[override]
        return cls.default_policy()

    def decide(self, tool: Tool) -> Permission:
        name = tool.name()
        for r in self.deny:
            if r.matches(name):
                return r.decision
        for r in self.ask:
            if r.matches(name):
                return r.decision
        for r in self.allow:
            if r.matches(name):
                return r.decision
        return self.default

    # ── builder helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def deny_(self, pattern: str) -> "PermissionPolicy":
        self.deny.append(PermissionRule.new(pattern, Permission.DENY))
        return self

    def ask_(self, pattern: str) -> "PermissionPolicy":
        self.ask.append(PermissionRule.new(pattern, Permission.ASK))
        return self

    def allow_(self, pattern: str) -> "PermissionPolicy":
        self.allow.append(PermissionRule.new(pattern, Permission.ALLOW))
        return self

    def with_default(self, d: Permission) -> "PermissionPolicy":
        self.default = d
        return self
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/registry.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/registry.py)

```python
"""rc_python.registry — the in-memory tool store (Python port of ``rc_core::registry``).

A thread-safe store of every loaded tool, indexed by name. The registry is
the spine of the framework: sources feed it, the executor reads it,
composition reads it to resolve steps, and the CLI lists it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

from .core import Tool, ToolError


@dataclass
class ToolInfo:
    """A read-only snapshot of one registered tool's identity."""

    name: str
    description: str
    category: str
    source: str
    version: str


class Registry:
    """A thread-safe registry of tools, keyed by ``tool.name()``."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._tools: Dict[str, Tool] = {}
        self._lock = threading.RLock()

    def register(self, tool: Tool) -> Optional[Tool]:
        """Register a tool. If one with the same name exists it is replaced
        (the new version wins — see the lifecycle manager for upgrade policy).
        Returns the previous tool if one was displaced.
        """
        with self._lock:
            prev = self._tools.get(tool.name())
            self._tools[tool.name()] = tool
            return prev

    def register_all(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> None:
        """Register many tools at once (e.g. from a source's ``tools()``)."""
        with self._lock:
            for t in tools:
                self._tools[t.name()] = t

    def get(self, name: str) -> Tool:
        """Look up a tool by name. Raises :class:`ToolError` if absent."""
        with self._lock:
            t = self._tools.get(name)
        if t is None:
            raise ToolError.not_found(name)
        return t

    def contains(self, name: str) -> bool:
        with self._lock:
            return name in self._tools

    def remove(self, name: str) -> Optional[Tool]:
        """Retire a tool. Returns the removed tool if present."""
        with self._lock:
            return self._tools.pop(name, None)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        with self._lock:
            return len(self._tools)

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return len(self) == 0

    def list(self) -> List[ToolInfo]:
        """A sorted snapshot of every tool's identity."""
        with self._lock:
            infos = [
                ToolInfo(
                    name=t.name(),
                    description=t.description(),
                    category=t.category(),
                    source=t.source().as_str,
                    version=t.version(),
                )
                for t in self._tools.values()
            ]
        infos.sort(key=lambda i: i.name)
        return infos

    def names(self) -> List[str]:
        """All registered tool names, sorted."""
        with self._lock:
            n = list(self._tools.keys())
        n.sort()
        return n
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sandbox.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sandbox.py)

```python
"""rc_python.sandbox — resource limits the executor enforces (Python port of ``rc_core::sandbox``).

A wall-clock timeout, an output-size cap, and network/filesystem allow-lists
that tools *should* consult before doing I/O. The shipped default is fully
open (network allowed, whole filesystem); :meth:`Sandbox.strict` remains as
an opt-in lockdown.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, List

from .core import ToolError


@dataclass
class Sandbox:
    """Resource limits for one execution."""

    timeout_ms: int = 30_000
    max_output_bytes: int = 1_000_000
    allow_net: bool = True
    # Whole filesystem by default (matching the Rust default); an explicitly
    # empty list disables FS access for tools that consult the list.
    allow_fs_paths: List[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["/"])
    max_read_bytes: int = 10_000_000

    @classmethod
    def strict(cls) -> "Sandbox":
        """A locked-down sandbox: no net, no fs, short timeout. Good default
        for untrusted/composed tools."""
        return cls(
            timeout_ms=5_000,
            max_output_bytes=100_000,
            allow_net=False,
            allow_fs_paths=[],
            max_read_bytes=100_000,
        )

    def check_net(self) -> None:
        """Raise :class:`ToolError` if network is not permitted."""
        if not self.allow_net:
            raise ToolError.sandbox("network access is disabled in this sandbox")

    def check_path(self, path: str) -> None:
        """Raise :class:`ToolError` if ``path`` is outside the allowed FS roots."""
        import os
        if not self.allow_fs_paths:
            raise ToolError.sandbox("filesystem access is disabled in this sandbox")
        canonical = os.path.realpath(path)
        for root in self.allow_fs_paths:
            root_canonical = os.path.realpath(root)
            if canonical == root_canonical or canonical.startswith(root_canonical + os.sep):
                return
        raise ToolError.sandbox(f"path `{path}` is outside the allowed filesystem roots")

    def clamp_output(self, value: Any) -> None:
        """Enforce the output-size cap **in place** where possible.

        If the value is a string, truncate it and append a marker. Otherwise
        serialise it to JSON and, if that exceeds the cap, raise
        :class:`ToolError` — non-string structures cannot be sensibly
        truncated without losing meaning.
        """
        if self.max_output_bytes == 0:
            return
        if isinstance(value, str):
            if len(value.encode("utf-8")) <= self.max_output_bytes:
                return
            max_chars = max(1, self.max_output_bytes - 40)
            head = value[:max_chars]
            value_marker = f"{head}… [truncated: output exceeded {self.max_output_bytes} bytes]"
            # truncate in place is not possible for an immutable str passed by
            # value; callers should use the returned value instead. We raise to
            # be safe, mirroring the Rust path for non-truncatable cases.
            raise ToolError.output_too_large(self.max_output_bytes)
        # non-string: serialise and size-check
        try:
            s = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return
        if len(s.encode("utf-8")) > self.max_output_bytes:
            raise ToolError.output_too_large(self.max_output_bytes)
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/schema.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/schema.py)

```python
"""rc_python.schema — tool input schemas (Python port of ``rc_core::schema``).

A :class:`Schema` is the contract a tool publishes about its input: the
parameters it accepts, their types, whether they are required, and their
defaults. :func:`rc_python.validator.validate` checks a Python dict against a
schema before the tool runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional


class ParamType:
    """The parameter types a schema can express.

    A Python ``bool`` is accepted for ``Boolean`` only (not ``Integer``),
    because in Python ``isinstance(True, int)`` is ``True`` — we must guard
    against that conflation explicitly. ``Array`` carries an inner type so
    ``["a", "b"]`` validates as ``Array(String)``.
    """

    STRING = "string"
    INTEGER = "integer"
    NUMBER = "number"
    BOOLEAN = "boolean"
    OBJECT = "object"
    ANY = "any"

    def __init__(self, kind: str, inner: Optional["ParamType"] = None) -> None:
        assert kind in (
            self.STRING, self.INTEGER, self.NUMBER, self.BOOLEAN,
            self.OBJECT, self.ANY,
        ) or (kind == "array" and inner is not None), f"bad ParamType kind: {kind!r}"
        self.kind = kind
        self.inner = inner

    # ── constructors ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    @classmethod
    def string(cls) -> "ParamType":
        return cls(cls.STRING)

    @classmethod
    def integer(cls) -> "ParamType":
        return cls(cls.INTEGER)

    @classmethod
    def number(cls) -> "ParamType":
        return cls(cls.NUMBER)

    @classmethod
    def boolean(cls) -> "ParamType":
        return cls(cls.BOOLEAN)

    @classmethod
    def object(cls) -> "ParamType":
        return cls(cls.OBJECT)

    @classmethod
    def any_(cls) -> "ParamType":
        return cls(cls.ANY)

    @classmethod
    def array(cls, inner: "ParamType") -> "ParamType":
        return cls("array", inner)

    # ── validation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def check(self, v: Any) -> None:
        """Raise ``ValueError`` if ``v`` does not match this type."""
        ok, why = self._matches(v)
        if not ok:
            raise ValueError(f"expected {self}, got {type_name(v)}" + (f": {why}" if why else ""))

    def _matches(self, v: Any) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        k = self.kind
        if k == self.ANY:
            return True, ""
        if k == self.STRING:
            return isinstance(v, str), ""
        if k == self.INTEGER:
            # bool is a subclass of int in Python; exclude it explicitly.
            return isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool), ""
        if k == self.NUMBER:
            return isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool), ""
        if k == self.BOOLEAN:
            return isinstance(v, bool), ""
        if k == self.OBJECT:
            return isinstance(v, dict), ""
        if k == "array":
            if not isinstance(v, list):
                return False, ""
            for i, item in enumerate(v):
                try:
                    self.inner.check(item)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                except ValueError as e:
                    return False, f"element {i}: {e}"
            return True, ""
        return False, "unknown type"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.kind == "array":
            return f"array<{self.inner}>"  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        return self.kind

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"ParamType({self})"

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, ParamType) and self.kind == other.kind and self.inner == other.inner

    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash((self.kind, self.inner))


def type_name(v: Any) -> str:
    if v is None:
        return "null"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "boolean"
    if isinstance(v, int):
        return "integer"
    if isinstance(v, float):
        return "number"
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return "string"
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return "array"
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return "object"
    return type(v).__name__


@dataclass
class Parameter:
    """One parameter of a tool's input schema."""

    name: str
    typ: ParamType
    description: str = ""
    required: bool = False
    default: Any = None
    enum_values: List[Any] = field(default_factory=list)

    @classmethod
    def required(cls, name: str, typ: ParamType) -> "Parameter":
        return cls(name=name, typ=typ, required=True)

    @classmethod
    def optional(cls, name: str, typ: ParamType) -> "Parameter":
        return cls(name=name, typ=typ, required=False)

    def with_desc(self, desc: str) -> "Parameter":
        self.description = desc
        return self

    def with_default(self, v: Any) -> "Parameter":
        self.default = v
        return self

    def with_enum(self, vs: List[Any]) -> "Parameter":
        self.enum_values = list(vs)
        return self


@dataclass
class Schema:
    """The full input schema of a tool: an ordered list of named parameters."""

    parameters: List[Parameter] = field(default_factory=list)

    @classmethod
    def new(cls) -> "Schema":
        return cls()

    def param(self, p: Parameter) -> "Schema":
        self.parameters.append(p)
        return self

    def to_json_schema(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Render as a JSON-Schema-ish dict, for OpenAI/Anthropic tool defs."""
        props: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        required: List[str] = []
        type_for = {
            ParamType.STRING: "string",
            ParamType.INTEGER: "integer",
            ParamType.NUMBER: "number",
            ParamType.BOOLEAN: "boolean",
            ParamType.OBJECT: "object",
            ParamType.ANY: None,
        }
        for p in self.parameters:
            entry: Dict[str, Any] = {}
            if p.typ.kind == "array":
                entry["type"] = "array"
            else:
                t = type_for.get(p.typ.kind)
                if t is not None:
                    entry["type"] = t
            if p.description:
                entry["description"] = p.description
            if p.enum_values:
                entry["enum"] = list(p.enum_values)
            if p.default is not None:
                entry["default"] = p.default
            props[p.name] = entry
            if p.required:
                required.append(p.name)
        return {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required}
```

"""rc_python.sources.builtin — the shipped tool catalog (Python port of ``rc_builtin``).

A representative subset of the eight Rust categories, every one a
:class:`~rc_python.core.Tool`:

| category | tools |
|----------|-------|
| `math`   | add, subtract, multiply, divide, sqrt |
| `text`   | upper, lower, length, reverse |
| `data`   | json_pretty |
| `code`   | base64_encode, base64_decode |
| `time`   | now, iso_now |

:meth:`builtin_all_tools` returns every built-in, ready to register. This is
the "source 1: builtin" mechanism; the others live in the sibling modules.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import datetime
import json
import math
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from ..core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind, ToolError
from ..schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema
from .source import SourceError, ToolSource


class _Binop(Tool):
    """A two-number operation. The ``op`` callable maps ``(a, b) -> result``."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, desc: str, op):
        self._name = name
        self._desc = desc
        self._op = op
        self._schema = (
            Schema.new()
            .param(Parameter.required("a", ParamType.number()))
            .param(Parameter.required("b", ParamType.number()))
        )

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> float:
        a = float(input["a"])
        b = float(input["b"])
        return self._op(a, b)


def _add() -> _Binop:
    return _Binop("math.add", "Add two numbers (a + b).", lambda a, b: a + b)


def _sub() -> _Binop:
    return _Binop("math.subtract", "Subtract b from a (a - b).", lambda a, b: a - b)


def _mul() -> _Binop:
    return _Binop("math.multiply", "Multiply two numbers (a × b).", lambda a, b: a * b)


def _div() -> _Binop:
    def _f(a: float, b: float) -> float:
        if b == 0.0:
            raise ToolError.tool_failed("math.divide", "division by zero")
        return a / b
    return _Binop("math.divide", "Divide a by b (a / b). Errors on zero.", _f)


class _Sqrt(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "math.sqrt"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Square root of a number."

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> float:
        return math.sqrt(float(input["n"]))


class _TextOp(Tool):

        self._name = name
        self._desc = desc
        self._fn = fn
        self._schema = Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("s", ParamType.string()))

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext):
        return self._fn(input["s"])


class _JsonPretty(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "data.json_pretty"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Pretty-print a JSON value (indent=2)."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("value", ParamType.any_()))

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> str:
        return json.dumps(input["value"], indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)


class _B64Encode(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "code.base64_encode"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Base64-encode a string."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("s", ParamType.string()))

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> str:
        return base64.b64encode(input["s"].encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")


class _B64Decode(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "code.base64_decode"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Base64-decode a string."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("s", ParamType.string()))

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> str:
        try:
            return base64.b64decode(input["s"]).decode("utf-8")
        except Exception as e:
            raise ToolError.tool_failed("code.base64_decode", str(e)) from None


class _Now(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "time.now"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Current Unix timestamp (seconds)."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new()

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> float:
        return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()


class _IsoNow(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "time.iso_now"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Current UTC time as an ISO-8601 string."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new()

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> str:
        return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def builtin_all_tools() -> List[Tool]:
    """Every built-in tool, across all categories, ready to register."""
    return [
        _add(), _sub(), _mul(), _div(), _Sqrt(),
        _TextOp("text.upper", "Uppercase a string.", str.upper),
        _TextOp("text.lower", "Lowercase a string.", str.lower),
        _TextOp("text.length", "Length of a string.", lambda s: len(s)),
        _TextOp("text.reverse", "Reverse a string.", lambda s: s[::-1]),
        _JsonPretty(),
        _B64Encode(), _B64Decode(),
        _Now(), _IsoNow(),
    ]


# exposed for parity with the Rust `rc_builtin::COUNT` / `CATEGORIES`.
COUNT: int = len(builtin_all_tools())
CATEGORIES = ("math", "text", "data", "code", "time")


class BuiltinSource(ToolSource):
    """Source 1 of the mechanisms — wraps :func:`builtin_all_tools`."""

    def kind(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    def id(self) -> str:
        return "builtin"

    async def tools(self) -> List[Tool]:
        return builtin_all_tools()

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sources/declarative.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sources/declarative.py)

```python
"""rc_python.sources.declarative — source 2: YAML/JSON spec → shell tools.

A declarative spec is a list of tool definitions, each with a name, a
description, a command template (``{{param}}`` placeholders), and a parameter
list. No code is written — the source turns each entry into a
:class:`~rc_python.sources.tools.ShellTool`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Union

from ..core import Tool, ToolSourceKind
from ..schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema
from .source import ToolSource
from .tools import ShellTool

_TYPE_MAP = {
    "string": ParamType.string,
    "integer": ParamType.integer,
    "number": ParamType.number,
    "boolean": ParamType.boolean,
    "object": ParamType.object,
    "any": ParamType.any_,
}


def _param_from_spec(p: Dict[str, Any]) -> Parameter:
    typ_name = p.get("type", "string")
    if typ_name.startswith("array<") and typ_name.endswith(">"):
        inner_name = typ_name[len("array<"):-1]
        inner_factory = _TYPE_MAP.get(inner_name, ParamType.string)
        typ = ParamType.array(inner_factory())
    else:
        factory = _TYPE_MAP.get(typ_name, ParamType.string)
        typ = factory()
    required = bool(p.get("required", False))
    par = Parameter(name=p["name"], typ=typ, description=p.get("description", ""), required=required)
    if "default" in p:
        par.with_default(p["default"])
    if "enum" in p:
        par.with_enum(list(p["enum"]))
    return par


def _schema_from_spec(params: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Schema:
    s = Schema.new()
    for p in params or []:
        s.param(_param_from_spec(p))
    return s


def _tool_from_spec(spec: Dict[str, Any]) -> ShellTool:
    schema = _schema_from_spec(spec.get("params", []))
    return ShellTool(
        name=spec["name"],
        description=spec.get("description", ""),
        schema=schema,
        command=spec["command"],
        source=ToolSourceKind.Declarative,
        cwd=spec.get("cwd"),
    )


class DeclarativeSource(ToolSource):
    """Build shell tools from a declarative spec.

    Pass either an in-memory list of spec dicts, or a path to a JSON file
    containing ``{"tools": [...]}``.
    """

    def __init__(self, specs: Union[List[Dict[str, Any]], str], source_id: str = "declarative") -> None:
        self._id = source_id
        if isinstance(specs, str):
            with open(specs, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            self._specs = data["tools"] if isinstance(data, dict) else data
        else:
            self._specs = list(specs)

    def kind(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Declarative

    def id(self) -> str:
        return self._id

    async def tools(self) -> List[Tool]:
        return [_tool_from_spec(s) for s in self._specs]
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sources/source.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sources/source.py)

```python
"""rc_python.sources.source — the ToolSource contract (Python port of ``rc_sources::source``).

Every tool-source mechanism implements :meth:`ToolSource.tools`: discover and
load in one step, returning fully-built, ready-to-register tools. The
lifecycle manager iterates a :class:`SourceRegistry` of sources and registers
their results.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import List

from ..core import Tool, ToolSourceKind


class SourceError(Exception):
    """Errors a source can surface during discovery or loading."""

    def __init__(self, src: str, detail: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"source `{src}`: {detail}")
        self.src = src
        self.detail = detail


class ToolSource(ABC):
    """The contract every tool source implements."""

    @abstractmethod
    def kind(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        """Which of the mechanisms this source is."""

    @abstractmethod
    def id(self) -> str:
        """A short id for this source instance (e.g. ``builtin``, ``rest:github``)."""

    @abstractmethod
    async def tools(self) -> List[Tool]:
        """Produce every tool this source can, fully built and ready to register."""


class SourceRegistry:
    """A registry of sources — what the lifecycle manager iterates over."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._sources: List[ToolSource] = []

    def add(self, source: ToolSource) -> None:
        self._sources.append(source)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._sources)

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return len(self) == 0

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._sources)

    async def all_tools(self) -> List[Tool]:
        """Run every source's ``tools()`` and flatten the results.

        Sources are awaited concurrently so a slow HTTP source does not block
        a fast builtin one.
        """
        import asyncio
        if not self._sources:
            return []
        batches = await asyncio.gather(
            *(s.tools() for s in self._sources), return_exceptions=True
        )
        out: List[Tool] = []
        for s, batch in zip(self._sources, batches):
            if isinstance(batch, Exception):
                raise SourceError(s.id(), str(batch)) from batch
            out.extend(batch)
        return out
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sources/tools.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/sources/tools.py)

```python
"""rc_python.sources.tools — reusable Tool impls the source adapters build on.

:class:`ShellTool` runs a templated shell command; :class:`HttpTool` calls an
HTTP endpoint. Both are full :class:`~rc_python.core.Tool` impls, so once a
source produces one it is indistinguishable from a built-in. This mirrors the
Rust ``rc_sources::tools`` module (``ShellTool`` / ``HttpTool``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import shlex
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from ..core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolSourceKind
from ..schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema


def _stringify(v: Any) -> str:
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return v
    if v is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "true" if v else "false"
    return str(v)


def _render_once(tmpl: str, values: Dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """One-pass ``{{param}}`` substitution.

    The template is scanned left to right exactly once; substituted values
    are never rescanned, so a value that itself contains ``{{...}}`` arrives
    as inert text instead of being re-expanded (mirrors the Rust one-pass
    renderer in ``rc_sources::tools``).
    """
    out: List[str] = []
    rest = tmpl
    while True:
        start = rest.find("{{")
        if start < 0:
            out.append(rest)
            break
        out.append(rest[:start])
        after = rest[start + 2:]
        end = after.find("}}")
        if end < 0:
            out.append("{{")
            rest = after
            continue
        name = after[:end]
        if name in values:
            out.append(values[name])
        else:
            out.append(rest[start:start + end + 4])
        rest = after[end + 2:]
    return "".join(out)


def one_string_param(name: str, desc: str) -> Schema:
    """Helper: a schema with one required string parameter."""
    return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required(name, ParamType.string()).with_desc(desc))


class ShellTool(Tool):
    """A tool backed by a shell command template.

    ``{{param}}`` placeholders are substituted with each param's stringified
    value, then the command runs under ``sh -c``. This is the engine behind
    the ``declarative`` and ``cli`` sources.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str,
        schema: Schema,
        command: str,
        source: ToolSourceKind = ToolSourceKind.Declarative,
        cwd: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._name = name
        self._desc = description
        self._schema = schema
        self.command = command
        self._source = source
        self.cwd = cwd

    # ── Tool impl ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return self._source

    def render(self, input: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        # Values are data, not code: every substituted value is quoted as a
        # single literal shell word (mirrors the Rust `shell_quote` contract).
        values = {
            p.name: shlex.quote(_stringify(input[p.name]))
            for p in self._schema.parameters
            if p.name in input
        }
        return _render_once(self.command, values)

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if ctx.cancelled:
            raise ToolError("cancelled before shell tool", kind="other")
        rendered = self.render(input)
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "sh", "-c", rendered,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            cwd=self.cwd,
        )
        stdout_b, stderr_b = await proc.communicate()
        return {
            "exit_code": proc.returncode if proc.returncode is not None else -1,
            "stdout": stdout_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
            "stderr": stderr_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
        }


class HttpTool(Tool):
    """A tool backed by an HTTP call.

    The URL and optional JSON body are templates with ``{{param}}``
    placeholders, substituted from the input. Uses ``urllib`` (stdlib) so the
    framework stays dependency-free; the blocking call is run in a thread via
    :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str,
        schema: Schema,
        method: str,
        url: str,
        source: ToolSourceKind = ToolSourceKind.Rest,
        body: Optional[str] = None,
        headers: Optional[List[Tuple[str, str]]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._name = name
        self._desc = description
        self._schema = schema
        self.method = method.upper()
        self.url = url
        self.body = body
        self.headers = headers or []
        self._source = source

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return self._source

    def render(self, input: Dict[str, Any], tmpl: str, in_url: bool = False) -> str:
        # One-pass substitution: substituted values are never rescanned. URL
        # placeholders get percent-encoding; body placeholders get JSON
        # escaping (the body template keeps its own surrounding quotes).
        values = {}
        for p in self._schema.parameters:
            if p.name in input:
                raw = _stringify(input[p.name])
                if in_url:
                    values[p.name] = urllib.parse.quote(raw, safe="")
                else:
                    values[p.name] = json.dumps(raw)[1:-1]
        return _render_once(tmpl, values)

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        ctx.check_net()
        url = self.render(input, self.url, in_url=True)
        body_bytes: Optional[bytes] = None
        headers = list(self.headers)
        if self.body is not None:
            body_str = self.render(input, self.body)
            # try JSON; fall back to raw string
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(body_str)
                body_bytes = json.dumps(parsed).encode("utf-8")
                headers.append(("content-type", "application/json"))
            except ValueError:
                body_bytes = body_str.encode("utf-8")

        def _do() -> Tuple[int, str]:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body_bytes, method=self.method)
            for k, v in headers:
                req.add_header(k, v)
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as resp:
                    status = resp.getcode()
                    raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                    return status, raw
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                raw = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                return e.code, raw

        status, text = await asyncio.to_thread(_do)
        try:
            parsed_body: Any = json.loads(text)
        except ValueError:
            parsed_body = text
        return {"status": status, "body": parsed_body}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/tools/python.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/tools/python.py)

```python
"""rc_python.tools.python — the Python language pack.

Seven developer-workflow tools, each a first-class
:class:`~rc_python.core.Tool`, that wrap the Python toolchain (`python3`,
`pip`, `black`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest`) behind the framework's sandbox +
permission gate. They are side-effecting (they spawn subprocesses), so the
default permission policy leaves them at `Ask`.

| tool | what it runs |
|------|--------------|
| `python.version`     | `python3 --version` |
| `python.pip_list`    | `python3 -m pip list --format=json` |
| `python.black`       | `black <path>` |
| `python.ruff`        | `ruff check <path>` |
| `python.mypy`        | `mypy <path>` |
| `python.pytest_run`  | `python3 -m pytest <path>` |
| `python.eval`        | evaluate a Python expression in-process |

Every subprocess tool returns the same shape the ``cli``/``declarative``
sources produce: ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str}``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from ..core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolSourceKind
from ..schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema


async def _run(argv: List[str], ctx: ToolContext, cwd: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Run ``argv`` and return ``{exit_code, stdout, stderr}``.

    Honours ``ctx.cancelled`` (returns early without spawning). Spawn failures
    (binary not on ``$PATH``) surface as :class:`ToolError`.
    """
    if ctx.cancelled:
        raise ToolError("cancelled before python tool", kind="other")
    try:
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            *argv,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            cwd=cwd,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        raise ToolError.tool_failed(argv[0], f"binary not found: {e.filename or argv[0]}") from None
    stdout_b, stderr_b = await proc.communicate()
    return {
        "exit_code": proc.returncode if proc.returncode is not None else -1,
        "stdout": stdout_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
        "stderr": stderr_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
    }


def _opt_str(input: Dict[str, Any], key: str) -> Optional[str]:
    v = input.get(key)
    return v if isinstance(v, str) else None


def _opt_str_array(input: Dict[str, Any], key: str) -> List[str]:
    v = input.get(key)
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return [x if isinstance(x, str) else str(x) for x in v]
    return []


# ─── python.version ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class Version(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "python.version"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Report the installed Python interpreter version."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new()

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        res = await _run(["python3", "--version"], ctx)
        line = res["stdout"].strip().splitlines()[0] if res["stdout"].strip() else ""
        return {"python": line, "exit_code": res["exit_code"]}


# ─── python.pip_list ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class PipList(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "python.pip_list"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "List installed pip packages as JSON."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new()

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        res = await _run(["python3", "-m", "pip", "list", "--format=json"], ctx)
        packages: Any
        try:
            packages = json.loads(res["stdout"])
        except ValueError:
            packages = []
        return {"packages": packages, "exit_code": res["exit_code"], "stderr": res["stderr"]}


# ─── the linter/test runner tools ────────────────────────────────────────────

def _path_schema(tool_desc_path: str) -> Schema:
    return (
        Schema.new()
        .param(Parameter.required("path", ParamType.string()).with_desc(tool_desc_path))
        .param(
            Parameter.optional("extra_args", ParamType.array(ParamType.string()))
            .with_desc("extra arguments forwarded after the path")
        )
    )


class _SubprocessTool(Tool):
    """Shared shape: one required ``path``, optional ``extra_args``, optional ``cwd``."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, desc: str, argv_prefix: List[str], path_desc: str) -> None:
        self._name = name
        self._desc = desc
        self._argv_prefix = list(argv_prefix)
        self._schema = _path_schema(path_desc)

    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._name

    def description(self) -> str:
        return self._desc

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return self._schema

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        path = input["path"]
        argv = self._argv_prefix + [path] + _opt_str_array(input, "extra_args")
        return await _run(argv, ctx, _opt_str(input, "cwd"))


def black() -> _SubprocessTool:
    return _SubprocessTool("python.black", "Run `black <path>` (format in place).", ["black"], "file or directory to format")


def ruff() -> _SubprocessTool:
    return _SubprocessTool("python.ruff", "Run `ruff check <path>` (lint).", ["ruff", "check"], "file or directory to lint")


def mypy() -> _SubprocessTool:
    return _SubprocessTool("python.mypy", "Run `mypy <path>` (type-check).", ["mypy"], "file or directory to type-check")


def pytest_run() -> _SubprocessTool:
    return _SubprocessTool("python.pytest_run", "Run `python -m pytest <path>`.", ["python3", "-m", "pytest"], "file or directory to test")


# ─── python.eval ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class Eval(Tool):
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "python.eval"

    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Evaluate a Python expression and return its value."

    def schema(self) -> Schema:
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("code", ParamType.string()).with_desc("the Python expression to evaluate"))

    def source(self) -> ToolSourceKind:
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input: Dict[str, Any], ctx: ToolContext) -> Any:
        import builtins
        code = input["code"]
        try:
            value = eval(code, {"__builtins__": builtins}, {})  # noqa: S307 — dev tool, user's own machine
        except Exception as e:
            raise ToolError.tool_failed("python.eval", f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}") from None
        # normalise non-JSON-serialisable values to their repr for transport
        try:
            json.dumps(value)
            return value
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return repr(value)


def all() -> List[Tool]:  # type: ignore[override]  # shadows builtin all() inside this module
    """Every `python.*` tool, ready to register."""
    return [Version(), PipList(), black(), ruff(), mypy(), pytest_run(), Eval()]


COUNT: int = 7
CATEGORY: str = "python"
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/validator.py`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-python/rc_python/validator.py)

```python
"""rc_python.validator — input validation (Python port of ``rc_core::validator``).

Check a Python dict against a tool's :class:`~rc_python.schema.Schema` before
the tool runs. Fills in defaults for missing optional parameters, so a tool's
``execute`` always sees a complete input.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict

from .core import ToolError
from .schema import Schema


def validate(schema: Schema, input: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate ``input`` against ``schema``.

    On success, returns a new dict with caller-supplied values copied through
    (after type-checking) and defaults applied for any missing optional
    parameters. Raises :class:`ToolError` on a type mismatch, a missing
    required parameter, or an out-of-enum value.
    """
    if not isinstance(input, dict):
        raise ToolError.validation("input must be a JSON object (dict)")

    out: Dict[str, Any] = {k: v for k, v in input.items()}

    for p in schema.parameters:
        if p.name in out:
            v = out[p.name]
            # type-check
            try:
                p.typ.check(v)
            except ValueError as detail:
                raise ToolError.bad_param(p.name, str(p.typ), str(detail)) from None
            # enum constraint
            if p.enum_values and v not in p.enum_values:
                raise ToolError.bad_param(
                    p.name, str(p.typ), f"value {v!r} is not one of the allowed values"
                ) from None
        else:
            if p.required:
                raise ToolError.validation(f"missing required parameter `{p.name}`")
            if p.default is not None:
                out[p.name] = p.default

    return out


class Validator:
    """Public facade matching the docs (``Validator.validate``)."""

    @staticmethod
    def validate(schema: Schema, input: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return validate(schema, input)
```

"""Compose layer tests — pipeline, parallel, branch over the builtin catalog."""
import asyncio

from rc_python import Lifecycle, BuiltinSource
from rc_python.compose import (
    BranchArm,
    BranchTool,
    ParallelStep,
    ParallelTool,
    PipelineStep,
    PipelineTool,
)


def _life():
    life = Lifecycle.permissive()
    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())
    asyncio.run(life.discover())
    return life


def test_pipeline_chains_add_then_sqrt():
    life = _life()
    pipe = PipelineTool(
        name="compose.pipe.sqrt_of_sum",
        description="add a+b then sqrt the sum",
        steps=[
            PipelineStep(tool="math.add"),                                  # {a,b} -> number
            PipelineStep(tool="math.sqrt", template={"n": "{{prev}}"}),     # prev -> sqrt
        ],
        executor=life.executor,
    )
    life.register(pipe)
    out = asyncio.run(life.execute("compose.pipe.sqrt_of_sum", {"a": 7, "b": 18}, True))
    # 7 + 18 = 25, sqrt(25) = 5.0
    assert out == 5.0


def test_parallel_fans_out():
    life = _life()
    par = ParallelTool(
        name="compose.par.sum_and_root",
        description="add a+b and sqrt n in parallel",
        steps=[
            ParallelStep(name="sum", tool="math.add", template={"a": "{{input.a}}", "b": "{{input.b}}"}),
            ParallelStep(name="root", tool="math.sqrt", template={"n": "{{input.n}}"}),
        ],
        executor=life.executor,
    )
    life.register(par)
    out = asyncio.run(life.execute("compose.par.sum_and_root", {"a": 2, "b": 3, "n": 9}, True))
    assert out == {"sum": 5.0, "root": 3.0}


def test_branch_first_match_wins_and_falls_through():
    life = _life()
    br = BranchTool(
        name="compose.branch.pick",
        description="sqrt when use_sqrt else add",
        arms=[
            BranchArm(tool="math.sqrt", when="{{input.use_sqrt}}", template={"n": "{{input.n}}"}),
            BranchArm(tool="math.add", when=None, template={"a": "{{input.a}}", "b": "{{input.b}}"}),
        ],
        executor=life.executor,
    )
    life.register(br)
    # first arm matches (truthy) -> sqrt(9) = 3.0
    out = asyncio.run(life.execute("compose.branch.pick", {"use_sqrt": "yes", "n": 9, "a": 1, "b": 1}, True))
    assert out == 3.0
    # first arm empty -> catch-all -> add(2,3) = 5.0
    out2 = asyncio.run(life.execute("compose.branch.pick", {"use_sqrt": "", "n": 0, "a": 2, "b": 3}, True))
    assert out2 == 5.0
