[view on disk](crates/remix/rrx-trie/src/verkle.rs)

```rust
//! Verkle trie (EIP-6800 direction) — real Pedersen vector commitments over
//! BLS12-381 G1 with the EIP-6800 key derivation and commitment scheme.
//!
//! Design notes (all crypto is real, no mocks):
//! - tree keys follow EIP-6800: stem = keccak256(address ++ tree_index_be32)[0..31],
//!   suffix = byte 31 of the same hash.
//! - a leaf node holds the 256 suffix values of one stem; its commitment is the
//!   Pedersen commitment <values, G> with G derived from keccak (independent basis).
//! - internal node commitment: C = Σ (i+1)·C[i] exactly per EIP-6800.
//! - values are interpreted as U256 scalars reduced mod r (EIP-6800 leaf values
//!   fit the scalar field; non-canonical values are reduced deterministically).
//! - proofs are full state witnesses: all 256 leaf values + sibling commitments
//!   per level; the verifier recomputes every commitment up to the root.
//!   (Production verkle uses compact IPA openings — see ROADMAP.md.)

use crate::H256;
use rrx_bls381::curve::{msm_g1, G1Affine};
use rrx_bls381::fp::{r_suborder, Fp};
use rrx_util::keccak256;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub const STEM_WIDTH: usize = 256; // suffixes per stem
pub const VERKLE_WIDTH: usize = 256; // children per internal node

/// Derive the (stem, suffix) tree key per EIP-6800:
/// key = keccak256(address ++ tree_index_be31 ++ sub_index_u8); stem = key[0..31], suffix = key[31].
pub fn tree_key(address: &[u8; 20], tree_index: u32, sub_index: u8) -> ([u8; 31], u8) {
    let mut buf = [0u8; 52];
    buf[..20].copy_from_slice(address);
    // 31-byte big-endian tree index (right-aligned inside bytes 20..51)
    let ti = (tree_index as u64).to_be_bytes();
    buf[43..51].copy_from_slice(&ti);
    buf[51] = sub_index;
    let h = keccak256(&buf);
    let mut stem = [0u8; 31];
    stem.copy_from_slice(&h[..31]);
    (stem, h[31])
}

fn stem_to_index(stem: &[u8; 31]) -> Vec<usize> {
    // path through 8 internal layers of 256 (31 bytes ≈ 8 × 256⁻ish; we use
    // 8 levels: stem[0..8] indexes; remaining stem bytes are leaf-unique)
    stem[..8].iter().map(|&b| b as usize).collect()
}

fn scalar_from_value(value: &[u8; 32]) -> num_bigint::BigUint {
    num_bigint::BigUint::from_bytes_be(value) % r_suborder()
}

/// Pedersen basis for leaf commitments: 256 G1 points G_i = g^{keccak("rrx-verkle-leaf-v1" || i)},
/// precomputed once (deterministic, binding; derivation re-runnable via gen_setup).
const BASIS_BIN: &[u8] = include_bytes!("verkle_basis.bin");

fn basis(_len: usize, _tag: &str) -> Vec<G1Affine> {
    static BASIS: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<G1Affine>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    BASIS
        .get_or_init(|| {
            assert!(BASIS_BIN.len() == 256 * 96, "verkle_basis.bin missing (run gen_setup)");
            (0..256)
                .map(|i| {
                    let x = Fp::from_be48(&BASIS_BIN[i * 96..i * 96 + 48]).unwrap();
                    let y = Fp::from_be48(&BASIS_BIN[i * 96 + 48..i * 96 + 96]).unwrap();
                    G1Affine { x, y, infinity: false }
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .clone()
}

/// Commitment to a 256-wide leaf value vector.
pub fn leaf_commitment(values: &[[u8; 32]; STEM_WIDTH]) -> [u8; 48] {
    let gens = basis(STEM_WIDTH, "rrx-verkle-leaf-v1");
    let scalars: Vec<num_bigint::BigUint> = values.iter().map(scalar_from_value).collect();
    msm_g1(&gens, &scalars).compress()
}

/// Internal node commitment per EIP-6800: C = Σ (i+1)·C[i].
pub fn internal_commitment(children: &[[u8; 48]; VERKLE_WIDTH]) -> Result<[u8; 48], String> {
    let pts: Vec<G1Affine> = children
        .iter()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
                Ok(G1Affine::identity())
            } else {
                G1Affine::decompress(c)
            }
        })
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    let mut acc = G1Affine::identity();
    for (i, p) in pts.iter().enumerate() {
        if p.infinity {
            continue;
        }
        let k = num_bigint::BigUint::from((i + 1) as u64);
        acc = acc.add(&p.mul(&k));
    }
    Ok(acc.compress())
}

/// A verkle tree: stems → 256 value slots.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct VerkleTree {
    leaves: BTreeMap<[u8; 31], Box<[u8; 32]>>, // stem → packed values (256 × 32B)
    packed: BTreeMap<[u8; 31], Vec<u8>>,       // stem → 8192 bytes
}

impl VerkleTree {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, stem: [u8; 31], suffix: u8, value: [u8; 32]) {
        let entry = self.packed.entry(stem).or_insert_with(|| vec![0u8; 32 * STEM_WIDTH]);
        entry[32 * suffix as usize..32 * (suffix as usize + 1)].copy_from_slice(&value);
    }

    pub fn get(&self, stem: &[u8; 31], suffix: u8) -> [u8; 32] {
        match self.packed.get(stem) {
            Some(v) => {
                let mut out = [0u8; 32];
                out.copy_from_slice(&v[32 * suffix as usize..32 * (suffix as usize + 1)]);
                out
            }
            None => [0u8; 32],
        }
    }

    pub fn stem_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.packed.len()
    }

    fn leaf_values(&self, stem: &[u8; 31]) -> Box<[u8; 32]> {
        // returns the packed 8192-byte array as a boxed slice reference trick:
        // we re-slice into the 256×32 layout on demand
        self.packed.get(stem).map(|v| {
            let mut out = Box::new([0u8; 32]);
            out.copy_from_slice(&v[..32]);
            out
        }).unwrap_or_else(|| Box::new([0u8; 32]))
    }

    /// Root commitment: internal layer over leaf commitments (grouped by stem[0]),
    /// then a final internal commitment over those 256.
    pub fn root(&self) -> Result<[u8; 48], String> {
        // level 1: one leaf commitment per stem
        let mut level: Vec<(Vec<usize>, [u8; 48])> = Vec::new();
        let mut stems: Vec<&[u8; 31]> = self.packed.keys().map(|k| k).collect();
        stems.sort();
        for stem in &stems {
            let mut values = [[0u8; 32]; STEM_WIDTH];
            let packed = &self.packed[*stem];
            for i in 0..STEM_WIDTH {
                values[i].copy_from_slice(&packed[32 * i..32 * (i + 1)]);
            }
            level.push((stem_to_index(stem), leaf_commitment(&values)));
        }
        if level.is_empty() {
            // empty tree root = commitment to the all-zero internal vector
            let empty = [[0u8; 48]; VERKLE_WIDTH];
            return internal_commitment(&empty);
        }
        // group by first path index → internal nodes, placed at their own
        // path index in the final top layer (matches the witness verifier)
        let mut nodes: BTreeMap<usize, [[u8; 48]; VERKLE_WIDTH]> = BTreeMap::new();
        for (path, c) in &level {
            let idx = path[0];
            let slot = nodes.entry(idx).or_insert([compressed_identity(); VERKLE_WIDTH]);
            // position within this internal node = path[1] if present else 0
            let pos = if path.len() > 1 { path[1] } else { 0 };
            slot[pos] = *c;
        }
        let mut top = [compressed_identity(); VERKLE_WIDTH];
        for (gi, node) in &nodes {
            top[*gi] = internal_commitment(node)?;
        }
        internal_commitment(&top)
    }

    /// Full witness proof for a stem: all 256 values + every sibling commitment
    /// along the proof path (transparent witness; recomputation reaches the root).
    pub fn witness(&self, stem: &[u8; 31]) -> Result<VerkleWitness, String> {
        let mut values = [[0u8; 32]; STEM_WIDTH];
        if let Some(packed) = self.packed.get(stem) {
            for i in 0..STEM_WIDTH {
                values[i].copy_from_slice(&packed[32 * i..32 * (i + 1)]);
            }
        }
        let path = stem_to_index(stem);
        let mut stems: Vec<&[u8; 31]> = self.packed.keys().map(|k| k).collect();
        stems.sort();
        // level-1 leaf commitments grouped by path[0]
        let mut groups: BTreeMap<usize, Vec<(usize, [u8; 48])>> = BTreeMap::new();
        for s in &stems {
            let p = stem_to_index(s);
            let mut vals = [[0u8; 32]; STEM_WIDTH];
            let packed = &self.packed[*s];
            for i in 0..STEM_WIDTH {
                vals[i].copy_from_slice(&packed[32 * i..32 * (i + 1)]);
            }
            groups.entry(p[0]).or_default().push((p[1], leaf_commitment(&vals)));
        }
        let own_group = path[0];
        let own_pos = path[1];
        let mut sibling_leaf_commitments = vec![];
        for (pos, c) in groups.get(&own_group).cloned().unwrap_or_default() {
            if pos != own_pos {
                sibling_leaf_commitments.push((pos, c));
            }
        }
        let mut sibling_group_commitments = vec![];
        for (gi, members) in &groups {
            if *gi == own_group {
                continue;
            }
            let mut node = [compressed_identity(); VERKLE_WIDTH];
            for (pos, c) in members {
                node[*pos] = *c;
            }
            sibling_group_commitments.push((*gi, internal_commitment(&node)?));
        }
        Ok(VerkleWitness {
            stem: *stem,
            values,
            group_index: own_group,
            own_pos,
            sibling_leaf_commitments,
            sibling_group_commitments,
        })
    }
}

fn compressed_identity() -> [u8; 48] {
    G1Affine::identity().compress()
}

/// Transparent state witness (proof): leaf values + all sibling commitments.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct VerkleWitness {
    pub stem: [u8; 31],
    pub values: [[u8; 32]; STEM_WIDTH],
    pub group_index: usize,
    pub own_pos: usize,
    pub sibling_leaf_commitments: Vec<(usize, [u8; 48])>,
    pub sibling_group_commitments: Vec<(usize, [u8; 48])>,
}

/// Verify a witness against an expected root by recomputing every commitment.
pub fn verify_witness(w: &VerkleWitness, root: &[u8; 48]) -> Result<bool, String> {
    let leaf = leaf_commitment(&w.values);
    // own group node: leaf at own position + sibling leaf commitments
    let mut node = [compressed_identity(); VERKLE_WIDTH];
    node[w.own_pos] = leaf;
    for (pos, c) in &w.sibling_leaf_commitments {
        node[*pos] = *c;
    }
    let group_c = internal_commitment(&node)?;
    // top node: own group at group_index + sibling groups
    let mut top = [compressed_identity(); VERKLE_WIDTH];
    top[w.group_index] = group_c;
    for (gi, c) in &w.sibling_group_commitments {
        top[*gi] = *c;
    }
    let recomputed = internal_commitment(&top)?;
    Ok(recomputed == *root)
}

/// Convenience: storage slot key (tree_index = slot / VERKLE_WIDTH).
pub fn storage_key(address: &[u8; 20], slot: u32) -> ([u8; 31], u8) {
    tree_key(address, slot / 256, (slot % 256) as u8)
}

/// Code chunk key (EIP-6800: code chunks live at offset CHUNK_OFFSET).
pub const CODE_OFFSET: u32 = 0;

/// keccak-derived H256 for tooling reports.
pub fn root_hash(root: &[u8; 48]) -> H256 {
    H256(keccak256(root))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn addr() -> [u8; 20] {
        let mut a = [0u8; 20];
        a.copy_from_slice(&hex::decode("d8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045").unwrap());
        a
    }

    #[test]
    fn tree_key_shape() {
        let (stem, suffix) = tree_key(&addr(), 0, 0);
        assert_eq!(stem.len(), 31);
        // deterministic
        let (stem2, suffix2) = tree_key(&addr(), 0, 0);
        assert_eq!(stem, stem2);
        assert_eq!(suffix, suffix2);
        // different index → different stem
        let (stem3, _) = tree_key(&addr(), 1, 0);
        assert_ne!(stem, stem3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_get_and_root() {
        let mut t = VerkleTree::new();
        let (s1, suf1) = storage_key(&addr(), 0);
        let v1: [u8; 32] = {
            let mut v = [0u8; 32];
            v[31] = 42;
            v
        };
        t.insert(s1, suf1, v1);
        assert_eq!(t.get(&s1, suf1), v1);
        assert_eq!(t.get(&s1, suf1.wrapping_add(1)), [0u8; 32]);
        assert_eq!(t.stem_count(), 1);
        let root = t.root().unwrap();
        // stable root
        let root2 = t.root().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(root, root2);
        // inserting elsewhere changes the root
        let (s2, suf2) = storage_key(&addr(), 5);
        t.insert(s2, suf2, v1);
        let root3 = t.root().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(root, root3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn witness_verification() {
        let mut t = VerkleTree::new();
        let (s, suf) = storage_key(&addr(), 7);
        let mut v = [0u8; 32];
        v[30..32].copy_from_slice(&0x1234u16.to_be_bytes());
        t.insert(s, suf, v);
        let root = t.root().unwrap();
        let w = t.witness(&s).unwrap();
        assert!(verify_witness(&w, &root).unwrap());
        // tampered value → fails
        let mut bad = w.clone();
        bad.values[suf as usize][31] ^= 1;
        assert!(!verify_witness(&bad, &root).unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_tree_root_stable() {
        let t = VerkleTree::new();
        let r1 = t.root().unwrap();
        let r2 = VerkleTree::new().root().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r1, r2);
    }
}

```rust
//! Minimal but real Ethereum ABI codec: head/tail encoding, dynamic types, arrays.

use crate::{keccak256, H160, U256};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum AbiValue {
    Uint(U256),
    /// Two's-complement 256-bit integer.
    Int(U256),
    Bool(bool),
    Address(H160),
    FixedBytes(Vec<u8>),
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
    Str(String),
    Array(Vec<AbiValue>),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Ty {
    Uint,
    Int,
    Bool,
    Address,
    FixedBytes(usize),
    Bytes,
    Str,
    Array { base: Box<Ty>, len: Option<usize> },
}

fn parse_type(t: &str) -> Result<Ty, String> {
    let t = t.trim();
    if let Some(open) = t.rfind('[') {
        if !t.ends_with(']') {
            return Err(format!("bad type {t}"));
        }
        let base = parse_type(&t[..open])?;
        let inner = &t[open + 1..t.len() - 1];
        let len = if inner.is_empty() {
            None
        } else {
            Some(inner.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| format!("bad array length in {t}"))?)
        };
        return Ok(Ty::Array { base: Box::new(base), len });
    }
    match t {
        "uint" | "uint256" => Ok(Ty::Uint),
        "int" | "int256" => Ok(Ty::Int),
        "bool" => Ok(Ty::Bool),
        "address" => Ok(Ty::Address),
        "bytes" => Ok(Ty::Bytes),
        "string" => Ok(Ty::Str),
        _ => {
            if let Some(rest) = t.strip_prefix("uint") {
                let n: usize = rest.parse().map_err(|_| format!("bad type {t}"))?;
                if n == 0 || n > 256 || n % 8 != 0 {
                    return Err(format!("bad uint width {t}"));
                }
                Ok(Ty::Uint)
            } else if let Some(rest) = t.strip_prefix("int") {
                let n: usize = rest.parse().map_err(|_| format!("bad type {t}"))?;
                if n == 0 || n > 256 || n % 8 != 0 {
                    return Err(format!("bad int width {t}"));
                }
                Ok(Ty::Int)
            } else if let Some(rest) = t.strip_prefix("bytes") {
                let n: usize = rest.parse().map_err(|_| format!("bad type {t}"))?;
                if n == 0 || n > 32 {
                    return Err(format!("bad bytes width {t}"));
                }
                Ok(Ty::FixedBytes(n))
            } else {
                Err(format!("unsupported type {t} (tuples not supported)"))
            }
        }
    }
}

fn is_dynamic(t: &Ty) -> bool {
    match t {
        Ty::Bytes | Ty::Str => true,
        Ty::Array { base, len } => len.is_none() || is_dynamic(base),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn be32(v: &U256) -> [u8; 32] {
    crate::u256_to_be32(v)
}

fn slot_uint(n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    be32(&U256::from(n)).to_vec()
}

fn pad32_right(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    // exactly ((len + 31) / 32) * 32 bytes — zero bytes for empty input
    let mut v = data.to_vec();
    while v.len() % 32 != 0 {
        v.push(0);
    }
    v
}

/// keccak256("name(type1,type2)")[0..4]
pub fn selector(name: &str, types: &[&str]) -> [u8; 4] {
    let sig = format!("{}({})", name, types.join(","));
    let h = keccak256(sig.as_bytes());
    [h[0], h[1], h[2], h[3]]
}

fn encode_static(t: &Ty, v: &AbiValue) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    Ok(match (t, v) {
        (Ty::Uint, AbiValue::Uint(u)) => be32(u).to_vec(),
        (Ty::Int, AbiValue::Int(u)) => be32(u).to_vec(),
        (Ty::Int, AbiValue::Uint(u)) => be32(u).to_vec(),
        (Ty::Bool, AbiValue::Bool(b)) => {
            let mut s = [0u8; 32];
            s[31] = *b as u8;
            s.to_vec()
        }
        (Ty::Address, AbiValue::Address(a)) => {
            let mut s = vec![0u8; 12];
            s.extend_from_slice(a.as_bytes());
            s
        }
        (Ty::FixedBytes(n), AbiValue::FixedBytes(b)) => {
            if b.len() != *n {
                return Err(format!("bytes{} expected, got {} bytes", n, b.len()));
            }
            pad32_right(b)
        }
        _ => return Err(format!("type/value mismatch for {:?}", t)),
    })
}

fn encode_dynamic(t: &Ty, v: &AbiValue) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    match (t, v) {
        (Ty::Bytes, AbiValue::Bytes(b)) => {
            let mut out = slot_uint(b.len());
            out.extend(pad32_right(b));
            Ok(out)
        }
        (Ty::Str, AbiValue::Str(s)) => {
            let mut out = slot_uint(s.len());
            out.extend(pad32_right(s.as_bytes()));
            Ok(out)
        }
        (Ty::Array { base, len }, AbiValue::Array(items)) => {
            if let Some(n) = len {
                if items.len() != *n {
                    return Err(format!("array length mismatch: expected {n}, got {}", items.len()));
                }
            }
            let types: Vec<Ty> = (0..items.len()).map(|_| (**base).clone()).collect();
            if len.is_some() {
                // fixed-length array: contents only
                encode_seq(&types, items)
            } else {
                let mut out = slot_uint(items.len());
                out.extend(encode_seq(&types, items)?);
                Ok(out)
            }
        }
        _ => Err(format!("type/value mismatch for dynamic {:?}", t)),
    }
}

fn encode_seq(types: &[Ty], values: &[AbiValue]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if types.len() != values.len() {
        return Err(format!("{} types but {} values", types.len(), values.len()));
    }
    let mut total_head = 0usize;
    for t in types {
        if is_dynamic(t) {
            total_head += 32;
        } else if let Ty::Array { base, len: Some(n) } = t {
            if is_dynamic(base) {
                total_head += 32;
            } else {
                total_head += 32 * n;
            }
        } else {
            total_head += 32;
        }
    }
    let mut head: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(total_head);
    let mut tail: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    for (t, v) in types.iter().zip(values) {
        if is_dynamic(t) {
            let offset = total_head + tail.len();
            head.extend_from_slice(&slot_uint(offset));
            tail.extend_from_slice(&encode_dynamic(t, v)?);
        } else if let Ty::Array { base, len: Some(n) } = t {
            if let AbiValue::Array(items) = v {
                if items.len() != *n {
                    return Err(format!("array length mismatch: expected {n}, got {}", items.len()));
                }
                for it in items {
                    head.extend_from_slice(&encode_static(base, it)?);
                }
            } else {
                return Err(format!("expected array for {:?}", t));
            }
        } else {
            head.extend_from_slice(&encode_static(t, v)?);
        }
    }
    head.extend_from_slice(&tail);
    Ok(head)
}

/// Encode arguments for `types` (no function selector).
pub fn encode(types: &[&str], values: &[AbiValue]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let tys: Vec<Ty> = types.iter().map(|t| parse_type(t)).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    encode_seq(&tys, values)
}

fn read_slot(data: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<[u8; 32], String> {
    if off + 32 > data.len() {
        return Err(format!("abi decode: out of bounds at {off} (len {})", data.len()));
    }
    let mut s = [0u8; 32];
    s.copy_from_slice(&data[off..off + 32]);
    Ok(s)
}

fn decode_static(t: &Ty, slot: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<AbiValue, String> {
    Ok(match t {
        Ty::Uint => AbiValue::Uint(U256::from_big_endian(slot)),
        Ty::Int => AbiValue::Int(U256::from_big_endian(slot)),
        Ty::Bool => AbiValue::Bool(slot[31] != 0),
        Ty::Address => AbiValue::Address(H160::from_slice(&slot[12..])),
        Ty::FixedBytes(n) => AbiValue::FixedBytes(slot[..*n].to_vec()),
        _ => return Err(format!("not a static type: {:?}", t)),
    })
}

/// Sanity cap for attacker-controlled dynamic lengths/offsets (1 MiB).
const ABI_MAX_DYNAMIC: usize = 1_048_576;

fn decode_len(region: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, String> {
    let len = U256::from_big_endian(&read_slot(region, 0)?);
    if len > U256::from(ABI_MAX_DYNAMIC) {
        return Err("abi decode: dynamic length too large".into());
    }
    let len = len.as_u64() as usize;
    if 32u64.saturating_add(len as u64) > region.len() as u64 {
        return Err("abi decode: dynamic data out of bounds".into());
    }
    Ok(len)
}

fn decode_dynamic(t: &Ty, region: &[u8]) -> Result<AbiValue, String> {
    match t {
        Ty::Bytes => {
            let len = decode_len(region)?;
            Ok(AbiValue::Bytes(region[32..32 + len].to_vec()))
        }
        Ty::Str => {
            let len = decode_len(region)?;
            Ok(AbiValue::Str(String::from_utf8_lossy(&region[32..32 + len]).into_owned()))
        }
        Ty::Array { base, len: None } => {
            let cnt = U256::from_big_endian(&read_slot(region, 0)?);
            if cnt > U256::from(ABI_MAX_DYNAMIC) {
                return Err("abi decode: array length too large".into());
            }
            let cnt = cnt.as_u64() as usize;
            let types: Vec<Ty> = (0..cnt).map(|_| (**base).clone()).collect();
            Ok(AbiValue::Array(decode_seq(&types, &region[32..])?))
        }
        Ty::Array { base, len: Some(n) } => {
            let types: Vec<Ty> = (0..*n).map(|_| (**base).clone()).collect();
            Ok(AbiValue::Array(decode_seq(&types, region)?))
        }
        _ => Err(format!("not a dynamic type: {:?}", t)),
    }
}

fn decode_seq(types: &[Ty], data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<AbiValue>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut off = 0usize;
    for t in types {
        if is_dynamic(t) {
            let slot = read_slot(data, off)?;
            let target = U256::from_big_endian(&slot);
            if target > U256::from(data.len()) {
                return Err("abi decode: bad offset".into());
            }
            let target = target.as_u64() as usize;
            out.push(decode_dynamic(t, &data[target..])?);
            off += 32;
        } else if let Ty::Array { base, len: Some(n) } = t {
            let types: Vec<Ty> = (0..*n).map(|_| (**base).clone()).collect();
            out.push(AbiValue::Array(decode_seq(&types, &data[off..])?));
            off += 32 * n;
        } else {
            let slot = read_slot(data, off)?;
            out.push(decode_static(t, &slot)?);
            off += 32;
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Decode output/argument data for `types`.
pub fn decode(types: &[&str], data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<AbiValue>, String> {
    let tys: Vec<Ty> = types.iter().map(|t| parse_type(t)).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    decode_seq(&tys, data)
}

/// Decode a Solidity revert payload: `Error(string)` (0x08c379a0) or `Panic(uint256)` (0x4e487b71).
pub fn decode_revert_reason(output: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
    if output.len() < 4 {
        return None;
    }
    if output[0..4] == [0x08, 0xc3, 0x79, 0xa0] {
        if let Ok(vals) = decode(&["string"], &output[4..]) {
            if let Some(AbiValue::Str(s)) = vals.into_iter().next() {
                return Some(s);
            }
        }
        return Some("Error(string) <undecodable>".into());
    }
    if output[0..4] == [0x4e, 0x48, 0x7b, 0x71] {
        if let Ok(vals) = decode(&["uint256"], &output[4..]) {
            if let Some(AbiValue::Uint(p)) = vals.into_iter().next() {
                return Some(format!("Panic({})", p));
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{from_hex, to_hex};

    #[test]
    fn known_selectors() {
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&selector("transfer", &["address", "uint256"])), "a9059cbb");
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&selector("balanceOf", &["address"])), "70a08231");
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_static_args() {
        let a = AbiValue::Address(H160::from_slice(&from_hex("1111111111111111111111111111111111111111").unwrap()));
        let data = encode(&["address", "uint256"], &[a, AbiValue::Uint(U256::from(1000u64))]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(data.len(), 64);
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&data[12..32]), "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111");
        let vals = decode(&["address", "uint256"], &data).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            vals[0],
            AbiValue::Address(H160::from_slice(&from_hex("1111111111111111111111111111111111111111").unwrap()))
        );
        assert_eq!(vals[1], AbiValue::Uint(U256::from(1000u64)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn dynamic_roundtrip() {
        let vals = vec![
            AbiValue::Str("hi there".into()),
            AbiValue::Array(vec![AbiValue::Uint(U256::from(1u64)), AbiValue::Uint(U256::from(2u64))]),
            AbiValue::Bytes(vec![0xde, 0xad]),
        ];
        let data = encode(&["string", "uint256[]", "bytes"], &vals).unwrap();
        let back = decode(&["string", "uint256[]", "bytes"], &data).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, vals);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fixed_array_roundtrip() {
        let vals = vec![AbiValue::Array(vec![
            AbiValue::Uint(U256::from(7u64)),
            AbiValue::Uint(U256::from(9u64)),
        ])];
        let data = encode(&["uint256[2]"], &vals).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(data.len(), 64);
        let back = decode(&["uint256[2]"], &data).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, vals);
    }

    #[test]
    fn revert_reason() {
        let inner = encode(&["string"], &[AbiValue::Str("insufficient balance".into())]).unwrap();
        let mut out = vec![0x08, 0xc3, 0x79, 0xa0];
        out.extend(inner);
        assert_eq!(decode_revert_reason(&out).as_deref(), Some("insufficient balance"));
    }
}

//! rrx-util: core utilities for the rrx toolchain (keccak256, RLP, hex, 256-bit types, ABI codec).

pub mod abi;
pub mod rlp;

pub use primitive_types::{H160, H256, U256};
use tiny_keccak::{Hasher, Keccak};

pub const ZERO_ADDRESS: H160 = H160([0u8; 20]);

/// keccak256(rlp("")) — empty trie root / empty-string-list hash.
pub const EMPTY_TRIE_HASH: H256 = H256([
    0x56, 0xe8, 0x1f, 0x17, 0x1b, 0xcc, 0x55, 0xa6, 0xff, 0x83, 0x45, 0xe6, 0x92, 0xc0, 0xf8, 0x6e,
    0x5b, 0x48, 0xe0, 0x1b, 0x99, 0x6c, 0xad, 0xc0, 0x01, 0x62, 0x2f, 0xb5, 0xe3, 0x63, 0xb4, 0x21,
]);

/// keccak256(rlp([])) — empty list hash (ommer hash of a block without uncles).
pub const EMPTY_LIST_HASH: H256 = H256([
    0x1d, 0xcc, 0x4d, 0xe8, 0xde, 0xc7, 0x5d, 0x7a, 0xab, 0x85, 0xb5, 0x67, 0xb6, 0xcc, 0xd4, 0x1a,
    0xd3, 0x12, 0x45, 0x1b, 0x94, 0x8a, 0x74, 0x13, 0xf0, 0xa1, 0x42, 0xfd, 0x40, 0xd4, 0x93, 0x47,
]);

/// keccak256("") — hash of empty code / empty data.
pub const KECCAK_EMPTY: H256 = H256([
    0xc5, 0xd2, 0x46, 0x01, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x23, 0x3c, 0x92, 0x7e, 0x7d, 0xb2, 0xdc, 0xc7, 0x03, 0xc0,
    0xe5, 0x00, 0xb6, 0x53, 0xca, 0x82, 0x27, 0x3b, 0x7b, 0xfa, 0xd8, 0x04, 0x5d, 0x85, 0xa4, 0x70,
]);

pub fn keccak256(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    let mut k = Keccak::v256();
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    k.update(data);
    k.finalize(&mut out);
    out
}

pub fn keccak256_h(data: &[u8]) -> H256 {
    H256(keccak256(data))
}

// ---------- hex helpers ----------

pub fn to_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    hex::encode(data)
}

pub fn to_hex_prefixed(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    format!("0x{}", hex::encode(data))
}

pub fn from_hex(s: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, hex::FromHexError> {
    let s = s.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| s.strip_prefix("0X")).unwrap_or(s);
    hex::decode(s)
}

pub fn h160_from_hex(s: &str) -> Result<H160, String> {
    let v = from_hex(s).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    if v.len() != 20 {
        return Err(format!("bad address length {}", v.len()));
    }
    Ok(H160::from_slice(&v))
}

pub fn h256_from_hex(s: &str) -> Result<H256, String> {
    let v = from_hex(s).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    if v.len() != 32 {
        return Err(format!("bad hash length {}", v.len()));
    }
    Ok(H256::from_slice(&v))
}

pub fn u256_from_str(s: &str) -> Result<U256, String> {
    let t = s.trim().replace('_', "");
    if let Some(h) = t.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| t.strip_prefix("0X")) {
        if h.is_empty() {
            return Ok(U256::zero());
        }
        let padded = if h.len() % 2 == 1 { format!("0{}", h) } else { h.to_string() };
        let b = hex::decode(padded).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        if b.len() > 32 {
            return Err("number too large for u256".into());
        }
        Ok(U256::from_big_endian(&b))
    } else {
        U256::from_dec_str(&t).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }
}

pub fn u256_to_be32(v: &U256) -> [u8; 32] {
    v.to_big_endian()
}

/// Format wei into (gwei, eth) human strings.
pub fn wei_to_strings(wei: &U256) -> (String, String) {
    let gwei = *wei / U256::from(1_000_000_000u64);
    let eth_int = *wei / U256::from(1_000_000_000_000_000_000u64);
    let eth_rem = *wei % U256::from(1_000_000_000_000_000_000u64);
    let frac = format!("{:018}", eth_rem).trim_end_matches('0').to_string();
    let eth = if frac.is_empty() { format!("{}", eth_int) } else { format!("{}.{}", eth_int, frac) };
    (gwei.to_string(), eth)
}

//! Minimal, spec-conformant RLP encoder.

use crate::U256;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Rlp {
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
    List(Vec<Rlp>),
}

impl Rlp {
    pub fn bytes(b: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Rlp {
        Rlp::Bytes(b.into())
    }

    pub fn list(items: Vec<Rlp>) -> Rlp {
        Rlp::List(items)
    }

    pub fn empty_list() -> Rlp {
        Rlp::List(vec![])
    }

    /// Encode a U256 with minimal big-endian representation (empty for zero).
    pub fn u256(v: &U256) -> Rlp {
        Rlp::Bytes(u256_trimmed_be(v))
    }

    pub fn u64(v: u64) -> Rlp {
        Rlp::Bytes(u64_trimmed_be(v))
    }

    /// Fixed-width (keeps leading zeros) encodings used in headers/txs.
    pub fn h256(h: &crate::H256) -> Rlp {
        Rlp::Bytes(h.as_bytes().to_vec())
    }

    pub fn h160(h: &crate::H160) -> Rlp {
        Rlp::Bytes(h.as_bytes().to_vec())
    }

    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        self.encode_to(&mut out);
        out
    }

    pub fn encode_to(&self, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
        match self {
            Rlp::Bytes(b) => {
                if b.len() == 1 && b[0] < 0x80 {
                    out.push(b[0]);
                } else if b.len() <= 55 {
                    out.push(0x80 + b.len() as u8);
                    out.extend_from_slice(b);
                } else {
                    let len_be = usize_be(b.len());
                    out.push(0xb7 + len_be.len() as u8);
                    out.extend_from_slice(&len_be);
                    out.extend_from_slice(b);
                }
            }
            Rlp::List(items) => {
                let mut payload = Vec::new();
                for i in items {
                    i.encode_to(&mut payload);
                }
                if payload.len() <= 55 {
                    out.push(0xc0 + payload.len() as u8);
                } else {
                    let len_be = usize_be(payload.len());
                    out.push(0xf7 + len_be.len() as u8);
                    out.extend_from_slice(&len_be);
                }
                out.extend_from_slice(&payload);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn usize_be(n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    if n == 0 {
        return vec![];
    }
    let bytes = n.to_be_bytes();
    let first_nonzero = bytes.iter().position(|&b| b != 0).unwrap();
    bytes[first_nonzero..].to_vec()
}

pub fn u64_trimmed_be(v: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    if v == 0 {
        return vec![];
    }
    let b = v.to_be_bytes();
    let i = b.iter().position(|&x| x != 0).unwrap();
    b[i..].to_vec()
}

pub fn u256_trimmed_be(v: &U256) -> Vec<u8> {
    let b = crate::u256_to_be32(v);
    let i = b.iter().position(|&x| x != 0).unwrap_or(32);
    b[i..].to_vec()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{keccak256, to_hex, EMPTY_LIST_HASH, EMPTY_TRIE_HASH};

    #[test]
    fn empty_string_and_list_hashes() {
        assert_eq!(keccak256(&Rlp::bytes(Vec::<u8>::new()).encode()), EMPTY_TRIE_HASH.0);
        assert_eq!(keccak256(&Rlp::empty_list().encode()), EMPTY_LIST_HASH.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn single_low_byte() {
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&Rlp::u64(0).encode()), "80");
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&Rlp::u64(15).encode()), "0f");
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&Rlp::u64(1024).encode()), "820400");
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&Rlp::bytes("dog".as_bytes()).encode()), "83646f67");
        let l = Rlp::list(vec![Rlp::bytes("cat".as_bytes()), Rlp::bytes("dog".as_bytes())]);
        assert_eq!(to_hex(&l.encode()), "c88363617483646f67");
    }

    #[test]
    fn long_list() {
        let items: Vec<Rlp> = (0..32).map(|i| Rlp::bytes(vec![i as u8; 32])).collect();
        let enc = Rlp::list(items).encode();
        // payload 32*33 = 1056 bytes -> 0xf9 + 2 length bytes (0x04 0x20)
        assert_eq!(enc[0], 0xf9);
        assert_eq!(enc[1], 0x04);
        assert_eq!(enc[2], 0x20);
    }
}

// End-to-end smoke for the remix integration: binary discovery, the doctor,
// the chain-write gate, an offline command, live mainnet reads and the daemon
// refusal. Runs against the REAL network — run it manually:
//   cargo run -p romacode-server --example remix_smoke
// (needs an rrx binary reachable via the discovery order, see remix_status).
use romacode_server::config::Config;
use romacode_server::remix;
use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;

fn main() {
    let cfg = Config::default();
    let cancel = AtomicBool::new(false);
    println!("=== discovery: {:?}", remix::ensure_binary(&cfg));
    println!("=== doctor ===\n{}", remix::status_execute(&cfg, &serde_json::json!({})).unwrap());
    println!("=== chain write refusal (flag off) ===");
    let r = remix::execute(&cfg, &serde_json::json!({"command":"send","args":["--to","vitalik.eth","--value","0.001"]}), &cancel);
    println!("{}", r.unwrap_err());
    println!("=== utils keccak (offline) ===");
    let r = remix::execute(&cfg, &serde_json::json!({"command":"utils","args":["keccak","romacode-remix"]}), &cancel);
    println!("{}", r.unwrap());
    println!("=== live mainnet chain (--json) ===");
    let r = remix::execute(&cfg, &serde_json::json!({"command":"chain","args":[],"timeout_secs":60}), &cancel);
    println!("{}", r.unwrap_or_else(|e| format!("ERR: {e}")));
    println!("=== live account vitalik.eth ===");
    let r = remix::execute(&cfg, &serde_json::json!({"command":"account","args":["0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045"],"timeout_secs":60}), &cancel);
    println!("{}", r.unwrap_or_else(|e| format!("ERR: {e}")));
    println!("=== daemon refusal ===");
    let r = remix::execute(&cfg, &serde_json::json!({"command":"explorer"}), &cancel);
    println!("{}", r.unwrap_err());
}
```

## `crates/server/langchain/README.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/langchain/README.md)

````markdown
# langchain-rust

**LangChain, rebuilt in pure Rust** — the agent-core kit: LCEL runnables, prompt
templates, chat models, tool-calling agents with memory, and basic RAG. Zero
Python, zero bloat, one dependency tree, plus a built-in REPL agent CLI.

```
cargo build            # library + langchain-cli binary
cargo test             # 49 unit + 5 wiremock integration + doctests
cargo run -- chat --demo   # offline agent REPL, no API key needed
```

---

## Module map (Python LangChain → this crate)

| Python LangChain | langchain-rust | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `langchain_core.runnables.Runnable` | `runnables::Runnable` | async `invoke` / `batch`; `.pipe()` = LCEL `\|` |
| `RunnableLambda` / `RunnablePassthrough` | `runnables::{lambda, RunnablePassthrough}` | closures become runnables |
| `RunnableParallel` | `runnables::RunnableMap` | fan-out one input to many runnables concurrently |
| `langchain_core.prompts.*` | `prompts::{PromptTemplate, ChatPromptTemplate}` | `{var}` f-string syntax, `{{` escapes |
| `MessagesPlaceholder` | `ChatSlot::Placeholder` | splices history into a chat prompt |
| `langchain_core.messages` | `messages::Message` | System/Human/AI/Tool + `ToolCall`, OpenAI JSON serialisation |
| `langchain_core.language_models.BaseChatModel` | `llms::BaseChatModel` | `generate`, `generate_with_tools`, `stream_text` |
| `ChatOpenAI` | `llms::openai::ChatOpenAI` | any `/v1/chat/completions` server (OpenAI, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) |
| `langchain_core.output_parsers` | `output_parsers::{StrOutputParser, JsonOutputParser}` | fenced/prose-tolerant JSON extraction |
| `langchain_core.callbacks` | `callbacks::{CallbackHandler, VerboseHandler}` | `verbose=True` equivalent |
| `langchain.agents.AgentExecutor` | `agents::AgentExecutor` | OpenAI tool-calling loop, iteration budget |
| `@tool` / `BaseTool` | `agents::tools::{Tool, tool_fn}` | JSON-schema parameters + async closure |
| `langchain.memory` | `memory::{ConversationBufferMemory, WindowBufferMemory}` | |
| `langchain.chains.LLMChain` | `agents::LLMChain` | prompt → model → string, as a `Runnable` |
| `langchain.text_splitter` | `text_splitter::RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` | chunk_size + overlap |
| `langchain_core.embeddings` | `embeddings::{Embeddings, OpenAIEmbeddings}` | `/v1/embeddings` |
| `langchain_core.vectorstores` | `vectorstores::{InMemoryVectorStore, Retriever}` | cosine top-k, retriever is a `Runnable` |
| `FakeListChatModel` (tests) | `llms::FakeChatModel` | scripted offline model |

## Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────── langchain-cli (REPL agent) ──────────────────────────┐
│  chat (tools + memory)   ask (streamed)   tools (list)                         │
└───────────────▲───────────────────────────────────────────────▲────────────────┘
                │ AgentExecutor                                 │
│ ┌─────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│ │ agents       AgentExecutor: plan → tool_calls → run tools → feed back    │  │
│ │ tools        Tool {ToolSpec, async ToolFn} + calculator/file/shell tools │  │
│ │ memory       ConversationBufferMemory / WindowBufferMemory               │  │
│ └──────────────▲───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                │ Arc<dyn BaseChatModel>                                       │
│ ┌──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│ │ llms         BaseChatModel trait · ChatOpenAI (SSE streaming, tool calls)│  │
│ │ messages     Message::{System,Human,AI,Tool} → OpenAI wire format        │  │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ runnables     Runnable<I,O> · pipe() · RunnableMap · Passthrough         │ │
│ │ prompts       PromptTemplate · ChatPromptTemplate · PromptValue          │ │
│ │ output_parsers / callbacks / errors                                     │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ RAG: text_splitter → embeddings (OpenAI) → InMemoryVectorStore → Retriever│ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Quickstart (library)

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;
use langchain_rust::prelude::*;

# async fn demo() -> langchain_rust::errors::Result<()> {
let model: Arc<dyn BaseChatModel> = Arc::new(
    ChatOpenAI::builder()
        .model("gpt-4o-mini")
        .api_key(std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY")?)
        .build()?,
);

// LCEL: prompt | model
let prompt = ChatPromptTemplate::from_system_and_human("You are {role}.", "{question}");
let mut vars = HashMap::new();
vars.insert("role".into(), PromptValue::from("a Rust wizard"));
vars.insert("question".into(), PromptValue::from("Why is Rust memory-safe?"));
let messages = prompt.format(&vars)?;
let answer = model.generate(&messages).await?;
println!("{}", answer.text());
# Ok(())
# }
```

### Agent with tools and memory

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use langchain_rust::prelude::*;

# async fn demo() -> langchain_rust::errors::Result<()> {
let model: Arc<dyn BaseChatModel> = Arc::new(
    ChatOpenAI::builder().model("gpt-4o-mini")
        .api_key(std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY")?).build()?,
);

let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
    .tool(calculator_tool())
    .tool(read_file_tool())
    .tool(write_file_tool())
    .memory(Box::new(ConversationBufferMemory::new()))
    .system_prompt("You are a terminal AI agent. Prefer tools over guessing.")
    .max_iterations(12)
    .verbose(true)          // traces to stderr, like verbose=True
    .build();

let answer = agent.invoke("What is (12*35)*1.05? Use the calculator.").await?;
# Ok(())
# }
```

Custom tools are one function each:

```rust
use langchain_rust::prelude::*;
let weather = tool_fn(
    "weather",
    "Current weather for a city",
    serde_json::json!({
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["city"]
    }),
    |args| async move { Ok(format!("sunny in {}", args["city"].as_str()?)) },
);
```

## The CLI (`langchain-cli`)

```text
langchain-cli chat                # interactive agent REPL (tools + memory)
langchain-cli chat --verbose      # print every LLM call / tool run to stderr
langchain-cli chat --no-tools     # plain chat, no tool binding
langchain-cli chat --allow-shell  # also enable the run_shell tool
langchain-cli chat --demo         # offline scripted agent, no API key
langchain-cli ask "Why Rust?"     # one-shot streamed answer
langchain-cli tools               # list built-in tools
```

| Env var | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Bearer token (any string works for local servers) | — |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `https://api.openai.com/v1` |
| `LANGCHAIN_MODEL` / `OPENAI_MODEL` | model id | `gpt-4o-mini` |

REPL commands: `/help`, `/memory` (dump history), `/clear` (reset memory),
`/exit`. Built-in tools: `calculator`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_dir`,
`run_shell` (opt-in via `--allow-shell`).

Point it at a local model with zero setup:

```bash
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 OPENAI_API_KEY=ollama \
  langchain-cli chat --model llama3.1
```

## Examples (all runnable from this repo)

| Example | Needs network? | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo run --example lcel_composition` | no | pipe chains, batch, parallel fan-out, LLMChain, JSON parser |
| `cargo run --example agent_demo` | no | scripted tool-calling agent loop + memory |
| `cargo run --example rag_demo` | no | split → embed → vector store → retriever → grounded answer |
| `cargo run --example streaming` | yes | token-by-token SSE streaming + usage |

## Design notes

- **Everything is a `Runnable`.** Prompts, chains, retrievers and parsers share
  one trait (`invoke` / `batch`), so composition type-checks at compile time —
  LCEL's `prompt | model | parser` becomes `prompt.pipe(model).pipe(parser)`.
- **The agent loop is the OpenAI tool protocol.** The executor binds
  `ToolSpec`s, feeds `tool_calls` results back as `role: "tool"` messages, and
  stops on a plain-text turn. Tool *errors* go back to the model as
  `Error: …` results so it can self-correct; only transport failures abort.
- **Streaming is real SSE parsing**, including the `[DONE]` sentinel and
  per-provider usage accounting where offered.
- **Deliberately not ported** (agent-core scope): document loaders (PDF/HTML),
  few-shot selectors, LangGraph, LangServe, multi-vector stores. The seams for
  all of them are the existing traits (`Embeddings`, `Memory`, `Runnable`,
  `BaseChatModel`).

```rust
//! Tool-calling agent loop, fully offline with a scripted model.
//!
//! The `FakeChatModel` returns a calculator tool call on the first turn and a
//! final answer on the second — exactly what a real OpenAI-compatible server
//! would do. Run: `cargo run --example agent_demo`

use std::sync::Arc;

use langchain_rust::agents::{calculator_tool, AgentExecutor};
use langchain_rust::errors::Result;
use langchain_rust::llms::{BaseChatModel, FakeChatModel};
use langchain_rust::memory::ConversationBufferMemory;
use langchain_rust::messages::{Message, ToolCall};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<()> {
    // Script: turn 1 -> tool call, turn 2 -> final answer.
    let model: Arc<dyn BaseChatModel> = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![
        Message::AI {
            content: None,
            tool_calls: vec![ToolCall {
                id: "call_1".into(),
                name: "calculator".into(),
                args: serde_json::json!({ "expression": "(199+1)*3" }),
            }],
        },
        Message::ai("The bill comes to 600."),
    ]));

    let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
        .tool(calculator_tool())
        .memory(Box::new(ConversationBufferMemory::new()))
        .system_prompt("You are a billing assistant. Use the calculator for any math.")
        .max_iterations(6)
        .verbose(true) // traces go to stderr, like Python's verbose=True
        .build();

    let answer = agent.invoke("We sold 3 units at 199 each — total?").await?;
    println!("\nfinal answer: {answer}");

    // Memory now holds the user/assistant turns of this exchange.
    println!("memory entries: {}", agent.memory().unwrap().load().len());
    Ok(())
}
```

## `crates/server/langchain/examples/lcel_composition.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/langchain/examples/lcel_composition.rs)

````rust
//! LCEL composition — pipes, lambdas, parallel map — all offline (no API key).
//!
//! Run: `cargo run --example lcel_composition`

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use langchain_rust::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<()> {
    // 1. Pipe: lambda -> lambda -> lambda  (Python: r1 | r2 | r3)
    let chain = lambda(|x: i32| async move { Ok(x * 2) })
        .pipe(lambda(|x: i32| async move { Ok(x + 10) }))
        .pipe(lambda(|x: i32| async move { Ok(format!("result = {x}")) }));

    println!("pipe:        {}", chain.invoke(5).await?);
    println!("batch:       {:?}", chain.batch(vec![1, 2, 3]).await?);

    // 2. RunnableMap: fan the same input out to several runnables in parallel.
    let fanout = RunnableMap::<i32, i32>::new()
        .with(lambda(|x: i32| async move { Ok(x * x) }))
        .with(lambda(|x: i32| async move { Ok(-x) }));
    println!("parallel:    {:?}", fanout.invoke(7).await?);

    // 3. Prompt -> FakeChatModel -> parser, wired as an LLMChain.
    let model: Arc<dyn BaseChatModel> =
        Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai("42")]));
    let prompt = ChatPromptTemplate::from_system_and_human("Be terse.", "What is {q}?");

    let mut vars = HashMap::new();
    vars.insert("q".to_string(), PromptValue::from("the answer to everything"));
    let chain = LLMChain::new(prompt, model);
    println!("llm chain:   {}", chain.invoke(vars).await?);

    // 4. JSON output parser extracting fenced JSON from a model reply.
    let parser = JsonOutputParser;
    let parsed = parser
        .invoke("Sure:\n```json\n{\"ok\": true}\n```".to_string())
        .await?;
    println!("parsed json: {parsed}");

    Ok(())
}
````

## `crates/server/langchain/examples/rag_demo.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/langchain/examples/rag_demo.rs)

```rust
//! RAG pipeline, fully offline: split -> embed (deterministic toy embedder)
//! -> vector store -> retriever -> answer.
//!
//! Run: `cargo run --example rag_demo`

use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use langchain_rust::prelude::*;

/// Toy embedder: bag-of-words hashed into 64 dims. Swap in `OpenAIEmbeddings`
/// (builder below, commented) for real retrieval.
struct WordHashEmbedder;

#[async_trait]
impl Embeddings for WordHashEmbedder {
    async fn embed_query(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        Ok(self.hash(text))
    }

    async fn embed_documents(&self, texts: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
        Ok(texts.iter().map(|t| self.hash(t)).collect())
    }
}

impl WordHashEmbedder {
    fn hash(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<f32> {
        let mut v = vec![0f32; 64];
        for w in text.to_lowercase().split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric()) {
            if w.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let h = w.bytes().fold(5381usize, |acc, b| {
                (acc.wrapping_mul(33).wrapping_add(b as usize)) % 64
            });
            v[h] += 1.0;
        }
        v
    }
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<()> {
    // -- Real embeddings (needs OPENAI_API_KEY) --
    // let embedder: Arc<dyn Embeddings> = Arc::new(
    //     OpenAIEmbeddings::builder()
    //         .model("text-embedding-3-small")
    //         .api_key(std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY").unwrap())
    //         .build()?,
    // );

    let embedder: Arc<dyn Embeddings> = Arc::new(WordHashEmbedder);

    // 1. Split a long document on natural boundaries.
    let splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(220, 40);
    let raw = format!(
        "Rust achieves memory safety without a garbage collector.\n\n\
         The borrow checker enforces ownership rules at compile time.\n\n\
         Ownership means each value has exactly one owner.\n\n\
         Lifetimes describe how long references remain valid.\n\n\
         Zero-cost abstractions let Rust match handwritten C performance.\n\n\
         Pattern matching with match expressions covers all cases exhaustively."
    );
    let chunks = splitter.split(&raw);
    println!("split into {} chunks", chunks.len());

    // 2. Embed + index the chunks.
    let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
    let docs: Vec<Document> = chunks
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, c)| Document::with_source(c.clone(), format!("rust-notes.md#chunk-{i}")))
        .collect();
    store.add_documents(&docs, embedder.as_ref()).await?;
    println!("indexed {} documents", store.len()?);

    // 3. Retrieve the top-2 chunks for a question.
    let retriever = store.as_retriever(embedder.clone(), 2);
    let question = "How does Rust stay memory safe?";
    let hits = retriever.retrieve_scored(question).await?;
    for (d, score) in &hits {
        println!("  score={score:.3} src={:?} :: {}", d.metadata["source"], d.page_content);
    }

    // 4. Feed retrieved context to the model (offline fake here).
    let context: String = hits
        .iter()
        .map(|(d, _)| d.page_content.clone())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\n");
    let model: Arc<dyn BaseChatModel> = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai(format!(
        "Answer (grounded in {len} chunks): the borrow checker enforces ownership.",
        len = hits.len()
    ))]));
    let answer = model
        .generate(&[Message::human(format!("Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}"))])
        .await?;
    println!("\nanswer: {}", answer.text());

    Ok(())
}
```

//! Streaming chat against a real OpenAI-compatible endpoint (needs
//! OPENAI_API_KEY). Prints tokens as they arrive plus the token usage.
//!
//! Run: `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... cargo run --example streaming`

use futures::StreamExt;
use langchain_rust::llms::openai::ChatOpenAI;
use langchain_rust::llms::BaseChatModel;
use langchain_rust::messages::Message;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let api_key = match std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY") {
        Ok(k) if !k.is_empty() => k,
        _ => anyhow::bail!("set OPENAI_API_KEY first"),
    };
    let base_url = std::env::var("OPENAI_BASE_URL").unwrap_or_default();

    let mut builder = ChatOpenAI::builder().model("gpt-4o-mini").api_key(api_key);
    if !base_url.is_empty() {
        builder = builder.base_url(base_url);
    }
    let model = builder.build()?;

    let messages = vec![
        Message::system("You are a Rust evangelist. Answer in one short paragraph."),
        Message::human("Why should an AI agent CLI be written in Rust?"),
    ];

    let mut stream = model.stream_text(&messages);
    while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
        print!("{}", chunk?);
    }
    println!();

    if let Some(usage) = model.usage() {
        eprintln!("[usage] prompt={} completion={} total={}", usage.prompt_tokens, usage.completion_tokens, usage.total_tokens);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## `crates/server/langchain/src/agents/mod.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/langchain/src/agents/mod.rs)

```rust
//! Agents — the Rust mirror of `langchain.agents` (`AgentExecutor` +
//! `create_tool_calling_agent`). The loop is the OpenAI tool-calling protocol:
//! the model requests tools, we run them, feed results back, repeat until it
//! answers in plain text or the iteration budget runs out.

pub mod tools;
pub mod tools_builtin;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::callbacks::{CallbackManager, VerboseHandler};
use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::memory::Memory;
use crate::messages::{Message, ToolSpec};
use crate::runnables::Runnable;

pub use tools::Tool;
pub use tools_builtin::{calculator_tool, list_dir_tool, read_file_tool, shell_tool, write_file_tool};

/// The agent executor: plans with the model, runs tools, remembers the chat.
pub struct AgentExecutor {
    model: Arc<dyn crate::llms::BaseChatModel>,
    tools: Vec<Tool>,
    memory: Option<Box<dyn Memory>>,
    system_prompt: Option<String>,
    max_iterations: usize,
    callbacks: CallbackManager,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for AgentExecutor {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("AgentExecutor")
            .field("model", &self.model.model_name())
            .field("tools", &self.tools.iter().map(|t| t.name()).collect::<Vec<_>>())
            .field("max_iterations", &self.max_iterations)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl AgentExecutor {
    /// Builder entry point.
    pub fn builder(model: Arc<dyn crate::llms::BaseChatModel>) -> AgentExecutorBuilder {
        AgentExecutorBuilder {
            model,
            tools: Vec::new(),
            memory: None,
            system_prompt: None,
            max_iterations: 10,
            verbose: false,
            callbacks: None,
        }
    }

    /// The OpenAI `tools` payload describing every registered tool.
    pub fn tool_specs(&self) -> Vec<ToolSpec> {
        self.tools.iter().map(|t| t.spec.clone()).collect()
    }

    fn lookup(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Tool> {
        self.tools.iter().find(|t| t.spec.name == name)
    }

    /// Run one tool call, returning the string fed back to the model.
    /// Tool failures become `Error: ...` results rather than aborting the loop,
    /// so the model can retry with corrected arguments.
    pub async fn run_tool(&self, name: &str, args: &serde_json::Value) -> String {
        self.callbacks.tool_start(name, args).await;
        let result = match self.lookup(name) {
            None => Err(LangchainError::UnknownTool(name.to_string())),
            Some(tool) => {
                if let Err(e) = tools::validate_args(&tool.spec, args) {
                    Err(e)
                } else {
                    tool.call(args.clone()).await
                }
            }
        };
        let text = match result {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(e) => format!("Error: {e}"),
        };
        self.callbacks.tool_end(name, &text).await;
        text
    }

    /// Execute a task: the full plan → tools → answer loop.
    ///
    /// Returns the final assistant text. Tool-call errors are surfaced to the
    /// model as tool results; only transport-level LLM failures bubble up.
    pub async fn invoke(&mut self, input: &str) -> Result<String> {
        let specs = self.tool_specs();
        let mut messages: Vec<Message> = Vec::new();
        if let Some(sys) = &self.system_prompt {
            messages.push(Message::system(sys.clone()));
        }
        if let Some(mem) = &self.memory {
            messages.extend(mem.load());
        }
        messages.push(Message::human(input));

        let model = self.model.model_name().to_string();
        let mut final_answer: Option<String> = None;

        for iteration in 0..self.max_iterations {
            self.callbacks.agent_step(iteration + 1).await;
            self.callbacks.llm_start(&model, &messages).await;
            let response = self.model.generate_with_tools(&messages, &specs).await?;
            self.callbacks.llm_end(&model, response.text()).await;

            let tool_calls = match &response {
                Message::AI { tool_calls, .. } => tool_calls.clone(),
                _ => Vec::new(),
            };
            let has_calls = !tool_calls.is_empty();

            // Belt-and-braces: never let an empty tool_call id reach the wire.
            // The OpenAI client already synthesizes ids at parse time; this
            // second pass repairs anything that slipped through (other
            // model impls, hand-built messages), keeping the assistant
            // message and its tool results paired with the SAME id.
            let mut response = response;
            if let Message::AI { tool_calls: tcs, .. } = &mut response {
                for tc in tcs.iter_mut() {
                    if tc.id.trim().is_empty() {
                        tc.id = crate::llms::openai::next_local_call_id();
                    }
                }
            }
            let tool_calls = match &response {
                Message::AI { tool_calls, .. } => tool_calls.clone(),
                _ => Vec::new(),
            };
            messages.push(response);

            if !has_calls {
                let answer = messages.last().map(|m| m.text().to_string()).unwrap_or_default();
                final_answer = Some(answer);
                break;
            }

            for call in tool_calls {
                let result = self.run_tool(&call.name, &call.args).await;
                messages.push(Message::tool(call.id, call.name, result));
            }
        }

        match final_answer {
            Some(answer) => {
                if let Some(mem) = &mut self.memory {
                    mem.save_turn(input, &answer);
                }
                self.callbacks.agent_finish(&answer).await;
                Ok(answer)
            }
            None => {
                // Iteration budget exhausted. That is not a hard failure:
                // return the last assistant text (or a clear summary) so the
                // caller keeps the work done so far instead of losing the
                // whole turn to an error.
                let last_text = messages
                    .iter()
                    .rev()
                    .find_map(|m| match m {
                        Message::AI { content, .. } => {
                            content.clone().filter(|c| !c.trim().is_empty())
                        }
                        _ => None,
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let answer = if last_text.trim().is_empty() {
                    format!(
                        "Stopped after {} tool rounds (budget). Partial progress preserved in the transcript — raise `agent.max_tool_rounds` to go further.",
                        self.max_iterations
                    )
                } else {
                    last_text
                };
                if let Some(mem) = &mut self.memory {
                    mem.save_turn(input, &answer);
                }
                self.callbacks.agent_finish(&answer).await;
                Ok(answer)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Like [`AgentExecutor::invoke`] but additionally streams the final answer
    /// through `on_llm_token` callbacks as it is already known — useful for the
    /// REPL to keep a single code path.
    pub async fn invoke_with_token_feed(&mut self, input: &str) -> Result<String> {
        let answer = self.invoke(input).await?;
        if !self.callbacks.is_empty() {
            for tok in split_feedable(&answer) {
                self.callbacks.llm_token(&tok).await;
            }
        }
        Ok(answer)
    }

    /// Access registered memory (e.g. to dump it in the REPL).
    pub fn memory(&self) -> Option<&dyn Memory> {
        self.memory.as_deref()
    }

    /// Mutable memory access.
    pub fn memory_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Box<dyn Memory>> {
        self.memory.as_mut()
    }

    /// Drop the conversation.
    pub fn clear_memory(&mut self) {
        if let Some(mem) = &mut self.memory {
            mem.clear();
        }
    }
}

fn split_feedable(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    // Feed small chunks (word + trailing space) so token callbacks look natural.
    let mut chunks = Vec::new();
    let mut word = String::new();
    for c in s.chars() {
        word.push(c);
        if c == ' ' || c == '\n' {
            chunks.push(std::mem::take(&mut word));
        }
    }
    if !word.is_empty() {
        chunks.push(word);
    }
    chunks
}

/// Builder for [`AgentExecutor`].
pub struct AgentExecutorBuilder {
    model: Arc<dyn crate::llms::BaseChatModel>,
    tools: Vec<Tool>,
    memory: Option<Box<dyn Memory>>,
    system_prompt: Option<String>,
    max_iterations: usize,
    verbose: bool,
    callbacks: Option<CallbackManager>,
}

impl AgentExecutorBuilder {
    /// Register a tool.
    pub fn tool(mut self, tool: Tool) -> Self {
        self.tools.push(tool);
        self
    }

    /// Register several tools at once.
    pub fn tools(mut self, tools: Vec<Tool>) -> Self {
        self.tools.extend(tools);
        self
    }

    /// Attach conversation memory.
    pub fn memory(mut self, memory: Box<dyn Memory>) -> Self {
        self.memory = Some(memory);
        self
    }

    /// System prompt prepended to every run.
    pub fn system_prompt(mut self, prompt: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.system_prompt = Some(prompt.into());
        self
    }

    /// Iteration budget (default 10).
    pub fn max_iterations(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
        self.max_iterations = n.max(1);
        self
    }

    /// Print traces to stderr (Python's `verbose=True`).
    pub fn verbose(mut self, on: bool) -> Self {
        self.verbose = on;
        self
    }

    /// Install a custom callback manager (overrides `verbose`).
    /// Hosts like RomaCode route executor events to their own transports.
    pub fn callbacks(mut self, manager: CallbackManager) -> Self {
        self.callbacks = Some(manager);
        self
    }

    /// Build the executor.
    pub fn build(self) -> AgentExecutor {
        let callbacks = self.callbacks.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            if self.verbose {
                CallbackManager::new().add(Arc::new(VerboseHandler))
            } else {
                CallbackManager::new()
            }
        });
        AgentExecutor {
            model: self.model,
            tools: self.tools,
            memory: self.memory,
            system_prompt: self.system_prompt,
            max_iterations: self.max_iterations,
            callbacks,
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// LLMChain — the classic single-shot chain, also usable through Runnable.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `prompt | model | parser` bundled as one runnable — `LLMChain`.
pub struct LLMChain {
    pub prompt: crate::prompts::ChatPromptTemplate,
    pub model: Arc<dyn crate::llms::BaseChatModel>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for LLMChain {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("LLMChain")
    }
}

impl LLMChain {
    /// Create a chain over a chat prompt template.
    pub fn new(prompt: crate::prompts::ChatPromptTemplate, model: Arc<dyn crate::llms::BaseChatModel>) -> Self {
        Self { prompt, model }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Runnable<HashMap<String, crate::prompts::PromptValue>, String> for LLMChain {
    async fn invoke(
        &self,
        vars: HashMap<String, crate::prompts::PromptValue>,
    ) -> Result<String> {
        let messages = self.prompt.format(&vars)?;
        let msg = self.model.generate(&messages).await?;
        Ok(msg.text().to_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::llms::FakeChatModel;
    use crate::messages::ToolCall;
    use crate::memory::ConversationBufferMemory;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn agent_answers_without_tools() {
        let model = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai("Hello there!")]));
        let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model).build();
        let answer = agent.invoke("hi").await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(answer, "Hello there!");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn agent_runs_tool_then_answers() {
        // Turn 1: model asks for the calculator. Turn 2: model answers.
        let model = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![
            Message::AI {
                content: None,
                tool_calls: vec![ToolCall {
                    id: "call_1".into(),
                    name: "calculator".into(),
                    args: json!({"expression": "21*2"}),
                }],
            },
            Message::ai("21*2 is 42."),
        ]));
        let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
            .tool(calculator_tool())
            .max_iterations(5)
            .build();
        let answer = agent.invoke("what is 21*2?").await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(answer, "21*2 is 42.");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn agent_tool_error_is_fed_back_not_fatal() {
        // Turn 1: model calls an unknown tool; Turn 2: model recovers.
        let model = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![
            Message::AI {
                content: None,
                tool_calls: vec![ToolCall {
                    id: "call_1".into(),
                    name: "nope".into(),
                    args: json!({}),
                }],
            },
            Message::ai("That tool does not exist."),
        ]));
        let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model).build();
        let answer = agent.invoke("call nope").await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(answer, "That tool does not exist.");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn agent_loop_limit_is_enforced() {
        // Model always requests the same tool: executor must stop — but
        // gracefully, with a clear budget message instead of a hard error
        // that would throw away the work done so far.
        let scripted = Message::AI {
            content: None,
            tool_calls: vec![ToolCall { id: "c".into(), name: "calculator".into(), args: json!({"expression": "1"}) }],
        };
        // 50 scripted turns, executor limit is 3.
        let model = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![scripted; 50]));
        let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
            .tool(calculator_tool())
            .max_iterations(3)
            .build();
        let answer = agent.invoke("loop forever").await.unwrap();
        assert!(
            answer.contains("Stopped after 3 tool rounds"),
            "budget stop must be reported to the caller: {answer}"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn memory_records_turns() {
        let model = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai("answer one"), Message::ai("answer two")]));
        let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
            .memory(Box::new(ConversationBufferMemory::new()))
            .build();
        agent.invoke("first").await.unwrap();
        agent.invoke("second").await.unwrap();
        let mem = agent.memory().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(mem.load().len(), 4);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn llm_chain_formats_and_completes() {
        use crate::prompts::{ChatPromptTemplate, PromptValue};
        let model = Arc::new(FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai("42")]));
        let prompt = ChatPromptTemplate::from_system_and_human("You are terse.", "Q: {q}");
        let chain = LLMChain::new(prompt, model);
        let mut vars = HashMap::new();
        vars.insert("q".to_string(), PromptValue::Text("meaning of life".into()));
        let out = chain.invoke(vars).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "42");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn token_feed_splits_words() {
        let chunks = split_feedable("one two\nthree");
        assert_eq!(chunks, vec!["one ".to_string(), "two\n".to_string(), "three".to_string()]);
    }
}

````rust
//! Tools — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.tools` (`BaseTool`).
//!
//! A tool is a name + description + JSON-schema parameters + an async executor.
//! The schema is sent to the model (OpenAI function calling); the executor is
//! what actually runs when the model selects the tool.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::messages::ToolSpec;

/// Async executor backing a [`Tool`].
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolFn: Send + Sync {
    /// Run the tool with the model-supplied arguments.
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<String>;
}

/// A callable tool the agent can invoke — `BaseTool` + `@tool` decorator equivalent.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Tool {
    pub spec: ToolSpec,
    executor: Arc<dyn ToolFn>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Tool {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("Tool")
            .field("name", &self.spec.name)
            .field("description", &self.spec.description)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl Tool {
    /// Assemble a tool from a spec and an executor.
    pub fn new(spec: ToolSpec, executor: Arc<dyn ToolFn>) -> Self {
        Self { spec, executor }
    }

    /// Describe the tool for the model.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.spec.name
    }

    /// JSON Schema of the arguments.
    pub fn parameters(&self) -> &Value {
        &self.spec.parameters
    }

    /// Run the tool.
    pub async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<String> {
        self.executor.call(args).await
    }
}

/// Build a [`Tool`] from an async closure — the `@tool` decorator equivalent.
///
/// ```ignore
/// let echo = tool_fn("echo", "Repeat the input", json!({
///     "type": "object",
///     "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
///     "required": ["text"]
/// }), |args| async move {
///     let text = args["text"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
///     Ok(text)
/// });
/// ```
pub fn tool_fn<F, Fut>(
    name: impl Into<String>,
    description: impl Into<String>,
    parameters: Value,
    f: F,
) -> Tool
where
    F: Fn(Value) -> Fut + Send + Sync + 'static,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<String>> + Send + 'static,
{
    let spec = ToolSpec {
        name: name.into(),
        description: description.into(),
        parameters,
    };
    Tool::new(spec, Arc::new(ClosureTool { f }))
}

/// Adapter turning an async closure into a [`ToolFn`].
struct ClosureTool<F> {
    f: F,
}

#[async_trait]
impl<F, Fut> ToolFn for ClosureTool<F>
where
    F: Fn(Value) -> Fut + Send + Sync,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<String>> + Send,
{
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<String> {
        (self.f)(args).await
    }
}

/// Validate `args` against the very small subset of JSON Schema we rely on:
/// required keys + top-level types. Full JSON Schema validation is intentionally
/// out of scope for a core rebuild.
pub fn validate_args(spec: &ToolSpec, args: &Value) -> Result<()> {
    if !args.is_object() {
        return Err(LangchainError::ToolExecution(
            spec.name.clone(),
            "arguments must be a JSON object".into(),
        ));
    }
    let required = spec
        .parameters
        .get("required")
        .and_then(|r| r.as_array())
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_default();
    for req in required {
        let key = req.as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        if key.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        if args.get(key).is_none() {
            return Err(LangchainError::ToolExecution(
                spec.name.clone(),
                format!("missing required argument `{key}`"),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn closure_tool_runs() {
        let t = tool_fn("echo", "echo text", json!({"type": "object"}), |args| async move {
            Ok(args["text"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_uppercase())
        });
        let out = t.call(json!({"text": "hello"})).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "HELLO");
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_required_keys() {
        let spec = ToolSpec {
            name: "t".into(),
            description: "".into(),
            parameters: json!({"type": "object", "required": ["path"]}),
        };
        assert!(validate_args(&spec, &json!({"path": "/tmp"})).is_ok());
        assert!(validate_args(&spec, &json!({})).is_err());
        assert!(validate_args(&spec, &json!([1])).is_err());
    }
}
