```rust
//! Built-in tools shipped with the crate: calculator, file I/O, directory
//! listing and an opt-in shell tool for CLI agents.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::agents::tools::{tool_fn, Tool, ToolFn};
use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};

/// Recursive-descent calculator: `+ - * / ^ %`, parentheses, unary minus,
/// and `sqrt`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `floor`, `ceil`, `log`, `exp` functions.
///
/// Parsing is hand-rolled (no dependencies) and evaluation is f64-safe:
/// division by zero and NaN results are reported as errors.
pub fn calculate(expression: &str) -> Result<f64> {
    let tokens = lex(expression)?;
    let mut parser = Parser { tokens, pos: 0 };
    let value = parser.parse_expr()?;
    if parser.pos != parser.tokens.len() {
        return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "unexpected token at position {}: `{:?}`",
            parser.pos, parser.tokens[parser.pos]
        )));
    }
    if value.is_nan() || value.is_infinite() {
        return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("expression evaluates to NaN/∞".into()));
    }
    Ok(value)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
enum Tok {
    Num(f64),
    Ident(String),
    Op(char),
    LParen,
    RParen,
    Comma,
}

fn lex(s: &str) -> Result<Vec<Tok>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = s.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(&c) = chars.peek() {
        match c {
            ' ' | '\t' | '\n' | '\r' => {
                chars.next();
            }
            '0'..='9' | '.' => {
                let mut num = String::new();
                while let Some(&c2) = chars.peek() {
                    if c2.is_ascii_digit() || c2 == '.' || c2 == 'e' || c2 == 'E' || ((c2 == '+' || c2 == '-') && num.ends_with(['e', 'E'])) {
                        num.push(c2);
                        chars.next();
                    } else {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                let v: f64 = num
                    .parse()
                    .map_err(|_| LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("bad number `{num}`")))?;
                out.push(Tok::Num(v));
            }
            'a'..='z' | 'A'..='Z' | '_' => {
                let mut id = String::new();
                while let Some(&c2) = chars.peek() {
                    if c2.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c2 == '_' {
                        id.push(c2);
                        chars.next();
                    } else {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                out.push(Tok::Ident(id));
            }
            '+' | '-' | '*' | '/' | '^' | '%' => {
                out.push(Tok::Op(c));
                chars.next();
            }
            '(' => {
                out.push(Tok::LParen);
                chars.next();
            }
            ')' => {
                out.push(Tok::RParen);
                chars.next();
            }
            ',' => {
                out.push(Tok::Comma);
                chars.next();
            }
            other => {
                return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("unexpected char `{other}`")));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

struct Parser {
    tokens: Vec<Tok>,
    pos: usize,
}

impl Parser {
    fn peek(&self) -> Option<&Tok> {
        self.tokens.get(self.pos)
    }

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Tok> {
        let t = self.tokens.get(self.pos).cloned();
        if t.is_some() {
            self.pos += 1;
        }
        t
    }

    // expr := term (('+'|'-') term)*
    fn parse_expr(&mut self) -> Result<f64> {
        let mut left = self.parse_term()?;
        while let Some(Tok::Op(op @ ('+' | '-'))) = self.peek() {
            let op = *op;
            self.pos += 1;
            let right = self.parse_term()?;
            left = if op == '+' { left + right } else { left - right };
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    // term := factor (('*'|'/'|'%') factor)*
    fn parse_term(&mut self) -> Result<f64> {
        let mut left = self.parse_factor()?;
        while let Some(Tok::Op(op @ ('*' | '/' | '%'))) = self.peek() {
            let op = *op;
            self.pos += 1;
            let right = self.parse_factor()?;
            left = match op {
                '*' => left * right,
                '/' => {
                    if right == 0.0 {
                        return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("division by zero".into()));
                    }
                    left / right
                }
                '%' => {
                    if right == 0.0 {
                        return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("modulo by zero".into()));
                    }
                    left % right
                }
                _ => unreachable!(),
            };
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    // factor := unary ('^' factor)?   (right associative)
    fn parse_factor(&mut self) -> Result<f64> {
        let base = self.parse_unary()?;
        if let Some(Tok::Op('^')) = self.peek() {
            self.pos += 1;
            let exp = self.parse_factor()?;
            return Ok(base.powf(exp));
        }
        Ok(base)
    }

    // unary := '-' unary | primary
    fn parse_unary(&mut self) -> Result<f64> {
        if let Some(Tok::Op('-')) = self.peek() {
            self.pos += 1;
            return Ok(-self.parse_unary()?);
        }
        if let Some(Tok::Op('+')) = self.peek() {
            self.pos += 1;
            return self.parse_unary();
        }
        self.parse_primary()
    }

    // primary := number | ident '(' args ')' | '(' expr ')'
    fn parse_primary(&mut self) -> Result<f64> {
        match self.next() {
            Some(Tok::Num(v)) => Ok(v),
            Some(Tok::Ident(name)) => {
                if self.next() != Some(Tok::LParen) {
                    return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("expected `(` after `{name}`")));
                }
                let mut args = vec![self.parse_expr()?];
                while self.peek() == Some(&Tok::Comma) {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    args.push(self.parse_expr()?);
                }
                if self.next() != Some(Tok::RParen) {
                    return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("expected `)` after `{name}(...`")));
                }
                apply_fn(&name, &args)
            }
            Some(Tok::LParen) => {
                let v = self.parse_expr()?;
                if self.next() != Some(Tok::RParen) {
                    return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("expected `)`".into()));
                }
                Ok(v)
            }
            other => Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("unexpected token {other:?}"))),
        }
    }
}

fn apply_fn(name: &str, args: &[f64]) -> Result<f64> {
    let take1 = |a: &[f64]| -> Result<f64> {
        if a.len() != 1 {
            return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("{name} takes 1 argument")));
        }
        Ok(a[0])
    };
    match name {
        "sqrt" => {
            let v = take1(args)?;
            if v < 0.0 {
                return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("sqrt of negative number".into()));
            }
            Ok(v.sqrt())
        }
        "abs" => Ok(take1(args)?.abs()),
        "floor" => Ok(take1(args)?.floor()),
        "ceil" => Ok(take1(args)?.ceil()),
        "log" => Ok(take1(args)?.ln()),
        "exp" => Ok(take1(args)?.exp()),
        "min" => {
            if args.is_empty() {
                return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("min needs at least 1 argument".into()));
            }
            Ok(args.iter().cloned().fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min))
        }
        "max" => {
            if args.is_empty() {
                return Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput("max needs at least 1 argument".into()));
            }
            Ok(args.iter().cloned().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max))
        }
        other => Err(LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("unknown function `{other}`"))),
    }
}

/// `calculator` tool — evaluates a math expression.
pub fn calculator_tool() -> Tool {
    tool_fn(
        "calculator",
        "Evaluate a math expression. Supports + - * / % ^ parentheses and sqrt, abs, min, max, floor, ceil, log, exp.",
        json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "expression": {"type": "string", "description": "e.g. (2+3)*4"}
            },
            "required": ["expression"]
        }),
        |args| async move {
            let expr = args["expression"]
                .as_str()
                .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::ToolExecution("calculator".into(), "`expression` must be a string".into()))?;
            let v = calculate(expr)?;
            // Render integers without a trailing .0
            if v.fract() == 0.0 && v.abs() < 1e15 {
                Ok(format!("{}", v as i64))
            } else {
                Ok(format!("{v}"))
            }
        },
    )
}

/// `read_file` tool — reads a UTF-8 text file from disk.
pub fn read_file_tool() -> Tool {
    tool_fn(
        "read_file",
        "Read a text file at the given path and return its contents.",
        json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["path"]
        }),
        |args| async move {
            let path = arg_str(&args, "path")?;
            match tokio::fs::read_to_string(&path).await {
                Ok(content) => {
                    let lines = content.lines().count();
                    Ok(format!("{} ({} lines)", content, lines))
                }
                Err(e) => Err(LangchainError::ToolExecution("read_file".into(), format!("{path}: {e}"))),
            }
        },
    )
}

/// `write_file` tool — writes text to a file (creating parents).
pub fn write_file_tool() -> Tool {
    tool_fn(
        "write_file",
        "Write text content to a file at the given path. Overwrites existing files.",
        json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "path": {"type": "string"},
                "content": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "required": ["path", "content"]
        }),
        |args| async move {
            let path = arg_str(&args, "path")?;
            let content = arg_str(&args, "content")?;
            if let Some(parent) = Path::new(&path).parent() {
                let _ = tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent).await;
            }
            tokio::fs::write(&path, &content)
                .await
                .map_err(|e| LangchainError::ToolExecution("write_file".into(), format!("{path}: {e}")))?;
            Ok(format!("wrote {} bytes to {path}", content.len()))
        },
    )
}

/// `list_dir` tool — lists a directory's entries with sizes.
pub fn list_dir_tool() -> Tool {
    tool_fn(
        "list_dir",
        "List the files and directories at the given path.",
        json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"path": {"type": "string", "description": "defaults to `.` if omitted"}},
            "required": []
        }),
        |args| async move {
            let path = args["path"].as_str().unwrap_or(".").to_string();
            let mut entries: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            let mut rd = tokio::fs::read_dir(&path)
                .await
                .map_err(|e| LangchainError::ToolExecution("list_dir".into(), format!("{path}: {e}")))?;
            while let Some(entry) = rd
                .next_entry()
                .await
                .map_err(|e| LangchainError::ToolExecution("list_dir".into(), e.to_string()))?
            {
                let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
                if let Ok(md) = entry.metadata().await {
                    if md.is_dir() {
                        entries.push(format!("{name}/ (dir)"));
                    } else {
                        entries.push(format!("{name} ({} bytes)", md.len()));
                    }
                } else {
                    entries.push(name);
                }
            }
            entries.sort();
            Ok(entries.join("\n"))
        },
    )
}

/// `run_shell` tool — executes a command with a timeout. Opt-in for CLI agents
/// because it can run arbitrary commands on the host.
pub struct ShellTool {
    pub timeout: Duration,
    pub allowed: bool,
}

#[async_trait]
impl ToolFn for ShellTool {
    async fn call(&self, args: Value) -> Result<String> {
        if !self.allowed {
            return Err(LangchainError::ToolExecution(
                "run_shell".into(),
                "shell tool disabled — start the CLI with --allow-shell".into(),
            ));
        }
        let cmd = args["command"]
            .as_str()
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::ToolExecution("run_shell".into(), "`command` must be a string".into()))?
            .to_string();
        let output = tokio::process::Command::new("sh")
            .arg("-c")
            .arg(&cmd)
            // The `timeout` below cancels the FUTURE, not the process: make
            // sure dropping the child handle kills the shell instead of
            // leaking a running process on the host.
            .kill_on_drop(true)
            .output();
        let out = tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, output)
            .await
            .map_err(|_| LangchainError::ToolExecution("run_shell".into(), "command timed out".into()))?
            .map_err(|e| LangchainError::ToolExecution("run_shell".into(), e.to_string()))?;
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout);
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr);
        Ok(format!(
            "exit={}\nstdout:\n{}\nstderr:\n{}",
            out.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),
            stdout,
            stderr
        ))
    }
}

/// Build the opt-in shell tool.
pub fn shell_tool(allowed: bool, timeout: Duration) -> Tool {
    let shell = Arc::new(ShellTool { timeout, allowed });
    Tool::new(
        crate::messages::ToolSpec {
            name: "run_shell".into(),
            description: "Run a shell command (`sh -c`) and return exit code, stdout and stderr. Use for searches, builds, git and any terminal task."
                .into(),
            parameters: json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["command"]
            }),
        },
        shell,
    )
}

fn arg_str(args: &Value, key: &str) -> Result<String> {
    args[key]
        .as_str()
        .map(|s| s.to_string())
        .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::InvalidInput(format!("`{key}` must be a string")))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn arithmetic() {
        assert!((calculate("2+3*4").unwrap() - 14.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((calculate("(2+3)*4").unwrap() - 20.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((calculate("2^3^2").unwrap() - 512.0).abs() < 1e-9); // right assoc
        assert!(calculate("-5+3").unwrap() < 0.0);
        assert!((calculate("10 % 3").unwrap() - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((calculate("sqrt(16)").unwrap() - 4.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((calculate("max(3, 7, 5)").unwrap() - 7.0).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((calculate("1e2 + 5").unwrap() - 105.0).abs() < 1e-9);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arithmetic_errors() {
        assert!(calculate("2/0").is_err());
        assert!(calculate("2 +").is_err());
        assert!(calculate("(1+2").is_err());
        assert!(calculate("sqrt(-1)").is_err());
        assert!(calculate("foo(1)").is_err());
        assert!(calculate("1 $ 2").is_err());
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn calculator_tool_renders_ints_cleanly() {
        let t = calculator_tool();
        let out = t.call(json!({"expression": "2+2"})).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "4");
        let out = t.call(json!({"expression": "1/2"})).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, "0.5");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn shell_tool_disabled_by_default() {
        let t = shell_tool(false, Duration::from_secs(5));
        let e = t.call(json!({"command": "echo hi"})).await.unwrap_err();
        assert!(e.to_string().contains("disabled"));
    }
}

//! Callback system — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.callbacks`
//! (`BaseCallbackHandler` + the `verbose=True` handler).

use async_trait::async_trait;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::messages::Message;

/// Observer hooks fired at key points of LLM / tool / agent execution.
///
/// Every method defaults to a no-op, so implement only what you need.
/// Handlers are shared behind `Arc` and must be `Send + Sync`.
#[async_trait]
pub trait CallbackHandler: Send + Sync {
    /// Called right before a chat model request.
    async fn on_llm_start(&self, _model: &str, _messages: &[Message]) {}

    /// Called after the chat model returned its message.
    async fn on_llm_end(&self, _model: &str, _output: &str) {}

    /// Called when the model requested a tool execution.
    async fn on_tool_start(&self, _tool: &str, _args: &serde_json::Value) {}

    /// Called with the raw string result of a tool execution.
    async fn on_tool_end(&self, _tool: &str, _result: &str) {}

    /// Called once per agent iteration (planning round).
    async fn on_agent_step(&self, _iteration: usize) {}

    /// Called with the agent's final answer.
    async fn on_agent_finish(&self, _output: &str) {}

    /// Called for every streamed token chunk.
    async fn on_llm_token(&self, _token: &str) {}
}

/// The Python `verbose=True` equivalent: prints every event to stderr.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct VerboseHandler;

#[async_trait]
impl CallbackHandler for VerboseHandler {
    async fn on_llm_start(&self, model: &str, messages: &[Message]) {
        eprintln!("\x1b[36m[llm:start]\x1b[0m model={model} messages={}", messages.len());
    }

    async fn on_llm_end(&self, model: &str, output: &str) {
        eprintln!("\x1b[36m[llm:end]\x1b[0m model={model} output={:?}" , truncate(output, 120));
    }

    async fn on_tool_start(&self, tool: &str, args: &serde_json::Value) {
        eprintln!("\x1b[33m[tool:start]\x1b[0m {tool} args={args}");
    }

    async fn on_tool_end(&self, tool: &str, result: &str) {
        eprintln!("\x1b[33m[tool:end]\x1b[0m {tool} result={:?}", truncate(result, 160));
    }

    async fn on_agent_step(&self, iteration: usize) {
        eprintln!("\x1b[35m[agent:step]\x1b[0m iteration={iteration}");
    }

    async fn on_agent_finish(&self, output: &str) {
        eprintln!("\x1b[35m[agent:finish]\x1b[0m {:?}", truncate(output, 200));
    }

    async fn on_llm_token(&self, token: &str) {
        eprint!("{token}");
    }
}

fn truncate(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() <= n {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        let cut: String = s.chars().take(n).collect();
        format!("{cut}…")
    }
}

/// A set of handlers dispatched together by runnables and the agent executor.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct CallbackManager {
    handlers: Vec<Arc<dyn CallbackHandler>>,
}

impl CallbackManager {
    /// Empty manager.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { handlers: Vec::new() }
    }

    /// Register an additional handler.
    pub fn add(mut self, handler: Arc<dyn CallbackHandler>) -> Self {
        self.handlers.push(handler);
        self
    }

    /// True when no handler is registered (fast path: skip event construction).
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.handlers.is_empty()
    }

    /// Fire `on_llm_start` on every handler.
    pub async fn llm_start(&self, model: &str, messages: &[Message]) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_llm_start(model, messages).await;
        }
    }

    /// Fire `on_llm_end` on every handler.
    pub async fn llm_end(&self, model: &str, output: &str) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_llm_end(model, output).await;
        }
    }

    /// Fire `on_tool_start` on every handler.
    pub async fn tool_start(&self, tool: &str, args: &serde_json::Value) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_tool_start(tool, args).await;
        }
    }

    /// Fire `on_tool_end` on every handler.
    pub async fn tool_end(&self, tool: &str, result: &str) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_tool_end(tool, result).await;
        }
    }

    /// Fire `on_agent_step` on every handler.
    pub async fn agent_step(&self, iteration: usize) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_agent_step(iteration).await;
        }
    }

    /// Fire `on_agent_finish` on every handler.
    pub async fn agent_finish(&self, output: &str) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_agent_finish(output).await;
        }
    }

    /// Fire `on_llm_token` on every handler.
    pub async fn llm_token(&self, token: &str) {
        for h in &self.handlers {
            h.on_llm_token(token).await;
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn empty_manager_is_fast_path() {
        let mgr = CallbackManager::new();
        assert!(mgr.is_empty());
        assert!(!mgr.clone().add(Arc::new(VerboseHandler)).is_empty());
    }
}

//! `langchain-cli` — a REPL agent CLI built entirely on the library in this
//! crate. Subcommands:
//!
//! - `chat`   interactive agent shell (tools + memory + verbose traces)
//! - `ask`    one-shot question, streamed token-by-token
//! - `tools`  list built-in tools


use std::sync::Arc;

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use clap::{Parser, Subcommand};
use futures::StreamExt;

use crate::agents::{
    calculator_tool, list_dir_tool, read_file_tool, shell_tool, write_file_tool, AgentExecutor,
};
use crate::llms::openai::ChatOpenAI;
use crate::llms::BaseChatModel;
use crate::memory::ConversationBufferMemory;
use crate::messages::{Message, ToolCall};

const DEFAULT_MODEL: &str = "gpt-4o-mini";
const DEFAULT_BASE_URL: &str = "https://api.openai.com/v1";

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(
    name = "langchain-cli",
    version,
    about = "LangChain rebuilt in Rust — REPL agent CLI"
)]
struct Cli {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    command: Commands,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum Commands {
    /// Interactive agent REPL: type a task, the agent plans, calls tools, answers.
    Chat {
        /// Model id (env LANGCHAIN_MODEL / OPENAI_MODEL, default gpt-4o-mini).
        #[arg(long)]
        model: Option<String>,
        /// OpenAI-compatible base URL (env OPENAI_BASE_URL).
        #[arg(long)]
        base_url: Option<String>,
        /// Run the model without any tools.
        #[arg(long = "no-tools")]
        no_tools: bool,
        /// Print agent traces (LLM calls, tool runs) to stderr.
        #[arg(long)]
        verbose: bool,
        /// Enable the `run_shell` tool (arbitrary commands — use with care).
        #[arg(long)]
        allow_shell: bool,
        /// Offline demo: scripted model, no API key or network needed.
        #[arg(long)]
        demo: bool,
    },
    /// One-shot question, answer streamed to the terminal.
    Ask {
        /// The question in quotes.
        question: String,
        #[arg(long)]
        model: Option<String>,
        #[arg(long)]
        base_url: Option<String>,
        /// Optional system prompt.
        #[arg(long)]
        system: Option<String>,
        /// Disable token streaming (print answer at once).
        #[arg(long)]
        no_stream: bool,
    },
    /// List the built-in tools the agent can use.
    Tools,
}

fn resolve(model_flag: Option<&str>, base_url_flag: Option<&str>) -> (String, String, String) {
    let model = model_flag
        .map(|s| s.to_string())
        .or_else(|| std::env::var("LANGCHAIN_MODEL").ok())
        .or_else(|| std::env::var("OPENAI_MODEL").ok())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_MODEL.to_string());
    let base_url = base_url_flag
        .map(|s| s.to_string())
        .or_else(|| std::env::var("OPENAI_BASE_URL").ok())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_BASE_URL.to_string());
    let api_key = std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY").unwrap_or_default();
    (model, base_url, api_key)
}

fn build_tools(allow_shell: bool) -> Vec<crate::agents::Tool> {
    let mut tools = vec![calculator_tool(), read_file_tool(), write_file_tool(), list_dir_tool()];
    if allow_shell {
        tools.push(shell_tool(true, std::time::Duration::from_secs(30)));
    }
    tools
}

fn build_model(
    model_flag: Option<&str>,
    base_url_flag: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn BaseChatModel>> {
    let (model, base_url, api_key) = resolve(model_flag, base_url_flag);
    if api_key.is_empty() {
        anyhow::bail!(
            "OPENAI_API_KEY is not set. Export it (or use `--base-url` with a local server \
             and any dummy key), or run `langchain-cli chat --demo` for an offline demo."
        );
    }
    let m = ChatOpenAI::builder()
        .model(model)
        .api_key(api_key)
        .base_url(base_url)
        .build()
        .context("building ChatOpenAI")?;
    Ok(Arc::new(m))
}

/// Offline scripted agent model: demonstrates the tool-calling loop with zero
/// network. Math-looking input triggers a calculator tool call; the follow-up
/// turn (after the tool result) answers using the tool output.
struct DemoChatModel;

impl DemoChatModel {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

/// Pull the longest digit-bearing math run out of a sentence so the demo
/// model can hand the calculator something valid.
fn extract_expression(q: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let digit_count = |s: &str| s.chars().filter(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).count();
    let mut best = String::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    for c in q.chars() {
        if c.is_ascii_digit() || "+-*/^().% ".contains(c) {
            cur.push(c);
        } else {
            if digit_count(&cur) > digit_count(&best) {
                best = cur.clone();
            }
            cur.clear();
        }
    }
    if digit_count(&cur) > digit_count(&best) {
        best = cur;
    }
    let t = best.trim().to_string();
    if digit_count(&t) >= 1 && t.chars().any(|c| "+-*/^%".contains(c)) {
        Some(t)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl BaseChatModel for DemoChatModel {
    fn model_name(&self) -> &str {
        "demo-model"
    }

    async fn generate(&self, messages: &[Message]) -> crate::errors::Result<Message> {
        // Inspect the tail of the conversation to decide the next scripted move.
        let last = messages.last();
        if let Some(Message::Tool { name, content, .. }) = last {
            return Ok(Message::ai(format!("The calculator says: {content} (via {name})")));
        }
        let question = messages
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find_map(|m| match m {
                Message::Human { content } => Some(content.clone()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();

        // Anything that smells mathy goes through the calculator tool.
        let mathy = question
            .chars()
            .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || "+-*/^().%".contains(*c))
            .count() as f64
            / question.chars().count().max(1) as f64;
        if let Some(expr) = extract_expression(&question)
            .filter(|_| question.contains("calculate") || question.contains("math") || mathy > 0.4)
        {
            return Ok(Message::AI {
                content: None,
                tool_calls: vec![ToolCall {
                    id: "call_demo_1".into(),
                    name: "calculator".into(),
                    args: serde_json::json!({ "expression": expr }),
                }],
            });
        }
        Ok(Message::ai(format!(
            "[demo] I received: “{question}”. I am a scripted model — run without --demo and \
             set OPENAI_API_KEY to talk to a real model."
        )))
    }

    async fn generate_with_tools(
        &self,
        messages: &[Message],
        _tools: &[crate::messages::ToolSpec],
    ) -> crate::errors::Result<Message> {
        self.generate(messages).await
    }
}

async fn run_chat(
    model_flag: Option<&str>,
    base_url_flag: Option<&str>,
    no_tools: bool,
    verbose: bool,
    allow_shell: bool,
    demo: bool,
) -> Result<()> {
    let model: Arc<dyn BaseChatModel> = if demo {
        Arc::new(DemoChatModel::new())
    } else {
        build_model(model_flag, base_url_flag)?
    };

    let mut builder = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
        .system_prompt(
            "You are a helpful AI agent running inside a terminal REPL. \
             Use tools when they help; be concise.",
        )
        .memory(Box::new(ConversationBufferMemory::new()))
        .verbose(verbose)
        .max_iterations(12);

    if !no_tools {
        builder = builder.tools(build_tools(allow_shell));
    }
    let mut agent = builder.build();

    println!("langchain-cli chat — type a task, /help for commands, /exit to quit");
    println!(
        "mode: {} | tools: {} | model: {}",
        if demo { "DEMO (offline)" } else { "live" },
        if no_tools { "off" } else { "on" },
        "auto"
    );

    let stdin = tokio::io::BufReader::new(tokio::io::stdin());
    use tokio::io::AsyncBufReadExt;
    let mut lines = stdin.lines();

    loop {
        print!("\x1b[32myou>\x1b[0m ");
        use std::io::Write as _;
        let _ = std::io::stdout().flush();

        let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? else {
            println!();
            break;
        };
        let line = line.trim().to_string();
        if line.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        match line.as_str() {
            "/exit" | "/quit" | "/q" => {
                println!("bye");
                break;
            }
            "/help" => {
                println!("commands: /help /memory /clear /exit — anything else goes to the agent");
                continue;
            }
            "/clear" => {
                agent.clear_memory();
                println!("memory cleared");
                continue;
            }
            "/memory" => {
                match agent.memory() {
                    Some(mem) => {
                        for m in mem.load() {
                            println!("  {:?}: {}", role_of(&m), m.text());
                        }
                    }
                    None => println!("  (no memory attached)"),
                }
                continue;
            }
            _ => {}
        }

        match agent.invoke(&line).await {
            Ok(answer) => println!("\x1b[36mai>\x1b[0m {answer}"),
            Err(e) => println!("\x1b[31merror>\x1b[0m {e}"),
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn role_of(m: &Message) -> &'static str {
    match m {
        Message::System { .. } => "system",
        Message::Human { .. } => "human",
        Message::AI { .. } => "ai",
        Message::Tool { .. } => "tool",
    }
}

async fn run_ask(
    question: &str,
    model_flag: Option<&str>,
    base_url_flag: Option<&str>,
    system: Option<&str>,
    no_stream: bool,
) -> Result<()> {
    let model = build_model(model_flag, base_url_flag)?;
    let mut messages: Vec<Message> = Vec::new();
    if let Some(sys) = system {
        messages.push(Message::system(sys));
    }
    messages.push(Message::human(question));



    if no_stream {
        let answer = model.generate(&messages).await?;
        println!("{}", answer.text());
    } else {
        let mut stream = model.stream_text(&messages);
        while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
            match chunk {
                Ok(t) => print!("{t}"),
                Err(e) => {
                    println!("\n\x1b[31merror>\x1b[0m {e}");
                    return Ok(());
                }
            }
        }
        println!();
    }
    if let Some(usage) = model.usage() {
        eprintln!(
            "[usage] prompt={} completion={} total={}",
            usage.prompt_tokens, usage.completion_tokens, usage.total_tokens
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn run_tools_list() {
    println!("built-in agent tools:");
    for (name, desc) in [
        ("calculator", "evaluates math expressions (+ - * / % ^, sqrt, abs, min, max…)"),
        ("read_file", "reads a UTF-8 text file"),
        ("write_file", "writes text to a file (creates parents)"),
        ("list_dir", "lists a directory"),
        ("run_shell", "runs `sh -c` commands — only with --allow-shell"),
    ] {
        println!("  {name:<12} {desc}");
    }
}

/// CLI entry point called from `main`.
pub async fn run() -> Result<()> {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    match cli.command {
        Commands::Chat {
            model,
            base_url,
            no_tools,
            verbose,
            allow_shell,
            demo,
        } => {
            run_chat(
                model.as_deref(),
                base_url.as_deref(),
                no_tools,
                verbose,
                allow_shell,
                demo,
            )
            .await
        }
        Commands::Ask {
            question,
            model,
            base_url,
            system,
            no_stream,
        } => {
            run_ask(
                &question,
                model.as_deref(),
                base_url.as_deref(),
                system.as_deref(),
                no_stream,
            )
            .await
        }
        Commands::Tools => {
            run_tools_list();
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

//! Embeddings — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.embeddings` (`Embeddings`
//! trait + `OpenAIEmbeddings` implementation).

pub mod openai;

use async_trait::async_trait;

use crate::errors::Result;

/// Turns text into a dense vector. Mirrors the Python `Embeddings` interface:
/// `embed_query` for search keys, `embed_documents` for corpus chunks.
#[async_trait]
pub trait Embeddings: Send + Sync {
    /// Embed a single query string.
    async fn embed_query(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>>;

    /// Embed many documents (batched by the implementation).
    async fn embed_documents(&self, texts: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>>;
}

/// Cosine similarity between two vectors. Returns 0 for zero-length inputs.
pub fn cosine_similarity(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    if a.len() != b.len() || a.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let dot: f32 = a.iter().zip(b.iter()).map(|(x, y)| x * y).sum();
    let na: f32 = a.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
    let nb: f32 = b.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
    if na == 0.0 || nb == 0.0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    dot / (na * nb)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn cosine_basics() {
        assert!((cosine_similarity(&[1.0, 0.0], &[1.0, 0.0]) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-6);
        assert!((cosine_similarity(&[1.0, 0.0], &[0.0, 1.0])).abs() < 1e-6);
        assert!((cosine_similarity(&[1.0, 0.0], &[-1.0, 0.0]) + 1.0).abs() < 1e-6);
        assert_eq!(cosine_similarity(&[], &[]), 0.0);
        assert_eq!(cosine_similarity(&[1.0], &[1.0, 2.0]), 0.0);
    }
}

//! `OpenAIEmbeddings` — calls `POST {base_url}/embeddings`.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use reqwest::header::{HeaderValue, AUTHORIZATION, CONTENT_TYPE};
use serde_json::json;

use crate::embeddings::Embeddings;
use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use std::time::Duration;

/// Embeddings backed by any OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint.
pub struct OpenAIEmbeddings {
    model: String,
    api_key: String,
    base_url: String,
    timeout: Duration,
    client: reqwest::Client,
}

impl OpenAIEmbeddings {
    /// Builder entry point.
    pub fn builder() -> OpenAIEmbeddingsBuilder {
        OpenAIEmbeddingsBuilder::default()
    }

    async fn embed(&self, inputs: Vec<String>) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
        let url = format!("{}/embeddings", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'));
        let body = json!({ "model": self.model, "input": inputs });
        let resp = self
            .client
            .post(&url)
            .header(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"))
            .header(AUTHORIZATION, format!("Bearer {}", self.api_key))
            .timeout(self.timeout)
            .json(&body)
            .send()
            .await?;

        let status = resp.status();
        let text = resp.text().await?;
        if !status.is_success() {
            return Err(LangchainError::LlmRequest(format!("HTTP {status}: {text}")));
        }
        let payload: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&text)
            .map_err(|e| LangchainError::LlmParse(format!("embeddings: {e}")))?;
        let arr = payload
            .get("data")
            .and_then(|d| d.as_array())
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::LlmParse("embeddings response missing `data`".into()))?;
        let mut vectors = arr
            .iter()
            .map(|item| {
                item.get("embedding")
                    .and_then(|e| e.as_array())
                    .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_f64()).map(|x| x as f32).collect::<Vec<f32>>())
                    .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::LlmParse("embedding entry missing".into()))
            })
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        // Some providers return unordered indices; sort by `index` when present.
        if let Some(first) = arr.first() {
            if first.get("index").is_some() {
                let mut paired: Vec<(usize, Vec<f32>)> = arr
                    .iter()
                    .zip(vectors.drain(..))
                    .map(|(item, v)| (item["index"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0) as usize, v))
                    .collect();
                paired.sort_by_key(|(i, _)| *i);
                vectors = paired.into_iter().map(|(_, v)| v).collect();
            }
        }
        Ok(vectors)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Embeddings for OpenAIEmbeddings {
    async fn embed_query(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
        let mut v = self.embed(vec![text.to_string()]).await?;
        v.pop()
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::LlmParse("empty embeddings response".into()))
    }

    async fn embed_documents(&self, texts: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
        self.embed(texts.to_vec()).await
    }
}

/// Builder for [`OpenAIEmbeddings`].
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct OpenAIEmbeddingsBuilder {
    model: Option<String>,
    api_key: Option<String>,
    base_url: Option<String>,
    timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
}

impl OpenAIEmbeddingsBuilder {
    /// Model id, e.g. `text-embedding-3-small`.
    pub fn model(mut self, model: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.model = Some(model.into());
        self
    }

    /// API key.
    pub fn api_key(mut self, key: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.api_key = Some(key.into());
        self
    }

    /// Base URL, default `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
    pub fn base_url(mut self, url: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.base_url = Some(url.into());
        self
    }

    /// Timeout seconds (default 60).
    pub fn timeout_secs(mut self, s: u64) -> Self {
        self.timeout_secs = Some(s);
        self
    }

    /// Validate and construct.
    pub fn build(self) -> Result<OpenAIEmbeddings> {
        let model = self.model.ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::InvalidInput("embeddings model is required".into()))?;
        let api_key = self.api_key.ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::InvalidInput("api_key is required".into()))?;
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| LangchainError::LlmRequest(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(OpenAIEmbeddings {
            model,
            api_key,
            base_url: self.base_url.unwrap_or_else(|| "https://api.openai.com/v1".into()),
            timeout: Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs.unwrap_or(60)),
            client,
        })
    }
}

//! Unified error type for the whole crate, mirroring `LangChainException` in Python.

use thiserror::Error;

/// The error type returned by every fallible operation in `langchain-rust`.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum LangchainError {
    /// A `{placeholder}` in a prompt template has no matching variable.
    #[error("missing template variable: {0}")]
    MissingVariable(String),

    /// The template contains unbalanced braces.
    #[error("invalid template: {0}")]
    InvalidTemplate(String),

    /// The configured model or provider rejected the request (HTTP or transport level).
    #[error("llm request failed: {0}")]
    LlmRequest(String),

    /// The provider answered with something this crate could not parse.
    #[error("failed to parse llm response: {0}")]
    LlmParse(String),

    /// A tool invocation failed.
    #[error("tool `{0}` failed: {1}")]
    ToolExecution(String, String),

    /// The agent executor exhausted `max_iterations` without producing a final answer.
    #[error("agent stopped after {0} iterations without a final answer")]
    AgentLoopLimit(usize),

    /// A tool requested by the model is not registered on the executor.
    #[error("unknown tool: {0}")]
    UnknownTool(String),

    /// Generic invalid input (e.g. malformed calculator expression).
    #[error("invalid input: {0}")]
    InvalidInput(String),

    /// The embedding dimension does not match the store dimension.
    #[error("dimension mismatch: expected {expected}, got {got}")]
    DimensionMismatch { expected: usize, got: usize },

    /// Anything else.
    #[error("{0}")]
    Other(String),
}

/// Convenience alias used across the crate.
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, LangchainError>;

impl From<serde_json::Error> for LangchainError {
    fn from(e: serde_json::Error) -> Self {
        LangchainError::LlmParse(e.to_string())
    }
}

impl From<reqwest::Error> for LangchainError {
    fn from(e: reqwest::Error) -> Self {
        LangchainError::LlmRequest(e.to_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn display_is_human_readable() {
        let e = LangchainError::MissingVariable("topic".into());
        assert_eq!(e.to_string(), "missing template variable: topic");
    }
}

//! Model abstractions — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.language_models`
//! (`BaseChatModel`) plus a deterministic `FakeChatModel` for tests.

pub mod openai;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use futures::stream::{once, BoxStream};

use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::messages::{Message, ToolSpec};

/// The chat-model interface every provider implements.
///
/// Mirrors `BaseChatModel` / `BaseChatModelWithToolCalling`:
/// - [`BaseChatModel::generate`] — plain completion.
/// - [`BaseChatModel::generate_with_tools`] — completion with tool definitions bound.
/// - [`BaseChatModel::stream_text`] — token streaming (defaults to one-shot).
#[async_trait]
pub trait BaseChatModel: Send + Sync {
    /// Model identifier reported in callbacks (e.g. `gpt-4o-mini`).
    fn model_name(&self) -> &str;

    /// Complete a conversation without tool bindings.
    async fn generate(&self, messages: &[Message]) -> Result<Message>;

    /// Complete a conversation with tool definitions available to the model.
    async fn generate_with_tools(&self, messages: &[Message], _tools: &[ToolSpec]) -> Result<Message> {
        // Providers without tool support degrade to plain generation.
        self.generate(messages).await
    }

    /// Stream the textual part of a completion as chunks.
    ///
    /// Default implementation: run `generate` and emit the whole text once.
    /// Tool calls are not surfaced through streaming; use `generate_with_tools`
    /// inside agent loops and keep streaming for display paths.
    fn stream_text<'a>(&'a self, messages: &'a [Message]) -> BoxStream<'a, Result<String>> {
        // Clone the messages so the future only borrows `self` with lifetime 'a.
        let msgs: Vec<Message> = messages.to_vec();
        let fut = async move {
            let msg = self.generate(&msgs).await?;
            Ok(msg.text().to_string())
        };
        Box::pin(once(fut))
    }

    /// Token counts reported by the provider, when available.
    fn usage(&self) -> Option<TokenUsage> {
        None
    }
}

/// Token accounting — `LLMResult.token_usage` in Python LangChain.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TokenUsage {
    pub prompt_tokens: u64,
    pub completion_tokens: u64,
    pub total_tokens: u64,
}

/// A scripted chat model for unit tests and `--demo` mode: returns the given
/// messages in order and errors when the script is exhausted.
///
/// If an item contains tool calls, they are returned verbatim so the agent
/// executor can be tested end-to-end without network access.
pub struct FakeChatModel {
    script: std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::VecDeque<Message>>,
    label: String,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for FakeChatModel {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("FakeChatModel")
    }
}

impl FakeChatModel {
    /// Queue the messages to return, one per `generate` call.
    pub fn new(script: Vec<Message>) -> Self {
        Self {
            script: std::sync::Mutex::new(script.into()),
            label: "fake".into(),
        }
    }

    /// Rename the model (shows up in callbacks).
    pub fn with_label(mut self, label: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.label = label.into();
        self
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BaseChatModel for FakeChatModel {
    fn model_name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.label
    }

    async fn generate(&self, _messages: &[Message]) -> Result<Message> {
        self.script
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| LangchainError::Other("fake model poisoned".into()))?
            .pop_front()
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::Other("fake model script exhausted".into()))
    }

    async fn generate_with_tools(&self, _messages: &[Message], _tools: &[ToolSpec]) -> Result<Message> {
        self.generate(_messages).await
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn fake_model_returns_script_in_order() {
        let m = FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai("one"), Message::ai("two")]);
        let m1 = m.generate(&[]).await.unwrap();
        let m2 = m.generate(&[]).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m1.text(), "one");
        assert_eq!(m2.text(), "two");
        assert!(m.generate(&[]).await.is_err());
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn default_stream_emits_whole_text() {
        use futures::StreamExt;
        let m = FakeChatModel::new(vec![Message::ai("hello world")]);
        let chunks: Vec<_> = m.stream_text(&[]).collect().await;
        assert_eq!(chunks[0].as_ref().unwrap(), "hello world");
    }
}

````rust
//! OpenAI-compatible chat client — `ChatOpenAI`.
//!
//! Works with any server exposing `/chat/completions`: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI,
//! LM Studio, vLLM, Ollama's OpenAI compatibility layer, llama.cpp server, etc.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let model = ChatOpenAI::builder()
//!     .model("gpt-4o-mini")
//!     .api_key(std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY").unwrap())
//!     .temperature(0.2)
//!     .build()?;
//! ```

use async_trait::async_trait;
use futures::future::FutureExt;
use futures::stream::{self, BoxStream, StreamExt};
use reqwest::header::{HeaderValue, AUTHORIZATION, CONTENT_TYPE};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::llms::{BaseChatModel, TokenUsage};
use crate::messages::{Message, ToolCall, ToolSpec};

/// Chat completion model for every OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
pub struct ChatOpenAI {
    model: String,
    api_key: String,
    base_url: String,
    temperature: f64,
    max_tokens: Option<u32>,
    timeout: Duration,
    client: reqwest::Client,
    usage: Mutex<TokenUsage>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for ChatOpenAI {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("ChatOpenAI")
            .field("model", &self.model)
            .field("base_url", &self.base_url)
            .field("temperature", &self.temperature)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl ChatOpenAI {
    /// Builder entry point.
    pub fn builder() -> ChatOpenAIBuilder {
        ChatOpenAIBuilder::default()
    }

    /// Serialise messages + tools into the request body.
    fn build_body(messages: &[Message], tools: &[ToolSpec]) -> Value {
        let mut body = json!({
            "messages": messages.iter().map(|m| m.to_openai_json()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        });
        if !tools.is_empty() {
            body["tools"] = Value::Array(tools.iter().map(|t| t.to_openai_json()).collect());
        }
        body
    }

    fn inject_options(&self, body: &mut Value) {
        body["model"] = json!(self.model);
        body["temperature"] = json!(self.temperature);
        if let Some(mt) = self.max_tokens {
            body["max_tokens"] = json!(mt);
        }
    }

    /// POST and read the full JSON response, mapping provider errors to
    /// [`LangchainError::LlmRequest`]. Transient provider failures
    /// (overloaded gateways, 429/5xx) are retried with backoff instead of
    /// killing the whole agent turn.
    async fn post(&self, body: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
        const MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 4;
        for attempt in 1..=MAX_ATTEMPTS {
            match self.post_once(body).await {
                Ok(v) => return Ok(v),
                Err(e) => {
                    let transient = match &e {
                        LangchainError::LlmRequest(t) => is_transient_text(t),
                        _ => false,
                    };
                    if !transient || attempt == MAX_ATTEMPTS {
                        return Err(e);
                    }
                    let wait = std::time::Duration::from_secs(2u64.pow(attempt - 1) * 2);
                    tokio::time::sleep(wait).await;
                }
            }
        }
        unreachable!("retry loop always returns")
    }

    async fn post_once(&self, body: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
        let url = format!("{}/chat/completions", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'));
        let resp = self
            .client
            .post(&url)
            .header(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"))
            .header(AUTHORIZATION, format!("Bearer {}", self.api_key))
            .timeout(self.timeout)
            .json(body)
            .send()
            .await?;

        let status = resp.status();
        let text = resp.text().await?;
        if !status.is_success() {
            return Err(LangchainError::LlmRequest(format!("HTTP {status}: {}", truncate(&text, 400))));
        }
        serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text).map_err(|e| {
            LangchainError::LlmParse(format!("non-JSON response: {e}: {}", truncate(&text, 200)))
        })
    }

    /// Extract the assistant `Message` (with tool calls) from a completion payload.
    fn parse_choice(payload: &Value) -> Result<Message> {
        let choice = payload
            .get("choices")
            .and_then(|c| c.get(0))
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::LlmParse("response missing `choices[0]`".into()))?;

        let content = choice
            .get("message")
            .and_then(|m| m.get("content"))
            .and_then(|c| c.as_str())
            .map(|s| s.to_string());

        let mut tool_calls = Vec::new();
        if let Some(tcs) = choice
            .get("message")
            .and_then(|m| m.get("tool_calls"))
            .and_then(|t| t.as_array())
        {
            for tc in tcs {
                // Several OpenAI-compatible gateways (NVIDIA NIM, minimax,
                // Coarena, …) omit `id` on tool calls. Echoing an empty id back
                // makes them reject the next request with "tool_call_id must
                // be a non-empty string" — synthesize a stable id instead so
                // the assistant tool_call and its tool result always match.
                let id = match tc.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
                    Some(s) if !s.trim().is_empty() => s.to_string(),
                    _ => next_local_call_id(),
                };
                let name = tc
                    .pointer("/function/name")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .unwrap_or("")
                    .to_string();
                let raw_args = tc
                    .pointer("/function/arguments")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .unwrap_or("{}");
                let args: Value = serde_json::from_str(raw_args)
                    .unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({ "_raw_arguments": raw_args }));
                tool_calls.push(ToolCall { id, name, args });
            }
        }

        Ok(Message::AI { content, tool_calls })
    }

    fn record_usage(&self, payload: &Value) {
        if let Some(u) = payload.get("usage") {
            let pt = u.get("prompt_tokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0);
            let ct = u.get("completion_tokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0);
            let tt = u.get("total_tokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0);
            if let Ok(mut guard) = self.usage.lock() {
                guard.prompt_tokens += pt;
                guard.completion_tokens += ct;
                guard.total_tokens += tt;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Open the SSE stream and return a `'static` stream of raw byte chunks.
    ///
    /// No total request timeout is applied here: reqwest's per-request
    /// `.timeout()` runs until the response BODY is fully read, which killed
    /// healthy long streams mid-generation. Connection establishment is
    /// still bounded by the client's `connect_timeout`.
    async fn open_sse(
        &self,
        messages: &[Message],
        tools: &[ToolSpec],
    ) -> Result<BoxStream<'static, Result<Vec<u8>>>> {
        let url = format!("{}/chat/completions", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'));
        let mut body = Self::build_body(messages, tools);
        self.inject_options(&mut body);
        body["stream"] = json!(true);

        let resp = self
            .client
            .post(&url)
            .header(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"))
            .header(AUTHORIZATION, format!("Bearer {}", self.api_key))
            // Intentionally no `.timeout(self.timeout)` — see doc comment.
            .json(&body)
            .send()
            .await?;

        let status = resp.status();
        if !status.is_success() {
            let text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(LangchainError::LlmRequest(format!("HTTP {status}: {}", truncate(&text, 400))));
        }

        Ok(Box::pin(resp.bytes_stream().map(|chunk| {
            chunk.map(|b| b.to_vec()).map_err(LangchainError::from)
        })))
    }

    /// Shared SSE driver: buffer raw bytes across TCP chunks, split complete
    /// events on `\n\n` boundaries, decode each event once and parse the
    /// `data:` payloads. Terminates the whole stream on `data: [DONE]`.
    fn sse_to_deltas(raw: BoxStream<'static, Result<Vec<u8>>>) -> BoxStream<'static, Result<String>> {
        stream::unfold(
            (raw, SseBuffer::default()),
            |(mut raw, mut st)| async move {
                loop {
                    if st.done {
                        return None;
                    }
                    // Yield deltas from complete buffered events first.
                    if let Some(event) = st.take_event() {
                        let delta = parse_sse_event(&event, &mut st);
                        if st.done && delta.is_none() {
                            return None;
                        }
                        if let Some(delta) = delta {
                            return Some((Ok(delta), (raw, st)));
                        }
                        continue;
                    }
                    // Need more bytes from the wire.
                    match raw.next().await {
                        Some(Ok(bytes)) => st.buf.extend_from_slice(&bytes),
                        Some(Err(e)) => return Some((Err(e), (raw, st))),
                        None => {
                            // Stream ended: flush any trailing unterminated event.
                            if st.buf.is_empty() {
                                return None;
                            }
                            let rest = std::mem::take(&mut st.buf);
                            let event = String::from_utf8_lossy(&rest).into_owned();
                            let delta = parse_sse_event(&event, &mut st);
                            match delta {
                                Some(d) if !st.done => return Some((Ok(d), (raw, st))),
                                _ => return None,
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            },
        )
        .boxed()
    }
}

/// Byte buffer that only hands out COMPLETE SSE events: an event ends at an
/// empty line (`\n\n`, or `\r\n\r\n`/`\n\r\n` for CRLF servers). Decoding at
/// event level keeps multi-byte UTF-8 sequences that straddle TCP chunk
/// boundaries intact.
#[derive(Default)]
struct SseBuffer {
    buf: Vec<u8>,
    done: bool,
}

impl SseBuffer {
    /// Extract the next complete event from the buffer, if one has fully
    /// arrived. Incomplete events stay buffered for the next chunk.
    fn take_event(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < self.buf.len() {
            if self.buf[i] == b'\n' {
                let boundary = if self.buf.get(i + 1) == Some(&b'\n') {
                    2
                } else if self.buf.get(i + 1) == Some(&b'\r') && self.buf.get(i + 2) == Some(&b'\n') {
                    3
                } else {
                    0
                };
                if boundary > 0 {
                    let event = self.buf.drain(..i).collect::<Vec<u8>>();
                    self.buf.drain(..boundary);
                    return Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&event).into_owned());
                }
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        None
    }
}

/// Parse one SSE event into its `data:` payload(s); returns the next text
/// delta, if any. Empty lines and `:`-prefixed commentary (keep-alives) are
/// skipped silently; a non-empty unparseable payload is logged and skipped.
fn parse_sse_event(event: &str, st: &mut SseBuffer) -> Option<String> {
    let mut data_lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for line in event.lines() {
        let line = line.trim_end_matches('\r');
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with(':') {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(data) = line.strip_prefix("data:") {
            // Strip the field name, then leading space — handles both the
            // `data: {...}` and the spaceless `data:{...}` SSE forms.
            let data = data.trim_start();
            if data.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            if data == "[DONE]" {
                st.done = true;
                continue;
            }
            data_lines.push(data.to_string());
        }
        // Other fields (`event:`, `id:`, `retry:`) carry no deltas.
    }
    if data_lines.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let payload = data_lines.join("\n");
    match serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&payload) {
        Ok(v) => v
            .pointer("/choices/0/delta/content")
            .and_then(|c| c.as_str())
            .filter(|t| !t.is_empty())
            .map(|t| t.to_string()),
        Err(e) => {
            // Do not swallow JSON failures invisibly.
            eprintln!(
                "langchain: skipping unparseable SSE data payload ({e}): {}",
                truncate(&payload, 200)
            );
            None
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BaseChatModel for ChatOpenAI {
    fn model_name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.model
    }

    async fn generate(&self, messages: &[Message]) -> Result<Message> {
        let mut body = Self::build_body(messages, &[]);
        self.inject_options(&mut body);
        let payload = self.post(&body).await?;
        self.record_usage(&payload);
        Self::parse_choice(&payload)
    }

    async fn generate_with_tools(&self, messages: &[Message], tools: &[ToolSpec]) -> Result<Message> {
        let mut body = Self::build_body(messages, tools);
        self.inject_options(&mut body);
        let payload = self.post(&body).await?;
        self.record_usage(&payload);
        Self::parse_choice(&payload)
    }

    /// Stream assistant text deltas. Terminates on the SSE `data: [DONE]` sentinel.
    fn stream_text<'a>(&'a self, messages: &'a [Message]) -> BoxStream<'a, Result<String>> {
        let this: &'a ChatOpenAI = self;
        let msgs: Vec<Message> = messages.to_vec();
        // Future: open the HTTP stream, then flatten it into the item stream.
        // Errors surface as the first stream item.
        let fut = async move {
            match this.open_sse(&msgs, &[]).await {
                Ok(raw) => ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw),
                Err(e) => stream::iter(vec![Err(e)]).boxed(),
            }
        };
        fut.flatten_stream().boxed()
    }

    fn usage(&self) -> Option<TokenUsage> {
        self.usage.lock().ok().map(|g| *g)
    }
}

fn truncate(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() <= n {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{}…", s.chars().take(n).collect::<String>())
    }
}

/// Builder for [`ChatOpenAI`].
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct ChatOpenAIBuilder {
    model: Option<String>,
    api_key: Option<String>,
    base_url: Option<String>,
    temperature: Option<f64>,
    max_tokens: Option<u32>,
    timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
}

impl ChatOpenAIBuilder {
    /// Model id, e.g. `gpt-4o-mini`.
    pub fn model(mut self, model: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.model = Some(model.into());
        self
    }

    /// API key (`Authorization: Bearer ...`).
    pub fn api_key(mut self, key: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.api_key = Some(key.into());
        self
    }

    /// Base URL, default `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
    pub fn base_url(mut self, url: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.base_url = Some(url.into());
        self
    }

    /// Sampling temperature (default 0.7).
    pub fn temperature(mut self, t: f64) -> Self {
        self.temperature = Some(t);
        self
    }

    /// Max completion tokens.
    pub fn max_tokens(mut self, n: u32) -> Self {
        self.max_tokens = Some(n);
        self
    }

    /// Request timeout in seconds (default 120).
    pub fn timeout_secs(mut self, s: u64) -> Self {
        self.timeout_secs = Some(s);
        self
    }

    /// Validate and construct.
    pub fn build(self) -> Result<ChatOpenAI> {
        let model = self
            .model
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::InvalidInput("model is required".into()))?;
        let api_key = self
            .api_key
            .ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::InvalidInput("api_key is required".into()))?;
        let base_url = self
            .base_url
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "https://api.openai.com/v1".to_string());
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            // Bound connection establishment + TLS handshake; body reads are
            // NOT limited (long-lived SSE streams) and non-streaming calls
            // carry their own per-request `.timeout(self.timeout)`.
            .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| LangchainError::LlmRequest(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(ChatOpenAI {
            model,
            api_key,
            base_url,
            temperature: self.temperature.unwrap_or(0.7),
            max_tokens: self.max_tokens,
            timeout: Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs.unwrap_or(120)),
            client,
            usage: Mutex::new(TokenUsage::default()),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parse_choice_extracts_tool_calls() {
        let payload = json!({
            "choices": [{
                "message": {
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "content": null,
                    "tool_calls": [{
                        "id": "call_1",
                        "type": "function",
                        "function": {"name": "calc", "arguments": "{\"x\":2}"}
                    }]
                }
            }],
            "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 5, "total_tokens": 15}
        });
        let m = ChatOpenAI::parse_choice(&payload).unwrap();
        match m {
            Message::AI { content, tool_calls } => {
                assert_eq!(content, None);
                assert_eq!(tool_calls.len(), 1);
                assert_eq!(tool_calls[0].name, "calc");
                assert_eq!(tool_calls[0].args["x"], 2);
            }
            other => panic!("wrong variant: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_choice_synthesizes_missing_tool_call_id() {
        // NVIDIA NIM / minimax / Coarena-style gateways stream tool calls
        // without an `id`. The parser must synthesize a non-empty one —
        // echoing "" back gets the request rejected ("tool_call_id must be
        // a non-empty string").
        let payload = json!({
            "choices": [{
                "message": {
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "content": null,
                    "tool_calls": [{
                        "type": "function",
                        "function": {"name": "calc", "arguments": "{}"}
                    }]
                }
            }]
        });
        let m = ChatOpenAI::parse_choice(&payload).unwrap();
        match m {
            Message::AI { tool_calls, .. } => {
                assert_eq!(tool_calls.len(), 1);
                assert!(!tool_calls[0].id.trim().is_empty(), "id must not be empty");
                assert!(tool_calls[0].id.starts_with("call_romacode_"));
            }
            other => panic!("wrong variant: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_choice_plain_text() {
        let payload = json!({"choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "hi"}}]});
        let m = ChatOpenAI::parse_choice(&payload).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.text(), "hi");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_choice_missing_choices_errors() {
        assert!(ChatOpenAI::parse_choice(&json!({"error": "x"})).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn builder_requires_model_and_key() {
        assert!(ChatOpenAI::builder().build().is_err());
        assert!(ChatOpenAI::builder().model("m").build().is_err());
        assert!(ChatOpenAI::builder().model("m").api_key("k").build().is_ok());
    }

    fn raw_stream(chunks: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> BoxStream<'static, Result<Vec<u8>>> {
        stream::iter(chunks.into_iter().map(Ok)).boxed()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_event_split_across_chunks_is_parsed_exactly_once() {
        // Regression (H3): each TCP chunk used to be decoded and parsed
        // independently, so a `data: {...}` event straddling a chunk
        // boundary failed to parse in BOTH halves and was silently dropped.
        let full = "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"hi\"}}]}\n\n";
        let bytes = full.as_bytes();
        let split = bytes.len() / 2; // mid-JSON
        let deltas: Vec<String> = ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw_stream(vec![
            bytes[..split].to_vec(),
            bytes[split..].to_vec(),
        ]))
        .map(|r| r.unwrap())
        .collect()
        .await;
        assert_eq!(deltas, vec!["hi".to_string()], "event must be received exactly once");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_multibyte_utf8_split_across_chunks() {
        // `é` is two UTF-8 bytes; split the byte stream INSIDE the character.
        let event = "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"héllo wörld\"}}]}\n\n";
        let bytes = event.as_bytes();
        let mid = event.find('é').unwrap() + 1;
        let deltas: Vec<String> = ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw_stream(vec![
            bytes[..mid].to_vec(),
            bytes[mid..].to_vec(),
        ]))
        .map(|r| r.unwrap())
        .collect()
        .await;
        assert_eq!(deltas, vec!["héllo wörld".to_string()]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_done_terminates_the_outer_stream() {
        // Regression: `break` on [DONE] only exited the inner line loop, so
        // the stream kept polling the wire after completion.
        let ev = "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"a\"}}]}\n\n";
        let done = "data: [DONE]\n\n";
        let never = "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"NEVER\"}}]}\n\n";
        let deltas: Vec<String> = ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw_stream(vec![
            format!("{ev}{done}").into_bytes(),
            never.as_bytes().to_vec(),
        ]))
        .map(|r| r.unwrap())
        .collect()
        .await;
        assert_eq!(deltas, vec!["a".to_string()]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_spaceless_data_prefix_and_commentary() {
        // Regression (M38c): `strip_prefix("data: ")` missed the spaceless
        // `data:{...}` form; keep-alive commentary lines must be skipped.
        let raw = raw_stream(vec![
            b": keep-alive\n\ndata:{\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"x\"}}]}\n\ndata: \n\n".to_vec(),
        ]);
        let deltas: Vec<String> = ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw).map(|r| r.unwrap()).collect().await;
        assert_eq!(deltas, vec!["x".to_string()]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_unparseable_payload_is_logged_and_skipped() {
        let raw = raw_stream(vec![
            b"data: {not-json}\n\ndata: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"ok\"}}]}\n\n".to_vec(),
        ]);
        let deltas: Vec<String> = ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw).map(|r| r.unwrap()).collect().await;
        assert_eq!(deltas, vec!["ok".to_string()], "bad payload skipped, good one parsed");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_crlf_event_boundaries() {
        let raw = raw_stream(vec![
            b"data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"c\"}}]}\r\n\r\n".to_vec(),
        ]);
        let deltas: Vec<String> = ChatOpenAI::sse_to_deltas(raw).map(|r| r.unwrap()).collect().await;
        assert_eq!(deltas, vec!["c".to_string()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn transient_detection_is_precise() {
        // Regression (M38b): bare numeric substrings ("500") matched
        // permanent 400 responses whose body mentioned e.g. max_tokens: 500.
        assert!(!is_transient_text(
            "HTTP 400 Bad Request: {\"error\":{\"message\":\"max_tokens must be at most 500\"}}"
        ));
        assert!(!is_transient_text("HTTP 401 Unauthorized: invalid api key"));
        assert!(!is_transient_text("HTTP 404 Not Found: model not found"));
        // Exact transient statuses still match at the status position.
        assert!(is_transient_text("HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: slow down"));
        assert!(is_transient_text("HTTP 500 Internal Server Error"));
        assert!(is_transient_text("HTTP 503: overloaded"));
        // Structured error types/phrases from the body.
        assert!(is_transient_text("HTTP 429: {\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}}"));
        assert!(is_transient_text("connection reset by peer"));
        assert!(is_transient_text("operation timed out"));
    }
}

/// Process-unique fallback id for tool calls that arrive without one.
/// Both the assistant `tool_calls[].id` and the matching `tool` message's
/// `tool_call_id` get the same value, so gateways that dropped the id still
/// see a consistent request/response pair.
pub fn next_local_call_id() -> String {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
    static N: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    format!("call_romacode_{}", N.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed))
}

/// Shared transient-failure detector for provider error text (overloaded
/// gateways, rate limits, 429/5xx). Used by the retry path in `ChatOpenAI`.
///
/// Detection is deliberately precise: exact HTTP status codes read from the
/// `HTTP <code>` prefix the client formats, plus structured error types and
/// established transient phrases. Bare numeric substrings ("500") must NOT
/// match — a permanent 400 whose body mentions e.g. `max_tokens: 500` used
/// to be retried as if it were transient.
fn is_transient_text(t: &str) -> bool {
    let l = t.to_lowercase();
    if let Some(rest) = l.strip_prefix("http ") {
        // Errors are formatted as `HTTP {status}: {body}`; match the status
        // position exactly instead of anywhere in the text.
        let code = rest.get(0..3).unwrap_or("");
        if matches!(code, "429" | "500" | "502" | "503" | "504") {
            return true;
        }
    }
    [
        "rate_limit",
        "rate limit",
        "overloaded",
        "overload",
        "over capacity",
        "too many requests",
        "service unavailable",
        "bad gateway",
        "gateway timeout",
        "internal server error",
        "server_error",
        "temporarily",
        "try again",
        "timed out",
        "timeout",
        "connection reset",
    ]
    .iter()
    .any(|k| l.contains(k))
}

//! Conversation memory — the Rust mirror of `langchain.memory`
//! (`ConversationBufferMemory`, windowed variant).

use crate::messages::Message;

/// Storage for conversation history used by chains and the agent executor.
pub trait Memory: Send + Sync {
    /// Current history, oldest first.
    fn load(&self) -> Vec<Message>;

    /// Record one user turn and the assistant's final answer.
    fn save_turn(&mut self, user_input: &str, ai_output: &str);

    /// Record arbitrary messages (e.g. full agent trajectory).
    fn push(&mut self, message: Message);

    /// Drop all history.
    fn clear(&mut self);
}

/// Keeps every message forever — `ConversationBufferMemory`.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ConversationBufferMemory {
    messages: Vec<Message>,
}

impl ConversationBufferMemory {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
}

impl Memory for ConversationBufferMemory {
    fn load(&self) -> Vec<Message> {
        self.messages.clone()
    }

    fn save_turn(&mut self, user_input: &str, ai_output: &str) {
        self.messages.push(Message::human(user_input));
        self.messages.push(Message::ai(ai_output));
    }

    fn push(&mut self, message: Message) {
        self.messages.push(message);
    }

    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.messages.clear();
    }
}

/// Keeps only the last `k` message pairs — `ConversationBufferWindowMemory`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct WindowBufferMemory {
    window: usize,
    messages: Vec<Message>,
}

impl WindowBufferMemory {
    /// `window` counts message *pairs*; `2 * window` messages are retained.
    pub fn new(window: usize) -> Self {
        Self { window: window.max(1), messages: Vec::new() }
    }
}

/// An exchange begins at a human (or system) turn; AI/tool messages belong
/// to the exchange that opened before them.
fn is_exchange_start(m: &Message) -> bool {
    matches!(m, Message::Human { .. } | Message::System { .. })
}

/// Index where the trimmed window must start: the last `keep` messages,
/// adjusted to an exchange boundary so the window never OPENS with an
/// orphaned AI/tool message (strict gateways reject mid-pair windows).
fn window_start(msgs: &[Message], keep: usize) -> usize {
    if msgs.len() <= keep {
        return 0;
    }
    let cut = msgs.len() - keep;
    // A clean boundary at or after the cut: drop the partial leading
    // exchange whole.
    let mut start = cut;
    while start < msgs.len() && !is_exchange_start(&msgs[start]) {
        start += 1;
    }
    if start >= msgs.len() {
        // The whole tail is one (in-flight) exchange with no boundary after
        // the cut — keep it intact by walking back to its first message. It
        // will be dropped whole once the next exchange opens.
        start = cut;
        while start > 0 && !is_exchange_start(&msgs[start]) {
            start -= 1;
        }
    }
    start
}

impl Memory for WindowBufferMemory {
    fn load(&self) -> Vec<Message> {
        let start = window_start(&self.messages, self.window * 2);
        self.messages[start..].to_vec()
    }

    fn save_turn(&mut self, user_input: &str, ai_output: &str) {
        self.push(Message::human(user_input));
        self.push(Message::ai(ai_output));
    }

    fn push(&mut self, message: Message) {
        self.messages.push(message);
        let keep = self.window * 2;
        if self.messages.len() > keep {
            let start = window_start(&self.messages, keep);
            self.messages.drain(..start);
        }
    }

    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.messages.clear();
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn buffer_keeps_everything() {
        let mut m = ConversationBufferMemory::new();
        m.save_turn("hi", "hello");
        m.save_turn("who", "me");
        assert_eq!(m.load().len(), 4);
        m.clear();
        assert!(m.load().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn window_keeps_last_pairs() {
        let mut m = WindowBufferMemory::new(2);
        for i in 0..5 {
            m.save_turn(&format!("q{i}"), &format!("a{i}"));
        }
        let msgs = m.load();
        assert_eq!(msgs.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(msgs[0].text(), "q3");
        assert_eq!(msgs[3].text(), "a4");
    }

    #[test]
    fn window_trims_on_pair_boundaries() {
        // Regression (M36): trimming by plain message count cut message
        // pairs in half — a window opening with an orphaned AI/tool message
        // is rejected by strict gateways. Trim must drop whole exchanges.
        let mut m = WindowBufferMemory::new(1); // keep = 2 messages
        m.push(Message::human("q1"));
        m.push(Message::ai("thinking"));
        m.push(Message::tool("call_1", "search", "result"));
        m.push(Message::ai("a1")); // first exchange complete
        m.push(Message::human("q2"));
        let msgs = m.load();
        // The window must OPEN at a human turn, never with the orphaned
        // AI/tool tail of the first exchange.
        assert!(!msgs.is_empty());
        assert!(matches!(msgs[0], Message::Human { .. }), "window opens mid-pair: {msgs:?}");
        assert_eq!(msgs[0].text(), "q2");

        // Same behavior via `load()` on a buffer trimmed only by `load`.
        let mut m2 = WindowBufferMemory::new(1);
        m2.push(Message::ai("orphan head"));
        m2.push(Message::human("q"));
        m2.push(Message::ai("a"));
        let msgs = m2.load();
        assert!(matches!(msgs[0], Message::Human { .. }), "window opens mid-pair: {msgs:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn window_keeps_in_flight_exchange_intact() {
        // When the entire tail is one incomplete exchange, it is kept whole
        // (from its human turn) rather than opening the window mid-pair.
        let mut m = WindowBufferMemory::new(1);
        m.push(Message::human("q1"));
        m.push(Message::ai("mid"));
        m.push(Message::tool("call_1", "calc", "4"));
        m.push(Message::ai("still working"));
        let msgs = m.load();
        assert!(matches!(msgs[0], Message::Human { .. }), "window opens mid-pair: {msgs:?}");
    }
}
