//! Chat message primitives — the Rust equivalent of
//! `langchain_core.messages` (`SystemMessage`, `HumanMessage`, `AIMessage`, `ToolMessage`).

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

/// A tool invocation requested by the model (`AIMessage.tool_calls`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolCall {
    /// OpenAI style call id (e.g. `call_abc123`).
    pub id: String,
    /// Name of the tool the model wants to run.
    pub name: String,
    /// Arguments as a JSON object.
    pub args: Value,
}

/// OpenAI `tools` parameter entry describing a callable function.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolSpec {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    /// JSON Schema for the tool arguments.
    pub parameters: Value,
}

impl ToolSpec {
    /// Build the full OpenAI request body fragment:
    /// `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": ..., "description": ..., "parameters": ...}}`.
    pub fn to_openai_json(&self) -> Value {
        serde_json::json!({
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": self.name,
                "description": self.description,
                "parameters": self.parameters,
            }
        })
    }
}

/// A single message in a chat conversation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "role", rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Message {
    /// `system` message — sets behaviour.
    System {
        content: String,
    },
    /// `user` message.
    Human {
        content: String,
    },
    /// `assistant` message; may carry tool invocations.
    AI {
        /// Text content, `None` when the model only requested tools.
        content: Option<String>,
        /// Tool calls requested by the model (empty for plain answers).
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
        tool_calls: Vec<ToolCall>,
    },
    /// `tool` message — the result of a tool call, addressed by `tool_call_id`.
    Tool {
        tool_call_id: String,
        name: String,
        content: String,
    },
}

impl Message {
    /// Shorthand constructor for a system message.
    pub fn system(content: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Message::System {
            content: content.into(),
        }
    }

    /// Shorthand constructor for a human message.
    pub fn human(content: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Message::Human {
            content: content.into(),
        }
    }

    /// Shorthand constructor for a plain (no tools) AI message.
    pub fn ai(content: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Message::AI {
            content: Some(content.into()),
            tool_calls: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Shorthand constructor for a tool result message.
    pub fn tool(tool_call_id: impl Into<String>, name: impl Into<String>, content: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Message::Tool {
            tool_call_id: tool_call_id.into(),
            name: name.into(),
            content: content.into(),
        }
    }

    /// The textual content of the message, ignoring tool calls.
    pub fn text(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            Message::System { content } | Message::Human { content } | Message::Tool { content, .. } => content,
            Message::AI { content, .. } => content.as_deref().unwrap_or(""),
        }
    }

    /// Serialise to the exact JSON shape the OpenAI chat-completions API expects.
    pub fn to_openai_json(&self) -> Value {
        match self {
            Message::System { content } => serde_json::json!({ "role": "system", "content": content }),
            Message::Human { content } => serde_json::json!({ "role": "user", "content": content }),
            Message::AI { content, tool_calls } => {
                let mut obj = serde_json::json!({ "role": "assistant", "content": content });
                if !tool_calls.is_empty() {
                    obj["tool_calls"] = Value::Array(
                        tool_calls
                            .iter()
                            .map(|tc| {
                                serde_json::json!({
                                    "id": tc.id,
                                    "type": "function",
                                    "function": {
                                        "name": tc.name,
                                        "arguments": tc.args.to_string(),
                                    }
                                })
                            })
                            .collect(),
                    );
                }
                obj
            }
            Message::Tool { tool_call_id, name, content } => serde_json::json!({
                "role": "tool",
                "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
                "name": name,
                "content": content,
            }),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn openai_serialisation_roundtrip() {
        let ai = Message::AI {
            content: None,
            tool_calls: vec![ToolCall {
                id: "call_1".into(),
                name: "calculator".into(),
                args: serde_json::json!({"expression": "2+2"}),
            }],
        };
        let j = ai.to_openai_json();
        assert_eq!(j["role"], "assistant");
        assert_eq!(j["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["name"], "calculator");
        assert_eq!(j["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["arguments"], r#"{"expression":"2+2"}"#);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tool_message_shape() {
        let m = Message::tool("call_1", "calculator", "4");
        let j = m.to_openai_json();
        assert_eq!(j["role"], "tool");
        assert_eq!(j["tool_call_id"], "call_1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn text_helper() {
        assert_eq!(Message::human("hi").text(), "hi");
        let ai = Message::AI { content: None, tool_calls: vec![] };
        assert_eq!(ai.text(), "");
    }
}

//! Output parsers — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.output_parsers`.
//!
//! Parsers are plain `Runnable`s taking the raw model text, so they compose
//! with `.pipe(...)` exactly like any other step.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::runnables::Runnable;

/// Returns the model text untouched — `StrOutputParser`.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct StrOutputParser;

#[async_trait]
impl Runnable<String, String> for StrOutputParser {
    async fn invoke(&self, input: String) -> Result<String> {
        Ok(input)
    }
}

/// Parses the first JSON object/array found in the text — `JsonOutputParser`.
///
/// Tolerates markdown fences and surrounding prose: if the whole string is not
/// valid JSON, the first balanced `{...}` / `[...]` block is extracted.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct JsonOutputParser;

#[async_trait]
impl Runnable<String, Value> for JsonOutputParser {
    async fn invoke(&self, input: String) -> Result<Value> {
        let trimmed = input.trim();
        // Strip markdown code fences like ```json ... ```
        let cleaned = if trimmed.starts_with("```") {
            let inner = trimmed.trim_start_matches("```json").trim_start_matches("```");
            inner.trim_end_matches("```").trim()
        } else {
            trimmed
        };

        if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(cleaned) {
            return Ok(v);
        }

        // Fall back: extract the first balanced JSON block.
        for (open, close) in [('{', '}'), ('[', ']')] {
            if let Some(v) = extract_balanced(cleaned, open, close) {
                if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&v) {
                    return Ok(v);
                }
            }
        }
        Err(LangchainError::LlmParse(format!("no valid JSON found in: {}", truncate(&input, 120))))
    }
}

fn extract_balanced(s: &str, open: char, close: char) -> Option<String> {
    let bytes: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    for (i, &c) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
        if c == open {
            let mut depth = 0usize;
            let mut in_string = false;
            let mut escape = false;
            for j in i..bytes.len() {
                let c = bytes[j];
                if escape {
                    escape = false;
                } else if in_string {
                    if c == '\\' {
                        escape = true;
                    } else if c == '"' {
                        in_string = false;
                    }
                } else if c == '"' {
                    in_string = true;
                } else if c == open {
                    depth += 1;
                } else if c == close {
                    depth -= 1;
                    if depth == 0 {
                        return Some(bytes[i..=j].iter().collect());
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn truncate(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() <= n {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{}…", s.chars().take(n).collect::<String>())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn str_parser_identity() {
        let p = StrOutputParser;
        assert_eq!(p.invoke("hi".into()).await.unwrap(), "hi");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn json_parser_plain() {
        let p = JsonOutputParser;
        assert_eq!(p.invoke(r#"{"a": 1}"#.into()).await.unwrap(), serde_json::json!({"a": 1}));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn json_parser_fenced_and_noisy() {
        let p = JsonOutputParser;
        let text = "Here you go:\n```json\n{\"name\": \"rust\", \"n\": 2}\n```\nHope that helps";
        assert_eq!(
            p.invoke(text.into()).await.unwrap(),
            serde_json::json!({"name": "rust", "n": 2})
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn json_parser_embedded_object() {
        let p = JsonOutputParser;
        let text = r#"prefix {"ok": true, "s": "a\"b}c"} suffix"#;
        assert_eq!(
            p.invoke(text.into()).await.unwrap(),
            serde_json::json!({"ok": true, "s": "a\"b}c"})
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn json_parser_failure() {
        let p = JsonOutputParser;
        assert!(p.invoke("no json here".into()).await.is_err());
    }
}

````rust
//! Prompt templates — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.prompts`
//! (`PromptTemplate`, `ChatPromptTemplate`, `MessagesPlaceholder`).
//!
//! Syntax is the Python f-string style used by LangChain: `{variable}`, with
//! `{{` and `}}` escaping literal braces.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use std::collections::HashMap;

use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::messages::Message;
use crate::runnables::Runnable;

/// One slot of a [`ChatPromptTemplate`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum ChatSlot {
    /// A templated system message.
    System(String),
    /// A templated human message.
    Human(String),
    /// A templated AI message (rarely used, but valid).
    AI(String),
    /// `MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name)` — splices message history.
    Placeholder(String),
}

/// A chat prompt assembled from ordered slots — `ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ChatPromptTemplate {
    slots: Vec<ChatSlot>,
}

/// Variables accepted by prompt formatting: plain text or message lists.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum PromptValue {
    Text(String),
    Messages(Vec<Message>),
}

impl From<String> for PromptValue {
    fn from(s: String) -> Self {
        PromptValue::Text(s)
    }
}

impl From<&str> for PromptValue {
    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {
        PromptValue::Text(s.to_string())
    }
}

impl From<Vec<Message>> for PromptValue {
    fn from(m: Vec<Message>) -> Self {
        PromptValue::Messages(m)
    }
}

/// Substitute `{var}` placeholders in `template` using `vars`.
/// `{{` and `}}` render as literal `{` and `}`.
///
/// ```ignore
/// format("Hello {name} {{literal}}", &[("name", "Rust")]) == "Hello Rust {literal}"
/// ```
pub fn format_template(template: &str, vars: &HashMap<String, PromptValue>) -> Result<String> {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(template.len());
    let mut chars = template.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        match c {
            '{' => {
                match chars.peek() {
                    Some('{') => {
                        chars.next();
                        out.push('{');
                    }
                    Some('}') => {
                        chars.next();
                        out.push('}');
                    }
                    Some(_) => {
                        let mut name = String::new();
                        let mut closed = false;
                        for c2 in chars.by_ref() {
                            if c2 == '}' {
                                closed = true;
                                break;
                            }
                            name.push(c2);
                        }
                        if !closed {
                            return Err(LangchainError::InvalidTemplate(
                                "unclosed '{' — expected '}'".into(),
                            ));
                        }
                        let name = name.trim();
                        if name.is_empty() {
                            return Err(LangchainError::InvalidTemplate("empty variable name {}".into()));
                        }
                        match vars.get(name) {
                            Some(PromptValue::Text(s)) => out.push_str(s),
                            Some(PromptValue::Messages(msgs)) => {
                                // Flatten message texts into the slot, newline-separated.
                                let joined: Vec<&str> = msgs.iter().map(|m| m.text()).collect();
                                out.push_str(&joined.join("\n"));
                            }
                            None => {
                                return Err(LangchainError::MissingVariable(name.to_string()));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    None => {
                        return Err(LangchainError::InvalidTemplate(
                            "unterminated '{' at end of template".into(),
                        ))
                    }
                }
            }
            '}' => {
                if chars.peek() == Some(&'}') {
                    chars.next();
                    out.push('}');
                } else {
                    return Err(LangchainError::InvalidTemplate(
                        "stray '}' without matching '{{'".into(),
                    ));
                }
            }
            other => out.push(other),
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

impl ChatPromptTemplate {
    /// Build from ordered slots, mirroring `ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([...])`.
    pub fn from_slots(slots: Vec<ChatSlot>) -> Self {
        Self { slots }
    }

    /// Common shape: one system message + one templated human message.
    pub fn from_system_and_human(system: impl Into<String>, human: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::from_slots(vec![ChatSlot::System(system.into()), ChatSlot::Human(human.into())])
    }

    /// Convenience builder: system message.
    pub fn with_system(mut self, template: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.slots.push(ChatSlot::System(template.into()));
        self
    }

    /// Convenience builder: templated human message.
    pub fn with_human(mut self, template: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.slots.push(ChatSlot::Human(template.into()));
        self
    }

    /// Convenience builder: message-history placeholder (`MessagesPlaceholder`).
    pub fn with_placeholder(mut self, variable: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.slots.push(ChatSlot::Placeholder(variable.into()));
        self
    }

    /// Format every slot into concrete [`Message`]s.
    pub fn format(&self, vars: &HashMap<String, PromptValue>) -> Result<Vec<Message>> {
        let mut msgs = Vec::new();
        for slot in &self.slots {
            match slot {
                ChatSlot::System(t) => msgs.push(Message::system(format_template(t, vars)?)),
                ChatSlot::Human(t) => msgs.push(Message::human(format_template(t, vars)?)),
                ChatSlot::AI(t) => msgs.push(Message::ai(format_template(t, vars)?)),
                ChatSlot::Placeholder(name) => match vars.get(name) {
                    Some(PromptValue::Messages(history)) => msgs.extend(history.iter().cloned()),
                    Some(PromptValue::Text(t)) => msgs.push(Message::human(t.clone())),
                    None => return Err(LangchainError::MissingVariable(name.clone())),
                },
            }
        }
        Ok(msgs)
    }

    /// Names every `{var}` the slots require (without braces).
    pub fn variables(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut names = Vec::new();
        for slot in &self.slots {
            let t = match slot {
                ChatSlot::System(t) | ChatSlot::Human(t) | ChatSlot::AI(t) => t,
                ChatSlot::Placeholder(n) => {
                    names.push(n.clone());
                    continue;
                }
            };
            names.extend(extract_variables(t));
        }
        names
    }
}

/// Extract variable names mentioned in a template.
pub fn extract_variables(template: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut vars = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = template.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c == '{' {
            if chars.peek() == Some(&'{') {
                chars.next();
                continue;
            }
            let mut name = String::new();
            for c2 in chars.by_ref() {
                if c2 == '}' {
                    break;
                }
                name.push(c2);
            }
            let name = name.trim().to_string();
            if !name.is_empty() {
                vars.push(name);
            }
        } else if c == '}' && chars.peek() == Some(&'}') {
            chars.next();
        }
    }
    vars
}

#[async_trait]
impl Runnable<HashMap<String, PromptValue>, Vec<Message>> for ChatPromptTemplate {
    async fn invoke(&self, input: HashMap<String, PromptValue>) -> Result<Vec<Message>> {
        self.format(&input)
    }
}

/// A single templated string prompt — `PromptTemplate.from_template("{x}")`.
/// Implements `Runnable`, producing a formatted [`Message::Human`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PromptTemplate {
    template: String,
}

impl PromptTemplate {
    /// Create from a `{var}` style template.
    pub fn new(template: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { template: template.into() }
    }

    /// Format to a plain string.
    pub fn format(&self, vars: &HashMap<String, PromptValue>) -> Result<String> {
        format_template(&self.template, vars)
    }

    /// Variable names required by this template.
    pub fn variables(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        extract_variables(&self.template)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Runnable<HashMap<String, PromptValue>, Message> for PromptTemplate {
    async fn invoke(&self, input: HashMap<String, PromptValue>) -> Result<Message> {
        Ok(Message::human(self.format(&input)?))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn vars(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> HashMap<String, PromptValue> {
        pairs
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), PromptValue::Text(v.to_string())))
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn basic_substitution() {
        let t = PromptTemplate::new("Tell me a joke about {topic} for {audience}.");
        assert_eq!(
            t.format(&vars(&[("topic", "Rust"), ("audience", "developers")])).unwrap(),
            "Tell me a joke about Rust for developers."
        );
        assert_eq!(t.variables(), vec!["topic", "audience"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn brace_escaping() {
        assert_eq!(format_template("{{literal}} {x}", &vars(&[("x", "1")])).unwrap(), "{literal} 1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_variable_errors() {
        let e = format_template("{nope}", &vars(&[])).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(e, LangchainError::MissingVariable(v) if v == "nope"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unbalanced_templates_error() {
        assert!(format_template("{unclosed", &vars(&[])).is_err());
        assert!(format_template("stray } brace", &vars(&[])).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn chat_prompt_with_placeholder() {
        let prompt = ChatPromptTemplate::from_system_and_human(
            "You are {role}.",
            "Question: {question}",
        )
        .with_placeholder("history");

        let mut v = vars(&[("role", "a pirate"), ("question", "hello?")]);
        let history = vec![Message::human("earlier"), Message::ai("yes")];
        v.insert("history".into(), PromptValue::Messages(history));

        let msgs = prompt.format(&v).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(msgs.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(msgs[0].text(), "You are a pirate.");
        assert_eq!(msgs[1].text(), "Question: hello?");
        assert_eq!(msgs[2].text(), "earlier");
        assert_eq!(msgs[3].text(), "yes");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn chat_prompt_is_runnable() {
        let prompt = ChatPromptTemplate::from_system_and_human("sys {a}", "user {b}");
        let m = prompt
            .invoke(vars(&[("a", "A"), ("b", "B")]))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.len(), 2);
    }
}

[view on disk](crates/server/langchain/src/runnables.rs)

````rust
//! LCEL — the LangChain Expression Language, rebuilt in Rust.
//!
//! Python LCEL composes runnables with `|` (pipe). Here the same idea is expressed
//! with the [`Runnable`] trait plus the [`RunnableExt::pipe`] combinator, which
//! type-checks the intermediate value at compile time instead of runtime:
//!
//! ```text
//! prompt | model | parser      (Python)
//! prompt.pipe(model).pipe(parser)   (this crate)
//! ```

use async_trait::async_trait;
use futures::stream::{self, StreamExt};
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};

/// Anything that can transform an input of type `I` into an output of type `O`.
///
/// This is `langchain_core.runnables.Runnable` in Rust: `invoke` is the primary
/// path, `batch` runs many inputs concurrently, `stream` yields partial outputs.
#[async_trait]
pub trait Runnable<I: Send + 'static, O: Send + 'static>: Send + Sync + Debug {
    /// Run once with `input`.
    async fn invoke(&self, input: I) -> Result<O>;

    /// Run concurrently over `inputs`, preserving order (like `Runnable.batch`).
    async fn batch(&self, inputs: Vec<I>) -> Result<Vec<O>> {
        let futs: Vec<_> = inputs.into_iter().map(|i| self.invoke(i)).collect();
        stream::iter(futs).buffered(16).collect::<Vec<_>>().await.into_iter().collect()
    }
}

// Debug is required on Runnable implementors so that derived Debug on containers works.
use std::fmt::Debug;

/// A `Runnable` implemented by any async closure — `RunnableLambda` in Python LCEL.
pub struct RunnableLambda<I, O, F, Fut>
where
    F: Fn(I) -> Fut + Send + Sync,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<O>> + Send,
{
    f: Arc<F>,
    _marker: std::marker::PhantomData<fn(I) -> (O, Fut)>,
}

impl<I, O, F, Fut> std::fmt::Debug for RunnableLambda<I, O, F, Fut>
where
    F: Fn(I) -> Fut + Send + Sync,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<O>> + Send,
{
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("RunnableLambda")
    }
}

impl<I, O, F, Fut> RunnableLambda<I, O, F, Fut>
where
    F: Fn(I) -> Fut + Send + Sync,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<O>> + Send,
{
    /// Wrap an async closure into a runnable.
    pub fn new(f: F) -> Self {
        Self { f: Arc::new(f), _marker: std::marker::PhantomData }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl<I, O, F, Fut> Runnable<I, O> for RunnableLambda<I, O, F, Fut>
where
    I: Send + 'static,
    O: Send + 'static,
    F: Fn(I) -> Fut + Send + Sync,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<O>> + Send,
{
    async fn invoke(&self, input: I) -> Result<O> {
        (self.f)(input).await
    }
}

/// Convenience constructor matching Python's `RunnableLambda(fn)`.
pub fn lambda<I, O, F, Fut>(f: F) -> Arc<dyn Runnable<I, O>>
where
    I: Send + 'static,
    O: Send + 'static,
    F: Fn(I) -> Fut + Send + Sync + 'static,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<O>> + Send + 'static,
{
    Arc::new(RunnableLambda::new(f))
}

/// Returns its input unchanged — `RunnablePassthrough`.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct RunnablePassthrough;

#[async_trait]
impl<I: Send + 'static> Runnable<I, I> for RunnablePassthrough
where
    I: Clone,
{
    async fn invoke(&self, input: I) -> Result<I> {
        Ok(input)
    }
}

/// Runs several runnables on the **same** input concurrently and returns all
/// outputs in order — the parallel half of Python's `RunnableParallel`.
pub struct RunnableMap<I, O> {
    runnables: Vec<Arc<dyn Runnable<I, O>>>,
}

impl<I, O> std::fmt::Debug for RunnableMap<I, O> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "RunnableMap(n={})", self.runnables.len())
    }
}

impl<I: Send + Clone + 'static, O: Send + 'static> RunnableMap<I, O> {
    /// Empty map.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { runnables: Vec::new() }
    }

    /// Register another runnable that consumes the same input.
    pub fn with(mut self, r: Arc<dyn Runnable<I, O>>) -> Self {
        self.runnables.push(r);
        self
    }
}

impl<I: Send + Clone + 'static, O: Send + 'static> Default for RunnableMap<I, O> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl<I: Send + Clone + 'static, O: Send + 'static> Runnable<I, Vec<O>> for RunnableMap<I, O> {
    async fn invoke(&self, input: I) -> Result<Vec<O>> {
        if self.runnables.is_empty() {
            return Err(LangchainError::Other("RunnableMap has no runnables".into()));
        }
        let input0 = input;
        let outs = stream::iter(self.runnables.iter())
            .then(move |r| {
                let inp = input0.clone();
                async move { r.invoke(inp).await }
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .await;
        outs.into_iter().collect()
    }
}

/// Sequential composition produced by [`RunnableExt::pipe`].
/// `RunnableSequence<A, B, I, M, O>: Runnable<I, O>` where `A: Runnable<I, M>`, `B: Runnable<M, O>`.
pub struct RunnableSequence<A, B, I, M, O> {
    pub first: A,
    pub then: B,
    _marker: std::marker::PhantomData<fn(I) -> (M, O)>,
}

impl<A, B, I, M, O> std::fmt::Debug for RunnableSequence<A, B, I, M, O> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("RunnableSequence")
    }
}

/// Composition helpers, the Rust `|` operator of LCEL.
pub trait RunnableExt<I: Send + 'static, O: Send + 'static>: Runnable<I, O> + Sized {
    /// Chain `self` with `next`: `self.invoke(x)` feeds `next.invoke`.
    ///
    /// ```ignore
    /// let chain = prompt.pipe(model).pipe(str_parser());
    /// let answer: String = chain.invoke(vars).await?;
    /// ```
    fn pipe<M: Send + 'static, N: Runnable<O, M>>(self, next: N) -> RunnableSequence<Self, N, I, O, M> {
        RunnableSequence { first: self, then: next, _marker: std::marker::PhantomData }
    }
}

impl<I: Send + 'static, O: Send + 'static, T: Runnable<I, O> + Sized> RunnableExt<I, O> for T {}

#[async_trait]
impl<I: Send + 'static, M: Send + 'static, O: Send + 'static, A, B> Runnable<I, O>
    for RunnableSequence<A, B, I, M, O>
where
    A: Runnable<I, M>,
    B: Runnable<M, O>,
{
    async fn invoke(&self, input: I) -> Result<O> {
        let mid = self.first.invoke(input).await?;
        self.then.invoke(mid).await
    }

    async fn batch(&self, inputs: Vec<I>) -> Result<Vec<O>> {
        let mids = self.first.batch(inputs).await?;
        self.then.batch(mids).await
    }
}

/// `Arc<dyn Runnable<I, O>>` is itself a `Runnable`, so boxed steps chain with
/// concrete ones interchangeably.
#[async_trait]
impl<I: Send + 'static, O: Send + 'static> Runnable<I, O> for Arc<dyn Runnable<I, O>> {
    async fn invoke(&self, input: I) -> Result<O> {
        self.as_ref().invoke(input).await
    }

    async fn batch(&self, inputs: Vec<I>) -> Result<Vec<O>> {
        self.as_ref().batch(inputs).await
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn double(x: i32) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<i32>> {
        async move { Ok(x * 2) }
    }

    fn add_ten(x: i32) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<i32>> {
        async move { Ok(x + 10) }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn pipe_composes() {
        let a = lambda(double);
        let b = lambda(add_ten);
        let chain = a.pipe(b); // (x*2) + 10
        assert_eq!(chain.invoke(5).await.unwrap(), 20);
        assert_eq!(chain.batch(vec![0, 1, 2]).await.unwrap(), vec![10, 12, 14]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn passthrough_and_map() {
        let pt: RunnablePassthrough = RunnablePassthrough;
        assert_eq!(pt.invoke(42i64).await.unwrap(), 42);

            .with(lambda(double))
            .with(lambda(add_ten));
        let outs = map.invoke(3).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(outs, vec![6, 13]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn three_stage_chain() {
        let chain = lambda(double)
            .pipe(lambda(add_ten))
            .pipe(lambda(|x: i32| async move { Ok(format!("result: {x}")) }));
        assert_eq!(chain.invoke(2).await.unwrap(), "result: 14");

//! `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` — chunks long text on natural boundaries
//! (`\n\n`, `\n`, `. `, ` `, ``) while honouring `chunk_size` and `chunk_overlap`.

/// Splits text into overlapping chunks, preferring the earliest separator that
/// keeps pieces under `chunk_size` — the port of
/// `langchain.text_splitter.RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter {
    chunk_size: usize,
    chunk_overlap: usize,
    separators: Vec<&'static str>,
}

impl Default for RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new(1000, 200)
    }
}

impl RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter {
    /// `chunk_size` max characters per chunk, `chunk_overlap` shared suffix/prefix.
    ///
    /// A `chunk_overlap >= chunk_size` used to PANIC via `assert!`; it is now
    /// clamped to `chunk_size - 1` (the largest overlap that can never
    /// produce an empty or oversized chunk) so the constructor stays
    /// non-panicking and API-stable.
    pub fn new(chunk_size: usize, chunk_overlap: usize) -> Self {
        let chunk_size = chunk_size.max(1);
        Self {
            chunk_size,
            chunk_overlap: chunk_overlap.min(chunk_size.saturating_sub(1)),
            separators: vec!["\n\n", "\n", ". ", " ", ""],
        }
    }

    /// Override the separator priority.
    pub fn with_separators(mut self, seps: Vec<&'static str>) -> Self {
        self.separators = seps;
        self
    }

    /// Split `text` into chunks.
    pub fn split(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        if text.chars().count() <= self.chunk_size {
            let t = text.trim();
            return if t.is_empty() { Vec::new() } else { vec![t.to_string()] };
        }
        let pieces = self.split_by_separators(text);
        self.merge(pieces)
    }

    /// Recursively split using separators; the final separator `""` cuts per char.
    fn split_by_separators(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        for (i, sep) in self.separators.iter().enumerate() {
            if text.contains(sep) && !sep.is_empty() {
                let parts: Vec<String> = text.split(sep).map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                // Try to keep sub-pieces intact if they fit; recurse on oversized ones.
                let mut out = Vec::new();
                for p in parts {
                    if p.chars().count() <= self.chunk_size {
                        if !p.trim().is_empty() {
                            out.push(p);
                        }
                    } else {
                        let sub = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter {
                            chunk_size: self.chunk_size,
                            chunk_overlap: self.chunk_overlap,
                            separators: self.separators[i + 1..].to_vec(),
                        };
                        out.extend(sub.split_by_separators(&p));
                    }
                }
                return out;
            }
        }
        // Fallback: hard character cut (sep == "" case).
        text.chars()
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .chunks(self.chunk_size)
            .map(|c| c.iter().collect::<String>())
            .collect()
    }

    /// Merge small pieces into chunks up to `chunk_size` with `chunk_overlap`
    /// carried between consecutive chunks.
    fn merge(&self, pieces: Vec<String>) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut chunks: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let mut current = String::new();
        for piece in pieces {
            let piece = piece.trim();
            if piece.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let plen = piece.chars().count();
            if !current.is_empty() && current.chars().count() + plen + 1 > self.chunk_size {
                chunks.push(current.clone());
                // Overlap: keep the tail of the previous chunk.
                if self.chunk_overlap > 0 {
                    let tail: String = current
                        .chars()
                        .rev()
                        .take(self.chunk_overlap)
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .into_iter()
                        .rev()
                        .collect();
                    current = tail.trim_start().to_string();
                } else {
                    current.clear();
                }
                // The overlap tail may leave no room for the piece (tail +
                // separator + piece > chunk_size): appending it anyway used to
                // emit chunks exceeding chunk_size by overlap + 1. Drop the
                // tail so the piece starts a fresh, in-bounds chunk.
                if !current.is_empty() && current.chars().count() + plen + 1 > self.chunk_size {
                    current.clear();
                }
            }
            if !current.is_empty() {
                current.push(' ');
            }
            current.push_str(piece);
        }
        if !current.trim().is_empty() {
            chunks.push(current);
        }
        chunks
    }
}

/// A chunk of text plus metadata — `langchain_core.documents.Document`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Document {
    /// The chunk text.
    pub page_content: String,
    /// Arbitrary metadata (source, page number, …).
    pub metadata: std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl Document {
    /// New document with empty metadata.
    pub fn new(page_content: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            page_content: page_content.into(),
            metadata: Default::default(),
        }
    }

    /// New document with a `source` metadata entry.
    pub fn with_source(page_content: impl Into<String>, source: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let mut metadata = std::collections::HashMap::new();
        metadata.insert("source".to_string(), source.into());
        Self {
            page_content: page_content.into(),
            metadata,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn short_text_is_single_chunk() {
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(100, 10);
        assert_eq!(s.split("hello world"), vec!["hello world"]);
        assert!(s.split("   ").is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn paragraphs_split_first() {
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(30, 0);
        let text = "First paragraph is short.\n\nSecond paragraph is considerably longer than thirty chars.";
        let chunks = s.split(text);
        assert!(chunks.len() >= 2);
        assert!(chunks[0].starts_with("First paragraph"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hard_cut_fallback() {
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(5, 0).with_separators(vec![""]);
        let chunks = s.split("abcdefghij");
        assert_eq!(chunks.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(chunks[0], "abcde");
        assert_eq!(chunks[1], "fghij");
    }

    #[test]
    fn overlap_is_applied() {
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(20, 5).with_separators(vec![" "]);
        let text = "aaaaa bbbbb ccccc ddddd eeeee fffff ggggg hhhhh";
        let chunks = s.split(text);
        assert!(chunks.len() >= 2);
        // With overlap, chunk n+1 must not start with a brand-new word boundary every time:
        // simply assert every chunk is <= chunk_size + slack.
        for c in &chunks {
            assert!(c.chars().count() <= 21 + 6);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn document_metadata() {
        let d = Document::with_source("text", "book.pdf");
        assert_eq!(d.metadata["source"], "book.pdf");
    }

    #[test]
    fn oversized_overlap_is_clamped_not_panic() {
        // Regression (M39): `chunk_overlap >= chunk_size` used to PANIC in
        // the constructor; it must clamp instead.
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(10, 25);
        let chunks = s.split("aaaaa bbbbb ccccc ddddd eeeee");
        assert!(!chunks.is_empty());
        for c in &chunks {
            assert!(c.chars().count() <= 10, "chunk exceeds chunk_size: {c:?}");
        }
        // Equal overlap is clamped too (and still must not panic).
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(8, 8);
        let chunks = s.split("one two three four five six seven");
        assert!(!chunks.is_empty());
        for c in &chunks {
            assert!(c.chars().count() <= 8, "chunk exceeds chunk_size: {c:?}");
        }
        // chunk_size 1 clamps overlap to 0.
        let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(1, 5);
        assert_eq!(s.split("ab"), vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn merged_chunks_never_exceed_chunk_size() {
        // Regression (M39): after a chunk flush, the overlap tail was
        // appended to unconditionally, so tail + separator + piece could
        // exceed chunk_size by overlap + 1.
        for overlap in [0usize, 1, 3, 7, 19] {
            let s = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(20, overlap).with_separators(vec![" "]);
            let text = "aaaaa bbbbb ccccc ddddd eeeee fffff ggggg hhhhh iiiii jjjjj kkkkk";
            let chunks = s.split(text);
            assert!(chunks.len() >= 2);
            for c in &chunks {
                assert!(
                    c.chars().count() <= 20,
                    "overlap {overlap}: chunk of {} chars exceeds chunk_size: {c:?}",
                    c.chars().count()
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Vector stores — the Rust mirror of `langchain_core.vectorstores`
//! (`InMemoryVectorStore` + `as_retriever`).

use async_trait::async_trait;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::RwLock;

use crate::embeddings::{cosine_similarity, Embeddings};
use crate::errors::{LangchainError, Result};
use crate::runnables::Runnable;
use crate::text_splitter::Document;

struct StoredDoc {
    doc: Document,
    vector: Vec<f32>,
}

/// In-memory similarity-search store. Thread-safe via `RwLock`.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct InMemoryVectorStore {
    docs: Arc<RwLock<Vec<StoredDoc>>>,
}

impl Default for InMemoryVectorStore {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for InMemoryVectorStore {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        let n = self.docs.read().map(|d| d.len()).unwrap_or(0);
        write!(f, "InMemoryVectorStore(docs={n})")
    }
}

impl InMemoryVectorStore {
    /// Empty store.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { docs: Arc::new(RwLock::new(Vec::new())) }
    }

    /// Embed `texts` with `embedder` and add them to the store.
    pub async fn add_texts(&self, texts: &[String], embedder: &dyn Embeddings) -> Result<usize> {
        let vectors = embedder.embed_documents(texts).await?;
        // Fewer embeddings than texts must be an ERROR — silently dropping
        // documents while reporting success hid data loss.
        if vectors.len() != texts.len() {
            return Err(LangchainError::Other(format!(
                "embedder returned {} vectors for {} texts",
                vectors.len(),
                texts.len()
            )));
        }
        // Validate EVERY vector against the first one (not just first() vs
        // first()) BEFORE storing anything, so a ragged batch fails whole.
        let expected = match vectors.first() {
            Some(v) => v.len(),
            None => return Ok(0),
        };
        if let Some(v) = vectors.iter().find(|v| v.len() != expected) {
            return Err(LangchainError::DimensionMismatch { expected, got: v.len() });
        }
        let mut guard = self
            .docs
            .write()
            .map_err(|_| LangchainError::Other("vector store lock poisoned".into()))?;
        if let Some(stored) = guard.first() {
            if stored.vector.len() != expected {
                return Err(LangchainError::DimensionMismatch {
                    expected: stored.vector.len(),
                    got: expected,
                });
            }
        }
        for (text, vector) in texts.iter().cloned().zip(vectors) {
            guard.push(StoredDoc { doc: Document::new(text), vector });
        }
        Ok(texts.len())
    }

    /// Add full documents (keeps metadata).
    pub async fn add_documents(&self, docs: &[Document], embedder: &dyn Embeddings) -> Result<usize> {
        let texts: Vec<String> = docs.iter().map(|d| d.page_content.clone()).collect();
        let vectors = embedder.embed_documents(&texts).await?;
        if vectors.len() != docs.len() {
            return Err(LangchainError::Other(format!(
                "embedder returned {} vectors for {} documents",
                vectors.len(),
                docs.len()
            )));
        }
        let expected = match vectors.first() {
            Some(v) => v.len(),
            None => return Ok(0),
        };
        if let Some(v) = vectors.iter().find(|v| v.len() != expected) {
            return Err(LangchainError::DimensionMismatch { expected, got: v.len() });
        }
        let mut guard = self
            .docs
            .write()
            .map_err(|_| LangchainError::Other("vector store lock poisoned".into()))?;
        if let Some(stored) = guard.first() {
            if stored.vector.len() != expected {
                return Err(LangchainError::DimensionMismatch {
                    expected: stored.vector.len(),
                    got: expected,
                });
            }
        }
        for (doc, vector) in docs.iter().cloned().zip(vectors) {
            guard.push(StoredDoc { doc, vector });
        }
        Ok(docs.len())
    }

    /// Top-`k` documents by cosine similarity to `query_embedding`.
    pub fn similarity_search_by_vector(&self, query_embedding: &[f32], k: usize) -> Result<Vec<(Document, f32)>> {
        let guard = self
            .docs
            .read()
            .map_err(|_| LangchainError::Other("vector store lock poisoned".into()))?;
        let mut scored: Vec<(Document, f32)> = guard
            .iter()
            .map(|s| (s.doc.clone(), cosine_similarity(query_embedding, &s.vector)))
            .collect();
        scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
        scored.truncate(k);
        Ok(scored)
    }

    /// Embed `query` then return the top-`k` documents — `similarity_search`.
    pub async fn similarity_search(&self, query: &str, k: usize, embedder: &dyn Embeddings) -> Result<Vec<(Document, f32)>> {
        let qv = embedder.embed_query(query).await?;
        self.similarity_search_by_vector(&qv, k)
    }

    /// Number of stored documents.
    pub fn len(&self) -> Result<usize> {
        Ok(self
            .docs
            .read()
            .map_err(|_| LangchainError::Other("vector store lock poisoned".into()))?
            .len())
    }

    /// True when the store holds no documents.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(self.len()? == 0)
    }

    /// Wrap this store into a retriever runnable (`as_retriever`).
    pub fn as_retriever(self, embedder: Arc<dyn Embeddings>, k: usize) -> Retriever {
        Retriever { store: self, embedder, k }
    }
}

/// `VectorStoreRetriever`: `Runnable<String, Vec<Document>>` that embeds the
/// query and returns the top-k documents (scores dropped).
pub struct Retriever {
    store: InMemoryVectorStore,
    embedder: Arc<dyn Embeddings>,
    k: usize,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Retriever {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "Retriever(k={})", self.k)
    }
}

impl Retriever {
    /// Return the top-k docs with their similarity scores.
    pub async fn retrieve_scored(&self, query: &str) -> Result<Vec<(Document, f32)>> {
        self.store.similarity_search(query, self.k, self.embedder.as_ref()).await
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Runnable<String, Vec<Document>> for Retriever {
    async fn invoke(&self, query: String) -> Result<Vec<Document>> {
        let scored = self.retrieve_scored(&query).await?;
        Ok(scored.into_iter().map(|(d, _)| d).collect())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    /// Deterministic embeddings: bag-of-words hashed into 64 dims. Shared words
    /// dominate similarity, which makes retrieval assertions predictable.
    struct HashEmbedder;

    fn hash_word(w: &str) -> usize {
        w.bytes().fold(5381usize, |h, b| (h.wrapping_mul(33).wrapping_add(b as usize)) % 64)
    }

    #[async_trait]
    impl Embeddings for HashEmbedder {
        async fn embed_query(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.embed_documents(&[text.to_string()]).await
                .and_then(|mut v| v.pop().ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::LlmParse("empty".into())))
        }

        async fn embed_documents(&self, texts: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
            Ok(texts
                .iter()
                .map(|t| {
                    let mut v = vec![0f32; 64];
                    for w in t.to_lowercase().split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric()) {
                        if w.is_empty() {
                            continue;
                        }
                        v[hash_word(w)] += 1.0;
                    }
                    v
                })
                .collect())
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn add_and_search() {
        let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
        let embedder = HashEmbedder;
        let texts: Vec<String> = vec![
            "the quick brown fox jumps".into(),
            "rust is a systems programming language".into(),
            "lazy dogs sleep all day".into(),
            "the fox and the dog are friends".into(),
        ];
        store.add_texts(&texts, &embedder).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(store.len().unwrap(), 4);

        let results = store.similarity_search("fox jumps", 2, &embedder).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(results.len(), 2);
        // Highest scored doc should mention the fox.
        assert!(results[0].0.page_content.contains("fox"));
        assert!(results[0].1 > results[1].1);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn retriever_is_runnable() {
        let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
        let embedder: Arc<dyn Embeddings> = Arc::new(HashEmbedder);
        store
            .add_texts(&["alpha beta".into(), "gamma delta".into()], embedder.as_ref())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let retriever = store.as_retriever(embedder, 1);
        let docs = retriever.invoke("alpha".into()).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(docs.len(), 1);
        assert!(docs[0].page_content.contains("alpha"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn documents_keep_metadata() {
        let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
        let embedder = HashEmbedder;
        let mut meta = HashMap::new();
        meta.insert("source".into(), "notes.md".into());
        let docs = vec![Document {
            page_content: "chunked content".into(),
            metadata: meta.clone(),
        }];
        store.add_documents(&docs, &embedder).await.unwrap();
        let hits = store.similarity_search("content", 1, &embedder).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(hits[0].0.metadata["source"], "notes.md");
    }

    /// Embedder whose vector count/dims deliberately disagree with the input.
    struct RaggedEmbedder {
        fewer: bool,
        ragged: bool,
    }

    #[async_trait]
    impl Embeddings for RaggedEmbedder {
        async fn embed_query(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.embed_documents(&[text.to_string()]).await
                .and_then(|mut v| v.pop().ok_or_else(|| LangchainError::LlmParse("empty".into())))
        }

        async fn embed_documents(&self, texts: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
            let mut out: Vec<Vec<f32>> = texts
                .iter()
                .map(|_| vec![0f32; 64])
                .collect();
            if self.fewer && !out.is_empty() {
                out.pop(); // one embedding short
            }
            if self.ragged {
                if let Some(last) = out.last_mut() {
                    last.push(1.0); // wrong dimension on the last vector
                }
            }
            Ok(out)
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn add_texts_count_mismatch_is_an_error() {
        // Regression (M37): fewer embeddings than texts silently dropped
        // documents while reporting success.
        let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
        let embedder = RaggedEmbedder { fewer: true, ragged: false };
        let texts = vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()];
        let err = store.add_texts(&texts, &embedder).await.unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("1 vectors for 2 texts"), "got: {err}");
        assert_eq!(store.len().unwrap(), 0, "nothing may be stored on mismatch");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn add_texts_rejects_ragged_vector_dimensions() {
        // Regression (M37): the dimension check compared only first() vs
        // first(); a ragged vector inside the batch slipped through.
        let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
        let embedder = RaggedEmbedder { fewer: false, ragged: true };
        let texts = vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()];
        assert!(store.add_texts(&texts, &embedder).await.is_err());
        assert_eq!(store.len().unwrap(), 0, "nothing may be stored on mismatch");

        // And an already-populated store rejects foreign dimensions.
        let good = HashEmbedder;
        store.add_texts(&["seed".to_string()], &good).await.unwrap();
        let embedder2 = RaggedEmbedder { fewer: false, ragged: true };
        assert!(store.add_texts(&["x".to_string(), "y".to_string()], &embedder2).await.is_err());
        assert_eq!(store.len().unwrap(), 1);
    }
}

```rust
//! End-to-end tests of the OpenAI protocol layer against a local mock server
//! (wiremock). No network access required — these prove the agent loop works
//! with the real `ChatOpenAI` client, not just the fake model.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use langchain_rust::agents::{calculator_tool, AgentExecutor};
use langchain_rust::llms::openai::ChatOpenAI;
use langchain_rust::llms::BaseChatModel;
use langchain_rust::embeddings::Embeddings;
use langchain_rust::vectorstores::InMemoryVectorStore;
use wiremock::matchers::{method, path};
use wiremock::{Mock, MockServer, ResponseTemplate};

fn completion_json(content: &str) -> ResponseTemplate {
    ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_body_json(serde_json::json!({
        "id": "chatcmpl-1",
        "object": "chat.completion",
        "choices": [{
            "index": 0,
            "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": content},
            "finish_reason": "stop"
        }],
        "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 9, "completion_tokens": 4, "total_tokens": 13}
    }))
}

fn tool_call_json(id: &str, name: &str, args: &str) -> ResponseTemplate {
    let body = serde_json::json!({
        "choices": [{
            "index": 0,
            "message": {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": null,
                "tool_calls": [{
                    "id": id,
                    "type": "function",
                    "function": {"name": name, "arguments": args}
                }]
            }
        }]
    });
    ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_body_json(body)
}

fn make_model(server: &MockServer) -> ChatOpenAI {
    ChatOpenAI::builder()
        .model("mock-gpt")
        .api_key("test-key")
        .base_url(server.uri())
        .build()
        .expect("model")
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn chat_openai_plain_completion() {
    let server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .and(path("/chat/completions"))
        .respond_with(completion_json("Rust is memory safe."))
        .mount(&server)
        .await;

    let model = make_model(&server);
    let messages = vec![langchain_rust::messages::Message::human("why rust?")];
    let answer = model.generate(&messages).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(answer.text(), "Rust is memory safe.");
    let usage = model.usage().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(usage.total_tokens, 13);

    // The client must have sent bearer auth + model id.
    let reqs = server.received_requests().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 1);
    let auth = reqs[0]
        .headers
        .iter()
        .find(|(k, _)| k.as_str() == "authorization")
        .map(|(_, v)| String::from_utf8_lossy(v.as_bytes()).to_string());
    assert_eq!(auth.as_deref(), Some("Bearer test-key"));
    let body: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&reqs[0].body).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(body["model"], "mock-gpt");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn agent_loop_with_real_openai_client() {
    let server = MockServer::start().await;

    // Turn 1: model requests the calculator with 21*2.
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .and(path("/chat/completions"))
        .respond_with(tool_call_json("call_x", "calculator", "{\"expression\":\"21*2\"}"))
        .up_to_n_times(1)
        .mount(&server)
        .await;
    // Turn 2: final answer.
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .and(path("/chat/completions"))
        .respond_with(completion_json("The answer is 42."))
        .mount(&server)
        .await;

    let model = make_model(&server);
    let mut agent = AgentExecutor::builder(std::sync::Arc::new(model))
        .tool(calculator_tool())
        .max_iterations(4)
        .build();

    let answer = agent.invoke("what is 21*2?").await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(answer, "The answer is 42.");

    let reqs = server.received_requests().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 2);
    // First request carries the tool schema, second carries the tool result.
    let b1 = String::from_utf8_lossy(&reqs[0].body).to_string();
    let b2 = String::from_utf8_lossy(&reqs[1].body).to_string();
    assert!(b1.contains("\"calculator\""), "first request must bind tools");
    assert!(b2.contains("tool_call_id"), "second request must include the tool result");
    assert!(b2.contains("call_x"));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn sse_streaming_is_parsed() {
    let server = MockServer::start().await;
    let sse_body = concat!(
        "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"Hel\"}}]}\n\n",
        "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"lo\"}}]}\n\n",
        "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{}}]}\n\n",
        "data: [DONE]\n\n"
    );
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .and(path("/chat/completions"))
        .respond_with(
            ResponseTemplate::new(200)
                .insert_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
                .set_body_string(sse_body),
        )
        .mount(&server)
        .await;

    let model = make_model(&server);
    let messages = vec![langchain_rust::messages::Message::human("hi")];
    use futures::StreamExt;
    let mut stream = model.stream_text(&messages);
    let mut out = String::new();
    while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
        out.push_str(&chunk.unwrap());
    }
    assert_eq!(out, "Hello");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn embeddings_roundtrip_into_store() {
    // Minimal deterministic embedding server: one 4-dim unit vector PER
    // input text, exactly like a real provider (a mock that returned fewer
    // embeddings than inputs encoded the old silent-drop behaviour).
    let server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .and(path("/embeddings"))
        .respond_with(|req: &wiremock::Request| {
            let n = req
                .body_json::<serde_json::Value>()
                .ok()
                .and_then(|v| v.get("input").and_then(|i| i.as_array()).map(Vec::len))
                .unwrap_or(1)
                .max(1);
            let data: Vec<serde_json::Value> = (0..n)
                .map(|i| serde_json::json!({"index": i, "embedding": [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]}))
                .collect();
            ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_body_json(serde_json::json!({ "data": data }))
        })
        .mount(&server)
        .await;

    struct OneHotEmbedder {
        url: String,
    }
    #[async_trait]
    impl Embeddings for OneHotEmbedder {
        async fn embed_query(&self, text: &str) -> langchain_rust::errors::Result<Vec<f32>> {
            self.embed_documents(&[text.to_string()])
                .await
                .and_then(|mut v| {
                    v.pop()
                        .ok_or_else(|| langchain_rust::errors::LangchainError::LlmParse("empty".into()))
                })
        }
        async fn embed_documents(
            &self,
            texts: &[String],
        ) -> langchain_rust::errors::Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>> {
            let emb = langchain_rust::embeddings::openai::OpenAIEmbeddings::builder()
                .model("mock-embed")
                .api_key("k")
                .base_url(&self.url)
                .build()?;
            emb.embed_documents(texts).await
        }
    }

    let embedder = OneHotEmbedder { url: server.uri() };
    let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();
    let texts: Vec<String> = vec!["alpha".into(), "beta".into()];
    assert_eq!(store.add_texts(&texts, &embedder).await.unwrap(), 2);
    let hits = store.similarity_search("alpha", 1, &embedder).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(hits[0].0.page_content, "alpha");
    assert!((hits[0].1 - 1.0).abs() < 1e-6);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn provider_error_maps_to_langchain_error() {
    let server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .and(path("/chat/completions"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(401).set_body_string(r#"{"error":"bad key"}"#))
        .mount(&server)
        .await;
    let model = make_model(&server);
    let err = model.generate(&[]).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("401"), "got: {err}");
}
