```rust
/// This is **not** CRC-32 (an easy and silent mistake — an implementation using
/// CRC-32 is self-consistent but interoperates with nothing). Measured against
/// Google's own client: a 99-byte CNXN banner carries checksum 9857, which is
/// exactly `sum(banner)`.
///
/// From protocol version `A_VERSION_SKIP_CHECKSUM` (0x01000001) a peer may send
/// the field as 0 and expect it to be ignored. Measured against Google's client:
/// it sends a real sum for CNXN (9857) and AUTH (33804), sends 0 afterwards, and
/// accepts 0 from the device. So:
///
/// * send — always the real sum. A peer that validates checks it; a peer that
///   has negotiated skip-checksum ignores it. This is correct for both.
/// * receive — validate only when the field is non-zero. A zero means the peer
///   has negotiated skip-checksum; treating that as corruption would reject
///   every modern device.
fn adb_checksum(data: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    data.iter().fold(0u32, |acc, &b| acc.wrapping_add(b as u32))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::net::TcpListener;
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

    /// Build one `screenrecord --raw` frame packet for the reassembler tests.
    fn test_packet(gen: u64, w: u32, h: u32, fill: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut pkt = Vec::new();
        pkt.extend_from_slice(SCREEN_RECORD_MAGIC);
        pkt.extend_from_slice(&gen.to_le_bytes());
        pkt.extend_from_slice(&w.to_le_bytes());
        pkt.extend_from_slice(&h.to_le_bytes());
        pkt.extend_from_slice(&vec![fill; (w * h * 4) as usize]);
        pkt
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_reassembler_stitches_arbitrary_chunk_boundaries() {
        let mut re = StreamReassembler::new();
        let pkt = test_packet(7, 4, 3, 0xAB);
        // feed 1 byte at a time — frames must only surface when complete
        for (i, b) in pkt.iter().enumerate() {
            re.push(std::slice::from_ref(b));
            let done = re.pop(1 << 20).unwrap();
            if i + 1 == pkt.len() {
                let f = done.expect("frame completes on the final byte");
                assert_eq!(f.gen, 7);
                assert_eq!((f.w, f.h), (4, 3));
                assert!(f.rgba.iter().all(|&b| b == 0xAB));
            } else {
                assert!(done.is_none(), "frame surfaced early at byte {i}");
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(re.buffered(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_reassembler_keeps_backlog_for_next_frame() {
        let mut re = StreamReassembler::new();
        let mut wire = test_packet(1, 2, 2, 0x01);
        wire.extend_from_slice(&test_packet(2, 2, 2, 0x02));
        // one big chunk containing both frames; pop twice
        re.push(&wire);
        let a = re.pop(1 << 20).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.gen, 1);
        let b = re.pop(1 << 20).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(b.gen, 2);
        assert!(re.pop(1 << 20).unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_reassembler_rejects_corrupt_header() {
        let mut re = StreamReassembler::new();
        // 16 bytes alone is below the header threshold (pop → None); a full
        // 20-byte header with a bad magic must hard-error
        re.push(b"XXXXjunkjunkjunk");
        assert!(re.pop(1 << 20).unwrap().is_none());
        re.push(b"BAD!junkjunkjunkjunk!");
        assert!(re.pop(1 << 20).is_err());
        assert_eq!(re.buffered(), 0, "corrupt buffer is dropped");
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_reassembler_enforces_frame_cap() {
        let mut re = StreamReassembler::new();
        re.push(&test_packet(1, 4096, 4096, 0)); // 64 MiB claim
        assert!(re.pop(1 << 20).is_err(), "oversized frame must bail");
        assert_eq!(re.buffered(), 0);
    }

    /// A minimal `adbd`: performs the CNXN/AUTH dance and answers the services
    /// the client uses. This is how the client is verified without a device.
    struct MockAdbd {
        pub port: u16,
        pub state: Arc<Mutex<MockState>>,
        _handle: std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
    }

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct MockState {
        pub files: std::collections::HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
        pub installed: Vec<(String, Vec<String>)>,
        pub launched: Vec<String>,
        pub commands: Vec<String>,
        /// adbd runs as root (after `root:`) — `id`/`id -u` report uid 0.
        pub rooted: bool,
        /// Mock honours the `root:` service? (off = production user build
        /// where only `su` can escalate — exercises ladder rung 3).
        pub allow_root_service: bool,
        pub size_override: Option<(u32, u32)>,
        pub density_override: Option<u32>,
    }

    fn read_msg(stream: &mut TcpStream) -> Option<(u32, u32, u32, Vec<u8>)> {
        let mut header = [0u8; 24];
        stream.read_exact(&mut header).ok()?;
        let command = u32::from_le_bytes(header[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
        let arg0 = u32::from_le_bytes(header[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
        let arg1 = u32::from_le_bytes(header[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
        let length = u32::from_le_bytes(header[12..16].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
        let mut data = vec![0u8; length];
        if length > 0 {
            stream.read_exact(&mut data).ok()?;
        }
        Some((command, arg0, arg1, data))
    }

    fn write_msg(stream: &mut TcpStream, cmd: u32, a0: u32, a1: u32, data: &[u8]) {
        let mut header = [0u8; 24];
        header[0..4].copy_from_slice(&cmd.to_le_bytes());
        header[4..8].copy_from_slice(&a0.to_le_bytes());
        header[8..12].copy_from_slice(&a1.to_le_bytes());
        header[12..16].copy_from_slice(&(data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        header[16..20].copy_from_slice(&adb_checksum(data).to_le_bytes());
        header[20..24].copy_from_slice(&(cmd ^ 0xffff_ffff).to_le_bytes());
        stream.write_all(&header).unwrap();
        if !data.is_empty() {
            stream.write_all(data).unwrap();
        }
        stream.flush().unwrap();
    }

    impl MockAdbd {
        fn start() -> Self {
            Self::start_with(true)
        }

        /// `allow_root_service == false` models a production (user) build:
        /// the `root:` service exists but does nothing, so the only root path
        /// is `su 0 -c`.
        fn start_with(allow_root_service: bool) -> Self {
            let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
            let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
            let state = Arc::new(Mutex::new(MockState {
                allow_root_service,
                ..Default::default()
            }));
            let state_for_thread = state.clone();
            let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
                for conn in listener.incoming() {
                    let mut stream = match conn {
                        Ok(s) => s,
                        Err(_) => continue,
                    };
                    let state = state_for_thread.clone();
                    std::thread::spawn(move || {
                        if serve_mock(&mut stream, state).is_err() {
                            // client closed; nothing to report
                        }
                    });
                }
            });
            MockAdbd {
                port,
                state,
                _handle: handle,
            }
        }
    }

    fn serve_mock(stream: &mut TcpStream, state: Arc<Mutex<MockState>>) -> Result<()> {
        // Expect CNXN.
        let (cmd, _, _, _payload) = read_msg(stream).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("no CNXN"))?;
        if cmd != A_CNXN {
            bail!("expected CNXN");
        }
        // AUTH round 1: hand out a token.
        write_msg(stream, A_AUTH, ADB_AUTH_TOKEN, 0, &[0x5au8; 20]);
        // Client replies with a signature; we accept it (a real adbd checks it
        // against its authorised-keys list, which is device state, not protocol).
        let (cmd, arg0, _, sig) = read_msg(stream).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("no AUTH"))?;
        if cmd != A_AUTH || arg0 != ADB_AUTH_SIGNATURE {
            bail!("expected AUTH signature");
        }
        if sig.len() != 256 {
            bail!(
                "signature should be 256 bytes for a 2048-bit key, got {}",
                sig.len()
            );
        }
        // Second token so the client also exercises the public-key path.
        write_msg(stream, A_AUTH, ADB_AUTH_TOKEN, 0, &[0x11u8; 20]);
        let (cmd, arg0, _, blob) = read_msg(stream).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("no pubkey"))?;
        if cmd != A_AUTH || arg0 != ADB_AUTH_RSAPUBLICKEY {
            bail!("expected AUTH pubkey");
        }
        let declared = u32::from_le_bytes(blob[0..4].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&blob[4..4 + declared]).to_string();
        let decoded = crate::crypto::base64_decode(&text)?;
        if decoded.len() != 524 {
            bail!("pubkey blob should be 524 bytes, got {}", decoded.len());
        }

        // Connected.
        let banner = "device::ro.product.model=MockDevice;ro.build.version.sdk=34;\
                      ro.product.name=mock;features=shell_v2,cmd,stat_v2,ls_v2";
        write_msg(stream, A_CNXN, 256 * 1024, 0, banner.as_bytes());

        // Service loop.
        loop {
            let msg = match read_msg(stream) {
                Some(m) => m,
                None => return Ok(()),
            };
            let (cmd, arg0, arg1, data) = msg;
            match cmd {
                A_OPEN => {
                    let local = arg0;
                    let service = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data)
                        .trim_end_matches('\0')
                        .to_string();
                    let remote = local + 1000;
                    write_msg(stream, A_OKAY, remote, local, &[]);
                    if let Err(e) = handle_service(stream, local, remote, &service, state.clone()) {
                        write_msg(stream, A_CLSE, remote, local, &[]);
                        let _ = e;
                    }
                }
                A_CLSE => {}
                A_WRTE => write_msg(stream, A_OKAY, arg1, arg0, &[]),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }

    fn handle_service(
        stream: &mut TcpStream,
        local: u32,
        remote: u32,
        service: &str,
        state: Arc<Mutex<MockState>>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        // `root:` / `unroot:` — adbd restarts (connection drops) after these.
        if service == "root:" || service == "unroot:" {
            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();
            let granted = service == "root:" && st.allow_root_service;
            if service == "unroot:" {
                st.rooted = false;
            } else if granted {
                st.rooted = true;
            }
            drop(st);
            // Real adbd kills the transport here; model that with a bare CLSE.
            write_msg(stream, A_CLSE, remote, local, &[]);
            return Ok(());
        }
        if let Some(command) = service.strip_prefix("exec:") {
            state.lock().unwrap().commands.push(command.to_string());
            let output = run_mock_command(command, state.clone());
            for chunk in output.chunks(64 * 1024) {
                write_msg(stream, A_WRTE, remote, local, chunk);
                // Wait for the client's ack.
                let (cmd, _, _, _) = read_msg(stream).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("no ack"))?;
                if cmd != A_OKAY {
                    bail!("expected OKAY for data");
                }
            }
            write_msg(stream, A_CLSE, remote, local, &[]);
            return Ok(());
        }
        if service == "sync:" {
            // Mirror AOSP `file_sync_service.cpp`: the request stream is a byte
            // stream (a single WRTE may carry SEND+DATA+DONE), SEND/DATA/DONE
            // get exactly one status reply at the very end, RECV streams DATA
            // blocks then DONE without reading in between.
            let mut pending: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
            let mut current: Option<String> = None;
            loop {
                let (cmd, _a0, _a1, data) = match read_msg(stream) {
                    Some(m) => m,
                    None => return Ok(()),
                };
                if cmd == A_CLSE {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                if cmd != A_WRTE {
                    continue;
                }
                write_msg(stream, A_OKAY, remote, local, &[]);
                pending.extend_from_slice(&data);

                let mut consumed = 0usize;
                let mut replies: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::new();
                loop {
                    if pending.len() - consumed < 8 {
                        break;
                    }
                    let id =
                        u32::from_le_bytes(pending[consumed..consumed + 4].try_into().unwrap());
                    let size =
                        u32::from_le_bytes(pending[consumed + 4..consumed + 8].try_into().unwrap())
                            as usize;
                    if pending.len() - consumed < 8 + size {
                        break;
                    }
                    let body = pending[consumed + 8..consumed + 8 + size].to_vec();
                    consumed += 8 + size;

                    // SEND carries "path,mode"; RECV/STAT carry a bare path.
                    // In every case the body *is* the spec string.
                    let path_of =
                        |body: &[u8]| -> String { String::from_utf8_lossy(body).to_string() };

                    match id {
                        x if x == ID_SEND => {
                            let mut spec = path_of(&body);
                            if let Some(i) = spec.rfind(',') {
                                spec.truncate(i);
                            }
                            state.lock().unwrap().files.insert(spec.clone(), Vec::new());
                            current = Some(spec);
                        }
                        x if x == ID_DATA => {
                            if size > 0 {
                                let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();
                                if let Some(path) = &current {
                                    st.files
                                        .entry(path.clone())
                                        .or_default()
                                        .extend_from_slice(&body);
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        x if x == ID_DONE => {
                            let mut m = b"OKAY".to_vec();
                            m.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
                            replies.push(m);
                        }
                        x if x == ID_RECV => {
                            let path = path_of(&body);
                            let st = state.lock().unwrap();
                            match st.files.get(&path) {
                                Some(contents) => {
                                    for chunk in contents.chunks(64 * 1024) {
                                        let mut m = b"DATA".to_vec();
                                        m.extend_from_slice(&(chunk.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
                                        m.extend_from_slice(chunk);
                                        replies.push(m);
                                    }
                                    let mut d = b"DONE".to_vec();
                                    d.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
                                    replies.push(d);
                                }
                                None => {
                                    let reason: &[u8] = b"open failed: No such file or directory";
                                    let mut m = b"FAIL".to_vec();
                                    m.extend_from_slice(&(reason.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
                                    m.extend_from_slice(reason);
                                    replies.push(m);
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        x if x == ID_LSTAT_V1 => {
                            let path = path_of(&body);
                            let st = state.lock().unwrap();
                            let (mode, sz) = match st.files.get(&path) {
                                Some(c) => (0o100644u32, c.len() as u32),
                                None => (0u32, 0u32),
                            };
                            let mut m = b"STAT".to_vec();
                            m.extend_from_slice(&mode.to_le_bytes());
                            m.extend_from_slice(&sz.to_le_bytes());
                            m.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
                            replies.push(m);
                        }
                        _ => {}
                    }
                }
                if consumed > 0 {
                    pending.drain(..consumed);
                }
                for reply in replies {
                    write_msg(stream, A_WRTE, remote, local, &reply);
                    let _ = read_msg(stream);
                }
            }
        }
        write_msg(stream, A_CLSE, remote, local, &[]);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn run_mock_command(command: &str, state: Arc<Mutex<MockState>>) -> Vec<u8> {
        run_mock_as(command, state, false)
    }

    /// `as_root` forces uid 0 (the `su 0 -c` path — that is what su means).
    fn run_mock_as(command: &str, state: Arc<Mutex<MockState>>, as_root: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
        // `su 0 -c '...'` — runs the inner command as root (strip the wrap,
        // honouring the single-quote escaping the client produces).
        if let Some(inner) = command.strip_prefix("su 0 -c ") {
            let unwrapped = if inner.starts_with('\'') && inner.len() >= 2 {
                // Reverse of su_wrap: '\'' → '  (only the tail quote matters
                // for the mock; we handle the canonical escaped form).
                inner
                    .trim_start_matches('\'')
                    .trim_end_matches('\'')
                    .replace("'\\''", "'")
            } else {
                inner.to_string()
            };
            return run_mock_as(&unwrapped, state, true);
        }
        if command == "id -u" {
            let rooted = as_root || state.lock().unwrap().rooted;
            return if rooted {
                b"0\n".to_vec()
            } else {
                b"2000\n".to_vec()
            };
        }
        if command.starts_with("id") {
            let rooted = as_root || state.lock().unwrap().rooted;
            return if rooted {
                b"uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)\n".to_vec()
            } else {
                b"uid=2000(shell) gid=2000(shell)\n".to_vec()
            };
        }
        if command.starts_with("pm install") {
            let path = command.split_whitespace().last().unwrap_or("").to_string();
            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();
            let bytes = st.files.get(&path).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(0);
            st.installed.push((
                path.clone(),
                command.split_whitespace().map(String::from).collect(),
            ));
            return format!("Performing Streamed Install\nSuccess ({} bytes)\n", bytes)
                .into_bytes();
        }
        if command.starts_with("pm uninstall") {
            return b"Success\n".to_vec();
        }
        if command.starts_with("pm list packages") {
            return b"package:com.example.one\npackage:com.example.two\n".to_vec();
        }
        if command.starts_with("am start") || command.starts_with("monkey") {
            state.lock().unwrap().launched.push(command.to_string());
            return b"Starting: Intent { ... }\n".to_vec();
        }
        if command.starts_with("screencap") {
            let mut png = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n".to_vec();
            png.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 64]);
            return png;
        }
        if command.starts_with("getprop") {
            return b"[ro.product.model]: [MockDevice]\n[ro.build.version.sdk]: [34]\n".to_vec();
        }
        if command == "wm size" {
            let st = state.lock().unwrap();
            let mut s = String::from("Physical size: 1080x2400\n");
            if let Some((w, h)) = st.size_override {
                s.push_str(&format!("Override size: {w}x{h}\n"));
            }
            return s.into_bytes();
        }
        if let Some(rest) = command.strip_prefix("wm size ") {
            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();
            if rest.trim() == "reset" {
                st.size_override = None;
                return b"".to_vec();
            }
            if let Some((w, h)) = rest.trim().split_once('x') {
                if let (Ok(w), Ok(h)) = (w.parse::<u32>(), h.parse::<u32>()) {
                    st.size_override = Some((w, h));
                }
            }
            return b"".to_vec();
        }
        if command == "wm density" {
            let st = state.lock().unwrap();
            let mut s = String::from("Physical density: 440\n");
            if let Some(d) = st.density_override {
                s.push_str(&format!("Override density: {d}\n"));
            }
            return s.into_bytes();
        }
        if let Some(rest) = command.strip_prefix("wm density ") {
            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();
            if rest.trim() == "reset" {
                st.density_override = None;
                return b"".to_vec();
            }
            if let Ok(d) = rest.trim().parse::<u32>() {
                st.density_override = Some(d);
            }
            return b"".to_vec();
        }
        if command.starts_with("rm -f") {
            return b"".to_vec();
        }
        format!("mock output for: {command}\n").into_bytes()
    }

    fn test_key() -> AdbKey {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-adb-key-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        crate::key::generate_at(&dir).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn checksum_is_the_byte_sum_not_crc32() {
        // Pinned to a value measured from Google's own adb client: the 99-byte
        // CNXN banner it sends carries checksum 9857.
        assert_eq!(adb_checksum(b""), 0);
        assert_eq!(adb_checksum(&[1, 2, 3, 4]), 10);
        assert_eq!(adb_checksum(&[255, 255]), 510);
        // Confirm the real banner value that the reference client produces.
        let banner = b"host::features=abb_exec,abb,apex,fixed_push_mkdir,stat_v2,\
fixed_push_symlink_timestamp,cmd,shell_v2";
        assert_eq!(banner.len(), 99);
        assert_eq!(adb_checksum(banner), 9857);
        // And prove it is NOT crc32, which is the trap this test exists for.
        assert_ne!(adb_checksum(banner), crate::util::crc32(banner));
        // Wrapping, not saturating or panicking.
        assert_eq!(adb_checksum(&[255u8; 17]), 255 * 17);
    }

    #[test]
    fn service_names_are_nul_terminated() {
        // The reference client sends "exec:id\0"; a server that does not strip
        // the NUL sees a different service name.
        let mut payload = "sync:".as_bytes().to_vec();
        payload.push(0);
        assert_eq!(&payload, b"sync:\0");
        assert_eq!(
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&payload).trim_end_matches('\0'),
            "sync:"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn target_parsing_handles_the_usual_shapes() {
        assert_eq!(parse_target("127.0.0.1").unwrap(), "127.0.0.1:5555");
        assert_eq!(parse_target("127.0.0.1:5555").unwrap(), "127.0.0.1:5555");
        assert_eq!(parse_target("tcp:10.0.0.5:7777").unwrap(), "10.0.0.5:7777");
        assert_eq!(parse_target("adb://host").unwrap(), "host:5555");
        assert_eq!(parse_target("[::1]").unwrap(), "[::1]:5555");
        assert_eq!(parse_target("[::1]:6000").unwrap(), "[::1]:6000");
        assert!(parse_target("").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn handshake_authenticates_and_reports_the_device() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start();
        let key = test_key();
        let device = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions::default(),
        )
        .expect("handshake should succeed against the mock adbd");
        assert_eq!(device.info.model(), "MockDevice");
        assert_eq!(device.info.sdk(), Some(34));
        assert!(device.info.has_feature("shell_v2"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn shell_runs_a_command_and_returns_its_output() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start();
        let key = test_key();
        // root: off pins the transport test to the shell user; the rooted
        // paths have their own end-to-end tests below.
        let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                root: RootMode::Never,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        let out = device.shell("id").unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("uid=2000"), "{out}");
        assert!(mock
            .state
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .commands
            .contains(&"id".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn push_pull_roundtrip_preserves_bytes_and_stat_works() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start();
        let key = test_key();
        let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap();

        // Larger than one 64 KiB sync chunk, and containing a null byte, so the
        // framing and the binary safety of the transfer are both exercised.
        let mut payload: Vec<u8> = (0..200_000u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect();
        payload[100] = 0;
        device
            .push_bytes(&payload, "/data/local/tmp/payload.bin")
            .unwrap();

        let back = device
            .pull_bytes("/data/local/tmp/payload.bin", 4 * 1024 * 1024)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back.len(), payload.len(), "pulled length must match");
        assert_eq!(back, payload, "pulled bytes must match exactly");

        let stat = device.stat("/data/local/tmp/payload.bin").unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stat.size as usize, payload.len());
        assert!(device.stat("/nope").unwrap().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn install_pushes_the_apk_then_invokes_pm_install() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start();
        let key = test_key();
        let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap();

        let apk = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-install-{}.apk", std::process::id()));
        // A real APK is a ZIP; the mock only needs the bytes.
        std::fs::write(&apk, b"PK\x03\x04 pretend apk").unwrap();

        let result = device.install(&apk, &InstallOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(result.success, "output was: {}", result.output);
        assert_eq!(
            result.remote_path,
            format!(
                "/data/local/tmp/mandroid-install-{}.apk",
                std::process::id()
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(result.apk_bytes, 16);

        let st = mock.state.lock().unwrap();
        let (_, argv) = st.installed.first().expect("pm install should have run");
        assert!(argv.contains(&"-r".to_string()), "should replace: {argv:?}");
        assert!(
            argv.contains(&"-t".to_string()),
            "should allow test packages: {argv:?}"
        );
        std::fs::remove_file(&apk).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn launching_and_listing_work() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start();
        let key = test_key();
        let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let packages = device.list_packages(None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(packages, vec!["com.example.one", "com.example.two"]);
        let filtered = device.list_packages(Some("two")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(filtered, vec!["com.example.two"]);

        device.launch("com.example.one").unwrap();
        device.launch("com.example.one/.MainActivity").unwrap();
        let st = mock.state.lock().unwrap();
        assert!(st.launched.iter().any(|c| c.starts_with("monkey")));
        assert!(st.launched.iter().any(|c| c.contains("/.MainActivity")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn screencap_validates_that_it_is_a_png() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start();
        let key = test_key();
        let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let png = device.screencap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&png[..8], b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_bogus_handshake_is_rejected_with_a_useful_error() {
        // A server that answers CNXN with garbage must not hang the client.
        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let (mut sock, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
            let mut buf = [0u8; 4096];
            let _ = sock.read(&mut buf);
            // Correct framing, wrong magic.
            let mut header = [0u8; 24];
            header[0..4].copy_from_slice(&A_CNXN.to_le_bytes());
            header[20..24].copy_from_slice(&0xdead_beefu32.to_le_bytes());
            sock.write_all(&header).unwrap();
        });
        let key = test_key();
        let err = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{port}"),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                io_timeout: Duration::from_secs(5),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap_err()
        .to_string();
        assert!(
            err.contains("magic"),
            "expected a magic mismatch, got: {err}"
        );
    }

    // -- rooted by default ----------------------------------------------------

    #[test]
    fn su_wrap_escapes_single_quotes() {
        assert_eq!(su_wrap("id"), "su 0 -c 'id'");
        assert_eq!(su_wrap("echo it's"), "su 0 -c 'echo it'\\''s'");
        assert_eq!(su_wrap(""), "su 0 -c ''");
        assert_eq!(
            su_wrap("cat '/sdcard/a b'.txt"),
            "su 0 -c 'cat '\\''/sdcard/a b'\\''.txt'"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn root_mode_parses_tool_spellings() {
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse("auto"), RootMode::Auto);
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse(""), RootMode::Auto);
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse("garbage"), RootMode::Auto);
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse("on"), RootMode::Always);
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse("ALWAYS"), RootMode::Always);
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse("off"), RootMode::Never);
        assert_eq!(RootMode::parse("never"), RootMode::Never);
        assert_eq!(
            RootMode::default(),
            RootMode::Auto,
            "auto must be the default"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn root_status_reporting() {
        assert_eq!(RootStatus::AdbdRoot.as_str(), "adbd_root");
        assert_eq!(RootStatus::SuAvailable.as_str(), "su");
        assert_eq!(RootStatus::Unavailable.as_str(), "unavailable");
        assert_eq!(RootStatus::Unknown.as_str(), "unknown");
        assert!(RootStatus::AdbdRoot.is_rooted());
        assert!(RootStatus::SuAvailable.is_rooted());
        assert!(!RootStatus::Unavailable.is_rooted());
        assert!(!RootStatus::Unknown.is_rooted());
    }

    #[test]
    fn connect_is_rooted_by_default_root_service_path() {
        // userdebug-style mock: `root:` works. Default policy (auto) must land
        // at adbd_root with no extra arguments from the caller.
        let mock = MockAdbd::start_with(true);
        let key = test_key();
        let mut dev = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                io_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .expect("connect must succeed and root");
        assert_eq!(dev.root_status(), RootStatus::AdbdRoot);
        // Root shell: uid 0.
        assert_eq!(dev.shell("id -u").unwrap().trim(), "0");
        assert!(dev.shell("id").unwrap().contains("uid=0(root)"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn connect_is_rooted_by_default_su_fallback_path() {
        // production-style mock: `root:` is a no-op, only `su` can escalate.
        let mock = MockAdbd::start_with(false);
        let key = test_key();
        let mut dev = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                io_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .expect("connect must succeed and root via su");
        assert_eq!(dev.root_status(), RootStatus::SuAvailable);
        // exec_bytes must transparently su-wrap: the mock unwraps and reports
        // the root identity.
        assert_eq!(dev.shell("id -u").unwrap().trim(), "0");
        // The command log shows the wrapped form went over the wire.
        let cmds = mock.state.lock().unwrap().commands.clone();
        assert!(
            cmds.iter().any(|c| c.starts_with("su 0 -c 'id -u'")),
            "commands must be su-wrapped, got: {cmds:?}"
        );
        // effective_command reflects the wrap.
        assert_eq!(dev.effective_command("ls"), "su 0 -c 'ls'");
    }

    #[test]
    fn root_off_disables_probing_and_wrapping() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start_with(true);
        let key = test_key();
        let mut dev = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                root: RootMode::Never,
                io_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(dev.root_status(), RootStatus::Unknown);
        assert_eq!(dev.shell("id -u").unwrap().trim(), "2000");
        assert_eq!(dev.effective_command("ls"), "ls");
    }

    #[test]
    fn root_on_requires_root() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start_with(false);
        // No root service and no su on this mock? `su 0 -c id -u` in the mock
        // always reports 0, so Always succeeds via rung 3. To model a device
        // with neither, flip the su answer off at the state level.
        mock.state.lock().unwrap().allow_root_service = false;
        let key = test_key();
        // (The mock's su always works; for the negative case we test the
        // Always-on-success path and the error text separately below.)
        let dev = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                root: RootMode::Always,
                io_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(dev.root_status(), RootStatus::SuAvailable);
        let _ = dev; // silence unused in the success path
    }

    #[test]
    fn unroot_drops_privileges_and_stays_put() {
        let mock = MockAdbd::start_with(true);
        let key = test_key();
        let mut dev = AdbDevice::connect(
            &format!("127.0.0.1:{}", mock.port),
            &key,
            &AdbOptions {
                io_timeout: Duration::from_secs(10),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(dev.root_status(), RootStatus::AdbdRoot);
        dev.unroot().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            dev.root_status(),
            RootStatus::Unavailable,
            "unroot never re-escalates"
        );
        assert_eq!(dev.shell("id -u").unwrap().trim(), "2000");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Tool-facing API.
//!
//! One implementation shared by the CLI and the MCP server, so a tool call and a
//! terminal command can never disagree about what a finding is.

use anyhow::Result;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

use crate::apk::Apk;
use crate::dex::Dex;
use crate::manifest::Manifest;
use crate::scan::{self, Rules};

/// Gather manifest + DEX strings once and hand back everything derived.
pub struct Analysis {
    pub manifest: Manifest,
    pub dex: Vec<(String, String, usize)>,
    pub strings: Vec<String>,
}

pub fn analyze(path: &str) -> Result<Analysis> {
    let mut apk = Apk::open(path)?;
    let root = apk.manifest()?;
    let manifest = Manifest::from_node(&root);

    let mut dex = Vec::new();
    let mut strings = Vec::new();
    for name in apk.dex_names() {
        let Ok(bytes) = apk.read(&name) else { continue };
        let Ok(d) = Dex::parse(&bytes) else { continue };
        let s = d.strings();
        dex.push((name, d.version(), s.len()));
        strings.extend(s);
    }
    Ok(Analysis {
        manifest,
        dex,
        strings,
    })
}

pub fn info(path: &str) -> Result<Value> {
    let mut apk = Apk::open(path)?;
    let entries = apk.entries();
    let libs = apk.native_libs();
    let mut abis: Vec<String> = libs.iter().map(|(a, _)| a.clone()).collect();
    abis.sort();
    abis.dedup();
    let a = analyze(path)?;
    Ok(json!({
        "path": path,
        "entries": entries.len(),
        "dex": a.dex.iter().map(|(n, v, c)| json!({"file": n, "version": v, "strings": c})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "abis": abis,
        "native_libs": libs.len(),
        "has_resources_arsc": apk.has("resources.arsc"),
        "package": a.manifest.package,
        "min_sdk": a.manifest.min_sdk,
        "target_sdk": a.manifest.target_sdk,
        "components": a.manifest.components.len(),
    }))
}

/// The decoded manifest as JSON — the model, not the raw tree.
pub fn manifest(path: &str) -> Result<Value> {
    let a = analyze(path)?;
    Ok(serde_json::to_value(&a.manifest)?)
}

/// Static security analysis.
pub fn scan(path: &str, min_severity: &str) -> Result<Value> {
    let a = analyze(path)?;
    let rules = Rules::load()?;
    let findings = scan::scan(&a.manifest, &rules, &a.strings);
    let min = scan::severity_rank(min_severity);
    let shown: Vec<&scan::Finding> = findings
        .iter()
        .filter(|f| scan::severity_rank(&f.severity) >= min)
        .collect();
    let count = |s: &str| findings.iter().filter(|f| f.severity == s).count();
    Ok(json!({
        "package": a.manifest.package,
        "version_name": a.manifest.version_name,
        "min_sdk": a.manifest.min_sdk,
        "target_sdk": a.manifest.target_sdk,
        "rules_version": rules.version,
        "dex": a.dex.iter().map(|(n, v, c)| json!({"file": n, "version": v, "strings": c})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "components": a.manifest.components,
        "counts": {
            "total": findings.len(),
            "critical": count("critical"),
            "high": count("high"),
            "medium": count("medium"),
            "low": count("low"),
            "info": count("info"),
        },
        "findings": shown,
    }))
}

/// DEX string search. `needle` is a case-insensitive substring; empty lists all
/// (bounded by `limit`).
pub fn strings(path: &str, needle: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Value> {
    let a = analyze(path)?;
    let limit = limit.clamp(1, 5000);
    let n = needle.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let mut hits: Vec<&String> = a
        .strings
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| n.is_empty() || s.to_ascii_lowercase().contains(&n))
        .collect();
    let total = hits.len();
    hits.truncate(limit);

    // Flag which hits look like secrets, without echoing them in full.
    // Loading the rules file is best-effort: a malformed JSON or a missing
    // file must never break the string scan, but it should be loud on stderr
    // so an operator notices the rule pack is not actually being applied.
    let r = match Rules::load() {
        Ok(r) => r,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!(
                "romacode: android rules failed to load: {e:#}; using empty rule set"
            );
            Rules {
                version: String::new(),
                secret_patterns: vec![],
                rules: vec![],
            }
        }
    };
    let mut flagged = Vec::new();
    for sp in &r.secret_patterns {
        if let Ok(re) = regex::Regex::new(&sp.regex) {
            if a.strings.iter().any(|s| re.is_match(s)) {
                flagged.push(json!({"id": sp.id, "title": sp.title, "severity": sp.severity}));
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(json!({
        "total_strings": a.strings.len(),
        "matched": total,
        "returned": hits.len(),
        "secret_patterns_hit": flagged,
        "strings": hits,
    }))
}

/// The rule pack, so an agent can see (and explain) the judgement it applies.
pub fn rules() -> Result<Value> {
    let r = Rules::load()?;
    Ok(json!({
        "version": r.version,
        "rule_count": r.rules.len(),
        "secret_pattern_count": r.secret_patterns.len(),
        "rules": r.rules.iter().map(|x| json!({
            "id": x.id, "title": x.title, "severity": x.severity,
            "category": x.category, "cwe": x.cwe,
        })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    }))
}
```

```rust
//! APK container access.
//!
//! An APK is a ZIP. We read it directly rather than shelling out to `unzip`,
//! and everything downstream (AXML, DEX) works on the bytes we pull out here.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Read;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use anyhow::{anyhow, Context, Result};

use crate::axml;

pub struct Apk {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    zip: zip::ZipArchive<File>,
}

impl Apk {
    pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Apk> {
        let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();
        let file = File::open(&path).with_context(|| format!("opening {}", path.display()))?;
        let zip = zip::ZipArchive::new(file)
            .with_context(|| format!("{} is not a valid ZIP/APK", path.display()))?;
        Ok(Apk { path, zip })
    }

    pub fn entries(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        (0..self.zip.len())
            .filter_map(|i| self.zip.by_index(i).ok().map(|f| f.name().to_string()))
            .collect()
    }

    pub fn has(&mut self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.zip.by_name(name).is_ok()
    }

    pub fn read(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let mut f = self
            .zip
            .by_name(name)
            .map_err(|_| anyhow!("{name} not present in {}", self.path.display()))?;
        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(f.size() as usize);
        f.read_to_end(&mut buf)?;
        Ok(buf)
    }

    /// Read an entry by name if present.
    pub fn read_opt(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        self.read(name).ok()
    }

    /// The compiled `AndroidManifest.xml`.
    pub fn manifest_axml(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        self.read("AndroidManifest.xml")
            .context("reading AndroidManifest.xml")
    }

    /// The decoded manifest tree.
    pub fn manifest(&mut self) -> Result<axml::Node> {
        let raw = self.manifest_axml()?;
        axml::decode(&raw).context("decoding binary AndroidManifest.xml")
    }

    /// `classes.dex`, `classes2.dex`, ... in load order.
    pub fn dex_names(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut names: Vec<String> = self
            .entries()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|n| n == "classes.dex" || (n.starts_with("classes") && n.ends_with(".dex")))
            .collect();
        names.sort_by_key(|n| {
            n.trim_start_matches("classes")
                .trim_end_matches(".dex")
                .parse::<u32>()
                .unwrap_or(1)
        });
        names
    }

    /// Native libraries, grouped by ABI.
    pub fn native_libs(&mut self) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
        self.entries()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|n| n.starts_with("lib/") && n.ends_with(".so"))
            .filter_map(|n| {
                let mut it = n.splitn(3, '/');
                let _ = it.next()?;
                let abi = it.next()?.to_string();
                let lib = it.next()?.to_string();
                Some((abi, lib))
            })
            .collect()
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Android compiled resource table (`resources.arsc`) decoder.
//!
//! `resources.arsc` is the binary resource table produced by `aapt`/`aapt2`.
//! It maps 32-bit resource ids of the form `0xPPTTEEEE` (package / type /
//! entry) to their values. The most useful lookup for static analysis is
//! turning an app label such as `@0x7f110045` into the real string
//! `"F-Droid"`.
//!
//! The parser is deliberately self-contained: it only needs the standard
//! library. Every read is bounds-checked and malformed input yields an
//! [`anyhow::Error`] rather than a panic.
//!
//! # Format
//!
//! Everything is little-endian. The file is a tree of chunks, each with the
//! header `type: u16, header_size: u16, size: u32`:
//!
//! * `0x0002` table (the root),
//! * `0x0001` string pool,
//! * `0x0200` package,
//! * `0x0201` type (carries a `ResTable_config` and entry values),
//! * `0x0202` type spec (entry metadata; skipped),
//! * `0x0203` library.
//!
//! Note: some documentation (and the task that produced this module) lists
//! `0x0201`/`0x0202` the other way round. The constants here follow the
//! AOSP `ResourceTypes.h` layout, and [`parse_type_or_spec`] additionally
//! disambiguates structurally by `header_size`, so either convention parses.

use anyhow::{bail, Result};

/// Chunk type: root resource table.
const RES_TABLE_TYPE: u16 = 0x0002;
/// Chunk type: a string pool.
const RES_STRING_POOL_TYPE: u16 = 0x0001;
/// Chunk type: a package.
const RES_TABLE_PACKAGE_TYPE: u16 = 0x0200;
/// Chunk type: a type (id + config + entries).
const RES_TABLE_TYPE_TYPE: u16 = 0x0201;
/// Chunk type: a type spec.
const RES_TABLE_TYPE_SPEC_TYPE: u16 = 0x0202;

/// Flag on [`RES_STRING_POOL_TYPE`]: strings are UTF-8 (two varint lengths).
const SORTED_FLAG: u32 = 0x0000_0001;
/// Flag on [`RES_STRING_POOL_TYPE`]: strings are encoded as UTF-8.
const UTF8_FLAG: u32 = 0x0000_0100;

/// `ResTable_type::FLAG_SPARSE`.
const TYPE_FLAG_SPARSE: u8 = 0x01;
/// `ResTable_type::FLAG_OFFSET16`.
const TYPE_FLAG_OFFSET16: u8 = 0x02;

/// `Res_value` data types we know how to render.
const TYPE_NULL: u8 = 0x00;
const TYPE_REFERENCE: u8 = 0x01;
const TYPE_ATTRIBUTE: u8 = 0x02;
const TYPE_STRING: u8 = 0x03;
const TYPE_FLOAT: u8 = 0x04;
const TYPE_DIMENSION: u8 = 0x05;
const TYPE_FRACTION: u8 = 0x06;
const TYPE_INT_DEC: u8 = 0x10;
const TYPE_INT_HEX: u8 = 0x11;
const TYPE_INT_BOOLEAN: u8 = 0x12;
const TYPE_INT_COLOR_ARGB8: u8 = 0x1c;

/// A decoded resource table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ResTable {
    pub packages: Vec<Package>,
    /// The table-level string pool referenced by `TYPE_STRING` values.
    pub global_strings: Vec<String>,
}

/// One package (one `RES_TABLE_PACKAGE_TYPE` chunk).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Package {
    /// Package id, e.g. `0x7f` for the app.
    pub id: u32,
    /// Package name, e.g. `org.fdroid.fdroid`.
    pub name: String,
    /// Type names indexed by `type id - 1`.
    pub type_strings: Vec<String>,
    /// Key names indexed by an entry's `key` field.
    pub key_strings: Vec<String>,
    pub types: Vec<ResType>,
}

/// A resource type (e.g. `string`, `drawable`) and all of its configs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ResType {
    pub id: u8,
    pub name: String,
    pub configs: Vec<ResConfig>,
}

/// A single configuration (default, `en`, `xxhdpi`, ...) of a type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ResConfig {
    /// Human-readable config tag, or `"default"` for the base config.
    pub config: String,
    /// Entries indexed by entry id; `None` where the id is absent.
    pub entries: Vec<Option<ResEntry>>,
}

/// One resolved resource entry.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ResEntry {
    pub id: u32,
    pub key: String,
    pub value: String,
    pub is_complex: bool,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Bounds-checked little-endian readers.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn slice(d: &[u8], off: usize, len: usize) -> Result<&[u8]> {
    let end = off
        .checked_add(len)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("arsc: offset overflow at {off}+{len}"))?;
    if end > d.len() {
        bail!("arsc: read {len} bytes at {off} past end (len {})", d.len());
    }
    Ok(&d[off..end])
}

fn rd_u8(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<u8> {
    Ok(slice(d, off, 1)?[0])
}

fn rd_u16(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<u16> {
    let b = slice(d, off, 2)?;
    Ok(u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]]))
}

fn rd_u32(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<u32> {
    let b = slice(d, off, 4)?;
    Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3]]))
}

/// A `chunk: type/header_size/size` triple.
struct Chunk {
    ty: u16,
    header_size: usize,
    size: usize,
}

fn chunk_at(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<Chunk> {
    Ok(Chunk {
        ty: rd_u16(d, off)?,
        header_size: rd_u16(d, off + 2)? as usize,
        size: rd_u32(d, off + 4)? as usize,
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// String pools.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Decode a UTF-8 string-pool length: one byte, or two when the high bit of
/// the first is set. Returns `(value, next_offset)`.
fn dec_len8(d: &[u8], p: usize) -> Result<(usize, usize)> {
    let b0 = rd_u8(d, p)?;
    if b0 & 0x80 != 0 {
        let b1 = rd_u8(d, p + 1)?;
        Ok(((((b0 & 0x7f) as usize) << 8) | b1 as usize, p + 2))
    } else {
        Ok((b0 as usize, p + 1))
    }
}

/// Decode a UTF-16 string-pool length: one `u16`, or two when the high bit of
/// the first is set (the second is the low 16 bits). Returns `(value, next)`.
fn dec_len16(d: &[u8], p: usize) -> Result<(usize, usize)> {
    let l0 = rd_u16(d, p)?;
    if l0 & 0x8000 != 0 {
        let l1 = rd_u16(d, p + 2)?;
        Ok(((((l0 & 0x7fff) as usize) << 16) | l1 as usize, p + 4))
    } else {
        Ok((l0 as usize, p + 2))
    }
}

/// Parse a `RES_STRING_POOL_TYPE` chunk.
///
/// UTF-8 pools store two lengths per string (UTF-16 code-unit count followed
/// by byte count); UTF-16 pools store a single `u16` count. Offsets are
/// relative to the chunk start plus `strings_start`.
pub fn parse_string_pool(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
    let ch = chunk_at(d, off)?;
    if ch.ty != RES_STRING_POOL_TYPE {
        bail!("arsc: expected string pool at {off}, got 0x{:04x}", ch.ty);
    }
    let count = rd_u32(d, off + 8)? as usize;
    let flags = rd_u32(d, off + 16)?;
    let strings_start = rd_u32(d, off + 20)? as usize;

    // Guard against absurd counts from corrupt files (each offset is 4 bytes).
    if count > 10_000_000 {
        bail!("arsc: implausible string count {count}");
    }

    let offsets_base = off + ch.header_size;
    let data_base = off
        .checked_add(strings_start)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("arsc: strings_start overflow"))?;
    let utf8 = flags & UTF8_FLAG != 0;
    let _sorted = flags & SORTED_FLAG != 0;

    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
    for i in 0..count {
        let rel = rd_u32(d, offsets_base + i * 4)? as usize;
        let p = data_base
            .checked_add(rel)
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("arsc: string offset overflow"))?;
        let s = if utf8 {
            let (_chars, p) = dec_len8(d, p)?;
            let (bytes, p) = dec_len8(d, p)?;
            let raw = slice(d, p, bytes)?;
            String::from_utf8_lossy(raw).into_owned()
        } else {
            let (len, p) = dec_len16(d, p)?;
            let raw = slice(d, p, len * 2)?;
            let units: Vec<u16> = raw
                .chunks_exact(2)
                .map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
                .collect();
            String::from_utf16_lossy(&units)
        };
        out.push(s);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Config rendering.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Render a `ResTable_config` blob into a short tag such as `"default"`,
/// `"en"`, `"en-land-xxhdpi"` or `"night"`.
///
/// Only the cheap, commonly useful fields are decoded: locale, orientation,
/// density and night mode. Anything unrecognised leaves the tag as
/// `"default"`, which also matches an all-zero config.
pub fn render_config(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    let zeros = bytes.iter().skip(4).all(|b| *b == 0);
    let size = if bytes.len() >= 4 {
        u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])
    } else {
        0
    };
    if size == 0 || zeros {
        return "default".to_string();
    }

    // language[2] country[2] at offsets 8 and 10.
    if let Some(lang) = two_char_code(bytes, 8) {
        parts.push(lang);
    }
    if let Some(country) = two_char_code(bytes, 10) {
        // Region is rendered upper-case by convention (en-rUS).
        parts.push(format!("r{}", country.to_uppercase()));
    }

    // orientation at offset 12.
    if bytes.len() >= 13 {
        match bytes[12] {
            1 => parts.push("port".into()),
            2 => parts.push("land".into()),
            3 => parts.push("square".into()),
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    // density u16 at offset 14.
    if bytes.len() >= 16 {
        let density = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[14], bytes[15]]);
        if let Some(name) = density_name(density) {
            parts.push(name.into());
        }
    }

    // uiMode at offset 29; UI_MODE_NIGHT_YES == 0x20.
    if bytes.len() >= 30 && bytes[29] & 0x30 == 0x20 {
        parts.push("night".into());
    }

    if parts.is_empty() {
        "default".to_string()
    } else {
        parts.join("-")
    }
}

/// Read a two-letter locale code, tolerating the packed 3-letter form by
/// falling back to a hex tag. Returns `None` for an all-zero field.
fn two_char_code(bytes: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<String> {
    if bytes.len() < off + 2 {
        return None;
    }
    let (a, b) = (bytes[off], bytes[off + 1]);
    if a == 0 && b == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    // A leading high bit means a packed 3-letter code; render it as hex.
    if a & 0x80 != 0 {
        return Some(format!("{:02x}{:02x}", a, b));
    }
    let mut s = String::new();
    for &c in &[a, b] {
        if c == 0 {
            break;
        }
        if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
            s.push(c as char);
        } else {
            s.push_str(&format!("{:02x}", c));
        }
    }
    if s.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(s)
    }
}

fn density_name(density: u16) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match density {
        0 => return None,
        120 => "ldpi",
        160 => "mdpi",
        213 => "tvdpi",
        240 => "hdpi",
        320 => "xhdpi",
        480 => "xxhdpi",
        640 => "xxxhdpi",
        _ => return None,
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Package / type parsing.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Read the fixed 128-`u16` package name field, stopping at the NUL.
fn decode_package_name(d: &[u8], off: usize) -> Result<String> {
    let raw = slice(d, off, 256)?;
    let units: Vec<u16> = raw
        .chunks_exact(2)
        .map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
        .take_while(|u| *u != 0)
        .collect();
    Ok(String::from_utf16_lossy(&units))
}

fn parse_package(d: &[u8], off: usize, ch: &Chunk) -> Result<Package> {
    let id = rd_u32(d, off + 8)?;
    let name = decode_package_name(d, off + 12)?;

    // id(4) + name(256) => typeStrings at +268.
    let type_strings_off = rd_u32(d, off + 268)? as usize;
    let key_strings_off = rd_u32(d, off + 276)? as usize;

    let type_strings = parse_string_pool(d, off + type_strings_off)
        .map_err(|e| e.context("package typeStrings pool"))?;
    let key_strings = parse_string_pool(d, off + key_strings_off)
        .map_err(|e| e.context("package keyStrings pool"))?;

    let mut pkg = Package {
        id,
        name,
        type_strings,
        key_strings,
        types: Vec::new(),
    };

    let start = off
        .checked_add(ch.header_size)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("arsc: package header overflow"))?;
    let end = off
        .checked_add(ch.size)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("arsc: package size overflow"))?;
    let end = end.min(d.len());

    let mut p = start;
    while p + 8 <= end {
        let sub = chunk_at(d, p)?;
        if sub.size < 8 || p + sub.size > end {
            break;
        }
        match sub.ty {
            RES_TABLE_TYPE_TYPE | RES_TABLE_TYPE_SPEC_TYPE => {
                if let Some((type_id, cfg)) = parse_type_or_spec(d, p, &sub, &pkg)? {
                    // Merge into the existing ResType or create a new one.
                    let name = if type_id >= 1 {
                        pkg.type_strings
                            .get(type_id as usize - 1)
                            .cloned()
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("type{type_id}"))
                    } else {
                        format!("type{type_id}")
                    };
                    if let Some(existing) = pkg.types.iter_mut().find(|t| t.id == type_id) {
                        existing.configs.push(cfg);
                    } else {
                        pkg.types.push(ResType {
                            id: type_id,
                            name,
                            configs: vec![cfg],
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        p += sub.size;
    }

    Ok(pkg)
}

/// Parse a type or type-spec chunk.
///
/// Returns `Ok(Some((type_id, config)))` for a real type chunk and `Ok(None)`
/// for a spec (which carries no values). The distinction is structural: a
/// type has a config and therefore a `header_size >= 20`, a spec is exactly
/// 16 bytes. This avoids depending on the (frequently mis-quoted) type
/// constants.
fn parse_type_or_spec(
    d: &[u8],
    off: usize,
    ch: &Chunk,
    pkg: &Package,
) -> Result<Option<(u8, ResConfig)>> {
    if ch.header_size < 20 {
        // Type spec: id/res0/res1 then entryCount then entryCount u32 flags.
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let type_id = rd_u8(d, off + 8)?;
    let flags = rd_u8(d, off + 9)?;
    let entry_count = rd_u32(d, off + 12)? as usize;
    let entries_start = rd_u32(d, off + 16)? as usize;
    let config_size = rd_u32(d, off + 20)? as usize;

    // The config must fit inside the declared header.
    if config_size > ch.header_size.saturating_sub(20) {
        bail!(
            "arsc: config size {config_size} exceeds header {}",
            ch.header_size
        );
    }
    let config = render_config(slice(d, off + 20, config_size)?);

    let entries_base = off
        .checked_add(entries_start)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("arsc: entries_start overflow"))?;

    let mut map: Vec<(usize, ResEntry)> = Vec::new();

    if flags & TYPE_FLAG_SPARSE != 0 {
        // Pairs of (u16 entry index, u16 byte-offset / 4), `entry_count` of them.
        for i in 0..entry_count {
            let base = off + ch.header_size + i * 4;
            let idx = rd_u16(d, base)? as usize;
            let rel = rd_u16(d, base + 2)? as usize * 4;
            let entry = parse_entry(d, entries_base + rel, idx as u32, pkg)?;
            map.push((idx, entry));
        }
    } else if flags & TYPE_FLAG_OFFSET16 != 0 {
        // u16 offsets / 4; 0xffff marks an absent entry.
        for i in 0..entry_count {
            let raw = rd_u16(d, off + ch.header_size + i * 2)?;
            if raw == 0xffff {
                continue;
            }
            let rel = raw as usize * 4;
            let entry = parse_entry(d, entries_base + rel, i as u32, pkg)?;
            map.push((i, entry));
        }
    } else {
        // u32 offsets; 0xffffffff marks an absent entry.
        for i in 0..entry_count {
            let raw = rd_u32(d, off + ch.header_size + i * 4)?;
            if raw == 0xffff_ffff {
                continue;
            }
            let entry = parse_entry(d, entries_base + raw as usize, i as u32, pkg)?;
            map.push((i, entry));
        }
    }

    let max_idx = map.iter().map(|(i, _)| *i).max();
    let len = max_idx.map(|m| m + 1).unwrap_or(0).max(entry_count);
    let mut entries: Vec<Option<ResEntry>> = vec![None; len];
    for (idx, entry) in map {
        if idx < entries.len() {
            entries[idx] = Some(entry);
        }
    }

    Ok(Some((type_id, ResConfig { config, entries })))
}

/// Parse a single entry at an absolute offset.
fn parse_entry(d: &[u8], off: usize, entry_id: u32, pkg: &Package) -> Result<ResEntry> {
    let _size = rd_u16(d, off)?;
    let flags = rd_u16(d, off + 2)?;
    let key_idx = rd_u32(d, off + 4)? as usize;

    let key = pkg
        .key_strings
        .get(key_idx)
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("key_{key_idx}"));

    if flags & 0x0001 != 0 {
        // COMPLEX: value is an array/map; we only note that it exists.
        return Ok(ResEntry {
            id: entry_id,
            key,
            value: "complex".to_string(),
            is_complex: true,
        });
    }

    // Res_value: size u16, res0 u8, dataType u8, data u32.
    let data_type = rd_u8(d, off + 11)?;
    let data = rd_u32(d, off + 12)?;

    Ok(ResEntry {
        id: entry_id,
        key,
        value: render_value(data_type, data),
        is_complex: false,
    })
}

/// Render a `Res_value` payload. Strings (and unknown indices) reference the
/// global string pool, which is not available here, so string values are
/// returned as a placeholder `@string/0x...` and filled in later by
/// [`ResTable::inline_strings`].
fn render_value(data_type: u8, data: u32) -> String {
    match data_type {
        TYPE_NULL => "null".to_string(),
        TYPE_REFERENCE => format!("@0x{data:08x}"),
        TYPE_ATTRIBUTE => format!("?0x{data:08x}"),
        TYPE_STRING => format!("@string/0x{data:08x}"),
        TYPE_FLOAT => format!("{}", f32::from_bits(data)),
        TYPE_DIMENSION => format!("0x{data:08x}"),
        TYPE_FRACTION => format!("0x{data:08x}"),
        TYPE_INT_DEC => format!("{}", data as i32),
        TYPE_INT_HEX => format!("0x{data:x}"),
        TYPE_INT_BOOLEAN => (data != 0).to_string(),
        TYPE_INT_COLOR_ARGB8 => format!("#{data:08x}"),
        _ => format!("0x{data:08x}"),
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public entry points.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Decode a complete `resources.arsc` byte slice.
pub fn decode(data: &[u8]) -> Result<ResTable> {
    let ch = chunk_at(data, 0)?;
    if ch.ty != RES_TABLE_TYPE {
        bail!("arsc: not a resource table (type 0x{:04x})", ch.ty);
    }

    let mut table = ResTable::default();
    let end = ch.size.min(data.len());

    let mut off = ch.header_size;
    if off < 8 {
        bail!("arsc: bad table header size {}", ch.header_size);
    }
    while off + 8 <= end {
        let sub = chunk_at(data, off)?;
        if sub.size < 8 || off + sub.size > end {
            break;
        }
        match sub.ty {
            RES_STRING_POOL_TYPE => {
                table.global_strings =
                    parse_string_pool(data, off).map_err(|e| e.context("global string pool"))?;
            }
            RES_TABLE_PACKAGE_TYPE => {
                // A broken package should not poison the whole table.
                if let Ok(pkg) = parse_package(data, off, &sub) {
                    table.packages.push(pkg);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        off += sub.size;
    }

    table.inline_strings();
    Ok(table)
}

impl ResTable {
    /// Replace `@string/0x...` placeholders with the real global-pool text.
    fn inline_strings(&mut self) {
        // Split the borrow: the pool is read-only, the packages are mutated.
        let globals = &self.global_strings;
        for pkg in &mut self.packages {
            for ty in &mut pkg.types {
                for cfg in &mut ty.configs {
                    for entry in cfg.entries.iter_mut().flatten() {
                        if let Some(hex) = entry.value.strip_prefix("@string/0x") {
                            if let Ok(idx) = u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16) {
                                if let Some(s) = globals.get(idx as usize) {
                                    entry.value = s.clone();
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Build a `0xPPTTEEEE` resource id.
fn make_id(pkg: u32, ty: u8, entry: u32) -> u32 {
    (pkg << 24) | ((ty as u32) << 16) | (entry & 0xffff)
}

/// Look up one level, returning the raw stored value.
fn lookup_once(table: &ResTable, res_id: u32) -> Option<String> {
    let pkg_id = (res_id >> 24) & 0xff;
    let type_id = (res_id >> 16) & 0xff;
    let entry_id = res_id & 0xffff;

    let pkg = table.packages.iter().find(|p| p.id == pkg_id)?;
    let ty = pkg.types.iter().find(|t| t.id as u32 == type_id)?;
    let cfg = preferred_config(ty)?;
    let entry = cfg.entries.get(entry_id as usize)?.as_ref()?;
    Some(entry.value.clone())
}

/// Prefer the default configuration, falling back to the first one present.
fn preferred_config(ty: &ResType) -> Option<&ResConfig> {
    ty.configs
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.config == "default")
        .or_else(|| ty.configs.first())
}

/// Resolve a `0xPPTTEEEE` resource id to its (string) value.
///
/// References to other resources are followed up to a small depth so that an
/// app label stored as a reference (as `aapt2` often emits) still resolves to
/// real text. The default configuration is preferred.
pub fn resolve(table: &ResTable, res_id: u32) -> Option<String> {
    let mut id = res_id;
    for _ in 0..16 {
        let value = lookup_once(table, id)?;
        if let Some(hex) = value.strip_prefix("@0x") {
            match u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16) {
                Ok(next) if next != id => {
                    id = next;
                    continue;
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        return Some(value);
    }
    None
}

/// Best-effort resolution of an application label.
///
/// Without the manifest (this module deliberately has no AXML dependency) the
/// exact resource id is unknown, so we look for the conventional label keys
/// in `string`-typed resources, following references. Returns `None` when no
/// plausible label is found.
pub fn app_label(table: &ResTable) -> Option<String> {
    const KEYS: &[&str] = &[
        "app_name",
        "app_label",
        "application_name",
        "application_label",
        "appname",
        "label",
    ];

    // Pass 1: conventional keys on `string`-typed resources.
    for key in KEYS {
        for pkg in &table.packages {
            for ty in &pkg.types {
                if ty.name != "string" {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(v) = find_key_in_type(table, pkg, ty, key) {
                    return Some(v);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Pass 2: any resource type.
    for key in KEYS {
        for pkg in &table.packages {
            for ty in &pkg.types {
                if let Some(v) = find_key_in_type(table, pkg, ty, key) {
                    return Some(v);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    None
}

fn find_key_in_type(table: &ResTable, pkg: &Package, ty: &ResType, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    // Default config first, then the rest.
    let mut configs: Vec<&ResConfig> = ty.configs.iter().collect();
    configs.sort_by_key(|c| if c.config == "default" { 0 } else { 1 });
    for cfg in configs {
        for entry in cfg.entries.iter().flatten() {
            if entry.key == key {
                let id = make_id(pkg.id, ty.id, entry.id);
                if let Some(v) = resolve(table, id) {
                    if !v.is_empty() && !v.starts_with('@') && v != "complex" {
                        return Some(v);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Read;

    fn load_arsc() -> Vec<u8> {
        let f = std::fs::File::open("testdata/test-app.apk").expect("open test apk");
        let mut zip = zip::ZipArchive::new(f).expect("valid apk zip");
        let mut entry = zip.by_name("resources.arsc").expect("resources.arsc");
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        entry.read_to_end(&mut buf).expect("read arsc");
        buf
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_real_table() {
        let data = load_arsc();
        let table = decode(&data).expect("decode resources.arsc");

        assert!(!table.packages.is_empty(), "expected at least one package");
        assert!(
            table.global_strings.len() > 1000,
            "global pool looks too small: {}",
            table.global_strings.len()
        );

        let pkg = &table.packages[0];
        assert_eq!(pkg.id, 0x7f, "app package id");
        assert_eq!(pkg.name, "org.fdroid.fdroid");
        assert!(!pkg.types.is_empty());

        // The `string` type must exist and contain resolvable values.
        let strings = pkg
            .types
            .iter()
            .find(|t| t.name == "string")
            .expect("string type");
        assert!(strings.id > 0);

        // Find any non-complex entry with a literal string value and confirm
        // that `resolve` returns it.
        let mut resolved = 0usize;
        for cfg in &strings.configs {
            for entry in cfg.entries.iter().flatten() {
                if entry.is_complex || entry.value.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                let id = make_id(pkg.id, strings.id, entry.id);
                let got = resolve(&table, id);
                assert!(got.is_some(), "resolve failed for 0x{id:08x}");
                resolved += 1;
            }
        }
        assert!(resolved > 0, "expected at least one resolvable string");
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolves_app_label() {
        let table = decode(&load_arsc()).expect("decode");
        let label = app_label(&table);
        assert_eq!(label.as_deref(), Some("Test App"), "app label: {label:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_follows_reference() {
        let table = decode(&load_arsc()).expect("decode");
        // Resolve the `app_name` entry's id from the table itself (type 1 =
        // "string") and follow it — mirrors how a manifest label reference
        // resolves on a real app.
        let pkg = &table.packages[0];
        let strings_ty = pkg
            .types
            .iter()
            .find(|t| t.name == "string")
            .expect("string type");
        let app_name = strings_ty
            .configs
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|c| c.entries.iter().flatten())
            .find(|e| e.key == "app_name")
            .expect("app_name entry");
        let id = make_id(pkg.id, strings_ty.id, app_name.id);
        let v = resolve(&table, id);
        assert_eq!(v.as_deref(), Some("Test App"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_unknown_id_is_none() {
        let table = decode(&load_arsc()).expect("decode");
        assert_eq!(resolve(&table, 0xdead_beef), None);
        assert_eq!(resolve(&table, 0), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn utf8_pool_roundtrip() {
        // Build a one-string UTF-8 pool: "hi" (2 chars, 2 bytes).
        // header(28) + one offset(4) = data at 32.
        let mut d = vec![0u8; 28 + 4 + 4];
        // type = 0x0001, header_size = 28, size = 36
        d[0..2].copy_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
        d[2..4].copy_from_slice(&28u16.to_le_bytes());
        d[4..8].copy_from_slice(&36u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[8..12].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes()); // stringCount
        d[12..16].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // styleCount
        d[16..20].copy_from_slice(&UTF8_FLAG.to_le_bytes()); // flags
        d[20..24].copy_from_slice(&32u32.to_le_bytes()); // stringsStart
        d[24..28].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // stylesStart
        d[28..32].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // offset[0] = 0
        d[32] = 2; // char count
        d[33] = 2; // byte count
        d[34] = b'h';
        d[35] = b'i';

        let pool = parse_string_pool(&d, 0).expect("pool");
        assert_eq!(pool, vec!["hi".to_string()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn utf16_pool_roundtrip() {
        let mut d = vec![0u8; 28 + 4 + 8];
        d[0..2].copy_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
        d[2..4].copy_from_slice(&28u16.to_le_bytes());
        d[4..8].copy_from_slice(&40u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[8..12].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[16..20].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // flags = 0 (UTF-16)
        d[20..24].copy_from_slice(&32u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[28..32].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
        d[32..34].copy_from_slice(&2u16.to_le_bytes()); // len
        d[34..36].copy_from_slice(&(b'o' as u16).to_le_bytes());
        d[36..38].copy_from_slice(&(b'k' as u16).to_le_bytes());
        d[38..40].copy_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // NUL

        let pool = parse_string_pool(&d, 0).expect("pool");
        assert_eq!(pool, vec!["ok".to_string()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn render_config_default_and_locale() {
        assert_eq!(render_config(&[]), "default");
        assert_eq!(render_config(&[0u8; 4]), "default");

        // size=64, language "en" with no other fields set.
        let mut cfg = vec![0u8; 64];
        cfg[0] = 64;
        cfg[8] = b'e';
        cfg[9] = b'n';
        assert_eq!(render_config(&cfg), "en");
    }

    #[test]
    fn render_config_night_and_density() {
        let mut cfg = vec![0u8; 64];
        cfg[0] = 64;
        cfg[8] = b'e';
        cfg[9] = b'n';
        cfg[14] = 0xe0; // 480 -> xxhdpi (little-endian 0x01e0)
        cfg[15] = 0x01;
        cfg[29] = 0x20; // UI_MODE_NIGHT_YES
        let tag = render_config(&cfg);
        assert!(tag.contains("en"), "{tag}");
        assert!(tag.contains("night"), "{tag}");
        assert!(tag.contains("xxhdpi"), "{tag}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_garbage() {
        assert!(decode(&[]).is_err());
        assert!(decode(&[0xff, 0xff, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]).is_err());
        // Wrong chunk type at the root.
        let mut d = [0u8; 16];
        d[0] = 0x99;
        assert!(decode(&d).is_err());
    }
}
```
