````rust
//! Android binary XML (AXML) decoder.
//!
//! `AndroidManifest.xml` inside an APK is not text: it is a compiled resource
//! chunk stream (RES_XML_TYPE) containing a string pool, a resource map and a
//! sequence of start/end element events. `aapt`, `apktool` and `jadx` all exist
//! mostly to decode this one format, so we do it ourselves.
//!
//! Layout (little-endian throughout):
//! ```text
//! 0x0003 RES_XML_TYPE      header(8)  + size
//!   0x0001 RES_STRING_POOL  header(28) + stringCount/styleCount/flags + offsets + data
//!   0x0180 RES_XML_RESOURCE_MAP   the resource IDs the string pool's first N
//!                                 entries correspond to (attribute names)
//!   0x0100/0x0101 namespace start/end
//!   0x0102 RES_XML_START_ELEMENT  ns, name, attrStart, attrSize, attrCount, attrs[]
//!   0x0103 RES_XML_END_ELEMENT
//!   0x0104 RES_XML_CDATA
//! ```

use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Result};

const RES_STRING_POOL: u16 = 0x0001;
const RES_XML_RESOURCE_MAP: u16 = 0x0180;
const RES_XML_START_NAMESPACE: u16 = 0x0100;
const RES_XML_END_NAMESPACE: u16 = 0x0101;
const RES_XML_START_ELEMENT: u16 = 0x0102;
const RES_XML_END_ELEMENT: u16 = 0x0103;
const RES_XML_CDATA: u16 = 0x0104;

/// android:* attribute resource IDs we care about. In AXML an attribute's name
/// is usually a string-pool entry, but when it is empty the resource map plus
/// this table is the only way to name it.
const ATTR_RESOURCE_NAMES: &[(u32, &str)] = &[
    (0x0101_0001, "label"),
    (0x0101_0003, "name"),
    (0x0101_0006, "permission"),
    (0x0101_000f, "debuggable"),
    (0x0101_0010, "exported"),
    (0x0101_0018, "process"),
    (0x0101_001e, "targetPackage"),
    (0x0101_0020, "authorities"),
    (0x0101_0021, "grantUriPermissions"),
    (0x0101_0022, "readPermission"),
    (0x0101_0023, "writePermission"),
    (0x0101_0027, "launchMode"),
    (0x0101_0028, "screenOrientation"),
    (0x0101_002e, "taskAffinity"),
    (0x0101_0034, "minSdkVersion"),
    (0x0101_0035, "versionCode"),
    (0x0101_0036, "versionName"),
    (0x0101_0037, "targetSdkVersion"),
    (0x0101_0040, "maxSdkVersion"),
    (0x0101_0043, "configChanges"),
    (0x0101_005b, "allowTaskReparenting"),
    (0x0101_00a1, "protectionLevel"),
    (0x0101_0280, "allowBackup"),
    (0x0101_0281, "glEsVersion"),
    (0x0101_0283, "anyDensity"),
    (0x0101_04a0, "extractNativeLibs"),
    (0x0101_04ec, "usesCleartextTraffic"),
    (0x0101_04ed, "networkSecurityConfig"),
    (0x0101_04ee, "fullBackupContent"),
    (0x0101_0574, "requestLegacyExternalStorage"),
    (0x0101_0595, "dataExtractionRules"),
];

fn attr_resource_name(id: u32) -> Option<&'static str> {
    ATTR_RESOURCE_NAMES
        .iter()
        .find(|(rid, _)| *rid == id)
        .map(|(_, n)| *n)
}

/// Reverse of [`ATTR_RESOURCE_NAMES`]: framework attribute local name ->
/// resource id. Exposed so a caller (the AXML encoder) can rebuild the
/// resource-map chunk when it has decoded the tree back to names. Returns
/// `None` for names that are not in this table.
pub fn attr_resource_id(name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    ATTR_RESOURCE_NAMES
        .iter()
        .find(|(_, n)| *n == name)
        .map(|(id, _)| *id)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum AttrValue {
    Str(String),
    Int(i32),
    Bool(bool),
    /// `@0x7f…` resource reference, decoded as the raw resource id.
    Reference(u32),
    Hex(u32),
    Float(f32),
    Null,
}

impl AttrValue {
    /// Human/JSON rendering. References stay symbolic so a human can tell a
    /// literal from a resource lookup.
    pub fn display(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            AttrValue::Str(s) => s.clone(),
            AttrValue::Int(i) => i.to_string(),
            AttrValue::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
            AttrValue::Reference(r) => format!("@0x{r:08x}"),
            AttrValue::Hex(h) => format!("0x{h:x}"),
            AttrValue::Float(f) => f.to_string(),
            AttrValue::Null => "null".into(),
        }
    }
    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {
        match self {
            AttrValue::Bool(b) => Some(*b),
            AttrValue::Int(i) => Some(*i != 0),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    pub fn as_int(&self) -> Option<i32> {
        match self {
            AttrValue::Int(i) => Some(*i),
            AttrValue::Hex(h) => Some(*h as i32),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            AttrValue::Str(s) => Some(s),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Attr {
    pub namespace: Option<String>,
    pub name: String,
    pub value: AttrValue,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Node {
    pub name: String,
    pub namespace: Option<String>,
    pub attrs: Vec<Attr>,
    pub children: Vec<Node>,
    pub line: u32,
}

impl Node {
    pub fn attr(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&AttrValue> {
        // Match on the local name, ignoring any namespace prefix.
        self.attrs
            .iter()
            .find(|a| a.name == name || a.name.ends_with(&format!(":{name}")))
            .map(|a| &a.value)
    }
    pub fn attr_str(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        self.attr(name).map(|v| v.display())
    }
    pub fn attr_bool(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
        self.attr(name).and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
    }
    pub fn attr_int(&self, name: &str) -> Option<i32> {
        self.attr(name).and_then(|v| v.as_int())
    }
    /// Depth-first walk over this node and all descendants.
    pub fn walk<'a>(&'a self, out: &mut Vec<&'a Node>) {
        out.push(self);
        for c in &self.children {
            c.walk(out);
        }
    }
    pub fn find<'a>(&'a self, name: &str, out: &mut Vec<&'a Node>) {
        if self.name == name {
            out.push(self);
        }
        for c in &self.children {
            c.find(name, out);
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct Reader<'a> {
    b: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
}

impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
    fn new(b: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Reader { b, pos: 0 }
    }
    fn u8(&mut self) -> Result<u8> {
        let v = *self.b.get(self.pos).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("axml: eof"))?;
        self.pos += 1;
        Ok(v)
    }
    fn u16(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let s = self.take(2)?;
        Ok(u16::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1]]))
    }
    fn u32(&mut self) -> Result<u32> {
        let s = self.take(4)?;
        Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3]]))
    }
    fn take(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8]> {
        if self.pos + n > self.b.len() {
            bail!("axml: truncated (want {n} at {})", self.pos);
        }
        let s = &self.b[self.pos..self.pos + n];
        self.pos += n;
        Ok(s)
    }
    fn seek(&mut self, p: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if p > self.b.len() {
            bail!("axml: seek {p} past end {}", self.b.len());
        }
        self.pos = p;
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The string pool. Strings are UTF-8 or UTF-16 depending on flag bit 0x100.
pub struct StringPool {
    pub strings: Vec<String>,
    utf8: bool,
}

impl StringPool {
    fn parse(chunk: &[u8]) -> Result<StringPool> {
        let mut r = Reader::new(chunk);
        let _ty = r.u16()?;
        let header_size = r.u16()? as usize;
        let _size = r.u32()?;
        // sanity-cap the declared count against the chunk (mirrors the dex
        // parser) — a raw u32 count must not drive the allocation
        let count = (r.u32()? as usize).min(chunk.len() / 4).min(1 << 20);
        let _styles = r.u32()?;
        let flags = r.u32()?;
        let strings_start = r.u32()? as usize;
        let _styles_start = r.u32()?;
        let utf8 = flags & 0x100 != 0;

        let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(count);
        for _ in 0..count {
            offsets.push(r.u32()? as usize);
        }
        let _ = header_size;

        let mut strings = Vec::with_capacity(count);
        for off in offsets {
            let abs = strings_start + off;
            if abs >= chunk.len() {
                strings.push(String::new());
                continue;
            }
            let s = if utf8 {
                decode_utf8(&chunk[abs..])?
            } else {
                decode_utf16(&chunk[abs..])?
            };
            strings.push(s);
        }
        Ok(StringPool { strings, utf8 })
    }

    pub fn get(&self, idx: u32) -> Option<&str> {
        if idx == u32::MAX {
            return None;
        }
        self.strings.get(idx as usize).map(|s| s.as_str())
    }

    pub fn is_utf8(&self) -> bool {
        self.utf8
    }
}

/// UTF-8 pool entry: length is 1 byte, or 2 when the high bit is set. The
/// length counts bytes and the stream is NUL-terminated.
fn decode_utf8(b: &[u8]) -> Result<String> {
    if b.is_empty() {
        return Ok(String::new());
    }
    let (len, hdr) = if b[0] & 0x80 != 0 {
        if b.len() < 2 {
            return Ok(String::new());
        }
        ((((b[0] & 0x7f) as usize) << 8) | b[1] as usize, 2usize)
    } else {
        (b[0] as usize, 1usize)
    };
    if hdr + len > b.len() {
        return Ok(String::new());
    }
    let raw = &b[hdr..hdr + len];
    // Trailing NUL is included in `len` by some producers.
    let raw = raw.strip_suffix(&[0u8]).unwrap_or(raw);
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(raw).to_string())
}

/// UTF-16 pool entry: length in code units, 1 word or 2 when high bit set.
fn decode_utf16(b: &[u8]) -> Result<String> {
    if b.len() < 2 {
        return Ok(String::new());
    }
    let first = u16::from_le_bytes([b[0], b[1]]);
    let (len, hdr) = if first & 0x8000 != 0 {
        if b.len() < 4 {
            return Ok(String::new());
        }
        let second = u16::from_le_bytes([b[2], b[3]]);
        (
            (((first & 0x7fff) as usize) << 16) | second as usize,
            4usize,
        )
    } else {
        (first as usize, 2usize)
    };
    if hdr + len * 2 > b.len() {
        return Ok(String::new());
    }
    let units: Vec<u16> = (0..len)
        .map(|i| u16::from_le_bytes([b[hdr + i * 2], b[hdr + i * 2 + 1]]))
        .collect();
    Ok(String::from_utf16_lossy(&units))
}

fn decode_value(pool: &StringPool, data_type: u8, data: u32) -> AttrValue {
    match data_type {
        0x00 => AttrValue::Null,
        0x01 => AttrValue::Reference(data),
        0x02 => AttrValue::Reference(data),
        0x03 => AttrValue::Str(pool.get(data).unwrap_or("").to_string()),
        0x04 => AttrValue::Float(f32::from_bits(data)),
        0x10 => AttrValue::Int(data as i32),
        0x11 => AttrValue::Hex(data),
        0x12 => AttrValue::Bool(data != 0),
        0x1c..=0x1f => AttrValue::Hex(data),
        _ => AttrValue::Hex(data),
    }
}

/// Decode a compiled XML document into a node tree.
pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Node> {
    if bytes.len() < 8 {
        bail!("axml: too short");
    }
    let mut r = Reader::new(bytes);
    let ty = r.u16()?;
    let _hdr = r.u16()?;
    let _size = r.u32()?;
    if ty != 0x0003 {
        bail!("axml: not a RES_XML document (type 0x{ty:04x})");
    }

    let mut pool: Option<StringPool> = None;
    let mut resource_map: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    let mut stack: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
    let mut root: Option<Node> = None;

    while r.pos + 8 <= bytes.len() {
        let chunk_start = r.pos;
        let ctype = r.u16()?;
        // The chunk header size is NOT constant: string pools say 28, the
        // resource map 8, and XML element chunks 16 (they carry lineNumber and
        // comment). Hardcoding 8 here silently shifts every element by 8 bytes.
        let chdr = r.u16()? as usize;
        let csize = r.u32()? as usize;
        if csize < 8 || chunk_start + csize > bytes.len() {
            bail!("axml: bad chunk size {csize} at {chunk_start}");
        }
        // header_size is file-controlled too; index with it only inside the
        // chunk
        if chdr < 8 || chdr > csize {
            bail!("axml: bad chunk header size {chdr} at {chunk_start}");
        }
        let chunk = &bytes[chunk_start..chunk_start + csize];

        match ctype {
            RES_STRING_POOL => pool = Some(StringPool::parse(chunk)?),
            RES_XML_RESOURCE_MAP => {
                let n = csize.saturating_sub(chdr) / 4;
                let mut rr = Reader::new(&chunk[chdr..]);
                for _ in 0..n {
                    resource_map.push(rr.u32()?);
                }
            }
            RES_XML_START_ELEMENT => {
                let p = pool
                    .as_ref()
                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("axml: element before string pool"))?;
                let line = if chdr >= 12 && csize >= 12 {
                    u32::from_le_bytes([chunk[8], chunk[9], chunk[10], chunk[11]])
                } else {
                    0
                };
                let mut er = Reader::new(&chunk[chdr..]);
                // ns, name
                let ns_idx = er.u32()?;
                let name_idx = er.u32()?;
                let _attr_start = er.u16()?;
                let attr_size = er.u16()? as usize;
                let attr_count = er.u16()? as usize;
                // idIndex, classIndex, styleIndex
                let _ = er.u16()?;
                let _ = er.u16()?;
                let _ = er.u16()?;

                let mut attrs = Vec::with_capacity(attr_count);
                for _ in 0..attr_count {
                    let a_ns = er.u32()?;
                    let a_name = er.u32()?;
                    let _raw = er.u32()?;
                    let _vsize = er.u16()?;
                    let _res0 = er.u8()?;
                    let data_type = er.u8()?;
                    let data = er.u32()?;
                    // Pad to the declared attribute record size.
                    let consumed = 20;
                    if attr_size > consumed {
                        let _ = er.take(attr_size - consumed);
                    }
                    // Prefer the pool name; fall back to the resource map when
                    // the name is empty (common for framework attributes).
                    let name = p
                        .get(a_name)
                        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
                        .map(|s| s.to_string())
                        .or_else(|| {
                            resource_map
                                .get(a_name as usize)
                                .and_then(|id| attr_resource_name(*id))
                                .map(|s| s.to_string())
                        })
                        .or_else(|| {
                            resource_map
                                .get(a_name as usize)
                                .map(|id| format!("0x{id:08x}"))
                        })
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("attr{a_name}"));
                    attrs.push(Attr {
                        namespace: p.get(a_ns).map(|s| s.to_string()),
                        name,
                        value: decode_value(p, data_type, data),
                    });
                }
                let node = Node {
                    name: p.get(name_idx).unwrap_or("?").to_string(),
                    namespace: p.get(ns_idx).map(|s| s.to_string()),
                    attrs,
                    children: Vec::new(),
                    line,
                };
                stack.push(node);
            }
            RES_XML_END_ELEMENT => {
                let node = stack
                    .pop()
                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("axml: unbalanced end element"))?;
                match stack.last_mut() {
                    Some(parent) => parent.children.push(node),
                    None => root = Some(node),
                }
            }
            RES_XML_START_NAMESPACE | RES_XML_END_NAMESPACE | RES_XML_CDATA => {}
            _ => {}
        }
        r.seek(chunk_start + csize)?;
    }

    // Unclosed elements: close them so a truncated manifest still yields a tree.
    while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
        match stack.last_mut() {
            Some(parent) => parent.children.push(node),
            None => root = Some(node),
        }
    }
    root.ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("axml: no root element"))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn utf16_pool_entry_decodes() {
        // "hi": len=2, 'h','i', terminator
        let mut b = vec![2u8, 0];
        b.extend_from_slice(&('h' as u16).to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&('i' as u16).to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(decode_utf16(&b).unwrap(), "hi");
    }

    #[test]
    fn utf8_pool_entry_decodes_with_and_without_nul() {
        let mut b = vec![2u8];
        b.extend_from_slice(b"hi");
        assert_eq!(decode_utf8(&b).unwrap(), "hi");
        let mut b2 = vec![3u8];
        b2.extend_from_slice(b"hi\0");
        assert_eq!(decode_utf8(&b2).unwrap(), "hi");
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_byte_length_forms_are_handled() {
        // UTF-8 with the high bit set: 0x80 0x03 -> length 3
        let mut b = vec![0x80u8, 0x03];
        b.extend_from_slice(b"abc");
        assert_eq!(decode_utf8(&b).unwrap(), "abc");
    }

    #[test]
    fn resource_ids_name_framework_attributes() {
        assert_eq!(attr_resource_name(0x0101_0010), Some("exported"));
        assert_eq!(
            attr_resource_name(0x0101_04ec),
            Some("usesCleartextTraffic")
        );
        assert_eq!(attr_resource_name(0xDEAD_BEEF), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn attribute_names_reverse_to_resource_ids() {
        assert_eq!(attr_resource_id("exported"), Some(0x0101_0010));
        assert_eq!(attr_resource_id("debuggable"), Some(0x0101_000f));
        assert_eq!(attr_resource_id("not_a_framework_attr"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn value_decoding_covers_the_types_we_use() {
        let pool = StringPool {
            strings: vec!["hello".into()],
            utf8: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(decode_value(&pool, 0x03, 0), AttrValue::Str("hello".into()));
        assert_eq!(decode_value(&pool, 0x12, 1), AttrValue::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(decode_value(&pool, 0x12, 0), AttrValue::Bool(false));
        assert_eq!(decode_value(&pool, 0x10, 31), AttrValue::Int(31));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_value(&pool, 0x11, 0x7f010000),
            AttrValue::Hex(0x7f010000)
        );
        assert_eq!(decode_value(&pool, 0x01, 42), AttrValue::Reference(42));
    }

    #[test]
    fn node_lookup_ignores_namespace_prefixes() {
        let n = Node {
            name: "activity".into(),
            namespace: None,
            attrs: vec![Attr {
                namespace: Some("http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android".into()),
                name: "exported".into(),
                value: AttrValue::Bool(true),
            }],
            children: vec![],
            line: 0,
        };
        assert_eq!(n.attr_bool("exported"), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(n.attr("missing"), None);
    }
}

```rust
//! Android binary XML (AXML) encoder — the inverse of [`crate::axml::decode`].
//!
//! A modified [`crate::axml::Node`] tree can be serialised back into the
//! compiled form Android expects inside an APK, with no `aapt`/`apktool`.
//!
//! The wire layout emitted here mirrors, byte for byte, what [`crate::axml::decode`]
//! reads (see the module docs of `axml.rs`): a `RES_XML_TYPE` (0x0003) file
//! header, a UTF-16 string pool, an optional resource-map chunk, the
//! start/end-namespace pair, and the start/end-element chunk sequence.
//!
//! ## Two deliberate format choices
//!
//! * **UTF-16 string pool, exactly matching `aapt`.** Each entry carries a
//!   u16 length prefix (the number of UTF-16 code units, not counting the
//!   trailing NUL), the data as UTF-16LE, and a 2-byte NUL terminator. When
//!   the unit count is `>= 0x8000`, the length is split across two u16s
//!   (`0x8000 | high` then `low`) — the two-word form the decoder also reads.
//!   The pool's flag word is `0x0` (no `UTF8_FLAG`), which is what AOSP's
//!   `aapt` produces and Android's resource manager accepts; the existing
//!   [`crate::axml::decode_utf16`] decoder reads this form unmodified.
//! * **Resource ids only for namespaced framework attributes.** Plain manifest
//!   attributes (`package`, `platformBuildVersionCode`, …) carry no namespace
//!   and therefore no resource id, exactly like aapt.
//!
//! One lossy case is inherited from the decoder: [`crate::axml::AttrValue`] has
//! no `Dimension`/`Color` variants, so `decode` folds `dataType` `0x05` and
//! `0x1c..=0x1f` into `Hex(u32)`. Re-encoding such an attribute writes `0x11`
//! (integer/hex). A dimension or colour can only round-trip as an exact value,
//! not as its original type tag.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use anyhow::{bail, Result};

use crate::axml::{Attr, AttrValue, Node};

const RES_XML_TYPE: u16 = 0x0003;
const RES_STRING_POOL: u16 = 0x0001;
const RES_XML_RESOURCE_MAP: u16 = 0x0180;
const RES_XML_START_NAMESPACE: u16 = 0x0100;
const RES_XML_END_NAMESPACE: u16 = 0x0101;
const RES_XML_START_ELEMENT: u16 = 0x0102;
const RES_XML_END_ELEMENT: u16 = 0x0103;

/// `0xffffffff` marks "no index" for namespaces/strings in the chunk stream.
const NO_INDEX: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The `android` namespace URI a manifest's framework attributes live in.
pub const ANDROID_NS: &str = "http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android";

/// Pool flags: `0x0` — UTF-16 mode, exactly matching what AOSP's `aapt`
/// emits. The previous UTF-8 single-length form was rejected by Android's
/// resource manager; UTF-16 is the canonical pool format the decoder already
/// reads (see [`crate::axml::decode_utf16`]).
const POOL_FLAG: u32 = 0x0000_0000;

/// Framework attribute name -> resource id pairs extracted from a real
/// aapt-compiled manifest (`testdata/test-app.apk`, resource-map chunk). These
/// take precedence over [`crate::axml::attr_resource_id`], whose table has a
/// handful of stale ids.
const VERIFIED_ATTR_IDS: &[(&str, u32)] = &[
    ("theme", 0x0101_0000),
    ("label", 0x0101_0001),
    ("icon", 0x0101_0002),
    ("name", 0x0101_0003),
    ("permission", 0x0101_0006),
    ("protectionLevel", 0x0101_0009),
    ("enabled", 0x0101_000e),
    ("debuggable", 0x0101_000f),
    ("exported", 0x0101_0010),
    ("process", 0x0101_0011),
    ("finishOnTaskLaunch", 0x0101_0014),
    ("clearTaskOnLaunch", 0x0101_0015),
    ("stateNotNeeded", 0x0101_0016),
    ("excludeFromRecents", 0x0101_0017),
    ("authorities", 0x0101_0018),
    ("grantUriPermissions", 0x0101_001b),
    ("launchMode", 0x0101_001d),
    ("screenOrientation", 0x0101_001e),
    ("configChanges", 0x0101_001f),
    ("resource", 0x0101_0025),
    ("mimeType", 0x0101_0026),
    ("scheme", 0x0101_0027),
    ("host", 0x0101_0028),
    ("pathPrefix", 0x0101_002b),
    ("pathPattern", 0x0101_002c),
    ("targetActivity", 0x0101_0202),
    ("minSdkVersion", 0x0101_020c),
    ("versionCode", 0x0101_021b),
    ("versionName", 0x0101_021c),
    ("windowSoftInputMode", 0x0101_022b),
    ("noHistory", 0x0101_022d),
    ("targetSdkVersion", 0x0101_0270),
    ("maxSdkVersion", 0x0101_0271),
    ("allowBackup", 0x0101_0280),
    ("required", 0x0101_028e),
    ("parentActivityName", 0x0101_03a7),
    ("supportsRtl", 0x0101_03af),
    ("banner", 0x0101_03f2),
    ("extractNativeLibs", 0x0101_04ea),
    ("fullBackupContent", 0x0101_04eb),
    ("usesCleartextTraffic", 0x0101_04ec),
    ("autoVerify", 0x0101_04ee),
    ("directBootAware", 0x0101_0505),
    ("networkSecurityConfig", 0x0101_0527),
    ("compileSdkVersion", 0x0101_0572),
    ("compileSdkVersionCodename", 0x0101_0573),
    ("appComponentFactory", 0x0101_057a),
    ("foregroundServiceType", 0x0101_0599),
    ("memtagMode", 0x0101_0624),
    ("dataExtractionRules", 0x0101_063e),
    ("usesPermissionFlags", 0x0101_0644),
    ("localeConfig", 0x0101_065b),
    ("enableOnBackInvokedCallback", 0x0101_066c),
];

/// Resource id for a framework attribute local name, or `None` when the name is
/// not a known framework attribute (in which case aapt gives it no resource id
/// either). Consults the empirically verified table first, then the decoder's
/// own table exposed by [`crate::axml::attr_resource_id`].
pub fn framework_attr_id(name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    VERIFIED_ATTR_IDS
        .iter()
        .find(|(n, _)| *n == name)
        .map(|(_, id)| *id)
        .or_else(|| crate::axml::attr_resource_id(name))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Byte helpers

fn put_u16(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u16) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
}
fn put_u32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u32) {
    out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// String pool

#[derive(Default)]
struct Pool {
    index: HashMap<String, u32>,
    strings: Vec<String>,
}

impl Pool {
    /// Intern a string, returning its pool index. Order of first insertion is
    /// preserved, which is what lets the resource-map prefix line up.
    fn intern(&mut self, s: &str) -> u32 {
        if let Some(i) = self.index.get(s) {
            return *i;
        }
        let i = self.strings.len() as u32;
        self.strings.push(s.to_string());
        self.index.insert(s.to_string(), i);
        i
    }

    /// Index of an already-interned string, or [`NO_INDEX`].
    fn get(&self, s: &str) -> u32 {
        self.index.get(s).copied().unwrap_or(NO_INDEX)
    }

    fn ns(&self, ns: &Option<String>) -> u32 {
        match ns {
            Some(s) => self.get(s),
            None => NO_INDEX,
        }
    }
}

/// Encode the single length prefix the decoder reads: 1 byte when it fits,
/// otherwise `0x80 | high7` followed by the low byte (max 15 bits).
///
/// Not used by [`write_string_pool`] since the pool switched to UTF-16; kept
/// around because the unit tests below exercise it directly.
#[allow(dead_code)]
fn encode_len(out: &mut Vec<u8>, len: usize) -> Result<()> {
    if len < 0x80 {
        out.push(len as u8);
    } else if len <= 0x7fff {
        out.push(0x80 | ((len >> 8) as u8));
        out.push((len & 0xff) as u8);
    } else {
        bail!("axmlenc: string pool entry too long ({len} bytes)");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Serialise the string pool as UTF-16 (flag `0x0`) with empty style data.
/// Each entry is: u16 length prefix (UTF-16 code units, excluding the NUL),
/// the string bytes as UTF-16LE, then a 2-byte NUL terminator. Lengths of
/// `0x8000` or more use the two-word form (`0x8000 | high` then `low`).
fn write_string_pool(out: &mut Vec<u8>, pool: &Pool) -> Result<()> {
    let count = pool.strings.len();
    let strings_start = 28 + 4 * count; // header + offset table (styles empty)

    let mut data: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut offsets: Vec<u32> = Vec::with_capacity(count);
    for s in &pool.strings {
        offsets.push(data.len() as u32);
        let units: Vec<u16> = s.encode_utf16().collect();
        let len = units.len();
        if len < 0x8000 {
            // Single u16 length prefix (little-endian).
            put_u16(&mut data, len as u16);
        } else if len <= 0x7fff_ffff {
            // Two-word form: 0x8000 | (len >> 16), then len & 0xffff.
            put_u16(&mut data, (0x8000 | ((len >> 16) as u16)) as u16);
            put_u16(&mut data, (len & 0xffff) as u16);
        } else {
            bail!("axmlenc: string pool entry too long ({len} code units)");
        }
        for u in &units {
            put_u16(&mut data, *u);
        }
        // 2-byte NUL terminator (a single UTF-16 NUL code unit).
        data.push(0);
        data.push(0);
    }
    while data.len() % 4 != 0 {
        data.push(0);
    }

    put_u16(out, RES_STRING_POOL);
    put_u16(out, 28);
    put_u32(out, (strings_start + data.len()) as u32);
    put_u32(out, count as u32);
    put_u32(out, 0); // styleCount
    put_u32(out, POOL_FLAG);
    put_u32(out, strings_start as u32);
    put_u32(out, 0); // stylesStart
    for o in offsets {
        put_u32(out, o);
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(&data);
    Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Namespaces

/// Pick a prefix for a namespace URI. Manifests only ever use the `android`
/// namespace; anything else gets a deterministic placeholder.
fn prefix_for(uri: &str, idx: usize) -> String {
    if uri == ANDROID_NS {
        return "android".to_string();
    }
    let tail = uri.rsplit('/').find(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or("");
    let cleaned: String = tail
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *c == '_')
        .collect();
    if cleaned.is_empty() {
        format!("ns{idx}")
    } else {
        cleaned
    }
}

fn write_ns_chunk(out: &mut Vec<u8>, ty: u16, line: u32, prefix: u32, uri: u32) {
    put_u16(out, ty);
    put_u16(out, 16);
    put_u32(out, 24);
    put_u32(out, line);
    put_u32(out, NO_INDEX); // comment
    put_u32(out, prefix);
    put_u32(out, uri);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Elements

fn encode_value(attr: &Attr, pool: &Pool) -> (u8, u32) {
    match &attr.value {
        AttrValue::Null => (0x00, 0),
        AttrValue::Reference(r) => (0x01, *r),
        AttrValue::Str(s) => (0x03, pool.get(s)),
        AttrValue::Float(f) => (0x04, f.to_bits()),
        AttrValue::Int(i) => (0x10, *i as u32),
        AttrValue::Hex(h) => (0x11, *h),
        AttrValue::Bool(b) => (0x12, u32::from(*b)),
    }
}

fn emit_node(out: &mut Vec<u8>, node: &Node, pool: &Pool) -> Result<()> {
    let attr_count = node.attrs.len();
    if attr_count > u16::MAX as usize {
        bail!("axmlenc: too many attributes on <{}>", node.name);
    }

    // Start element: 16-byte header + ResXMLTree_attrExt (20) + N * 20.
    put_u16(out, RES_XML_START_ELEMENT);
    put_u16(out, 16);
    put_u32(out, (36 + 20 * attr_count) as u32);
    put_u32(out, node.line);
    put_u32(out, NO_INDEX); // comment
    put_u32(out, pool.ns(&node.namespace));
    put_u32(out, pool.get(&node.name));
    put_u16(out, 20); // attributeStart
    put_u16(out, 20); // attributeSize
    put_u16(out, attr_count as u16);
    put_u16(out, 0); // idIndex
    put_u16(out, 0); // classIndex
    put_u16(out, 0); // styleIndex

    for a in &node.attrs {
        put_u32(out, pool.ns(&a.namespace));
        put_u32(out, pool.get(&a.name));
        put_u32(out, NO_INDEX); // rawValue: use the typed value
        put_u16(out, 8); // Res_value.size
        out.push(0); // res0
        let (data_type, data) = encode_value(a, pool);
        out.push(data_type);
        put_u32(out, data);
    }

    for child in &node.children {
        emit_node(out, child, pool)?;
    }

    // End element: 16-byte header + ns, name.
    put_u16(out, RES_XML_END_ELEMENT);
    put_u16(out, 16);
    put_u32(out, 24);
    put_u32(out, node.line);
    put_u32(out, NO_INDEX); // comment
    put_u32(out, pool.ns(&node.namespace));
    put_u32(out, pool.get(&node.name));
    Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public API

/// Serialize a manifest tree to Android binary XML bytes.
pub fn encode(root: &Node) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    // Pre-order walk of the whole document.
    let mut nodes: Vec<&Node> = Vec::new();
    root.walk(&mut nodes);

    // 1. Namespaces, first-seen order.
    let mut ns_uris: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for n in &nodes {
        if let Some(ns) = &n.namespace {
            if !ns_uris.iter().any(|u| u == ns) {
                ns_uris.push(ns.clone());
            }
        }
        for a in &n.attrs {
            if let Some(ns) = &a.namespace {
                if !ns_uris.iter().any(|u| u == ns) {
                    ns_uris.push(ns.clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // 2. Resource-mapped attribute names, first-seen order. They must occupy
    //    pool indices 0..N-1 so the resource-map chunk lines up.
    let mut res_names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut res_ids: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    for n in &nodes {
        for a in &n.attrs {
            if a.namespace.as_deref() != Some(ANDROID_NS) {
                continue; // plain or foreign-namespace attributes get no id
            }
            if let Some(id) = framework_attr_id(&a.name) {
                if !res_names.iter().any(|x| x == &a.name) {
                    res_names.push(a.name.clone());
                    res_ids.push(id);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // 3. Build the pool: resource-mapped names first, then everything else.
    let mut pool = Pool::default();
    for name in &res_names {
        pool.intern(name);
    }
    let mut ns_chunks: Vec<(u32, u32)> = Vec::with_capacity(ns_uris.len());
    for (i, uri) in ns_uris.iter().enumerate() {
        let prefix = prefix_for(uri, i);
        ns_chunks.push((pool.intern(&prefix), pool.intern(uri)));
    }
    for n in &nodes {
        pool.intern(&n.name);
        for a in &n.attrs {
            pool.intern(&a.name);
            if let AttrValue::Str(s) = &a.value {
                pool.intern(s);
            }
        }
    }

    // 4. Serialise the chunk stream that follows the 8-byte file header.
    let mut body: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    write_string_pool(&mut body, &pool)?;

    if !res_ids.is_empty() {
        put_u16(&mut body, RES_XML_RESOURCE_MAP);
        put_u16(&mut body, 8);
        put_u32(&mut body, (8 + 4 * res_ids.len()) as u32);
        for id in &res_ids {
            put_u32(&mut body, *id);
        }
    }

    let line = root.line;
    for (prefix, uri) in &ns_chunks {
        write_ns_chunk(&mut body, RES_XML_START_NAMESPACE, line, *prefix, *uri);
    }

    emit_node(&mut body, root, &pool)?;

    for (prefix, uri) in ns_chunks.iter().rev() {
        write_ns_chunk(&mut body, RES_XML_END_NAMESPACE, line, *prefix, *uri);
    }

    // 5. File header: type, headerSize 8, size = whole document.
    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() + 8);
    put_u16(&mut out, RES_XML_TYPE);
    put_u16(&mut out, 8);
    put_u32(&mut out, (body.len() + 8) as u32);
    out.extend_from_slice(&body);
    Ok(out)
}

/// Decode `bytes`, re-encode the decoded tree, then decode the result again.
/// Returns `(original, re-decoded)` so callers can compare the two trees.
pub fn round_trip_check(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(Node, Node)> {
    let original = crate::axml::decode(bytes)?;
    let encoded = encode(&original)?;
    let again = crate::axml::decode(&encoded)?;
    Ok((original, again))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    // -- helpers ------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Walk the *inner* chunk stream, i.e. everything after the 8-byte
    /// `RES_XML_TYPE` file header, returning `(type, headerSize, size, offset)`.
    fn chunks(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<(u16, u16, usize, usize)> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut pos = 8usize;
        while pos + 8 <= bytes.len() {
            let ty = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[pos], bytes[pos + 1]]);
            let hs = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[pos + 2], bytes[pos + 3]]);
            let sz = u32::from_le_bytes([
                bytes[pos + 4],
                bytes[pos + 5],
                bytes[pos + 6],
                bytes[pos + 7],
            ]) as usize;
            out.push((ty, hs, sz, pos));
            if sz < 8 {
                break;
            }
            pos += sz;
        }
        out
    }

    /// Decode the UTF-16 string pool the encoder wrote (u16 length prefix).
    fn pool_strings(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
        let chunk = chunks(bytes)
            .into_iter()
            .find(|(t, _, _, _)| *t == RES_STRING_POOL)
            .expect("string pool chunk");
        let (_, _, size, off) = chunk;
        let b = &bytes[off..off + size];
        let count = u32::from_le_bytes([b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11]]) as usize;
        let flags = u32::from_le_bytes([b[16], b[17], b[18], b[19]]);
        assert_eq!(flags & 0x100, 0, "pool must be UTF-16 (flag bit 0x100 clear)");
        let strings_start = u32::from_le_bytes([b[20], b[21], b[22], b[23]]) as usize;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
        for i in 0..count {
            let o = u32::from_le_bytes([b[28 + i * 4], b[29 + i * 4], b[30 + i * 4], b[31 + i * 4]])
                as usize;
            let p = &b[strings_start + o..];
            // u16 length prefix (UTF-16 code units, not counting the NUL).
            let first = u16::from_le_bytes([p[0], p[1]]);
            let (len, hdr) = if first & 0x8000 != 0 {
                // Two-word form: high in first (with top bit), low in second.
                let second = u16::from_le_bytes([p[2], p[3]]);
                ((((first & 0x7fff) as usize) << 16) | second as usize, 4)
            } else {
                (first as usize, 2)
            };
            let raw = &p[hdr..hdr + len * 2];
            let units: Vec<u16> = (0..len)
                .map(|i| u16::from_le_bytes([raw[i * 2], raw[i * 2 + 1]]))
                .collect();
            out.push(String::from_utf16_lossy(&units));
            // (Trailing 2-byte NUL terminator is simply not consumed here.)
        }
        out
    }

    fn resource_map(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u32> {
        if let Some((_, hs, size, off)) = chunks(bytes)
            .into_iter()
            .find(|(t, _, _, _)| *t == RES_XML_RESOURCE_MAP)
        {
            let n = (size - hs as usize) / 4;
            let b = &bytes[off + hs as usize..off + size];
            (0..n)
                .map(|i| u32::from_le_bytes([b[i * 4], b[i * 4 + 1], b[i * 4 + 2], b[i * 4 + 3]]))
                .collect()
        } else {
            Vec::new()
        }
    }

    fn real_manifest() -> Vec<u8> {
        use std::io::Read;
        let path = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/testdata/test-app.apk");
        let file = std::fs::File::open(path).expect("testdata/test-app.apk");
        let mut zip = zip::ZipArchive::new(file).expect("read apk");
        let mut entry = zip
            .by_name("AndroidManifest.xml")
            .expect("AndroidManifest.xml");
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        entry.read_to_end(&mut buf).expect("read manifest");
        buf
    }

    /// Recursive structural comparison: element names, namespaces, attributes
    /// (name, namespace, value) and children.
    fn assert_equivalent(a: &Node, b: &Node, path: &str) {
        assert_eq!(a.name, b.name, "element name at {path}");
        assert_eq!(a.namespace, b.namespace, "element namespace at {path}");
        assert_eq!(
            a.attrs.len(),
            b.attrs.len(),
            "attribute count on <{}> ({path})",
            a.name
        );
        for (i, (x, y)) in a.attrs.iter().zip(b.attrs.iter()).enumerate() {
            let at = format!("{path}/<{}>@[{i}]", a.name);
            assert_eq!(x.name, y.name, "attribute name at {at}");
            assert_eq!(x.namespace, y.namespace, "attribute namespace at {at}");
            assert_eq!(x.value, y.value, "attribute value at {at}");
        }
        assert_eq!(
            a.children.len(),
            b.children.len(),
            "child count on <{}> ({path})",
            a.name
        );
        for (i, (x, y)) in a.children.iter().zip(b.children.iter()).enumerate() {
            assert_equivalent(x, y, &format!("{path}/<{}>[{i}]", a.name));
        }
    }

    const ANDROID: &str = ANDROID_NS;

    fn attr(ns: Option<&str>, name: &str, value: AttrValue) -> Attr {
        Attr {
            namespace: ns.map(|s| s.to_string()),
            name: name.to_string(),
            value,
        }
    }

    // -- tests --------------------------------------------------------------

    #[test]
    fn axmlenc_round_trips_the_real_apk_manifest() {
        let original_bytes = real_manifest();
        assert!(original_bytes.len() > 8, "manifest present");

        let original = crate::axml::decode(&original_bytes).expect("decode real manifest");
        let encoded = encode(&original).expect("encode real manifest");
        let again = crate::axml::decode(&encoded).expect("re-decode real manifest");

        assert_equivalent(&original, &again, "$");

        // The tree really is non-trivial (guards against a vacuous pass).
        let mut nodes = Vec::new();
        original.walk(&mut nodes);
        // Calibrated to the generated fixture's manifest (uses-sdk + 6
        // permissions + application + activity + intent-filter + action +
        // category + service + receiver + filter + action ≈ 17 nodes).
        assert!(
            nodes.len() >= 15,
            "expected a substantial manifest, got {}",
            nodes.len()
        );

        println!(
            "fmandroid AndroidManifest.xml: original {} bytes, re-encoded {} bytes",
            original_bytes.len(),
            encoded.len()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn axmlenc_chunks_tile_the_buffer_exactly() {
        let original = crate::axml::decode(&real_manifest()).expect("decode");
        let encoded = encode(&original).expect("encode");

        // File header: type, headerSize 8, size = whole buffer.
        let file_ty = u16::from_le_bytes([encoded[0], encoded[1]]);
        let file_hs = u16::from_le_bytes([encoded[2], encoded[3]]);
        let file_sz = u32::from_le_bytes([encoded[4], encoded[5], encoded[6], encoded[7]]) as usize;
        assert_eq!(file_ty, 0x0003, "starts with RES_XML_TYPE");
        assert_eq!(file_hs, 8, "file header size");
        assert_eq!(file_sz, encoded.len(), "file chunk covers whole buffer");

        // Inner chunks start right after the 8-byte file header and must tile
        // the rest of the buffer with no gaps and no overruns.
        let mut pos = 8usize;
        let mut seen = 0usize;
        while pos + 8 <= encoded.len() {
            let ty = u16::from_le_bytes([encoded[pos], encoded[pos + 1]]);
            let sz = u32::from_le_bytes([
                encoded[pos + 4],
                encoded[pos + 5],
                encoded[pos + 6],
                encoded[pos + 7],
            ]) as usize;
            assert!(sz >= 8, "chunk 0x{ty:04x} has bogus size {sz}");
            assert!(
                pos + sz <= encoded.len(),
                "chunk 0x{ty:04x} at {pos} overruns the buffer"
            );
            pos += sz;
            seen += 1;
        }
        assert_eq!(pos, encoded.len(), "chunks tiled exactly");
        assert!(
            seen >= 3,
            "expected string pool + elements, saw {seen} chunks"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn axmlenc_preserves_framework_resource_ids() {
        let original = crate::axml::decode(&real_manifest()).expect("decode");
        let encoded = encode(&original).expect("encode");

        // The android namespace URI survives in the UTF-16 string pool. We
        // compare against its UTF-16LE byte encoding so the assertion is
        // encoding-faithful (the URI is ASCII-only, so each unit is `b, 0x00`).
        let android_utf16: Vec<u8> = ANDROID
            .encode_utf16()
            .flat_map(|u| u.to_le_bytes())
            .collect();
        assert!(
            encoded.windows(android_utf16.len()).any(|w| w == &android_utf16[..]),
            "android namespace URI missing from the pool"
        );

        let ids = resource_map(&encoded);
        assert!(!ids.is_empty(), "resource map emitted");
        assert!(ids.iter().any(|id| *id != 0), "at least one non-zero id");

        let strings = pool_strings(&encoded);
        // `android:exported` is used by the fmandroid manifest; its id must be in
        // the map at the same index as its name in the pool.
        let exported = ids
            .iter()
            .position(|id| *id == 0x0101_0010)
            .expect("exported id present in resource map");
        assert_eq!(strings[exported], "exported");
        // ... and `versionCode` resolves too.
        let vc = ids
            .iter()
            .position(|id| *id == 0x0101_021b)
            .expect("versionCode id present");
        assert_eq!(strings[vc], "versionCode");
    }

    #[test]
    fn axmlenc_round_trips_a_synthetic_manifest() {
        let root = Node {
            name: "manifest".into(),
            namespace: None,
            line: 1,
            attrs: vec![
                attr(None, "package", AttrValue::Str("com.example.app".into())),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "versionCode", AttrValue::Int(7)),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "versionName", AttrValue::Str("1.2.3".into())),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "debuggable", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "theme", AttrValue::Reference(0x7f0e0001)),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "targetSdkVersion", AttrValue::Int(33)),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "configChanges", AttrValue::Hex(0x4a0)),
                attr(Some(ANDROID), "minSdkVersion", AttrValue::Int(21)),
                attr(None, "customFloat", AttrValue::Float(1.5)),
                attr(None, "customNull", AttrValue::Null),
            ],
            children: vec![Node {
                name: "application".into(),
                namespace: None,
                line: 2,
                attrs: vec![
                    attr(Some(ANDROID), "label", AttrValue::Str("Example".into())),
                    attr(Some(ANDROID), "allowBackup", AttrValue::Bool(false)),
                ],
                children: vec![Node {
                    name: "activity".into(),
                    namespace: None,
                    line: 3,
                    attrs: vec![
                        attr(Some(ANDROID), "name", AttrValue::Str(".Main".into())),
                        attr(Some(ANDROID), "exported", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
                    ],
                    children: vec![Node {
                        name: "intent-filter".into(),
                        namespace: None,
                        line: 4,
                        attrs: vec![],
                        children: vec![],
                    }],
                }],
            }],
        };

        let encoded = encode(&root).expect("encode synthetic");
        let decoded = crate::axml::decode(&encoded).expect("decode synthetic");
        assert_equivalent(&root, &decoded, "$");

        // Sanity: namespaced values keep their types.
        let app = &decoded.children[0];
        assert_eq!(app.attr_bool("allowBackup"), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(
            app.children[0].attr("exported"),
            Some(&AttrValue::Bool(true))
        );
        assert_eq!(app.children[0].attr_str("name").as_deref(), Some(".Main"));

        // Ids and namespaces survive in the synthetic document too.
        let ids = resource_map(&encoded);
        assert!(ids.contains(&0x0101_000f), "debuggable id 0x0101000f");
        assert!(ids.contains(&0x0101_0010), "exported id 0x01010010");
        assert!(ids.contains(&0x0101_021b), "versionCode id 0x0101021b");
        assert!(
            {
                let android_utf16: Vec<u8> = ANDROID
                    .encode_utf16()
                    .flat_map(|u| u.to_le_bytes())
                    .collect();
                encoded.windows(android_utf16.len()).any(|w| w == &android_utf16[..])
            },
            "android namespace URI in pool"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn axmlenc_public_round_trip_check_agrees() {
        let bytes = real_manifest();
        let (a, b) = round_trip_check(&bytes).expect("round trip");
        assert_equivalent(&a, &b, "$");
    }

    #[test]
    fn axmlenc_length_prefixes_cover_both_forms() {
        let mut short = Vec::new();
        encode_len(&mut short, 0x7f).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(short, vec![0x7f]);

        let mut long = Vec::new();
        encode_len(&mut long, 0x123).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(long, vec![0x80 | 0x01, 0x23]);

        assert!(encode_len(&mut Vec::new(), 0x8000).is_err());
    }
}

````rust
//! Cryptography for APK signing and ADB authentication.
//!
//! Pure Rust: the `rsa` crate for the maths, and a small hand-written DER/ASN.1
//! writer for the X.509 certificate. No OpenSSL, no `keytool`, no `jarsigner`,
//! no `apksigner`.
//!
//! Two consumers:
//! * [`sign_sha256`] / [`sign_sha1`] — PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures for APK v1/v2
//!   signing and for the ADB AUTH handshake.
//! * [`self_signed_cert_der`] — the signing certificate an APK carries.

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use num_bigint_dig::BigUint;
use rsa::pkcs1v15::Pkcs1v15Sign;
use rsa::pkcs8::{DecodePrivateKey, EncodePrivateKey, LineEnding};
use rsa::traits::PublicKeyParts;
use rsa::{RsaPrivateKey, RsaPublicKey};
use sha1::Sha1;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

/// RSA key size for generated signing identities. 2048 is what Android tooling
/// uses and what ADB expects.
pub const RSA_BITS: usize = 2048;
/// `RSANUMBYTES` in the Android ADB public-key structure.
pub const RSA_NUM_BYTES: usize = 256;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Signing
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// PKCS#1 v1.5 signature over the SHA-256 digest of `msg`.
pub fn sign_sha256(key: &RsaPrivateKey, msg: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let digest = Sha256::digest(msg);
    sign_prehashed_sha256(key, &digest)
}

/// PKCS#1 v1.5 over an already-computed SHA-256 digest.
pub fn sign_prehashed_sha256(key: &RsaPrivateKey, digest: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    key.sign(Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<Sha256>(), digest)
        .context("RSA signing failed")
}

/// PKCS#1 v1.5 signature over the SHA-1 digest of `msg`.
///
/// SHA-1 is *required* here: the ADB AUTH handshake signs its 20-byte token
/// with SHA-1/RSA, and that is not a choice this tool gets to make. It is not
/// used for anything else — APK signatures go through SHA-256.
pub fn sign_sha1(key: &RsaPrivateKey, msg: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let digest = Sha1::digest(msg);
    key.sign(Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<Sha1>(), &digest)
        .context("RSA SHA-1 signing failed")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Key generation / serialisation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn generate_key(bits: usize) -> Result<RsaPrivateKey> {
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    RsaPrivateKey::new(&mut rng, bits).context("generating an RSA key")
}

pub fn to_pkcs8_pem(key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> Result<String> {
    Ok(key
        .to_pkcs8_pem(LineEnding::LF)
        .context("encoding PKCS#8")?
        .to_string())
}

pub fn from_pkcs8_pem(pem: &str) -> Result<RsaPrivateKey> {
    RsaPrivateKey::from_pkcs8_pem(pem).context("parsing PKCS#8 private key")
}

/// Big-endian modulus and public exponent.
pub fn public_numbers(key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
    let public = RsaPublicKey::from(key);
    (public.n().to_bytes_be(), public.e().to_bytes_be())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Minimal DER / ASN.1 writer
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn der_length(n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    if n < 0x80 {
        vec![n as u8]
    } else {
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        let mut v = n;
        while v > 0 {
            bytes.insert(0, (v & 0xff) as u8);
            v >>= 8;
        }
        let mut out = vec![0x80 | bytes.len() as u8];
        out.extend_from_slice(&bytes);
        out
    }
}

pub fn der_tlv(tag: u8, content: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = vec![tag];
    out.extend_from_slice(&der_length(content.len()));
    out.extend_from_slice(content);
    out
}

pub fn der_concat(parts: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
    parts.iter().flatten().copied().collect()
}

pub fn der_sequence(parts: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0x30, &der_concat(parts))
}

pub fn der_set(parts: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0x31, &der_concat(parts))
}

/// Positive INTEGER: prepend 0x00 when the high bit would make it negative.
pub fn der_integer(bytes_be: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let trimmed = {
        let mut i = 0;
        while i + 1 < bytes_be.len() && bytes_be[i] == 0 {
            i += 1;
        }
        &bytes_be[i..]
    };
    let mut content = Vec::with_capacity(trimmed.len() + 1);
    if trimmed.first().map(|b| b & 0x80 != 0).unwrap_or(false) {
        content.push(0);
    }
    content.extend_from_slice(trimmed);
    der_tlv(0x02, &content)
}

pub fn der_oid(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0x06, bytes)
}

pub fn der_null() -> Vec<u8> {
    vec![0x05, 0x00]
}

pub fn der_utf8(s: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0x0c, s.as_bytes())
}

pub fn der_bit_string(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut content = vec![0x00]; // zero unused bits
    content.extend_from_slice(bytes);
    der_tlv(0x03, &content)
}

pub fn der_octet_string(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0x04, bytes)
}

pub fn der_boolean(v: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
    vec![0x01, 0x01, if v { 0xff } else { 0x00 }]
}

/// Context-specific constructed tag, e.g. `[0]` -> 0xA0, `[3]` -> 0xA3.
pub fn der_context(n: u8, content: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0xA0 | n, content)
}

/// UTCTime, e.g. `250101000000Z`.
pub fn der_utc_time(s: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_tlv(0x17, s.as_bytes())
}

/// Namespaced DER surface for other modules (PKCS#7 lives in `sign.rs`).
pub mod der {
    pub use super::der_bit_string as bit_string;
    pub use super::der_boolean as boolean;
    pub use super::der_integer as integer;
    pub use super::der_null as null;
    pub use super::der_octet_string as octet_string;
    pub use super::der_oid as oid;
    pub use super::der_sequence as sequence;
    pub use super::der_set as set;
    pub use super::der_utf8 as utf8;

    /// PKCS#7 `data` content type.
    pub const OID_PKCS7_DATA: [u8; 9] = [0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x07, 0x01];
    /// PKCS#7 `signedData` content type.
    pub const OID_PKCS7_SIGNED_DATA: [u8; 9] =
        [0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x07, 0x02];

    /// `[n] EXPLICIT` — a context-specific constructed tag wrapping content.
    pub fn explicit(n: u8, content: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        super::der_context(n, content)
    }

    /// `[n] IMPLICIT SET OF` — a context tag standing in for a SET.
    pub fn implicit_set(n: u8, parts: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
        super::der_tlv(0xA0 | n, &super::der_concat(parts))
    }

    pub fn algorithm_identifier_sha256() -> Vec<u8> {
        super::algorithm_identifier(super::OID_SHA256_WITH_RSA)
    }

    pub fn algorithm_identifier_rsa() -> Vec<u8> {
        super::algorithm_identifier(super::OID_RSA_ENCRYPTION)
    }
}

// OIDs
const OID_RSA_ENCRYPTION: &[u8] = &[0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01];
const OID_SHA256_WITH_RSA: &[u8] = &[0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x0b];
const OID_COMMON_NAME: &[u8] = &[0x55, 0x04, 0x03];
const OID_BASIC_CONSTRAINTS: &[u8] = &[0x55, 0x1d, 0x13];
const OID_KEY_USAGE: &[u8] = &[0x55, 0x1d, 0x0f];

pub fn algorithm_identifier(oid: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_sequence(&[der_oid(oid), der_null()])
}

pub fn subject_public_key_info(key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> Vec<u8> {
    let (n, e) = public_numbers(key);
    let rsa_pub = der_sequence(&[der_integer(&n), der_integer(&e)]);
    der_sequence(&[
        algorithm_identifier(OID_RSA_ENCRYPTION),
        der_bit_string(&rsa_pub),
    ])
}

pub fn rdn(oid: &[u8], value: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    der_sequence(&[der_set(&[der_sequence(&[der_oid(oid), der_utf8(value)])])])
}

/// The pieces of a signing certificate that a PKCS#7 `SignerInfo` also needs:
/// the DER certificate itself, plus its issuer name and serial number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CertMaterial {
    pub der: Vec<u8>,
    pub issuer: Vec<u8>,
    pub serial: Vec<u8>,
    pub subject: String,
}

/// The DER `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` for an RSA key.
pub fn spki_der(key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    Ok(subject_public_key_info(key))
}

/// A self-signed X.509 v3 certificate in DER, valid for `days` from now.
///
/// This is the "signing certificate" an APK carries. Android treats APK signing
/// like JAR signing: the certificate is an identity, not a chain — a self-signed
/// cert is exactly what `keytool -genkeypair` produces for this purpose.
pub fn self_signed_cert_der(key: &RsaPrivateKey, cn: &str, days: i64) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    Ok(self_signed_cert_material(key, cn, days)?.der)
}

/// Like [`self_signed_cert_der`], but also returns the issuer name and serial
/// so a PKCS#7 signer can reference the certificate.
pub fn self_signed_cert_material(key: &RsaPrivateKey, cn: &str, days: i64) -> Result<CertMaterial> {
    let (n, _) = public_numbers(key);
    // Deterministic-but-unique serial derived from the modulus.
    let digest = Sha256::digest(&n);
    let serial = &digest[..16];

    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .context("system clock is before the epoch")?
        .as_secs() as i64;
    let (nb, na) = (now - 86_400, now + days * 86_400);

    let name = rdn(OID_COMMON_NAME, cn);

    let spki = subject_public_key_info(key);

    // Extensions: basicConstraints CA:TRUE (harmless, matches keytool defaults)
    // and keyUsage digitalSignature (what an APK signature needs).
    let bc = der_sequence(&[
        der_oid(OID_BASIC_CONSTRAINTS),
        der_boolean(true),
        der_octet_string(&der_sequence(&[der_boolean(true)])),
    ]);
    let ku = der_sequence(&[
        der_oid(OID_KEY_USAGE),
        der_boolean(true),
        // BIT STRING, bit 7 set = digitalSignature (first bit of the byte).
        der_octet_string(&der_bit_string(&[0x80])),
    ]);
    let extensions = der_context(3, &der_sequence(&[bc, ku]));

    let tbs = der_sequence(&[
        der_context(0, &der_integer(&2u64.to_be_bytes())), // v3
        der_integer(serial),
        algorithm_identifier(OID_SHA256_WITH_RSA),
        name.clone(),
        der_sequence(&[der_utc_time(&utc_time(nb)), der_utc_time(&utc_time(na))]),
        name,
        spki,
        extensions,
    ]);

    let signature = sign_sha256(key, &tbs)?;
    Ok(CertMaterial {
        der: der_sequence(&[
            tbs,
            algorithm_identifier(OID_SHA256_WITH_RSA),
            der_bit_string(&signature),
        ]),
        issuer: rdn(OID_COMMON_NAME, cn),
        serial: serial.to_vec(),
        subject: cn.to_string(),
    })
}

/// Days-since-epoch independent UTC timestamp: computes the civil date from the
/// Unix timestamp so we do not need a date library.
fn utc_time(unix: i64) -> String {
    let days = unix.div_euclid(86_400);
    let secs = unix.rem_euclid(86_400);
    let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(days);
    format!(
        "{:02}{:02}{:02}{:02}{:02}{:02}Z",
        y % 100,
        m,
        d,
        secs / 3600,
        (secs % 3600) / 60,
        secs % 60
    )
}

/// Howard Hinnant's `civil_from_days` — correct for the whole proleptic
/// Gregorian calendar, no dependencies.
fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (z - era * 146_097) as u64; // [0, 146096]
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365; // [0, 399]
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100); // [0, 365]
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153; // [0, 11]
    let d = (doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1) as u32; // [1, 31]
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32; // [1, 12]
    (if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y }, m, d)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Android ADB public key format
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The 524-byte `RSAPublicKey` structure ADB exchanges during AUTH.
///
/// ```text
/// u32 len      = 256
/// u32 n0inv    = -1 / n[0] mod 2^32
/// u8  n[256]   modulus, little-endian
/// u8  rr[256]  R^2 mod n (R = 2^2048), little-endian
/// u32 exponent
/// ```
pub fn android_public_key_blob(key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let public = RsaPublicKey::from(key);
    let n_be = public.n().to_bytes_be();
    // ADB's `RSAPublicKey` structure is a fixed 524-byte blob with a 256-byte
    // modulus field — it only ever carries 2048-bit keys. Reject anything
    // whose modulus is not exactly 256 bytes (no left-padding fudge: a key
    // that is shorter would have leading zero bytes silently injected, and a
    // 4096-bit key would be silently truncated by the receiver).
    if n_be.len() != RSA_NUM_BYTES {
        anyhow::bail!(
            "RSA modulus is {} bytes; ADB's RSAPublicKey structure is fixed at {} bytes \
             (2048-bit keys only)",
            n_be.len(),
            RSA_NUM_BYTES
        );
    }
    // Reverse the big-endian modulus in place to get the little-endian form
    // the ADB structure expects.
    let mut n_le = n_be;
    n_le.reverse();

    let n0 = u32::from_le_bytes([n_le[0], n_le[1], n_le[2], n_le[3]]);
    let n0inv = modular_inverse_2_32(n0).wrapping_neg();

    let modulus = public.n().clone();
    let r = BigUint::from(1u32) << (RSA_NUM_BYTES * 8);
    let r_squared = (&r * &r) % &modulus;
    let rr_le = biguint_to_le(&r_squared, RSA_NUM_BYTES)?;

    let exponent = public.e().to_bytes_be();
    let exp = if exponent.len() <= 4 {
        let mut b = [0u8; 4];
        b[4 - exponent.len()..].copy_from_slice(&exponent);
        u32::from_be_bytes(b)
    } else {
        anyhow::bail!("unexpected RSA exponent size {}", exponent.len());
    };

    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + 4 + RSA_NUM_BYTES * 2 + 4);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(RSA_NUM_BYTES as u32).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&n0inv.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&n_le);
    out.extend_from_slice(&rr_le);
    out.extend_from_slice(&exp.to_le_bytes());
    Ok(out)
}

/// `base64(blob)` — the exact text of an `adbkey.pub` file.
pub fn adbkey_pub_text(key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> Result<String> {
    Ok(base64_encode(&android_public_key_blob(key)?))
}

/// Inverse of an odd number modulo 2^32, by Newton iteration (each step doubles
/// the number of correct bits).
fn modular_inverse_2_32(a: u32) -> u32 {
    let mut x = 1u32;
    for _ in 0..5 {
        x = x.wrapping_mul(2u32.wrapping_sub(a.wrapping_mul(x)));
    }
    x
}

fn biguint_to_le(value: &BigUint, width: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let be = value.to_bytes_be();
    if be.len() > width {
        anyhow::bail!(
            "value needs {} bytes, more than the {} available",
            be.len(),
            width
        );
    }
    let mut le = vec![0u8; width - be.len()];
    le.extend_from_slice(&be);
    le.reverse();
    Ok(le)
}

/// Standard base64 (with padding). Small enough not to justify a dependency.
pub fn base64_encode(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
    let mut out = String::with_capacity((data.len() + 2) / 3 * 4);
    for chunk in data.chunks(3) {
        let b0 = chunk[0] as u32;
        let b1 = *chunk.get(1).unwrap_or(&0) as u32;
        let b2 = *chunk.get(2).unwrap_or(&0) as u32;
        let triple = (b0 << 16) | (b1 << 8) | b2;
        out.push(ALPHABET[(triple >> 18) as usize & 63] as char);
        out.push(ALPHABET[(triple >> 12) as usize & 63] as char);
        out.push(if chunk.len() > 1 {
            ALPHABET[(triple >> 6) as usize & 63] as char
        } else {
            '='
        });
        out.push(if chunk.len() > 2 {
            ALPHABET[triple as usize & 63] as char
        } else {
            '='
        });
    }
    out
}

pub fn base64_decode(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    fn val(c: u8) -> Option<u32> {
        match c {
            b'A'..=b'Z' => Some((c - b'A') as u32),
            b'a'..=b'z' => Some((c - b'a') as u32 + 26),
            b'0'..=b'9' => Some((c - b'0') as u32 + 52),
            b'+' => Some(62),
            b'/' => Some(63),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    let cleaned: Vec<u8> = text.bytes().filter(|b| !b.is_ascii_whitespace()).collect();
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(cleaned.len() / 4 * 3);
    for chunk in cleaned.chunks(4) {
        if chunk.len() < 2 {
            break;
        }
        let mut acc = 0u32;
        let mut count = 0;
        for &c in chunk {
            if c == b'=' {
                break;
            }
            let v = val(c).ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid base64 byte {c:?}"))?;
            acc = (acc << 6) | v;
            count += 1;
        }
        match count {
            2 => out.push((acc >> 4) as u8),
            3 => {
                out.push((acc >> 10) as u8);
                out.push((acc >> 2) as u8);
            }
            4 => {
                out.push((acc >> 16) as u8);
                out.push((acc >> 8) as u8);
                out.push(acc as u8);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rsa::pkcs1v15::Pkcs1v15Sign;

    fn key() -> RsaPrivateKey {
        // One 2048-bit key for the whole suite: generation is the slow part.
        generate_key(RSA_BITS).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn der_primitive_encodings_are_correct() {
        // Lengths: short form under 128, long form at/over.
        assert_eq!(der_length(0), vec![0x00]);
        assert_eq!(der_length(127), vec![0x7f]);
        assert_eq!(der_length(128), vec![0x81, 0x80]);
        assert_eq!(der_length(256), vec![0x82, 0x01, 0x00]);
        // INTEGER strips leading zeros and adds one when the high bit is set.
        assert_eq!(der_integer(&[0x00, 0x00, 0x01]), vec![0x02, 0x01, 0x01]);
        assert_eq!(der_integer(&[0x80]), vec![0x02, 0x02, 0x00, 0x80]);
        // SEQUENCE of NULL is the well-known `30 02 05 00`.
        assert_eq!(der_sequence(&[der_null()]), vec![0x30, 0x02, 0x05, 0x00]);
        // Context tag [0] wraps in 0xA0.
        assert_eq!(
            der_context(0, &[0x02, 0x01, 0x02]),
            vec![0xa0, 0x03, 0x02, 0x01, 0x02]
        );
        // BIT STRING carries the unused-bit count first.
        assert_eq!(der_bit_string(&[0xaa]), vec![0x03, 0x02, 0x00, 0xaa]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn utc_time_matches_known_instants() {
        assert_eq!(utc_time(0), "700101000000Z");
        assert_eq!(utc_time(1_000_000_000), "010909014640Z"); // 2001-09-09T01:46:40Z
        assert_eq!(utc_time(1_735_689_600), "250101000000Z"); // 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z
    }

    #[test]
    fn signs_and_verifies_sha256() {
        let k = key();
        let msg = b"the quick brown fox";
        let sig = sign_sha256(&k, msg).unwrap();
        let pub_key = RsaPublicKey::from(&k);
        let digest = Sha256::digest(msg);
        assert!(pub_key
            .verify(Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<Sha256>(), &digest, &sig)
            .is_ok());
        // A different message must not verify with the same signature.
        let other = Sha256::digest(b"something else");
        assert!(pub_key
            .verify(Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<Sha256>(), &other, &sig)
            .is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn base64_matches_known_vectors() {
        assert_eq!(base64_encode(b""), "");
        assert_eq!(base64_encode(b"f"), "Zg==");
        assert_eq!(base64_encode(b"fo"), "Zm8=");
        assert_eq!(base64_encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
        assert_eq!(base64_encode(b"foob"), "Zm9vYg==");
        assert_eq!(base64_encode(b"foobar"), "Zm9vYmFy");
        for sample in [
            &b""[..],
            b"f",
            b"fo",
            b"foo",
            b"foob",
            b"foobar",
            &[0u8, 255, 1][..],
        ] {
            assert_eq!(base64_decode(&base64_encode(sample)).unwrap(), sample);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn android_public_key_blob_has_the_documented_shape() {
        let k = key();
        let blob = android_public_key_blob(&k).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            blob.len(),
            4 + 4 + 256 + 256 + 4,
            "ADB structure is 524 bytes"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            u32::from_le_bytes([blob[0], blob[1], blob[2], blob[3]]),
            256
        );
        assert_eq!(
            u32::from_le_bytes([blob[520], blob[521], blob[522], blob[523]]),
            65537,
            "exponent must be 65537"
        );
        // n0inv must satisfy n0 * n0inv == -1 (mod 2^32).
        let n0 = u32::from_le_bytes([blob[8], blob[9], blob[10], blob[11]]);
        let n0inv = u32::from_le_bytes([blob[4], blob[5], blob[6], blob[7]]);
        assert_eq!(n0.wrapping_mul(n0inv), u32::MAX, "n0inv is -1/n0 mod 2^32");
        // The modulus, little-endian, must be the key's modulus.
        let mut n_le = blob[8..264].to_vec();
        n_le.reverse();
        assert_eq!(BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_le), *RsaPublicKey::from(&k).n());
    }

    #[test]
    fn certificates_are_well_formed_der() {
        let k = key();
        let der = self_signed_cert_der(&k, "mandroid", 3650).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(der[0], 0x30, "Certificate is a SEQUENCE");
        assert_eq!(der.len() as usize, der.len());
        // The outer length field must exactly cover the rest of the buffer.
        let (len, header) = if der[1] < 0x80 {
            (der[1] as usize, 2usize)
        } else {
            let n = (der[1] & 0x7f) as usize;
            let mut v = 0usize;
            for i in 0..n {
                v = (v << 8) | der[2 + i] as usize;
            }
            (v, 2 + n)
        };
        assert_eq!(header + len, der.len(), "outer DER length must be exact");
    }

    #[test]
    fn android_pubkey_text_is_pure_base64() {
        let k = key();
        let text = adbkey_pub_text(&k).unwrap();
        assert!(text
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '+' || c == '/' || c == '='));
        assert_eq!(base64_decode(&text).unwrap().len(), 524);
    }
}

//! Physical device hardware profile.
//!
//! MANDROID carries the hardware profile of the physical handset it drives:
//! RAM, ROM, CPU/SoC shape, screen geometry, **dual eSIM with two factory-
//! registered profiles**, the **out-of-the-box app roster** (Play Store,
//! Gmail, Maps — everything a new phone ships with) and the **pre-
//! provisioned Google account slot**.
//!
//! The defaults come from the device identity (see [`crate::identity`]) —
//! **16 GB RAM, 1 TB ROM (931 GiB usable), a Google Tensor G4 (8 cores:
//! 1× Cortex-X4 + 3× Cortex-A720 + 4× Cortex-A520), 720x1560 @ 420dpi** —
//! and every identifier (serial, IMEI/IMEI2, chip EID, baseband) is
//! deterministic, so the handset keeps the same identity across boots.
//!
//! Account handling, stated plainly: the profile stores **identifiers only**
//! (the account e-mail and its alternate). Passwords are never written to disk,
//! never embedded in the binary and never echoed into tool output — the single
//! supported source is the `MANDROID_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD` environment variable,
//! read at render time and surfaced only as `password_set: true|false`. Nothing
//! here contacts Google: there are no online verification flows to satisfy or
//! bypass.
//!
//! The profile is used in three places:
//!
//! * `mandroid profile` / `android_device_profile` render it as JSON.
//! * Manifest presets can read the SDK level / ABIs when targeting a build.
//! * Screen defaults (720x1560 @ 420dpi) seed [`crate::screen`] when a device
//!   reports nothing.

/// Honest statement about what this sandbox/runtime can virtualise: a real
/// Android system image needs KVM + binder/ashmem kernel support. Where that
/// is absent (containers, most CI), the handset runs as a full in-process OS
/// runtime (compositor + adbd + radio model), not a system VM.
fn kernel_support_note() -> &'static str {
    let kvm = std::path::Path::new("/dev/kvm").exists();
    let binder = std::path::Path::new("/dev/binder").exists();
    match (kvm, binder) {
        (true, true) => "host supports KVM + binder; profile can additionally back a full system image",
        (true, false) => "KVM present, binder absent; in-process OS runtime (compositor + adbd + radio)",
        (false, true) => "binder present, KVM absent; in-process OS runtime (compositor + adbd + radio)",
        (false, false) => "no KVM/binder on this host; the handset runs as the in-process OS runtime (compositor + adbd + radio model)",
    }
}

use std::path::PathBuf;

use serde_json::{json, Value};

use crate::key::default_dir;

/// Where account identifiers persist (`~/.android/device.json`). Passwords
/// are deliberately absent from this file forever.
pub fn config_path() -> PathBuf {
    default_dir().join("device.json")
}

/// Built-in account identifiers: a fresh install reports the device as signed
/// in with these, out of the box (identifiers only — never secrets). Override
/// any time with `mandroid profile --set-account ...`; `--clear-account`
/// writes an explicit empty state which is always respected.
pub const DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_EMAIL: &str = "owner@romacode.local";
pub const DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ALT_EMAIL: &str = "alt-owner@romacode.local";

/// The pre-provisioned account: identifiers only.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AccountConfig {
    pub email: Option<String>,
    pub alternate_email: Option<String>,
}

impl AccountConfig {
    /// Load account identifiers (config file, else the built-in defaults).
    pub fn load() -> Self {
        Self::load_from(&config_path())
    }

    /// Testable core of [`load`]: no file → built-in defaults (fresh install
    /// is signed-in ready); a file present is respected verbatim, explicit
    /// nulls included (that is what clear-account persists).
    pub fn load_from(path: &std::path::Path) -> Self {
        let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(path) else {
            return Self {
                email: Some(DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_EMAIL.into()),
                alternate_email: Some(DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ALT_EMAIL.into()),
            };
        };
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) else {
            return Self::default();
        };
        Self {
            email: v["account_email"].as_str().map(String::from),
            alternate_email: v["account_alt_email"].as_str().map(String::from),
        }
    }

    /// Persist account identifiers (never secrets).
    pub fn save(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let path = config_path();
        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
        }
        let body = json!({
            "account_email": self.email,
            "account_alt_email": self.alternate_email,
            "note": "identifiers only; passwords come from MANDROID_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD at render time and are never stored",
        });
        std::fs::write(path, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&body).unwrap())
    }
}

/// Product-spec hardware profile for the MANDROID virtual device.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DeviceProfile {
    /// Marketing name of the profile.
    pub name: String,
    /// RAM in MiB (spec: 16 GB = 16384 MiB).
    pub ram_mib: u64,
    /// Internal storage in GiB (spec: 1 TB = 931 GiB usable).
    pub rom_gib: u64,
    /// CPU cores, matched to the host processor.
    pub cpu_cores: u32,
    /// Host/device CPU architecture (e.g. `x86_64`, `aarch64`).
