```rust
//! Native HTTP(S) fetch — no `curl`, no `reqwest`, no external process.
//!
//! TLS is rustls with the webpki root store, matching the rest of this stack.
//! Used to acquire an APK from a URL the way an agent would be told to.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::net::TcpStream;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Context, Result};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

/// Refuse anything larger than this by default — a runaway download on a
/// metered or hostile link is not a useful outcome.
pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 512 * 1024 * 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FetchOptions {
    pub max_bytes: u64,
    pub max_redirects: usize,
    pub timeout: Duration,
    /// Extra request headers, e.g. an Authorization or User-Agent override.
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Only accept this content type family (substring match, case-insensitive).
    pub expect_content_type: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for FetchOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            max_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
            max_redirects: 5,
            timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),
            headers: vec![(
                "User-Agent".into(),
                format!(
                    "mandroid/{} (native android engine)",
                    env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
                ),
            )],
            expect_content_type: None,
        }
    }
}

/// What a completed download produced. Never contains file contents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FetchResult {
    pub final_url: String,
    pub status: u16,
    pub content_type: Option<String>,
    pub content_length: Option<u64>,
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub sha256: String,
    pub path: PathBuf,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct ParsedUrl {
    https: bool,
    host: String,
    port: u16,
    path: String,
}

fn parse_url(url: &str) -> Result<ParsedUrl> {
    let (https, rest) = if let Some(r) = url.strip_prefix("https://") {
        (true, r)
    } else if let Some(r) = url.strip_prefix("http://") {
        (false, r)
    } else {
        bail!("unsupported URL scheme (expected http:// or https://): {url}");
    };
    // The authority ends at the first '/', '?' or '#'.
    let (authority, path) = match rest.find(['/', '?', '#']) {
        Some(i) if rest[i..].starts_with('/') => (&rest[..i], rest[i..].to_string()),
        Some(i) if rest[i..].starts_with('?') => (&rest[..i], format!("/{}", &rest[i..])),
        Some(i) => (&rest[..i], "/".to_string()), // bare fragment
        None => (rest, "/".to_string()),
    };
    if authority.is_empty() {
        bail!("URL has no host: {url}");
    }
    let (host, port) = match authority.rsplit_once(':') {
        Some((h, p)) if !h.is_empty() && p.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) => {
            (h.to_string(), p.parse::<u16>().context("bad port")?)
        }
        _ => (authority.to_string(), if https { 443 } else { 80 }),
    };
    Ok(ParsedUrl {
        https,
        host,
        port,
        path,
    })
}

/// A `Read + Write` stream that is either plain TCP or TLS over TCP.
enum Stream {
    Plain(TcpStream),
    Tls(Box<rustls::StreamOwned<rustls::ClientConnection, TcpStream>>),
}

impl Read for Stream {
    fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
        match self {
            Stream::Plain(s) => s.read(buf),
            Stream::Tls(s) => s.read(buf),
        }
    }
}

impl Write for Stream {
    fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
        match self {
            Stream::Plain(s) => s.write(buf),
            Stream::Tls(s) => s.write(buf),
        }
    }
    fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        match self {
            Stream::Plain(s) => s.flush(),
            Stream::Tls(s) => s.flush(),
        }
    }
}

fn tls_config() -> Arc<rustls::ClientConfig> {
    let roots: rustls::RootCertStore = webpki_roots::TLS_SERVER_ROOTS.iter().cloned().collect();
    Arc::new(
        rustls::ClientConfig::builder()
            .with_root_certificates(roots)
            .with_no_client_auth(),
    )
}

fn connect(u: &ParsedUrl, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Stream> {
    let addr = format!("{}:{}", u.host, u.port);
    let tcp = TcpStream::connect(&addr).with_context(|| format!("connecting to {addr}"))?;
    tcp.set_read_timeout(Some(timeout))?;
    tcp.set_write_timeout(Some(timeout))?;
    tcp.set_nodelay(true).ok();
    if !u.https {
        return Ok(Stream::Plain(tcp));
    }
    let name = rustls_pki_types::ServerName::try_from(u.host.clone())
        .map_err(|_| anyhow!("invalid TLS server name: {}", u.host))?;
    let conn = rustls::ClientConnection::new(tls_config(), name).context("starting TLS session")?;
    Ok(Stream::Tls(Box::new(rustls::StreamOwned::new(conn, tcp))))
}

/// One HTTP/1.1 GET. Header names are echoed in the response struct only as far
/// as we need them; the body is streamed to the caller.
struct HttpResponse {
    status: u16,
    headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl HttpResponse {
    fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.headers
            .iter()
            .find(|(k, _)| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
            .map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
    }
}

fn send_request(
    stream: &mut Stream,
    u: &ParsedUrl,
    headers: &[(String, String)],
) -> Result<HttpResponse> {
    let mut req = format!(
        "GET {} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {}\r\nAccept: */*\r\nAccept-Encoding: identity\r\nConnection: close\r\n",
        u.path, u.host
    );
    for (k, v) in headers {
        req.push_str(&format!("{k}: {v}\r\n"));
    }
    req.push_str("\r\n");
    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes())?;
    stream.flush()?;

    // Read headers, byte at a time up to the blank line (keeps back-pressure
    // sane and avoids swallowing body bytes).
    let mut head = Vec::with_capacity(1024);
    let mut b = [0u8; 1];
    loop {
        let n = stream.read(&mut b)?;
        if n == 0 {
            bail!("connection closed before HTTP headers were complete");
        }
        head.push(b[0]);
        if head.len() >= 4 && &head[head.len() - 4..] == b"\r\n\r\n" {
            break;
        }
        if head.len() > 64 * 1024 {
            bail!("HTTP response headers exceeded 64 KiB");
        }
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head).to_string();
    let mut lines = text.split("\r\n");
    let status_line = lines.next().unwrap_or("");
    let status = status_line
        .split_whitespace()
        .nth(1)
        .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed HTTP status line: {status_line:?}"))?;
    let mut headers_out = Vec::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {
            headers_out.push((k.trim().to_string(), v.trim().to_string()));
        }
    }
    Ok(HttpResponse {
        status,
        headers: headers_out,
    })
}

/// Body reader that yields at most the fixed content-length (or everything up
/// to EOF when the server closes, which is what `Connection: close` gives us).
struct Body<'a> {
    stream: &'a mut Stream,
    remaining: Option<u64>,
    max_bytes: u64,
    read: u64,
}

impl<'a> Body<'a> {
    fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64 * 1024];
        let want = match self.remaining {
            Some(r) if r == 0 => return Ok(None),
            Some(r) => buf.len().min(r as usize),
            None => buf.len(),
        };
        if want == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        buf.truncate(want);
        let n = self.stream.read(&mut buf)?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        buf.truncate(n);
        self.read += n as u64;
        if self.read > self.max_bytes {
            bail!("download exceeded the {} byte limit", self.max_bytes);
        }
        if let Some(r) = self.remaining.as_mut() {
            *r -= n as u64;
        }
        Ok(Some(buf))
    }
}

/// Fetch a URL to a file, following redirects. Returns the digest so the caller
/// can pin/verify what actually arrived.
pub fn fetch(url: &str, dest: &Path, opts: &FetchOptions) -> Result<FetchResult> {
    let mut current = url.to_string();
    for hop in 0..=opts.max_redirects {
        let parsed = parse_url(&current)?;
        let mut stream = connect(&parsed, opts.timeout)?;
        let resp = send_request(&mut stream, &parsed, &opts.headers)?;

        if (300..400).contains(&resp.status) {
            let location = resp
                .header("location")
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("HTTP {} with no Location header", resp.status))?;
            if hop == opts.max_redirects {
                bail!("too many redirects (> {})", opts.max_redirects);
            }
            current = if location.starts_with("http://") || location.starts_with("https://") {
                // Absolute URL — use it verbatim. parse_url on the next loop
                // iteration will reject anything malformed.
                location.to_string()
            } else if location.starts_with("//") {
                // Protocol-relative: `//host/path` → `scheme://host/path`.
                if location.contains('\0') || location.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) {
                    bail!("relative redirect contains a NUL or control character: {location:?}");
                }
                let scheme = if parsed.https { "https" } else { "http" };
                format!("{scheme}:{location}")
            } else if let Some(stripped) = location.strip_prefix('/') {
                // Server-absolute: `/path` → `scheme://host:port/path`.
                if location.contains('\0') || location.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) {
                    bail!("relative redirect contains a NUL or control character: {location:?}");
                }
                let scheme = if parsed.https { "https" } else { "http" };
                format!("{scheme}://{}:{}/{stripped}", parsed.host, parsed.port)
            } else {
                // Path-relative: resolve against the directory of the current
                // request URL (RFC 3986 §5.2), honouring `..` and ignoring `.`.
                if location.contains('\0') || location.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) {
                    bail!("relative redirect contains a NUL or control character: {location:?}");
                }
                let scheme = if parsed.https { "https" } else { "http" };
                // Take everything up to and including the last '/' as the base
                // directory (so `/api/v1/models` becomes `/api/v1/`).
                let base_dir = match parsed.path.rfind('/') {
                    Some(i) => &parsed.path[..=i],
                    None => "/",
                };
                let mut segs: Vec<&str> = base_dir
                    .split('/')
                    .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
                    .collect();
                for part in location.split('/') {
                    match part {
                        ".." => {
                            segs.pop();
                        }
                        "." | "" => {} // ignore single-dot and empty segments
                        other => segs.push(other),
                    }
                }
                let joined = segs.join("/");
                format!("{scheme}://{}:{}/{joined}", parsed.host, parsed.port)
            };
            continue;
        }
        if resp.status != 200 {
            bail!("HTTP {} fetching {current}", resp.status);
        }

        let content_type = resp.header("content-type").map(|s| s.to_string());
        if let Some(want) = &opts.expect_content_type {
            let ct = content_type
                .clone()
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .to_ascii_lowercase();
            if !ct.contains(&want.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
                bail!("unexpected content type {ct:?} (wanted something like {want:?})");
            }
        }
        let declared = resp
            .header("content-length")
            .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok());
        if let Some(len) = declared {
            if len > opts.max_bytes {
                bail!(
                    "server advertises {len} bytes, over the {} byte limit",
                    opts.max_bytes
                );
            }
        }

        if let Some(parent) = dest.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
                .with_context(|| format!("creating {}", parent.display()))?;
        }
        let tmp = dest.with_extension("part");
        let mut file =
            std::fs::File::create(&tmp).with_context(|| format!("creating {}", tmp.display()))?;
        let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
        let mut total: u64 = 0;
        let mut body = Body {
            stream: &mut stream,
            remaining: declared,
            max_bytes: opts.max_bytes,
            read: 0,
        };
        while let Some(chunk) = body.next_chunk()? {
            hasher.update(&chunk);
            file.write_all(&chunk)?;
            total += chunk.len() as u64;
        }
        file.flush()?;
        drop(file);
        if let Some(expect) = declared {
            if total != expect {
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
                bail!("short read: got {total} of {expect} bytes");
            }
        }
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, dest).with_context(|| format!("finalising {}", dest.display()))?;
        return Ok(FetchResult {
            final_url: current,
            status: resp.status,
            content_type,
            content_length: declared,
            bytes: total,
            sha256: hex::encode(hasher.finalize()),
            path: dest.to_path_buf(),
        });
    }
    bail!("internal error: redirect loop exhausted without resolution");
}

pub fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {
    let mut f = std::fs::File::open(path).with_context(|| format!("opening {}", path.display()))?;
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; 256 * 1024];
    loop {
        let n = f.read(&mut buf)?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }
        hasher.update(&buf[..n]);
    }
    Ok(hex::encode(hasher.finalize()))
}

/// Cheap sanity check that what we downloaded is the thing we asked for: a ZIP
/// archive (every APK is one) and, when we can see the manifest without
/// decoding, not obviously HTML (a captive portal or error page).
pub fn looks_like_apk(path: &Path) -> Result<bool> {
    let mut f = std::fs::File::open(path)?;
    let mut magic = [0u8; 4];
    if f.read_exact(&mut magic).is_err() {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    Ok(&magic == b"PK\x03\x04")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_urls() {
        // fixture uses the real F-Droid host so the same string is a live,
        // fetchable link (see phone/examples/linkcheck.rs)
        let u = parse_url("https://f-droid.org/F-Droid.apk").unwrap();
        assert!(u.https);
        assert_eq!(u.host, "f-droid.org");
        assert_eq!(u.port, 443);
        assert_eq!(u.path, "/F-Droid.apk");

        let u = parse_url("http://127.0.0.1:8080/a/b?c=d").unwrap();
        assert!(!u.https);
        assert_eq!(u.port, 8080);
        assert_eq!(u.path, "/a/b?c=d");

        let u = parse_url("https://example.com").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(u.path, "/");

        // query directly after the host (no slash) must not leak into the host
        let u = parse_url("https://example.com?x=1").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(u.host, "example.com");
        assert_eq!(u.path, "/?x=1");

        assert!(parse_url("ftp://x/y").is_err());
        assert!(parse_url("https://").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_bad_scheme_with_a_clear_message() {
        let e = parse_url("file:///etc/passwd").unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(e.contains("unsupported URL scheme"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn local_fetch_roundtrip_and_digest() {
        // A tiny plain-HTTP server so the fetch path is exercised without TLS or
        // the network. Proves redirect handling, length accounting and hashing.
        use std::io::Read as _;
        let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        let body = b"PK\x03\x04fake apk payload".to_vec();
        let body_for_thread = body.clone();
        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for _ in 0..2 {
                let (mut sock, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
                let mut req = [0u8; 2048];
                let _ = sock.read(&mut req);
                let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&req);
                // First request redirects, second serves the payload.
                let resp = if text.contains("GET /redirect") {
                    "HTTP/1.1 302 Found\r\nLocation: /real.apk\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n".to_string()
                } else {
                    format!(
                        "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/vnd.android.package-archive\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
                        body_for_thread.len()
                    )
                };
                use std::io::Write as _;
                sock.write_all(resp.as_bytes()).unwrap();
                if !text.contains("GET /redirect") {
                    sock.write_all(&body_for_thread).unwrap();
                }
                sock.flush().ok();
            }
        });

        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-net-test-{port}"));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let dest = dir.join("out.apk");
        let opts = FetchOptions {
            expect_content_type: Some("android.package-archive".into()),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let r = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/redirect"), &dest, &opts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.bytes, body.len() as u64);
        assert_eq!(r.final_url, format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/real.apk"));
        assert_eq!(
            r.sha256,
            hex::encode(Sha256::digest(&body)),
            "digest must cover the bytes actually written"
        );
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&dest).unwrap(), body);
        assert!(looks_like_apk(&dest).unwrap());
        handle.join().unwrap();
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_wrong_content_type() {
        use std::io::Read as _;
        let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let (mut sock, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
            let mut req = [0u8; 2048];
            let _ = sock.read(&mut req);
            use std::io::Write as _;
            sock.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\nhello")
                .unwrap();
        });
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-net-test-ct-{port}"));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let err = fetch(
            &format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/x"),
            &dir.join("x.apk"),
            &FetchOptions {
                expect_content_type: Some("android.package-archive".into()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap_err()
        .to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("content type"), "{err}");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn enforces_the_size_cap() {
        use std::io::Read as _;
        let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let (mut sock, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
            let mut req = [0u8; 2048];
            let _ = sock.read(&mut req);
            use std::io::Write as _;
            sock.write_all(
                b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 100000\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
            )
            .unwrap();
            let junk = vec![b'x'; 100_000];
            sock.write_all(&junk).ok();
        });
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-net-test-cap-{port}"));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let err = fetch(
            &format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/big"),
            &dir.join("big.apk"),
            &FetchOptions {
                max_bytes: 1024,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap_err()
        .to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("limit"), "{err}");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The end-to-end workflow: acquire, analyse, modify, rebuild, sign, install, run.
//!
//! Each step is also usable on its own; [`workflow`] chains them and returns a
//! step-by-step report so an agent can narrate exactly what happened and where
//! it stopped.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};

use crate::adb::{self, AdbDevice, AdbOptions, InstallOptions};
use crate::api;
use crate::crypto;
use crate::key::AdbKey;
use crate::modify::{self, ManifestEdit};
use crate::net::{self, FetchOptions};
use crate::repack;
use crate::sign::{self, ApkSigner, SignOptions};

/// A signing identity that stays stable across runs, so successive builds of
/// the same app share a certificate and can update one another.
pub struct SigningIdentity {
    pub signer: ApkSigner,
    pub key_path: PathBuf,
    pub cert_path: PathBuf,
}

impl SigningIdentity {
    /// Load `<dir>/signing-key.pem` + `signing-cert.der`, generating both on
    /// first use.
    pub fn load_or_create(dir: &Path, cn: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).with_context(|| format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
        let key_path = dir.join("signing-key.pem");
        let cert_path = dir.join("signing-cert.der");

        if key_path.exists() && cert_path.exists() {
            restrict_private_permissions(&key_path)?;
            let pem = std::fs::read_to_string(&key_path)?;
            let key = crypto::from_pkcs8_pem(&pem)?;
            let der = std::fs::read(&cert_path)?;
            let certificate = rustls::pki_types::CertificateDer::from(der.as_slice());
            let parsed = rustls::server::ParsedCertificate::try_from(&certificate)
                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid signing certificate: {e}"))?;
            let key_spki = crypto::spki_der(&key)?;
            if parsed.subject_public_key_info().as_ref() != key_spki {
                bail!(
                    "signing certificate public key does not match {}",
                    key_path.display()
                );
            }
            // The issuer name and serial are derived from the key, so they can
            // be recomputed; only the DER bytes need persisting.
            let mut cert = crypto::self_signed_cert_material(&key, cn, 3650)?;
            cert.der = der;
            return Ok(SigningIdentity {
                signer: ApkSigner { key, cert },
                key_path,
                cert_path,
            });
        }

        let signer = ApkSigner::generate(cn)?;
        write_private_key(&key_path, &crypto::to_pkcs8_pem(&signer.key)?)?;
        std::fs::write(&cert_path, &signer.cert.der)?;
        Ok(SigningIdentity {
            signer,
            key_path,
            cert_path,
        })
    }
}

fn write_private_key(path: &Path, pem: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if path.exists() {
        restrict_private_permissions(path)?;
    }
    let mut options = std::fs::OpenOptions::new();
    options.write(true).create(true).truncate(true);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
        options.mode(0o600);
    }
    let mut file = options
        .open(path)
        .with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
    file.write_all(pem.as_bytes())
        .with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
    file.sync_all()
        .with_context(|| format!("flushing {}", path.display()))?;
    restrict_private_permissions(path)?;
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn restrict_private_permissions(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
    let mut permissions = std::fs::metadata(path)?.permissions();
    permissions.set_mode(0o600);
    std::fs::set_permissions(path, permissions)
        .with_context(|| format!("restricting permissions on {}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn restrict_private_permissions(_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    Ok(())
}

/// One step of the workflow, as reported back.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Step {
    pub name: String,
    pub detail: String,
    pub ok: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct WorkflowReport {
    pub apk: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub steps: Vec<Step>,
}

impl WorkflowReport {
    fn add(&mut self, name: impl Into<String>, detail: impl Into<String>) {
        self.steps.push(Step {
            name: name.into(),
            detail: detail.into(),
            ok: true,
        });
    }

    fn fail(&mut self, name: impl Into<String>, detail: impl Into<String>) {
        self.steps.push(Step {
            name: name.into(),
            detail: detail.into(),
            ok: false,
        });
    }

    pub fn succeeded(&self) -> bool {
        self.steps.iter().all(|s| s.ok)
    }

    pub fn render(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for step in &self.steps {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "{} {:<22} {}\n",
                if step.ok { "ok  " } else { "FAIL" },
                step.name,
                step.detail
            ));
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Fetch an APK from a URL, or accept a local path as-is.
pub fn acquire(source: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<(PathBuf, FetchOptions)> {
    if source.starts_with("http://") || source.starts_with("https://") {
        let name = source
            .rsplit('/')
            .next()
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .unwrap_or("download.apk");
        let name = name.split('?').next().unwrap_or("download.apk");
        let dest = dir.join(sanitise(name));
        let opts = FetchOptions::default();
        let result = net::fetch(source, &dest, &opts)?;
        if !net::looks_like_apk(&dest)? {
            bail!(
                "{} is not a ZIP/APK (first bytes are not PK\\x03\\x04) — got {} bytes of {:?}",
                result.final_url,
                result.bytes,
                result.content_type
            );
        }
        Ok((dest, opts))
    } else {
        let path = PathBuf::from(source);
        if !path.exists() {
            bail!("{} does not exist", path.display());
        }
        Ok((path, FetchOptions::default()))
    }
}

fn sanitise(name: &str) -> String {
    let cleaned: String = name
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '.' || c == '-' || c == '_' {
                c
            } else {
                '_'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if cleaned.is_empty() {
        "download.apk".into()
    } else {
        cleaned
    }
}

/// Analysis of an APK: container summary, decoded manifest, static findings.
pub fn analyze(apk: &Path) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    let path = apk.to_string_lossy().to_string();
    let info = api::info(&path)?;
    let manifest = api::manifest(&path)?;
    let scan = api::scan(&path, "info")?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({
        "apk": path,
        "info": info,
        "manifest": manifest,
        "scan": scan,
    }))
}

/// Apply manifest edits and rebuild the APK, leaving it unsigned.
pub fn modify(apk: &Path, output: &Path, edits: &[ManifestEdit]) -> Result<(Vec<String>, u64)> {
    let entries = repack::read_apk(apk)?;
    let manifest_entry = entries
        .iter()
        .find(|e| e.name == "AndroidManifest.xml")
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("{} has no AndroidManifest.xml", apk.display()))?;
    let (new_manifest, changes) = modify::modify_manifest(&manifest_entry.data, edits)?;
    sign::repack_apk(
        apk,
        output,
        &[("AndroidManifest.xml".to_string(), new_manifest)],
    )?;
    let size = std::fs::metadata(output)?.len();
    Ok((changes, size))
}

/// Sign an APK.
pub fn sign_with(
    apk: &Path,
    output: &Path,
    identity: &SigningIdentity,
    opts: &SignOptions,
) -> Result<sign::SignReport> {
    sign::sign_apk(apk, output, &identity.signer, opts)
}

/// Verify an APK's signatures the way a device would, structurally.
pub fn verify(apk: &Path) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    let v2 = sign::verify_v2(apk)?;
    let v1 = sign::verify_v1(apk)?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({
        "v1": {
            "present": v1.present,
            "signed_entries": v1.signed_entries,
            "x_android_apk_signed": v1.x_android_apk_signed,
        },
        "v2": {
            "present": v2.found,
            "signers": v2.signers,
            "algorithm": format!("{:#06x}", v2.algorithm),
            "digest_ok": v2.digest_ok,
            "signature_ok": v2.signature_ok,
            "certificate_bytes": v2.certificate_bytes,
            "certificate_sha256": v2.certificate_sha256,
            "errors": v2.errors,
        },
        "valid": v2.valid(),
    }))
}

/// Connect to a device and install an APK.
pub fn install(
    apk: &Path,
    target: &str,
    key: &AdbKey,
    opts: &InstallOptions,
) -> Result<(adb::InstallResult, adb::DeviceInfo)> {
    let verification = sign::verify_v2(apk).context("verifying APK before installation")?;
    if !verification.valid() {
        bail!(
            "refusing to install APK whose v2 signature did not verify: {}",
            verification.errors.join("; ")
        );
    }
    let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(target, key, &AdbOptions::default())?;
    let info = device.info.clone();
    let result = device.install(apk, opts)?;
    Ok((result, info))
}

/// Connect and launch a package (or an explicit component).
pub fn launch(target: &str, key: &AdbKey, component: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let mut device = AdbDevice::connect(target, key, &AdbOptions::default())?;
    device.launch(component)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct WorkflowRequest {
    pub source: String,
    pub work_dir: PathBuf,
    pub edits: Vec<ManifestEdit>,
    /// Optional device target; when absent the workflow stops after signing.
    pub device: Option<String>,
    pub launch: bool,
    pub install: bool,
}

/// Run the full workflow and report every step.
pub fn workflow(
    req: &WorkflowRequest,
    identity: &SigningIdentity,
) -> Result<(WorkflowReport, PathBuf)> {
    let mut report = WorkflowReport::default();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&req.work_dir).ok();

    let (apk, _) = acquire(&req.source, &req.work_dir)?;
    report.add("acquire", format!("{}", apk.display()));

    let analysis = analyze(&apk)?;
    let package = analysis["manifest"]["package"]
        .as_str()
        .unwrap_or("?")
        .to_string();
    let findings = analysis["scan"]["counts"]["total"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);
    report.add(
        "analyze",
        format!("{package}: {findings} static finding(s)"),
    );

    let unsigned = req.work_dir.join(format!("{package}-unsigned.apk"));
    let (changes, size) = modify(&apk, &unsigned, &req.edits)?;
    report.add(
        "modify",
        format!(
            "{} change(s) -> {} ({} bytes)",
            changes.len(),
            unsigned.display(),
            size
        ),
    );

    let signed = req.work_dir.join(format!("{package}-signed.apk"));
    let sign_report = sign_with(&unsigned, &signed, identity, &SignOptions::default())?;
    report.add(
        "sign",
        format!(
            "v1={} v2={}, digest {}",
            sign_report.v1,
            sign_report.v2,
            &sign_report.content_digest[..16]
        ),
    );

    let verification = verify(&signed)?;
    let valid = verification["valid"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false);
    if valid {
        report.add("verify", "v2 digest and signature check out");
    } else {
        report.fail("verify", format!("{verification}"));
    }

    if let Some(target) = &req.device {
        if !valid {
            if req.install {
                report.fail("install", "refused: APK verification failed");
            }
            if req.launch {
                report.fail("launch", "refused: APK verification failed");
            }
        } else {
            let key = crate::key::load_or_generate(&crate::key::default_dir())?;
            if req.install {
                match install(&signed, target, &key, &InstallOptions::default()) {
                    Ok((result, info)) => {
                        if result.success {
                            report.add(
                                "install",
                                format!("{} on {} (sdk {:?})", package, info.model(), info.sdk()),
                            );
                        } else {
                            report.fail("install", result.output.trim().replace('\n', " | "));
                        }
                    }
                    Err(e) => report.fail("install", format!("{e:#}")),
                }
            }
            if req.launch {
                match launch(target, &key, &package) {
                    Ok(out) => report.add(
                        "launch",
                        out.lines().next().unwrap_or("started").to_string(),
                    ),
                    Err(e) => report.fail("launch", format!("{e:#}")),
                }
            }
        }
    } else {
        report.add("device", "none given — stopping after signing");
    }

    Ok((report, signed))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn real_apk() -> PathBuf {
        PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("testdata/test-app.apk")
    }

    fn temp_dir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-flow-{tag}-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        dir
    }

    #[test]
    fn signing_identity_is_stable_across_loads() {
        let dir = temp_dir("ident");
        let first = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "mandroid").unwrap();
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            assert_eq!(
                std::fs::metadata(&first.key_path)
                    .unwrap()
                    .permissions()
                    .mode()
                    & 0o777,
                0o600,
                "persisted APK signing key must be owner-only"
            );
        }
        let second = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "mandroid").unwrap();
        // The same certificate bytes and the same public modulus must come back.
        assert_eq!(first.signer.cert.der, second.signer.cert.der);
        assert_eq!(
            crypto::public_numbers(&first.signer.key).0,
            crypto::public_numbers(&second.signer.key).0
        );
        assert_eq!(first.signer.subject(), "mandroid");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn signing_identity_rejects_a_certificate_for_a_different_key() {
        let dir = temp_dir("identity-mismatch");
        let identity = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "original").unwrap();
        let other = ApkSigner::generate("other").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&identity.cert_path, other.cert.der).unwrap();
        let error = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "original")
            .err()
            .expect("mismatched certificate must be rejected");
        assert!(error.to_string().contains("does not match"), "{error:#}");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn acquire_accepts_a_local_path_and_rejects_a_missing_one() {
        let dir = temp_dir("acq");
        assert!(acquire("testdata/test-app.apk", &dir).is_ok());
        let err = acquire("does/not/exist.apk", &dir).unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("does not exist"), "{err}");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    /// The whole point of this module: take a real, signed APK, change its
    /// declared behaviour, rebuild and re-sign it, and confirm the result is
    /// still a valid, verifiable APK whose manifest really did change.
    #[test]
    fn full_modify_and_resign_of_a_real_apk() {
        let apk = real_apk();
        if !apk.exists() {
            eprintln!("skipping: {} not present", apk.display());
            return;
        }
        let dir = temp_dir("e2e");
        let before = crate::api::manifest(&apk.to_string_lossy()).unwrap();
        assert_ne!(
            before["application"]["debuggable"].as_bool(),
            Some(true),
            "the fixture should not already be debuggable"
        );

        // Make it debuggable without changing the package name — an app whose
        // package changed would install alongside rather than replace.
        let unsigned = dir.join("unsigned.apk");
        let (changes, _) = modify(
            &apk,
            &unsigned,
            &[
                ManifestEdit::SetDebuggable(true),
                ManifestEdit::SetAllowBackup(true),
            ],
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(changes.len(), 2);

        let identity = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "mandroid e2e").unwrap();
        let signed = dir.join("signed.apk");
        let report = sign_with(&unsigned, &signed, &identity, &SignOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(report.v1 && report.v2);
        assert_eq!(
            report.removed_signatures, 0,
            "the rebuilt APK carried no signatures"
        );

        // Our own verifier must accept it...
        let verification = verify(&signed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            verification["valid"], true,
            "signed APK must verify: {verification}"
        );
        assert_eq!(verification["v2"]["digest_ok"], true);
        assert_eq!(verification["v2"]["signature_ok"], true);
        // ...and so must an independent ZIP reader.
        let archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(std::fs::File::open(&signed).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(archive.len() >= 15, "entries should survive the rebuild");

        // The modification must be visible in the signed APK's manifest.
        let after = crate::api::manifest(&signed.to_string_lossy()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(after["application"]["debuggable"], true);
        assert_eq!(after["application"]["allow_backup"], true);
        assert_eq!(
            after["package"], before["package"],
            "the package name must not change or the install would be a different app"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            after["components"].as_array().map(|a| a.len()),
            before["components"].as_array().map(|a| a.len()),
            "every component must survive the manifest round-trip"
        );

        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_preset_drives_the_same_pipeline() {
        let apk = real_apk();
        if !apk.exists() {
            return;
        }
        let dir = temp_dir("preset");
        let edits = modify::preset("debug").unwrap();
        let unsigned = dir.join("u.apk");
        let (changes, _) = modify(&apk, &unsigned, &edits).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(changes.len(), edits.len());

        let identity = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "preset").unwrap();
        let signed = dir.join("s.apk");
        sign_with(&unsigned, &signed, &identity, &SignOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(verify(&signed).unwrap()["valid"].as_bool().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(
            crate::api::manifest(&signed.to_string_lossy()).unwrap()["application"]["debuggable"],
            true
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn verify_reports_a_v2_only_or_v1_only_apk_honestly() {
        let dir = temp_dir("unverified");
        let unsigned = dir.join("plain.apk");
        let entries = vec![repack::Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![3, 0, 8, 0])];
        let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            &unsigned,
            repack::assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, 1),
        )
        .unwrap();

        let report = verify(&unsigned).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report["v2"]["present"], false);
        assert_eq!(report["v1"]["present"], false);
        assert_eq!(report["valid"], false, "an unsigned APK is not valid");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn direct_install_refuses_an_unverified_apk_before_connecting() {
        let dir = temp_dir("install-unverified");
        let unsigned = dir.join("unsigned.apk");
        let entries = vec![repack::Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![3, 0, 8, 0])];
        let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            &unsigned,
            repack::assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, 1),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let adb_key = crate::key::generate_at(&dir.join("adb")).unwrap();
        let error = install(
            &unsigned,
            "127.0.0.1:1",
            &adb_key,
            &InstallOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            error.to_string().contains("refusing to install"),
            "{error:#}"
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn workflow_stops_after_signing_when_no_device_is_given() {
        let apk = real_apk();
        if !apk.exists() {
            return;
        }
        let dir = temp_dir("wf");
        let identity = SigningIdentity::load_or_create(&dir, "wf").unwrap();
        let req = WorkflowRequest {
            source: apk.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
            work_dir: dir.clone(),
            edits: vec![ManifestEdit::SetDebuggable(true)],
            device: None,
            install: false,
            launch: false,
        };
        let (report, signed) = workflow(&req, &identity).unwrap();
        assert!(report.succeeded(), "{}", report.render());
        let names: Vec<&str> = report.steps.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            names,
            vec!["acquire", "analyze", "modify", "sign", "verify", "device"]
        );
        assert!(signed.exists());
        assert!(verify(&signed).unwrap()["valid"].as_bool().unwrap());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }
}
```

```rust
//! ZIP read/rebuild for APK packaging.
//!
//! The `zip` crate reads entries for us, but signing needs byte-exact control
//! over the layout — the APK Signing Block is spliced between the last entry and
//! the central directory, and the signature covers each of those regions
//! separately. So we build the archive ourselves and hand the caller the three
//! regions the APK signature schemes digest.

use std::io::Read;
use std::path::Path;

use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Context, Result};
use flate2::write::DeflateEncoder;
use flate2::Compression;
use std::io::Write;

use crate::util::crc32;

/// One entry of an APK, decompressed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Entry {
    pub name: String,
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    /// 0 = stored, 8 = deflate.
    pub method: u16,
    pub dos_time: u16,
    pub dos_date: u16,
}

impl Entry {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, data: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
        Entry {
            name: name.into(),
            data,
            method: 8,
            dos_time: 0,
            dos_date: 0x21, // 1980-01-01, the ZIP epoch
        }
    }

    /// Entries that must not be compressed: the resource table (required
    /// uncompressed from API 30) and native libraries (kept uncompressed so a
    /// `extractNativeLibs=false` APK stays installable).
    pub fn must_stay_stored(&self) -> bool {
        self.name == "resources.arsc" || self.name.ends_with(".so")
    }

    pub fn is_signature_file(&self) -> bool {
        let upper = self.name.to_ascii_uppercase();
        if !upper.starts_with("META-INF/") {
            return false;
        }
        upper == "META-INF/MANIFEST.MF"
            || upper.ends_with(".SF")
            || upper.ends_with(".RSA")
            || upper.ends_with(".DSA")
            || upper.ends_with(".EC")
    }

    fn encoded(&self) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, u16)> {
        if self.method == 0 || self.must_stay_stored() {
            return Ok((self.data.clone(), 0));
        }
        let mut encoder = DeflateEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::new(6));
        encoder.write_all(&self.data)?;
        let compressed = encoder.finish()?;
        // If deflating made it bigger, storing is the better legal choice.
        if compressed.len() >= self.data.len() {
            Ok((self.data.clone(), 0))
        } else {
            Ok((compressed, 8))
        }
    }
}

/// Read every entry of an APK, decompressed, keeping the original method hint.
pub fn read_apk(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<Entry>> {
    let file = std::fs::File::open(path).with_context(|| format!("opening {}", path.display()))?;
    let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(file)
        .with_context(|| format!("reading {} as a ZIP/APK", path.display()))?;
    let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(archive.len());
    for i in 0..archive.len() {
        let mut member = archive.by_index(i)?;
        if member.is_dir() {
            continue;
        }
        let name = member.name().to_string();
        let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(member.size() as usize);
        member
            .read_to_end(&mut data)
            .with_context(|| format!("decompressing {name}"))?;
        entries.push(Entry {
            name,
            data,
            method: match member.compression() {
                zip::CompressionMethod::Stored => 0,
                _ => 8,
            },
            dos_time: member.last_modified().map(dos_time_of).unwrap_or(0),
            dos_date: member.last_modified().map(dos_date_of).unwrap_or(0x21),
        });
    }
    if entries.is_empty() {
        bail!("{} contains no entries", path.display());
    }
    Ok(entries)
}

fn dos_time_of(dt: zip::DateTime) -> u16 {
    ((dt.hour() as u16) << 11) | ((dt.minute() as u16) << 5) | (dt.second() as u16 / 2)
}

fn dos_date_of(dt: zip::DateTime) -> u16 {
    (((dt.year() as u16).saturating_sub(1980)) << 9) | ((dt.month() as u16) << 5) | dt.day() as u16
}

/// The three ZIP regions an APK signature covers, plus the raw EOCD record.
///
/// `content` is everything before where the signing block goes; `central_directory`
/// and `eocd` follow it. The signing block is spliced between `content` and
/// `central_directory`, and the EOCD has to be rewritten once its final size is
/// known — hence [`eocd`] being a separate function.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sections {
    pub content: Vec<u8>,
    pub central_directory: Vec<u8>,
    pub eocd: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Build the archive regions with no signing block.
pub fn build_sections(entries: &[Entry]) -> Result<Sections> {
    let mut content = Vec::new();
    let mut central = Vec::new();
    let mut count: u16 = 0;

    for entry in entries {
        let (payload, method) = entry.encoded()?;
        let name = entry.name.as_bytes();
        let crc = crc32(&entry.data);
        let offset = content.len() as u32;

        // Align stored payloads (notably resources.arsc) to 4 bytes, which is
        // what the platform expects for the resource table.
        let mut extra: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        if method == 0 {
            let pad = (4 - ((content.len() + 30 + name.len()) % 4)) % 4;
            // `pad` is always in 0..=3 by construction.
            debug_assert!(pad <= 3, "alignment pad is at most 3 bytes");
            if pad > 0 {
                // A self-describing ZIP extra field: id 0xd935 (Android's
                // alignment field), data_size = `pad` (declares the field
                // body is exactly `pad` bytes long), then `pad` zero bytes
                // which double as the alignment padding itself. Total
                // field = 4 + pad bytes; combined with the 30-byte fixed
                // local-header prefix and the name, the data offset lands
                // on a 4-byte boundary by construction:
                //   (30 + name.len() + 4 + pad) ≡ (30 + name.len() + pad) ≡ 0 (mod 4).
                extra.push(0x35);
                extra.push(0xd9);
                extra.extend_from_slice(&(pad as u16).to_le_bytes());
                for _ in 0..pad {
                    extra.push(0);
                }
            }
        }

        let mut local = Vec::with_capacity(30 + name.len() + extra.len() + payload.len());
        local.extend_from_slice(&0x04034b50u32.to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&20u16.to_le_bytes()); // version needed
        local.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // flags
        local.extend_from_slice(&method.to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&entry.dos_time.to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&entry.dos_date.to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&(entry.data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&(name.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(&(extra.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
        local.extend_from_slice(name);
        local.extend_from_slice(&extra);
        local.extend_from_slice(&payload);
        content.extend_from_slice(&local);

        central.extend_from_slice(&0x02014b50u32.to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&20u16.to_le_bytes()); // version made by
        central.extend_from_slice(&20u16.to_le_bytes()); // version needed
        central.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // flags
        central.extend_from_slice(&method.to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&entry.dos_time.to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&entry.dos_date.to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&(entry.data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&(name.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&(extra.len() as u16).to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // comment length
        central.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // disk number start
        central.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // internal attributes
        central.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // external attributes
        central.extend_from_slice(&offset.to_le_bytes());
        central.extend_from_slice(name);
        central.extend_from_slice(&extra);

        count += 1;
    }

    let eocd = eocd(content.len() as u32, central.len() as u32, count);
    Ok(Sections {
        content,
        central_directory: central,
        eocd,
    })
}

/// Build the ZIP End of Central Directory record.
pub fn eocd(cd_offset: u32, cd_size: u32, entries: u16) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(22);
    out.extend_from_slice(&0x06054b50u32.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // this disk
    out.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // disk with CD
    out.extend_from_slice(&entries.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&entries.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&cd_size.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&cd_offset.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // comment length
    out
}

/// Assemble the final file: content, optional signing block, central directory,
/// End of Central Directory.
pub fn assemble(content: &[u8], block: Option<&[u8]>, cd: &[u8], entries: u16) -> Vec<u8> {
    let block_len = block.map(|b| b.len() as u32).unwrap_or(0);
    let cd_offset = content.len() as u32 + block_len;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(content.len() + block_len as usize + cd.len() + 22);
    out.extend_from_slice(content);
    if let Some(b) = block {
        out.extend_from_slice(b);
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(cd);
    out.extend_from_slice(&eocd(cd_offset, cd.len() as u32, entries));
    out
}

/// Locate the APK Signing Block. Returns `(offset of the block's first size
/// field, start of the ID-value pairs, block size)`.
pub fn find_signing_block(data: &[u8]) -> Option<(usize, usize, u64)> {
    const MAGIC: &[u8; 16] = b"APK Sig Block 42";
    if data.len() < 22 + 32 {
        return None;
    }
    let eocd_off = data.len() - 22;
    if &data[eocd_off..eocd_off + 4] != b"PK\x05\x06" {
        return None;
    }
    let cd_off = u32::from_le_bytes(data[eocd_off + 16..eocd_off + 20].try_into().ok()?) as usize;
    if cd_off < 32 || cd_off > data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    if &data[cd_off - 16..cd_off] != MAGIC {
        return None;
    }
    let size = u64::from_le_bytes(data[cd_off - 24..cd_off - 16].try_into().ok()?);
    let start = (cd_off as u64).checked_sub(size + 8)? as usize;
    let leading = u64::from_le_bytes(data[start..start + 8].try_into().ok()?);
    if leading != size {
        return None;
    }
    Some((start, start + 8, size))
}

/// Split a signed APK into the three regions a signature covers.
/// Returns `(content, central_directory, eocd_off)`.
pub fn split_signed(data: &[u8]) -> Result<(usize, usize, usize)> {
    let eocd_off = data.len() - 22;
    if &data[eocd_off..eocd_off + 4] != b"PK\x05\x06" {
        bail!("no ZIP End of Central Directory at the end of the file");
    }
    let cd_off =
        u32::from_le_bytes(data[eocd_off + 16..eocd_off + 20].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
    let (block_start, _, _) =
        find_signing_block(data).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("no APK Signing Block found"))?;
    Ok((block_start, cd_off, eocd_off))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample() -> Vec<Entry> {
        vec![
            Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![0x03, 0x00, 0x08, 0x00]),
            Entry::new(
                "classes.dex",
                (0..5000u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect(),
            ),
            Entry::new("resources.arsc", vec![0x02, 0x00, 0x0c, 0x00, 0xff]),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn crc32_of_a_zip_entry_is_computed_over_uncompressed_data() {
        assert_eq!(crc32(b""), 0);
        assert_eq!(crc32(b"abc"), 0x3524_41c2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn built_archive_is_readable_by_a_zip_reader() {
        let entries = sample();
        let sections = build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        let bytes = assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, 3);
        let mut archive = zip::ZipArchive::new(std::io::Cursor::new(bytes)).expect("valid zip");
        assert_eq!(archive.len(), 3);
        let mut dex = Vec::new();
        archive
            .by_name("classes.dex")
            .unwrap()
            .read_to_end(&mut dex)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(dex, entries[1].data, "deflate round-trip must be lossless");
        let mut arsc = Vec::new();
        archive
            .by_name("resources.arsc")
            .unwrap()
            .read_to_end(&mut arsc)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(arsc, entries[2].data);
    }

    #[test]
    fn resources_arsc_is_stored_uncompressed() {
        let entries = vec![Entry::new("resources.arsc", vec![7u8; 4096])];
        let sections = build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        // Find the local header and check the method field.
        assert_eq!(&sections.content[0..4], &0x04034b50u32.to_le_bytes());
        let method = u16::from_le_bytes([sections.content[8], sections.content[9]]);
        assert_eq!(method, 0, "resources.arsc must be stored, not deflated");
    }

    #[test]
    fn signature_entries_are_recognised_for_removal() {
        assert!(Entry::new("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF", vec![]).is_signature_file());
        assert!(Entry::new("META-INF/CERT.SF", vec![]).is_signature_file());
        assert!(Entry::new("META-INF/CERT.RSA", vec![]).is_signature_file());
        assert!(Entry::new("META-INF/cert.rsa", vec![]).is_signature_file());
        assert!(!Entry::new("META-INF/services/foo", vec![]).is_signature_file());
        assert!(!Entry::new("classes.dex", vec![]).is_signature_file());
    }

    #[test]
    fn eocd_points_at_the_central_directory_it_was_given() {
        let e = eocd(1234, 567, 9);
        assert_eq!(e.len(), 22);
        assert_eq!(&e[0..4], b"PK\x05\x06");
        assert_eq!(u16::from_le_bytes([e[8], e[9]]), 9);
        assert_eq!(u32::from_le_bytes(e[12..16].try_into().unwrap()), 567);
        assert_eq!(u32::from_le_bytes(e[16..20].try_into().unwrap()), 1234);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Static analysis rule engine.
//!
//! The rules table owns the judgement (severity, CWE, wording); this file owns
//! the mechanics. Same split as the dbx taxonomy: knowledge is data, so it can
//! be corrected without a rebuild.

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use regex::Regex;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::manifest::{Component, Manifest};

pub const EMBEDDED: &str = include_str!("../data/android-rules.json");

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Rules {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub version: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub secret_patterns: Vec<SecretPattern>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub rules: Vec<Rule>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct SecretPattern {
    pub id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub severity: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub cwe: Option<String>,
    pub regex: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub severity: String,
    pub category: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub cwe: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub detail: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub remediation: String,
    pub check: Check,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Check {
    /// An application-level boolean flag must equal `equals`.
    ApplicationFlag {
        flag: String,
        equals: bool,
    },
    /// An attribute must be explicitly false (absent counts as a failure).
    AttributeNotFalse {
        attribute: String,
    },
    AttributeAbsent {
        attribute: String,
    },
    SdkBelow {
        field: String,
        value: i32,
    },
    ExportedComponent {
        component: String,
    },
    ProviderGrantUri,
    ImplicitExportComponent,
    DangerousPermission {
        permissions: Vec<String>,
    },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Finding {
    pub id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub severity: String,
    pub category: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub cwe: Option<String>,
    /// Component or attribute the finding is about.
    pub subject: String,
    pub detail: String,
    pub remediation: String,
    pub evidence: String,
}

pub fn severity_rank(s: &str) -> u8 {
    match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
        "critical" => 4,
        "high" => 3,
        "medium" => 2,
        "low" => 1,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

impl Rules {
    pub fn load() -> Result<Rules> {
        let text = match std::env::var("DROID_RULES") {
            Ok(p) if !p.trim().is_empty() => std::fs::read_to_string(p.trim())
                .with_context(|| format!("reading DROID_RULES {p}"))?,
            _ => EMBEDDED.to_string(),
        };
        serde_json::from_str(&text).context("parsing android-rules.json")
    }
}

fn app_flag(m: &Manifest, flag: &str) -> Option<bool> {
    match flag {
        "debuggable" => Some(m.application.debuggable),
        "allow_backup" => m.application.allow_backup,
        "uses_cleartext_traffic" => m.application.uses_cleartext_traffic,
        "request_legacy_external_storage" => m.application.request_legacy_external_storage,
        "extract_native_libs" => m.application.extract_native_libs,
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn make(r: &Rule, subject: String, evidence: String) -> Finding {
    Finding {
        id: r.id.clone(),
        title: r.title.clone(),
        severity: r.severity.clone(),
        category: r.category.clone(),
        cwe: r.cwe.clone(),
        subject,
        detail: r.detail.clone(),
        remediation: r.remediation.clone(),
        evidence,
    }
}

/// Run every rule against a decoded manifest (and, optionally, DEX strings).
pub fn scan(m: &Manifest, rules: &Rules, dex_strings: &[String]) -> Vec<Finding> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();

    for r in &rules.rules {
        match &r.check {
            Check::ApplicationFlag { flag, equals } => {
                if let Some(v) = app_flag(m, flag) {
                    if v == *equals {
                        out.push(make(r, "application".into(), format!("{flag}={v}")));
                    }
                }
            }
            Check::AttributeNotFalse { attribute } => {
                // Absent or true both fail: the safe state is an explicit false.
                let v = app_flag(m, attribute).unwrap_or(true);
                if v {
                    let shown = match app_flag(m, attribute) {
                        Some(b) => format!("{attribute}={b}"),
                        None => format!("{attribute} not set (defaults to true)"),
                    };
                    out.push(make(r, "application".into(), shown));
                }
            }
            Check::AttributeAbsent { attribute } => {
                let present = match attribute.as_str() {
                    "networkSecurityConfig" => m.application.network_security_config.is_some(),
                    "dataExtractionRules" => false,
                    _ => false,
                };
                if !present {
                    out.push(make(r, "application".into(), format!("{attribute} absent")));
                }
            }
            Check::SdkBelow { field, value } => {
                let got = match field.as_str() {
                    "min_sdk" => m.min_sdk,
                    "target_sdk" => m.target_sdk,
                    _ => None,
                };
                if let Some(v) = got {
                    if v < *value {
                        out.push(make(
                            r,
                            "manifest".into(),
                            format!("{field}={v} (< {value})"),
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
            Check::ExportedComponent { component } => {
                for c in m.components.iter().filter(|c| &c.kind == component) {
                    if c.effectively_exported && !c.has_permission_guard() {
                        out.push(make(r, c.name.clone(), describe(c)));
                    }
                }
            }
            Check::ProviderGrantUri => {
                for c in m.components.iter().filter(|c| c.is_provider()) {
                    if c.effectively_exported && c.grant_uri_permissions == Some(true) {
                        out.push(make(r, c.name.clone(), describe(c)));
                    }
                }
            }
            Check::ImplicitExportComponent => {
                for c in m.components.iter() {
                    if c.implicitly_exported {
                        out.push(make(
                            r,
                            c.name.clone(),
                            format!("{}: intent filters but no android:exported", c.kind),
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
            Check::DangerousPermission { permissions } => {
                for p in &m.permissions {
                    if permissions.iter().any(|d| d == p) {
                        out.push(make(r, p.clone(), format!("declared {p}")));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Hardcoded secrets in the DEX string pool.
    for sp in &rules.secret_patterns {
        let Ok(re) = Regex::new(&sp.regex) else {
            continue;
        };
        for s in dex_strings {
            if let Some(mt) = re.find(s) {
                // Never echo a full secret back into a report.
                let hit = mt.as_str();
                let shown = if hit.len() > 12 {
                    format!("{}…({} chars)", &hit[..8], hit.len())
                } else {
                    format!("<{} chars>", hit.len())
                };
                out.push(Finding {
                    id: format!("secret-{}", sp.id),
                    title: sp.title.clone(),
                    severity: sp.severity.clone(),
                    category: "hardcoded-secret".into(),
                    cwe: sp.cwe.clone(),
                    subject: "dex".into(),
                    detail: format!(
                        "A string in the DEX pool matches the {} pattern. Hardcoded credentials in an APK are extractable by anyone who has the file.",
                        sp.title.to_lowercase()
                    ),
                    remediation: "Move the secret server-side, rotate it, and load it at runtime."
                        .into(),
                    evidence: shown,
                });
                break; // one hit per pattern is enough to raise the finding
            }
        }
    }

    out.sort_by(|a, b| {
        severity_rank(&b.severity)
            .cmp(&severity_rank(&a.severity))
            .then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
    });
    out.dedup_by(|a, b| a.id == b.id && a.subject == b.subject);
    out
}

fn describe(c: &Component) -> String {
    match (&c.exported, c.permission.as_deref()) {
        (Some(true), _) => format!("{}: exported=true", c.kind),
        (None, _) => format!("{}: exported implied by intent filter", c.kind),
        _ => format!("{}", c.kind),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::axml::{Attr, AttrValue, Node};

    fn n(name: &str, attrs: &[(&str, AttrValue)]) -> Node {
        Node {
            name: name.into(),
            namespace: None,
            attrs: attrs
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| Attr {
                    namespace: Some("android".into()),
                    name: (*k).into(),
                    value: v.clone(),
                })
                .collect(),
            children: vec![],
            line: 0,
        }
    }

    fn manifest_with(children: Vec<Node>) -> Manifest {
        let root = Node {
            name: "manifest".into(),
            namespace: None,
            attrs: vec![Attr {
                namespace: None,
                name: "package".into(),
                value: AttrValue::Str("com.test".into()),
            }],
            children,
            line: 0,
        };
        Manifest::from_node(&root)
    }

    #[test]
    fn embedded_rules_parse_and_are_unique() {
        let r = Rules::load().unwrap();
        assert!(
            r.rules.len() >= 12,
            "expected a real rule set, got {}",
            r.rules.len()
        );
        let mut ids: Vec<&str> = r.rules.iter().map(|x| x.id.as_str()).collect();
        ids.sort();
        let before = ids.len();
        ids.dedup();
        assert_eq!(before, ids.len(), "duplicate rule ids");
        // `info` is a legitimate severity and ranks 0, so validate the
        // vocabulary rather than the rank.
        for rule in &r.rules {
            assert!(
                matches!(
                    rule.severity.as_str(),
                    "critical" | "high" | "medium" | "low" | "info"
                ),
                "{} has an unknown severity {:?}",
                rule.id,
                rule.severity
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn debuggable_and_cleartext_are_flagged() {
        let app = n(
            "application",
            &[
                ("debuggable", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
                ("usesCleartextTraffic", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
            ],
        );
        let m = manifest_with(vec![
            n(
                "uses-sdk",
                &[
                    ("minSdkVersion", AttrValue::Int(21)),
                    ("targetSdkVersion", AttrValue::Int(30)),
                ],
            ),
            app,
        ]);
        let f = scan(&m, &Rules::load().unwrap(), &[]);
        let ids: Vec<&str> = f.iter().map(|x| x.id.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(ids.contains(&"app-debuggable"));
        assert!(ids.contains(&"cleartext-traffic"));
        assert!(ids.contains(&"min-sdk-too-low"));
        assert!(ids.contains(&"target-sdk-too-low"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn exported_components_without_guards_are_flagged_and_guarded_ones_are_not() {
        let open = n(
            "provider",
            &[
                ("name", AttrValue::Str(".Open".into())),
                ("exported", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
            ],
        );
        let guarded = n(
            "provider",
            &[
                ("name", AttrValue::Str(".Guarded".into())),
                ("exported", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
                ("readPermission", AttrValue::Str("com.test.READ".into())),
            ],
        );
        let m = manifest_with(vec![open, guarded]);
        let f = scan(&m, &Rules::load().unwrap(), &[]);
        let subjects: Vec<&str> = f
            .iter()
            .filter(|x| x.id == "exported-provider-no-permission")
            .map(|x| x.subject.as_str())
            .collect();
        assert!(subjects.contains(&".Open"));
        assert!(
            !subjects.contains(&".Guarded"),
            "a permission guard must suppress the finding"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn implicit_export_is_reported_separately() {
        let mut act = n("activity", &[("name", AttrValue::Str(".Implicit".into()))]);
        act.children.push(n("intent-filter", &[]));
        let m = manifest_with(vec![act]);
        let f = scan(&m, &Rules::load().unwrap(), &[]);
        let ids: Vec<&str> = f.iter().map(|x| x.id.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(ids.contains(&"implicit-export"));
        assert!(ids.contains(&"exported-activity-no-permission"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn secrets_are_detected_and_never_echoed_in_full() {
        let m = manifest_with(vec![]);
        let strings = vec![
            "com.example.app".to_string(),
            "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE".to_string(),
            "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----".to_string(),
        ];
        let f = scan(&m, &Rules::load().unwrap(), &strings);
        let sec: Vec<&Finding> = f
            .iter()
            .filter(|x| x.category == "hardcoded-secret")
            .collect();
        assert!(
            sec.len() >= 2,
            "expected aws + private key, got {:?}",
            sec.iter().map(|s| &s.id).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        for s in &sec {
            assert!(
                !s.evidence.contains("AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"),
                "full secret leaked: {}",
                s.evidence
            );
            assert!(
                !s.evidence.contains("PRIVATE KEY-----"),
                "full secret leaked: {}",
                s.evidence
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn findings_sort_worst_first() {
        let app = n("application", &[("debuggable", AttrValue::Bool(true))]);
        let prov = n(
            "provider",
            &[
                ("name", AttrValue::Str(".P".into())),
                ("exported", AttrValue::Bool(true)),
            ],
        );
        let m = manifest_with(vec![app, prov]);
        let f = scan(&m, &Rules::load().unwrap(), &[]);
        let ranks: Vec<u8> = f.iter().map(|x| severity_rank(&x.severity)).collect();
        let mut sorted = ranks.clone();
        sorted.sort_by(|a, b| b.cmp(a));
        assert_eq!(ranks, sorted);
        assert_eq!(
            f[0].severity, "critical",
            "exported provider is the worst finding here"
        );
    }
}
```
