## `crates/server/mandroid/src/screen.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/mandroid/src/screen.rs)

```rust
//! Resizable, adjustable screen: geometry read/override/reset and PNG
//! capture with box-filter rescaling.
//!
//! Two halves:
//!
//! * **Geometry** — `wm size` / `wm density` over the native ADB shell.
//!   Android reports `Physical` and `Override` lines; the effective geometry
//!   is the Override when present. `set_size` / `set_density` apply overrides
//!   (the agent's resize lever), `reset` clears them back to the panel.
//! * **Capture** — `screencap -p` (PNG straight off the device), then an
//!   optional rescale: decode → normalize to RGBA8 → box-filter (area
//!   average) → re-encode. The agent can therefore capture at native size and
//!   deliver at any size, which is exactly what a model wants.

use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};

use crate::adb::AdbDevice;

/// Effective screen geometry (px + density).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Geometry {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub density: u32,
}

/// Sane bounds so a typo cannot send `wm size` into a 0x0 or 64K screen.
pub const MIN_SIDE_PX: u32 = 1;
pub const MAX_SIDE_PX: u32 = 16384;
pub const MIN_DENSITY: u32 = 16;
pub const MAX_DENSITY: u32 = 4096;

/// Read the effective geometry. `Override` wins over `Physical`, matching what
/// Android itself renders with. Missing density falls back to the device
/// profile default (440).
pub fn get_geometry(device: &mut AdbDevice) -> Result<Geometry> {
    let size = device.shell("wm size")?;
    let density = device.shell("wm density")?;
    let (width, height) =
        parse_wm_size(&size).context("`wm size` did not report a WxH geometry")?;
    let d = parse_wm_density(&density).unwrap_or(440);
    Ok(Geometry {
        width,
        height,
        density: d,
    })
}

/// Apply a resolution override (`wm size WxH`). Returns the effective geometry.
pub fn set_size(device: &mut AdbDevice, width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Geometry> {
    for (label, v) in [("width", width), ("height", height)] {
        if !(MIN_SIDE_PX..=MAX_SIDE_PX).contains(&v) {
            bail!("{label} {v} out of range ({MIN_SIDE_PX}..={MAX_SIDE_PX})");
        }
    }
    device.shell(&format!("wm size {width}x{height}"))?;
    get_geometry(device)
}

/// Apply a density override (`wm density DPI`). Returns the effective geometry.
pub fn set_density(device: &mut AdbDevice, density: u32) -> Result<Geometry> {
    if !(MIN_DENSITY..=MAX_DENSITY).contains(&density) {
        bail!("density {density} out of range ({MIN_DENSITY}..={MAX_DENSITY})");
    }
    device.shell(&format!("wm density {density}"))?;
    get_geometry(device)
}

/// Clear all overrides — back to the physical panel.
pub fn reset(device: &mut AdbDevice) -> Result<Geometry> {
    device.shell("wm size reset")?;
    device.shell("wm density reset")?;
    get_geometry(device)
}

/// Parse `wm size` output. Both lines are accepted; `Override` wins.
/// Format: `Physical size: 1080x2400` (optionally with `Override size: ...`).
pub fn parse_wm_size(out: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    let mut physical = None;
    let mut override_ = None;
    for line in out.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        let (label, rest) = if let Some(r) = line.strip_prefix("Override size:") {
            ("o", r.trim())
        } else if let Some(r) = line.strip_prefix("Physical size:") {
            ("p", r.trim())
        } else {
            continue;
        };
        // Some builds append a rotation marker like `1080x2400:rot0`; the
        // digits we want are the leading WxH token.
        // Some builds append a rotation marker like `1080x2400:rot0` with no
        // whitespace; cut at the first ':' as well.
        let token = rest
            .split_whitespace()
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("")
            .split(':')
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("");
        let mut it = token.split('x');
        let (w, h) = (it.next()?, it.next()?);
        let parsed = (w.parse::<u32>().ok()?, h.parse::<u32>().ok()?);
        if label == "o" {
            override_ = Some(parsed);
        } else {
            physical = Some(parsed);
        }
    }
    override_.or(physical)
}

/// Parse `wm density` output; `Override` wins. Returns raw dpi.
pub fn parse_wm_density(out: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let mut best: Option<u32> = None;
    for line in out.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        let val = if let Some(r) = line.strip_prefix("Override density:") {
            r.trim()
        } else if let Some(r) = line.strip_prefix("Physical density:") {
            r.trim()
        } else {
            continue;
        };
        let token = val.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("");
        if let Ok(d) = token.parse::<u32>() {
            let is_override = line.starts_with("Override");
            if is_override {
                return Some(d);
            }
            best = Some(d);
        }
    }
    best
}

/// Capture the screen and optionally rescale: `scale` multiplies (must be in
/// (0, 1] — growing beyond the panel adds no information), `target_width`
/// forces an exact width with the height keeping aspect and wins over scale.
/// Returns the (possibly resized) PNG bytes and the captured source size.
pub fn capture(
    device: &mut AdbDevice,
    scale: Option<f32>,
    target_width: Option<u32>,
) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, (u32, u32))> {
    let png = device.screencap()?;
    let src = png_dimensions(&png).context("screencap output is not a PNG")?;
    if let Some(w) = target_width {
        if w == 0 || w > MAX_SIDE_PX {
            bail!("target width {w} out of range (1..={MAX_SIDE_PX})");
        }
        if w == src.0 {
            return Ok((png, src));
        }
        let h = ((src.1 as u64 * w as u64) / src.0 as u64).max(1) as u32;
        let out = reshape_bytes(&png, w, h)?;
        return Ok((out, src));
    }
    if let Some(s) = scale {
        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&s) || s == 0.0 {
            bail!("scale {s} out of range (0,1]");
        }
        if (s - 1.0).abs() < f32::EPSILON {
            return Ok((png, src));
        }
        let w = ((src.0 as f32 * s).round() as u32).clamp(1, MAX_SIDE_PX);
        let h = ((src.1 as f32 * s).round() as u32).clamp(1, MAX_SIDE_PX);
        let out = reshape_bytes(&png, w, h)?;
        return Ok((out, src));
    }
    Ok((png, src))
}

/// [`capture`] straight to a file.
pub fn capture_to_file(
    device: &mut AdbDevice,
    path: &str,
    scale: Option<f32>,
    target_width: Option<u32>,
) -> Result<(u32, u32)> {
    let (png, src) = capture(device, scale, target_width)?;
    std::fs::write(path, &png).with_context(|| format!("writing {path}"))?;
    Ok(src)
}

/// PNG signature + IHDR width/height sniff (big-endian at fixed offsets) —
/// enough to know a screencap's size without a full decode.
pub fn png_dimensions(png: &[u8]) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    const SIG: [u8; 8] = [0x89, b'P', b'N', b'G', 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a];
    if png.len() < 24 || png[..8] != SIG || &png[12..16] != b"IHDR" {
        return None;
    }
    let w = u32::from_be_bytes([png[16], png[17], png[18], png[19]]);
    let h = u32::from_be_bytes([png[20], png[21], png[22], png[23]]);
    Some((w, h))
}

/// Decode a PNG, resample to `width x height` with a box filter, re-encode.
pub fn resize_png(png: &[u8], width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    if width == 0 || height == 0 || width > MAX_SIDE_PX || height > MAX_SIDE_PX {
        bail!("target {width}x{height} out of range");
    }
    reshape_bytes(png, width, height)
}

/// Device-less core of the rescale pipeline.
fn reshape_bytes(png: &[u8], width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let decoder = png::Decoder::new(std::io::Cursor::new(png));
    let mut reader = decoder.read_info().context("decoding PNG")?;
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; reader.output_buffer_size()];
    let info = reader.next_frame(&mut buf).context("reading PNG frame")?;
    let (sw, sh) = (info.width, info.height);
    let src = &buf[..info.buffer_size()];

    // Normalize any input layout to RGBA8.
    let rgba: Vec<u8> = match info.color_type {
        png::ColorType::Rgba => src.to_vec(),
        png::ColorType::Rgb => src
            .chunks_exact(3)
            .flat_map(|c| [c[0], c[1], c[2], 0xff])
            .collect(),
        png::ColorType::Grayscale => src.iter().flat_map(|g| [*g, *g, *g, 0xff]).collect(),
        png::ColorType::GrayscaleAlpha => src
            .chunks_exact(2)
            .flat_map(|g| [g[0], g[0], g[0], g[1]])
            .collect(),
        other => bail!("unsupported PNG colour type {other:?}"),
    };

    let out_rgba = if (width, height) == (sw, sh) {
        rgba
    } else {
        box_filter(&rgba, sw, sh, width, height)
    };

    encode_png(&out_rgba, width, height)
}

/// Area-average (box) resample over RGBA8: each destination pixel averages
/// every source pixel that overlaps it. Sharp on downscale (the capture
/// deliver path), acceptable on the rare upscale, and simple enough to be
/// obviously correct.
pub fn box_filter(src: &[u8], sw: u32, sh: u32, dw: u32, dh: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = vec![0u8; (dw * dh * 4) as usize];
    let (sx, sy) = (sw as f64 / dw as f64, sh as f64 / dh as f64);
    for dy in 0..dh {
        let y0 = (dy as f64 * sy).floor() as u32;
        let y1 = (((dy + 1) as f64 * sy).ceil() as u32).clamp(y0 + 1, sh);
        for dx in 0..dw {
            let x0 = (dx as f64 * sx).floor() as u32;
            let x1 = (((dx + 1) as f64 * sx).ceil() as u32).clamp(x0 + 1, sw);
            let (mut r, mut g, mut b, mut a) = (0u64, 0u64, 0u64, 0u64);
            for y in y0..y1 {
                for x in x0..x1 {
                    let i = ((y * sw + x) * 4) as usize;
                    r += src[i] as u64;
                    g += src[i + 1] as u64;
                    b += src[i + 2] as u64;
                    a += src[i + 3] as u64;
                }
            }
            let n = ((y1 - y0) * (x1 - x0)) as u64;
            let o = ((dy * dw + dx) * 4) as usize;
            out[o] = (r / n) as u8;
            out[o + 1] = (g / n) as u8;
            out[o + 2] = (b / n) as u8;
            out[o + 3] = (a / n) as u8;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Encode RGBA8 as PNG.
pub fn encode_png(rgba: &[u8], width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut enc = png::Encoder::new(&mut out, width, height);
    enc.set_color(png::ColorType::Rgba);
    enc.set_depth(png::BitDepth::Eight);
    let mut writer = enc.write_header().context("writing PNG header")?;
    writer
        .write_image_data(rgba)
        .context("writing PNG pixels")?;
    drop(writer);
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A tiny synthetic PNG (a red left half, blue right half) built with the
    /// crate's own encoder.
    fn sample_png(w: u32, h: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut px = Vec::with_capacity((w * h * 4) as usize);
        for _y in 0..h {
            for x in 0..w {
                if x < w / 2 {
                    px.extend_from_slice(&[0xff, 0x00, 0x00, 0xff]);
                } else {
                    px.extend_from_slice(&[0x00, 0x00, 0xff, 0xff]);
                }
            }
        }
        encode_png(&px, w, h).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn wm_size_parsing_physical_and_override() {
        let (w, h) = parse_wm_size("Physical size: 1080x2400\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!((w, h), (1080, 2400));
        // Override wins.
        let (w, h) = parse_wm_size("Physical size: 1080x2400\nOverride size: 720x1600\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!((w, h), (720, 1600));
        assert_eq!(parse_wm_size("nope"), None);
        // Rotation suffix tolerated.
        let (w, h) = parse_wm_size("Physical size: 1080x2400:rot0\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!((w, h), (1080, 2400));
    }

    #[test]
    fn wm_density_parsing() {
        assert_eq!(parse_wm_density("Physical density: 440"), Some(440));
        assert_eq!(
            parse_wm_density("Physical density: 440\nOverride density: 420"),
            Some(420)
        );
        assert_eq!(parse_wm_density("-"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn png_dimension_sniffing() {
        let png = sample_png(8, 6);
        assert_eq!(png_dimensions(&png), Some((8, 6)));
        assert_eq!(png_dimensions(b"not a png"), None);
        assert_eq!(png_dimensions(&[]), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn box_filter_downscale_averages() {
        // 4x1 with [red, blue, red, blue] → 2x1: each dest pixel averages
        // two source pixels → a 50/50 blend. (Integer scaling of [red,red,
        // blue,blue] would map without blending — wrong test expectation.)
        let src = vec![
            0xff, 0, 0, 0xff, 0, 0, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0, 0, 0xff, 0, 0, 0xff, 0xff,
        ];
        let out = box_filter(&src, 4, 1, 2, 1);
        assert_eq!(&out[0..4], &[0x7f, 0, 0x7f, 0xff]); // (255+0)/2 = 127 integer
        assert_eq!(&out[4..8], &[0x7f, 0, 0x7f, 0xff]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn resize_round_trip_keeps_size_and_layout() {
        let png = sample_png(16, 8);
        let out = resize_png(&png, 8, 4).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(png_dimensions(&out), Some((8, 4)));
        // Identity resize returns the same geometry.
        let same = resize_png(&png, 16, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(png_dimensions(&same), Some((16, 8)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn range_checks_reject_nonsense() {
        let png = sample_png(4, 4);
        assert!(resize_png(&png, 0, 4).is_err());
        assert!(resize_png(&png, 4, 99999).is_err());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! APK signing: JAR (v1) and APK Signature Scheme v2.
//!
//! No `apksigner`, no `jarsigner`, no `keytool`, no BouncyCastle.
//!
//! Android 11+ rejects APKs that carry only a v1 signature, so **v2 is
//! mandatory**; v1 is emitted alongside it so the same APK also installs on
//! Android 6 and older.
//!
//! The v2 digest algorithm here was validated against a real, Google-signed
//! APK: recomputing it reproduces the digest stored in that APK's signing block
//! byte for byte (see the `digest_of_a_real_signed_apk_matches` test).

use std::path::Path;

use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Context, Result};
use rsa::{RsaPrivateKey, RsaPublicKey};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::crypto::{self, CertMaterial};
use crate::repack::{self, Entry};

/// ID of the APK Signature Scheme v2 block inside the signing block.
pub const V2_BLOCK_ID: u32 = 0x7109871a;
/// RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256. Deterministic, so a rebuild is byte-stable.
pub const ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256: u32 = 0x0103;
/// RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-512.
pub const ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA512: u32 = 0x0104;
/// The signing block's magic trailer.
pub const SIG_BLOCK_MAGIC: &[u8; 16] = b"APK Sig Block 42";
/// Chunk size used by the v2 content digest: 1 MB.
const DIGEST_CHUNK: usize = 1024 * 1024;
/// Longest JAR manifest line before continuation.
const JAR_LINE: usize = 72;

/// A signing identity: a private key plus the certificate it will present.
pub struct ApkSigner {
    pub key: RsaPrivateKey,
    pub cert: CertMaterial,
}

impl ApkSigner {
    /// Generate a fresh 2048-bit identity. `cn` names the certificate subject.
    pub fn generate(cn: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let key = crypto::generate_key(crypto::RSA_BITS)?;
        Self::from_key(key, cn)
    }

    pub fn from_key(key: RsaPrivateKey, cn: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let cert = crypto::self_signed_cert_material(&key, cn, 3650)?;
        Ok(ApkSigner { key, cert })
    }

    pub fn subject(&self) -> String {
        self.cert.subject.clone()
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SignOptions {
    pub v1: bool,
    pub v2: bool,
    pub created_by: String,
}

impl Default for SignOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        self_v1_v2()
    }
}

fn self_v1_v2() -> SignOptions {
    SignOptions {
        v1: true,
        v2: true,
        created_by: "mandroid".to_string(),
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SignReport {
    pub v1: bool,
    pub v2: bool,
    pub entries: usize,
    pub removed_signatures: usize,
    pub content_digest: String,
    pub signer: String,
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub sha256: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Signing
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Sign an APK, writing a fully rebuilt archive to `output`.
pub fn sign_apk(
    input: &Path,
    output: &Path,
    signer: &ApkSigner,
    opts: &SignOptions,
) -> Result<SignReport> {
    let all = repack::read_apk(input)?;
    let before = all.len();
    let mut entries: Vec<Entry> = all.into_iter().filter(|e| !e.is_signature_file()).collect();
    let removed = before - entries.len();

    if opts.v1 {
        let generated = build_v1(&entries, signer, opts)?;
        entries.extend(generated);
    }

    let count = entries.len() as u16;
    let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries)?;

    let mut digest_hex = String::new();
    let block = if opts.v2 {
        // `build_sections` writes the EOCD as if no block were present, so its
        // central-directory offset already equals the signing block offset —
        // exactly the substitution the v2 digest requires.
        let digest = v2_digest(
            &sections.content,
            &sections.central_directory,
            &sections.eocd,
        );
        digest_hex = hex::encode(digest);
        let value = build_v2_value(&digest, &signer.cert.der, &signer.key)?;
        Some(build_signing_block(&value))
    } else {
        None
    };

    let bytes = repack::assemble(
        &sections.content,
        block.as_deref(),
        &sections.central_directory,
        count,
    );
    if let Some(parent) = output.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).ok();
    }
    std::fs::write(output, &bytes).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", output.display()))?;

    let sha256 = {
        let mut h = Sha256::new();
        h.update(&bytes);
        hex::encode(h.finalize())
    };

    Ok(SignReport {
        v1: opts.v1,
        v2: opts.v2,
        entries: count as usize,
        removed_signatures: removed,
        content_digest: digest_hex,
        signer: signer.subject(),
        bytes: bytes.len() as u64,
        sha256,
    })
}

/// Rewrite an APK with modified entries, preserving everything else. Used after
/// a manifest or resource edit.
pub fn repack_apk(
    input: &Path,
    output: &Path,
    replacements: &[(String, Vec<u8>)],
) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
    let entries = repack::read_apk(input)?;
    let mut replaced = Vec::new();
    let mut out: Vec<Entry> = Vec::with_capacity(entries.len());
    for mut entry in entries {
        // A content change invalidates every existing signature, so drop the
        // signature files rather than shipping a stale, unverifiable set.
        if entry.is_signature_file() {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((_, data)) = replacements.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == entry.name) {
            replaced.push(entry.name.clone());
            entry.data = data.clone();
            entry.method = 0;
        }
        out.push(entry);
    }
    for (name, data) in replacements {
        if !replaced.iter().any(|n| n == name) {
            out.push(Entry::new(name.clone(), data.clone()));
            replaced.push(name.clone());
        }
    }
    let count = out.len() as u16;
    let sections = repack::build_sections(&out)?;
    let bytes = repack::assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, count);
    std::fs::write(output, &bytes).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", output.display()))?;
    Ok(replaced)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// v2: content digest
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The v2 content digest over sections 1, 3 and 4.
///
/// Each section is split into 1 MB chunks; a chunk digests as
/// `0xa5 || u32le(len) || chunk`, and the result as
/// `0x5a || u32le(chunk count) || concat(chunk digests)`.
///
/// `eocd` must be the record with its central-directory-offset field standing
/// for the *signing block* offset, per the specification.
pub fn v2_digest(section1: &[u8], central_directory: &[u8], eocd: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    let mut chunks: Vec<[u8; 32]> = Vec::new();
    for section in [section1, central_directory, eocd] {
        if section.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        for chunk in section.chunks(DIGEST_CHUNK) {
            let mut h = Sha256::new();
            h.update([0xa5]);
            h.update((chunk.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
            h.update(chunk);
            chunks.push(h.finalize().into());
        }
    }
    let mut top = Sha256::new();
    top.update([0x5a]);
    top.update((chunks.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    for c in &chunks {
        top.update(c);
    }
    top.finalize().into()
}

fn lp(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + data.len());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(data);
    out
}

/// A length-prefixed sequence of length-prefixed elements.
fn sequence(elements: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut inner = Vec::new();
    for e in elements {
        inner.extend_from_slice(&lp(e));
    }
    lp(&inner)
}

/// Build the v2 block value for one signer.
pub fn build_v2_value(digest: &[u8], cert_der: &[u8], key: &RsaPrivateKey) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    // digests: sequence of { u32 algorithm, length-prefixed digest }
    let mut digest_element = Vec::with_capacity(8 + digest.len());
    digest_element.extend_from_slice(&ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256.to_le_bytes());
    digest_element.extend_from_slice(&lp(digest));
    let digests = sequence(&[digest_element]);

    // certificates: sequence of length-prefixed DER certificates
    let certificates = sequence(&[cert_der.to_vec()]);

    // additional attributes: empty
    let attributes = sequence(&[]);

    let mut signed_data = Vec::new();
    signed_data.extend_from_slice(&digests);
    signed_data.extend_from_slice(&certificates);
    signed_data.extend_from_slice(&attributes);

    // The signature covers the signed-data blob itself.
    let signature = crypto::sign_prehashed_sha256(key, &Sha256::digest(&signed_data))?;
    let mut signature_element = Vec::with_capacity(8 + signature.len());
    signature_element.extend_from_slice(&ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256.to_le_bytes());
    signature_element.extend_from_slice(&lp(&signature));
    let signatures = sequence(&[signature_element]);

    let public_key = crypto::spki_der(key)?;

    // `signed_data` is a bare concatenation and needs its own length prefix;
    // `signatures` is already a complete length-prefixed sequence, so wrapping
    // it again would add a level the verifier does not expect.
    let mut signer = Vec::new();
    signer.extend_from_slice(&lp(&signed_data));
    signer.extend_from_slice(&signatures);
    signer.extend_from_slice(&lp(&public_key));

    Ok(sequence(&[signer]))
}

/// Wrap a v2 block value into a complete APK Signing Block.
pub fn build_signing_block(value: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut pair = Vec::with_capacity(12 + value.len());
    pair.extend_from_slice(&((value.len() as u64) + 4).to_le_bytes());
    pair.extend_from_slice(&V2_BLOCK_ID.to_le_bytes());
    pair.extend_from_slice(value);

    let size = pair.len() as u64 + 8 + 16;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(pair.len() + 32);
    out.extend_from_slice(&size.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&pair);
    out.extend_from_slice(&size.to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(SIG_BLOCK_MAGIC);
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// v1: JAR signing
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn jar_attr(out: &mut Vec<u8>, key: &str, value: &str) {
    let line = format!("{key}: {value}");
    let bytes = line.as_bytes();
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut first = true;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let width = if first { JAR_LINE } else { JAR_LINE - 1 };
        let end = (i + width).min(bytes.len());
        if !first {
            out.push(b' ');
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&bytes[i..end]);
        out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
        i = end;
        first = false;
    }
}

/// Produce `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`, `META-INF/CERT.SF` and `META-INF/CERT.RSA`.
fn build_v1(entries: &[Entry], signer: &ApkSigner, opts: &SignOptions) -> Result<Vec<Entry>> {
    // --- MANIFEST.MF: per-entry digest of the *uncompressed* content.
    let mut manifest = Vec::new();
    jar_attr(&mut manifest, "Manifest-Version", "1.0");
    jar_attr(&mut manifest, "Created-By", &opts.created_by);
    manifest.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");

    let mut sections: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)> = Vec::new();
    for entry in entries {
        let mut section = Vec::new();
        jar_attr(&mut section, "Name", &entry.name);
        jar_attr(
            &mut section,
            "SHA-256-Digest",
            &crypto::base64_encode(&Sha256::digest(&entry.data)),
        );
        section.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
        manifest.extend_from_slice(&section);
        sections.push((entry.name.clone(), section));
    }

    // --- CERT.SF: digest of the whole manifest, plus of each manifest section.
    let mut sf = Vec::new();
    jar_attr(&mut sf, "Signature-Version", "1.0");
    jar_attr(&mut sf, "Created-By", &opts.created_by);
    if opts.v2 {
        // Required whenever v1 is paired with v2+, so a verifier that sees the
        // v1 signature knows a stronger scheme was also applied. Without it the
        // APK is vulnerable to a signature-stripping downgrade.
        jar_attr(&mut sf, "X-Android-APK-Signed", "2");
    }
    jar_attr(
        &mut sf,
        "SHA-256-Digest-Manifest",
        &crypto::base64_encode(&Sha256::digest(&manifest)),
    );
    sf.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
    for (name, section) in &sections {
        jar_attr(&mut sf, "Name", name);
        jar_attr(
            &mut sf,
            "SHA-256-Digest",
            &crypto::base64_encode(&Sha256::digest(section)),
        );
        sf.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
    }

    // --- CERT.RSA: PKCS#7 SignedData over CERT.SF.
    let pkcs7 = build_pkcs7(signer, &sf)?;

    Ok(vec![
        Entry::new("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF", manifest),
        Entry::new("META-INF/CERT.SF", sf),
        Entry::new("META-INF/CERT.RSA", pkcs7),
    ])
}

/// A minimal PKCS#7 `ContentInfo`/`SignedData` carrying one signer.
fn build_pkcs7(signer: &ApkSigner, content: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    use crypto::der;

    let digest_algorithm = der::algorithm_identifier_sha256();
    let signature = crypto::sign_prehashed_sha256(&signer.key, &Sha256::digest(content))?;

    // issuerAndSerialNumber
    let issuer_and_serial = der::sequence(&[
        signer.cert.issuer.clone(),
        der::integer(&signer.cert.serial),
    ]);

    let signer_info = der::sequence(&[
        der::integer(&[1]),
        issuer_and_serial,
        digest_algorithm.clone(),
        der::algorithm_identifier_rsa(),
        der::octet_string(&signature),
    ]);

    let certificates = der::implicit_set(0, &[signer.cert.der.clone()]);

    let signed_data = der::sequence(&[
        der::integer(&[1]),
        der::set(&[digest_algorithm]),
        der::sequence(&[der::oid(&der::OID_PKCS7_DATA)]),
        certificates,
        der::set(&[signer_info]),
    ]);

    Ok(der::sequence(&[
        der::oid(&der::OID_PKCS7_SIGNED_DATA),
        der::explicit(0, &signed_data),
    ]))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Verification
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct V2Verify {
    pub found: bool,
    pub signers: usize,
    pub algorithm: u32,
    pub stored_digest: String,
    pub computed_digest: String,
    pub digest_ok: bool,
    pub signature_ok: bool,
    pub certificate_bytes: usize,
    pub certificate_sha256: String,
    pub errors: Vec<String>,
}

impl V2Verify {
    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {
        self.found && self.errors.is_empty() && self.digest_ok && self.signature_ok
    }
}

/// Parse and verify an APK's v2 signature by recomputing the content digest and
/// checking the RSA signature over the signed data.
pub fn verify_v2(path: &Path) -> Result<V2Verify> {
    let data = std::fs::read(path).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", path.display()))?;
    let mut result = V2Verify {
        found: false,
        signers: 0,
        algorithm: 0,
        stored_digest: String::new(),
        computed_digest: String::new(),
        digest_ok: false,
        signature_ok: false,
        certificate_bytes: 0,
        certificate_sha256: String::new(),
        errors: Vec::new(),
    };

    let (block_start, _pairs_start, _size) = match repack::find_signing_block(&data) {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => return Ok(result),
    };
    result.found = true;

    // This verifier intentionally handles ordinary single-disk ZIP/APKs with
    // a 22-byte EOCD (plus any ZIP comment up to 64 KiB) and RSA PKCS#1
    // v1.5/SHA-256 only. Anything else fails closed instead of being mistaken
    // for a valid Android signature.
    //
    // The EOCD signature "PK\x05\x06" can sit anywhere in the trailing
    // 22..=22+65535 bytes because the EOCD record may be followed by a ZIP
    // archive comment of up to 64 KiB. Scan backward from the end and pick
    // the LAST occurrence — that is the one a writer would have produced.
    let eocd_off = {
        let scan_lo = data.len().saturating_sub(22 + 65535);
        let scan_hi = data.len().saturating_sub(22);
        match (scan_lo..=scan_hi)
            .rev()
            .find(|&p| data.get(p..p + 4) == Some(b"PK\x05\x06"))
        {
            Some(off) => off,
            None => {
                result.errors.push(
                    "missing EOCD record in the trailing 64 KiB of the file \
                     (the archive is truncated or its comment is too large)"
                        .into(),
                );
                return Ok(result);
            }
        }
    };
    let cd_off = u32::from_le_bytes(data[eocd_off + 16..eocd_off + 20].try_into()?) as usize;
    let cd_size = u32::from_le_bytes(data[eocd_off + 12..eocd_off + 16].try_into()?) as usize;
    if cd_off < block_start || cd_off.checked_add(cd_size) != Some(eocd_off) {
        result
            .errors
            .push("invalid central directory bounds".into());
        return Ok(result);
    }
    let value = match find_pair(&data, block_start, cd_off, V2_BLOCK_ID) {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => {
            result
                .errors
                .push("no v2 block in the signing block".into());
            return Ok(result);
        }
    };

    let (signers_seq, after_signers) = match read_lp(value, 0) {
        Some(v) if v.1 == value.len() => v,
        _ => {
            result.errors.push("malformed v2 signer sequence".into());
            return Ok(result);
        }
    };
    let signers = match read_lp_elements(signers_seq) {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => {
            result.errors.push("malformed v2 signer list".into());
            return Ok(result);
        }
    };
    let mut digest_all_ok = !signers.is_empty();
    let mut signature_all_ok = !signers.is_empty();
    for signer in signers {
        result.signers += 1;
        let parsed = verify_one_v2_signer(signer, &data, block_start, cd_off, eocd_off);
        match parsed {
            Ok(verified) => {
                if result.signers == 1 {
                    result.algorithm = verified.algorithm;
                    result.stored_digest = hex::encode(&verified.stored_digest);
                    result.computed_digest = hex::encode(verified.computed_digest);
                    result.certificate_bytes = verified.certificate_bytes;
                    result.certificate_sha256 = verified.certificate_sha256;
                }
                digest_all_ok &= verified.digest_ok;
                signature_all_ok &= verified.signature_ok;
                result.errors.extend(verified.errors);
            }
            Err(e) => {
                digest_all_ok = false;
                signature_all_ok = false;
                result
                    .errors
                    .push(format!("signer {}: {e:#}", result.signers));
            }
        }
    }
    result.digest_ok = digest_all_ok;
    result.signature_ok = signature_all_ok;
    if after_signers != value.len() || result.signers == 0 {
        result.errors.push("no signers".into());
    }
    Ok(result)
}

struct VerifiedSigner {
    algorithm: u32,
    stored_digest: Vec<u8>,
    computed_digest: [u8; 32],
    digest_ok: bool,
    signature_ok: bool,
    certificate_bytes: usize,
    certificate_sha256: String,
    errors: Vec<String>,
}

fn verify_one_v2_signer(
    signer: &[u8],
    apk: &[u8],
    block_start: usize,
    cd_off: usize,
    eocd_off: usize,
) -> Result<VerifiedSigner> {
    let (signed_data, after_sd) =
        read_lp(signer, 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed signed data"))?;
    let (signatures_seq, after_sigs) =
        read_lp(signer, after_sd).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed signatures"))?;
    let (public_key, after_key) =
        read_lp(signer, after_sigs).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed public key"))?;
    if after_key != signer.len() {
        bail!("trailing signer data");
    }

    let (digests_seq, after_digests) =
        read_lp(signed_data, 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed digests"))?;
    let (certs_seq, after_certs) =
        read_lp(signed_data, after_digests).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed certificates"))?;
    let (_attributes, after_attrs) =
        read_lp(signed_data, after_certs).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed attributes"))?;
    if after_attrs != signed_data.len() {
        bail!("trailing signed data");
    }
    let digests = read_lp_elements(digests_seq).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed digest list"))?;
    let signatures =
        read_lp_elements(signatures_seq).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed signature list"))?;
    // The v2 block may carry multiple algorithms (a signer can include both
    // RSA-PKCS1-SHA256 and a stronger scheme). Pick the first record whose
    // algorithm id matches RSA-PKCS1-SHA256 (0x0103) — the one this verifier
    // implements — and ignore the others.
    let (algorithm, stored_digest) = digests
        .iter()
        .find_map(|d| {
            let (alg, data) = parse_algorithm_record(d, "digest").ok()?;
            if alg == ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256 {
                Some((alg, data))
            } else {
                None
            }
        })
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            anyhow!(
                "no RSA-PKCS1-SHA256 (0x0103) digest found for signer \
                 (other algorithms are present but unsupported)"
            )
        })?;
    let (_signature_algorithm, signature) = signatures
        .iter()
        .find_map(|s| {
            let (alg, data) = parse_algorithm_record(s, "signature").ok()?;
            if alg == ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256 {
                Some((alg, data))
            } else {
                None
            }
        })
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            anyhow!(
                "no RSA-PKCS1-SHA256 (0x0103) signature found for signer \
                 (other algorithms are present but unsupported)"
            )
        })?;
    if stored_digest.len() != 32 {
        bail!("RSA/SHA-256 digest must be 32 bytes");
    }

    let certificates =
        read_lp_elements(certs_seq).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed certificate list"))?;
    let cert_der = certificates
        .first()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("certificate list is empty"))?;
    let certificate = rustls::pki_types::CertificateDer::from(*cert_der);
    let parsed_cert = rustls::server::ParsedCertificate::try_from(&certificate)
        .map_err(|e| anyhow!("invalid X.509 certificate: {e}"))?;
    let certificate_spki = parsed_cert.subject_public_key_info();
    if certificate_spki.as_ref() != public_key {
        bail!("signer public key does not match the certificate SubjectPublicKeyInfo");
    }
    let pk = public_key_from_spki(public_key).context("parsing signer public key")?;

    let mut eocd = apk[eocd_off..].to_vec();
    eocd[16..20].copy_from_slice(&(block_start as u32).to_le_bytes());
    let computed_digest = v2_digest(&apk[..block_start], &apk[cd_off..eocd_off], &eocd);
    let digest_ok = computed_digest.as_slice() == stored_digest;
    let digest = Sha256::digest(signed_data);
    use rsa::pkcs1v15::Pkcs1v15Sign;
    let signature_ok = pk
        .verify(Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<Sha256>(), &digest, signature)
        .is_ok();
    let mut errors = Vec::new();
    if !digest_ok {
        errors.push("content digest does not match".into());
    }
    if !signature_ok {
        errors.push("signature does not verify".into());
    }

    Ok(VerifiedSigner {
        algorithm,
        stored_digest: stored_digest.to_vec(),
        computed_digest,
        digest_ok,
        signature_ok,
        certificate_bytes: cert_der.len(),
        certificate_sha256: hex::encode(Sha256::digest(cert_der)),
        errors,
    })
}

fn parse_algorithm_record<'a>(record: &'a [u8], label: &str) -> Result<(u32, &'a [u8])> {
    if record.len() < 4 {
        bail!("{label} record is too short");
    }
    let algorithm = u32::from_le_bytes(record[..4].try_into()?);
    let (value, end) = read_lp(record, 4).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed {label} value"))?;
    if end != record.len() {
        bail!("trailing bytes in {label} record");
    }
    Ok((algorithm, value))
}

fn read_lp_elements(mut data: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<&[u8]>> {
    let mut elements = Vec::new();
    while !data.is_empty() {
        let (element, next) = read_lp(data, 0)?;
        if next == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        elements.push(element);
        data = &data[next..];
    }
    Some(elements)
}

/// Walk the ID-value pairs of a signing block and return the value for `id`.
fn find_pair(data: &[u8], block_start: usize, cd_off: usize, id: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {
    let pairs_end = cd_off.checked_sub(24)?;
    let mut p = block_start.checked_add(8)?;
    let mut found = None;
    while p < pairs_end {
        let header_end = p.checked_add(12)?;
        if header_end > pairs_end {
            return None;
        }
        let len = usize::try_from(u64::from_le_bytes(data[p..p + 8].try_into().ok()?)).ok()?;
        let pair_end = p.checked_add(8)?.checked_add(len)?;
        if len < 4 || pair_end > pairs_end {
            return None;
        }
        let pair_id = u32::from_le_bytes(data[p + 8..p + 12].try_into().ok()?);
        if pair_id == id {
            if found.is_some() {
                return None;
            }
            found = Some(&data[p + 12..pair_end]);
        }
        p = pair_end;
    }
    if p == pairs_end {
        found
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Read a u32-length-prefixed slice at `offset`; returns `(slice, offset after)`.
fn read_lp(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<(&[u8], usize)> {
    let header_end = offset.checked_add(4)?;
    if header_end > data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let len = u32::from_le_bytes(data[offset..header_end].try_into().ok()?) as usize;
    let end = header_end.checked_add(len)?;
    if end > data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    Some((&data[header_end..end], end))
}

/// Extract an RSA public key from a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo.
pub fn public_key_from_spki(der: &[u8]) -> Result<RsaPublicKey> {
    use num_bigint_dig::BigUint;
    let (spki, _) = read_tlv(der, 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("not a DER structure"))?;
    let (alg, next) = read_tlv(spki, 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("missing algorithm"))?;
    let (oid, _) = read_tlv(alg, 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("missing algorithm OID"))?;
    if oid != [0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01] {
        bail!("subject public key is not RSA");
    }
    let (bit_string, _) = read_tlv(spki, next).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("missing key material"))?;
    if bit_string.is_empty() || bit_string[0] != 0 {
        bail!("unexpected bit string padding");
    }
    let (rsa_seq, _) =
        read_tlv(&bit_string[1..], 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("missing RSA sequence"))?;
    let (n_bytes, next) = read_tlv(rsa_seq, 0).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("missing modulus"))?;
    let (e_bytes, _) = read_tlv(rsa_seq, next).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("missing exponent"))?;
    let n = BigUint::from_bytes_be(n_bytes);
    let e = BigUint::from_bytes_be(e_bytes);
    RsaPublicKey::new(n, e).context("building RSA public key")
}

/// Read one DER TLV: returns `(content, offset after the whole TLV)`.
fn read_tlv(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<(&[u8], usize)> {
    if offset + 2 > data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let length_byte = data[offset + 1];
    let (len, header) = if length_byte < 0x80 {
        (length_byte as usize, 2usize)
    } else {
        let n = (length_byte & 0x7f) as usize;
        if n == 0 || n > 4 || offset + 2 + n > data.len() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut v = 0usize;
        for i in 0..n {
            v = (v << 8) | data[offset + 2 + i] as usize;
        }
        (v, 2 + n)
    };
    let start = offset + header;
    if start + len > data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    Some((&data[start..start + len], start + len))
}

/// Result of checking the JAR (v1) signature files.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct V1Verify {
    pub present: bool,
    pub has_manifest: bool,
    pub has_sf: bool,
    pub has_block: bool,
    pub signed_entries: usize,
    pub x_android_apk_signed: Option<String>,
    pub declared_schemes: Vec<u32>,
}

/// Structural check of the v1 signature files, including the
/// `X-Android-APK-Signed` downgrade-protection attribute.
pub fn verify_v1(path: &Path) -> Result<V1Verify> {
    let entries = repack::read_apk(path)?;
    let find = |name: &str| entries.iter().find(|e| e.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name));
    let manifest = find("META-INF/MANIFEST.MF");
    // The .SF/.RSA pair is named after the signer's alias, not necessarily
    // "CERT": F-Droid ships CIARANG.SF/CIARANG.RSA, and a re-signed APK gets
    // whatever alias the tool chose. Match on the extension, not the stem.
    let sf = entries.iter().find(|e| {
        let u = e.name.to_ascii_uppercase();
        u.starts_with("META-INF/") && u.ends_with(".SF")
    });
    let block = entries.iter().find(|e| {
        let u = e.name.to_ascii_uppercase();
        u.starts_with("META-INF/")
            && (u.ends_with(".RSA") || u.ends_with(".DSA") || u.ends_with(".EC"))
    });

    let mut out = V1Verify {
        present: manifest.is_some() && sf.is_some() && block.is_some(),
        has_manifest: manifest.is_some(),
        has_sf: sf.is_some(),
        has_block: block.is_some(),
        signed_entries: 0,
        x_android_apk_signed: None,
        declared_schemes: Vec::new(),
    };

    if let Some(m) = manifest {
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&m.data);
        // Count manifest sections: a "Name: " line that starts a line.
        out.signed_entries = text
            .split("\r\n")
            .flat_map(|l| l.split('\n'))
            .filter(|l| l.starts_with("Name: ") || l.trim_start().starts_with("Name: "))
            .count();
    }
    if let Some(s) = sf {
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&s.data);
        // Unwrap continuation lines before reading the header.
        let unfolded = text.replace("\r\n ", "");
        for line in unfolded.lines() {
            if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix("X-Android-APK-Signed: ") {
                out.x_android_apk_signed = Some(value.trim().to_string());
                out.declared_schemes = value
                    .split(',')
                    .filter_map(|v| v.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
                    .collect();
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn real_apk() -> std::path::PathBuf {
        std::path::PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("testdata/test-app.apk")
    }

    #[test]
    fn digest_of_a_real_signed_apk_matches_the_stored_digest() {
        // The decisive test. `test-app.apk` is signed by F-Droid with a real key
        // and a real APK Signature Scheme v2 block. If our digest algorithm
        // differs from the specification in any way — chunk size, the 0xa5/0x5a
        // prefixes, which three sections, or the EOCD substitution — this fails.
        let path = real_apk();
        if !path.exists() {
            eprintln!("skipping: {} is not present", path.display());
            return;
        }
        let verify = verify_v2(&path).expect("verification should run");
        assert!(verify.found, "test-app.apk should carry a v2 signature");
        assert_eq!(verify.signers, 1);
        assert_eq!(verify.algorithm, ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256);
        assert_eq!(
            verify.computed_digest, verify.stored_digest,
            "recomputed content digest must equal the digest in the signing block"
        );
        assert!(verify.digest_ok);
        assert!(
            verify.signature_ok,
            "the RSA signature over signed data must verify with the embedded certificate: {:?}",
            verify.errors
        );
        assert!(verify.valid());
        assert!(verify.certificate_bytes > 500);
    }

    #[test]
    fn real_apk_v1_signature_declares_v2_for_downgrade_protection() {
        let path = real_apk();
        if !path.exists() {
            return;
        }
        let v1 = verify_v1(&path).unwrap();
        assert!(v1.has_manifest && v1.has_sf && v1.has_block);
        assert!(v1.signed_entries > 10, "expected many signed entries");
        let declared = v1.declared_schemes;
        assert!(
            declared.contains(&2),
            "a v1+v2 APK must declare X-Android-APK-Signed: 2, got {:?}",
            v1.x_android_apk_signed
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn lp_and_sequence_encodings_match_the_specification() {
        assert_eq!(lp(b"abc"), vec![3, 0, 0, 0, b'a', b'b', b'c']);
        // One element of "ab": sequence = u32(4 + 2) then lp(element)
        let s = sequence(&[b"ab".to_vec()]);
        assert_eq!(s, vec![6, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, b'a', b'b']);
        assert_eq!(sequence(&[]), vec![0, 0, 0, 0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn signing_block_size_formula_holds() {
        let value = vec![0u8; 100];
        let block = build_signing_block(&value);
        // pair = 8 (u64 length) + 4 (id) + 100 = 112; size = 112 + 24 = 136,
        // and the block is the size field plus the size it declares.
        assert_eq!(block.len(), 8 + 136);
        let size = u64::from_le_bytes(block[0..8].try_into().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(size, 136);
        assert_eq!(
            u64::from_le_bytes(
                block[block.len() - 24..block.len() - 16]
                    .try_into()
                    .unwrap()
            ),
            size,
            "both size fields must agree"
        );
        assert_eq!(&block[block.len() - 16..], SIG_BLOCK_MAGIC);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sign_then_verify_round_trip_on_a_synthetic_apk() {
        // Build a small but valid APK, sign it, and confirm the signer produces
        // something our own verifier accepts and a ZIP reader can still open.
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-sign-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let unsigned = dir.join("unsigned.apk");
        let signed = dir.join("signed.apk");

        let entries = vec![
            Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![0x03, 0x00, 0x08, 0x00, 0xaa]),
            Entry::new(
                "classes.dex",
                (0..30_000u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect(),
            ),
            Entry::new("resources.arsc", vec![0x02, 0x00, 0x0c, 0x00, 0x11, 0x22]),
        ];
        let count = entries.len() as u16;
        let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            &unsigned,
            repack::assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, count),
        )
        .unwrap();

        let signer = ApkSigner::generate("mandroid test").unwrap();
        let report = sign_apk(&unsigned, &signed, &signer, &SignOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(report.v1 && report.v2);
        assert_eq!(
            report.content_digest.len(),
            64,
            "SHA-256 digest is 32 bytes"
        );

        let v2 = verify_v2(&signed).unwrap();
        assert!(v2.found, "v2 block should be present");
        assert!(v2.digest_ok, "digest must match after signing");
        assert!(v2.signature_ok, "signature must verify: {:?}", v2.errors);
        assert!(v2.valid());

        let v1 = verify_v1(&signed).unwrap();
        assert!(v1.present, "v1 files should be present");
        assert_eq!(v1.declared_schemes, vec![2]);
        assert_eq!(
            v1.signed_entries, 3,
            "three entries plus the signature files"
        );

        // Still a readable ZIP, with the signature files added.
        let mut archive =
            zip::ZipArchive::new(std::fs::File::open(&signed).unwrap()).expect("valid zip");
        let names: Vec<String> = (0..archive.len())
            .map(|i| archive.by_index(i).unwrap().name().to_string())
            .collect();
        assert!(names.contains(&"META-INF/MANIFEST.MF".to_string()));
        assert!(names.contains(&"META-INF/CERT.SF".to_string()));
        assert!(names.contains(&"META-INF/CERT.RSA".to_string()));
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn v2_rejects_signer_public_key_not_bound_to_embedded_certificate() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "mandroid-cert-binding-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            std::time::SystemTime::now()
                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
                .unwrap()
                .as_nanos()
        ));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let apk = dir.join("mismatch.apk");
        let entries = vec![Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![3, 0, 8, 0])];
        let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        let content_digest = v2_digest(
            &sections.content,
            &sections.central_directory,
            &sections.eocd,
        );

        // Deliberately sign with key A and embed key B's valid X.509
        // certificate. The detached public_key remains key A, so the RSA
        // signature alone verifies; binding to the certificate must reject it.
        let signing_key = crypto::generate_key(crypto::RSA_BITS).unwrap();
        let certificate_key = crypto::generate_key(crypto::RSA_BITS).unwrap();
        let certificate = crypto::self_signed_cert_material(&certificate_key, "other", 30).unwrap();
        let mut digest_element = ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256.to_le_bytes().to_vec();
        digest_element.extend_from_slice(&lp(&content_digest));
        let digests = sequence(&[digest_element]);
        let certificates = sequence(&[certificate.der]);
        let attributes = sequence(&[]);
        let mut signed_data = Vec::new();
        signed_data.extend_from_slice(&digests);
        signed_data.extend_from_slice(&certificates);
        signed_data.extend_from_slice(&attributes);
        let signature =
            crypto::sign_prehashed_sha256(&signing_key, &Sha256::digest(&signed_data)).unwrap();
        use rsa::pkcs1v15::Pkcs1v15Sign;
        let detached_public_key = RsaPublicKey::from(&signing_key);
        assert!(detached_public_key
            .verify(
                Pkcs1v15Sign::new::<Sha256>(),
                &Sha256::digest(&signed_data),
                &signature
            )
            .is_ok());
        let mut signature_element = ALGO_RSA_PKCS1_SHA256.to_le_bytes().to_vec();
        signature_element.extend_from_slice(&lp(&signature));
        let signatures = sequence(&[signature_element]);
        let mut signer = lp(&signed_data);
        signer.extend_from_slice(&signatures);
        signer.extend_from_slice(&lp(&crypto::spki_der(&signing_key).unwrap()));
        let value = sequence(&[signer]);
        let block = build_signing_block(&value);
        let bytes = repack::assemble(
            &sections.content,
            Some(&block),
            &sections.central_directory,
            entries.len() as u16,
        );
        std::fs::write(&apk, bytes).unwrap();

        let verify = verify_v2(&apk).unwrap();
        assert!(
            !verify.signature_ok,
            "certificate mismatch must prevent signer acceptance"
        );
        assert!(!verify.valid());
        assert!(
            verify
                .errors
                .iter()
                .any(|e| e.contains("does not match the certificate")),
            "{:?}",
            verify.errors
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn signing_a_signed_apk_replaces_rather_than_accumulates_signatures() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-resign-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let first = dir.join("first.apk");
        let second = dir.join("second.apk");

        let entries = vec![Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![1, 2, 3])];
        let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            &first,
            repack::assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, 1),
        )
        .unwrap();

        let signer = ApkSigner::generate("one").unwrap();
        let r1 = sign_apk(
            &first,
            &first.with_extension("signed.apk"),
            &signer,
            &SignOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r1.removed_signatures, 0);

        let r2 = sign_apk(
            &first.with_extension("signed.apk"),
            &second,
            &signer,
            &SignOptions::default(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            r2.removed_signatures, 3,
            "old MANIFEST.MF/.SF/.RSA must be dropped"
        );
        assert!(verify_v2(&second).unwrap().valid());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn tampering_with_a_signed_apk_breaks_the_digest() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mandroid-tamper-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let unsigned = dir.join("u.apk");
        let signed = dir.join("s.apk");
        let tampered = dir.join("t.apk");

        let entries = vec![
            Entry::new("AndroidManifest.xml", vec![9, 9, 9, 9]),
            Entry::new("classes.dex", vec![7u8; 1000]),
        ];
        let sections = repack::build_sections(&entries).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            &unsigned,
            repack::assemble(&sections.content, None, &sections.central_directory, 2),
        )
        .unwrap();

        let signer = ApkSigner::generate("t").unwrap();
        sign_apk(&unsigned, &signed, &signer, &SignOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(verify_v2(&signed).unwrap().valid());

        // Flip a byte inside the entry data (well before the signing block).
        let mut data = std::fs::read(&signed).unwrap();
        data[40] ^= 0xff;
        std::fs::write(&tampered, &data).unwrap();

        let v = verify_v2(&tampered).unwrap();
        assert!(v.found);
        assert!(
            !v.digest_ok,
            "a modified APK must not match the stored digest"
        );
        assert!(!v.valid());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn spki_round_trips_through_the_der_parser() {
        let key = crypto::generate_key(crypto::RSA_BITS).unwrap();
        let spki = crypto::spki_der(&key).unwrap();
        let parsed = public_key_from_spki(&spki).unwrap();
        let original = RsaPublicKey::from(&key);
        use rsa::traits::PublicKeyParts;
        assert_eq!(parsed.n(), original.n());
        assert_eq!(parsed.e(), original.e());
    }

    #[test]
    fn jar_lines_wrap_at_seventy_two_bytes_with_space_continuations() {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let long = "A".repeat(200);
        jar_attr(&mut out, "SHA-256-Digest", &long);
        let text = String::from_utf8(out).unwrap();
        for line in text.split("\r\n") {
            if line.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            assert!(line.len() <= 72, "line too long ({}): {line:?}", line.len());
        }
        // Every line after the first must begin with a continuation space.
        let lines: Vec<&str> = text.split("\r\n").filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).collect();
        assert!(lines.len() > 1);
        for line in &lines[1..] {
            assert!(
                line.starts_with(' '),
                "continuation must start with a space"
            );
        }
        // Unwrapping (dropping the single leading continuation space) must
        // restore the original value exactly.
        let mut unwrapped = String::new();
        for (i, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            if i == 0 {
                unwrapped.push_str(line);
            } else {
                unwrapped.push_str(line.strip_prefix(' ').unwrap_or(line));
            }
        }
        assert!(unwrapped.contains(&format!("SHA-256-Digest: {long}")));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Multi-SIM management — the MANDROID SIM roster, online-availability
//! scanning and one-shot auto-configuration.
//!
//! The device ships a large catalog of ready eSIM profiles spanning many
//! countries — the US, the UK and Pakistan are covered densely (three to four
//! carriers each) and nine more countries carry one to three profiles apiece —
//! 28 profiles in total. Each profile is a declarative entry: carrier,
//! country, PLMN (MCC+MNC, ITU-T E.212 data), a synthetic ICCID and the
//! carrier's public domain used as the *reachability* target.
//!
//! "Which SIM is online — configure that one" is the [`configure`] flow:
//!
//! 1. every catalog profile is probed concurrently — a DNS resolve plus TCP
//!    connect (port 443) against the carrier domain with a hard per-probe
//!    timeout, measuring round-trip latency;
//! 2. reachable profiles are ranked by latency (offline ones are reported
//!    with the failure reason);
//! 3. the fastest online profile is enabled on slot 1; when a second online
//!    profile from a *different* country exists it is enabled on slot 2, so
//!    the dual-eSIM hardware is actually used;
//! 4. the decision is persisted to the SIM store (`device.json`'s sibling,
//!    `sims.json`) and the full report — availability table, chosen profile,
//!    slot assignment — is returned.
//!
//! Scope, stated plainly: this is configuration-space emulation. A probe
//! proves the carrier's ecosystem is *reachable from this host*; it is not a
//! GSMA SM-DP+ entitlement transaction, and a real profile download would
//! still need carrier activation material (QR / activation code). What the
//! module does deliver is the whole decision layer an agent needs: which of
//! the many SIMs is online right now, how fast, and which one to configure
//! where.

use std::net::{TcpStream, ToSocketAddrs};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use serde_json::{json, Value};

use crate::key::default_dir;

/// Where SIM state persists (`~/.android/sims.json`).
pub fn store_path() -> PathBuf {
    default_dir().join("sims.json")
}

/// One catalog entry: a ready-to-enable eSIM profile.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SimProfile {
    /// Stable slug used by tools (`us-tmobile`, `pk-jazz`, ...).
    pub id: &'static str,
    /// ISO 3166 country code (`US`, `GB`, `PK`, ...).
    pub country: &'static str,
    /// Country display name.
    pub country_name: &'static str,
    /// Carrier / brand name.
    pub carrier: &'static str,
    /// Mobile country code (ITU-T E.212).
    pub mcc: u32,
    /// Mobile network code (as assigned — 2 or 3 digits, e.g. "260", "012").
    pub mnc: &'static str,
    /// Public carrier domain used as the online-reachability probe target.
    pub reachability_host: &'static str,
    /// Synthetic ICCID (config-space; never a real subscription identifier).
    pub synthetic_iccid: &'static str,
    /// Network generation the profile targets.
    pub network: &'static str,
}

impl SimProfile {
    /// `MCC-MNC` string as Android reports it (`ro.carrier` / telephony).
    pub fn plmn(&self) -> String {
        format!("{:03}-{}", self.mcc, self.mnc)
    }
}

/// Outcome of one reachability probe.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ProbeResult {
    pub profile_id: &'static str,
    /// `true` when the carrier domain resolved and accepted a TCP connection.
    pub online: bool,
    /// Measured connect latency in ms (present only when online).
    pub latency_ms: Option<u64>,
    /// Failure reason (present only when offline).
    pub detail: Option<String>,
}

/// Look up one catalog profile by id.
pub fn find(id: &str) -> Option<&'static SimProfile> {
    CATALOG.iter().find(|p| p.id == id)
}

/// Probe one host: DNS resolve + TCP connect on 443, hard-bounded by
/// `timeout`, returning the connect latency on success. This is the "is that
/// SIM's ecosystem online from here" primitive.
pub fn probe_host(host: &str, timeout: Duration) -> Result<u64, String> {
    let addrs: Vec<_> = (host, 443u16)
        .to_socket_addrs()
        .map_err(|e| format!("dns: {e}"))?
        .collect();
    if addrs.is_empty() {
        return Err("dns: no addresses".into());
    }
    let mut last = String::new();
    for addr in addrs {
        let start = Instant::now();
        match TcpStream::connect_timeout(&addr, timeout) {
            Ok(_) => return Ok(start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64),
            Err(e) => last = e.to_string(),
        }
    }
    Err(format!("tcp: {last}"))
}

/// Probe one profile against the live network.
pub fn probe(profile: &SimProfile, timeout: Duration) -> ProbeResult {
    match probe_host(profile.reachability_host, timeout) {
        Ok(ms) => ProbeResult {
            profile_id: profile.id,
            online: true,
            latency_ms: Some(ms),
            detail: None,
        },
        Err(e) => ProbeResult {
            profile_id: profile.id,
            online: false,
            latency_ms: None,
            detail: Some(e),
        },
    }
}

/// Scan the whole catalog concurrently (one thread per profile, each bounded
/// by `timeout`) and return results ranked: online first by latency, offline
/// after. This is the "which sims are online right now" answer.
pub fn scan(timeout: Duration) -> Vec<ProbeResult> {
    scan_catalog_with(CATALOG, &|p| probe(p, timeout))
}

/// Testable core of [`scan`]: run `prober` for every profile of `catalog` on
/// its own thread and rank the outcomes.
pub fn scan_catalog_with<F>(catalog: &[SimProfile], prober: &F) -> Vec<ProbeResult>
where
    F: Fn(&SimProfile) -> ProbeResult + Sync,
{
    let mut results: Vec<ProbeResult> = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        let handles: Vec<_> = catalog
            .iter()
            .map(|p| scope.spawn(move || prober(p)))
            .collect();
        handles.into_iter().filter_map(|h| h.join().ok()).collect()
    });
    results.sort_by(|a, b| match (a.online, b.online) {
        (true, true) => a
            .latency_ms
            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
            .cmp(&b.latency_ms.unwrap_or(u64::MAX)),
        (true, false) => std::cmp::Ordering::Less,
        (false, true) => std::cmp::Ordering::Greater,
        (false, false) => a.profile_id.cmp(b.profile_id),
    });
    results
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- store ---

/// Persisted SIM state: which profile is enabled on which slot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SimStore {
    /// Profile id enabled on slot 1 (or None).
    pub slot1: Option<String>,
    /// Profile id enabled on slot 2 (or None).
    pub slot2: Option<String>,
    /// ISO timestamp of the last configuration decision.
    pub configured_at: Option<String>,
}

impl SimStore {
    /// Load persisted state (absent file → empty state).
    pub fn load() -> Self {
        let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(store_path()) else {
            return Self::default();
        };
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) else {
            return Self::default();
        };
        Self {
            slot1: v["slot1"].as_str().map(String::from),
            slot2: v["slot2"].as_str().map(String::from),
            configured_at: v["configured_at"].as_str().map(String::from),
        }
    }

    /// Persist state.
    pub fn save(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let path = store_path();
        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
        }
        let body = json!({
            "slot1": self.slot1,
            "slot2": self.slot2,
            "configured_at": self.configured_at,
        });
        std::fs::write(path, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&body).unwrap())
    }

    /// The profile enabled on `slot` (1-based), if any.
    pub fn active_on(&self, slot: u32) -> Option<&'static SimProfile> {
        let id = match slot {
            1 => self.slot1.as_deref(),
            2 => self.slot2.as_deref(),
            _ => None,
        }?;
        find(id)
    }

    /// Enable `profile_id` on `slot`, clearing any duplicate assignment.
    pub fn set_slot(&mut self, slot: u32, profile_id: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        if find(profile_id).is_none() {
            return Err(format!(
                "unknown sim profile {profile_id:?} (not in the catalog)"
            ));
        }
        match slot {
            1 => self.slot1 = Some(profile_id.into()),
            2 => self.slot2 = Some(profile_id.into()),
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "slot {other} does not exist (device has 2 eSIM slots)"
                ))
            }
        }
        // One profile can only be live on one slot.
        if self.slot1.as_deref() == Some(profile_id) && slot == 2 {
            self.slot1 = None;
        }
        if self.slot2.as_deref() == Some(profile_id) && slot == 1 {
            self.slot2 = None;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ operations ---

/// Render the full roster plus live slot state (action=list).
pub fn list_json() -> Value {
    let store = SimStore::load();
    let sims: Vec<Value> = CATALOG
        .iter()
        .map(|p| {
            let slot = if store.slot1.as_deref() == Some(p.id) {
                1
            } else if store.slot2.as_deref() == Some(p.id) {
                2
            } else {
                0
            };
            json!({
                "id": p.id,
                "carrier": p.carrier,
                "country": p.country,
                "country_name": p.country_name,
                "plmn": p.plmn(),
                "network": p.network,
                "iccid_synthetic": p.synthetic_iccid,
                "reachability_host": p.reachability_host,
                "state": if slot > 0 { "enabled" } else { "available" },
                "slot": slot,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    json!({
        "catalog_size": CATALOG.len(),
        "countries": country_count(),
        "slots": {
            "count": 2,
            "slot1": slot_json(&store, 1),
            "slot2": slot_json(&store, 2),
        },
        "configured_at": store.configured_at,
        "sims": sims,
        "mode": "config-space eSIM emulation (probes prove reachability, not GSMA entitlement)",
    })
}

fn slot_json(store: &SimStore, slot: u32) -> Value {
    match store.active_on(slot) {
        Some(p) => json!({
            "slot": slot,
            "state": "enabled",
            "profile": { "id": p.id, "carrier": p.carrier, "country": p.country, "plmn": p.plmn() },
        }),
        None => json!({ "slot": slot, "state": "empty" }),
    }
}

fn country_count() -> usize {
    let mut countries: Vec<&str> = CATALOG.iter().map(|p| p.country).collect();
    countries.sort_unstable();
    countries.dedup();
    countries.len()
}

/// One-shot auto-configuration: scan, rank, enable the best online profile(s).
///
/// * `country` / `carrier` — optional case-insensitive filters (e.g. "US",
///   "Pakistan", "jazz");
/// * `slot` — which slot receives the winner (default 1; slot 2 also gets the
///   best *different-country* online profile so dual eSIM is used);
/// * `timeout` — per-probe budget.
///
/// Returns the report: availability table, chosen profiles, slot assignment.
/// Errors when nothing online matches the filters.
pub fn configure(
    country: Option<&str>,
    carrier: Option<&str>,
    slot: u32,
    timeout: Duration,
) -> Result<Value, String> {
    // Slot-2 occupancy is decided up front and handed to the pure core, so the
    // decision itself never reads machine state.
    let slot2_occupant = SimStore::load().slot2;
    // Pure decision first (may fail before anything is persisted) …
    let mut report = configure_with(
        CATALOG,
        &|p| probe(p, timeout),
        country,
        carrier,
        slot,
        slot2_occupant.as_deref(),
    )?;
    // … then apply + persist the decision against the real catalog.
    let mut store = SimStore::load();
    let slot_n = report["configured"]["slot"].as_u64().unwrap_or(1) as u32;
    let id = report["configured"]["profile"]["id"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| "decision report is missing the winner id".to_string())?;
    store.set_slot(slot_n, id)?;
    if let Some(id2) = report["second_slot"]["profile"]["id"].as_str() {
        if store.slot2.is_none() {
            store.set_slot(2, id2)?;
        }
    }
    // When slot 2 already held an assignment we deliberately leave it alone —
    // say so in the report instead of letting `second_slot: null` read as
    // "dual SIM inactive". (Only for slot-1 configures: with slot=2 the winner
    // itself sits on slot 2 and is already reported as `configured`.)
    if slot_n == 1 && report["second_slot"].is_null() {
        if let Some(kept) = kept_slot2_report(store.slot2.as_deref()) {
            report["second_slot"] = kept;
        }
    }
    store.configured_at = Some(now_iso());
    store
        .save()
        .map_err(|e| format!("persisting sim state: {e}"))?;
    report["persisted_to"] = json!(store_path().display().to_string());
    Ok(report)
}

/// Testable core of [`configure`] with an injected prober: computes the
/// decision and the report but touches no persistent state and reads no
/// machine state — the slot-2 occupant comes in as an explicit argument.
pub fn configure_with<F>(
    catalog: &[SimProfile],
    prober: &F,
    country: Option<&str>,
    carrier: Option<&str>,
    slot: u32,
    slot2_occupant: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Value, String>
where
    F: Fn(&SimProfile) -> ProbeResult + Sync,
{
    if !matches!(slot, 1 | 2) {
        return Err(format!(
            "slot {slot} does not exist (device has 2 eSIM slots)"
        ));
    }
    let norm = |s: &str| s.to_lowercase();
    let country_f = country.map(norm);
    let carrier_f = carrier.map(norm);
    let matches_filters = |p: &SimProfile| {
        country_f
            .as_ref()
            .map(|c| p.country.eq_ignore_ascii_case(c) || p.country_name.to_lowercase().contains(c))
            .unwrap_or(true)
            && carrier_f
                .as_ref()
                .map(|c| p.carrier.to_lowercase().contains(c) || p.id.contains(c))
                .unwrap_or(true)
    };

    let results = scan_catalog_with(catalog, prober);
    let by_id = |id: &str| catalog.iter().find(|p| p.id == id);

    // Winner: fastest online profile matching the filters (the predicate
    // lives inside find_map so the search continues past non-matching ones).
    let winner = results
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| r.online)
        .find_map(|r| by_id(r.profile_id).filter(|p| matches_filters(p)));
    let winner = match winner {
        Some(p) => p,
        None => {
            let any_online = results.iter().any(|r| r.online);
            return Err(if any_online {
                format!(
                    "no online sim matches the filters (country={country:?}, carrier={carrier:?}); {} of {} profiles are online",
                    results.iter().filter(|r| r.online).count(),
                    catalog.len()
                )
            } else {
                format!(
                    "no sim is online: none of the {} carrier ecosystems were reachable within the probe timeout (is this host online?)",
                    catalog.len()
                )
            });
        }
    };

    // Dual-slot bonus: the best online profile from a different country takes
    // the other slot. Slot 2 is refillable when it is empty — or when its
    // occupant is about to move to slot 1 (the winner itself), which frees it.
    // A different, deliberate slot-2 assignment is never clobbered.
    let mut second = None;
    let slot2_effective_free = slot2_occupant.is_none() || slot2_occupant == Some(winner.id);
    if slot == 1 && slot2_effective_free {
        second = results
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.online)
            .find_map(|r| by_id(r.profile_id).filter(|p| p.country != winner.country));
    }

    let table: Vec<Value> = results
        .iter()
        .map(|r| {
            let p = by_id(r.profile_id).expect("probe ids come from the catalog");
            json!({
                "id": p.id,
                "carrier": p.carrier,
                "country": p.country,
                "online": r.online,
                "latency_ms": r.latency_ms,
                "detail": r.detail,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    let online_count = results.iter().filter(|r| r.online).count();

    Ok(json!({
        "configured": {
            "slot": slot,
            "profile": profile_json(winner),
            "latency_ms": results.iter().find(|r| r.profile_id == winner.id).and_then(|r| r.latency_ms),
        },
        "second_slot": second.map(|p| json!({
            "slot": 2,
            "profile": profile_json(p),
        })),
        "scan": {
            "probed": catalog.len(),
            "online": online_count,
            "offline": catalog.len() - online_count,
            "results": table,
        },
        "mode": "config-space eSIM emulation (reachability-proved, not GSMA entitlement)",
    }))
}

fn profile_json(p: &SimProfile) -> Value {
    json!({
        "id": p.id,
        "carrier": p.carrier,
        "country": p.country,
        "country_name": p.country_name,
        "plmn": p.plmn(),
        "network": p.network,
        "iccid_synthetic": p.synthetic_iccid,
    })
}

/// Report entry for a slot-2 assignment that configure deliberately left
/// untouched (`None` when slot 2 is empty or holds an unknown id). Pure so the
/// wording and shape stay testable without touching the store file.
fn kept_slot2_report(slot2: Option<&str>) -> Option<Value> {
    slot2.and_then(find).map(|p| {
        json!({
            "slot": 2,
            "profile": profile_json(p),
            "note": "kept — configured earlier, left untouched",
        })
    })
}

/// Enable one specific profile on one slot (action=activate).
pub fn activate(profile_id: &str, slot: u32) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let p = find(profile_id).ok_or_else(|| {
        format!(
            "unknown sim profile {profile_id:?}; try android_sim action=list to see the catalog"
        )
    })?;
    let mut store = SimStore::load();
    store.set_slot(slot, p.id)?;
    store.configured_at = Some(now_iso());
    store
        .save()
        .map_err(|e| format!("persisting sim state: {e}"))?;
    Ok(json!({
        "activated": { "slot": slot, "profile": profile_json(p) },
        "persisted_to": store_path().display().to_string(),
    }))
}

/// Disable one slot (action=deactivate).
pub fn deactivate(slot: u32) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let mut store = SimStore::load();
    let removed = match slot {
        1 => store.slot1.take(),
        2 => store.slot2.take(),
        other => {
            return Err(format!(
                "slot {other} does not exist (device has 2 eSIM slots)"
            ))
        }
    };
    store
        .save()
        .map_err(|e| format!("persisting sim state: {e}"))?;
    Ok(json!({
        "deactivated": { "slot": slot, "was": removed },
        "slot": slot_json(&store, slot),
    }))
}

/// Small RFC-3339-ish timestamp without pulling chrono in.
fn now_iso() -> String {
    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let secs = now.as_secs();
    let days = secs / 86_400;
    // civil-from-days (Howard Hinnant's algorithm), enough for a timestamp.
    let z = days as i64 + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z.rem_euclid(146_097);
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    let hms = secs % 86_400;
    format!(
        "{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z",
        y,
        m,
        d,
        hms / 3600,
        (hms % 3600) / 60,
        hms % 60
    )
}
```
