## `crates/server/phone/src/compose.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/phone/src/compose.rs)

```rust
//! The compositor — turns [`OsState`] into pixels and routes touches.
//!
//! One thread ticks this at ~30 fps: drain the input queue, advance
//! animations/clock/battery, recompose the framebuffer if anything changed,
//! and commit it (`fb` + `fb_gen`). Everything else (adbd connections, the
//! screenshot path) reads the committed frame.

use std::time::SystemTime;

use crate::gfx::{in_rect, mix, Canvas};
use crate::state::*;
use crate::theme::*;
use crate::theme::{ACCENT, BG, DIM, DIMMER, GREEN, RED, SURFACE, SURFACE_HI, TEXT};

pub const STATUS_H: i32 = 48;
pub const NAV_H: i32 = 64;
pub const KB_ROWS: i32 = 4;
pub const KB_H: i32 = 56 * KB_ROWS + 16;

pub fn now() -> SystemTime {
    SystemTime::now()
}

/// Advance the device by one frame: input, events, clock/battery, re-render.
pub fn tick(st: &mut OsState) {
    // battery simulation: 1% / 90 s discharge, or +2% / 30 s on charger
    if st.last_battery_tick.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_secs() >= 30 {
        let secs = st.last_battery_tick.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_secs();
        st.last_battery_tick = now();
        if st.charging {
            st.battery = (st.battery + (secs / 15) as u8).min(100);
        } else {
            st.battery = st.battery.saturating_sub((secs / 45) as u8);
        }
        st.dirty = true;
        st.persist_dirty = true;
    }

    // the radio model advances every 2 s: RSRP drifts, bars move, Wi-Fi
    // fluctuates — the status bar shows a live modem, not a static icon
    if st.last_radio_tick.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_millis() >= 2000 {
        st.last_radio_tick = now();
        let t = now_ms();
        for (i, slot) in [1u32, 2].iter().enumerate() {
            let snap = mandroid::identity::sample_radio(
                *slot,
                &st.esim,
                st.airplane_mode,
                st.mobile_data,
                t,
            );
            if st.radio[i] != snap {
                st.radio[i] = snap;
                st.dirty = true;
            }
        }
        let wifi_on = st.settings.get("wifi").map(String::as_str) == Some("on");
        let wifi = mandroid::identity::sample_wifi(wifi_on, t);
        if st.wifi != wifi {
            st.wifi = wifi;
            st.dirty = true;
        }
    }

    // the boot chain: bootloader → (OS flash when an installer is armed) →
    // kernel/init (dmesg plays) → boot animation → home. Each stage does the
    // real work (the flash writes the image; the kernel stage fills dmesg).
    match st.boot.clone() {
        BootPhase::PowerOn { t0 } => {
            if t0.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_millis() >= 800 {
                st.boot = if st.installer.is_some() {
                    BootPhase::Flash
                } else {
                    BootPhase::Kernel { t0: now(), line: 0 }
                };
            }
            st.dirty = true;
        }
        BootPhase::Flash => {
            // one installer chunk per tick: the progress screen is the real
            // flash work, not an animation over nothing
            let mut finished = false;
            if let Some(inst) = st.installer.as_mut() {
                finished = !inst.step();
            }
            st.dirty = true;
            if finished {
                if let Some(inst) = st.installer.take() {
                    for l in inst.log() {
                        st.log_line(format!("I/installer( 1): {l}"));
                    }
                    st.log_line(format!(
                        "I/installer( 1): OS image flashed: {}",
                        crate::os::version_line(&st.data_dir)
                    ));
                }
                st.boot = BootPhase::Kernel { t0: now(), line: 0 };
                st.persist_dirty = true;
            }
        }
        BootPhase::Kernel { t0, line } => {
            // play the kernel/init log into dmesg one line per tick
            let script = crate::os::boot_script(&st.identity);
            if let Some(l) = script.get(line) {
                push_dmesg(st, l.clone());
                st.log_line(format!(
                    "I/init( 1): {}",
                    l.trim_start_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphabetic())
                        .to_string()
                ));
                st.boot = BootPhase::Kernel { t0, line: line + 1 };
            } else {
                st.boot = BootPhase::Splash { t0: now() };
            }
            st.dirty = true;
        }
        BootPhase::Splash { t0 } => {
            if t0.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_millis() >= 1500 {
                st.boot = BootPhase::Home;
                st.booted_at = now();
                st.logs
                    .push_back("I/roma-os( 1): boot completed (sys.boot_completed=1)".to_string());
                st.persist_dirty = true;
            }
            st.dirty = true;
        }
        _ => {}
    }

    // toast banner expiry
    if let Some((_, _, at)) = &st.banner {
        if at.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_millis() > 2600 {
            st.banner = None;
            st.dirty = true;
        }
    }

    // process events from background threads (browser loads, toasts, OS
    // install / reboot requests from Settings, recovery and adb shell)
    let pending: Vec<OsEvent> = st
        .inbox
        .lock()
        .map(|mut q| q.drain(..).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    for ev in pending {
        match ev {
            OsEvent::Toast(t) => {
                st.notify("System", &t, None);
            }
            OsEvent::OsInstall => {
                // Settings → System update, recovery, or `adb shell os install`:
                // the handset reboots through the bootloader and re-flashes
                st.installer = Some(crate::os::Installer::new(&st.data_dir, &st.identity));
                st.boot = BootPhase::PowerOn { t0: now() };
                st.current = None;
                st.recents_screen_open = false;
                st.recovery_open = false;
                st.screen_off = false;
                st.log_line(
                    "I/installer( 1): OS install requested — rebooting to bootloader".to_string(),
                );
                st.dirty = true;
            }
            OsEvent::Reboot => reboot_now(st),
            OsEvent::RebootRecovery => {
                st.recovery_open = true;
                st.recovery_sel = 0;
                st.recovery_confirm = false;
                st.current = None;
                st.recents_screen_open = false;
                st.boot = BootPhase::Recovery;
                st.logs
                    .push_back("I/roma-os( 1): booting into recovery".to_string());
                st.dirty = true;
            }
            OsEvent::BrowserLoaded {
                url,
                ok,
                detail,
                body_path,
                status,
            } => {
                let ui = &mut st.app.browser;
                ui.loading = false;
                if ok {
                    let html = std::fs::read_to_string(&body_path).unwrap_or_default();
                    ui.lines = crate::apps::html_to_lines(&html, &url);
                    ui.status = status;
                    ui.error = None;
                    ui.scroll = 0;
                    // back/forward reloads keep their slot; a fresh navigation
                    // drops any forward entries and appends after the current one
                    let is_history_load = ui
                        .history_idx
                        .and_then(|i| ui.history.get(i))
                        .map_or(false, |h| *h == url);
                    if !is_history_load {
                        let keep = ui.history_idx.map_or(0, |i| i + 1).min(ui.history.len());
                        ui.history.truncate(keep);
                        ui.history.push(url.clone());
                        ui.history_idx = Some(ui.history.len() - 1);
                    }
                    ui.url_bar = url.clone();
                    ui.url_bar_focus = false;
                    ui.kb.visible = false;
                } else {
                    ui.error = Some(detail);
                    ui.lines.clear();
                }
                st.dirty = true;
            }
        }
    }

    // input
    while let Some(ev) = st.inq.pop_front() {
        st.dirty = true;
        match ev {
            InputEvent::Key(KeyCode::Power) => {
                st.screen_off = !st.screen_off;
            }
            _ if st.screen_off => {
                if matches!(
                    ev,
                    InputEvent::Touch(TouchEvent {
                        action: TouchAction::Up,
                        ..
                    })
                ) || matches!(
                    ev,
                    InputEvent::Key(KeyCode::Back) | InputEvent::Key(KeyCode::Home)
                ) {
                    st.screen_off = false; // any touch or Back/Home wakes
                }
            }
            // a real handset's input pipeline only comes up once the system
            // has booted (sys.boot_completed=1) — touches/keys during the
            // flash or kernel stage are dropped, not mis-routed into apps
            InputEvent::Key(KeyCode::Back)
                if matches!(st.boot, BootPhase::Recovery) || st.recovery_open =>
            {
                // Back leaves the recovery menu (like rebooting the system)
                st.recovery_open = false;
                if matches!(st.boot, BootPhase::Recovery) {
                    st.boot = BootPhase::Home;
                }
            }
            InputEvent::Touch(t) if matches!(st.boot, BootPhase::Recovery) || st.recovery_open => {
                recovery_tap(st, t);
            }
            _ if !st.boot.boot_completed() => {
                // still booting: input is not wired up yet — dropped like on
                // a real device
            }
            InputEvent::Key(k) => handle_key(st, k),
            InputEvent::Text(t) => handle_text(st, &t.text),
            InputEvent::Touch(t) => handle_touch(st, t),
        }
    }

    // titanium backup runs one package per tick while a batch is active
    if st.app.titanium.progress.is_some() {
        crate::apps::titanium_step(st);
        st.dirty = true;
    }

    // clock app + stopwatch invalidate every second
    if st.current == Some(AppId::Clock) || st.app.clock.started.is_some() {
        st.dirty = true;
    }

    if st.dirty {
        let (w, h) = st.effective_size();
        let mut canvas = Canvas::new(w, h);
        draw(&mut canvas, st);
        st.fb = canvas.px;
        st.fb_gen += 1;
        st.dirty = false;
    }

    // periodic persistence
    if st.persist_dirty && st.last_save.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_secs() >= 3 {
        if crate::persist::save(st).is_ok() {
            st.persist_dirty = false;
        }
        st.last_save = now();
    }
}

// ── screen composition ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn draw(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    match &st.boot {
        BootPhase::PowerOn { .. } => draw_bootloader(c),
        BootPhase::Flash => draw_flash(c, st),
        BootPhase::Kernel { .. } => draw_kernel(c, st),
        BootPhase::Splash { t0 } => {
            let p = (t0.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_millis() as f32 / 1500.0).min(1.0);
            draw_boot(c, p);
        }
        BootPhase::Recovery => draw_recovery(c, st),
        BootPhase::Home => {
            if st.screen_off {
                draw_screen_off(c);
                return;
            }
            draw_wallpaper(c, 0, 0, c.h as i32);
            if let Some(app) = st.current.clone() {
                if st.recents_screen_open {
                    draw_recents(c, st);
                } else {
                    draw_running_app(c, st, &app);
                }
            } else if st.recents_screen_open {
                draw_recents(c, st);
            } else {
                draw_launcher(c, st);
            }
            draw_status(c, st);
            draw_nav(c, st);
            draw_banner(c, st);
            if st.recovery_open {
                draw_recovery(c, st);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Bootloader: the vendor wordmark, the unlock state, and what happens next.
fn draw_bootloader(c: &mut Canvas) {
    c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
    let cx = c.w as i32 / 2;
    let cy = c.h as i32 / 2 - 120;
    // soft halo behind the wordmark
    c.glow(cx, cy + 60, 240, [64, 84, 150], 70);
    c.text_center(cx, cy, "G", 14, TEXT);
    c.text_center(cx, cy + 130, "caiman bootloader", 3, DIM);
    c.text_center(
        cx,
        cy + 180,
        "bootloader unlocked — verified boot state: orange",
        2,
        YELLOW,
    );
    c.text_center(
        cx,
        cy + 220,
        "flashing os image / booting kernel…",
        2,
        DIMMER,
    );
    // the classic orange unlocked-bootloader underline
    c.fill_rect(cx - 160, cy + 260, 320, 4, ORANGE);
}

/// OS flash progress — the installer's real work (partition table, file
/// extraction, checksum verification, manifest stamp).
fn draw_flash(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    c.fill([4, 6, 10]);
    let (w, h) = (c.w as i32, c.h as i32);
    let done = st.installer.as_ref().map(|i| i.progress()).unwrap_or((
        1,
        1,
        "Install complete".to_string(),
    ));
    let (files_done, files_total, label) = done;
    let p = (files_done as f32 / files_total.max(1) as f32).min(1.0);
    c.text_center(w / 2, h / 2 - 190, "Installing OS update", 4, TEXT);
    c.text_center(w / 2, h / 2 - 140, &label, 3, ACCENT);
    // progress bar
    let bw = 480;
    let bx = w / 2 - bw / 2;
    let by = h / 2 - 90;
    c.round_rect(bx, by, bw, 14, 7, [30, 36, 46]);
    c.round_rect(bx, by, (bw as f32 * p).round() as i32, 14, 7, GREEN);
    c.text_center(
        w / 2,
        by + 46,
        &format!("{files_done} / {files_total} files written"),
        3,
        DIM,
    );
    // partition map (what a factory flash touches)
    let y0 = h / 2 + 20;
    for (i, part) in crate::os::PARTITIONS.iter().enumerate() {
        let y = y0 + i as i32 * 40;
        let col = if part.readonly { DIM } else { GREEN };
        c.text(
            60,
            y,
            &format!(
                "{:<11} {:<12} {:>7} MiB  {}",
                part.name,
                part.mount,
                part.size_kib / 1024,
                if part.readonly { "ro" } else { "rw" }
            ),
            2,
            col,
        );
    }
}

/// Kernel/init stage: the dmesg feed scrolling on a black panel.
fn draw_kernel(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
    let lines: Vec<&String> = st.dmesg.iter().rev().take(26).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let mut y = c.h as i32 - 60;
    for l in lines {
        c.text(16, y, l, 1, [120, 220, 140]);
        y -= 34;
        if y < 40 {
            break;
        }
    }
    if y >= 40 {
        c.text(16, 20, "ANDROID!", 2, DIM);
    }
}

fn draw_boot(c: &mut Canvas, p: f32) {
    c.fill([6, 8, 12]);
    let cx = c.w as i32 / 2;
    let cy = c.h as i32 / 2 - 60;
    // ambient halo: the wordmark breathes out of the dark
    c.glow(cx, cy + 40, 300, [46, 62, 120], 90);
    c.glow(cx, cy + 40, 140, [70, 96, 180], 60);
    // wordmark
    c.text_center(cx, cy, "romacode", 8, TEXT);
    c.text_center(cx, cy + 80, "P H O N E", 3, DIM);
    // progress bar: gradient fill over a dark track, glass track outline
    let bw = 320;
    let bx = cx - bw / 2;
    let by = cy + 200;
    c.round_rect(bx, by, bw, 10, 5, [24, 30, 42]);
    let fill = (bw as f32 * p).round() as i32;
    if fill > 8 {
        c.round_rect_gradient_v(bx, by, fill, 10, 5, ACCENT_HI, ACCENT_LO);
        // moving sheen on the leading edge
        let edge = bx + fill - 4;
        c.fill_rect(edge, by + 1, 3, 8, ACCENT_HI);
    }
    c.round_rect_outline(bx, by, bw, 10, 5, [58, 68, 88]);
    // three easing dots below — breathe in sequence
    for i in 0..3 {
        let phase = (p * 6.0 - i as f32 * 0.4).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        let a = (phase * 255.0) as u8;
        let dcol = mix(ACCENT_LO, BG, 1.0 - a as f32 / 255.0);
        let dx = cx - 40 + i * 40;
        c.glow(dx, by + 60, 14, ACCENT_LO, (a / 3).max(24));
        c.circle(dx, by + 60, 8, dcol);
    }
}

fn draw_screen_off(c: &mut Canvas) {
    c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
}

// ── recovery ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// The recovery menu — the real recovery text: reboot, apply OS update
/// (re-flash the image), wipe data, power off.
pub const RECOVERY_ROWS: [&str; 4] = [
    "Reboot system now",
    "Apply OS update (flash image)",
    "Wipe data / factory reset",
    "Power off",
];

fn draw_recovery(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    let (w, h) = st.effective_size();
    let wi = w as i32;
    // dim the system underneath (when shown as a Home overlay)
    c.fill_rect(0, 0, wi, h as i32, [0, 0, 0]);
    c.text(24, 28, "Android recovery — caiman", 3, ACCENT);
    c.text(
        24,
        66,
        "e:Unable to open LUN file (expected in emu)",
        1,
        DIMMER,
    );
    c.fill_rect(0, 96, wi, 2, DIM);
    let y0 = 130;
    let rh = 92;
    for (i, label) in RECOVERY_ROWS.iter().enumerate() {
        let y = y0 + i as i32 * rh;
        let sel = st.recovery_sel == i;
        if sel {
            c.fill_rect(0, y, wi, rh, [24, 34, 26]);
        }
        c.text(48, y + 26, if sel { "→ " } else { "  " }, 3, GREEN);
        c.text(100, y + 26, label, 3, if sel { TEXT } else { DIM });
    }
    // wipe confirmation row (real recovery: extra confirmation step)
    let cy = y0 + RECOVERY_ROWS.len() as i32 * rh;
    if st.recovery_confirm {
        c.text(
            48,
            cy + 8,
            "! wipe data: tap 'Wipe data / factory reset' again to confirm",
            2,
            YELLOW,
        );
    }
    c.text(
        24,
        cy + 70,
        "Back — leave recovery · select a row by tapping it",
        2,
        DIMMER,
    );
    let ver = crate::os::read_manifest(&st.data_dir)
        .map(|m| format!("installed: Android {} ({})", m.version, m.build_id))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "installed: no OS image".to_string());
    c.text(24, h as i32 - 60, &ver, 2, DIM);
}

/// Tap inside the recovery menu: pick a row, run its action.
fn recovery_tap(st: &mut OsState, t: TouchEvent) {
    if t.action != TouchAction::Up {
        return;
    }
    let (_, h) = st.effective_size();
    let y0 = 130;
    let rh = 92;
    let idx = ((t.y as i32 - y0) / rh).max(0) as usize;
    if (t.y as i32) >= (h as i32 - 70) && (t.x as i32) < 200 {
        // the "Back" hint strip at the bottom
        st.recovery_open = false;
        if matches!(st.boot, BootPhase::Recovery) {
            st.boot = BootPhase::Home;
        }
        st.dirty = true;
        return;
    }
    if idx >= RECOVERY_ROWS.len() {
        return;
    }
    st.recovery_sel = idx;
    match idx {
        0 => {
            // reboot system now: back through the full boot chain
            st.recovery_open = false;
            st.boot = BootPhase::Recovery;
            reboot_now(st);
        }
        1 => {
            // apply OS update: re-flash the image through the bootloader
            st.recovery_open = false;
            st.installer = Some(crate::os::Installer::new(&st.data_dir, &st.identity));
            st.boot = BootPhase::PowerOn { t0: now() };
            st.logs
                .push_back("I/recovery( 1): applying OS update (factory image)".to_string());
        }
        2 => {
            if st.recovery_confirm {
                wipe_data(st);
            } else {
                st.recovery_confirm = true;
            }
        }
        _ => {
            // power off: screen goes dark; any touch wakes it
            st.recovery_open = false;
            st.boot = BootPhase::Home;
            st.screen_off = true;
            st.logs
                .push_back("I/roma-os( 1): power off requested from recovery".to_string());
        }
    }
    st.dirty = true;
}

/// Factory reset: /data is wiped (user content, grants, the /data side of the
/// image skeleton); the system partitions stay, then the image re-flashes the
/// userdata skeleton — exactly what a factory reset + reflash does.
fn wipe_data(st: &mut OsState) {
    let dir = st.data_dir.clone();
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(crate::persist::state_path(&dir));
    for sub in ["sdcard", "photos", "cache", "termux", "adb_keys"] {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir.join(sub));
    }
    if let Some(data_host) = crate::os::host_path(&dir, "/data") {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&data_host);
    }
    st.sms.clear();
    st.calls.clear();
    st.photos.clear();
    st.notifications.clear();
    st.logs
        .push_back("I/recovery( 1): data wipe complete — restoring the factory image".to_string());
    st.installer = Some(crate::os::Installer::new(&dir, &st.identity));
    st.boot = BootPhase::PowerOn { t0: now() };
    st.current = None;
    st.recents_screen_open = false;
    st.recovery_open = false;
    st.recovery_confirm = false;
}

// ── boot helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Reboot through the real chain (bootloader → kernel → animation → home).
pub fn reboot_now(st: &mut OsState) {
    st.boot = BootPhase::PowerOn { t0: now() };
    st.current = None;
    st.recents_screen_open = false;
    st.screen_off = false;
    st.recovery_open = false;
    st.dmesg.clear();
    st.reboots += 1;
    st.log_line(format!(
        "I/roma-os( 1): reboot #{} — bootloader handshake",
        st.reboots
    ));
    st.dirty = true;
}

/// Append to the kernel ring buffer (dmesg), capped like a real ring buffer.
pub fn push_dmesg(st: &mut OsState, line: String) {
    if st.dmesg.len() >= 1024 {
        st.dmesg.pop_front();
    }
    st.dmesg.push_back(line);
}

/// Status bar: time, notification dot, wifi, cellular, battery.
/// Rendered as a translucent scrim over the wallpaper — the premium look —
/// fading to nothing at its lower edge.
fn draw_status(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    c.fill_rect_alpha(0, 0, c.w as i32, STATUS_H, STATUS_BG, 165);
    c.gradient_v_alpha(0, STATUS_H / 2, STATUS_H, c.w as i32, STATUS_BG, 60, 0);
    let (_, _h) = st.effective_size();
    let top = (STATUS_H / 2 - 8) as i32;
    // time (HH:MM, device clock = host clock)
    let time = time_hhmm();
    c.text(28, top, &time, 3, TEXT);
    if !st.notifications.is_empty() {
        let nx = c.w as i32 / 2 - 6;
        c.glow(nx, STATUS_H / 2, 14, ACCENT, 110);
        c.circle(nx, STATUS_H / 2, 5, ACCENT);
        c.circle(nx, STATUS_H / 2, 2, ACCENT_HI);
    }
    // right cluster
    let mut x = c.w as i32 - 28;
    // battery: rounded shell + rounded fill + charge glow
    let bw = 36;
    let by = top + 1;
    c.round_rect_outline(x - bw, by, bw, 16, 4, DIM);
    let fill = ((bw - 6) as u32 * st.battery as u32 / 100) as i32;
    let bcol = if st.charging {
        GREEN
    } else if st.battery <= 15 {
        RED
    } else {
        TEXT
    };
    if st.charging {
        c.glow(x - bw + 2 + fill, by + 8, 12, GREEN, 60);
    }
    if fill > 0 {
        c.round_rect(x - bw + 3, by + 3, fill, 10, 3, bcol);
    }
    c.fill_rect(x - 3, by + 5, 3, 6, DIM);
    x -= bw + 12;
    let pct = format!("{}%", st.battery);
    x -= Canvas::text_w(&pct, 2);
    c.text(x + 8, top + 1, &pct, 2, DIM);
    // wifi arcs (level follows the live RSSI)
    if st.settings.get("wifi").map(String::as_str) == Some("on") {
        x -= 22;
        let arcs = st.wifi.1.clamp(1, 3) as i32;
        for (i, w) in [10, 16, 22].iter().enumerate() {
            let row = 3 - i as i32;
            let col = if row <= arcs { TEXT } else { DIMMER };
            let seg = w / 3;
            for k in 0..row {
                let yy = top + 14 - k * 5;
                let half = (w / 2 - k * 3).max(1);
                let cx0 = x - 12;
                c.hline(cx0 - half, yy, seg, col);
                c.hline(cx0 + half - seg, yy, seg, col);
            }
        }
    }
    // cellular: airplane glyph when powered off, otherwise live bars per slot
    // with the default data slot's network tag (5G/LTE)
    let data = &st.radio[(st.esim.data_slot - 1) as usize];
    if st.airplane_mode {
        draw_airplane(c, x - 20, top);
    } else {
        // network tag of the default data slot, next to its bars
        let tag = if data.registered {
            data.network_display.clone()
        } else {
            "No service".to_string()
        };
        x -= Canvas::text_w(&tag, 2) + 6;
        c.text(x, top + 4, &tag, 2, if data.registered { DIM } else { RED });
        // the non-data slot first (leftmost), then the data slot's bars
        for slot in [1u32, 2].iter().rev() {
            let r = &st.radio[(*slot - 1) as usize];
            let bars = if r.registered { r.bars } else { 0 };
            x -= 34;
            draw_signal_bars(c, x, top, bars, r.registered, *slot == st.esim.data_slot);
            if *slot == 2 && r.registered {
                // small carrier initial between the two bar groups
                let initial = r
                    .operator_alpha
                    .chars()
                    .next()
                    .map(|c| c.to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                x -= Canvas::text_w(&initial, 2) + 4;
                c.text(x, top + 4, &initial, 2, DIMMER);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// One signal-bar group (Android style: 4 ascending bars, dim when the
/// radio has no service; the data slot renders brighter).
fn draw_signal_bars(c: &mut Canvas, x0: i32, top: i32, bars: u32, registered: bool, is_data: bool) {
    let lit = if is_data { TEXT } else { DIM };
    for i in 0..4u32 {
        let bh = 6 + i * 4;
        let col = if registered && i < bars { lit } else { DIMMER };
        c.fill_rect(x0 + i as i32 * 7, top + 16 - bh as i32, 5, bh as i32, col);
    }
}

/// A small airplane glyph (fuselage + swept wings + tail).
fn draw_airplane(c: &mut Canvas, cx: i32, top: i32) {
    c.fill_rect(cx - 2, top + 1, 4, 15, TEXT); // fuselage
    c.fill_rect(cx - 11, top + 6, 22, 3, TEXT); // wings
    c.fill_rect(cx - 7, top + 12, 14, 2, TEXT); // rear wing
    c.fill_rect(cx - 1, top + 15, 2, 3, TEXT); // tail fin
}

/// Navigation bar: back, home, recents — glass strip, crisp glyphs.
fn draw_nav(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    let (_, h) = st.effective_size();
    let y0 = h as i32 - NAV_H;
    // glass strip: translucent fill + soft top fade + hairline edge light
    c.fill_rect_alpha(0, y0, c.w as i32, NAV_H, NAV_BG, 150);
    c.gradient_v_alpha(0, y0 - 14, y0, c.w as i32, NAV_BG, 0, 110);
    c.fill_rect_alpha(0, y0, c.w as i32, 1, [255, 255, 255], 70);
    let cy = y0 + NAV_H / 2;
    let cx = c.w as i32;
    // back triangle — layered strokes give it a subtle anti-aliased feel
    let bx = cx / 6;
    for i in (0..12).rev() {
        let alpha = if i < 4 { 200 + i * 12 } else { 130 };
        c.fill_rect_alpha(
            bx + 12 - i,
            cy - i,
            i * 2 + 2,
            1,
            TEXT,
            alpha.min(255) as u8,
        );
    }
    // home ring — thin double ring reads crisper than a fat one
    c.ring(cx / 2, cy, 14, mix(TEXT, NAV_BG, 0.55));
    c.ring(cx / 2, cy, 13, TEXT);
    // recents square — 1 px outline now that the primitive is crisp
    let rx = cx * 5 / 6;
    c.round_rect_outline(rx - 12, cy - 12, 24, 24, 4, TEXT);
}

/// Home launcher: clock widget, glass search pill, app grid, glass dock, dots.
fn draw_launcher(c: &mut Canvas, st: &OsState) {
    let (w, h) = st.effective_size();
    let wi = w as i32;
    let top = STATUS_H;
    let bottom = h as i32 - NAV_H;
    // clock widget: halo glow behind large, thin-feeling numerals
    c.glow(wi / 2, top + 70, 220, [90, 110, 200], 46);
    c.text_center(wi / 2, top + 40, &time_hhmm(), 9, TEXT);
    c.text_center(wi / 2, top + 130, &date_str(), 3, DIM);
    // search pill: floating dark glass with a drop shadow and top sheen
    let pw = wi - 96;
    let py = top + 190;
    c.shadow(48, py, pw, 64, 32, 55);
    c.round_rect_alpha(48, py, pw, 64, 32, [10, 14, 22], 150);
    c.round_rect_alpha(50, py + 2, pw - 4, 26, 24, [255, 255, 255], 22);
    c.round_rect_outline(48, py, pw, 64, 32, mix(SURFACE_HI, [255, 255, 255], 0.25));
    // search glyph: accent ring + handle
    c.glow(48 + 34, py + 32, 16, ACCENT, 60);
    c.circle(48 + 34, py + 32, 12, ACCENT);
    c.circle(
        48 + 34,
        py + 32,
        8,
        mix([10, 14, 22], [255, 255, 255], 0.16),
    );
    c.line(48 + 42, py + 40, 48 + 50, py + 48, ACCENT_HI, 4);
    c.text(48 + 60, py + 22, "Search", 3, DIM);
    // pages: page 0 = built-in launchables, page 1 = user-installed
    let page = st.home_page.min(1);
    let apps: Vec<AppId> = builtin_launchables()
        .into_iter()
        .chain(
            st.packages
                .iter()
                .filter(|p| !p.system)
                .map(|p| AppId::User(p.package.clone())),
        )
        .collect();
    let per_page = 12usize;
    let pages = apps.len().div_ceil(per_page).max(1);
    let page = page.min(pages - 1);
    let slice: Vec<AppId> = apps
        .iter()
        .skip(page * per_page)
        .take(per_page)
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    let cols = 4usize;
    let cell_w = wi / cols as i32;
    let grid_y = py + 110;
    for (i, app) in slice.iter().enumerate() {
        let cx = (i % cols) as i32 * cell_w + cell_w / 2;
        let cy = grid_y + (i / cols) as i32 * 170;
        draw_app_icon(c, app, cx - 44, cy, 88);
        // ellipsize like a real launcher (cell fits ~11 chars at this size)
        let label = {
            let l = app.label();
            if l.chars().count() > 11 {
                format!("{}…", l.chars().take(10).collect::<String>())
            } else {
                l
            }
        };
        // label with a soft contact shadow for legibility over the wallpaper
        c.text_center(cx + 1, cy + 105, &label, 2, [0, 0, 0]);
        c.text_center(cx, cy + 104, &label, 2, TEXT);
    }
    // dock: floating glass tray with sheen and hairline edge
    let dock_apps = [
        AppId::Dialer,
        AppId::Messages,
        AppId::Browser,
        AppId::Settings,
    ];
    let dy = bottom - 150;
    c.shadow(40, dy - 12, wi - 80, 128, 36, 70);
    c.round_rect_alpha(40, dy - 12, wi - 80, 128, 36, [10, 14, 22], 130);
    c.round_rect_alpha(44, dy - 10, wi - 88, 40, 30, [255, 255, 255], 18);
    c.round_rect_outline(
        40,
        dy - 12,
        wi - 80,
        128,
        36,
        mix(SURFACE_HI, [255, 255, 255], 0.22),
    );
    let dw = (wi - 80) / 4;
    for (i, app) in dock_apps.iter().enumerate() {
        let i = i as i32;
        draw_app_icon(c, app, 40 + i * dw + dw / 2 - 40, dy, 80);
    }
    // page dots: the active page is a pill, the rest are quiet dots
    let dots_y = dy - 34;
    for i in 0..pages as i32 {
        let dx = wi / 2 - (pages as i32 * 24) / 2 + i * 24;
        if i as usize == page {
            c.round_rect(dx - 10, dots_y - 5, 24, 10, 5, ACCENT);
        } else {
            c.circle(dx + 2, dots_y, 5, DIMMER);
        }
    }
}

pub fn builtin_launchables() -> Vec<AppId> {
    vec![
        AppId::Settings,
        AppId::Calculator,
        AppId::Clock,
        AppId::Files,
        AppId::Messages,
        AppId::Dialer,
        AppId::Browser,
        AppId::Photos,
        AppId::Termux,
        // the root stack — installed apps, on the launcher like any other
        AppId::Magisk,
        AppId::RootExplorer,
        AppId::TitaniumBackup,
    ]
}

fn draw_running_app(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState, app: &AppId) {
    // app surface over the wallpaper
    c.fill_rect(0, STATUS_H, c.w as i32, c.h as i32 - STATUS_H - NAV_H, BG);
    crate::apps::render_app(c, st, app);
}

/// Recents screen: horizontal cards for the running/recent apps.
pub fn draw_recents(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    let (w, h) = st.effective_size();
    let wi = w as i32;
    c.fill_rect_alpha(
        0,
        STATUS_H,
        wi,
        h as i32 - STATUS_H - NAV_H,
        [8, 10, 14],
        235,
    );
    c.text_center(wi / 2, STATUS_H + 40, "Recent apps", 3, TEXT);
    if st.recents.is_empty() {
        c.text_center(wi / 2, h as i32 / 2, "No recent items", 3, DIM);
        return;
    }
    // card strip
    let card_w = (wi / 3).min(300);
    let card_h = (card_w as f32 * 1.9) as i32;
    let y = STATUS_H + 120;
    for (i, app) in st.recents.iter().enumerate().take(5) {
        let x = wi / 2 - card_w / 2 + (i as i32 - 2) * (card_w + 24);
        if x + card_w < 0 || x > wi {
            continue;
        }
        // side cards recede: dimmed and desaturated by distance from centre
        let dist = (i as i32 - 2).abs();
        let dim_t = (dist as f32 * 0.22).min(0.55);
        let is_active = dist == 0;
        c.shadow(x, y, card_w, card_h, 26, if is_active { 85 } else { 40 });
        c.round_rect(x, y, card_w, card_h, 26, SURFACE);
        // inner preview area: a quiet gradient with the app icon
        c.round_rect_gradient_v(
            x + 12,
            y + 12,
            card_w - 24,
            card_h - 130,
            18,
            mix(BG, [255, 255, 255], 0.05),
            mix(BG, [0, 0, 0], 0.25),
        );
        draw_app_icon(c, app, x + card_w / 2 - 40, y + 40, 80);
        c.text_center(x + card_w / 2, y + 150, &app.label(), 2, TEXT);
        // active card gets the accent hairline
        if is_active {
            c.round_rect_outline(x, y, card_w, card_h, 26, ACCENT);
        } else {
            c.round_rect_outline(
                x,
                y,
                card_w,
                card_h,
                26,
                mix(SURFACE_HI, [255, 255, 255], 0.15),
            );
        }
        // recede overlay: translucent black veil, flat — not over the icon glyph
        if dim_t > 0.0 {
            let a = (dim_t * 255.0) as u8;
            c.round_rect_alpha(x, y, card_w, card_h, 26, [0, 0, 0], a);
        }
    }
}

/// Notification banner at the top of the screen — floating glass card.
fn draw_banner(c: &mut Canvas, st: &mut OsState) {
    if let Some((title, body, at)) = &st.banner {
        if at.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_millis() < 2600 {
            let w = c.w as i32;
            let bx = 16;
            let by = STATUS_H + 8;
            let bw = w - 32;
            c.shadow(bx, by, bw, 96, 24, 80);
            c.round_rect_alpha(bx, by, bw, 96, 24, [14, 18, 26], 225);
            c.round_rect_alpha(bx + 3, by + 2, bw - 6, 30, 20, [255, 255, 255], 16);
            c.round_rect_outline(bx, by, bw, 96, 24, mix(SURFACE_HI, [255, 255, 255], 0.2));
            // accent bar — rounded, glowing
            c.glow(bx + 4, by + 48, 26, ACCENT, 70);
            c.round_rect(bx, by + 12, 6, 72, 3, ACCENT);
            c.text(bx + 28, by + 24, title, 3, TEXT);
            c.text_fit(bx + 28, by + 58, body, 2, bw - 60, DIM);
        }
    }
}

fn time_hhmm() -> String {
    let secs = crate::state::now_secs() as u64;
    let (_, hh, mm) = hms(secs);
    format!("{hh:02}:{mm:02}")
}

fn hms(secs: u64) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
    let ss = secs % 60;
    let mm = (secs / 60) % 60;
    let hh = (secs / 3600) % 24;
    (ss, hh, mm)
}

fn date_str() -> String {
    // days since epoch → YYYY-MM-DD (proleptic Gregorian, no deps)
    let days = crate::state::now_secs() as u64 / 86400;
    let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(days as i64);
    format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}")
}

pub fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = (doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1) as u32;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32;
    (if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y }, m, d)
}

// ── touch routing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn handle_touch(st: &mut OsState, t: TouchEvent) {
    let (w, h) = st.effective_size();

    match t.action {
        TouchAction::Down => {
            st.drag = Some((t.x as i32, t.y as i32));
        }
        TouchAction::Move => {}
        TouchAction::Up => {
            let Some((sx, sy)) = st.drag.take() else {
                return;
            };
            let dx = t.x as i32 - sx;
            let dy = t.y as i32 - sy;
            let x = t.x as i32;
            let y = t.y as i32;

            // nav bar zone (press or release inside it)
            if sy >= h as i32 - NAV_H || y >= h as i32 - NAV_H {
                nav_tap(st, x, y, h as i32);
                return;
            }
            // fling gestures
            if dx.abs() > 140 && dx.abs() > dy.abs() {
                if st.current.is_none() {
                    if dx < 0 && st.home_page == 0 {
                        st.home_page = 1;
                    } else if dx > 0 && st.home_page > 0 {
                        st.home_page = 0;
                    }
                    st.dirty = true;
                    return;
                }
                if st.current == Some(AppId::Browser) {
                    crate::apps::browser_nav(st, if dx > 0 { -1 } else { 1 });
                    st.dirty = true;
                    return;
                }
            }
            // everything else is a tap at the release point
            tap(st, x, y, w as i32, h as i32);
        }
    }
}

/// A tap at device coordinates (recents screen, home, or the open app).
fn tap(st: &mut OsState, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32) {
    if y >= h - NAV_H {
        nav_tap(st, x, y, h);
        return;
    }
    if st.recents_screen_open {
        // tap a card
        let card_w = (w / 3).min(300);
        let card_h = (card_w as f32 * 1.9) as i32;
        let ry = STATUS_H + 120;
        for (i, app) in st.recents.iter().enumerate().take(5) {
            let cx = w / 2 - card_w / 2 + (i as i32 - 2) * (card_w + 24);
            if in_rect(x, y, cx, ry, card_w, card_h) {
                let app = app.clone();
                st.recents_screen_open = false;
                st.launch_app(app);
                return;
            }
        }
        st.recents_screen_open = false;
        st.dirty = true;
        return;
    }
    if st.current.is_none() {
        home_tap(st, x, y, w, h);
    } else {
        let app = st.current.clone().unwrap_or(AppId::Settings);
        crate::apps::touch_app(st, &app, x, y);
    }
}

fn nav_tap(st: &mut OsState, x: i32, y: i32, h: i32) {
    let (w, _) = st.effective_size();
    let nav_y = h - NAV_H;
    if y < nav_y {
        return;
    }
    let cy = nav_y + NAV_H / 2;
    let _ = cy;
    let cx = w as i32;
    if x < cx / 3 {
        // back
        if st.recents_screen_open {
            st.recents_screen_open = false;
            st.dirty = true;
            return;
        }
        if let Some(app) = &st.current {
            let app = app.clone();
            if !crate::apps::go_back(st, &app) {
                st.current = None; // close app → home
                st.dirty = true;
            }
        }
    } else if x < cx * 2 / 3 {
        // home
        st.recents_screen_open = false;
        st.current = None;
        st.home_page = 0;
    } else {
        // recents
        st.recents_screen_open = !st.recents_screen_open;
    }
    st.dirty = true;
}

fn home_tap(st: &mut OsState, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32) {
    // recents screen?
    if st.recents_screen_open {
        // tap a card
        let card_w = (w / 3).min(300);
        let card_h = (card_w as f32 * 1.9) as i32;
        let ry = STATUS_H + 120;
        for (i, app) in st.recents.iter().enumerate().take(5) {
            let cx = w / 2 - card_w / 2 + (i as i32 - 2) * (card_w + 24);
            if in_rect(x, y, cx, ry, card_w, card_h) {
                let app = app.clone();
                st.recents_screen_open = false;
                st.launch_app(app);
                return;
            }
        }
        st.recents_screen_open = false;
        st.dirty = true;
        return;
    }
    let top = STATUS_H;
    let bottom = h - NAV_H;
    // search pill → browser
    let py = top + 190;
    if in_rect(x, y, 48, py, w - 96, 64) {
        st.launch_app(AppId::Browser);
        return;
    }
    // dock
    let dock_apps = [
        AppId::Dialer,
        AppId::Messages,
        AppId::Browser,
        AppId::Settings,
    ];
    let dy = bottom - 150;
    if y >= dy - 12 && y < dy + 116 {
        let dw = (w - 80) / 4;
        for (i, app) in dock_apps.iter().enumerate() {
            if in_rect(x, y, 40 + i as i32 * dw, dy, dw, 116) {
                let app = app.clone();
                st.launch_app(app);
                return;
            }
        }
    }
    // grid icons
    let page = st.home_page.min(1);
    let apps: Vec<AppId> = builtin_launchables()
        .into_iter()
        .chain(
            st.packages
                .iter()
                .filter(|p| !p.system)
                .map(|p| AppId::User(p.package.clone())),
        )
        .collect();
    let per_page = 12usize;
    let pages = apps.len().div_ceil(per_page).max(1);
    let page = page.min(pages - 1);
    let slice: Vec<AppId> = apps
        .iter()
        .skip(page * per_page)
        .take(per_page)
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    let cols = 4usize;
    let cell_w = w / cols as i32;
    let grid_y = py + 110;
    for (i, app) in slice.iter().enumerate() {
        let cx = (i % cols) as i32 * cell_w + cell_w / 2;
        let cy = grid_y + (i / cols) as i32 * 170;
        if in_rect(x, y, cx - 48, cy - 8, 96, 150) {
            let app = app.clone();
            st.launch_app(app);
            return;
        }
    }
}

fn handle_key(st: &mut OsState, k: KeyCode) {
    match k {
        KeyCode::Home => {
            st.current = None;
            st.recents_screen_open = false;
            st.screen_off = false;
        }
        KeyCode::Back => {
            if let Some(app) = &st.current {
                let app = app.clone();
                if !crate::apps::go_back(st, &app) {
                    st.current = None;
                }
            }
        }
        KeyCode::Enter => {
            if let Some(app) = st.current.clone() {
                crate::apps::key_enter(st, &app);
            }
        }
        KeyCode::Del => {
            if let Some(app) = st.current.clone() {
                crate::apps::key_del(st, &app);
            }
        }
        KeyCode::VolumeUp | KeyCode::VolumeDown | KeyCode::Power => {}
    }
    st.dirty = true;
}

fn handle_text(st: &mut OsState, text: &str) {
    if let Some(app) = &st.current {
        let app = app.clone();
        crate::apps::text_input(st, &app, text);
    }
    st.dirty = true;
}
```

[view on disk](crates/server/phone/src/gfx.rs)

```rust
//! Framebuffer drawing — a small integer raster library over an RGBA buffer.
//!
//! Everything the phone renders goes through [`Canvas`]: flat fills, rounded
//! rects, circles, lines and bitmap-font text (the classic 8x8 glyph set,
//! scaled). No image assets anywhere; every icon is drawn from shapes.

use font8x8::UnicodeFonts;

/// Maximum supported canvas side. Anything larger is almost certainly a
/// misconfiguration (e.g. a typo in `--display 10000x10000`) and is rejected
/// up front to avoid allocating gigabytes of pixel memory or tripping a u32
/// multiplication overflow on 32-bit targets.
const MAX_SIDE: u32 = 4096;

/// Reject obviously-wrong canvas dimensions before we allocate. This is a
/// developer-visible config error (typically a typo on `--display WxH`), not
/// untrusted input — panicking with a clear message is the right behaviour
/// because silently allocating ~67 GB (`4096*4096*4 * 4`) would OOM the host.
fn assert_valid_dims(w: u32, h: u32) {
    if w == 0 || h == 0 || w > MAX_SIDE || h > MAX_SIDE {
        panic!(
            "phone gfx: invalid canvas dims {w}x{h} (max {MAX_SIDE}x{MAX_SIDE}, min 1x1)"
        );
    }
}

pub type Rgb = [u8; 3];

pub struct Canvas {
    pub w: u32,
    pub h: u32,
    /// RGBA8, row-major, alpha always 255 (screencap encodes RGBA like a
    /// real device's screencap does).
    pub px: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Canvas {
    pub fn new(w: u32, h: u32) -> Self {
        assert_valid_dims(w, h);
        Self {
            w,
            h,
            px: vec![0; (w as usize) * (h as usize) * 4],
        }
    }

    pub fn resize(&mut self, w: u32, h: u32) {
        if self.w != w || self.h != h {
            assert_valid_dims(w, h);
            self.w = w;
            self.h = h;
            self.px = vec![0; (w as usize) * (h as usize) * 4];
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn idx(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> usize {
        ((y * self.w + x) * 4) as usize
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn set(&mut self, x: u32, y: u32, c: Rgb) {
        if x >= self.w || y >= self.h {
            return;
        }
        let i = self.idx(x, y);
        self.px[i] = c[0];
        self.px[i + 1] = c[1];
        self.px[i + 2] = c[2];
        self.px[i + 3] = 255;
    }

    pub fn fill(&mut self, c: Rgb) {
        for y in 0..self.h {
            for x in 0..self.w {
                self.set(x, y, c);
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn fill_rect(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, c: Rgb) {
        // Clamp in i32 BEFORE casting: a negative (x+w) or (y+h) cast to u32
        // would wrap to ~4 billion and iterate forever (bug seen on the
        // wallpaper's off-screen circle tops).
        let x0 = x.max(0) as u32;
        let y0 = y.max(0) as u32;
        let x1 = (x + w).max(0).min(self.w as i32) as u32;
        let y1 = (y + h).max(0).min(self.h as i32) as u32;
        for yy in y0..y1 {
            for xx in x0..x1 {
                self.set(xx, yy, c);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Vertical gradient between two colours across `y0..y1`.
    pub fn gradient_v(&mut self, x: i32, y0: i32, y1: i32, w: i32, top: Rgb, bottom: Rgb) {
        let span = (y1 - y0).max(1) as f32;
        for yy in y0.max(0)..y1.min(self.h as i32) {
            let t = (yy - y0) as f32 / span;
            let c = mix(top, bottom, t);
            self.fill_rect(x, yy, w, 1, c);
        }
    }

    pub fn hline(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, c: Rgb) {
        self.fill_rect(x, y, w, 1, c);
    }

    pub fn vline(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, h: i32, c: Rgb) {
        self.fill_rect(x, y, 1, h, c);
    }

    /// Filled rounded rectangle with a vertical gradient across its shape —
    /// every row is clipped to the rounded silhouette while the colour slides
    /// from `top` to `bottom`. The premium icon-tile primitive.
    pub fn round_rect_gradient_v(
        &mut self,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        w: i32,
        h: i32,
        r: i32,
        top: Rgb,
        bottom: Rgb,
    ) {
        if w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
            return;
        }
        let r = r.min(w / 2).min(h / 2).max(0);
        let span = (h - 1).max(1) as f32;
        for row in 0..h {
            // row span inset: inside the top/bottom corner arcs the row narrows
            let (x0, x1) = if row < r || row >= h - r {
                let dy = if row < r { r - row } else { row - (h - r) + 1 };
                // chord of the circle at this row offset: dx = r - sqrt(r²-dy²)
                let dy = dy.min(r);
                let dx = r - ((r * r - dy * dy) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
                (x + dx, x + w - dx)
            } else {
                (x, x + w)
            };
            let t = row as f32 / span;
            let c = mix(top, bottom, t);
            self.fill_rect(x0, y + row, x1 - x0, 1, c);
        }
    }

    /// Filled rounded rectangle.
    pub fn round_rect(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb) {
        if w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
            return;
        }
        let r = r.min(w / 2).min(h / 2).max(0);
        // centre slab + two side slabs + quarter circles at the corners
        self.fill_rect(x, y + r, w, h - 2 * r, c);
        self.fill_rect(x + r, y, w - 2 * r, r, c);
        self.fill_rect(x + r, y + h - r, w - 2 * r, r, c);
        for (cx, cy) in [
            (x + r, y + r),
            (x + w - r - 1, y + r),
            (x + r, y + h - r - 1),
            (x + w - r - 1, y + h - r - 1),
        ] {
            self.quarter_circle(cx, cy, r, c);
        }
    }

    fn quarter_circle(&mut self, cx: i32, cy: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb) {
        for dy in -r..=r {
            let dx = ((r * r - dy * dy) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
            if dy <= 0 {
                // top half: fill from cx-dx..cx+dx at row cy+dy
                self.fill_rect(cx - dx, cy + dy, dx * 2, 1, c);
            } else {
                self.fill_rect(cx - dx, cy + dy, dx * 2, 1, c);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Outline of a rounded rectangle (1 px stroke).
    pub fn round_rect_outline(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb) {
        let r = r.min(w / 2).min(h / 2).max(1);
        // top and bottom edges, straight segments between the corner arcs
        let x0 = x + r;
        let x1 = x + w - r;
        let y0 = y + r;
        let y1 = y + h - r;
        self.hline(x0, y, x1 - x0, c);
        self.hline(x0, y + h - 1, x1 - x0, c);
        self.vline(x, y0, y1 - y0, c);
        self.vline(x + w - 1, y0, y1 - y0, c);
        // corner arcs: walk each quarter circle and plot the two edge points
        for dy in 0..=r {
            let dx = ((r * r - dy * dy) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
            // top-left / top-right
            self.set((x + r - dx).max(0) as u32, (y + r - dy).max(0) as u32, c);
            self.set(
                (x + w - r + dx - 1).max(0) as u32,
                (y + r - dy).max(0) as u32,
                c,
            );
            // bottom-left / bottom-right
            self.set(
                (x + r - dx).max(0) as u32,
                (y + h - r + dy - 1).max(0) as u32,
                c,
            );
            self.set(
                (x + w - r + dx - 1).max(0) as u32,
                (y + h - r + dy - 1).max(0) as u32,
                c,
            );
        }
    }

    pub fn rect_outline(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, c: Rgb) {
        self.hline(x, y, w, c);
        self.hline(x, y + h - 1, w, c);
        self.vline(x, y, h, c);
        self.vline(x + w - 1, y, h, c);
    }

    // ── premium layer: alpha blending, shadows, glows, gradients ────────────

    /// Read the pixel currently at (x, y).
    pub fn get(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> Rgb {
        if x >= self.w || y >= self.h {
            return [0, 0, 0];
        }
        let i = self.idx(x, y);
        [self.px[i], self.px[i + 1], self.px[i + 2]]
    }

    /// Alpha-blend `c` over the existing pixel (`alpha` 0..=255).
    pub fn set_alpha(&mut self, x: u32, y: u32, c: Rgb, alpha: u8) {
        if x >= self.w || y >= self.h || alpha == 0 {
            return;
        }
        if alpha == 255 {
            self.set(x, y, c);
            return;
        }
        let base = self.get(x, y);
        let a = alpha as u32;
        let blend = |b: u8, o: u8| ((b as u32 * (255 - a) + o as u32 * a) / 255) as u8;
        let out = [
            blend(base[0], c[0]),
            blend(base[1], c[1]),
            blend(base[2], c[2]),
        ];
        let i = self.idx(x, y);
        self.px[i] = out[0];
        self.px[i + 1] = out[1];
        self.px[i + 2] = out[2];
        self.px[i + 3] = 255;
    }

    /// Alpha-blended flat rect (glass panels, scrims).
    pub fn fill_rect_alpha(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, c: Rgb, alpha: u8) {
        let x0 = x.max(0) as u32;
        let y0 = y.max(0) as u32;
        let x1 = (x + w).max(0).min(self.w as i32) as u32;
        let y1 = (y + h).max(0).min(self.h as i32) as u32;
        for yy in y0..y1 {
            for xx in x0..x1 {
                self.set_alpha(xx, yy, c, alpha);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Alpha-blended rounded rect — the workhorse of the glass look.
    pub fn round_rect_alpha(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb, alpha: u8) {
        if w <= 0 || h <= 0 || alpha == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let r = r.min(w / 2).min(h / 2).max(0);
        self.fill_rect_alpha(x, y + r, w, h - 2 * r, c, alpha);
        self.fill_rect_alpha(x + r, y, w - 2 * r, r, c, alpha);
        self.fill_rect_alpha(x + r, y + h - r, w - 2 * r, r, c, alpha);
        for (cx, cy) in [
            (x + r, y + r),
            (x + w - r - 1, y + r),
            (x + r, y + h - r - 1),
            (x + w - r - 1, y + h - r - 1),
        ] {
            self.quarter_circle_alpha(cx, cy, r, c, alpha);
        }
    }

    fn quarter_circle_alpha(&mut self, cx: i32, cy: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb, alpha: u8) {
        for dy in -r..=r {
            let dx = ((r * r - dy * dy) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
            let yy = cy + dy;
            self.fill_rect_alpha(cx - dx, yy, dx * 2, 1, c, alpha);
        }
    }

    /// Soft drop shadow under a rounded rect: concentric translucent rings,
    /// strongest at the edge, fading outward. Draw BEFORE the panel itself.
    pub fn shadow(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, r: i32, strength: u8) {
        let layers = 6;
        for l in (0..layers).rev() {
            let spread = l * 3;
            // falloff: outermost ~10% of strength → edge ~55%
            let t = 1.0 - l as f32 / layers as f32;
            let a = (strength as f32 * (0.10 + 0.45 * t)) as u8;
            self.round_rect_alpha(
                x - spread,
                y - spread,
                w + spread * 2,
                h + spread * 2,
                r + spread,
                [0, 0, 0],
                a,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Radial glow: a soft orb whose brightness falls off smoothly from the
    /// centre (`alpha` = centre intensity, 0..=255). This is what makes the
    /// wallpaper orbs luminous instead of flat circles.
    pub fn glow(&mut self, cx: i32, cy: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb, alpha: u8) {
        if r <= 0 || alpha == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let x0 = (cx - r).max(0);
        let x1 = (cx + r).min(self.w as i32 - 1);
        let y0 = (cy - r).max(0);
        let y1 = (cy + r).min(self.h as i32 - 1);
        let rr = (r * r) as f32;
        for py in y0..=y1 {
            let dy = py - cy;
            for px in x0..=x1 {
                let dx = px - cx;
                let d2 = (dx * dx + dy * dy) as f32;
                if d2 >= rr {
                    continue;
                }
                // quadratic falloff (smooth, no hard edge)
                let t = 1.0 - d2 / rr;
                let a = (alpha as f32 * t * t) as u8;
                if a > 0 {
                    self.set_alpha(px as u32, py as u32, c, a);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Horizontal gradient across `x0..x0+w` (progress bars, sheens).
    pub fn gradient_h(&mut self, x0: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32, left: Rgb, right: Rgb) {
        let span = w.max(1) as f32;
        for i in 0..w {
            let t = i as f32 / span;
            let c = mix(left, right, t);
            self.fill_rect(x0 + i, y, 1, h, c);
        }
    }

    /// Vertical gradient with alpha start → alpha end (scrims, status bar tint).
    pub fn gradient_v_alpha(&mut self, x: i32, y0: i32, y1: i32, w: i32, c: Rgb, a0: u8, a1: u8) {
        let span = (y1 - y0).max(1) as f32;
        for yy in y0.max(0)..y1.min(self.h as i32) {
            let t = (yy - y0) as f32 / span;
            let a = (a0 as f32 * (1.0 - t) + a1 as f32 * t).round() as u8;
            self.fill_rect_alpha(x, yy, w, 1, c, a);
        }
    }

    /// Darken the frame edges (photographic vignette) for depth.
    pub fn vignette(&mut self, strength: u8) {
        let w = self.w as i32;
        let h = self.h as i32;
        let cx = w as f32 / 2.0;
        let cy = h as f32 / 2.0;
        let max_d = (cx * cx + cy * cy).sqrt();
        for y in 0..h {
            for x in 0..w {
                let dx = x as f32 - cx;
                let dy = y as f32 - cy;
                let t = ((dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt() / max_d).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
                // only the outer 30% gets darkened, smoothly
                let edge = ((t - 0.7) / 0.3).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
                let a = (strength as f32 * edge) as u8;
                if a > 0 {
                    self.set_alpha(x as u32, y as u32, [0, 0, 0], a);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn circle(&mut self, cx: i32, cy: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb) {
        for dy in -r..=r {
            let dx = ((r * r - dy * dy) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
            self.fill_rect(cx - dx, cy + dy, dx * 2, 1, c);
        }
    }

    pub fn ring(&mut self, cx: i32, cy: i32, r: i32, c: Rgb) {
        for dy in -r..=r {
            let dx = ((r * r - dy * dy) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
            self.set((cx - dx).max(0) as u32, (cy + dy).max(0) as u32, c);
            self.set((cx + dx - 1).max(0) as u32, (cy + dy).max(0) as u32, c);
        }
        for dx in -r..=r {
            let dy = ((r * r - dx * dx) as f32).sqrt().round() as i32;
            self.set((cx + dx).max(0) as u32, (cy - dy).max(0) as u32, c);
            self.set((cx + dx).max(0) as u32, (cy + dy - 1).max(0) as u32, c);
        }
    }

    pub fn line(&mut self, x0: i32, y0: i32, x1: i32, y1: i32, c: Rgb, width: i32) {
        let dx = (x1 - x0).abs();
        let dy = (y1 - y0).abs();
        let sx = if x0 < x1 { 1 } else { -1 };
        let sy = if y0 < y1 { 1 } else { -1 };
        let mut err = dx - dy;
        let (mut x, mut y) = (x0, y0);
        let hw = (width / 2).max(0);
        loop {
            self.fill_rect(x - hw, y - hw, width.max(1), width.max(1), c);
            if x == x1 && y == y1 {
                break;
            }
            let e2 = 2 * err;
            if e2 > -dy {
                err -= dy;
                x += sx;
            }
            if e2 < dx {
                err += dx;
                y += sy;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Draw one character with the 8x8 bitmap font scaled to `px` pixels,
    /// smoothed: the glyph is resampled bilinearly and the edge is pushed
    /// through a smoothstep, so strokes stay crisp but diagonals and curves
    /// lose the chunky "scaled pixel" staircase. Returns the advance width
    /// (always `8 * px`, so layout is unchanged).
    pub fn char_at(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, ch: char, px: u32, c: Rgb) -> i32 {
        let s = px.max(1) as i32;
        let adv = 8 * s;
        let Some(glyph) = glyph_for(ch) else {
            return adv;
        };
        if glyph.iter().all(|&r| r == 0) {
            return adv;
        }
        let sf = s as f32;
        for oy in 0..adv {
            let py = y + oy;
            if py < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let v = (oy as f32 + 0.5) / sf - 0.5;
            for ox in 0..adv {
                let pxx = x + ox;
                if pxx < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let u = (ox as f32 + 0.5) / sf - 0.5;
                let cov = glyph_coverage(&glyph, u, v);
                if cov > 0.0 {
                    self.set_alpha(pxx as u32, py as u32, c, (cov * 255.0 + 0.5) as u8);
                }
            }
        }
        adv
    }

    /// Draw a string; returns the advance width in pixels.
    pub fn text(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, s: &str, px: u32, c: Rgb) -> i32 {
        let mut cx = x;
        for ch in s.chars() {
            cx += self.char_at(cx, y, ch, px, c);
        }
        cx - x
    }

    /// Width of a string at the given pixel size. The bitmap glyphs advance
    /// 8 scaled pixels per character (see `char_at`), so width = chars * 8 * px.
    pub fn text_w(s: &str, px: u32) -> i32 {
        (s.chars().count() as i32) * (px as i32 * 8)
    }

    /// Draw `s` centered horizontally at `xc`.
    pub fn text_center(&mut self, xc: i32, y: i32, s: &str, px: u32, c: Rgb) -> i32 {
        let w = Self::text_w(s, px);
        self.text(xc - w / 2, y, s, px, c)
    }

    /// Truncate with an ellipsis to fit `max_w` pixels, then draw.
    pub fn text_fit(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, s: &str, px: u32, max_w: i32, c: Rgb) {
        let adv = px as i32 * 8;
        let mut out = String::new();
        let mut w = 0;
        let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
        for (i, ch) in chars.iter().enumerate() {
            if w + adv + adv > max_w && i + 1 < chars.len() {
                out.push('…');
                break;
            }
            out.push(*ch);
            w += adv;
        }
        self.text(x, y, &out, px, c);
    }

    /// Blit a small RGBA patch (icons from PNG data use this via decode).
    pub fn blit(&mut self, x: i32, y: i32, w: u32, h: u32, rgba: &[u8]) {
        for yy in 0..h {
            for xx in 0..w {
                let i = ((yy * w + xx) * 4) as usize;
                if i + 3 < rgba.len() && rgba[i + 3] > 128 {
                    self.set(
                        (x + xx as i32).max(0) as u32,
                        (y + yy as i32).max(0) as u32,
                        [rgba[i], rgba[i + 1], rgba[i + 2]],
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
/// Look up an 8x8 glyph: ASCII, then Latin-1, plus hand-drawn bitmaps for the
/// typographic characters the UI uses (the stock tables have no `…` or `•`)
/// and plain fallbacks for curly quotes and dashes.
fn glyph_for(ch: char) -> Option<[u8; 8]> {
    match ch {
        '\u{2026}' => return Some([0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x49, 0x49]), // …
        '\u{2022}' => return Some([0, 0, 0x18, 0x3C, 0x3C, 0x18, 0, 0]), // •
        '\u{00B7}' => return Some([0, 0, 0, 0x18, 0x18, 0, 0, 0]), // ·
        '\u{2018}' | '\u{2019}' => return glyph_for('\''),
        '\u{201C}' | '\u{201D}' => return glyph_for('"'),
        '\u{2013}' | '\u{2014}' | '\u{2212}' => return glyph_for('-'),
        '\u{00A0}' => return Some([0; 8]),
        '\u{00D7}' => return glyph_for('x'),
        _ => {}
    }
    font8x8::BASIC_FONTS
        .get(ch)
        .or_else(|| font8x8::LATIN_FONTS.get(ch))
        .or(Some([0; 8]))
}

/// Anti-aliased coverage (0..=1) of an 8x8 bitmap at fractional glyph
/// coordinates `(u, v)` (texel centres sit on integers).
fn glyph_coverage(g: &[u8; 8], u: f32, v: f32) -> f32 {
    let bit = |x: i32, y: i32| -> f32 {
        if (0..8).contains(&x) && (0..8).contains(&y) {
            ((g[y as usize] >> x) & 1) as f32
        } else {
            0.0
        }
    };
    let (x0, y0) = (u.floor(), v.floor());
    let (fx, fy) = (u - x0, v - y0);
    let (xi, yi) = (x0 as i32, y0 as i32);
    let top = bit(xi, yi) * (1.0 - fx) + bit(xi + 1, yi) * fx;
    let bot = bit(xi, yi + 1) * (1.0 - fx) + bit(xi + 1, yi + 1) * fx;
    let val = top * (1.0 - fy) + bot * fy;
    // edge shaping: slightly below 0.5 keeps strokes a touch bolder/clearer
    let t = ((val - 0.28) / (0.62 - 0.28)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
    t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
}

pub fn mix(a: Rgb, b: Rgb, t: f32) -> Rgb {
    let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
    [
        (a[0] as f32 * (1.0 - t) + b[0] as f32 * t).round() as u8,
        (a[1] as f32 * (1.0 - t) + b[1] as f32 * t).round() as u8,
        (a[2] as f32 * (1.0 - t) + b[2] as f32 * t).round() as u8,
    ]
}

/// Chebyshev distance for hit-testing helpers.
pub fn in_circle(px: i32, py: i32, cx: i32, cy: i32, r: i32) -> bool {
    let dx = px - cx;
    let dy = py - cy;
    dx * dx + dy * dy <= r * r
}

pub fn in_rect(px: i32, py: i32, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32) -> bool {
    px >= x && px < x + w && py >= y && py < y + h
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn wallpaper_draw_terminates_quickly() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(720, 1560);
        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
        crate::theme::draw_wallpaper(&mut c, 0, 0, 1560);
        eprintln!("wallpaper took {:?}", t0.elapsed());
        assert!(t0.elapsed().as_secs() < 5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn launcher_screen_draw_terminates() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(720, 1560);
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("phone-gfx-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let mut st = crate::persist::fresh(&dir);
        st.boot = crate::state::BootPhase::Home;
        st.dirty = true;
        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
        // draw one full home frame via the public compositor draw path
        crate::compose::tick(&mut st);
        eprintln!("home frame took {:?}, fb_gen={}", t0.elapsed(), st.fb_gen);
        assert!(st.fb_gen >= 1);
        assert!(t0.elapsed().as_secs() < 10);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    // ── premium primitives ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

    #[test]
    fn alpha_blend_is_exact_and_monotonic() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(8, 8);
        c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
        c.set_alpha(0, 0, [255, 255, 255], 0);
        assert_eq!(c.get(0, 0), [0, 0, 0], "alpha 0 must not change the pixel");
        c.set_alpha(1, 0, [255, 255, 255], 255);
        assert_eq!(c.get(1, 0), [255, 255, 255], "alpha 255 must fully replace");
        c.set_alpha(2, 0, [255, 255, 255], 128);
        assert_eq!(c.get(2, 0), [128, 128, 128], "half blend over black");
        // monotonic ramp
        let mut prev = 0u8;
        for a in 0..=255u8 {
            c.set_alpha(3, 0, [255, 0, 0], a);
            let v = c.get(3, 0)[0];
            assert!(v >= prev, "red channel must be non-decreasing in alpha");
            prev = v;
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn shadow_darkens_without_leaving_artifacts() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(120, 120);
        c.fill([200, 200, 200]);
        c.shadow(20, 20, 80, 80, 12, 90);
        // just inside the shadow ring the pixel must be darker than the base
        let edge = c.get(16, 60);
        assert!(edge[0] < 200, "shadow must darken the surround");
        // far corner must be untouched
        assert_eq!(c.get(119, 0), [200, 200, 200]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn glow_falls_off_smoothly_to_zero() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(100, 100);
        c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
        c.glow(50, 50, 30, [255, 255, 255], 255);
        let centre = c.get(50, 50)[0];
        let mid = c.get(50 + 15, 50)[0];
        let rim = c.get(50 + 29, 50)[0];
        assert!(centre > mid && mid > rim, "brightness must fall outward");
        assert!(rim < 40, "rim must be near-black, not a hard edge");
        assert_eq!(
            c.get(50 + 31, 50),
            [0, 0, 0],
            "outside the radius untouched"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn outline_is_one_pixel_thick() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(60, 60);
        c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
        c.round_rect_outline(10, 10, 40, 40, 10, [255, 255, 255]);
        // top edge is lit, and exactly one pixel tall
        assert_eq!(c.get(30, 10), [255, 255, 255]);
        assert_eq!(
            c.get(30, 11),
            [0, 0, 0],
            "no second row — crisp 1 px stroke"
        );
        assert_eq!(c.get(30, 49), [255, 255, 255]);
        assert_eq!(c.get(30, 48), [0, 0, 0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn gradients_and_vignette_terminate() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(200, 200);
        c.fill([10, 10, 10]);
        c.gradient_h(0, 100, 200, 4, [255, 0, 0], [0, 0, 255]);
        c.gradient_v_alpha(0, 0, 48, 200, [0, 0, 0], 180, 0);
        c.vignette(120);
        // vignette keeps the centre intact and darkens the corner
        assert!(c.get(100, 100)[0] >= 10, "centre not vignetted");
        let corner = c.get(199, 199);
        assert!(corner[0] < 10 + 1, "corner darker than base");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! RomaCode's legacy in-process handset simulator. This is not Android and it
//! does not execute Android APKs; the TUI's production target uses host ADB.
//!
//! One process, two halves, no external binaries:
//!
//! * **Simulated UI** — a compositor that renders a mock launcher and apps,
//!   status/nav bars, soft keyboard) into a real RGBA framebuffer, plus the
//!   input pipeline (touch, keys, text), notifications, persistence.
//! * **Legacy protocol stub** — a local ADB-like service retained for tests;
//!   it is not a compatible Android runtime or a security boundary.
//!
//! Standalone test/development use only (`phone serve`).

pub mod adbd;
pub mod apps;
pub mod compose;
pub mod gfx;
pub mod net_fetch;
pub mod os;
pub mod persist;
pub mod shell;
pub mod state;
pub mod theme;

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

pub use state::OsState;

/// Boot configuration.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct PhoneConfig {
    /// Attach RomaCode to the host ADB server rather than booting this simulator.
    pub external_adb: bool,
    /// Exact `adb devices` serial; empty requires a sole online target.
    pub adb_serial: String,
    /// Android Platform-Tools executable path (or `adb` from PATH).
    pub adb_path: String,
    /// Preferred ADB port (5555 default; busy ports step +2 like real
    /// devices). Ignored when 0.
    pub port: u16,
    /// Data directory (state.json, sdcard, photos, adb_keys).
    pub data_dir: std::path::PathBuf,
    /// Display panel: (width, height) in px.
    pub display: (u32, u32),
    /// Display density in dpi.
    pub density: u32,
    /// When non-empty and `external_adb` is false, the bridge speaks the ADB
    /// wire protocol directly to this `host:port` instead of booting the
    /// in-process simulator. Empty = boot the simulator (legacy mode).
    pub native_target: String,
}

impl Default for PhoneConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            external_adb: false,
            adb_serial: String::new(),
            adb_path: "adb".into(),
            port: 5555,
            data_dir: persist::data_dir(),
            display: (state::PANEL_W, state::PANEL_H),
            density: state::PANEL_DPI,
            native_target: String::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// A live phone. Drop or [`shutdown`] to stop it.
pub struct PhoneHandle {
    pub port: u16,
    pub serial: String,
    pub state: Arc<Mutex<OsState>>,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    os_thread: Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>,
    adbd_thread: Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>,
}

impl PhoneHandle {
    /// Stop the compositor and adbd, flush persistence.
    pub fn shutdown(mut self) {
        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        if let Some(t) = self.os_thread.take() {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
        if let Some(t) = self.adbd_thread.take() {
            let _ = t.join();
        }
        if let Ok(st) = self.state.lock() {
            let _ = persist::save(&st);
        }
    }

    /// A screenshot of the current frame as PNG bytes.
    pub fn screenshot_png(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let st = self.state.lock().unwrap();
        shell::screencap_png(&st)
    }
}

impl Drop for PhoneHandle {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

/// Boot the phone: compositor thread + adbd listener. Returns once adbd is
/// actually listening (so callers know the real port).
pub fn boot(cfg: PhoneConfig) -> anyhow::Result<PhoneHandle> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&cfg.data_dir)?;
    let mut st = persist::load(&cfg.data_dir)?;
    st.display = cfg.display;
    st.density = cfg.density;
    // the handset goes through the real boot chain: bootloader → (OS flash
    // when no image is on disk yet) → kernel/init → boot animation → home
    st.boot = state::BootPhase::PowerOn {
        t0: std::time::SystemTime::now(),
    };
    st.dirty = true;
    if !os::is_installed(&cfg.data_dir) {
        // factory flash: the image is written to disk (partitioned, real
        // files, checksummed) before the kernel stage plays
        st.installer = Some(os::Installer::new(&cfg.data_dir, &st.identity));
        st.logs
            .push_back("I/boot( 1): no OS image on disk — factory flash scheduled".to_string());
    }
    let state = Arc::new(Mutex::new(st));

    let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));

    // compositor thread
    let (comp_state, comp_stop) = (state.clone(), stop.clone());
    let os_thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("phone-compositor".into())
        .spawn(move || loop {
            {
                let mut st = comp_state.lock().unwrap();
                compose::tick(&mut st);
            }
            if comp_stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                // final flush
                let st = comp_state.lock().unwrap();
                let _ = persist::save(&st);
                return;
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(33));
        })?;

    // adbd thread
    let adbd_state = state.clone();
    let adbd_stop = stop.clone();
    let bound = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None::<u16>));
    let bound_wait = bound.clone();
    // The old code did `let _ = daemon.serve()`: a bind failure (all ADB
    // ports taken, no permissions) vanished and boot died with the vague
    // "did not bind a port in time". Capture the actual error and surface it.
    let adbd_err = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None::<String>));
    let adbd_err_slot = adbd_err.clone();
    let adbd_thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
        .name("phone-adbd".into())
        .spawn(move || {
            let daemon = adbd::Adbd {
                state: adbd_state,
                stop: adbd_stop,
                bound_port: bound,
            };
            if let Err(e) = daemon.serve() {
                *adbd_err_slot.lock().unwrap() = Some(format!("{e:#}"));
            }
        })?;

    // wait until adbd has bound its port (bounded wait — 10 s; on a loaded
    // host the old 2 s window could expire before the listener came up)
    let mut port = None;
    for _ in 0..500 {
        if let Some(p) = *bound_wait.lock().unwrap() {
            port = Some(p);
            break;
        }
        if let Some(err) = adbd_err.lock().unwrap().clone() {
            anyhow::bail!("phone adbd failed to start: {err}");
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
    }
    let Some(port) = port else {
        let cause = adbd_err
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "no free ADB port in 5555..=5615".to_string());
        // Do NOT join: the listener may have bound at the exact moment we
        // gave up, and the thread then lives in its accept loop. Detach it
        // (the handle's Drop / stop flag reaps it when the phone is rebuilt).
        anyhow::bail!("adbd did not bind a port in time: {cause}");
    };

    // adopt the physical serial (the transport stays host:port for clients;
    // the device itself reports its physical serial, like a real handset)
    let serial = {
        let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();
        st.serial = st.identity.serial.clone();
        st.serial.clone()
    };

    Ok(PhoneHandle {
        port,
        serial,
        state,
        stop,
        os_thread: Some(os_thread),
        adbd_thread: Some(adbd_thread),
    })
}

/// Box-filter RGBA downscale (the same resampler the engine's screen module
/// uses for screenshots).
pub fn scale_rgba(src: &[u8], sw: u32, sh: u32, dw: u32, dh: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    mandroid::screen::box_filter(src, sw, sh, dw, dh)
}
```

```rust
//! `phone` — run the legacy in-process handset simulator for development only.
//!
//!     phone serve [--port N] [--display WxH] [--density D] [--data-dir P]
//!
//! This synthetic runtime is not Android and does not execute APKs. It listens
//! on 127.0.0.1:<port> with an ADB-like protocol for legacy tests only.
//!
//!     mandroid device 127.0.0.1:5555
//!     mandroid screen --target 127.0.0.1:5555 --screenshot home.png

use clap::Parser;

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(
    name = "phone",
    about = "Legacy RomaCode handset simulator (not an Android OS; APKs do not execute)"
)]
struct Cli {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    cmd: Cmd,
}

#[derive(clap::Subcommand)]
enum Cmd {
    /// Run the legacy simulator protocol server until the process is stopped.
    Serve {
        /// Preferred ADB port (default 5555; steps +2 when busy).
        #[arg(long, default_value_t = 5555)]
        port: u16,
        /// Display panel size WxH (default 720x1560).
        #[arg(long)]
        display: Option<String>,
        /// Display density dpi (default 420).
        #[arg(long, default_value_t = 420)]
        density: u32,
        /// Data directory (default ~/.romacode/android).
        #[arg(long)]
        data_dir: Option<String>,
        /// Quiet: suppress the startup banner.
        #[arg(long)]
        quiet: bool,
    },
}

fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    match cli.cmd {
        Cmd::Serve {
            port,
            display,
            density,
            data_dir,
            quiet,
        } => {
            let display = display
                .map(|d| -> anyhow::Result<(u32, u32)> {
                    let (w, h) = d
                        .split_once('x')
                        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("--display expects WxH"))?;
                    let w: u32 = w.parse()?;
                    let h: u32 = h.parse()?;
                    // Cap dimensions before they reach the pixel allocator: a
                    // typo like `--display 10000x10000` would otherwise try to
                    // allocate ~400 MB per framebuffer and trip the u32 multiply
                    // overflow check inside `Canvas::new`. 4096 matches the
                    // hardware ceiling of every shipping Android panel.
                    const MAX_SIDE: u32 = 4096;
                    if w == 0 || h == 0 || w > MAX_SIDE || h > MAX_SIDE {
                        anyhow::bail!(
                            "--display {w}x{h} out of range (min 1x1, max {MAX_SIDE}x{MAX_SIDE})"
                        );
                    }
                    Ok((w, h))
                })
                .transpose()?;
            let mut cfg = phone::PhoneConfig {
                port,
                density,
                ..Default::default()
            };
            if let Some((w, h)) = display {
                cfg.display = (w, h);
            }
            if let Some(d) = data_dir {
                cfg.data_dir = std::path::PathBuf::from(d);
            }
            let phone = phone::boot(cfg)?;
            if !quiet {
                eprintln!(
                    "RomaCode legacy simulator (not Android) — serial {} — local ADB-like server on 127.0.0.1:{} — data {}",
                    phone.serial,
                    phone.port,
                    phone.state.lock().unwrap().data_dir.display()
                );
            }
            // State is persisted every few seconds by the compositor, so a
            // SIGINT/SIGTERM from the terminal ends the run cleanly. On
            // graceful shutdown (romacode embeds the phone via the library
            // API), PhoneHandle::shutdown flushes and joins both threads.
            loop {
                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(600));
            }
        }
    }
}
```
