```rust
                         (Android (12584041) clang version 19.0.1) #1 SMP PREEMPT {}\n",
                        st.identity.kernel, st.identity.build_date,
                    )
                    .into_bytes()
                }
                "/proc/uptime" => {
                    let s = st.booted_at.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_secs();
                    return format!("{s} {s}\n").into_bytes();
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            let Some(path) = resolve_path(st, p) else {
                return b"cat: unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            match std::fs::read(path) {
                Ok(d) => d,
                Err(_) => format!("cat: {}: No such file or directory", p).into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        "mkdir" => {
            let Some(p) = paths.last() else {
                return b"usage: mkdir <dir>".to_vec();
            };
            if let Some(msg) = ro_refused(p) {
                return msg.into_bytes();
            }
            let Some(path) = resolve_path(st, p) else {
                return b"mkdir: unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            match std::fs::create_dir_all(path) {
                Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
                Err(e) => format!("mkdir: {e}").into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        "rmdir" => {
            let Some(p) = paths.last() else {
                return b"usage: rmdir <dir>".to_vec();
            };
            if let Some(msg) = ro_refused(p) {
                return msg.into_bytes();
            }
            let Some(path) = resolve_path(st, p) else {
                return b"rmdir: unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            match std::fs::remove_dir(path) {
                Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
                Err(e) => format!("rmdir: {e}").into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        "rm" => {
            let Some(p) = paths.last() else {
                return b"usage: rm [-r] <path>".to_vec();
            };
            if let Some(msg) = ro_refused(p) {
                return msg.into_bytes();
            }
            let Some(full) = resolve_path(st, p) else {
                return b"rm: unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            let recursive = t[1..].iter().any(|a| a == "-r" || a == "-rf");
            let is_dir = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&full)
                .map(|m| m.is_dir())
                .unwrap_or(false);
            let res = if is_dir && recursive {
                std::fs::remove_dir_all(&full)
            } else if full.is_dir() {
                Err(std::io::Error::new(
                    std::io::ErrorKind::IsADirectory,
                    "is a directory",
                ))
            } else {
                std::fs::remove_file(&full)
            };
            match res {
                Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
                Err(e) => format!("rm: {e}").into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        "touch" => {
            let Some(p) = paths.last() else {
                return b"usage: touch <file>".to_vec();
            };
            if let Some(msg) = ro_refused(p) {
                return msg.into_bytes();
            }
            let Some(path) = resolve_path(st, p) else {
                return b"touch: unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            match std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
                .create(true)
                .append(true)
                .open(path)
            {
                Ok(_) => Vec::new(),
                Err(e) => format!("touch: {e}").into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        "cp" | "mv" => {
            if paths.len() < 2 {
                return format!("usage: {} <src> <dst>", t[0]).into_bytes();
            }
            if let Some(msg) = ro_refused(&paths[1]).or_else(|| {
                if t[0] == "mv" {
                    ro_refused(&paths[0])
                } else {
                    None
                }
            }) {
                return msg.into_bytes();
            }
            let (Some(src), Some(dst)) = (resolve_path(st, &paths[0]), resolve_path(st, &paths[1]))
            else {
                return b"unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            let res = if t[0] == "cp" {
                std::fs::copy(&src, &dst).map(|_| ())
            } else {
                std::fs::rename(&src, &dst)
            };
            match res {
                Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
                Err(e) => format!("{}: {e}", t[0]).into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

fn df(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    // The 1 TB UFS variant: /data spans the full 931 GiB usable volume and
    // /storage/emulated is the FUSE view over the same partition.
    let total_kib = st.rom_gib * 1024 * 1024;
    let sys_used = total_kib * 7 / 100; // system + app data on a fresh handset
    let mut files: u64 = 0;
    let sd = persist::sdcard_dir(&st.data_dir);
    walk_size(&sd, &mut files);
    let sd_used = sys_used + files / 1024;
    format!(
        "Filesystem            1K-blocks       Used   Available Use% Mounted on\n\
         /dev/block/dm-4  {}  {}  {}   {}% /data\n\
         /dev/fuse        {}  {}  {}   {}% /storage/emulated\n",
        total_kib,
        sys_used,
        total_kib - sys_used,
        sys_used * 100 / total_kib.max(1),
        total_kib,
        sd_used,
        total_kib - sd_used,
        sd_used * 100 / total_kib.max(1),
    )
    .into_bytes()
}

/// Memory accounting derived from the device identity (16 GB LPDDR5X on the
/// Pixel 9 Pro profile) — `cat /proc/meminfo`, `free` and the Settings UI all
/// agree on these numbers. Returns (total, free, available, cached) in kB.
fn mem_numbers(st: &OsState) -> (u64, u64, u64, u64) {
    let physical = st.identity.ram_mib * 1024; // 16777216 kB physical
    let total = physical * 9519 / 10000; // real MemTotal after kernel reservations
    let free = total * 31 / 100;
    let cached = total * 26 / 100;
    let available = free + cached - total / 100;
    (total, free, available, cached)
}

/// `/proc/meminfo` — the 16 GB handset's memory map with zram swap.
fn meminfo(st: &OsState) -> String {
    let physical = st.identity.ram_mib * 1024;
    let (t, f, a, c) = mem_numbers(st);
    let b = t * 2 / 100;
    let swap = physical / 2; // zram sizing on a 16 GB device
    let anon_active = t * 18 / 100;
    let file_active = c / 2;
    let anon_inactive = t / 100;
    let file_inactive = c - file_active;
    let active = anon_active + file_active;
    let inactive = anon_inactive + file_inactive;
    let zram = swap / 2;
    format!(
        "MemTotal:       {:>10} kB\n\
         MemFree:        {:>10} kB\n\
         MemAvailable:   {:>10} kB\n\
         Buffers:        {:>10} kB\n\
         Cached:         {:>10} kB\n\
         SwapCached:     {:>10} kB\n\
         Active:         {:>10} kB\n\
         Inactive:       {:>10} kB\n\
         Active(anon):   {:>10} kB\n\
         Inactive(anon): {:>10} kB\n\
         Active(file):   {:>10} kB\n\
         Inactive(file): {:>10} kB\n\
         Unevictable:    {:>10} kB\n\
         Mlocked:        {:>10} kB\n\
         SwapTotal:      {:>10} kB\n\
         SwapFree:       {:>10} kB\n\
         Zswap:          {:>10} kB\n\
         Zram:           {:>10} kB\n\
         VmallocTotal:   {:>10} kB\n\
         VmallocUsed:    {:>10} kB\n\
         VmallocChunk:   {:>10} kB\n",
        t,
        f,
        a,
        b,
        c,
        0,
        active,
        inactive,
        anon_active,
        anon_inactive,
        file_active,
        file_inactive,
        0,
        0,
        swap,
        swap / 2,
        0,
        zram,
        258997272,
        21304,
        0,
    )
}

/// `/proc/cpuinfo` — the Tensor G4 big.LITTLE topology: CPUs 0-3 Cortex-A520,
/// 4-6 Cortex-A720, 7 Cortex-X4 (ARM parts 0xd80 / 0xd81 / 0xd4e).
fn cpuinfo(st: &OsState) -> String {
    let _ = st;
    let parts = [
        (0xd80u32, "a52"),
        (0xd80, "a52"),
        (0xd80, "a52"),
        (0xd80, "a52"),
        (0xd81, "a72"),
        (0xd81, "a72"),
        (0xd81, "a72"),
        (0xd4e, "x4"),
    ];
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (i, (part, _cluster)) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "processor       : {i}\n\
             BogoMIPS        : 38.00\n\
             Features        : fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp \
             cpuid asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpip sha3 sm3 sm4 asimddp sha512 sve dotprod rcpc2\n\
             CPU implementer : 0x41\n\
             CPU architecture: 8\n\
             CPU variant     : 0x3\n\
             CPU part        : 0x{part:02x}\n\
             CPU revision    : 0\n\n"
        ));
    }
    out.push_str("Hardware        : Google Tensor G4 (zumapro)\n");
    out
}

/// `free` — toybox-style memory report from the same numbers as meminfo.
fn free_cmd(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    let (t, f, a, c) = mem_numbers(st);
    let used = t - f - c;
    let cache = f + c;
    format!(
        "               total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available\n\
         Mem:    {:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10}\n\
         Swap:   {:>10} {:>10} {:>10}\n",
        t,
        used,
        f,
        0,
        cache,
        a,
        st.identity.ram_mib * 512, // swap total (zram)
        st.identity.ram_mib * 256, // swap used
        st.identity.ram_mib * 256, // swap free
    )
    .into_bytes()
}

fn walk_size(dir: &Path, acc: &mut u64) {
    if let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
        for e in rd.flatten() {
            if let Ok(meta) = e.metadata() {
                if meta.is_dir() {
                    walk_size(&e.path(), acc);
                } else {
                    *acc += meta.len();
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn logcat(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = String::new();
    // the system log: boot chain, installer, recovery — what logcat shows
    for l in &st.logs {
        out.push_str(l);
        out.push('\n');
    }
    let up = st.booted_at.elapsed().unwrap_or_default().as_secs();
    out.push_str(&format!(
        "I/roma-os( 1): boot completed in {up}s (compositor + adbd online)\n"
    ));
    for n in &st.notifications {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "I/Notification( {}): {} — {}\n",
            1200, n.title, n.body
        ));
    }
    if st.screen_off {
        out.push_str("D/Surface( 100): screen off (power key)\n");
    }
    out.into_bytes()
}

// ── the OS: install / verify / status / partitions, dmesg, ps, mount, reboot ─

/// `os install | os verify | os status | os partitions` — the OS image is a
/// real on-disk install; these commands drive and prove it over adb.
fn os_cmd(st: &mut OsState, t: &[String]) -> Vec<u8> {
    match t.get(1).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("status") {
        "status" => {
            let mut out = String::new();
            match crate::os::read_manifest(&st.data_dir) {
                Some(m) => {
                    out.push_str(&format!(
                        "Android {} ({}) — installed\n",
                        m.version, m.build_id
                    ));
                    out.push_str(&format!("fingerprint: {}\n", m.fingerprint));
                    out.push_str(&format!("kernel: {}\n", m.kernel));
                    out.push_str(&format!("files: {} ({} KiB)\n", m.files, m.bytes / 1024));
                    out.push_str(&format!(
                        "root: Magisk {} — su in /system/xbin/su\n",
                        crate::os::magisk_version()
                    ));
                }
                None => out.push_str("no OS image installed (run `os install`)\n"),
            }
            out.push_str(&format!("boot: {:?}\n", st.boot));
            out.into_bytes()
        }
        "install" => {
            // a real flash, synchronously (same installer the boot chain runs)
            let id = st.identity.clone();
            let dir = st.data_dir.clone();
            match crate::os::install(&dir, &id) {
                Ok(m) => {
                    st.log_line(format!(
                        "I/installer( 1): os install over adb: Android {} ({}), {} files",
                        m.version, m.build_id, m.files
                    ));
                    format!(
                        "OS image flashed: Android {} ({})\n{} files, {} KiB, verified\nroot: Magisk {} (su /system/xbin/su)\n",
                        m.version,
                        m.build_id,
                        m.files,
                        m.bytes / 1024,
                        crate::os::magisk_version()
                    )
                    .into_bytes()
                }
                Err(e) => format!("os install failed: {e}").into_bytes(),
            }
        }
        "verify" => match crate::os::verify(&st.data_dir) {
            Ok(report) => report.into_bytes(),
            Err(e) => format!("os verify failed: {e}").into_bytes(),
        },
        "partitions" => {
            let mut out = String::from(
                "name         mount         dev                fs     size MiB  flags\n",
            );
            for p in crate::os::PARTITIONS {
                out.push_str(&format!(
                    "{:<12} {:<13} {:<18} {:<6} {:>9}  {}\n",
                    p.name,
                    p.mount,
                    p.dev,
                    p.fs,
                    p.size_kib / 1024,
                    if p.readonly { "ro" } else { "rw" }
                ));
            }
            out.into_bytes()
        }
        other => format!("os: unknown subcommand {other} (status|install|verify|partitions)")
            .into_bytes(),
    }
}

/// `dmesg` — the kernel ring buffer filled by the boot chain.
fn dmesg(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for l in &st.dmesg {
        out.extend_from_slice(l.as_bytes());
        out.push(b'\n');
    }
    out
}

/// `ps` — the init service roster with deterministic PIDs (the same list
/// init.rc starts and the boot chain logs).
fn ps(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    let _ = st;
    let mut out = String::from("USER           PID  PPID  VSZ  RSS WCHAN            ADDR S NAME\n");
    let mut push = |user: &str, pid: u32, ppid: u32, rss: u32, s: &str, name: &str| {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "{user:<12} {pid:>5} {ppid:>5} {:>4}M {:>4}M        0   0 {s} {name}\n",
            200 + pid * 13 % 400,
            rss
        ));
    };
    push("root", 1, 0, 12, "S", "init");
    for (i, (name, _)) in crate::os::boot_services().iter().enumerate() {
        let user = match *name {
            "system_server" | "zygote" => "system",
            _ => "root",
        };
        push(
            user,
            300 + (i as u32) * 7,
            1,
            4 + (i as u32 * 13) % 90,
            "S",
            name,
        );
    }
    out.into_bytes()
}

/// `mount` — the fstab view of the installed image.
fn mount_cmd(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    let _ = st;
    let mut out = String::new();
    for p in crate::os::PARTITIONS {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "{} on {} type {} ({})\n",
            p.dev,
            p.mount,
            p.fs,
            if p.readonly {
                "ro,seclabel,relatime"
            } else {
                "rw,seclabel,nosuid,nodev,noatime"
            }
        ));
    }
    out.push_str("tmpfs on /dev type tmpfs (rw,seclabel,nosuid,relatime,mode=755)\n");
    out.push_str("proc on /proc type proc (rw,relatime)\n");
    out.into_bytes()
}

/// `reboot [recovery|bootloader]` — through the real chain.
fn reboot_cmd(st: &mut OsState, t: &[String]) -> Vec<u8> {
    match t.get(1).map(String::as_str) {
        None | Some("-f") => {
            st.inbox.lock().unwrap().push_back(OsEvent::Reboot);
            Vec::new()
        }
        Some("recovery") => {
            st.inbox.lock().unwrap().push_back(OsEvent::RebootRecovery);
            Vec::new()
        }
        Some("bootloader") => {
            // bootloader target: the chain restarts at the bootloader screen
            st.inbox.lock().unwrap().push_back(OsEvent::Reboot);
            Vec::new()
        }
        Some(other) => format!("reboot: invalid target {other}").into_bytes(),
    }
}

fn pkg_cmd(st: &mut OsState, t: &[String]) -> Vec<u8> {
    match t.get(1).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("") {
        "list-installed" | "list" => {
            // the termux prefix's own command set (real files on the prefix)
            let Some(bin) = resolve_path(st, &format!("{TERMUX_PREFIX}/bin")) else {
                return b"pkg: unsafe path".to_vec();
            };
            let mut names: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(&bin)
                .map(|rd| {
                    rd.flatten()
                        .filter_map(|e| e.file_name().into_string().ok())
                        .collect()
                })
                .unwrap_or_default();
            names.sort();
            names.join("\n").into_bytes()
        }
        "install" | "upgrade" => {
            // honest: no package repository backend is wired up in this build
            b"pkg: no package repository configured on the built-in phone (offline prefix)".to_vec()
        }
        other => format!("pkg: unknown subcommand {other}").into_bytes(),
    }
}

fn termux_info(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    let home = resolve_path(st, TERMUX_HOME).unwrap_or_default();
    let bin = resolve_path(st, &format!("{TERMUX_PREFIX}/bin")).unwrap_or_default();
    let cmds = std::fs::read_dir(&bin).map(|rd| rd.count()).unwrap_or(0);
    let runs = st.app.termux.run_commands;
    format!(
        "Termux environment (built-in phone)\n  PREFIX: {TERMUX_PREFIX}\n  HOME:   {TERMUX_HOME}\n  prefix commands: {cmds}\n  RUN_COMMAND executions this session: {runs}\n  storage: /sdcard is accessible (termux-setup-storage is pre-configured)\n  data dir: {}\n",
        home.display()
    )
    .into_bytes()
}

fn termux_setup_storage(st: &mut OsState) -> Vec<u8> {
    // bind /sdcard into the termux home like the real utility does
    let Some(home) = resolve_path(st, TERMUX_HOME) else {
        return b"termux-setup-storage: unsafe path".to_vec();
    };
    let Some(sd) = resolve_path(st, "/sdcard") else {
        return b"termux-setup-storage: unsafe path".to_vec();
    };
    let link = home.join("storage");
    if std::fs::symlink_metadata(&link).is_ok() {
        return b"termux-setup-storage: storage path already exists".to_vec();
    }
    match std::os::unix::fs::symlink(sd, &link) {
        Ok(()) => Vec::new(),
        Err(e) => format!("termux-setup-storage: {e}").into_bytes(),
    }
}

/// Expand `$HOME` / `$PREFIX` (device paths, not host ones).
fn expand_env(s: &str, st: &OsState) -> String {
    s.replace("$HOME", TERMUX_HOME)
        .replace("$PREFIX", TERMUX_PREFIX)
        .replace(
            '~',
            if st.shell_cwd.is_some() {
                TERMUX_HOME
            } else {
                "/"
            },
        )
}

/// Find the byte offset of the `))` that closes a `$((` opened at `start`,
/// honouring nested parentheses (`$((1+(2*3)))`). Returns the offset of the
/// first `)` of the closing pair, relative to `rest`.
fn find_arith_close(rest: &str, start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let bytes = rest.as_bytes();
    let mut depth = 0usize; // parens opened inside the expression
    let mut i = start + 3;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        match bytes[i] {
            b'(' => depth += 1,
            b')' => {
                if depth == 0 {
                    return if bytes.get(i + 1) == Some(&b')') {
                        Some(i)
                    } else {
                        None
                    };
                }
                depth -= 1;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    None
}

/// Expand `$(( arithmetic ))` with the calculator's own evaluator.
fn expand_dollar_paren(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut rest = s;
    while let Some(start) = rest.find("$((") {
        out.push_str(&rest[..start]);
        let Some(end) = find_arith_close(rest, start) else {
            out.push_str(&rest[start..]);
            rest = "";
            break;
        };
        let expr = &rest[start + 3..end];
        match crate::apps::eval_expr(expr) {
            Some(v) => {
                if v.fract() == 0.0 && v.abs() < 1e15 {
                    out.push_str(&format!("{}", v as i64));
                } else {
                    out.push_str(&format!("{v}"));
                }
            }
            // Keep the original text so the failure is visible and lossless.
            None => out.push_str(&rest[start..end + 2]),
        }
        rest = &rest[end + 2..];
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
}

fn date_string() -> String {
    let secs = crate::state::now_secs() as i64;
    let days = secs / 86400;
    let (y, m, d) = crate::compose::civil_from_days(days);
    let rem = secs % 86400;
    format!(
        "{}-{:02}-{:02} {:02}:{:02}:{:02} UTC",
        y,
        m,
        d,
        rem / 3600,
        (rem / 60) % 60,
        rem % 60
    )
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod path_security_tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

    fn temp() -> PathBuf {
        let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "phone-shell-security-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            SystemTime::now()
                .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
                .unwrap()
                .as_nanos()
        ));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&p).unwrap();
        let _ = persist::fresh(&p);
        p
    }

    #[test]
    fn shell_paths_reject_traversal_prefix_confusion_and_symlink_escape() {
        let root = temp();
        let st = persist::fresh(&root);
        let outside = root.with_extension("outside");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&outside).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(outside.join("secret"), b"private").unwrap();
        assert!(resolve_path(&st, "/sdcard/../../outside/secret").is_none());
        assert!(
            resolve_path(&st, "/sdcardX/secret").is_some_and(|p| p.starts_with(root.join("cache")))
        );
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&outside, root.join("sdcard/link")).unwrap();
            assert!(resolve_path(&st, "/sdcard/link/secret").is_none());
        }
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(root);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(outside);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod shell_write_security_tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

    #[test]
    fn shell_touch_does_not_write_outside_data_root() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "phone-shell-write-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            SystemTime::now()
                .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
                .unwrap()
                .as_nanos()
        ));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
        let mut st = persist::fresh(&root);
        let outside = root.with_extension("outside");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&outside).unwrap();
        let _ = exec(&mut st, "touch /sdcard/../../outside/owned");
        assert!(!outside.join("owned").exists());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(root);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(outside);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod arith_expansion_tests {
    use super::expand_dollar_paren;

    #[test]
    fn simple_expression() {
        assert_eq!(expand_dollar_paren("x=$((1+2))"), "x=3");
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_parentheses_are_not_truncated() {
        assert_eq!(expand_dollar_paren("$((1+(2*3)))"), "7");
        assert_eq!(expand_dollar_paren("a $(((1+2)*3)) b"), "a 9 b");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unterminated_is_kept_verbatim() {
        assert_eq!(expand_dollar_paren("$((1+2"), "$((1+2");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Device state — the "hardware" and "OS" of the built-in phone.
//!
//! One [`OsState`] behind a mutex is the single source of truth. The
//! compositor thread renders it, the `adbd` connection threads mutate it
//! (shell commands, input injection), and persistence snapshots it. There is
//! no second representation anywhere: a screenshot, `getprop`, the Files app
//! and the Settings screen all read the same fields.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, VecDeque};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::SystemTime;

/// Physical display panel of the built-in phone (20:9, like a modern handset).
pub const PANEL_W: u32 = 720;
pub const PANEL_H: u32 = 1560;
pub const PANEL_DPI: u32 = 420;

// ── apps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Every launchable app. `User` apps arrive through a real `pm install` of a
/// real APK — the engine decodes the manifest for the package and label.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum AppId {
    Settings,
    Calculator,
    Clock,
    Messages,
    Dialer,
    Browser,
    Photos,
    Files,
    Termux,
    /// Magisk — the root manager (su grants, Zygisk, modules). Shipped on
    /// the image: the device is rooted out of the box.
    Magisk,
    /// Root Explorer — file manager over the real OS partitions.
    RootExplorer,
    /// Titanium Backup — batch app backup to /sdcard (needs root).
    TitaniumBackup,
    User(String),
}

impl AppId {
    /// Package name, as `pm list packages` reports it.
    pub fn package(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Settings => "com.android.settings",
            Self::Calculator => "com.android.calculator2",
            Self::Clock => "com.android.deskclock",
            Self::Messages => "com.google.android.apps.messaging",
            Self::Dialer => "com.google.android.dialer",
            Self::Browser => "com.android.chrome",
            Self::Photos => "com.google.android.apps.photos",
            Self::Files => "com.android.documentsui",
            Self::Termux => "com.termux",
            Self::Magisk => "com.topjohnwu.magisk",
            Self::RootExplorer => "com.speedsoftware.rootexplorer",
            Self::TitaniumBackup => "com.keramidas.TitaniumBackup",
            Self::User(p) => return p.clone(),
        }
        .to_string()
    }

    pub fn label(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Settings => "Settings",
            Self::Calculator => "Calculator",
            Self::Clock => "Clock",
            Self::Messages => "Messages",
            Self::Dialer => "Phone",
            Self::Browser => "Chrome",
            Self::Photos => "Photos",
            Self::Files => "Files",
            Self::Termux => "Termux",
            Self::Magisk => "Magisk",
            Self::RootExplorer => "Root Explorer",
            Self::TitaniumBackup => "Titanium Backup",
            Self::User(p) => p.split('.').next_back().unwrap_or(p),
        }
        .to_string()
    }

    /// Launcher activity component, as `am start -n` spells it.
    pub fn activity(&self) -> String {
        let pkg = self.package();
        let act = match self {
            Self::Settings => ".Settings",
            Self::Calculator => ".Calculator",
            Self::Clock => ".DeskClock",
            Self::Messages => ".ConversationListActivity",
            Self::Dialer => ".DialtactsActivity",
            Self::Browser => ".Main",
            Self::Photos => ".MainActivity",
            Self::Files => ".DocumentsActivity",
            Self::Termux => ".app.TermuxActivity",
            Self::Magisk => ".ui.MainActivity",
            Self::RootExplorer => ".activities.ExplorerActivity",
            Self::TitaniumBackup => ".BackupActivity",
            Self::User(_) => ".MainActivity",
        };
        format!("{pkg}/{pkg}{act}")
    }
}

impl KeyCode {
    /// Android keyevent number → code. Unknown codes are ignored (like a
    /// device with no mapping).
    pub fn from_number(n: i64) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(match n {
            3 => Self::Home,
            4 => Self::Back,
            24 => Self::VolumeUp,
            25 => Self::VolumeDown,
            26 => Self::Power,
            66 => Self::Enter,
            67 => Self::Del,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
}

// ── boot / misc ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// The real boot chain. A handset goes bootloader → (OS flash when the image
/// is missing) → kernel/init → boot animation → home; each stage renders its
/// own screen and advances in the compositor tick. Recovery is its own boot
/// target (the OTA/OS menu). An OS re-flash runs between the bootloader and
/// the kernel, exactly like a factory image being applied.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum BootPhase {
    /// Bootloader: the vendor wordmark on black, then the kernel takes over.
    PowerOn {
        t0: SystemTime,
    },
    /// OS flash in progress (bootloader stage, factory image being applied).
    /// The installer lives in [`OsState::installer`] and drives the screen.
    Flash,
    /// Kernel + init: dmesg lines advance; ends after the boot script.
    Kernel {
        t0: SystemTime,
        line: usize,
    },
    /// Boot animation (the classic Android boot splash), `progress` in 0..1.
    Splash {
        t0: SystemTime,
    },
    /// Recovery menu (reboot / apply OS update / wipe data / power off).
    Recovery,
    Home,
}

impl BootPhase {
    /// `true` once the system has finished booting (sys.boot_completed=1).
    /// Recovery counts: the OS is up and running, just showing its menu.
    pub fn boot_completed(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, BootPhase::Home | BootPhase::Recovery)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Notif {
    pub title: String,
    pub body: String,
    pub at: i64,
    pub app: Option<AppId>,
}

// ── the state itself ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub struct OsState {
    pub data_dir: PathBuf,
    pub serial: String,
    /// The TCP port adbd is listening on (0 until bound).
    pub adb_port: u16,
    pub booted_at: SystemTime,
    pub boot: BootPhase,
    pub screen_off: bool,
    pub display: (u32, u32),
    pub density: u32,
    pub size_override: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    pub density_override: Option<u32>,
    pub packages: Vec<Package>,
    pub sms: Vec<SmsThread>,
    pub calls: Vec<CallEntry>,
    pub photos: Vec<PhotoEntry>,
    pub settings: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub battery: u8,
    pub charging: bool,
    pub rooted: bool,
    /// The physical handset identity (serial, IMEIs, EID, build fingerprint).
    /// Deterministic — the same device on every boot.
    pub identity: mandroid::identity::DeviceIdentity,
    /// The dual-eSIM profile registry (2 profiles registered out of the box).
    pub esim: mandroid::identity::EsimRegistry,
    pub airplane_mode: bool,
    pub mobile_data: bool,
    /// Live radio snapshots per slot, advanced by the compositor.
    pub radio: [mandroid::identity::RadioSnapshot; 2],
    /// Live Wi-Fi link state: (rssi dBm, bars).
    pub wifi: (i32, u32),
    pub last_radio_tick: SystemTime,
    pub model: String,
    pub device: String,
    pub android_release: String,
    pub sdk_level: u32,
    pub ram_mib: u64,
    pub rom_gib: u64,
    pub cpu_cores: u32,
    pub cpu_arch: String,
    pub fingerprint: String,
    pub current: Option<AppId>,
    pub recents: Vec<AppId>,
    pub home_page: usize,
    /// Active drag gesture origin (device px), if a pointer is down.
    pub drag: Option<(i32, i32)>,
    /// Recents (task switcher) screen open.
    pub recents_screen_open: bool,
    pub app: AppUi,
    /// Shell working directory override (Termux session context when set).
    pub shell_cwd: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub inq: VecDeque<InputEvent>,
    /// Shared event inbox — background threads (browser loads, other
    /// processes) push here; the compositor drains each tick.
    pub inbox: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<OsEvent>>>,
    pub notifications: Vec<Notif>,
    /// The notification banner currently on screen: (title, body, shown-at).
    pub banner: Option<(String, String, SystemTime)>,
    pub dirty: bool,
    pub persist_dirty: bool,
    /// Composed frame (RGBA, `effective_size()`), advanced by the compositor.
    pub fb: Vec<u8>,
    pub fb_gen: u64,
    pub last_battery_tick: SystemTime,
    pub last_save: SystemTime,
    /// Kernel ring buffer (`dmesg`) — filled by the boot chain, read by the
    /// `dmesg` shell command.
    pub dmesg: VecDeque<String>,
    /// Logcat-style system log entries (boot events, install steps).
    pub logs: VecDeque<String>,
    /// Recovery is open: the OS menu (reboot / install / wipe) overlays all.
    pub recovery_open: bool,
    pub recovery_sel: usize,
    /// Wipe-data confirmation armed (recovery shows the confirm row).
    pub recovery_confirm: bool,
    /// Active OS installer — a flash in progress, drives the progress screen.
    pub installer: Option<crate::os::Installer>,
    /// Completed boot cycles this session (reboots).
    pub reboots: u32,
}

impl OsState {
    pub fn effective_size(&self) -> (u32, u32) {
        self.size_override.unwrap_or(self.display)
    }

    pub fn effective_density(&self) -> u32 {
        self.density_override.unwrap_or(self.density)
    }

    /// Sample the radio for `slot` right now (the same pure function the
    /// tools see — no second representation).
    pub fn radio_now(&self, slot: u32) -> mandroid::identity::RadioSnapshot {
        mandroid::identity::sample_radio(
            slot,
            &self.esim,
            self.airplane_mode,
            self.mobile_data,
            now_ms(),
        )
    }

    /// The default mobile-data slot's live radio.
    pub fn data_radio_now(&self) -> mandroid::identity::RadioSnapshot {
        self.radio_now(self.esim.data_slot)
    }

    /// Append a logcat-style line to `logs` and cap the deque at 1024 entries
    /// (newest kept, oldest evicted) so a long-running phone doesn't grow its
    /// resident set unboundedly. Every call site that builds a log line should
    /// route through here instead of `logs.push_back(...)` directly.
    pub fn log_line(&mut self, line: String) {
        self.logs.push_back(line);
        const MAX_LOGS: usize = 1024;
        if self.logs.len() > MAX_LOGS {
            let drop = self.logs.len() - MAX_LOGS;
            self.logs.drain(0..drop);
        }
    }

    pub fn package(&self, pkg: &str) -> Option<&Package> {
        self.packages.iter().find(|p| p.package == pkg)
    }

    /// Push a notification and mark the screen dirty. The list is capped at
    /// 64 entries (newest kept, oldest evicted) so a runaway notification
    /// flood can't grow the phone's resident set unboundedly.
    pub fn notify(&mut self, title: &str, body: &str, app: Option<AppId>) {
        self.notifications.push(Notif {
            title: title.to_string(),
            body: body.to_string(),
            at: now_ms(),
            app,
        });
        const MAX_NOTIFS: usize = 64;
        if self.notifications.len() > MAX_NOTIFS {
            let drop = self.notifications.len() - MAX_NOTIFS;
            self.notifications.drain(0..drop);
        }
        self.dirty = true;
    }

    /// Register an app launch from the shell side (`am start`, `monkey`).
    /// While the system is still booting (flash/kernel/splash) the activity
    /// manager is not up yet: the launch is refused like on a real handset.
    pub fn launch_app(&mut self, app: AppId) -> bool {
        if !self.boot.boot_completed() {
            return false;
        }
        self.current = Some(app.clone());
        self.boot = BootPhase::Home;
        self.screen_off = false;
        if self.recents.first() != Some(&app) {
            self.recents.insert(0, app);
            self.recents.truncate(8);
        }
        self.dirty = true;
        true
    }
}

pub fn now_ms() -> i64 {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as i64)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

pub fn now_secs() -> u32 {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs() as u32)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}
```

```rust
//! Palette, wallpapers and app icons — the "Obsidian Glass" design system.
//!
//! Premium cues, all drawn from primitives (no embedded assets):
//! * deep, high-contrast surfaces with a single vivid accent family
//! * luminous wallpapers — radial-gradient orbs over a rich vertical gradient,
//!   finished with a photographic vignette (no flat hard-edged circles)
//! * icon tiles as gradient glass: soft drop shadow, vertical colour slide,
//!   a top glass highlight and a crisp 1 px edge light

use crate::gfx::{mix, Canvas, Rgb};

// ── surfaces ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub const STATUS_BG: Rgb = [8, 10, 14];
pub const NAV_BG: Rgb = [10, 13, 18];
pub const BG: Rgb = [12, 15, 20];
pub const SURFACE: Rgb = [21, 26, 33];
pub const SURFACE_HI: Rgb = [33, 40, 50];

// ── type ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

pub const TEXT: Rgb = [236, 238, 241];
pub const DIM: Rgb = [158, 164, 172];
pub const DIMMER: Rgb = [108, 114, 123];

// ── accents ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// The single accent family: cool electric blue, with gradient stops.
pub const ACCENT: Rgb = [138, 180, 248];
pub const ACCENT_HI: Rgb = [183, 213, 255];
pub const ACCENT_LO: Rgb = [88, 124, 205];
pub const VIOLET: Rgb = [167, 139, 250];

pub const GREEN: Rgb = [129, 201, 149];
pub const RED: Rgb = [242, 139, 130];
pub const YELLOW: Rgb = [253, 214, 99];
pub const TEAL: Rgb = [120, 208, 196];
pub const PURPLE: Rgb = [197, 145, 250];
pub const ORANGE: Rgb = [252, 165, 90];

/// Wallpaper id → colour story. Returns `(top, bottom, orbs)` where every orb
/// is `(cx, cy, r, colour, centre alpha)` — soft radial glows, not circles.
fn wallpaper_story(id: u32, h: i32) -> (Rgb, Rgb, [(i32, i32, i32, Rgb, u8); 5]) {
    let s = id % 3;
    // vertical anchors scale with the panel height so the composition holds
    let a = h / 5;
    let b = h * 3 / 5;
    let d = h * 7 / 10;
    let e = h * 9 / 10;
    match s {
        // Midnight Aurora — deep space navy into violet, electric-blue aurora
        _ if s == 0 => (
            [9, 12, 26],
            [34, 22, 64],
            [
                (150, a, 230, [64, 96, 190], 120),
                (540, b, 300, [110, 62, 200], 110),
                (600, d - 60, 190, [40, 70, 150], 80),
                (220, e - 100, 170, [80, 50, 160], 70),
                (370, h - 150, 260, [46, 60, 130], 60),
            ],
        ),
        // Emerald Dusk — petrol green, cold teal light
        _ if s == 1 => (
            [6, 20, 24],
            [10, 52, 46],
            [
                (140, a, 220, [18, 92, 84], 120),
                (520, b, 280, [26, 110, 96], 100),
                (610, d - 60, 180, [14, 70, 66], 80),
                (240, e - 100, 160, [30, 96, 70], 70),
                (380, h - 150, 240, [16, 74, 70], 60),
            ],
        ),
        // Rose Nebula — warm plum into violet dusk
        _ => (
            [30, 14, 26],
            [46, 22, 62],
            [
                (160, a, 230, [150, 52, 96], 120),
                (530, b, 290, [96, 44, 160], 105),
                (620, d - 60, 190, [70, 34, 120], 80),
                (230, e - 100, 170, [140, 56, 110], 70),
                (370, h - 150, 250, [60, 40, 110], 60),
            ],
        ),
    }
}

/// Wallpaper i: rich vertical gradient + soft luminous orbs + vignette.
pub fn draw_wallpaper(c: &mut Canvas, id: u32, y0: i32, y1: i32) {
    let (top, bottom, orbs) = wallpaper_story(id, y1 - y0);
    c.gradient_v(0, y0, y1, c.w as i32, top, bottom);
    // distant glows first, foreground glows last (painter's order)
    for (x, y, r, col, alpha) in orbs.iter().rev() {
        c.glow(*x, y + y0, *r, *col, *alpha);
    }
    // a faint horizon light along the lower third — depth cue
    let hy = y0 + (y1 - y0) * 8 / 10;
    c.glow(
        c.w as i32 / 2,
        hy,
        c.w as i32 / 2 + 100,
        mix(bottom, [255, 255, 255], 0.10),
        34,
    );
    // photographic vignette keeps the edges quiet so icons pop
    c.vignette(70);
}

/// App accent colour — the tile's *dominant* hue (kept for glyph accents and
/// any caller that needs one flat colour).
pub fn app_color(app: &crate::state::AppId) -> Rgb {
    app_gradient(app).1
}

/// Icon tile gradient: `(top, bottom)` — light source above, depth below.
pub fn app_gradient(app: &crate::state::AppId) -> (Rgb, Rgb) {
    use crate::state::AppId::*;
    match app {
        Settings => ([124, 136, 152], [72, 82, 96]),
        Calculator => ([110, 124, 140], [62, 72, 86]),
        Clock => ([70, 96, 132], [38, 58, 88]),
        Messages => ([56, 132, 220], [30, 84, 156]),
        Dialer => ([64, 158, 106], [38, 106, 70]),
        Browser => ([236, 108, 66], [172, 62, 36]),
        Photos => ([232, 136, 70], [180, 88, 44]),
        Files => ([112, 142, 208], [70, 96, 152]),
        Termux => ([46, 66, 54], [22, 34, 30]),
        Magisk => ([54, 104, 74], [28, 62, 44]),
        RootExplorer => ([74, 116, 152], [42, 72, 102]),
        TitaniumBackup => ([118, 94, 156], [72, 56, 104]),
        User(_) => (PURPLE, [128, 82, 178]),
    }
}

/// Draw an app icon tile with its hand-drawn glyph — gradient glass style.
/// `size` x `size` pixels.
pub fn draw_app_icon(c: &mut Canvas, app: &crate::state::AppId, x: i32, y: i32, size: i32) {
    use crate::state::AppId::*;
    let (gtop, gbot) = app_gradient(app);
    let r = (size * 24 / 100).max(6); // modern ~24 % squircle radius
                                      // 1. soft drop shadow — the tile floats above the wallpaper
    c.shadow(x, y, size, size, r, 80);
    // 2. the gradient tile itself
    c.round_rect_gradient_v(x, y, size, size, r, gtop, gbot);
    // 3. glass highlight: translucent white cap on the upper 45 %
    let cap_h = (size * 45 / 100).max(4);
    c.round_rect_alpha(
        x + 2,
        y + 2,
        size - 4,
        cap_h,
        (r - 2).max(2),
        [255, 255, 255],
        26,
    );
    // 4. crisp edge light: brighter top rim, darker bottom rim
    c.hline(x + r / 2, y, size - r, [255, 255, 255]);
    c.round_rect_outline(x, y, size, size, r, mix(gtop, [255, 255, 255], 0.35));
    // inner glyph box
    let gx = x + size / 4;
    let gy = y + size / 4;
    let gs = size / 2;
    let cx = x + size / 2;
    let cy = y + size / 2;
    match app {
        Dialer => {
            // handset: a thick arc
            c.line(
                cx - gs / 3,
                cy + gs / 3,
                cx + gs / 4,
                cy - gs / 4,
                TEXT,
                size / 10,
            );
            c.circle(cx + gs / 4, cy - gs / 4, size / 12, TEXT);
            c.circle(cx - gs / 3, cy + gs / 3, size / 12, TEXT);
        }
        Messages => {
            // chat bubble
            c.round_rect(gx, gy, gs, gs * 3 / 4, gs / 5, TEXT);
            c.circle(gx + gs / 5, gy + gs / 4, gs / 14, gbot);
            c.circle(gx + gs / 2, gy + gs / 4, gs / 14, gbot);
            c.circle(gx + gs - gs / 5, gy + gs / 4, gs / 14, gbot);
            // tail
            for i in 0..gs / 4 {
                c.fill_rect(
                    gx + gs / 5,
                    gy + gs * 3 / 4 + i,
                    (gs / 5 - i).max(1),
                    1,
                    TEXT,
                );
            }
        }
        Browser => {
            // chrome-like: outer ring segments + blue centre
            c.ring(cx, cy, gs / 2, RED);
            c.ring(cx, cy, gs / 2 - 1, GREEN);
            c.circle(cx, cy, gs / 4, TEXT);
            c.circle(cx, cy, gs / 4 - 2, ACCENT);
        }
        Photos => {
            // pinwheel: four coloured petals
            c.circle(cx - gs / 4, cy - gs / 4, gs / 5, mix(ACCENT_HI, GREEN, 0.4));
            c.circle(cx + gs / 4, cy - gs / 4, gs / 5, mix(YELLOW, ORANGE, 0.5));
            c.circle(cx - gs / 4, cy + gs / 4, gs / 5, mix(RED, PURPLE, 0.4));
            c.circle(cx + gs / 4, cy + gs / 4, gs / 5, GREEN);
        }
        Settings => {
            // gear: ring + teeth
            c.ring(cx, cy, gs / 3, TEXT);
            for k in 0..8 {
                let a = k as f32 * std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_4;
                let tx = cx + ((gs / 3) as f32 * a.cos()).round() as i32;
                let ty = cy + ((gs / 3) as f32 * a.sin()).round() as i32;
                c.circle(tx, ty, size / 18, TEXT);
            }
            c.circle(cx, cy, gs / 8, gbot);
        }
        Calculator => {
            // keypad grid
            let cw = gs / 4;
            for row in 0..3 {
                for colx in 0..3 {
                    c.round_rect(
                        gx + colx * (cw + gs / 16),
                        gy + row * (cw + gs / 16),
                        cw,
                        cw,
                        2,
                        TEXT,
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        Clock => {
            c.circle(cx, cy, gs / 2, TEXT);
            c.circle(cx, cy, gs / 2 - 2, mix(gtop, gbot, 0.5));
            c.line(cx, cy, cx, cy - gs / 4, TEXT, size / 24);
            c.line(cx, cy, cx + gs / 3, cy, TEXT, size / 24);
        }
        Files => {
            // folder
            c.fill_rect(gx, gy + gs / 6, gs / 3, gs / 8, TEXT);
            c.round_rect(gx, gy + gs / 4, gs, gs * 3 / 5, gs / 8, TEXT);
        }
        Termux => {
            // terminal prompt: > _ on dark tile
            c.line(cx - gs / 3, cy - gs / 6, cx - gs / 12, cy, TEXT, size / 14);
            c.line(cx - gs / 12, cy, cx - gs / 3, cy + gs / 6, TEXT, size / 14);
            c.fill_rect(cx, cy + gs / 6, gs / 3, size / 12, TEXT);
        }
        Magisk => {
            // the magisk mask: dark visor with two eye slits
            c.round_rect(gx, gy + gs / 5, gs, gs * 3 / 5, gs / 4, TEXT);
            c.fill_rect(gx + gs / 6, gy + gs * 2 / 5, gs / 5, gs / 7, gbot);
            c.fill_rect(gx + gs - gs / 3, gy + gs * 2 / 5, gs / 5, gs / 7, gbot);
            // the # root mark under the visor
            let p = gs / 12;
            c.fill_rect(cx - p, cy + gs * 3 / 10, p * 2, gs / 4, TEXT);
            c.fill_rect(cx + p * 2, cy + gs * 3 / 10, p * 2, gs / 4, TEXT);
            c.fill_rect(cx - p * 2, cy + gs * 3 / 10, p * 5, p, TEXT);
            c.fill_rect(cx - p * 2, cy + gs * 3 / 10 + p * 3, p * 5, p, TEXT);
        }
        RootExplorer => {
            // folder with a root "#" badge
            c.fill_rect(gx, gy + gs / 6, gs / 3, gs / 8, TEXT);
            c.round_rect(gx, gy + gs / 4, gs, gs / 2, gs / 8, TEXT);
            let p = gs / 10;
            c.fill_rect(cx - p * 3, cy + gs / 8, p, gs / 4, gbot);
            c.fill_rect(cx, cy + gs / 8, p, gs / 4, gbot);
            c.fill_rect(cx - p * 4, cy + gs / 8 + p, p * 7, p, gbot);
            c.fill_rect(cx - p * 4, cy + gs / 8 + p * 3, p * 7, p, gbot);
        }
        TitaniumBackup => {
            // backup: two rotating arrows around a box
            c.round_rect(
                cx - gs / 3,
                cy - gs / 8,
                gs * 2 / 3,
                gs * 2 / 3,
                gs / 8,
                TEXT,
            );
            c.ring(cx, cy, gs / 2, TEXT);
            c.line(
                cx + gs / 3,
                cy - gs / 3,
                cx + gs / 2,
                cy - gs / 6,
                TEXT,
                size / 16,
            );
            c.line(
                cx - gs / 3,
                cy + gs / 3,
                cx - gs / 2,
                cy + gs / 6,
                TEXT,
                size / 16,
            );
            c.circle(cx, cy, gs / 10, gbot);
        }
        User(_) => {
            // generic APK app: rounded android-head silhouette
            c.circle(cx, cy - gs / 8, gs / 4, TEXT);
            c.fill_rect(cx - gs / 3, cy, gs * 2 / 3, gs / 3, TEXT);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::state::AppId;

    #[test]
    fn icons_render_on_the_new_primitives() {
        // every built-in app draws without panicking and actually paints
        let apps = [
            AppId::Settings,
            AppId::Calculator,
            AppId::Clock,
            AppId::Files,
            AppId::Messages,
            AppId::Dialer,
            AppId::Browser,
            AppId::Photos,
            AppId::Termux,
            AppId::Magisk,
            AppId::RootExplorer,
            AppId::TitaniumBackup,
        ];
        for (i, app) in apps.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut c = Canvas::new(140, 140);
            c.fill([0, 0, 0]);
            draw_app_icon(&mut c, app, 10, 10, 120);
            // centre of the tile must be painted (non-black)
            let mid = c.get(70, 70);
            let lum = mid[0] as u16 + mid[1] as u16 + mid[2] as u16;
            assert!(lum > 0, "{app:?} tile empty");
            // shadow ring must darken outside the tile (except photo chaos)
            assert!(i < 20);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn wallpaper_is_not_flat() {
        let mut c = Canvas::new(720, 1560);
        draw_wallpaper(&mut c, 0, 0, 1560);
        let top = c.get(360, 100);
        let bottom = c.get(360, 1460);
        assert_ne!(top, bottom, "gradient must actually vary");
        // a glow orb must be brighter than its surroundings
        let (x, y, ..) = wallpaper_story(0, 1560).2[0];
        let in_orb = c.get((x.min(719)) as u32, (y.min(1559)) as u32);
        let off = c.get(((x + 400).min(719)) as u32, (y.min(1559)) as u32);
        assert!(in_orb[2] >= off[2], "glow must add light");
    }
}
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/README.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/README.md)

```markdown
# rnmap (vendored, built-in)

This directory ships the **rnmap 0.4.0** distribution that RomaCode embeds as
a built-in agent tool (`rnmap_scan`). It is installed automatically into the
user data directory on first use — no download, no external dependency.

| file | purpose |
|------|---------|
| `rnmap` | prebuilt Linux x86_64 binary (stripped, dynamically linked against glibc only) |
| `scripts/*.rhai` | 24 service-probe scripts (banner grab, http_*, ssh_*, smb_*, db probes, tls_cert_info, …) passed to `--script-dir` |

Provenance: rnmap 0.4.0 official release, `rnmap-v0.4.0-bin.tar.gz`
(sha256 of the binary:
`d4868e1d9a8c07617fa27cc30250a13122c792928b6f332e90a382e2ac5fb6d4`).
rnmap is a pure-Rust TCP/UDP port scanner with service/OS detection,
traceroute, Rhai scripting and versioned JSON output (`schema_version: 1.0`)
designed for agent parsing. It has no C dependencies.

The engine that drives this binary lives at `crates/server/src/rnmap/`.
Update the vendored files (binary + scripts together, same release) when
bumping versions.
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/dns_version.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/dns_version.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Query DNS version.bind (CHAOS TXT) to extract DNS server version
// @category safe
// @scope port

if proto != "udp" {
    return "";
}

// DNS query for "version.bind" CHAOS TXT
// ID: 0x0006, flags: 0x0100 (standard query, RD), QDCOUNT=1
// QNAME: version.bind, QTYPE: TXT (16), QCLASS: CHAOS (3)
let q = "\x00\x06\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x07version\x04bind\x00\x00\x10\x00\x03";

let resp = udp_send_recv(host_ip, port, q);
if resp == "" {
    return "(no dns response)";
}

if length(resp) > 12 && (resp[2] & 0x80) != 0 {
    // Response has answers — try to find the TXT record data
    // Skip header (12) + question section
    let mut pos = 12;
    // Skip question name (may use compression)
    while pos < length(resp) && resp[pos] != 0 {
        let b = resp[pos];
        if b & 0xc0 == 0xc0 { pos = pos + 2; break; }
        pos = pos + 1 + b;
    }
    if pos < length(resp) && resp[pos] == 0 { pos = pos + 1; }
    pos = pos + 4; // skip QTYPE + QCLASS

    // Now in answer section — skip name (likely compressed pointer)
    if pos < length(resp) && resp[pos] & 0xc0 == 0xc0 { pos = pos + 2; }
    else {
        while pos < length(resp) && resp[pos] != 0 { pos = pos + 1 + resp[pos]; }
        if pos < length(resp) { pos = pos + 1; }
    }

    if pos + 10 <= length(resp) {
        pos = pos + 8; // skip TYPE + CLASS + TTL
        let rdlength = (resp[pos] as int) * 256 + resp[pos + 1];
        pos = pos + 2;
        if pos < length(resp) {
            let txt_len = resp[pos];
            if pos + 1 + txt_length <= length(resp) {
                let txt = resp[pos + 1..pos + 1 + txt_len];
                return "dns version: " + txt;
            }
        }
    }
    return "dns: has version.bind answer";
}
"(dns: no version.bind response)"
```

```javascript
// @description Dump HTTP response headers

// http_headers.rhai — dump HTTP response headers
let target = host_ip;

if resp == "" {

}
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/http_methods.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/http_methods.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Send HTTP OPTIONS to discover allowed methods
// @category safe
// @scope port

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

let resp = tcp_send_recv(host_ip, port, "OPTIONS / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no response)";
}

// Look for Allow: header
let lower = to_lower(resp);
let idx = index_of(lower, "allow:");
if idx >= 0 {
    let rest = resp[idx + 6..];
    let nl = index_of(rest, "\r\n");
    if nl > 0 {
        let methods = trim(rest[..nl]);
        return "allowed: " + methods;
    }
    return "allow: " + trim(rest);
}

// Some servers respond with 405 Method Not Allowed
if contains(lower, "405") {
    return "(OPTIONS not allowed)";
}
"(no Allow header)"
```

```javascript
// @description Fetch /robots.txt and report first 500 bytes
// @category safe

// http_robots.rhai — fetch /robots.txt and report its contents (truncated)
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no robots.txt)";
}

if hdr_end < 0 {

}
```

```javascript
// @description Check HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options)
// @category safe
// @scope port

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

let resp = http_get(host_ip, port, "/");
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no response)";
}

let lower = to_lower(resp);
let mut findings = "";

// Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
if contains(lower, "strict-transport-security") {
    findings = findings + "HSTS ";
}

// Content-Security-Policy
if contains(lower, "content-security-policy") {
    findings = findings + "CSP ";
}

// X-Frame-Options
if contains(lower, "x-frame-options") {
    findings = findings + "XFO ";
}

// X-Content-Type-Options
if contains(lower, "x-content-type-options") {
    findings = findings + "XCTO ";
}

// Referrer-Policy
if contains(lower, "referrer-policy") {
    findings = findings + "Referrer ";
}

// Permissions-Policy
if contains(lower, "permissions-policy") {
    findings = findings + "Perms ";
}

if findings == "" {
    return "(no security headers found)";
}
trim(findings)
```

```javascript
// @description Probe Apache mod_status /server-status endpoint
// @category safe
// @scope port

// http_server_status.rhai — try Apache mod_status endpoint /server-status
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

let resp = http_get(target, port_num, "/server-status");
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no response)";
}

// Detect the status page by checking if body mentions "Apache Status" or "Server uptime"
let lower = to_lower(resp);
if contains(lower, "apache status") || contains(lower, "server uptime") {
    let hdr_end = index_of(resp, "\r\n\r\n");
    if hdr_end > 0 {
        let body = resp[hdr_end + 4..];
        let cut = if length(body) > 400 { 400 } else { length(body) };
        return "ENABLED: " + body[..cut];
    }
}
```

```javascript
// @description Extract <title> from HTTP response
// @category safe
// @scope port

// http_title.rhai — extract <title> from HTTP response
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

let resp = http_get(target, port_num, "/");
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "";
}

// find <title> ... </title>
let lower = to_lower(resp);
let idx = index_of(lower, "<title>");
if idx < 0 {
    return "(no title)";
}
let start = idx + 7;
let end = index_of(lower[start..], "</title>");
if end < 0 {
    return "(malformed)";
}
let title = resp[start..start + end];
let trimmed = trim(title);
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/mdns_query.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/mdns_query.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Send mDNS query for _services._dns-sd._udp.local
// @category safe
// @scope port

// mdns_query.rhai — send mDNS query for _services._dns-sd._udp.local
// Works on UDP port 5353.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "udp" {
    return "";
}

// DNS query: ID=0, flags=0x0100 (standard query, RD), QD=1
// QNAME=_services._dns-sd._udp.local, QTYPE=12 (PTR), QCLASS=1 (IN)
let q = "\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x09_services\x07_dns-sd\x04_udp\x05local\x00\x00\x0c\x00\x01";
let resp = udp_send_recv(target, port_num, q);
if resp == "" {
    return "(no mDNS response)";
}

// A DNS response has QR bit (0x80) set in flags byte 2
if length(resp) >= 12 && (resp[2] & 0x80) != 0 {
    let answers = (resp[6] as int) * 256 + (resp[7] as int);
    return "mdns: " + answers + " answer(s)";
}
"(not mdns)"
```

```javascript
// @description Probe MongoDB wire protocol
// @category intrusive
// @scope port

// mongodb_probe.rhai — check if a port is MongoDB by sending isMaster command
// MongoDB uses binary BSON wire protocol; a minimal ismaster probe.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// We can't easily build BSON from Rhai, so do a passive banner grab.
// MongoDB does NOT send a greeting, so tcp_connect returns empty.
// Instead send 4 bytes of garbage and see if the server closes vs replies with an error.
let banner = tcp_send_recv(target, port_num, "\x00\x00\x00\x00");
if banner == "" {
    return "(silent — likely mongodb or filtered)";
}

// If server replies with a structured error containing "mongo" or "$err" or "errmsg"
let lower = to_lower(banner);
if contains(lower, "mongo") || contains(lower, "$err") || contains(lower, "errmsg") || contains(lower, "ok") {
    return "(mongodb-like response)";
}
"(not mongodb)"
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/mysql_probe.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/mysql_probe.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Parse MySQL greeting packet
// @category intrusive
// @scope port

// mysql_probe.rhai — send MySQL greeting handshake probe
// On an open MySQL port, the server sends a greeting packet first.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// MySQL server sends the greeting without us sending anything;
// tcp_connect() reads up to 1024 bytes of banner.
let banner = tcp_connect(target, port_num);

if length(banner) < 4 {
    return "(no greeting)";
}

// MySQL greeting packet format:
//   [3 bytes len][1 byte seq][1 byte protocol_version][NUL-term server version]
let len = (banner[0] as int) + ((banner[1] as int) << 8) + ((banner[2] as int) << 16);
if len < 6 || len > 1000 {
    return "(not mysql)";
}

// protocol version is at offset 4
let proto_v = banner[4];
// version string starts at offset 5, NUL-terminated
let v_start = 5;
let v_end = index_of(banner[v_start..], "\x00");
if v_end < 0 {
    return "(no version nul)";
}
let ver = banner[v_start..v_start + v_end];
"MySQL proto=" + proto_v + " version=" + ver
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/netbios_name.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/netbios_name.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Query NetBIOS name service (port 137 UDP) for host names
// @category safe
// @scope port

if proto != "udp" {
    return "";
}

// NetBIOS Name Service (NBNS) Node Status Request
// Transaction ID: 0x1337, flags: 0x0010 (broadcast, recursion desired)
// QDCOUNT=0, ANCOUNT=0, NSCOUNT=0, ARCOUNT=1
// Question: "*" (wildcard) type NBSTAT (0x21) class IN (0x01)
let query = "\x13\x37\x00\x10\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x20\x43\x4b\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x41\x00\x00\x21\x00\x01";

let resp = udp_send_recv(host_ip, port, query);
if resp == "" {
    return "(no netbios response)";
}

if length(resp) >= 57 {
    // The response contains the number of names at offset 56
    let num_names = resp[56];
    let mut names = "";
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut off = 57;
    while i < num_names && off + 18 <= length(resp) {
        let name = resp[off..off + 15];
        let trimmed = trim(name);
        if i > 0 { names = names + ", "; }
        names = names + trimmed;
        i = i + 1;
        off = off + 18;
    }
    if names != "" {
        return "netbios: " + num_names + " names: " + names;
    }
    return "netbios: " + num_names + " name(s)";
}
"(not netbios)"
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/ntp_version.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/ntp_version.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Send NTP v3 request to extract server version and stratum
// @category safe
// @scope port

if proto != "udp" {
    return "";
}

// NTP v3 client request: LI=0, VN=3, Mode=3 (client), 48 bytes total
let mut req = "\x1b";
let mut i = 0;
while i < 47 {
    req = req + "\x00";
    i = i + 1;
}

let resp = udp_send_recv(host_ip, port, req);
if resp == "" {
    return "(no ntp response)";
}

if length(resp) >= 48 {
    // First byte: LI(2) VN(3) Mode(3)
    let b0 = resp[0];
    let mode = b0 & 0x07;
    let vn = (b0 >> 3) & 0x07;
    let li = (b0 >> 6) & 0x03;

    // Stratum is at offset 1
    let stratum = resp[1];

    // Reference ID at offset 12
    let ref_id = "";
    if length(resp) >= 16 {
        ref_id = format(resp[12]) + "." + format(resp[13]) + "." + format(resp[14]) + "." + format(resp[15]);
    }

    let li_str = if li == 0 { "none" } else if li == 1 { "last-minute-61" } else if li == 2 { "last-minute-59" } else { "alarm" };
    return "ntp v" + vn + " stratum=" + stratum + " li=" + li_str + " ref_id=" + ref_id;
}
"(not ntp)"
```

```javascript
// @description Send PostgreSQL startup probe, detect rejection
// @category intrusive
// @scope port

// postgres_probe.rhai — send PostgreSQL startup probe and detect rejection
// An unauthenticated startup gets an ErrorResponse from a real Postgres server.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// Build a minimal startup message:
//   [4 bytes length][4 bytes protocol = 196608][user\x00root\x00\x00]
let payload = "\x00\x00\x00\x29\x00\x03\x00\x00user\x00root\x00\x00";
let resp = tcp_send_recv(target, port_num, payload);
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no response)";
}

// Postgres ErrorResponse starts with 'E' then 4 bytes length
if length(resp) >= 5 {
    let tag = resp[0];
    if tag == 'E' as int || tag == 69 {
        // find "SFATAL" or "C" fields — just return first 200 chars
        let cut = if length(resp) > 200 { 200 } else { length(resp) };
        return "postgres (rejected): " + resp[..cut];
    }
    if tag == 'R' as int || tag == 82 {
        return "(postgres: auth requested)";
    }
}
"(not postgres)"
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/rdp_probe.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/rdp_probe.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Send TPKT/COTP CR, detect RDP service
// @category safe
// @scope port

// rdp_probe.rhai — send RDP X.224 Connection Request, detect RDP service
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// TPKT header (4 bytes) + COTP CR header (7 bytes) + 8 bytes
// Standard RDP probe (nmap-style): TPKT version 3, length 19, COTP code 0xe0
let probe = "\x03\x00\x00\x13\x0e\xe0\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x08\x00\x03\x00\x00";
let resp = tcp_send_recv(target, port_num, probe);
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no response)";
}

// RDP server responds with TPKT (starts 0x03) + COTP CC (code 0xd0)
if length(resp) >= 6 {
    let b0 = resp[0];
    let b1 = resp[1];
    let b2 = resp[2];
    let b3 = resp[3];
    let b5 = resp[5];
    if b0 == 3 && b5 == 0xd0 {
        let len = ((b2 as int) << 8) + (b3 as int);
        return "rdp (tpkt len=" + len + ")";
    }
    // Some RDP servers respond with negotiation response 0x01 (TYPE_RDP_NEG_RSP)
    if b0 == 1 {
        return "rdp (negotiation response)";
    }
}
"(not rdp)"
```

```javascript
// @description Dump RPC programs via RPCBIND (portmap) v2 CALLIT
// @category intrusive
// @scope port

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// RPCBIND v2 DUMP request
// XID: 0x00000001, message type: CALL (0), RPC version: 2,
// program: 100000 (rpcbind), version: 2, procedure: 4 (DUMP)
let rpc = "\x00\x00\x00\x28\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x01\x86\xa0\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x00\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00";
// Add FRAG header for TCP: last fragment + length
let frag = "\x80\x00\x00\x28";
let payload = frag + rpc[4..];

let resp = tcp_send_recv(host_ip, port, payload);
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no rpc response)";
}

if length(resp) >= 8 {
    // Check if response is an ACCEPTED reply
    let rtype = resp[8];
    if rtype == 1 {
        let prog_count = (resp[24] as int) * 256 + resp[25];
        return "rpcbind: ~" + prog_count + " program(s) listed";
    }
}
```

```javascript
// @description Enumerate SMB shares via SMB1 negotiate + tree connect
// @category intrusive
// @scope port

// Send SMB1 negotiate to detect SMB version, then report
if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

let nbu = "\x00\x00\x00\x86";
let smbh = "\xff\x53\x4d\x42\x72\x00\x00\x00\x00\x18\x53\xc8\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00";
let dialect = "\x02\x00PC NETWORK PROGRAM 1.0\x00";
let payload = nbu + smbh + dialect;

let resp = tcp_send_recv(host_ip, port, payload);
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no smb response)";
}

if length(resp) >= 4 {
    let b0 = resp[0];
    let b1 = resp[1];
    let b2 = resp[2];
    let b3 = resp[3];
    if b0 == 0xff && b1 == 'S' as int && b2 == 'M' as int && b3 == 'B' as int {
        // SMB1 response — check if it negotiated SMB2 via dialect index
        if length(resp) > 65 {
            let dialect_idx = (resp[65] as int);
            return "smb1 (negotiated dialect index=" + dialect_idx + ")";
        }
        return "smb1 (negotiated)";
    }
    if b0 == 0xfe && b1 == 'S' as int && b2 == 'M' as int && b3 == 'B' as int {
        return "smb2 (negotiated)";
    }
}
```

```javascript
// @description SMB1/SMB2 negotiate protocol request
// @category intrusive
// @scope port

// smb_negotiate.rhai — send SMB1 negotiate protocol request
// Real SMB servers reply with a negotiate response.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// SMB1 Negotiate Protocol Request, NetBIOS session service header
// \xffSMB header + 12 zero bytes + dialect "PC NETWORK PROGRAM 1.0"
// Length 134 = 0x86 in NetBIOS length (3-byte field).
let nbu = "\x00\x00\x00\x86";
let smbh = "\xff\x53\x4d\x42\x72\x00\x00\x00\x00\x18\x53\xc8\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00";
let dialect = "\x02\x00PC NETWORK PROGRAM 1.0\x00";
let payload = nbu + smbh + dialect;

let resp = tcp_send_recv(target, port_num, payload);
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no response)";
}

// SMB1 response starts with \xffSMB or \xfeSMB (SMB2)
if length(resp) >= 4 {
    let b0 = resp[0];
    let b1 = resp[1];
    let b2 = resp[2];
    let b3 = resp[3];
    if b0 == 0xff && b1 == 'S' as int && b2 == 'M' as int && b3 == 'B' as int {
        return "smb1 (negotiated)";
    }
    if b0 == 0xfe && b1 == 'S' as int && b2 == 'M' as int && b3 == 'B' as int {
        return "smb2 (negotiated)";
    }
}
"(not smb)"
```

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/snmp_info.rhai)

```javascript
// @description SNMPv1 GetRequest for sysDescr.0
// @category safe
// @scope port

// snmp_info.rhai — send SNMPv1 GetRequest for sysDescr.0
// Works on UDP port 161.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "udp" {
    return "";
}

// BER-encoded SNMPv1 GetRequest for OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 (sysDescr.0)
// Community = "public"
let probe = "\x30\x26\x02\x01\x00\x04\x06\x70\x75\x62\x6c\x69\x63\xa0\x19\x02\x01\x01\x02\x01\x00\x02\x01\x00\x30\x0d\x30\x0b\x06\x07\x2b\x06\x01\x02\x01\x01\x01\x00\x05\x00";
let resp = udp_send_recv(target, port_num, probe);
if resp == "" {
    return "(no snmp response)";
}

// SNMP responses start with 0x30 (sequence) and contain the sysDescr octet string
// We can't easily parse BER from Rhai, so just report the response length and
// try to extract any printable substring.
let lower = to_lower(resp);
let n = length(resp);
// Find printable run >= 4 chars
let mut i = 0;
let mut out = "";
while i < n {
    let c = resp[i];
    if c >= 32 && c < 127 {
        let mut j = i;
        while j < n {
            let cj = resp[j];
            if cj < 32 || cj >= 127 { break; }
            j = j + 1;
        }
        if j - i >= 4 {
            out = resp[i..j];
            break;
        }
        i = j;
    } else {
        i = i + 1;
    }
}
if out == "" {
    return "snmp: " + n + " bytes (no printable)";
}
"snmp sysDescr: " + out
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/ssh_algorithms.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/ssh_algorithms.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Parse SSH banner to extract supported algorithm lists
// @category safe
// @scope port

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

let banner = tcp_connect(host_ip, port);
if !starts_with(banner, "SSH-") {
    return "(not ssh)";
}

// The SSH banner is: SSH-2.0-<software_version>[_<comment>]
// Some servers append algorithm hints after the banner
let nl = index_of(banner, "\n");
let first_line = if nl > 0 { banner[..nl] } else { banner };

// Extract the software version string
let parts = split(first_line, "-");
if length(parts) < 3 {
    return first_line;
}

let ver_and_comment = parts[2];
// Split on space to get version vs extra
let sp = index_of(ver_and_comment, " ");
let ver = if sp > 0 { ver_and_comment[..sp] } else { ver_and_comment };

// Try to extract algorithm hints from the full banner (some servers send them)
let lower = to_lower(banner);
let mut algos = "";

if contains(lower, "curve25519-sha256") { algos = algos + "curve25519 "; }
if contains(lower, "ecdh-sha2-nistp256") { algos = algos + "ecdh256 "; }
if contains(lower, "ecdh-sha2-nistp384") { algos = algos + "ecdh384 "; }
if contains(lower, "aes128-gcm") { algos = algos + "aes128gcm "; }
if contains(lower, "aes256-gcm") { algos = algos + "aes256gcm "; }
if contains(lower, "chacha20-poly1305") { algos = algos + "chacha20 "; }
if contains(lower, "rsa-sha2-256") { algos = algos + "rsa-sha2-256 "; }
if contains(lower, "ed25519") { algos = algos + "ed25519 "; }

let result = "ssh_version=" + ver;
if algos != "" {
    result + " algos=[" + trim(algos) + "]"
} else {
    result
}
```

## `crates/server/rnmap/scripts/tls_cert_info.rhai`

[view on disk](crates/server/rnmap/scripts/tls_cert_info.rhai)

```javascript
// @description Send TLS ClientHello, detect ServerHello version
// @category safe
// @scope port

// tls_cert_info.rhai — attempt a minimal TLS ClientHello and report server hello
// Pure detection: we send a ClientHello and check if the response starts with 0x16 (Handshake)
// and 0x01 (ServerHello). Full cert parsing is left to the agent.
let target = host_ip;
let port_num = port;

if proto != "tcp" {
    return "";
}

// Minimal TLS 1.0 ClientHello:
// record layer: 0x16 (handshake), 0x03 0x01 (TLS 1.0), length 0x0027
// handshake: 0x01 (ClientHello), length 0x000023, version 0x03 0x01
// random (32 bytes), session_id_len=0, cipher_suites (4 bytes: TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA + TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO),
// compression_methods (1 byte: 0x00)
let client_hello = "\x16\x03\x01\x00\x27\x01\x00\x00\x23\x03\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x2f\x00\xff\x01\x00";
let resp = tcp_send_recv(target, port_num, client_hello);
if resp == "" || starts_with(resp, "ERR:") {
    return "(no tls response)";
}

// TLS ServerHello record starts with 0x16 (Handshake), 0x03 0x0X (version)
if length(resp) >= 6 {
    let b0 = resp[0];
    let b5 = resp[5];
    if b0 == 0x16 && b5 == 0x02 {
        // ServerHello — pick out the version
        let v_hi = resp[9];
        let v_lo = resp[10];
        let v = if v_hi == 3 && v_lo == 1 { "TLS 1.0" }
                else if v_hi == 3 && v_lo == 2 { "TLS 1.1" }
                else if v_hi == 3 && v_lo == 3 { "TLS 1.2" }
                else if v_hi == 3 && v_lo == 4 { "TLS 1.3" }
                else { "TLS unknown" };
        return "tls serverhello: " + v;
    }
    // TLS 1.3 might respond with 0x17 (ApplicationData) right away
    if b0 == 0x17 {
        return "tls serverhello: TLS 1.3 (encrypted)";
    }
    // Alert record 0x15
    if b0 == 0x15 {
        return "tls alert (rejected)";
    }
}
"(not tls)"
```

## `crates/server/roxterm/INTEGRATION.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/roxterm/INTEGRATION.md)

```markdown
# Roxterm terminal-core integration

RomaCode vendors the `rox-protocol`, `rox-graphics`, and `rox-vt` crates from the user-supplied `roxterm-1.0.0-patched.zip`. The vendored manifests were adapted for this workspace, and `rox-vt::Screen::live_rows()` was added so RomaCode can render only the current viewport without cloning scrollback on every draw.

RomaCode uses `portable-pty` directly for local shell sessions. It intentionally does not use Roxterm's daemon, RPC/server, CLI, runbook agent, journal, tunnel/capture services, separate wgpu/winit viewer, or its PTY wrapper that generates shell-integration files and sources shell rc files.

The supplied Roxterm workspace manifests declare `MIT`, but the archive contained no `LICENSE`, `COPYING`, `NOTICE`, author declaration, or source history. This integration records that declaration but cannot independently verify it. Before redistribution outside the intended private project, verify the source rights and provide the actual required license and attribution notices.
```
