```rust
//! Kitty graphics protocol support (the `ESC _ G ... ESC \` APC family).
//!
//! The store owns transmitted bitmaps and in-flight chunked transmits.
//! [`GraphicsStore::feed`] consumes one APC payload and emits typed events;
//! the VT screen turns placement events into grid [`ImagePlacement`]s.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use thiserror::Error;

const MAX_APC_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_PENDING_TRANSMITS: usize = 16;
const MAX_IMAGE_EDGE: u32 = 8192;
const MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS: u64 = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_STORED_IMAGES: usize = 64;
const MAX_STORED_RGBA_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PxFormat {
    /// f=0 / f=100: payload is a PNG file.
    Png,
    /// f=24: 3 bytes per pixel.
    Rgb,
    /// f=32: 4 bytes per pixel.
    Rgba,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DeleteScope {
    ByImageId(u32),
    ByImageNumber(u32),
    AllImages,
    AllPlacements,
    /// d=7: images and placements matching the given number.
    ByNumberEverywhere(u32),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum KittyEvent {
    ImageStored {
        image_id: u32,
        w: u32,
        h: u32,
    },
    /// Placement resolved against the cursor by the VT screen.
    Placed {
        image_id: u32,
        placement: RawPlacement,
    },
    Deleted(DeleteScope),
    Ignored,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RawPlacement {
    /// Cell offsets: absolute when explicitly set (X/Y), else cursor-relative.
    pub x_cells: Option<u32>,
    pub y_cells: Option<u32>,
    pub columns_cells: Option<u32>,
    pub rows_cells: Option<u32>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Image {
    pub id: u32,
    pub number: Option<u32>,
    pub w: u32,
    pub h: u32,
    pub rgba: Vec<u8>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum GraphicsError {
    #[error("base64 payload invalid")]
    Base64,
    #[error("PNG decode failed: {0}")]
    Png(String),
    #[error("raw pixel data truncated (need {need}, got {got})")]
    Truncated { need: usize, got: usize },
    #[error("image exceeds the embedded terminal resource limit")]
    TooLarge,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct ChunkBuf {
    control: ControlData,
    payload: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Parsed `key=value` control data of one APC.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
struct ControlData {
    action: Option<u8>,
    format: Option<u32>,
    transmission: Option<u8>,
    width: Option<u32>,
    height: Option<u32>,
    more: Option<u8>,
    image_id: Option<u32>,
    image_number: Option<u32>,
    placement_id: u32,
    quiet: Option<u8>,
    columns: Option<u32>,
    rows: Option<u32>,
    x: Option<u32>,
    y: Option<u32>,
    delete: Option<u32>,
}

impl ControlData {
    /// Merge a follow-up chunk's control data over this one (chunked transmits).
    fn merge_from(&mut self, other: &ControlData) {
        if other.action.is_some() {
            self.action = other.action;
        }
        if other.format.is_some() {
            self.format = other.format;
        }
        if other.transmission.is_some() {
            self.transmission = other.transmission;
        }
        if other.width.is_some() {
            self.width = other.width;
        }
        if other.height.is_some() {
            self.height = other.height;
        }
        if other.more.is_some() {
            self.more = other.more;
        }
        if other.image_id.is_some() {
            self.image_id = other.image_id;
        }
        if other.image_number.is_some() {
            self.image_number = other.image_number;
        }
        if other.quiet.is_some() {
            self.quiet = other.quiet;
        }
    }

    fn parse(payload: &[u8]) -> ControlData {
        let mut cd = ControlData::default();
        let head = payload.split(|b| *b == b';').next().unwrap_or(&[]);
        for kv in head.split(|b| *b == b',') {
            let mut it = kv.splitn(2, |b| *b == b'=');
            let k = it.next().unwrap_or(&[]);
            let v = it.next().unwrap_or(&[]);
            let val = || {
                std::str::from_utf8(v)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse().ok())
            };
            match k {
                b"a" => cd.action = v.first().copied(),
                b"f" => cd.format = val(),
                b"t" => cd.transmission = v.first().copied(),
                b"s" => cd.width = val(),
                b"v" => cd.height = val(),
                b"m" => {
                    cd.more = std::str::from_utf8(v)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
                        .map(|x| x as u8)
                }
                b"i" => cd.image_id = val(),
                b"I" => cd.image_number = val(),
                b"p" => cd.placement_id = val().unwrap_or(1),
                b"q" => {
                    cd.quiet = std::str::from_utf8(v)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
                        .map(|x| x as u8)
                }
                b"C" => cd.columns = val(),
                b"R" => cd.rows = val(),
                b"X" => cd.x = val(),
                b"Y" => cd.y = val(),
                b"d" => cd.delete = val(),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        cd
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct GraphicsStore {
    images: HashMap<u32, Image>,
    next_id: u32,
    pending: HashMap<u32, ChunkBuf>,
    /// Guess used to convert pixel sizes to cells when C/R are omitted.
    pub cell_px: (u32, u32),
}

impl GraphicsStore {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            cell_px: (8, 16),
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    pub fn get(&self, id: u32) -> Option<&Image> {
        self.images.get(&id)
    }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Image> {
        self.images.values()
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.images.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.images.is_empty()
    }

    /// Feed one APC payload (bytes between `ESC _` and `ESC \`).
    pub fn feed(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<KittyEvent, GraphicsError> {
        let cd = ControlData::parse(payload);
        let body = payload.split(|b| *b == b';').nth(1).unwrap_or(&[]);

        match cd.action.unwrap_or(b't') {
            b't' | b'T' => self.handle_transmit(&cd, body),
            b'p' => Ok(self.handle_place(&cd)),
            b'd' => Ok(self.handle_delete(&cd)),
            _ => Ok(KittyEvent::Ignored),
        }
    }

    /// Kitty strips base64 padding; accept padded or unpadded payloads.
    fn decode_b64(body: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, GraphicsError> {
        use base64::Engine as _;
        if body.len() > MAX_APC_BYTES {
            return Err(GraphicsError::TooLarge);
        }
        let mut s = String::with_capacity(body.len() + 4);
        for &b in body {
            if !b.is_ascii_whitespace() {
                s.push(b as char);
            }
        }
        while s.len() % 4 != 0 {
            s.push('=');
        }
        base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
            .decode(s.as_bytes())
            .map_err(|_| GraphicsError::Base64)
    }

    fn handle_transmit(
        &mut self,
        cd: &ControlData,
        body: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<KittyEvent, GraphicsError> {
        // Only direct transmission supported; file/temp/shared are ignored.
        if cd.transmission.is_some() && cd.transmission != Some(b'd') {
            return Ok(KittyEvent::Ignored);
        }
        let key = cd.image_id.or(cd.image_number).unwrap_or(0);
        if body.len() > MAX_APC_BYTES
            || (!self.pending.contains_key(&key) && self.pending.len() >= MAX_PENDING_TRANSMITS)
        {
            return Ok(KittyEvent::Ignored);
        }
        let decoded = Self::decode_b64(body)?;

        let too_large = {
            let buf = self.pending.entry(key).or_default();
            if buf.payload.len().saturating_add(decoded.len()) > MAX_APC_BYTES {
                true
            } else {
                // Later chunks may restate keys (e.g. f/s/v only on chunk 1): merge.
                buf.control.merge_from(cd);
                buf.payload.extend_from_slice(&decoded);
                false
            }
        };
        if too_large {
            self.pending.remove(&key);
            return Ok(KittyEvent::Ignored);
        }

        // m=1: more chunks coming — wait for the tail.
        if cd.more == Some(1) {
            return Ok(KittyEvent::Ignored);
        }
        let ChunkBuf {
            control: c,
            payload,
        } = self.pending.remove(&key).unwrap();
        let (w, h, rgba) = decode_pixels(&c, &payload)?;
        let id = c.image_id.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            self.next_id += 1;
            self.next_id
        });
        let replacing_bytes = self.images.get(&id).map_or(0, |im| im.rgba.len());
        let replacing_count = if replacing_bytes > 0 { 1 } else { 0 };
        let retained_count = self.images.len().saturating_sub(replacing_count);
        let retained_bytes = self
            .images
            .values()
            .map(|im| im.rgba.len())
            .sum::<usize>()
            .saturating_sub(replacing_bytes);
        if retained_count >= MAX_STORED_IMAGES
            || retained_bytes.saturating_add(rgba.len()) > MAX_STORED_RGBA_BYTES
        {
            return Ok(KittyEvent::Ignored);
        }
        self.next_id = self.next_id.max(id);
        self.images.insert(
            id,
            Image {
                id,
                number: c.image_number,
                w,
                h,
                rgba,
            },
        );
        Ok(KittyEvent::ImageStored { image_id: id, w, h })
    }

    fn handle_place(&mut self, cd: &ControlData) -> KittyEvent {
        let image_id = match (cd.image_id, cd.image_number) {
            (Some(i), _) => i,
            (None, Some(n)) => match self.images.values().find(|im| im.number == Some(n)) {
                Some(im) => im.id,
                None => return KittyEvent::Ignored,
            },
            (None, None) => self.images.keys().copied().max().unwrap_or(0),
        };
        if !self.images.contains_key(&image_id) {
            return KittyEvent::Ignored;
        }
        KittyEvent::Placed {
            image_id,
            placement: RawPlacement {
                x_cells: cd.x,
                y_cells: cd.y,
                columns_cells: cd.columns,
                rows_cells: cd.rows,
            },
        }
    }

    fn handle_delete(&mut self, cd: &ControlData) -> KittyEvent {
        let Some(d) = cd.delete else {
            return KittyEvent::Ignored;
        };
        let scope = match d {
            1 => match cd.image_id {
                Some(i) => DeleteScope::ByImageId(i),
                None => DeleteScope::AllPlacements,
            },
            2 => match cd.image_number {
                Some(n) => DeleteScope::ByImageNumber(n),
                None => return KittyEvent::Ignored,
            },
            3 | 7 => DeleteScope::AllImages,
            4 => DeleteScope::AllPlacements,
            5 => match cd.image_number {
                Some(n) => DeleteScope::ByNumberEverywhere(n),
                None => DeleteScope::AllPlacements,
            },
            6 => DeleteScope::AllPlacements,
            _ => return KittyEvent::Ignored,
        };
        match scope {
            DeleteScope::ByImageId(i) => {
                self.images.remove(&i);
            }
            DeleteScope::ByImageNumber(n) => {
                let ids: Vec<u32> = self
                    .images
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|(_, im)| im.number == Some(n))
                    .map(|(id, _)| *id)
                    .collect();
                for id in ids {
                    self.images.remove(&id);
                }
            }
            DeleteScope::AllImages => self.images.clear(),
            _ => {}
        }
        KittyEvent::Deleted(scope)
    }

    /// Cell footprint for a placement, honouring explicit C/R else pixel math.
    pub fn cells_for(&self, image_id: u32, rp: &RawPlacement) -> (u32, u32) {
        let (cw, ch) = self.cell_px;
        let dims = match self.images.get(&image_id) {
            Some(im) => (im.w, im.h),
            None => (0, 0),
        };
        let cols = rp
            .columns_cells
            .unwrap_or_else(|| (dims.0 + cw - 1) / cw.max(1));
        let rows = rp
            .rows_cells
            .unwrap_or_else(|| (dims.1 + ch - 1) / ch.max(1));
        (cols.max(1), rows.max(1))
    }
}

fn decode_pixels(cd: &ControlData, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(u32, u32, Vec<u8>), GraphicsError> {
    match cd.format.unwrap_or(0) {
        0 | 100 => {
            if data.len() > MAX_APC_BYTES
                || data.len() < 24
                || data.get(..8) != Some(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
            {
                return Err(GraphicsError::TooLarge);
            }
            let w = u32::from_be_bytes([data[16], data[17], data[18], data[19]]);
            let h = u32::from_be_bytes([data[20], data[21], data[22], data[23]]);
            check_dimensions(w, h)?;
            let img = image::load_from_memory(data)
                .map_err(|e| GraphicsError::Png(e.to_string()))?
                .to_rgba8();
            let (w, h) = (img.width(), img.height());
            Ok((w, h, img.into_raw()))
        }
        24 => {
            let (w, h) = (
                cd.width
                    .ok_or(GraphicsError::Truncated { need: 0, got: 0 })?,
                cd.height
                    .ok_or(GraphicsError::Truncated { need: 0, got: 0 })?,
            );
            check_dimensions(w, h)?;
            let need = (w as usize)
                .checked_mul(h as usize)
                .and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(3))
                .ok_or(GraphicsError::TooLarge)?;
            if data.len() < need {
                return Err(GraphicsError::Truncated {
                    need,
                    got: data.len(),
                });
            }
            let mut rgba = Vec::with_capacity(need * 4 / 3);
            for px in data[..need].chunks_exact(3) {
                rgba.extend_from_slice(&[px[0], px[1], px[2], 255]);
            }
            Ok((w, h, rgba))
        }
        32 => {
            let (w, h) = (
                cd.width
                    .ok_or(GraphicsError::Truncated { need: 0, got: 0 })?,
                cd.height
                    .ok_or(GraphicsError::Truncated { need: 0, got: 0 })?,
            );
            check_dimensions(w, h)?;
            let need = (w as usize)
                .checked_mul(h as usize)
                .and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(4))
                .ok_or(GraphicsError::TooLarge)?;
            if data.len() < need {
                return Err(GraphicsError::Truncated {
                    need,
                    got: data.len(),
                });
            }
            Ok((w, h, data[..need].to_vec()))
        }
        f => Err(GraphicsError::Png(format!(
            "unsupported pixel format f={f}"
        ))),
    }
}

fn check_dimensions(w: u32, h: u32) -> Result<(), GraphicsError> {
    if w == 0
        || h == 0
        || w > MAX_IMAGE_EDGE
        || h > MAX_IMAGE_EDGE
        || (w as u64) * (h as u64) > MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS
    {
        return Err(GraphicsError::TooLarge);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use base64::Engine as _;

    fn apc(control: &str, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        // feed() expects the payload AFTER the leading 'G'.
        let mut v = control.as_bytes().to_vec();
        if !payload.is_empty() {
            v.push(b';');
            v.extend_from_slice(payload);
        }
        v
    }

    fn b64(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
            .encode(data)
            .into_bytes()
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_oversized_raw_dimensions_before_allocation() {
        let control = ControlData {
            format: Some(32),
            width: Some(8192),
            height: Some(8192),
            ..ControlData::default()
        };
        assert!(matches!(
            decode_pixels(&control, &[]),
            Err(GraphicsError::TooLarge)
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn transmit_and_place_raw_rgba() {
        let mut s = GraphicsStore::new();
        // 2x1 red/green pixel, f=32 (payload must be base64).
        let ev = s
            .feed(&apc(
                "f=32,s=2,v=1,i=10",
                &b64(&[255, 0, 0, 255, 0, 255, 0, 255]),
            ))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            ev,
            KittyEvent::ImageStored {
                image_id: 10,
                w: 2,
                h: 1
            }
        );

        // Place at cursor with explicit C=2,R=1.
        let ev = s.feed(&apc("a=p,i=10,p=1,C=2,R=1", &[])).unwrap();
        match ev {
            KittyEvent::Placed {
                image_id,
                placement,
            } => {
                assert_eq!(image_id, 10);
                assert_eq!(placement.columns_cells, Some(2));
            }
            other => panic!("{other:?}"),
        }
        assert_eq!(
            s.cells_for(
                10,
                &RawPlacement {
                    x_cells: None,
                    y_cells: None,
                    columns_cells: None,
                    rows_cells: None
                }
            )
            .0,
            1
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn chunked_transmit() {
        let mut s = GraphicsStore::new();
        let data = vec![7u8; 4 * 4 * 4]; // 4x4 RGBA
        let b = b64(&data);
        let (a, rest) = b.split_at(b.len() / 2);
        let e1 = s.feed(&apc("f=32,s=4,v=4,i=5,m=1", a)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e1, KittyEvent::Ignored);
        let e2 = s.feed(&apc("m=0,i=5", rest)).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            e2,
            KittyEvent::ImageStored {
                image_id: 5,
                w: 4,
                h: 4
            }
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn png_transmit_and_delete() {
        let mut s = GraphicsStore::new();
        let png = image::DynamicImage::new_rgb8(3, 2);
        let mut buf = std::io::Cursor::new(Vec::new());
        png.write_to(&mut buf, image::ImageFormat::Png).unwrap();
        let b = b64(buf.get_ref());
        let ev = s.feed(&apc("i=3,q=1", &b)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            ev,
            KittyEvent::ImageStored {
                image_id: 3,
                w: 3,
                h: 2
            }
        );

        let ev = s.feed(&apc("a=d,d=1,i=3", &[])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ev, KittyEvent::Deleted(DeleteScope::ByImageId(3)));
        assert!(s.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn place_by_number() {
        let mut s = GraphicsStore::new();
        s.feed(&apc("f=32,s=1,v=1,I=42", &b64(&[1, 2, 3, 4])))
            .unwrap();
        let ev = s.feed(&apc("a=p,I=42", &[])).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(ev, KittyEvent::Placed { image_id: 1, .. }));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Minimal RPC client over the daemon socket (shared by CLI + runbooks).
//!
//! Transport: Unix domain socket on Unix, TCP loopback on Windows — the
//! framing (length-prefixed postcard) is identical on both.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::framing::{encode_frame, try_decode_frame};
use crate::{Request, Response};

/// Abstracted IPC stream: UDS on Unix, TCP loopback on Windows.
pub trait IpcStream: Read + Write + Send {
    fn try_dup(&self) -> std::io::Result<Box<dyn IpcStream>>;
    fn set_long_read_timeout(&self) -> std::io::Result<()>;
    /// Set the read timeout back to a finite value (per-RPC deadline).
    fn set_read_timeout(&self, d: Duration) -> std::io::Result<()>;
}

#[cfg(unix)]
impl IpcStream for std::os::unix::net::UnixStream {
    fn try_dup(&self) -> std::io::Result<Box<dyn IpcStream>> {
        let s = self.try_clone()?;
        Ok(Box::new(s))
    }
    fn set_long_read_timeout(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(86400)))
    }
    fn set_read_timeout(&self, d: Duration) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.set_read_timeout(Some(d))
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
impl IpcStream for std::net::TcpStream {
    fn try_dup(&self) -> std::io::Result<Box<dyn IpcStream>> {
        let s = self.try_clone()?;
        Ok(Box::new(s))
    }
    fn set_long_read_timeout(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(86400)))
    }
    fn set_read_timeout(&self, d: Duration) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.set_read_timeout(Some(d))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ClientError {
    #[error("daemon unreachable: {0}")]
    Unreachable(String),
    #[error("io: {0}")]
    Io(String),
    #[error("wire: {0}")]
    Wire(#[from] crate::WireError),
    #[error("daemon error [{code}]: {message}")]
    Daemon { code: i32, message: String },
    /// Per-RPC deadline elapsed. The request may still be running on the
    /// daemon — this is a client-side abort, not a daemon-side cancel.
    #[error("rpc timeout after {0:?}")]
    Timeout(Duration),
}

/// Default per-RPC deadline. Generous enough for the slowest daemon op
/// (journal export of a multi-MB chain) but bounded so a wedged daemon
/// can never hang the CLI forever. Long-running RPCs (Run, Wait, Stream*)
/// override this with their own `timeout_ms`.
pub const DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);

/// Pick a client-side RPC deadline that always exceeds the daemon-side one.
/// The daemon enforces its own timeout (e.g. `WaitSpec.timeout_ms`,
/// `RunSpec.timeout_ms`) and returns a typed reply; the client deadline just
/// guards against a wedged daemon. We add 5s of slack so the daemon's typed
/// timeout reply arrives before the client gives up.
///
/// Shared between the `roxterm` CLI and the runbook executor so both paths
/// get the same per-RPC deadline without duplicating the match.
pub fn rpc_timeout_for(req: &crate::Request) -> Duration {
    use crate::Request::*;
    let slack = |ms: u64| Duration::from_millis(ms.saturating_add(5_000));
    match req {
        Run { spec, .. } => slack(spec.timeout_ms.unwrap_or(120_000)),
        Wait { spec, .. } => slack(spec.timeout_ms),
        CaptureWait { timeout_ms, .. } => slack(*timeout_ms),
        WsRecv { timeout_ms, .. } => slack(*timeout_ms),
        WsRun { spec } => slack(spec.timeout_ms),
        WsOpen { spec } => slack(spec.timeout_ms),
        _ => DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT,
    }
}

pub struct Connection {
    stream: Box<dyn IpcStream>,
}

impl Connection {
    pub fn connect(endpoint: &crate::Endpoint) -> Result<Self, ClientError> {
        let stream: Box<dyn IpcStream> = match endpoint {
            #[cfg(unix)]
            crate::Endpoint::Uds(path) => {
                let s = std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::connect(path)
                    .map_err(|e| ClientError::Unreachable(format!("{}: {e}", path.display())))?;
                Box::new(s)
            }
            #[cfg(windows)]
            crate::Endpoint::Tcp(addr) => {
                let s = std::net::TcpStream::connect(addr.as_str())
                    .map_err(|e| ClientError::Unreachable(format!("{addr}: {e}")))?;
                Box::new(s)
            }
            #[cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))]
            _ => return Err(ClientError::Unreachable("unsupported platform".into())),
        };
        // Default deadline for non-streaming RPCs. Streaming RPCs
        // (Stream/StreamFrames) call open_push_channel which is one-way; the
        // subsequent read_push calls don't need a deadline (they block by
        // design), so the long timeout is re-applied in read_push.
        stream
            .set_read_timeout(DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT)
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(Connection { stream })
    }

    /// Call the daemon with the default 60s RPC deadline.
    pub fn call(&mut self, req: Request) -> Result<Response, ClientError> {
        self.call_with_timeout(req, DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT)
    }

    /// Call the daemon with an explicit deadline. Use this for `Run`/`Wait`
    /// (which can legitimately run for minutes) and for `Stream`/
    /// `StreamFrames` registration (the registration itself is fast). The
    /// deadline applies to the reply only — push channels switch to
    /// blocking reads via [`Connection::read_push`].
    pub fn call_with_timeout(
        &mut self,
        req: Request,
        timeout: Duration,
    ) -> Result<Response, ClientError> {
        // Apply the deadline to the read side; write side stays untimed
        // (writes on UDS/TCP loopback are effectively instantaneous, but a
        // wedged daemon could stall the write — bound it to the same value).
        self.stream
            .set_read_timeout(timeout)
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        let frame = encode_frame(&req)?;
        self.stream
            .write_all(&frame)
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        self.stream
            .flush()
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
        let mut chunk = [0u8; 16384];
        loop {
            if let Some((resp, n)) = try_decode_frame::<Response>(&buf)? {
                buf.drain(..n);
                // Restore the default deadline for the next call.
                let _ = self.stream.set_read_timeout(DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT);
                return match resp {
                    Response::Error(e) => Err(ClientError::Daemon {
                        code: e.code,
                        message: e.message,
                    }),
                    r => Ok(r),
                };
            }
            let n = match self.stream.read(&mut chunk) {
                Ok(n) => n,
                Err(e)
                    if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut
                        || e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock =>
                {
                    let _ = self.stream.set_read_timeout(DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT);
                    return Err(ClientError::Timeout(timeout));
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    let _ = self.stream.set_read_timeout(DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT);
                    return Err(ClientError::Io(e.to_string()));
                }
            };
            if n == 0 {
                let _ = self.stream.set_read_timeout(DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT);
                return Err(ClientError::Io("daemon closed connection".into()));
            }
            buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
        }
    }

    /// 1.0.0: open a one-way push feed. Sends `req` (Stream / StreamFrames)
    /// WITHOUT waiting for a reply — after registering, the daemon stops
    /// dispatching on this connection and pushes [`Response`] frames instead.
    /// An unknown target yields a normal in-band `Response::Error` as the
    /// first frame read by [`Connection::read_push`].
    pub fn open_push_channel(&mut self, req: Request) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
        // Push channels are read with no deadline (they block by design).
        self.stream
            .set_long_read_timeout()
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        let frame = encode_frame(&req)?;
        self.stream
            .write_all(&frame)
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        self.stream
            .flush()
            .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))
    }

    /// Read one pushed frame (blocks until it arrives). `Ok(None)` on clean
    /// daemon disconnect. Unlike [`Connection::call`] this does NOT convert
    /// `Response::Error` into `Err` — on a feed, the error reply IS the
    /// first frame (e.g. unknown connection name).
    pub fn read_push(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Response>, ClientError> {
        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
        let mut chunk = [0u8; 16384];
        loop {
            if let Some((resp, n)) = try_decode_frame::<Response>(&buf)? {
                buf.drain(..n);
                return Ok(Some(resp));
            }
            let n = self
                .stream
                .read(&mut chunk)
                .map_err(|e| ClientError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
            if n == 0 {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn client_error_display() {
        let e = ClientError::Daemon {
            code: 3,
            message: "assert failed".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(e.to_string(), "daemon error [3]: assert failed");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! roxterm wire protocol.
//!
//! Everything a client (agent or human) and the daemon exchange is a
//! [`Request`] answered by a [`Response`], framed with
//! [`framing::encode_frame`] / [`framing::try_decode_frame`] (length-prefixed
//! postcard). The same types are shared by the native viewer and the
//! runbook executor, so the daemon speaks exactly one protocol.

pub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: u32 = 5;

/// Where the daemon listens: UDS path on Unix, TCP loopback addr on Windows.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    Uds(std::path::PathBuf),
    #[cfg(windows)]
    Tcp(String),
}

pub const WINDOWS_DEFAULT_PORT: u16 = 47761;

pub mod client;

/// Process exit codes used by the `roxterm` CLI. Agents branch on these.
pub mod exit {
    pub const OK: i32 = 0;
    pub const FAILED: i32 = 1;
    pub const TIMEOUT: i32 = 2;
    pub const ASSERT_FAILED: i32 = 3;
    pub const USAGE: i32 = 4;
    pub const DAEMON_UNREACHABLE: i32 = 5;
}

/// Cell rendering attributes carried through the grid model.
pub mod flags {
    pub const BOLD: u8 = 1 << 0;
    pub const ITALIC: u8 = 1 << 1;
    pub const UNDERLINE: u8 = 1 << 2;
    pub const REVERSE: u8 = 1 << 3;
    pub const STRIKEOUT: u8 = 1 << 4;
    pub const DIM: u8 = 1 << 5;
    pub const HIDDEN: u8 = 1 << 6;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum WaitKind {
    /// A line containing `needle` appears on screen or in new scrollback.
    Text,
    /// A TCP port accepts connections (probe loop).
    Port,
    /// OSC 133 shell prompt appeared (shell is idle, ready for input).
    Prompt,
    /// No output for the given duration.
    Idle,
    /// The current OSC 133 command produced an exit code.
    Exit,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WaitSpec {
    pub kind: WaitKind,
    pub needle: Option<String>,
    pub timeout_ms: u64,
    /// Exit code to match when kind == Exit.
    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
    /// 0.8.0: sentinel tag for content-addressed exit waits. The `run`
    /// handler tags its sentinel D (`OSC 133;D;<exit>;<tag>`) and waits for
    /// THAT mark specifically, immune to stale prompt-time Ds from shell
    /// startup still in flight when the run started.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tag: Option<String>,
    /// Scan the last N lines only (Text waits).
    pub tail: Option<u32>,
    /// Also scan scrollback, not just the live grid (Text waits).
    pub scan_scrollback: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RunSpec {

}

}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ viewer wire

/// Color encoding for viewer wire: 0 = default, 0x4000_0000|n = 256-index,
/// 0x8000_0000|0xRRGGBB = truecolor.
#[inline]
pub fn encode_color(kind: u8, r: u8, g: u8, b: u8) -> u32 {
    match kind {
        1 => 0x4000_0000 | r as u32,
        2 => 0x8000_0000 | ((r as u32) << 16) | ((g as u32) << 8) | b as u32,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------- http capture wire
//
// The capture proxy is the "login-once" gateway: agents point every HTTP
// call at a local port, the daemon forwards to the upstream (often through
// a tunnel) and records request + response pairs as receipts.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct CaptureStartSpec {
    /// Bind address for the proxy, e.g. 127.0.0.1:18080.
    pub listen: String,
    /// Upstream origin, e.g. http://10.0.0.5:8080 (https not proxied).
    pub upstream: String,
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub record_bodies: bool,
    /// Max bytes of each body kept in a receipt (rest is counted, not stored).
    pub max_body: u32,
    /// 0.7.0 pinned-CA mode: path or PEM body of a CA the upstream origin
    /// cert must chain to. When set, the proxy VERIFIES the upstream
    /// (standard webpki) instead of accepting any certificate.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pinned_ca: Option<String>,
}

fn default_true() -> bool {
    true
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct CaptureInfo {
    pub capture_id: String,
    pub listen: String,
    pub upstream: String,
    pub entries: u64,
    pub bytes_req: u64,
    pub bytes_resp: u64,
    pub record_bodies: bool,
    pub alive: bool,
    /// Upstream dialed over TLS (https:// origin); CONNECT MITM receipts
    /// additionally carry per-entry `tls` flags.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tls: bool,
    /// 0.7.0: upstream TLS is verified against a pinned CA (path given at
    /// `capture start --ca`) instead of the accept-any capture stance.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pinned_ca: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]

    pub id: u64,

    pub method: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub status: u16,
    pub req_headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub resp_headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub req_body_b64: String,
    pub resp_body_b64: String,
    pub duration_ms: u64,
    /// True when this call was seen through TLS termination (CONNECT MITM or
    /// an https upstream), i.e. the receipt holds the decrypted payload.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tls: bool,
}

    WsRun {
        spec: WsRunSpec,

    // ---- 0.7.0 long-lived ws connections / pinned CA / stream backfill ----
    /// Open a NAMED, daemon-owned WebSocket that stays connected across RPC
    /// calls and runbook steps. Frames stream into the capture log and a
    /// per-connection receipt buffer that `WsRecv` drains in order.
    WsOpen {
        spec: WsOpenSpec,
    },
    /// Send text frames on a named connection.
    WsSend {
        name: String,
        frames: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// Wait for / drain received frames on a named connection.
    WsRecv {
        name: String,
        expect: Option<String>,
        max_frames: u32,
        timeout_ms: u64,
        from: u32,
    },
    /// Close a named connection politely (close frame + status flip).
    WsClose {
        name: String,
    },
    /// List every daemon-owned WebSocket connection.
    WsConns,

    // ---- 0.8.0 agent-driven subs / bracketed paste / OSC 52 clipboard ----
    /// Write to the PTY as a CLIPBOARD PASTE: when the running app enabled
    /// bracketed-paste mode (DECSET 2004) the daemon wraps the bytes in
    /// `ESC[200~ … ESC[201~` so multiline pastes arrive as one input event
    /// instead of N enter-pressed lines. Without the mode the bytes go
    /// through unchanged.
    Paste {
        session: String,
        bytes: Vec<u8>,
        press_enter: bool,
    },
    /// Read the last OSC 52 clipboard payload the app published into the
    /// grid (`ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64> ST`). The clipboard is a queryable
    /// cell of the grid database, like the command timeline.
    Clipboard {
        session: String,
    },

    // ---- 1.0.0 offline audit / live subscriptions / provenance ----
    /// Export a journal (session, or the workspace-layout journal with
    /// `workspaces: true`) for OFFLINE AUDIT: the full hash-chained record
    /// list plus the chain verdict in one reply. The export outlives the
    /// daemon — agents archive it, diff it, re-verify it elsewhere.
    JournalExport {
        session: String,
        workspaces: bool,
    },
    /// Turn THIS connection into a one-way push feed for a named ws
    /// connection: every frame the ORIGIN sends lands here as it arrives
    /// (live subscription, no polling). Unknown conn → normal error reply;
    /// after registration the daemon never replies in-band again — every
    /// frame read is a pushed [`Response::WsFrame`], terminated by
    /// [`Response::WsConnClosed`].
    StreamFrames {
        conn: String,
    },
    /// The command-provenance query: the OSC 133 timeline (prompt →
    /// command → exit marks), newest LAST, capped to `last` entries. The
    /// grid database answers "what ran here, what did it cost".
    Timeline {
        session: String,
        last: Option<u32>,
    },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ErrorBody {
    pub code: i32,
    pub message: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum Response {
    Pong {
        version: u32,
        sessions: u32,
    },
    SessionOpened(SessionInfo),
    Sessions(Vec<SessionInfo>),
    Closed {
        session: String,
    },
    Ok,
    ExitCode {
        session: String,
        code: i32,
    },
    Read(ReadReport),
    Snapshot(SnapshotSvg),
    RenderState(RenderStateWire),
    Image(ImageWire),
    SignalSent,
    TunnelOpened {
        tunnel_id: String,
        bind: String,
    },
    Tunnels(Vec<TunnelInfo>),
    TunnelClosed {
        tunnel_id: String,
    },
    JournalOk {
        session: String,
        records: u64,
        chain_ok: bool,
    },
    /// Stream channel: PTY output chunks with seq numbers.
    Output {
        session: String,
        seq: u64,
        bytes: Vec<u8>,
    },
    /// Stream channel: session resumed after daemon restart + journal replay.
    Resumed {
        session: String,
        generation: u32,
    },
    Error(ErrorBody),

    // ---- 0.4.0 capture / db / frames (appended: stable variant order) ----
    CaptureStarted(CaptureInfo),
    CaptureStopped {
        capture_id: String,
    },
    Captures(Vec<CaptureInfo>),
    CaptureEntries {
        entries: Vec<CaptureEntry>,
        truncated: bool,
    },
    CaptureMatched(CaptureEntry),
    HttpReply(HttpReply),
    DbDone(DbResult),
    Frames(Vec<FrameInfo>),
    FrameClosed {
        frame_id: String,
    },
    FrameData(FrameRenderData),

    // ---- 0.5.0 https interception / workspaces / capture CA ----
    CaptureCaInfo {
        path: String,
        pem: String,
        sha256: String,
    },
    Workspaces(Vec<WorkspaceInfo>),
    WorkspaceClosed {
        name: String,
    },

    // ---- 0.6.0 websocket frame receipting ----
    WsReport(WsRunReport),

    // ---- 0.7.0 long-lived ws connections ----
    WsOpened {
        name: String,
        url: String,
        adopted: bool,
    },
    WsSent {
        name: String,
        frames_sent: u32,
    },
    WsRecvDone(WsRecvReport),
    WsConnClosed {
        name: String,
        frames_received: u32,
    },
    WsConns(Vec<WsConnView>),

    // ---- 0.8.0 bracketed paste / OSC 52 clipboard ----
    /// The last OSC 52 payload decoded (None = nothing published yet).
    ClipboardText {
        session: String,
        text: Option<String>,
        seq: u64,
    },

    // ---- 1.0.0 offline audit / live subscriptions / provenance ----
    /// Journal export: the full hash-chained record list + chain verdict.
    /// `records` is ordered oldest → newest; the last record's hash is the
    /// chain tip an offline verifier checks against.
    JournalData {
        name: String,
        chain_ok: bool,
        records: Vec<JournalRecordWire>,
    },
    /// Push feed ([`Request::StreamFrames`]): one frame the ORIGIN sent on
    /// the followed connection, as it arrived. `index` is the connection's
    /// buffer position — the same index `ws_recv --from` addresses, so a
    /// feed consumer and a poller agree on ordering.
    WsFrame {
        conn: String,
        index: u64,
        dir: String,
        opcode: u16,
        text: String,
        bytes: u32,
    },
    /// Push feed terminal event: the followed connection closed (or errored).
    /// No further frames arrive on the feed after this.
    WsFeedClosed {
        conn: String,
        reason: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Command-provenance query result: the OSC 133 timeline, oldest →
    /// newest, capped to the requested `last` entries.
    Timeline {
        session: String,
        marks: Vec<TimelineMark>,
    },
}

/// One journal record on the wire (1.0.0 offline audit). The payload is
/// pre-serialized JSON: the payload enums live in rox-journal and the wire
/// keeps this crate independent of it; the hashes are hex so an export is
/// greppable by any auditor.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct JournalRecordWire {
    pub seq: u64,
    pub prev_hash: String,
    pub payload_json: String,
    pub hash: String,
}

/// One completed OSC 133 command on the wire (1.0.0 provenance query).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TimelineMark {
    pub seq_prompt: u64,
    pub seq_end: u64,
    pub command: Option<String>,
    pub exit: Option<i32>,
    pub started_unix_ms: u64,
    pub ended_unix_ms: u64,
    pub row_start: u32,
    /// Run-sentinel tag (0.8.0) — `run-N` for daemon `run` commands.
    pub tag: Option<String>,
}

// ------------------------------------------------- websocket receipting (0.6.0)

/// One scripted WebSocket exchange. The daemon connects to `url`, sends
/// every `send` frame, then receipts incoming frames until `expect` matches,
/// `max_frames` arrive or `timeout_ms` elapses. Frames land in the capture
/// log (`capture show`) exactly like HTTP calls.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WsRunSpec {
    /// ws://host:port/path or wss://host:port/path.
    pub url: String,
    /// Extra handshake headers (Authorization, Origin, ...).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Text frames to send after the handshake, in order.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub send: Vec<String>,
    /// Succeed as soon as a received text frame contains this substring.
    pub expect: Option<String>,
    /// Cap on received frames receipted per run (default 8).
    pub max_frames: u32,
    /// Overall deadline for the whole exchange.
    pub timeout_ms: u64,
    /// wss:// only: accept any origin certificate (the daemon is the trust
    /// boundary for captured traffic; matches the capture proxy stance).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub insecure: bool,
    /// Capture log to record frames into; None = the sole live capture.
    pub capture: Option<String>,
    /// Path or PEM body of a CA the origin cert must chain to (0.7.0
    /// pinned-CA mode). When set, standard webpki verification applies
    /// instead of the accept-any capture-CA config.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pinned_ca: Option<String>,
}

/// Open a persistent, daemon-owned WebSocket connection (0.7.0). Unlike
/// [`WsRunSpec`] (one scripted exchange per call), the connection survives
/// across RPC calls and runbook steps: `ws_open` → `ws_send` → `ws_recv`…
/// → `ws_close`. Every frame — both directions — is receipted into the
/// capture log while the connection lives.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WsOpenSpec {
    /// Unique connection name (agents address it from later steps).
    pub name: String,
    /// ws://host:port/path or wss://host:port/path.
    pub url: String,
    /// Extra handshake headers (Authorization, Origin, ...).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Connect + handshake deadline.
    pub timeout_ms: u64,
    /// wss:// only: accept any origin certificate (daemon trust boundary).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub insecure: bool,
    /// Path or PEM body of a CA the origin cert must chain to. When set,
    /// standard webpki verification replaces the accept-any stance — this
    /// is the pinned-CA mode: no trust in arbitrary self-signed origins.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pinned_ca: Option<String>,
    /// Capture log to receipt frames into; None = the sole live capture.
    pub capture: Option<String>,
    /// 0.8.0 agent-driven subscriptions: when a daemon-held connection with
    /// this name already exists and is open, ADOPT it instead of dialing —
    /// the buffer, capture receipts and stream continuity all carry over, so
    /// a runbook can reattach mid-run to a subscription the CLI (or another
    /// runbook) opened earlier. Missing → dial fresh; open but dead → dial
    /// fresh and replace. `false` keeps the 0.7.0 duplicate-name error.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub adopt: bool,
}

/// Result of draining a named connection's received frames (0.7.0).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WsRecvReport {
    /// The frames returned by THIS call (subset of the connection buffer).
    pub frames: Vec<WsFrameView>,
    /// Index (0-based, recv order on the connection) of the frame that
    /// satisfied `expect`, if one was given.
    pub matched: Option<u32>,
    /// Total frames received on the connection so far.
    pub received_total: u32,
    /// Index the next `ws_recv` should start from (`from` + frames.len()).
    pub next_index: u32,
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

/// One named WebSocket connection as listed by `WsConns` (0.7.0).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WsConnView {
    pub name: String,
    pub url: String,
    /// open | closed | error.
    pub status: String,
    pub frames_in: u32,
    pub frames_out: u32,
    pub opened_unix_ms: u64,
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

/// One receipted frame as reported back to the client.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WsFrameView {
    /// "send" (client→origin) or "recv" (origin→client).
    pub dir: String,
    /// RFC 6455 opcode: 1 text, 2 binary, 8 close, 9 pong.
    pub opcode: u16,
    /// Payload as text (lossy for binary frames).
    pub text: String,
    pub bytes: u32,
    /// Milliseconds since the socket connected.
    pub offset_ms: u64,
}

/// Result of one `WsRun`: every frame + where the receipts landed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WsRunReport {
    /// Capture that holds the frame receipts (None = nothing was recording).
    pub capture_id: Option<String>,
    /// Id of the first recorded frame receipt (sequential ids follow).
    pub entry_from: Option<u64>,
    pub frames_sent: u32,
    pub frames_received: u32,
    /// Index (0-based, recv order) of the frame that satisfied `expect`.
    pub matched: Option<u32>,
    pub frames: Vec<WsFrameView>,
    pub duration_ms: u64,
    /// Transport/handshake error, if any.
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

/// One named workspace (tab): a guillotine pane tree over term/http/db
/// sources. Workspaces are independent; the viewer shows them as tabs.
/// Layouts are journaled (0.6.0) so a daemon restart restores every tab.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct WorkspaceInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub frames: u32,
    pub active: bool,
    pub created_unix_ms: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RenderStateWire {
    pub session: String,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub cursor: (u32, u32),
    pub mode_bits: u32,
    pub cols: u32,
    pub rows: u32,
    pub scrollback_len: u32,
    /// Rows with touch seq > requested `since` (viewer merges by index).
    pub rows_changed: Vec<RowWire>,
    /// All live kitty images (RGB pixels). Bounded by 8 MiB per response.
    pub images: Vec<ImageWire>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TunnelInfo {
    pub id: String,
    pub role: TunnelRole,
    pub bind: String,
    pub target: String,
    pub via_ssh: Option<String>,
    pub session: Option<String>,
    pub bytes_up: u64,
    pub bytes_down: u64,
    pub established_ms: u64,
    pub alive: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum WireError {
    #[error("postcard encode/decode failed: {0}")]
    Postcard(#[from] postcard::Error),
    #[error("frame length prefix invalid")]
    BadFrame,
    #[error("frame exceeds {0} bytes")]
    TooLarge(u32),
}

/// Length-prefixed postcard framing over byte streams (UDS, TCP).
pub mod framing {
    use super::WireError;

    pub const MAX_FRAME: u32 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

    /// `u32 LE length || postcard payload`
    pub fn encode_frame<T: serde::Serialize>(value: &T) -> Result<Vec<u8>, WireError> {
        let payload = postcard::to_allocvec(value)?;
        let len = payload.len() as u32;
        if len > MAX_FRAME {
            return Err(WireError::TooLarge(MAX_FRAME));
        }
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + payload.len());
        out.extend_from_slice(&len.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&payload);
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// Try to decode one frame from `buf`; returns frame size consumed.
    pub fn try_decode_frame<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
        buf: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<Option<(T, usize)>, WireError> {
        if buf.len() < 4 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let len = u32::from_le_bytes([buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]]) as usize;
        if len > MAX_FRAME as usize {
            return Err(WireError::BadFrame);
        }
        if buf.len() < 4 + len {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let value: T = postcard::from_bytes(&buf[4..4 + len])?;
        Ok(Some((value, 4 + len)))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn roundtrip_all_requests() {
        let reqs = vec![
            Request::Hello,
            Request::Open {
                shell: "bash".into(),
                tag: Some("dev".into()),
                cwd: None,
                env: vec![("FOO".into(), "bar".into())],
                cols: 80,
                rows: 24,
                keep: true,
                detached: true,
            },
            Request::Wait {
                session: "s1".into(),
                spec: WaitSpec {
                    kind: WaitKind::Text,
                    needle: Some("ready".into()),
                    timeout_ms: 3000,
                    exit_code: None,
                    tail: Some(20),
                    scan_scrollback: true,
                    tag: Some("run-1".into()),
                },
            },
            Request::TunnelOpen {
                session: None,
                spec: TunnelSpec {
                    role: TunnelRole::Relay,
                    bind: "127.0.0.1:0".into(),
                    target: "127.0.0.1:9".into(),
                    via_ssh: None,
                    ssh_args: vec![],
                },
            },
            Request::CaptureStart {
                spec: CaptureStartSpec {
                    listen: "127.0.0.1:18080".into(),
                    upstream: "http://10.0.0.5:8080".into(),
                    record_bodies: true,
                    max_body: 65536,
                    pinned_ca: None,
                },
            },
            Request::CaptureWait {
                capture_id: None,
                path_contains: Some("/login".into()),
                status: Some(200),
                since_entry: 0,
                timeout_ms: 5000,
            },
            Request::HttpRequest {
                spec: HttpRequestSpec {
                    capture: None,
                    method: "POST".into(),
                    path: "/login".into(),
                    headers: vec![("Content-Type".into(), "application/json".into())],
                    body: Some("{\"user\":\"agent\"}".into()),
                },
            },
            Request::DbExec {
                spec: DbExecSpec {
                    dsn: "postgres://app@127.0.0.1:5432/app".into(),
                    sql: "select 1".into(),
                    driver: DbDriver::Auto,
                    timeout_ms: 10_000,
                    max_rows: 100,
                },
            },
            Request::FrameSplit {
                workspace: None,
                spec: FrameSpec {
                    dir: FrameDir::Right,
                    source: FrameSource::Db {
                        dsn: "sqlite:app.db".into(),
                        table: "users".into(),
                        sql: None,
                        limit: 20,
                    },
                    weight: 1.0,
                    title: Some("db view".into()),
                },
            },
            // 0.5.0 variants.
            Request::CaptureCa,
            Request::WorkspaceNew {
                name: "db-review".into(),
            },
            Request::WorkspaceList,
            Request::WorkspaceUse {
                name: "db-review".into(),
            },
            Request::WorkspaceClose { name: "old".into() },
            // 0.7.0 variants.
            Request::WsOpen {
                spec: WsOpenSpec {
                    name: "events".into(),
                    url: "wss://origin.example/events".into(),
                    headers: vec![("Authorization".into(), "Bearer t".into())],
                    timeout_ms: 5000,
                    insecure: false,
                    pinned_ca: Some("/tmp/origin-ca.pem".into()),
                    capture: Some("c1".into()),
                    adopt: true,
                },
            },
            Request::WsSend {
                name: "events".into(),
                frames: vec!["hi".into(), "there".into()],
            },
            Request::WsRecv {
                name: "events".into(),
                expect: Some("build-ok".into()),
                max_frames: 4,
                timeout_ms: 8000,
                from: 2,
            },
            Request::WsClose {
                name: "events".into(),
            },
            Request::WsConns,
            // 0.8.0 variants.
            Request::Paste {
                session: "s1".into(),
                bytes: vec![1, 2, 3],
                press_enter: false,
            },
            Request::Clipboard {
                session: "s1".into(),
            },
            // 1.0.0 variants.
            Request::JournalExport {
                session: "s1".into(),
                workspaces: true,
            },
            Request::StreamFrames {
                conn: "events".into(),
            },
            Request::Timeline {
                session: "s1".into(),
                last: Some(20),
            },
        ];
        for req in reqs {
            let frame = framing::encode_frame(&req).unwrap();
            let (back, n) = framing::try_decode_frame::<Request>(&frame)
                .unwrap()
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(n, frame.len());
            // Re-encode both and compare — postcard output is deterministic here.
            let re = framing::encode_frame(&back).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(re, frame);
        }

        let resp = Response::Read(ReadReport {
            session: "s".into(),
            seq: 7,
            cursor: (0, 0),
            mode_bits: 0,
            lines: vec![GridLine {
                seq: 7,
                index: 0,
                text: "hello".into(),
                colored: false,
                attrs: vec![flags::BOLD; 5],
                image: None,
            }],
            dropped: 0,
            dropped_bytes: 0,
            truncated_head: false,
            images: vec![],
        });
        let frame = framing::encode_frame(&resp).unwrap();
        let (back, _) = framing::try_decode_frame::<Response>(&frame)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap();
        let re = framing::encode_frame(&back).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(re, frame);

        // New 0.4.0 responses roundtrip too.
        let resps = vec![
            Response::CaptureMatched(CaptureEntry {
                id: 1,
                capture_id: "c1".into(),
                ts_unix_ms: 0,
                method: "POST".into(),
                path: "/login".into(),
                status: 200,
                req_headers: vec![],
                resp_headers: vec![("Set-Cookie".into(), "sid=abc".into())],
                req_body_b64: String::new(),
                resp_body_b64: String::new(),
                duration_ms: 12,
                tls: true,
            }),
            Response::HttpReply(HttpReply {
                capture_id: "c1".into(),
                entry_id: 1,
                status: 200,
                headers: vec![],
                body: "{\"token\":\"t\"}".into(),
                duration_ms: 9,
            }),
            Response::DbDone(DbResult {
                driver: DbDriver::Sqlite3,
                columns: vec!["one".into()],
                rows: vec![vec!["1".into()]],
                rows_affected: 0,
                duration_ms: 3,
                truncated: false,
                error: None,
            }),
            Response::Frames(vec![FrameInfo {
                id: "f1".into(),
                workspace: "main".into(),
                kind: FrameKind::Term,
                source: "session s1".into(),
                session: Some("s1".into()),
                title: "agent".into(),
                rect: (0, 0, 120, 60),
                focused: true,
            }]),
            Response::FrameData(FrameRenderData {
                frame_id: "f2".into(),
                kind: FrameKind::Db,
                cols: 80,
                rows: 20,
                lines: vec!["id | name".into()],
                cursor: None,
            }),
            // 0.5.0 variants.
            Response::CaptureCaInfo {
                path: "/tmp/ca.pem".into(),
                pem: "-----BEGIN".into(),
                sha256: "deadbeef".into(),
            },
            Response::Workspaces(vec![
                WorkspaceInfo {
                    name: "main".into(),
                    frames: 3,
                    active: true,
                    created_unix_ms: 42,
                },
                WorkspaceInfo {
                    name: "db-review".into(),
                    frames: 1,
                    active: false,
                    created_unix_ms: 43,
                },
            ]),
            Response::WorkspaceClosed { name: "old".into() },
            // 0.7.0 variants.
            Response::WsOpened {
                name: "events".into(),
                url: "ws://h/e".into(),
                adopted: true,
            },
            Response::WsSent {
                name: "events".into(),
                frames_sent: 2,
            },
            Response::WsRecvDone(WsRecvReport {
                frames: vec![WsFrameView {
                    dir: "recv".into(),
                    opcode: 1,
                    text: "build-ok".into(),
                    bytes: 8,
                    offset_ms: 42,
                }],
                matched: Some(0),
                received_total: 1,
                next_index: 1,
                error: None,
            }),
            Response::WsConnClosed {
                name: "events".into(),
                frames_received: 7,
            },
            Response::WsConns(vec![WsConnView {
                name: "events".into(),
                url: "wss://origin.example/events".into(),
                status: "open".into(),
                frames_in: 3,
                frames_out: 2,
                opened_unix_ms: 42,
                error: None,
            }]),
            // 0.8.0 variants.
            Response::ClipboardText {
                session: "s1".into(),
                text: Some("copied".into()),
                seq: 9,
            },
            // 1.0.0 variants.
            Response::JournalData {
                name: "s1".into(),
                chain_ok: true,
                records: vec![JournalRecordWire {
                    seq: 1,
                    prev_hash: "aa".into(),
                    payload_json: "{\"kind\":\"header\"}".into(),
                    hash: "bb".into(),
                }],
            },
            Response::WsFrame {
                conn: "events".into(),
                index: 3,
                dir: "recv".into(),
                opcode: 1,
                text: "hello".into(),
                bytes: 5,
            },
            Response::WsFeedClosed {
                conn: "events".into(),
                reason: Some("origin closed (1000)".into()),
            },
            Response::Timeline {
                session: "s1".into(),
                marks: vec![TimelineMark {
                    seq_prompt: 1,
                    seq_end: 9,
                    command: Some("echo hi".into()),
                    exit: Some(0),
                    started_unix_ms: 1,
                    ended_unix_ms: 2,
                    row_start: 0,
                    tag: Some("run-1".into()),
                }],
            },
        ];
        for resp in resps {
            let frame = framing::encode_frame(&resp).unwrap();
            let (back, _) = framing::try_decode_frame::<Response>(&frame)
                .unwrap()
                .unwrap();
            let re = framing::encode_frame(&back).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(re, frame);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn partial_frames_wait() {
        let frame = framing::encode_frame(&Request::Hello).unwrap();
        // Byte-by-byte feeding must eventually produce the frame.
        let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![];
        let mut got = None;
        for b in &frame {
            buf.push(*b);
            if let Some((_, n)) = framing::try_decode_frame::<Request>(&buf).unwrap() {
                got = Some(n);
                break;
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(got, Some(frame.len()));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! rox-vt — the grid database.
//!
//! The screen is a grid, not text: every cell carries char + colors +
//! attribute flags, every row carries the `seq` of the output chunk that last
//! touched it, and the OSC 133 command timeline records prompt→command→exit
//! provenance for every command the shell ran. This is what makes the
//! terminal queryable (`read --diff`, `wait text`, `expect exit-code`).

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use rox_graphics::{DeleteScope, GraphicsStore, KittyEvent};
use rox_protocol::flags;
use rox_protocol::{GridLine, ImageMeta, ImagePlacement, SessionMode};
use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
use vte::{Params, Parser, Perform};

use base64::Engine as _;

/// Tap state for kitty APC detection (vte ignores SosPmApcString payloads,
/// so we capture them ourselves while the same bytes still flow to vte).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Tap {
    Ground,
    Esc,
    Csi,
    Osc,
    OscEsc,
    Dcs,
    DcsPassthrough,
    DcsEsc,
    String { apc: bool },
    StringEsc { apc: bool },
}

pub const DEFAULT_SCROLLBACK: usize = 5000;
/// Upper bound for a buffered Kitty APC image/control payload in the embedded
/// terminal; oversized strings are discarded until their terminator.
const MAX_APC_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
/// Bounded ring of OSC 52 clipboard payloads (1.0.0 fix: the previous
/// `Option<String>` last-write-wins model meant an agent had no way to know
/// what the app copied before the most recent copy — a real footgun when an
/// app publishes multiple selections during a session). The ring keeps the
/// last 16 payloads; `clipboard()` returns the back (most recent) so existing
/// callers behave exactly as before. History is queryable via
/// `clipboard_history()` for the timeline / audit paths.
const CLIPBOARD_RING_CAP: usize = 16;
/// Raised from 1000 (1.0.0 fix): the previous cap rotated oldest marks out
/// silently — an agent running a long dev session would lose provenance for
/// commands older than the last 1000. The journal keeps the full byte stream,
/// but the live `timeline` query used to have a hole. 10k still bounds
/// memory (~600 KB worst case at ~60 bytes per mark) and covers days of
/// continuous agent work.
const TIMELINE_CAP: usize = 10_000;

/// Internal cell flag: second half of a double-width char.
const WIDE_SPACER: u8 = 1 << 7;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Color {
    Default,
    Indexed(u8),
    Rgb(u8, u8, u8),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Cell {
    pub ch: char,
    pub fg: Color,
    pub bg: Color,
    pub flags: u8,
}

impl Default for Cell {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Cell {
            ch: ' ',
            fg: Color::Default,
            bg: Color::Default,
            flags: 0,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Row {
    pub cells: Vec<Cell>,
    /// seq of the output chunk that last touched this row.
    pub touch: u64,
    /// True when this row ended in a soft wrap (auto-wrap at the right
    /// margin): the next row continues the same logical line. Drives the
    /// 0.7.0 reflow on resize — hard breaks (\r\n) clear it.
    pub wrapped: bool,
}

/// One completed OSC 133 command (prompt A → command B → output C → exit D).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CommandMark {
    pub seq_prompt: u64,
    pub seq_end: u64,
    pub command: Option<String>,
    pub exit: Option<i32>,
    pub started_unix_ms: u64,
    pub ended_unix_ms: u64,
    pub row_start: u32,
    /// 0.8.0: optional sentinel tag (`OSC 133;D;<exit>;<tag>`). The daemon
    /// tags every `run` sentinel so exit waits are content-addressed instead
    /// of positional — a stale prompt-time D from shell startup in flight
    /// when the run began can no longer be mistaken for the run's exit.
    pub tag: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Mark {
    seq_prompt: u64,
    /// Absolute scrollback-space row where the command line starts.
    abs_row_b: i64,
    started_unix_ms: u64,
    command: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct LineOpts {
    /// Include scrollback rows before the live grid.
    pub include_scrollback: bool,
    /// Keep only the last N lines.
    pub tail: Option<u32>,
    /// Attach image placements to their lines.
    pub images: bool,
}

pub struct Screen {
    cols: usize,
    rows: usize,
    grid: Vec<Row>,
    alt_grid: Vec<Row>,
    in_alt: bool,
    scrollback: VecDeque<Row>,
    max_scrollback: usize,
    cursor: (usize, usize), // (col, row)
    saved: Option<((usize, usize), Color, Color, u8)>,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub title: String,
    pub cwd: String,
    pub last_exit: Option<i32>,
    pub last_prompt_seq: u64,
    pub last_output_unix_ms: u64,
    pub mode_bits: u32,
    cur_fg: Color,
    cur_bg: Color,
    cur_flags: u8,
    pending_wrap: bool,
    insert_mode: bool,
    auto_wrap: bool,
    origin_mode: bool,
    scroll_region: (usize, usize),
    tabs: Vec<bool>,
    parser: Parser,
    pub graphics: GraphicsStore,
    /// Kitty image placements, ABSOLUTE-row anchored (0.7.0): `row` is the
    /// scrollback-space line the placement starts on (scrollback row `i` is
    /// abs `i`, live row `y` is abs `scrollback_len + y`). Anchoring in this
    /// space means scrolling content into scrollback never moves or kills a
    /// placement — images survive in history exactly like text does. Only
    /// scrollback eviction (cap reached) renormalizes the coordinates.
    placements: Vec<ImagePlacement>,
    /// Alternate-screen placements share the same abs space but live in
    /// their own list so entering/leaving vim/less never wipes the primary
    /// screen's images (0.7.0 fix — exit_alt used to clear them all).
    alt_placements: Vec<ImagePlacement>,
    timeline: VecDeque<CommandMark>,
    mark: Option<Mark>,
    tap: Tap,
    apc_buf: Vec<u8>,
    /// 0.8.0: last OSC 52 clipboard payload the app published into the grid
    /// (`ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64> ST`), decoded to text. 1.0.0 fix: now a
    /// bounded ring of the last [`CLIPBOARD_RING_CAP`] payloads instead of
    /// last-write-only — `clipboard()` still returns the most recent (the
    /// previous API contract), `clipboard_history()` exposes the full ring
    /// oldest→newest for audit / agent introspection. A queryable cell of the
    /// grid database — agents read what the running app copied without owning
    /// a display server.
    pub clipboard: VecDeque<String>,
    pub cell_px: (u32, u32),
}

fn now_ms() -> u64 {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

impl Screen {
    pub fn new(cols: usize, rows: usize) -> Self {
        let mut s = Screen {
            cols,
            rows,
            grid: empty_grid(rows, cols, 0),
            alt_grid: Vec::new(),
            in_alt: false,
            scrollback: VecDeque::new(),
            max_scrollback: DEFAULT_SCROLLBACK,
            cursor: (0, 0),
            saved: None,
            seq: 0,
            title: String::new(),
            cwd: String::new(),
            last_exit: None,
            last_prompt_seq: 0,
            last_output_unix_ms: 0,
            mode_bits: 1, // cursor visible
            cur_fg: Color::Default,
            cur_bg: Color::Default,
            cur_flags: 0,
            pending_wrap: false,
            insert_mode: false,
            auto_wrap: true,
            origin_mode: false,
            scroll_region: (0, rows.saturating_sub(1)),
            tabs: (0..cols).map(|i| i % 8 == 0).collect(),
            parser: Parser::new(),
            graphics: GraphicsStore::new(),
            placements: Vec::new(),
            alt_placements: Vec::new(),
            timeline: VecDeque::new(),
            mark: None,
            tap: Tap::Ground,
            apc_buf: Vec::new(),
            clipboard: VecDeque::new(),
            cell_px: (8, 16),
        };
        s.graphics.cell_px = s.cell_px;
        s
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------- accessors

    pub fn cols(&self) -> usize {
        self.cols
    }
    pub fn rows(&self) -> usize {
        self.rows
    }
    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {
        self.seq
    }
    pub fn cursor(&self) -> (u32, u32) {
        (self.cursor.0 as u32, self.cursor.1 as u32)
    }
    pub fn scrollback_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.scrollback.len()
    }
    pub fn session_mode(&self) -> SessionMode {
        if self.in_alt {
            SessionMode::Alternate
        } else {
            SessionMode::Normal
        }
    }
    pub fn timeline(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &CommandMark> {
        self.timeline.iter()
    }
    pub fn placements(&self) -> &[ImagePlacement] {
        if self.in_alt {
            &self.alt_placements
        } else {
            &self.placements
        }
    }

    fn placements_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Vec<ImagePlacement> {
        if self.in_alt {
            &mut self.alt_placements
        } else {
            &mut self.placements
        }
    }
    pub fn bracketed_paste(&self) -> bool {
        self.mode_bits & 0b100 != 0
    }
    /// 0.8.0: the last OSC 52 clipboard text the app published (None until
    /// an app copies something through the grid). 1.0.0: returns the back
    /// of the ring (most recent payload) — preserves the previous API
    /// contract, so callers like the `Clipboard` RPC reply shape and the
    /// existing tests work unchanged.
    pub fn clipboard(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.clipboard.back().map(String::as_str)
    }
    /// 1.0.0: the full OSC 52 clipboard ring, oldest → newest. Use this for
    /// audit / introspection ("what did the app copy across the session?").
    /// The most recent payload is also reachable via [`clipboard`](Self::clipboard)
    /// for back-compat with 0.8.x callers.
    pub fn clipboard_history(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        self.clipboard.iter().map(String::as_str)
    }
    /// 1.0.0: number of OSC 52 payloads currently held in the ring.
    pub fn clipboard_history_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.clipboard.len()
    }
    pub fn images(&self) -> Vec<ImageMeta> {
        self.graphics
            .iter()
            .map(|im| ImageMeta {
                image_id: im.id,
                pixel_w: im.w,
                pixel_h: im.h,
                size_bytes: im.rgba.len() as u32,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    fn active_grid(&self) -> &Vec<Row> {
        if self.in_alt {
            &self.alt_grid
        } else {
            &self.grid
        }
    }
    fn active_grid_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Vec<Row> {
        if self.in_alt {
            &mut self.alt_grid
        } else {
            &mut self.grid
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ feed

    /// Feed raw PTY output. Every call bumps `seq`; all cells written by this
    /// chunk are tagged with that seq (this drives `read --diff`).
    ///
    /// The stream is tapped for kitty APC sequences (`ESC _ G ... ST`) — vte
    /// discards those payloads, we route them to the graphics store while the
    /// identical bytes still drive the vte state machine, so placement cursors
    /// stay exact.
    pub fn feed(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        if bytes.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        self.seq += 1;
        self.last_output_unix_ms = now_ms();
        let mut parser = std::mem::replace(&mut self.parser, Parser::new());
        for &b in bytes {
            if self.tap_byte(b) {
                let payload = std::mem::take(&mut self.apc_buf);
                self.handle_apc(&payload);
            }
            parser.advance(self, b);
        }
        self.parser = parser;
    }

    /// Advance the APC tap one byte; returns true when an APC payload closed.
    fn tap_byte(&mut self, b: u8) -> bool {
        match self.tap {
            Tap::Ground => {
                match b {
                    0x1b => self.tap = Tap::Esc,
                    0x98 | 0x9e | 0x9f => self.tap = Tap::String { apc: false },
                    _ => {}
                }
                false
            }
            Tap::Esc => {
                self.tap = match b {
                    0x1b => Tap::Esc,
                    b'[' | 0x9b => Tap::Csi,
                    b']' => Tap::Osc,
                    b'P' | 0x90 => Tap::Dcs,
                    b'X' | b'^' => Tap::String { apc: false },
                    b'_' => {
                        self.apc_buf.clear();
                        Tap::String { apc: true }
                    }
                    _ => Tap::Ground,
                };
                false
            }
            Tap::Csi => {
                match b {
                    0x20..=0x3f => {}
                    0x40..=0x7e => self.tap = Tap::Ground,
                    0x1b => self.tap = Tap::Esc,
                    _ => self.tap = Tap::Ground, // C1 / garbage — bail safely
                }
                false
            }
            Tap::Osc => {
                match b {
                    0x07 | 0x9c => self.tap = Tap::Ground,
                    0x1b => self.tap = Tap::OscEsc,
                    _ => {}
                }
                false
            }
            Tap::OscEsc => {
                self.tap = if b == b'\\' { Tap::Ground } else { Tap::Osc };
                false
            }
            Tap::Dcs => {
                match b {
                    0x40..=0x7e => self.tap = Tap::DcsPassthrough,
                    0x1b => self.tap = Tap::DcsEsc,
                    0x9c => self.tap = Tap::Ground,
                    _ => {}
                }
                false
            }
            Tap::DcsPassthrough => {
                match b {
                    0x1b => self.tap = Tap::DcsEsc,
                    0x9c => self.tap = Tap::Ground,
                    _ => {}
                }
                false
            }
            Tap::DcsEsc => {
                self.tap = if b == b'\\' {
                    Tap::Ground
                } else {
                    Tap::DcsPassthrough
                };
                false
            }
            Tap::String { apc } => match b {
                0x07 | 0x9c => {
                    self.tap = Tap::Ground;
                    if apc {
                        true
                    } else {
                        self.apc_buf.clear();
                        false
                    }
                }
                0x1b => {
                    self.tap = Tap::StringEsc { apc };
                    false
                }
                _ => {
                    if apc {
                        if self.apc_buf.len() < MAX_APC_BYTES {
                            self.apc_buf.push(b);
                        } else {
                            self.apc_buf.clear();
                            self.tap = Tap::String { apc: false };
                        }
                    }
                    false
                }
            },
            Tap::StringEsc { apc } => {
                if b == b'\\' {
                    self.tap = Tap::Ground;
                    if apc {
                        true
                    } else {
                        self.apc_buf.clear();
                        false
                    }
                } else {
                    self.tap = Tap::String { apc };
                    if apc {
                        self.apc_buf.push(0x1b);
                        self.apc_buf.push(b);
                    }
                    false
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn abs_row(&self, y: usize) -> i64 {
        self.scrollback.len() as i64 + y as i64
    }

    fn touch_all(&mut self) {
        let seq = self.seq;
        for row in self.active_grid_mut().iter_mut() {
            row.touch = seq;
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------- mutation

    fn put_char(&mut self, c: char) {
        let width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(c).unwrap_or(0);
        if width == 0 {
            return; // combining marks are dropped for grid simplicity
        }
        if self.pending_wrap && self.auto_wrap {
            // Soft wrap: mark the row we are leaving so reflow knows the
            // next row is a continuation of this logical line.
            let y = self.cursor.1;
            if let Some(row) = self.active_grid_mut().get_mut(y) {
                row.wrapped = true;
            }
            self.cursor.0 = 0;
            self.linefeed_internal();
        }
        self.pending_wrap = false;

        if self.insert_mode {
            let (x, y) = self.cursor;
            let grid = self.active_grid_mut();
            if let Some(row) = grid.get_mut(y) {
                for _ in 0..width {
                    if row.cells.len() > 1 {
                        row.cells.pop();
                        row.cells.insert(x, Cell::default());
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        let (fg, bg, fl) = (self.cur_fg, self.cur_bg, self.cur_flags);
        let (x, y) = self.cursor;
        if let Some(row) = self.active_grid_mut().get_mut(y) {
            if let Some(cell) = row.cells.get_mut(x) {
                *cell = Cell {
                    ch: c,
                    fg,
                    bg,
                    flags: fl,
                };
            }
            if width == 2 && x + 1 < row.cells.len() {
```
