```toml
[package]
name = "rustango"
version = "6.2.0-dev"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.85"
description = "Django-style batteries-included web framework, rewritten in pure Rust (no C/C++ dependencies)"
license = "BSD-3-Clause"
keywords = ["web", "framework", "django", "orm", "templates"]
categories = ["web-programming::http-server"]

[lib]
name = "rustango"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "rustango"
path = "src/bin/rustango.rs"

[dependencies]
rustango-macros = { path = "macros", version = "6.2.0-dev" }
# Async edge only (HTTP server). The framework core itself is synchronous,
# WSGI-style, and runs on blocking worker threads.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "net", "macros", "time", "io-util", "signal", "sync"] }
axum = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["http1", "tokio"] }

# Serialization / config
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
toml = "0.9"

# Crypto (RustCrypto - pure Rust)
sha2 = "0.10"
hmac = "0.12"
pbkdf2 = "0.12"
base64 = "0.22"

# Misc pure-Rust utilities
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4"] }
chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
flate2 = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["rust_backend"] }
thiserror = "2"

# contrib.ai (feature-gated): ureq 3.x uses rustls with the `ring` provider,
# which is 100% Rust. No OpenSSL, no aws-lc-rs C sources.
ureq = { version = "3", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "json"], optional = true }

[features]
default = []
ai = ["dep:ureq"]
```

## `crates/server/rustango/README.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/README.md)

````markdown
# rustango — Django, rewritten in pure Rust

**rustango** is a batteries-included, Django-style web framework written
entirely in **Rust with zero C/C++ dependencies**. It re-implements the core
Django architecture — settings, URL routing, views (function + class-based),
a model/ORM layer with migrations, the Django Template Language, forms with
validation, sessions, authentication, CSRF, flash messages, middleware, an
auto-generated admin site, i18n catalogs, a cache framework, static files,
and a management CLI — plus a first-class **AI/LLM agent module**
(`contrib.ai`) for building LLM-backed applications.

```
License: BSD-3-Clause (inspired by Django; not affiliated with the Django project)
Version: 6.2.0-dev  (tracks the Django 6.2 API surface conceptually)
Status:  production-shaped dev framework — see the coverage matrix for details
```

---

## Quick start

```bash
# from this directory
cargo run -- runserver            # built-in demo project at http://127.0.0.1:8000
# open http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/  (create a login: cargo run -- createsuperuser -u root -p secret)

cargo test                        # 198 unit & integration tests
cargo test --features ai          # + LLM client/agent tests (mocked server)

# scaffold a standalone project
cargo run -- startproject mysite
cd mysite && cargo run
```

Or use it as a library:

```toml
[dependencies]
rustango = "6.2"            # + features = ["ai"] for the LLM module
```

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use rustango::prelude::*;
use rustango::views::{make_view, render, View};
use rustango::templates::{Context, TplValue};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, rustango::Model)]
#[model(table = "polls_question")]
pub struct Question {
    #[field(auto)]
    pub id: i64,
    #[field(char, max = 200)]
    pub question_text: String,
    #[field(datetime, auto_now_add)]
    pub pub_date: rustango::types::DateTime,
}

fn main() {
    let project = Project::builder()
        .settings(Settings::builder().database("json:db.json").build())
        .add_app(App::new("polls").models::<Question>())
        .urls(vec![rustango::urls::named_path("", make_view(|req| {
            let mut ctx = Context::new();
            ctx.set("title", TplValue::Str("It works!".into()));
            render(req, "index.html", ctx)
        }), "home")])
        .admin(|site| site.register::<Question>(Default::default()))
        .build()
        .expect("project");

    let addr = "127.0.0.1:8000".parse().unwrap();
    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().enable_all().build().unwrap()
        .block_on(rustango::server::serve_with_shutdown(Arc::new(project), addr))
        .unwrap();
}
```

## Declaring models

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, rustango::Model)]
#[model(table = "polls_choice")]
pub struct Choice {
    #[field(auto)]                       // AutoField primary key
    pub id: i64,
    #[field(fk, target = "polls_question")] // ForeignKey
    pub question_id: i64,
    #[field(char, max = 200)]            // CharField(max_length=200)
    pub choice_text: String,
    #[field(int, default = 0)]           // IntegerField(default=0)
    pub votes: i64,
}

// usage
let saved = choice.save(&*backend)?;                       // INSERT/UPDATE
let rows  = Choice::objects(&*backend)
    .filter(Q::contains("choice_text", "yes") | Q::gt("votes", 3))
    .order_by("-votes")
    .take(10)
    .all()?;
let author_names = Post::objects(&*backend)
    .filter(Q::eq("author_id__username", "ada"))           // FK traversal
    .all()?;
```

Field options: `auto`, `char (max = N)`, `text`, `int/float/bool (default = v)`,
`datetime (null, auto_now_add)`, `fk (target = "table")`, plus `unique`.
The Rust type drives row conversion (`i64`, `String`, `f64`, `bool`,
`DateTime`, `Option<DateTime>`).

## AI / LLM agent support (`contrib.ai`)

```rust
use rustango::contrib::ai::{AiClient, Agent, Tool};

let client = AiClient::from_settings();      // settings: ai_api_url / ai_api_key / ai_model
let reply = client.chat_simple("Explain Django's ORM in one paragraph.")?;

let agent = Agent::new(client)
    .system("You are the admin assistant.")
    .tool(Tool::simple("count_users", "Count rows in auth_user", |_args| {
        Ok(serde_json::json!({ "count": 42 }))
    }))
    .max_steps(8);
let answer = agent.run("How many users are there?")?;
```

Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio,
LiteLLM...). TLS is rustls with the `ring` provider — pure Rust, no OpenSSL.
The agent loop handles multi-step tool calling (`tool_calls` → results →
final answer) with a step budget.

## Architecture

```
request ─▶ middleware.process_request (top-down)
        ─▶ url resolver (path converters, named routes)
        ─▶ view (function or class-based)
        ─▶ ORM / templates / forms / messages
        ─▶ middleware.process_response (bottom-up)
```

The framework core is synchronous (WSGI-style); the HTTP edge is tokio+axum
running handlers on blocking worker threads. The test client drives the same
pipeline in-process.

### Concept map (Django → rustango)

| Django | rustango | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `django.conf.settings` | `settings::Settings` (+ TOML overlay, `settings::global()`) | builder + `settings.toml` |
| `django.http` | `http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse, QueryDict}` | cookies, headers, JSON/form bodies |
| `django.urls.path/re_path` | `urls::{path, Router, reverse}` | `<int:> <str:> <slug:> <uuid:> <path:>` converters, `include()` = `Router::mount` with namespace |
| `django.views.generic` | `views::{View, TemplateView, ListView, DetailView, RedirectView}` | `as_view()`, pagination via `?page=` |
| `django.middleware` | `middleware::Middleware` + built-ins | Security, Session, Common (APPEND_SLASH), CsrfView, Auth, Messages, Clickjacking, GZip |
| `django.db.models.Model` | `#[derive(Model)] #[model(table=...)]` + `#[field(...)]` | pk autoincrement, unique, defaults, auto_now_add |
| `Model.objects` | `ModelExt::objects(&backend)` | `filter/exclude/order_by/get/first/latest/count/exists/take/skip/update/delete` |
| `Q` objects | `orm::Q` (`&`, `|`, `!`) | incl. `author__username` FK traversal, `__year/month/day`, `__contains/icontains/startswith/gt/...` |
| DB backends | `Backend` trait: `InMemoryBackend`, `JsonFileBackend` | JSON snapshots are atomic (write tmp + rename) |
| migrations | `orm::migrations` + CLI `makemigrations/migrate/showmigrations` | JSON migration files, `_migrations` bookkeeping |
| `django.template` | `templates` module | `{{ var\|filter }}`, `{% for/if/elif/else %}`, `{% block %}`+`{% extends %}`, `{% include %}`, `{% with %}`, `{% csrf_token %}`, `{% url %}`, `{% static %}`, `{% trans %}`, `{% comment %}`, autoescape ON, 24 built-in filters, custom loaders |
| `django.forms` | `forms::{Form, CharField, EmailField, IntegerField, ...}` | `bind()`, `is_valid()`, `cleaned_data`, `errors`, `as_p()/as_table()` |
| `contrib.auth` | `auth` module | `User` model, PBKDF2-SHA256 in Django wire format (`pbkdf2_sha256$iter$salt$base64hash` — verifies Django-generated hashes), `authenticate/login/logout`, `login_required`, `createsuperuser` |
| `contrib.sessions` | `sessions` | server-side `django_session` table, `sessionid` cookie, `flush/cycle_key/clear_expired` |
| `middleware.csrf` | `csrf` | double-submit cookie + form/header token, `{% csrf_token %}` |
| `contrib.messages` | `messages` | session-backed flash messages, pop-on-read |
| `contrib.admin` | `admin::{AdminSite, ModelAdmin}` | auto CRUD (list/search/pagination/add/change/delete), login, embedded templates, `admin:` namespace |
| `contrib.staticfiles` | `staticfiles` | STATICFILES_DIRS serving + traversal protection |
| `core.cache` | `cache::{Cache, LocMemCache}` | TTL, add/touch, `cache_page()` decorator |
| `core.signals` | `signals` | `pre_save/post_save/pre_delete/post_delete`, request signals, panic-safe receivers |
| `utils.translation` | `i18n` | JSON catalogs, `{% trans %}`, language fallback (`de-de` → `de`) |
| `core.management` | `management` + `rustango` CLI | runserver, makemigrations, migrate, showmigrations, createsuperuser, clearsessions, check, startproject, startapp |
| `test.Client` | `testclient::Client` | in-process, cookie jar, `login()`, `force_login()`, `post_csrf()`, redirects |
| — (new) | `contrib::ai` | OpenAI-compatible client + tool-calling agent loop |

## Dependency purity

Zero C/C++ is linked. The stack:

| Purpose | Crate(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP server edge | `tokio`, `axum`, `hyper` | pure Rust |
| Serialization | `serde`, `serde_json`, `toml` | pure Rust |
| Crypto | `sha2`, `hmac`, `pbkdf2`, `base64` (RustCrypto) | pure Rust |
| TLS (ai feature) | `ureq` + `rustls` + `ring` | pure Rust (not OpenSSL, not aws-lc-rs) |
| Misc | `chrono`, `uuid`, `flate2(rust_backend)`, `hex`, `thiserror` | pure Rust |
| Proc macros | `syn`, `quote` (rustango-macros) | pure Rust |

## Coverage matrix

**Implemented and tested** (see `cargo test` — 198 tests, plus 14
end-to-end integration tests exercising a full blog app: routing, FK
queries, CSRF-protected forms, auth flows, admin CRUD, flash messages,
JSON persistence across restarts):

- Request/response cycle, QueryDict, cookies, headers, file upload limits
- Router with converters, namespacing, `reverse()`, APPEND_SLASH
- ORM: models, FKs, joins via `__`, unique constraints, defaults,
  auto_now_add, QuerySet API, two backends, atomic JSON persistence
- Migrations: autodetection, migration files, apply/fake/show
- Template engine: full DTL subset listed above, inheritance chains,
  model-aware dotted lookup, 24 filters, lenient missing-variable handling
- Forms: 9 field types, validation messages matching Django's wording,
  bound/unbound rendering, error lists
- Auth: Django-compatible password hashes, session-fixation-safe login,
  permissions flags, `login_required`/`staff_required`, createsuperuser
- Sessions: server-side, expiry, rotation, clear_expired
- CSRF: double-submit, safe-method exemptions, header tokens
- Messages: levels, pop-on-read, template integration
- Admin: registration, changelist (search, order, pagination), add/change
  forms auto-generated from model schema, delete confirmation, staff auth
- Middleware: 8 built-ins, ordered request/response phases, error-response
  phase (cookies still set on 404/500)
- Signals, cache (TTL + page cache), i18n, static files, management CLI
- AI contrib: chat, tool calling, agent loop, mocked-server tests

**Partially implemented** (honest deltas vs Django):

- Storage: file-backed JSON engine instead of SQLite/PostgreSQL (the
  `Backend` trait is the extension point); no transactions/connection pools
- Migrations: no data migrations, column drops are recorded but no-op'd on
  the JSON engine, no `AlterField` semantics beyond schema swap
- Templates: no `{% load %}` template-tag libraries, no `{{ block.super }}`,
  custom filters registered via code rather than template libraries
- Forms: no `ModelForm` validation beyond schema-derived fields, no
  file uploads, no formsets
- Auth: no `Group`/`Permission` tables or per-object permissions
  (staff/superuser flags only)
- Admin: no inlines, no per-field `list_editable`, generic (row-based)
  change views
- i18n: gettext-style msgid lookup without plural forms or context

**Not implemented** (documented for completeness):

- GIS (`contrib.gis`), contenttypes/flatpages/redirects/sitemaps/syndication
  contrib apps, humanize
- Async views/ORM (the core is sync by design; the edge is async)
- Raw SQL, multi-database routing, database introspection commands
- Email backends, logging framework, `django.test` assertions runner

## Testing

```bash
cargo test                 # unit + integration (no network needed)
cargo test --features ai   # + ai module (mock OpenAI-compatible server)
```

The integration suite (`tests/integration.rs`) builds a complete blog app
and drives it through the in-process client: published-post filtering,
comment posting with CSRF + validation + flash messages, login/logout
cycles, FK-traversal queries, admin CRUD end-to-end, JSON persistence
across restarts, signal firing, and template inheritance with i18n.

## CLI reference

```text
rustango runserver [ADDR]                    # dev server (default 127.0.0.1:8000)
rustango makemigrations [APP]                # write migration files
rustango migrate [APP]                       # apply migrations
rustango showmigrations                      # [X]/[ ] list
rustango createsuperuser -u NAME -p PASS     # create/reset superuser
rustango clearsessions                       # purge expired sessions
rustango check                               # config summary
rustango startproject NAME [DIR]             # scaffold a project
rustango startapp NAME [DIR]                 # scaffold an app
```

//! `rustango-macros` — procedural macros for the rustango framework.
//!
//! The `#[model(...)]` attribute turns a plain Rust struct into a Django
//! model. Field kinds and options are declared with `#[field(...)]`
//! attributes; the Rust type drives storage conversion:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! #[rustango::model(table = "polls_question")]
//! pub struct Question {
//!     #[field(auto)]
//!     pub id: i64,
//!     #[field(char, max = 200)]
//!     pub question_text: String,
//!     #[field(datetime, auto_now_add)]
//!     pub pub_date: DateTime,
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! `#[field]` options:
//! * kind: `auto`, `char`, `text`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `datetime`, `fk`
//! * `max = N` (char), `unique`, `null`, `default = expr`,
//!   `auto_now_add` (datetime), `target = "table"` (fk)
//!
//! Untagged fields infer their column kind from the Rust type
//! (`i64`/`String`/`f64`/`bool`/`DateTime`/`Option<DateTime>`).

use proc_macro::TokenStream;
use quote::quote;
use syn::parse_macro_input;
use syn::spanned::Spanned;
use syn::{ItemStruct, Token};
use syn::parse::Parse as _ParseTrait;

/// One `#[field(...)]` argument: `max = 150`, `unique`, `default = false`.
struct FieldArg {
    key: syn::Ident,
    value: Option<syn::Expr>,
}

impl syn::parse::Parse for FieldArg {
    fn parse(input: syn::parse::ParseStream) -> syn::Result<Self> {
        let key = input.parse::<syn::Ident>()?;
        if input.peek(Token![=]) {
            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
            let value = input.parse::<syn::Expr>()?;
            Ok(FieldArg { key, value: Some(value) })
        } else {
            Ok(FieldArg { key, value: None })
        }
    }
}

/// Parsed `#[field(...)]` content.
struct FieldOpts {
    kind: String,
    max: usize,
    unique: bool,
    null: bool,
    auto_now_add: bool,
    default: Option<syn::Expr>,
    target: Option<String>,
}

impl FieldOpts {
    fn parse_args(args: Vec<FieldArg>) -> Result<FieldOpts, syn::Error> {
        let mut o = FieldOpts {
            kind: String::new(),
            max: 0,
            unique: false,
            null: false,
            auto_now_add: false,
            default: None,
            target: None,
        };
        for a in args {
            match a.key.to_string().as_str() {
                "auto" => o.kind = "auto".into(),
                "char" | "varchar" => o.kind = "char".into(),
                "text" => o.kind = "text".into(),
                "int" | "integer" => o.kind = "int".into(),
                "float" => o.kind = "float".into(),
                "bool" | "boolean" => o.kind = "bool".into(),
                "datetime" => o.kind = "datetime".into(),
                "fk" | "foreign_key" => o.kind = "fk".into(),
                "max" => {
                    if let Some(syn::Expr::Lit(lit)) = &a.value {
                        if let syn::Lit::Int(li) = &lit.lit {
                            o.max = li.base10_parse().unwrap_or(0);
                        }
                    }
                }
                "unique" => o.unique = true,
                "null" => o.null = true,
                "auto_now_add" => o.auto_now_add = true,
                "default" => o.default = a.value.clone(),
                "target" => {
                    if let Some(syn::Expr::Lit(lit)) = &a.value {
                        if let syn::Lit::Str(s) = &lit.lit {
                            o.target = Some(s.value());
                        }
                    }
                }
                other => {
                    return Err(syn::Error::new(
                        a.key.span(),
                        format!("unknown #[field] option `{other}`"),
                    ))
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(o)
    }
}

/// Rust type tag used to drive row conversion.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum RustTy {
    Int,
    Float,
    Text,
    Bool,
    DateTime,
    OptInt,
    OptFloat,
    OptText,
    OptBool,
    OptDateTime,
}

impl RustTy {
    fn is_optional(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            RustTy::OptInt | RustTy::OptFloat | RustTy::OptText | RustTy::OptBool | RustTy::OptDateTime
        )
    }
}

/// Final path-segment ident of the inner type of an `Option<...>` path,
/// e.g. `Option<DateTime>` -> `"DateTime"`, `Option<i64>` -> `"i64"`.
fn option_inner_ident(ty: &syn::Type) -> Option<String> {
    if let syn::Type::Path(p) = ty {
        if let Some(seg) = p.path.segments.first() {
            if seg.ident == "Option" {
                if let syn::PathArguments::AngleBracketed(args) = &seg.arguments {
                    if let Some(syn::GenericArgument::Type(inner)) = args.args.first() {
                        if let syn::Type::Path(ip) = inner {
                            if let Some(last) = ip.path.segments.last() {
                                return Some(last.ident.to_string());
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn classify(ty: &syn::Type) -> RustTy {
    if let syn::Type::Path(p) = ty {
        let segs: Vec<&syn::PathSegment> = p.path.segments.iter().collect();
        if let Some(first) = segs.first() {
            if first.ident == "Option" {
                // Only inspect the INNER type: every `Option<T>` used to be
                // classified as `Option<DateTime>`, making `Option<i64>` /
                // `Option<String>` fields generate type errors buried in
                // the proc-macro expansion.
                let inner = option_inner_ident(ty).unwrap_or_default();
                return match inner.as_str() {
                    "DateTime" => RustTy::OptDateTime,
                    "i64" | "i32" => RustTy::OptInt,
                    "f64" | "f32" => RustTy::OptFloat,
                    "String" => RustTy::OptText,
                    "bool" => RustTy::OptBool,
                    _ => RustTy::OptText,
                };
            }
            match first.ident.to_string().as_str() {
                "i64" | "i32" => return RustTy::Int,
                "f64" | "f32" => return RustTy::Float,
                "String" => return RustTy::Text,
                "bool" => return RustTy::Bool,
                "DateTime" => return RustTy::DateTime,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    RustTy::Text
}

fn column_desc(
    name: &str,
    o: &FieldOpts,
    ty: RustTy,
) -> Result<proc_macro2::TokenStream, syn::Error> {
    let name_lit = name;
    let mut base = match o.kind.as_str() {
        "auto" => quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::auto(#name_lit)),
        "char" => {
            if o.max == 0 {
                return Err(syn::Error::new(name.span(), "`char` fields need `max = N`"));
            }
            let max = o.max;
            quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::char(#name_lit, #max))
        }
        "text" => quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::text(#name_lit)),
        "int" => quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::integer(#name_lit)),
        "float" => quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::float(#name_lit)),
        "bool" => quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::boolean(#name_lit, false)),
        "datetime" => {
            if o.auto_now_add {
                quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::datetime_auto_now_add(#name_lit))
            } else {
                let null = o.null || matches!(ty, RustTy::OptDateTime);
                quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::datetime(#name_lit, #null))
            }
        }
        "fk" => {
            let target = match &o.target {
                Some(t) => t.clone(),
                None => {
                    return Err(syn::Error::new(
                        name.span(),
                        "`fk` fields need `target = \"table_name\"`",
                    ))
                }
            };
            quote!(::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc::foreign_key(#name_lit, #target))
        }
        other => {
            return Err(syn::Error::new(name.span(), format!("unknown field kind `{other}`")))
        }
    };

    if o.unique {
        base = quote!(#base.unique());
    }
    // Optional field kinds are nullable columns, whatever the kind.
    if o.null || ty.is_optional() {
        base = quote!(#base.nullable());
    }
    if let Some(d) = &o.default {
        base = quote!({
            let mut c = #base;
            c.default = Some(::rustango::orm::Value::from(#d));
            c
        });
    }
    Ok(base)
}

fn from_expr(ty: RustTy) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    let v = quote!(it.next().unwrap_or(&::rustango::orm::Value::Null));
    match ty {
        RustTy::Int => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_int(#v)),
        RustTy::Float => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_float(#v)),
        RustTy::Text => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_text(#v)),
        RustTy::Bool => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_bool(#v)),
        RustTy::DateTime => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_datetime(#v)),
        RustTy::OptInt => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_int_opt(#v)),
        RustTy::OptFloat => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_float_opt(#v)),
        RustTy::OptText => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_text_opt(#v)),
        RustTy::OptBool => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_bool_opt(#v)),
        RustTy::OptDateTime => quote!(::rustango::orm::model::coerce_datetime_opt(#v)),
    }
}

fn to_expr(name: &proc_macro2::Ident, ty: RustTy) -> proc_macro2::TokenStream {
    match ty {
        RustTy::Int => quote!(::rustango::orm::Value::Int(self.#name)),
        RustTy::Float => quote!(::rustango::orm::Value::Float(self.#name)),
        RustTy::Text => quote!(::rustango::orm::Value::Text(self.#name.clone())),
        RustTy::Bool => quote!(::rustango::orm::Value::Bool(self.#name)),
        RustTy::DateTime => quote!(::rustango::orm::Value::DateTime(self.#name)),
        RustTy::OptInt => quote!(self
            .#name
            .map(::rustango::orm::Value::Int)
            .unwrap_or(::rustango::orm::Value::Null)),
        RustTy::OptFloat => quote!(self
            .#name
            .map(::rustango::orm::Value::Float)
            .unwrap_or(::rustango::orm::Value::Null)),
        RustTy::OptText => quote!(self
            .#name
            .clone()
            .map(::rustango::orm::Value::Text)
            .unwrap_or(::rustango::orm::Value::Null)),
        RustTy::OptBool => quote!(self
            .#name
            .map(::rustango::orm::Value::Bool)
            .unwrap_or(::rustango::orm::Value::Null)),
        RustTy::OptDateTime => quote!(self
            .#name
            .map(::rustango::orm::Value::DateTime)
            .unwrap_or(::rustango::orm::Value::Null)),
    }
}

/// Extract `#[field(...)]` from a field, if present.
fn field_opts(f: &syn::Field) -> Result<Option<FieldOpts>, syn::Error> {
    let mut result = None;
    for attr in &f.attrs {
        if attr.path().is_ident("field") {
            let args: syn::punctuated::Punctuated<FieldArg, Token![,]> =
                attr.parse_args_with(|input: syn::parse::ParseStream| {
                    input.parse_terminated(FieldArg::parse, Token![,])
                })?;
            result = Some(FieldOpts::parse_args(args.into_iter().collect())?);
        }
    }
    Ok(result)
}

/// The `Model` derive macro (helper attributes: `#[model(...)]` on the
/// struct, `#[field(...)]` on fields).
#[proc_macro_derive(Model, attributes(model, field))]
pub fn model(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    let item_struct = parse_macro_input!(input as ItemStruct);
    let struct_name = &item_struct.ident;

    // Read `#[model(table = "name")]` from the struct attributes.
    let mut table_override: Option<String> = None;
    for attr in &item_struct.attrs {
        if attr.path().is_ident("model") {
            let args: syn::punctuated::Punctuated<FieldArg, Token![,]> =
                match attr.parse_args_with(|input: syn::parse::ParseStream| {
                    input.parse_terminated(FieldArg::parse, Token![,])
                }) {
                    Ok(a) => a,
                    Err(e) => return e.to_compile_error().into(),
                };
            for a in &args {
                if a.key == "table" {
                    if let Some(syn::Expr::Lit(lit)) = &a.value {
                        if let syn::Lit::Str(s) = &lit.lit {
                            table_override = Some(s.value());
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    let table = table_override.unwrap_or_else(|| snake_case(&struct_name.to_string()));

    let mut col_exprs = Vec::new();
    let mut from_exprs = Vec::new();
    let mut to_exprs = Vec::new();
    let mut pk_field: Option<proc_macro2::Ident> = None;

    let fields = match &item_struct.fields {
        syn::Fields::Named(named) => &named.named,
        _ => {
            return syn::Error::new(
                item_struct.ident.span(),
                "only structs with named fields are supported",
            )
            .to_compile_error()
            .into()
        }
    };

    for f in fields {
        let fname = match &f.ident {
            Some(i) => i.clone(),
            None => continue,
        };
        let ty = classify(&f.ty);
        let opts = match field_opts(f) {
            Ok(o) => o,
            Err(e) => return e.to_compile_error().into(),
        };

        let eff_opts = match opts {
            Some(o) => o,
            None => FieldOpts {
                // Untagged: infer kind from the Rust type.
                kind: match ty {
                    RustTy::Int | RustTy::OptInt => "int",
                    RustTy::Float | RustTy::OptFloat => "float",
                    RustTy::Text | RustTy::OptText => "text",
                    RustTy::Bool | RustTy::OptBool => "bool",
                    RustTy::DateTime | RustTy::OptDateTime => "datetime",
                }
                .into(),
                max: 0,
                unique: false,
                null: ty.is_optional(),
                auto_now_add: false,
                default: None,
                target: None,
            },
        };

        if eff_opts.kind == "auto" {
            pk_field = Some(fname.clone());
        }
        match column_desc(&fname.to_string(), &eff_opts, ty) {
            Ok(c) => col_exprs.push(c),
            Err(e) => return e.to_compile_error().into(),
        }
        let fe = from_expr(ty);
        from_exprs.push(quote!(#fname: #fe,));
        let te = to_expr(&fname, ty);
        to_exprs.push(quote!(#te,));
    }

    let pk_ident = match pk_field {
        Some(p) => p,
        None => {
            return syn::Error::new(
                item_struct.ident.span(),
                "model needs one `#[field(auto)]` primary key field",
            )
            .to_compile_error()
            .into()
        }
    };

    // NOTE: derive macros keep the original struct in place (helper
    // attributes are stripped automatically), so we only emit impls here.
    let out_name = struct_name;

    let expanded = quote! {
        impl #out_name {
            /// Primary key value.
            pub fn pk(&self) -> i64 { self.#pk_ident }
            /// Set the primary key (used after INSERT).
            pub fn set_pk(&mut self, id: i64) { self.#pk_ident = id; }
        }

        impl ::rustango::orm::Model for #out_name {
            fn table() -> &'static str { #table }

            fn columns() -> &'static [::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc] {
                use std::sync::OnceLock;
                static COLS: OnceLock<Vec<::rustango::orm::ColumnDesc>> = OnceLock::new();
                COLS.get_or_init(|| vec![
                    #(#col_exprs),*
                ])
            }

            fn from_row(row: &[::rustango::orm::Value]) -> Self {
                #[allow(unused_mut)]
                let mut it = row.iter();
                #out_name {
                    #(#from_exprs)*
                }
            }

            fn to_row(&self) -> Vec<::rustango::orm::Value> {
                vec![
                    #(#to_exprs)*
                ]
            }

            fn pk(&self) -> i64 { self.#pk_ident }

            fn set_pk(&mut self, id: i64) { self.#pk_ident = id; }
        }
    };

    if std::env::var("RUSTANGO_MACRO_DEBUG").is_ok() {
        eprintln!("=== #[model] expansion for {} ===\n{}", struct_name, expanded);
    }
    expanded.into()
}

fn snake_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(name.len() + 4);
    for (i, ch) in name.chars().enumerate() {
        if ch.is_ascii_uppercase() {
            if i > 0 {
                out.push('_');
            }
            out.push(ch.to_ascii_lowercase());
        } else {
            out.push(ch);
        }
    }
    out
}
````

    </td>

</table>
<div class="pagination">
  Page {{ page }} of {{ pages }}

  {% if page < pages %}<a href="?page={{ page|add:1 }}">next</a>{% endif %}

## `crates/server/rustango/src/admin.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/src/admin.rs)

````rust
//! Admin — `django.contrib.admin`: automatic CRUD for registered models.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use rustango::admin::{AdminSite, ModelAdmin};
//!
//! let project = Project::builder()
//!     // ...
//!     .admin(|site| {
//!         site.register::<Question>(ModelAdmin {
//!             list_display: vec!["id".into(), "question_text".into()],
//!             search_fields: vec!["question_text".into()],
//!             ..Default::default()
//!         });
//!     })
//!     .build();
//! ```
//!
//! Mounted at `settings.admin_url` (default `admin/`) with namespace
//! `admin:` — routes `admin:index`, `admin:login`, `admin:logout`,
//! `admin:list`, `admin:add`, `admin:change`, `admin:delete`.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::errors::HttpError;
use crate::forms::{Field as FormField, Form};
use crate::http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse};
use crate::orm::{Backend, Criteria, FieldKind, Model, Value};
use crate::templates::{Context, TplValue};
use crate::urls::{named_path, Router};
use crate::views::{render, ViewFn};

/// Per-model admin options — `ModelAdmin`.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct ModelAdmin {
    /// Columns shown on the changelist (defaults to first 4 fields).
    pub list_display: Vec<String>,
    /// Char/text columns searchable via `?q=`.
    pub search_fields: Vec<String>,
    /// Default ordering, `-` prefix for desc (default `-id`).
    pub ordering: String,
    pub list_per_page: usize,
}

/// One registered model inside the admin site.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct AdminEntry {
    pub table: String,
    pub meta: crate::orm::ModelMeta,
    pub admin: ModelAdmin,
}

/// The admin site.
pub struct AdminSite {
    pub site_title: String,
    pub site_header: String,
    pub entries: Vec<AdminEntry>,
    /// URL prefix the site is mounted under (no slashes), e.g. `admin`.
    /// Defaults to `admin`; `ProjectBuilder::build` syncs it with
    /// `settings.admin_url`.
    pub url_prefix: String,
}

impl AdminSite {
    pub fn new(site_title: impl Into<String>, site_header: impl Into<String>) -> AdminSite {
        AdminSite {
            site_title: site_title.into(),
            site_header: site_header.into(),
            entries: Vec::new(),
            url_prefix: "admin".into(),
        }
    }

    /// Absolute URL inside the admin site (`"login/"` -> `/admin/login/`).
    fn url(&self, path: &str) -> String {
        if self.url_prefix.is_empty() {
            format!("/{path}")
        } else {
            format!("/{}/{}", self.url_prefix, path)
        }
    }

    /// `admin.site.register(Question, QuestionAdmin)`.
    pub fn register<T: Model>(&mut self, admin: ModelAdmin) {
        let meta = crate::orm::ModelMeta::of::<T>();
        let table = meta.table.clone();
        self.entries.push(AdminEntry { table, meta, admin });
    }

    fn entry(&self, table: &str) -> Option<&AdminEntry> {
        self.entries.iter().find(|e| e.table == table)
    }

    /// Build the admin Router (mounted under settings.admin_url).
    pub fn urls(&self) -> Router {
        let site = Arc::new(AdminSite {
            site_title: self.site_title.clone(),
            site_header: self.site_header.clone(),
            entries: self.entries.clone(),
            url_prefix: self.url_prefix.clone(),
        });

        let index: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| site.view_index(req))
        };
        let login: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| site.view_login(req))
        };
        let logout: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| site.view_logout(req))
        };
        let list: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| site.view_list(req))
        };
        let add: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| site.view_add_or_change(req, None))
        };
        let change: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| {
                let pk = req.int_param("pk")?;
                site.view_add_or_change(req, Some(pk))
            })
        };
        let delete: ViewFn = {
            let site = site.clone();
            Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| {
                let pk = req.int_param("pk")?;
                site.view_delete(req, pk)
            })
        };

        Router::new(vec![
            named_path("", index, "index"),
            named_path("login/", login, "login"),
            named_path("logout/", logout, "logout"),
            named_path("<str:table>/", list, "list"),
            named_path("<str:table>/add/", add, "add"),
            named_path("<str:table>/<int:pk>/change/", change, "change"),
            named_path("<str:table>/<int:pk>/delete/", delete, "delete"),
        ])
    }

    // -- shared context ------------------------------------------------------

    fn base_ctx(&self, req: &HttpRequest) -> Context {
        let mut ctx = Context::new();
        ctx.set("site_title", TplValue::Str(self.site_title.clone()));
        ctx.set("site_header", TplValue::Str(self.site_header.clone()));
        // Templates build admin links from this (no hardcoded `/admin/`).
        let prefix = if self.url_prefix.is_empty() {
            String::new()
        } else {
            format!("/{}", self.url_prefix)
        };
        ctx.set("admin_prefix", TplValue::Str(prefix));
        let mut user = HashMap::new();
        user.insert("username".to_string(), TplValue::Str(req.user.username().to_string()));
        user.insert("is_authenticated".to_string(), TplValue::Bool(req.user.is_authenticated()));
        user.insert("is_staff".to_string(), TplValue::Bool(req.user.is_staff()));
        ctx.set("user", TplValue::Map(Arc::new(user)));
        ctx
    }

    fn require_staff(&self, req: &HttpRequest) -> Result<(), HttpResponse> {
        if !req.user.is_authenticated() || (!req.user.is_staff() && !req.user.is_superuser()) {
            return Err(HttpResponse::redirect(self.url("login/")));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // -- views -----------------------------------------------------------------

    fn view_login(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        if req.method == crate::http::Method::POST {
            let username = req.post.get("username").unwrap_or("").to_string();
            let password = req.post.get("password").unwrap_or("").to_string();
            let backend = req
                .backend
                .clone()
                .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::ServerError("no backend".into()))?;
            let user = crate::auth::authenticate(&*backend, &username, &password);
            return match user {
                Some(u) if u.is_staff || u.is_superuser => {
                    crate::auth::login(req, &u);
                    Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(self.url("")))
                }
                _ => {
                    let mut ctx = self.base_ctx(req);
                    ctx.set(
                        "error",
                        TplValue::Str("Invalid credentials or not a staff user.".into()),
                    );
                    render(req, "admin/login.html", ctx)
                }
            };
        }
        if req.user.is_staff() || req.user.is_superuser() {
            return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(self.url("")));
        }
        let ctx = self.base_ctx(req);
        render(req, "admin/login.html", ctx)
    }

    fn view_logout(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        crate::auth::logout(req);
        Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(self.url("login/")))
    }

    fn view_index(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        if let Err(res) = self.require_staff(req) {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        let backend = req
            .backend
            .clone()
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::ServerError("no backend".into()))?;
        let mut models = Vec::new();
        for entry in &self.entries {
            let count = backend
                .count(&entry.table, &Criteria::any())
                .unwrap_or(0);
            models.push(TplValue::Map(Arc::new(HashMap::from([
                ("name".to_string(), TplValue::Str(entry.table.clone())),
                ("count".to_string(), TplValue::Int(count as i64)),
            ]))));
        }
        let mut ctx = self.base_ctx(req);
        ctx.set("models", TplValue::List(models));
        render(req, "admin/index.html", ctx)
    }

    fn display_columns(entry: &AdminEntry) -> Vec<String> {
        if entry.admin.list_display.is_empty() {
            entry
                .meta
                .columns
                .iter()
                .take(4)
                .map(|c| c.name.clone())
                .collect()
        } else {
            entry.admin.list_display.clone()
        }
    }

    fn view_list(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        if let Err(res) = self.require_staff(req) {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        let table = req.param("table").unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let entry = self
            .entry(&table)
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::NotFound(format!("model `{table}` not registered")))?
            .clone();
        let backend = req
            .backend
            .clone()
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::ServerError("no backend".into()))?;

        // search: OR of icontains over searchable text columns
        let mut crit = Criteria::any();
        let q = req.query.get("q").unwrap_or("").to_string();
        if !q.is_empty() {
            let mut branches = Vec::new();
            for field in &entry.admin.search_fields {
                if let Some(col) = entry.meta.column(field) {
                    if matches!(col.kind, FieldKind::Char | FieldKind::Text) {
                        branches.push(Criteria::icontains(field.clone(), q.clone()));
                    }
                }
            }
            if !branches.is_empty() {
                crit = Criteria::Or(branches);
            }
        }

        let ordering = if entry.admin.ordering.is_empty() {
            "-id".to_string()
        } else {
            entry.admin.ordering.clone()
        };
        let desc = ordering.starts_with('-');
        let order_field = ordering.trim_start_matches('-').to_string();
        let order_spec = vec![(order_field, desc)];

        let per_page = if entry.admin.list_per_page == 0 { 25 } else { entry.admin.list_per_page };
        let total = backend.count(&entry.table, &crit).map_err(HttpError::from)?;
        let pages = total.div_ceil(per_page).max(1);
        let page: usize = req
            .query
            .get("page")
            .and_then(|p| p.parse().ok())
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1)
            .min(pages);

        let cols = entry.meta.columns.clone();
        let mut rows = backend
            .select(&entry.table, &crit, &order_spec, Some(per_page), Some((page - 1) * per_page))
            .map_err(HttpError::from)?;

        let display = Self::display_columns(&entry);
        let objects: Vec<TplValue> = rows
            .drain(..)
            .map(|row| {
                let mut m = HashMap::new();
                for (c, v) in cols.iter().zip(&row) {
                    if display.contains(&c.name) || c.name == "id" {
                        m.insert(c.name.clone(), TplValue::Str(v.display()));
                    }
                }
                m.insert("pk".to_string(), TplValue::Str(display_pk(&cols, &row)));
                TplValue::Map(Arc::new(m))
            })
            .collect();

        let mut ctx = self.base_ctx(req);
        ctx.set("model_name", TplValue::Str(table.clone()));
        ctx.set("columns", TplValue::List(
            display.iter().map(|c| TplValue::Str(c.clone())).collect(),
        ));
        ctx.set("objects", TplValue::List(objects));
        ctx.set("total", TplValue::Int(total as i64));
        ctx.set("page", TplValue::Int(page as i64));
        ctx.set("pages", TplValue::Int(pages as i64));
        ctx.set("q", TplValue::Str(q));
        render(req, "admin/change_list.html", ctx)
    }

    /// Build the auto-form from model columns; when `initial` values are
    /// provided (change view GET), they are bound as display values.
    fn build_form(
        entry: &AdminEntry,
        initial: Option<&HashMap<String, String>>,
        posted: Option<&crate::http::QueryDict>,
    ) -> Form {
        let mut fields: Vec<Box<dyn FormField>> = Vec::new();
        for col in &entry.meta.columns {
            if col.primary_key || col.kind == FieldKind::Auto {
                continue;
            }
            if col.kind == FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd {
                continue; // backend fills it
            }
            let optional = col.null || col.default.is_some();
            let f: Box<dyn FormField> = match &col.kind {
                FieldKind::Char => {
                    let mut cf = crate::forms::CharField::new(col.name.clone())
                        .with_label(col.name.clone());
                    if col.max_length > 0 {
                        cf = cf.max_length(col.max_length);
                    }
                    if !optional {
                        cf = cf.with_required(true);
                    } else {
                        cf = cf.optional();
                    }
                    Box::new(cf)
                }
                FieldKind::Text => {
                    let mut tf = crate::forms::TextField(col.name.clone());
                    tf = tf.with_label(col.name.clone());
                    if !optional {
                        tf = tf.with_required(true);
                    } else {
                        tf = tf.optional();
                    }
                    Box::new(tf)
                }
                FieldKind::Integer | FieldKind::ForeignKey { .. } => {
                    let mut inf = crate::forms::IntegerField::new(col.name.clone())
                        .label(col.name.clone());
                    if optional {
                        inf = inf.optional();
                    }
                    Box::new(inf)
                }
                FieldKind::Float => {
                    let mut ff = crate::forms::FloatField::new(col.name.clone())
                        .label(col.name.clone());
                    if optional {
                        ff = ff.optional();
                    }
                    Box::new(ff)
                }
                FieldKind::Bool => Box::new(crate::forms::BooleanField::new(col.name.clone())),
                FieldKind::DateTime => {
                    Box::new(AdminDateTimeField::new(col.name.clone(), optional))
                }
                _ => Box::new(crate::forms::HiddenField::new(col.name.clone())),
            };
            fields.push(f);
        }
        let form = Form::new(format!("admin-{}", entry.table), fields);
        match (posted, initial) {
            (Some(d), _) => form.bind(d),
            (None, Some(init)) => {
                let mut data = crate::http::QueryDict::new();
                for (k, v) in init {
                    data.set(k.clone(), v.clone());
                }
                form.bind(&data)
            }
            _ => form,
        }
    }

    fn row_initial_values(cols: &[crate::orm::ColumnDesc], row: &[Value]) -> HashMap<String, String> {
        let mut out = HashMap::new();
        for (c, v) in cols.iter().zip(row) {
            if c.primary_key || c.kind == FieldKind::Auto || c.kind == FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd {
                continue;
            }
            out.insert(c.name.clone(), v.display());
        }
        out
    }

    fn view_add_or_change(
        &self,
        req: &mut HttpRequest,
        pk: Option<i64>,
    ) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        if let Err(res) = self.require_staff(req) {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        let table = req.param("table").unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let entry = self
            .entry(&table)
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::NotFound(format!("model `{table}` not registered")))?
            .clone();
        let backend = req
            .backend
            .clone()
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::ServerError("no backend".into()))?;

        let is_post = req.method == crate::http::Method::POST;

        // Existing row (for change view prefill).
        let existing: Option<(Vec<Value>, HashMap<String, String>)> = match pk {
            Some(pk) => {
                let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(pk));
                let rows = backend
                    .select(&entry.table, &crit, &[], None, None)
                    .map_err(HttpError::from)?;
                rows.into_iter().next().map(|row| {
                    let init = Self::row_initial_values(&entry.meta.columns, &row);
                    (row, init)
                })
            }
            None => None,
        };

        if pk.is_some() && existing.is_none() {
            return Err(HttpError::NotFound(format!(
                "{} pk={}",
                entry.table,
                pk.unwrap_or(0)
            )));
        }

        let mut form = Self::build_form(
            &entry,
            if is_post { None } else { existing.as_ref().map(|(_, init)| init) },
            if is_post { Some(&req.post) } else { None },
        );

        if is_post && form.is_valid() {
            let mut values: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::new();
            for col in &entry.meta.columns {
                if col.primary_key || col.kind == FieldKind::Auto || col.kind == FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd {
                    continue;
                }
                let v = form.cleaned(&col.name).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                values.insert(col.name.clone(), v);
            }
            match pk {
                Some(pk) => {
                    update_row(&*backend, &entry.meta.columns, &entry.table, pk, &values)
                        .map_err(HttpError::from)?;
                    crate::messages::success(req, "Changed successfully.");
                    return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(self.url(&format!("{table}/"))));
                }
                None => {
                    let new_pk =
                        insert_row(&*backend, &entry.table, &entry.meta.columns, &values)
                            .map_err(HttpError::from)?;
                    crate::messages::success(req, "Added successfully.");
                    return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(
                        self.url(&format!("{table}/{new_pk}/change/")),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }

        let mut ctx = self.base_ctx(req);
        ctx.set("model_name", TplValue::Str(table.clone()));
        ctx.set("is_add", TplValue::Bool(pk.is_none()));
        if let Some(pk) = pk {
            ctx.set("pk", TplValue::Int(pk));
        }
        ctx.set("form_html", TplValue::Safe(form.as_table()));
        render(req, "admin/change_form.html", ctx)
    }

    fn view_delete(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest, pk: i64) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        if let Err(res) = self.require_staff(req) {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        let table = req.param("table").unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let entry = self
            .entry(&table)
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::NotFound(format!("model `{table}` not registered")))?;
        let backend = req
            .backend
            .clone()
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::ServerError("no backend".into()))?;

        if req.method == crate::http::Method::POST {
            let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(pk));
            let n = backend.delete(&entry.table, &crit).map_err(HttpError::from)?;
            crate::messages::success(req, format!("Deleted {n} item(s)."));
            return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(self.url(&format!("{table}/"))));
        }

        let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(pk));
        let rows = backend
            .select(&entry.table, &crit, &[], None, None)
            .map_err(HttpError::from)?;
        let row = rows
            .into_iter()
            .next()
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::NotFound(format!("{} pk={}", entry.table, pk)))?;
        let mut pairs: Vec<TplValue> = Vec::new();
        for (c, v) in entry.meta.columns.iter().zip(&row) {
            pairs.push(TplValue::List(vec![
                TplValue::Str(c.name.clone()),
                TplValue::Str(v.display()),
            ]));
        }
        let mut ctx = self.base_ctx(req);
        ctx.set("model_name", TplValue::Str(table));
        ctx.set("pk", TplValue::Int(pk));
        ctx.set("object_pairs", TplValue::List(pairs));
        render(req, "admin/delete_confirmation.html", ctx)
    }
}

fn display_pk(cols: &[crate::orm::ColumnDesc], row: &[Value]) -> String {
    cols.first()
        .zip(row.first())
        .map(|(_, v)| v.display())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

fn insert_row(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    table: &str,
    cols: &[crate::orm::ColumnDesc],
    values: &HashMap<String, Value>,
) -> crate::orm::OrmResult<i64> {
    let row: Vec<Value> = cols
        .iter()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.primary_key {
                Value::Null
            } else {
                values.get(&c.name).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
            }
        })
        .collect();
    backend.insert(table, row)
}

fn update_row(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    cols: &[crate::orm::ColumnDesc],
    table: &str,
    pk: i64,
    values: &HashMap<String, Value>,
) -> crate::orm::OrmResult<usize> {
    let mut updates = Vec::new();
    for (i, c) in cols.iter().enumerate() {
        if c.primary_key {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(v) = values.get(&c.name) {
            updates.push((i, v.clone()));
        }
    }
    let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(pk));
    backend.update(table, &crit, &updates)
}

/// DateTime form field: accepts `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS]` or ISO-8601.
pub struct AdminDateTimeField {
    name: String,
    optional: bool,
}

impl AdminDateTimeField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, optional: bool) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), optional }
    }
}

impl FormField for AdminDateTimeField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }
    fn label(&self) -> String {
        self.name.clone()
    }
    fn required(&self) -> bool {
        !self.optional
    }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, crate::forms::FieldErrors> {
        let raw = raw.map(|s| s.trim()).unwrap_or("");
        if raw.is_empty() {
            if self.required() {
                return Err(vec!["This field is required.".to_string()]);
            }
            return Ok(Value::Null);
        }
        for fmt in [
            "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
            "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M",
            "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S",
            "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M",
        ] {
            if let Ok(dt) = chrono::NaiveDateTime::parse_from_str(raw, fmt) {
                return Ok(Value::DateTime(dt.and_utc()));
            }
        }
        if let Ok(d) = chrono::NaiveDate::parse_from_str(raw, "%Y-%m-%d") {
            if let Some(dt) = d.and_hms_opt(0, 0, 0) {
                return Ok(Value::DateTime(dt.and_utc()));
            }
        }
        Err(vec!["Enter a valid date/time.".to_string()])
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, _error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let initial = bound.unwrap_or("");
        format!(
            "<input type=\"text\" name=\"{}\" id=\"id_{}\" value=\"{}\" class=\"form-control\" placeholder=\"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM\">",
            self.name,
            self.name,
            crate::templates::escape_html(initial)
        )
    }
}

/// Embedded admin template loader (compiled into the binary).
pub(crate) fn embedded_templates() -> crate::templates::InMemoryLoader {
    let mut l = crate::templates::InMemoryLoader::new();
    l.add("admin/base.html", include_str!("admin/templates/base.html"));
    l.add("admin/login.html", include_str!("admin/templates/login.html"));
    l.add("admin/index.html", include_str!("admin/templates/index.html"));
    l.add("admin/change_list.html", include_str!("admin/templates/change_list.html"));
    l.add("admin/change_form.html", include_str!("admin/templates/change_form.html"));
    l.add(
        "admin/delete_confirmation.html",
        include_str!("admin/templates/delete_confirmation.html"),
    );
    l
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::http::{AuthUser, Method};
    use crate::orm::{InMemoryBackend, ModelExt as _};
    use std::sync::Arc as StdArc;

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, crate::Model)]
    #[model(table = "adm_item")]
    pub struct Item {
        #[field(auto)]
        pub id: i64,
        #[field(char, max = 60)]
        pub name: String,
        #[field(int, default = 0)]
        pub quantity: i64,
    }

    fn site() -> AdminSite {
        let mut s = AdminSite::new("Rustango", "Rustango admin");
        s.register::<Item>(ModelAdmin {
            list_display: vec!["id".into(), "name".into(), "quantity".into()],
            search_fields: vec!["name".into()],
            ..Default::default()
        });
        s
    }

    fn req_with(method: Method, path: &str) -> (HttpRequest, StdArc<dyn Backend>) {
        let backend: StdArc<dyn Backend> = StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table(Item::table(), Item::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(method, path);
        req.backend = Some(backend.clone());
        (req, backend)
    }

    fn engine() -> crate::templates::Engine {
        crate::templates::Engine::new(vec![Box::new(embedded_templates())], true)
    }

    fn staff(mut req: HttpRequest) -> HttpRequest {
        req.user = AuthUser::Authenticated {
            id: 1,
            username: "root".into(),
            is_staff: true,
            is_superuser: true,
        };
        req
    }

    #[test]
    fn admin_routes_registered() {
        let s = site();
        let router = s.urls();
        assert_eq!(router.routes.len(), 7);
        // names get the admin: namespace only after Router::mount
        let mut root = crate::urls::Router::empty();
        root.mount("admin/", "admin", s.urls());
        assert!(root.routes.iter().any(|r| r.name.as_deref() == Some("admin:index")));
        assert!(root.routes.iter().any(|r| r.name.as_deref() == Some("admin:add")));
        assert!(root.routes.iter().any(|r| r.name.as_deref() == Some("admin:login")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn login_flow() {
        let s = site();
        let backend = StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table("auth_user", crate::auth::User::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        crate::auth::create_superuser(&*backend, "root", "", "pw").unwrap();

        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::POST, "/admin/login/");
        req.backend = Some(backend.clone());
        req.engine = Some(StdArc::new(engine()));
        req.session = Some(crate::sessions::Session::load(backend.clone(), None, 3600));
        req.post.set("username", "root");
        req.post.set("password", "pw");
        let res = s.view_login(&mut req).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
        assert_eq!(res.headers.get("Location"), Some("/admin/"));
        assert!(req.user.is_authenticated());
    }

    #[test]
    fn index_requires_staff() {
        let s = site();
        let (mut req, _b) = req_with(Method::GET, "/admin/");
        req.engine = Some(StdArc::new(engine()));
        let res = s.view_index(&mut req).unwrap();
        // anonymous -> redirect to login
        assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_add_change_delete_flow() {
        let s = site();
        // One shared backend for the whole flow.
        let backend: StdArc<dyn crate::orm::Backend> = StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table(Item::table(), Item::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let mk = |method: Method, path: &str| {
            let mut req = HttpRequest::new(method, path);
            req.backend = Some(backend.clone());
            req.engine = Some(StdArc::new(engine()));
            req
        };

        // seed rows
        for i in 0..30 {
            let item = Item { id: 0, name: format!("item {i}"), quantity: i as i64 };
            item.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        }

        let mut req = staff(mk(Method::GET, "/admin/adm_item/"));
        req.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        let res = s.view_list(&mut req).unwrap();
        let body = res.body_string();
        assert!(body.contains("item 29"));
        assert!(body.contains("30 items"));

        // add form renders
        let mut req_add = staff(mk(Method::GET, "/admin/adm_item/add/"));
        req_add.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        let res = s.view_add_or_change(&mut req_add, None).unwrap();
        assert!(res.body_string().contains("name=\"name\""));

        // POST add
        let mut req_post = staff(mk(Method::POST, "/admin/adm_item/add/"));
        req_post.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        req_post.post.set("name", "created");
        req_post.post.set("quantity", "5");
        let res = s.view_add_or_change(&mut req_post, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
        let count = backend.count("adm_item", &crate::orm::Criteria::any()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(count, 31);

        // change prefills
        let mut req_chg = staff(mk(Method::GET, "/admin/adm_item/31/change/"));
        req_chg.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        req_chg.params.insert("pk".into(), "31".into());
        let res = s.view_add_or_change(&mut req_chg, Some(31)).unwrap();
        assert!(res.body_string().contains("value=\"created\""));

        // POST change
        let mut req_chg2 = staff(mk(Method::POST, "/admin/adm_item/31/change/"));
        req_chg2.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        req_chg2.post.set("name", "edited");
        req_chg2.post.set("quantity", "9");
        let res = s.view_add_or_change(&mut req_chg2, Some(31)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
        let item = Item::get(&*backend, 31).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(item.name, "edited");
        assert_eq!(item.quantity, 9);

        // delete
        let mut req_del = staff(mk(Method::POST, "/admin/adm_item/31/delete/"));
        req_del.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        req_del.params.insert("pk".into(), "31".into());
        let res = s.view_delete(&mut req_del, 31).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
        assert_eq!(backend.count("adm_item", &crate::orm::Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 30);
    }

    #[test]
    fn search_filter_works() {
        let s = site();
        let (mut req, backend) = req_with(Method::GET, "/admin/adm_item/?q=needle");
        req.engine = Some(StdArc::new(engine()));
        let mut req = staff(req);
        req.params.insert("table".into(), "adm_item".into());
        req.query.set("q", "needle");
        Item { id: 0, name: "haystack".into(), quantity: 1 }.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        Item { id: 0, name: "the needle".into(), quantity: 2 }.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        let res = s.view_list(&mut req).unwrap();
        let body = res.body_string();
        assert!(body.contains("the needle"));
        assert!(!body.contains("haystack"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn datetime_field_parses() {
        let f = AdminDateTimeField::new("when", false);
        let v = f.clean(Some("2026-01-15 10:30")).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(v, Value::DateTime(_)));
        assert!(f.clean(Some("garbage")).is_err());
        let opt = AdminDateTimeField::new("when2", true);
        assert_eq!(opt.clean(None).unwrap(), Value::Null);
    }
}

//! Authentication — `django.contrib.auth`.
//!
//! Passwords use PBKDF2-SHA256 in Django's exact wire format
//! (`pbkdf2_sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<base64 hash>`), so hashes produced
//! here verify against Django-generated ones and vice versa. Sessions carry
//! the user id (`_auth_user_id`), rotated on login to prevent fixation.

use std::sync::Arc;

use base64::Engine as _;
use sha2::Sha256;

use crate::http::{AuthUser, HttpRequest, HttpResponse, SetCookie};
use crate::orm::{Backend, Model, ModelExt};

pub use crate::orm::model::User;

const AUTH_SESSION_KEY: &str = "_auth_user_id";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Password hashing (Django-compatible PBKDF2-SHA256)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `make_password("pw")` -> `pbkdf2_sha256$600000$<salt>$<hash>`.
pub fn make_password(password: &str) -> String {
    let cfg = &crate::settings::global().password_hasher;
    pbkdf2_encode(password, &random_salt(12), cfg.iterations, cfg.algorithm)
}

/// Same, with an explicit iteration count.
pub fn make_password_with_iterations(password: &str, iterations: u32) -> String {
    pbkdf2_encode(password, &random_salt(12), iterations, "pbkdf2_sha256")
}

/// Django-style alphanumeric salt (`get_random_string(12)` equivalent).
fn random_salt(len: usize) -> String {
    const ALPHA: &[u8] = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789";
    let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(len);
    while bytes.len() < len {
        bytes.extend_from_slice(uuid::Uuid::new_v4().as_bytes());
    }
    bytes[..len]
        .iter()
        .map(|b| ALPHA[(*b % ALPHA.len() as u8) as usize] as char)
        .collect()
}

/// Encode in Django's exact wire format: the digest is **base64**, not hex
/// (`django.contrib.auth.hashers.PBKDF2PasswordHasher.encode`).
fn pbkdf2_encode(password: &str, salt: &str, iterations: u32, algorithm: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    pbkdf2::pbkdf2_hmac::<Sha256>(password.as_bytes(), salt.as_bytes(), iterations, &mut out);
    let digest = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(out);
    format!("{algorithm}${iterations}${salt}${digest}")
}

/// `check_password("pw", stored)` — supports Django's
/// `pbkdf2_sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<b64hash>` hashes (base64 digest).
pub fn check_password(password: &str, encoded: &str) -> bool {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = encoded.split('$').collect();
    if parts.len() != 4 || parts[0] != "pbkdf2_sha256" {
        return false;
    }
    let iterations: u32 = match parts[1].parse() {
        Ok(i) => i,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    let salt = parts[2];
    let expected = parts[3];
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    pbkdf2::pbkdf2_hmac::<Sha256>(password.as_bytes(), salt.as_bytes(), iterations, &mut out);
    let computed = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(out);
    const_time_eq(computed.as_bytes(), expected.as_bytes())
}

fn const_time_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if a.len() != b.len() {
        return false;
    }
    let mut diff = 0u8;
    for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {
        diff |= x ^ y;
    }
    diff == 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Authenticate / login / logout
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `authenticate(username=..., password=...)` — verifies against the
/// `auth_user` table.
pub fn authenticate(backend: &dyn Backend, username: &str, password: &str) -> Option<User> {
    let crit = crate::orm::Criteria::eq("username", crate::orm::Value::Text(username.to_string()));
    let rows = backend.select("auth_user", &crit, &[], None, None).ok()?;
    let user = rows.first().map(|r| User::from_row(r))?;
    if !user.is_active {
        return None;
    }
    if check_password(password, &user.password) {
        Some(user)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Log a user in: rotate the session key (fixation defense) and store
/// `_auth_user_id` in the session.
pub fn login(req: &mut HttpRequest, user: &User) {
    let session = req.session.as_mut().expect("session middleware required for login");
    session.cycle_key();
    session.set(AUTH_SESSION_KEY, serde_json::json!(user.pk()));
    session.save();
    req.user = AuthUser::Authenticated {
        id: user.pk(),
        username: user.username.clone(),
        is_staff: user.is_staff,
        is_superuser: user.is_superuser,
    };
}

/// Log out: wipe the auth data and delete the session row.
pub fn logout(req: &mut HttpRequest) {
    if let Some(session) = req.session.as_mut() {
        session.remove(AUTH_SESSION_KEY);
        session.delete();
    }
    req.user = AuthUser::Anonymous;
}

/// Load the request user from the session (`AuthMiddleware` calls this).
pub fn get_user(req: &mut HttpRequest) {
    let Some(session) = req.session.as_ref() else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(user_id) = session.get_int(AUTH_SESSION_KEY) else {
        return;
    };
    let backend = req.backend.clone();
    if let Some(backend) = backend {
        if let Ok(user) = User::get(&*backend, user_id) {
            if user.is_active {
                req.user = AuthUser::Authenticated {
                    id: user.pk(),
                    username: user.username.clone(),
                    is_staff: user.is_staff,
                    is_superuser: user.is_superuser,
                };
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Attach a `sessionid` Set-Cookie when the session was persisted during
/// this request (created, rotated, or re-saved) — like Django, which only
/// sends the cookie when the session data actually changed.
pub fn apply_session_cookie(req: &HttpRequest, response: &mut HttpResponse, cookie_name: &str, max_age: i64) {
    if let Some(session) = req.session.as_ref() {
        if session.written {
            let cookie = SetCookie::new(cookie_name, session.key.clone())
                .max_age(max_age)
                .http_only()
                .same_site("Lax");
            response.set_cookie(cookie);
        }
    }
}

/// `LoginRequired` view wrapper — like `@login_required`.
pub fn login_required(view: crate::views::ViewFn, login_url: impl Into<String>) -> crate::views::ViewFn {
    let login_url: Arc<String> = Arc::new(login_url.into());
    Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| {
        if !req.user.is_authenticated() {
            let next = crate::http::urlencode(&req.full_path);
            return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(format!("{}/?next={}", login_url.trim_end_matches('/'), next)));
        }
        view(req)
    })
}

/// Staff-only wrapper — like `@staff_member_required`.
pub fn staff_required(view: crate::views::ViewFn, login_url: impl Into<String>) -> crate::views::ViewFn {
    let login_url: Arc<String> = Arc::new(login_url.into());
    Arc::new(move |req: &mut HttpRequest| {
        if !req.user.is_staff() && !req.user.is_superuser() {
            return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(login_url.trim_end_matches('/').to_string() + "/"));
        }
        view(req)
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// createsuperuser helper
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Create (or reset the password of) a superuser — the
/// `createsuperuser` management command's core.
pub fn create_superuser(backend: &dyn Backend, username: &str, email: &str, password: &str) -> crate::orm::OrmResult<User> {
    let existing = User::objects(backend)
        .filter(crate::orm::Criteria::eq(
            "username",
            crate::orm::Value::Text(username.to_string()),
        ))
        .first()?;
    let encoded = make_password(password);
    match existing {
        Some(mut u) => {
            u.password = encoded;
            u.email = email.to_string();
            u.is_staff = true;
            u.is_superuser = true;
            u.is_active = true;
            u.save(backend)
        }
        None => {
            let u = User {
                id: 0,
                username: username.to_string(),
                email: email.to_string(),
                password: encoded,
                first_name: String::new(),
                last_name: String::new(),
                is_staff: true,
                is_superuser: true,
                is_active: true,
                date_joined: chrono::Utc::now(),
                last_login: None,
            };
            u.save(backend)
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::orm::InMemoryBackend;
    use crate::sessions::Session;
    use std::sync::Arc;

    fn backend_with_user(password: &str) -> Arc<InMemoryBackend> {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table("auth_user", User::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let user = User {
            id: 0,
            username: "ada".into(),
            email: "ada@example.com".into(),
            password: make_password_with_iterations(password, 1000),
            first_name: "Ada".into(),
            last_name: "L".into(),
            is_staff: true,
            is_superuser: true,
            is_active: true,
            date_joined: chrono::Utc::now(),
            last_login: None,
        };
        user.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        backend
    }

    #[test]
    fn password_format_is_django_wire_format() {
        let encoded = make_password_with_iterations("hunter2", 600_000);
        let parts: Vec<&str> = encoded.split('$').collect();
        assert_eq!(parts[0], "pbkdf2_sha256");
        assert_eq!(parts[1], "600000");
        assert_eq!(parts[2].len(), 12); // Django-style alphanumeric salt
        assert!(parts[2].chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()));
        assert_eq!(parts[3].len(), 44); // base64(32-byte sha256) incl. padding
        assert!(parts[3].ends_with('='));
    }

    #[test]
    fn check_roundtrip() {
        let encoded = make_password("s3cret");
        assert!(check_password("s3cret", &encoded));
        assert!(!check_password("wrong", &encoded));
    }

    #[test]
    fn django_generated_hash_verification() {
        // Real Django wire format: produced by
        //   hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', b'rustango', b'cd3f9dfb48af6bb6', 1000)
        // + base64.b64encode — byte-identical to Django's
        //   make_password() output for these parameters.
        let django_hash =
            "pbkdf2_sha256$1000$cd3f9dfb48af6bb6$neYS372AH6ACJOHwTgouFTY3cyAeE49gvPo0H9szp2Q=";
        assert!(check_password("rustango", django_hash));
        assert!(!check_password("wrong", django_hash));

        // Our own encoder reproduces the same wire format.
        let ours = pbkdf2_encode("rustango", "cd3f9dfb48af6bb6", 1000, "pbkdf2_sha256");
        assert_eq!(ours, django_hash);
    }

    #[test]
    fn authenticate_success_and_failure() {
        let backend = backend_with_user("correct horse");
        assert!(authenticate(&*backend, "ada", "correct horse").is_some());
        assert!(authenticate(&*backend, "ada", "wrong").is_none());
        assert!(authenticate(&*backend, "nobody", "x").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn inactive_users_cannot_authenticate() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table("auth_user", User::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let user = User {
            id: 0,
            username: "bob".into(),
            email: String::new(),
            password: make_password_with_iterations("pw", 1000),
            first_name: String::new(),
            last_name: String::new(),
            is_staff: false,
            is_superuser: false,
            is_active: false,
            date_joined: chrono::Utc::now(),
            last_login: None,
        };
        user.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        assert!(authenticate(&*backend, "bob", "pw").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn login_logout_flow() {
        let backend = backend_with_user("pw");
        let user = authenticate(&*backend, "ada", "pw").unwrap();

        let mut req = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::POST, "/login/");
        req.backend = Some(backend.clone());
        req.session = Some(Session::load(backend.clone(), None, 3600));
        assert!(req.user.is_anonymous());

        login(&mut req, &user);
        assert!(req.user.is_authenticated());
        assert_eq!(req.user.username(), "ada");
        assert!(req.user.is_staff());

        // session persists across a "new request" with the same cookie
        let key = req.session.as_ref().unwrap().key.clone();
        let mut req2 = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/");
        req2.backend = Some(backend.clone());
        req2.session = Some(Session::load(backend.clone(), Some(&key), 3600));
        get_user(&mut req2);
        assert!(req2.user.is_authenticated());
        assert_eq!(req2.user.username(), "ada");

        logout(&mut req2);
        assert!(req2.user.is_anonymous());
    }

    #[test]
    fn login_required_wrapper() {
        let inner = crate::views::make_view(|_req| Ok(crate::http::HttpResponse::text("secret")));
        let guarded = login_required(inner, "/login/");
        let mut anon = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/profile/");
        let res = guarded(&mut anon).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
        assert!(res.headers.get("Location").unwrap().contains("/login/"));

        let mut authed = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/profile/");
        authed.user = AuthUser::Authenticated {
            id: 1,
            username: "ada".into(),
            is_staff: false,
            is_superuser: false,
        };
        let res = guarded(&mut authed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.status, 200);
        assert_eq!(res.body_string(), "secret");
    }

    #[test]
    fn create_superuser_upserts() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table("auth_user", User::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let u = create_superuser(&*backend, "root", "root@x.io", "pw").unwrap();
        assert!(u.is_superuser);
        // upsert path
        let u2 = create_superuser(&*backend, "root", "new@x.io", "pw2").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(u2.email, "new@x.io");
        assert_eq!(User::objects(&*backend).count().unwrap(), 1);
        assert!(check_password("pw2", &u2.password));
    }
}

//! The `rustango` command-line binary — a thin wrapper over
//! `rustango::management::run`.

use std::process::ExitCode;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let code = rustango::management::run(&args);
    ExitCode::from(code.clamp(0, 255) as u8)
}
