```rust
//! Cache framework — `django.core.cache` with a `LocMemCache` backend.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// Cache backend trait (only LocMem ships; the trait allows custom ones).
pub trait Cache: Send + Sync {
    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String>;
    fn set(&self, key: &str, value: String, timeout: Option<Duration>);
    fn add(&self, key: &str, value: String, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> bool;
    fn delete(&self, key: &str);
    fn clear(&self);
    fn touch(&self, key: &str, timeout: Duration) -> bool;
}

struct Entry {
    value: String,
    expires: Option<Instant>,
}

impl Entry {
    fn alive(&self) -> bool {
        match self.expires {
            Some(t) => Instant::now() < t,
            None => true,
        }
    }
}

/// `LocMemCache` — process-local, TTL-aware, evicts on access.
pub struct LocMemCache {
    inner: Mutex<HashMap<String, Entry>>,
    max_entries: usize,
}

impl LocMemCache {
    pub fn new(max_entries: usize) -> Self {
        Self { inner: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()), max_entries: max_entries.max(1) }
    }

    fn purge_expired(map: &mut HashMap<String, Entry>) {
        map.retain(|_, e| e.alive());
    }
}

impl Default for LocMemCache {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new(300)
    }
}

impl Cache for LocMemCache {
    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
        let mut map = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
        Self::purge_expired(&mut map);
        map.get(key).map(|e| e.value.clone())
    }

    fn set(&self, key: &str, value: String, timeout: Option<Duration>) {
        let mut map = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
        Self::purge_expired(&mut map);
        if map.len() >= self.max_entries && !map.contains_key(key) {
            // simple eviction: drop an arbitrary entry
            if let Some(k) = map.keys().next().cloned() {
                map.remove(&k);
            }
        }
        map.insert(
            key.to_string(),
            Entry { value, expires: timeout.map(|t| Instant::now() + t) },
        );
    }

    fn add(&self, key: &str, value: String, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> bool {
        let mut map = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
        Self::purge_expired(&mut map);
        if map.contains_key(key) {
            return false;
        }
        map.insert(
            key.to_string(),
            Entry { value, expires: timeout.map(|t| Instant::now() + t) },
        );
        true
    }

    fn delete(&self, key: &str) {
        self.inner.lock().unwrap().remove(key);
    }

    fn clear(&self) {
        self.inner.lock().unwrap().clear();
    }

    fn touch(&self, key: &str, timeout: Duration) -> bool {
        let mut map = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
        Self::purge_expired(&mut map);
        match map.get_mut(key) {
            Some(e) => {
                e.expires = Some(Instant::now() + timeout);
                true
            }
            None => false,
        }
    }
}

/// The default cache from settings (`cache_backend: locmem`).
pub fn default_cache() -> Arc<dyn Cache> {
    match crate::settings::global().cache_backend.as_str() {
        "locmem" | "" => Arc::new(LocMemCache::default()),
        other => {
            // Unknown alias falls back to locmem (documented behavior).
            let _ = other;
            Arc::new(LocMemCache::default())
        }
    }
}

/// `@cache_page(seconds)` — wraps a view with page caching.
pub fn cache_page(
    seconds: u64,
    view: crate::views::ViewFn,
) -> crate::views::ViewFn {
    let cache = Arc::new(LocMemCache::default());
    std::sync::Arc::new(move |req: &mut crate::http::HttpRequest| {
        if !req.method.is_safe() {
            return view(req);
        }
        let key = format!("cache_page:{}:{}", req.full_path, req.user.username());
        if let Some(hit) = cache.get(&key) {
            return Ok(http_response_from_bytes(hit));
        }
        let res = view(req)?;
        // Pages containing a rendered CSRF token are per-session: serving a
        // cached token to other visitors makes every later form POST fail
        // with a mismatch. Never cache those.
        if res
            .body_string()
            .contains("name=\"csrfmiddlewaretoken\"")
        {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        cache.set(&key, http_response_to_bytes(&res), Some(Duration::from_secs(seconds)));
        Ok(res)
    })
}

/// A cached page snapshot: status, content type, redirect target and body.
/// Caching the body alone replayed 302/404 responses as empty 200s.
#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct CachedPage {
    status: u16,
    content_type: String,
    location: Option<String>,
    body: String,
}

fn http_response_to_bytes(res: &crate::http::HttpResponse) -> String {
    let snap = CachedPage {
        status: res.status,
        content_type: res.headers.get("Content-Type").unwrap_or("text/html; charset=utf-8").to_string(),
        location: res.headers.get("Location").map(|s| s.to_string()),
        body: res.body_string(),
    };
    serde_json::to_string(&snap).unwrap_or_default()
}

fn http_response_from_bytes(data: String) -> crate::http::HttpResponse {
    let snap: CachedPage = match serde_json::from_str(&data) {
        Ok(s) => s,
        Err(_) => {
            // Defensive: unparseable cache entries fall back to a plain page.
            return crate::http::HttpResponse::html(data);
        }
    };
    let mut res = crate::http::HttpResponse::with_body(snap.status, &snap.content_type, snap.body);
    if let Some(loc) = snap.location {
        res.headers.set("Location", loc);
    }
    res
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::thread::sleep;

    #[test]
    fn set_get_delete() {
        let c = LocMemCache::default();
        c.set("k", "v".into(), None);
        assert_eq!(c.get("k"), Some("v".into()));
        c.delete("k");
        assert_eq!(c.get("k"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ttl_expiry() {
        let c = LocMemCache::default();
        c.set("short", "x".into(), Some(Duration::from_millis(20)));
        assert_eq!(c.get("short"), Some("x".into()));
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(40));
        assert_eq!(c.get("short"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn add_is_atomic_setifabsent() {
        let c = LocMemCache::default();
        assert!(c.add("lock", "1".into(), None));
        assert!(!c.add("lock", "2".into(), None));
        assert_eq!(c.get("lock"), Some("1".into()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn touch_extends() {
        let c = LocMemCache::default();
        c.set("t", "v".into(), Some(Duration::from_millis(30)));
        assert!(c.touch("t", Duration::from_secs(60)));
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
        assert_eq!(c.get("t"), Some("v".into()));
        assert!(!c.touch("missing", Duration::from_secs(1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn eviction_and_clear() {
        let c = LocMemCache::new(2);
        c.set("a", "1".into(), None);
        c.set("b", "2".into(), None);
        c.set("c", "3".into(), None);
        let count = ["a", "b", "c"].iter().filter(|k| c.get(k).is_some()).count();
        assert!(count <= 3);
        c.clear();
        assert_eq!(c.get("a"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cache_page_wrapper() {
        let counter = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let c2 = counter.clone();
        let view: crate::views::ViewFn = Arc::new(move |_req| {
            c2.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
            Ok(crate::http::HttpResponse::text("generated"))
        });
        let cached = cache_page(60, view);
        let mut req = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/p/");
        let r1 = cached(&mut req).unwrap();
        let r2 = cached(&mut req).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r1.body_string(), "generated");
        assert_eq!(r2.body_string(), "generated");
        assert_eq!(counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cache_page_replays_status_faithfully() {
        // Regression: cached 404/302 responses were reconstructed as
        // status-200 HTML pages.
        let counter = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let c2 = counter.clone();
        let view: crate::views::ViewFn = Arc::new(move |_req| {
            c2.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
            let mut res = crate::http::HttpResponse::with_body(404, "text/html; charset=utf-8", "nope");
            res.headers.set("Location", "/elsewhere/");
            Ok(res)
        });
        let cached = cache_page(60, view);
        let mut req = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/missing/");
        let r1 = cached(&mut req).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r1.status, 404);
        let r2 = cached(&mut req).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r2.status, 404, "cached response must keep the status code");
        assert_eq!(r2.body_string(), "nope");
        assert_eq!(r2.headers.get("Location"), Some("/elsewhere/"));
        assert_eq!(counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cache_page_skips_csrf_pages() {
        // Regression: pages containing a rendered `{% csrf_token %}` were
        // cached — later visitors got a foreign token and every form POST
        // failed with a mismatch.
        let counter = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let c2 = counter.clone();
        let view: crate::views::ViewFn = Arc::new(move |_req| {
            c2.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
            Ok(crate::http::HttpResponse::html(
                "<form><input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrfmiddlewaretoken\" value=\"abc\"></form>",
            ))
        });
        let cached = cache_page(60, view);
        let mut req = crate::http::HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/form/");
        cached(&mut req).unwrap();
        cached(&mut req).unwrap();
        // Not cached: the view ran for every request.
        assert_eq!(counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst), 2);
    }
}

````rust
//! `contrib.ai` — LLM/agent support for rustango apps.
//!
//! An OpenAI-compatible chat client (works with OpenAI, Anthropic-style
//! gateways, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio — anything exposing
//! `POST {base}/chat/completions`) plus an agent loop with Rust tool
//! calling. The HTTP client is `ureq` + rustls(`ring`) — 100% Rust, no C.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use rustango::contrib::ai::{AiClient, Agent, Tool};
//!
//! let client = AiClient::from_settings();
//! // single completion
//! let reply = client.chat_simple("Summarize Django in one sentence.")?;
//!
//! // agent loop with tools
//! let agent = Agent::new(client)
//!     .system("You are a helpful admin assistant.")
//!     .tool(Tool::new("count_users", "Count users in the DB", |args| {
//!         Ok(serde_json::json!({ "count": 42 }))
//!     }));
//! let answer = agent.run("How many users do we have?")?;
//! ```
//!
//! Enable with `features = ["ai"]` in your Cargo.toml.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// Chat message roles.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Role {
    System,
    User,
    Assistant,
    Tool,
}

/// One chat message.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChatMessage {
    pub role: Role,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub content: Option<String>,
    /// OpenAI-compatible tool call requests (assistant messages).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub tool_calls: Option<Vec<ToolCall>>,
    /// Tool results (role = tool).
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub tool_call_id: Option<String>,
}

impl ChatMessage {
    pub fn system(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { role: Role::System, content: Some(text.into()), tool_calls: None, tool_call_id: None }
    }
    pub fn user(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { role: Role::User, content: Some(text.into()), tool_calls: None, tool_call_id: None }
    }
    pub fn assistant(text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { role: Role::Assistant, content: Some(text.into()), tool_calls: None, tool_call_id: None }
    }
    pub fn tool_result(call_id: impl Into<String>, text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            role: Role::Tool,
            content: Some(text.into()),
            tool_calls: None,
            tool_call_id: Some(call_id.into()),
        }
    }
}

/// A tool call requested by the model.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolCall {
    pub id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub kind: String,
    pub function: ToolCallFn,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolCallFn {
    pub name: String,
    /// JSON-encoded arguments object.
    pub arguments: String,
}

/// Tool definition sent to the model (JSON-schema subset).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ToolSpec {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub kind: String,
    pub function: ToolSpecFn,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ToolSpecFn {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub parameters: serde_json::Value,
}

/// The Rust side of a tool call: takes JSON args, returns JSON (or an error).
pub type ToolHandler = dyn Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> + Send + Sync;

/// A callable tool with its spec — the Rust side of function calling.
pub struct Tool {
    pub spec: ToolSpec,
    handler: Arc<ToolHandler>,
}

impl Tool {
    pub fn new<F>(
        name: impl Into<String>,
        description: impl Into<String>,
        parameters: serde_json::Value,
        handler: F,
    ) -> Self
    where
        F: Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> + Send + Sync + 'static,
    {
        Tool {
            spec: ToolSpec {
                kind: "function".into(),
                function: ToolSpecFn {
                    name: name.into(),
                    description: description.into(),
                    parameters,
                },
            },
            handler: Arc::new(handler),
        }
    }

    /// Tool without a JSON schema (parameters default to a free object).
    pub fn simple<F>(name: impl Into<String>, description: impl Into<String>, handler: F) -> Self
    where
        F: Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> + Send + Sync + 'static,
    {
        Self::new(
            name,
            description,
            serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {},
                "additionalProperties": true
            }),
            handler,
        )
    }

    pub fn invoke(&self, args: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
        (self.handler)(args)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Client
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// OpenAI-compatible chat-completions client (blocking, rustls TLS).
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct AiClient {
    pub base_url: String,
    pub api_key: String,
    pub model: String,
    pub timeout_secs: u64,
}

impl AiClient {
    /// Build from global settings (`ai_api_url`, `ai_api_key`, `ai_model`).
    pub fn from_settings() -> Self {
        let s = crate::settings::global();
        Self {
            base_url: s.ai_api_url.clone(),
            api_key: s.ai_api_key.clone(),
            model: s.ai_model.clone(),
            timeout_secs: 120,
        }
    }

    pub fn new(base_url: impl Into<String>, api_key: impl Into<String>, model: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            base_url: base_url.into(),
            api_key: api_key.into(),
            model: model.into(),
            timeout_secs: 120,
        }
    }

    fn endpoint(&self) -> String {
        let base = self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/');
        format!("{base}/chat/completions")
    }

    /// Full chat completion: send messages (+ optional tools), get the
    /// assistant's reply message.
    pub fn chat(
        &self,
        messages: &[ChatMessage],
        tools: Option<&[Tool]>,
    ) -> Result<ChatMessage, AiError> {
        #[derive(Serialize)]
        struct Body<'a> {
            model: &'a str,
            messages: &'a [ChatMessage],
            #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
            tools: Option<Vec<ToolSpec>>,
        }

        let body = Body {
            model: &self.model,
            messages,
            tools: tools.map(|ts| ts.iter().map(|t| t.spec.clone()).collect()),
        };

        let agent: ureq::Agent = ureq::Agent::config_builder()
            .timeout_global(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs)))
            .build()
            .into();
        let mut req = agent
            .post(self.endpoint())
            .header("Authorization", &format!("Bearer {}", self.api_key));
        let json_body = serde_json::to_string(&body)
            .map_err(|e| AiError::Encoding(e.to_string()))?;
        req = req.header("Content-Type", "application/json");
        let mut res = req
            .send(json_body.as_bytes())
            .map_err(|e| AiError::Http(format!("{e}")))?;
        let text = res
            .body_mut()
            .read_to_string()
            .map_err(|e| AiError::Http(format!("read: {e}")))?;

        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        struct Choices {
            message: ChatMessage,
        }
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        struct ApiResponse {
            choices: Vec<Choices>,
        }
        let parsed: ApiResponse = serde_json::from_str(&text)
            .map_err(|e| AiError::Decoding(format!("{e}; body: {}", truncate(&text, 300))))?;
        parsed
            .choices
            .into_iter()
            .next()
            .map(|c| c.message)
            .ok_or_else(|| AiError::Decoding("no choices in response".into()))
    }

    /// Convenience: one user message, return the text content.
    pub fn chat_simple(&self, prompt: &str) -> Result<String, AiError> {
        let reply = self.chat(&[ChatMessage::user(prompt)], None)?;
        Ok(reply.content.unwrap_or_default())
    }
}

fn truncate(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    if s.len() > n {
        // Cut at a CHAR boundary: this runs on provider error bodies, and
        // slicing a multi-byte UTF-8 char in half at byte n panicked the
        // request exactly when a remote server sent non-ASCII text.
        let cut = s
            .char_indices()
            .nth(n)
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .unwrap_or(s.len());
        format!("{}...", &s[..cut])
    } else {
        s.to_string()
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum AiError {
    #[error("http error: {0}")]
    Http(String),
    #[error("encoding error: {0}")]
    Encoding(String),
    #[error("response decode error: {0}")]
    Decoding(String),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Agent loop
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A tool-calling agent: loop `chat -> tool calls -> results` until the
/// model answers with plain text or `max_steps` is reached.
pub struct Agent {
    client: AiClient,
    system: Option<String>,
    tools: Vec<Tool>,
    max_steps: usize,
}

impl Agent {
    pub fn new(client: AiClient) -> Self {
        Self { client, system: None, tools: Vec::new(), max_steps: 8 }
    }

    pub fn system(mut self, prompt: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.system = Some(prompt.into());
        self
    }

    pub fn tool(mut self, tool: Tool) -> Self {
        self.tools.push(tool);
        self
    }

    pub fn max_steps(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
        self.max_steps = n.max(1);
        self
    }

    /// Run the agent loop for one user prompt; returns the final text.
    pub fn run(&self, prompt: &str) -> Result<String, AiError> {
        let mut history: Vec<ChatMessage> = Vec::new();
        if let Some(sys) = &self.system {
            history.push(ChatMessage::system(sys.clone()));
        }
        history.push(ChatMessage::user(prompt));

        for _ in 0..self.max_steps {
            let reply = self.client.chat(&history, Some(&self.tools))?;

            if let Some(calls) = &reply.tool_calls {
                if !calls.is_empty() {
                    history.push(ChatMessage {
                        role: Role::Assistant,
                        content: reply.content.clone(),
                        tool_calls: Some(calls.clone()),
                        tool_call_id: None,
                    });
                    for call in calls {
                        let result = match self.tools.iter().find(|t| t.spec.function.name == call.function.name) {
                            Some(tool) => {
                                let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&call.function.arguments)
                                    .unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({}));
                                match tool.invoke(&parsed) {
                                    Ok(v) => serde_json::to_string(&v)
                                        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "null".into()),
                                    Err(e) => format!("tool error: {e}"),
                                }
                            }
                            None => format!("unknown tool: {}", call.function.name),
                        };
                        history.push(ChatMessage::tool_result(&call.id, result));
                    }
                    continue;
                }
            }

            return Ok(reply.content.unwrap_or_default());
        }
        Err(AiError::Decoding("agent exceeded max_steps".into()))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::{Read, Write};
    use std::net::TcpListener;

    /// Spawn a tiny mock OpenAI-compatible server on a random port:
    /// first call returns a tool call, second call returns plain text.
    fn mock_server(script: Vec<String>) -> (String, std::thread::JoinHandle<()>) {
        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for want in script {
                let (mut stream, _) = listener.accept().unwrap();
                // Read until the end of request headers+body (or short read).
                let mut buf = Vec::new();
                let mut chunk = [0u8; 8192];
                loop {
                    match stream.read(&mut chunk) {
                        Ok(0) => break,
                        Ok(n) => {
                            buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
                            // stop once we've seen headers and (if declared)
                            // enough body bytes
                            let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);
                            if let Some(pos) = text.find("\r\n\r\n") {
                                let declared = text
                                    .to_lowercase()
                                    .split("content-length:")
                                    .nth(1)
                                    .and_then(|v| {
                                        v.trim()
                                            .split(|c: char| c == '\r' || !c.is_ascii_digit())
                                            .next()
                                            .and_then(|x| x.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())
                                    })
                                    .unwrap_or(0);
                                let body_read = buf.len() - (pos + 4);
                                if body_read >= declared || declared == 0 {
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        Err(_) => break,
                    }
                }
                let body = format!(
                    "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{}",
                    want.len(),
                    want
                );
                stream.write_all(body.as_bytes()).unwrap();
                let _ = stream.flush();
                let _ = stream.shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Both);
            }
        });
        (format!("http://{addr}"), handle)
    }

    fn json_response(v: serde_json::Value) -> String {
        serde_json::json!({ "choices": [ { "message": v } ] }).to_string()
    }

    #[test]
    fn chat_simple_against_mock() {
        let (url, handle) = mock_server(vec![json_response(serde_json::json!({
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": "Hello from the mock!"
        }))]);
        let client = AiClient::new(url, "test-key", "mock-model");
        let reply = client.chat_simple("hi").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reply, "Hello from the mock!");
        handle.join().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn agent_tool_loop() {
        let tool_call = serde_json::json!({
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": null,
            "tool_calls": [ {
                "id": "call_1",
                "type": "function",
                "function": {
                    "name": "get_count",
                    "arguments": "{\"table\": \"users\"}"
                }
            } ]
        });
        let (url, handle) = mock_server(vec![
            json_response(tool_call),
            json_response(serde_json::json!({
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": "There are 42 users."
            })),
        ]);
        let client = AiClient::new(url, "k", "m");
        let agent = Agent::new(client)
            .system("You are a data assistant.")
            .tool(Tool::simple("get_count", "Count rows in a table", |args| {
                let table = args.get("table").and_then(|t| t.as_str()).unwrap_or("?").to_string();
                Ok(serde_json::json!({ "table": table, "count": 42 }))
            }));
        let answer = agent.run("how many users?").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(answer, "There are 42 users.");
        handle.join().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_tool_reports_error() {
        let tool_call = serde_json::json!({
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": null,
            "tool_calls": [ {
                "id": "call_x",
                "type": "function",
                "function": { "name": "does_not_exist", "arguments": "{}" }
            } ]
        });
        let (url, handle) = mock_server(vec![
            json_response(tool_call),
            json_response(serde_json::json!({
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": "Sorry, that tool is missing."
            })),
        ]);
        let client = AiClient::new(url, "k", "m");
        let agent = Agent::new(client);
        let answer = agent.run("boom").unwrap();
        assert!(answer.contains("missing"));
        handle.join().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn message_serde_roundtrip() {
        let m = ChatMessage::user("hello");
        let j = serde_json::to_string(&m).unwrap();
        assert!(j.contains("\"role\":\"user\""));
        let tr = ChatMessage::tool_result("id1", "result text");
        let jt = serde_json::to_string(&tr).unwrap();
        assert!(jt.contains("\"tool_call_id\":\"id1\""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn max_steps_guard() {
        let tool_call = serde_json::json!({
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": null,
            "tool_calls": [ {
                "id": "c",
                "type": "function",
                "function": { "name": "noop", "arguments": "{}" }
            } ]
        });
        let (url, handle) = mock_server(vec![json_response(tool_call); 3]);
        let mut client = AiClient::new(url, "k", "m");
        client.timeout_secs = 10;
        let agent = Agent::new(client)
            .tool(Tool::simple("noop", "no-op", |_| Ok(serde_json::json!("ok"))))
            .max_steps(3);
        assert!(agent.run("loop forever").is_err());
        handle.join().unwrap();
    }

````rust
//! CSRF protection — `django.middleware.csrf`.
//!
//! Django's double-submit pattern: a random `csrftoken` cookie is paired
//! with a hidden form field (`csrfmiddlewaretoken`) or an `X-CSRFToken`
//! header. Unsafe methods (POST/PUT/DELETE) must present a matching token.
//! Routes can opt out with `Route::csrf_exempt()` (like `@csrf_exempt`).

use crate::http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse, SetCookie};

/// Request flag set by the router when the matched route is exempt.
pub(crate) const EXEMPT_FLAG: &str = "__csrf_exempt";

/// Generate a fresh CSRF token (64 hex chars, like Django's 32 bytes).
pub fn new_token() -> String {
    format!(
        "{}{}",
        uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple(),
        uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple()
    )
    [..64]
    .to_string()
}

/// Session-data key holding the per-session CSRF secret (128-bit random hex,
/// generated on first use and persisted with the session; never sent raw to
/// the client).
const SECRET_KEY: &str = "_csrf_secret";
/// Request-params key holding this request's CSRF secret when no session
/// exists (a fresh ephemeral secret, kept server-side in the request).
const SECRET_FLAG: &str = "__csrf_secret";

/// The server-side secret this request's tokens are derived from.
fn request_secret(req: &mut HttpRequest) -> String {
    if let Some(session) = req.session.as_mut() {
        if session.get(SECRET_KEY).and_then(|v| v.as_str()).is_none() {
            session.set(
                SECRET_KEY,
                serde_json::Value::String(uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string()),
            );
        }
        if let Some(secret) = session.get(SECRET_KEY).and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
            return secret.to_string();
        }
    }
    if let Some(secret) = req.params.get(SECRET_FLAG) {
        return secret.clone();
    }
    let secret = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string();
    req.params.insert(SECRET_FLAG.into(), secret.clone());
    secret
}

/// Expected CSRF token: `sha256(secret || session_key)` hex. It depends on a
/// server-side secret rather than being equal to any stored or sent value,
/// so a cookie-injection primitive alone cannot mint a valid token.
pub fn derive_token(secret: &str, session_key: &str) -> String {
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(secret.as_bytes());
    hasher.update(session_key.as_bytes());
    let digest = hasher.finalize();
    digest.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// Ensure the CSRF secret exists and expose the derived token to the
/// view/template.
pub fn process_request(req: &mut HttpRequest, cookie_name: &str) {
    let secret = request_secret(req);
    let session_key = req
        .session
        .as_ref()
        .map(|s| s.key.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let _ = cookie_name;
    req.csrf_token = Some(derive_token(&secret, &session_key));
}

/// Verify unsafe requests; returns an error message when rejected.
pub fn process_view(req: &HttpRequest) -> Result<(), String> {
    if req.method.is_safe() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    // Route-level exemption (`Route::csrf_exempt()`), set by the dispatcher.
    if req.params.get(EXEMPT_FLAG).map(|v| v == "1").unwrap_or(false) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    // The expected token is DERIVED from the server-side secret — never read
    // back from the cookie (the old pure double-submit scheme made the
    // cookie the trust anchor, so any cookie-injection primitive bypassed
    // it).
    let secret = req.params.get(SECRET_FLAG).cloned().or_else(|| {
        req.session
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|s| s.get(SECRET_KEY))
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))
    });
    let session_key = req
        .session
        .as_ref()
        .map(|s| s.key.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let expected = match secret {
        Some(secret) => derive_token(&secret, &session_key),
        None => return Err("CSRF cookie not set.".into()),
    };
    let presented = req
        .post
        .get("csrfmiddlewaretoken")
        .map(|s| s.to_string())
        .or_else(|| {
            req.headers
                .get("x-csrftoken")
                .map(|s| s.to_string())
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    if presented.is_empty() {
        return Err("CSRF token missing.".into());
    }
    if !tokens_match(&expected, &presented) {
        return Err("CSRF token has incorrect value.".into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn tokens_match(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
    // Django allows the token with rotated secret prefixes; for our
    // server-side scheme an exact match suffices.
    a.len() == b.len()
        && a.bytes()
            .zip(b.bytes())
            .fold(0u8, |acc, (x, y)| acc | (x ^ y))
            == 0
}

/// Middleware instance for the stack.
pub struct CsrfMiddleware {
    pub cookie_name: String,
}

impl crate::middleware::Middleware for CsrfMiddleware {
    fn process_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> crate::middleware::Next {
        process_request(req, &self.cookie_name);
        crate::middleware::Next::Continue
    }

    fn process_view(&self, req: &HttpRequest) -> Result<(), crate::errors::HttpError> {
        match process_view(req) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(reason) => Err(crate::errors::HttpError::CsrfFailure(reason)),
        }
    }

    fn process_response(
        &self,
        req: &mut HttpRequest,
        res: &mut HttpResponse,
    ) {
        let token = req.csrf_token.clone();
        if let Some(token) = token {
            let present = res.cookies.iter().any(|c| c.name == self.cookie_name);
            if !present {
                res.set_cookie(
                    SetCookie::new(self.cookie_name.clone(), token.clone())
                        .same_site("Lax"),
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Mark a route as exempt from CSRF verification — `@csrf_exempt`.
///
/// ```ignore
/// use rustango::urls::path;
///
/// let route = csrf_exempt(path("webhook/", receiver_view));
/// ```
pub fn csrf_exempt(route: crate::urls::Route) -> crate::urls::Route {
    route.csrf_exempt()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::http::Method;
    use crate::middleware::Middleware as _;

    #[test]
    fn token_format() {
        let t = new_token();
        assert_eq!(t.len(), 64);
        assert!(t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn safe_methods_pass() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        process_request(&mut req, "csrftoken");
        assert!(process_view(&req).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn unsafe_without_token_rejected() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::POST, "/");
        process_request(&mut req, "csrftoken");
        let mut data = crate::http::QueryDict::new();
        data.set("x", "1");
        req.post = data;
        assert!(process_view(&req).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn form_token_matches() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::POST, "/");
        process_request(&mut req, "csrftoken");
        let token = req.csrf_token.clone().unwrap();
        let mut data = crate::http::QueryDict::new();
        data.set("csrfmiddlewaretoken", token);
        req.post = data;
        assert!(process_view(&req).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn header_token_matches() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::POST, "/");
        process_request(&mut req, "csrftoken");
        let token = req.csrf_token.clone().unwrap();
        req.headers.set("X-CSRFToken", token);
        assert!(process_view(&req).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn wrong_token_rejected() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::POST, "/");
        process_request(&mut req, "csrftoken");
        let mut data = crate::http::QueryDict::new();
        data.set("csrfmiddlewaretoken", "forged");
        req.post = data;
        assert!(process_view(&req).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn exempt_route_is_skipped() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::POST, "/webhook/");
        process_request(&mut req, "csrftoken");
        req.params.insert(EXEMPT_FLAG.into(), "1".into());
        assert!(process_view(&req).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn middleware_sets_cookie_on_response() {
        let mw = CsrfMiddleware { cookie_name: "csrftoken".into() };
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        mw.process_request(&mut req);
        let mut res = HttpResponse::text("ok");
        mw.process_response(&mut req, &mut res);
        assert_eq!(res.cookie_value("csrftoken"), req.csrf_token);
    }
}

```rust
//! Error types: HTTP exceptions (`HttpError`), ORM errors
//! (`DoesNotExist`, `MultipleObjectsReturned`) and the general framework
//! error, mirroring `django.http.Http404`, `django.core.exceptions`, etc.

use thiserror::Error;

/// An error raised inside a view — the equivalent of raising
/// `Http404`, `PermissionDenied` or `SuspiciousOperation` in Django.
#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone)]
pub enum HttpError {
    #[error("not found: {0}")]
    NotFound(String),
    #[error("permission denied: {0}")]
    PermissionDenied(String),
    #[error("bad request: {0}")]
    BadRequest(String),
    #[error("method not allowed: {0}")]
    MethodNotAllowed(String),
    #[error("csrf verification failed: {0}")]
    CsrfFailure(String),
    #[error("server error: {0}")]
    ServerError(String),
}

impl HttpError {
    pub fn status(&self) -> u16 {
        match self {
            HttpError::NotFound(_) => 404,
            HttpError::PermissionDenied(_) => 403,
            HttpError::BadRequest(_) => 400,
            HttpError::MethodNotAllowed(_) => 405,
            HttpError::CsrfFailure(_) => 403,
            HttpError::ServerError(_) => 500,
        }
    }
}

impl From<std::io::Error> for OrmError {
    fn from(e: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        OrmError::Backend(format!("io error: {e}"))
    }
}

impl From<serde_json::Error> for OrmError {
    fn from(e: serde_json::Error) -> Self {
        OrmError::Backend(format!("json error: {e}"))
    }
}

impl From<crate::orm::OrmError> for HttpError {
    fn from(e: crate::orm::OrmError) -> Self {
        match e {
            crate::orm::OrmError::DoesNotExist(_) => HttpError::NotFound(e.to_string()),
            crate::orm::OrmError::MultipleObjectsReturned(_) => HttpError::BadRequest(e.to_string()),
            crate::orm::OrmError::PermissionDenied(_) => HttpError::PermissionDenied(e.to_string()),
            other => HttpError::ServerError(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
}

impl From<std::io::Error> for HttpError {
    fn from(e: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        HttpError::ServerError(format!("io error: {e}"))
    }
}

/// ORM-level errors, mirroring `django.db` exception hierarchy.
#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum OrmError {
    #[error("query returned no results for {0}")]
    DoesNotExist(String),
    #[error("query returned multiple results for {0}")]
    MultipleObjectsReturned(String),
    #[error("permission denied: {0}")]
    PermissionDenied(String),
    #[error("invalid value for field `{0}`: {1}")]
    InvalidValue(String, String),
    #[error("unknown field `{0}`")]
    UnknownField(String),
    #[error("migration error: {0}")]
    Migration(String),
    #[error("backend error: {0}")]
    Backend(String),
}

/// Anything the framework can produce at runtime.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum RustangoError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Http(#[from] HttpError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Orm(#[from] crate::orm::OrmError),
    #[error("template error: {0}")]
    Template(String),
    #[error("form error: {0}")]
    Form(String),
    #[error("io error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("json error: {0}")]
    Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),
    #[error("{0}")]
    Other(String),
}

pub type Result<T, E = RustangoError> = std::result::Result<T, E>;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn statuses() {
        assert_eq!(HttpError::NotFound("x".into()).status(), 404);
        assert_eq!(HttpError::CsrfFailure("bad token".into()).status(), 403);
        assert_eq!(HttpError::MethodNotAllowed("POST only".into()).status(), 405);
    }

    #[test]
    fn orm_to_http_conversion() {
        let e: HttpError = OrmError::DoesNotExist("polls".into()).into();
        assert_eq!(e.status(), 404);
        let e: HttpError = OrmError::Backend("disk full".into()).into();
        assert_eq!(e.status(), 500);
    }
}

## `crates/server/rustango/src/forms.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/src/forms.rs)

````rust
//! Forms — `django.forms`: field definitions, validation, `cleaned_data`,
//! errors and widget rendering.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use rustango::forms::{Form, CharField, EmailField, IntegerField};
//!
//! let form = Form::new("contact", vec![
//!     Box::new(CharField::new("name").max_length(100).required()),
//!     Box::new(EmailField::new("email")),
//!     Box::new(IntegerField::new("age").min_value(0).max_value(150)),
//! ]);
//!
//! let bound = form.bind(&req.post);
//! if bound.is_valid() {
//!     let name = bound.cleaned("name");
//! }
//! ```

use std::collections::HashMap;

use crate::http::QueryDict;
use crate::orm::Value;

/// Validation error messages for one field.
pub type FieldErrors = Vec<String>;

/// A form field: validation + widget rendering.
pub trait Field: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn label(&self) -> String;
    fn required(&self) -> bool { true }
    /// Validate raw input; returns the cleaned value or error messages.
    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors>;
    /// Render the widget for unbound or bound display.
    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String;
    /// Render a full row: label + widget + errors (as_p style).
    fn render_row(&self, bound: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let label = format!(
            "<label for=\"id_{}\">{}{}</label>",
            self.name(),
            self.label(),
            if self.required() { " <span class=\"required\">*</span>" } else { "" }
        );
        let widget = self.render(bound, None);
        format!("<p>{} {}</p>", label, widget)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Shared builder state
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
struct CommonOpts {
    required: bool,
    label: Option<String>,
    initial: Option<String>,
    help_text: Option<String>,
    widget_attrs: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl CommonOpts {
    fn label_of(&self, name: &str) -> String {
        self.label
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
                let mut s = name.replace('_', " ");
                if let Some(first) = s.chars().next() {
                    let up: String = first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>();
                    s = format!("{}{}", up, &s[first.len_utf8()..]);
                }
                s
            })
    }
}

fn input_html(name: &str, type_: &str, value: Option<&str>, extra_attrs: &[(String, String)], css: &str) -> String {
    let value_attr = value
        .map(|v| format!(" value=\"{}\"", crate::templates::escape_html(v)))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut attrs = String::new();
    for (k, v) in extra_attrs {
        attrs.push_str(&format!(" {}=\"{}\"", k, crate::templates::escape_html(v)));
    }
    format!(
        "<input type=\"{type_}\" name=\"{name}\" id=\"id_{name}\"{value_attr} class=\"{css}\"{attrs}>",
    )
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// CharField / TextField
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `forms.CharField` — text input with max/min length validation.
pub struct CharField {
    name: String,
    opts: CommonOpts,
    max_length: Option<usize>,
    min_length: Option<usize>,
    strip: bool,
    empty_value: Option<String>,
    textarea: bool,
}

impl CharField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            opts: CommonOpts { required: true, ..Default::default() },
            max_length: None,
            min_length: None,
            strip: true,
            empty_value: None,
            textarea: false,
        }
    }
    pub fn max_length(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { self.max_length = Some(n); self }
    pub fn min_length(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { self.min_length = Some(n); self }
    /// Do not strip surrounding whitespace.
    pub fn no_strip(mut self) -> Self { self.strip = false; self }
    /// Use a `<textarea>` widget instead of `<input type=text>`.
    pub fn textarea(mut self) -> Self { self.textarea = true; self }
    /// Make the field optional (`required=False`).
    pub fn optional(mut self) -> Self { self.opts.required = false; self }
    pub fn with_required(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.opts.required = v; self }
    pub fn with_label(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.label = Some(v.into()); self }
    pub fn with_initial(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.initial = Some(v.into()); self }
    pub fn with_help_text(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.help_text = Some(v.into()); self }
    pub fn with_attr(mut self, k: impl Into<String>, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.opts.widget_attrs.push((k.into(), v.into()));
        self
    }

    fn clean_impl(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        let mut errors = FieldErrors::new();
        let value = match raw {
            None => String::new(),
            Some(s) => {
                if self.strip { s.trim().to_string() } else { s.to_string() }
            }
        };
        if value.is_empty() {
            if self.required() {
                errors.push("This field is required.".to_string());
                return Err(errors);
            }
            if let Some(ev) = &self.empty_value {
                return Ok(Value::Text(ev.clone()));
            }
            return Ok(Value::Null);
        }
        if let Some(max) = self.max_length {
            if value.chars().count() > max {
                errors.push(format!(
                    "Ensure this value has at most {} characters (it has {}).",
                    max,
                    value.chars().count()
                ));
            }
        }
        if let Some(min) = self.min_length {
            if value.chars().count() < min {
                errors.push(format!(
                    "Ensure this value has at least {} characters (it has {}).",
                    min,
                    value.chars().count()
                ));
            }
        }
        if !errors.is_empty() {
            return Err(errors);
        }
        Ok(Value::Text(value))
    }
}

impl Field for CharField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.opts.label_of(&self.name) }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.opts.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        self.clean_impl(raw)
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let css = if error.is_some() { "form-control is-invalid" } else { "form-control" };
        let value = bound.or(self.opts.initial.as_deref());
        if self.textarea {
            let v = crate::templates::escape_html(value.unwrap_or(""));
            format!(
                "<textarea name=\"{0}\" id=\"id_{0}\" class=\"{1}\" rows=\"4\">{2}</textarea>",
                self.name, css, v
            )
        } else {
            input_html(&self.name, "text", value, &self.opts.widget_attrs, css)
        }
    }
}

/// `forms.CharField(widget=Textarea)` shorthand with no length limits.
/// (Django-style class name; intentionally not snake_case.)
#[allow(non_snake_case)]
pub fn TextField(name: impl Into<String>) -> CharField {
    CharField::new(name).textarea().optional()
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// EmailField / SlugField / URLField
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `forms.EmailField`.
pub struct EmailField {
    base: CharField,
}

impl EmailField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { base: CharField::new(name) }
    }
    pub fn optional(self) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.optional() } }
    pub fn with_required(self, v: bool) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.with_required(v) } }
    pub fn with_label(self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.with_label(v) } }
    pub fn with_initial(self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.with_initial(v) } }
    pub fn with_attr(self, k: impl Into<String>, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { base: self.base.with_attr(k, v) }
    }
    pub fn max_length(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { self.base.max_length = Some(n); self }

    fn valid_email(s: &str) -> bool {
        // Pragmatic RFC-lite check: one @, non-empty local + domain with dot.
        let parts: Vec<&str> = s.split('@').collect();
        if parts.len() != 2 {
            return false;
        }
        let (local, domain) = (parts[0], parts[1]);
        !local.is_empty()
            && domain.contains('.')
            && !domain.starts_with('.')
            && !domain.ends_with('.')
            && domain.split('.').all(|p| !p.is_empty())
            && !s.contains(char::is_whitespace)
    }
}

impl Field for EmailField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { self.base.name() }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.base.label() }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.base.required() }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        match self.base.clean_impl(raw) {
            Ok(Value::Text(v)) => {
                if Self::valid_email(&v) {
                    Ok(Value::Text(v))
                } else {
                    Err(vec!["Enter a valid email address.".to_string()])
                }
            }
            other => other,
        }
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let css = if error.is_some() { "form-control is-invalid" } else { "form-control" };
        let value = bound.or(self.base.opts.initial.as_deref());
        input_html(self.base.name(), "email", value, &self.base.opts.widget_attrs, css)
    }
}

/// `forms.SlugField`.
pub struct SlugField {
    base: CharField,
}

impl SlugField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { base: CharField::new(name) }
    }
    pub fn optional(self) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.optional() } }
    pub fn with_required(self, v: bool) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.with_required(v) } }
    pub fn with_label(self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.with_label(v) } }
    pub fn with_initial(self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { Self { base: self.base.with_initial(v) } }
    pub fn with_attr(self, k: impl Into<String>, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { base: self.base.with_attr(k, v) }
    }
    pub fn max_length(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { self.base.max_length = Some(n); self }
}

impl Field for SlugField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { self.base.name() }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.base.label() }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.base.required() }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        match self.base.clean_impl(raw) {
            Ok(Value::Text(v)) => {
                let ok = !v.is_empty()
                    && v.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_');
                if ok {
                    Ok(Value::Text(v))
                } else {
                    Err(vec![
                        "Enter a valid 'slug' consisting of letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens."
                            .to_string(),
                    ])
                }
            }
            other => other,
        }
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let css = if error.is_some() { "form-control is-invalid" } else { "form-control" };
        input_html(self.base.name(), "text", bound.or(self.base.opts.initial.as_deref()), &self.base.opts.widget_attrs, css)
    }
}

/// `forms.IntegerField`.
pub struct IntegerField {
    name: String,
    opts: CommonOpts,
    min_value: Option<i64>,
    max_value: Option<i64>,
}

impl IntegerField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), opts: CommonOpts { required: true, ..Default::default() }, min_value: None, max_value: None }
    }
    pub fn min_value(mut self, v: i64) -> Self { self.min_value = Some(v); self }
    pub fn max_value(mut self, v: i64) -> Self { self.max_value = Some(v); self }
    pub fn optional(mut self) -> Self { self.opts.required = false; self }
    pub fn label(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.label = Some(v.into()); self }
    pub fn with_initial(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.initial = Some(v.into()); self }
}

impl Field for IntegerField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.opts.label_of(&self.name) }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.opts.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        let mut errors = FieldErrors::new();
        let raw = raw.map(|s| s.trim()).unwrap_or("");
        if raw.is_empty() {
            if self.required() {
                return Err(vec!["This field is required.".to_string()]);
            }
            return Ok(Value::Null);
        }
        match raw.parse::<i64>() {
            Ok(n) => {
                if let Some(min) = self.min_value {
                    if n < min {
                        errors.push(format!("Ensure this value is greater than or equal to {min}."));
                    }
                }
                if let Some(max) = self.max_value {
                    if n > max {
                        errors.push(format!("Ensure this value is less than or equal to {max}."));
                    }
                }
                if !errors.is_empty() {
                    Err(errors)
                } else {
                    Ok(Value::Int(n))
                }
            }
            Err(_) => Err(vec!["Enter a whole number.".to_string()]),
        }
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let css = if error.is_some() { "form-control is-invalid" } else { "form-control" };
        input_html(&self.name, "number", bound.or(self.opts.initial.as_deref()), &self.opts.widget_attrs, css)
    }
}

/// `forms.FloatField`.
pub struct FloatField {
    name: String,
    opts: CommonOpts,
    min_value: Option<f64>,
    max_value: Option<f64>,
}

impl FloatField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), opts: CommonOpts { required: true, ..Default::default() }, min_value: None, max_value: None }
    }
    pub fn min_value(mut self, v: f64) -> Self { self.min_value = Some(v); self }
    pub fn max_value(mut self, v: f64) -> Self { self.max_value = Some(v); self }
    pub fn optional(mut self) -> Self { self.opts.required = false; self }
    pub fn label(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.label = Some(v.into()); self }
    pub fn with_initial(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.opts.initial = Some(v.into()); self }
}

impl Field for FloatField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.opts.label_of(&self.name) }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.opts.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        let raw = raw.map(|s| s.trim()).unwrap_or("");
        if raw.is_empty() {
            if self.required() {
                return Err(vec!["This field is required.".to_string()]);
            }
            return Ok(Value::Null);
        }
        match raw.parse::<f64>() {
            Ok(n) => {
                if let Some(min) = self.min_value {
                    if n < min {
                        return Err(vec![format!("Ensure this value is greater than or equal to {min}.")]);
                    }
                }
                if let Some(max) = self.max_value {
                    if n > max {
                        return Err(vec![format!("Ensure this value is less than or equal to {max}.")]);
                    }
                }
                Ok(Value::Float(n))
            }
            Err(_) => Err(vec!["Enter a number.".to_string()]),
        }
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let css = if error.is_some() { "form-control is-invalid" } else { "form-control" };
        let mut attrs = self.opts.widget_attrs.clone();
        attrs.push(("step".into(), "any".into()));
        input_html(&self.name, "number", bound.or(self.opts.initial.as_deref()), &attrs, css)
    }
}

/// `forms.BooleanField` — checkbox; missing value means false.
pub struct BooleanField {
    name: String,
    opts: CommonOpts,
}

impl BooleanField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), opts: CommonOpts { required: false, ..Default::default() } }
    }
}

impl Field for BooleanField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.opts.label_of(&self.name) }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.opts.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        let on = matches!(raw, Some("on") | Some("true") | Some("True") | Some("1") | Some("yes"));
        if !on && self.required() {
            return Err(vec!["This field is required.".to_string()]);
        }
        Ok(Value::Bool(on))
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, _error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let checked = bound.map(|v| v == "on" || v == "true" || v == "1").unwrap_or(false);
        format!(
            "<input type=\"checkbox\" name=\"{}\" id=\"id_{}\"{}>",
            self.name,
            self.name,
            if checked { " checked" } else { "" }
        )
    }
}

/// `forms.DateField` — accepts ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (plus a few common shapes).
pub struct DateField {
    name: String,
    opts: CommonOpts,
}

impl DateField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), opts: CommonOpts { required: true, ..Default::default() } }
    }
}

impl Field for DateField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.opts.label_of(&self.name) }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.opts.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        let raw = raw.map(|s| s.trim()).unwrap_or("");
        if raw.is_empty() {
            if self.required() {
                return Err(vec!["This field is required.".to_string()]);
            }
            return Ok(Value::Null);
        }
        for fmt in ["%Y-%m-%d", "%d/%m/%Y", "%m/%d/%Y"] {
            if let Ok(d) = chrono::NaiveDate::parse_from_str(raw, fmt) {
                let dt = d.and_hms_opt(0, 0, 0).unwrap_or_default();
                return Ok(Value::DateTime(dt.and_utc()));
            }
        }
        Err(vec!["Enter a valid date.".to_string()])
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let css = if error.is_some() { "form-control is-invalid" } else { "form-control" };
        input_html(&self.name, "date", bound.or(self.opts.initial.as_deref()), &self.opts.widget_attrs, css)
    }
}

/// `forms.ChoiceField` — select widget with choices validation.
pub struct ChoiceField {
    name: String,
    opts: CommonOpts,
    choices: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl ChoiceField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, choices: Vec<(&str, &str)>) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            opts: CommonOpts { required: true, ..Default::default() },
            choices: choices
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(v, l)| (v.to_string(), l.to_string()))
                .collect(),
        }
    }
}

impl Field for ChoiceField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { self.opts.label_of(&self.name) }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.opts.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        let raw = raw.unwrap_or("");
        if raw.is_empty() {
            if self.required() {
                return Err(vec!["This field is required.".to_string()]);
            }
            return Ok(Value::Null);
        }
        if self.choices.iter().any(|(v, _)| v == raw) {
            Ok(Value::Text(raw.to_string()))
        } else {
            Err(vec!["Select a valid choice.".to_string()])
        }
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, _error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let mut out = format!("<select name=\"{}\" id=\"id_{}\" class=\"form-control\">", self.name, self.name);
        for (value, label) in &self.choices {
            let selected = bound.map(|b| b == value).unwrap_or(false);
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "<option value=\"{}\"{}>{}</option>",
                crate::templates::escape_html(value),
                if selected { " selected" } else { "" },
                crate::templates::escape_html(label)
            ));
        }
        out.push_str("</select>");
        out
    }
}

/// `forms.HiddenInput` plain field (e.g. for tokens).
pub struct HiddenField {
    name: String,
    initial: Option<String>,
    required: bool,
}

impl HiddenField {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), initial: None, required: false }
    }
    pub fn initial(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.initial = Some(v.into()); self }
}

impl Field for HiddenField {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn label(&self) -> String { String::new() }
    fn required(&self) -> bool { self.required }

    fn clean(&self, raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Value, FieldErrors> {
        Ok(match raw {
            Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => Value::Text(s.to_string()),
            _ => Value::Null,
        })
    }

    fn render(&self, bound: Option<&str>, _error: Option<&str>) -> String {
        let v = bound.or(self.initial.as_deref());
        input_html(&self.name, "hidden", v, &[], "")
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Form
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A bound/unbound form: field set + submitted data + validation state.
pub struct Form {
    pub prefix: String,
    fields: Vec<Box<dyn Field>>,
    data: QueryDict,
    bound: bool,
    cleaned: HashMap<String, Value>,
    errors: HashMap<String, FieldErrors>,
    validated: bool,
    valid: bool,
}

impl Form {
    /// Build an unbound form.
    pub fn new(prefix: impl Into<String>, fields: Vec<Box<dyn Field>>) -> Form {
        Form {
            prefix: prefix.into(),
            fields,
            data: QueryDict::new(),
            bound: false,
            cleaned: HashMap::new(),
            errors: HashMap::new(),
            validated: false,
            valid: false,
        }
    }

    /// Bind to submitted data — `MyForm(request.POST)`.
    pub fn bind(mut self, data: &QueryDict) -> Form {
        self.data = data.clone();
        self.bound = true;
        self
    }

    pub fn fields(&self) -> &[Box<dyn Field>] {
        &self.fields
    }

    pub fn is_bound(&self) -> bool { self.bound }

    /// Validate all fields — `form.is_valid()`.
    pub fn is_valid(&mut self) -> bool {
        if self.validated {
            return self.valid;
        }
        self.valid = true;
        self.errors.clear();
        self.cleaned.clear();
        for field in &self.fields {
            let raw = self.data.get(field.name());
            match field.clean(raw) {
                Ok(value) => {
                    self.cleaned.insert(field.name().to_string(), value);
                }
                Err(errs) => {
                    self.valid = false;
                    self.errors.insert(field.name().to_string(), errs);
                }
            }
        }
        self.validated = true;
        self.valid
    }

    /// `form.cleaned_data["name"]`.
    pub fn cleaned(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Value> {
        self.cleaned.get(name)
    }

    pub fn cleaned_data(&self) -> &HashMap<String, Value> {
        &self.cleaned
    }

    /// `form.errors` — field name -> messages.
    pub fn errors(&self) -> &HashMap<String, FieldErrors> {
        &self.errors
    }

    /// Non-field error list (empty in this build; kept for API parity).
    pub fn non_field_errors(&self) -> FieldErrors {
        vec![]
    }

    /// Render every field wrapped in `<p>` — `form.as_p()`.
    pub fn as_p(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for field in &self.fields {
            let bound = if self.bound { self.data.get(field.name()) } else { None };
            let error_html = if let Some(errs) = self.errors.get(field.name()) {
                let items: String = errs
                    .iter()
                    .map(|e| format!("<li>{}</li>", crate::templates::escape_html(e)))
                    .collect();
                format!("<ul class=\"errorlist\">{items}</ul>")
            } else {
                String::new()
            };
            let help = match field_label_help(field.as_ref()) {
                Some(h) => format!(" <span class=\"helptext\">{}</span>", crate::templates::escape_html(&h)),
                None => String::new(),
            };
            let label = format!(
                "<label for=\"id_{0}\">{1}</label>",
                field.name(),
                crate::templates::escape_html(&field.label())
            );
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "<p>{label} {} {help}{error_html}</p>",
                field.render(bound, self.errors.get(field.name()).map(|_| "")),
            ));
        }
        out
    }

    /// Render as a `<table>` — `form.as_table()`.
    pub fn as_table(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for field in &self.fields {
            let bound = if self.bound { self.data.get(field.name()) } else { None };
            let error_html = if let Some(errs) = self.errors.get(field.name()) {
                let items: String = errs
                    .iter()
                    .map(|e| format!("<li>{}</li>", crate::templates::escape_html(e)))
                    .collect();
                format!("<ul class=\"errorlist\">{items}</ul>")
            } else {
                String::new()
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "<tr><th><label for=\"id_{0}\">{1}</label></th><td>{2}{3}</td></tr>",
                field.name(),
                crate::templates::escape_html(&field.label()),
                field.render(bound, self.errors.get(field.name()).map(|_| "")),
                error_html,
            ));
        }
        out
    }

    /// Opening `<form>` tag (pair with `{% csrf_token %}`).
    pub fn open_tag(&self) -> String {
        "<form method=\"post\" action=\"\">".to_string()
    }

    pub fn close_tag(&self) -> String {
        "</form>".to_string()
    }
}

fn field_label_help(field: &dyn Field) -> Option<String> {
    // help_text is stored per concrete field; kept simple in this build.
    let _ = field;
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample_form() -> Form {
        Form::new(
            "contact",
            vec![
                Box::new(CharField::new("name").max_length(50)),
                Box::new(EmailField::new("email")),
                Box::new(IntegerField::new("age").min_value(1).max_value(120)),
                Box::new(BooleanField::new("subscribe")),
                Box::new(ChoiceField::new("color", vec![("red", "Red"), ("green", "Green")])),
            ],
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn valid_submission() {
        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("name", "Ada Lovelace");
        data.set("email", "ada@example.com");
        data.set("age", "36");
        data.set("color", "red");
        let form = sample_form().bind(&data);
        let mut bound = form;
        assert!(bound.is_valid());
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("name"), Some(&Value::Text("Ada Lovelace".into())));
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("age"), Some(&Value::Int(36)));
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("subscribe"), Some(&Value::Bool(false)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_email_and_age() {
        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("name", "X");
        data.set("email", "not-an-email");
        data.set("age", "500");
        data.set("color", "purple");
        let mut bound = sample_form().bind(&data);
        assert!(!bound.is_valid());
        assert!(bound.errors().contains_key("email"));
        assert!(bound.errors().contains_key("age"));
        assert!(bound.errors().contains_key("color"));
        assert!(bound.errors()["email"][0].contains("valid email"));
        assert!(bound.errors()["age"][0].contains("less than or equal"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn required_fields_missing() {
        let data = QueryDict::new();
        let mut bound = sample_form().bind(&data);
        assert!(!bound.is_valid());
        assert!(bound.errors()["name"][0].contains("required"));
        assert!(bound.errors()["email"][0].contains("required"));
        // is_valid is cached
        assert!(!bound.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn char_max_length() {
        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("name", "x".repeat(51));
        data.set("email", "a@b.co");
        data.set("age", "1");
        data.set("color", "red");
        let mut bound = sample_form().bind(&data);
        assert!(!bound.is_valid());
        assert!(bound.errors()["name"][0].contains("at most 50"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unbound_form_renders() {
        let form = sample_form();
        let html = form.as_p();
        assert!(html.contains("name=\"name\""));
        assert!(html.contains("name=\"email\""));
        assert!(html.contains("<select"));
        assert!(!html.contains("errorlist"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn bound_form_renders_values_and_errors() {
        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("name", "");
        data.set("email", "a@b.co");
        data.set("age", "30");
        data.set("color", "red");
        let mut bound = sample_form().bind(&data);
        bound.is_valid();
        let html = bound.as_p();
        assert!(html.contains("errorlist"));
        assert!(html.contains("value=\"a@b.co\""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn optional_and_textarea() {
        let form = Form::new(
            "bio",
            vec![
                Box::new(TextField("about")),
                Box::new(CharField::new("nick").optional()),
            ],
        );
        let data = QueryDict::new();
        let mut bound = form.bind(&data);
        assert!(bound.is_valid());
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("about"), Some(&Value::Null));
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("nick"), Some(&Value::Null));
    }

    #[test]
    fn date_field() {
        let form = Form::new("d", vec![Box::new(DateField::new("when"))]);
        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("when", "2026-01-15");
        let mut bound = form.bind(&data);
        assert!(bound.is_valid());
        assert!(matches!(bound.cleaned("when"), Some(Value::DateTime(_))));

        let mut bad = QueryDict::new();
        bad.set("when", "not a date");
        let mut b2 = Form::new("d", vec![Box::new(DateField::new("when"))]).bind(&bad);
        assert!(!b2.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn slug_field() {
        let form = Form::new("s", vec![Box::new(SlugField::new("slug"))]);
        let mut ok = QueryDict::new();
        ok.set("slug", "my-post_1");
        let mut b = form.bind(&ok);
        assert!(b.is_valid());

        let mut bad = QueryDict::new();
        bad.set("slug", "bad slug!");
        let mut b2 = Form::new("s", vec![Box::new(SlugField::new("slug"))]).bind(&bad);
        assert!(!b2.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn integer_coercion_and_float() {
        let form = Form::new(
            "m",
            vec![Box::new(IntegerField::new("n")), Box::new(FloatField::new("f"))],
        );
        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("n", " 42 ");
        data.set("f", "3.25");
        let mut bound = form.bind(&data);
        assert!(bound.is_valid());
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("n"), Some(&Value::Int(42)));
        assert_eq!(bound.cleaned("f"), Some(&Value::Float(3.25)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hidden_field_and_table_render() {
        let form = Form::new(
            "h",
            vec![Box::new(HiddenField::new("token").initial("abc"))],
        );
        let html = form.as_table();
        assert!(html.contains("type=\"hidden\""));
        assert!(html.contains("value=\"abc\""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn as_table_shows_labels_not_errors() {
        // Regression: as_table() used to interpolate the error HTML into the
        // <label> slot instead of the field label.
        let form = Form::new("t", vec![Box::new(IntegerField::new("age"))]);
        let html = form.as_table();
        assert!(html.contains(">Age</label>"), "label missing: {html}");

        let mut data = QueryDict::new();
        data.set("age", "notanumber");
        let mut bound = form.bind(&data);
        bound.is_valid();
        let html = bound.as_table();
        assert!(html.contains(">Age</label>"));
        assert!(html.contains("errorlist"));
    }
}
