## `crates/server/rustango/src/http.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/src/http.rs)

```rust
//! HTTP primitives — the `django.http` equivalent.
//!
//! [`HttpRequest`] mirrors `django.http.HttpRequest` (method, path, GET/POST
//! [`QueryDict`], COOKIES, headers, plus framework-injected `user`, `session`
//! and resolver match data). [`HttpResponse`] mirrors `HttpResponse` with the
//! usual shortcut constructors (`html`, `json`, `redirect`, ...).

use std::collections::HashMap;

use serde_json::Value as JsonValue;

use crate::errors::HttpError;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Headers & cookies
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Case-insensitive header map.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Headers {
    items: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl Headers {
    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }

    pub fn set(&mut self, name: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) {
        let name = name.into();
        let value = value.into();
        if let Some(existing) = self.items.iter_mut().find(|(n, _)| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&name)) {
            existing.1 = value;
        } else {
            self.items.push((name, value));
        }
    }

    pub fn add(&mut self, name: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) {
        self.items.push((name.into(), value.into()));
    }

    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.items
            .iter()
            .find(|(n, _)| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
            .map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
    }

    /// All values for a header, in order (headers may repeat,
    /// e.g. multiple `Cookie:` lines).
    pub fn get_all(&self, name: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
        self.items
            .iter()
            .filter(|(n, _)| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
            .map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
            .collect()
    }

    pub fn remove(&mut self, name: &str) {
        self.items.retain(|(n, _)| !n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name));
    }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &str)> {
        self.items.iter().map(|(n, v)| (n.as_str(), v.as_str()))
    }
}

/// Parse a `Cookie:` header value into a map.
pub fn parse_cookie_header(header: &str) -> HashMap<String, String> {
    let mut out = HashMap::new();
    for part in header.split(';') {
        let part = part.trim();
        if part.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((k, v)) = part.split_once('=') {
            out.insert(urldecode(k.trim()), urldecode(v.trim()));
        }
    }
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// QueryDict — the multi-value GET/POST bag
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Multi-value string map, like `django.http.QueryDict`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct QueryDict {
    data: HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
}

impl QueryDict {
    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }

    /// Parse `a=1&b=2&b=3` form/query-string encoding.
    pub fn parse(encoded: &str) -> Self {
        let mut qd = Self::new();
        for pair in encoded.split('&') {
            if pair.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let (k, v) = pair.split_once('=').unwrap_or((pair, ""));
            qd.add(urldecode(k), urldecode(v.replace('+', " ").as_str()));
        }
        qd
    }

    pub fn add(&mut self, key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) {
        self.data.entry(key.into()).or_default().push(value.into());
    }

    /// Last value, like `QueryDict.__getitem__` / `.get()`.
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.data.get(key).and_then(|v| v.last()).map(|s| s.as_str())
    }

    /// First value (like `QueryDict.__getitem__` which returns the last;
    /// we expose both).
    pub fn get_first(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.data.get(key).and_then(|v| v.first()).map(|s| s.as_str())
    }

    /// All values for a key, like `QueryDict.getlist()`.
    pub fn getlist(&self, key: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
        self.data
            .get(key)
            .map(|v| v.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    pub fn set(&mut self, key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) {
        self.data.insert(key.into(), vec![value.into()]);
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, key: &str) -> bool { self.data.contains_key(key) }

    pub fn keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> { self.data.keys().map(|k| k.as_str()) }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.data.is_empty() }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.data.len() }

    /// Encode back to form-urlencoded.
    pub fn encode(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for (k, vs) in &self.data {
            for v in vs {
                if !out.is_empty() {
                    out.push('&');
                }
                out.push_str(&urlencode(k));
                out.push('=');
                out.push_str(&urlencode(v));
            }
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Percent-decode a URL component.
pub fn urldecode(s: &str) -> String {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        match bytes[i] {
            b'%' if i + 2 < bytes.len() => {
                let hex_str = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[i + 1..i + 3]).unwrap_or("");
                if let Ok(b) = u8::from_str_radix(hex_str, 16) {
                    out.push(b);
                    i += 3;
                } else {
                    out.push(bytes[i]);
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            b'+' => {
                out.push(b' ');
                i += 1;
            }
            b => {
                out.push(b);
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()
}

/// Percent-encode a URL component (RFC 3986 unreserved set kept).
pub fn urlencode(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for b in s.bytes() {
        match b {
            b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'.' | b'_' | b'~' => {
                out.push(b as char)
            }
            _ => out.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}")),
        }
    }
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Request
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Method { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE }

impl Method {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Method::GET => "GET",
            Method::POST => "POST",
            Method::PUT => "PUT",
            Method::PATCH => "PATCH",
            Method::DELETE => "DELETE",
            Method::HEAD => "HEAD",
            Method::OPTIONS => "OPTIONS",
            Method::TRACE => "TRACE",
        }
    }

    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Method> {
        match s.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str() {
            "GET" => Some(Method::GET),
            "POST" => Some(Method::POST),
            "PUT" => Some(Method::PUT),
            "PATCH" => Some(Method::PATCH),
            "DELETE" => Some(Method::DELETE),
            "HEAD" => Some(Method::HEAD),
            "OPTIONS" => Some(Method::OPTIONS),
            "TRACE" => Some(Method::TRACE),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Django's "safe methods" for CSRF: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE.
    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Method::GET | Method::HEAD | Method::OPTIONS | Method::TRACE)
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Method {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.as_str())
    }
}

/// Authenticated-or-anonymous user attached by the auth middleware.
/// Full `User` model lives in [`crate::auth`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub enum AuthUser {
    #[default]
    Anonymous,
    Authenticated {
        id: i64,
        username: String,
        is_staff: bool,
        is_superuser: bool,
    },
}

impl AuthUser {
    pub fn is_authenticated(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, AuthUser::Authenticated { .. })
    }
    pub fn is_anonymous(&self) -> bool { !self.is_authenticated() }
    pub fn id(&self) -> Option<i64> {
        match self {
            AuthUser::Anonymous => None,
            AuthUser::Authenticated { id, .. } => Some(*id),
        }
    }
    pub fn username(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            AuthUser::Anonymous => "",
            AuthUser::Authenticated { username, .. } => username,
        }
    }
    pub fn is_staff(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, AuthUser::Authenticated { is_staff: true, .. })
    }
    pub fn is_superuser(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, AuthUser::Authenticated { is_superuser: true, .. })
    }
}

/// The request object. Framework middleware populates `user`, `session`,
/// `params` (path kwargs) and `csrf_token` before the view runs.
pub struct HttpRequest {
    pub method: Method,
    /// Path portion, e.g. `/polls/3/vote/`.
    pub path: String,
    /// Full path incl. query string (like `request.get_full_path()`).
    pub full_path: String,
    pub query: QueryDict,
    pub post: QueryDict,
    pub headers: Headers,
    pub cookies: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
    /// Path kwargs resolved by the router (`<int:pk>` -> `pk`).
    pub params: HashMap<String, String>,
    /// Name of the matched route (like `resolver_match.url_name`).
    pub url_name: Option<String>,
    /// Set by SessionMiddleware.
    pub session: Option<crate::sessions::Session>,
    /// Set by AuthMiddleware.
    pub user: AuthUser,
    /// Set by CsrfMiddleware; used by `{% csrf_token %}`.
    pub csrf_token: Option<String>,
    /// Flash messages loaded by MessagesMiddleware.
    pub messages: Vec<crate::messages::Message>,
    /// Remote address string.
    pub remote_addr: String,
    /// Template engine (set by the dispatcher), for `views::render`.
    pub engine: Option<std::sync::Arc<crate::templates::Engine>>,
    /// Database backend (set by the dispatcher), for ORM access in views.
    pub backend: Option<std::sync::Arc<dyn crate::orm::Backend>>,
}

impl HttpRequest {
    pub fn new(method: Method, path: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let path = path.into();
        let (p, q) = path.split_once('?').unwrap_or((&path, ""));
        Self {
            method,
            path: p.to_string(),
            full_path: if q.is_empty() { p.to_string() } else { format!("{p}?{q}") },
            query: QueryDict::parse(q),
            post: QueryDict::new(),
            headers: Headers::new(),
            cookies: HashMap::new(),
            body: Vec::new(),
            params: HashMap::new(),
            url_name: None,
            session: None,
            user: AuthUser::Anonymous,
            csrf_token: None,
            messages: Vec::new(),
            remote_addr: "127.0.0.1".into(),
            engine: None,
            backend: None,
        }
    }

    /// `request.GET` in Django.
    #[allow(non_snake_case)]
    pub fn GET(&self) -> &QueryDict { &self.query }

    /// `request.POST` in Django (form-encoded bodies are parsed eagerly).
    #[allow(non_snake_case)]
    pub fn POST(&self) -> &QueryDict { &self.post }

    pub fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> { self.headers.get(name) }

    pub fn cookie(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.cookies.get(name).map(|s| s.as_str())
    }

    /// Path parameter captured by the router.
    pub fn param(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> { self.params.get(name).map(|s| s.as_str()) }

    /// Path parameter parsed as i64 (`<int:pk>`).
    pub fn int_param(&self, name: &str) -> Result<i64, HttpError> {
        self.param(name)
            .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
            .ok_or_else(|| HttpError::NotFound(format!("invalid `{name}` path parameter")))
    }

    /// True when the request was made over HTTPS (X-Forwarded-Proto aware).
    pub fn is_secure(&self) -> bool {
        self.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto").map(|p| p == "https").unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// `request.is_ajax()`-style helper: X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest.
    pub fn is_ajax(&self) -> bool {
        self.headers.get("x-requested-with").map(|v| v.eq_ignore_ascii_case("XMLHttpRequest")).unwrap_or(false)
    }

    pub fn get_full_path(&self) -> &str { &self.full_path }

    /// Build an absolute URI for this request.
    pub fn build_absolute_uri(&self, location: &str) -> String {
        if location.starts_with("http://") || location.starts_with("https://") {
            return location.to_string();
        }
        let host = self.headers.get("host").unwrap_or("localhost");
        let scheme = if self.is_secure() { "https" } else { "http" };
        if location.starts_with('/') {
            format!("{scheme}://{host}{location}")
        } else {
            format!("{scheme}://{host}/{location}")
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for HttpRequest {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("HttpRequest")
            .field("method", &self.method)
            .field("path", &self.path)
            .field("user", &self.user.username())
            .finish()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Response
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct SetCookie {
    pub name: String,
    pub value: String,
    pub max_age: Option<i64>,
    pub path: String,
    pub http_only: bool,
    pub secure: bool,
    pub same_site: Option<String>,
}

impl SetCookie {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.into(),
            value: value.into(),
            max_age: None,
            path: "/".into(),
            http_only: false,
            secure: false,
            same_site: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn max_age(mut self, secs: i64) -> Self { self.max_age = Some(secs); self }
    pub fn http_only(mut self) -> Self { self.http_only = true; self }
    pub fn secure(mut self) -> Self { self.secure = true; self }
    pub fn same_site(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.same_site = Some(v.into()); self }

    pub fn expired(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { name: name.into(), value: String::new(), max_age: Some(0), ..Self::new("", "") }
    }

    pub fn to_header(&self) -> String {
        let mut s = format!("{}={}", urlencode(&self.name), urlencode(&self.value));
        s.push_str(&format!("; Path={}", self.path));
        if let Some(ma) = self.max_age {
            s.push_str(&format!("; Max-Age={ma}"));
        }
        if self.http_only {
            s.push_str("; HttpOnly");
        }
        if self.secure {
            s.push_str("; Secure");
        }
        if let Some(ss) = &self.same_site {
            s.push_str(&format!("; SameSite={ss}"));
        }
        s
    }
}

/// The response object — status, headers, cookies and a byte body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct HttpResponse {
    pub status: u16,
    pub headers: Headers,
    pub cookies: Vec<SetCookie>,
    body: Vec<u8>,
}

impl HttpResponse {
    pub fn new(status: u16) -> Self {
        Self { status, headers: Headers::new(), cookies: Vec::new(), body: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn with_body(status: u16, content_type: &str, body: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Self {
        let mut r = Self::new(status);
        r.headers.set("Content-Type", content_type);
        r.body = body.into();
        r
    }

    /// 200 text/html — like `HttpResponse("<h1>..</h1>")`.
    pub fn html(body: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Self {
        Self::with_body(200, "text/html; charset=utf-8", body)
    }

    /// 200 text/plain.
    pub fn text(body: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::with_body(200, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", body.into().into_bytes())
    }

    /// 200 application/json — like `JsonResponse`.
    pub fn json(value: &JsonValue) -> Self {
        Self::with_body(200, "application/json", serde_json::to_string(value).unwrap_or_default())
    }

    /// Any status + JSON body.
    pub fn json_status(status: u16, value: &JsonValue) -> Self {
        Self::with_body(status, "application/json", serde_json::to_string(value).unwrap_or_default())
    }

    /// 302 redirect — like `HttpResponseRedirect`. Relative or absolute.
    pub fn redirect(to: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let mut r = Self::new(302);
        r.headers.set("Location", to.into());
        r
    }

    /// 301 permanent redirect.
    pub fn redirect_permanent(to: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let mut r = Self::new(301);
        r.headers.set("Location", to.into());
        r
    }

    pub fn status(status: u16) -> Self { Self::new(status) }

    /// HttpResponseNotAllowed equivalent.
    pub fn not_allowed(allowed: &[Method]) -> Self {
        let list: Vec<&str> = allowed.iter().map(|m| m.as_str()).collect();
        let mut r = Self::with_body(405, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", format!("Method not allowed. Allowed: {}", list.join(", ")));
        r.headers.set("Allow", list.join(", "));
        r
    }

    pub fn body(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.body }

    pub fn body_string(&self) -> String {
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.body).into_owned()
    }

    pub fn set_body(&mut self, body: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) {
        self.body = body.into();
    }

    pub fn content_length(&self) -> usize { self.body.len() }

    pub fn set_cookie(&mut self, cookie: SetCookie) {
        self.cookies.push(cookie);
    }

    pub fn delete_cookie(&mut self, name: impl Into<String>, path: &str) {
        let mut c = SetCookie::expired(name);
        c.path = path.to_string();
        self.cookies.push(c);
    }

    /// Extract a single Set-Cookie value for a name (test helper).
    pub fn cookie_value(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        self.cookies
            .iter()
            .find(|c| c.name == name)
            .map(|c| c.value.clone())
    }
}

impl Default for HttpResponse {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new(200) }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn querydict_roundtrip() {
        let qd = QueryDict::parse("a=1&b=hello+world&b=second&name=a%20b");
        assert_eq!(qd.get("a"), Some("1"));
        assert_eq!(qd.get("b"), Some("second"));
        assert_eq!(qd.getlist("b"), vec!["hello world", "second"]);
        assert_eq!(qd.get("name"), Some("a b"));
        let encoded = qd.encode();
        let reparsed = QueryDict::parse(&encoded);
        assert_eq!(reparsed.getlist("b").len(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn querydict_add_get() {
        let mut qd = QueryDict::new();
        qd.add("tag", "rust");
        qd.add("tag", "django");
        qd.set("only", "one");
        assert_eq!(qd.getlist("tag"), vec!["rust", "django"]);
        assert!(qd.contains("only"));
        assert!(!qd.contains("nope"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn header_case_insensitive() {
        let mut h = Headers::new();
        h.set("Content-Type", "text/html");
        assert_eq!(h.get("content-type"), Some("text/html"));
        assert_eq!(h.get("CONTENT-TYPE"), Some("text/html"));
        h.set("content-type", "application/json");
        assert_eq!(h.get("Content-Type"), Some("application/json"));
        assert_eq!(h.iter().count(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cookies() {
        let c = SetCookie::new("sessionid", "abc123").max_age(3600).http_only().same_site("Lax");
        let header = c.to_header();
        assert!(header.starts_with("sessionid=abc123"));
        assert!(header.contains("Max-Age=3600"));
        assert!(header.contains("HttpOnly"));
        assert!(header.contains("SameSite=Lax"));

        let expired = SetCookie::expired("csrftoken");
        assert!(expired.to_header().contains("Max-Age=0"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn multiple_cookie_headers_are_joined() {
        let mut h = Headers::new();
        h.add("Cookie", "a=1");
        h.add("Cookie", "b=2");
        assert_eq!(h.get_all("cookie"), vec!["a=1", "b=2"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn request_basics() {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/polls/3/?page=2&tag=a&tag=b");
        assert_eq!(req.path, "/polls/3/");
        assert_eq!(req.query.get("page"), Some("2"));
        assert_eq!(req.query.getlist("tag"), vec!["a", "b"]);
        assert_eq!(req.method, Method::GET);

        req.params.insert("pk".into(), "3".into());
        assert_eq!(req.int_param("pk").unwrap(), 3);
        assert!(req.int_param("missing").is_err());

        let full = req.build_absolute_uri("/next/");
        assert_eq!(full, "http://localhost/next/");
    }

    #[test]
    fn methods() {
        assert!(Method::GET.is_safe());
        assert!(!Method::POST.is_safe());
        assert_eq!(Method::parse("post"), Some(Method::POST));
        assert_eq!(Method::parse("bogus"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn response_helpers() {
        let r = HttpResponse::html("<h1>hi</h1>");
        assert_eq!(r.status, 200);
        assert_eq!(r.headers.get("Content-Type"), Some("text/html; charset=utf-8"));

        let r = HttpResponse::json(&serde_json::json!({"ok": true}));
        assert!(r.body_string().contains("\"ok\":true"));

        let r = HttpResponse::redirect("/next/");
        assert_eq!(r.status, 302);
        assert_eq!(r.headers.get("Location"), Some("/next/"));

        let r = HttpResponse::not_allowed(&[Method::POST]);
        assert_eq!(r.status, 405);
        assert_eq!(r.headers.get("Allow"), Some("POST"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cookie_header_parse() {
        let jar = parse_cookie_header("sessionid=abc; csrftoken=x%20y; empty=");
        assert_eq!(jar.get("sessionid").map(String::as_str), Some("abc"));
        assert_eq!(jar.get("csrftoken").map(String::as_str), Some("x y"));
        assert_eq!(jar.get("empty").map(String::as_str), Some(""));
    }
}

```rust
//! Internationalization (lite) — `django.utils.translation`.
//!
//! Translations live in JSON catalogs (`<lang>.json`, mapping msgid →
//! translated string) inside `LOCALE_PATHS` dirs. Activate a language with
//! the `rustango_language` cookie or the settings default, then use
//! `{% trans "key" %}` or the `t()` helper.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::RwLock;

static CATALOGS: RwLock<Option<HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>>>> = RwLock::new(None);

/// Load catalogs from locale dirs: every `<lang>.json` file.
pub fn load_locale_dirs(dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> usize {
    let mut catalogs: HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>> = HashMap::new();
    for dir in dirs {
        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
            Ok(e) => e,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        for entry in entries.filter_map(|e| e.ok()) {
            let path = entry.path();
            if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) == Some("json") {
                let lang = path
                    .file_stem()
                    .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
                    .unwrap_or_default()
                    .to_string();
                if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
                    if let Ok(map) = serde_json::from_str::<HashMap<String, String>>(&text) {
                        let entry = catalogs.entry(lang).or_default();
                        for (k, v) in map {
                            entry.insert(k, v);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let n = catalogs.len();
    *CATALOGS.write().unwrap() = Some(catalogs);
    n
}

/// Install catalogs directly (tests / programmatic setup).
pub fn set_catalogs(catalogs: HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>>) {
    *CATALOGS.write().unwrap() = Some(catalogs);
}

fn catalogs() -> HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>> {
    CATALOGS.read().unwrap().clone().unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Translate `msgid` in `lang`; falls back through language prefixes
/// (`de-de` → `de`) then to the msgid itself (gettext behavior).
pub fn translate(lang: &str, msgid: &str) -> String {
    if msgid.is_empty() {
        return String::new();
    }
    let cats = catalogs();
    if let Some(cat) = cats.get(lang) {
        if let Some(t) = cat.get(msgid) {
            return t.clone();
        }
    }
    if let Some((base, _)) = lang.split_once('-') {
        if let Some(cat) = cats.get(base) {
            if let Some(t) = cat.get(msgid) {
                return t.clone();
            }
        }
    }
    msgid.to_string()
}

/// The `t()` helper — translate with optional interpolation:
/// `t("hello {name}", &[("name", "Ada")])`.
pub fn t(lang: &str, msgid: &str, params: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String {
    let mut out = translate(lang, msgid);
    for (k, v) in params {
        out = out.replace(&format!("{{{k}}}"), v);
    }
    out
}

/// Pick the language for a request: cookie > settings default.
pub fn activate(req: &crate::http::HttpRequest) -> String {
    let settings = crate::settings::global();
    if let Some(lang) = req.cookie(&settings.language_cookie_name) {
        if settings.languages.is_empty()
            || settings.languages.iter().any(|l| l.eq_ignore_ascii_case(lang))
        {
            return lang.to_string();
        }
    }
    settings.language_code.clone()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    fn demo() {
        let mut cats = HashMap::new();
        let mut de = HashMap::new();
        de.insert("Welcome".to_string(), "Willkommen".to_string());
        de.insert("hello {name}".to_string(), "Hallo {name}".to_string());
        let mut de_de = HashMap::new();
        de_de.insert("Bye".to_string(), "Auf Wiedersehen".to_string());
        cats.insert("de".to_string(), de);
        cats.insert("de-de".to_string(), de_de);
        set_catalogs(cats);
    }

    #[test]
    fn translate_basic() {
        demo();
        assert_eq!(translate("de", "Welcome"), "Willkommen");
        assert_eq!(translate("en", "Welcome"), "Welcome"); // fallback to msgid
        assert_eq!(translate("de", "Unknown key"), "Unknown key");
    }

    #[test]
    fn language_prefix_fallback() {
        demo();
        assert_eq!(translate("de-de", "Bye"), "Auf Wiedersehen");
        // de-at falls back to `de`, which lacks "Bye" -> msgid
        assert_eq!(translate("de-at", "Bye"), "Bye");
        assert_eq!(translate("de-at", "Welcome"), "Willkommen");
        assert_eq!(translate("de-de", "Welcome"), "Willkommen"); // de-de -> de
    }

    #[test]
    fn interpolation() {
        demo();
        assert_eq!(t("de", "hello {name}", &[("name", "Ada")]), "Hallo Ada");
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_msgid() {
        demo();
        assert_eq!(translate("de", ""), "");
    }
}

````rust
//! # rustango — Django, rewritten in pure Rust
//!
//! `rustango` is a batteries-included, Django-style web framework written
//! entirely in Rust with **zero C/C++ dependencies** (the HTTP edge uses
//! tokio/axum; the crypto stack uses RustCrypto; TLS for `contrib.ai` uses
//! rustls + ring).
//!
//! The framework core is synchronous (WSGI-style, thread-per-request at the
//! edge), mirroring Django's request/response model:
//!
//! ```text
//! request -> middleware.request -> url router -> view
//!         <- middleware.response <- template/forms/orm <- view
//! ```
//!
//! ## Module map (Django -> rustango)
//!
//! | Django                  | rustango                        |
//! |-------------------------|---------------------------------|
//! | `django.conf.settings`  | [`settings::Settings`]          |
//! | `django.http`           | [`http`]                        |
//! | `django.urls`           | [`urls`] (`path()`, `reverse()`)|
//! | `django.views`          | [`views`] (+ class-based views) |
//! | `django.middleware`     | [`middleware`]                  |
//! | `django.db.models`      | [`orm`] (`#[derive(Model)]`)    |
//! | `django.template`       | [`templates`]                   |
//! | `django.forms`          | [`forms`]                       |
//! | `django.contrib.auth`   | [`auth`]                        |
//! | `django.contrib.sessions`| [`sessions`]                   |
//! | `django.middleware.csrf`| [`csrf`]                        |
//! | `django.contrib.messages`| [`messages`]                   |
//! | `django.contrib.admin`  | [`admin`]                       |
//! | `django.core.signals`   | [`signals`]                     |
//! | `django.utils.translation` | [`i18n`]                     |
//! | `django.core.cache`     | [`cache`]                       |
//! | `django.contrib.staticfiles` | [`staticfiles`]            |
//! | `django.core.management`| [`management`] + `rustango` CLI |
//! | (new) LLM/agent support | [`contrib::ai`]                 |

// Allow the proc-macros to emit `::rustango::...` paths even when used
// inside this crate.
extern crate self as rustango;

pub mod admin;
pub mod auth;
pub mod cache;
pub mod contrib;
pub mod csrf;
pub mod errors;
pub mod forms;
pub mod http;
pub mod i18n;
pub mod management;
pub mod messages;
pub mod middleware;
pub mod orm;
pub mod project;
pub mod server;
pub mod sessions;
pub mod settings;
pub mod signals;
pub mod staticfiles;
pub mod templates;
pub mod testclient;
pub mod urls;
pub mod views;

/// Shared type re-exports so user crates don't need `chrono` directly.
pub mod types {
    pub use chrono::Utc;
    /// UTC timestamp used by all `DateTime` model fields.
    pub type DateTime = chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>;
    pub type DateTimeTz = chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>;
}

/// Re-exported derive macro: `#[derive(Model)] #[model(table = "...")]`.
pub use rustango_macros::Model;

/// Everything a typical app needs, in one `use rustango::prelude::*;`.
pub mod prelude {
    // config + errors
    pub use crate::errors::{HttpError, RustangoError};
    pub use crate::settings::Settings;
    // http
    pub use crate::http::{AuthUser, HttpRequest, HttpResponse, Method, QueryDict};
    // routing + views
    pub use crate::urls::{named_path, path, reverse, reverse_with, Router};
    pub use crate::views::{make_view, redirect, render, View, ViewFn};
    // ORM
    pub use crate::orm::{Criteria, Model, ModelExt, Op, Q, QuerySet, Value};
    // templates
    pub use crate::templates::{Context, TplValue};
    // projects
    pub use crate::project::{App, Project, ProjectBuilder};
    // contrib-style helpers
    pub use crate::auth::{authenticate, check_password, login, logout, make_password};
    pub use crate::messages;
    pub use crate::signals;
}

/// Framework version, mirrors the Django release this API surface tracks.
pub const VERSION: &str = "6.2.0.dev0";

//! Management commands — `django.core.management` (`manage.py` / `django-admin`).
//!
//! ```text
//! rustango runserver [addr]          start the dev server
//! rustango makemigrations [app]      detect schema changes, write migration files
//! rustango migrate [app]             apply pending migrations
//! rustango showmigrations            list applied/pending migrations
//! rustango createsuperuser -u root -p secret   create or reset a superuser
//! rustango clearsessions             purge expired sessions
//! rustango check                     validate settings + registry
//! rustango startproject NAME [DIR]   scaffold a new project
//! rustango startapp NAME [DIR]       scaffold a new app
//! ```

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::project::Project;
use crate::settings::Settings;

pub const HELP: &str = r#"rustango — Django-style web framework in pure Rust

USAGE:
    rustango <COMMAND> [ARGS]

COMMANDS:
    runserver [ADDR]              Start the development server (default 127.0.0.1:8000)
    makemigrations [APP]          Write migration files for schema changes
    migrate [APP]                 Apply pending migrations
    showmigrations                Show applied/pending migrations
    createsuperuser -u NAME -p PW Create (or reset) a superuser
    clearsessions                 Delete expired sessions
    check                         Validate configuration
    startproject NAME [DIR]       Scaffold a new project
    startapp NAME [DIR]           Scaffold a new app inside a project
    help                          Show this help
"#;

/// Build the built-in demo project used by `runserver` and DB commands when
/// invoked inside the framework checkout (no user project configured).
/// Set `RUSTANGO_DB=json:<path>` for a persistent demo database and
/// `RUSTANGO_MIGRATIONS_DIR=<path>` to relocate migration files.
pub fn demo_project() -> Project {
    let database = std::env::var("RUSTANGO_DB").unwrap_or_else(|_| "memory".into());
    let migrations_dir =
        std::env::var("RUSTANGO_MIGRATIONS_DIR").map(PathBuf::from).unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("migrations"));
    let project = crate::project::Project::builder()
        .settings(
            Settings::builder()
                .database(database)
                .migrations_dir(migrations_dir)
                .build(),
        )
        .add_app(crate::project::App::new("core"))
        .urls(vec![crate::urls::named_path(
            "",
            crate::views::make_view(|_req| {
                let html = format!(
                    "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>rustango</title></head><body>\
                     <h1>It works! (rustango {})</h1>\
                     <p>This is the built-in demo project. Visit <a href=\"/admin/\">/admin/</a>.</p>\
                     </body></html>",
                    crate::VERSION
                );
                Ok(crate::http::HttpResponse::html(html))
            }),
            "home"),
        ])
        .admin(|site| {
            site.register::<crate::auth::User>(crate::admin::ModelAdmin {
                list_display: vec!["id".into(), "username".into(), "email".into(), "is_staff".into()],
                search_fields: vec!["username".into(), "email".into()],
                ..Default::default()
            });
        })
        .build();
    match project {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => panic!("demo project failed to build: {e}"),
    }
}

/// Run one management command; returns a process exit code.
pub fn run(args: &[String]) -> i32 {
    let cmd = args.first().map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("help");
    let rest = &args[1.min(args.len())..];
    match cmd {
        "help" | "--help" | "-h" => {
            println!("{HELP}");
            0
        }
        "version" | "--version" => {
            println!("rustango {}", crate::VERSION);
            0
        }
        "runserver" => {
            let addr: std::net::SocketAddr = rest
                .first()
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1:8000".to_string())
                .parse()
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| {
                    eprintln!("invalid address `{}`", rest.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default());
                    std::process::exit(2);
                });
            let project = Arc::new(demo_project());
            let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread()
                .enable_all()
                .build()
                .expect("tokio runtime");
            match runtime.block_on(crate::server::serve_with_shutdown(project, addr)) {
                Ok(()) => 0,
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("server error: {e}");
                    1
                }
            }
        }
        "makemigrations" => {
            let project = demo_project();
            let app = rest.first().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| "core".to_string());
            let metas: Vec<crate::orm::ModelMeta> =
                crate::orm::registry().read().unwrap().models.clone();
            let dir = project.settings.migrations_dir.clone();
            match crate::orm::migrations::makemigrations(
                &*project.backend,
                &dir,
                &app,
                &metas,
                false,
            ) {
                Ok(Some(m)) => {
                    println!("Wrote {} ({} ops)", dir.join(m.file_name()).display(), m.ops.len());
                    for op in &m.ops {
                        println!("  - {}", op.describe());
                    }
                    0
                }
                Ok(None) => {
                    println!("No changes detected in app `{app}`");
                    0
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("makemigrations failed: {e}");
                    1
                }
            }
        }
        "migrate" => {
            let project = demo_project();
            let dir = project.settings.migrations_dir.clone();
            let app = rest.first().map(|s| s.as_str());
            match crate::orm::migrations::migrate(&*project.backend, &dir, app) {
                Ok(applied) => {
                    if applied.is_empty() {
                        println!("Nothing to apply.");
                    }
                    for line in applied {
                        println!("Applying {line}... OK");
                    }
                    0
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("migrate failed: {e}");
                    1
                }
            }
        }
        "showmigrations" => {
            let project = demo_project();
            match crate::orm::migrations::show_migrations(&*project.backend, &project.settings.migrations_dir) {
                Ok(text) => {
                    print!("{text}");
                    0
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("showmigrations failed: {e}");
                    1
                }
            }
        }
        "createsuperuser" => {
            let project = demo_project();
            let mut username = String::new();
            let mut password = String::new();
            let mut i = 0;
            while i < rest.len() {
                match rest[i].as_str() {
                    "-u" | "--username" => {
                        username = rest.get(i + 1).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
                        i += 2;
                    }
                    "-p" | "--password" => {
                        password = rest.get(i + 1).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
                        i += 2;
                    }
                    _ => i += 1,
                }
            }
            if username.is_empty() || password.is_empty() {
                eprintln!("usage: rustango createsuperuser -u NAME -p PASSWORD");
                return 2;
            }
            match crate::auth::create_superuser(&*project.backend, &username, "", &password) {
                Ok(u) => {
                    println!("Superuser `{}` created (pk {}).", u.username, u.pk());
                    0
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("createsuperuser failed: {e}");
                    1
                }
            }
        }
        "clearsessions" => {
            let project = demo_project();
            let n = crate::sessions::Session::clear_expired(&*project.backend);
            println!("Deleted {n} expired session(s).");
            0
        }
        "check" => {
            let project = demo_project();
            let models = crate::orm::registry().read().unwrap().models.len();
            println!("rustango {} — OK", crate::VERSION);
            println!("  backend:      {}", project.settings.database);
            println!("  debug:        {}", project.settings.debug);
            println!("  admin:        {} (at /{})", project.admin.is_some(), project.settings.admin_url);
            println!("  models:       {models} registered");
            println!("  routes:       {} top-level", project.router.routes.len());
            println!("  middleware:   {}", project.stack.middlewares.len());
            0
        }
        "startproject" => startproject(rest),
        "startapp" => startapp(rest),
        other => {
            eprintln!("Unknown command `{other}`.\n\n{HELP}");
            2
        }
    }
}

fn startproject(rest: &[String]) -> i32 {
    let name = match rest.first() {
        Some(n) if !n.is_empty() => n.clone(),
        _ => {
            eprintln!("usage: rustango startproject NAME [DIR]");
            return 2;
        }
    };
    let dir = PathBuf::from(rest.get(1).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| name.clone()));
    let root = dir.join(&name);

    if root.exists() {
        eprintln!("`{}` already exists", root.display());
        return 1;
    }
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(root.join("src"));
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(root.join("templates"));

    // Locate the framework checkout so the scaffold can depend on it via a
    // path (rustango is not published to crates.io). Walk up from the
    // running executable: target/{debug,release}/rustango -> ../../Cargo.toml
    let framework_root = find_framework_root();
    let rustango_dep = match &framework_root {
        Some(path) => format!(
            "rustango = {{ path = \"{}\" }}  # or \"6.2\" once published",
            path.display()
        ),
        None => "rustango = \"6.2\"  # set RUSTANGO_SRC or a path dependency until published"
            .to_string(),
    };
    let cargo_toml = format!(
        r#"[package]
name = "{name}"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
{rustango_dep}
tokio = {{ version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }}
"#
    );
    let main_rs = r#"use rustango::prelude::*;
use rustango::views::{make_view, render};
use rustango::templates::{Context, TplValue};

fn index(req: &mut rustango::http::HttpRequest) -> Result<rustango::http::HttpResponse, rustango::errors::HttpError> {
    let mut ctx = Context::new();
    ctx.set("title", TplValue::Str("It works!".into()));
    render(req, "index.html", ctx)
}

fn main() {
    // Settings: builder defaults, overlaid by settings.toml when present.
    let mut settings = Settings::builder()
        .template_dirs(vec![std::path::PathBuf::from("templates")])
        .build();
    if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string("settings.toml") {
        settings.load_toml(&text).expect("invalid settings.toml");
    }

    let project = Project::builder()
        .settings(settings)
        .urls(vec![rustango::urls::named_path("", make_view(index), "home")])
        .admin(|_site| {
            // _site.register::<MyModel>(Default::default());
        })
        .build()
        .expect("project");

    let addr = std::env::var("RUSTANGO_ADDR")
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "127.0.0.1:8000".into())
        .parse()
        .expect("addr");
    let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread()
        .enable_all()
        .build()
        .expect("runtime");
    runtime.block_on(rustango::server::serve_with_shutdown(std::sync::Arc::new(project), addr))
        .expect("server");
}
"#;
    let index_html = r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><title>{{ title }}</title></head>
<body><h1>{{ title }}</h1>
<p>Edit <code>templates/index.html</code> and <code>src/main.rs</code> to get started.</p>
</body></html>
"#;
    let settings_toml = r#"debug = true
database = "json:db.json"
language_code = "en-us"
"#;

    let w = |p: &std::path::Path, c: &str| {
        std::fs::write(p, c).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    };
    let results = vec![
        w(&root.join("Cargo.toml"), &cargo_toml),
        w(&root.join("src/main.rs"), main_rs),
        w(&root.join("templates/index.html"), index_html),
        w(&root.join("settings.toml"), settings_toml),
    ];
    for r in results {
        if let Err(e) = r {
            eprintln!("startproject failed: {e}");
            return 1;
        }
    }
    println!("Project scaffolded at {}:", root.display());
    println!("  cd {}", root.display());
    println!("  cargo run        # starts http://127.0.0.1:8000");
    0
}

fn find_framework_root() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if let Ok(env_path) = std::env::var("RUSTANGO_SRC") {
        let p = PathBuf::from(env_path);
        if p.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
            return Some(p);
        }
    }
    let exe = std::env::current_exe().ok()?;
    let mut dir = exe.parent()?.to_path_buf();
    for _ in 0..4 {
        dir = dir.parent()?.to_path_buf();
        let cargo = dir.join("Cargo.toml");
        if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&cargo) {
            if text.contains("name = \"rustango\"") {
                return Some(dir);
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn startapp(rest: &[String]) -> i32 {
    let name = match rest.first() {
        Some(n) if !n.is_empty() && n.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c == '_') => n.clone(),
        _ => {
            eprintln!("usage: rustango startapp NAME  (lowercase name)");
            return 2;
        }
    };
    let dir = PathBuf::from(rest.get(1).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| name.clone()));
    let app_dir = dir.join(&name);
    if app_dir.exists() {
        eprintln!("`{}` already exists", app_dir.display());
        return 1;
    }
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(app_dir.join("templates"));
    let models_rs = format!(
        r#"use rustango::orm::{{Model, ModelExt, QuerySet}};
use rustango::types::DateTime;

// Declare models with the derive macro:
// #[derive(Clone, Debug, rustango::Model)]
// #[model(table = "{name}_thing")]
// pub struct Thing {{
//     #[field(auto)]
//     pub id: i64,
//     #[field(char, max = 100)]
//     pub name: String,
//     #[field(datetime, auto_now_add)]
//     pub created: DateTime,
// }}
"#
    );
    let views_rs = r#"use rustango::errors::HttpError;
use rustango::http::HttpResponse;
use rustango::http::HttpRequest;
use rustango::views::render;
use rustango::templates::Context;
"#;
    let w = |p: &std::path::Path, c: &str| std::fs::write(p, c).map_err(|e| e.to_string());
    let results = vec![
        w(&app_dir.join("models.rs"), &models_rs),
        w(&app_dir.join("views.rs"), views_rs),
        w(&app_dir.join("templates/.gitkeep"), ""),
    ];
    for r in results {
        if let Err(e) = r {
            eprintln!("startapp failed: {e}");
            return 1;
        }
    }
    println!("App `{name}` scaffolded at {}", app_dir.display());
    println!("  Wire it up in your project builder: .urls(vec![...]) and .add_app(...)");
    0
}

```rust
//! Flash messages — `django.contrib.messages`.
//!
//! Messages are stored in the session between requests, loaded into
//! `request.messages` by MessagesMiddleware, and consumed on read
//! (pop-on-read semantics, like Django).

use serde_json::json;

use crate::http::HttpRequest;

/// Message severity levels with the same tags as Django's default
/// `messages.constants`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Level {
    Debug,
    Info,
    Success,
    Warning,
    Error,
}

impl Level {
    pub fn tag(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Level::Debug => "debug",
            Level::Info => "info",
            Level::Success => "success",
            Level::Warning => "warning",
            Level::Error => "error",
        }
    }

    pub fn from_tag(tag: &str) -> Option<Level> {
        match tag {
            "debug" => Some(Level::Debug),
            "info" => Some(Level::Info),
            "success" => Some(Level::Success),
            "warning" => Some(Level::Warning),
            "error" => Some(Level::Error),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// One flash message.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Message {
    pub level: Level,
    pub text: String,
}

impl Message {
    pub fn new(level: Level, text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self { level, text: text.into() }
    }

    /// The CSS class Django's default template context produces
    /// (`message.level_tag` + `message.message`).
    pub fn css_class(&self) -> String {
        self.level.tag().to_string()
    }
}

const MESSAGES_KEY: &str = "_messages";

/// `messages.add_message(request, messages.INFO, "...")`
pub fn add_message(req: &mut HttpRequest, level: Level, text: impl Into<String>) {
    req.messages.push(Message::new(level, text));
    persist(req);
}

/// Convenience shorthands matching Django's `messages.info(request, ..)`.
pub fn info(req: &mut HttpRequest, text: impl Into<String>) { add_message(req, Level::Info, text) }
pub fn success(req: &mut HttpRequest, text: impl Into<String>) { add_message(req, Level::Success, text) }
pub fn warning(req: &mut HttpRequest, text: impl Into<String>) { add_message(req, Level::Warning, text) }
pub fn error(req: &mut HttpRequest, text: impl Into<String>) { add_message(req, Level::Error, text) }

/// Called by MessagesMiddleware at request start: load from session.
pub fn load(req: &mut HttpRequest) {
    if let Some(session) = &mut req.session {
        let stored = session
            .get(MESSAGES_KEY)
            .and_then(|v| v.as_array().cloned())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let msgs: Vec<Message> = stored
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|item| {
                let level = item.get("level").and_then(|l| l.as_str()).and_then(Level::from_tag)?;
                let text = item.get("text").and_then(|t| t.as_str())?.to_string();
                Some(Message::new(level, text))
            })
            .collect();
        req.messages = msgs;
        // Pop-on-read: clear stored copy immediately (Django semantics).
        if !stored.is_empty() {
            session.remove(MESSAGES_KEY);
        }
    }
}

/// Called by MessagesMiddleware after the view: persist newly added ones.
pub fn persist(req: &mut HttpRequest) {
    if let Some(session) = &mut req.session {
        let arr: Vec<serde_json::Value> = req
            .messages
            .iter()
            .map(|m| json!({"level": m.level.tag(), "text": m.text}))
            .collect();
        if arr.is_empty() {
            // Only mark the session modified when a stored message list is
            // actually being dropped — never touch untouched sessions.
            if session.contains(MESSAGES_KEY) {
                session.remove(MESSAGES_KEY);
            }
        } else {
            session.set(MESSAGES_KEY, json!(arr));
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::orm::InMemoryBackend;
    use std::sync::Arc;

    fn req_with_session() -> HttpRequest {
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(crate::http::Method::GET, "/");
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        req.session = Some(crate::sessions::Session::load(backend, None, 3600));
        req
    }

    #[test]
    fn levels_and_tags() {
        assert_eq!(Level::Success.tag(), "success");
        assert_eq!(Level::from_tag("warning"), Some(Level::Warning));
        assert_eq!(Level::from_tag("bogus"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn add_and_load_roundtrip() {
        let mut req = req_with_session();
        success(&mut req, "Profile saved");
        error(&mut req, "Oops");
        persist(&mut req);

        // simulate a new request with same session
        let mut req2 = req_with_session();
        let key = req.session.as_ref().unwrap().key.clone();
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()); // replaced below
        let _ = backend;
        req2.session = req.session; // move session across "requests"
        load(&mut req2);
        assert_eq!(req2.messages.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(req2.messages[0].level, Level::Success);
        assert_eq!(req2.messages[0].text, "Profile saved");
        assert_eq!(req2.messages[1].text, "Oops");
        let _ = key;
    }

    #[test]
    fn pop_on_read() {
        let mut req = req_with_session();
        info(&mut req, "note");
        persist(&mut req);
        // first read delivers the message...
        let mut req2 = req_with_session();
        req2.session = req.session;
        load(&mut req2);
        assert_eq!(req2.messages.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(req2.messages[0].text, "note");
        // ...and the second read finds nothing (pop-on-read)
        let mut req3 = req_with_session();
        req3.session = req2.session;
        load(&mut req3);
        assert_eq!(req3.messages.len(), 0);
    }
}

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/src/middleware.rs)

```rust
//! Middleware — `django.middleware`.
//!
//! The stack runs `process_request` top-down, then the view, then
//! `process_response` bottom-up — WSGI-style, exactly like Django's
//! `MIDDLEWARE` setting order.

use crate::errors::HttpError;
use crate::http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse};
use crate::views::ViewFn;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// What a request-phase middleware can do: continue down the chain or
/// short-circuit with a response (like returning a response from
/// `process_request`).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Next {
    Continue,
    ShortCircuit(HttpResponse),
}

/// A middleware component.
pub trait Middleware: Send + Sync {
    fn process_request(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
        Next::Continue
    }

    /// Return Ok(()) to proceed to the view; Err to abort (CSRF etc.).
    fn process_view(&self, _req: &HttpRequest) -> Result<(), HttpError> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn process_response(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest, _res: &mut HttpResponse) {}
}

/// The assembled chain: middlewares + the terminal view.
pub struct MiddlewareStack {
    pub middlewares: Vec<Arc<dyn Middleware>>,
}

impl MiddlewareStack {
    pub fn new(middlewares: Vec<Arc<dyn Middleware>>) -> Self {
        Self { middlewares }
    }

    /// Run the full pipeline for one request.
    pub fn dispatch(
        &self,
        req: &mut HttpRequest,
        view: &ViewFn,
    ) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
        // process_request top-down; short-circuits skip the view.
        for (i, mw) in self.middlewares.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Next::ShortCircuit(res) = mw.process_request(req) {
                let mut res = res;
                // Django semantics: the response phase only runs for the
                // middlewares up to and including the one that produced the
                // response (the ones below never saw the request).
                self.run_response_phase(req, &mut res, Some(&self.middlewares[..=i]));
                return Ok(res);
            }
        }

        // process_view phase (CSRF etc.)
        for mw in &self.middlewares {
            mw.process_view(req)?;
        }

        let mut result = view(req);

        if let Ok(res) = &mut result {
            self.run_response_phase(req, res, None);
        }
        result
    }

    /// Run only the response phase (used for error responses so cookies
    /// like CSRF/session still get set — Django does the same).
    pub fn run_response(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        self.run_response_phase(req, res, None);
    }

    fn run_response_phase(
        &self,
        req: &mut HttpRequest,
        res: &mut HttpResponse,
        up_to: Option<&[Arc<dyn Middleware>]>,
    ) {
        let list: &[Arc<dyn Middleware>] = up_to.unwrap_or(&self.middlewares);
        for mw in list.iter().rev() {
            mw.process_response(req, res);
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Built-in middlewares
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// `SecurityMiddleware` — sets hardened security headers.
pub struct SecurityMiddleware;

impl Middleware for SecurityMiddleware {
    fn process_response(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        res.headers
            .set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff");
        res.headers.set("Referrer-Policy", "same-origin");
        res.headers.set(
            "Strict-Transport-Security",
            "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains",
        );
    }
}

/// `ClickjackingMiddleware` — X-Frame-Options (default DENY, like Django).
pub struct ClickjackingMiddleware {
    pub value: String,
}

impl Middleware for ClickjackingMiddleware {
    fn process_response(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        if !res.headers.get("X-Frame-Options").is_some() {
            res.headers.set("X-Frame-Options", self.value.clone());
        }
    }
}

/// `GZipMiddleware` — compress large text responses (miniz_oxide, pure Rust).
pub struct GZipMiddleware {
    pub min_length: usize,
}

impl Middleware for GZipMiddleware {
    fn process_response(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        let accepts = req
            .headers
            .get("accept-encoding")
            .map(|v| v.to_lowercase().contains("gzip"))
            .unwrap_or(false);
        if !accepts {
            return;
        }
        if res.content_length() < self.min_length {
            return;
        }
        let compressible = res
            .headers
            .get("Content-Type")
            .map(|t| {
                t.starts_with("text/")
                    || t.contains("json")
                    || t.contains("javascript")
                    || t.contains("xml")
            })
            .unwrap_or(false);
        if !compressible {
            return;
        }
        let mut encoder = flate2::write::GzEncoder::new(
            Vec::with_capacity(res.content_length() / 2),
            flate2::Compression::default(),
        );
        if std::io::Write::write_all(&mut encoder, res.body()).is_ok() {
            if let Ok(compressed) = encoder.finish() {
                res.set_body(compressed);
                res.headers.set("Content-Encoding", "gzip");
                res.headers.remove("Content-Length");
            }
        }
    }
}

/// `CommonMiddleware` — APPEND_SLASH: redirect `/missing` to `/missing/`
/// when the latter resolves, and set Content-Length.
pub struct CommonMiddleware {
    pub router: Arc<crate::urls::Router>,
    pub append_slash: bool,
}

impl Middleware for CommonMiddleware {
    fn process_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
        if self.append_slash
            && !req.path.ends_with('/')
            && req.method.is_safe()
        {
            let with_slash = format!("{}/", req.path);
            if self.router.matches(&with_slash) {
                // Preserve the query string (`/search?q=rust` must redirect
                // to `/search/?q=rust`, not lose `?q=rust` — the old code
                // dropped it, and browsers cached the broken target).
                // Django issues a permanent (301) redirect for APPEND_SLASH;
                // with the query preserved the redirect is correct, so the
                // permanent status is safe to keep.
                let target = match req.full_path.split_once('?') {
                    Some((_, qs)) => format!("{with_slash}?{qs}"),
                    None => with_slash,
                };
                return Next::ShortCircuit(HttpResponse::redirect_permanent(target));
            }
        }
        Next::Continue
    }

    fn process_response(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        res.headers
            .set("Content-Length", res.content_length().to_string());
    }
}

/// `SessionMiddleware` — loads `request.session` from the cookie and
/// persists it after the view.
pub struct SessionMiddleware {
    pub cookie_name: String,
    pub cookie_age: i64,
    pub backend: Arc<dyn crate::orm::Backend>,
}

impl Middleware for SessionMiddleware {
    fn process_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
        let key = req.cookie(&self.cookie_name).map(|s| s.to_string());
        req.session = Some(crate::sessions::Session::load(
            self.backend.clone(),
            key.as_deref(),
            self.cookie_age,
        ));
        Next::Continue
    }

    fn process_response(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        crate::messages::persist(req);
        // Django only writes the session when it was modified during the
        // request — never for untouched anonymous sessions.
        if let Some(session) = req.session.as_mut() {
            if session.modified {
                session.save();
            }
        }
        crate::auth::apply_session_cookie(req, res, &self.cookie_name, self.cookie_age);
    }
}

/// `AuthMiddleware` — resolves `request.user` from the session.
pub struct AuthMiddleware;

impl Middleware for AuthMiddleware {
    fn process_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
        crate::auth::get_user(req);
        Next::Continue
    }
}

/// `MessagesMiddleware` — loads flash messages into the request and
/// persists new ones after the view.
pub struct MessagesMiddleware;

impl Middleware for MessagesMiddleware {
    fn process_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
        crate::messages::load(req);
        Next::Continue
    }

    fn process_response(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest, _res: &mut HttpResponse) {
        // messages::add_message already persists to the session on write
        // (pop-on-read semantics), so nothing to do here.
    }
}

/// Build the default middleware stack, mirroring Django's default order:
/// Security -> Session -> Common -> Csrf -> Auth -> Messages ->
/// Clickjacking -> GZip.
pub fn default_stack(
    settings: &crate::settings::Settings,
    backend: Arc<dyn crate::orm::Backend>,
    router: Arc<crate::urls::Router>,
) -> Vec<Arc<dyn Middleware>> {
    let mut stack: Vec<Arc<dyn Middleware>> = Vec::new();
    if settings.use_security {
        stack.push(Arc::new(SecurityMiddleware));
    }
    stack.push(Arc::new(SessionMiddleware {
        cookie_name: settings.session_cookie_name.clone(),
        cookie_age: settings.session_cookie_age,
        backend: backend.clone(),
    }));
    stack.push(Arc::new(CommonMiddleware {
        router: router.clone(),
        append_slash: true,
    }));
    if settings.csrf_enabled {
        stack.push(Arc::new(crate::csrf::CsrfMiddleware {
            cookie_name: settings.csrf_cookie_name.clone(),
        }));
    }
    stack.push(Arc::new(AuthMiddleware));
    stack.push(Arc::new(MessagesMiddleware));
    if settings.use_clickjacking {
        stack.push(Arc::new(ClickjackingMiddleware {
            value: settings.x_frame_options.clone(),
        }));
    }
    if settings.use_gzip {
        stack.push(Arc::new(GZipMiddleware {
            min_length: settings.gzip_min_length,
        }));
    }
    stack
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::http::Method;
    use crate::orm::InMemoryBackend;
    use crate::views::{make_view, ViewFn};
    use std::sync::Arc as StdArc;

    fn ok_view() -> ViewFn {
        make_view(|req| {
            Ok(HttpResponse::html(format!("hello {}", req.user.username())))
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn stack_request_and_response_order() {
        struct Add(String);
        impl Middleware for Add {
            fn process_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
                let mut m = req.params.clone();
                m.insert("trace".into(), self.0.clone());
                req.params = m;
                Next::Continue
            }
            fn process_response(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest, res: &mut HttpResponse) {
                let body = res.body_string();
                res.set_body(format!("{}<{}", body, self.0));
            }
        }

        let stack = MiddlewareStack::new(vec![
            StdArc::new(Add("A".into())),
            StdArc::new(Add("B".into())),
        ]);
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        let res = stack.dispatch(&mut req, &ok_view()).unwrap();
        // request phase top-down (B overwrites A), response phase bottom-up
        assert!(res.body_string().contains("<B<A"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn short_circuit_skips_view() {
        struct Block;
        impl Middleware for Block {
            fn process_request(&self, _req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Next {
                Next::ShortCircuit(HttpResponse::text("blocked"))
            }
        }
        let stack = MiddlewareStack::new(vec![StdArc::new(Block)]);
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        let res = stack.dispatch(&mut req, &ok_view()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(res.body_string(), "blocked");
    }

    #[test]
    fn process_view_can_abort() {
        struct Deny;
        impl Middleware for Deny {
            fn process_view(&self, _req: &HttpRequest) -> Result<(), HttpError> {
                Err(HttpError::PermissionDenied("no".into()))
            }
        }
        let stack = MiddlewareStack::new(vec![StdArc::new(Deny)]);
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        let err = stack.dispatch(&mut req, &ok_view()).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.status(), 403);
    }

    #[test]
    fn append_slash_redirect() {
        use crate::urls::{path, Router};
        let view = make_view(|_req| Ok(HttpResponse::text("")));
        let router = StdArc::new(Router::new(vec![path("polls/", view)]));
        let mw = CommonMiddleware { router, append_slash: true };
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/polls");
        match mw.process_request(&mut req) {
            Next::ShortCircuit(res) => {
                // Django semantics: permanent (301) redirect, now with the
                // query string preserved so the cached target is correct.
                assert_eq!(res.status, 301);
                assert_eq!(res.headers.get("Location"), Some("/polls/"));
            }
            _ => panic!("expected redirect"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn append_slash_preserves_query_string() {
        use crate::urls::{path, Router};
        // Regression: `/search?q=rust` used to redirect to bare `/search/`,
        // dropping the query string; browsers then cached the broken target.
        let view = make_view(|_req| Ok(HttpResponse::text("")));
        let router = StdArc::new(Router::new(vec![path("search/", view)]));
        let mw = CommonMiddleware { router, append_slash: true };
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/search?q=rust");
        match mw.process_request(&mut req) {
            Next::ShortCircuit(res) => {
                assert_eq!(res.status, 301);
                assert_eq!(res.headers.get("Location"), Some("/search/?q=rust"));
            }
            _ => panic!("expected redirect"),
        }
        // No query string -> no `?` appended.
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/search");
        match mw.process_request(&mut req) {
            Next::ShortCircuit(res) => {
                assert_eq!(res.headers.get("Location"), Some("/search/"));
            }
            _ => panic!("expected redirect"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn gzip_compresses_large_text() {
        let mw = GZipMiddleware { min_length: 100 };
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        req.headers.set("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate");
        let mut res = HttpResponse::html("x".repeat(1000));
        mw.process_response(&mut req, &mut res);
        assert_eq!(res.headers.get("Content-Encoding"), Some("gzip"));
        assert!(res.content_length() < 1000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn security_headers() {
        let mw = SecurityMiddleware;
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        let mut res = HttpResponse::text("x");
        mw.process_response(&mut req, &mut res);
        assert_eq!(res.headers.get("X-Content-Type-Options"), Some("nosniff"));
        let cj = ClickjackingMiddleware { value: "DENY".into() };
        cj.process_response(&mut req, &mut res);
        assert_eq!(res.headers.get("X-Frame-Options"), Some("DENY"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_middleware_load_and_persist() {
        let backend: StdArc<dyn crate::orm::Backend> = StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mw = SessionMiddleware {
            cookie_name: "sessionid".into(),
            cookie_age: 3600,
            backend: backend.clone(),
        };
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        assert!(matches!(mw.process_request(&mut req), Next::Continue));
        assert!(req.session.is_some());
        // write something and persist via response phase
        req.session.as_mut().unwrap().set("k", serde_json::json!(1));
        let mut res = HttpResponse::text("ok");
        mw.process_response(&mut req, &mut res);
        assert!(res.cookie_value("sessionid").is_some());
        // new request with cookie sees data
        let key = res.cookie_value("sessionid").unwrap();
        let mut req2 = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        req2.cookies.insert("sessionid".into(), key);
        mw.process_request(&mut req2);
        assert_eq!(req2.session.as_ref().unwrap().get_int("k"), Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn untouched_session_is_not_persisted() {
        // Django does not create a session row (or send a cookie) for a
        // request that never touches request.session.
        let backend: StdArc<dyn crate::orm::Backend> = StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mw = SessionMiddleware {
            cookie_name: "sessionid".into(),
            cookie_age: 3600,
            backend: backend.clone(),
        };
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        mw.process_request(&mut req);
        let mut res = HttpResponse::text("ok");
        mw.process_response(&mut req, &mut res);
        assert!(res.cookie_value("sessionid").is_none());
        assert_eq!(backend.count("django_session", &crate::orm::Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 0);
    }
}
