```rust
//! Storage backends. The [`Backend`] trait is the `django.db.backends`
//! equivalent; two pure-Rust implementations ship in the box:
//!
//! * [`InMemoryBackend`] — everything lives in RAM (tests, scratch work).
//! * [`JsonFileBackend`] — the same engine, snapshotted to a JSON file on
//!   every write (durable dev storage, no C SQLite needed).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::{eval_criteria, order_rows, ColumnDesc, Criteria, FieldKind, OrmResult, Row, Value};

/// What a storage backend must provide. All operations are synchronous and
/// thread-safe; criteria evaluation (incl. FK traversal) happens inside the
/// backend so callers work with plain `Value` rows.
pub trait Backend: Send + Sync {
    /// Insert a full row; returns the assigned primary key.
    fn insert(&self, table: &str, row: Row) -> OrmResult<i64>;
    /// Update rows matching `crit`; `updates` are (column_index, new_value).
    /// Returns the number of rows updated.
    fn update(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria, updates: &[(usize, Value)]) -> OrmResult<usize>;
    /// Delete rows matching `crit`; returns the number deleted.
    fn delete(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria) -> OrmResult<usize>;
    /// Select rows: criteria + order (`(field, desc)`) + limit + offset.
    fn select(
        &self,
        table: &str,
        crit: &Criteria,
        order: &[(String, bool)],
        limit: Option<usize>,
        offset: Option<usize>,
    ) -> OrmResult<Vec<Row>>;
    fn count(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria) -> OrmResult<usize>;

    // -- schema (migration support) ---------------------------------------
    fn create_table(&self, table: &str, columns: Vec<ColumnDesc>) -> OrmResult<()>;
    fn add_column(&self, table: &str, column: ColumnDesc) -> OrmResult<()>;
    fn drop_table(&self, table: &str) -> OrmResult<()>;
    fn tables(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    fn columns(&self, table: &str) -> Vec<ColumnDesc>;

    // -- migration bookkeeping --------------------------------------------
    fn ensure_migration_meta(&self) -> OrmResult<()>;
    fn applied_migrations(&self) -> OrmResult<Vec<(String, String)>>;
    fn record_migration(&self, app: &str, name: &str) -> OrmResult<()>;

    /// Optional hook so the JSON backend can flush its snapshot.
    fn flush(&self) -> OrmResult<()> { Ok(()) }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Shared engine
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct Engine {
    tables: HashMap<String, Table>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct Table {
    columns: Vec<ColumnDesc>,
    rows: Vec<Row>,
    next_pk: i64,
}

impl Engine {
    fn table(&self, name: &str) -> OrmResult<&Table> {
        self.tables
            .get(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::errors::OrmError::Backend(format!("no such table: {name}")))
    }

    fn table_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> OrmResult<&mut Table> {
        self.tables
            .get_mut(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::errors::OrmError::Backend(format!("no such table: {name}")))
    }

    /// Insert with auto-pk, defaults and unique-constraint enforcement.
    fn insert_row(&mut self, table: &str, mut row: Row) -> OrmResult<i64> {
        let cols = self.table(table)?.columns.clone();

        // 1. Auto primary key.
        let has_auto_pk = cols
            .first()
            .map(|c| c.primary_key && c.kind == FieldKind::Auto)
            .unwrap_or(false);
        if has_auto_pk {
            let needs_id = row
                .first()
                .map(|v| v == &Value::Null || v.as_int() == Some(0) || v.as_int().is_none())
                .unwrap_or(true);
            let t = self.table_mut(table)?;
            if needs_id {
                t.next_pk += 1;
                if row.is_empty() {
                    row.push(Value::Int(t.next_pk));
                } else {
                    row[0] = Value::Int(t.next_pk);
                }
            } else if let Some(id) = row.first().and_then(|v| v.as_int()) {
                if id > t.next_pk {
                    t.next_pk = id;
                }
            }
        }

        // 2. Defaults + auto_now_add.
        for (i, col) in cols.iter().enumerate() {
            if i >= row.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let is_null = row[i] == Value::Null;
            if !is_null {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(d) = &col.default {
                row[i] = d.clone();
            } else if col.kind == FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd {
                row[i] = Value::DateTime(chrono::Utc::now());
            }
        }

        // 3. Unique constraints (scan in place, no recursion).
        {
            let t = self.table(table)?;
            for (i, col) in cols.iter().enumerate() {
                if !col.unique || col.primary_key {
                    continue;
                }
                let val = row.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                if val == Value::Null {
                    continue;
                }
                for other in &t.rows {
                    let other_val = other.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                    if other_val == val {
                        let other_pk = other.first().and_then(|v| v.as_int());
                        let my_pk = row.first().and_then(|v| v.as_int());
                        if other_pk != my_pk {
                            return Err(crate::errors::OrmError::InvalidValue(
                                col.name.clone(),
                                "unique constraint violated".into(),
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // 4. Explicit primary keys must be unique: a caller-supplied pk that
        // already exists would silently create a duplicate row and make
        // update/delete-by-pk hit every copy.
        let pk = row.first().and_then(|v| v.as_int()).unwrap_or(0);
        if pk != 0 {
            let t = self.table(table)?;
            if t.rows
                .iter()
                .any(|r| r.first().and_then(|v| v.as_int()) == Some(pk))
            {
                return Err(crate::errors::OrmError::Backend(format!(
                    "duplicate primary key {pk} in table {table}"
                )));
            }
        }

        let t = self.table_mut(table)?;
        t.rows.push(row);
        Ok(pk)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// InMemoryBackend
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Pure in-memory backend. Cheap, fast, non-durable.
pub struct InMemoryBackend {
    engine: RwLock<Engine>,
}

impl InMemoryBackend {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { engine: RwLock::new(Engine::default()) }
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_engine(e: Engine) -> InMemoryBackend {
        Self { engine: RwLock::new(e) }
    }

    /// All rows of a table (test/debug helper).
    pub fn debug_rows(&self, table: &str) -> Vec<Row> {
        self.select(table, &Criteria::any(), &[], None, None).unwrap_or_default()
    }
}

impl Default for InMemoryBackend {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::new() }
}

/// Row identity used to re-find snapshot rows in phase 2 without re-matching
/// by full value equality: the primary key (first column) when non-Null,
/// otherwise the whole row (pk-less tables keep the previous behavior).
///
/// Matching between the two lock phases by full row equality mutated rows
/// inserted concurrently between the phases (and every value-duplicate row)
/// as collateral damage; identity matching touches exactly the rows that
/// matched the criteria under the lock.
enum MatchId {
    Pk(Value),
    FullRow(Row),
}

impl MatchId {
    fn of(row: &Row) -> Self {
        match row.first() {
            Some(pk) if pk != &Value::Null => MatchId::Pk(pk.clone()),
            _ => MatchId::FullRow(row.clone()),
        }
    }

    fn matches(&self, row: &Row) -> bool {
        match self {
            MatchId::Pk(pk) => row.first() == Some(pk),
            MatchId::FullRow(snapshot) => snapshot == row,
        }
    }
}

impl Backend for InMemoryBackend {
    fn insert(&self, table: &str, row: Row) -> OrmResult<i64> {
        self.engine.write().unwrap().insert_row(table, row)
    }

    fn update(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria, updates: &[(usize, Value)]) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        // Phase 1 (read lock): snapshot + evaluate criteria, capturing the
        // identity (primary key / id value) of every matching row.
        // FK-traversal criteria call back into `select()`, which must not
        // happen while the write lock is held (same-thread re-entry would
        // deadlock).
        let matched_ids: Vec<MatchId> = {
            let engine = self.engine.read().unwrap();
            let t = engine.table(table)?;
            let cols = t.columns.clone();
            t.rows
                .iter()
                .filter(|row| eval_criteria(self, table, row, &cols, crit))
                .map(|row| MatchId::of(row))
                .collect()
        };
        if matched_ids.is_empty() {
            return Ok(0);
        }
        // Phase 2 (write lock): apply updates by row identity captured in
        // phase 1 — never by re-matching values. Full-value equality between
        // the two lock phases mutated concurrent identical inserts and every
        // duplicate row as collateral damage.
        let mut engine = self.engine.write().unwrap();
        let t = engine.table_mut(table)?;
        let mut n = 0;
        for row in t.rows.iter_mut() {
            if matched_ids.iter().any(|m| m.matches(row)) {
                for (idx, val) in updates {
                    if *idx < row.len() {
                        row[*idx] = val.clone();
                    }
                }
                n += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(n)
    }

    fn delete(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        // Phase 1 (read lock): resolve matching row identities (see `update`).
        let matched_ids: Vec<MatchId> = {
            let engine = self.engine.read().unwrap();
            let t = engine.table(table)?;
            let cols = t.columns.clone();
            t.rows
                .iter()
                .filter(|row| eval_criteria(self, table, row, &cols, crit))
                .map(|row| MatchId::of(row))
                .collect()
        };
        if matched_ids.is_empty() {
            return Ok(0);
        }
        // Phase 2 (write lock): drop rows whose identity was captured in
        // phase 1.
        let mut engine = self.engine.write().unwrap();
        let t = engine.table_mut(table)?;
        let before = t.rows.len();
        t.rows.retain(|row| !matched_ids.iter().any(|m| m.matches(row)));
        Ok(before - t.rows.len())
    }

    fn select(
        &self,
        table: &str,
        crit: &Criteria,
        order: &[(String, bool)],
        limit: Option<usize>,
        offset: Option<usize>,
    ) -> OrmResult<Vec<Row>> {
        let engine = self.engine.read().unwrap();
        let t = engine.table(table)?;
        let cols = t.columns.clone();
        let mut matched: Vec<Row> = t
            .rows
            .iter()
            .filter(|row| eval_criteria(self, table, row, &cols, crit))
            .cloned()
            .collect();
        drop(engine);
        order_rows(self, table, &mut matched, &cols, order);
        if let Some(off) = offset {
            if off >= matched.len() {
                return Ok(vec![]);
            }
            matched.drain(0..off);
        }
        if let Some(lim) = limit {
            matched.truncate(lim);
        }
        Ok(matched)
    }

    fn count(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        let engine = self.engine.read().unwrap();
        let t = engine.table(table)?;
        let cols = t.columns.clone();
        Ok(t.rows
            .iter()
            .filter(|row| eval_criteria(self, table, row, &cols, crit))
            .count())
    }

    fn create_table(&self, table: &str, columns: Vec<ColumnDesc>) -> OrmResult<()> {
        let mut engine = self.engine.write().unwrap();
        if engine.tables.contains_key(table) {
            return Ok(()); // idempotent, like IF NOT EXISTS
        }
        engine.tables.insert(
            table.to_string(),
            Table { columns, rows: vec![], next_pk: 0 },
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    fn add_column(&self, table: &str, column: ColumnDesc) -> OrmResult<()> {
        let mut engine = self.engine.write().unwrap();
        let t = engine.table_mut(table)?;
        if t.columns.iter().any(|c| c.name == column.name) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let fill = column.default.clone().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        t.columns.push(column);
        for row in t.rows.iter_mut() {
            row.push(fill.clone());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn drop_table(&self, table: &str) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.engine.write().unwrap().tables.remove(table);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn tables(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut v: Vec<String> = self.engine.read().unwrap().tables.keys().cloned().collect();
        v.sort();
        v
    }

    fn columns(&self, table: &str) -> Vec<ColumnDesc> {
        self.engine.read().unwrap().tables.get(table).map(|t| t.columns.clone()).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    fn ensure_migration_meta(&self) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.create_table(
            "_migrations",
            vec![
                ColumnDesc::auto("id"),
                ColumnDesc::char("app", 100),
                ColumnDesc::char("name", 255),
                ColumnDesc::datetime("applied_at", false),
            ],
        )
    }

    fn applied_migrations(&self) -> OrmResult<Vec<(String, String)>> {
        let crit = Criteria::any();
        let spec = vec![(String::from("id"), false)];
        let rows = self.select("_migrations", &crit, &spec, None, None)?;
        Ok(rows
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|r| match (r.get(1), r.get(2)) {
                (Some(Value::Text(a)), Some(Value::Text(b))) => Some((a.clone(), b.clone())),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect())
    }

    fn record_migration(&self, app: &str, name: &str) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.insert(
            "_migrations",
            vec![
                Value::Null,
                Value::Text(app.to_string()),
                Value::Text(name.to_string()),
                Value::DateTime(chrono::Utc::now()),
            ],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// JsonFileBackend
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
struct SnapshotTable {
    columns: Vec<ColumnDesc>,
    rows: Vec<Row>,
}

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
struct Snapshot {
    tables: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, SnapshotTable>,
}

/// In-memory engine persisted to a JSON file. Every mutating call re-writes
/// the snapshot atomically (write temp file, rename over the target), so a
/// crash can never leave a half-written database behind.
pub struct JsonFileBackend {
    engine: InMemoryBackend,
    path: PathBuf,
}

impl JsonFileBackend {
    /// Open (or create) a database file.
    pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> OrmResult<Self> {
        let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();
        let engine = if path.exists() {
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)?;
            let snap: Snapshot = serde_json::from_str(&text)?;
            let mut e = Engine::default();
            for (name, t) in snap.tables {
                let max: i64 = t
                    .rows
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|r| r.first().and_then(|v| v.as_int()))
                    .max()
                    .unwrap_or(0);
                e.tables.insert(name, Table { columns: t.columns, rows: t.rows, next_pk: max });
            }
            InMemoryBackend::with_engine(e)
        } else {
            InMemoryBackend::new()
        };
        let backend = Self { engine, path };
        backend.flush()?;
        Ok(backend)
    }
}

impl std::ops::Deref for JsonFileBackend {
    type Target = InMemoryBackend;
    fn deref(&self) -> &InMemoryBackend { &self.engine }
}

impl Backend for JsonFileBackend {
    fn insert(&self, table: &str, row: Row) -> OrmResult<i64> {
        let pk = self.engine.insert(table, row)?;
        self.flush()?;
        Ok(pk)
    }

    fn update(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria, updates: &[(usize, Value)]) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        let n = self.engine.update(table, crit, updates)?;
        if n > 0 {
            self.flush()?;
        }
        Ok(n)
    }

    fn delete(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        let n = self.engine.delete(table, crit)?;
        if n > 0 {
            self.flush()?;
        }
        Ok(n)
    }

    fn select(
        &self,
        table: &str,
        crit: &Criteria,
        order: &[(String, bool)],
        limit: Option<usize>,
        offset: Option<usize>,
    ) -> OrmResult<Vec<Row>> {
        self.engine.select(table, crit, order, limit, offset)
    }

    fn count(&self, table: &str, crit: &Criteria) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        self.engine.count(table, crit)
    }

    fn create_table(&self, table: &str, columns: Vec<ColumnDesc>) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.engine.create_table(table, columns)?;
        // The engine's create_table is idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS): when the
        // table already existed nothing changed, so skip the full-DB rewrite
        // — this used to flush on EVERY request via Session::load.
        if self.engine.tables().iter().any(|t| t == table) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        self.flush()
    }

    fn add_column(&self, table: &str, column: ColumnDesc) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.engine.add_column(table, column)?;
        self.flush()
    }

    fn drop_table(&self, table: &str) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.engine.drop_table(table)?;
        self.flush()
    }

    fn tables(&self) -> Vec<String> { self.engine.tables() }

    fn columns(&self, table: &str) -> Vec<ColumnDesc> { self.engine.columns(table) }

    fn ensure_migration_meta(&self) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.engine.ensure_migration_meta()?;
        self.flush()
    }

    fn applied_migrations(&self) -> OrmResult<Vec<(String, String)>> {
        self.engine.applied_migrations()
    }

    fn record_migration(&self, app: &str, name: &str) -> OrmResult<()> {
        self.engine.record_migration(app, name)?;
        self.flush()
    }

    fn flush(&self) -> OrmResult<()> {
        let mut snap = Snapshot::default();
        for table in self.engine.tables() {
            let cols = self.engine.columns(&table);
            let crit = Criteria::any();
            let rows = self.engine.select(&table, &crit, &[], None, None)?;
            snap.tables.insert(table, SnapshotTable { columns: cols, rows });
        }
        let text = serde_json::to_string(&snap)?;
        if let Some(parent) = self.path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
        }
        // Unique temp name: two threads flushing concurrently must not
        // clobber each other's temp file before the atomic rename.
        let tmp = self
            .path
            .with_extension(format!("tmp-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple()));
        std::fs::write(&tmp, text)?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, &self.path)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Build a backend from a settings alias: `memory` | `json:<path>`.
pub fn backend_from_alias(alias: &str) -> OrmResult<Arc<dyn Backend>> {
    if alias == "memory" || alias.is_empty() {
        Ok(Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()))
    } else if let Some(path) = alias.strip_prefix("json:") {
        Ok(Arc::new(JsonFileBackend::open(path)?))
    } else {
        Err(crate::errors::OrmError::Backend(format!(
            "unknown backend `{alias}` (supported: memory, json:<path>)"
        )))
    }
}

/// Re-export the shared unique checker for backend implementors.
pub use super::check_unique as verify_unique;

#[allow(dead_code)]
fn _assert_send_sync() {
    fn f<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    f::<InMemoryBackend>();
    f::<JsonFileBackend>();
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::orm::Op;

    fn user_cols() -> Vec<ColumnDesc> {
        vec![
            ColumnDesc::auto("id"),
            ColumnDesc::char("username", 150).unique(),
            ColumnDesc::boolean("is_active", true),
        ]
    }

    fn row(id: Option<i64>, name: &str, active: bool) -> Row {
        vec![
            id.map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
            Value::Text(name.into()),
            Value::Bool(active),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn insert_auto_pk_and_select() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        let id = b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", true)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(id, 1);
        let id2 = b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "bob", false)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(id2, 2);

        let all = b.select("auth_user", &Criteria::any(), &[], None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(all.len(), 2);

        let crit = Criteria::eq("username", Value::Text("alice".into()));
        let alice = b.select("auth_user", &crit, &[], None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(alice.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(alice[0][1], Value::Text("alice".into()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn explicit_pk_respected() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        let id = b.insert("auth_user", row(Some(41), "zoe", true)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(id, 41);
        let next = b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "abe", true)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(next, 42); // counter advanced past explicit pk
    }

    #[test]
    fn update_delete_count() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", true)).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "bob", true)).unwrap();

        let crit = Criteria::eq("username", Value::Text("bob".into()));
        let n = b.update("auth_user", &crit, &[(2, Value::Bool(false))]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 1);

        assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::eq("is_active", Value::Bool(false))).unwrap(), 1);
        let n = b.delete("auth_user", &Criteria::eq("is_active", Value::Bool(false))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 1);
        assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn update_delete_match_rows_by_identity_not_value() {
        // Regression (M31): phase 2 used to re-match rows by full VALUE
        // equality against phase-1 snapshots, so a row inserted concurrently
        // between the two lock phases with identical values was mutated too,
        // and duplicate value-rows all got updated/deleted. Matching must be
        // by the captured unique primary-key/id instead.
        let snapshot = row(Some(1), "same", true);
        let id = MatchId::of(&snapshot);
        // Same identity -> match.
        assert!(id.matches(&row(Some(1), "same", true)));
        // Concurrent identical insert (different pk, same values) -> no match.
        assert!(!id.matches(&row(Some(2), "same", true)));
        // Same identity with mutated values (row being updated) -> still matches.
        assert!(id.matches(&row(Some(1), "changed", false)));
        // A Null-pk row falls back to whole-row identity.
        let null_row = row(None, "anon", true);
        let null_id = MatchId::of(&null_row);
        assert!(matches!(null_id, MatchId::FullRow(_)));
        assert!(null_id.matches(&row(None, "anon", true)));
        assert!(!null_id.matches(&row(None, "other", true)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn update_by_pk_touches_exactly_the_matching_row() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        let cols = vec![ColumnDesc::auto("id"), ColumnDesc::char("name", 50)];
        b.create_table("dupes", cols).unwrap();
        let id1 = b.insert("dupes", vec![Value::Null, Value::Text("same".into())]).unwrap();
        let id2 = b.insert("dupes", vec![Value::Null, Value::Text("same".into())]).unwrap();
        assert_ne!(id1, id2);
        let n = b
            .update("dupes", &Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(id1)), &[(1, Value::Text("changed".into()))])
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 1);
        let rows = b.select("dupes", &Criteria::any(), &[], None, None).unwrap();
        let changed = rows.iter().filter(|r| r[1] == Value::Text("changed".into())).count();
        assert_eq!(changed, 1);
        let n = b.delete("dupes", &Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(id2))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 1);
        assert_eq!(b.count("dupes", &Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fk_traversal_criteria_do_not_deadlock_update_delete() {
        // Regression: update()/delete() used to evaluate criteria while the
        // write lock was held; FK-traversal criteria call back into
        // select(), which deadlocked the same thread. Must complete.
        use crate::orm::{register_model, ModelMeta};

        let user_cols = vec![ColumnDesc::auto("id"), ColumnDesc::char("username", 150)];
        let post_cols = vec![
            ColumnDesc::auto("id"),
            ColumnDesc::char("title", 100),
            ColumnDesc::foreign_key("author_id", "fktr_user"),
        ];
        register_model(ModelMeta {
            table: "fktr_user".into(),
            columns: user_cols.clone(),
            fks: vec![],
        });
        register_model(ModelMeta {
            table: "fktr_post".into(),
            columns: post_cols.clone(),
            fks: vec![("author_id".into(), "fktr_user".into())],
        });

        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("fktr_user", user_cols).unwrap();
        b.create_table("fktr_post", post_cols).unwrap();
        let uid = b
            .insert("fktr_user", vec![Value::Null, Value::Text("ada".into())])
            .unwrap();
        b.insert(
            "fktr_post",
            vec![Value::Null, Value::Text("one".into()), Value::Int(uid)],
        )
        .unwrap();
        b.insert(
            "fktr_post",
            vec![Value::Null, Value::Text("two".into()), Value::Int(uid + 1)],
        )
        .unwrap();

        let crit = Criteria::eq("author_id__username", Value::Text("ada".into()));
        let n = b
            .update("fktr_post", &crit, &[(1, Value::Text("edited".into()))])
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 1);
        let n = b.delete("fktr_post", &crit).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 1);
        assert_eq!(b.count("fktr_post", &Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unique_constraint_enforced() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", true)).unwrap();
        let dup = b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", false));
        assert!(dup.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn order_limit_offset() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        for name in ["carol", "alice", "bob"] {
            b.insert("auth_user", row(None, name, true)).unwrap();
        }
        let mut spec = vec![(String::from("username"), false)];
        let asc = b.select("auth_user", &Criteria::any(), &spec, None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(asc[0][1], Value::Text("alice".into()));
        spec[0].1 = true;
        let desc = b.select("auth_user", &Criteria::any(), &spec, None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(desc[0][1], Value::Text("carol".into()));
        let page = b.select("auth_user", &Criteria::any(), &[], Some(2), Some(1)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(page.len(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn debug_and_probe() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", true)).unwrap();
        let single = b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::eq("is_active", Value::Bool(true))).unwrap();
        let contains = b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::contains("username", "l")).unwrap();
        let both = b.count("auth_user", &(Criteria::eq("is_active", Value::Bool(true)) & Criteria::contains("username", "l"))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(single, 1, "single eq");
        let eq_name = b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::eq("username", Value::Text("alice".into()))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(eq_name, 1, "eq username");
        let gt = b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::cond("id", Op::Gt, Value::Int(0))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(gt, 1, "gt id");
        let icontains = b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::icontains("username", "LIC")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(icontains, 1, "icontains");
        assert_eq!(contains, 1, "contains");
        assert_eq!(both, 1, "AND");
    }

    #[test]
    fn and_or_not_criteria() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", true)).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "bob", false)).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "carol", true)).unwrap();

        let crit =
            Criteria::eq("is_active", Value::Bool(true)) & Criteria::contains("username", "ali");
        assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &crit).unwrap(), 1); // alice

        let crit = Criteria::eq("username", Value::Text("bob".into()))
            | Criteria::eq("username", Value::Text("carol".into()));
        assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &crit).unwrap(), 2);

        let crit = !Criteria::eq("is_active", Value::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &crit).unwrap(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn in_lookup() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        for name in ["alice", "bob", "carol"] {
            b.insert("auth_user", row(None, name, true)).unwrap();
        }
        let crit = Criteria::in_(
            "username",
            vec![Value::Text("alice".into()), Value::Text("carol".into())],
        );
        assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &crit).unwrap(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn defaults_and_add_column() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
        b.insert("auth_user", vec![Value::Null, Value::Text("alice".into()), Value::Null]).unwrap();
        // boolean default true was applied
        let rows = b.select("auth_user", &Criteria::any(), &[], None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rows[0][2], Value::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(rows[0][0], Value::Int(1));

        b.add_column("auth_user", ColumnDesc::char("email", 100)).unwrap();
        let rows = b.select("auth_user", &Criteria::any(), &[], None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rows[0].len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(rows[0][3], Value::Null);
    }

    #[test]
    fn json_backend_persistence() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("rustango-test-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let db = dir.join("db.json");

        {
            let b = JsonFileBackend::open(&db).unwrap();
            b.create_table("auth_user", user_cols()).unwrap();
            b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "alice", true)).unwrap();
        }
        // reopen: data must survive
        {
            let b = JsonFileBackend::open(&db).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 1);
            b.insert("auth_user", row(None, "bob", false)).unwrap();
        }
        {
            let b = JsonFileBackend::open(&db).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(b.count("auth_user", &Criteria::any()).unwrap(), 2);
        }
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn migrations_meta() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.ensure_migration_meta().unwrap();
        assert!(b.applied_migrations().unwrap().is_empty());
        b.record_migration("polls", "0001_initial").unwrap();
        let applied = b.applied_migrations().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(applied, vec![("polls".into(), "0001_initial".into())]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn field_kinds_roundtrip() {
        let c = ColumnDesc::foreign_key("author_id", "auth_user");
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&c).unwrap();
        let back: ColumnDesc = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back.kind, FieldKind::ForeignKey { target_table: "auth_user".into() });
    }
}

```rust
//! Migrations — `makemigrations` / `migrate`.
//!
//! Migration files are JSON documents next to the project (default
//! `migrations/`), recording schema operations. Applied migrations are
//! tracked in the `_migrations` table.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::backend::Backend;
use super::{ColumnDesc, FieldKind, OrmResult};

/// One schema operation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
#[serde(tag = "op")]
pub enum MigrationOp {
    CreateTable { table: String, columns: Vec<ColumnDesc> },
    AddColumn { table: String, column: ColumnDesc },
    DropColumn { table: String, name: String },
    DropTable { table: String },
}

impl MigrationOp {
    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            MigrationOp::CreateTable { table, columns } => {
                format!("create table `{}` ({} columns)", table, columns.len())
            }
            MigrationOp::AddColumn { table, column } => {
                format!("add column `{}` to `{}` ({})", column.name, table, column.type_name())
            }
            MigrationOp::DropColumn { table, name } => format!("drop column `{name}` from `{table}`"),
            MigrationOp::DropTable { table } => format!("drop table `{table}`"),
        }
    }
}

/// A named migration file for one app.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Migration {
    pub app: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub ops: Vec<MigrationOp>,
}

impl Migration {
    pub fn new(app: &str, name: &str, ops: Vec<MigrationOp>) -> Self {
        Self { app: app.to_string(), name: name.to_string(), ops }
    }

    pub fn file_name(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}_{}.json", self.app, self.name)
    }

    pub fn write(&self, dir: &Path) -> OrmResult<PathBuf> {
        fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
        let path = dir.join(self.file_name());
        let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self)?;
        fs::write(&path, text)?;
        Ok(path)
    }

    pub fn read(dir: &Path, file: &str) -> OrmResult<Migration> {
        let text = fs::read_to_string(dir.join(file))?;
        serde_json::from_str(&text)
            .map_err(|e| crate::errors::OrmError::Migration(format!("bad migration file {file}: {e}")))
    }

    /// List all migration files for an app, sorted by name.
    pub fn list(dir: &Path, app: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut files: Vec<String> = fs::read_dir(dir)
            .map(|rd| {
                rd.filter_map(|e| e.ok())
                    .filter_map(|e| e.file_name().into_string().ok())
                    .filter(|f| f.starts_with(&format!("{app}_")) && f.ends_with(".json"))
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        files.sort();
        files
    }

    /// Apply unapplied ops + record. Idempotent.
    pub fn apply(&self, backend: &dyn Backend) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        backend.ensure_migration_meta()?;
        let applied = backend.applied_migrations()?;
        let key = (self.app.clone(), self.name.clone());
        if applied.contains(&key) {
            return Ok(0);
        }
        let mut n = 0;
        for op in &self.ops {
            match op {
                MigrationOp::CreateTable { table, columns } => {
                    backend.create_table(table, columns.clone())?;
                    n += 1;
                }
                MigrationOp::AddColumn { table, column } => {
                    backend.add_column(table, column.clone())?;
                    n += 1;
                }
                MigrationOp::DropColumn { table, name } => {
                    let _ = name;
                    // Column drops are recorded but no-op'd on file stores;
                    // the JSON engine keeps column layouts append-only.
                    let _ = table;
                }
                MigrationOp::DropTable { table } => {
                    backend.drop_table(table)?;
                    n += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        backend.record_migration(&self.app, &self.name)?;
        Ok(n)
    }
}

/// Diff the registry's declared schema against the backend and produce the
/// migration ops needed — Django's `autodetector`.
pub fn detect_changes(backend: &dyn Backend, app: &str, metas: &[super::ModelMeta]) -> Vec<MigrationOp> {
    let mut ops = Vec::new();
    for meta in metas {
        let existing_cols = backend.columns(&meta.table);
        if existing_cols.is_empty() && !backend.tables().contains(&meta.table) {
            ops.push(MigrationOp::CreateTable {
                table: meta.table.clone(),
                columns: meta.columns.clone(),
            });
            continue;
        }
        for col in &meta.columns {
            if !existing_cols.iter().any(|c| c.name == col.name) {
                ops.push(MigrationOp::AddColumn { table: meta.table.clone(), column: col.clone() });
            }
        }
    }
    let _ = app;
    ops
}

/// Build (and optionally write) the next migration for an app.
pub fn makemigrations(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    dir: &Path,
    app: &str,
    metas: &[super::ModelMeta],
    dry_run: bool,
) -> OrmResult<Option<Migration>> {
    let ops = detect_changes(backend, app, metas);
    if ops.is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let existing = Migration::list(dir, app);
    let next_num = existing.len() + 1;
    let name = if existing.is_empty() {
        "0001_initial".to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{:04}_auto", next_num)
    };
    let m = Migration::new(app, &name, ops);
    if !dry_run {
        m.write(dir)?;
    }
    Ok(Some(m))
}

/// Apply all unapplied migrations for every app found in `dir`.
pub fn migrate(backend: &dyn Backend, dir: &Path, app: Option<&str>) -> OrmResult<Vec<String>> {
    backend.ensure_migration_meta()?;
    let mut applied = Vec::new();
    let files: Vec<String> = fs::read_dir(dir)
        .map(|rd| {
            rd.filter_map(|e| e.ok())
                .filter_map(|e| e.file_name().into_string().ok())
                .filter(|f| f.ends_with(".json"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut files = files;
    files.sort();

    for file in files {
        let m = Migration::read(dir, &file)?;
        if let Some(want) = app {
            if m.app != want {
                continue;
            }
        }
        let n = m.apply(backend)?;
        if n > 0 || !backend.applied_migrations()?.contains(&(m.app.clone(), m.name.clone())) {
            backend.record_migration(&m.app, &m.name)?;
        }
        applied.push(format!("{}/{} ({} ops)", m.app, m.name, m.ops.len()));
    }
    Ok(applied)
}

/// Fake a migration (mark applied without running) — `migrate --fake`.
pub fn fake_migration(backend: &dyn Backend, app: &str, name: &str) -> OrmResult<()> {
    backend.ensure_migration_meta()?;
    backend.record_migration(app, name)
}

/// Human-readable list: applied vs pending — `showmigrations`.
pub fn show_migrations(backend: &dyn Backend, dir: &Path) -> OrmResult<String> {
    backend.ensure_migration_meta()?;
    let applied = backend.applied_migrations()?;
    let mut out = String::new();
    let files: Vec<String> = fs::read_dir(dir)
        .map(|rd| {
            rd.filter_map(|e| e.ok())
                .filter_map(|e| e.file_name().into_string().ok())
                .filter(|f| f.ends_with(".json"))
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut files = files;
    files.sort();
    for f in files {
        let m = Migration::read(dir, &f)?;
        let done = applied.contains(&(m.app.clone(), m.name.clone()));
        out.push_str(&format!("[{}] {}/{}\n", if done { "X" } else { " " }, m.app, m.name));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Whether a column kind is migration-significant (admin introspection).
pub fn is_relation(kind: &FieldKind) -> bool {
    matches!(kind, FieldKind::ForeignKey { .. })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::orm::{InMemoryBackend, Model, ModelExt};
    use std::sync::Arc;

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, crate::Model)]
#[model(table = "mig_post")]
    pub struct Post {
        #[field(auto)]
        pub id: i64,
        #[field(char, max = 80)]
        pub title: String,
    }

    fn meta() -> super::super::ModelMeta {
        super::super::ModelMeta::of::<Post>()
    }

    #[test]
    fn detect_create_table() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        let ops = detect_changes(&b, "blog", &[meta()]);
        assert_eq!(ops.len(), 1);
        assert!(matches!(&ops[0], MigrationOp::CreateTable { table, .. } if table == "mig_post"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn detect_add_column() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.create_table("mig_post", Post::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let mut richer = meta();
        richer.columns.push(ColumnDesc::char("slug", 100));
        let ops = detect_changes(&b, "blog", &[richer]);
        assert_eq!(ops.len(), 1);
        assert!(matches!(&ops[0], MigrationOp::AddColumn { column, .. } if column.name == "slug"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn makemigrate_and_migrate_flow() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("rustango-mig-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
        let b = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());

        // fresh backend -> initial migration detected
        let m = makemigrations(&*b, &dir, "blog", &[meta()], false)
            .unwrap()
            .expect("initial migration expected");
        assert_eq!(m.name, "0001_initial");
        assert!(dir.join("blog_0001_initial.json").exists());

        // apply
        let applied = migrate(&*b, &dir, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(applied.len(), 1);
        assert!(b.tables().contains(&"mig_post".to_string()));
        assert!(b.applied_migrations().unwrap().contains(&("blog".into(), "0001_initial".into())));

        // re-migrate: idempotent
        let again = migrate(&*b, &dir, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(again.len(), 1); // seen but not re-applied

        // no further changes when schema matches
        let nochange = makemigrations(&*b, &dir, "blog", &[meta()], false).unwrap();
        assert!(nochange.is_none());

        // add a column -> auto migration
        let mut richer = meta();
        richer.columns.push(ColumnDesc::char("slug", 100));
        let m2 = makemigrations(&*b, &dir, "blog", &[richer], false).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(m2.name.starts_with("0002"));
        migrate(&*b, &dir, None).unwrap();
        let cols = b.columns("mig_post");
        assert!(cols.iter().any(|c| c.name == "slug"));

        let report = show_migrations(&*b, &dir).unwrap();
        assert!(report.contains("[X] blog/0001_initial"));
        assert!(report.contains("[X] blog/0002_auto"));

        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn migration_file_roundtrip() {
        let m = Migration::new("blog", "0003_x", vec![
            MigrationOp::DropTable { table: "old".into() },
        ]);
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("rustango-mig2-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
        let p = m.write(&dir).unwrap();
        let back = Migration::read(&dir, &m.file_name()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, m);
        std::fs::remove_file(p).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn fake_migration_marks_applied() {
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        b.ensure_migration_meta().unwrap();
        fake_migration(&b, "blog", "0001_initial").unwrap();
        assert!(b.applied_migrations().unwrap().contains(&("blog".into(), "0001_initial".into())));
    }

    #[test]
    fn apply_creates_and_inserts_work() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("rustango-mig3-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
        let b = InMemoryBackend::new();
        let m = Migration::new("blog", "0001_initial", vec![MigrationOp::CreateTable {
            table: "mig_post".into(),
            columns: Post::columns().to_vec(),
        }]);
        m.write(&dir).unwrap();
        migrate(&b, &dir, None).unwrap();
        let p = Post { id: 0, title: "hello".into() };
        let saved = p.save(&b).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved.pk(), 1);
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }
}

````rust
//! Object-relational mapping — the `django.db.models` equivalent.
//!
//! Models are declared with the [`model!`](model) macro:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! model! {
//!     #[table = "polls_question"]
//!     pub struct Question {
//!         pub id: AutoId,
//!         pub question_text: Char(200),
//!         pub pub_date: DateTimeAuto,
//!     }
//! }
//!
//! let q = Question { id: 0, question_text: "What's new?".into(), pub_date: Utc::now() };
//! let q = q.save(&*backend)?;
//! let rows: Vec<Question> = Question::objects(&*backend)
//!     .filter(Q::contains("question_text", "new"))
//!     .order_by("-pub_date")
//!     .all()?;
//! ```

pub mod backend;
pub mod migrations;
pub mod model;
pub mod query;

pub use backend::{Backend, InMemoryBackend, JsonFileBackend};
pub use migrations::{Migration, MigrationOp};
pub use model::{Model, ModelExt};
pub use query::QuerySet;

// Common error alias, so users can write `orm::OrmError`.
pub use crate::errors::OrmError;

use std::sync::{OnceLock, RwLock};

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

pub type OrmResult<T> = Result<T, crate::errors::OrmError>;
pub type Row = Vec<Value>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Value — the dynamic column value
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Dynamic value stored in a column. `Serialize`/`Deserialize` via a tagged
/// JSON representation so the file backend can persist rows verbatim.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Value {
    Null,
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
    Text(String),
    Bool(bool),
    DateTime(DateTime<Utc>),
}

impl Value {
    pub fn as_int(&self) -> Option<i64> {
        match self { Value::Int(i) => Some(*i), _ => None }
    }
    pub fn as_float(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        match self { Value::Float(f) => Some(*f), Value::Int(i) => Some(*i as f64), _ => None }
    }
    pub fn as_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self { Value::Text(s) => Some(s), _ => None }
    }
    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {
        match self { Value::Bool(b) => Some(*b), _ => None }
    }
    pub fn as_datetime(&self) -> Option<DateTime<Utc>> {
        match self { Value::DateTime(d) => Some(*d), _ => None }
    }

    /// Coerce to the string form used in comparisons and templates.
    pub fn display(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Value::Null => String::new(),
            Value::Int(i) => i.to_string(),
            Value::Float(f) => {
                if f.fract() == 0.0 { format!("{f:.1}") } else { f.to_string() }
            }
            Value::Text(s) => s.clone(),
            Value::Bool(b) => (if *b { "True" } else { "False" }).to_string(),
            Value::DateTime(d) => d.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").to_string(),
        }
    }
}

impl From<i64> for Value { fn from(v: i64) -> Self { Value::Int(v) } }
impl From<i32> for Value { fn from(v: i32) -> Self { Value::Int(v as i64) } }
impl From<f64> for Value { fn from(v: f64) -> Self { Value::Float(v) } }
impl From<&str> for Value { fn from(v: &str) -> Self { Value::Text(v.to_string()) } }
impl From<String> for Value { fn from(v: String) -> Self { Value::Text(v) } }
impl From<bool> for Value { fn from(v: bool) -> Self { Value::Bool(v) } }
impl From<DateTime<Utc>> for Value { fn from(v: DateTime<Utc>) -> Self { Value::DateTime(v) } }
impl From<Option<String>> for Value {
    fn from(v: Option<String>) -> Self { v.map(Value::Text).unwrap_or(Value::Null) }
}

impl Serialize for Value {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, s: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        #[derive(Serialize)]
        #[serde(tag = "t", content = "v")]
        enum Tagged<'a> {
            N,
            I(i64),
            F(&'a f64),
            T(&'a str),
            B(bool),
            D(String),
        }
        match self {
            Value::Null => Tagged::N.serialize(s),
            Value::Int(i) => Tagged::I(*i).serialize(s),
            Value::Float(f) => Tagged::F(f).serialize(s),
            Value::Text(t) => Tagged::T(t).serialize(s),
            Value::Bool(b) => Tagged::B(*b).serialize(s),
            Value::DateTime(d) => Tagged::D(d.to_rfc3339()).serialize(s),
        }
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Value {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        #[serde(tag = "t", content = "v")]
        enum Tagged {
            N,
            I(i64),
            F(f64),
            T(String),
            B(bool),
            D(String),
        }
        match Tagged::deserialize(d)? {
            Tagged::N => Ok(Value::Null),
            Tagged::I(i) => Ok(Value::Int(i)),
            Tagged::F(f) => Ok(Value::Float(f)),
            Tagged::T(t) => Ok(Value::Text(t)),
            Tagged::B(b) => Ok(Value::Bool(b)),
            Tagged::D(r) => DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&r)
                .map(|dt| Value::DateTime(dt.with_timezone(&Utc)))
                .map_err(serde::de::Error::custom),
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Column descriptors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Field kinds, mirroring `django.db.models` field classes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum FieldKind {
    /// `models.AutoField` — primary key with auto increment.
    Auto,
    /// `models.CharField(max_length=N)`
    Char,
    /// `models.TextField`
    Text,
    /// `models.IntegerField`
    Integer,
    /// `models.FloatField`
    Float,
    /// `models.BooleanField(default=..)`
    Bool,
    /// `models.DateTimeField`
    DateTime,
    /// `models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)`
    DateTimeAutoNowAdd,
    /// `models.ForeignKey(other_model)`
    ForeignKey { target_table: String },
}

/// One model field / table column.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ColumnDesc {
    pub name: String,
    pub kind: FieldKind,
    pub max_length: usize,
    pub null: bool,
    pub unique: bool,
    pub primary_key: bool,
    /// Optional default applied when inserting Null.
    pub default: Option<Value>,
}

impl ColumnDesc {
    fn new(name: &str, kind: FieldKind) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            kind,
            max_length: 0,
            null: false,
            unique: false,
            primary_key: false,
            default: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn auto(name: &str) -> Self {
        let mut c = Self::new(name, FieldKind::Auto);
        c.primary_key = true;
        c
    }
    pub fn char(name: &str, max_length: usize) -> Self {
        let mut c = Self::new(name, FieldKind::Char);
        c.max_length = max_length;
        c
    }
    pub fn text(name: &str) -> Self { Self::new(name, FieldKind::Text) }
    pub fn integer(name: &str) -> Self { Self::new(name, FieldKind::Integer) }
    pub fn float(name: &str) -> Self { Self::new(name, FieldKind::Float) }
    pub fn boolean(name: &str, default: bool) -> Self {
        let mut c = Self::new(name, FieldKind::Bool);
        c.default = Some(Value::Bool(default));
        c
    }
    pub fn datetime(name: &str, null: bool) -> Self {
        let mut c = Self::new(name, FieldKind::DateTime);
        c.null = null;
        c
    }
    pub fn datetime_auto_now_add(name: &str) -> Self { Self::new(name, FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd) }
    pub fn foreign_key(name: &str, target_table: &str) -> Self {
        Self::new(name, FieldKind::ForeignKey { target_table: target_table.to_string() })
    }

    pub fn unique(mut self) -> Self { self.unique = true; self }
    pub fn nullable(mut self) -> Self { self.null = true; self }

    /// Apply a flag by name — used by the `model!` macro expansion
    /// (`Char(50, unique, null)`).
    pub fn with_flag_pub(self, flag: &str) -> ColumnDesc {
        crate::orm::model::apply_flag(self, flag)
    }

    /// Python-ish repr for error messages and admin.
    pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self.kind {
            FieldKind::Auto => "AutoField",
            FieldKind::Char => "CharField",
            FieldKind::Text => "TextField",
            FieldKind::Integer => "IntegerField",
            FieldKind::Float => "FloatField",
            FieldKind::Bool => "BooleanField",
            FieldKind::DateTime => "DateTimeField",
            FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd => "DateTimeField(auto_now_add)",
            FieldKind::ForeignKey { .. } => "ForeignKey",
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Lookup operators — `field__gt`, `field__contains`, ...
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Query operators, mirroring Django's lookup suffixes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Op {
    Exact,
    IExact,
    Contains,
    IContains,
    StartsWith,
    IStartsWith,
    EndsWith,
    IEndsWith,
    Gt,
    Gte,
    Lt,
    Lte,
    Year,
    Month,
    Day,
}

impl Op {
    pub fn from_lookup(word: &str) -> Option<Op> {
        match word {
            "exact" => Some(Op::Exact),
            "iexact" => Some(Op::IExact),
            "contains" => Some(Op::Contains),
            "icontains" => Some(Op::IContains),
            "startswith" => Some(Op::StartsWith),
            "istartswith" => Some(Op::IStartsWith),
            "endswith" => Some(Op::EndsWith),
            "iendswith" => Some(Op::IEndsWith),
            "gt" => Some(Op::Gt),
            "gte" => Some(Op::Gte),
            "lt" => Some(Op::Lt),
            "lte" => Some(Op::Lte),
            "year" => Some(Op::Year),
            "month" => Some(Op::Month),
            "day" => Some(Op::Day),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Criteria (Q objects)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Query criteria — the equivalent of Django's `Q` objects, combinable with
/// `&` (AND), `|` (OR) and `!` (NOT), and nestable.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Criteria {
    And(Vec<Criteria>),
    Or(Vec<Criteria>),
    Not(Box<Criteria>),
    /// `field__op=value` where `field` may traverse FKs with `__`
    /// (`author_id__username__icontains`).
    Cond { field: String, op: Op, value: Value },
    /// `field__in=[..]`
    In { field: String, values: Vec<Value> },
    /// `field__isnull=True/False`
    IsNull { field: String, negated: bool },
}

/// Alias so call sites read like Django: `Q::eq("published", true)`.
pub type Q = Criteria;

impl Criteria {
    pub fn eq(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::Cond { field: field.into(), op: Op::Exact, value: value.into() }
    }
    pub fn ne(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::Not(Box::new(Criteria::eq(field, value)))
    }
    pub fn cond(field: impl Into<String>, op: Op, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::Cond { field: field.into(), op, value: value.into() }
    }
    pub fn contains(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::cond(field, Op::Contains, value.into())
    }
    pub fn icontains(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::cond(field, Op::IContains, value.into())
    }
    pub fn gt(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::cond(field, Op::Gt, value)
    }
    pub fn gte(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::cond(field, Op::Gte, value)
    }
    pub fn lt(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::cond(field, Op::Lt, value)
    }
    pub fn lte(field: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::cond(field, Op::Lte, value)
    }
    pub fn in_(field: impl Into<String>, values: Vec<Value>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::In { field: field.into(), values }
    }
    pub fn isnull(field: impl Into<String>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::IsNull { field: field.into(), negated: false }
    }
    pub fn not_null(field: impl Into<String>) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::IsNull { field: field.into(), negated: true }
    }
    /// True criteria (matches everything) — `Q()`.
    pub fn any() -> Criteria { Criteria::And(vec![]) }

    pub fn is_any(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Criteria::And(v) if v.is_empty())
    }
}

impl std::ops::BitAnd for Criteria {
    type Output = Criteria;
    fn bitand(self, rhs: Criteria) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::And(vec![self, rhs])
    }
}

impl std::ops::BitOr for Criteria {
    type Output = Criteria;
    fn bitor(self, rhs: Criteria) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::Or(vec![self, rhs])
    }
}

impl std::ops::Not for Criteria {
    type Output = Criteria;
    fn not(self) -> Criteria {
        Criteria::Not(Box::new(self))
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Model registry (for FK traversal, migrations and the admin)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Runtime metadata for one registered model.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ModelMeta {
    pub table: String,
    pub columns: Vec<ColumnDesc>,
    /// (fk column name, target table)
    pub fks: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl ModelMeta {
    pub fn column(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&ColumnDesc> {
        self.columns.iter().find(|c| c.name == name)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Registry {
    pub models: Vec<ModelMeta>,
}

impl Registry {
    pub fn add(&mut self, meta: ModelMeta) {
        if let Some(existing) = self.models.iter_mut().find(|m| m.table == meta.table) {
            *existing = meta;
        } else {
            self.models.push(meta);
        }
    }

    pub fn get(&self, table: &str) -> Option<&ModelMeta> {
        self.models.iter().find(|m| m.table == table)
    }
}

static REGISTRY: OnceLock<RwLock<Registry>> = OnceLock::new();

/// The global model registry.
pub fn registry() -> &'static RwLock<Registry> {
    REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| RwLock::new(Registry::default()))
}

/// Register a model's metadata (called by `App::models::<T>()`).
pub fn register_model(meta: ModelMeta) {
    registry().write().unwrap().add(meta);
}

/// snake_case of a CamelCase model name — used for default table names.
pub fn snake_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(name.len() + 4);
    for (i, ch) in name.chars().enumerate() {
        if ch.is_ascii_uppercase() {
            if i > 0 {
                out.push('_');
            }
            out.push(ch.to_ascii_lowercase());
        } else {
            out.push(ch);
        }
    }
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Criteria evaluation (with FK traversal)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Resolve `field__path__op` against the registry.
/// Returns (final table, column name, op-from-path) — the op is `Some`
/// when the path carried a lookup suffix (`pub_date__year`), `None` when
/// the path is just a field (the caller's own op applies).
pub fn resolve_field_path(
    start_table: &str,
    path: &str,
) -> OrmResult<(String, String, Option<Op>)> {
    let segs: Vec<&str> = path.split("__").collect();
    let mut cur_table = start_table.to_string();
    let mut col: Option<String> = None;
    let mut op: Option<Op> = None;

    for (i, seg) in segs.iter().enumerate() {
        let meta = registry().read().unwrap().get(&cur_table).cloned();

        // An explicit lookup suffix after a resolved column.
        if col.is_some() {
            if let Some(o) = Op::from_lookup(seg) {
                op = Some(o);
                break;
            }
        }

        match meta {
            Some(m) => {
                // FK traversal — unless the next segment is an op suffix
                // (`author_id__gt=5` compares the fk column value itself).
                if let Some((fk_col, target)) = m.fks.iter().find(|(c, _)| c == seg) {
                    let next_is_op = segs.get(i + 1).and_then(|n| Op::from_lookup(n));
                    if next_is_op.is_some() {
                        col = Some(fk_col.clone());
                        op = next_is_op;
                        break;
                    }
                    cur_table = target.clone();
                    col = None;
                    continue;
                }
                // Plain column?
                if m.column(seg).is_some() {
                    col = Some(seg.to_string());
                    continue;
                }
                // FK column referenced directly as a value column.
                if m.fks.iter().any(|(c, _)| c == seg) {
                    col = Some(seg.to_string());
                    continue;
                }
                return Err(crate::errors::OrmError::UnknownField(format!(
                    "{path} (at `{seg}`)"
                )));
            }
            None => {
                // No registry entry: treat the segment as a plain column
                // (single-table backends / unregistered models).
                col = Some(seg.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    let col = col.ok_or_else(|| crate::errors::OrmError::UnknownField(path.to_string()))?;
    Ok((cur_table, col, op))
}

/// Extract the comparison target for a date op.
fn date_part(v: &Value, op: Op) -> Option<i64> {
    let d = v.as_datetime()?;
    match op {
        Op::Year => Some(d.format("%Y").to_string().parse().ok()?),
        Op::Month => Some(d.format("%m").to_string().parse().ok()?),
        Op::Day => Some(d.format("%d").to_string().parse().ok()?),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn compare(op: Op, left: &Value, right: &Value) -> bool {
    match op {
        Op::Exact => left == right,
        Op::IExact => match (left.as_text(), right.as_text()) {
            // Unicode-consistent folding: `iexact` and `icontains` must agree
            // for non-ASCII text (`eq_ignore_ascii_case` disagreed with
            // `icontains`'s `to_lowercase`).
            (Some(a), Some(b)) => a.to_lowercase() == b.to_lowercase(),
            _ => left == right,
        },
        Op::Contains => contains_like(left, right, false),
        Op::IContains => contains_like(left, right, true),
        Op::StartsWith => text_like(left, right, true, false),
        Op::IStartsWith => text_like(left, right, true, true),
        Op::EndsWith => text_like(left, right, false, false),
        Op::IEndsWith => text_like(left, right, false, true),
        Op::Gt | Op::Gte | Op::Lt | Op::Lte => ordered_cmp(op, left, right),
        Op::Year | Op::Month | Op::Day => match (date_part(left, op), right.as_int()) {
            (Some(a), Some(b)) => a == b,
            _ => false,
        },
    }
}

fn contains_like(left: &Value, right: &Value, insensitive: bool) -> bool {
    let (l, r) = (left.display(), right.display());
    if insensitive {
        l.to_lowercase().contains(&r.to_lowercase())
    } else {
        l.contains(&r)
    }
}

fn text_like(left: &Value, right: &Value, start: bool, insensitive: bool) -> bool {
    let (mut l, mut r) = (left.display(), right.display());
    if insensitive {
        l = l.to_lowercase();
        r = r.to_lowercase();
    }
    if start { l.starts_with(&r) } else { l.ends_with(&r) }
}

fn ordered_cmp(op: Op, left: &Value, right: &Value) -> bool {
    let ord = if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (left.as_datetime(), right.as_datetime()) {
        Some(a.cmp(&b))
    } else if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (left.as_float(), right.as_float()) {
        Some(a.partial_cmp(&b).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
    } else {
        left.display().partial_cmp(&right.display())
    };
    match ord {
        Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Greater) => matches!(op, Op::Gt | Op::Gte),
        Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Less) => matches!(op, Op::Lt | Op::Lte),
        Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal) => matches!(op, Op::Gte | Op::Lte),
        None => false,
    }
}

/// Evaluate a criteria tree against a row of `table`.
/// FK paths fetch related rows from `backend` as needed.
pub fn eval_criteria(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    table: &str,
    row: &Row,
    cols: &[ColumnDesc],
    crit: &Criteria,
) -> bool {
    match crit {
        Criteria::And(list) => list.iter().all(|c| eval_criteria(backend, table, row, cols, c)),
        Criteria::Or(list) => list.iter().any(|c| eval_criteria(backend, table, row, cols, c)),
        Criteria::Not(inner) => !eval_criteria(backend, table, row, cols, inner),
        Criteria::Cond { field, op, value } => {
            // Fast path: plain column without `__` traversal.
            if !field.contains("__") {
                if let Some(idx) = cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == *field) {
                    if let Some(v) = row.get(idx) {
                        return compare(*op, v, value);
                    }
                }
                return false;
            }
            match resolve_field_path(table, field) {
                Ok((target_table, col_name, path_op)) => {
                    let effective = path_op.unwrap_or(*op);
                    let row_value =
                        follow_path(backend, table, row, cols, field, &target_table, &col_name);
                    match row_value {
                        Some(v) => compare(effective, &v, value),
                        None => false,
                    }
                }
                Err(_) => false,
            }
        }
        Criteria::In { field, values } => {
            if !field.contains("__") {
                if let Some(idx) = cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == *field) {
                    if let Some(v) = row.get(idx) {
                        return values.contains(v);
                    }
                }
                return false;
            }
            match resolve_field_path(table, field) {
                Ok((target_table, col_name, _)) => {
                    match follow_path(backend, table, row, cols, field, &target_table, &col_name) {
                        Some(v) => values.contains(&v),
                        None => false,
                    }
                }
                Err(_) => false,
            }
        }
        Criteria::IsNull { field, negated } => {
            if !field.contains("__") {
                if let Some(idx) = cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == *field) {
                    let v = row.get(idx).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                    return match v {
                        Value::Null => !*negated,
                        _ => *negated,
                    };
                }
                return false;
            }
            match resolve_field_path(table, field) {
                Ok((target_table, col_name, _)) => {
                    match follow_path(backend, table, row, cols, field, &target_table, &col_name) {
                        Some(Value::Null) => !*negated,
                        Some(_) => *negated,
                        None => !*negated,
                    }
                }
                Err(_) => false,
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Walk an FK path: `author_id__username` fetches the related row.
fn follow_path(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    table: &str,
    row: &Row,
    cols: &[ColumnDesc],
    path: &str,
    target_table: &str,
    col_name: &str,
) -> Option<Value> {
    // If the path only touches the base table, just read the column.
    if target_table == table && col_name != "id" || path.split("__").count() == 1 {
        let idx = cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == col_name)?;
        return row.get(idx).cloned();
    }

    // Walk FK by FK: collect the fk columns along the path.
    let segs: Vec<&str> = path.split("__").collect();
    let mut cur_table = table.to_string();
    let mut cur_row: Row = row.to_vec();
    let mut cur_cols: Vec<ColumnDesc> = cols.to_vec();

    for (i, seg) in segs.iter().enumerate() {
        let last = i + 1 == segs.len();
        let meta = registry().read().unwrap().get(&cur_table).cloned();

        if let Some(meta) = &meta {
            if let Some((fk_col, target)) = meta.fks.iter().find(|(c, _)| c == seg) {
                let idx = cur_cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == *fk_col)?;
                let fk_val = cur_row.get(idx).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                if last {
                    // the fk column itself was requested
                    return Some(fk_val);
                }
                let pk = fk_val.as_int()?;
                let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(pk));
                let related = backend.select(target, &crit, &[], None, None).ok()?;
                let rel_row = related.into_iter().next()?;
                let rel_cols = backend.columns(target);
                cur_table = target.clone();
                cur_row = rel_row;
                cur_cols = rel_cols;
                continue;
            }
        }

        // Final column on the current row.
        let idx = cur_cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == *seg)?;
        return cur_row.get(idx).cloned();
    }

    let idx = cur_cols.iter().position(|c| c.name == col_name)?;
    cur_row.get(idx).cloned()
}

/// Order rows by `order` spec (`name` asc, `-name` desc), FK-aware.
pub fn order_rows(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    table: &str,
    rows: &mut [Row],
    cols: &[ColumnDesc],
    order: &[(String, bool)],
) {
    if order.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let resolved: Vec<(String, String, bool, Op)> = order
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|(field, desc)| {
            resolve_field_path(table, field)
                .ok()
                .map(|(t, c, op)| (t, c, *desc, op.unwrap_or(Op::Exact)))
        })
        .collect();
    if resolved.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let cols_snapshot: Vec<ColumnDesc> = cols.to_vec();
    rows.sort_by(|a, b| {
        for (t, col, desc, op) in &resolved {
            let va = follow_path(backend, table, a, &cols_snapshot, &field_for(t, col), t, col)
                .unwrap_or(Value::Null);
            let vb = follow_path(backend, table, b, &cols_snapshot, &field_for(t, col), t, col)
                .unwrap_or(Value::Null);
            // date ops are not orderable this way; treat as Exact value compare
            let cmp = cmp_values(&va, &vb, *op);
            let cmp = if *desc { cmp.reverse() } else { cmp };
            if cmp != std::cmp::Ordering::Equal {
                return cmp;
            }
        }
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal
    });
}

fn field_for(_t: &str, col: &str) -> String { col.to_string() }

fn cmp_values(a: &Value, b: &Value, op: Op) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
    if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (a.as_datetime(), b.as_datetime()) {
        return x.cmp(&y);
    }
    if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (a.as_float(), b.as_float()) {
        return x.partial_cmp(&y).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal);
    }
    if matches!(op, Op::Year | Op::Month | Op::Day) {
        if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (date_part(a, op), date_part(b, op)) {
            return x.cmp(&y);
        }
    }
    a.display().cmp(&b.display())
}

/// Unique-constraint check shared by backends.
pub fn check_unique(
    backend: &dyn Backend,
    table: &str,
    cols: &[ColumnDesc],
    row: &Row,
    exclude_pk: Option<i64>,
) -> OrmResult<()> {
    for (i, col) in cols.iter().enumerate() {
        if !col.unique || col.primary_key {
            continue;
        }
        let val = row.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        if val == Value::Null {
            continue;
        }
        let crit = Criteria::eq(&col.name, val);
        let found = backend.select(table, &crit, &[], None, None)?;
        if let Some(other) = found.first() {
            let other_pk = other.first().cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null).as_int();
            if other_pk != exclude_pk {
                return Err(crate::errors::OrmError::InvalidValue(
                    col.name.clone(),
                    "unique constraint violated".into(),
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn value_coercion_and_display() {
        assert_eq!(Value::Int(3).display(), "3");
        assert_eq!(Value::Float(3.0).display(), "3.0");
        assert_eq!(Value::Float(3.5).display(), "3.5");
        assert_eq!(Value::Bool(true).display(), "True");
        assert_eq!(Value::Text("x".into()).as_text(), Some("x"));
        assert_eq!(Value::from(7i64).as_int(), Some(7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn value_serde_roundtrip() {
        let v = Value::DateTime(Utc::now());
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&v).unwrap();
        let back: Value = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v, back);
        let v = Value::Text("hi".into());
        let back: Value = serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&v).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v, back);
    }

    #[test]
    fn snake_case_names() {
        assert_eq!(snake_case("Question"), "question");
        assert_eq!(snake_case("AuthUser"), "auth_user");
        assert_eq!(snake_case("HTTPError"), "h_t_t_p_error"); // documented quirk
    }

    #[test]
    fn q_operators() {
        let a = Q::eq("a", 1);
        let b = Q::eq("b", 2);
        let both = a & b;
        let either = Q::eq("a", 1) | Q::eq("b", 2);
        let neg = !Q::eq("a", 1);
        assert!(matches!(both, Criteria::And(_)));
        assert!(matches!(either, Criteria::Or(_)));
        assert!(matches!(neg, Criteria::Not(_)));
        assert!(Q::any().is_any());
    }

    #[test]
    fn compare_ops() {
        assert!(compare(Op::Exact, &Value::Int(3), &Value::Int(3)));
        assert!(!compare(Op::Exact, &Value::Int(3), &Value::Int(4)));
        assert!(compare(Op::IExact, &Value::Text("ABC".into()), &Value::Text("abc".into())));
        // Regression (M35): `iexact` used `eq_ignore_ascii_case` while
        // `icontains` folded with `to_lowercase` — the two disagreed for
        // non-ASCII text. They must agree.
        assert!(compare(
            Op::IExact,
            &Value::Text("ÄPFEL".into()),
            &Value::Text("äpfel".into())
        ));
        assert!(compare(
            Op::IContains,
            &Value::Text("ÄPFEL".into()),
            &Value::Text("pfel".into())
        ));
        assert!(compare(Op::Contains, &Value::Text("hello world".into()), &Value::Text("world".into())));
        assert!(compare(Op::IContains, &Value::Text("HELLO".into()), &Value::Text("ell".into())));
        assert!(compare(Op::StartsWith, &Value::Text("rust".into()), &Value::Text("ru".into())));
        assert!(compare(Op::EndsWith, &Value::Text("rust".into()), &Value::Text("st".into())));
        assert!(compare(Op::Gt, &Value::Int(5), &Value::Int(3)));
        assert!(!compare(Op::Gt, &Value::Int(3), &Value::Int(3)));
        assert!(compare(Op::Gte, &Value::Int(3), &Value::Int(3)));
        assert!(compare(Op::Lt, &Value::Text("a".into()), &Value::Text("b".into())));
        let d1 = Value::DateTime(Utc::now());
        assert!(compare(Op::Exact, &d1, &d1));
    }
}
