//! Model trait, the `#[model]` declaration attribute and model-level
//! operations (`save`, `delete`, `objects`) — `django.db.models.Model`.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use super::backend::Backend;
use super::query::QuerySet;
use super::{check_unique, ColumnDesc, Criteria, OrmResult, Value};
use crate::types::DateTime;

/// A persistent model. Generated by the `#[model]` attribute macro.
pub trait Model: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// Table name (`Meta.db_table`).
    fn table() -> &'static str;
    /// Column descriptors in declaration order; column 0 is the pk.
    fn columns() -> &'static [ColumnDesc];
    fn from_row(row: &[Value]) -> Self;
    fn to_row(&self) -> Vec<Value>;
    /// Primary key value (column 0).
    fn pk(&self) -> i64;
    fn set_pk(&mut self, id: i64);
}

/// Model operations, blanket-implemented for every `Model` — this is what
/// makes `User::objects(&*backend).filter(...)` work and what `save()`
/// means for instances.
pub trait ModelExt: Model {
    /// INSERT or UPDATE depending on pk state — `obj.save()`.
    fn save(&self, backend: &dyn Backend) -> OrmResult<Self> {
        let cols = Self::columns();
        let table = Self::table();
        let row = self.to_row();
        if self.pk() > 0 {
            crate::signals::emit("pre_save", table, self.pk());
            check_unique(backend, table, cols, &row, Some(self.pk()))?;
            let updates: Vec<(usize, Value)> =
                row.iter().enumerate().skip(1).map(|(i, v)| (i, v.clone())).collect();
            let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(self.pk()));
            let n = backend.update(table, &crit, &updates)?;
            if n == 0 {
                return Err(crate::errors::OrmError::DoesNotExist(format!(
                    "{} pk={}",
                    table,
                    self.pk()
                )));
            }
            crate::signals::emit("post_save", table, self.pk());
            Ok(self.clone())
        } else {
            crate::signals::emit("pre_save", table, 0);
            check_unique(backend, table, cols, &row, None)?;
            let id = backend.insert(table, row)?;
            crate::signals::emit("post_save", table, id);
            let mut me = self.clone();
            me.set_pk(id);
            Ok(me)
        }
    }

    /// DELETE this row — `obj.delete()`.
    fn delete(&self, backend: &dyn Backend) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        let table = Self::table();
        crate::signals::emit("pre_delete", table, self.pk());
        let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(self.pk()));
        let n = backend.delete(table, &crit)?;
        crate::signals::emit("post_delete", table, self.pk());
        Ok(n)
    }

    /// `Model.objects` — a query set over all rows.
    fn objects(backend: &dyn Backend) -> QuerySet<'_, Self> {
        QuerySet::new(backend)
    }

    /// Fetch by primary key — `Model.objects.get(pk=..)` shortcut.
    fn get(backend: &dyn Backend, pk: i64) -> OrmResult<Self> {
        let crit = Criteria::eq("id", Value::Int(pk));
        let rows = backend.select(Self::table(), &crit, &[], None, None)?;
        rows.first()
            .map(|r| Self::from_row(r))
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::errors::OrmError::DoesNotExist(format!("{} pk={}", Self::table(), pk)))
    }

    /// Column index for bulk updates — `Book::column_index("pages")`.
    fn column_index(name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        Self::columns().iter().position(|c| c.name == name)
    }

    /// Field/value map — used by templates and the admin.
    fn to_map(&self) -> HashMap<String, Value> {
        Self::columns()
            .iter()
            .zip(self.to_row())
            .map(|(c, v)| (c.name.clone(), v))
            .collect()
    }
}

impl<T: Model> ModelExt for T {}

impl super::ModelMeta {
    /// Build registry metadata from a `Model` type.
    pub fn of<T: Model>() -> Self {
        let columns = T::columns().to_vec();
        let fks = columns
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|c| match &c.kind {
                super::FieldKind::ForeignKey { target_table } => {
                    Some((c.name.clone(), target_table.clone()))
                }
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        Self { table: T::table().to_string(), columns, fks }
    }
}

// -- coercion helpers (referenced from #[model] codegen) ---------------------

pub fn coerce_text(v: &Value) -> String {
    match v {
        Value::Text(s) => s.clone(),
        Value::Null => String::new(),
        other => other.display(),
    }
}
pub fn coerce_int(v: &Value) -> i64 { v.as_int().unwrap_or(0) }
pub fn coerce_float(v: &Value) -> f64 { v.as_float().unwrap_or(0.0) }
pub fn coerce_bool(v: &Value) -> bool { v.as_bool().unwrap_or(false) }
pub fn coerce_text_opt(v: &Value) -> Option<String> {
    match v {
        Value::Null => None,
        other => Some(other.display()),
    }
}
pub fn coerce_int_opt(v: &Value) -> Option<i64> { v.as_int() }
pub fn coerce_float_opt(v: &Value) -> Option<f64> { v.as_float() }
pub fn coerce_bool_opt(v: &Value) -> Option<bool> { v.as_bool() }
/// Stable sentinel for missing/invalid stored datetimes in non-null fields.
pub fn coerce_datetime_default() -> crate::types::DateTime {
    chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(0, 0).unwrap_or_else(chrono::Utc::now)
}
pub fn coerce_datetime(v: &Value) -> crate::types::DateTime {
    // Missing/invalid values used to be substituted with `Utc::now()`, which
    // made every non-null DateTime field silently mutate on each load
    // (`date_joined` changed every read, and a save persisted the drift).
    // Fall back to a deterministic sentinel instead.
    v.as_datetime().unwrap_or_else(coerce_datetime_default)
}
pub fn coerce_datetime_opt(v: &Value) -> Option<crate::types::DateTime> { v.as_datetime() }

pub fn apply_flag(mut c: ColumnDesc, flag: &str) -> ColumnDesc {
    match flag {
        "unique" => c.unique = true,
        "null" => c.null = true,
        _ => {}
    }
    c
}

mod tests {

#[model(table = "test_widget")]
    pub struct Widget {

        pub id: i64,

        let cols = Widget::columns();
        assert_eq!(cols.len(), 7);
        assert_eq!(cols[0].name, "id");
        assert!(cols[0].primary_key);
        assert_eq!(cols[1].name, "name");
        assert_eq!(cols[1].max_length, 50);
        assert!(cols[1].unique);
        assert_eq!(cols[2].kind, crate::orm::FieldKind::Integer);
        assert_eq!(cols[3].kind, crate::orm::FieldKind::Float);
        assert_eq!(cols[5].kind, crate::orm::FieldKind::DateTimeAutoNowAdd);
        assert_eq!(cols[6].kind, crate::orm::FieldKind::DateTime);
        assert!(cols[6].null);
    }

    #[test]
    fn table_name_from_attribute() {
        assert_eq!(Widget::table(), "test_widget");

    fn row_roundtrip() {
        let w = Widget {
            id: 0,
            name: "gear".into(),
            quantity: 5,
            price: 2.5,
            in_stock: true,
            created: now(),
            retired_at: None,
        };
        let row = w.to_row();
        let back = Widget::from_row(&row);
        assert_eq!(back.name, "gear");
        assert_eq!(back.quantity, 5);
        assert_eq!(back.price, 2.5);
        assert!(back.in_stock);
        assert_eq!(back.created, w.created);
        assert!(back.retired_at.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn coerce_datetime_does_not_fabricate_now() {
        // Regression (M32): missing/invalid stored datetimes were
        // substituted with `Utc::now()`, so non-null DateTime fields
        // silently mutated on every read (`date_joined` changed each load).
        let first = coerce_datetime(&Value::Null);
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(15));
        let second = coerce_datetime(&Value::Null);
        assert_eq!(first, second, "missing datetime must coerce to a stable value");
        assert_ne!(
            first,
            chrono::Utc::now(),
            "must not be fabricated from the clock"
        );
        // Valid values still pass through unchanged.
        let d = now();
        assert_eq!(coerce_datetime(&Value::DateTime(d)), d);
        // Nullable datetime coercion is unaffected.
        assert_eq!(coerce_datetime_opt(&Value::DateTime(d)), Some(d));
        assert_eq!(coerce_datetime_opt(&Value::Null), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn optional_field_codegen_roundtrip() {
        // Regression (M33): the derive classified EVERY `Option<T>` field as
        // `Option<DateTime>`, so `Option<i64>` / `Option<String>` fields
        // generated type errors buried in the proc-macro expansion. These
        // model definitions only compile when the classification is right.
        #[derive(Clone, Debug, crate::Model)]
        #[model(table = "test_optional")]
        pub struct Optional {
            #[field(auto)]
            pub id: i64,
            #[field(int, null)]
            pub score: Option<i64>,
            #[field(text, null)]
            pub nickname: Option<String>,
            #[field(bool, null)]
            pub verified: Option<bool>,
            #[field(float, null)]
            pub ratio: Option<f64>,
            #[field(datetime, null)]
            pub retired_at: Option<DateTime>,
        }
        use crate::orm::Model as _;

        let m = Optional {
            id: 7,
            score: Some(42),
            nickname: Some("ada".into()),
            verified: Some(true),
            ratio: Some(0.5),
            retired_at: None,
        };
        let row = m.to_row();
        assert_eq!(row[1], Value::Int(42));
        assert_eq!(row[2], Value::Text("ada".into()));
        assert_eq!(row[3], Value::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(row[4], Value::Float(0.5));
        assert_eq!(row[5], Value::Null);
        let back = Optional::from_row(&row);
        assert_eq!(back.score, Some(42));
        assert_eq!(back.nickname.as_deref(), Some("ada"));
        assert_eq!(back.verified, Some(true));
        assert_eq!(back.ratio, Some(0.5));
        assert!(back.retired_at.is_none());

        // Null stored values round-trip to None (not zero-coerced).
        let m2 = Optional {
            id: 8,
            score: None,
            nickname: None,
            verified: None,
            ratio: None,
            retired_at: None,
        };
        let back2 = Optional::from_row(&m2.to_row());
        assert_eq!(back2.score, None);
        assert_eq!(back2.nickname, None);
        assert_eq!(back2.verified, None);
        assert_eq!(back2.ratio, None);

        // Column nullability: optional fields must produce nullable columns.
        let cols = Optional::columns();
        for name in ["score", "nickname", "verified", "ratio", "retired_at"] {
            let c = cols.iter().find(|c| c.name == name).unwrap();
            assert!(c.null, "column {name} must be nullable");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn save_insert_then_update() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table(Widget::table(), Widget::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();

        let w = Widget {
            id: 0,
            name: "gear".into(),
            quantity: 1,
            price: 1.0,
            in_stock: true,
            created: now(),
            retired_at: None,
        };
        let mut saved = w.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved.pk(), 1);
        assert_eq!(w.pk(), 0); // original untouched; save returns a new instance

        saved.quantity = 9;
        let saved2 = saved.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved2.pk(), 1);
        let fetched = Widget::get(&*backend, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fetched.quantity, 9);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unique_violation_on_save() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table(Widget::table(), Widget::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let w = Widget { id: 0, name: "gear".into(), quantity: 0, price: 0.0, in_stock: true, created: now(), retired_at: None };
        w.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        let w2 = Widget { id: 0, name: "gear".into(), ..w.clone() };
        let err = w2.save(&*backend);
        assert!(err.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn delete_and_missing() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table(Widget::table(), Widget::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        let w = Widget { id: 0, name: "gear".into(), quantity: 0, price: 0.0, in_stock: true, created: now(), retired_at: None };
        let saved = w.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved.delete(&*backend).unwrap(), 1);
        assert!(Widget::get(&*backend, saved.pk()).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn to_map_fields() {
        let w = Widget { id: 3, name: "x".into(), quantity: 2, price: 1.5, in_stock: false, created: now(), retired_at: None };
        let m = w.to_map();
        assert_eq!(m.get("name"), Some(&Value::Text("x".into())));
        assert_eq!(m.get("quantity"), Some(&Value::Int(2)));
        assert_eq!(m.len(), 7);
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_model_defaults() {
        let cols = User::columns();
        assert_eq!(User::table(), "auth_user");
        let username = cols.iter().find(|c| c.name == "username").unwrap();
        assert!(username.unique);
        assert_eq!(username.max_length, 150);
        let is_staff = cols.iter().find(|c| c.name == "is_staff").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(is_staff.default, Some(Value::Bool(false)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn auto_now_add_filled_by_backend() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        backend.create_table(Widget::table(), Widget::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        // insert with Null created column -> backend fills auto_now_add
        let row = vec![
            Value::Null,
            Value::Text("auto".into()),
            Value::Int(0),
            Value::Float(0.0),
            Value::Bool(true),
            Value::Null, // created
            Value::Null,
        ];
        backend.insert(Widget::table(), row).unwrap();
        let fetched = Widget::get(&*backend, 1).unwrap();
        let year = fetched.created.format("%Y").to_string();
        assert!(year.starts_with("20"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn fk_column_desc() {
        #[derive(Clone, Debug, crate::Model)]
#[model(table = "test_part")]
        pub struct Part {
            #[field(auto)]
            pub id: i64,
            #[field(fk, target = "test_widget")]
            pub widget_id: i64,
            #[field(char, max = 30)]
            pub label: String,

        let fk = cols.iter().find(|c| c.name == "widget_id").unwrap();

```rust
//! Lazy query sets — `django.db.models.QuerySet` with chaining:
//! `filter`, `exclude`, `order_by`, `count`, `exists`, `first`, `get`,
//! `take` (Django slicing), `delete`, `update` and `latest`.

use std::marker::PhantomData;

use super::backend::Backend;
use super::model::{Model, ModelExt};
use super::{Criteria, OrmResult, Row, Value};

/// A chainable, lazy query. `filter()`/`exclude()` return new query sets;
/// terminal methods hit the backend.
pub struct QuerySet<'a, T> {
    backend: &'a dyn Backend,
    crit: Criteria,
    order: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    limit: Option<usize>,
    offset: Option<usize>,
    _pd: PhantomData<T>,
}

impl<'a, T: Model> QuerySet<'a, T> {
    pub fn new(backend: &'a dyn Backend) -> Self {
        Self {
            backend,
            crit: Criteria::any(),
            order: Vec::new(),
            limit: None,
            offset: None,
            _pd: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    /// AND a criteria into the filter — `.filter(Q(...))`.
    pub fn filter(mut self, crit: Criteria) -> Self {
        self.crit = match (self.crit.is_any(), crit.is_any()) {
            (true, _) => crit,
            (_, true) => self.crit,
            _ => Criteria::And(vec![self.crit, crit]),
        };
        self
    }

    /// `filter(field__op=value)` shorthand.
    pub fn filter_field(
        self,
        field: impl Into<String>,
        op: super::Op,
        value: impl Into<Value>,
    ) -> Self {
        self.filter(Criteria::cond(field, op, value))
    }

    /// NOT the criteria — `.exclude(Q(...))`.
    pub fn exclude(self, crit: Criteria) -> Self {
        self.filter(Criteria::Not(Box::new(crit)))
    }

    /// `order_by("name")` / `order_by("-pub_date")`.
    pub fn order_by(mut self, field: &str) -> Self {
        let desc = field.starts_with('-');
        let name = field.trim_start_matches('-').to_string();
        self.order.push((name, desc));
        self
    }

    /// Django's `qs[:n]` slice.
    pub fn take(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
        self.limit = Some(n);
        self
    }

    /// Django's `qs[a:]` slice start.
    pub fn skip(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
        self.offset = Some(n);
        self
    }

    /// Evaluate to rows.
    pub fn rows(&self) -> OrmResult<Vec<Row>> {
        self.backend.select(
            T::table(),
            &self.crit,
            &self.order,
            self.limit,
            self.offset,
        )
    }

    /// Evaluate to model instances — iterating the QuerySet.
    pub fn all(&self) -> OrmResult<Vec<T>> {
        Ok(self.rows()?.iter().map(|r| T::from_row(r)).collect())
    }

    /// `qs.count()`.
    pub fn count(&self) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        self.backend.count(T::table(), &self.crit)
    }

    /// `qs.exists()`.
    pub fn exists(&self) -> OrmResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.count()? > 0)
    }

    /// `qs.first()` — None when empty.
    pub fn first(&self) -> OrmResult<Option<T>> {
        let qs = Self {
            backend: self.backend,
            crit: self.crit.clone(),
            order: self.order.clone(),
            limit: Some(1),
            offset: self.offset,
            _pd: PhantomData,
        };
        Ok(qs.rows()?.into_iter().next().map(|r| T::from_row(&r)))
    }

    /// `qs.latest("field")` — first row under reversed order.
    pub fn latest(self, field: &str) -> OrmResult<T> {
        let desc = !field.starts_with('-');
        let name = field.trim_start_matches('-').to_string();
        let qs = self.order_by(&if desc { format!("-{name}") } else { name }).take(1);
        qs.first()?
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::errors::OrmError::DoesNotExist(format!("{} latest({})", T::table(), field)))
    }

    /// `qs.get(pk=..)` / `qs.get(Q(..))` — exactly one row or an error.
    pub fn get(self, crit: Criteria) -> OrmResult<T> {
        let qs = self.filter(crit).take(2);
        let rows = qs.rows()?;
        match rows.len() {
            0 => Err(crate::errors::OrmError::DoesNotExist(format!(
                "{} matching query does not exist",
                T::table()
            ))),
            1 => Ok(T::from_row(&rows[0])),
            _ => Err(crate::errors::OrmError::MultipleObjectsReturned(format!(
                "get() returned more than one {}",
                T::table()
            ))),
        }
    }

    /// Bulk UPDATE — `qs.update(values)` where values are (column_index,
    /// new_value). Use [`QuerySet::column_index`] to resolve indexes.
    pub fn update(&self, updates: &[(usize, Value)]) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        self.backend.update(T::table(), &self.crit, updates)
    }

    /// Bulk DELETE — returns number of rows removed.
    pub fn delete(&self) -> OrmResult<usize> {
        // FK traversal criteria may reference other tables; delete row by row
        // so model signals fire (Django also fires signals per-instance here).
        let rows = self.rows()?;
        let mut n = 0;
        for row in rows {
            let obj = T::from_row(&row);
            n += obj.delete(self.backend)?;
        }
        Ok(n)
    }
}

impl<'a, T: Model> Clone for QuerySet<'a, T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            backend: self.backend,
            crit: self.crit.clone(),
            order: self.order.clone(),
            limit: self.limit,
            offset: self.offset,
            _pd: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::orm::InMemoryBackend;
    use std::sync::Arc;

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, crate::Model)]
#[model(table = "test_book")]
    pub struct Book {
        #[field(auto)]
        pub id: i64,
        #[field(char, max = 100)]
        pub title: String,
        #[field(int, default = 0)]
        pub author_id: i64,
        #[field(int, default = 0)]
        pub pages: i64,
        #[field(bool, default = false)]
        pub published: bool,
    }

    fn backend() -> Arc<InMemoryBackend> {
        let b = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        b.create_table(Book::table(), Book::columns().to_vec()).unwrap();
        for (t, a, p, pubd) in [
            ("Rust Book", 1, 300, true),
            ("Django Book", 2, 450, true),
            ("Go Book", 1, 250, false),
            ("Zig Book", 3, 180, true),
        ] {
            let b0 = Book { id: 0, title: t.into(), author_id: a, pages: p, published: pubd };
            b0.save(&*b).unwrap();
        }
        b
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_and_count() {
        let b = backend();
        assert_eq!(Book::objects(&*b).all().unwrap().len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(Book::objects(&*b).count().unwrap(), 4);
        assert!(Book::objects(&*b).exists().unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn filter_chain() {
        let b = backend();
        let qs = Book::objects(&*b)
            .filter(Criteria::eq("published", Value::Bool(true)))
            .filter(Criteria::gt("pages", Value::Int(200)));
        let books = qs.all().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(books.len(), 2); // rust(300), django(450)
        assert_eq!(qs.count().unwrap(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn exclude() {
        let b = backend();
        let qs = Book::objects(&*b)
            .exclude(Criteria::eq("author_id", Value::Int(1)));
        assert_eq!(qs.count().unwrap(), 2); // django, zig
    }

    #[test]
    fn order_and_slice() {
        let b = backend();
        let books = Book::objects(&*b)
            .order_by("-pages")
            .all()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(books[0].title, "Django Book");

        let top2 = Book::objects(&*b).order_by("-pages").take(2).all().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(top2.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(top2[0].pages, 450);
        assert_eq!(top2[1].pages, 300);

        let skipped = Book::objects(&*b).order_by("pages").skip(1).take(2).all().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(skipped[0].pages, 250);
    }

    #[test]
    fn get_semantics() {
        let b = backend();
        let one = Book::objects(&*b)
            .get(Criteria::eq("title", Value::Text("Go Book".into())))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(one.author_id, 1);

        assert!(Book::objects(&*b)
            .get(Criteria::eq("title", Value::Text("Nope".into())))
            .is_err());

        // two matches -> MultipleObjectsReturned
        let err = Book::objects(&*b).get(Criteria::gt("pages", Value::Int(200)));
        assert_eq!(
            err.unwrap_err(),
            crate::errors::OrmError::MultipleObjectsReturned("get() returned more than one test_book".into())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn first_and_latest() {
        let b = backend();
        let f = Book::objects(&*b).order_by("title").first().unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(f.title, "Django Book");
        assert!(Book::objects(&*b)
            .filter(Criteria::eq("title", Value::Text("zzz".into())))
            .first()
            .unwrap()
            .is_none());

        let latest = Book::objects(&*b).latest("pages").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(latest.pages, 450);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bulk_update() {
        let b = backend();
        let idx = Book::column_index("published").unwrap();
        let n = Book::objects(&*b)
            .filter(Criteria::eq("author_id", Value::Int(1)))
            .update(&[(idx, Value::Bool(true))])
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 2);
        assert_eq!(
            Book::objects(&*b)
                .filter(Criteria::eq("published", Value::Bool(true)))
                .count()
                .unwrap(),
            4
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn bulk_delete() {
        let b = backend();
        let n = Book::objects(&*b)
            .filter(Criteria::eq("author_id", Value::Int(1)))
            .delete()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(n, 2);
        assert_eq!(Book::objects(&*b).count().unwrap(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn q_or_semantics() {
        let b = backend();
        let qs = Book::objects(&*b).filter(
            Criteria::eq("author_id", Value::Int(2)) | Criteria::eq("author_id", Value::Int(3)),
        );
        assert_eq!(qs.count().unwrap(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn queryset_clone_and_reuse() {
        let b = backend();
        let base = Book::objects(&*b).filter(Criteria::eq("published", Value::Bool(true)));
        let a = base.clone().order_by("pages").all().unwrap();
        let c = base.clone().count().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(c, 3);
        // original unchanged
        assert_eq!(base.count().unwrap(), 3);
    }
}

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/src/project.rs)

````rust
//! `Project` — the settings module + ROOT_URLCONF + app registry, assembled
//! in code:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use rustango::prelude::*;
//!
//! let mut project = Project::builder()
//!     .settings(Settings::builder().debug(true).build())
//!     .add_app(App::new("polls").models::<Question>().models::<Choice>())
//!     .urls(vec![path("polls/", polls_index)])
//!     .admin(|site| { site.register::<Question>(); })
//!     .build();
//! let res = project.handle_request(&mut req);
//! ```

use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::errors::HttpError;
use crate::http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse};
use crate::middleware::{Middleware, MiddlewareStack};
use crate::orm::backend::backend_from_alias;
use crate::orm::{Backend, InMemoryBackend, ModelMeta};
use crate::settings::Settings;
use crate::templates::{Engine, FileSystemLoader};
use crate::urls::Router;

/// Callback that configures the admin site (`.admin(|site| ...)`).
type AdminConfig = Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut crate::admin::AdminSite) + Send>;

/// An app: a name plus the models it declares — `INSTALLED_APPS` + models.py.
pub struct App {
    pub name: String,
    pub models: Vec<ModelMeta>,
}

impl App {
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> App {
        App { name: name.into(), models: Vec::new() }
    }

    /// Register a model with this app and the global registry.
    pub fn models<T: crate::orm::Model>(mut self) -> App {
        let meta = ModelMeta::of::<T>();
        crate::orm::register_model(meta.clone());
        self.models.push(meta);
        self
    }
}

/// The assembled project: settings + backend + engine + router + middleware.
pub struct Project {
    pub settings: Settings,
    pub backend: Arc<dyn Backend>,
    pub engine: Arc<Engine>,
    pub router: Arc<Router>,
    pub stack: MiddlewareStack,
    pub admin: Option<Arc<crate::admin::AdminSite>>,
}

pub struct ProjectBuilder {
    settings: Settings,
    backend: Option<Arc<dyn Backend>>,
    apps: Vec<App>,
    routes: Vec<crate::urls::Route>,
    extra_middleware: Vec<Arc<dyn Middleware>>,
    admin_config: Option<AdminConfig>,
    admin_enabled: bool,
    extra_loaders: Vec<Box<dyn crate::templates::TemplateLoader>>,
}

impl Default for ProjectBuilder {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl ProjectBuilder {
    pub fn new() -> ProjectBuilder {
        ProjectBuilder {
            settings: Settings::default(),
            backend: None,
            apps: Vec::new(),
            routes: Vec::new(),
            extra_middleware: Vec::new(),
            admin_config: None,
            admin_enabled: true,
            extra_loaders: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn settings(mut self, s: Settings) -> Self {
        self.settings = s;
        self
    }

    pub fn backend(mut self, b: Arc<dyn Backend>) -> Self {
        self.backend = Some(b);
        self
    }

    pub fn add_app(mut self, app: App) -> Self {
        self.apps.push(app);
        self
    }

    pub fn urls(mut self, routes: Vec<crate::urls::Route>) -> Self {
        self.routes.extend(routes);
        self
    }

    /// Append user middleware AFTER the default stack.
    pub fn middleware(mut self, mw: Arc<dyn Middleware>) -> Self {
        self.extra_middleware.push(mw);
        self
    }

    /// Configure the admin site.
    pub fn admin<F>(mut self, f: F) -> Self
    where
        F: FnOnce(&mut crate::admin::AdminSite) + Send + 'static,
    {
        self.admin_config = Some(Box::new(f));
        self.admin_enabled = true;
        self
    }

    /// Additional template loaders (checked after DIRS, before admin ones).
    pub fn template_loader(mut self, loader: Box<dyn crate::templates::TemplateLoader>) -> Self {
        self.extra_loaders.push(loader);
        self
    }

    /// Assemble everything.
    pub fn build(self) -> Result<Project, String> {
        let settings = self.settings;

        let backend: Arc<dyn Backend> = match self.backend {
            Some(b) => b,
            None => backend_from_alias(&settings.database)
                .map_err(|e| format!("backend error: {e}"))?,
        };

        // Built-in framework tables (auth_user, django_session, ...).
        ensure_builtin_schema(&*backend).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

        // Ensure every registered model's table exists (dev convenience —
        // production runs `rustango migrate`).
        {
            let reg = crate::orm::registry().read().unwrap().models.clone();
            for meta in &reg {
                backend
                    .create_table(&meta.table, meta.columns.clone())
                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            }
        }

        // Admin site.
        let admin = if self.admin_enabled && settings.admin_enabled {
            let mut site = crate::admin::AdminSite::new(
                settings.site_title.clone(),
                settings.site_header.clone(),
            );
            if let Some(f) = self.admin_config {
                f(&mut site);
            }
            // Keep redirects/templates in sync with the configured mount point.
            site.url_prefix = settings.admin_url.trim_matches('/').to_string();
            Some(Arc::new(site))
        } else {
            None
        };

        // Template engine: DIRS first, then extra loaders, then embedded
        // admin templates.
        let mut loaders: Vec<Box<dyn crate::templates::TemplateLoader>> = vec![Box::new(
            FileSystemLoader::new(settings.template_dirs.clone()),
        )];
        for l in self.extra_loaders {
            loaders.push(l);
        }
        loaders.push(Box::new(crate::admin::embedded_templates()));
        let engine = Arc::new(Engine::new(loaders, settings.debug));

        // Router: user urls + admin + static.
        let mut router = Router::new(self.routes);
        if let Some(admin) = &admin {
            let admin_router = admin.urls();
            router.mount(&settings.admin_url, "admin", admin_router);
        }
        if !settings.staticfiles_dirs.is_empty() {
            let static_pattern = format!("{}<path:asset>", settings.static_url);
            router
                .routes
                .push(crate::urls::path(&static_pattern, crate::views::make_view(|req| {
                    crate::staticfiles::serve(req)
                })));
        }
        let router = Arc::new(router);
        crate::urls::set_route_registry((*router).clone());

        // Middleware.
        let mut middlewares = crate::middleware::default_stack(&settings, backend.clone(), router.clone());
        for mw in self.extra_middleware {
            middlewares.push(mw);
        }

        // Global settings snapshot (django.conf.settings equivalent).
        let _ = crate::settings::set_global(settings.clone());

        Ok(Project {
            settings,
            backend,
            engine,
            router,
            stack: MiddlewareStack::new(middlewares),
            admin,
        })
    }
}

fn ensure_builtin_schema(backend: &dyn Backend) -> crate::orm::OrmResult<()> {
    use crate::orm::{ColumnDesc, Model as _};
    backend.create_table("auth_user", crate::auth::User::columns().to_vec())?;
    backend.create_table("django_session", crate::sessions::session_columns())?;
    backend.create_table(
        "_migrations",
        vec![
            ColumnDesc::auto("id"),
            ColumnDesc::char("app", 100),
            ColumnDesc::char("name", 255),
            ColumnDesc::datetime("applied_at", false),
        ],
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

impl Project {
    pub fn builder() -> ProjectBuilder {
        ProjectBuilder::new()
    }

    /// The full request pipeline — what `runserver` and the test client call.
    pub fn handle_request(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> HttpResponse {
        req.engine = Some(self.engine.clone());
        req.backend = Some(self.backend.clone());

        crate::signals::emit_request(&req.full_path, "request_started");
        let view = self.resolve_view(req);
        let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
            self.stack.dispatch(req, &view)
        }));

        let response = match result {
            Ok(Ok(res)) => res,
            Ok(Err(err)) => {
                let mut res = self.render_error(req, err);
                // Error responses still pass through the response phase so
                // cookies/headers (CSRF, session, security) are applied.
                self.stack.run_response(req, &mut res);
                res
            }
            Err(panic) => {
                let msg = panic
                    .downcast_ref::<&str>()
                    .map(|s| s.to_string())
                    .or_else(|| panic.downcast_ref::<String>().cloned())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "view panicked".to_string());
                let mut res =
                    self.render_error(req, HttpError::ServerError(msg));
                self.stack.run_response(req, &mut res);
                res
            }
        };

        crate::signals::emit_request(&req.full_path, "request_finished");
        response
    }

    fn resolve_view(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest) -> crate::views::ViewFn {
        match self.router.match_path(&req.path) {
            Some((route, params)) => {
                req.params = params;
                req.url_name = route.name.clone();
                if route.csrf_exempt {
                    req.params
                        .insert(crate::csrf::EXEMPT_FLAG.to_string(), "1".to_string());
                }
                route.view
            }
            None => crate::views::make_view(|_req| {
                Err(HttpError::NotFound("no route matched".into()))
            }),
        }
    }

    /// DEBUG pretty errors; terse production ones.
    fn render_error(&self, req: &mut HttpRequest, err: HttpError) -> HttpResponse {
        let status = err.status();
        let _ = req;
        if self.settings.debug {
            let html = format!(
                "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>{status} — rustango</title>\
                 <style>body{{font-family:sans-serif;max-width:720px;margin:40px auto;color:#222}}\
                 h1{{color:#b00}} pre{{background:#f4f4f4;padding:12px;border-radius:6px}}</style></head>\
                 <body><h1>{status}</h1><h2>{kind}</h2><pre>{msg}</pre>\
                 <p><small>rustango {version} — DEBUG page (set debug=false to hide)</small></p>\
                 </body></html>",
                status = status,
                kind = kind_of(&err),
                msg = crate::templates::escape_html(&err.to_string()),
                version = crate::VERSION,
            );
            HttpResponse::with_body(status, "text/html; charset=utf-8", html)
        } else {
            HttpResponse::with_body(
                status,
                "text/plain; charset=utf-8",
                format!("{} {}", status, kind_of(&err)),
            )
        }
    }

    /// Convenience for tests/REPL: a request straight through the pipeline.
    pub fn test_request(&self, mut req: HttpRequest) -> HttpResponse {
        self.handle_request(&mut req)
    }
}

fn kind_of(err: &HttpError) -> &'static str {
    match err {
        HttpError::NotFound(_) => "Not Found",
        HttpError::PermissionDenied(_) => "Permission Denied",
        HttpError::BadRequest(_) => "Bad Request",
        HttpError::MethodNotAllowed(_) => "Method Not Allowed",
        HttpError::CsrfFailure(_) => "CSRF Verification Failed",
        HttpError::ServerError(_) => "Server Error",
    }
}

/// In-memory project helper for tests.
pub fn memory_project() -> Project {
    Project::builder()
        .settings(Settings::builder().build())
        .backend(Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()))
        .urls(vec![])
        .build()
        .expect("memory project")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::http::Method;
    use crate::orm::ModelExt as _;
    use crate::templates::InMemoryLoader;
    use crate::urls::{path, named_path};
    use std::sync::Arc as StdArc;

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, crate::Model)]
    #[model(table = "proj_greeting")]
    pub struct Greeting {
        #[field(auto)]
        pub id: i64,
        #[field(char, max = 60)]
        pub text: String,
    }

    #[test]
    fn project_dispatch_full_pipeline() {
        let index = crate::views::make_view(|req| {
            let mut ctx = crate::templates::Context::new();
            ctx.set("path", crate::templates::TplValue::Str(req.path.clone()));
            crate::views::render(req, "index.html", ctx)
        });
        let project = Project::builder()
            .settings(Settings::builder().build())
            .backend(StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()))
            .urls(vec![
                named_path("", index, "home"),
                path("missing/", crate::views::make_view(|_r| Ok(HttpResponse::text("x")))),
            ])
            .template_loader(Box::new({
                let mut l = InMemoryLoader::new();
                l.add("index.html", "PATH={{ request.path }} U={{ user.username }}");
                l
            }))
            .build()
            .unwrap();

        // normal dispatch through middleware + router + template
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/");
        let res = project.handle_request(&mut req);
        assert_eq!(res.status, 200);
        assert!(res.body_string().contains("PATH=/"));

        // 404 handling (debug page)
        let mut req404 = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/nowhere/");
        let res404 = project.handle_request(&mut req404);
        assert_eq!(res404.status, 404);
        assert!(res404.body_string().contains("Not Found"));

        // APPEND_SLASH via CommonMiddleware — Django-style permanent (301)
        // redirect, query string preserved.
        let mut reqslash = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/missing");
        let resslash = project.handle_request(&mut reqslash);
        assert_eq!(resslash.status, 301);
        assert_eq!(resslash.headers.get("Location"), Some("/missing/"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn panicking_view_becomes_500() {
        let boom = crate::views::make_view(|_req| -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
            panic!("intentional")
        });
        let project = Project::builder()
            .backend(StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()))
            .urls(vec![path("boom/", boom)])
            .build()
            .unwrap();
        let mut req = HttpRequest::new(Method::GET, "/boom/");
        let res = project.handle_request(&mut req);
        assert_eq!(res.status, 500);
        assert!(res.body_string().contains("intentional"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn model_tables_created_on_build() {
        let project = Project::builder()
            .backend(StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()))
            .add_app(App::new("test").models::<Greeting>())
            .build()
            .unwrap();
        assert!(project.backend.tables().contains(&"proj_greeting".to_string()));
        // auth tables exist too
        assert!(project.backend.tables().contains(&"auth_user".to_string()));
        assert!(project.backend.tables().contains(&"django_session".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn model_save_through_project_backend() {
        let project = Project::builder()
            .backend(StdArc::new(InMemoryBackend::new()))
            .add_app(App::new("test").models::<Greeting>())
            .build()
            .unwrap();
        let g = Greeting { id: 0, text: "hello".into() };
        let saved = g.save(&*project.backend).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved.pk(), 1);
    }
}

```rust
//! HTTP server glue — tokio + axum at the edge, sync framework core on
//! blocking worker threads (WSGI-style thread-per-request).

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;

use axum::extract::Request as AxumRequest;
use axum::response::Response as AxumResponse;
use tokio::net::TcpListener;

use crate::http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse, Method};
use crate::project::Project;

/// Verbs outside the known set must be rejected with 405. The old
/// `unwrap_or(Method::GET)` downgraded unknown methods (PROPFIND, FOO, …)
/// to GET, which `is_safe()` treats as CSRF-exempt and routes to
/// `View::get()` — an attacker-controlled verb silently became a safe GET.
fn resolve_method(raw: &str) -> Result<Method, HttpResponse> {
    Method::parse(raw).ok_or_else(|| {
        let mut res = HttpResponse::with_body(
            405,
            "text/plain; charset=utf-8",
            format!("Method `{raw}` not allowed"),
        );
        res.headers
            .set("Allow", "GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE");
        res
    })
}

/// Convert an axum request into a rustango `HttpRequest`. Unknown verbs
/// short-circuit into a 405 response instead of becoming `Method::GET`.
async fn to_internal(req: AxumRequest) -> Result<HttpRequest, HttpResponse> {
    let method = resolve_method(req.method().as_str())?;
    let path = req.uri().path().to_string();
    let query = req.uri().query().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let full = if query.is_empty() {
        path.clone()
    } else {
        format!("{path}?{query}")
    };
    let mut internal = HttpRequest::new(method, full);
    for (k, v) in req.headers() {
        if let Ok(v) = v.to_str() {
            internal.headers.add(k.as_str().to_string(), v.to_string());
        }
    }
    // Join every Cookie header (clients/proxies may send several).
    let cookie_header = internal.headers.get_all("cookie").join("; ");
    if !cookie_header.is_empty() {
        internal.cookies = crate::http::parse_cookie_header(&cookie_header);
    }
    internal.remote_addr = req
        .extensions()
        .get::<std::net::SocketAddr>()
        .map(|a| a.to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into());
    let body = axum::body::to_bytes(req.into_body(), 64 * 1024 * 1024)
        .await
        .unwrap_or_default();
    internal.body = body.to_vec();
    let content_type = internal.headers.get("content-type").unwrap_or("").to_string();
    if content_type.starts_with("application/x-www-form-urlencoded") {
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&internal.body);
        internal.post = crate::http::QueryDict::parse(&text);
    } else if content_type.starts_with("application/json") {
        if let Ok(serde_json::Value::Object(map)) =
            serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&internal.body)
        {
            for (k, val) in map {
                let s = match val {
                    serde_json::Value::String(s) => s,
                    other => other.to_string(),
                };
                internal.post.set(k, s);
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(internal)
}

fn to_axum(res: HttpResponse) -> AxumResponse {
    let mut builder = AxumResponse::builder().status(res.status);
    for (k, v) in res.headers.iter() {
        builder = builder.header(k, v);
    }
    for cookie in &res.cookies {
        builder = builder.header("Set-Cookie", cookie.to_header());
    }
    builder
        .body(axum::body::Body::from(res.body().to_vec()))
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| AxumResponse::new("internal error".into()))
}

/// Serve the project on `addr`.
pub async fn serve(project: Arc<Project>, addr: SocketAddr) -> Result<(), String> {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("bind {addr}: {e}"))?;
    println!(
        "rustango {} starting server at http://{} (DEBUG: {}) — press Ctrl-C to stop",
        crate::VERSION,
        addr,
        project.settings.debug
    );
    let app = axum::Router::new().fallback(move |req: AxumRequest| {
        let project = project.clone();
        async move {
            let internal = match to_internal(req).await {
                Ok(r) => r,
                Err(res) => return to_axum(res),
            };
            let res = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                let mut r = internal;
                project.handle_request(&mut r)
            })
            .await
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| HttpResponse::status(500));
            to_axum(res)
        }
    });
    axum::serve(listener, app).await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// Bind and run with graceful shutdown on Ctrl-C.
pub async fn serve_with_shutdown(project: Arc<Project>, addr: SocketAddr) -> Result<(), String> {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("bind {addr}: {e}"))?;
    println!(
        "rustango {} serving http://{} (DEBUG: {})",
        crate::VERSION,
        addr,
        project.settings.debug
    );
    let app = axum::Router::new().fallback(move |req: AxumRequest| {
        let project = project.clone();
        async move {
            let internal = match to_internal(req).await {
                Ok(r) => r,
                Err(res) => return to_axum(res),
            };
            let res = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                let mut r = internal;
                project.handle_request(&mut r)
            })
            .await
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| HttpResponse::status(500));
            to_axum(res)
        }
    });
    axum::serve(listener, app)
        .with_graceful_shutdown(shutdown_signal())
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

async fn shutdown_signal() {
    let _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await;
    println!("\nshutting down...");
}

/// Build an axum Router from a project (for embedding rustango into a
/// larger axum application).
pub fn axum_router(project: Arc<Project>) -> axum::Router {
    axum::Router::new().fallback(move |req: AxumRequest| {
        let project = project.clone();
        async move {
            let internal = match to_internal(req).await {
                Ok(r) => r,
                Err(res) => return to_axum(res),
            };
            let res = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                let mut r = internal;
                project.handle_request(&mut r)
            })
            .await
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| HttpResponse::status(500));
            to_axum(res)
        }
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn unknown_verbs_get_405_not_get() {
        // Regression: unknown verbs used to fall back to `Method::GET`, which
        // is_safe() exempts from CSRF and routes to `View::get()`.
        for verb in ["PROPFIND", "FOO", "BREW", "CONNECT"] {
            let err = resolve_method(verb).expect_err("unknown verb must be rejected");
            assert_eq!(err.status, 405, "verb {verb} must map to 405");
            assert!(err.headers.get("Allow").is_some());
        }
        // All known verbs still resolve (case-insensitive like `parse`).
        for (raw, expect) in [
            ("GET", Method::GET),
            ("get", Method::GET),
            ("POST", Method::POST),
            ("put", Method::PUT),
            ("PATCH", Method::PATCH),
            ("DELETE", Method::DELETE),
            ("HEAD", Method::HEAD),
            ("OPTIONS", Method::OPTIONS),
            ("TRACE", Method::TRACE),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(resolve_method(raw).unwrap(), expect, "verb {raw}");
        }
    }
}

```rust
//! Server-side sessions — `django.contrib.sessions` with database backend.
//!
//! The session data lives in the `django_session` table (same name as
//! Django's own default table) as a JSON blob, keyed by a 32-char session
//! key stored in the `sessionid` cookie.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use serde_json::Value as JsonValue;

use crate::orm::{Backend, Criteria, Op, Value};

pub const SESSION_TABLE: &str = "django_session";
const SESSION_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;

/// A user session, attached to `request.session` by SessionMiddleware.
pub struct Session {
    pub key: String,
    data: HashMap<String, JsonValue>,
    pub modified: bool,
    pub expiry: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub cookie_age: i64,
    backend: Arc<dyn Backend>,
    pub flushed: bool,
    pub new: bool,
    /// Set when this session was persisted during the request — the cookie
    /// must be re-sent (key rotation / creation).
    pub written: bool,
}

impl Session {
    /// Load an existing session by cookie key, or create a fresh one.
    pub fn load(backend: Arc<dyn Backend>, key: Option<&str>, cookie_age: i64) -> Session {
        // Creating the table flushes the whole JSON file — skip it when the
        // table already exists (in-memory check) so a request neither
        // rewrites the DB nor races a concurrent flush.
        if !backend.tables().iter().any(|t| t == SESSION_TABLE) {
            let _ = backend.create_table(SESSION_TABLE, session_columns());
        }
        if let Some(key) = key {
            if key.len() >= 8 && key.len() <= 64 {
                let crit = Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(key.to_string()));
                if let Ok(rows) = backend.select(SESSION_TABLE, &crit, &[], None, None) {
                    if let Some(row) = rows.first() {
                        let data = row
                            .get(1)
                            .and_then(|v| v.as_text())
                            .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str::<HashMap<String, JsonValue>>(s).ok())
                            .unwrap_or_default();
                        let expiry = row
                            .get(2)
                            .and_then(|v| v.as_datetime())
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| Utc::now() + Duration::seconds(cookie_age));
                        // Expired sessions are treated as absent (Django's
                        // SessionMiddleware drops them at load time).
                        if Utc::now() < expiry {
                            return Session {
                                key: key.to_string(),
                                data,
                                modified: false,
                                expiry,
                                cookie_age,
                                backend,
                                flushed: false,
                                new: false,
                                written: false,
                            };
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Self::fresh(backend, cookie_age)
    }

    fn fresh(backend: Arc<dyn Backend>, cookie_age: i64) -> Session {
        Session {
            key: new_session_key(),
            data: HashMap::new(),
            modified: false,
            expiry: Utc::now() + Duration::seconds(cookie_age),
            cookie_age,
            backend,
            flushed: false,
            new: true,
            written: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_expired(&self) -> bool { Utc::now() >= self.expiry }

    /// `request.session["k"] = v`
    pub fn set(&mut self, key: impl Into<String>, value: JsonValue) {
        self.data.insert(key.into(), value);
        self.modified = true;
    }

    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&JsonValue> { self.data.get(key) }

    /// `request.session.get("k", default)`
    pub fn get_or(&self, key: &str, default: &str) -> String {
        self.data
            .get(key)
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .unwrap_or(default)
            .to_string()
    }

    pub fn get_int(&self, key: &str) -> Option<i64> {
        self.data.get(key).and_then(|v| v.as_i64())
    }

    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &str) -> Option<JsonValue> {
        self.modified = true;
        self.data.remove(key)
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, key: &str) -> bool { self.data.contains_key(key) }

    pub fn keys(&self) -> Vec<String> { self.data.keys().cloned().collect() }

    /// `session.clear()` — keeps the same key, empties data.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.data.clear();
        self.modified = true;
    }

    /// `session.flush()` — delete the old session and start a new key.
    pub fn flush(&mut self) {
        self.data.clear();
        self.flushed = true;
        self.modified = true;
        if !self.new {
            let _ = self.backend.delete(
                SESSION_TABLE,
                &Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(self.key.clone())),
            );
        }
        self.key = new_session_key();
        self.expiry = Utc::now() + Duration::seconds(self.cookie_age);
        self.new = true;
    }

    /// `session.cycle_key()` — keep data, rotate the key (used on login to
    /// prevent session fixation, exactly like Django).
    pub fn cycle_key(&mut self) {
        let data = self.data.clone();
        self.flush();
        self.data = data;
    }

    /// Persist to the backend if modified. Called by SessionMiddleware.
    pub fn save(&mut self) {
        if !self.modified && !self.new {
            return;
        }
        self.written = true;
        if self.flushed {
            // flush() already rotated the key; write the (possibly empty)
            // new session row.
            self.flushed = false;
        }
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&self.data).unwrap_or_default();
        let row = vec![
            Value::Text(self.key.clone()),
            Value::Text(json.clone()),
            Value::DateTime(self.expiry),
        ];
        let crit = Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(self.key.clone()));
        match self.backend.update(
            SESSION_TABLE,
            &crit,
            &[(1usize, Value::Text(json.clone())), (2usize, Value::DateTime(self.expiry))],
        ) {
            Ok(0) => {
                let _ = self.backend.insert(SESSION_TABLE, row);
            }
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(_) => {
                let _ = self.backend.insert(SESSION_TABLE, row);
            }
        }
        self.modified = false;
        self.new = false;
    }

    /// Delete this session entirely (logout).
    pub fn delete(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.backend.delete(
            SESSION_TABLE,
            &Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(self.key.clone())),
        );
        self.data.clear();
        self.modified = true;
        self.new = true;
        self.key = new_session_key();
    }

    /// Purge expired sessions (like `clearsessions` management command).
    pub fn clear_expired(backend: &dyn Backend) -> usize {
        backend
            .delete(SESSION_TABLE, &Criteria::cond("expire_date", Op::Lt, Value::DateTime(Utc::now())))
            .unwrap_or(0)
    }
}

/// Random 32-char lowercase session key, exactly like Django's format.
pub fn new_session_key() -> String {
    // Generate directly from the RNG bytes formatted as hex: 16 random
    // bytes -> 32 uniform hex digits (128 bits). The old `pair % 16` scheme
    // mapped ASCII hex chars through a modulo, skewing the digit
    // distribution (~83 bits effective entropy).
    let uuid = uuid::Uuid::new_v4();
    let bytes = uuid.as_bytes();
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(SESSION_KEY_LEN);
    for b in bytes {
        if s.len() >= SESSION_KEY_LEN {
            break;
        }
        s.push_str(&format!("{b:02x}"));
    }
    s
}

/// Column layout of `django_session` for schema registration.
pub fn session_columns() -> Vec<crate::orm::ColumnDesc> {
    vec![
        crate::orm::ColumnDesc::char("session_key", 40).unique(),
        crate::orm::ColumnDesc::text("session_data"),
        crate::orm::ColumnDesc::datetime("expire_date", false),
    ]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::orm::InMemoryBackend;

    #[test]
    fn session_set_get_persist() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mut s = Session::load(backend.clone(), None, 3600);
        assert!(s.new);
        s.set("user_id", JsonValue::from(7i64));
        s.set("theme", JsonValue::from("dark"));
        s.save();

        let key = s.key.clone();
        let reloaded = Session::load(backend, Some(&key), 3600);
        assert!(!reloaded.new);
        assert_eq!(reloaded.get_int("user_id"), Some(7));
        assert_eq!(reloaded.get_or("theme", "light"), "dark");
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_flush_rotates_key_and_deletes_old() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mut s = Session::load(backend.clone(), None, 3600);
        s.set("x", JsonValue::from(1));
        s.save();
        let old_key = s.key.clone();
        s.flush();
        assert_ne!(s.key, old_key);
        // old row gone
        let crit = Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(old_key));
        assert_eq!(backend.count(SESSION_TABLE, &crit).unwrap(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_cycle_key_keeps_data() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mut s = Session::load(backend, None, 3600);
        s.set("cart", JsonValue::from("apples"));
        let old_key = s.key.clone();
        s.cycle_key();
        assert_ne!(s.key, old_key);
        assert_eq!(s.get_or("cart", "empty"), "apples");
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_delete() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mut s = Session::load(backend.clone(), None, 3600);
        s.set("a", JsonValue::from(1));
        s.save();
        let key = s.key.clone();
        s.delete();
        let crit = Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(key));
        assert_eq!(backend.count(SESSION_TABLE, &crit).unwrap(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_key_gets_fresh_session() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let s = Session::load(backend, Some("doesnotexist123456"), 3600);
        assert!(s.new);
        assert!(s.data.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_key_format() {
        let k = new_session_key();
        assert_eq!(k.len(), 32);
        assert!(k.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()));
        // Keys must be lowercase hex (Django's format).
        assert!(k.chars().all(|c| !c.is_ascii_uppercase()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn session_key_hex_digits_are_uniform() {
        // Regression: `pair % 16` mapped ASCII hex chars through a modulo,
        // skewing the digit distribution (~83 bits effective entropy).
        // Generating straight from RNG bytes must produce every hex digit
        // across a batch of keys, and no two keys may collide.
        let keys: Vec<String> = (0..200).map(|_| new_session_key()).collect();
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        let mut digits = [0usize; 16];
        for k in &keys {
            assert!(seen.insert(k.clone()), "duplicate session key");
            for c in k.chars() {
                let idx = c.to_digit(16).unwrap() as usize;
                digits[idx] += 1;
            }
        }
        assert!(
            digits.iter().all(|d| *d > 0),
            "every hex digit must occur; counts: {digits:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn expired_session_is_rejected() {
        let backend = Arc::new(InMemoryBackend::new());
        let mut s = Session::load(backend.clone(), None, 3600);
        s.set("k", JsonValue::from(1));
        s.save();
        let key = s.key.clone();
        // Force the stored expiry into the past.
        backend
            .update(
                SESSION_TABLE,
                &Criteria::eq("session_key", Value::Text(key.clone())),
                &[(2, Value::DateTime(Utc::now() - Duration::seconds(10)))],
            )
            .unwrap();
        let reloaded = Session::load(backend, Some(&key), 3600);
        assert!(reloaded.new, "expired session must be treated as absent");
        assert!(reloaded.get("k").is_none());
    }
}

//! Global framework settings — the equivalent of `django.conf.settings`.
//!
//! Settings are built programmatically through [`Settings::builder`] and can
//! be overridden from a `settings.toml` file. Every knob has a default that
//! mirrors Django's own defaults.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

/// How passwords are hashed. Mirrors Django's default PBKDF2-SHA256.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PasswordHasherConfig {
    /// Algorithm tag written into the hash string (`pbkdf2_sha256`), so
    /// hashes are byte-compatible with Django's `make_password` output.
    pub algorithm: &'static str,
    pub iterations: u32,
}

impl Default for PasswordHasherConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { algorithm: "pbkdf2_sha256", iterations: 600_000 }
    }
}

/// The full settings object.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// DEV mode: pretty 404/500 pages, template caching off.
    pub debug: bool,
    /// Secret key used for signing (kept for parity; sessions are server-side).
    pub secret_key: String,
    /// Allowed hosts — `["*"]` skips the check (dev default).
    pub allowed_hosts: Vec<String>,
    /// Root URL prefix for the admin site.
    pub admin_url: String,
    /// Serve the admin at all?
    pub admin_enabled: bool,
    /// Site title shown in admin.
    pub site_title: String,
    pub site_header: String,

    /// Template search dirs, first match wins (like DIRS + APP_DIRS).
    pub template_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Static files search dirs.
    pub staticfiles_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// URL prefix under which static files are served.
    pub static_url: String,

    /// Database backend alias: `memory` or `json:<path>`.
    pub database: String,
    /// Where migration files live.
    pub migrations_dir: PathBuf,

    /// i18n
    pub language_code: String,
    pub languages: Vec<String>,
    pub locale_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,

    /// CSRF protection on/off.
    pub csrf_enabled: bool,
    /// Cookie names.
    pub session_cookie_name: String,
    pub csrf_cookie_name: String,
    pub language_cookie_name: String,

    /// Middleware toggles for the built-ins.
    pub use_gzip: bool,
    pub use_security: bool,
    pub use_clickjacking: bool,
    pub x_frame_options: String,

    /// Gzip only compresses responses above this many bytes.
    pub gzip_min_length: usize,
    /// Sessions expire after this many seconds (default 2 weeks, like Django).
    pub session_cookie_age: i64,

    /// Cache: `locmem` (the only built-in backend).
    pub cache_backend: String,

    pub password_hasher: PasswordHasherConfig,

    /// contrib.ai configuration (OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
    pub ai_api_url: String,
    pub ai_api_key: String,
    pub ai_model: String,

    /// Extra user-defined settings bag.
    pub extra: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            debug: true,
            secret_key: "rustango-insecure-dev-key".into(),
            allowed_hosts: vec!["*".into()],
            admin_url: "admin/".into(),
            admin_enabled: true,
            site_title: "Rustango site admin".into(),
            site_header: "Rustango administration".into(),
            template_dirs: vec![],
            staticfiles_dirs: vec![],
            static_url: "static/".into(),
            database: "memory".into(),
            migrations_dir: PathBuf::from("migrations"),
            language_code: "en-us".into(),
            languages: vec!["en-us".into()],
            locale_dirs: vec![],
            csrf_enabled: true,
            session_cookie_name: "sessionid".into(),
            csrf_cookie_name: "csrftoken".into(),
            language_cookie_name: "rustango_language".into(),
            use_gzip: true,
            use_security: true,
            use_clickjacking: true,
            x_frame_options: "DENY".into(),
            gzip_min_length: 200,
            session_cookie_age: 14 * 24 * 3600,
            cache_backend: "locmem".into(),
            password_hasher: PasswordHasherConfig::default(),
            ai_api_url: "https://api.openai.com/v1".into(),
            ai_api_key: String::new(),
            ai_model: "gpt-4o-mini".into(),
            extra: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl Settings {
    pub fn builder() -> SettingsBuilder {
        SettingsBuilder { s: Settings::default() }
    }

    /// Overlay values from a TOML file (missing keys keep current values).
    pub fn load_toml(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let val: toml::Value = toml::from_str(text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let map = val.as_table().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        let g = |k: &str| map.get(k);
        if let Some(toml::Value::Boolean(b)) = g("debug") { self.debug = *b; }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("secret_key") { self.secret_key = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("database") { self.database = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("language_code") { self.language_code = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("static_url") { self.static_url = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("admin_url") { self.admin_url = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::Boolean(b)) = g("admin_enabled") { self.admin_enabled = *b; }
        if let Some(toml::Value::Boolean(b)) = g("csrf_enabled") { self.csrf_enabled = *b; }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("ai_api_url") { self.ai_api_url = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("ai_api_key") { self.ai_api_key = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::String(s)) = g("ai_model") { self.ai_model = s.clone(); }
        if let Some(toml::Value::Array(a)) = g("template_dirs") {
            self.template_dirs = a.iter().filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(PathBuf::from)).collect();
        }
        if let Some(toml::Value::Array(a)) = g("staticfiles_dirs") {
            self.staticfiles_dirs = a.iter().filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(PathBuf::from)).collect();
        }
        if let Some(toml::Value::Array(a)) = g("locale_dirs") {
            self.locale_dirs = a.iter().filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(PathBuf::from)).collect();
        }
        if let Some(toml::Value::Table(t)) = g("extra") {
            for (k, v) in t {
                if let Some(s) = v.as_str() {
                    self.extra.insert(k.clone(), s.to_string());
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Fluent builder for [`Settings`].
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct SettingsBuilder {
    s: Settings,
}

impl SettingsBuilder {
    pub fn build(self) -> Settings { self.s }

    pub fn debug(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.s.debug = v; self }
    pub fn secret_key(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.secret_key = v.into(); self }
    pub fn allowed_hosts(mut self, v: Vec<String>) -> Self { self.s.allowed_hosts = v; self }
    pub fn admin_url(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.admin_url = v.into(); self }
    pub fn admin_enabled(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.s.admin_enabled = v; self }
    pub fn template_dirs(mut self, v: Vec<PathBuf>) -> Self { self.s.template_dirs = v; self }
    pub fn staticfiles_dirs(mut self, v: Vec<PathBuf>) -> Self { self.s.staticfiles_dirs = v; self }
    pub fn static_url(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.static_url = v.into(); self }
    pub fn database(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.database = v.into(); self }
    pub fn migrations_dir(mut self, v: PathBuf) -> Self { self.s.migrations_dir = v; self }
    pub fn language_code(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.language_code = v.into(); self }
    pub fn languages(mut self, v: Vec<String>) -> Self { self.s.languages = v; self }
    pub fn locale_dirs(mut self, v: Vec<PathBuf>) -> Self { self.s.locale_dirs = v; self }
    pub fn csrf_enabled(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.s.csrf_enabled = v; self }
    pub fn session_cookie_name(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.session_cookie_name = v.into(); self }
    pub fn csrf_cookie_name(mut self, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self { self.s.csrf_cookie_name = v.into(); self }
    pub fn use_gzip(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.s.use_gzip = v; self }
    pub fn use_security(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.s.use_security = v; self }
    pub fn use_clickjacking(mut self, v: bool) -> Self { self.s.use_clickjacking = v; self }
    pub fn session_cookie_age(mut self, v: i64) -> Self { self.s.session_cookie_age = v; self }
    pub fn password_iterations(mut self, v: u32) -> Self { self.s.password_hasher.iterations = v; self }
    pub fn ai(mut self, url: impl Into<String>, key: impl Into<String>, model: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.s.ai_api_url = url.into();
        self.s.ai_api_key = key.into();
        self.s.ai_model = model.into();
        self
    }
    pub fn extra(mut self, k: impl Into<String>, v: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.s.extra.insert(k.into(), v.into());
        self
    }
}

/// Process-global settings, like `django.conf.settings`.
/// Set once at project startup; falls back to defaults.
static GLOBAL_SETTINGS: OnceLock<Settings> = OnceLock::new();

pub fn set_global(s: Settings) -> bool {
    GLOBAL_SETTINGS.set(s).is_ok()
}

pub fn global() -> &'static Settings {
    GLOBAL_SETTINGS.get_or_init(Settings::default)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn defaults_match_django_spirit() {
        let s = Settings::default();
        assert!(s.debug);
        assert_eq!(s.session_cookie_name, "sessionid");
        assert_eq!(s.csrf_cookie_name, "csrftoken");
        assert_eq!(s.password_hasher.algorithm, "pbkdf2_sha256");
        assert_eq!(s.x_frame_options, "DENY");
        assert_eq!(s.session_cookie_age, 14 * 24 * 3600);
    }

    #[test]
    fn toml_overlay() {
        let mut s = Settings::default();
        s.load_toml(
            r#"
            debug = false
            database = "json:db.json"
            language_code = "de"
            [extra]
            flavor = "rusty"
            "#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(!s.debug);
        assert_eq!(s.database, "json:db.json");
        assert_eq!(s.language_code, "de");
        assert_eq!(s.extra["flavor"], "rusty");
    }

    #[test]
    fn builder_chain() {
        let s = Settings::builder().debug(false).secret_key("abc").admin_enabled(false).build();
        assert!(!s.debug);
        assert_eq!(s.secret_key, "abc");
        assert!(!s.admin_enabled);
    }
}

````rust
//! Signals — `django.core.signals` receiver/dispatcher.
//!
//! Signals are global named events with `table`/`pk` payloads for model
//! lifecycle signals and a free-form note for request signals:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use rustango::signals;
//!
//! signals::connect("post_save", |payload| {
//!     if payload.table == "polls_question" {
//!         println!("question {} saved", payload.pk);
//!     }
//! });
//! ```

use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};

/// Payload carried by every signal emission.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SignalPayload {
    /// Signal name: `pre_save`, `post_save`, `pre_delete`, `post_delete`,
    /// `request_started`, `request_finished`, `got_request_exception`.
    pub name: &'static str,
    /// Model table the signal relates to ("" for request signals).
    pub table: String,
    /// Model primary key (0 when not applicable).
    pub pk: i64,
    /// Extra note (e.g. the request path for request signals).
    pub note: String,
}

type Receiver = Box<dyn Fn(&SignalPayload) + Send + Sync>;

struct SignalRegistry {
    receivers: Vec<Receiver>,
}

static REGISTRY: OnceLock<Mutex<SignalRegistry>> = OnceLock::new();

fn registry() -> &'static Mutex<SignalRegistry> {
    REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(SignalRegistry { receivers: Vec::new() }))
}

/// Register a receiver for a signal name — `signal.connect(receiver)`.
pub fn connect<F>(name: &'static str, f: F)
where
    F: Fn(&SignalPayload) + Send + Sync + 'static,
{
    let mut reg = registry().lock().unwrap();
    let filter_name = name;
    reg.receivers.push(Box::new(move |payload| {
        if payload.name == filter_name {
            f(payload);
        }
    }));
}

/// Register a receiver that fires for every signal (like connecting to
/// several `django.db.models.signals` at once).
pub fn connect_all<F>(f: F)
where
    F: Fn(&SignalPayload) + Send + Sync + 'static,
{
    registry().lock().unwrap().receivers.push(Box::new(f));
}

/// Number of registered receivers (tests/metrics).
pub fn receiver_count() -> usize {
    registry().lock().unwrap().receivers.len()
}

/// Fire a signal — `Model.save()` sends `pre_save`/`post_save`, the request
/// cycle sends `request_started`/`request_finished`. Receiver panics are
/// caught and reported to `tracing`-style stderr, never propagated into the
/// request (matching Django's `send_robust` spirit).
pub fn send(name: &'static str, table: &str, pk: i64, note: &str) {
    let payload = SignalPayload {
        name,
        table: table.to_string(),
        pk,
        note: note.to_string(),
    };
    let reg = registry().lock().unwrap();
    for rx in &reg.receivers {
        let _ = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| rx(&payload)));
    }
}

/// Model-lifecycle shortcuts used by the ORM.
pub fn emit(name: &'static str, table: &str, pk: i64) {
    send(name, table, pk, "");
}

pub fn emit_request(note: &str, name: &'static str) {
    send(name, "", 0, note);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    use std::sync::Arc;

    #[test]
    fn connect_and_send() {
        let hits = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let h2 = hits.clone();
        connect("post_save", move |p| {
            if p.table == "test_a" {
                h2.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            }
        });
        emit("post_save", "test_a", 1);
        emit("post_save", "test_b", 1);
        emit("pre_save", "test_a", 1);
        assert_eq!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn connect_all_fires_for_everything() {
        let hits = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let h2 = hits.clone();
        connect_all(move |_| {
            h2.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        });
        emit("pre_save", "x", 0);
        emit_request("/path/", "request_started");
        assert!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst) >= 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn panicking_receivers_do_not_break_dispatch() {
        connect("got_request_exception", |_| panic!("boom"));
        // must not panic
        emit_request("err", "got_request_exception");
    }
}
````
