## `crates/server/rustango/tests/integration.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/rustango/tests/integration.rs)

```rust
//! End-to-end integration tests — a full "blog" app exercising every
//! framework layer through the in-process test client, mirroring the kinds
//! of flows the official Django tutorial covers.

use std::sync::Arc;

use rustango::admin::ModelAdmin;
use rustango::auth::User;
use rustango::forms::{CharField, EmailField, IntegerField};
use rustango::http::{HttpRequest, HttpResponse, Method, QueryDict};
use rustango::messages as msgs;
use rustango::orm::ModelExt as _;
use rustango::project::{App, Project};
use rustango::settings::Settings;
use rustango::templates::{Context, TplValue};
use rustango::testclient::Client;
use rustango::urls::{named_path, path};
use rustango::views::{make_view, render};

// -- models -------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Clone, Debug, rustango::Model)]
#[model(table = "blog_post")]
pub struct Post {
    #[field(auto)]
    pub id: i64,
    #[field(char, max = 200)]
    pub title: String,
    #[field(text)]
    pub body: String,
    #[field(fk, target = "auth_user")]
    pub author_id: i64,
    #[field(bool, default = false)]
    pub published: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, rustango::Model)]
#[model(table = "blog_comment")]
pub struct Comment {
    #[field(auto)]
    pub id: i64,
    #[field(fk, target = "blog_post")]
    pub post_id: i64,
    #[field(char, max = 500)]
    pub text: String,
}

// -- views ---------------------------------------------------------------------

fn home(req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, rustango::errors::HttpError> {
    let backend = req.backend.clone().unwrap();
    let posts: Vec<TplValue> = Post::objects(&*backend)
        .filter(rustango::orm::Criteria::eq("published", true))
        .order_by("-id")
        .all()
        .unwrap()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|p| TplValue::Model(Arc::new(p)))
        .collect();
    let mut ctx = Context::new();
    ctx.set("posts", TplValue::List(posts));
    render(req, "home.html", ctx)
}

fn post_detail(req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, rustango::errors::HttpError> {
    let backend = req.backend.clone().unwrap();
    let pk = req.int_param("pk")?;
    let post = Post::get(&*backend, pk)
        .map_err(|_| rustango::errors::HttpError::NotFound("post".into()))?;
    let comments: Vec<TplValue> = Comment::objects(&*backend)
        .filter(rustango::orm::Criteria::eq("post_id", rustango::orm::Value::Int(pk)))
        .all()
        .unwrap()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|c| TplValue::Model(Arc::new(c)))
        .collect();
    let mut ctx = Context::new();
    ctx.set("post", TplValue::Model(Arc::new(post)));
    ctx.set("comments", TplValue::List(comments));
    render(req, "detail.html", ctx)
}

fn add_comment(req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, rustango::errors::HttpError> {
    if req.method != Method::POST {
        return Err(rustango::errors::HttpError::MethodNotAllowed("POST only".into()));
    }
    let backend = req.backend.clone().unwrap();
    let pk = req.int_param("pk")?;
    let form = rustango::forms::Form::new(
        "comment",
        vec![
            Box::new(CharField::new("text").min_length(2).max_length(500)),
            Box::new(EmailField::new("email").optional()),
        ],
    )
    .bind(&req.post);
    let mut form = form;
    if form.is_valid() {
        let c = Comment {
            id: 0,
            post_id: pk,
            text: form.cleaned("text").unwrap().as_text().unwrap().to_string(),
        };
        c.save(&*backend).unwrap();
        msgs::success(req, "Comment added!");
        Ok(HttpResponse::redirect(format!("/blog/{pk}/")))
    } else {
        Err(rustango::errors::HttpError::BadRequest("invalid comment".into()))
    }
}

fn stats(req: &mut HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, rustango::errors::HttpError> {
    let backend = req.backend.clone().unwrap();
    Ok(HttpResponse::json(&serde_json::json!({
        "posts": Post::objects(&*backend).count().unwrap(),
        "published": Post::objects(&*backend)
            .filter(rustango::orm::Criteria::eq("published", true))
            .count()
            .unwrap(),
        "user": req.user.username(),
    })))
}

// -- fixtures --------------------------------------------------------------------

fn templates() -> Box<rustango::templates::InMemoryLoader> {
    let mut l = rustango::templates::InMemoryLoader::new();
    l.add(
        "home.html",
        "<h1>Blog</h1>{% for p in posts %}<article><a href=\"/blog/{{ p.id }}/\">{{ p.title }}</a></article>{% empty %}<p>No posts yet.</p>{% endfor %}",
    );
    l.add(
        "detail.html",
        "<h1>{{ post.title }}</h1><div>{{ post.body }}</div>\
         {% for c in comments %}<p class=\"c\">{{ c.text }}</p>{% empty %}<p>No comments.</p>{% endfor %}\
         {% for m in messages %}<span class=\"flash\">{{ m.message }}</span>{% endfor %}",
    );
    l.add("login.html", "LOGIN FORM {% csrf_token %}");
    Box::new(l)
}

fn build_project() -> Arc<Project> {
    Arc::new(
        Project::builder()
            .settings(Settings::builder().database("memory").build())
            .add_app(App::new("blog").models::<Post>().models::<Comment>())
            .urls(vec![
                named_path("", make_view(home), "home"),
                path("blog/", make_view(home)).name("blog"),
                named_path("blog/<int:pk>/", make_view(post_detail), "post_detail"),
                named_path("blog/<int:pk>/comment/", make_view(add_comment), "add_comment"),
                named_path("stats/", make_view(stats), "stats"),
                path(
                    "login/",
                    make_view(|req: &mut HttpRequest| {
                        if req.method == Method::POST {
                            let backend = req.backend.clone().unwrap();
                            let u = rustango::auth::authenticate(
                                &*backend,
                                req.post.get("username").unwrap_or(""),
                                req.post.get("password").unwrap_or(""),
                            );
                            if let Some(user) = u {
                                rustango::auth::login(req, &user);
                                msgs::success(req, "Welcome back!");
                                return Ok(HttpResponse::redirect("/"));
                            }
                            return Err(rustango::errors::HttpError::PermissionDenied(
                                "bad credentials".into(),
                            ));
                        }
                        render(req, "login.html", Context::new())
                    }),
                )
                .name("login"),
            ])
            .admin(|site| {
                site.register::<Post>(ModelAdmin {
                    list_display: vec!["id".into(), "title".into(), "published".into()],
                    search_fields: vec!["title".into()],
                    list_per_page: 5,
                    ..Default::default()
                });
                site.register::<User>(Default::default());
            })
            .template_loader(templates())
            .build()
            .expect("project"),
    )
}

fn seed(blog: &Arc<Project>) -> (Post, User) {
    let backend = blog.backend.clone();
    let user = rustango::auth::create_superuser(&*backend, "ada", "ada@example.com", "pw123456")
        .expect("superuser");
    let post = Post {
        id: 0,
        title: "Hello Rust".into(),
        body: "Django concepts, Rust implementation.".into(),
        author_id: user.pk(),
        published: true,
    };
    let post = post.save(&*backend).unwrap();
    let draft = Post {
        id: 0,
        title: "Draft post".into(),
        body: "Not public yet.".into(),
        author_id: user.pk(),
        published: false,
    };
    draft.save(&*backend).unwrap();
    (post, user)
}

#[test]
fn detail_with_comments_and_404() {
    let blog = build_project();
    let (post, _) = seed(&blog);
    let backend = blog.backend.clone();
    Comment {
        id: 0,
        post_id: post.pk(),
        text: "First!".into(),
    }
    .save(&*backend)
    .unwrap();

    let mut client = Client::new(blog);
    let res = client.get(&format!("/blog/{}/", post.pk()));
    assert!(res.body.contains("Hello Rust"));
    assert!(res.body.contains("First!"));

    let missing = client.get("/blog/9999/");
    assert_eq!(missing.status, 404);

#[test]
fn comment_form_validation_and_csrf() {
    let blog = build_project();
    let (post, _) = seed(&blog);
    let mut client = Client::new(blog);
    let url = format!("/blog/{}/comment/", post.pk());

    // GET -> 405
    let res = client.get(&url);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 405);

    // CSRF missing -> 403
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("text", "hi");
    let res = client.post(&url, &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 403);

    // with csrf token + invalid (too short) -> 400
    client.get("/"); // pick up the csrf cookie
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("text", "x");
    let res = client.post_csrf(&url, &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 400);

    // valid -> redirect to detail, comment visible
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("text", "Great post, learned a lot!");
    let res = client.post_csrf(&url, &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 200); // followed redirect
    assert!(res.body.contains("Great post, learned a lot!"));
    assert!(res.body.contains("Comment added!")); // flash message
}

#[test]
fn auth_login_logout_cycle() {
    let blog = build_project();
    let (_, user) = seed(&blog);
    let mut client = Client::new(blog);

    // stats shows anonymous
    let res = client.get("/stats/");
    assert_eq!(res.json()["user"], serde_json::json!(""));

    // login page renders with csrf
    let res = client.get("/login/");
    assert!(res.body.contains("LOGIN FORM"));
    assert!(client.csrf_token().is_some());

    // wrong password -> 403
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("username", "ada");
    data.set("password", "nope");
    let res = client.post_csrf("/login/", &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 403);

    // correct -> redirect + session
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("username", "ada");
    data.set("password", "pw123456");
    let res = client.post_csrf("/login/", &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 200);
    let res = client.get("/stats/");
    assert_eq!(res.json()["user"], serde_json::json!("ada"));

    // logout
    client.logout();
    let res = client.get("/stats/");
    assert_eq!(res.json()["user"], serde_json::json!(""));
    let _ = user;
}

#[test]
fn admin_full_crud_cycle() {
    let blog = build_project();
    seed(&blog);
    let mut client = Client::new(blog.clone());
    client.follow_redirects = false;

    // anonymous -> redirected to login
    let res = client.get("/admin/");
    assert_eq!(res.status, 302);
    assert!(res.header("Location").unwrap().contains("/admin/login/"));
    client.follow_redirects = true;

    // staff login via admin login form
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("username", "ada");
    data.set("password", "pw123456");
    let res = client.post_csrf("/admin/login/", &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 200);

    // index lists models
    let res = client.get("/admin/");
    assert!(res.body.contains("blog_post"));
    assert!(res.body.contains("auth_user"));

    // changelist with pagination (5 per page, 1 post)
    let res = client.get("/admin/blog_post/");
    assert!(res.body.contains("Hello Rust"));

    // search
    let res = client.get("/admin/blog_post/?q=hello");
    assert!(res.body.contains("Hello Rust"));
    let res = client.get("/admin/blog_post/?q=zebra");
    assert!(res.body.contains("No items."));

    // add via admin
    client.get("/admin/blog_post/add/");
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("title", "Added via admin");
    data.set("body", "Through the auto-generated CRUD.");
    data.set("author_id", "1");
    data.set("published", "on");
    let res = client.post_csrf("/admin/blog_post/add/", &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 200);
    assert!(res.body.contains("Added via admin"));

    // change it
    let mut data = QueryDict::new();
    data.set("title", "Edited via admin");
    data.set("body", "Updated body.");
    data.set("author_id", "1");
    let res = client.post_csrf("/admin/blog_post/2/change/", &data);
    assert_eq!(res.status, 200);
    let backend = client_get_backend(&blog);
    let p = Post::get(&*backend, 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.title, "Edited via admin");

    // delete it
    let res = client.post_csrf("/admin/blog_post/2/delete/", &QueryDict::new());
    assert_eq!(res.status, 200);
    assert!(Post::get(&*backend, 2).is_err());
}

fn client_get_backend(blog: &Arc<Project>) -> Arc<dyn rustango::orm::Backend> {
    blog.backend.clone()
}

    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let db = dir.join("db.json");

    let blog = Arc::new(
        Project::builder()
            .settings(Settings::builder().database(alias.clone()).build())
            .add_app(App::new("blog").models::<Post>())

    );
    // tables auto-created on build; write data, reopen project, data survives
    let post = Post {

        author_id: 0,
        published: true,
    };

            .build()
            .unwrap(),

    assert_eq!(found.title, "Persisted");

    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
}

#[test]
fn signals_fire_on_save_and_delete() {
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    static SAVES: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    rustango::signals::connect("post_save", |p| {
        if p.table == "blog_post" {
            SAVES.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
    });
    let blog = build_project();
    let backend = blog.backend.clone();
    let before = SAVES.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
    let p = Post { id: 0, title: "sig".into(), body: String::new(), author_id: 0, published: false };
    let saved = p.save(&*backend).unwrap();
    saved.delete(&*backend).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(SAVES.load(Ordering::SeqCst), before + 1);
}

    loader.add("base.html", "<title>{% block t %}Base{% endblock %}</title>{% trans \"Welcome\" %}");
    loader.add("child.html", "{% extends \"base.html\" %}{% block t %}Child{% endblock %}");
    let mut cats = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    let mut de = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    de.insert("Welcome".to_string(), "Willkommen".to_string());
    cats.insert("de".to_string(), de);

    ctx.set("_lang", TplValue::Str("de".into()));
    let out = engine.render("child.html", &mut ctx).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, "<title>Child</title>Willkommen");
}

## `crates/server/skills/android-setup/SKILL.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/skills/android-setup/SKILL.md)

```markdown
---
name: android-setup
description: Bootstrap a working Android target from a bare machine - discover or install the SDK platform-tools, create an AVD with a system image, boot the emulator detached and wait for full boot completion, all through the android_setup tool (status/doctor/create_avd/boot/wait) instead of giving up when no device is online. Use whenever the user asks to turn on, start, build or set up Android and adb shows no target, or before any android_* tool on a fresh host.
---

# Android Setup Playbook

Never conclude "no device, cannot power on" while the host has no Android
environment — set one up. Every step maps to the `android_setup` tool, which
works without a live device and needs no `android.serial`.

## Order of operations

1. **`android_setup {"action": "status"}`** — one call, full audit:
   adb path resolution, SDK root (ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, platform
   defaults like `~/Android/Sdk`), emulator/avdmanager/sdkmanager presence,
   existing AVDs, installed system images, online devices, KVM verdict.
   Read this JSON before anything else.
2. **`android_setup {"action": "doctor"}`** — when status reports gaps, doctor
   returns the exact host commands to close them (apt/dnf/brew lines,
   sdkmanager license acceptance, KVM group fix). Show the plan, then run the
   pieces through Bash.
3. **`android_setup {"action": "create_avd", "image": "system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64"}`**
   — installs the system image through sdkmanager when missing (this can take
   minutes; the tool caps the wait and reports progress), then
   `avdmanager create avd -n <name> -k <image> -d pixel_5 --force`.
   Omit `name` for the default `romacode`.
4. **`android_setup {"action": "boot", "name": "<avd>"}`** — spawns
   `emulator -avd <name> -no-snapshot-load -no-boot-anim -gpu auto` DETACHED
   (survives the tool call), then polls `adb wait-for-device` +
   `sys.boot_completed` up to 300 s. Returns the adb serial when green.
5. **`android_setup {"action": "wait", "timeout": 120}`** — re-check only.
6. **Hand over to the device tools.** Only now call `android_device` first,
   then `android_shell`, `android_install`, `android_screenshot`, ...
   (the standard rule: query properties from the device, never fabricate).

## Honest fallbacks

* No KVM (`/dev/kvm` missing or not writable): say so, offer
  `-accel off` boot (slow) or installing the kvm group packages from doctor.
* No emulator binary but platform-tools exist: doctor prints the
  cmdline-tools + emulator install lines; run them, re-run status.
* sdkmanager needs license acceptance: run
  `yes | sdkmanager --licenses` via Bash, retry create_avd.
* Physical device instead of emulator: plug in, enable USB debugging, approve
  the key; `android_setup status` shows it as an online target and the
  playbook ends at step 6.

## What NOT to do

* Do not probe with ad-hoc Bash commands (`emulator -list-avds`,
  `adb devices -l`) when `android_setup status` answers them in one call.
* Do not boot an emulator twice — status already lists online devices.
* Do not claim a device exists until `android_device` returns real properties.
```

## `crates/server/skills/claude-parity/SKILL.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/skills/claude-parity/SKILL.md)

```markdown
---
name: claude-parity
description: Feature-parity map between Claude Code (the TypeScript/Ink CLI this project mirrors) and RomaCode v0.7.x - which Claude concepts are ported (tool registry, SKILL.md skills, slash commands, hooks, MCP, permission modes, compaction), which are adapted (client-server split, LangChain engine), and which have no RomaCode equivalent. Use when porting another Claude-Code feature or arguing about "how Claude Code does it".
---

# Claude Code → RomaCode Parity Map

Baseline: the Claude Code source tree measured at 1,899 files / ~512k lines of
TypeScript; RomaCode measured at ~93k lines of Rust. This skill is the honest
crosswalk: what exists on both sides, what is adapted, what is absent.

## 1. Concepts ported one-to-one

| Claude Code | RomaCode | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tool registry (`claude/tools/`, 43 entries, 22 in the default pool) | `crates/server/src/tools/mod.rs` (`definitions()` + `execute()`) | Claude gates registration per feature flags; RomaCode registers all 20 always. 14 Claude tools are referenced by the registry but their packages are absent — dead code eliminated at compile time; RomaCode has no such gap. |
| SKILL.md packages (14 built-in skills) | `crates/server/src/skills.rs` + `crates/server/skills/*/SKILL.md` | Same frontmatter (`name`/`description`), same progressive disclosure, 32,000-char body cap on both sides. |
| Slash commands (86 command dirs) | `Hub::run_command` in `api.rs` + client whitelist in `client-tui/src/app.rs` | Claude ships each command as a dir with prompt + tests; RomaCode matches arms in one function. |
| Hooks (104 hook files) | no hook engine | RomaCode has none; pre/post tool-call behavior is hard-coded in `agent.rs`. |
| MCP client (23 files) | `rc-tools` MCP bridge (`rc-sources/src/mcp.rs`) | RomaCode bridges MCP servers into the rc-* framework, not yet into the live 20-tool registry. |
| Permission modes (5: default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions, delegate) | `security::authorize` with `Permission::Allow/Deny/Ask` per tool group | Owner removed the gating — default posture is autoaccept. Plan mode survives as `Mode::Plan` prompt text. |
| Context compaction (`compact_threshold_pct`) | `auto_compact` + `compact_threshold_pct` config | Same idea: summarize the transcript when the context window fills. |
| Subagents (Task tool) | none | RomaCode has no subagent spawn; long work is a loop of tool calls in one turn. |

## 2. Concepts adapted to the client-server split

Claude Code is one Ink process: the React tree, the agent loop and the tools
share address space. RomaCode splits them:

* **Brain** — `romacode-server` owns the agent loop, provider calls, the tool
  registry, the security gate, config and sessions. The TUI (the `romacode`
  binary) is a screen: HTTP + WebSocket mirror of `SessionSnapshot`, requests
  in `protocol.rs`, events in `events.rs`.
* **Two engines** — the native loop (`agent.rs`) and a LangChain
  `AgentExecutor` clone (`langchain_bridge.rs`) share the same registry and
  gate; Claude Code has a single engine.
* **50,000-char tool-result cap** (Claude) becomes
  `max_tool_output_bytes` (default 100,000) with a hard truncation notice in
  `agent.rs`.

## 3. Claude-Code features with no RomaCode equivalent

1. Plugins and marketplaces.
2. OAuth account login (RomaCode: API keys per provider in config.json only).
3. Background bash shells and shell-snapshot forwarding.
4. IDE integrations (VS Code / JetBrains extensions).
5. `@`-file mentions and drag-and-drop image paste (screenshots arrive via
   `android_screenshot` paths instead).
6. Telemetry/analytics service (RomaCode has a `telemetry: false` flag and
   nothing else).

## 4. Using this map

When porting a Claude-Code behavior: find the row above, keep the RomaCode
seam rules (one registry, one gate, wire contract additive, config stays in
the brain), and prefer the smallest surface: prompt text > config key > tool >
protocol change. Verify with `cargo build --workspace --locked` and the
`api.rs` approval end-to-end test.
```

description: Produce a professional Word (.docx) report with python-docx - styled cover, table of contents, numbered sections, tables with header shading, figure captions and a final postcheck (open the file again, verify headings/tables/images, search for leftover placeholders). Use when the user asks for a report, catalog, comparison or any Word deliverable.

# DOCX Report Production

Deliverable rule: a report lands as a real `.docx` in the download directory
plus a PDF render for visual verification. Never finish by printing text in
the chat.

## Pipeline

1. **Design first.** Fix audience, depth (catalog vs summary), length and what
   must stay out (e.g. secrets — keep config keys, drop URLs and client ids).
2. **Content from measurements, not memory.** Extract facts with a script
   (`rg`/walk the tree), print intermediate results, re-check every number
   that goes into the document against that output.
3. **Generate with python-docx** (pip module `python-docx`):
   * Styles: set `Normal` font (e.g. Calibri 10.5pt) and heading styles once;
     never inline-format every run.
   * Cover: title, subtitle, date, version block — then a page break.
   * TOC: insert a real TOC field (`w:fldSimple` `TOC \o "1-3" \h \z \u`) so
     Word populates it; LibreOffice renders it on `--convert-to pdf`.
   * Sections: `Heading 1` per chapter, `Heading 2` per subsection; body
     paragraphs of 3-5 sentences, 150+ words per section.
   * Tables: one `Table` per dataset, bold header row with shading
     (`w:shd` fill), `Table Grid` style, no empty cells — use `n/a`.
   * Figures: add picture, then `Caption`-styled paragraph under it.
4. **Postprocess** (`postprocess_docx.py` pattern):
   * de-duplicate the first TOC entry if the field renders twice;
   * widen table columns that break words badly (`autofit True`, set column
     widths explicitly);
   * replace any `【...】` placeholders or fail the build.
5. **Postcheck (must pass before delivery).** Reopen with python-docx:
   print heading list, table count, image count; `rg` the docx XML for
   `TODO`, `XXX`, `【`, `placeholder`. Then
   `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf` and `pdftoppm -r 60` every page,
   look at the JPEGs: repeated sections, broken tables, blank pages or
   markdown symbols (`**`, `#`, `|---|`) in rendered text fail the run — fix
   the generator, regenerate, re-verify. Keep the PDF next to the docx.

## Sizing rules

* Catalog depth: one table row per item, one chapter per subsystem; the
  Claude Code extraction report (17 pages, 40+ tools, 8 subsystems) is the
  reference shape.
* Length bands excluding cover/TOC/appendix: short ~500 words, standard
  ~1,500, catalog 3,000+.
* Every explicit user requirement (part, deliverable, length, naming,
  audience) maps to a section before writing starts.
```

## `crates/server/skills/remix-chain-forensics/SKILL.md`

````markdown
---
name: remix-chain-forensics
description: Live Ethereum mainnet investigation with the native rrx toolchain — endpoint health, blocks, tx replay with gas delta, call-tree traces, ENS/tokens/logs, arbitrary view calls at any block, verified sources, locally-verified MPT state proofs, forks, and the fake-asset detection stack. Evidence discipline included.
---

# remix-chain-forensics: on-chain investigation

Every command here is a REAL mainnet read through the built-in endpoint list
(live probing + automatic failover). `--rpc <url>` overrides per call;
`remix.rpc` in the config overrides globally (passed as `RRX_RPC`). No
simulation anywhere. Evidence discipline: the final answer cites the block
numbers, proof verdicts, and Δ% figures the tools returned — never "the
node said".

## 1. Establish ground truth

- `remix net` — probe ALL endpoints live (latency, head block, client).
  Run this first when numbers look stale or two calls disagree.
- `remix chain` — client, head block, base fee, priority fees.
- `remix chains [slug] [--json]` — the multi-chain network list.
- `remix block <n|latest|finalized>` — one block summary.
- `remix gasprice` — the current fee landscape.

## 2. Transactions

- `remix tx 0x<hash>` — full tx + receipt report (status, gas, logs).
- `remix trace 0x<hash>` — call-tree trace (callTracer): who called whom
  with what value.
- `remix debugtx 0x<hash> [--max-steps n] [--top n]` — **the flagship**.
  Fetches tx + receipt + header, reads the PRE-tx state over RPC, executes
  the calldata in the built-in EVM at the correct fork spec (Istanbul…
  Cancun by real activation heights), then compares:
  `chain SUCCESS 45,160 gas | replay SUCCESS 46,428 gas [Δ 2.81%]` plus an
  opcode gas profile and step trace. Interpretation: a small Δ is normal
  (state growth, warm/cold slots); a **big Δ% is a finding** — report it
  with the opcode table, do not silently average it away.

## 3. Accounts, names, tokens

- `remix ens <name>` / `remix ens --reverse <addr>` — real registry
  resolution, forward and reverse. Resolve names **before** addresses so
  reports stay readable.
- `remix account <ADDRESS|ens.name>` — balance / nonce / code.
- `remix token <addr> [--holder <h>]` — ERC-20/721/1155 inspector
  (decimals, supply, holder balances).
- `remix ethcall <to> <fn> [args…] [--types "address,uint256"]
  [--returns "uint256"] [--block n]` — arbitrary view call **at any block**;
  the `--block` switch is how you answer "what did this look like before
  the incident".

## 4. Events and history

- `remix logs --address <a> [--topic0 "Transfer(address,address,uint256)"]
  [--from latest] [--to …]` — filtered event history.
- Compose topic hashes from signatures when only the event name is known:
  `remix utils selector "Event(types)"`, `remix utils keccak <hex>`,
  `remix utils namehash <name>`, `remix utils unit <wei|gwei|eth>`.
- `remix index` — index recent blocks into `rrx-index.json` for quick scans.

## 5. Proofs and sources — verify, don't trust

- `remix proof <addr> [--slot n] [--block tag]` — account + storage MPT
  proofs, RLP-decoded and Merkle-walked locally against the block
  stateRoot. `PROOF VALID ✓ … slot 0x1 = 84298736466239384` — a lying node
  cannot pass. Use it whenever a node's claim matters: balances,
  approvals, critical storage slots.
- `remix sources <addr> [--chain 1]` — fetch VERIFIED sources
  (Sourcify → Etherscan V2) before judging what a contract does.
- `remix bytediff <addr> <Contract>` — on-chain bytecode vs a local build;
  catches proxy/implementation swaps and quietly-redeployed lookalikes.

## 6. Fake-asset stack (detection only)

- `remix fakeasset registry [--verify-live]` — the canonical USDT/USDC/
  WETH(WBNB) table per chain (live symbol/decimals check with
  `--verify-live`); rebrand aliases included (e.g. `USD₮0` on L2s).
- `remix fakeasset registry --compare 0x<addr> --chain ethereum` — verdict
  `CLONE / REAL / UNKNOWN` from ticker, decimals, name, and live supply
  comparison.
- `remix fakeasset variants|audit|pending` — known fake variants, honeypot
  auditing, pending detections. `remix fakeasset source|compile|verify` —
  inspect the teaching demo. The `deploy`/`flasher` sub-actions are demo
  tooling and count as chain writes (`remix.allow_chain_writes=true`
  required). **Scope note:** this stack is the detection side — it finds
  clones, recognizes honeypots, fact-checks screenshots; it does not
  produce scam material.
- `remix wildtoken source|compile|demo` — the teaching demo token.

## 7. Local forks and EVM internals

- `remix fork <usdt|usdc|weth|dai|0x…> [--chain] [--block]` — preload real
  mainnet state into the built-in EVM for offline experimentation.
- `remix blob` — blob-carrying txs (4844); `remix verkle` — verkle trees;
  `remix build-block` — build a block locally; `remix precompiles 1..9` —
  precompile behavior.

## Investigation playbook (typical order)

```text
remix_status                        # doctor first, every session
remix net && remix chain            # ground truth
remix ens victim.eth                # resolve names first
remix tx 0x<hash> && remix trace 0x<hash>
remix debugtx 0x<hash> --max-steps 20 --top 10   # replay + Δ%
remix account 0x<addr> && remix token 0x<tok> --holder 0x<addr>
remix ethcall 0x<tok> allowance(address,address) --types "address,address" \
      --returns "uint256" --block <pre-incident>
remix proof 0x<tok> --slot 1        # locally verified storage claim
remix sources 0x<tok>               # verified source before judgment
remix fakeasset registry --compare 0x<tok> --chain ethereum
```

## Usage

Activate for "look into this tx/address/token", "is this token a scam",
"prove this balance", "what did this transaction actually do", gas/fee
questions, or any mainnet state question. Cite endpoint evidence (block
numbers, proof verdicts, Δ%) in the final answer. Master reference:
`remix-ethereum`; authoring loop: `remix-contract-dev`.
````

## `crates/server/skills/remix-contract-dev/SKILL.md`

[view on disk](crates/server/skills/remix-contract-dev/SKILL.md)

````markdown
---
name: remix-contract-dev
description: The full Solidity development loop with the native rrx toolchain — scaffold a workspace, compile with real solc, static-analyze, unit/fuzz/invariant test, measure gas, script-run, flatten, document, deploy (gated), verify, byte-diff, and debug. Stage-by-stage playbook with checkpoints.
---

# remix-contract-dev: the Solidity development loop

The `remix` tool runs the whole Remix IDE contract workflow headlessly. This
skill is the loop, in order, with the checkpoint after each green stage. All
commands go through the `remix` tool (`command` + `args`), never the shell.

## Stage 0 — Doctor

`remix_status` first: binary found, version, RPC policy, chain-write flag.
If the flag is off and the task will end in a deploy, say so now — the user
sets `remix.allow_chain_writes=true` themselves; do not promise a broadcast
you cannot make.

## Stage 1 — Scaffold

- `remix workspace init <template> [name]` with template `storage`, `erc20`,
  or `blank` — creates the project tree. Run it in the intended parent
  directory.
- `remix file tree` / `remix file ls` to see the scaffold; `remix file cat`
  to read files; `remix file write` to edit; `remix search <pattern>
  [--regex]` across the workspace.
- `remix git init`, then `remix git add|commit|status|log` — the built-in
  dgit. **Commit after every green stage** so a bad experiment is
  revertible.

## Stage 2 — Compile (real solc)

- `remix compile [file] [--solc <version>] [--evm-version cancun]
  [--no-opt]`. The solc manager handles versions: `remix solc list`,
  `remix solc install 0.8.24`, `remix solc use <v>` on first use.
- Fix errors top-down; recompile after every fix. `--no-opt` isolates
  optimizer-caused surprises; drop it once clean.

## Stage 3 — Static analysis

- `remix analyze` — the Remix static-analysis checks (tx.origin,
  delegatecall, unbounded loops, unchecked calls…).
- `remix reentrancy` — the dynamic reentrancy mode.
- `remix layout <Old> <New>` — storage-layout upgrade safety between two
  versions of a contract; run it before any upgrade deploy.
- Treat analyzer findings as questions to answer, not noise to silence. Fix
  or document why each is acceptable, then commit.

## Stage 4 — Test

- `remix test` — Solidity unit tests (remix-tests conventions, real chain).
- `remix fuzz <Contract> <fn> [--runs n] [--seed s]` — property testing.
  **Keep the seed** when a failure needs replaying.
- `remix invariant <Contract> [--sequences n] [--depth n]` — foundry-style
  invariant runs; start small (`--sequences 10 --depth 20`), scale up only
  when green.
- `remix coverage` — find what the suite never executes; close the gaps that
  guard invariants, not just lines.
- Slow suites: pass `timeout_secs` on the tool call (up to 1800 s).

## Stage 5 — Gas, docs, script run

- `remix gas estimate` — per-call estimate; `remix gas report` — full
  analytics; `remix gas price` — current fee landscape; `remix gas trace` —
  where the gas goes.
- `remix flatten <file>` — flattened source for verification.
- `remix uml` — mermaid UML from the AST; `remix doc` — natspec → markdown.
- `remix script scripts/demo.rrx` — the deploy/transfer/assert DSL runner
  with a gas report. Note: a script that deploys is a chain write (§7).

## Stage 6 — Byte-level sanity

- `remix bytediff <addr> <Contract>` — compare deployed bytecode against the
  local build. After any deploy or upgrade, bytediff is the receipt that
  what is on chain matches what was compiled. Also use it to clone-audit a
  third-party contract whose address you are integrating with.

## Stage 7 — Deploy and verify (REAL chain, gated)

- Deploys broadcast real transactions: they need
  **`remix.allow_chain_writes=true`** in the config plus `RRX_PRIVATE_KEY`
  in the server environment. If the tool refuses, hand the refusal text to
  the user verbatim and stop — do not work around it with Bash, and never
  pass `--yes` yourself (the tool refuses it).
- Dry-run first: `remix gas estimate`, `remix fork <token>` to test against
  real mainnet state offline, `remix ethcall` for view/pure probing.
- `remix deploy <Contract> [--args "T,T,1000e18"]` — deploy from the
  workspace.
- `remix verify <addr> …` — Sourcify/Etherscan verification (uses
  `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY` when set; `remix flatten` output is the input).
- `remix sources <addr>` — re-fetch the verified source as a cross-check.
- Commit the deployed address + bytediff verdict in the repo notes.

## Stage 8 — Debug

- `remix debug <Contract> <Function> [--max-steps n] [--json]` — step through
  the local run with the real interpreter.
- `remix debugtx 0x<hash> [--max-steps n] [--top n]` — replay a REAL mainnet
  tx (fork spec by actual activation heights) with an opcode gas profile.
- `remix trace 0x<hash>` — call-tree trace from the node (callTracer).

## Worked micro-loop (erc20)

```text
remix_status
remix workspace init erc20 demo
remix compile                       # fix until clean
remix analyze && remix reentrancy   # answer every finding
remix test && remix fuzz Token transfer --runs 500 --seed 42
remix invariant Token --sequences 10 --depth 20
remix coverage                      # close invariant-relevant gaps
remix gas report                    # optimize the hot path
remix git add -A && remix git commit -m "green"
# deploy is gated: user sets remix.allow_chain_writes=true first
remix deploy Token --args "Demo,DEM,1000e18"
remix bytediff 0x<deployed> Token   # receipt: chain == build
remix verify 0x<deployed>
```

## Usage

Activate for contract authoring tasks: "write/deploy/verify a contract",
"why does my test fail", "measure gas", "check upgrade safety", "is the
deployed code the code I compiled". Hand the chain-write refusal text to the
user verbatim when the flag is off. Master reference: `remix-ethereum`.
````

## `crates/server/skills/remix-ethereum/SKILL.md`

````markdown
---
name: remix-ethereum
description: RomaCode's native Remix/Ethereum toolchain (rrx) — run Solidity compile/test/fuzz/deploy/verify and live mainnet inspection (ethcall, trace, debugtx, MPT proofs, ENS, tokens) through the remix tool. Master playbook: tool schemas, the full 52-command catalog by plane, safety gates, timeout/output policy, and failure recovery.
---

# remix-ethereum: the native Remix toolchain (master playbook)

RomaCode ships **rrx** — Remix IDE tools rebuilt in pure Rust — as a built-in
native tool, wired the same way as rnmap/browser/android. One binary, no
simulation: a real EVM interpreter (Istanbul → Cancun by real activation
heights), real MPT state, real gas metering, real solc, real secp256k1
signing, and every chain-facing command hard-wired to **Ethereum mainnet**
with live endpoint probing and automatic failover.

Architecture in one line: `rrx-evm::Host` is the seam — the same interpreter
runs against local state (`WorldState`) and against live network state
(`RemoteHost`), which is how `debugtx` replays real mainnet transactions.

## 1. The two agent tools

**`remix`** — run one rrx command:

```json
{"command": "ethcall",
 "args": ["0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7", "totalSupply()", "--returns", "uint256"]}
```

| param | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | one rrx command word (§2), or `help` for the full syntax reference |
| `args` | string[] | one argument per element: `["latest"]`, `["0x<txhash>"]`, `["--rpc", "https://…"]` |
| `timeout_secs` | integer | per-call timeout override, 1..1800 |

**`remix_status`** — the doctor, no arguments. Reports: which rrx binary was
found and where, its version, the active RPC policy, the command allowlist,
the chain-write flag, timeout and output cap.

Session discipline:

1. Call `remix_status` **before the first remix command of a session**.
2. If any remix call fails oddly, call `remix_status` again before
   improvising — the doctor names the failing layer (binary, RPC, policy).
3. `command="help"` returns the complete per-command syntax reference; prefer
   it over guessing flags.

If the binary is missing, build it from the workspace (rrx is a first-party
member at `crates/remix/rrx-cli` — the doctor prints exactly the paths it
searched):

```bash
cargo build --release                # at the romacode workspace root
cp target/release/rrx bin/rrx        # next to the romacode binary, or:
# set "remix": {"binary": "/abs/path/to/rrx"} in the config
```

## 2. Command catalog (the 52 allowed commands)

**Project plane** — run inside a workspace (`workspace init` first):

- `workspace init <storage|erc20|blank> [name]` — scaffold from Template
  Explorer; `file ls|tree|cat|write|rm|mv|mkdir` — file explorer;
  `search <pattern> [--regex]` — workspace search
- `compile [file] [--solc <version>] [--evm-version cancun] [--no-opt]` —
  real solc; `test` — solidityUnitTesting conventions
- `analyze` — static analysis (tx.origin, delegatecall, unbounded loops…);
  `reentrancy` — dynamic reentrancy mode
- `coverage` — what the suite never executes
- `fuzz <Contract> <fn> [--runs n] [--seed s]`,
  `invariant <Contract> [--sequences n] [--depth n]`
- `gas estimate|report|price|trace` — hardhat-style analytics
- `flatten <file>`, `uml` (mermaid from the AST), `doc` (natspec → markdown)
- `debug <Contract> <Function> [--max-steps n] [--json]` — local debugger;
  `layout <Old> <New>` — storage-layout upgrade safety;
  `bytediff <addr> <Contract>` — deployed vs local bytecode
- `verify <addr> …` — Etherscan V2 / Sourcify; `script <file.rrx>` — the
  deploy/transfer/assert DSL runner; `git init|add|commit|status|log`

**Account plane** (offline, secp256k1/EIP-191): `keys new|list|dev`,
`sign`, `precompiles` (0x01–0x09), `aa` (account abstraction).

**Chain-read plane** — LIVE mainnet, no key needed:

- `net` — probe ALL endpoints (latency, head, client); run when numbers look
  stale. `chain` — client/head/base fee/priority fees. `chains [slug] [--json]`
- `block <n|latest|finalized>`, `tx 0x<hash>` (tx + receipt report),
  `trace 0x<hash>` (callTracer call tree)
- `debugtx 0x<hash> [--max-steps n] [--top n]` — replay a REAL mainnet tx in
  the built-in EVM and compare chain gas vs replay gas with an opcode profile
- `account <ADDRESS|ens.name>` (balance/nonce/code; resolve via `ens` first),
  `ethcall <to> <fn signature> [args…] [--types "address,uint256"]
  [--returns "uint256"] [--block n]` — arbitrary view call at any block
- `logs --address <a> [--topic0 "Event(types)"] [--from …] [--to …]`
- `ens <name>` / `ens --reverse <addr>`, `token <addr> [--holder <h>]`
  (ERC-20/721/1155), `sources <addr> [--chain 1]` (Sourcify → Etherscan V2)
- `proof <addr> [--slot n] [--block tag]` — MPT account/storage proofs
  verified locally against the block stateRoot (own RLP + Merkle walk; a
  lying node cannot pass)
- `gasprice`, `fork <usdt|usdc|weth|dai|0x…> [--chain] [--block]` — preload
  real mainnet state offline, `blob`, `verkle`, `build-block`, `index`

**Chain-write plane** — REAL broadcasts, gated (§3): `send --to <who>
--value <eth> [--fn "sig"] [--args "…"]`, `deploy <Contract>
[--args "…"]`, `call`.

**Meta**: `wildtoken` (teaching demo token), `fakeasset` (detection stack:
`registry [--verify-live]`, `registry --compare 0x… --chain ethereum`,
`variants`, `audit`, `pending`), `utils keccak|unit|selector|namehash`,
`solc install|list|use`, `plugins` (the full 38-tool registry).

**Never available as tools** (daemon commands, they never return): `node`,
`explorer`, `follow`, `mcp`, `lsp`, `ws`. If a task truly needs one, start it
with the Bash tool and manage the process yourself.

## 3. Safety model (do not work around any of these)

- Chain-writing commands (`send`, `deploy`, `call`, `script` runs, demo
  deploys incl. `wildtoken|fakeasset deploy`) broadcast REAL transactions to
  chain id 1. They are refused unless **`remix.allow_chain_writes=true`** in
  the config **and** `RRX_PRIVATE_KEY` is exported in the server environment.
  While the flag is off, the key env var is stripped from the child process.
- Never pass `--yes` yourself — the tool refuses it; a broadcast is a human
  decision made in the config. rrx itself layers no-key → no-`--yes` →
  balance-check before any broadcast.
- Never echo a private key, seed phrase, or keystore password into args,
  output, or reports.
- Prefer the read-only equivalent: `ethcall` over `call`, `gas estimate`
  over deploy-to-measure, `fork` for mainnet-state experiments, `debugtx`
  over re-broadcasting.

## 4. Output, timeouts, failure recovery

- Add `--json` where supported when the next step must parse the result.
- Output is capped by `remix.max_output_chars` (default 20 000, clamped
  1 000..200 000). If output truncates, narrow the query (filter logs by
  topic, read one slot, one function) instead of paging.
- Whole-command timeout `remix.timeout_secs` (default 300 s, clamp 0..3600).
  The slow commands are `compile` on big trees, `test`, `fuzz --runs 1000`,
  `invariant --sequences 50`, `coverage`; pass `timeout_secs` per call up to
  1800 s.
- Missing binary → doctor names the search order (`remix.binary` config →
  exe-adjacent `bin/rrx` → `<data_dir>/romacode/bin/rrx` → PATH → project
  `bin/`); build per §1.
- Endpoint trouble → `remix net` probes every endpoint with latency and head
  info; set `remix.rpc` in the config (global `RRX_RPC`) or `--rpc <url>`
  per call.
- The `/remix` slash command (TUI): `on|off`, `status` (the doctor),
  `writes on|off`, `help`.

## Usage

Activate when the task touches Ethereum: Solidity contracts, EVM behavior,
gas, mainnet state, transactions, ENS, tokens, MPT proofs, fake-asset
auditing, or "remix" workflows. Do not shell out to `forge`/`cast`/web
explorers for what rrx already does natively. For the full dev loop see
`remix-contract-dev`; for investigations see `remix-chain-forensics`.
````

# RomaCode Architecture Map (romacode-fixed-v3, CHANGES v0.7.6)

Measured statically: 316 files, ~99,800 text lines across the workspace. Cargo
workspace: 17 members, resolver 2, edition 2021, rust-version 1.75, MIT. Release
profile: opt-level 3, thin LTO, codegen-units 1, strip. Binaries: `romacode-server`
(brain) and `romacode` (screen). Brain binds 127.0.0.1:7712; the screen auto-spawns it
detached (setsid) and reconnects losslessly from snapshots.

```markdown
---
name: romacode-customization
description: Exact customization recipes for RomaCode, the Rust client-server coding agent (romacode-fixed-v3 source tree, CHANGES v0.7.6 state). Use this skill whenever the user wants to modify, extend, reconfigure, rebuild or integrate RomaCode - adding an agent tool (brain tool, rc-* declarative/CLI/REST/OpenAPI/MCP tool), changing the security gate or permission defaults, adding a slash command or a provider, tuning the agent loop or config, wiring the rc-tools framework into the brain, or re-shipping the binaries. Triggers on any mention of RomaCode, romacode-server, the romacode TUI, its tools (web_fetch, rnmap_scan, browser, rag_index, rag_search, webapp_scaffold, webapp_check, android_*, Read/Edit/Bash), its config.json, its rc-tools workspace, or porting Claude-Code-style features into it.
---

# RomaCode Customization

RomaCode is a Rust client-server coding agent: `romacode-server` (the brain) owns the
agent loop, sessions, the 20-tool registry and the security gate; `romacode` (the TUI
screen) only mirrors state over HTTP + WebSocket. Every customization lands in one of
six seams. Work server-side first: the brain owns the config file, the tool registry
and the policy, and the screen adapts.

Assume the tree root is the extracted workspace (here:
`/home/z/my-project/analysis/romacode/romacode/`). All paths below are relative to it.

## Golden rules

1. **One registry, one gate.** Agent tools live in `crates/server/src/tools/mod.rs`
   (`definitions()` + `execute()`). Any tool call - both engines - passes
   `security::authorize` first. Never add a second dispatch point.
2. **Both engines must keep working.** The native loop and the langchain
   `AgentExecutor` share the registry and gate. A new tool needs only a `definitions()`
   entry plus an `execute()` arm; both engines pick it up automatically.
3. **The posture is fully open by design.** FIXES.md records that all restriction
   policy was removed at the owner's request. Do not silently re-add gating; do not
   silently remove the residual safeguards (unknown-tool refusal, cancel/timeout,
   output caps, scaffold traversal checks). See
   `references/security-posture.md` before touching policy.
4. **The wire contract is the freeze boundary.** Requests live in
   `crates/shared/src/protocol.rs`, events in `events.rs`. Extending either is
   additive only, or old screens desync (they resync from `SessionSnapshot`).
5. **Keys and config never touch the screen.** Providers, keys and settings persist in
   the brain's `~/.config/romacode/config.json`; the screen sends empty keys on
   purpose. Keep it that way.
6. **Build locked, test everything.** `cargo build --workspace --locked` then
   `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Binaries: `target/release/romacode-server` and
   `target/release/romacode`. `scripts/install.sh` is the packaging path.

## Pick the seam

| Goal | Anchor files | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| Add an agent tool the model can call | `crates/server/src/tools/mod.rs`, new module under `crates/server/src/tools/` | Recipe A (below) + `references/tool-recipes.md` |
| Add a tool without Rust changes | `crates/rc-tools/rc-sources/` | Recipe B |
| Wire the rc-* framework's tools into the brain | `tools/mod.rs` + `rc-builtin`/`rc-sources` | Recipe B2 |
| Change policy / permissions / defaults | `crates/server/src/security.rs`, `config.rs`, `config.example.json` | `references/security-posture.md` |
| Add a slash command | `crates/server/src/api.rs` (`Hub::run_command`) + `crates/client-tui/src/app.rs` (`send`) | Recipe C |
| Add a provider | `crates/shared/src/catalog.rs` (`KNOWN`) or `providers` config map | Recipe D |
| Tune the loop / context / prompts | `agent`, `model_params`, `system_prompt` config keys | Recipe E |
| Extend the wire protocol | `crates/shared/src/protocol.rs`, `events.rs`, `api.rs` | Rule 4; mirror in `client-tui/src/net.rs` |

## Recipe A - add an agent tool (brain)

1. Create `crates/server/src/tools/<name>.rs` with two functions, copying the shape of
   `webfetch.rs` (simplest example):
   - `definition() -> serde_json::Value` in Anthropic shape: `name` (lowercase
     snake_case; `Read`/`Edit`/`Bash` are the only CamelCase exceptions), one-sentence
     `description` (the model reads it), `input_schema` (object, properties, required).
   - `execute(cfg, input, cancel) -> Result<String, String>`: pure, cancel-aware
     (poll `cancel` in loops like `rnmap/mod.rs` does), returns user-facing `Err`
     strings, caps output size (see `max_tool_output_bytes` consumer in `agent.rs`).
2. Register in `tools/mod.rs`: `pub mod <name>;` then inside `definitions()` add your
   definition to **both** the Anthropic branch and the OpenAI branch (the OpenAI branch
   wraps via the `wrap` closure automatically - just push into `defs` in both arms).
   Make it conditional on a config flag if it launches processes (pattern:
   `if cfg.<section>.enabled { defs.push(<name>::definition()); }`).
3. Dispatch in `tools/mod.rs::execute()`: add the match arm. Keep it dispatch-only -
   permission checks belong to `security.rs`, work to the module.
4. Add unit tests next to the executor plus an end-to-end test in
   `crates/server/src/api.rs` tests if the tool changes snapshots/events.
5. Document the tool in README.md's tool list and (if it needs config) extend
   `config.rs` + `config.example.json` with a clamped section (pattern: `rnmap`).

## Recipe B - add a tool with no Rust code (rc-sources)

The `rc-tools` stack is a self-contained framework (its own registry, lifecycle, CLI)
that is a workspace member but is **not yet merged into the brain's live registry** -
the brain's 20 tools are entirely `tools/mod.rs`. For tool authoring it offers:

- **declarative**: a YAML/JSON spec becomes a shell tool (`rc-sources/src/declarative.rs`)
- **cli**: binary + arg-template (`cli.rs`, uses `shell_quote` escaping)
- **rest / openapi**: one endpoint -> one tool; an OpenAPI 3 spec -> N tools
- **mcp**: an MCP `tools/list` manifest bridged to tools (`mcp.rs`)
- **marketplace / llm_gen**: manifests and natural-language specs

Author the spec, then verify through the framework's own CLI/lifecycle
(`rc-lifecycle`: discover -> register -> validate -> load -> execute).

## Recipe B2 - wire rc-* tools into the brain

If the user wants rc-* tools (38 builtins, composed tools, imported MCP/REST tools)
agent-callable:

1. Add `rc-builtin` (and `rc-sources` if importing) to
   `crates/server/Cargo.toml` (workspace path deps already exist in the root
   `[workspace.dependencies]`).
2. In `tools/mod.rs::definitions()`, build descriptors from the rc tools:
   `rc_core::Tool` exposes name/description/schema - map each into the same JSON
   definition shape (anthropic branch) / `wrap` (OpenAI branch).
3. In `execute()`, route their namespace to
   `rc_lifecycle`'s `Executor` (it applies sandbox + timeout + metrics). Keep the
   security gate in front: authorize first, executor second.
4. Guard with a config flag (new `rc_tools.enabled` section) so the default 20-tool
   surface stays stable for prompt caching.

## Recipe C - add a slash command

1. Server arm in `Hub::run_command` (`crates/server/src/api.rs`, ~line 436): match the
   name, read/write `cfg` (it is `Mutex<Config>`), call `cfg.save()`, return a
   user-facing notice string. Unknown names fall through to
   `Err(format!("unknown command /{other}"))`.
2. Client whitelist in `crates/client-tui/src/app.rs` `send()` (~line 569): add the
   name to the `provider_cmd` `matches!` list so it routes as
   `ClientRequest::Command` instead of a chat message. (Known gap in the tree:
   `/rnmap` and `/settings` exist server-side but are missing from this list, so they
   currently go to the model as text - fix by adding them.)
3. Local-only commands (`new`, `clear`, `panel`, `quit`) instead map to `Cmd::` in the
   second match (~line 588).
4. If the command should also be editable in the Ctrl+P panel, add a catalog row in
   `crates/shared/src/tui_settings.rs` - every panel row writes `tui.<path>` back to
   the brain's config.

## Recipe D - add a provider

- No code: `providers` config map entry or `/customprovider <id> <base-url>
  [openai|anthropic]`.
- Cataloged: append a `Known { id, name, kind, base_url, key_env, needs_key,
  default_model, models }` row to `KNOWN` in `crates/shared/src/catalog.rs` (31 rows
  today; pick `ApiKind::Anthropic` for `/v1/messages` wire, `ApiKind::OpenAi` for
  chat-completions). Keep model lists a superset across any duplicated vendor rows.
- RAG requires the provider to expose an embeddings endpoint
  (`ROMACODE_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` overrides the model id).

## Recipe D2 - the modeldata seam (per-model official rules)

`crates/shared/modeldata/<provider>/<model>.json` (35 provider folders, v0.8.0)
is the official profile library every selected model follows: context window,
max output, param ranges, wire rules, endpoints, pricing, sources. Registry =
`crates/shared/src/modeldata.rs` (`profile_for` is TOTAL - exact/normalized/
family/name-shape/_provider/_default). When adding a model: edit the dataset in
`scripts/gen_modeldata.py`, rerun it (it regenerates the JSONs AND
`src/modeldata_gen.rs`), keep numbers sourced or flagged `unverified_fields`.
Request shaping lives in `agent.rs::anthropic_body` / `openai_body` and the
langchain builder - both engines clamp through `profile_for`, keep them in
sync. TUI annotation is render-time in `palette.rs` (never touch the raw id
string; selection must keep saving exact ids).

## Recipe E - tune the loop

Everything is a config key under `agent` / `model_params` / top level (full key map in
`references/architecture-map.md`): `engine` (native | langchain), `default_mode`,
`max_tool_rounds` (200, clamp 10 000), `tool_timeout_secs`, `max_tool_output_bytes`,
`auto_compact` + `compact_threshold_pct`, `context_window`, `system_prompt`,
`system_prompt_append`, and `instruction_files` (ROMACODE.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md are
auto-loaded from the project). Project-level behavior overrides go in the project's
`ROMACODE.md`.

## Verify before you ship

1. `cargo build --workspace --locked` - zero errors; `cargo test --workspace --locked`
   - the rnmap engine tests (15) and the approval end-to-end test in `api.rs` must stay
   green.
2. `romacode-server --print-config` shows your new keys merged with defaults.
3. Run the brain (`romacode-server serve --cwd /tmp/proj`) and drive one turn over
   `scripts/e2e_ws.py` or the TUI: the new tool must appear in the model's tool list,
   execute, and stream `ToolStart`/`ToolEnd`.
4. Re-check the gate: unknown tool names still refuse with
   `tool <name> is unavailable`.
```

```markdown
---
name: romacode-security-posture
description: RomaCode security posture reference - what the original restriction policy was, what was removed at the owner request (permissions autoaccept, no SSRF guard, tools pre-approved), which residual safeguards remain (unknown-tool refusal, cancel, timeouts, output caps, traversal checks) and the exact code anchors for each. Read before touching security.rs, config permissions or tool gating.
---

# Security Posture - What Was Removed, What Remains, How to Re-Enable

Source of truth: `FIXES.md` in the tree root ("Fully open tools framework
(restrictions removed)") plus static reading of `crates/server/src/security.rs` (392
lines), `tools/coding.rs`, `webfetch/`, `rnmap/mod.rs`, `config.rs`,
`tui_settings.rs`, `config.example.json`.

## The removal set (v0.7.x "fixed" state, owner-requested)

| Area | Removed behavior | Where it used to live |
|---|---|---|
| Gate | deny rules, ask/allow rules, Plan-mode hard stops, protected paths, Android host-access confinement | security.rs policy evaluation |
| Bash | fail-closed block when confine_to_project + protected_paths set | tools/coding.rs |
| File tools | confinement, protected-path check, hard-link refusal, symlink refusal (now resolves to real targets) | coding.rs descriptor-anchored backend + fallback |
| rnmap_scan | permissions.net deny refusal, external-target refusal, IDS-evasion gating (decoy/fragment now always allowed), max_targets 256 -> 4096 | rnmap/mod.rs |
| web_fetch | permissions.web deny refusal, SSRF private/loopback guard default-off (allow_private_hosts true), userinfo URLs now supported (basic auth) instead of rejected | webfetch/mod.rs, webfetch/url.rs |
| Android | "bridge unavailable" failure -> auto fallback to host adb CLI | tools/android.rs::execute_via_host_adb |
| Defaults | every permission class allow, no deny/ask lists, confine_to_project false, tui.session.permissions autoaccept, startup warnings removed | config.rs, tui_settings.rs, config.example.json |
| Prompts | "public internet refused", "state-changing actions require approval", "Plan is read-only" removed; Plan advisory only | agent system prompt assembly |

Consequence to keep in mind while customizing: any new tool you add is callable in
every mode without a prompt, and web/network/file tools reach localhost, private
ranges and the public internet. Do not restore gating silently - but also do not
weaken the remaining safeguards.

## Residual safeguards (keep them green)

1. Unknown-tool refusal: `tools/mod.rs::execute` - `tool {name} is unavailable`.
2. Cancel/timeout plumbing: Bash, rnmap_scan, browser poll the shared
   `AtomicBool`; agent.rs enforces tool_timeout_secs and max_tool_output_bytes.
3. Output caps: webfetch.max_output_chars, rnmap.max_output_chars,
   browser.max_output_chars; bash output capped before it enters the transcript.
4. webapp_scaffold traversal validation: name/path/rustango_path rejected on `..`,
   quotes, empty, `crate` (tests in rustango_bridge.rs).
5. GitHub client: SSRF filter + curl `resolve` pinning, token via stdin config (never
   argv), 16 MiB / 10k-item pagination caps.
6. Approval machinery (dormant but intact): Security approval registry, oneshot
   answer slots, ApprovalRequest wire event, TUI modal y/n popup,
   SessionSnapshot.pending_approvals restore, `resolve_approval`. End-to-end test:
   `api::tests::approval_flow_end_to_end_through_the_hub`.

## How to re-enable restrictions (if ever asked)

The enforcement code is deleted, not disabled - config keys still parse and
serialize but nothing reads them. Re-enabling means re-implementing checks at the
exact choke points (all traffic crosses them, so coverage is total):

1. `security::authorize` (security.rs): re-add policy evaluation before returning
   Allow - match the class (read/edit/bash/web/net/android), evaluate
   `permissions.allow/ask/deny` glob lists (the glob matcher with memoization is
   still in security.rs), consult `session.mode` for Plan hard stops.
2. `tools/coding.rs::execute`: re-add protected-path + confinement checks for the
   descriptor-anchored backend and the non-Linux fallback.
3. `webfetch/mod.rs::execute` + `webfetch/url.rs`: re-enable the private/loopback
   guard when `webfetch.allow_private_hosts` is false.
4. `rnmap/mod.rs::execute`: re-check `allow_external_targets`, `allow_evasion`,
   `allow_scripts`, max_targets clamp before spawning the scanner.
5. Config defaults (config.rs, config.example.json, tui_settings.rs): flip
   `permissions.*` defaults to `ask`, `tui.session.permissions` to `prompt`, and
   restore the startup warnings.
6. UI is already wired: an `Ask` decision broadcasts ApprovalRequest and every
   attached screen raises the modal - no TUI work needed.

Test plan: revive/extend the gate tests (the net-class gate test and approval
end-to-end test are the templates), then drive one denied, one asked and one allowed
call through both engines.

## Hygiene for new code

- Never log or hardcode API keys; keys live in the brain's config file only and never
  round-trip through the screen (save_model deliberately ignores empty keys).
- Treat all web/browser/rnmap output as untrusted data - the tool descriptions say so
  verbatim; keep that sentence when editing descriptions.
- Keep cancel-aware loops and output caps on anything process-spawning or streaming.
- New config keys need clamps and a config.example.json entry (the rnmap pattern);
  unknown spellings must fall back to the safe behavior.
```

# Tool Recipes - Code Skeletons

All skeletons are verified against the tree (romacode-fixed-v3). Shape sources:
`crates/server/src/tools/webfetch.rs` (definition + execute), `tools/mod.rs`
(registration + dispatch), `crates/rc-tools/rc-core/src/tool.rs` (rc contract).

## A. Brain tool (the next registered tool)

### `crates/server/src/tools/mytool.rs`

```rust
//! One-line purpose. Keep the description model-facing and specific.

use crate::config::Config;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

/// Anthropic-shaped definition; tools/mod.rs wraps it for OpenAI providers.
pub fn definition() -> Value {
    json!({
        "name": "mytool",
        "description": "What it does, when to use it, what it returns.",
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "path":  { "type": "string", "description": "..." },
                "limit": { "type": "integer", "description": "..." }
            },
            "required": ["path"]
        }
    })
}

pub fn execute(cfg: &Config, input: &Value, cancel: &AtomicBool) -> Result<String, String> {
    if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
        return Err("cancelled".into());
    }
    let path = input.get("path").and_then(|v| v.as_str())
        .ok_or("missing 'path'")?;
    // ... real work; poll cancel in loops; cap output chars;
    // Err(String) is user-facing: explain policy/bad input, never panic.
    Ok(format!("done: {path}"))
}
```

### Register in `crates/server/src/tools/mod.rs`

```rust
pub mod mytool;

// inside definitions(): BOTH branches
if cfg.mytool.enabled { defs.push(mytool::definition()); }          // anthropic arm
if cfg.mytool.enabled { defs.push(wrap(mytool::definition())); }    // openai arm

// inside execute():
"mytool" => mytool::execute(cfg, input, cancel),
```

### Config section (config.rs + config.example.json)

Follow the `rnmap` pattern: a serde struct with `Default` + clamps in
`config.rs` (`Default::default()`, `apply_clamps`), a matching block in
`config.example.json`, and an `/mytool on|off` arm in `Hub::run_command` if the tool
is toggleable.

### Tests

- Unit tests next to `execute` (input shapes, caps, cancel).
- If the tool touches sessions/events: an `api.rs` test like
  `approval_flow_end_to_end_through_the_hub`.
- rnmap keeps 15 engine tests including a real local scan - imitate that depth for
  anything process-spawning.

## B. rc-* tool (framework side, not the brain)

### Rust (rc-core contract)

```rust

use rc_core::schema::Schema;
use rc_core::error::ToolResult;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde_json::Value;

struct Upper;

#[async_trait]
impl Tool for Upper {
    fn name(&self) -> &str { "upper" }
    fn description(&self) -> &str { "Uppercase the input text" }
    fn schema(&self) -> Schema { /* params: text: Text (required) */ }
    async fn run(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult<String> {
        // ctx: correlation_id, timeout_ms, live cancel flag (Arc<AtomicBool>),
        // allow_net, allow_fs_paths - self-check before I/O.
    }
}
// Register: Registry::new().register_all(vec![arc]) or ship via rc-builtin's
// category all() pattern (see rc-builtin/src/text.rs).
```

- Composition: wrap steps with rc-compose primitives (pipeline, parallel, branch,
  dag, iter); composed tools report `ToolSourceKind::Compose(kind)` and inherit the
  live cancel flag.
- Import paths: declarative YAML/JSON -> ShellTool; REST/OpenAPI -> HttpTool
  (`shell_quote` for any shell interpolation); MCP `tools/list` -> mcp source.
- Lifecycle: `rc_lifecycle::Lifecycle` walks a `SourceRegistry`:
  discover -> register -> validate -> load -> execute (timed, monitored).
- Python mirror: same contract in `rc-python/rc_python/` (core, schema, validator,
  registry, executor, sandbox, permissions, manifest, lifecycle, compose, sources).

## C. Slash command skeleton

Server (`api.rs`, `Hub::run_command`):

```rust
"mysetting" if arg.is_empty() => format!("My setting: {}", cfg.mytool.enabled),
"mysetting" => match arg.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
    "on" | "off" => { cfg.mytool.enabled = arg == "on"; cfg.save();
                      format!("My tool {}.", if arg == "on" {"enabled"} else {"disabled"}) }
    other => format!("unknown value '{other}' - use /mysetting on or off"),
},
```

Missing this step sends the text to the model as a normal message (this is exactly
the current `/rnmap` / `/settings` gap).

````markdown
---
name: unlock
description: Unlock any local LLM - download, quantize and edit any downloadable HuggingFace model with the Heretic engine, then run it in RomaCode as a local provider. Covers size/memory estimation for every precision from the model id, license checking, honest untested-model labeling, doctor.py and setup.py usage, llama.cpp/LM Studio/Ollama paths. Use when the user wants to run a local model, remove fine-tuned refusals, or reshape a model's persona or knowledge.
---

# Unlock: local model editing with Heretic

Unlock is model-agnostic: ANY downloadable local model works — Llama, Mistral,
Qwen, Gemma, Phi, DeepSeek, Heretic-generated hybrids — not only the measured
Qwen3-4B anchor. The engine is Heretic (p-e-w's GGUF-editing tool, AGPL);
the original model file is never touched and every run produces hashed
before/after evidence.

## 1. Pick and size the model first

Estimate from the id before downloading — the parameter count in the id and
the precision decide everything:

| Precision | Bytes/param | 4B model | 8B model |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q2_K | ~2.6 bpw | ~1.3 GB | ~2.6 GB |
| Q4_K_M | ~4.8 bpw | ~2.4 GB | ~4.9 GB |
| Q8_0 | ~8.5 bpw | ~4.3 GB | ~8.5 GB |
| FP16 | 2.0 B/param | ~8.0 GB | ~16 GB |

RAM needed ≈ file size + 0.5-1.0 GB context/KV overhead. Parse the id:
`qwen3-4b-instruct` → 4B params; a bare id like `hermes-3` → look the config
up on the hub page, never guess. GPU offload layers are optional; CPU-only
works with lower thread count.

License check before use: read the model card license (llama-3 community,
gemma, apache-2.0, MIT all allow local editing; verify redistribution terms
for the EDITED artifact separately).

## 2. Setup and doctor

`setup.py` downloads Heretic plus llama.cpp binaries and reports the real
download size for the chosen model (dynamic, not hardcoded). `doctor.py`
verifies the toolchain and accepts `--model-id` and `--dtype` so the plan is
computed for YOUR model, not the tested anchor:

```bash
python setup.py                       # toolchain + Heretic
python doctor.py --model-id qwen3-4b-instruct --dtype Q4_K_M
```

Doctor prints: estimated file size, RAM need, disk free verdict, license note,
and an UNTESTED-model warning when the id is not the calibrated anchor.

## 3. Run the unlock

```bash
heretic run <model-id> --dtype Q4_K_M   # or a local GGUF path
```

Heretic steers itself with contradictory-pair prompts, edits weights, and
writes to `heretic-workspace/`:
* `README.md` — what changed, KL divergence vs baseline, the KL ceiling it
  hit;
* before/after SHA-256 hashes of the GGUF;
* the final edited GGUF (the original is untouched).

Claim honestly: an untested model gets "estimated" numbers, not measured
ones. Never fabricate benchmark results.

## 4. Serve it in RomaCode

Point a local provider at the edited GGUF — llama.cpp `llama-server`,
LM Studio or Ollama all expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```bash
llama-server -m heretic-workspace/model-Q4_K_M.gguf --port 8321
# config.json → providers: {"local-heretic": {"base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8321/v1", "api": "openai"}}
```

Then `/models` in RomaCode picks it up (fetched catalogs persist into the
model options since v0.7.7). Keep the hash pair with the artifact so anyone
can verify which file was edited.
````

## `crates/server/src/agent.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/src/agent.rs)

````rust
//! The think-act-observe loop. `spawn_run` starts a background thread that
//! streams wire `Event`s to every attached client through the api bus. Two
//! engines are available (see `agent.engine` in the config):
//!
//! * **native** (default) - the audited in-house loop below. Two wire
//!   protocols are supported, chosen by the active provider:
//!
//! * **Anthropic** — Messages API with SSE streaming;
//! * **OpenAI-compatible** — Chat Completions with SSE streaming, which covers
//!   OpenAI, OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral, xAI, Together,
//!   Fireworks, Cerebras, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and any custom endpoint.
//!
//! * **langchain** - the vendored `langchain-rust` engine
//!   (`crate::langchain_bridge`): LCEL agent executor, langchain memory and
//!   the RAG tool set, with every tool still passing the same security gate.
//!
//! In both engines permitted coding tools operate on the selected project,
//! web fetch reads remote pages, and Android calls use the official host ADB
//! client against an explicitly selected real target. There is no
//! canned/offline reply: provider errors are reported in chat.
use crate::api::Bus;
use crate::config::{ApiKind, Config, Resolved};
use crate::security::{Decision, Security};
use crate::session::Mode;
use romacode_shared::events::Event;
use serde_json::json;
use std::io::{BufReader, Read};
use std::time::Instant;
use std::sync::{
    atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    Arc,
};

/// Event emitter: one agent run -> the api bus (all attached clients).
/// Cheap to clone; langchain tool closures hold copies.
impl Clone for Emit {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            bus: self.bus.clone(),
            session_id: self.session_id,
            // A clone is a fresh emitter context; the flag tracks one attempt.
            streamed_text: AtomicBool::new(false),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Emit {
    bus: Bus,
    pub session_id: usize,
    /// Set whenever a text delta reached the wire during the current
    /// attempt. The retry loop reads (and resets) it so a retry after a
    /// dropped stream can separate the partial answer from the fresh one.
    streamed_text: AtomicBool,
}

impl Emit {
    pub fn new(bus: Bus, session_id: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            bus,
            session_id,
            streamed_text: AtomicBool::new(false),
        }
    }
    /// Did any text delta already stream in this attempt? Resets the flag.
    pub fn take_streamed_text(&self) -> bool {
        self.streamed_text.swap(false, Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
    pub fn bus(&self) -> Bus {
        self.bus.clone()
    }
    pub fn text(&self, t: &str) {
        // Without this the retry loop could never tell that a partial answer
        // had already reached the screen, so the separator notice never fired.
        self.streamed_text.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::Text {
            session_id: self.session_id,
            delta: t.to_string(),
        });
    }
    pub fn tool_start(&self, id: &str, name: &str, arg: &serde_json::Value) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::ToolStart {
            session_id: self.session_id,
            id: id.to_string(),
            name: name.to_string(),
            arg: arg.to_string(),
        });
    }
    pub fn tool_end(&self, id: &str, ok: bool, extra: Option<String>) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::ToolEnd {
            session_id: self.session_id,
            id: id.to_string(),
            ok,
            extra,
        });
    }
    pub fn usage(&self, input: u64, output: u64) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::Usage {
            session_id: self.session_id,
            input,
            output,
        });
    }
    pub fn notice(&self, text: impl Into<String>) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::Notice {
            session_id: Some(self.session_id),
            text: text.into(),
        });
    }
    /// A tool call waits for the user's y/n. Broadcast as a real
    /// `ApprovalRequest` event so every attached screen can raise its allow
    /// popup and answer with `ClientRequest::Approval` (request_id-scoped).
    /// The transcript notice is rendered by the session mirror on both sides
    /// from this one event — no separate Notice is broadcast for it.
    pub fn approval_request(&self, request_id: &str, name: &str, effect: &str) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::ApprovalRequest {
            session_id: self.session_id,
            request_id: request_id.to_string(),
            name: name.to_string(),
            effect: effect.to_string(),
        });
    }
    pub fn error(&self, msg: impl Into<String>) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::Error {
            session_id: Some(self.session_id),
            message: msg.into(),
        });
    }
    pub fn done(&self, secs: f32) {
        self.bus.broadcast(Event::Done {
            session_id: self.session_id,
            secs,
        });
    }
}

/// One running turn. The api layer stores this on the session.
pub struct Spawned {
    pub cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

/// Start the think-act-observe loop on a background thread. Text, tool
/// activity, usage, approvals and completion all flow out through `bus`.
/// `security` is THE gate: no tool runs except through it.
pub fn spawn_run(
    cfg: &Config,
    session_id: usize,
    history: Vec<(&'static str, String)>,
    mode: Mode,
    bus: Bus,
    security: std::sync::Arc<Security>,
    android: Option<crate::android::AndroidAgent>,
    cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    steer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
    started: std::time::Instant,
) -> Spawned {
    let emit = Emit::new(bus, session_id);
    let cfg = cfg.clone();
    let engine = cfg.agent.engine.clone();
    let cancel_thread = cancel.clone();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let cancel = cancel_thread;
        let run_once = |cfg: &crate::config::Config,
                        provider: &crate::config::Resolved|
         -> Result<(), String> {
            match engine.as_str() {
                "langchain" if crate::tools::langchain_compatible(provider.kind) => {
                    crate::langchain_bridge::run_langchain(
                        cfg,
                        provider,
                        &history,
                        mode,
                        &emit,
                        &security,
                        android.as_ref(),
                        &cancel,
                    )
                }
                "langchain" => {
                    emit.notice(format!(
                        "langchain engine speaks the OpenAI-compatible protocol; {} uses Anthropic - falling back to the native engine",
                        provider.name
                    ));
                    run_provider(
                        cfg,
                        provider,
                        &history,
                        mode,
                        &emit,
                        &security,
                        &cancel,
                        &steer,
                        android.as_ref(),
                    )
                }
                _ => run_provider(
                    cfg,
                    provider,
                    &history,
                    mode,
                    &emit,
                    &security,
                    &cancel,
                    &steer,
                    android.as_ref(),
                ),
            }
        };
        // A panic unwinding out of this thread would never emit Event::Error
        // or Event::Done, leaving the session busy forever. Run the whole
        // attempt (primary + fallback models) under catch_unwind and turn an
        // unwind into the same Err path an ordinary failed turn takes.
        let attempt = || -> Result<(), String> {
            let mut res = match cfg.resolve() {
                Ok(provider) => run_once(&cfg, &provider),
                Err(e) => Err(e),
            };
            // `fallback_models` was a dead config field. Try each entry when the
            // primary fails, so one provider's outage does not end the task.
            // "provider/model" switches provider too; a bare id keeps the current
            // endpoint and only changes the model.
            if res.is_err() {
                for fb in cfg.model_params.fallback_models.clone() {
                    if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) || fb.trim().is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let Ok(mut alt) = cfg.resolve() else { break };
                    match fb.split_once('/') {
                        Some((pid, mid)) => {
                            if let Some(pc) = cfg.providers.get(pid) {
                                alt.id = pid.to_string();
                                alt.name = if pc.name.is_empty() {
                                    pid.to_string()
                                } else {
                                    pc.name.clone()
                                };
                                if !pc.base_url.is_empty() {
                                    alt.base_url = pc.base_url.clone();
                                }
                                if !pc.api_key.is_empty() {
                                    alt.api_key = Some(pc.api_key.clone());
                                }
                                if let Some(kind) = pc.kind {
                                    alt.kind = kind;
                                }
                                alt.model = mid.to_string();
                            } else {
                                alt.model = fb.clone();
                            }
                        }
                        None => alt.model = fb.clone(),
                    }
                    emit.notice(format!("primary provider failed — trying fallback model {fb}"));
                    res = run_once(&cfg, &alt);
                    if res.is_ok() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            res
        };
        let res = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(attempt))
