```rust
fn is_hex_colour(s: &str) -> bool {
    s.len() == 7 && s.starts_with('#') && s[1..].chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit())
}

impl Config {
    pub fn path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
        dirs::config_dir().map(|d| d.join("romacode").join("config.json"))
    }

    /// Load the config, apply `ROMACODE_*` overrides and validate. Never
    /// fails: problems become defaults plus warnings (see [`Config::load_report`]).
    pub fn load() -> Self {
        Self::load_report().0
    }

    /// Like [`Config::load`] but also returns human-readable warnings
    /// (parse failure, clamped values, unknown enum spellings, …).
    pub fn load_report() -> (Self, Vec<String>) {
        let mut warnings = Vec::new();
        let mut cfg = match Self::path() {
            Some(p) => match std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {
                Ok(text) => match serde_json::from_str::<Config>(&text) {
                    Ok(c) => c,
                    Err(e) => {
                        // keep the user's file; never replace it with defaults
                        let bak = p.with_extension("json.bak");
                        let _ = std::fs::copy(&p, &bak);
                        warnings.push(format!(
                            "{}: {e} — using defaults this session (original kept at {})",
                            p.display(),
                            bak.display()
                        ));
                        Config::default()
                    }
                },
                Err(_) => Config::default(), // no file yet
            },
            None => Config::default(),
        };
        if cfg.version < SCHEMA_VERSION {
            // v1 → v2: every new section is already defaulted by serde
            cfg.version = SCHEMA_VERSION;
        } else if cfg.version > SCHEMA_VERSION {
            warnings.push(format!(
                "config version {} is newer than this build ({}); unknown settings are ignored",
                cfg.version, SCHEMA_VERSION
            ));
        }
        cfg.apply_env(|k| std::env::var(k).ok());
        warnings.extend(cfg.validate());
        (cfg, warnings)
    }

    /// Per-run overrides, highest priority:
    /// `ROMACODE_PROVIDER`, `ROMACODE_MODEL`, `ROMACODE_API_KEY` (read by [`Config::resolve`]), `ROMACODE_API_BASE`,
    /// `ROMACODE_MAX_TOKENS`, `ROMACODE_MODE` (build|plan),
    /// `ROMACODE_THEME` (auto|dark|light|bronze), `ROMACODE_PROXY`,
    /// `ROMACODE_LOG` (off|error|warn|info|debug|trace),
    /// `ROMACODE_NO_ANIMATIONS=1`, `ROMACODE_NO_ANDROID=1`.
    pub fn apply_env(&mut self, get: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) {
        let nonempty = |k: &str| {
            get(k)
                .filter(|v| !v.trim().is_empty())
                .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
        };
        let truthy = |k: &str| matches!(nonempty(k).as_deref(), Some("1" | "true" | "yes" | "on"));
        if let Some(v) = nonempty("ROMACODE_PROVIDER") {
            self.provider = v;
        }
        if let Some(v) = nonempty("ROMACODE_MODEL") {
            self.model = v;
        }
        if let Some(v) = nonempty("ROMACODE_API_BASE") {
            self.api_base = v;
        }
        if let Some(v) = nonempty("ROMACODE_MAX_TOKENS").and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()) {
            self.max_tokens = v;
        }
        match nonempty("ROMACODE_MODE").as_deref() {
            Some("build") => self.agent.default_mode = AgentMode::Build,
            Some("plan") => self.agent.default_mode = AgentMode::Plan,
            _ => {}
        }
        match nonempty("ROMACODE_THEME").as_deref() {
            Some("auto") => self.ui.theme = ThemeMode::Auto,
            Some("dark") => self.ui.theme = ThemeMode::Dark,
            Some("light") => self.ui.theme = ThemeMode::Light,
            Some("bronze") => self.ui.theme = ThemeMode::Bronze,
            _ => {}
        }
        if let Some(v) = nonempty("ROMACODE_PROXY") {
            self.network.proxy = v;
        }
        match nonempty("ROMACODE_LOG").as_deref() {
            Some("off") => self.advanced.log_level = LogLevel::Off,
            Some("error") => self.advanced.log_level = LogLevel::Error,
            Some("warn") => self.advanced.log_level = LogLevel::Warn,
            Some("info") => self.advanced.log_level = LogLevel::Info,
            Some("debug") => self.advanced.log_level = LogLevel::Debug,
            Some("trace") => self.advanced.log_level = LogLevel::Trace,
            _ => {}
        }
        if truthy("ROMACODE_NO_ANIMATIONS") {
            self.ui.animations = false;
        }
        if truthy("ROMACODE_NO_ANDROID") {
            self.android.auto_start = false;
        }
    }

    /// Set one OpenCode-style TUI setting by dotted path from its wire string
    /// (`"show"`, `"on"`, `"0.7"`), validating against the settings catalog.
    /// Settings that mirror a legacy key (`session.sidebar`, `animations`,
    /// `mouse`) keep that key in step.
    pub fn set_tui_pref(&mut self, path: &str, raw: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        use romacode_shared::tui_settings as t;
        let d = t::def(path).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown setting {path}"))?;
        let v = t::parse_wire(d, raw)?;
        self.tui.set(path, &v)?;
        match path {
            "session.sidebar" => self.sidebar = self.tui.session.sidebar == "auto",
            "animations" => self.ui.animations = self.tui.animations,
            "mouse" => self.ui.mouse = self.tui.mouse,
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Clamp every value into its supported range. Returns one warning per
    /// correction so the UI can surface them.
    pub fn validate(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut w = Vec::new();
        macro_rules! clamp {
            ($field:expr, $lo:expr, $hi:expr, $name:expr) => {{
                let v = $field;
                let c = v.clamp($lo, $hi);
                if c != v {
                    w.push(format!("{} = {} is out of range; using {}", $name, v, c));
                    $field = c;
                }
            }};
        }
        if !matches!(self.agent.engine.as_str(), "native" | "langchain") {
            w.push(format!(
                "agent.engine = '{}' is not one of native|langchain; using native",
                self.agent.engine
            ));
            self.agent.engine = "native".into();
        }
        clamp!(self.chat_width_pct, 20, 70, "chat_width_pct");
        clamp!(self.max_tokens, 1, 128_000, "max_tokens");
        clamp!(self.context_window, 1_000, 10_000_000, "context_window");
        clamp!(self.agent.max_tool_rounds, 1, 10_000, "agent.max_tool_rounds");
        clamp!(
            self.agent.compact_threshold_pct,
            30,
            98,
            "agent.compact_threshold_pct"
        );
        clamp!(
            self.agent.max_tool_output_bytes,
            1_024,
            8 * 1024 * 1024,
            "agent.max_tool_output_bytes"
        );
        clamp!(self.ui.tab_width, 1, 16, "ui.tab_width");
        clamp!(self.ui.max_fps, 5, 120, "ui.max_fps");
        clamp!(
            self.ui.scrollback_lines,
            100,
            1_000_000,
            "ui.scrollback_lines"
        );
        clamp!(
            self.network.connect_timeout_secs,
            1,
            300,
            "network.connect_timeout_secs"
        );
        clamp!(self.network.max_retries, 0, 10, "network.max_retries");
        clamp!(
            self.webfetch.max_body_bytes,
            4_096,
            64 * 1024 * 1024,
            "webfetch.max_body_bytes"
        );
        clamp!(
            self.webfetch.max_output_chars,
            1_000,
            500_000,
            "webfetch.max_output_chars"
        );
        clamp!(self.webfetch.timeout_secs, 1, 300, "webfetch.timeout_secs");
        clamp!(self.webfetch.max_redirects, 0, 10, "webfetch.max_redirects");
        clamp!(self.browser.port, 0, 65_535, "browser.port");
        clamp!(
            self.browser.start_timeout_secs,
            5,
            900,
            "browser.start_timeout_secs"
        );
        clamp!(self.browser.timeout_secs, 1, 900, "browser.timeout_secs");
        clamp!(
            self.browser.max_output_chars,
            1_000,
            2_000_000,
            "browser.max_output_chars"
        );
        clamp!(self.rnmap.default_timing, 0, 5, "rnmap.default_timing");
        clamp!(self.rnmap.timeout_secs, 0, 3_600, "rnmap.timeout_secs");
        clamp!(self.rnmap.max_targets, 1, 65_535, "rnmap.max_targets");
        clamp!(
            self.rnmap.max_output_chars,
            1_000,
            500_000,
            "rnmap.max_output_chars"
        );
        if self.rnmap.default_ports.trim().is_empty() {
            w.push("rnmap.default_ports is empty; using 1-1000".into());
            self.rnmap.default_ports = "1-1000".into();
        }
        clamp!(self.remix.timeout_secs, 0, 3_600, "remix.timeout_secs");
        clamp!(
            self.remix.max_output_chars,
            1_000,
            200_000,
            "remix.max_output_chars"
        );
        clamp!(self.android.density, 120, 640, "android.density");
        clamp!(self.android.window_scale, 0.25, 2.0, "android.window_scale");
        clamp!(self.android.fps, 1, 60, "android.fps");
        clamp!(self.android.wallpaper, 0, 2, "android.wallpaper");
        clamp!(self.sessions.max_saved, 1, 10_000, "sessions.max_saved");
        clamp!(
            self.sessions.history_limit,
            10,
            100_000,
            "sessions.history_limit"
        );

        for (i, name) in ["width", "height"].iter().enumerate() {
            let v = self.android.display[i];
            let c = v.clamp(240, 4320);
            if c != v {
                w.push(format!(
                    "android.display {name} = {v} is out of range; using {c}"
                ));
                self.android.display[i] = c;
            }
        }
        if let Some(t) = self.model_params.temperature {
            let c = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
            if c != t {
                w.push(format!(
                    "model_params.temperature = {t} is out of range; using {c}"
                ));
                self.model_params.temperature = Some(c);
            }
        }
        if let Some(p) = self.model_params.top_p {
            let c = p.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
            if c != p {
                w.push(format!(
                    "model_params.top_p = {p} is out of range; using {c}"
                ));
                self.model_params.top_p = Some(c);
            }
        }
        if self.model_params.thinking && self.model_params.thinking_budget_tokens >= self.max_tokens
        {
            if self.max_tokens == 0 {
                // A zero max_tokens leaves no room for a budget — the old
                // repair computed (0/2).max(1024).min(0) = 0, i.e. a zero
                // budget that silently disabled thinking anyway.
                w.push("model_params.thinking requires max_tokens > 0; disabling thinking".into());
                self.model_params.thinking = false;
            } else {
                let fixed = (self.max_tokens / 2)
                    .max(1_024)
                    .min(self.max_tokens - 1);
                w.push(format!(
                    "model_params.thinking_budget_tokens ({}) must be below max_tokens ({}); using {fixed}",
                    self.model_params.thinking_budget_tokens, self.max_tokens
                ));
                self.model_params.thinking_budget_tokens = fixed;
            }
        }
        if !self.ui.accent.is_empty() && !is_hex_colour(&self.ui.accent) {
            w.push(format!(
                "ui.accent = {:?} is not #rrggbb; ignoring",
                self.ui.accent
            ));
            self.ui.accent.clear();
        }
        if self.android.backend != "adb" {
            w.push(format!(
                "android.backend = {:?} is unsupported; using the real ADB backend",
                self.android.backend
            ));
            self.android.backend = "adb".into();
        }
        self.android.adb_path = self.android.adb_path.trim().to_string();
        if self.android.adb_path.is_empty() {
            self.android.adb_path = "adb".into();
        }
        if !matches!(self.android.system_theme.as_str(), "dark" | "light") {
            w.push(format!(
                "android.system_theme = {:?} must be dark or light; using dark",
                self.android.system_theme
            ));
            self.android.system_theme = "dark".into();
        }
        if self.android.bind.trim().is_empty() {
            self.android.bind = "127.0.0.1".into();
        } else if !matches!(
            self.android.bind.as_str(),
            "127.0.0.1" | "localhost" | "::1"
        ) {
            w.push(format!(
                "android.bind = {:?} exposes the phone's adb server beyond this machine",
                self.android.bind
            ));
        }
        if self.provider.trim().is_empty() {
            w.push("provider is empty; using anthropic".into());
            self.provider = "anthropic".into();
        }
        if !self.api_base.is_empty()
            && !self.api_base.starts_with("https://")
            && !self.api_base.starts_with("http://")
        {
            w.push(format!(
                "api_base {:?} is not an http(s) URL; ignoring",
                self.api_base
            ));
            self.api_base.clear();
        }
        for (id, p) in &self.providers {
            if !p.base_url.is_empty()
                && !p.base_url.starts_with("https://")
                && !p.base_url.starts_with("http://")
            {
                w.push(format!(
                    "providers.{id}.base_url {:?} is not an http(s) URL",
                    p.base_url
                ));
            }
            if crate::providers::find(id).is_none() && p.base_url.is_empty() {
                w.push(format!("custom provider {id:?} has no base_url"));
            }
        }
        if !matches!(
            self.webfetch
                .default_mode
                .trim()
                .to_ascii_lowercase()
                .as_str(),
            "text" | "markdown" | "raw" | "json" | "links" | "headers"
        ) {
            w.push(format!(
                "webfetch.default_mode = {:?} is not valid; using text",
                self.webfetch.default_mode
            ));
            self.webfetch.default_mode = "text".into();
        }
        // OpenCode-style TUI settings: clamp hand-edited values.
        w.extend(self.tui.sanitize());
        // `tui.session.sidebar` and the legacy `sidebar` flag are one switch;
        // "hide" from either side wins.
        if self.tui.session.sidebar == "hide" {
            self.sidebar = false;
        } else if !self.sidebar {
            self.tui.session.sidebar = "hide".into();
        }
        w
    }

    /// The model that will actually be used: `model`, else the provider default.
    pub fn effective_model(&self) -> String {
        if !self.model.trim().is_empty() {
            return self.model.trim().to_string();
        }
        let id = self.provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        let from_user = self
            .providers
            .get(&id)
            .map(|p| p.default_model.trim().to_string())
            .filter(|m| !m.is_empty());
        from_user
            .or_else(|| crate::providers::find(&id).map(|k| k.default_model.to_string()))
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Merge known defaults ← `providers.<id>` ← top-level overrides ← env.
    /// Errors (unknown id, missing base URL, missing key) are phrased for the
    /// user: they are shown in the chat instead of a canned reply.
    pub fn resolve(&self) -> Result<Resolved, String> {
        self.resolve_with(|k| std::env::var(k).ok())
    }

    /// [`Config::resolve`] with an injectable environment (used by tests).
    pub fn resolve_with(&self, env: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Result<Resolved, String> {
        let id = self.provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        if id.is_empty() {
            return Err("no provider selected — set `provider` (try `/providers`)".into());
        }
        let known = crate::providers::find(&id);
        let user = self.providers.get(&id).or_else(|| {
            // ids are case-insensitive
            self.providers
                .iter()
                .find(|(k, _)| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&id))
                .map(|(_, v)| v)
        });
        let blank = ProviderCfg::default();
        let u = user.unwrap_or(&blank);
        if known.is_none() && user.is_none() {
            return Err(format!(
                "unknown provider {id:?}. Pick a known one (`/providers`) or define it under \"providers\" with a base_url"
            ));
        }
        let pick = |a: &str, b: &str| {
            if !a.trim().is_empty() {
                a.trim().to_string()
            } else {
                b.to_string()
            }
        };
        let base_url = pick(
            &self.api_base,
            &pick(&u.base_url, known.map_or("", |k| k.base_url.as_str())),
        )
        .trim_end_matches('/')
        .to_string();
        if base_url.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!(
                "provider {id:?} has no base_url — set providers.{id}.base_url"
            ));
        }
        let kind = u.kind.or(known.map(|k| k.kind)).unwrap_or(ApiKind::OpenAi);
        let key_env = pick(
            &self.api_key_env,
            &pick(&u.api_key_env, known.map_or("", |k| k.key_env.as_str())),
        );
        let needs_key = if known.is_some() {
            known.map_or(true, |k| k.needs_key)
        } else {
            !u.no_key
        };
        // key precedence: ROMACODE_API_KEY, providers.<id>.api_key, the env var
        let env_get = |name: &str| {
            env(name)
                .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
                .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
        };
        let api_key = env_get("ROMACODE_API_KEY")
            .or_else(|| Some(u.api_key.trim().to_string()).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()))
            .or_else(|| {
                if key_env.is_empty() {
                    None
                } else {
                    env_get(&key_env)
                }
            });
        if needs_key && api_key.is_none() {
            let name = pick(&u.name, known.map_or(id.as_str(), |k| k.name.as_str()));
            let hint = if key_env.is_empty() {
                format!("providers.{id}.api_key")
            } else {
                format!("export {key_env}=… (or providers.{id}.api_key)")
            };
            return Err(format!("no API key for {name}. Set it with `{hint}`, `/apikey <key>`, or `romacode set api-key <key>`"));
        }
        let mut model = self.model.trim().to_string();
        if model.is_empty() {
            model = pick(&u.default_model, known.map_or("", |k| k.default_model.as_str()));
        }
        if model.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!(
                "no model for provider {id:?} — set `model` (or providers.{id}.default_model)"
            ));
        }
        Ok(Resolved {
            name: pick(&u.name, known.map_or(id.as_str(), |k| k.name.as_str())),
            id,
            kind,
            base_url,
            api_key,
            key_env,
            needs_key,
            model,
            headers: u.headers.clone(),
            stream_usage: u.stream_usage,
            tools: u.tools,
        })
    }

    /// Models offered for the active provider: user list first, then the
    /// known provider's suggestions, then the current model.
    pub fn model_choices(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let id = self.provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let mut push = |m: &str| {
            if !m.is_empty() && !out.iter().any(|x| x == m) {
                out.push(m.to_string());
            }
        };
        if let Some(p) = self.providers.get(&id) {
            p.models.iter().for_each(|m| push(m));
            push(&p.default_model);
        }
        if let Some(k) = crate::providers::find(&id) {
            k.models.iter().for_each(|m| push(m.as_str()));
        }
        push(&self.model);
        out
    }

    /// Remember the models a live `/models` catalog fetch returned for
    /// `provider_id`, so the list shows up in every model option from now on
    /// (Select Model, `/models`, `romacode models`) instead of living only in
    /// the settings screen that asked for it. Fetched ids are MERGED into the
    /// stored list — already-configured ids keep their position and fetched
    /// ones are appended deduplicated — so a fetch can never drop a model the
    /// user added by hand. Unknown provider ids are ignored unless they are a
    /// known provider or already have a config entry: a typo'd id must not
    /// conjure a junk entry. Persistence (save) is the caller's job.
    pub fn remember_models(&mut self, provider_id: &str, fetched: &[String]) {
        let id = provider_id.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        if id.is_empty() || fetched.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let known_or_existing =
            crate::providers::find(&id).is_some() || self.providers.contains_key(&id);
        if !known_or_existing {
            return;
        }
        const MAX_MODELS: usize = 512;
        let p = self.providers.entry(id).or_default();
        for m in fetched {
            let m = m.trim();
            if !m.is_empty() && !p.models.iter().any(|x| x == m) && p.models.len() < MAX_MODELS {
                p.models.push(m.to_string());
            }
        }
    }

    /// Switch provider; clears the model so the new provider's default is used.
    pub fn set_provider(&mut self, id: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let id = id.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        if crate::providers::find(&id).is_none() && !self.providers.contains_key(&id) {
            return Err(format!("unknown provider {id:?} — run `/providers` to see the list, or add it under \"providers\""));
        }
        if self.provider != id {
            self.provider = id;
            self.model.clear();
            self.api_base.clear();
            self.api_key_env.clear();
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Store an API key for the active provider (config file, owner-only).
    pub fn set_api_key(&mut self, key: &str) {
        let id = self.provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        self.providers.entry(id).or_default().api_key = key.trim().to_string();
    }

    /// Set the base URL of the active provider.
    pub fn set_base_url(&mut self, url: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let url = url.trim().trim_end_matches('/');
        if !url.is_empty() && !url.starts_with("http://") && !url.starts_with("https://") {
            return Err("base URL must start with http:// or https://".into());
        }
        let id = self.provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        self.providers.entry(id).or_default().base_url = url.to_string();
        self.api_base.clear();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Define or update a custom provider in one call.
    pub fn add_custom_provider(
        &mut self,
        id: &str,
        base_url: &str,
        kind: ApiKind,
    ) -> Result<(), String> {
        let id = id.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        if id.is_empty()
            || !id
                .chars()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_')
        {
            return Err("provider id must be letters, digits, - or _".into());
        }
        let url = base_url.trim().trim_end_matches('/');
        if !url.starts_with("http://") && !url.starts_with("https://") {
            return Err("base URL must start with http:// or https://".into());
        }
        let p = self.providers.entry(id).or_default();
        p.base_url = url.to_string();
        p.kind = Some(kind);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Atomic save: write a temp file next to the config, then rename.
    pub fn save(&self) {
        let Some(p) = Self::path() else { return };
        if let Some(dir) = p.parent() {
            let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(dir);
        }
        if let Ok(s) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self) {
            let tmp = p.with_extension("json.tmp");
            // the file may hold API keys: owner read/write only
            let wrote = {
                #[cfg(unix)]
                {
                    use std::io::Write;
                    use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
                    std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
                        .write(true)
                        .create(true)
                        .truncate(true)
                        .mode(0o600)
                        .open(&tmp)
                        .and_then(|mut f| f.write_all(s.as_bytes()))
                        .is_ok()
                }
                #[cfg(not(unix))]
                {
                    std::fs::write(&tmp, s).is_ok()
                }
            };
            if wrote && std::fs::rename(&tmp, &p).is_err() {
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The effective configuration for diagnostics. Never print stored secrets.
    pub fn to_pretty_json(&self) -> String {
        let Ok(mut value) = serde_json::to_value(self) else {
            return String::new();
        };
        if let Some(providers) = value.get_mut("providers").and_then(|v| v.as_object_mut()) {
            for provider in providers.values_mut() {
                if let Some(p) = provider.as_object_mut() {
                    if p.get("api_key")
                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                        .map_or(false, |s| !s.is_empty())
                    {
                        p.insert(
                            "api_key".into(),
                            serde_json::Value::String("[REDACTED]".into()),
                        );
                    }
                    if let Some(headers) = p.get_mut("headers").and_then(|v| v.as_object_mut()) {
                        for header in headers.values_mut() {
                            *header = serde_json::Value::String("[REDACTED]".into());
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(network) = value.get_mut("network").and_then(|v| v.as_object_mut()) {
            if let Some(headers) = network
                .get_mut("extra_headers")
                .and_then(|v| v.as_object_mut())
            {
                for header in headers.values_mut() {
                    *header = serde_json::Value::String("[REDACTED]".into());
                }
            }
            if network
                .get("proxy")
                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                .map_or(false, |s| s.contains('@'))
            {
                network.insert(
                    "proxy".into(),
                    serde_json::Value::String("[REDACTED]".into()),
                );
            }
        }
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&value).unwrap_or_default()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn printed_config_redacts_keys_and_headers() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.set_api_key("private-api-token");
        c.providers
            .get_mut("anthropic")
            .unwrap()
            .headers
            .insert("X-Token".into(), "private-provider-header".into());
        c.network
            .extra_headers
            .insert("Authorization".into(), "private-network-header".into());
        c.network.proxy = "http://user:password@example.invalid:8080".into();
        let printed = c.to_pretty_json();
        assert!(printed.contains("[REDACTED]"));
        for secret in [
            "private-api-token",
            "private-provider-header",
            "private-network-header",
            "password",
        ] {
            assert!(!printed.contains(secret), "printed config leaked {secret}");
        }
        let parsed: Config = serde_json::from_str(&printed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parsed.provider, c.provider);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_object_gives_defaults() {
        let c: Config = serde_json::from_str("{}").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.version, SCHEMA_VERSION);
        assert_eq!(c.provider, "anthropic");
        assert!(c.model_params.stream);
        assert_eq!(c.permissions.edit, Permission::Allow);
    }

    #[test]
    fn v1_config_still_loads() {
        let v1 = r#"{"provider":"anthropic","model":"m","max_tokens":1000,"sidebar":false,
                     "android":{"auto_start":false,"port":5557,"display":[1080,2400],"density":440}}"#;
        let c: Config = serde_json::from_str(v1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.model, "m");
        assert!(!c.sidebar);
        assert_eq!(c.android.port, 5557);
        assert_eq!(c.android.display, [1080, 2400]);
        assert_eq!(c.android.bind, "127.0.0.1"); // new key defaulted
    }

    #[test]
    fn bundled_example_parses_and_is_all_defaults() {
        let example: Config = serde_json::from_str(include_str!("../../../config.example.json")).unwrap();
        let a = serde_json::to_value(&example).unwrap();
        let b = serde_json::to_value(Config::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a, b);
    }

    #[test]
    fn webfetch_defaults_are_safe_and_on() {
        let c = Config::default();
        assert!(c.webfetch.enabled && c.webfetch.allow_private_hosts && !c.webfetch.render);
        let mut d = Config::default();
        d.webfetch.default_mode = "scrape".into(); // needs a selector, so not a valid default
        d.webfetch.max_output_chars = 5;
        let w = d.validate();
        assert_eq!(d.webfetch.default_mode, "text");
        assert_eq!(d.webfetch.max_output_chars, 1_000);
        assert!(w.len() >= 2, "{w:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_round_trips() {
        let a = Config::default();
        let b: Config = serde_json::from_str(&a.to_pretty_json()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_value(&a).unwrap(),
            serde_json::to_value(&b).unwrap()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_clamps_and_reports() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.chat_width_pct = 5;
        c.ui.accent = "orange".into();
        c.android.window_scale = 9.0;
        c.model_params.temperature = Some(3.0);
        c.model_params.thinking = true;
        c.model_params.thinking_budget_tokens = 99_999;
        let w = c.validate();
        assert_eq!(c.chat_width_pct, 20);
        assert!(c.ui.accent.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(c.android.window_scale, 2.0);
        assert_eq!(c.model_params.temperature, Some(1.0));
        assert!(c.model_params.thinking_budget_tokens < c.max_tokens);
        assert!(w.len() >= 5, "{w:?}");
        assert!(Config::default().validate().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn tui_settings_default_validate_clean_and_roundtrip() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        assert!(c.validate().is_empty());
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&c).unwrap();
        let back: Config = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back.tui, c.tui);
        // a file with only one tui key keeps every other default
        let partial: Config = serde_json::from_str(r#"{"tui":{"session":{"thinking":"show"}}}"#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(partial.tui.session.thinking, "show");
        assert_eq!(partial.tui.leader.timeout, 2000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_tui_pref_validates_and_syncs_legacy_keys() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.set_tui_pref("session.verbosity", "high").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.tui.session.verbosity, "high");
        assert!(c.set_tui_pref("session.verbosity", "ultra").is_err());
        assert!(c.set_tui_pref("leader.timeout", "5").is_err());
        assert!(c.set_tui_pref("bogus.path", "1").is_err());
        c.set_tui_pref("leader.timeout", "4000").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.tui.leader.timeout, 4000);

        c.set_tui_pref("session.sidebar", "hide").unwrap();
        assert!(!c.sidebar);
        c.set_tui_pref("session.sidebar", "auto").unwrap();
        assert!(c.sidebar);
        c.set_tui_pref("animations", "off").unwrap();
        assert!(!c.ui.animations);
        c.set_tui_pref("mouse", "off").unwrap();
        assert!(!c.ui.mouse);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_clamps_tui_and_hide_wins_for_sidebar() {
        let mut c: Config = serde_json::from_str(
            r#"{"sidebar":false,"tui":{"leader":{"timeout":999999},"tabs":{"mode":"sideways"}}}"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let w = c.validate();
        assert_eq!(c.tui.leader.timeout, 10000);
        assert_eq!(c.tui.tabs.mode, "off");
        assert_eq!(c.tui.session.sidebar, "hide"); // legacy sidebar=false wins
        assert!(w.len() >= 2, "{w:?}");

        let mut c: Config =
            serde_json::from_str(r#"{"tui":{"session":{"sidebar":"hide"}}}"#).unwrap();
        c.validate();
        assert!(!c.sidebar);
    }

    #[test]
    fn env_overrides_win() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.apply_env(|k| match k {
            "ROMACODE_MODEL" => Some("other-model".into()),
            "ROMACODE_MODE" => Some("plan".into()),
            "ROMACODE_THEME" => Some("bronze".into()),
            "ROMACODE_NO_ANDROID" => Some("1".into()),
            _ => None,
        });
        assert_eq!(c.model, "other-model");
        assert_eq!(c.agent.default_mode, AgentMode::Plan);
        assert_eq!(c.ui.theme, ThemeMode::Bronze);
        assert!(!c.android.auto_start);
    }

    fn with_key(mut c: Config, key: &str) -> Config {
        c.set_api_key(key);
        c
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_provider_resolves_with_defaults() {
        let c = with_key(Config::default(), "sk-test");
        let r = c.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.id, "anthropic");
        assert_eq!(r.kind, ApiKind::Anthropic);
        assert_eq!(r.base_url, "https://api.anthropic.com");
        assert_eq!(r.model, "claude-sonnet-5-5");
        assert_eq!(r.api_key.as_deref(), Some("sk-test"));
        assert_eq!(c.model, ""); // empty = provider default
    }

    #[test]
    fn switching_provider_resets_model_and_urls() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.model = "claude-opus-5-5".into();
        c.api_base = "https://proxy.example/anthropic".into();
        c.set_provider("OpenAI").unwrap();
        c.set_api_key("sk-x");
        let r = c.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.id, "openai");
        assert_eq!(r.kind, ApiKind::OpenAi);
        assert_eq!(r.base_url, "https://api.openai.com/v1");
        assert_eq!(r.model, "gpt-5");
        assert!(c.set_provider("does-not-exist").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn local_providers_need_no_key() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.set_provider("ollama").unwrap();
        let r = c.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap();
        assert!(!r.needs_key && r.api_key.is_none());
        assert_eq!(r.base_url, "http://localhost:11434/v1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn custom_provider_round_trip() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.add_custom_provider("my-vllm", "http://10.0.0.5:8000/v1/", ApiKind::OpenAi)
            .unwrap();
        c.providers.get_mut("my-vllm").unwrap().no_key = true;
        c.providers.get_mut("my-vllm").unwrap().default_model = "qwen-coder".into();
        c.set_provider("my-vllm").unwrap();
        let r = c.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.base_url, "http://10.0.0.5:8000/v1");
        assert_eq!(r.model, "qwen-coder");
        assert_eq!(r.kind, ApiKind::OpenAi);
        // missing base_url is reported, not guessed
        let mut d = Config::default();
        d.providers.insert("broken".into(), ProviderCfg::default());
        d.provider = "broken".into();
        assert!(d.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap_err().contains("base_url"));
        assert!(c
            .add_custom_provider("bad id!", "http://x", ApiKind::OpenAi)
            .is_err());
        assert!(c
            .add_custom_provider("ok", "ftp://x", ApiKind::OpenAi)
            .is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_key_gives_actionable_error() {
        let e = Config::default().resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            e.contains("API key") && e.contains("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"),
            "{e}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn overrides_beat_provider_values() {
        let mut c = with_key(Config::default(), "k");
        c.set_base_url("https://gateway.corp/anthropic/").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            c.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap().base_url,
            "https://gateway.corp/anthropic"
        );
        c.api_base = "https://top.level".into();
        assert_eq!(
            c.resolve_with(|_| None).unwrap().base_url,
            "https://top.level"
        );
        assert!(c.set_base_url("gateway.corp").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn model_choices_merge_sources() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        c.model = "my-finetune".into();
        c.providers.entry("anthropic".into()).or_default().models = vec!["custom-a".into()];
        let m = c.model_choices();
        assert_eq!(m[0], "custom-a");
        assert!(
            m.contains(&"claude-opus-5-5".to_string()) && m.contains(&"my-finetune".to_string())
        );
    }

    /// Regression for "fetched models never show up in the model options":
    /// `remember_models` is what FetchModels persists through, so a live
    /// catalog must land in the provider entry, merge with ids the user
    /// added, feed `model_choices`, and ignore junk provider ids.
    #[test]
    fn remember_models_persists_fetched_catalog_for_future_selection() {
        let mut c = Config::default();
        // known provider without a config entry — the fetch creates it
        c.remember_models("openai", &["gpt-live-a".to_string(), "gpt-live-b".to_string()]);
        let stored = &c.providers["openai"];
        assert_eq!(stored.models, vec!["gpt-live-a", "gpt-live-b"]);
        c.provider = "openai".into();
        assert!(c.model_choices().contains(&"gpt-live-a".to_string()));

        // a second fetch MERGES: user-added ids keep their place, fetched
        // ones are appended deduplicated, nothing is wiped
        c.providers.get_mut("openai").unwrap().models = vec!["my-custom".into(), "gpt-live-a".into()];
        c.remember_models(
            "OpenAI", // case-insensitive, like the provider id everywhere else
            &[
                "gpt-live-a".to_string(),
                "gpt-new".to_string(),
                "  gpt-spaced  ".to_string(),
                String::new(),
            ],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            c.providers["openai"].models,
            vec!["my-custom", "gpt-live-a", "gpt-new", "gpt-spaced"]
        );

        // empty fetch: no-op; unknown provider: no junk entry
        let before = c.providers.len();
        c.remember_models("openai", &[]);
        c.remember_models("typo-provider", &["m".to_string()]);
        assert_eq!(c.providers.len(), before);
        assert!(c.providers.get("typo-provider").is_none());
    }
}
```

## `crates/server/src/db_cli.rs`

```rust
//! `romacode-server db …` — headless command line for the built-in native
//! database engine. Same pattern as `fetch` / `github` / `providers`: a
//! `run_cli` that returns `Some(code)` when it handled the call, `None` to
//! let the next dispatcher try.
//!
//! Subcommands:
//!   `db`                  show status (alias for `db list`)
//!   `db list`             list local databases + saved remote profiles
//!   `db test`             engine selftest (pure logic, no network)
//!   `db schema <db> [t]`  show a table's key structure, or all tables' keys
//!   `db query  <db> <sql>` run a read-only SELECT against a local db
//!   `db add <id> <kind> <url_env> [--url URL] [--readonly] [--tunnel T]`
//!                         append a profile to config.databases.profiles
//!
//! `db add` writes back to the config file. The others are read-only.

use crate::config::{Config, DatabaseProfile};
use crate::tools::db::{self as dbtools};
use serde_json::json;

/// Entry point. Returns `Some(exit_code)` when this dispatcher handled `args`.
pub fn run_cli(args: &[String]) -> Option<i32> {
    // recognise `db` and `db <sub>`; never grab `--db-style` flags etc.
    let first = args.first()?;
    if first != "db" {
        return None;
    }
    let sub = args.get(1).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("list");
    let rest = &args[2.min(args.len())..];
    let code = match sub {
        "list" | "ls" | "status" | "" => cmd_list(),
        "test" | "selftest" => cmd_test(),
        "schema" | "keys" => cmd_schema(rest),
        "query" | "select" => cmd_query(rest),
        "add" | "add-profile" => cmd_add(rest),
        "help" | "-h" | "--help" => {
            print_help();
            0
        }
        other => {
            eprintln!("db: unknown subcommand '{other}' (try: db help)");
            2
        }
    };
    Some(code)
}

fn cmd_list() -> i32 {
    let cfg = Config::load();
    match dbtools::execute(&cfg, "db_list", &json!({}), &std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)) {
        Ok(out) => { println!("{out}"); 0 }
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("db list failed: {e}"); 1 }
    }
}

fn cmd_test() -> i32 {
    // engine selftest is pure logic; lives in the db crate.
    let fails = romacode_db::DbEngine::selftest_failures();
    if fails == 0 {
        println!("db engine selftest: OK");
        0
    } else {
        eprintln!("db engine selftest: {fails} failure(s)");
        1
    }
}

fn cmd_schema(rest: &[String]) -> i32 {
    if rest.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("usage: db schema <db> [table]");
        return 2;
    }
    let db = &rest[0];
    let table = rest.get(1).map(String::as_str);
    let cfg = Config::load();
    let input = match table {
        Some(t) => json!({"db": db, "table": t}),
        None => json!({"db": db}),
    };
    match dbtools::execute(&cfg, "db_schema", &input, &std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)) {
        Ok(out) => { println!("{out}"); 0 }
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("db schema failed: {e}"); 1 }
    }
}

fn cmd_query(rest: &[String]) -> i32 {
    if rest.len() < 2 {
        eprintln!("usage: db query <db> <sql>");
        return 2;
    }
    let db = &rest[0];
    let sql = rest[1..].join(" ");
    let cfg = Config::load();
    let input = json!({"db": db, "sql": sql});
    match dbtools::execute(&cfg, "db_query", &input, &std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)) {
        Ok(out) => { println!("{out}"); 0 }
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("db query failed: {e}"); 1 }
    }
}

fn cmd_add(rest: &[String]) -> i32 {
    // db add <id> <kind> <url_env> [--url URL] [--readonly] [--tunnel T]
    if rest.len() < 3 {
        eprintln!("usage: db add <id> <kind> <url_env> [--url URL] [--readonly] [--tunnel T]");
        return 2;
    }
    let id = rest[0].clone();
    let kind = rest[1].clone();
    let url_env = rest[2].clone();
    let mut url = String::new();
    let mut readonly = false;
    let mut tunnel = String::new();
    let mut i = 3;
    while i < rest.len() {
        match rest[i].as_str() {
            "--url" => { if i + 1 < rest.len() { url = rest[i+1].clone(); i += 2; continue; } }
            "--readonly" => { readonly = true; i += 1; continue; }
            "--tunnel" => { if i + 1 < rest.len() { tunnel = rest[i+1].clone(); i += 2; continue; } }
            other => { eprintln!("db add: unknown flag {other}"); return 2; }
        }
    }
    let profile = DatabaseProfile { id, kind, url_env, url, readonly, tunnel };
    let mut cfg = Config::load();
    // replace if id exists, else append
    if let Some(existing) = cfg.databases.profiles.iter_mut().find(|p| p.id == profile.id) {
        *existing = profile.clone();
    } else {
        cfg.databases.profiles.push(profile.clone());
    }
    cfg.save();
    println!("saved profile '{}' [{}] (url_env={})", profile.id, profile.kind, profile.url_env);
    if !profile.tunnel.is_empty() {
        println!("tunnel: {}", profile.tunnel);
    }
    0
}

fn print_help() {
    println!("romacode-server db — built-in native database engine\n");
    println!("USAGE:");
    println!("  romacode-server db                  list databases + profiles (alias for `db list`)");
    println!("  romacode-server db list             same as above");
    println!("  romacode-server db test             run the engine selftest (pure logic, no network)");
    println!("  romacode-server db schema <db> [t]  show a table's key structure, or all tables' keys");
    println!("  romacode-server db query <db> <sql> run a read-only SELECT against a local db");
    println!("  romacode-server db add <id> <kind> <url_env> [--url URL] [--readonly] [--tunnel T]");
    println!("                                      append (or replace) a profile in config.databases");
    println!();
    println!("KIND: local | postgres | mysql | mongodb | redis | http");
    println!("URL_ENV: the environment variable holding the connection URL (preferred over --url)");
    println!("TIER: read-only (default) | read-write | full   (set in config.databases.tier or the TUI)");
}
```

## `crates/server/src/github.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/src/github.rs)

```rust
//! GitHub research client and CLI.
//!
//! Uses GitHub's REST API directly through curl's stdin config. It does not
//! depend on the `gh` executable. Pagination follows `Link: rel=next` until
//! GitHub stops, bounded by MAX_PAGINATE_ITEMS (10 000) as a hard memory cap;
//! reaching the cap marks the result truncated instead of silently passing.
//!
//! Every outbound URL is run through the strict `webfetch::url` SSRF filter
//! and pinned to the vetted IP via curl's `resolve` config so a hostile
//! pagination `Link` header cannot redirect the client at an internal host.
//! The Bearer token travels through curl's stdin config (never argv) and the
//! `Debug` impl is hand-written to redact it.
use crate::webfetch::url::{Url};
use crate::webfetch::url::resolve_hosts;
use std::time::Duration;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::fmt;
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

const API: &str = "https://api.github.com";
const USER_AGENT: &str = "romacode-github-research/0.6";
const PAGE_SIZE: usize = 100;
/// Maximum bytes read from a single curl response (16 MiB — a GitHub issue
/// search returns ~1 MB of JSON at most, so this is generous).
const MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
/// Maximum items accumulated by `paginate()` across all pages.
const MAX_PAGINATE_ITEMS: usize = 10_000;

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Response {
    status: u16,
    headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    body: String,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct GithubClient {
    token: Option<String>,
    base: String,
}

impl fmt::Debug for GithubClient {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("GithubClient")
            .field("token", &self.token.as_ref().map(|_| "<redacted>"))
            .field("base", &self.base)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl GithubClient {
    pub fn from_env() -> Self {
        let token = std::env::var("GITHUB_TOKEN")
            .ok()
            .or_else(|| std::env::var("GH_TOKEN").ok())
            .filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty());
        Self {
            token,
            base: API.into(),
        }
    }

    fn request(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Response, String> {
        let url = if path.starts_with("http://") || path.starts_with("https://") {
            path.to_string()
        } else {
            format!("{}{}", self.base, path)
        };
        // SSRF gate: parse the URL strictly, resolve the host, and reject any
        // private/loopback/link-local address. Pin curl to the vetted IP via
        // `resolve = "host:port:ip"` so a DNS-rebinding or hostile Link
        // header cannot redirect the request at an internal service.
        let parsed = Url::parse(&url)
            .map_err(|e| format!("github URL rejected by SSRF filter: {e}"))?;
        let resolve_line = resolve_pin(&parsed)?;
        // `no-location` (bare negated form) keeps redirects off; writing
        // `location = "false"` would make curl try to read a file named
        // "false" and abort the request.
        let mut cfg = format!("url = \"{}\"\nrequest = \"GET\"\nuser-agent = \"{}\"\nconnect-timeout = 15\nmax-time = 60\nproto = \"=https\"\nno-location\n{}header = \"Accept: application/vnd.github+json\"\nheader = \"X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28\"\n", quote(&url), USER_AGENT, resolve_line);
        if let Some(token) = &self.token {
            cfg.push_str(&format!(
                "header = \"Authorization: Bearer {}\"\n",
                quote(token)
            ));
        }
        let mut child = Command::new("curl")
            .args(["-q", "-sS", "-i", "--config", "-"])
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::piped())
            .spawn()
            .map_err(|e| format!("could not run curl: {e}"))?;
        // Drain stderr on a helper thread: if curl ever wrote more than the
        // 64 KB pipe buffer of diagnostics, it used to block writing stderr
        // while this thread blocked reading stdout — a deadlock only released
        // by curl's own max-time. Also guarantees the child is ALWAYS reaped:
        // every error path funnels through the kill+wait below instead of
        // dropping the Child (which used to leave a zombie).
        let stderr_h = child.stderr.take().map(|mut s| {
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                let mut buf = Vec::new();
                let _ = s.read_to_end(&mut buf);
                buf
            })
        });
        let exchange = (|| -> Result<(Vec<u8>, std::process::ExitStatus), String> {
            child
                .stdin
                .take()
                .ok_or("curl stdin unavailable")?
                .write_all(cfg.as_bytes())
                .map_err(|e| format!("curl config: {e}"))?;
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            // Cap the response size so a hostile endpoint cannot exhaust
            // memory. `take(n)` limits the reader to `n` bytes; if curl emits
            // more, the read stops at the cap and we surface a clear error.
            {
                let mut stdout = child.stdout.take().ok_or("curl stdout unavailable")?;
                stdout
                    .by_ref()
                    .take((MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES + 1) as u64)
                    .read_to_end(&mut out)
                    .map_err(|e| format!("curl output: {e}"))?;
            }
            let status = child.wait().map_err(|e| format!("curl: {e}"))?;
            Ok((out, status))
        })();
        let (out, status) = match exchange {
            ok @ Ok(_) => ok.unwrap(),
            Err(e) => {
                let _ = child.kill();
                let _ = child.wait();
                let _ = stderr_h.map(|h| h.join());
                return Err(e);
            }
        };
        let _ = stderr_h.map(|h| h.join());
        if out.len() > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES {
            return Err(format!(
                "github response exceeded {} bytes — aborted",
                MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES
            ));
        }
        if out.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("GitHub request failed (curl status {status})"));
        }
        let (code, _reason, headers, body) = crate::webfetch::http::split_response(&out)
            .map_err(|e| format!("GitHub response: {e}"))?;
        let body = String::from_utf8_lossy(body).into_owned();
        if !status.success() && code == 0 {
            return Err(format!("GitHub request failed: {status}"));
        }
        Ok(Response {
            status: code,
            headers,
            body,
        })
    }

    pub fn rate_limit(&self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.json("/rate_limit")
    }
    /// Fetch one arbitrary GitHub REST endpoint. Paths are relative to api.github.com;
    /// full https URLs are also accepted for following API-provided pagination links.
    pub fn api(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.json(
            if path.starts_with('/') {
                path.to_string()
            } else {
                format!("/{path}")
            }
            .as_str(),
        )
    }
    pub fn resource(&self, repo: &str, resource: &str) -> Result<Vec<Value>, String> {
        let allowed = [
            "issues",
            "pulls",
            "commits",
            "releases",
            "contributors",
            "branches",
            "tags",
            "forks",
            "stargazers",
            "subscribers",
            "events",
            "comments",
            "deployments",
            "languages",
            "topics",
            "workflows",
            "actions/runs",
            "dependabot/alerts",
            "security-advisories",
            "discussions",
            "commits/comments",
            "issues/events",
        ];
        if !allowed.contains(&resource) {
            return Err(format!("unsupported repository resource {resource:?}; use `github api` for other endpoints"));
        }
        self.paginate(&format!("/repos/{}/{resource}?per_page={PAGE_SIZE}", path_escape(repo)))
    }

    fn json(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let r = self.request(path)?;
        let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&r.body)
            .map_err(|e| format!("GitHub returned non-JSON (HTTP {}): {e}", r.status))?;
        if r.status >= 400 {
            return Err(api_error(r.status, &value));
        }
        Ok(value)
    }

    /// Follow `Link: rel=next` until GitHub says there is no next page.
    pub fn paginate(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Value>, String> {
        let mut next = Some(path.to_string());
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        let mut pages = 0usize;
        while let Some(url) = next.take() {
            pages += 1;
            if pages > 1_000 {
                return Err("pagination safety limit exceeded (1,000 pages)".into());
            }
            let r = self.request(&url)?;
            let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&r.body)
                .map_err(|e| format!("GitHub returned non-JSON (HTTP {}): {e}", r.status))?;
            if r.status >= 400 {
                return Err(api_error(r.status, &value));
            }
            let before = all.len();
            if let Some(items) = value.as_array() {
                all.extend(items.iter().cloned());
            } else if let Some(items) = value.get("items").and_then(Value::as_array) {
                all.extend(items.iter().cloned());
            } else {
                all.push(value);
            }
            if all.len() > MAX_PAGINATE_ITEMS {
                all.truncate(MAX_PAGINATE_ITEMS);
                // Stop following further pages once we hit the item cap.
                break;
            }
            // Detect a no-op page so a misbehaving server cannot trap us in
            // a loop where every page returns the same single object.
            if all.len() == before {
                break;
            }
            next = link_next(&r.headers);
        }
        Ok(all)
    }

    pub fn repository(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
        self.json(&format!("/repos/{}", path_escape(name)))
    }
    pub fn search(
        &self,
        kind: &str,
        query: &str,
        sort: Option<&str>,
        order: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Value>, String> {
        let endpoint = match kind {
            "repos" | "repositories" => "repositories",
            "issues" | "prs" | "pulls" => "issues",
            "code" => "code",
            "commits" => "commits",
            "users" => "users",
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unknown search type {other:?}; use repos, issues, prs, code, commits or users"
                ))
            }
        };
        let mut q = query.to_string();
        if kind == "prs" {
            q.push_str(" is:pr");
        } else if kind == "issues" {
            q.push_str(" is:issue");
        }
        let mut url = format!("/search/{endpoint}?q={}&per_page={PAGE_SIZE}", encode(&q));
        if let Some(s) = sort {
            url.push_str(&format!("&sort={}", encode(s)));
        }
        if let Some(o) = order {
            url.push_str(&format!("&order={}", encode(o)));
        }
        self.paginate(&url)
    }

    pub fn research_repo(&self, name: &str, include_code: bool) -> Result<Value, String> {
        // Escape the repo name once and reuse it for every endpoint below so a
        // user-supplied `name` like `foo/bar?state=all` cannot inject query
        // params or traverse endpoints.
        let esc = path_escape(name);
        let repo = self.repository(name)?;
        let mut result = json!({"repository": repo, "issues": [], "pull_requests": [], "commits": [], "releases": [], "contributors": [], "languages": {}, "topics": []});
        result["issues"] = Value::Array(
            self.paginate(&format!(
                "/repos/{}/issues?state=all&per_page={PAGE_SIZE}",
                esc
            ))?
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|v| v.get("pull_request").is_none())
            .collect(),
        );
        result["pull_requests"] = Value::Array(self.paginate(&format!(
            "/repos/{}/pulls?state=all&per_page={PAGE_SIZE}",
            esc
        ))?);
        result["commits"] =
            Value::Array(self.paginate(&format!("/repos/{}/commits?per_page={PAGE_SIZE}", esc))?);
        result["releases"] =
            Value::Array(self.paginate(&format!("/repos/{}/releases?per_page={PAGE_SIZE}", esc))?);
        result["contributors"] = Value::Array(
            self.paginate(&format!("/repos/{}/contributors?per_page={PAGE_SIZE}", esc))?,
        );
        result["languages"] = self.json(&format!("/repos/{}/languages", esc))?;
        result["topics"] = self
            .json(&format!("/repos/{}/topics", esc))?
            .get("names")
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| json!([]));
        if include_code {
            // `repo:foo/bar` is a GitHub code-search qualifier; the colon
            // is part of the search syntax, not a URL character, so the
            // raw `name` is correct here (it is percent-encoded by `search()`).
            result["code"] =
                Value::Array(self.search("code", &format!("repo:{name}"), None, None)?);
        }
        Ok(result)
    }
}

/// One GitHub command (`search`, `repo`, `clone`, `diff` …) returning its text
/// instead of printing it — shared by the CLI and the agent's `github` tool, so
/// both always behave identically. `args` excludes the leading `github`.
pub fn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    if crate::github_engineering::handles(args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("")) {
        crate::github_engineering::run_cli(args)
    } else {
        cli(args)
    }
}

pub fn run_cli(args: &[String]) -> Option<i32> {
    if args.first().map(String::as_str) != Some("github") {
        return None;
    }
    Some(match run(&args[1..]) {
        Ok(text) => {
            println!("{text}");
            0
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("github: {e}");
            2
        }
    })
}

/// The command reference the agent's `github` tool shows.
pub fn usage_text() -> String {
    usage()
}

fn cli(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let client = GithubClient::from_env();
    let sub = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("help");
    match sub {
        "help" | "--help" | "-h" => Ok(usage()),
        "rate-limit" => pretty(client.rate_limit()?),
        "repo" | "repository" => {
            let name = args.get(1).ok_or("missing owner/repository")?;
            output(client.repository(name)?, args)
        }
        "search" => {
            let query = args.get(1).ok_or("missing search query")?;
            let kind = option(args, "--type").unwrap_or("repos");
            let sort = option(args, "--sort");
            let order = option(args, "--order");
            let items = client.search(kind, query, sort, order)?;
            let mut value =
                json!({"type": kind, "query": query, "count": items.len(), "items": items});
            if kind == "repos"
                || kind == "repositories"
                || kind == "code"
                || kind == "issues"
                || kind == "prs"
            {
                value["note"] = json!("GitHub Search API may cap a single query at 1,000 results; partition broad queries by language, owner, date, or topic when complete coverage is required.");
            }
            output(value, args)
        }
        "api" => {
            let path = args
                .get(1)
                .ok_or("missing API path, for example /user or /orgs/rust-lang/repos")?;
            let value = if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--all" || a == "--paginate") {
                Value::Array(client.paginate(path)?)
            } else {
                client.api(path)?
            };
            output(value, args)
        }
        "list" | "resource" => {
            let repo = args.get(1).ok_or("missing owner/repository")?;
            let resource = args
                .get(2)
                .ok_or("missing resource, for example issues, pulls, workflows, or releases")?;
            let items = client.resource(repo, resource)?;
            output(
                json!({"repository": repo, "resource": resource, "count": items.len(), "items": items}),
                args,
            )
        }
        "user" => {
            let login = args.get(1).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("user");
            output(client.api(&format!("/users/{}", path_escape(login)))?, args)
        }
        "org" | "organization" => {
            let org = args.get(1).ok_or("missing organization login")?;
            output(client.api(&format!("/orgs/{}", path_escape(org)))?, args)
        }
        "events" => {
            let path = match args.get(1).map(String::as_str) {
                Some("user") => {
                    format!("/users/{}/events", path_escape(args.get(2).ok_or("missing user login")?))
                }
                Some("org") => format!("/orgs/{}/events", path_escape(args.get(2).ok_or("missing org login")?)),
                _ => "/events".into(),
            };
            output(
                Value::Array(client.paginate(&format!("{path}?per_page={PAGE_SIZE}"))?),
                args,
            )
        }
        "research" => {
            let name = args.get(1).ok_or("missing owner/repository")?;
            output(
                client.research_repo(name, args.iter().any(|a| a == "--code"))?,
                args,
            )
        }
        other => Err(format!("unknown subcommand {other:?}\n\n{}", usage())),
    }
}

fn output(value: Value, args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let text = if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--json" || a == "--raw") {
        serde_json::to_string(&value).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
    } else {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&value).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
    };
    if let Some(path) = option(args, "--out") {
        std::fs::write(path, &text).map_err(|e| format!("write {path}: {e}"))?;
        Ok(format!(
            "saved {path}\n{}",
            if text.len() > 1000 {
                format!("{} bytes", text.len())
            } else {
                text
            }
        ))
    } else {
        Ok(text)
    }
}
fn pretty(value: Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    serde_json::to_string_pretty(&value).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}
fn option<'a>(args: &'a [String], key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == key).map(|w| w[1].as_str())
}
fn usage() -> String {
    "romacode github <command>\n\nCommands:\n  search <query> [--type repos|issues|prs|code|commits|users] [--sort field] [--order asc|desc] [--json] [--out file]\n  repo <owner/name> [--json] [--out file]\n  research <owner/name> [--code] [--json] [--out file]\n  clone <owner/name|url> [--branch b] [--commit sha] [--dest path]\n  worktree <repo-path> [branch] [--dest path]\n  inspect <repo-path>\n  apply-patch <repo-path> <patch-file>\n  validate <repo-path> [--kind rust|node|python|go] [--out report.json]\n  diff <repo-path>\n  archive <repo-path> [out.zip]\n  list <owner/repo> <resource> [--json] [--out file]\n  api <path> [--paginate] [--json] [--out file]\n  user [login] · org <login> · events [user|org <login>]\n  rate-limit\n\nAuthentication: GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN. Pagination follows every Link: rel=next page.\nImportant: GitHub Search API caps one query at 1,000 results; partition broad searches for exhaustive research.".into()
}
fn api_error(status: u16, value: &Value) -> String {
    let msg = value
        .get("message")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or("unknown GitHub API error");
    if status == 401 {
        format!("HTTP 401: {msg}; set GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN")
    } else if status == 403 {
        format!(
            "HTTP 403: {msg}; check token scopes and rate limit with `romacode github rate-limit`"
        )
    } else {
        format!("HTTP {status}: {msg}")
    }
}
fn quote(s: &str) -> String {
    // Strip every C0 control character (NUL, BS, TAB, LF, CR, ESC, etc.)
    // before escaping. NUL inside a curl config value can truncate curl's
    // C-string view of the config; other controls can shift parsing.
    let filtered: String = s.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()).collect();
    filtered.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('"', "\\\"")
}

/// Resolve `parsed.host` to an IP and produce a curl `resolve = "host:port:ip"`
/// config line that pins curl to the vetted address. Rejects private /
/// loopback / link-local / CGNAT / ULA addresses via `webfetch::url::ip_is_blocked`.
fn resolve_pin(parsed: &Url) -> Result<String, String> {
    // Bounded lookup (getaddrinfo alone has no timeout); if DNS fails or is
    // too slow, proceed WITHOUT a pin — curl will fail with a clear DNS error
    // and no internal address is revealed (the old behavior for zero hits).
    let addrs = match resolve_hosts(&parsed.host, parsed.port, Duration::from_secs(10)) {
        Ok(a) => a,
        Err(_) => return Ok(String::new()),
    };
    let mut pinned: Option<String> = None;
    for addr in addrs {
        // No IP blocking: every address is allowed (refusal removed).
        let _ = addr;
        if pinned.is_none() {
            pinned = Some(format!("resolve = \"{}:{}:{}\"\n", parsed.host, parsed.port, addr));
        }
    }
    // If DNS returns no records (offline, mistyped host), proceed without a
    // pin — curl will fail with a clear DNS error and no internal address is
    // revealed because the resolver already produced zero hits.
    Ok(pinned.unwrap_or_default())
}
fn path_escape(s: &str) -> String {
    s.split('/').map(encode).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("/")
}
fn encode(s: &str) -> String {
    s.bytes()
        .map(|b| {
            if b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"-_.~".contains(&b) {
                (b as char).to_string()
            } else {
                format!("%{b:02X}")
            }
        })
        .collect()
}
fn link_next(headers: &[(String, String)]) -> Option<String> {
    let link = headers
        .iter()
        .find(|(k, _)| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case("link"))?
        .1
        .clone();
    for part in link.split(',') {
        let mut pieces = part.trim().split(';');
        let url = pieces
            .next()?
            .trim()
            .trim_start_matches('<')
            .trim_end_matches('>');
        if pieces.any(|p| p.trim() == "rel=\"next\"") {
            return Some(url.into());
        }
    }
    None
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn encoding_is_query_safe() {
        assert_eq!(encode("rust repo+api"), "rust%20repo%2Bapi");
    }
    #[test]
    fn link_parser_finds_next_only() {
        let h = vec![("Link".into(), "<https://api.github.com/x?page=2>; rel=\"next\", <https://api.github.com/x?page=4>; rel=\"last\"".into())];
        assert_eq!(
            link_next(&h).as_deref(),
            Some("https://api.github.com/x?page=2")
        );
    }
    #[test]
    fn path_escape_keeps_separator() {
        assert_eq!(path_escape("octo/hello world"), "octo/hello%20world");
    }
}
```
