```rust
//! Local repository engineering primitives used by the GitHub framework.
//! The module deliberately works through Git and project-native build tools,
//! while keeping orchestration, manifests, and reports in Rust.
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

fn run(program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut c = Command::new(program);
    c.args(args);
    if let Some(dir) = cwd {
        c.current_dir(dir);
    }
    let out = c
        .output()
        .map_err(|e| format!("could not run {program}: {e}"))?;
    if !out.status.success() {
        return Err(format!(
            "{program} failed ({}): {}",
            out.status,
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim()
        ));
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned())
}
fn stamp() -> u64 {
    SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

pub fn clone_repo(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let remote = args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository URL or owner/name")?;
    // Scheme allow-list: only https:// is accepted verbatim. The owner/name
    // shorthand is rewritten to https://github.com/<owner>/<name>.git. Any
    // other scheme (file://, ssh://, git@, http://) is rejected — `file://`
    // can read local paths and `ssh://`/`git@` can probe or exfiltrate from
    // internal hosts.
    let source = if remote.starts_with("https://") {
        remote.to_string()
    } else if remote.contains("://") || remote.starts_with("git@") {
        return Err(format!(
            "refusing remote {remote:?}: only https:// URLs and the owner/name shorthand are accepted"
        ));
    } else {
        // owner/name shorthand — validate the characters so a value like
        // `../etc/passwd` cannot traverse.
        if !remote
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '/' | '-' | '_' | '.' | '~'))
        {
            return Err(format!(
                "refusing owner/name shorthand {remote:?}: contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9/_.~-]"
            ));
        }
        format!("https://github.com/{remote}.git")
    };
    let dest = option(args, "--dest")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            PathBuf::from(
                remote
                    .rsplit('/')
                    .next()
                    .unwrap_or("repository")
                    .trim_end_matches(".git"),
            )
        });
    // Sandbox --dest: must be a relative path inside the current working
    // directory. Rejects absolute paths and `..` traversal.
    let cwd = std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cwd: {e}"))?;
    let dest_abs = cwd.join(&dest);
    let canonical_parent = dest_abs
        .parent()
        .and_then(|p| std::fs::canonicalize(p).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("--dest parent directory does not exist: {}", dest.display()))?;
    if !canonical_parent.starts_with(&cwd) {
        return Err(format!(
            "--dest {} escapes the current working directory — refusing",
            dest.display()
        ));
    }
    // Validate option values: --depth must be a positive integer; --branch
    // and --commit must not start with `-` (argument-injection guard).
    let mut git: Vec<String> = vec!["clone".into()];
    if let Some(depth) = option(args, "--depth") {
        if !depth.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) || depth.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("--depth must be a positive integer, got {depth:?}"));
        }
        git.push("--depth".to_string());
        git.push(depth.to_string());
    }
    if let Some(branch) = option(args, "--branch") {
        validate_git_value(&branch, "--branch")?;
        git.push("--branch".to_string());
        git.push(branch.to_string());
    }
    git.push(source.clone());
    git.push(dest.display().to_string());
    run("git", &git, None)?;
    if let Some(revision) = option(args, "--commit") {
        validate_git_value(&revision, "--commit")?;
        run(
            "git",
            &["checkout".to_string(), revision.to_string()],
            Some(&dest),
        )?;
    }
    let manifest = manifest(&dest, &source)?;
    write_manifest(&dest, &manifest)?;
    Ok(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&manifest).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)
}

/// Reject values that begin with `-` (git argument-injection guard) or
/// contain path separators where git would not expect them. Git branch and
/// commit names accept a wide character set, but a leading `-` makes git
/// treat the value as an option, which is the classic injection class.
fn validate_git_value(value: &str, flag: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if value.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("{flag} value must not be empty"));
    }
    if value.starts_with('-') {
        return Err(format!(
            "{flag} value {value:?} starts with '-' — refusing (argument-injection guard)"
        ));
    }
    if value.contains('\0') || value.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) {
        return Err(format!(
            "{flag} value {value:?} contains a NUL or control character"
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn worktree(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let repo = PathBuf::from(args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository path")?);
    let branch = args
        .get(2)
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("romacode/task-{}", stamp()));
    validate_git_value(&branch, "worktree branch")?;
    let dest = option(args, "--dest")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            repo.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).join(format!(
                "{}-worktree",
                repo.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("repo")
            ))
        });
    run(
        "git",
        &[
            "worktree".into(),
            "add".into(),
            "-b".into(),
            branch.clone(),
            dest.display().to_string(),
        ],
        Some(&repo),
    )?;
    let m = manifest(
        &dest,
        &run(
            "git",
            &["remote".into(), "get-url".into(), "origin".into()],
            Some(&repo),
        )
        .unwrap_or_default(),
    )?;
    write_manifest(&dest, &m)?;
    Ok(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&m).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)
}

pub fn inspect(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let dir = PathBuf::from(args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository path")?);
    let source = run("git", &["status".into(), "--short".into()], Some(&dir)).unwrap_or_default();
    let commit: String = run("git", &["rev-parse".into(), "HEAD".into()], Some(&dir))
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .trim()
        .into();
    let branch: String = run(
        "git",
        &["branch".into(), "--show-current".into()],
        Some(&dir),
    )
    .unwrap_or_default()
    .trim()
    .into();
    let remote: String = run(
        "git",
        &["remote".into(), "get-url".into(), "origin".into()],
        Some(&dir),
    )
    .unwrap_or_default()
    .trim()
    .into();
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_files(&dir, &dir, &mut files, 0);
    let kind = detect_kind(&dir, &files);
    let tests = files
        .iter()
        .filter(|f| f.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("test") || f.contains("spec"))
        .count();
    let result = json!({"path": dir, "remote": remote, "branch": branch, "commit": commit, "kind": kind, "file_count": files.len(), "test_file_count": tests, "dirty": !source.trim().is_empty(), "status": source.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>(), "files": files});
    serde_json::to_string_pretty(&result).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

pub fn apply_patch(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let dir = PathBuf::from(args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository path")?);
    let patch = PathBuf::from(args.get(2).ok_or("missing patch file")?);
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&patch).map_err(|e| format!("read patch: {e}"))?;
    if text.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err("patch is empty".into());
    }
    let out = Command::new("git")
        .args([
            "apply",
            "--check",
            patch.to_str().ok_or("invalid patch path")?,
        ])
        .current_dir(&dir)
        .output()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    if !out.status.success() {
        return Err(format!(
            "patch check failed: {}",
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim()
        ));
    }
    run(
        "git",
        &["apply".into(), patch.display().to_string()],
        Some(&dir),
    )?;
    Ok(json!({"applied": true, "repository": dir, "patch_bytes": text.len(), "status": run("git", &["status".into(), "--short".into()], Some(&dir)).unwrap_or_default()}).to_string())
}

pub fn validate(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let dir = PathBuf::from(args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository path")?);
    let kind = option(args, "--kind")
        .map(str::to_string)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| detect_kind(&dir, &Vec::new()));
    let commands: Vec<Vec<String>> = match kind.as_str() {
        "rust" => vec![
            vec!["cargo".into(), "fmt".into(), "--check".into()],
            vec!["cargo".into(), "check".into(), "--all-targets".into()],
            vec!["cargo".into(), "test".into(), "--workspace".into()],
        ],
        "node" => vec![vec!["npm".into(), "test".into()]],
        "python" => vec![vec!["python3".into(), "-m".into(), "pytest".into()]],
        "go" => vec![vec!["go".into(), "test".into(), "./...".into()]],
        _ => vec![vec!["git".into(), "diff".into(), "--check".into()]],
    };
    let mut checks = Vec::new();
    let mut passed = true;
    for command in commands {
        let program = command[0].clone();
        let args2 = command[1..].to_vec();
        match run(&program, &args2, Some(&dir)) {
            Ok(out) => {
                checks.push(json!({"command": command.join(" "), "passed": true, "output": out}))
            }
            Err(e) => {
                passed = false;
                checks.push(json!({"command": command.join(" "), "passed": false, "error": e}));
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    let report = json!({"repository": dir, "kind": kind, "passed": passed, "checks": checks, "generated_at": stamp()});
    let out = option(args, "--out").unwrap_or("romacode-validation.json");
    std::fs::write(out, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report).unwrap())
        .map_err(|e| format!("write report: {e}"))?;
    Ok(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report).unwrap())
}

pub fn diff(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let dir = PathBuf::from(args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository path")?);
    run("git", &["diff".into(), "--stat".into()], Some(&dir)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}
pub fn archive(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let dir = PathBuf::from(args.get(1).ok_or("missing repository path")?);
    let out = args.get(2).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| {
        format!(
            "{}-romacode.zip",
            dir.file_name()
                .and_then(|x| x.to_str())
                .unwrap_or("repository")
        )
    });
    run(
        "git",
        &[
            "archive".into(),
            "--format=zip".into(),
            "-o".into(),
            out.clone(),
            "HEAD".into(),
        ],
        Some(&dir),
    )?;
    Ok(json!({"archive": out, "repository": dir}).to_string())
}

fn manifest(dir: &Path, remote: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    Ok(
        json!({"repository": dir, "remote": remote.trim(), "branch": run("git", &["branch".into(), "--show-current".into()], Some(dir)).unwrap_or_default().trim(), "commit": run("git", &["rev-parse".into(), "HEAD".into()], Some(dir)).unwrap_or_default().trim(), "created_at": stamp(), "dirty": !run("git", &["status".into(), "--short".into()], Some(dir)).unwrap_or_default().trim().is_empty()}),
    )
}
fn write_manifest(dir: &Path, value: &Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    std::fs::write(
        dir.join(".romacode-manifest.json"),
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(value).unwrap(),
    )
    .map_err(|e| format!("write manifest: {e}"))
}
fn collect_files(root: &Path, dir: &Path, files: &mut Vec<String>, depth: usize) {
    if depth > 8 {
        return;
    }
    if let Ok(read) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
        for item in read.flatten() {
            let p = item.path();
            let name = item.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
            if name == ".git" || name == "target" || name == "node_modules" {
                continue;
            }
            if p.is_dir() {
                collect_files(root, &p, files, depth + 1);
            } else if p.is_file() {
                if let Ok(r) = p.strip_prefix(root) {
                    files.push(r.display().to_string());
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
fn detect_kind(dir: &Path, files: &[String]) -> String {
    if dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() || files.iter().any(|f| f == "Cargo.toml") {
        "rust"
    } else if dir.join("package.json").exists() {
        "node"
    } else if dir.join("pyproject.toml").exists() || dir.join("setup.py").exists() {
        "python"
    } else if dir.join("go.mod").exists() {
        "go"
    } else if dir.join("pom.xml").exists() || dir.join("build.gradle").exists() {
        "java"
    } else {
        "unknown"
    }
    .into()
}
fn option<'a>(args: &'a [String], key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    args.windows(2).find(|w| w[0] == key).map(|w| w[1].as_str())
}
pub fn handles(s: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(
        s,
        "clone"
            | "download"
            | "worktree"
            | "inspect"
            | "apply-patch"
            | "validate"
            | "diff"
            | "archive"
    )
}
pub fn run_cli(args: &[String]) -> Result<String, String> {
    match args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("") {
        "clone" | "download" => clone_repo(args),
        "worktree" => worktree(args),
        "inspect" => inspect(args),
        "apply-patch" => apply_patch(args),
        "validate" => validate(args),
        "diff" => diff(args),
        "archive" => archive(args),
        _ => Err("unknown engineering command".into()),
    }
}
```

[view on disk](crates/server/src/langchain_bridge.rs)

```rust
//! LangChain-native integration — the vendored `langchain-rust` crate wired
//! into the brain as a first-class engine.
//!
//! Three pieces live here:
//!
//! 1. **Engine** — `run_langchain` drives langchain's `AgentExecutor` (the
//!    plan → tools → answer loop) with a `ChatOpenAI` model built from the
//!    resolved provider. Every tool the executor sees is a *romacode tool*:
//!    the executor calls them through the same [`Security`] gate the native
//!    engine uses, so approvals, Plan mode and deny rules behave identically.
//!    A callback bridge streams tool activity and per-step text to clients.
//!
//! 2. **Memory** — the session transcript is preloaded into langchain's
//!    `ConversationBufferMemory`, and `WindowBufferMemory` is available for
//!    long sessions (`agent.engine = "langchain"`, `memory.window` in a
//!    future config rev; buffer is the default, matching the native loop).
//!
//! 3. **RAG** — `rag_index` / `rag_search` tools back onto langchain's
//!    `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`, `OpenAIEmbeddings` and
//!    `InMemoryVectorStore`. Indexing reads files directly from disk (the
//!    permission policy ships fully open — nothing gates file reads).

use crate::agent::{system_prompt_for_mode, Emit};
use crate::config::{Config, Resolved};
use crate::security::{Decision, Security};
use crate::session::Mode;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use langchain_rust::agents::tools::{tool_fn, Tool};
use langchain_rust::agents::AgentExecutor;
use langchain_rust::callbacks::CallbackHandler;
use langchain_rust::errors::LangchainError;
use langchain_rust::llms::openai::ChatOpenAI;
use langchain_rust::memory::{ConversationBufferMemory, Memory};
use langchain_rust::messages::{Message as LcMessage, ToolSpec};
use langchain_rust::text_splitter::{Document as LcDocument, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter};
use langchain_rust::vectorstores::InMemoryVectorStore;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::sync::{
    atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering},
    Arc, Mutex, OnceLock,
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. The engine.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Callback bridge: langchain executor events → wire events on the bus.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct BridgeHandler {
    emit: Emit,
    last_tool_id: Arc<Mutex<String>>,
    counter: Arc<AtomicU64>,
}

impl BridgeHandler {
    fn new(emit: Emit) -> Self {
        Self {
            emit,
            last_tool_id: Arc::new(Mutex::new(String::new())),
            counter: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(1)),
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl CallbackHandler for BridgeHandler {
    async fn on_llm_start(&self, _model: &str, _messages: &[LcMessage]) {}

    async fn on_llm_end(&self, _model: &str, output: &str) {
        // Each model step's text lands as one delta; clients append it to the
        // current assistant block exactly like a native-engine stream chunk.
        if !output.trim().is_empty() {
            self.emit.text(output);
        }
    }

    async fn on_tool_start(&self, tool: &str, args: &serde_json::Value) {
        let id = format!("lc-{}", self.counter.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed));
        if let Ok(mut g) = self.last_tool_id.lock() {
            *g = id.clone();
        }
        self.emit.tool_start(&id, tool, args);
    }

    async fn on_tool_end(&self, _tool: &str, result: &str) {
        let id = self
            .last_tool_id
            .lock()
            .map(|mut g| std::mem::take(&mut *g))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let extra = result
            .lines()
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("")
            .chars()
            .take(80)
            .collect::<String>();
        self.emit
            .tool_end(&id, true, if extra.is_empty() { None } else { Some(extra) });
    }

    async fn on_agent_step(&self, iteration: usize) {
        if iteration > 1 {
            self.emit.notice(format!("langchain agent step {iteration}"));
        }
    }

    async fn on_agent_finish(&self, _output: &str) {}
}

/// Build the langchain `ChatOpenAI` from the resolved provider.
fn build_model(cfg: &Config, r: &Resolved) -> Result<Arc<ChatOpenAI>, String> {
    let mut b = ChatOpenAI::builder()
        .model(&r.model)
        .base_url(&r.base_url);
    // `0 = no request timeout` (the documented default). The old
    // `.max(1)` turned the shipped default into a ONE-SECOND total
    // timeout on every model call, so the langchain engine could not
    // complete a single turn. `timeout_secs` bounds non-streaming calls
    // only; SSE streams are unbounded either way.
    if cfg.network.request_timeout_secs > 0 {
        b = b.timeout_secs(cfg.network.request_timeout_secs as u64);
    }
    if let Some(k) = &r.api_key {
        b = b.api_key(k);
    }
    // Profile-driven sampling: the model's official rules (modeldata) bound
    // temperature the same way the native loop clamps it — an Anthropic-wire
    // model must never receive 2.0, a reasoning model never any temperature.
    let profile = romacode_shared::modeldata::profile_for(&r.id, &r.model);
    if let Some(t) = cfg.model_params.temperature {
        let clamped = match profile.params.temperature {
            Some(spec) if !spec.supported => None,
            Some(spec) if spec.max >= spec.min && spec.max > 0.0 => {
                Some(t.clamp(spec.min, spec.max))
            }
            _ => Some(t.clamp(0.0, 2.0)),
        };
        if let Some(t) = clamped {
            b = b.temperature(t as f64);
        }
    }
    let max_out = if profile.max_output_tokens > 0 {
        cfg.max_tokens.min(profile.max_output_tokens)
    } else {
        cfg.max_tokens
    };
    b = b.max_tokens(max_out.min(u32::MAX as u32) as u32);
    let m = b.build().map_err(|e| format!("langchain model: {e}"))?;
    Ok(Arc::new(m))
}

/// Every romacode tool as a langchain `Tool`: schema from the registry,
/// executor = security gate → tools::execute. The gate decides Deny/Ask/Run
/// exactly like the native loop, so approvals and Plan mode are identical.
fn romacode_tools(
    cfg: &Config,
    mode: Mode,
    emit: Emit,
    security: Arc<Security>,
    android: Option<&crate::android::AndroidAgent>,
    cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
) -> Vec<Tool> {
    let android = android.cloned();
    crate::tools::definitions(cfg, false)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|def| {
            let name = def["name"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            let description = def["description"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            let parameters = def
                .get("input_schema")
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({"type": "object"}));
            let spec = ToolSpec {
                name: name.clone(),
                description,
                parameters,
            };
            let emit = emit.clone();
            let security = security.clone();
            let cfg = cfg.clone();
            let cancel = cancel.clone();
            let android = android.clone();
            let m = mode;
            tool_fn(
                name.clone(),
                spec.description.clone(),
                spec.parameters.clone(),
                move |args| {
                    let emit = emit.clone();
                    let security = security.clone();
                    let cfg = cfg.clone();
                    let cancel = cancel.clone();
                    let android = android.clone();
                    let name = name.clone();
                    let mode = m;
                    async move {
                        // THE gate — identical semantics to the native engine.
                        let fail =
                            |msg: String| LangchainError::ToolExecution(name.clone(), msg);
                        match security.authorize(&cfg, mode, &name, &args) {
                            Decision::Deny(reason) => Err(fail(reason)),
                            Decision::Run => {
                                crate::tools::execute(&cfg, &name, &args, android.as_ref(), &cancel)
                                    .map_err(fail)
                            }
                            Decision::Ask { request_id, effect } => {
                                // Same contract as the native loop: register
                                // first (so an instant Allow can never race the
                                // registry), then broadcast the real
                                // ApprovalRequest event for the screens.
                                let rx = security.register(&request_id);
                                emit.approval_request(&request_id, &name, &effect);
                                let mut answered: Option<bool> = None;
                                loop {
                                    if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                                        break;
                                    }
                                    match rx.recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100)) {
                                        Ok(v) => {
                                            answered = Some(v);
                                            break;
                                        }
                                        Err(std::sync::mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => continue,
                                        Err(_) => break,
                                    }
                                }
                                match answered {
                                    Some(true) => crate::tools::execute(
                                        &cfg,
                                        &name,
                                        &args,
                                        android.as_ref(),
                                        &cancel,
                                    )
                                    .map_err(fail),
                                    Some(false) => {
                                        Err(fail("denied by user; action not run".into()))
                                    }
                                    None => Err(fail(
                                        "cancelled while awaiting approval; action not run".into(),
                                    )),
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                },
            )
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Run the whole turn on the langchain engine. Returns Ok(final_answer) or a
/// provider/engine error (both are already streamed to clients; the error is
/// additionally reported in chat by the caller).
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub fn run_langchain(
    cfg: &Config,
    r: &Resolved,
    history: &[(&'static str, String)],
    mode: Mode,
    emit: &Emit,
    security: &Arc<Security>,
    android: Option<&crate::android::AndroidAgent>,
    cancel: &Arc<AtomicBool>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let model = build_model(cfg, r)?;

    // Transcript → langchain memory (preloaded so multi-turn context works
    // exactly like the native engine's plain-text history). The final user
    // entry is this turn's input and is passed to `invoke` instead, so it is
    // not duplicated.
    let input = history
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|(role, _)| *role == "user")
        .map(|(_, t)| t.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut preload_len = history.len();
    if let Some(pos) = history
        .iter()
        .rposition(|(role, _)| *role == "user")
    {
        if history[pos].1 == input {
            preload_len = pos;
        }
    }
    let mut memory = ConversationBufferMemory::new();
    for (role, text) in &history[..preload_len] {
        match *role {
            "assistant" => memory.push(LcMessage::ai(text.clone())),
            // Tool summaries ride along as human turns — the same compromise
            // the native loop makes for providers without native tool roles.
            _ => memory.push(LcMessage::human(text.clone())),
        }
    }
    let memory: Box<dyn Memory> = Box::new(memory);

    let tools = romacode_tools(
        cfg,
        mode,
        emit.clone(),
        security.clone(),
        android,
        cancel.clone(),
    );
    let mut executor = AgentExecutor::builder(model)
        .tools(tools)
        .memory(memory)
        .system_prompt(system_prompt_for_mode(cfg, mode))
        .max_iterations(cfg.agent.max_tool_rounds as usize)
        .callbacks(langchain_rust::callbacks::CallbackManager::new().add(Arc::new(
            BridgeHandler::new(emit.clone()),
        )))
        .build();

    // The user message for this turn was already pushed by the api layer
    // into `history`; the executor needs just the new input.
    let input = history
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|(role, _)| *role == "user")
        .map(|(_, t)| t.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default();

    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
        .enable_all()
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| format!("langchain runtime: {e}"))?;

    let answer = rt.block_on(async {
        if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return Err(LangchainError::Other("cancelled".into()));
        }
        executor.invoke(&input).await
    });

    match answer {
        Ok(_text) => {
            // The final answer (and each step's text) already reached clients
            // through the callback bridge; usage comes from the model when
            // the provider reports it (native engine path).
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => Err(format!("langchain engine: {e}")),
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. RAG — index + search over project files.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct RagState {
    store: InMemoryVectorStore,
    embedder: Arc<dyn langchain_rust::embeddings::Embeddings>,
    label: String,
}

static RAG: OnceLock<Mutex<Option<RagState>>> = OnceLock::new();

fn rag_slot() -> &'static Mutex<Option<RagState>> {
    RAG.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(None))
}

fn embedder_from(cfg: &Config) -> Result<(Arc<dyn langchain_rust::embeddings::Embeddings>, String), String> {
    let r = cfg.resolve()?;
    let model = std::env::var("ROMACODE_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL")
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "text-embedding-3-small".to_string());
    let mut b = langchain_rust::embeddings::openai::OpenAIEmbeddings::builder()
        .model(model.clone())
        .base_url(&r.base_url);
    // 0 = none (same contract as the native engine); never clamp to 1s.
    if cfg.network.request_timeout_secs > 0 {
        b = b.timeout_secs(cfg.network.request_timeout_secs as u64);
    }
    if let Some(k) = &r.api_key {
        b = b.api_key(k);
    }
    let e = b.build().map_err(|err| format!("embeddings: {err}"))?;
    Ok((Arc::new(e), format!("{} @ {}", model, r.name)))
}

/// Walk `root` for files matching a `**`/`*` glob (project-relative, `/`
/// separators). Skips VCS/build dirs, respects the file cap and per-file size.
fn walk_glob(root: &std::path::Path, pattern: &str, max_files: usize) -> Vec<std::path::PathBuf> {
    use crate::security::glob;
    fn rec(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        rel: &str,
        pattern: &str,
        out: &mut Vec<std::path::PathBuf>,
        budget: usize,
    ) {
        if out.len() >= budget {
            return;
        }
        let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
            return;
        };
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            if out.len() >= budget {
                return;
            }
            let Ok(ft) = entry.file_type() else { continue };
            let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            if ft.is_dir() {
                if matches!(name.as_str(), ".git" | "target" | "node_modules" | ".hg" | ".svn" | "__pycache__") {
                    continue;
                }
                let child_rel = if rel.is_empty() { name.clone() } else { format!("{rel}/{name}") };
                rec(&entry.path(), &child_rel, pattern, out, budget);
            } else if ft.is_file() {
                let child_rel = if rel.is_empty() { name.clone() } else { format!("{rel}/{name}") };
                if glob(pattern, &child_rel, true) {
                    out.push(entry.path());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    rec(root, "", pattern, &mut out, max_files.max(1));
    out.sort();
    out
}

const RAG_CHUNK_CHARS: usize = 1200;
const RAG_MAX_FILE_BYTES: u64 = 512 * 1024;

/// Dispatch a RAG tool call. Files are read directly from disk (the
/// permission policy ships fully open — nothing gates file reads).
pub fn rag_execute(cfg: &Config, name: &str, input: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    match name {
        "rag_index" => rag_index(cfg, input),
        "rag_search" => rag_search(input),
        other => Err(format!("unknown rag tool {other}")),
    }
}

fn rag_index(cfg: &Config, input: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    let pattern = input["glob"]
        .as_str()
        .filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty())
        .ok_or("missing string glob")?;
    let max_files = input["max_files"].as_u64().unwrap_or(200).min(2_000) as usize;
    let root = crate::security::root()?;

    let files = walk_glob(&root, pattern, max_files);
    if files.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("no files match '{pattern}' under {}", root.display()));
    }

    let (embedder, label) = embedder_from(cfg)?;
    let splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter::new(RAG_CHUNK_CHARS, 150);
    let store = InMemoryVectorStore::new();

    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
        .enable_all()
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| format!("langchain runtime: {e}"))?;

    let mut indexed_files = 0usize;
    let mut chunks = 0usize;
    let mut skipped = 0usize;
    for path in &files {
        let rel = path
            .strip_prefix(&root)
            .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| path.display().to_string());
        // Binary-ish guard: skip files containing a NUL in the first 8 KiB.
        let meta = match std::fs::metadata(path) {
            Ok(m) if m.len() <= RAG_MAX_FILE_BYTES => m,
            _ => {
                skipped += 1;
                continue;
            }
        };
        let _ = meta;
        let bytes = match std::fs::read(path) {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(_) => {
                skipped += 1;
                continue;
            }
        };
        if bytes.iter().take(8192).any(|&b| b == 0) {
            skipped += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let text = match String::from_utf8(bytes) {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(_) => {
                skipped += 1;
                continue;
            }
        };
        let pieces = splitter.split(&text);
        if pieces.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let docs: Vec<LcDocument> = pieces
            .into_iter()
            .map(|c| LcDocument::with_source(c, rel.clone()))
            .collect();
        let added = rt
            .block_on(store.add_documents(&docs, embedder.as_ref()))
            .map_err(|e| format!("embed {rel}: {e}"))?;
        chunks += added;
        indexed_files += 1;
    }
    if indexed_files == 0 {
        return Err("nothing indexable matched (all skipped as binary/oversized/unreadable)".into());
    }

    *rag_slot()
        .lock()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(RagState {
        store,
        embedder,
        label: label.clone(),
    });

    Ok(format!(
        "Indexed {chunks} chunks from {indexed_files} files (skipped {skipped}) with {label}. Use rag_search to query."
    ))
}

fn rag_search(input: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    let query = input["query"]
        .as_str()
        .filter(|s| !s.trim().is_empty())
        .ok_or("missing string query")?;
    let k = input["k"].as_u64().unwrap_or(6).clamp(1, 20) as usize;

    let state = rag_slot().lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
    let Some(st) = state.as_ref() else {
        return Err("the vector store is empty — call rag_index first".into());
    };

    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
        .enable_all()
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| format!("langchain runtime: {e}"))?;
    let vector = rt
        .block_on(async { st.embedder.embed_query(query).await })
        .map_err(|e| format!("embed query: {e}"))?;
    let hits = st
        .store
        .similarity_search_by_vector(&vector, k)
        .map_err(|e| format!("search: {e}"))?;
    if hits.is_empty() {
        return Ok("No matches. Index something with rag_index first.".into());
    }
    let mut out = String::from("Semantic matches (score = cosine similarity):\n");
    for (i, (doc, score)) in hits.iter().enumerate() {
        let src = doc
            .metadata
            .get("source")
            .map(String::as_str)
            .unwrap_or("(unknown)");
        let snippet: String = doc.page_content.chars().take(600).collect();
        out.push_str(&format!("\n{}. [{score:.3}] {src}\n{snippet}\n", i + 1));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Current store size, for the welcome payload / status lines.
pub fn rag_stats() -> Option<(usize, String)> {
    let state = rag_slot().lock().ok()?;
    let st = state.as_ref()?;
    Some((st.store.len().ok()?, st.label.clone()))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::AgentMode;

    #[test]
    fn walk_glob_matches_relative_patterns() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("romacode-rag-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src/deep")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("src/a.rs"), "fn a() {}").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("src/deep/b.rs"), "fn b() {}").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("README.md"), "# x").unwrap();
        let hits = walk_glob(&dir, "src/**/*.rs", 100);
        assert_eq!(hits.len(), 2, "{hits:?}");
        let hits = walk_glob(&dir, "*.md", 100);
        assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1, "{hits:?}");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rag_search_without_index_is_a_clean_error() {
        let e = rag_search(&json!({"query": "hello"}));
        assert!(e.is_err() && e.unwrap_err().contains("rag_index"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn tool_bridge_shapes_openai_specs() {
        let mut cfg = Config::default();
        cfg.agent.default_mode = AgentMode::Build;
        // definitions(cfg, false) must produce OpenAI function fragments.
        let defs = crate::tools::definitions(&cfg, false);
        let read = defs.iter().find(|d| d["function"]["name"] == "Read").unwrap();
        assert!(read["function"]["parameters"].is_object());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! `romacode-server` — the brain. Starts the HTTP/WS server that owns the
//! agent loop (native + langchain engines), sessions, security gate, tools
//! and engines. The TUI (`romacode` binary in crates/client-tui) is just a
//! screen that connects to it.
//!
//! CLI utilities that belong to the brain also live here (they operate on
//! config/providers/webfetch/adb rather than pixels):
//! `--print-config`, `--config-path`, `--verify-android`, `fetch`, `providers`,
//! `github`, `models`, `serve` (default).

use anyhow::Result;
use romacode_server::config::Config;

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let first = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("serve");

    // headless agent-server (the default: `romacode-server` alone serves)
    if let Some(code) = romacode_server::webfetch::run_cli(&args) {
        std::process::exit(code);
    }
    if let Some(code) = romacode_server::providers_cli::run_cli(&args) {
        std::process::exit(code);
    }
    if let Some(code) = romacode_server::github::run_cli(&args) {
        std::process::exit(code);
    }
    if let Some(code) = romacode_server::db_cli::run_cli(&args) {
        std::process::exit(code);
    }
    if let Some(code) = romacode_server::tunnel_cli::run_cli(&args) {
        std::process::exit(code);
    }
    if let Some(code) = romacode_server::cli_tools::run_cli(&args) {
        std::process::exit(code);
    }
    match first {
        "--verify-android" => return verify_android(),
        "--print-config" => {
            let (cfg, warnings) = Config::load_report();
            for w in &warnings {
                eprintln!("warning: {w}");
            }
            println!("{}", cfg.to_pretty_json());
            return Ok(());
        }
        "--config-path" => {
            println!(
                "{}",
                Config::path()
                    .map(|p| p.display().to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_default()
            );
            return Ok(());
        }
        "--version" | "-V" => {
            println!("romacode-server {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
            return Ok(());
        }
        "--help" | "-h" => {
            print_help();
            return Ok(());
        }
        "serve" => {
            let mut bind = "127.0.0.1:7712".to_string();
            let mut it = args.iter().skip(1);
            while let Some(a) = it.next() {
                match a.as_str() {
                    "--bind" | "-b" => {
                        if let Some(v) = it.next() {
                            bind = v.clone();
                        }
                    }
                    "--cwd" => {
                        if let Some(v) = it.next() {
                            std::env::set_current_dir(v)
                                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("--cwd {v}: {e}"))?;
                        }
                    }
                    other => anyhow::bail!("unknown option {other} (try --help)"),
                }
            }
            let (cfg, warnings) = Config::load_report();
            for w in &warnings {
                eprintln!("warning: {w}");
            }
            // First run: drop the starter persona template at the default
            // path so the standing-instructions channel works out of the box.
            romacode_server::persona::ensure_starter(&cfg);
            eprintln!("project directory: {}", std::env::current_dir().map(|p| p.display().to_string()).unwrap_or_default());
            // Initialise the built-in native database engine against the
            // configured (or default) home dir before serving. Failures here
            // are non-fatal: the db tools fall back to an ephemeral home.
            let db_home = if cfg.databases.home.is_empty() {
                dirs::home_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::PathBuf::from("."))
                    .join(".romacode").join("db")
            } else {
                std::path::PathBuf::from(&cfg.databases.home)
            };
            if let Err(e) = romacode_server::tools::db::init(db_home) {
                eprintln!("warning: db engine init failed (db tools will use an ephemeral home): {e}");
            }
            return romacode_server::api::serve(cfg, &bind);
        }
        other => {
            anyhow::bail!("unknown command {other} (try --help)");
        }
    }
}

fn print_help() {
    println!(
        "romacode-server {}\n\nUSAGE:\n  romacode-server serve [--bind 127.0.0.1:7712] [--cwd /path/to/project]\n      start the brain: agent loop (native + langchain engines), sessions,\n      security gate, tools and engines over HTTP + WebSocket.\n\nUTILITY COMMANDS\n  fetch <url> [--mode text|markdown|raw|json|links|scrape|headers] [--selector css]\n  providers · models · provider [id] · model [name]\n  github <search|repo|resource|api> … · git <clone|status|diff|log|branches>\n  db list · db test · db schema <db> [t] · db query <db> <sql> · db add <id> <kind> <url_env>\n  tunnel server|client|forward  open a chisel tunnel so the agent can reach remote DBs\n  tools [list|describe <n>|search <w>|run <n> '<json>'] [--json]   everything the agent can call\n  doctor [--json]      health check: config, provider, key, engine, tools, git/adb, state dir\n\nDIAGNOSTICS\n  --verify-android     run non-destructive checks against the selected real Android target\n  --print-config       show the effective settings (after env overrides)\n  --config-path        print the config file location\n  --version · --help\n\nCONFIG  {}\nAPI KEY  export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... (or OPENAI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, …)\nENGINE   agent.engine = native | langchain   (langchain = built-in LangChain in Rust:\n         agent executor, memory and RAG tools; OpenAI-compatible providers)",
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        Config::path()
            .map(|p| p.display().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    );
}

/// Non-destructive checks against the selected real Android target.
fn verify_android() -> Result<()> {
    let mut cfg = Config::load();
    // Running this explicit diagnostic is an intentional connection request.
    cfg.android.auto_start = true;
    println!("ROMACODE ANDROID — real ADB target checks");
    println!("  connecting through Android Platform-Tools; no simulator fallback");
    let mut android =
        romacode_server::android::Android::spawn(romacode_server::android::Android::config_from(&cfg));
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(30);
    loop {
        android.poll();
        match android.status().map(|s| s.phase) {
            Some(romacode_server::android::Phase::Online) => break,
            Some(romacode_server::android::Phase::Error(error)) => {
                anyhow::bail!("real Android target unavailable: {error}")
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
            anyhow::bail!("timed out waiting for the selected authorized Android target");
        }
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
    let (pass, fail, log) = romacode_server::android::verify(&mut android);
    for line in log {
        println!("  {line}");
    }
    println!("\nRESULT: {pass} passed, {fail} failed");
    if fail > 0 {
        anyhow::bail!("real Android target verification failed");
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
//! User-owned persona instructions, loaded into the system prompt.
//!
//! The persona file is the user's standing-instructions channel: a plain
//! markdown file (default `~/.config/romacode/persona.md`) whose content is
//! appended to the agent's system prompt on every turn. It hot-reloads —
//! edit the file and the next message already speaks with the new voice,
//! no restart, no config reload.
//!
//! Design rules:
//! - The file is entirely user-owned. RomaCode only ever WRITES it once,
//!   when it does not exist (the starter template). Edits are preserved.
//! - Loading is best-effort: a missing, empty or unreadable file silently
//!   contributes nothing, so a broken persona can never break the loop.
//! - Reads are capped (`PERSONA_MAX_BYTES`); oversized files are truncated
//!   with an explicit note instead of silently eating the context window.
//! - `agent.persona_file` in config.json switches the path; the spellings
//!   `""`, `off`, `none`, `disabled`, `false`, `0` switch the feature off.

use crate::config::Config;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// Persona file read cap. Anything larger is truncated with a note.
pub const PERSONA_MAX_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;

/// File name used when [`Config`]'s `agent.persona_file` is unset.
pub const PERSONA_FILE_NAME: &str = "persona.md";

/// Config spellings that switch persona loading off.
const OFF_SPELLINGS: [&str; 6] = ["", "off", "none", "disabled", "false", "0"];

/// The file written on first run, when the default persona file is missing.
/// Deliberately short: tone and priorities only. The base prompt keeps
/// owning tool behavior; anything the user writes here speaks as standing
/// instructions to their own model.
const STARTER_TEMPLATE: &str = r#"<!--
RomaCode persona file — standing instructions appended to the system prompt.

- Hot-reloaded: edit it and the NEXT message already uses the new text.
- This default file lives at ~/.config/romacode/persona.md.
- Point it at another file or switch it off with agent.persona_file in
  ~/.config/romacode/config.json ("off" disables; a path switches files).
- Keep it short: a few sharp lines beat a wall of text. The base prompt
  (tools, engine behavior) stays in effect; this file tunes style and
  priorities only.
-->

# Persona

Answer directly and to the point: lead with the answer or the diff, explain
only what earns its place. No filler, no hedging, no restating the request.

Terminal-first output: fenced code blocks with the file path or language in
the info string, one shell command per line, real paths instead of
placeholders.

When a request is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable interpretation, state
the assumption in one line, and keep moving. Stop and ask only when a wrong
guess would waste real work.

Prefer concrete artifacts over descriptions of artifacts: write the file,
run the command, show the diff.
"#;

/// Default persona path: `<config_dir>/romacode/persona.md`
/// (e.g. `~/.config/romacode/persona.md` on Linux).
pub fn default_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    dirs::config_dir().map(|d| d.join("romacode").join(PERSONA_FILE_NAME))
}

/// Expand a leading `~/` (or bare `~`) against `home`. `~user/...` is left
/// untouched — resolving other users' homes is not RomaCode's business.
fn expand_tilde(home: &Path, p: &str) -> PathBuf {
    if p == "~" {
        return home.to_path_buf();
    }
    if let Some(rest) = p.strip_prefix("~/") {
        return home.join(rest);
    }
    PathBuf::from(p)
}

/// Resolve the effective persona path from the config.
///
/// - `None` (key absent / null): the default path — feature on.
/// - an `OFF_SPELLINGS` value: `None` — feature off.
/// - anything else: that path, `~/` expanded, trimmed.
pub fn resolve(cfg: &Config) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    match cfg.agent.persona_file.as_deref().map(str::trim) {
        None => default_path(),
        Some(s) if OFF_SPELLINGS.contains(&s) => None,
        Some(s) => match dirs::home_dir() {
            Some(home) => Some(expand_tilde(&home, s)),
            None => Some(PathBuf::from(s)),
        },
    }
}

/// Read the persona file and return its content, trimmed, ready to append
/// to the system prompt. `None` = no persona this turn (missing file,
/// disabled, empty content, unreadable). Oversized files are truncated at
/// [`PERSONA_MAX_BYTES`] with an explicit note — never a silent cut.
pub fn load(cfg: &Config) -> Option<String> {
    let path = resolve(cfg)?;
    let meta = std::fs::metadata(&path).ok()?;
    if !meta.is_file() {
        return None;
    }
    let (text, truncated) = if meta.len() as usize > PERSONA_MAX_BYTES {
        let raw = std::fs::read(&path).ok()?;
        // The file can shrink between metadata and read; min() keeps the
        // slice in bounds even in that race.
        let end = raw.len().min(PERSONA_MAX_BYTES);
        (String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[..end]).into_owned(), true)
    } else {
        let raw = std::fs::read(&path).ok()?;
        (String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw).into_owned(), false)
    };
    // Strip a UTF-8 BOM if the file was saved by a Windows editor.
    let text = text.strip_prefix('\u{feff}').unwrap_or(&text);
    let text = text.trim();
    if text.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if truncated {
        Some(format!(
            "{text}\n\n[persona file truncated at {PERSONA_MAX_BYTES} bytes]"
        ))
    } else {
        Some(text.to_string())
    }
}

/// Write the starter template to `path` if nothing is there yet. Returns
/// whether it created the file. Never overwrites: if the user already has
/// a persona there (even an empty one), it stays untouched.
fn write_starter_if_missing(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<bool> {
    if path.exists() {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    }
    std::fs::write(path, STARTER_TEMPLATE)?;
    Ok(true)
}

/// First-run convenience, called from the `serve` startup path: if the
/// persona feature points at the DEFAULT path and that file is missing,
/// drop the starter template there so the mechanism is usable immediately.
/// Custom paths are respected, never created or overwritten.
pub fn ensure_starter(cfg: &Config) {
    let on_default = cfg.agent.persona_file.is_none();
    if !on_default {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(path) = resolve(cfg) {
        match write_starter_if_missing(&path) {
            Ok(true) => eprintln!("persona file created: {} (edit it; hot-reloads every turn)", path.display()),
            Ok(false) => {}
            Err(e) => eprintln!("warning: could not create persona file {}: {e}", path.display()),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Write;

    fn cfg_with_persona(value: Option<&str>) -> Config {
        let mut cfg = Config::default();
        cfg.agent.persona_file = value.map(str::to_string);
        cfg
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_default_uses_config_dir() {
        let p = resolve(&cfg_with_persona(None)).expect("default persona path");
        assert!(p.ends_with("romacode/persona.md"), "got {}", p.display());
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_off_spellings_disable() {
        for s in OFF_SPELLINGS {
            assert!(resolve(&cfg_with_persona(Some(s))).is_none(), "'{s}' must disable");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn resolve_custom_path_and_whitespace() {
        let cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(" /tmp/pers.md "));
        assert_eq!(resolve(&cfg).unwrap(), PathBuf::from("/tmp/pers.md"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn expand_tilde_forms() {
        let home = Path::new("/home/u");
        assert_eq!(expand_tilde(home, "~/a.md"), PathBuf::from("/home/u/a.md"));
        assert_eq!(expand_tilde(home, "~"), PathBuf::from("/home/u"));
        assert_eq!(expand_tilde(home, "/abs/x"), PathBuf::from("/abs/x"));
        // ~user stays literal: no passwd lookups.
        assert_eq!(expand_tilde(home, "~other/x"), PathBuf::from("~other/x"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn load_appends_trimmed_content() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = dir.path().join("persona.md");
        std::fs::write(&p, "\n\nfirst line\nsecond line\n\n").unwrap();
        let cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(p.to_str().unwrap()));
        assert_eq!(load(&cfg).unwrap(), "first line\nsecond line");
    }

    #[test]
    fn load_missing_or_empty_is_none() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(dir.path().join("nope.md").to_str().unwrap()));
        assert!(load(&cfg).is_none());

        let empty = dir.path().join("empty.md");
        std::fs::write(&empty, "   \n\t\n").unwrap();
        let cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(empty.to_str().unwrap()));
        assert!(load(&cfg).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn load_truncates_oversized_files_with_a_note() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = dir.path().join("big.md");
        let mut f = std::fs::File::create(&p).unwrap();
        let chunk = "x".repeat(4096);
        for _ in 0..(PERSONA_MAX_BYTES / 4096 + 8) {
            f.write_all(chunk.as_bytes()).unwrap();
        }
        drop(f);
        let cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(p.to_str().unwrap()));
        let loaded = load(&cfg).unwrap();
        assert!(loaded.contains("[persona file truncated at"), "note missing");
        // Truncated body + note, never the whole 100+ KiB file.
        assert!(loaded.len() < PERSONA_MAX_BYTES + 128);
    }

    #[test]
    fn load_hot_reloads_between_turns() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = dir.path().join("persona.md");
        std::fs::write(&p, "v1 persona").unwrap();
        let cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(p.to_str().unwrap()));
        assert_eq!(load(&cfg).unwrap(), "v1 persona");
        std::fs::write(&p, "v2 persona, sharper").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(load(&cfg).unwrap(), "v2 persona, sharper");
    }

    #[test]
    fn starter_is_created_once_and_never_clobbers() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = dir.path().join("romacode").join("persona.md");
        assert!(write_starter_if_missing(&p).unwrap(), "first run creates");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(&p).unwrap(), STARTER_TEMPLATE);
        assert!(!write_starter_if_missing(&p).unwrap(), "second run is a no-op");
        // User edits survive: the file is never rewritten.
        std::fs::write(&p, "my own persona").unwrap();
        assert!(!write_starter_if_missing(&p).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(&p).unwrap(), "my own persona");
    }

    #[test]
    fn starter_uses_bom_free_utf8() {
        assert!(!STARTER_TEMPLATE.starts_with('\u{feff}'));
        assert!(STARTER_TEMPLATE.contains("# Persona"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn system_prompt_picks_up_the_persona_and_its_off_switch() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = dir.path().join("persona.md");
        std::fs::write(&p, "speak tersely, ship diffs").unwrap();

        let mut cfg = cfg_with_persona(Some(p.to_str().unwrap()));
        let with = crate::agent::system_prompt(&cfg);
        assert!(with.contains("speak tersely, ship diffs"), "persona missing from prompt");

        cfg.agent.persona_file = Some("off".into());
        let without = crate::agent::system_prompt(&cfg);
        assert!(!without.contains("speak tersely"), "off must remove the persona");
    }
}
```

## `crates/server/src/provider_engine.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/src/provider_engine.rs)

```rust
//! Provider engine — the bridge between RomaCode's existing config/agent-loop
//! types and the new OpenCode-structured `romacode-providers` crate.
//!
//! This module is the load-bearing change for long-task resilience. It
//! replaces the old 4-retry no-jitter loop in `agent.rs::run_provider` with
//! the OpenCode retry policy (10 retries, exponential 2s→10s with jitter,
//! Retry-After header honoring, separate 1-hour budget for unreachable hosts,
//! 3-retry cap for timeouts). The policy is implemented in
//! `romacode_providers::client::RetryPolicy`; this module feeds it the
//! failures from the existing curl-backed transport and decides whether to
//! retry or give up — and crucially, it NEVER returns `Err` on a transient
//! failure until the full budget is exhausted.
//!
//! ## What this replaces
//!
//! Before: `agent.rs:343` ran a `loop { request_anthropic|request_openai;
//! if attempt > 4 || !transient { return Err(e) } }` — 4 retries, no jitter,
//! no Retry-After, and `return Err(e)` killed the turn.
//!
//! After: this module runs the same `request_anthropic|request_openai` calls
//! (curl-backed, unchanged transport) but wraps them in
//! [`retry_with_policy`], which uses `romacode_providers::RetryPolicy` to
//! classify each failure and decide retry/give-up per OpenCode's schedule.
//!
//! ## Catalog
//!
//! The provider/model catalog is now dynamic: `catalog()` returns the cached
//! [`romacode_providers::Catalog`] (network-fetched with a 5-minute TTL,
//! bundled fallback). The TUI settings panel and `providers_cli` read this
//! instead of the old static `KNOWN` slice.

use crate::config::{ApiKind, Config, Resolved};
use romacode_providers::{
    adapter_for, catalog, AuthScheme, FailureClass, OpenAiCompatible, ProviderAdapter,
    Protocol, RetryDecision, RetryPolicy,
};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// A retry callback the agent loop uses to emit a `RetryScheduled`-style
/// notice to the UI (mirrors OpenCode's `SessionEvent.RetryScheduled`).
pub type RetryNotifier = Box<dyn FnMut(&RetryDecision)>;

/// Run one provider call through the OpenCode retry policy.
///
/// `do_call` is the closure that performs the actual HTTP request (curl-backed
/// in the current transport). It returns `Ok(())` on success or `Err(msg)` on
/// failure; this function classifies the failure and retries per the policy,
/// calling `on_retry` for each scheduled retry.
///
/// Returns `Ok(())` if the call eventually succeeded, or `Err` with the final
/// failure reason if the budget was exhausted.
pub fn retry_with_policy<F>(
    cfg: &Config,
    cancel: &Arc<AtomicBool>,
    mut do_call: F,
    mut on_retry: impl FnMut(&RetryDecision),
) -> Result<(), String>
where
    F: FnMut() -> Result<(), String>,
{
    let allow_retry = cfg.network.max_retries > 0;
    let mut policy = RetryPolicy::new(allow_retry);
    loop {
        if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return Err("cancelled".into());
        }
        match do_call() {
            Ok(()) => return Ok(()),
            Err(e) => {
                let class = classify(&e);
                let decision = policy.decide(class, None);
                if !decision.retry {
                    return Err(format!("{} ({})", e, decision.reason));
                }
                on_retry(&decision);
                sleep_or_cancel(decision.delay, cancel);
                if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                    return Err("cancelled during retry backoff".into());
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Classify a RomaCode provider error string into the new `FailureClass`.
/// Delegates to `romacode_providers::FailureClass::from_response` so the
/// classification rules stay in one place.
pub fn classify(err: &str) -> FailureClass {
    FailureClass::from_response(0, "", err)
}

/// Sleep, but poll the cancel flag every 100ms so an interrupt is responsive.
fn sleep_or_cancel(d: Duration, cancel: &Arc<AtomicBool>) {
    if d.is_zero() { return; }
    let mut waited = Duration::ZERO;
    let step = Duration::from_millis(100);
    while waited < d {
        if cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) { return; }
        let remaining = d - waited;
        let s = step.min(remaining);
        std::thread::sleep(s);
        waited += s;
    }
}

/// Resolve the adapter for a RomaCode `Resolved` provider. Returns a boxed
/// `ProviderAdapter` (built-in for known ids, `OpenAiCompatible` for custom
/// base URLs).
///
/// BUG FIXED: `adapter_for` only hand-implements 16 providers. Every other
/// provider the bundled catalog knows about — ~300 entries in
/// `catalog_snapshot.rs`, including `nvidia`, `azure`, `vercel`,
/// `huggingface`, `cohere` — used to fall through to a bare
/// `OpenAiCompatible` with an EMPTY base URL whenever `r.base_url` wasn't
/// separately populated, and a guessed `<ID>_API_KEY` env var that may not
/// match the provider's real convention. A request built from that adapter
/// would hit `"/chat/completions"` with no host at all. This now consults
/// `romacode_providers::catalog::bundled_meta`, which already carries the
/// correct base URL, key env var, and wire protocol for every bundled
/// provider, before falling back further.
pub fn adapter_for_resolved(r: &Resolved) -> Box<dyn ProviderAdapter> {
    if let Some(a) = adapter_for(&r.id) {
        return a;
    }
    let meta = romacode_providers::catalog::bundled_meta(&r.id);
    let env_var = if !r.key_env.is_empty() {
        r.key_env.clone()
    } else if let Some(m) = &meta {
        if !m.key_env.is_empty() {
            m.key_env.to_string()
        } else {
            format!("{}_API_KEY", r.id.to_uppercase().replace('-', "_"))
        }
    } else {
        format!("{}_API_KEY", r.id.to_uppercase().replace('-', "_"))
    };
    let base_url = if !r.base_url.is_empty() {
        r.base_url.clone()
    } else if let Some(m) = &meta {
        m.base_url.to_string()
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    if meta.as_ref().map(|m| m.anthropic).unwrap_or(false) {
        return Box::new(AnthropicCompatible {
            id: r.id.clone(),
            name: r.name.clone(),
            base_url,
            env_var,
        });
    }
    Box::new(OpenAiCompatible {
        id: r.id.clone(),
        name: r.name.clone(),
        base_url,
        env_var,
    })
}

/// A generic Anthropic-Messages-compatible adapter for catalog-known
/// providers that speak the Anthropic wire protocol but have no hand-written
/// adapter (mirrors `OpenAiCompatible`, just for the other protocol family).
pub struct AnthropicCompatible {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub base_url: String,
    pub env_var: String,
}
impl ProviderAdapter for AnthropicCompatible {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.id }
    fn name(&self) -> &str { &self.name }
    fn default_base_url(&self) -> &str { &self.base_url }
    fn auth(&self) -> AuthScheme {
        AuthScheme::ApiKey { header: "x-api-key".into(), env_var: self.env_var.clone() }
    }
    fn protocol(&self) -> Protocol { Protocol::AnthropicMessages }
    fn build_request(
        &self,
        base_url: &str,
        api_key: Option<&str>,
        messages: &[Value],
        max_tokens: u32,
        model: &str,
        extra_headers: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
        stream: bool,
    ) -> romacode_providers::ResolvedRequest {
        let mut r = self.default_build_request(base_url, api_key, messages, max_tokens, model, extra_headers, stream);
        r.headers.insert("anthropic-version".into(), "2023-06-01".into());
        r
    }
}

/// Map a RomaCode `ApiKind` to the new `Protocol`. Used so the agent loop's
/// existing `r.kind` dispatch still works while the transport is curl-backed.
pub fn protocol_for_kind(kind: ApiKind) -> Protocol {
    match kind {
        ApiKind::Anthropic => Protocol::AnthropicMessages,
        ApiKind::OpenAi => Protocol::OpenAiChat,
    }
}

/// The active provider + model catalog (cached, TTL-refreshed). Reads through
/// to `romacode_providers::catalog::cached()`.
pub fn catalog() -> romacode_providers::Catalog {
    catalog::cached()
}

/// Force a catalog refresh (after a credential is added).
pub fn refresh_catalog() -> romacode_providers::Catalog {
    catalog::refresh()
}

/// Resolve the effective model id for a config + resolved provider, checking
/// the new dynamic catalog first and falling back to the resolved model.
pub fn effective_model(cfg: &Config, r: &Resolved) -> String {
    let sel_model = if r.model.is_empty() { cfg.model.clone() } else { r.model.clone() };
    if !sel_model.is_empty() {
        return sel_model;
    }
    // Fall back to the catalog's first model for this provider.
    let c = catalog();
    if let Some(p) = c.provider(&r.id) {
        if let Some((mid, _)) = p.models.iter().next() {
            return mid.as_str().to_string();
        }
    }
    String::new()
}

/// Build the headers for a provider request from `Resolved` + config.
/// Mirrors what `request_anthropic`/`request_openai` build inline today.
pub fn request_headers(r: &Resolved) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    let mut h = BTreeMap::new();
    let adapter = adapter_for_resolved(r);
    match adapter.auth() {
        AuthScheme::ApiKey { header, .. } => {
            if let Some(k) = &r.api_key { h.insert(header, k.clone()); }
        }
        AuthScheme::Bearer { .. } => {
            if let Some(k) = &r.api_key { h.insert("Authorization".into(), format!("Bearer {k}")); }
        }
        AuthScheme::None => {}
    }
    if r.kind == ApiKind::Anthropic {
        h.insert("anthropic-version".into(), "2023-06-01".into());
    }
    for (k, v) in &r.headers { h.insert(k.clone(), v.clone()); }
    h
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::Config;

    #[test]
    fn classify_transient() {
        assert_eq!(classify("http 502 bad gateway"), FailureClass::Transient);
        assert_eq!(classify("rate limit exceeded"), FailureClass::Transient);
        assert_eq!(classify("temporarily overloaded"), FailureClass::Transient);
    }

    #[test]
    fn classify_permanent() {
        assert_eq!(classify("401 unauthorized"), FailureClass::Permanent);
        assert_eq!(classify("unknown model"), FailureClass::Permanent);
    }

    #[test]
    fn classify_unreachable() {
        assert_eq!(classify("Name or service not known"), FailureClass::Unreachable);
        assert_eq!(classify("ENOTFOUND api.x.com"), FailureClass::Unreachable);
    }

    #[test]
    fn classify_timeout() {
        assert_eq!(classify("operation timed out"), FailureClass::Timeout);
    }

    #[test]
    fn retry_policy_runs_ten_times_then_gives_up() {
        let cfg = Config::default();
        let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let mut attempts = 0u32;
        let result = retry_with_policy(&cfg, &cancel, || {
            attempts += 1;
            Err("http 502 bad gateway".into())
        }, |_| {});
        assert!(result.is_err());
        // 1 initial + 10 retries = 11 calls total
        assert_eq!(attempts, 11);
    }

    #[test]
    fn retry_succeeds_on_third_attempt() {
        let cfg = Config::default();
        let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let mut attempts = 0u32;
        let result = retry_with_policy(&cfg, &cancel, || {
            attempts += 1;
            if attempts < 3 { Err("http 503".into()) } else { Ok(()) }
        }, |_| {});
        assert!(result.is_ok(), "expected Ok, got Err: {:?}", result.err());
        assert_eq!(attempts, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn retry_does_not_retry_permanent() {
        let cfg = Config::default();
        let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let mut attempts = 0u32;
        let result = retry_with_policy(&cfg, &cancel, || {
            attempts += 1;
            Err("401 unauthorized".into())
        }, |_| {});
        assert!(result.is_err());
        assert_eq!(attempts, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn retry_respects_cancel() {
        let cfg = Config::default();
        let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let result = retry_with_policy(&cfg, &cancel, || {
            cancel.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            Err("http 502".into())
        }, |_| {});
        assert!(result.is_err());
        assert!(result.unwrap_err().contains("cancel"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn retry_disabled_when_max_retries_zero() {
        let mut cfg = Config::default();
        cfg.network.max_retries = 0;
        let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let mut attempts = 0u32;
        let _ = retry_with_policy(&cfg, &cancel, || {
            attempts += 1;
            Err("http 502".into())
        }, |_| {});
        assert_eq!(attempts, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn protocol_for_kind_maps() {
        assert_eq!(protocol_for_kind(ApiKind::Anthropic), Protocol::AnthropicMessages);
        assert_eq!(protocol_for_kind(ApiKind::OpenAi), Protocol::OpenAiChat);
    }

    #[test]
    fn catalog_returns_providers() {
        let c = catalog();
        assert!(c.provider_ids().len() >= 10);
    }

    /// Regression test: a catalog-known provider with no hand-written
    /// adapter (nvidia) must resolve to its real base URL and key env var,
    /// not an empty-base-URL guess.
    #[test]
    fn adapter_for_resolved_falls_back_to_bundled_meta_for_nvidia() {
        let r = Resolved {
            id: "nvidia".into(),
            name: "NVIDIA".into(),
            kind: ApiKind::OpenAi,
            base_url: "".into(),
            api_key: Some("test-key".into()),
            key_env: "".into(),
            needs_key: true,
            model: "".into(),
            headers: BTreeMap::new(),
            stream_usage: false,
            tools: true,
        };
        let a = adapter_for_resolved(&r);
        assert!(!a.default_base_url().is_empty(), "nvidia must not resolve to an empty base URL");
        assert!(a.default_base_url().contains("nvidia"), "got {:?}", a.default_base_url());
    }

    #[test]
    fn adapter_for_resolved_respects_explicit_config_override() {
        let r = Resolved {
            id: "nvidia".into(),
            name: "NVIDIA".into(),
            kind: ApiKind::OpenAi,
            base_url: "https://my-gateway.internal/v1".into(),
            api_key: Some("test-key".into()),
            key_env: "MY_NVIDIA_KEY".into(),
            needs_key: true,
            model: "".into(),
            headers: BTreeMap::new(),
            stream_usage: false,
            tools: true,
        };
        let a = adapter_for_resolved(&r);
        assert_eq!(a.default_base_url(), "https://my-gateway.internal/v1");
    }
}
```
