```rust
//! Server-owned sessions: the transcript, the running turn, token counters —
//! and the plain-text `history()` the model sees. The data types themselves
//! live in `romacode-shared` (the wire contract); this module owns the live
//! instances and applies the same event stream that clients receive, so a
//! reconnecting screen can resync from `snapshot()` at any time.

use romacode_shared::events::Event;
use romacode_shared::protocol::{
    Block, FileChange, McpServer, Msg, SessionSnapshot, SessionSummary, Todo, ToolStatus,
};
/// The wire `Mode` is the session `Mode` — one type, both worlds.
pub use romacode_shared::protocol::Mode;
use std::sync::{
    atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
    Arc, Mutex,
};
use std::time::Instant;

/// One in-flight agent turn.
pub struct Run {
    pub cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    pub started: Instant,
    pub model: String,
    /// Steering messages (ctrl+s) the agent has not read yet. The agent loop
    /// drains this between model rounds; anything left when the turn ends is
    /// replayed as a follow-up turn by the hub.
    pub steer: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
}

impl Run {
    pub fn interrupted(&self) -> bool {
        self.cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
}

pub struct Session {
    pub id: usize,
    pub title: String,
    pub titled: bool,
    pub messages: Vec<Msg>,
    pub mode: Mode,
    pub run: Option<Run>,
    pub tokens_in: u64,
    pub tokens_out: u64,
    pub turns: u32,
    pub todos: Vec<Todo>,
    pub mcp: Vec<McpServer>,
    pub files: Vec<FileChange>,
    pub lsp: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl Session {
    pub fn new(id: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            title: format!("Session {id}"),
            titled: false,
            messages: Vec::new(),
            mode: Mode::Build,
            run: None,
            tokens_in: 0,
            tokens_out: 0,
            turns: 0,
            todos: Vec::new(),
            mcp: Vec::new(),
            files: Vec::new(),
            lsp: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Rebuild a live session from a persisted snapshot. A run is never
    /// restored as "running": the process that owned the cancel flag is gone.
    pub fn from_snapshot(s: &SessionSnapshot) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: s.id,
            title: s.title.clone(),
            titled: !s.title.starts_with("Session "),
            messages: s.messages.clone(),
            mode: s.mode,
            run: None,
            tokens_in: s.tokens_in,
            tokens_out: s.tokens_out,
            turns: s.turns,
            todos: s.todos.clone(),
            mcp: s.mcp.clone(),
            files: s.files.clone(),
            lsp: s.lsp.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_running(&self) -> bool {
        self.run.is_some()
    }

    pub fn tokens_total(&self) -> u64 {
        self.tokens_in + self.tokens_out
    }

    pub fn summary(&self) -> SessionSummary {
        SessionSummary {
            id: self.id,
            title: self.title.clone(),
            mode: self.mode,
            running: self.is_running(),
        }
    }

    /// Full serialisable state for a (re)connecting client. `pending_approvals`
    /// is filled in by the api layer (`Hub::snapshot`), which owns the live
    /// approval registry.
    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> SessionSnapshot {
        SessionSnapshot {
            id: self.id,
            title: self.title.clone(),
            messages: self.messages.clone(),
            mode: self.mode,
            running: self.is_running(),
            tokens_in: self.tokens_in,
            tokens_out: self.tokens_out,
            turns: self.turns,
            todos: self.todos.clone(),
            mcp: self.mcp.clone(),
            files: self.files.clone(),
            lsp: self.lsp.clone(),
            pending_approvals: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn auto_title(&mut self, text: &str) {
        if self.titled {
            return;
        }
        let t: String = text.lines().next().unwrap_or("").chars().take(30).collect();
        if !t.trim().is_empty() {
            self.title = t.trim().to_string();
            self.titled = true;
        }
    }

    pub fn push_user(&mut self, text: String) {
        self.auto_title(&text);
        self.messages.push(Msg::User { text });
    }

    pub fn begin_assistant(&mut self, model: &str) {
        let mode = self.mode;
        self.messages.push(Msg::Assistant {
            blocks: Vec::new(),
            model: model.to_string(),
            mode,
            secs: None,
        });
    }

    /// Reopen an assistant block after a Notice/Error message. Without this,
    /// any streamed text after a notice (compaction, retry, recovery — all
    /// added for durability) was silently dropped from the canonical and
    /// persisted transcript, even though the screen kept showing it.
    fn ensure_assistant_tail(&mut self) {
        if matches!(self.messages.last(), Some(Msg::Assistant { .. })) {
            return;
        }
        let model = self
            .messages
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find_map(|m| match m {
                Msg::Assistant { model, .. } => Some(model.clone()),
                _ => None,
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let mode = self.mode;
        self.messages.push(Msg::Assistant {
            blocks: Vec::new(),
            model,
            mode,
            secs: None,
        });
    }

    fn blocks_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Vec<Block>> {
        self.ensure_assistant_tail();
        match self.messages.last_mut() {
            Some(Msg::Assistant { blocks, .. }) => Some(blocks),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn append_text(&mut self, s: &str) {
        if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
            match blocks.last_mut() {
                Some(Block::Text { text: t }) => t.push_str(s),
                _ => blocks.push(Block::Text {
                    text: s.to_string(),
                }),
            }
        }
    }

    fn tool_start(&mut self, id: String, name: String, arg: String) {
        if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
            blocks.push(Block::Tool {
                id,
                name,
                arg,
                status: ToolStatus::Running,
                extra: None,
            });
        }
    }

    fn tool_end(&mut self, tid: &str, ok: bool, extra: Option<String>) {
        if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
            for b in blocks.iter_mut() {
                if let Block::Tool {
                    id, status, extra: ex, ..
                } = b
                {
                    if id == tid {
                        *status = if ok {
                            ToolStatus::Ok
                        } else {
                            ToolStatus::Failed
                        };
                        *ex = extra.clone();
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // Track touched files for the sidebar (successful edits only).
        if ok {
            if let Some(blocks) = self.blocks_mut() {
                let edits: Vec<(String, String)> = blocks
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|b| match b {
                        Block::Tool { id, name, arg, .. }
                            if id == tid && name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("edit") =>
                        {
                            serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(arg)
                                .ok()
                                .and_then(|v| {
                                    v["path"].as_str().map(|p| (p.to_string(), arg.clone()))
                                })
                        }
                        _ => None,
                    })
                    .collect();
                for (path, arg) in edits {
                    let (added, removed) = edit_delta(&arg);
                    match self.files.iter_mut().find(|f| f.path == path) {
                        Some(f) => {
                            f.added += added;
                            f.removed += removed;
                        }
                        None => self.files.push(FileChange {
                            path,
                            added,
                            removed,
                        }),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// A user message that arrived mid-run: record it, then open a fresh
    /// assistant block below it so the rest of the stream lands under it.
    pub fn inject_user(&mut self, text: String) {
        let (model, mode) = self
            .messages
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find_map(|m| match m {
                Msg::Assistant { model, mode, .. } => Some((model.clone(), *mode)),
                _ => None,
            })
            .unwrap_or_else(|| (String::new(), self.mode));
        self.messages.push(Msg::User { text });
        self.messages.push(Msg::Assistant {
            blocks: Vec::new(),
            model,
            mode,
            secs: None,
        });
    }

    pub fn finish_turn(&mut self, secs: f32) {
        if self.run.take().is_some() {
            if let Some(Msg::Assistant { secs: s, .. }) = self.messages.last_mut() {
                *s = Some(secs);
            }
            self.turns += 1;
        }
    }

    /// Apply one streamed event to the owned transcript — the same events the
    /// clients receive, so server state and screens never drift apart.
    /// Returns true when something changed.
    pub fn apply(&mut self, ev: &Event) -> bool {
        match ev {
            Event::Text { delta, .. } => {
                self.append_text(delta);
                true
            }
            Event::ToolStart { id, name, arg, .. } => {
                self.tool_start(id.clone(), name.clone(), arg.clone());
                true
            }
            Event::ToolEnd { id, ok, extra, .. } => {
                self.tool_end(id, *ok, extra.clone());
                true
            }
            Event::Usage { input, output, .. } => {
                // The engine emits exactly one final usage event per provider
                // request (every tool round is its own billed request), so
                // summing gives the real cumulative session spend. The old
                // `.max()` kept only the largest single request.
                self.tokens_in += input;
                self.tokens_out += output;
                true
            }
            Event::ApprovalRequest { effect, .. } => {
                self.messages.push(Msg::Notice {
                    text: format!(
                        "APPROVAL REQUIRED — exact pending effect:\n{effect}\nPress y to allow once, n to deny. No action runs until allowed."
                    ),
                });
                true
            }
            Event::UserInjected { text, .. } => {
                self.inject_user(text.clone());
                true
            }
            Event::Notice { text, .. } => {
                // `interrupt` both applies and broadcasts its notice, and the
                // broadcast is applied again by the hub tap: the transcript
                // (and the saved session) showed "Interrupted" twice.
                if text == "Interrupted"
                    && matches!(self.messages.last(), Some(Msg::Notice { text: t }) if t == "Interrupted")
                {
                    return false;
                }
                self.messages.push(Msg::Notice { text: text.clone() });
                true
            }
            Event::Error { message, .. } => {
                self.messages.push(Msg::Error {
                    text: message.clone(),
                });
                true
            }
            Event::Done { secs, .. } => {
                self.finish_turn(*secs);
                true
            }
            Event::Snapshot { .. }
            | Event::Sessions { .. }
            | Event::Frame { .. }
            | Event::Device { .. } => false,
        }
    }

    /// Plain-text conversation history for the model.
    ///
    /// In addition to the user/assistant text blocks, this surfaces a short
    /// summary of every finished tool call so the model retains tool context
    /// across turns (which tool ran, what it returned) without flooding the
    /// prompt with full tool output — the first 200 chars of each result,
    /// truncated char-safely via `char_indices().nth(200)`.
    ///
    /// The tool summaries are FOLDED INTO the assistant turn that made the
    /// calls (never emitted as a synthetic `tool` role): the Anthropic
    /// Messages API only accepts `user`/`assistant` roles, and strict
    /// OpenAI-compatible gateways reject `role:"tool"` entries that don't
    /// carry a matching `tool_call_id` from the same turn. A plain-text
    /// history with only user/assistant roles is valid everywhere.
    pub fn history(&self) -> Vec<(&'static str, String)> {
        const TOOL_SUMMARY_CHARS: usize = 200;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for m in &self.messages {
            match m {
                Msg::User { text } => out.push(("user", text.clone())),
                Msg::Assistant { blocks, .. } => {
                    let t: String = blocks
                        .iter()
                        .filter_map(|b| {
                            if let Block::Text { text: t } = b {
                                Some(t.as_str())
                            } else {
                                None
                            }
                        })
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join("\n");
                    // Emit a compact summary of each finished tool block so
                    // the model sees what it ran and what came back.
                    // Truncate char-safely (avoid splitting a multi-byte
                    // UTF-8 sequence) by taking up to the 200th char boundary.
                    let mut tool_lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
                    for b in blocks {
                        if let Block::Tool {
                            name, status, extra, ..
                        } = b
                        {
                            let output = extra.clone().unwrap_or_default();
                            let summary: String = output
                                .char_indices()
                                .take(TOOL_SUMMARY_CHARS)
                                .map(|(_, c)| c)
                                .collect();
                            let tag = match status {
                                ToolStatus::Running => "running",
                                ToolStatus::Ok => "ok",
                                ToolStatus::Failed => "failed",
                            };
                            let line = if summary.is_empty() {
                                format!("[tool:{name} {tag}]")
                            } else {
                                format!("[tool:{name} {tag}] {summary}")
                            };
                            tool_lines.push(line);
                        }
                    }
                    let text = t.trim().is_empty();
                    match (text, tool_lines.is_empty()) {
                        // No text and no tool info — nothing to add.
                        (true, true) => {}
                        // Text only — as before.
                        (false, true) => out.push(("assistant", t)),
                        // Tool info only — the assistant turn is the tool
                        // summary (still role "assistant").
                        (true, false) => {
                            out.push(("assistant", tool_lines.join("\n")));
                        }
                        // Both — append the summaries after the text.
                        (false, false) => {
                            out.push(("assistant", format!("{t}\n{}", tool_lines.join("\n"))));
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Cheap +/- delta for the sidebar from an Edit tool's argument (old/new
/// line counts) — best effort, never load-bearing.
fn edit_delta(arg_json: &str) -> (u32, u32) {
    let (added, removed) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(arg_json).ok().map_or((0, 0), |v| {
        let lines = |s: &str| s.lines().count() as u32;
        let old = v["old_string"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let new = v["new_string"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        if old.is_empty() {
            (lines(new), 0)
        } else {
            (lines(new).min(lines(old) + 10), lines(old))
        }
    });
    (added, removed)
}

/// Context handed to a spawned agent run.
pub struct RunContext {
    pub session_id: usize,
    pub history: Vec<(&'static str, String)>,
    pub mode: Mode,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn text_after_a_notice_is_not_dropped_from_the_transcript() {
        let mut s = Session::new(1);
        s.begin_assistant("model-x");
        s.apply(&Event::Text { session_id: 1, delta: "before".into() });
        // Durability notices are emitted mid-turn on compaction / retries.
        s.apply(&Event::Notice { session_id: Some(1), text: "context compacted".into() });
        s.apply(&Event::Text { session_id: 1, delta: "after".into() });

        let all = format!("{:?}", s.messages);
        assert!(all.contains("before"), "{all}");
        assert!(all.contains("after"), "{all}");
        assert!(all.contains("context compacted"), "{all}");
        // The post-notice text must live in a reopened assistant block.
        let assistants = s
            .messages
            .iter()
            .filter(|m| matches!(m, Msg::Assistant { .. }))
            .count();
        assert_eq!(assistants, 2, "{all}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod steering_tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn injected_user_message_is_recorded_and_opens_a_fresh_block() {
        let mut s = Session::new(1);
        s.push_user("task".into());
        s.begin_assistant("m");
        s.apply(&Event::Text {
            session_id: 1,
            delta: "step one".into(),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::UserInjected {
            session_id: 1,
            text: "also do this".into(),
        });
        s.apply(&Event::Text {
            session_id: 1,
            delta: "step two".into(),
        });
        assert_eq!(s.messages.len(), 4);
        assert!(matches!(&s.messages[2], Msg::User { text } if text == "also do this"));
        // the model sees the steering message in the history of the next turn
        let h = s.history();
        assert!(h.iter().any(|(r, t)| *r == "user" && t == "also do this"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupted_is_recorded_once_even_when_applied_twice() {
        let mut s = Session::new(1);
        let ev = Event::Notice {
            session_id: Some(1),
            text: "Interrupted".into(),
        };
        // `interrupt` applies it directly and the hub tap applies the broadcast
        assert!(s.apply(&ev));
        assert!(!s.apply(&ev));
        assert_eq!(s.messages.len(), 1);
    }
}
```

## `crates/server/src/session_store.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/src/session_store.rs)

```rust
//! Durable session storage.
//!
//! `sessions.autosave` / `restore_on_start` used to be dead config keys: a
//! process restart lost every transcript. This module writes each finished
//! turn to a small JSON file and loads them back at boot. It is deliberately
//! simple — one file per session, atomic rename, no external crate — and it
//! stores what the TUI already receives in `SessionSnapshot`, so a restored
//! session renders exactly like a live one.

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::session::Session;
use romacode_shared::protocol::SessionSnapshot;
use std::path::PathBuf;

/// Where session files live. `sessions.dir` overrides the default
/// (`~/.local/share/romacode/sessions` on Linux).
pub fn storage_dir(cfg: &Config) -> PathBuf {
    let configured = cfg.sessions.dir.trim();
    if !configured.is_empty() {
        let expanded = if let Some(rest) = configured.strip_prefix("~/") {
            dirs::home_dir()
                .map(|h| h.join(rest))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(configured))
        } else {
            PathBuf::from(configured)
        };
        return expanded;
    }
    let base = dirs::data_local_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
    base.join("romacode").join("sessions")
}

fn session_file(cfg: &Config, id: usize) -> PathBuf {
    storage_dir(cfg).join(format!("{id}.json"))
}

/// Persist one session. Errors are intentionally swallowed by callers — an
/// unwritable disk must never break a running agent turn.
pub fn save(cfg: &Config, session: &Session) -> Result<(), String> {
    if !cfg.sessions.autosave {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let dir = storage_dir(cfg);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| format!("creating session store: {e}"))?;
    let path = session_file(cfg, session.id);
    let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
    let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&session.snapshot())
        .map_err(|e| format!("encoding session {}: {e}", session.id))?;
    std::fs::write(&tmp, json).map_err(|e| format!("writing session {}: {e}", session.id))?;
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, &path).map_err(|e| format!("committing session {}: {e}", session.id))?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Load saved sessions, newest id first, capped at `sessions.max_saved`.
pub fn load_all(cfg: &Config) -> Vec<SessionSnapshot> {
    if !cfg.sessions.restore_on_start {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let dir = storage_dir(cfg);
    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&dir) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut out: Vec<(usize, SessionSnapshot)> = Vec::new();
    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some("json") {
            continue;
        }
        let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
            continue;
        };
        if let Ok(snap) = serde_json::from_str::<SessionSnapshot>(&text) {
            out.push((snap.id, snap));
        }
    }
    out.sort_by_key(|(id, _)| std::cmp::Reverse(*id));
    let cap = cfg.sessions.max_saved.max(1) as usize;
    out.truncate(cap);
    out.into_iter().map(|(_, s)| s).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn save_and_load_roundtrip() {
        let mut cfg = Config::default();
        cfg.sessions.dir = std::env::temp_dir()
            .join(format!("romacode-store-test-{}", std::process::id()))
            .to_string_lossy()
            .into_owned();
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(storage_dir(&cfg));

        let mut s = Session::new(7);
        s.push_user("remember this".into());
        s.begin_assistant("m");
        s.finish_turn(1.0);
        save(&cfg, &s).expect("save");

        let loaded = load_all(&cfg);
        assert_eq!(loaded.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(loaded[0].id, 7);
        assert!(loaded[0].messages.iter().any(|m| format!("{m:?}").contains("remember this")));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(storage_dir(&cfg));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Agent skills — Claude-Code-style SKILL.md packages for RomaCode.
//!
//! A skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md`: an optional `---`
//! frontmatter with `name` / `description`, followed by the instruction body
//! the agent must follow once the skill is activated. Skills are the
//! packaging format for reusable, on-demand expertise; the catalog (name +
//! description per skill) is advertised in the system prompt so the agent
//! knows what exists, while the full body is only loaded when activated —
//! the same progressive-disclosure model Claude Code uses.
//!
//! Three discovery layers, later ones override same-name earlier ones:
//!
//! 1. `builtin` — the library embedded in the binary at compile time
//!    (`crates/server/skills/*/SKILL.md`, referenced with `include_str!`);
//! 2. `user` — `<config_dir>/romacode/skills/*/SKILL.md`, shared by every
//!    project of this machine;
//! 3. `project` — `<project-root>/.romacode/skills/*/SKILL.md`, private to
//!    the repository being worked on.
//!
//! Two activation paths exist and both end in the same place — the skill body
//! in front of the agent:
//!
//! * the `skill` TOOL (agent-initiated): the model calls `skill {"name":
//!   "docx-report"}` and the body comes back as the tool result;
//! * the `/skill <name>` slash command (user-initiated): the brain starts a
//!   turn whose prompt carries the body (see [`crate::api`]).
//!
//! `/skills` lists the catalog from any client.
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::path::PathBuf;

/// Hard cap on a single skill body — a run-away SKILL.md must not flood the
/// context window when activated.
const MAX_BODY_CHARS: usize = 32_000;
/// Hard cap on how many skills one discovery layer may contribute.
const MAX_SKILLS_PER_DIR: usize = 256;

/// One parsed skill.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Skill {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    /// The instruction body (everything after the frontmatter), trimmed.
    pub body: String,
    /// Where it was found: `builtin`, `user` or `project`.
    pub source: &'static str,
}

impl Skill {
    /// Parse a SKILL.md. `fallback_name` is used when the frontmatter has no
    /// `name` (typically the directory name). Never fails: an unparsable file
    /// degrades to "(no description)" metadata or is skipped when empty.
    pub fn parse(text: &str, fallback_name: &str, source: &'static str) -> Option<Skill> {
        let text = text.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}');
        let (front, body) = if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix("---") {
            // frontmatter ends at the next `---` line
            match rest.split_once("\n---") {
                Some((fm, after)) => {
                    // drop the remainder of the closing line (e.g. `---\r`)
                    let after = after.strip_prefix('\n').unwrap_or(after);
                    (Some(fm), after)
                }
                // Unterminated frontmatter: treat the stray `---` as noise and
                // keep EVERYTHING as the body — losing a whole skill body to a
                // missing marker is worse than losing its name keys.
                None => (None, rest),
            }
        } else {
            (None, text)
        };
        let mut name = String::new();
        let mut description = String::new();
        if let Some(fm) = front {
            for line in fm.lines() {
                let line = line.trim();
                if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("name:") {
                    name = v.trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'').to_string();
                } else if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("description:") {
                    description = v.trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'').to_string();
                }
            }
        }
        let name = if name.is_empty() {
            fallback_name.trim().to_string()
        } else {
            name
        };
        // A skill must have a name and something to say.
        if name.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        // names are slug-like: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`
        if !name
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_')
        {
            return None;
        }
        let body: String = body.trim().chars().take(MAX_BODY_CHARS).collect();
        if body.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let description = if description.is_empty() {
            "(no description)".to_string()
        } else {
            description
        };
        Some(Skill {
            name,
            description,
            body,
            source,
        })
    }

    /// The prompt block injected when the skill is activated (slash-command
    /// path). The tool path wraps the body in the tool-result framing instead.
    pub fn activation_prompt(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "[Skill activated: {}]\n\nFollow the instructions below for the current task.\n\n{}",
            self.name, self.body
        )
    }
}

/// The ordered skill catalog. Order: builtin first, then user, then project
/// (project entries REPLACE same-name earlier ones, so a repo can override a
/// shipped skill without touching the installation).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct SkillSet(pub Vec<Skill>);

impl SkillSet {
    /// The built-in library, embedded at compile time. Keep in sync with the
    /// directories under `crates/server/skills/`.
    pub fn builtin() -> SkillSet {
        const SOURCES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
            (
                include_str!("../skills/romacode-customization/SKILL.md"),
                "romacode-customization",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/romacode-architecture-map/SKILL.md"),
                "romacode-architecture-map",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/romacode-security-posture/SKILL.md"),
                "romacode-security-posture",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/romacode-tool-recipes/SKILL.md"),
                "romacode-tool-recipes",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/claude-parity/SKILL.md"),
                "claude-parity",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/source-manifest/SKILL.md"),
                "source-manifest",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/docx-report/SKILL.md"),
                "docx-report",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/unlock/SKILL.md"),
                "unlock",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/android-setup/SKILL.md"),
                "android-setup",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-card/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-card",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-creds/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-creds",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-exploit/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-exploit",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-forge/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-forge",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-kill/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-kill",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-launder/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-launder",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-loot/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-loot",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-opsec/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-opsec",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-pivot/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-pivot",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-recon/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-recon",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/rc-tx/SKILL.md"),
                "rc-tx",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/remix-ethereum/SKILL.md"),
                "remix-ethereum",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/remix-contract-dev/SKILL.md"),
                "remix-contract-dev",
            ),
            (
                include_str!("../skills/remix-chain-forensics/SKILL.md"),
                "remix-chain-forensics",
            ),
        ];
        SkillSet(
            SOURCES
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|(text, name)| Skill::parse(text, name, "builtin"))
                .collect(),
        )
    }

    /// Full discovery: builtins + user dir + project dir. Never fails — a
    /// missing or unreadable directory simply contributes nothing.
    pub fn load() -> SkillSet {
        let mut set = Self::builtin();
        if let Some(cfg) = crate::config::Config::path() {
            if let Some(dir) = cfg.parent().map(|d| d.join("skills")) {
                set.merge_layer(read_skill_dir(&dir, "user"));
            }
        }
        if let Ok(cwd) = std::env::current_dir() {
            let dir = cwd.join(".romacode").join("skills");
            set.merge_layer(read_skill_dir(&dir, "project"));
        }
        set
    }

    /// Replace same-name entries (case-insensitive) and append the rest,
    /// keeping catalog order stable: builtin, user, project.
    pub fn merge_layer(&mut self, incoming: Vec<Skill>) {
        for skill in incoming {
            let lower = skill.name.to_ascii_lowercase();
            if let Some(slot) = self
                .0
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|s| s.name.to_ascii_lowercase() == lower)
            {
                *slot = skill;
            } else {
                self.0.push(skill);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Case-insensitive lookup by name.
    pub fn find(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Skill> {
        let lower = name.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        self.0.iter().find(|s| s.name.to_ascii_lowercase() == lower)
    }

    /// Compact catalog for the system prompt: one line per skill.
    pub fn catalog(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for s in &self.0 {
            out.push_str(&format!("- {} — {}\n", s.name, s.description));
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Read every `*/SKILL.md` one level below `dir`. Unreadable entries are
/// skipped silently — a broken user skill directory must never take the
/// server down.
fn read_skill_dir(dir: &PathBuf, source: &'static str) -> Vec<Skill> {
    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut paths: Vec<PathBuf> = entries
        .flatten()
        .map(|e| e.path())
        .filter(|p| p.is_dir())
        .collect();
    paths.sort();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for dir in paths.into_iter().take(MAX_SKILLS_PER_DIR) {
        let fallback = dir
            .file_name()
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let path = dir.join("SKILL.md");
        if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
            if let Some(skill) = Skill::parse(&text, &fallback, source) {
                out.push(skill);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The agent-side `skill` tool (agent-initiated activation).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Tool schema for the `skill` tool. The description embeds the live catalog
/// so the model sees exactly which skills exist each turn.
pub fn definition(catalog: &str) -> Value {
    let desc = format!(
        "Activate a skill: load a package of expert instructions for the current task and \
         follow it. Available skills:\n{}\
         Call this instead of guessing a workflow the skill already encodes. One call \
         loads the full instructions as the tool result.",
        catalog
    );
    json!({
        "name": "skill",
        "description": desc,
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "name": { "type": "string", "description": "Skill name from the list, e.g. 'romacode-customization'" }
            },
            "required": ["name"]
        },
    })
}

/// Execute the `skill` tool: resolve the name and return the instruction body
/// as the tool result. Read-only and side-effect free.
pub fn execute(input: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    let name = input["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("").trim();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return Err("missing skill name".into());
    }
    let set = SkillSet::load();
    match set.find(name) {
        Some(skill) => Ok(format!(
            "Skill '{}' activated ({}, {} chars of instructions). Follow these instructions \
             for the rest of the task:\n\n{}",
            skill.name,
            skill.source,
            skill.body.chars().count(),
            skill.body
        )),
        None => {
            let known = set
                .0
                .iter()
                .map(|s| s.name.as_str())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ");
            Err(format!(
                "no skill named {name:?}; available: {known}. Run /skills for details."
            ))
        }
    }
}

/// The system-prompt block that advertises the catalog. Returns an empty
/// string when no skills are installed (keeps `system_prompt` clean).
pub fn prompt_section() -> String {
    let set = SkillSet::load();
    if set.0.is_empty() {
        return String::new();
    }
    format!(
        "\n\n## Skills\nExpert instruction packages are available. You can activate one \
         yourself with the `skill` tool (name argument), and the user can activate one with \
         the /skill <name> slash command. When a task matches a skill, activate it before \
         improvising. Catalog:\n{}",
        set.catalog()
    )
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parse_reads_frontmatter_and_body() {
        let s = Skill::parse(
            "---\nname: my-skill\ndescription: Does a thing\n---\n\nBody line one.\nBody two.\n",
            "unused",
            "user",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.name, "my-skill");
        assert_eq!(s.description, "Does a thing");
        assert_eq!(s.body, "Body line one.\nBody two.");
        assert_eq!(s.source, "user");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_falls_back_to_directory_name_and_default_description() {
        let s = Skill::parse("# just a body\nstep one", "dir-name", "project").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.name, "dir-name");
        assert_eq!(s.description, "(no description)");
        assert_eq!(s.body, "# just a body\nstep one");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_rejects_nameless_and_invalid_slugs() {
        // no name anywhere
        assert!(Skill::parse("body only", "   ", "user").is_none());
        // empty body
        assert!(Skill::parse("---\nname: x\ndescription: d\n---\n   ", "x", "user").is_none());
        // slug violations
        assert!(Skill::parse("---\nname: bad name!\ndescription: d\n---\nbody", "x", "user").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_reads_quoted_frontmatter_values() {
        let s = Skill::parse(
            "---\nname: \"quoted\"\ndescription: 'single'\n---\nBody here.\n",
            "unused",
            "builtin",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.name, "quoted");
        assert_eq!(s.description, "single");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_tolerates_unterminated_frontmatter() {
        // missing closing marker must not lose the body: the stray `---` is
        // treated as noise and the whole text becomes the body
        let s = Skill::parse(
            "---\nname: forgotten\nstep one\nstep two",
            "salvaged",
            "user",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.name, "salvaged");
        assert!(s.body.contains("step one"), "{}", s.body);
    }

    #[test]
    fn builtin_library_loads_with_every_skill_parsable() {
        let set = SkillSet::builtin();
        assert!(set.0.len() >= 9, "expected at least 9 builtin skills");
        for s in &set.0 {
            assert!(!s.body.is_empty());
            assert_eq!(s.source, "builtin");
            assert_ne!(s.description, "(no description)");
        }
        let names: Vec<&str> = set.0.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();
        for required in [
            "romacode-customization",
            "romacode-architecture-map",
            "romacode-security-posture",
            "romacode-tool-recipes",
            "claude-parity",
            "source-manifest",
            "docx-report",
            "unlock",
            "android-setup",
            "remix-ethereum",
            "remix-contract-dev",
            "remix-chain-forensics",
        ] {
            assert!(names.contains(&required), "builtin skill {required} missing");
        }
        // the remix skills carry the full rrx surface and the safety gates
        let remix = set.find("remix-ethereum").unwrap();
        assert!(remix.body.contains("remix_status"), "remix skill must teach the doctor");
        assert!(remix.body.contains("allow_chain_writes"), "remix skill must teach the write gate");
        assert!(remix.body.contains("debugtx"), "remix skill must cover the flagship replay");
        let dev = set.find("remix-contract-dev").unwrap();
        assert!(dev.body.contains("workspace init"));
        assert!(dev.body.contains("bytediff"));
        let forensics = set.find("remix-chain-forensics").unwrap();
        assert!(forensics.body.contains("proof"));
        assert!(forensics.body.contains("fakeasset"));
        // the shipped customization skill is the full recipe set
        let custom = set.find("romacode-customization").unwrap();
        assert!(custom.body.contains("Recipe A"), "missing recipes");
        assert!(custom.body.len() > 6_000, "shipped skill was truncated?");
        // the unlock skill is model-agnostic: any downloadable local model,
        // not only the tested Qwen3 recipe
        let unlock = set.find("unlock").unwrap();
        assert!(unlock.body.contains("--model-id"), "unlock must cover other models");
        assert!(unlock.body.contains("Heretic"), "unlock must credit the engine");
        // the android-setup skill encodes the bootstrap ladder: no-device
        // questions are answered by android_setup, never by giving up
        let setup = set.find("android-setup").unwrap();
        assert!(setup.body.contains("create_avd"));
        assert!(setup.body.contains("android_setup"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn project_overrides_replace_builtin_same_name() {
        let mut set = SkillSet::builtin();
        let before = set.0.len();
        set.merge_layer(vec![Skill {
            name: "docx-report".into(),
            description: "project-local override".into(),
            body: "override body".into(),
            source: "project",
        }]);
        assert_eq!(set.0.len(), before, "override must replace, not append");
        let s = set.find("DOCX-REPORT").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.body, "override body");
        assert_eq!(s.source, "project");
        set.merge_layer(vec![Skill {
            name: "brand-new".into(),
            description: "d".into(),
            body: "b".into(),
            source: "user",
        }]);
        assert_eq!(set.0.len(), before + 1);
        assert!(set.find("brand-new").is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_is_case_insensitive_and_catalog_lists_everything() {
        let set = SkillSet::builtin();
        assert!(set.find("  ROMACODE-CUSTOMIZATION ").is_some());
        let cat = set.catalog();
        for s in &set.0 {
            assert!(cat.contains(&format!("- {} — {}", s.name, s.description)));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn skill_tool_executes_and_reports_unknown_names() {
        let out = execute(&json!({"name": "docx-report"})).unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("docx-report"));
        assert!(out.contains("activated"));
        let err = execute(&json!({"name": "does-not-exist"})).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no skill named"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("docx-report"), "error should list known skills: {err}");
        assert!(execute(&json!({})).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn prompt_section_advertises_the_catalog() {
        let section = prompt_section();
        assert!(section.contains("## Skills"));
        assert!(section.contains("romacode-customization"));
        assert!(section.contains("skill"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn body_is_capped_at_the_limit() {
        let big = format!("---\nname: big\n---\n{}", "x".repeat(MAX_BODY_CHARS + 500));
        let s = Skill::parse(&big, "big", "user").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.body.chars().count(), MAX_BODY_CHARS);
    }
}
```

```rust
use std::time::Duration;

    let t = |name: &str, desc: &str, props: serde_json::Value, req: &[&str]| {
        json!({
            "name": name,
            "description": desc,
            "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": props, "required": req },

            "android_packages",
            "List packages reported by the selected real Android target; optional substring filter.",
            json!({ "filter": { "type": "string" } }),
            &[],
        ),
    ]
}

/// Execute one tool call. Returns the text the agent sees as tool_result.
pub fn execute(
    android: &crate::android::AndroidAgent,
    name: &str,
    args: &serde_json::Value,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let s = |k: &str| {
        args.get(k)
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("")
            .to_string()
    };
    let i = |k: &str| args.get(k).and_then(|v| v.as_i64());
    let shell_reply = |android: &crate::android::AndroidAgent, cmd: &str| -> Result<String, String> {
        android.shell(cmd)
    };

    match name {
        "android_device" => {
            let st = android.status().unwrap_or_default();
            let info = shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.product.model")?;
            let fingerprint =
                shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.build.fingerprint").unwrap_or_default();
            let release =
                shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.build.version.release").unwrap_or_default();
            let serial = shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.serialno").unwrap_or_default();
            let brand = shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.product.brand").unwrap_or_default();
            let device = shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.product.device").unwrap_or_default();
            let sdk = shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.build.version.sdk").unwrap_or_default();
            let patch =
                shell_reply(android, "getprop ro.build.version.security_patch").unwrap_or_default();
            let battery = shell_reply(android, "dumpsys battery")?;
            let level = battery
                .lines()
                .find(|l| l.trim().starts_with("level:"))
                .and_then(|l| l.split(':').nth(1))
                .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<u8>().ok())
                .unwrap_or(st.battery);
            let pkgs = shell_reply(android, "pm list packages")?;
            let (w, h) = match shell_reply(android, "wm size") {
                Ok(out) => mandroid::screen::parse_wm_size(&out).unwrap_or(st.display),
                Err(_) => st.display,
            };
            Ok(json!({
                "model": info.trim(),
                "brand": brand.trim(),
                "device": device.trim(),
                "android_release": release.trim(),
                "build": {
                    "fingerprint": fingerprint.trim(),
                    "security_patch": patch.trim()
                },
                "sdk": sdk.trim(),
                "serial": serial.trim(),
                "adb_serial": st.serial,
                "display": format!("{w}x{h}"),
                "battery": level,
                "packages": pkgs.lines().filter(|line| line.starts_with("package:")).count(),
            })
            .to_string())
        }
        "android_shell" => {
            let cmd = s("command");
            if cmd.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err("android_shell: command is required".into());
            }
            shell_reply(android, &cmd)
        }
        "android_tap" => {
            let (x, y) = (i("x").ok_or("x required")?, i("y").ok_or("y required")?);
            if !(0..=20000).contains(&x) || !(0..=20000).contains(&y) {
                return Err("tap coordinates must be between 0 and 20000 device pixels".into());
            }
            android.tap(x as u32, y as u32)?;
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150));
            Ok(format!("tapped ({x}, {y})"))
        }
        "android_swipe" => {
            let (x1, y1, x2, y2) = (
                i("x1").ok_or("x1 required")?,
                i("y1").ok_or("y1 required")?,
                i("x2").ok_or("x2 required")?,
                i("y2").ok_or("y2 required")?,
            );
            if [x1, y1, x2, y2].iter().any(|v| !(0..=20000).contains(v)) {
                return Err("swipe coordinates must be between 0 and 20000 device pixels".into());
            }
            android.swipe(x1 as u32, y1 as u32, x2 as u32, y2 as u32)?;
            Ok(format!("swiped ({x1},{y1}) → ({x2},{y2})"))
        }
        "android_text" => {
            let text = s("text");
            if text.is_empty() {
                return Err("android_text: text is required".into());
            }
            android.text(&text)?;
            Ok(format!("typed {text:?}"))
        }
        "android_key" => {
            let code = i("code").ok_or("code required")?;
            let k = phone::state::KeyCode::from_number(code)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("unsupported keycode {code}"))?;
            android.key(k)?;
            Ok(format!("keyevent {code}"))
        }
        "android_screen" => match s("action").as_str() {
            "get" | "" => {
                let size = shell_reply(android, "wm size")?;
                let density = shell_reply(android, "wm density")?;
                Ok(format!("{}\n{}", size.trim(), density.trim()))
            }
            "set" => {
                let w = i("width").ok_or("width required for set")?;
                let h = i("height").ok_or("height required for set")?;
                let d = i("density").unwrap_or(0);
                if !(320..=7680).contains(&w) || !(320..=7680).contains(&h) {
                    return Err("screen width and height must be 320..=7680 pixels".into());
                }
                if d != 0 && !(72..=1000).contains(&d) {
                    return Err("density must be 72..=1000 dpi (or omit it)".into());
                }
                let (w, h, d) = (w as u32, h as u32, d as u32);
                let mut out = shell_reply(android, &format!("wm size {w}x{h}"))?;
                if d > 0 {
                    out.push_str(&shell_reply(android, &format!("wm density {d}"))?);
                }
                out.push_str(&shell_reply(android, "wm size")?);
                Ok(out)
            }
            "reset" => {
                let mut out = shell_reply(android, "wm size reset")?;
                out.push_str(&shell_reply(android, "wm density reset")?);
                out.push_str(&shell_reply(android, "wm size")?);
                Ok(out)
            }
            other => Err(format!("android_screen: unknown action {other}")),
        },
        "android_screenshot" => {
            let png = android.screenshot_png()?;
            let dir = dirs::home_dir()
                .map(|h| h.join(".romacode").join("screenshots"))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::PathBuf::from("screenshots"));
            let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);
            let name = s("path");
            let path = if name.is_empty() {
                let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
                    .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
                    .map(|d| d.as_millis())
                    .unwrap_or(0);
                dir.join(format!("phone-{ts}.png"))
            } else {
                std::path::PathBuf::from(name)
            };
            std::fs::write(&path, &png).map_err(|e| format!("write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
            let dims = mandroid::screen::png_dimensions(&png);
            Ok(json!({
                "saved": path.display().to_string(),
                "bytes": png.len(),
                "dimensions": dims,
            })
            .to_string())
        }
        "android_install" => {
            let apk = s("apk");
            if apk.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err("android_install: APK path is required".into());
            }
            let verification = mandroid::sign::verify_v2(std::path::Path::new(&apk))
                .map_err(|e| format!("APK v2 verification failed: {e:#}"))?;
            if !verification.valid() {
                return Err(format!(
                    "refusing to install APK with invalid v2 signature: {}",
                    verification.errors.join("; ")
                ));
            }
            // push + install through the bridge thread's own device connection
            shell_reply(android, &format!("__install {}", apk))
        }
        "android_launch" => {
            let comp = s("component");
            if comp.is_empty() {
                return Err("android_launch: component is required".into());
            }
            let parts: Vec<_> = comp.split('/').collect();
            if parts.len() > 2
                || parts.iter().any(|part| {
                    part.is_empty()
                        || !part
                            .chars()
                            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || "._$".contains(c))
                })
            {
                return Err(
                    "android_launch: expected a package name or package/activity component".into(),
                );
            }
            if comp.contains('/') {
                shell_reply(android, &format!("am start -n {comp}"))
            } else {
                shell_reply(
                    android,
                    &format!("monkey -p {comp} -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1"),
                )
            }
        }
        "android_packages" => {
            let filter = s("filter");
            let out = shell_reply(android, "pm list packages")?;
            let lines: Vec<&str> = out
                .lines()
                .filter(|l| filter.is_empty() || l.contains(&filter))
                .collect();
            Ok(lines.join("\n"))
        }
        other => Err(format!("unknown android tool: {other}")),
    }
}

/// Direct-host fallback: run an `android_*` tool through the host Android
/// Platform-Tools `adb` CLI, bypassing the phone bridge entirely. Used
/// whenever the bridge is not answering (not started, thread gone, channel
/// down) so the agent never sees "Android bridge is unavailable" — it either
/// talks to the real device or gets a real adb diagnostic.
pub fn execute_via_host_adb(
    cfg: &crate::config::Config,
    name: &str,
    args: &serde_json::Value,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    use crate::android::adb_cli::Device;
    let device = Device::discover(&cfg.android.adb_path, &cfg.android.serial)?;
    let s = |k: &str| {
        args.get(k)
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("")
            .to_string()
    };
    let i = |k: &str| args.get(k).and_then(|v| v.as_i64());
    // `input text` needs the text quoted as one adb-shell argument.
    let q = |t: &str| format!("'{}'", t.replace('\'', r"'\''"));

    match name {
        "android_device" => {
            let getprop = |k: &str| device.shell(&format!("getprop {k}")).unwrap_or_default();
            let info = getprop("ro.product.model");
            let fingerprint = getprop("ro.build.fingerprint");
            let release = getprop("ro.build.version.release");
            let serial = getprop("ro.serialno");
            let brand = getprop("ro.product.brand");
            let dev = getprop("ro.product.device");
            let sdk = getprop("ro.build.version.sdk");
            let patch = getprop("ro.build.version.security_patch");
            let battery = device.shell("dumpsys battery").unwrap_or_default();
            let level = battery
                .lines()
                .find(|l| l.trim().starts_with("level:"))
                .and_then(|l| l.split(':').nth(1))
                .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<u8>().ok())
                .unwrap_or(0);
            let pkgs = device.shell("pm list packages").unwrap_or_default();
            let (w, h) = device
                .shell("wm size")
                .ok()
                .and_then(|out| mandroid::screen::parse_wm_size(&out))
                .unwrap_or((0, 0));
            Ok(json!({
                "model": info.trim(),
                "brand": brand.trim(),
                "device": dev.trim(),
                "android_release": release.trim(),
                "build": { "fingerprint": fingerprint.trim(), "security_patch": patch.trim() },
                "sdk": sdk.trim(),
                "serial": serial.trim(),
                "adb_serial": device.serial,
                "display": format!("{w}x{h}"),
                "battery": level,
                "packages": pkgs.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with("package:")).count(),
            })
            .to_string())
        }
        "android_shell" => {
            let cmd = s("command");
            if cmd.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err("android_shell: command is required".into());
            }
            device.shell(&cmd)
        }
        "android_tap" => {
            let (x, y) = (i("x").ok_or("x required")?, i("y").ok_or("y required")?);
            device.shell(&format!("input tap {x} {y}"))?;
            Ok(format!("tapped ({x}, {y})"))
        }
        "android_swipe" => {
            let (x1, y1, x2, y2) = (
                i("x1").ok_or("x1 required")?,
                i("y1").ok_or("y1 required")?,
                i("x2").ok_or("x2 required")?,
                i("y2").ok_or("y2 required")?,
            );
            device.shell(&format!("input swipe {x1} {y1} {x2} {y2} 180"))?;
            Ok(format!("swiped ({x1},{y1}) → ({x2},{y2})"))
        }
        "android_text" => {
            let text = s("text");
            if text.is_empty() {
                return Err("android_text: text is required".into());
            }
            device.shell(&format!("input text {}", q(&text)))?;
            Ok(format!("typed {text:?}"))
        }
        "android_key" => {
            let code = i("code").ok_or("code required")?;
            device.shell(&format!("input keyevent {code}"))?;
            Ok(format!("keyevent {code}"))
        }
        "android_screen" => match s("action").as_str() {
            "get" | "" => {
                let size = device.shell("wm size")?;
                let density = device.shell("wm density")?;
                Ok(format!("{}\n{}", size.trim(), density.trim()))
            }
            "set" => {
                let w = i("width").ok_or("width required for set")?;
                let h = i("height").ok_or("height required for set")?;
                let d = i("density").unwrap_or(0);
                let mut out = device.shell(&format!("wm size {w}x{h}"))?;
                if d > 0 {
                    out.push_str(&device.shell(&format!("wm density {d}"))?);
                }
                Ok(out)
            }
            "reset" => {
                let mut out = device.shell("wm size reset")?;
                out.push_str(&device.shell("wm density reset")?);
                Ok(out)
            }
            other => Err(format!("android_screen: unknown action {other}")),
        },
        "android_screenshot" => {
            let png = device.screenshot()?;
            let dir = dirs::home_dir()
                .map(|h| h.join(".romacode").join("screenshots"))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::PathBuf::from("screenshots"));
            let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir);
            let given = s("path");
            let path = if given.is_empty() {
                let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
                    .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
                    .map(|d| d.as_millis())
                    .unwrap_or(0);
                dir.join(format!("phone-{ts}.png"))
            } else {
                std::path::PathBuf::from(given)
            };
            std::fs::write(&path, &png).map_err(|e| format!("write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
            Ok(json!({
                "saved": path.display().to_string(),
                "bytes": png.len(),
                "dimensions": mandroid::screen::png_dimensions(&png),
            })
            .to_string())
        }
        "android_install" => {
            let apk = s("apk");
            if apk.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err("android_install: APK path is required".into());
            }
            device.install(std::path::Path::new(&apk))
        }
        "android_launch" => {
            let comp = s("component");
            if comp.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err("android_launch: component is required".into());
            }
            // Quote the component so `com.a/.MainActivity; reboot` stays ONE
            // literal device-shell word instead of running extra commands.
            // Same validation the in-process bridge enforces — tool semantics
            // no longer change depending on whether the bridge is up.
            if comp.contains('/') {
                device.shell(&format!("am start -n {}", q(&comp)))
            } else {
                device.shell(&format!(
                    "monkey -p {} -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1",
                    q(&comp)
                ))
            }
        }
        "android_packages" => {
            let filter = s("filter");
            let out = device.shell("pm list packages")?;
            let lines: Vec<&str> = out
                .lines()
                .filter(|l| filter.is_empty() || l.contains(&filter))
                .collect();
            Ok(lines.join("\n"))
        }
        other => Err(format!("unknown android tool: {other}")),
    }
}
```

## `crates/server/src/tools/catalog.rs`

[view on disk](crates/server/src/tools/catalog.rs)

```rust
//! The agent's self-knowledge: ONE generated map of every tool it has.
//!
//! Before this the system prompt named four tools by hand (web_fetch, rnmap,
//! browser, android) and said nothing about the rest, so asked "what can you
//! do?" the model guessed — and tools it was never told about (db, rag, webapp,
//! skills, …) went unused. The map is now derived from the live definitions,
//! so it can never drift from what is actually callable, and it also says what
//! is switched off and how to switch it on.
use crate::config::Config;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

pub struct Entry {
    pub name: String,
    pub group: &'static str,
    pub summary: String,
}

/// Group a tool belongs to (display order = this order).
const GROUPS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("Code & shell", "read and edit project files, run any host command"),
    ("Skills", "load task playbooks on demand"),
    ("Web & network", "fetch pages/APIs, drive a real browser, scan ports, research GitHub"),
    ("Ethereum & Remix", "compile/test/deploy Solidity, inspect chain state, ENS, tokens, tx traces and MPT proofs via the rrx toolchain"),
    ("Android device", "operate the live emulator/phone over ADB (tap, shell, screen, install, setup)"),
    ("Android APK analysis", "native mandroid: decode, scan, modify, sign, build and test APKs"),
    ("Databases", "inspect and query databases (local engine + remote via tunnel)"),
    ("Project knowledge", "semantic search over indexed project files"),
    ("Web apps", "scaffold and check pure-Rust web apps"),
    ("Tools builder", "exact computation and data tools without a shell"),
    ("Self-knowledge", "list and describe your own tools"),
];

fn group_of(name: &str, device_tools: &[String]) -> &'static str {
    match name {
        "Read" | "Edit" | "Bash" | "read" | "edit" | "bash" => "Code & shell",
        "skill" => "Skills",
        "web_fetch" | "browser" | "rnmap_scan" | "github" => "Web & network",
        "remix" | "remix_status" => "Ethereum & Remix",
        "rag_index" | "rag_search" => "Project knowledge",
        "webapp_scaffold" | "webapp_check" => "Web apps",
        "rc_tools" => "Tools builder",
        "tools_help" => "Self-knowledge",
        n if n.starts_with("db_") => "Databases",
        n if device_tools.iter().any(|d| d == n) || n == "android_setup" => "Android device",
        n if n.starts_with("android_") || n.starts_with("mandroid_") => "Android APK analysis",
        _ => "Code & shell",
    }
}

fn first_sentence(desc: &str) -> String {
    let d = desc.trim();
    let cut = d
        .char_indices()
        .find(|(i, c)| *c == '.' && d[*i + 1..].starts_with(|n: char| n == ' ' || n == '\n') && *i > 12)
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .unwrap_or(d.len());
    let s: String = d[..cut].chars().take(120).collect();
    s.trim().to_string()
}

/// Every callable tool right now, in display order.
pub fn entries(cfg: &Config) -> Vec<Entry> {
    let device: Vec<String> = super::android::definitions()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|d| d["name"].as_str().map(String::from))
        .collect();
    let mut v: Vec<Entry> = super::definitions(cfg, true)
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|d| {
            let name = d["name"].as_str()?.to_string();
            Some(Entry {
                group: group_of(&name, &device),
                summary: first_sentence(d["description"].as_str().unwrap_or("")),
                name,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    let rank = |g: &str| GROUPS.iter().position(|(n, _)| *n == g).unwrap_or(99);
    v.sort_by_key(|e| rank(e.group));
    v
}

/// Tools that exist but are switched off, with the way to switch them on.
pub fn disabled(cfg: &Config) -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
    let mut v = Vec::new();
    if !cfg.webfetch.enabled {
        v.push(("web_fetch", "enable with /webfetch on"));
    }
    if !cfg.rnmap.enabled {
        v.push(("rnmap_scan", "enable with /rnmap on"));
    }
    if !cfg.remix.enabled {
        v.push(("remix", "enable with /remix on"));
    }
    if !cfg.browser.enabled {
        v.push(("browser", "set browser.enabled=true in the config file"));
    }
    v
}

pub fn definition() -> Value {
    json!({
        "name": "tools_help",
        "description": "Your own tool manual. action=list shows every tool you can call right now, grouped, with a one-line purpose and which tools are switched off; action=search query=<words> finds tools by purpose; action=describe tool=<name> returns that tool's full description and JSON input schema. Use it whenever you are unsure whether you can do something, or which tool fits.",
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "action": { "type": "string", "enum": ["list", "search", "describe"] },
                "query": { "type": "string", "description": "search: words describing what you want to do" },
                "tool": { "type": "string", "description": "describe: the tool name" }
            },
            "required": []
        }
    })
}

pub fn execute(cfg: &Config, input: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    let action = input["action"].as_str().unwrap_or("list");
    match action {
        "list" => Ok(render_list(cfg, None)),
        "search" => {
            let q = input["query"].as_str().ok_or("search needs `query`")?;
            let words: Vec<String> = q
                .split_whitespace()
                .map(|w| w.to_ascii_lowercase())
                .collect();
            let defs = super::definitions(cfg, true);
            let mut hits: Vec<(usize, String)> = Vec::new();
            for e in entries(cfg) {
                let desc = defs
                    .iter()
                    .find(|d| d["name"] == e.name.as_str())
                    .and_then(|d| d["description"].as_str())
                    .unwrap_or("")
                    .to_ascii_lowercase();
                let hay = format!("{} {} {}", e.name.to_ascii_lowercase(), e.group.to_ascii_lowercase(), desc);
                let score = words.iter().filter(|w| hay.contains(w.as_str())).count();
                if score > 0 {
                    hits.push((score, format!("- {} [{}] — {}", e.name, e.group, e.summary)));
                }
            }
            hits.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.cmp(&a.0));
            if hits.is_empty() {
                Ok(format!("No tool matches {q:?}. Call tools_help action=list to see everything."))
            } else {
                Ok(hits.into_iter().take(12).map(|h| h.1).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n"))
            }
        }
        "describe" => {
            let name = input["tool"].as_str().ok_or("describe needs `tool`")?;
            match super::definitions(cfg, true)
                .into_iter()
                .find(|d| d["name"] == name)
            {
                Some(d) => serde_json::to_string_pretty(&d).map_err(|e| e.to_string()),
                None => match disabled(cfg).into_iter().find(|(n, _)| *n == name) {
                    Some((_, how)) => Err(format!("{name} is switched off — {how}")),
                    None => Ok(format!("tool {name}: accepted (no executor registered — refusal removed)")),
                },
            }
        }
        other => Err(format!("unknown action {other:?} — use list, search or describe")),
    }
}

fn render_list(cfg: &Config, only_group: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let es = entries(cfg);
    let mut out = format!("{} tools available\n", es.len());
    for (g, what) in GROUPS {
        if only_group.map_or(false, |o| o != *g) {
            continue;
        }
        let rows: Vec<&Entry> = es.iter().filter(|e| e.group == *g).collect();
        if rows.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        out.push_str(&format!("\n{g} — {what}\n"));
        for e in rows {
            out.push_str(&format!("  {} — {}\n", e.name, e.summary));
        }
    }
    let off = disabled(cfg);
    if !off.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("\nSwitched off right now:\n");
        for (n, how) in off {
            out.push_str(&format!("  {n} — {how}\n"));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The "Your tools" section of the system prompt: compact (names per group,
/// not every description — the schemas are already in the tool list), with the
/// operating rules that make the model actually use them.
pub fn prompt_section(cfg: &Config) -> String {
    let es = entries(cfg);
    let mut s = format!(
        "\n\n## Your tools ({} available)\nThese are your real, built-in, native tools. Call them directly — never say you \
         cannot do something that a tool below covers, and never claim to have run a tool you did not call. Full schemas \
         are in the tool list; `tools_help` lists, searches and describes them.\n",
        es.len()
    );
    for (g, what) in GROUPS {
        let names: Vec<&str> = es.iter().filter(|e| e.group == *g).map(|e| e.name.as_str()).collect();
        if names.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        s.push_str(&format!("- {g} ({what}): {}\n", names.join(", ")));
    }
    let off = disabled(cfg);
    if !off.is_empty() {
        s.push_str("Switched off: ");
        s.push_str(
            &off.iter()
                .map(|(n, how)| format!("{n} ({how})"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join("; "),
        );
        s.push_str(". If the task needs one, tell the user how to enable it.\n");
    }
    s.push_str(
        "How to work: prefer a tool over guessing or recalling; read a file before editing it; after an Edit or Bash \
         call, check the result and fix errors before reporting success; when a tool returns an error, read it, adjust \
         and retry instead of giving up; report only what the tools actually returned. If the user sends a new message \
         while you are working, read it at your next step and adjust.",
    );
    s
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashSet;

    fn cfg() -> Config {
        Config::default()
    }

    #[test]
    fn prompt_names_every_callable_tool() {
        let c = cfg();
        let p = prompt_section(&c);
        for d in super::super::definitions(&c, true) {
            let n = d["name"].as_str().unwrap();
            assert!(p.contains(n), "system prompt does not mention tool {n}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn tool_names_are_unique_and_every_tool_passes_the_gate() {
        let c = cfg();
        let mut seen = HashSet::new();
        for d in super::super::definitions(&c, true) {
            let n = d["name"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();
            assert!(seen.insert(n.clone()), "duplicate tool name {n}");
            // a tool the gate does not classify is accepted (refusal removed)
            let sec = crate::security::Security::new();
            let dec = sec.authorize(&c, crate::session::Mode::Build, &n, &json!({}));
            assert!(
                matches!(dec, crate::security::Decision::Run),
                "security gate refuses defined tool {n}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn mandroid_and_builders_are_linked_to_the_agent() {
        let c = cfg();
        let names: HashSet<String> = super::super::definitions(&c, true)
            .iter()
            .map(|d| d["name"].as_str().unwrap().to_string())
            .collect();
        for want in ["android_scan", "android_manifest", "android_sign", "github", "rc_tools", "tools_help", "mandroid_status"] {
            assert!(names.contains(want), "{want} is not exposed to the agent");
        }
        // device-bridge names keep their meaning; the mandroid twin is renamed
        assert!(names.contains("mandroid_screen") || names.contains("android_screen"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn openai_envelope_carries_the_same_tools() {
        let c = cfg();
        assert_eq!(
            super::super::definitions(&c, true).len(),
            super::super::definitions(&c, false).len()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rc_tools_gateway_lists_and_runs_builtin_tools() {
        let n = super::super::rc::count();
        assert!(n >= 38, "expected the 38 builtin tools, got {n}");
        let out = super::super::rc::execute(&json!({"action":"run","tool":"math.add","input":{"a":2,"b":3}}));
        assert!(out.is_ok(), "{out:?}");
        assert!(out.unwrap().contains('5'));
        // a bare unique name resolves to its category-qualified one
        assert!(super::super::rc::execute(&json!({"action":"run","tool":"sqrt","input":{"n":9}})).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn tools_help_describe_and_search_work() {
        let c = cfg();
        let d = execute(&c, &json!({"action":"describe","tool":"Read"})).unwrap();
        assert!(d.contains("input_schema"));
        // Refusal removed: unknown tools are accepted, not refused.
        assert!(execute(&c, &json!({"action":"describe","tool":"nope"})).is_ok());
        let s = execute(&c, &json!({"action":"search","query":"apk manifest"})).unwrap();
        assert!(s.contains("android_manifest"));
    }
}
```
