```rust
//! RomaCode shared contract.
//!
//! This crate is the single source of truth for everything that crosses the
//! wire between the two halves of RomaCode:
//!
//! * the **server** (`crates/server`) — the brain: agent loop, sessions,
//!   tools, security gate, engines;
//! * the **client TUI** (`crates/client-tui`) — the screen: keyboard, mouse
//!   and pixels.
//!
//! `protocol` defines the request/response messages; `events` defines the
//! stream of things the server pushes to attached clients. Both sides depend
//! only on this crate, so the wire format can never drift apart.

pub mod offense;
pub mod catalog;
pub mod events;
pub mod modeldata;
pub mod protocol;
pub mod tui_settings;

pub use events::Event;
pub use protocol::{ClientEnvelope, ClientRequest, Reply, ServerEnvelope, Welcome};
```

## `crates/shared/src/modeldata.rs`

[view on disk](crates/shared/src/modeldata.rs)

```rust
//! Model profile library — the official "running rules and setup" for every
//! model RomaCode knows about, one JSON file per model under
//! `crates/shared/modeldata/<provider>/<model>.json`, plus a per-provider
//! `_provider.json` default and a global `_default.json` fallback.
//!
//! What a profile carries (all values are taken from the provider's official
//! documentation or flagged `unverified`):
//!
//! * identity: provider folder, family, display name, wire protocol, status;
//! * limits: context window, max output tokens — the server clamps
//!   `max_tokens` so a request can never exceed the model's output limit;
//! * param rules: which sampling parameters the model accepts and their
//!   legal ranges (reasoning families reject `temperature`/`top_p`; the
//!   Anthropic wire range is 0..=1; some models accept temperature OR
//!   top_p, never both);
//! * wire rules: `max_tokens` vs `max_completion_tokens`, whether `stop`
//!   is accepted;
//! * endpoints, pricing (when officially listed), docs and source URLs.
//!
//! Resolution is deliberately total: [`profile_for`] NEVER fails and NEVER
//! blocks a request. It walks
//! exact → normalized → family (vendor-prefixed aggregator ids) → the
//! provider's `_provider.json` → the global `_default.json`. An unknown
//! model on an unknown host still runs with permissive defaults.
//!
//! The JSON files are embedded at compile time via [`modeldata_gen::SOURCES`]
//! (generated by `scripts/gen_modeldata.py`); nothing is read from disk at
//! runtime, and the TUI reads the same embedded library — one source of
//! truth for both sides, like `catalog`.

/// Generated include_str! table (scripts/gen_modeldata.py). A file-module
/// child would resolve under src/modeldata/, so the path is pinned here.
#[path = "modeldata_gen.rs"]
mod modeldata_gen;

use serde::Deserialize;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

/// Whether one sampling parameter is accepted and its legal range.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct ParamSpec {
    /// Does the model accept this parameter at all? `false` = the request
    /// must OMIT it (sending it is a 400 on the reasoning families).
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub supported: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub min: f32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max: f32,
}

/// Parameter rules for one model.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct Params {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub temperature: Option<ParamSpec>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub top_p: Option<ParamSpec>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub reasoning_effort: Option<ParamSpec>,
}

/// Capability flags (missing = false; absent data is not invented).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct Features {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub vision: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tools: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub json_mode: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub reasoning: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub prefix_caching: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub computer_use: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub web_search: bool,
}

/// Wire-level request rules.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Wire {
    /// `"max_tokens"`, `"max_completion_tokens"`, or `""` (= decide from the
    /// provider id, the legacy behavior).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_tokens_param: String,
    /// Some models accept temperature OR top_p but not both (Anthropic 4.5).
    #[serde(default, rename = "temperature_or_top_p_exclusive")]
    pub temperature_or_top_p_exclusive: bool,
    /// Reasoning models reject `stop`.
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub stop_supported: bool,
}

impl Default for Wire {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            max_tokens_param: String::new(),
            temperature_or_top_p_exclusive: false,
            stop_supported: true,
        }
    }
}

/// One model's official running rules.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct ModelProfile {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub provider: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub family: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub display_name: String,
    /// `openai` or `anthropic` — mirrors `catalog::ApiKind`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub api: String,
    /// `stable | preview | beta | legacy | provider-default | unknown`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub status: String,
    /// 0 = unknown (never clamp).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub context_window: u64,
    /// 0 = unknown (never clamp).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_output_tokens: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub features: Features,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub params: Params,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub wire: Wire,
    /// Officially listed pricing, when published. Display-only.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pricing: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub endpoints: serde_json::Value,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub wire_notes: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub docs: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub sources: Vec<String>,
    /// Fields that could not be verified against official documentation.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub unverified_fields: Vec<String>,
}

fn default_true() -> bool {
    true
}

/// Provider-family routing for aggregator ids: the first path segment maps
/// to the vendor folder whose profiles apply.
fn family_of(first_segment: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match first_segment {
        "anthropic" => Some("anthropic"),
        "openai" => Some("openai"),
        "google" | "gemini" => Some("google"),
        "deepseek" => Some("deepseek"),
        "xai" | "grok" => Some("xai"),
        "zai" | "glm" | "z-ai" => Some("zai"),
        "moonshot" | "kimi" => Some("moonshot"),
        "qwen" | "alibaba" => Some("qwen"),
        "minimax" => Some("minimax"),
        "mistral" => Some("mistral"),
        "cohere" => Some("cohere"),
        "perplexity" => Some("perplexity"),
        "google-vertex" | "amazon-bedrock" => None, // hosted variants, not ids
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Family routing from the MODEL NAME itself: a model served through an
/// aggregator keeps its vendor identity in the id (`gpt-5.2` on Azure is
/// still an OpenAI model). Conservative prefixes only — anything ambiguous
/// stays with the provider's own defaults.
fn family_from_name(norm: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let starts = |p: &[&str]| p.iter().any(|prefix| norm.starts_with(prefix));
    if starts(&["gpt-", "o1", "o3-", "o4-"]) {
        Some("openai")
    } else if starts(&["claude"]) {
        Some("anthropic")
    } else if starts(&["gemini"]) {
        Some("google")
    } else if starts(&["deepseek"]) {
        Some("deepseek")
    } else if starts(&["grok"]) {
        Some("xai")
    } else if starts(&["glm"]) {
        Some("zai")
    } else if starts(&["kimi"]) {
        Some("moonshot")
    } else if starts(&["qwen"]) {
        Some("qwen")
    } else if starts(&["minimax"]) {
        Some("minimax")
    } else if starts(&["mistral", "codestral", "magistral"]) {
        Some("mistral")
    } else if starts(&["command-"]) {
        Some("cohere")
    } else if starts(&["sonar"]) {
        Some("perplexity")
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Normalize a raw model id so tolerant lookup can match it against a
/// profile's canonical id:
///
/// * vendor path prefixes drop (`anthropic/…`, `accounts/fireworks/models/…`);
/// * `:` tags drop (`:latest`, `:free`, `:high`);
/// * `.` and `_` unify to `-` (`claude-sonnet-5.5` == `claude-sonnet-5-5`);
/// * release-date suffixes drop (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`,
///   `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05`).
///
/// Conservative by design: anything it does not recognize stays, and a miss
/// falls through to the provider default — never an error.
pub fn normalize(raw: &str) -> String {
    let s0 = raw.trim();
    // Reserved registry namespace: `_provider` / `_default` are looked up by
    // their literal names, never normalized.
    if s0.starts_with('_') {
        return s0.to_ascii_lowercase();
    }
    let mut s = s0.to_ascii_lowercase();
    // colon tags first (`openai/gpt-5.2:high` → `openai/gpt-5.2`)
    if let Some(pos) = s.find(':') {
        s.truncate(pos);
    }
    // last path segment
    if let Some(pos) = s.rfind('/') {
        s = s[pos + 1..].to_string();
    }
    s = s.replace(['.', '_'], "-");
    // collapse runs of '-' and trim ends
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut prev_dash = false;
    for c in s.chars() {
        if c == '-' {
            if !prev_dash {
                out.push('-');
            }
            prev_dash = true;
        } else {
            out.push(c);
            prev_dash = false;
        }
    }
    let mut out = out.trim_matches('-').to_string();
    // release-date suffixes: `-20250929`, `-2025-12-11`, `-MM-DD` (then any
    // `-preview`), `-latest` — each strip is conservative and exact-length
    let bytes = out.as_bytes();
    let digits = |b: u8| b.is_ascii_digit();
    if out.len() > 9 && bytes[out.len() - 9] == b'-' && bytes[out.len() - 8..].iter().all(|&b| digits(b)) {
        out.truncate(out.len() - 9);
    } else if out.len() > 11
        && bytes[out.len() - 11] == b'-'
        && (0..10).all(|i| i == 4 || i == 7 || digits(bytes[out.len() - 10 + i]))
    {
        out.truncate(out.len() - 11);
    } else if out.len() > 6
        && bytes[out.len() - 6] == b'-'
        && digits(bytes[out.len() - 5])
        && digits(bytes[out.len() - 4])
        && bytes[out.len() - 3] == b'-'
        && digits(bytes[out.len() - 2])
        && digits(bytes[out.len() - 1])
    {
        // `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05` → `gemini-2.5-pro-preview`
        out.truncate(out.len() - 6);
    }
    // preview / latest suffixes
    for suffix in ["-preview", "-latest"] {
        if let Some(stripped) = out.strip_suffix(suffix) {
            out = stripped.to_string();
        }
    }
    let mut out2 = String::with_capacity(out.len());
    let mut prev_dash = false;
    for c in out.chars() {
        if c == '-' {
            if !prev_dash {
                out2.push('-');
            }
            prev_dash = true;
        } else {
            out2.push(c);
            prev_dash = false;
        }
    }
    out2.trim_matches('-').to_string()
}

struct Registry {
    by_key: HashMap<(String, String), usize>,
    all: Vec<ModelProfile>,
}

fn registry() -> &'static Registry {
    static REG: OnceLock<Registry> = OnceLock::new();
    REG.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        let mut by_key = HashMap::new();
        for (provider, _path) in modeldata_gen::SOURCES {
            // include_str! guarantees presence; parse failure would be a
            // build bug, so a broken file is skipped loudly in tests and
            // quietly (profile falls back) at runtime.
            let Ok(p) = serde_json::from_str::<ModelProfile>(_path) else {
                continue;
            };
            let key = (provider.to_string(), normalize(&p.id));
            by_key.insert(key, all.len());
            all.push(p);
        }
        Registry { by_key, all }
    })
}

/// Exact (provider, model) lookup with normalized ids.
pub fn find(provider: &str, model: &str) -> Option<&'static ModelProfile> {
    let reg = registry();
    let provider = provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let norm = normalize(model);
    if norm.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    reg.by_key
        .get(&(provider.clone(), norm.clone()))
        .map(|&i| &reg.all[i])
        // vendor-prefixed aggregator id: route to the family folder
        .or_else(|| {
            let first = model.trim().split('/').next().unwrap_or("").to_ascii_lowercase();
            family_of(&first).and_then(|fam| {
                if fam == provider {
                    None
                } else {
                    reg.by_key.get(&(fam.to_string(), norm.clone())).map(|&i| &reg.all[i])
                }
            })
        })
        // no path prefix: route by the model-name shape (gpt-5.2 on Azure,
        // claude-… on a proxy, deepseek-chat on a custom host)
        .or_else(|| {
            family_from_name(&norm).and_then(|fam| {
                if fam == provider {
                    None
                } else {
                    reg.by_key.get(&(fam.to_string(), norm)).map(|&i| &reg.all[i])
                }
            })
        })
}

/// TOTAL resolution: a profile for every (provider, model) pair, always.
///
/// Order: exact/normalized/family match → the provider's `_provider.json`
/// default → the global `_default.json`. Never errors, never blocks: an
/// unknown model keeps running with permissive rules.
pub fn profile_for(provider: &str, model: &str) -> &'static ModelProfile {
    if let Some(p) = find(provider, model) {
        return p;
    }
    let reg = registry();
    let provider = provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if let Some(&i) = reg.by_key.get(&(provider, "_provider".to_string())) {
        return &reg.all[i];
    }
    let di = reg
        .by_key
        .get(&("_default".to_string(), "_default".to_string()))
        .expect("global default profile missing from SOURCES");
    &reg.all[*di]
}

/// Every concrete model profile for one provider (sorted by id; no
/// `_provider` entry). Feeds pickers on both sides.
pub fn catalog_for(provider: &str) -> Vec<&'static ModelProfile> {
    let reg = registry();
    let provider = provider.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let mut out: Vec<&ModelProfile> = reg
        .all
        .iter()
        .filter(|p| p.provider == provider && p.id != "_provider")
        .collect();
    out.sort_by(|a, b| a.id.cmp(&b.id));
    out
}

/// Short human-readable line for pickers/status: context, output limit,
/// headline features.
pub fn summary(p: &ModelProfile) -> String {
    let ctx = if p.context_window >= 1_000_000 {
        format!("{}M", p.context_window / 1_000_000)
    } else if p.context_window > 0 {
        format!("{}K", p.context_window / 1_000)
    } else {
        "?".to_string()
    };
    let out = if p.max_output_tokens >= 1_000 {
        format!("{}K", p.max_output_tokens / 1_000)
    } else if p.max_output_tokens > 0 {
        format!("{}", p.max_output_tokens)
    } else {
        "?".to_string()
    };
    let mut feats: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    if p.features.vision {
        feats.push("vision");
    }
    if p.features.tools {
        feats.push("tools");
    }
    if p.features.reasoning {
        feats.push("reasoning");
    }
    format!("{ctx} ctx · {out} out{}", if feats.is_empty() {
        String::new()
    } else {
        format!(" · {}", feats.join("+"))
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::catalog;

    #[test]
    fn every_embedded_profile_parses() {
        let reg = registry();
        assert!(reg.all.len() >= 80, "library looks truncated: {}", reg.all.len());
        for p in &reg.all {
            assert!(!p.display_name.is_empty(), "{}: missing display_name", p.id);
            for (i, src) in p.sources.iter().enumerate() {
                assert!(src.starts_with("https://"), "{}: source {i} not a URL", p.id);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn keys_are_unique_and_folders_match() {
        let reg = registry();
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for p in &reg.all {
            let key = (p.provider.clone(), normalize(&p.id));
            assert!(seen.insert(key.clone()), "duplicate profile {key:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_unifies_known_id_shapes() {
        assert_eq!(normalize("claude-sonnet-5-5"), "claude-sonnet-5-5");
        assert_eq!(normalize("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5"), "claude-sonnet-5-5");
        assert_eq!(normalize("claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929"), "claude-sonnet-4-5");
        assert_eq!(normalize("openai/gpt-5.2:high"), "gpt-5-2");
        assert_eq!(normalize("accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3p3-70b-instruct"), "llama-v3p3-70b-instruct");
        assert_eq!(normalize("gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05"), "gemini-2-5-pro");
        assert_eq!(normalize("MiniMax-M3.1-Flash"), "minimax-m3-1-flash");
        assert_eq!(normalize("deepseek-chat"), "deepseek-chat");
        assert_eq!(normalize("meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo"), "llama-3-3-70b-instruct-turbo");
    }

    #[test]
    fn family_routing_resolves_vendor_prefixed_ids() {
        let p = find("openrouter", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5").expect("family route");
        assert_eq!(p.provider, "anthropic");
        let d = find("openrouter", "deepseek/deepseek-chat").expect("family route");
        assert_eq!(d.provider, "deepseek");
        // same-provider prefix must not self-route to a wrong folder
        assert!(find("groq", "openai/gpt-oss-120b").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn date_suffixed_snapshot_ids_resolve() {
        let p = find("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929").expect("snapshot id");
        assert_eq!(p.id, "claude-sonnet-4-5");
    }

    #[test]
    fn profile_for_is_total_and_never_blocks() {
        // the exact report scenario: a model nobody knows, on a host nobody
        // configured — still a profile, still permissive, never an error
        let p = profile_for("some-unknown-host", "totally-made-up-model");
        assert_eq!(p.id, "_default");
        assert!(p.params.temperature.as_ref().map(|t| t.supported).unwrap_or(true));
        // known provider without a model file → provider defaults
        let g = profile_for("google", "brand-new-gemini-something");
        assert_eq!(g.id, "_provider");
        assert_eq!(g.provider, "google");
    }

    #[test]
    fn reasoning_wire_rules_are_explicit() {
        let g = find("openai", "gpt-5.2").expect("gpt-5.2 profile");
        assert_eq!(g.wire.max_tokens_param, "max_completion_tokens");
        assert!(!g.params.temperature.as_ref().expect("temperature spec").supported);
        assert!(!g.wire.stop_supported);
        assert!(g.params.reasoning_effort.as_ref().expect("effort").supported);
    }

    #[test]
    fn anthropic_temperature_range_is_clamped_to_official_bounds() {
        for m in ["claude-sonnet-5-5", "claude-opus-4-5", "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"] {
            let p = find("anthropic", m).expect(m);
            let t = p.params.temperature.as_ref().expect("anthropic temperature spec");
            assert!(t.max <= 1.0, "{m}: temperature max {} exceeds the Anthropic 0..=1 range", t.max);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_known_provider_default_model_resolves() {
        // "must not get stuck due to lack of requirement": resolution must
        // always return a usable profile. The detailed profile library covers
        // the core adapter providers; the long tail of catalog providers has
        // no hand-written profiles and intentionally uses the graceful global
        // fallback (profile_for never errors).
        for k in catalog::known() {
            assert!(!k.default_model.is_empty(), "{}: no default model in catalog", k.id);
            let p = profile_for(k.id.as_str(), k.default_model.as_str());
            assert!(!p.id.is_empty(), "{}: profile resolution returned nothing", k.id);
            let is_core = romacode_providers::catalog::BUILTIN_SNAPSHOT
                .iter()
                .any(|e| e.id.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&k.id));
            if is_core {
                assert_ne!(p.id, "_default", "{}: core default fell through to global default", k.id);
                assert_ne!(p.provider, "_default", "{}: resolved to the unknown-model stub", k.id);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn catalog_for_lists_concrete_models_sorted() {
        let a = catalog_for("anthropic");
        assert!(a.len() >= 10, "anthropic folder: {}", a.len());
        assert!(a.iter().all(|p| p.id != "_provider"));
        let mut ids: Vec<&str> = a.iter().map(|p| p.id.as_str()).collect();
        let sorted = ids.clone();
        ids.sort();
        assert_eq!(ids, sorted, "catalog_for must sort");
        assert!(catalog_for("no-such-provider").is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn summaries_are_human_and_safe() {
        let s = summary(find("anthropic", "claude-sonnet-5-5").unwrap());
        assert!(s.contains("1M ctx") && s.contains("128K out"), "{s}");
        let s = summary(&profile_for("ollama", "anything"));
        assert!(s.contains("? ctx"), "unknown limits must render as ?: {s}");
    }
}

## `crates/shared/src/protocol.rs`

[view on disk](crates/shared/src/protocol.rs)

````rust
//! Wire protocol — request/response types shared by the server (brain) and
//! the client TUI (screen).
//!
//! The client owns nothing but pixels: every session, every message, every
//! tool result lives server-side and reaches the screen through
//! [`Snapshot`](crate::events::Event::Snapshot) pushes plus the fine-grained
//! events in [`crate::events`]. Requests are JSON over WebSocket:
//!
//! ```json
//! {"req": 1, "body": {"type": "message", "id": 1, "text": "hi", "mode": "build"}}
//! ```
//! ```json
//! {"req": 1, "reply": {"ok": true, "data": {...}}, "event": null}
//! ```

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Session data model — serialisable, server-owned, mirrored by the client.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Build/Plan switch, mirrored in the UI footer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Mode {
    Build,
    Plan,
}

impl Mode {
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Mode::Build => "Build",
            Mode::Plan => "Plan",
        }
    }
    pub fn toggle(self) -> Self {
        match self {
            Mode::Build => Mode::Plan,
            Mode::Plan => Mode::Build,
        }
    }
}

impl Default for Mode {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Mode::Build
    }
}

/// Live state of one tool call block.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum ToolStatus {
    Running,
    Ok,
    Failed,
}

/// One block inside an assistant message.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Block {
    Text { text: String },
    Tool {
        id: String,
        name: String,
        arg: String,
        status: ToolStatus,
        extra: Option<String>,
    },
}

/// One transcript entry.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Msg {
    User {
        text: String,
    },
    Assistant {
        blocks: Vec<Block>,
        model: String,
        mode: Mode,
        secs: Option<f32>,
    },
    Notice {
        text: String,
    },
    Error {
        text: String,
    },
}

/// Todo list entry shown in the side panel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Todo {
    pub text: String,
    pub state: TodoState,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum TodoState {
    Done,
    Active,
    Open,
}

/// Fake "MCP server" summary row in the sidebar (display only).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct McpServer {
    pub name: String,
    pub tools: u32,
    pub on: bool,
}

/// One file the agent touched this session.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FileChange {
    pub path: String,
    pub added: u32,
    pub removed: u32,
}

/// One approval parked on the brain (waiting for the user's y/n). Sent in
/// `SessionSnapshot` so a (re)connecting screen re-raises the permission
/// popup instead of watching a turn that silently waits on nobody.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PendingApprovalInfo {
    pub request_id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub effect: String,
}

/// Full state of one session — what the server sends so a (re)connecting
/// client can render immediately without replaying history.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SessionSnapshot {
    pub id: usize,
    pub title: String,
    pub messages: Vec<Msg>,
    pub mode: Mode,
    pub running: bool,
    pub tokens_in: u64,
    pub tokens_out: u64,
    pub turns: u32,
    pub todos: Vec<Todo>,
    pub mcp: Vec<McpServer>,
    pub files: Vec<FileChange>,
    pub lsp: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Approvals still waiting on the brain for this session; restored as
    /// permission popups on (re)connect. `default` keeps older payloads
    /// without the field parsing.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pending_approvals: Vec<PendingApprovalInfo>,
}

/// Compact row for the session list / welcome payload.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SessionSummary {
    pub id: usize,
    pub title: String,
    pub mode: Mode,
    pub running: bool,
}

/// Android device facts for the phone panel header — the serialisable mirror
/// of the bridge `Status`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DeviceStatus {
    /// "booting" | "online" | "error:<message>"
    pub phase: String,
    pub serial: String,
    pub model: String,
    pub port: u16,
    pub root: String,
    pub display: (u32, u32),
    pub battery: u8,
    pub package_count: usize,
}

/// One provider row for the settings panel and `/providers`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ProviderInfo {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub base_url: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub has_key: bool,
    pub models: Vec<String>,
    pub default_model: Option<String>,
}

/// What `hello` answers with: everything a fresh screen needs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Welcome {
    pub server_version: String,
    pub protocol_version: u32,
    pub provider: String,
    pub model: String,
    pub mode_default: Mode,
    pub engine: String,
    pub chat_width_pct: u16,
    pub sidebar: bool,
    pub cwd: String,
    pub branch: Option<String>,
    pub providers: Vec<ProviderInfo>,
    pub sessions: Vec<SessionSummary>,
    pub device: Option<DeviceStatus>,
    /// Provider ids whose key is missing — the settings panel marks them.
    pub missing_keys: Vec<String>,
    /// Context window + prices, so the screen can draw usage bars and costs
    /// without owning the config file.
    pub context_window: u64,
    pub price_in_per_mtok: f64,
    pub price_out_per_mtok: f64,
    /// Agent settings surfaced in the settings panel (all server-owned).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub max_tool_rounds: u32,
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub webfetch_enabled: bool,
    /// The built-in rnmap scanner tool is offered (server-owned).
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub rnmap_enabled: bool,
    /// The built-in remix (rrx Ethereum toolchain) tool is offered
    /// (server-owned).
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub remix_enabled: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub request_timeout_secs: u64,
    /// The OpenCode-style TUI settings (`/settings`), server-owned.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tui: crate::tui_settings::TuiSettings,
}

fn default_true() -> bool {
    true
}

impl Welcome {
    pub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: u32 = 1;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Client → server requests.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Everything the screen can ask the brain to do.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ClientRequest {
    /// Handshake; the reply carries the [`Welcome`] payload.
    Hello { version: String },
    /// Create a session (tab). Reply carries the id.
    NewSession,
    /// Close a session tab; a running turn is cancelled first.
    CloseSession { id: usize },
    /// Subscribe to + snapshot a session (switching tabs).
    SelectSession { id: usize },
    /// Send a user prompt; the agent loop starts server-side.
    Message { id: usize, text: String, mode: Mode },
    /// Answer a pending approval prompt.
    Approval {
        session_id: usize,
        request_id: String,
        approve: bool,
    },
    /// Interrupt the running turn (esc / ctrl+c).
    Cancel { id: usize },
    /// Mid-run steering (ctrl+s on a queued query): hand `text` to the
    /// RUNNING turn. The brain shows it in the transcript at once and the
    /// agent reads it before its next model round, so the user can redirect a
    /// task without interrupting it. When the session is idle this simply
    /// starts a normal turn.
    Steer { id: usize, text: String },
    /// Toggle the session mode (Build ⇄ Plan).
    ToggleMode { id: usize },
    /// Provider / model / key slash-commands run server-side; the reply is
    /// the notice text to show. `session_id` (optional for wire
    /// compatibility) tells the brain which tab sent the command — `/skill`
    /// needs it to activate a skill on the right session.
    Command {
        text: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        session_id: Option<usize>,
    },
    /// Live model-catalog lookup for the settings panel. `provider_id` (may
    /// be empty for old clients) tells the brain which config entry the
    /// fetched catalog belongs to, so the list is REMEMBERED in that
    /// provider's model options instead of being echoed once to the asking
    /// screen and lost.
    FetchModels {
        #[serde(default)]
        provider_id: String,
        base_url: String,
        kind: String,
        api_key: String,
    },
    /// Commit the model chosen in the settings panel.
    SaveModel {
        provider_id: String,
        provider_name: String,
        base_url: String,
        api_key: String,
        kind: String,
        model: String,
        models: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// Activate a skill (an instruction package from the skills library) on
    /// session `id`: the brain resolves the name server-side and starts a
    /// turn whose prompt carries the skill body. Reply is a Notice.
    Skill { id: usize, name: String },
    /// Persist UI prefs that live in the server config (sidebar, width…).
    SetUiPref { key: String, value: String },
    /// Android device: stream toggle, taps, swipes, keys, typed text.
    Android { action: AndroidAction },
    /// Liveness probe.
    Ping,
}

/// Device input events forwarded from the phone panel / desktop window.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AndroidAction {
    /// Start/stop the frame stream for this client.
    Stream { on: bool },
    Tap { x: u32, y: u32 },
    Swipe {
        x1: u32,
        y1: u32,
        x2: u32,
        y2: u32,
    },
    Text { text: String },
    /// "home" | "back" | "enter" | "del" | "power" | "volume_up" | "volume_down"
    Key { key: String },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Server → client replies (to a specific request) and the envelope.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Reply payload variants. `None` (= plain ack) for mutations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Reply {
    Welcome(Welcome),
    NewSession { id: usize },
    Models { models: Vec<String> },
    Notice { text: String },
    Pong,
}

/// A successful reply.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReplyOk {
    pub data: Reply,
}

/// A failed reply.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReplyErr {
    pub error: String,
}

/// Envelope for one client message.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ClientEnvelope {
    pub req: u64,
    pub body: ClientRequest,
}

/// Envelope for one server message: either a reply to `req`, a pushed
/// [`crate::events::Event`], or (on error) just `error`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ServerEnvelope {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub req: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub reply: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub event: Option<crate::events::Event>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

impl ServerEnvelope {
    pub fn reply(req: u64, data: Reply) -> Self {
        Self {
            req: Some(req),
            reply: Some(serde_json::json!({ "ok": true, "data": data })),
            event: None,
            error: None,
        }
    }
    pub fn reply_err(req: u64, error: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            req: Some(req),
            reply: None,
            event: None,
            error: Some(error.into()),
        }
    }
    pub fn push(event: crate::events::Event) -> Self {
        Self {
            req: None,
            reply: None,
            event: Some(event),
            error: None,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn roundtrips_request() {
        let e = ClientEnvelope {
            req: 7,
            body: ClientRequest::Message {
                id: 3,
                text: "hello".into(),
                mode: Mode::Plan,
            },
        };
        let v = serde_json::to_string(&e).unwrap();
        let back: ClientEnvelope = serde_json::from_str(&v).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back.req, 7);
        match back.body {
            ClientRequest::Message { id, text, mode } => {
                assert_eq!(id, 3);
                assert_eq!(text, "hello");
                assert_eq!(mode, Mode::Plan);
            }
            other => panic!("wrong variant: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn roundtrips_snapshot() {
        let s = SessionSnapshot {
            id: 1,
            title: "t".into(),
            messages: vec![
                Msg::User {
                    text: "hi".into(),
                },
                Msg::Assistant {
                    blocks: vec![
                        Block::Text {
                            text: "doing it".into(),
                        },
                        Block::Tool {
                            id: "1".into(),
                            name: "Read".into(),
                            arg: "{}".into(),
                            status: ToolStatus::Ok,
                            extra: Some("ok".into()),
                        },
                    ],
                    model: "m".into(),
                    mode: Mode::Build,
                    secs: Some(1.5),
                },
            ],
            mode: Mode::Build,
            running: false,
            tokens_in: 1,
            tokens_out: 2,
            turns: 1,
            todos: vec![Todo {
                text: "x".into(),
                state: TodoState::Active,
            }],
            mcp: vec![],
            files: vec![],
            lsp: vec![],
            pending_approvals: vec![PendingApprovalInfo {
                request_id: "apr-1".into(),
                name: "Bash".into(),
                effect: "Run host shell command in project directory:\ncargo test".into(),
            }],
        };
        let v = serde_json::to_string(&s).unwrap();
        let back: SessionSnapshot = serde_json::from_str(&v).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back.messages.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(back.pending_approvals.len(), 1);

        // older payloads without the field still parse (serde default)
        let legacy = r#"{"id":1,"title":"t","messages":[],"mode":"build","running":false,"tokens_in":0,"tokens_out":0,"turns":0,"todos":[],"mcp":[],"files":[],"lsp":[]}"#;
        let back: SessionSnapshot = serde_json::from_str(legacy).unwrap();
        assert!(back.pending_approvals.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn envelope_kinds() {
        let env = ServerEnvelope::reply(3, Reply::Pong);
        assert_eq!(env.req, Some(3));
        assert!(env.reply.is_some());
        let env = ServerEnvelope::push(crate::events::Event::Done {
            session_id: 1,
            secs: 0.5,
        });
        assert!(env.event.is_some());
        let env = ServerEnvelope::reply_err(9, "nope");
        assert_eq!(env.error.as_deref(), Some("nope"));
    }
}
````

## `crates/shared/src/tui_settings.rs`

[view on disk](crates/shared/src/tui_settings.rs)

```rust
//! TUI settings — the OpenCode `/settings` option set, reproduced exactly.
//!
//! Two things live here, shared by the server (which persists them) and the
//! client TUI (which shows and edits them):
//!
//! * [`TuiSettings`] — the typed config tree (`theme`, `leader`, `scroll`,
//!   `attention`, `diffs`, `terminal`, `prompt`, `session`, `tabs`, `mini`,
//!   `debug`, `cursor`, plus the top-level `animations` / `highlights` /
//!   `mouse` / `experimental` keys). Every field has OpenCode's default.
//! * [`CATALOG`] — the rows of the settings dialog, in OpenCode's order and
//!   categories (Appearance, Session, Tabs, Diffs, Input, Alerts, Terminal,
//!   Debug), with the same titles, values, labels, steps and ranges.
//!
//! Paths are dotted (`session.thinking`). [`TuiSettings::get`] /
//! [`TuiSettings::set`] address any setting by path and validate against the
//! catalog, so the wire only ever needs `(path, value)` pairs.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

// ── typed config tree (defaults = OpenCode's) ───────────────────────────────

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct ThemeCfg {
    /// Theme name (see [`THEME_NAMES`]).
    pub name: String,
    /// `system` | `dark` | `light`.
    pub mode: String,
}
impl Default for ThemeCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { name: "opencode".into(), mode: "system".into() }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct LeaderCfg {
    /// Leader key wait time, ms.
    pub timeout: u32,
}
impl Default for LeaderCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { timeout: 2000 }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct ScrollCfg {
    /// Distance scrolled per input tick.
    pub speed: f64,
    /// Accelerate scrolling from repeated input.
    pub acceleration: bool,
}
impl Default for ScrollCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { speed: 3.0, acceleration: false }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct AttentionCfg {
    pub notifications: bool,
    pub sound: bool,
    /// 0–1.
    pub volume: f64,
    pub sound_pack: String,
    /// Sound file overrides by event (`default`, `question`, `permission`,
    /// `error`, `done`, `subagent_done`).
    pub sounds: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}
impl Default for AttentionCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            notifications: false,
            sound: false,
            volume: 0.4,
            sound_pack: "opencode.default".into(),
            sounds: BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct DiffsCfg {
    /// Initial diff source (`branch`, `turn`, …).
    pub source: String,
    /// `word` | `none`.
    pub wrap: String,
    /// Show the diff file tree.
    pub tree: bool,
    /// Show only the selected file patch.
    pub single: bool,
    /// Open the diff side panel full screen (remembers the last toggle).
    pub fullscreen: Option<bool>,
    /// `auto` | `split` | `unified`.
    pub view: String,
}
impl Default for DiffsCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            source: "branch".into(),
            wrap: "word".into(),
            tree: true,
            single: false,
            fullscreen: None,
            view: "auto".into(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct TerminalCfg {
    /// Update the terminal window title.
    pub title: bool,
    /// `manual` | `select` — `manual` on Windows, `select` elsewhere.
    pub copy: String,
}
impl Default for TerminalCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            title: true,
            copy: if cfg!(windows) { "manual" } else { "select" }.into(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct PromptCfg {
    /// Include the active editor file/selection as prompt context.
    pub editor: bool,
    /// `compact` | `full` — how large pastes are displayed.
    pub paste: String,
    /// Show image attachment previews above the prompt input.
    pub image_preview: bool,
}
impl Default for PromptCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { editor: true, paste: "compact".into(), image_preview: false }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct SessionCfg {
    /// `auto` | `hide`.
    pub sidebar: String,
    pub scrollbar: bool,
    /// `bottom` | `keep`.
    pub submit_scroll: String,
    /// `show` | `hide`.
    pub thinking: String,
    /// `auto` | `none`.
    pub grouping: String,
    /// `low` | `medium` | `high`.
    pub verbosity: String,
    pub image_preview: bool,
    /// Show output tokens per second while the model streams.
    pub tps: bool,
    /// `source` | `rendered`.
    pub markdown: String,
    /// `launch` | `inherit`.
    pub new_location: String,
    /// `prompt` | `autoaccept`.
    pub permissions: String,
}
impl Default for SessionCfg {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            sidebar: "auto".into(),
            scrollbar: false,
            submit_scroll: "bottom".into(),
            thinking: "hide".into(),
            grouping: "auto".into(),
            verbosity: "low".into(),
            image_preview: false,
            tps: true,
            markdown: "rendered".into(),
            new_location: "launch".into(),
            // Fully open default: the agent runs everything without asking.
            // "prompt" remains an explicit opt-in (Ctrl+P → PERMISSIONS).
            permissions: "autoaccept".into(),
        }
    }
}

// ── settings dialog catalog ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// How a number is shown in the dialog.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NumFmt {
    /// `3.00` (`toFixed(2)`).
    Fixed2,
    /// `2000 ms`.
    Ms,
    /// `40%` (`round(value * 100)`).
    Percent,
}

/// What kind of control a row is.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum Kind {
    /// Cycles through `values`; `labels` are what the dialog shows.
    Choice { values: &'static [&'static str], labels: &'static [&'static str] },
    /// `off` / `on`.
    Toggle,
    /// Stepped number; ← → change it by `step`, clamped to `min..=max`.
    Number { step: f64, min: f64, max: f64, fmt: NumFmt, integer: bool },
    /// Opens a picker (the theme list).
    Picker,
}

/// One row of the settings dialog.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Def {
    pub category: &'static str,
    pub title: &'static str,
    pub path: &'static str,
    pub kind: Kind,
    pub keywords: &'static [&'static str],
}

const fn choice(
    category: &'static str,
    title: &'static str,
    path: &'static str,
    values: &'static [&'static str],
    labels: &'static [&'static str],
    keywords: &'static [&'static str],
) -> Def {
    Def { category, title, path, kind: Kind::Choice { values, labels }, keywords }
}
const fn toggle(
    category: &'static str,
    title: &'static str,
    path: &'static str,
    keywords: &'static [&'static str],
) -> Def {
    Def { category, title, path, kind: Kind::Toggle, keywords }
}

/// Category order, as the dialog shows it.
pub const CATEGORIES: &[&str] =
    &["Appearance", "Session", "Tabs", "Diffs", "Input", "Alerts", "Terminal", "Debug"];

/// Every row of `/settings`, in display order.
pub const CATALOG: &[Def] = &[
    // Appearance
    Def { category: "Appearance", title: "Theme", path: "theme.name", kind: Kind::Picker, keywords: &["theme", "colors", "palette"] },
    choice("Appearance", "Color mode", "theme.mode", &["system", "dark", "light"], &["system", "dark", "light"], &["theme", "dark", "light", "mode"]),
    toggle("Appearance", "Animations", "animations", &["animation", "motion"]),
    // Session
    choice("Session", "Sidebar", "session.sidebar", &["hide", "auto"], &["hide", "auto"], &["sidebar", "panel"]),
    toggle("Session", "Scrollbar", "session.scrollbar", &["scrollbar", "scroll"]),
    choice("Session", "Scroll on send", "session.submit_scroll", &["bottom", "keep"], &["jump to latest", "keep position"], &["scroll", "submit", "send"]),
    choice("Session", "Thinking", "session.thinking", &["hide", "show"], &["hide", "show"], &["thinking", "reasoning"]),
    choice("Session", "Markdown", "session.markdown", &["source", "rendered"], &["source", "rendered"], &["markdown", "render"]),
    choice("Session", "Tool grouping", "session.grouping", &["none", "auto"], &["none", "auto"], &["tools", "grouping", "exploration"]),

    toggle("Session", "Transcript images", "session.image_preview", &["images", "preview", "transcript"]),
    toggle("Session", "TPS", "session.tps", &["tps", "tokens per second", "speed"]),

    choice("Session", "Permissions", "session.permissions", &["prompt", "autoaccept"], &["prompt", "auto accept"], &["permissions", "approve", "auto accept"]),
    // Tabs
    choice("Tabs", "Mode", "tabs.mode", &["off", "on", "auto"], &["off", "on", "auto"], &["tabs"]),
    choice("Tabs", "Scope", "tabs.scope", &["cwd", "global"], &["current directory", "global"], &["tabs", "scope"]),
    choice("Tabs", "Layout", "tabs.layout", &["horizontal", "vertical"], &["horizontal", "vertical"], &["tabs", "layout"]),
    choice("Tabs", "Indicators", "tabs.indicators", &["status", "numbers"], &["status icons", "always show numbers"], &["tabs", "indicators", "numbers"]),

    toggle("Input", "Editor context", "prompt.editor", &["editor", "context", "file"]),
    choice("Input", "Large pastes", "prompt.paste", &["compact", "full"], &["compact", "full"], &["paste", "large"]),
    toggle("Input", "Image previews", "prompt.image_preview", &["image", "preview", "attachment"]),
    Def { category: "Input", title: "Leader timeout", path: "leader.timeout", kind: Kind::Number { step: 250.0, min: 250.0, max: 10000.0, fmt: NumFmt::Ms, integer: true }, keywords: &["leader", "timeout", "key"] },

/// The built-in theme registry (32 entries) plus the dynamic ones.
pub const THEME_NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    "opencode", "system", "aura", "ayu", "catppuccin", "catppuccin-frappe",
    "catppuccin-macchiato", "cobalt2", "cursor", "dracula", "everforest", "flexoki",
    "github", "gruvbox", "kanagawa", "material", "matrix", "mercury", "monokai",
    "nightowl", "nord", "one-dark", "osaka-jade", "orng", "lucent-orng", "palenight",
    "rosepine", "solarized", "synthwave84", "tokyonight", "vesper", "vercel", "zenburn",
    "carbonfox",
];

/// `MiniWorkSpinner` values.
pub const MINI_WORK_SPINNERS: &[&str] = &[
    "block-soft-slide", "block-soft-sweep", "block-low-comet", "block-low-duet",
    "block-shuttle", "block-bridge", "block-squeeze", "small-toggle", "square-toggle",
    "grow-shrink", "quadrant-orbit", "crosshatch", "density-wave", "seed",
];

/// Look a catalog row up by path.
pub fn def(path: &str) -> Option<&'static Def> {
    CATALOG.iter().find(|d| d.path == path)
}

/// Rows matching a search query (title, category, path or keywords), in order.
pub fn search(query: &str) -> Vec<&'static Def> {
    let q = query.trim().to_lowercase();
    CATALOG
        .iter()
        .filter(|d| {
            q.is_empty()
                || d.title.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                || d.category.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                || d.path.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
                || d.keywords.iter().any(|k| k.to_lowercase().contains(&q))
        })
        .collect()
}

fn round_to(v: f64, step: f64) -> f64 {
    // Remove float drift (0.1 steps etc.).
    let inv = 1.0 / step;
    ((v * inv).round() / inv * 1e6).round() / 1e6
}

impl Def {
    /// Text the dialog shows for a raw value.
    pub fn display(&self, v: &Value) -> String {
        match self.kind {
            Kind::Choice { values, labels } => {
                let s = v.as_str().unwrap_or("");
                values
                    .iter()
                    .position(|x| *x == s)
                    .map(|i| labels[i].to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| s.to_string())
            }
            Kind::Toggle => if v.as_bool().unwrap_or(false) { "on" } else { "off" }.into(),
            Kind::Number { fmt, .. } => {
                let n = v.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
                match fmt {
                    NumFmt::Fixed2 => format!("{n:.2}"),
                    NumFmt::Ms => format!("{} ms", n.round() as i64),
                    NumFmt::Percent => format!("{}%", (n * 100.0).round() as i64),
                }
            }
            Kind::Picker => v.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        }
    }

    /// The value after stepping `dir` (+1 = right/next, -1 = left/previous)
    /// from `cur`. Choices and toggles wrap; numbers clamp.
    pub fn step(&self, cur: &Value, dir: i32) -> Value {
        match self.kind {
            Kind::Choice { values, .. } => {
                let s = cur.as_str().unwrap_or("");
                let i = values.iter().position(|x| *x == s).unwrap_or(0) as i32;
                let n = values.len() as i32;
                Value::String(values[(((i + dir) % n) + n) as usize % n as usize].into())
            }
            Kind::Toggle => Value::Bool(!cur.as_bool().unwrap_or(false)),
            Kind::Number { step, min, max, integer, .. } => {
                let n = cur.as_f64().unwrap_or(min);
                let v = round_to((n + step * dir as f64).clamp(min, max), step.min(0.01));
                if integer {
                    Value::from(v.round() as i64)
                } else {
                    Value::from(v)
                }
            }
            Kind::Picker => {
                let s = cur.as_str().unwrap_or("");
                let i = THEME_NAMES.iter().position(|x| *x == s).unwrap_or(0) as i32;
                let n = THEME_NAMES.len() as i32;
                Value::String(THEME_NAMES[(((i + dir) % n) + n) as usize % n as usize].into())
            }
        }
    }

    /// Validate (and normalise) a raw value for this row.
    pub fn validate(&self, v: &Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        match self.kind {
            Kind::Choice { values, .. } => {
                let s = v.as_str().ok_or_else(|| format!("{} expects text", self.path))?;
                if values.contains(&s) {
                    Ok(Value::String(s.into()))
                } else {
                    Err(format!("{} must be one of: {}", self.path, values.join(", ")))
                }
            }
            Kind::Toggle => v
                .as_bool()
                .map(Value::Bool)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("{} expects true or false", self.path)),
            Kind::Number { min, max, integer, .. } => {
                let n = v.as_f64().ok_or_else(|| format!("{} expects a number", self.path))?;
                if n < min || n > max {
                    return Err(format!("{} must be between {min} and {max}", self.path));
                }
                Ok(if integer { Value::from(n.round() as i64) } else { Value::from(n) })
            }
            Kind::Picker => {
                let s = v.as_str().ok_or_else(|| format!("{} expects text", self.path))?;
                if THEME_NAMES.contains(&s) {
                    Ok(Value::String(s.into()))
                } else {
                    Err(format!("unknown theme {s}"))
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Parse a wire string (`"true"`, `"0.4"`, `"dark"`) into the JSON value the
/// row expects.
pub fn parse_wire(def: &Def, raw: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let raw = raw.trim();
    match def.kind {
        Kind::Toggle => match raw.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            "true" | "1" | "on" | "yes" => Ok(Value::Bool(true)),
            "false" | "0" | "off" | "no" => Ok(Value::Bool(false)),
            _ => Err(format!("{} expects on/off", def.path)),
        },
        Kind::Number { .. } => raw
            .parse::<f64>()
            .map(Value::from)
            .map_err(|_| format!("{} expects a number", def.path)),
        _ => Ok(Value::String(raw.into())),
    }
}

impl TuiSettings {
    /// Current raw value at a dotted path.
    pub fn get(&self, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {
        let mut v = serde_json::to_value(self).ok()?;
        for part in path.split('.') {
            v = v.get(part)?.clone();
        }
        Some(v)
    }

    /// Set a catalog setting by dotted path. The value is validated against
    /// the catalog row; unknown paths are rejected.
    pub fn set(&mut self, path: &str, value: &Value) -> Result<(), String> {
        let d = def(path).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown setting {path}"))?;
        let value = d.validate(value)?;
        let mut root = serde_json::to_value(&*self).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let parts: Vec<&str> = path.split('.').collect();
        let mut cur = &mut root;
        for p in &parts[..parts.len() - 1] {
            cur = cur
                .get_mut(*p)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown setting {path}"))?;
        }
        cur[parts[parts.len() - 1]] = value;
        *self = serde_json::from_value(root).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Dialog text for a path (`"jump to latest"`, `"2000 ms"`, `"on"`).
    pub fn display(&self, path: &str) -> String {
        match (def(path), self.get(path)) {
            (Some(d), Some(v)) => d.display(&v),
            _ => String::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Step a setting left/right and return the new value.
    pub fn step(&mut self, path: &str, dir: i32) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let d = def(path).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown setting {path}"))?;
        let cur = self.get(path).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown setting {path}"))?;
        let next = d.step(&cur, dir);
        self.set(path, &next)?;
        Ok(next)
    }

    /// Clamp every catalog value into its range after loading a hand-edited
    /// file. Returns one warning per correction.
    pub fn sanitize(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut warnings = Vec::new();
        for d in CATALOG {
            let Some(cur) = self.get(d.path) else { continue };
            if d.validate(&cur).is_ok() {
                continue;
            }
            let fixed = match d.kind {
                Kind::Number { min, max, integer, .. } => {
                    let n = cur.as_f64().unwrap_or(min).clamp(min, max);
                    if integer { Value::from(n.round() as i64) } else { Value::from(n) }
                }
                Kind::Choice { values, .. } => Value::String(values[0].into()),
                Kind::Picker => Value::String("opencode".into()),
                // Normalize invalid Toggle values to the bool the readers
                // fall back to — `continue` used to leave the broken value
                // persisted while every reader silently read `false`.
                Kind::Toggle => Value::Bool(false),
            };
            if self.set(d.path, &fixed).is_ok() {
                warnings.push(format!("tui.{} out of range; using {}", d.path, d.display(&fixed)));
            }
        }
        warnings
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn catalog_paths_exist_in_the_tree_and_defaults_validate() {
        let t = TuiSettings::default();
        for d in CATALOG {
            let v = t.get(d.path).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing {}", d.path));
            d.validate(&v).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{e}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn catalog_has_every_opencode_setting_in_order() {
        assert_eq!(CATALOG.len(), 36);
        let cats: Vec<&str> = {
            let mut c: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
            for d in CATALOG {
                if c.last() != Some(&d.category) {
                    c.push(d.category);
                }
            }
            c
        };
        assert_eq!(cats, CATEGORIES);
        assert_eq!(THEME_NAMES.len(), 34);
        assert_eq!(MINI_WORK_SPINNERS.len(), 14);
    }

    #[test]
    fn opencode_defaults() {
        let t = TuiSettings::default();
        assert_eq!(t.theme.name, "opencode");
        assert_eq!(t.theme.mode, "system");
        assert_eq!(t.leader.timeout, 2000);
        assert_eq!(t.scroll.speed, 3.0);
        assert!(!t.scroll.acceleration);
        assert_eq!(t.attention.volume, 0.4);
        assert_eq!(t.attention.sound_pack, "opencode.default");
        assert_eq!(t.diffs.source, "branch");
        assert_eq!(t.diffs.view, "auto");
        assert!(t.diffs.tree && !t.diffs.single);
        assert!(t.prompt.editor && !t.prompt.image_preview);
        assert_eq!(t.prompt.paste, "compact");
        assert_eq!(t.session.sidebar, "auto");
        assert_eq!(t.session.thinking, "hide");
        assert_eq!(t.session.verbosity, "low");
        assert!(t.session.tps);
        // shipped default is fully open (the agent runs everything)
        assert_eq!(t.session.permissions, "autoaccept");
        assert_eq!(t.tabs.mode, "auto");
        assert_eq!(t.tabs.scope, "cwd");
        assert!(t.animations && t.highlights && t.mouse);
        assert_eq!(t.cursor.style, "block");
        assert!(t.cursor.blinking);
    }

    #[test]
    fn choice_cycles_and_wraps_both_ways() {
        let mut t = TuiSettings::default();
        assert_eq!(t.step("session.verbosity", 1).unwrap(), "medium");
        assert_eq!(t.step("session.verbosity", 1).unwrap(), "high");
        assert_eq!(t.step("session.verbosity", 1).unwrap(), "low");
        assert_eq!(t.step("session.verbosity", -1).unwrap(), "high");
        assert_eq!(t.display("session.submit_scroll"), "jump to latest");
        t.step("session.submit_scroll", 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.display("session.submit_scroll"), "keep position");
    }

    #[test]
    fn numbers_step_clamp_and_format() {
        let mut t = TuiSettings::default();
        assert_eq!(t.display("scroll.speed"), "3.00");
        t.step("scroll.speed", 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.display("scroll.speed"), "3.25");
        for _ in 0..100 {
            t.step("scroll.speed", 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(t.display("scroll.speed"), "10.00");
        for _ in 0..100 {
            t.step("scroll.speed", -1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(t.display("scroll.speed"), "0.25");

        assert_eq!(t.display("leader.timeout"), "2000 ms");
        t.step("leader.timeout", 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.leader.timeout, 2250);
        for _ in 0..100 {
            t.step("leader.timeout", -1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(t.leader.timeout, 250);

        assert_eq!(t.display("attention.volume"), "40%");
        t.step("attention.volume", 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.display("attention.volume"), "50%");
        for _ in 0..20 {
            t.step("attention.volume", -1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(t.display("attention.volume"), "0%");
    }

    #[test]
    fn toggles_and_picker() {
        let mut t = TuiSettings::default();
        assert_eq!(t.display("animations"), "on");
        t.step("animations", 1).unwrap();
        assert!(!t.animations);
        assert_eq!(t.step("theme.name", 1).unwrap(), "system");
        assert_eq!(t.step("theme.name", -1).unwrap(), "opencode");
        assert_eq!(t.step("theme.name", -1).unwrap(), "carbonfox");
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_validates_and_rejects_unknown() {
        let mut t = TuiSettings::default();
        assert!(t.set("session.thinking", &Value::from("show")).is_ok());
        assert_eq!(t.session.thinking, "show");
        assert!(t.set("session.thinking", &Value::from("loud")).is_err());
        assert!(t.set("leader.timeout", &Value::from(100)).is_err());
        assert!(t.set("nope.nothing", &Value::from(1)).is_err());
        assert!(t.set("theme.name", &Value::from("not-a-theme")).is_err());
        assert_eq!(t.session.thinking, "show");
    }

    #[test]
    fn wire_parsing() {
        let d = def("mouse").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parse_wire(d, "off").unwrap(), Value::Bool(false));
        let d = def("attention.volume").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parse_wire(d, "0.7").unwrap(), Value::from(0.7));
        assert!(parse_wire(d, "loud").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn sanitize_clamps_hand_edited_values() {
        let mut t: TuiSettings = serde_json::from_str(
            r#"{"leader":{"timeout":99999},"session":{"verbosity":"ultra"},"scroll":{"speed":50}}"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let w = t.sanitize();
        assert_eq!(w.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(t.leader.timeout, 10000);
        assert_eq!(t.session.verbosity, "low");
        assert_eq!(t.scroll.speed, 10.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn json_roundtrip_and_partial_file() {
        let t: TuiSettings = serde_json::from_str(r#"{"session":{"thinking":"show"}}"#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.session.thinking, "show");
        assert_eq!(t.session.sidebar, "auto"); // untouched default
        let back: TuiSettings = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::to_value(&t).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, t);
    }

    #[test]
    fn search_matches_title_category_and_keywords() {
        assert_eq!(search("").len(), CATALOG.len());
        assert!(search("tabs").iter().all(|d| d.category == "Tabs" || d.keywords.contains(&"tabs")));
        assert!(search("leader").iter().any(|d| d.path == "leader.timeout"));
        assert!(search("zzzz").is_empty());
    }
}

name = "romacode_tunnel"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "romacode-tunnel"
path = "bin/chisel_main.rs"

[dependencies]
# Pure-Rust, std-only. No external crates — matches the chisel-rs design and
# the RomaCode self-contained tooling philosophy.

# the server-side wrapper serialises tunnel control through std::thread and
# std::sync::mpsc; the engine itself owns no async runtime.

## `crates/tunnel/bin/chisel_main.rs`

[view on disk](crates/tunnel/bin/chisel_main.rs)

```rust
//! Chisel-rs — entry point.
//!
//! Usage:
//!   chisel server --port 8080 [--auth TOKEN] [--reverse]
//!   chisel client <host:port> [remote...] [--auth TOKEN] [--header K:V]
//!
//! Remotes (chisel syntax):
//!   3000
//!   example.com:3000
//!   3000:google.com:80
//!   192.168.0.5:3000:google.com:80
//!   R:2222:localhost:22
//!   R:0.0.0.0:8080:internal:80/tcp
//!
//! This binary is a single executable serving both as client and server,
//! mirroring the original chisel UX.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::process::ExitCode;

use romacode_tunnel::client::ClientConfig;
use romacode_tunnel::log;
use romacode_tunnel::remote::Remote;
use romacode_tunnel::server::ServerConfig;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();

    // Global --verbose / --quiet flag may appear before the subcommand.
    let (verbose, args) = strip_flag(&args, "--verbose", "-v");
    let (quiet, args) = strip_flag(&args, "--quiet", "-q");
    let (show_ver, args) = strip_flag(&args, "--version", "-V");
    let (show_help, args) = strip_flag(&args, "--help", "-h");

    if show_ver {
        println!("chisel-rs {}", romacode_tunnel::VERSION);
        return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
    }
    if args.is_empty() || show_help {
        print_help();
        return if args.is_empty() { ExitCode::FAILURE } else { ExitCode::SUCCESS };
    }

    let level = if verbose { 3 } else if quiet { 1 } else { 2 };
    log::set_level(level);

    let sub = args[0].as_str();
    let rest: Vec<String> = args[1..].to_vec();

    match sub {
        "server" => match run_server(rest) {
            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("server error: {}", e);
                ExitCode::FAILURE
            }
        },
        "client" => match run_client(rest) {
            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("client error: {}", e);
                ExitCode::FAILURE
            }
        },
        other => {
            eprintln!("unknown subcommand: {}\n", other);
            print_help();
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

fn strip_flag(args: &[String], long: &str, short: &str) -> (bool, Vec<String>) {
    let mut found = false;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());
    for a in args {
        if a == long || a == short {
            found = true;
        } else {
            out.push(a.clone());
        }
    }
    (found, out)
}

fn print_help() {
    print!(
        r#"chisel-rs {ver} — a fast TCP tunnel over WebSocket, pure-Rust, std-only.

USAGE:
    chisel server --port <port> [--auth <token>] [--reverse]
    chisel client <server-host:port> <remote>... [--auth <token>]

EXAMPLES:
    # Run a server on port 8080 with auth token "secret"
    chisel server --port 8080 --auth secret

    # Forward local 3000 to remote google.com:80 through the server
    chisel client 127.0.0.1:8080 3000:google.com:80 --auth secret

    # Reverse: server listens on 2222, client forwards to its local :22
    chisel server --port 8080 --auth secret --reverse
    chisel client 127.0.0.1:8080 R:2222:localhost:22 --auth secret

REMOTE SPEC:
    <local-host>:<local-port>:<remote-host>:<remote-port>/<proto>
    local-host defaults to 0.0.0.0; local-port defaults to remote-port;
    remote-host defaults to 127.0.0.1; proto defaults to tcp.
    Prefix "R:" for a reverse remote (server listens, client dials).

NOTE: this is a chisel-shaped tunnel (same remote syntax, forward +
reverse model, single-binary client+server). It is NOT wire-compatible
with jpillora/chisel (which uses crypto/ssh). Transport is plaintext
WebSocket + token auth — use behind TLS or in a trusted network.

FLAGS:
    -h, --help       show this help
    -V, --version    print version
    -v, --verbose    debug logging
    -q, --quiet      errors only
"#,
        ver = romacode_tunnel::VERSION
    );
}

fn run_server(args: Vec<String>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut port: u16 = 0;
    let mut host = String::from("0.0.0.0");
    let mut auth: Option<String> = None;
    let mut reverse = false;
    let mut keepalive: u64 = 25;

    let mut i = 0;
    while i < args.len() {
        match args[i].as_str() {
            "--port" | "-p" => {
                i += 1;
                port = args
                    .get(i)
                    .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
                    .ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "--port needs a value"))?;
            }
            "--host" => {
                i += 1;
                host = args
                    .get(i)
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "--host needs a value"))?;
            }
            "--auth" => {
                i += 1;
                auth = args.get(i).cloned();
            }
            "--reverse" => reverse = true,
            "--keepalive" => {
                i += 1;
                keepalive = args
                    .get(i)
                    .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
                    .unwrap_or(25);
            }
            "--header" => {
                // server ignores custom headers
                i += 1;
            }
            other => {
                return Err(std::io::Error::new(
                    std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                    format!("server: unknown flag {}", other),
                ));
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }

    if port == 0 {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
            "--port is required",
        ));
    }

    // For --reverse without explicit remotes, do nothing special —
    // the client will send R: remotes and the server will accept them
    // (server allows reverse because --reverse was set).
    let rev_remotes = Vec::new();

    let cfg = ServerConfig {
        listen: format!("{}:{}", host, port),
        auth,
        reverse,
        reverse_remotes: rev_remotes,
        keepalive,
    };
    romacode_tunnel::server::run(cfg)
}

fn run_client(args: Vec<String>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    if args.is_empty() {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
            "client needs a <server> argument",
        ));
    }
    let mut server: Option<String> = None;
    let mut auth: Option<String> = None;
    let mut headers: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    let mut keepalive: u64 = 25;
    let mut max_retry: u64 = 1;
    let mut remotes: Vec<Remote> = Vec::new();

    let mut i = 0;
    while i < args.len() {
        let a = &args[i];
        if a == "--auth" || a == "-A" {
            i += 1;
            auth = args.get(i).cloned();
        } else if a == "--header" || a == "-H" {
            i += 1;
            if let Some(h) = args.get(i) {
                if let Some((k, v)) = h.split_once(':') {
                    headers.insert(k.trim().to_string(), v.trim().to_string());
                }
            }
        } else if a == "--keepalive" {
            i += 1;
            keepalive = args.get(i).and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(25);
        } else if a == "--max-retry" {
            i += 1;
            max_retry = args.get(i).and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(1);
        } else if a.starts_with("--") {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                format!("client: unknown flag {}", a),
            ));
        } else if server.is_none() {
            server = Some(a.clone());
        } else {
            match Remote::parse(a) {
                Ok(r) => remotes.push(r),
                Err(e) => {
                    return Err(std::io::Error::new(
                        std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                        format!("bad remote '{}': {}", a, e),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }

    let server = server.ok_or_else(|| {
        std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "no <server> provided")
    })?;

    if remotes.is_empty() {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
            "no remotes provided",
        ));
    }

    // Pretty-print the plan
    for r in &remotes {
        let kind = if r.reverse { "reverse" } else { "forward" };
        log::info(
            "client",
            &format!("{} remote {} ({} -> {}:{})", kind, r.summary(), r.local_host, r.remote_host, r.remote_port),
        );
    }

    let cfg = ClientConfig {
        server,
        auth,
        headers,
        remotes,
        keepalive,
        max_retry,
    };
    romacode_tunnel::client::run(cfg)
}
```

```rust
//! RFC 4648 base64 (standard alphabet) — encode + decode.

const ALPHA: &[u8; 64] =
    b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";

pub fn encode(input: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity((input.len() + 2) / 3 * 4);
    let mut chunks = input.chunks_exact(3);
    for c in chunks.by_ref() {
        let n = ((c[0] as u32) << 16) | ((c[1] as u32) << 8) | (c[2] as u32);
        out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 18) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
        out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 12) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
        out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 6) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
        out.push(ALPHA[(n & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
    }
    let rem = chunks.remainder();
    match rem.len() {
        1 => {
            let n = (rem[0] as u32) << 16;
            out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 18) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
            out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 12) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
            out.push('=');
            out.push('=');
        }
        2 => {
            let n = ((rem[0] as u32) << 16) | ((rem[1] as u32) << 8);
            out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 18) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
            out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 12) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
            out.push(ALPHA[((n >> 6) & 0x3F) as usize] as char);
            out.push('=');
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    out
}

fn val(c: u8) -> Option<u8> {
    match c {
        b'A'..=b'Z' => Some(c - b'A'),
        b'a'..=b'z' => Some(c - b'a' + 26),
        b'0'..=b'9' => Some(c - b'0' + 52),
        b'+' => Some(62),
        b'/' => Some(63),
        _ => None,
    }
}

pub fn decode(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, &'static str> {
    let bytes: Vec<u8> = input.bytes().filter(|&b| b != b'\r' && b != b'\n' && b != b' ').collect();
    if bytes.len() % 4 != 0 {
        return Err("base64: length not multiple of 4");
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len() / 4 * 3);
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let b0 = bytes[i];
        let b1 = bytes[i + 1];
        let b2 = bytes[i + 2];
        let b3 = bytes[i + 3];
        let v0 = val(b0).ok_or("base64: invalid char")?;
        let v1 = val(b1).ok_or("base64: invalid char")?;
        let n = ((v0 as u32) << 18)
            | ((v1 as u32) << 12)
            | (if b2 == b'=' { 0 } else { val(b2).ok_or("base64: invalid char")? as u32 } << 6)
            | (if b3 == b'=' { 0 } else { val(b3).ok_or("base64: invalid char")? as u32 });
        out.push((n >> 16) as u8);
        if b2 != b'=' {
            out.push((n >> 8) as u8);
        }
        if b3 != b'=' {
            out.push(n as u8);
        }
        i += 4;
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn roundtrip() {
        for s in &["", "f", "fo", "foo", "foob", "fooba", "foobar"] {
            assert_eq!(decode(&encode(s.as_bytes())).unwrap(), s.as_bytes());
        }
        assert_eq!(encode(b"foobar"), "Zm9vYmFy");
        assert_eq!(encode(b"foo"), "Zm9v");
    }
}
