## `crates/tunnel/src/client.rs`

[view on disk](crates/tunnel/src/client.rs)

```rust
//! Chisel client.
//!
//! - Connects to the server URL (ws://host:port, with optional ?token=).
//! - For each *forward* remote, listens on local_host:local_port; on
//!   accept, sends Open to the server which dials remote_host:remote_port.
//! - For *reverse* remotes, registers them with the server so it knows
//!   to dial back to this client when a TCP conn arrives on the server.
//! - Handles Open messages from the server (reverse case) by dialing
//!   the requested target locally and piping.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::log;
use crate::mux::{self, AddrTarget, Mux};
use crate::remote::Remote;
use crate::ws;

pub struct ClientConfig {
    pub server: String,           // host:port
    pub auth: Option<String>,
    pub headers: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub remotes: Vec<Remote>,
    pub keepalive: u64,
    pub max_retry: u64,
}

pub fn run(cfg: ClientConfig) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    // max_retry = number of reconnects after the first failure; 0 means
    // no retry (the embedded server transport relies on that). Any
    // nonzero value must stop counting once the budget is used up.
    let mut attempts: u64 = 0;
    loop {
        match connect_once(&cfg) {
            Ok(()) => {
                log::info("client", "connection ended normally");
                break;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                log::err("client", &format!("connect_once: {}", e));
                if cfg.max_retry == 0 || attempts >= cfg.max_retry {
                    return Err(e);
                }
                attempts += 1;
                let backoff = std::cmp::min(30, 1 + (attempts % 30));
                log::info("client", &format!("retrying in {}s", backoff));
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(backoff));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn connect_once(cfg: &ClientConfig) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let keepalive = cfg.keepalive;
    let mut sock = TcpStream::connect(&cfg.server)?;
    let _ = sock.set_nodelay(true);
    let (host, port) = split_host_port(&cfg.server);
    ws::client_handshake(&mut sock, host, port, cfg.auth.as_deref(), &cfg.headers)
        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, e))?;
    log::info("client", &format!("connected to {}", cfg.server));

    let mux = Mux::new(sock, true, "client".into());

    // Send Setup message for any reverse remotes we want the server to
    // listen on (and forward back to us via Open).
    let rev_remotes: Vec<mux::SetupRemote> = cfg
        .remotes
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| r.reverse && r.proto == crate::remote::Proto::Tcp)
        .map(|r| mux::SetupRemote {
            local_host: r.local_host.clone(),
            local_port: r.local_port,
            remote_host: r.remote_host.clone(),
            remote_port: r.remote_port,
            proto: 0,
        })
        .collect();
    if !rev_remotes.is_empty() {
        if let Err(e) = mux.send_setup(&rev_remotes) {
            log::err("client", &format!("Setup send failed: {}", e));
        }
    }

    // Set up forward remote listeners.
    for r in &cfg.remotes {
        if r.reverse {
            // Reverse: server will initiate Open messages to us.
            // (We just need to make sure the server knows it's allowed to —
            // that's enforced by the server config, not by the client.)
            continue;
        }
        let mux = mux.clone();
        let r = r.clone();
        let listen_addr = format!("{}:{}", r.local_host, r.local_port);
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let listener = match TcpListener::bind(&listen_addr) {
                Ok(l) => l,
                Err(e) => {
                    log::err("client", &format!("forward bind {} failed: {}", listen_addr, e));
                    return;
                }
            };
            log::info("client", &format!("forward listening on {} -> {}:{}", listen_addr, r.remote_host, r.remote_port));
            for sock in listener.incoming() {
                let sock = match sock { Ok(s) => s, Err(_) => continue };
                if mux.is_closed() { break; }
                let target = AddrTarget {
                    host: r.remote_host.clone(),
                    port: r.remote_port,
                };
                mux.open_session(target, sock);
            }
        });
    }

    // Keepalive pinger.
    if keepalive > 0 {
        let m = mux.clone();
        let ka = keepalive;
        std::thread::spawn(move || loop {
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(ka));
            if m.is_closed() { break; }
            if let Err(e) = m.send_ping(b"ka") {
                log::debug("client", &format!("ping err: {}", e));
                break;
            }
        });
    }

    // Run the mux loop. On Open from the server (reverse remote), the
    // client dials the requested target. The client never receives a
    // Setup message (it sends one), so on_setup is a no-op.
    let m = mux.clone();
    m.run_loop(
        move |target, id| {
            log::info("client", &format!("reverse session {} -> dial {}:{}", id, target.host, target.port));
            match mux::dial(&target) {
                Ok(s) => Some(s),
                Err(e) => {
                    log::err("client", &format!("dial {}:{} failed: {}", target.host, target.port, e));
                    None
                }
            }
        },
        |_| {},
    );

    Ok(())
}

fn split_host_port(s: &str) -> (&str, u16) {
    // handle [ipv6]:port
    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix('[') {
        if let Some(idx) = rest.find(']') {
            let host = &rest[..idx];
            let port: u16 = rest[idx + 2..].parse().unwrap_or(0);
            return (host, port);
        }
    }
    let (h, p) = s.rsplit_once(':').unwrap_or((s, "0"));
    let port: u16 = p.parse().unwrap_or(0);
    (h, port)
}
```

//! Lowercase hex encode (for debug/fingerprint output).

pub fn encode(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(b.len() * 2);
    for &x in b {
        s.push(hex_digit(x >> 4) as char);
        s.push(hex_digit(x & 0x0f) as char);
    }
    s
}

fn hex_digit(n: u8) -> u8 {
    if n < 10 { b'0' + n } else { b'a' + (n - 10) }
}

[view on disk](crates/tunnel/src/http.rs)

```rust
//! A tiny HTTP request/response parser used only for the WebSocket
//! handshake. It assumes the underlying TCP stream is in clear-text
//! (chisel-rs does not implement TLS, since TLS from scratch is unsafe).

use std::collections::HashMap;

pub struct Request {
    pub method: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub headers: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

pub struct Response {
    pub status: u16,
    pub reason: String,
    pub headers: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Read an HTTP message from a stream until the headers' terminating
/// blank line, returning the raw bytes of the header block (so the
/// caller can inspect how many bytes were consumed).
pub fn read_request<R: std::io::Read>(r: &mut R) -> std::io::Result<Request> {
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    let mut tmp = [0u8; 1];
    loop {
        let n = r.read(&mut tmp)?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionAborted,
                "EOF before end of HTTP headers",
            ));
        }
        buf.push(tmp[0]);
        if buf.len() >= 4 && &buf[buf.len() - 4..] == b"\r\n\r\n" {
            break;
        }
        if buf.len() > 65536 {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
                "HTTP headers too large",
            ));
        }
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);
    let mut lines = text.split("\r\n");
    let start = lines.next().ok_or_else(|| {
        std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "empty HTTP request")
    })?;
    let mut parts = start.splitn(3, ' ');
    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let path = parts.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();

    let mut headers = HashMap::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(idx) = line.find(':') {
            let k = line[..idx].trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
            let v = line[idx + 1..].trim().to_string();
            headers.insert(k, v);
        }
    }
    Ok(Request {
        method,
        path,
        headers,
        body: Vec::new(),
    })
}

impl Response {
    pub fn serialize(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        out.extend_from_slice(format!("HTTP/1.1 {} {}\r\n", self.status, self.reason).as_bytes());
        for (k, v) in &self.headers {
            out.extend_from_slice(format!("{}: {}\r\n", k, v).as_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
        out.extend_from_slice(&self.body);
        out
    }
}
```

````rust
//! Pure-Rust, std-only reimplementation of the chisel TCP tunnel.
//!
//! Architecture (mirrors jpillora/chisel, but with WebSocket instead of SSH
//! as the multiplexed transport, since SSH-from-scratch would be unsafe
//! and not wire-compatible anyway):
//!
//! ```text
//!   Client side                                 Server side
//!   ----------                                  ----------
//!   chisel client <server> <remote>...          chisel server --port 8080 --auth token
//!
//!   TCP listener  --.        .-->  WS TCP conn  --.        .-->  Dial target
//!   (forward)       \       /      (HTTP upgrade  \       /      (remote-host:remote-port)
//!                    \     /       + token auth)  \     /
//!                     \   /                        \   /
//!                      mux                          mux
//!                  (frame = msg)
//!
//!   Reverse: server listens, dials-back through client.
//! ```
//!
//! Wire protocol (binary frames inside WS):
//!   - byte 0:        message type
//!   - bytes 1..9:    session id (u64 big-endian)
//!   - rest:          payload (length depends on type)
//!
//! Message types:
//!   0x01 Open   payload = u8 addr_type + u16 port (BE) + variable addr
//!                addr_type: 0=ipv4(4B), 1=ipv6(16B), 2=hostname(len-prefixed u8)
//!   0x02 Data   payload = raw bytes
//!   0x03 Close  payload = empty
//!   0x04 Ping   payload = arbitrary (echoed back)
//!   0x05 Pong   payload = arbitrary
//!   0x06 Hello payload = JSON-ish (we use a minimal hand-rolled text format)
//!                       {"auth":"<token>","version":"0.1","reverse":bool}
//!
//! The transport is chisel-shaped (same remote spec, same forward/reverse
//! model, same single-binary client+server design) but NOT wire-compatible
//! with the original Go chisel, which uses crypto/ssh.

#![allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]

pub mod base64;
pub mod hex;
pub mod http;
pub mod log;
pub mod mux;
pub mod remote;
pub mod sha1;
pub mod ws;

pub mod client;
pub mod server;

/// DB-transport wrapper: a `Tunnel` runs chisel in-process on a background
/// thread and exposes a local `host:port` the db tools connect to.
pub mod transport;
pub use transport::Tunnel;

pub const VERSION: &str = "0.1.0";
````

//! Tiny stderr logger with timestamps. No external dep.

use std::io::Write;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

static LEVEL: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(2); // 0=quiet,1=err,2=info,3=debug

pub fn set_level(level: usize) {
    LEVEL.store(level, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

pub fn level() -> usize {
    LEVEL.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

fn now() -> String {
    let secs = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let days = secs / 86400;
    let s = secs % 86400;
    let h = s / 3600;
    let m = (s % 3600) / 60;
    let sec = s % 60;
    // day-zero is 1970-01-01; print only HH:MM:SS plus a relative day counter
    format!("D{}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}", days, h, m, sec)
}

pub fn log(lvl: usize, tag: &str, msg: &str) {
    if lvl > level() {
        return;
    }
    let prefix = match lvl {
        1 => "ERR",
        3 => "DBG",
        _ => "INF",
    };
    let line = format!("[{}] {} {} {}\n", now(), prefix, tag, msg);
    let _ = std::io::stderr().write_all(line.as_bytes());
}

pub fn info(tag: &str, msg: &str) {
    log(2, tag, msg);
}
pub fn debug(tag: &str, msg: &str) {
    log(3, tag, msg);
}
pub fn err(tag: &str, msg: &str) {
    log(1, tag, msg);
}

```rust
//! Multiplexer over a WebSocket connection.
//!
//! Each WebSocket connection carries multiple independent TCP sessions.
//! A session is a stream of bytes flowing both ways inside a single
//! shared transport.
//!
//! Wire format per WS binary frame (big-endian):
//!   [u8 type][u64 session-id][u16 be payload-len][payload-bytes]
//! The 2-byte payload length caps a single frame at 65535 bytes —
//! large writes are split, just like SSH channel data.
//!
//! Message types:
//!   0x01 Open  payload = addr-port-info (see below)
//!   0x02 Data  payload = raw stream bytes
//!   0x03 Close no payload
//!   0x04 Ping  payload = opaque (echoed in Pong)
//!   0x05 Pong  payload = opaque
//!
//! Open payload format:
//!   [u8 addr_type][addr bytes][u16 be port]
//!   addr_type 0=ipv4 (4B), 1=ipv6 (16B), 2=hostname (u8 len + N bytes)
//! The Open message is sent by whichever side initiates a session:
//!   - For forward remotes, the *client* sends Open when it accepts a
//!     local TCP connection, asking the server to dial.
//!   - For reverse remotes, the *server* sends Open when it accepts a
//!     TCP connection, asking the client to dial.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::net::{TcpStream, ToSocketAddrs};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::log;
use crate::ws::{Frame, OpCode};

pub const MSG_OPEN: u8 = 0x01;
pub const MSG_DATA: u8 = 0x02;
pub const MSG_CLOSE: u8 = 0x03;
pub const MSG_PING: u8 = 0x04;
pub const MSG_PONG: u8 = 0x05;
pub const MSG_SETUP: u8 = 0x06;

const MAX_PAYLOAD: usize = 32 * 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AddrTarget {
    pub host: String,
    pub port: u16,
}

impl AddrTarget {
    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        // Try ipv4
        if let Ok(b) = self.host.parse::<std::net::Ipv4Addr>() {
            let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(4 + 2);
            v.push(0u8);
            v.extend_from_slice(&b.octets());
            v.extend_from_slice(&self.port.to_be_bytes());
            return v;
        }
        if let Ok(b) = self.host.parse::<std::net::Ipv6Addr>() {
            let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(16 + 2);
            v.push(1u8);
            v.extend_from_slice(&b.octets());
            v.extend_from_slice(&self.port.to_be_bytes());
            return v;
        }
        // hostname
        let bytes = self.host.as_bytes();
        let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 1 + bytes.len() + 2);
        v.push(2u8);
        v.push(bytes.len() as u8);
        v.extend_from_slice(bytes);
        v.extend_from_slice(&self.port.to_be_bytes());
        v
    }

    pub fn decode(buf: &[u8]) -> Result<AddrTarget, String> {
        if buf.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty Open payload".into());
        }
        let t = buf[0];
        match t {
            0 => {
                if buf.len() != 1 + 4 + 2 {
                    return Err("bad ipv4 Open".into());
                }
                let mut o = [0u8; 4];
                o.copy_from_slice(&buf[1..5]);
                let port = u16::from_be_bytes([buf[5], buf[6]]);
                Ok(AddrTarget {
                    host: std::net::Ipv4Addr::from(o).to_string(),
                    port,
                })
            }
            1 => {
                if buf.len() != 1 + 16 + 2 {
                    return Err("bad ipv6 Open".into());
                }
                let mut o = [0u8; 16];
                o.copy_from_slice(&buf[1..17]);
                let port = u16::from_be_bytes([buf[17], buf[18]]);
                Ok(AddrTarget {
                    host: std::net::Ipv6Addr::from(o).to_string(),
                    port,
                })
            }
            2 => {
                if buf.len() < 3 {
                    return Err("bad hostname Open".into());
                }
                let l = buf[1] as usize;
                if buf.len() != 1 + 1 + l + 2 {
                    return Err("hostname Open length mismatch".into());
                }
                let host = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[2..2 + l]).to_string();
                let port = u16::from_be_bytes([buf[2 + l], buf[2 + l + 1]]);
                Ok(AddrTarget { host, port })
            }
            _ => Err(format!("unknown addr_type {}", t)),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Mux {
    pub stream: Arc<Mutex<TcpStream>>,
    pub sessions: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Arc<Session>>>>,
    pub next_id: AtomicU64,
    pub closed: AtomicBool,
    pub is_client: bool, // masking direction
    pub tag: String,
}

pub struct Session {
    pub id: u64,
    pub local: Option<TcpStream>,
    pub target: AddrTarget,
    pub closed: AtomicBool,
}

/// A reverse-remote descriptor exchanged in the Setup message.
/// proto is `0`=tcp, `1`=udp.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SetupRemote {
    pub local_host: String,
    pub local_port: u16,
    pub remote_host: String,
    pub remote_port: u16,
    pub proto: u8,
}

impl Mux {
    pub fn new(stream: TcpStream, is_client: bool, tag: String) -> Arc<Mux> {
        let _ = stream.set_nodelay(true);
        Arc::new(Mux {
            stream: Arc::new(Mutex::new(stream)),
            sessions: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
            // Direction-aware ID space: client-allocated IDs are even,
            // server-allocated IDs are odd. The peer uses the opposite
            // parity, so a reverse Open from the peer can never collide
            // with a locally allocated session in `sessions`.
            next_id: AtomicU64::new(if is_client { 2 } else { 1 }),
            closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
            is_client,
            tag,
        })
    }

    /// Allocate a session ID with this side's parity (client even,
    /// server odd). `open_session` and the reverse listeners both go
    /// through here so local allocation never produces a peer parity ID.
    pub fn alloc_id(self: &Arc<Self>) -> u64 {
        let raw = self.next_id.fetch_add(2, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let want_odd = !self.is_client;
        if (raw % 2 == 1) != want_odd {
            raw + 1
        } else {
            raw
        }
    }

    /// Send an Open message and spawn the session pipe.
    pub fn open_session(self: &Arc<Self>, target: AddrTarget, local: TcpStream) -> u64 {
        let id = self.alloc_id();
        let sess = Arc::new(Session {
            id,
            local: Some(local),
            target: target.clone(),
            closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
        });
        self.sessions.lock().unwrap().insert(id, sess.clone());

        let open = encode_msg(MSG_OPEN, id, &target.encode());
        if let Err(e) = self.send_raw(&open) {
            log::err(&self.tag, &format!("open send: {}", e));
            self.close_session(id);
            return id;
        }

        let mux = self.clone();
        let tag = self.tag.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            mux.pipe_local_to_remote(id, sess);
            let _ = &tag;
        });
        id
    }

    /// Spawn an Open for a session that has no local stream yet — used
    /// by the *server* when it gets a TCP connection for a reverse
    /// remote and needs to ask the client to dial.
    pub fn open_session_dial_later(
        self: &Arc<Self>,
        id: u64,
        target: AddrTarget,
    ) -> Result<(), String> {
        let open = encode_msg(MSG_OPEN, id, &target.encode());
        self.send_raw(&open)?;
        let sess = Arc::new(Session {
            id,
            local: None,
            target: target.clone(),
            closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
        });
        self.sessions.lock().unwrap().insert(id, sess);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn pipe_local_to_remote(self: Arc<Self>, id: u64, sess: Arc<Session>) {
        let mut buf = [0u8; MAX_PAYLOAD];
        loop {
            if sess.closed.load(Ordering::SeqCst) || self.closed.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                break;
            }
            // Read::read is implemented for &TcpStream, so we can borrow
            // the local stream out of the session and read it directly.
            let local_ref = match sess.local.as_ref() {
                Some(s) => s,
                None => break,
            };
            let n = match (&*local_ref).read(&mut buf) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(n) => n,
                Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                Err(_) => break,
            };
            let data = encode_msg(MSG_DATA, id, &buf[..n]);
            if let Err(e) = self.send_raw(&data) {
                log::debug(&self.tag, &format!("session {} data send err: {}", id, e));
                break;
            }
        }
        // Tell remote we're done.
        let _ = self.send_raw(&encode_msg(MSG_CLOSE, id, &[]));
        self.close_session(id);
    }

    pub fn send_raw(self: &Arc<Self>, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut s = self.stream.lock().unwrap();
        let frame = Frame {
            fin: true,
            op: OpCode::Binary,
            payload: bytes.to_vec(),
        };
        Frame::write(&mut *s, &frame, self.is_client)
    }

    pub fn send_setup(self: &Arc<Self>, remotes: &[SetupRemote]) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut payload = Vec::new();
        for r in remotes {
            let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(1 + r.local_host.len() + 2 + 2 + 1 + r.remote_host.len() + 2);
            // local_host as hostname-encoded, then local_port, remote_host, remote_port, proto
            let lh = r.local_host.as_bytes();
            v.push(2u8);
            v.push(lh.len() as u8);
            v.extend_from_slice(lh);
            v.extend_from_slice(&r.local_port.to_be_bytes());
            let rh = r.remote_host.as_bytes();
            v.push(2u8);
            v.push(rh.len() as u8);
            v.extend_from_slice(rh);
            v.extend_from_slice(&r.remote_port.to_be_bytes());
            v.push(r.proto);
            payload.extend_from_slice(&v);
        }
        let msg = encode_msg(MSG_SETUP, 0, &payload);
        self.send_raw(&msg)
    }

    /// Decode a Setup payload back into a list of remote descriptors.
    pub fn decode_setup(buf: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<SetupRemote>, String> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < buf.len() {
            if buf[i] != 2 {
                return Err(format!("bad local addr_type {} in Setup", buf[i]));
            }
            i += 1;
            if i >= buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (local len)".into()); }
            let lh_len = buf[i] as usize;
            i += 1;
            if i + lh_len > buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (local)".into()); }
            let local_host = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[i..i + lh_len]).to_string();
            i += lh_len;
            if i + 2 > buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (local port)".into()); }
            let local_port = u16::from_be_bytes([buf[i], buf[i + 1]]);
            i += 2;
            if i >= buf.len() || buf[i] != 2 {
                return Err("bad remote addr_type in Setup".into());
            }
            i += 1;
            if i >= buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (remote len)".into()); }
            let rh_len = buf[i] as usize;
            i += 1;
            if i + rh_len > buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (remote)".into()); }
            let remote_host = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[i..i + rh_len]).to_string();
            i += rh_len;
            if i + 2 > buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (remote port)".into()); }
            let remote_port = u16::from_be_bytes([buf[i], buf[i + 1]]);
            i += 2;
            if i >= buf.len() { return Err("truncated Setup (proto)".into()); }
            let proto = buf[i];
            i += 1;
            out.push(SetupRemote {
                local_host,
                local_port,
                remote_host,
                remote_port,
                proto,
            });
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    pub fn send_ping(self: &Arc<Self>, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut s = self.stream.lock().unwrap();
        let frame = Frame {
            fin: true,
            op: OpCode::Ping,
            payload: payload.to_vec(),
        };
        Frame::write(&mut *s, &frame, self.is_client)
    }

    pub fn close_session(&self, id: u64) {
        let mut map = self.sessions.lock().unwrap();
        if let Some(s) = map.remove(&id) {
            s.closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
    }

    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
        self.closed.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    pub fn shutdown(&self) {
        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let s = self.stream.lock().unwrap();
        let _ = s.shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Both);
    }

    /// Main read loop: dispatch WS frames to sessions.
    /// On receipt of an Open message, calls `on_open(target, id)`.
    /// On receipt of a Setup message (reverse remotes), calls
    /// `on_setup(remotes)`. The returned Option<TcpStream> is the local
    /// connection to use for piping data back to the remote (None if the
    /// dial failed).
    pub fn run_loop<F, G>(self: Arc<Self>, mut on_open: F, mut on_setup: G)
    where
        F: FnMut(AddrTarget, u64) -> Option<TcpStream>,
        G: FnMut(Vec<SetupRemote>),
    {
        let mut stream_clone = match self.stream.lock() {
            Ok(g) => g.try_clone().expect("clone"),
            Err(_) => {
                // Mutex poisoned — transport state is unrecoverable.
                self.closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
                return;
            }
        };
        let tag = self.tag.clone();
        loop {
            if self.closed.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                break;
            }
            let frame = match Frame::read(&mut stream_clone) {
                Ok(f) => f,
                Err(e) => {
                    if !self.closed.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                        log::info(&tag, &format!("read loop end: {}", e));
                    }
                    break;
                }
            };
            match frame.op {
                OpCode::Binary => {
                    if frame.payload.is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let mtype = frame.payload[0];
                    if frame.payload.len() < 9 {
                        log::err(&tag, "frame too short");
                        continue;
                    }
                    let id = u64::from_be_bytes(frame.payload[1..9].try_into().unwrap());
                    let plen = u16::from_be_bytes([
                        frame.payload[9],
                        frame.payload[10],
                    ]) as usize;
                    if frame.payload.len() != 11 + plen {
                        log::err(&tag, &format!("frame length mismatch ({} != {})", frame.payload.len(), 11+plen));
                        continue;
                    }
                    let payload = &frame.payload[11..11 + plen];
                    match mtype {
                        MSG_OPEN => {
                            let target = match AddrTarget::decode(payload) {
                                Ok(t) => t,
                                Err(e) => {
                                    log::err(&tag, &format!("Open decode: {}", e));
                                    let _ = self.send_raw(&encode_msg(MSG_CLOSE, id, &[]));
                                    continue;
                                }
                            };
                            log::debug(&tag, &format!("Open id={} -> {}:{}", id, target.host, target.port));
                            match on_open(target.clone(), id) {
                                Some(local) => {
                                    let sess = Arc::new(Session {
                                        id,
                                        local: Some(local),
                                        target,
                                        closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
                                    });
                                    self.sessions.lock().unwrap().insert(id, sess.clone());
                                    let m = self.clone();
                                    std::thread::spawn(move || {
                                        m.pipe_local_to_remote(id, sess);
                                    });
                                }
                                None => {
                                    log::info(&tag, &format!("Open id={} rejected (dial failed)", id));
                                    let _ = self.send_raw(&encode_msg(MSG_CLOSE, id, &[]));
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        MSG_DATA => {
                            // Look the session up under the lock, clone the
                            // local stream, then write *outside* the lock: a
                            // slow TCP consumer must not stall the whole
                            // multiplexer (this is the single reader thread).
                            let writer = {
                                let map = self.sessions.lock().unwrap();
                                match map.get(&id) {
                                    Some(sess) => {
                                        Some(sess.local.as_ref().and_then(|l| l.try_clone().ok()))
                                    }
                                    None => None,
                                }
                            };
                            match writer {
                                Some(Some(mut local)) => {
                                    if let Err(e) = local.write_all(payload) {
                                        log::debug(&tag, &format!("session {} write err: {}", id, e));
                                        // Re-lock only to drop the dead session.
                                        self.close_session(id);
                                    }
                                }
                                Some(None) => { /* known session, local not dialed yet: drop */ }
                                None => {
                                    // Unknown session; tell peer to close.
                                    let _ = self.send_raw(&encode_msg(MSG_CLOSE, id, &[]));
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        MSG_CLOSE => {
                            self.close_session(id);
                        }
                        MSG_PING => {
                            let _ = self.send_raw(&encode_msg(MSG_PONG, id, payload));
                        }
                        MSG_PONG => { /* keepalive ack */ }
                        MSG_SETUP => {
                            match Self::decode_setup(payload) {
                                Ok(remotes) => {
                                    log::info(&tag, &format!("Setup: {} reverse remote(s)", remotes.len()));
                                    on_setup(remotes);
                                }
                                Err(e) => {
                                    log::err(&tag, &format!("Setup decode: {}", e));
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        _ => log::err(&tag, &format!("unknown msg type {}", mtype)),
                    }
                }
                OpCode::Ping => {
                    let pong = Frame {
                        fin: true,
                        op: OpCode::Pong,
                        payload: frame.payload.clone(),
                    };
                    let mut s = self.stream.lock().unwrap();
                    let _ = Frame::write(&mut *s, &pong, self.is_client);
                }
                OpCode::Close => {
                    log::info(&tag, "WS Close received");
                    break;
                }
                OpCode::Pong => {}
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        self.shutdown();
        // mark all sessions closed
        let map = self.sessions.lock().unwrap();
        for (_, s) in map.iter() {
            s.closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
    }
}

/// Encode a tunnel message: [type][id][len][payload]
pub fn encode_msg(mtype: u8, id: u64, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(11 + payload.len());
    v.push(mtype);
    v.extend_from_slice(&id.to_be_bytes());
    let len = payload.len();
    if len > u16::MAX as usize {
        // truncate would be a bug; just send 65535 chunk
        v.extend_from_slice(&u16::MAX.to_be_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(&payload[..u16::MAX as usize]);
    } else {
        v.extend_from_slice(&(len as u16).to_be_bytes());
        v.extend_from_slice(payload);
    }
    v
}

/// Convenience: dial a host:port with a connect timeout.
pub fn dial(target: &AddrTarget) -> std::io::Result<TcpStream> {
    let addr = format!("{}:{}", target.host, target.port);
    let mut last_err = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, "no addresses");
    for sa in addr.to_socket_addrs()? {
        match TcpStream::connect_timeout(&sa, Duration::from_secs(10)) {
            Ok(s) => {
                let _ = s.set_nodelay(true);
                return Ok(s);
            }
            Err(e) => last_err = e,
        }
    }
    Err(last_err)
}

```rust
//! Parses the chisel `<remote>` spec.
//!
//! Syntax:
//!   <local-host>:<local-port>:<remote-host>:<remote-port>/<proto>
//!   R:<local-interface>:<local-port>:<remote-host>:<remote-port>/<proto>
//!   stdio:<remote-host>:<remote-port>   (client stdio -> remote)
//!
//! Defaults:
//!   local-host  = 0.0.0.0
//!   local-port  = remote-port
//!   remote-host = 127.0.0.1
//!   proto       = tcp

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Proto {
    Tcp,
    Udp,
}

impl Proto {
    pub fn from_str(s: &str) -> Option<Proto> {
        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "tcp" => Some(Proto::Tcp),
            "udp" => Some(Proto::Udp),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Proto::Tcp => "tcp",
            Proto::Udp => "udp",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Remote {
    pub reverse: bool,
    pub local_host: String,  // "stdio" is special
    pub local_port: u16,
    pub remote_host: String,
    pub remote_port: u16,
    pub proto: Proto,
}

impl Remote {
    pub fn parse(spec: &str) -> Result<Remote, String> {
        let spec = spec.trim();
        if spec.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty remote".into());
        }
        let (reverse, rest) = if let Some(rest) = spec.strip_prefix("R:") {
            (true, rest)
        } else if spec == "R" {
            return Err("reverse remote without body".into());
        } else {
            (false, spec)
        };

        // split off protocol suffix
        let (rest, proto) = match rest.rsplit_once('/') {
            Some((l, p)) => (l, Proto::from_str(p).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown proto: {}", p))?),
            None => (rest, Proto::Tcp),
        };

        let parts: Vec<&str> = rest.split(':').collect();
        let (local_host, local_port, remote_host, remote_port);

        match parts.len() {
            // "remote-port"  (forward, port-only)
            1 => {
                local_host = "0.0.0.0".into();
                remote_port = parse_port(parts[0])?;
                local_port = remote_port;
                remote_host = "127.0.0.1".into();
            }
            // "remote-host:remote-port" or "local-port:remote-port"
            2 => {
                if parts[0].parse::<u16>().is_ok() {
                    // first is a port number -> local-port:remote-port
                    local_host = "0.0.0.0".into();
                    local_port = parse_port(parts[0])?;
                    remote_host = "127.0.0.1".into();
                    remote_port = parse_port(parts[1])?;
                } else {
                    local_host = "0.0.0.0".into();
                    remote_port = parse_port(parts[1])?;
                    local_port = remote_port;
                    remote_host = parts[0].into();
                }
            }
            // "local-port:remote-host:remote-port"
            3 => {
                local_host = "0.0.0.0".into();
                local_port = parse_port(parts[0])?;
                remote_host = parts[1].into();
                remote_port = parse_port(parts[2])?;
            }
            // "local-host:local-port:remote-host:remote-port"
            4 => {
                local_host = parts[0].into();
                local_port = parse_port(parts[1])?;
                remote_host = parts[2].into();
                remote_port = parse_port(parts[3])?;
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("invalid remote spec: {}", spec)),
        }

        if remote_port == 0 {
            return Err("remote-port must be non-zero".into());
        }

        Ok(Remote {
            reverse,
            local_host,
            local_port,
            remote_host,
            remote_port,
            proto,
        })
    }

    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {
        let r = if self.reverse { "R:" } else { "" };
        format!(
            "{}{}:{}:{}:{}/{}",
            r,
            self.local_host,
            self.local_port,
            self.remote_host,
            self.remote_port,
            self.proto.as_str()
        )
    }
}

fn parse_port(s: &str) -> Result<u16, String> {
    s.parse::<u16>()
        .map_err(|_| format!("invalid port: {}", s))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn port_only() {
        let r = Remote::parse("3000").unwrap();
        assert!(!r.reverse);
        assert_eq!(r.local_port, 3000);
        assert_eq!(r.remote_port, 3000);
        assert_eq!(r.remote_host, "127.0.0.1");
        assert_eq!(r.local_host, "0.0.0.0");
    }
    #[test]
    fn host_port() {
        let r = Remote::parse("example.com:3000").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.remote_host, "example.com");
        assert_eq!(r.remote_port, 3000);
        assert_eq!(r.local_port, 3000);
    }
    #[test]
    fn full_forward() {
        let r = Remote::parse("192.168.0.5:3000:google.com:80").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.local_host, "192.168.0.5");
        assert_eq!(r.local_port, 3000);
        assert_eq!(r.remote_host, "google.com");
        assert_eq!(r.remote_port, 80);
    }
    #[test]
    fn reverse() {
        let r = Remote::parse("R:2222:localhost:22").unwrap();
        assert!(r.reverse);
        assert_eq!(r.local_port, 2222);
        assert_eq!(r.remote_port, 22);
        assert_eq!(r.remote_host, "localhost");
    }
    #[test]
    fn proto() {
        let r = Remote::parse("1.1.1.1:53/udp").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.proto, Proto::Udp);
        assert_eq!(r.remote_port, 53);
    }
}

## `crates/tunnel/src/server.rs`

[view on disk](crates/tunnel/src/server.rs)

```rust
//! Chisel server.
//!
//! - Listens on a TCP port for WS upgrade requests.
//! - Authenticates the client via the `Auth:` header (token).
//! - Receives Open messages from the client and dials the requested
//!   target (forward remotes).
//! - Optionally listens on local ports for *reverse* remotes; when a
//!   connection arrives, asks the client (over the same WS) to dial
//!   and pipe.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::log;
use crate::mux::{self, Mux};
use crate::remote::Remote;
use crate::ws;

pub struct ServerConfig {
    pub listen: String,
    pub auth: Option<String>,
    pub reverse: bool,
    pub reverse_remotes: Vec<Remote>,
    pub keepalive: u64,
}

/// Is a requested reverse remote allowed by the server policy?
/// - `reverse == false`: nothing is allowed.
/// - empty `reverse_remotes`: everything is allowed (reverse enabled
///   without an explicit allow-list).
/// - otherwise: an entry must match a configured remote on port, and on
///   host too when the policy names a concrete (non-wildcard) host.
fn reverse_allowed(policy: &[Remote], r: &mux::SetupRemote) -> bool {
    policy.iter().any(|p| {
        p.local_port == r.local_port
            && (p.local_host.is_empty()
                || p.local_host == "0.0.0.0"
                || p.local_host == r.local_host)
    })
}

pub fn run(cfg: ServerConfig) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind(&cfg.listen)?;
    log::info("server", &format!("listening on {}", cfg.listen));

    for sock in listener.incoming() {
        let sock = match sock {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(e) => {
                log::err("server", &format!("accept: {}", e));
                continue;
            }
        };
        let auth = cfg.auth.clone();
        let reverse = cfg.reverse;
        let reverse_remotes = cfg.reverse_remotes.clone();
        let keepalive = cfg.keepalive;
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            handle_client(sock, auth, reverse, reverse_remotes, keepalive);
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn handle_client(
    mut sock: TcpStream,
    auth: Option<String>,
    reverse: bool,
    reverse_remotes: Vec<Remote>,
    keepalive: u64,
) {
    let peer = sock.peer_addr().map(|a| a.to_string()).unwrap_or_default();
    let tag = format!("server[{}]", peer);

    // WS handshake
    let custom_headers: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    match ws::server_handshake(&mut sock, auth.as_deref(), &custom_headers) {
        Ok(_) => log::info(&tag, "WS upgrade OK"),
        Err(e) => {
            log::err(&tag, &format!("handshake failed: {}", e));
            let body = format!("Unauthorized: {}\n", e);
            let resp = format!(
                "HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{}",
                body.len(),
                body
            );
            let _ = sock.write_all(resp.as_bytes());
            return;
        }
    }

    let mux = Mux::new(sock, false, tag.clone());

    // Keepalive pinger
    if keepalive > 0 {
        let m = mux.clone();
        let tag_ping = tag.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || loop {
            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(keepalive));
            if m.is_closed() { break; }
            if let Err(e) = m.send_ping(b"ka") {
                log::debug(&tag_ping, &format!("ping err: {}", e));
                break;
            }
        });
    }

    // Run the mux loop.
    //  - on_open:  client asked us to dial a target (forward remote).
    //             Unless --reverse is disabled, we also allow reverse
    //             Open messages from the client (i.e. the client dials
    //             on our behalf); this is the symmetric Open path and
    //             is always permitted.
    //  - on_setup: client wants us to listen on a list of reverse ports
    //             and forward incoming connections back to it — only for
    //             remotes the server's reverse policy allows, and only
    //             on THIS client's mux.
    let m2 = mux.clone();
    let tag2 = tag.clone();
    // This client's own mux, moved into the on_setup closure so reverse
    // connections are piped through the same session table the read loop
    // dispatches on (no shared "latest client" slot).
    let setup_mux = mux.clone();
    m2.run_loop(
        move |target, id| {
            log::info(&tag2, &format!("session {} -> dial {}:{}", id, target.host, target.port));
            match mux::dial(&target) {
                Ok(s) => Some(s),
                Err(e) => {
                    log::err(&tag2, &format!("dial {}:{} failed: {}", target.host, target.port, e));
                    None
                }
            }
        },
        move |remotes| {
            for r in &remotes {
                if !reverse || !(reverse_remotes.is_empty() || reverse_allowed(&reverse_remotes, r)) {
                    log::err(&tag, &format!(
                        "reverse remote {}:{} not permitted by server policy; rejecting",
                        r.local_host, r.local_port
                    ));
                    // Signal the rejection on the wire: a CLOSE for the
                    // Setup message's session id (0).
                    let _ = setup_mux.send_raw(&mux::encode_msg(mux::MSG_CLOSE, 0, &[]));
                    continue;
                }
                let mux = setup_mux.clone();
                let listen_addr = format!("{}:{}", r.local_host, r.local_port);
                let target = mux::AddrTarget {
                    host: r.remote_host.clone(),
                    port: r.remote_port,
                };
                let tag_listen = tag.clone();
                std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    let listener = match TcpListener::bind(&listen_addr) {
                        Ok(l) => l,
                        Err(e) => {
                            log::err("server", &format!("reverse bind {} failed: {}", listen_addr, e));
                            return;
                        }
                    };
                    log::info(&tag_listen, &format!("reverse listening on {} -> {}:{}", listen_addr, target.host, target.port));
                    for sock in listener.incoming() {
                        let sock = match sock { Ok(s) => s, Err(_) => continue };
                        if mux.is_closed() { break; }
                        let id = mux.alloc_id();
                        if let Err(e) = mux.open_session_dial_later(id, target.clone()) {
                            log::err("server", &format!("reverse open send: {}", e));
                            continue;
                        }
                        let sess = Arc::new(mux::Session {
                            id,
                            local: Some(sock),
                            target: target.clone(),
                            closed: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
                        });
                        mux.sessions.lock().unwrap().insert(id, sess.clone());
                        let m = mux.clone();
                        let t = tag_listen.clone();
                        std::thread::spawn(move || {
                            m.pipe_local_to_remote(id, sess);
                            let _ = &t;
                        });
                    }
                });
            }
        },
    );
}

## `crates/tunnel/src/sha1.rs`

[view on disk](crates/tunnel/src/sha1.rs)

```rust
//! Minimal SHA-1 implementation (FIPS 180-4) for the WebSocket handshake.
//! This is for the Sec-WebSocket-Accept hash only — not a general security
//! primitive — so a textbook implementation is fine.

pub fn sha1(input: &[u8]) -> [u8; 20] {
    let mut h0: u32 = 0x67452301;
    let mut h1: u32 = 0xEFCDAB89;
    let mut h2: u32 = 0x98BADCFE;
    let mut h3: u32 = 0x10325476;
    let mut h4: u32 = 0xC3D2E1F0;

    // Pre-processing: pad to a multiple of 64 bytes.
    let ml_bits = (input.len() as u64) * 8;
    let mut msg = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() + 72);
    msg.extend_from_slice(input);
    msg.push(0x80);
    while msg.len() % 64 != 56 {
        msg.push(0);
    }
    msg.extend_from_slice(&ml_bits.to_be_bytes());

    for chunk in msg.chunks_exact(64) {
        let mut w = [0u32; 80];
        for i in 0..16 {
            w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([
                chunk[i * 4],
                chunk[i * 4 + 1],
                chunk[i * 4 + 2],
                chunk[i * 4 + 3],
            ]);
        }
        for i in 16..80 {
            w[i] = (w[i - 3] ^ w[i - 8] ^ w[i - 14] ^ w[i - 16]).rotate_left(1);
        }

        let mut a = h0;
        let mut b = h1;
        let mut c = h2;
        let mut d = h3;
        let mut e = h4;

        for i in 0..80 {
            let (f, k) = if i < 20 {
                ((b & c) | ((!b) & d), 0x5A827999u32)
            } else if i < 40 {
                (b ^ c ^ d, 0x6ED9EBA1)
            } else if i < 60 {
                ((b & c) | (b & d) | (c & d), 0x8F1BBCDC)
            } else {
                (b ^ c ^ d, 0xCA62C1D6)
            };
            let temp = a
                .rotate_left(5)
                .wrapping_add(f)
                .wrapping_add(e)
                .wrapping_add(k)
                .wrapping_add(w[i]);
            e = d;
            d = c;
            c = b.rotate_left(30);
            b = a;
            a = temp;
        }

        h0 = h0.wrapping_add(a);
        h1 = h1.wrapping_add(b);
        h2 = h2.wrapping_add(c);
        h3 = h3.wrapping_add(d);
        h4 = h4.wrapping_add(e);
    }

    let mut out = [0u8; 20];
    out[0..4].copy_from_slice(&h0.to_be_bytes());
    out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&h1.to_be_bytes());
    out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&h2.to_be_bytes());
    out[12..16].copy_from_slice(&h3.to_be_bytes());
    out[16..20].copy_from_slice(&h4.to_be_bytes());
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn empty() {
        assert_eq!(hex(&sha1(b"")), "da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709");
    }
    #[test]
    fn abc() {
        assert_eq!(hex(&sha1(b"abc")), "a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d");
    }
    fn hex(b: &[u8]) -> String {
        b.iter().map(|x| format!("{:02x}", x)).collect()
    }
}

## `crates/tunnel/src/transport.rs`

````rust
//! DB-transport wrapper over the vendored chisel tunnel.
//!
//! The RomaCode database tools talk to local databases (the built-in engine)
//! and to remote ones (postgres / mysql / mongodb / redis behind a chisel
//! tunnel). Instead of forcing the agent to manage a separate chisel process,
//! this module runs the tunnel **in-process** on a background thread and
//! hands back a local `host:port` the db tools connect to as if it were a
//! local database.
//!
//! Typical flow (from `romacode-server`):
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use romacode_tunnel::Tunnel;
//!
//! // forward a remote postgres (5432 on db.internal) to a local ephemeral port
//! let t = Tunnel::forward("tunnel.romacode.dev:8080",
//!                         "db.internal:5432",
//!                         Some("token".into()))?;
//! let local = t.local_addr(); // e.g. "127.0.0.1:5432"
//! // db_use profile pointing at local, then db_query hits the remote DB.
//! ```
//!
//! The tunnel is bidirectional — `Tunnel::reverse` lets the server side dial
//! back through a chisel client (the `R:port:host:port` syntax), which is how
//! you reach a database that lives behind a NAT.

use crate::client::ClientConfig;
use crate::remote::Remote;
use crate::server::ServerConfig;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::JoinHandle;

/// One live tunnel. Dropping it stops the background thread.
pub struct Tunnel {
    local: String,
    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    handle: Mutex<Option<JoinHandle<()>>>,
}

impl Tunnel {
    /// Forward a remote endpoint through a chisel server to a local port.
    ///
    /// * `server`  — chisel server address, e.g. `"tunnel.example.com:8080"`
    /// * `remote`  — remote target as a chisel remote spec, e.g.
    ///               `"db.internal:5432"` or `"5432:db.internal:5432"`
    /// * `auth`    — optional shared token (must match the server's `--auth`)
    ///
    /// The local listener binds on `127.0.0.1:<same port as remote>` when the
    /// remote spec pins a port; otherwise an ephemeral port is chosen by the
    /// OS and reported via [`Tunnel::local_addr`].
    pub fn forward(server: &str, remote: &str, auth: Option<String>) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let r = Remote::parse(remote).map_err(|e| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, e))?;
        let local = format!("127.0.0.1:{}", r.local_port);
        let cfg = ClientConfig {
            server: server.to_string(),
            auth,
            headers: HashMap::new(),
            remotes: vec![r],
            keepalive: 25,
            max_retry: 0, // do not retry forever inside the server process
        };
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let stop_t = stop.clone();
        let handle = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("romacode-tunnel-client".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let _ = crate::client::run(cfg);
                // run() returns when the tunnel ends; mark stopped so the
                // owner can detect the tunnel is gone.
                stop_t.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            })?;
        Ok(Self { local, stop, handle: Mutex::new(Some(handle)) })
    }

    /// Run a chisel *server* that exposes the local machine's ports to remote
    /// clients. Used by `romacode-server tunnel server` so a remote RomaCode
    /// instance can reach this machine's local DBs.
    pub fn serve(listen: &str, auth: Option<String>, reverse: bool) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let cfg = ServerConfig {
            listen: listen.to_string(),
            auth,
            reverse,
            reverse_remotes: Vec::new(),
            keepalive: 25,
        };
        let local = listen.to_string();
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let stop_t = stop.clone();
        let handle = std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("romacode-tunnel-server".into())
            .spawn(move || {
                let _ = crate::server::run(cfg);
                stop_t.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            })?;
        Ok(Self { local, stop, handle: Mutex::new(Some(handle)) })
    }

    /// The local address db tools should connect to.
    pub fn local_addr(&self) -> &str { &self.local }

    /// `true` when the background thread has exited (tunnel broken).
    pub fn is_stopped(&self) -> bool { self.stop.load(Ordering::SeqCst) }

    /// Stop the tunnel. Best-effort: chisel's blocking `run` has no cancel
    /// handle, so this drops the thread and lets it finish its current
    /// operation. A subsequent bind to the same local port will work.
    pub fn stop(&self) {
        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        // We cannot truly cancel the blocking accept; detaching is the safest
        // option. The thread becomes orphaned and will exit when the
        // connection drops.
        if let Ok(mut g) = self.handle.lock() {
            if let Some(h) = g.take() {
                let _ = h.join();
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Tunnel {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.stop();
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn forward_parses_remote_spec() {
        // We don't actually start a tunnel here (no server to connect to);
        // we just verify the remote spec is accepted and the local port is
        // derived. The Tunnel::forward call will spawn a thread that fails
        // to connect, but is_stopped will become true quickly.
        let t = Tunnel::forward("127.0.0.1:1", "5432:db.internal:5432", None);
        // Port 1 is privileged — bind will fail, but the parse path runs first.
        // We accept either Ok (thread spawned) or an immediate io error.
        match t {
            Ok(t) => {
                assert_eq!(t.local_addr(), "127.0.0.1:5432");
                t.stop();
            }
            Err(_) => { /* connection refused is acceptable in a unit test */ }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn remote_spec_with_invalid_input_errors() {
        let r = Remote::parse("not a remote spec at all !!!");
        assert!(r.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn remote_spec_simple_port_parses() {
        let r = Remote::parse("5432").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.local_port, 5432);
    }
}

```rust
//! RFC 6455 WebSocket — handshake + binary framing, std-only.
//!
//! Server side:
//!   read GET, validate Upgrade, compute Sec-WebSocket-Accept, reply.
//! Client side:
//!   send GET, read response, validate Sec-WebSocket-Accept.
//!
//! Framing: implements text/binary/close/ping/pong with masking on the
//! client side and unmasked frames on the server side, per RFC 6455.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::net::TcpStream;

use crate::base64;
use crate::sha1;

const WS_GUID: &str = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11";
const WS_PATH: &str = "/chisel";

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Handshake {
    pub accept_key: String,
    pub auth_header: Option<String>,
}

/// Compute the server's Sec-WebSocket-Accept value for a client key.
pub fn accept_key(client_key: &str) -> String {
    let mut cat = String::from(client_key);
    cat.push_str(WS_GUID);
    let h = sha1::sha1(cat.as_bytes());
    base64::encode(&h)
}

/// Constant-time string equality: XOR-folds every byte of both inputs
/// (zero-padded to the longer length) plus the length delta into one
/// accumulator, so timing does not reveal where two tokens first differ.
fn ct_eq(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
    let (a, b) = (a.as_bytes(), b.as_bytes());
    let mut acc: u64 = (a.len() as u64) ^ (b.len() as u64);
    let n = a.len().max(b.len());
    for i in 0..n {
        let x = a.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0) as u64;
        let y = b.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0) as u64;
        acc |= x ^ y;
    }
    acc == 0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Server handshake (read request, write response)

pub fn server_handshake(
    stream: &mut TcpStream,
    auth_token: Option<&str>,
    custom_headers: &HashMap<String, String>,
) -> Result<Handshake, String> {
    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
    loop {
        let n = stream.read(&mut byte).map_err(|e| format!("read: {}", e))?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Err("client closed before WS handshake".into());
        }
        buf.push(byte[0]);
        if buf.len() >= 4 && &buf[buf.len() - 4..] == b"\r\n\r\n" {
            break;
        }
        if buf.len() > 65536 {
            return Err("headers too large".into());
        }
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);
    let mut lines = text.split("\r\n");
    let start = lines.next().unwrap_or("");
    if !start.starts_with("GET ") {
        return Err(format!("expected GET, got: {}", start));
    }
    let path = start.split(' ').nth(1).unwrap_or("");
    if path != WS_PATH {
        // We accept any path that doesn't conflict with our health check.
        if path != "/health" && !path.starts_with(WS_PATH) {
            return Err(format!("unexpected path: {}", path));
        }
    }

    let mut headers: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(idx) = line.find(':') {
            headers.insert(
                line[..idx].trim().to_ascii_lowercase(),
                line[idx + 1..].trim().to_string(),
            );
        }
    }

    // Validate Upgrade + Connection
    let upgrade = headers.get("upgrade").map(|s| s.to_ascii_lowercase());
    let connection = headers.get("connection").map(|s| s.to_ascii_lowercase());
    if upgrade.as_deref() != Some("websocket")
        || !connection
            .map(|c| c.split(',').any(|t| t.trim() == "upgrade"))
            .unwrap_or(false)
    {
        return Err("not a websocket upgrade".into());
    }

    let client_key = match headers.get("sec-websocket-key") {
        Some(k) => k.clone(),
        None => return Err("missing Sec-WebSocket-Key".into()),
    };

    // Token auth: client sends it as Basic-like header, or in a custom
    // "Auth" header, or as ?token= query string. We accept the custom
    // header "Auth" or "Authorization: Bearer <token>".
    if let Some(tok) = auth_token {
        let got = headers.get("auth")
            .cloned()
            .or_else(|| {
                headers
                    .get("authorization")
                    .and_then(|a| a.strip_prefix("Bearer ").map(|s| s.to_string()))
            })
            .or_else(|| {
                // ?token= on the path
                path.split('?').nth(1).and_then(|q| {
                    q.split('&')
                        .find_map(|kv| {
                            let (k, v) = kv.split_once('=')?;
                            if k == "token" { Some(v.to_string()) } else { None }
                        })
                })
            });
        let ok = match got.as_deref() {
            Some(g) => ct_eq(g, tok),
            None => false,
        };
        if !ok {
            return Err("authentication failed".into());
        }
    }

    let accept = accept_key(&client_key);

    let mut resp = String::new();
    resp.push_str("HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n");
    resp.push_str("Upgrade: websocket\r\n");
    resp.push_str("Connection: Upgrade\r\n");
    resp.push_str(&format!("Sec-WebSocket-Accept: {}\r\n", accept));
    for (k, v) in custom_headers {
        resp.push_str(&format!("{}: {}\r\n", k, v));
    }
    resp.push_str("\r\n");
    stream
        .write_all(resp.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| format!("write: {}", e))?;

    Ok(Handshake {
        accept_key: accept,
        auth_header: None,
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Client handshake (write request, read response)

pub fn client_handshake(
    stream: &mut TcpStream,
    host: &str,
    port: u16,
    auth_token: Option<&str>,
    headers: &HashMap<String, String>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let key_bytes: [u8; 16] = rand16();
    let client_key = base64::encode(&key_bytes);

    let mut req = String::new();
    req.push_str(&format!("GET {} HTTP/1.1\r\n", WS_PATH));
    req.push_str(&format!("Host: {}:{}\r\n", host, port));
    req.push_str("Upgrade: websocket\r\n");
    req.push_str("Connection: Upgrade\r\n");
    req.push_str(&format!("Sec-WebSocket-Key: {}\r\n", client_key));
    req.push_str("Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n");
    if let Some(tok) = auth_token {
        req.push_str(&format!("Auth: {}\r\n", tok));
    }
    for (k, v) in headers {
        req.push_str(&format!("{}: {}\r\n", k, v));
    }
    req.push_str("\r\n");
    stream
        .write_all(req.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| format!("write: {}", e))?;

    // read response
    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
    loop {
        let n = stream.read(&mut byte).map_err(|e| format!("read: {}", e))?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Err("server closed before WS handshake".into());
        }
        buf.push(byte[0]);
        if buf.len() >= 4 && &buf[buf.len() - 4..] == b"\r\n\r\n" {
            break;
        }
        if buf.len() > 65536 {
            return Err("headers too large".into());
        }
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf);
    let mut lines = text.split("\r\n");
    let status = lines.next().unwrap_or("");
    if !status.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 101") {
        return Err(format!("bad WS response: {}", status));
    }
    let mut resp_h: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        if let Some(idx) = line.find(':') {
            resp_h.insert(
                line[..idx].trim().to_ascii_lowercase(),
                line[idx + 1..].trim().to_string(),
            );
        }
    }
    let expected = accept_key(&client_key);
    let got = resp_h
        .get("sec-websocket-accept")
        .ok_or("missing Sec-WebSocket-Accept")?;
    if got != &expected {
        return Err(format!(
            "Sec-WebSocket-Accept mismatch (expected {}, got {})",
            expected, got
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Frame I/O

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OpCode {
    Continuation,
    Text,
    Binary,
    Close,
    Ping,
    Pong,
}

impl OpCode {
    fn from_byte(b: u8) -> Option<OpCode> {
        match b & 0x0f {
            0x0 => Some(OpCode::Continuation),
            0x1 => Some(OpCode::Text),
            0x2 => Some(OpCode::Binary),
            0x8 => Some(OpCode::Close),
            0x9 => Some(OpCode::Ping),
            0xA => Some(OpCode::Pong),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    fn to_byte(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            OpCode::Continuation => 0x0,
            OpCode::Text => 0x1,
            OpCode::Binary => 0x2,
            OpCode::Close => 0x8,
            OpCode::Ping => 0x9,
            OpCode::Pong => 0xA,
        }
    }
}

pub struct Frame {
    pub fin: bool,
    pub op: OpCode,
    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Frame {
    /// Read one frame from the stream. The stream may be either masked
    /// (client->server) or unmasked (server->client); both are handled.
    pub fn read<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> Result<Frame, String> {
        let mut hdr = [0u8; 2];
        read_exact(r, &mut hdr).map_err(|e| format!("frame hdr: {}", e))?;
        let fin = hdr[0] & 0x80 != 0;
        let op = OpCode::from_byte(hdr[0]).ok_or("invalid opcode")?;
        let masked = hdr[1] & 0x80 != 0;
        let mut len = (hdr[1] & 0x7f) as u64;
        if len == 126 {
            let mut ext = [0u8; 2];
            read_exact(r, &mut ext).map_err(|e| format!("frame ext len: {}", e))?;
            len = u16::from_be_bytes(ext) as u64;
        } else if len == 127 {
            let mut ext = [0u8; 8];
            read_exact(r, &mut ext).map_err(|e| format!("frame ext len: {}", e))?;
            len = u64::from_be_bytes(ext);
        }
        let mask = if masked {
            let mut m = [0u8; 4];
            read_exact(r, &mut m).map_err(|e| format!("frame mask: {}", e))?;
            Some(m)
        } else {
            None
        };
        if len > 64 * 1024 * 1024 {
            return Err(format!("frame too large: {}", len));
        }
        let mut payload = vec![0u8; len as usize];
        read_exact(r, &mut payload).map_err(|e| format!("frame payload ({}): {}", len, e))?;
        if let Some(m) = mask {
            for (i, b) in payload.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                *b ^= m[i & 3];
            }
        }
        Ok(Frame { fin, op, payload })
    }

    /// Write a frame. If `mask` is true (client -> server), payload is
    /// masked with a random key.
    pub fn write<W: Write>(w: &mut W, frame: &Frame, mask: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut hdr = Vec::with_capacity(14);
        let mut b0 = if frame.fin { 0x80 } else { 0 };
        b0 |= frame.op.to_byte();
        hdr.push(b0);

        let len = frame.payload.len();
        let mask_bit = if mask { 0x80 } else { 0 };
        if len < 126 {
            hdr.push(mask_bit | (len as u8));
        } else if len <= u16::MAX as usize {
            hdr.push(mask_bit | 126);
            hdr.extend_from_slice(&(len as u16).to_be_bytes());
        } else {
            hdr.push(mask_bit | 127);
            hdr.extend_from_slice(&(len as u64).to_be_bytes());
        }
        if mask {
            let m = rand16_arr();
            hdr.extend_from_slice(&m[..4]);
            w.write_all(&hdr).map_err(|e| format!("write hdr: {}", e))?;
            let mut masked = Vec::with_capacity(frame.payload.len());
            for (i, &b) in frame.payload.iter().enumerate() {
                masked.push(b ^ m[i & 3]);
            }
            w.write_all(&masked).map_err(|e| format!("write payload: {}", e))?;
        } else {
            w.write_all(&hdr).map_err(|e| format!("write hdr: {}", e))?;
            w.write_all(&frame.payload).map_err(|e| format!("write payload: {}", e))?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn read_exact<R: Read>(r: &mut R, buf: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut read = 0;
    while read < buf.len() {
        let n = r.read(&mut buf[read..])?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof,
                "EOF mid-frame",
            ));
        }
        read += n;
    }
    Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A simple PRNG for masking keys. Not cryptographic — RFC 6455 only requires
// the mask be "difficult to predict" to avoid cache poisoning on
// intermediaries; the tunnel itself is auth'd at handshake time.

fn rand16() -> [u8; 16] {
    let mut a = rand16_arr();
    // Take 16 of 32 bytes
    let mut out = [0u8; 16];
    out.copy_from_slice(&a[..16]);
    a.rotate_left(16);
    out
}

fn rand16_arr() -> [u8; 32] {
    // 32-bit xorshift seeded from time + pid + a counter
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
    static STATE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
    let mut s = STATE.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    if s == 0 {
        let t = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)
            .unwrap_or(1);
        s = t.wrapping_mul(2_862_933_555_777_941_757).wrapping_add(1);
    }
    let next = {
        let mut x = s;
        x ^= x << 13;
        x ^= x >> 7;
        x ^= x << 17;
        x
    };
    STATE.store(next, Ordering::Relaxed);

    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    let mut x = next;
    for chunk in out.chunks_mut(8) {
        x ^= x << 13;
        x ^= x >> 7;
        x ^= x << 17;
        chunk.copy_from_slice(&x.to_le_bytes());
    }
    out
}
```
